remarks: Water ~1ft high above substrate, ~4m east from Toad River. 2m from river's edge small amount of Phalaris along edge. Not a floating mat. Wet meadow edge 10-20m wide. Black spruce/ tamarack is beyond that. Firm close to river's edge but more spongy away from.
Forest in ravine in pasture. Probably recoverable. Very little buckthorn.
Outermost zone of large calcareous fen on large peat mound. Located between low sedge zone on mound flank and Phalaris -dom'd creek bottom. Water table presently below ground surface.
Downslope flank of peat mound in calcareous fen. Water at ground surface and in several small pools. Soil surface very whitish with marl deposits. Plants very stunted.
In wettest zone on top of calcareous fen mound. Water table at ground surface.

Prairie on upper part of lower half of slope in small ravine near Chanarambie Ck. Last grazed over 50 years ago. No herbicide use; no fire in recent decades. Heavy thatch of dead graminoids present. On loamy till of Bemis Moraine.
Prairie on level ground w/in Chanarambie Ck. Valley. Never grazed. Hayed in late season +/- annually. Some burns including a burn in May 2006.
Floating mat in seep on toe slope on side of Chanarambie Ck. Valley.  Within hammered pasture. Amorpha forms fringe on edge of floating mat. Cows do not venture into this part of the wetland.
Seepage zone on mineral soil on toe slope on side of Chanarambie Ck. Valley. Some trampling by cows present. Within a heavily grazed pasture.
Prairie on upper hillslope that has never been grazed. Brome invasion from roadside. Burned in spring 2006. On gravelly loam formed in Des Moines Lobe till.
Fen on toe slope. Very wet w/ abundant pools. Much marl accumulation on surfaces of peat in pools.
Outer zone of calcareous fen in formerly grazed pasture. Located near top of long ravine. Very saturated and slightly springy. On deep fibric peat.
Meadow in middle of a draw. Much groundwater present at soil surface. Very hummocky. Grazed in past; now managed by SNA.

Mid slope on steep W-facing hillside. Thinly-vegetated sandy-gravelly soil - approx 10% of ground surface is bare sand/gravel patches. In actively grazed pasture on steep slopes bordering Yellow Medicine River Valley. Soils formed in glacial outwash.
Seepage meadow on toe slope on side of Yellow Medicine River Valley. In formerly grazed pasture on glacial outwash deposits. Water table is at the surface between Carex hummocks.

place_name: Hole in the Mountain Preserve Main
remarks: At upper end of lower half of slope. Site was last grazed 2-3 decades ago. Managed w/ periodic controlled burns. Presently has heavy Poa thatch. On till of Verdi position of Des Moines Lobe just SW of Bemis Moraine. Season has been very dry and plants are somewhat stunted.
Mesic prairie on nearly level ground. Past mowing for native seed.

place_name: Hole in the Mountain Preserve North
remarks: Burned in late spring this year. Tremendous floral display. On steep hillside on S. edge of town of Lake Benton. On soil formed in gravelly till.

place_name: Hole in the Mountain WMA W
remarks: Seepage wetland in bottom of small ravine. Zone is ~20 m wide total. Water presently at the ground surface (this during a droughty year). Slight slope to W.
Fen on toe slope along Kanaranzi Creek Valley. Several small pools present w/ standing water and lined w/ Rhynchospora.
Meadow on shallow slope w/ groundwater seepage in Kanaranzi Ck. Valley. Adjacent to calcareous fen.
A very rare example of ungrazed dry prairie. Excellent diversity. On dry knoll.
Ungrazed prairie on small hill in corner of section. A few large boulders present. Burned in spring. This is as good as it gets.

Prairie on very shallow slope in Flandreau Creek Valley. Located ~25 m west of old road. To W. it grades into sedge meadow and cattail marsh. Probably was grazed many years ago before acquisition as WMA. Cypripedium candidum abundant in dense thatch. Frequent gopher mounds present. Notes: Big healthy Formica mound nearby. WP seems to be on a shallow terrace here.

Nearly level forest 65-75% canopy coverage dominated by a few large bur oak, basswood, elm, and green ash. Subcanopy and shrub layers sparse with hackberry, elm, hawthorne, and common elderberry. Ground layer continous with wood nettle, cleavers, and sweet cicely dominant. Former pasture with few signs of wood cutting evident (>40YBP). Tree diameters were recorded.
Prairie on nearly level ground just 10 m N. of old R.R. bed. On better-drained upland surrounded by reed canary grass. Site was grazed in the past before WMA acquisition.

Dry-mesic woodland on ice ridge, east side of Bergdahl Lake rising approx. 1 meter higher than forest area to east. Oldest trees open grown bur oak w/ small elm, hackberry, scattered. Hawthorn most common sub-tree. Shrub layer moderage-sparse with diverse ground layer.

Floodplain forest along Watonwan River. nearly continuous to continuous canopy dominated by silver maple. Subcanopy sparse and includes boxelder and hackberry. Shrub layer also sparse and short with gooseberry, currant, elder, and (wh.) mulberry. Ground layer is species rich and of good quality for his community type.

npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: Nearly closed to closed canopy forest in floodplain of Blue Earth River. Cottonwood, elm, green ash, hackberry and basswood are dominant canopy trees some reaching 50" DBH. Subcanopy dominated by young ash, elm, hackberry and hawthorn in area. Ground layer dominated by wood nettle, Virginia waterleaf.
Nearly closed to closed canopy forest on slightly rolling on ridge over Blue Earth River. Dominant trees include red oak with lesser amounts of basswood.

Terrace forest just upslope of Blue Earth River with large trees forming complete canopy. Given somewhat high ranking due to lack of invasives and good overal species composition. Throughout all structural layers. Notes: Several trees w/in 2m of plot >23"DBH. Given high rank due to good species richness quality structure and lack of invasives in area.
Diverse forest with large red (pin) oak, diverse, structurally as well. Forest occurs on MN/DOT property on slope over Blue Earth River. Ground layer diverse. Few to no invasives in entire forest.

Prairie between CR2 and Union Pacific RR. Approximately 3/4 mile west of Butterfield. Prairie was part mowed by road maintener in 2008. Dry-mesic prairie with purple prairie clover, big bluestem, and Indian grass most common. Substantial amount of gravel at soil surface. Notes: Other nearby areas are more species rich, but of a size/configuration that makes releve sampling impractical.

High quality mesic prairie approximately 200 meters west of intersection of CR116 and RR R/W. Co dominant plants include big bluestem, Indian grass, switchgrass and approximately 10 species of forbs, including rattlesnake master.
High quality mesic prairie along highway 4 just south of Echo, on DNR WMA. Species rich.
Dry-mesic prairie within WMA on west side of Hwy 4 - Dominant grass is big bluestem.
Nice quality mesic prairie between Hwy 4 and DNR WMA. site is slightly crowned, topographically.
Wet(-mesic) prairie between Hwy 4 and WMA - inclusion of wet-mesic prairie in mesic prairie polygon.
Wet meadow/wet prairie on mineral soils within floodplain.
Very nice, dry, sand-gravel prairie.
Good quality mesic prairie between State Hwy 22 and Canadian Pacific rail line. Some minor nonnative grass and weed levels here. Supports population of ~50 Eryngium yuccifolium.
Nice quality prairie in RR-ROW.

Area of drying mud 0.5-3.0 cm deep in bottom of deep depression on top of Sioux Quartzite bedrock. This depression was a 20 cm deep rainwater pool in early June. Mud presently has cracked dry crust on top w/ moist mud below. Soil 1 Texture: Shallow silt over bedrock.
Growing in 1-3 cm moist, drying mud on bottom of deep depression on top of Sioux Quartzite bedrock. Was a rainwater pool in early June. Soil 1 Texture: Silt over bedrock.
In active pasture on level bottomland just W. of creek. Very hummocky. Phalaris abundant along ck. margin but sparse elsewhere. Soil 1 Texture: Black silt.
In low portion of gap between areas of Typha marsh. Water table at ground surface. Soil 1 Texture: Black Peaty Muck.
On higher ground w/ shallow slope. Surrounded by wetter ground w/ much Typha. Located just to E. of tall Salix clump.
E facing slope just below former RR track. To E, this grades into wet meadow.
Standing water ~ 10-20 cm deep between cattail clumps. urrounded by wet meadow.

Level meadow on slightly higher terrace w/in broad, shallow drainageway. Lower ground to W. in middle of drainage has dense Phalaris cover. Formerly grazed. Water table presently just at ground surface and soil is quite wet. On very shallow slope and slightly wetter ground than surrounding areas due to groundwater seepage.
Low wet area of meadow. Water table at ground surface. Along creek w/in broad drainageway. Former pasture
In very wet, bouncy portion of large seepage wetland on long shallow W-slope near top of drainageway. Within active pasture. Upwelling groundwater.
Seepage wetland within active pasture. Not very bouncy here. Water table below ground surface. Soil 1 Texture: Peaty muck/mucky peat.
On nearly level ground on bottom of broad river valley. Grazed in the past. Water table presently below the ground surface. Soil 1 Texture: Silt loam black and gummy. Definitely a mineral soil.
On bottom of drainageway adjacent to flowing creek. Grazed in past. Water table presently below ground surface.

Prairie in managed area that was grazed this spring. Controlled burns in recent years. Boulders present on ground surface. Releve done by 8 people on training day. Notes: Litter ~ 1cm thick and continuous. Soil well drained sandy loam w/ gravel. Humus prairie mull.

Water table below surface. Located west of beach ridge on slightly higher level ground between cattail marshes. Soil wet throughout. Broad low zone adj to marshes - lower ground than nearby wet prairie. (i.e. on edge of a broad swale). Saline variant- possibly WPn53d.
In broad, elongated depression between beach ridges. Water table presently at ground surface. Very hummocky underfoot with small hummocks.

On terrace and located ca. 20 feet from Coon Ck. Relatively intact portion of woods that had sel. cutting 30 years ago. Even-aged stand dom by trees 35-45cm dbh. 16 Arisaema dracontium scattered throughout.
Dom'd by semi-open grown oaks. One of best examples of a common community in landscape. Oaks even-aged: 40-50 cm dbh. Heavy leaf litter but little duff

place_name: Hole in the Mountain Preserve East
remarks: Typical stand of open-grown oaks (20-45 cm dbh). Tract is still grazed.

Along steep slope on south side of creek valley. Much light reaching the ground. Dom'd by very open-grown oaks and moderately open-grown Tilia. Smooth brome is at upper end of plot near transition to open field. oaks range from 20-50 cm dbh. Basswood is 35-45 cm dbh. Galium b. also at top end of plot. Stand not typical of NPC type, ecotonal.
Prairie slope on side of Blue Earth River Valley. Ungrazed. Past landowner used to burn it often. Much brome and quack grass at tops and bottoms along ag fields.
Plot straddles top of narrow ridge. Site was grazed several decades ago but not since. In outwash deposit on top of ridge. Notes: 920C2: Clarion-Estherville Complex.

Water table at ground surface. On shallow W-facing slope on side of beach ridge. Notes: Went as far as I could go w/ soil core - ~1 m. Did not hit sand. Very little sand or other grit in upper 1 m. Clayey subsoil at 40+ cm.
On shallow W-facing slope of beach ridge. Water table is just above ground surface. Marl present in upper soil layers. Notes: Several large ant mounds w/ Carex stricta growing on top.

Large forest stand on undulating upland about one mile N. of Wild Rice River Valley. A few old, rotted stumps present. May have had grazing several decades ago. Dominant trees are ~40-50 cm dbh. Oaks have semi-open crowns. Abundant well-rotted deadfalls. Notes: Tallest trees are 22-25 m. tall.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Even-aged forest dom'd by 30-40 cm dbh trees. Scattered woody debris from branches. No stumps visible. Possible clearcut ~50 years ago. Classification uncertain.
On terrace in Blue Earth River Valley. Other parts of stand are dom'd by younger trees. Parthenocissus forms large vines on trees. Downed trees in area. Much rotted debris.

Wetland in elongated depression parallel to beach ridges in the area. Very wet - water table just at the surface. Located near to and probably influenced by Hwy. 102. To NE, grades into cattails. Groundwater feels quite cold. Soils very black and appear to lack marl. Mineral soil at 12+ cm depth.

Long narrow plot on bottom of small ravine that drains S. into Wild Rice R. Length of plot is bisected by 2 ft-wide crek w/ clear, running water. Soils are very moist. Black ash trees reach 45 cm dbh. Much groundwater seepage in places. Notes: Adjacent woods on uplands are young, evenaged basswood/aspen woods w/ much Carex pensylvanica cover (appears past grazed and logged). NPC classification uncertain.

Dom'd by even-aged, mid-aged, multi-stemmed Tilia w/ stems 20-45 cm dbh. Oaks all have dead lower limbs (due to shading?) but top leaves appear healthy. Notes: Soil: Much leaf litter and thin duff layer present. Well-drained, friable sandy loam. Oaks look scrubby - 4 in plot. They are scarce in these woods (due to logging?). Soil =Poppleton loamy sand. NPC Classification uncertain.

On terrace within Wild Rice river Valley. Basswoods are mostly multi-stemmed. Very very dense herbs to 2-3 ft. No Laportea (!?). Notes: Soil-Black, crumbly silt loam. Some leaf litter and virtually 0 duff.

On top of deep deposit of river sand along the Wild Rice River (15-20 ft. above current river level). Dense forest is on SW side of plot. Loose, dry, bare sand on NE side of plot. Typical... Notes: To west is basswood/black ash forest on very sandy soil.
In moist river sand on high (2nd) terrace along Wild Rice River. First terrace is bare, sand/gravel beach along river. Possible Bromus pumpellianus present (looks like B. inermis).

Woods on level terrain near Wild Rice River Valley. Thin canopy - much light reaching ground. Numerous deadfalls. Thin leaf layer; little to no duff. Very sandy soils. Notes: Soils - light brown and very sandy - loamy sand?

On level ground near edge of steep south-facing slope of Wild Rice River Valley. Basswoods even-aged mid-sized, and multi-stemmed. Notes: Several large black ash in the area -don't see green ash. Soil =Poppleton loamy sand.

Level upland near edge of Wild Rice River Valley. Basswood mid-aged and multi-stemmed. On high terrace in W.R. Valley. Notes: Soil - Nice thick 'humusy' soil on top, sandy silt loam below. Soil =Kittson loam.

On terrace near Wild Rice River. Undulating ground surface w/ several flood channels. Channels hold standing water in places. Soils are heavy silty clay and very moist. Many multi-stemmed trees. Notes: Releve located between channels. Canopy measured to 25 m high. Soil: heavy silt or silty clay.
Forest on undulating ground located just E of sand dunes. Oaks are semi open grown and average ~20-30 cm dbh. Canopy tops out just below 20 m.
Large shrubby zone on very shallow slope west of beach ridge. Ground fairly hummocky. Water table well below surface. Numerous ant mounds w/ small black ants.
Meadow in small shallow swale. Located west of toe of beach ridge. Water table well below surface at present. Hummocky surface due to Deschampsia.
Long, narrow fen 10-20 m. wide in N-S zone near top of beach ridge. Water table above ground surface. Shrubs dense and ~2 m. tall
Meadow in shallow depression that is at least 70 m. wide. Water table below ground surface. Dense thatch. Sandy-clayey suboil at 10+ cm deep.
Meadow in lowest, wettest part of swale. Water table presently below ground surface. Silty clay loam subsoil at 10+ cm deep.
Dom'd by semi-open grown oaks just under 20 m. tall. Oak dbh range from 20 to 60. On steep slope facing lake. No signs of logging or recent grazing. Soil = Barnes loam.

Patch in a mosaic with areas of Schoenoplectus acutus marsh and Typha marsh. Grades into wet prairie on slightly higher ground to W. Soil very wet but no standing water present. Very dense thatch present. In marsh-meadow complex on low ground between Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridges. Pair of cranes flying around and bugling. Notes: This NPC forms a fringe on the margins of wetland basins in transition between wet prairie and marsh. See photos. Silty clayey subsoil at 10+ cm deep.

Patch of marsh just S. of dense Typha angust./T. x glauca and just NE of Carex sartwellii. Water table is right at surface - foot prints fill with water. In large wetland complex in low ground between glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridges. Notes: Dense root mass and fibric peat in top 20 cm. Water very cold. At 20-50 cm = sandy clay. At 50-60 cm, I hit very light grey sand w/ whitish clay in it.

In large marsh in low ground beween Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridges. Dense moss cover is suspended in 1 foot of standing water at bases of plants. Dense mat of dead Scirpus stems. In the rain - Dan owes me a beer for this one. Sandy clay at 20+ cm deep.
Fen-like wetland in wetland depression. Water table at ground surface. Notes: White specks in black silty clay. Never hit sand. Silty clay at 50+ cm deep.
Tussock meadow on higher ground near margin of wet meadow basin. Water table is about 1 foot below surface. Silty clay at 50-100+ cm deep.
Wet swale approx. 80 m wide. Standing water about 6 inches deep. To W. in deeper standing water is dense Typha angustifolia/Typha x glauca. Dense Carex thatch ~30 cm deep.
Large shallow basin. Water table just below ground surface. Sedge cover is very, very dense. Dense thatch of dead sedge leaves. Cattails are present in deeper water just to E.

Floating mat of Typha latifolia with open channels. Mat makes up ~80% of area, open channels make up ~20% of area. 20 cm of loose muck over sandy clay mineral soil (as sampled in channels). Top 10 cm of MINERAL soil is strongly colored with organic material. Mineral soil deeper than 10 cm is strongly gleyed, light blue-gray color. Floating mat is ~30 cm thick.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Tip-ups common, much microtopography of +/-15cm. Trees have buttressed roots. Old ATV trail through area, now a game trail. Layer of fine sand at 56-60cm, clay below that from 60-70+cm. Black ash canopy grades gradually into subcanopy.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Local area is a mix of shrub patches and open sedge meadow with a pattern at 15-25 m. Plot is located to capture the shrub and open communities together and is representative of the general (>200m) area. Microtopography of sedge hummocks, 50cm wide x 15cm high. Area is in a broad, shallow depression. Mosses mostly on base of willow and on dead wood. Water table at surface. Borderline between WMn82 and WMs83.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Peat to >1m, sedge origin but tamarack needles are identifiable around 20 cm. Small (<10m) patches of quaking aspen are scattered throughout the general area. Hummocky, microtopoography +/-20cm. Phragmites communis in scattered clumps throughout the area but not in releve. This area may be impacted occasionally by managed hydrology, it is probably very wet in the spring. Last prescribed fire in 2006.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Site is at the crest of a raised peatland. Though not present in the plot, tamarack makes up ~5% of the canopy in the surrounding area. Previous personal experience in this area suggests the peat is >2m thick and subtended by gleyed glaciolacustrine clay. Peat is mostly sphagnum peat but there is a considerable presence of wood in it.

This area appears to be a drainage for the forested peatland that surrounds it. Drainage appears to be to the NNW. About 50m to the west and to the east there is an abrupt transition to conifer swamp (black spruce APn81). Water table at 50cm. Microtopography ~15cm. Mucky peat to >100cm of sedge origin with a lot of wood. Refuge staff recall this area was mowed (hydroaxe) in the winter of 1985 or 1986.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: This area appears to be part of the drainage network for the raised peatland (APn81a) to the west. Hydrology is also likely impacted by spring precipitation and management (Middle CCC Pool) though pool management is probably not a major factor. Mucky peat of sedge origin with a lot of wood. Thin layer of charcoal at 10cm deep. Microtopography ~20cm, higher around alder bases. Water table at 60cm. Aspen are encroaching on this area, scattered trees of <10cm dbh throughout area.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: This appears to be a Northern Poor Fen (APn91) transitioning to a Northern Wet Meadow/Carr (WMn82). Large (~10km) open grown aspen are scattered throughout the area, about half are dead. To the north, west, and south, tamarack become larger and more abundant and an APn81 community starts about 200m away in these directions.  Ditching in the 1920s may have altered the hydrology here, though the nearest ditch is >500m away and plugged by beaver dams. Water table at 35cm.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Wooded community on slope, prairie 10m north, floodplain forest immediately to south. Releve just fits between adjacent communities. Soil is coarse unsorted till. Some non-native species. Slope is steep and there is some shifting soil but overall the slope is held together well by plants.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Floodplain forest. This area probably floods every few years, flooded this spring. Debris piles and litter snagged on trees. Soil is typical of floodplain forests, fine sand and silt in thin layers. Tree seedlings are very abundant. Some scour channels through releve, these are about 30-40cm lower than surrounding area.
Gravel bar on the outside of stream meander. Below bankfull stage. Most species are seedlings or very small. Releve includes edge of river.

High sand bar on the outside of a stream meander, upstream of an oxbow channel. This would have been a point bar before the oxbow was cut off. Mix of prairie and weed species. Sandbar willow is abundant but currently <1m tall. Sand was probably deposited when old channel was active. Upper 11 cm of soil (clay loam) is probably more recent. This releve was positioned above the bankfull stage, this area probably floods only occasionally, about 2m above bankfull.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Bottomland forest between active river channel and old channel. Scour channels give microtopography of about 30cm. Much woody debris, in piles, from flooding. Area was probably flooded this spring. River channel was changed when dam (to the SE) was built. Soil has organic material (mostly from roots) incorporated into the upper 15cm.

Very diverse. Mucky peat over glaciolacustrine clay sediments. Water table is at the level of the hollow bottoms. Some woody debris from broken off trees, a few tip-ups in the area. Mucky peat has a lot of wood remains.

This general area is a mix of alder and willow with many ash, American elm, and balsam poplar scattered. Dense tall shrubs and much downed alder and willow. Outside the releve plot Bebb's willow is more abundant and alder less abundant. Microtopographic variation of 20cm. Water table 20cm below surface. Hydrology does not seem to be impacted by ditch to east.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: General area is a mosaic of dense cedar patches and more open shrubby patches with occasional cedar. Releve was located in a dense cedar patch. Microtopography 20cm. The mineral soil has alternating bands of loamy sand and sandy clay below 40cm, mostly sandy clay. Pit fills with water at 25cm with water entering through loamy sand layer.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Water table 10cm below surface. Releve is representative of the general area, tamarack and black spruce are scattered in the general area, about four trees per hectare. In between FPn73 and WMn82, muck depth and landscape setting favor FPn73. Moving west from releve site the bog birch gradually declines and the alder increases in size and abundance until alder solely dominates about 100m to the west. Microtopography ~15cm.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Microtopography of 40cm. General area's topography is undulating, drier places around here have aspen and balsam fir. Pool-hummock sequences at about 3m apart, hummocks 40cm higher than pools. Pools make up about 20% of area. Few recent tip-ups evident. This releve has a mix of species common to WFn54, WFn55, and WFn64, the best fit is WFn55c. Difficult to classify.

Microtopography (Carex stricta hummocks mostly) of 40cm. Hollows make up about 25% of area. Releve is a good representation of general area but the relative proportions of tamarack, black spruce, and black ash vary. Within 100m of plot it is pretty similar. Lots of wood in the muck.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: In the general area the graminoid layer alternates between Carex stricta dominating and Carex lacustris dominating. Calamagrostis stricta is well represented but has little cover. Microtopography of 15cm (sedge tussocks and around willow). Water table is at surface.

Plot on edge of Clearwater River on old Agassiz lakebed north of Clearbrook. Has swales of silver maple and fresh alluvium, as well as slightly higher ground with more tree spp. and established vegetation. Heavy deer browse. On loamy fine sand.
Large, exposed boulder present in scoured river "back" floodplain. Soil is loamy fine sand. Stand is matrix of 2 types--plot is in scour area.
Adjacent to Clearwater River; vast terrace forest in good condition dominated by Laportea. Dissected by deep natural channels which are currently dry. Found wetland easement signs posted.

Terrace forest with strong graminoid and herbaceous cover composed mostly of black ash and silver maple. First silver along Clearwater River sighted today (below dam @ lake). Some exposed alluvium, otherwise vegetated. This releve represents the lowest part of the terrace. Adjacent upland with grazing. Many patches of prickly ash.

Resurvey of small southwest slope where releve 8389 is sited. Thatch fairly continuous, not much bare soil. Dry year but plants not obviously senescent. Top 10cm soil dark, organic enriched, sandy texture to 60cm, then some gravel. Large (1m diameter) rock is ca. exact center of plot.

Plot in general area of good quality: other parts of site have more exotic grasses and more abundant Solidago canadensis and Helianthus. Scattered Cornus throughout area surrounding plot. Old field ca. 50m to west, cattail marsh ca. 100m to north. overall site level with gentle topography.

Site upland area slightly convex; Artemisia dracunculus on north side of site on more convex area; Liatris aspera, Amorpha canescens, and Symphyotrichum sericeum scattered on east half of site. West half (uphill) has more Carex filifolia, Helianthus pauciflorus. Rocky on north edge.
Prairie (mesic) community dominated by Andropogon gerardii. Original plot twice as large as this plot (200 square miles). Marker in SW corner; bearing to SE corner = 85°, bearing to NW corner = 345°.

Releve to characterize a wet prairie community. Relocated area different in terms of composition from last visit in 1992. Appears to have been burned in past few years. Notes: Lack of litter due to recent burn. JRRNOTE: RELEVE DOT ACTUALLY IN UPn23b ADJACENT TO WPn53b ACCORDING TO MAPPED MCBS PLANT COMMUNITIES. Marker in NW corner of plot; bearing to SW corner is due south, to NE corner is due east.

Releve to characterize dry upland prairie community. Moved releve further east to area similar to data recorded in 1986 releve form. GPS coordinates recorded in UTM Zone 14. Graminoid dominated. SW pt marked; bearing to NW pt = 5°, bearing to SE pt = 95°.

Prairie with increasing amounts of Poa pratensis -- SW corner near GPS pt. Unable to find area described during past site review. Plant assembly did not appear to match what had been documented before. This could be a factor of increasing competition by non-natives. SW corner marked; bearing to NW corner = 0°, bearing to SE corner = 90°.

Wet to mesic prairie community south of active ag. land. Notes: Releve moved from pt. given, since that point was in a different community type. Chose location nearby based on comments by NPS. JRRNOTE: MCBS MAPPED COMMUNITIES SHOWS UPn23b. NOT SURE WHAT ORIG. REL#5190 HAD FOR COMMUNITY. Marker at SW pt; bearing to NW pt = 0°, bearing to SE pt = 90°.

Open prairie community, graminoid dominated. Near original area as described by NPS when original releve was conducted. Not great in terms of forb diversity. Marker in SW corner; bearing to NW corner = 0°, to NE corner = 45°, to SE corner = 90°.

Mesic upland prairie on flat to the east of a north-south running depression of wet prairie. This drainage curves to the south and east of plot. Scattered large rocks and boulders across gently rolling topography.

Mesic upland prairie in slightly rolling topography dissected by minor drainages and depressions. Scattered rocks and boulders. Huge boulder in depression to south of plot. Releve is typical of stand, especially to south of plot; to north is lower quality with snowberry encroachment.

Dry to mesic prairie on mid- to upper slope of a north-south running ridge. East side of ridge is wooded. Plot on west facing grassy slope, which had scattered trees and shrubs at base. Few scattered large rocks and old cow pats scattered along slope. Landowner said plot grazed two years previous.

Wet-mesic prairie on mostly flat, but very shallowly undulating topography. Never plowed. Hayed until two years previous. Stand is typical of matrix community. Some scattered cattail and reed canary grass wet areas. Notes: Approximately one second off from previous releve #7805, according to the GPS, though community is similar. Same location as 9259 done one year later, but different permanent plot markers mark this one.
Upland mesic prairie on nearly level topography. Very slight slope to the SE. Scattered cattail marshes and sedge meadow depressions to north and south of plot.

Dry upland prairie on crest and upper slope of a NW-SE running ridge. Ravines on either side of ridge have shrubby wet prairie and woods. Stand is mostly typical, though some nearby ridge crests are dominated by exotic grasses. Notes: Plot includes crest; so slope is 0-11 degrees.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: This is an attempt to redo releve 7817 originally completed by Fred Harris in 1998. Coordinates from GIS file did not seem to match the map in the original releve form, nor did the area match in terms of plant composition. Moved location to match as best as possible. Note from NPC class field: "right on margin of being WPs54".

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Placed around patch of Eryngium yuccifolium to match notes from N. Sather's original 1989 releve. Coordinates seemed incorrect - new GPS reading taken. This is the only E. yuccifolium patch or plants we can see! Not really representative of the prairie as a whole.

This was a 10x15m plot marked on TNC land. I'm not really sure if it corresponds to a previous releve or some other monitoring that TNC is doing. Matt and I thought we were supposed to do one releve at this site, and this was the only marked plot, so we guessed this was the intended releve location. SW corner is marked w/ a 8" magnetic spike. Also at SW corner is a metal pipe, marking a 10m x 15m plot. We did our plot 10m x 10m.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Grass dominated. Good representation of big bluestem and Sporobolus heterolepis w/ a high diversity of native forbs that are common to community class. Manager says surrounding areas were mowed to control invasives such as butter-n-eggs and Daucus carota. Releve very near area w/ Platanthera praeclara. No orchids found within releve. This is a resampling of an old releve, either 6644 or 7940, or both. Janeen Ruby added stratum codes after the fact (in office, not in field).

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Grass dominated area. Good representation of Bouteloua curtipendula and Liatris aspera along with other grasses and forbs that are typical of UPs13 plant communities, Rhus glabra also found in good abundance and could become a problem if not managed by fire or mowing. JRR added stratum codes during QC process. Observer had not used stratum codes.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Prairie is burned periodically by SNA burn crew from Windom. Owner says there is a clay layer underneath, so it is very wet in the spring. Site had been mowed for hay for many years. Part of a 'Century Farm'. Releve was sited based on coordinates I was given. May not match up exactly w/ Fred Harris' 1998 releve. I was not looking at his form when I sited it. Species composition is somewhat different. Photos taken by J. Ibberson. Kept w/ other prairie monitoring photos. Sara Simmers sited a releve (#9251) here #9251 done in 2008. Location of permanent marker from 2009 should be within 1-2m of 2008 marker. Observer didn't realize that and marked releve again. Permanent markers probably overlap  which could cause confusion in the future.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Mesic prairie dominated by graminoids (Sorghastrum nutans, Andropogon gerardii). Not much height on these two species at this date. Area surrounding is consistent with releve.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Wet meadow to wet prairie overtaken by shrubs with reduced diversity. Dominated by Betula pumila and Potentilla fruticosa.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Wet prairie with aspen moving in (WPn53). GPS readings at all 4 corners (waypoint numbers 239 to 242).

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Dry prairie community dominated by graminoids with diverse forb component. Shrubs sprouting from base, so not sure what recent activities occurred. 4 pts marked w/nails and washers.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Dry prairie community dominated by big blue stem. Forb diversity low. At edge of dense cluster of bur oaks (5"DBH). 4 pts marked with nails and washers.

place_name: Two Rivers Aspen Prairie Parkland SNA
permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Mesic to wet prairie community -- graminoid dominated. 3cm duff/thatch. 4 pts staked.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Wet prairie - shrub dominated (dwarf birch) and graminoid dominant (Muhlenbergia richardsonii). Meter tall aspen moving in. Litter varies within plot, not as thick under shrub component. Notes: Evidence of past burn. Sisyrinchim mucronatum spathe fused, filiform.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Wet prairie community (maybe wet meadow) dominated by Spartina pectinata with Muhlen. rich. with forbs including Gent proc, Aster lanc., Aster eric. Shrubs moving in (willows <1m).

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Wet to mesic prairie dominated by shrubs and experiencing ongoing grazing. Shrubs not grazed with cows cutting paths while targeting herbaceous layer. Plot typical of surrounding area.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Dry prairie community, fairly open and graminoid dominant.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: WP/WM community becoming invaded by woody species, thus affecting composition of herb layer.
Dry prairie with surrounding landscape planted in smooth brome, which is also in this plot. Notes: Releve moved to the one location with native vegetation. Original location all smooth brome.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Mesic prairie with scattered shrubs. Surrounding area ranges from completely open to dense shrubs. Releve placed in area of scattered shrubs.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Uneven surface of large mounds. Mesic brush prairie at margin of more dense shrubs and more open prairie. Smooth brome patch along west side of plot.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Mesic brush prairie within large area of similar vegetation, with field to west and aspen woodland to east. Some patches of shrubs and young aspen also in surrounding area. Recently burned. Notes: In northernmost unit of Higinbotham.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Photo taken from north boundary to south. Mesic prairie on flat topography with shrub (bog birch and shrubby cinquefoil primarily) and aspen encroachment to the east of releve.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Photo taken from north to south. Wet sedge meadow in slight depression, surrounded by small patches of mesic prairie or mesic prairie/wet meadow complex of mixed species composition. Shrubs numerous, but scattered.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Low, mesic prairie west of beach ridge. Consistent, similar species composition in all directions, with even distribution of grasses and forbs. Small depressions of sedges were common within the prairie, and one of these depressions was present in the NE corner of releve.

Dry upland prairie on the upper slope of a large ridge (kame). Surface was gravelly. Bare ground at base of plants probably over 50%. Site is typical of ridge. Recently burned. Notes: Couldn't exactly match composition of original releve. Entire ridge did not have Schi scop patches (though common in park as a whole). Original releve was much larger. Found spot representative of ridge.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Dry prairie. Soil somewhat gravelly at surface. Several gopher mounds in releve. Bare ground 5-15%. Area not grazed but burned regularly.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Dry-mesic prairie on Minnesota River Terrace. Slight depression to east and west. Regularly burned. Scattered boulders.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Dry mesic prairie on level Minnesota River terrace. Burned regularly. Surrounding topography mostly flat, with some shallow depressions with a slightly more mesic composition. Scattered boulders.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Dry-mesic prairie. Near two shallow linear depressions to the west and east (run NW-SE). Mostly flat. Regularly burned.
Flora on this slope is so rich that I can't help but wonder if CCC imported flowers as well as trees.
Level terrace by bench along Indian Creek.

Releve is on an area that is dry enough to walk in between a very active back seep and active discharge on immediate banks of Indian Creek. Typical forest species are associated with the root area of the few woody species. Typical wetland or spring species are in the wetter internal springs. Only one ash tree in releve - dbh 45.

Releve collected as part of MCBS SW MN Forest Foray to acquaint ecologists with SW MN forests. We attempted to get as close as possible to former EJC releve for purposes of comparison. JRRNOTE: ADDED SMILAX ECHIRRATA TO H1-2 STRATUM.
Gentle, open, long terracelike slope irregularly sloping into ravine.

Releve is just far east enough of trail to be out of trail influence zone and still be on the nearly level upland and only very upper slope. Upper slope forests generally severely infested with Rhamnus cathartica.

The upper slopes in this area are severely degraded. D rank with thick buckthorn invasion. This woods would not normally qualify for a releve for plant community classification purposes because of its condition but I wanted to document it. It is interesting to note that this is one of the former pastures that has revegetated since the 1938 photo. (I wonder if they are more subject to invasives 70 years later?!)

Odd releve size because that is the size of the community. This is the "back seep" separated from stream by releve CA05190603 with rivulets running through the latter. Discharge more active in this area. You can hear the water gurgling through. Note: Precision of GPS less precise than description. This is the open, hydrologically active facies.

Attempt to get into what I perceived on photo to be a conifer swamp (tamarack or spruce) but no matter where I go it is dominated by balsam fir. No community type exists for a conifer swamp dominated by fir.
Releve characterizes a very narrow band of fir birch between upland and conifer swamp. This linear transitional community is typical of this physiographic setting in Mahnomen County.

The dot location of this releve is very imprecise. I was uncertain in the field of my exact location but certain of the type of community I was in. West of releve 111-03 and southeast of releves 111-05 and 111-06. Pretty typical of successional woods in this area, sandy soils. Bagley outwash plain. Notes: Predates use of GPS! From back of form: "successional aspen on sandy soil".
Forest in this area more mesic than in section 14 despite being one of higher hills in site. Note that the Acer here is rubrum.
Water depth about 1/2m, rapidly increasing to 1m. Feels as if recently raised. nice Carex meadow but not very diverse.
No idea how to rank - oak woodland in what should be oak savannah zone of county. South end of same stand (out of releve) becomes impenetrable Zanthoxylum.

Releve reflects a small island of mixed forest with pink signature on photos from conifers but may not be typical because of recent beaver work. Later photos suggest actual releve site harvested between 1995 and 2003. Not mapped as MCBS community for that reason.

Accessed site from road. SW of small lake in sec 18 - many open iron-stained pools. I was trying to get over to conifers along Ray Lake Creek. Area is a fairly open minerotropic swamp with tip up hummocks that support the species more typical of northern forests. JRRNOTE: ACORUS CALAMUS NEEDS TO BE MOVED TO DIFFERENT STRATA. ENTERED AS CANT FIND.
This releve is from the far SE end of the conifer swamp. Marvelous liverworts in tipup mounds with Impatiens. Much heavy dead and down impedes quality of releve.

Level, dense black spruce with little "hummock and hollow" microtopography. this is the closed facies? of a wetland system that has much open area. Notes: This work predates GPS. Releve characterizes a community type not an ablsolute location on ground.
Regen. aspen on coarse, sandy soils. Probably a successional phase of FDc25.
This is an example of the predominant mixed hardwood type of the area, somewhat unusual in the absence of elm.
Releve is on mid N facing slope on east side of small ravine. Ravine below releve is heavily overcome with woodies at the base.

Concave area on north facing hill, heavily occupied by large clone of Lespedeza capitata with presence of an apparent hybrid or other Lespedeza. This area should be re-checked for L. leptostachya. Very rank mesic prairie.
Steep south facing, upper slope of forby hill. Much more typical of UPs13d in this region of state than the north-facing slopes, fairly dry in area of releve.
Very forby hill which WMA staff and local contacts all insist is natural. Odd mix of mesic and dry prairie spp. More Coreopsis than I've ever seen in my life.
Releve just east of impoundment, 1st concave N-facing draw. Lespedeza leptostachya previously undocumented in county. This releve in area with small Lespedeza population. Larger population to east.

This long known tiny prairie has a well documented flora in U of M Herbarium but appears to be getting less diverse over time as its size is reduced by various incursions. Some locals believe this is planted but this one is original. Planting is across road. Releve almost same size as prairie remnant. Releve is centered in the middle of the tiny remnant.
Some true silver maple floodplain forest. [Species list only, no cover data].

Along east side of Rock River only 2 miles from Iowa border. Area forested at time of land survey. Acer saccharinum are huge but widely scattered. Some of the largest trees I've ever seen (4 huge trees over a meter diam, one 128cm). Notes: Waypt 24 on map.

About 30 meters from Rock River on level terrace about one meter above river level. No evidence of any recent flooding. Some downed coarse woody debris on sightly undulating terrain with silty soil to about 0.5m, no differentiation of layers. Evidence of nightcrawlers-castings. Mature stand here, very large Celtis. Plot typical of best condition in heterogeneous patch. Likely past grazed.
Litter largely not present. Lower portions appear to be active floodplain. Very degraded floodplain forest dominated by boxelder with scattered green ash and hackberry. Notes: Waypoint 17 on map.

Typical of ~120 acres in large peatland complex east of Goose Lake. Maturing stand, trees 10-30cm dbh, larger ones mostly Larix. No stumps. Windthrow appears to be a periodic disturbance event here. Substrate of wet troughs and mesic hummocks to 24 inches tall. Saturated peat >40cm deep. Grades to areas with more / less cedar.

Typical of broad zone of semi-terrestrial cedar between mesic hardwood forest and cedar swamp. Mature stand: Thuja 20-45cm dbh, Abies to 35cm. Freguent snags, lots of CWD. No stumps. Thick dark organic layer over grey sand with mottles. No surface water.

Typical of better condition (~80 acres) in ~400-acre patch on gently-rolling drumlins south-southwest of Sebeka. Mature stand here, trees 25-45cm dbh. Aspen selectively removed in 1996, scattered stumps remain (also a few older oak stumps). +/-Even-aged, trees often multi-stemmed. CWD sparse. Snags occas. Rocky sandy-loam, few worms, thick leaf litter. Vernal wetlands nearby at this elevation. One of better (and larger) mesic hardwood forest remnants in Wadena County.

Typical of ~80 acres of heterogeneous wet forest on broad terrace in rolling drumlin plain south of Mayo Creek. Saturated fibric peat >35cm deep; wet hollows and moist hummocks to 18 inches high. Occasional very old stumps. Trees 15-40cm dbh. Snags occasional. Moderate amound of CWD. Grades variously to denser black ash, denser black spruce, and areas with more abundant coarse sedges.

Typical of ~35 acres of poor black spruce in shallow ~40-acre basin on rolling drumlin plain south of Mayo Creek. Rather even-aged, trees 5-20cm dbh. Snags rare. No stumps. Sparse CWD. Deep saturated peat (>50cm deep). Hummocks to 24" tall, shallow water in troughs. Pine River Drumlin Plain.

Typical of much of ~100 acres east of old Burlington-Northern railroad grade in large wetland complex on rolling sand plain south of Menahga. Maturing stand, trees 10-30cm dbh, mode 15-20cm. No stumps. No snags. Sparse CWD. Saturated peat >50cm, hummocks to 45cm tall. Quite different from releve 3815 in same wetland, similar setting, ~600m to northwest.

Typical of less dense canopy areas in 100 acres in inter-drumlin wetland along Minn-Can Pipeline. Uneven-aged, trees all sizes, to 30+cm dbh. Few snags. No stumps. Sparse CWD. Deep peat, no surface water. Deer trails deeply cut into peat - no water in them. Notes: Wadena Drumlin Plain.

Typical of denser canopy portions (~40 acres) of ~65-acre patch of tamarack in interdrumlin wetland along the Minn-Can Pipeline. Trees 15-32cm dbh. Deep peat (>50cm deep), no surface water. No stumps. Rather sparse CWD. Snags occas, patchy. Limited windthrow in spots. Naturally depauperate ground layer? Wadena Drumlin Plain.

Best quality portion of fragmented ~50-acre patch on drumlin northeast of Blue Grass. Mid to upper portion of 40-foot, east-southeast-facing slope. Rocky sandy-loam with large boulders. Litter fairly intact, earthworms not abundant. Uneven-aged stand, trees 20-70 cm dbh. No stumps. Sparse CWD. Light grazing history, heavery past grazing across property line ~40m to east.

Lower to mid portion of long, gradual, NW-facing slope of 40-foot drumlin NE of Blue Grass. Even-aged stand ~50 years old, trees 20-35cm dbh, often multi-stemmed. Scattered old stumps. Few snags. CWD rather sparse. Dark sandy-loam with stones. Mesic to moist, moderately well-drained. Wadena Drumlin Plain.

Typical of once extensive patch, now ~50 acres, on level sand plain along the Crow Wing River south of Knob Hill. Trees mostly healthy (10-20% mortality- budworm?), mature, 15-35cm dbh. Snags occasional. Sparse CWD. Shrub layer variable- patchy to rather dense. Moderately coarse sand with shallow organic A horizon.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Typical of slightly higher areas of terrace in ~80-acre patch of alluvial forest along Crow Wing River SE of Knob Hill. Trees 20-45cm dbh. Few snags. No stumps. Sparse CWD. No flooding debris piles. Floods are rare and of short duration. Loamy silt. Abundant earthworm evidence. Microtopography of subtle, elevational undulations of 1-3 feet. Denser patches of Zanthoxylum invading in vicinity (moderate past grazing history?).

Typical of higher quality portion of 30 acres in wetland complex in nearly level sandy terrain (outwash) southeast of Stocking Lake. Immature, even-aged stand, trees 10-25cm dbh. Few snags here, more common elsewhere. No stumps. Some windthrow. Saturated peat >50cm deep. Water in shallow hollows. Plot centrally located in rather narrow strip of swamp. Grades to more mature but more disturbed eastward. Park Rapids Sand Plain.

Typical of 80 acres in inter-drumlin wetland NE of Blue Grass. Saturated quaky peat >50cm deep. No surface water. No stumps or large woody debris. Plot centrally located; south of shallow, hand-dug CCC ditch which apparently has little effect on fen. Carex oligosperma abundant along wildlife trail / CCC ditch, rare/absent elsewhere. Grades to areas with denser and larger tamarack. Wadena Drumlin Plain.

Typical of broad band (~100m wide) of sedge fen on western side of large wetland complex at the junction of the Nimrod Drumlin Plain and Park Rapids Sand Plain (nearly level sandy forested terrain). Deep, saturated, partially-decomposed mucky sedge peat (>40cm deep), water 6" deep in foot tracks. No woody remains on ground or in peat. Plot 50m from upland. Salix cover 25% to the east, dense Typha to the southeast.

Typical of, and centrally located in, 20-acre patch in large inter-drumlin wetland complex southeast of Huntersville. Moderately quaky deep (>40cm) saturated sedge peat. No woody remains. No surface water. Sub-surface water very cold (<40 degrees @ 40cm down). Plot ~100m from small lake, ~75m from upland margin. Nimrod Drumlin Plain (sandy, level to gently-rolling forested terrain).

Typical of, and centrally-located in, ~25-acre patch in large wetland complex on sandy outwash between the Redeye and Crow Wing rivers. Partially decomposed mucky sedge peat (>40cm deep); black, organic, and quite decomposed at 50cm. Water iron-stained; subsurface water icy cold. Widely scattered large old Larix snags. ~5% of shrubs are dead.  Grades to young tamarack swamp to west & southwest (was tamarack swamp prior to fire ~40-50 years ago?), denser and taller willow to east. (Borderline rich shrub fen?)

Typical of denser-canopied portion (~30 acres) in ~60-acre tamarack patch in large wetland complex on Swan Creek Sand Plain. Maturing stand, trees mostly 15-25cm dbh. No stumps. Snags rare. CWD very sparse. Fire-scarred old snag nearby (burned ~40-50 years ago?). Deep peat (>40cm). Iron-stained water in shallow troughs. Tamarack patch expanding into adjacent willow swamp / shrub fen. Not sure if Northern or Southern floristic region?

Typical of, and centrally located in, ~40 acres in irregularly-shaped shallow depression in level sandy outwash. Deep (>50cm), quaky, saturated peat. No old woody remains. Shallow (<2cm) surface water in places; water level has receeded ~5-10cm due to drought. Several small patches of Chamaedaphne ~20m from plot. Scattered willows in northern part of wetland.

Typical of, and centrally located in, ~75 acres on gently-rolling terrain of Verndale Sand Plain. Dark loamy sand. Trees 20-60cm dbh, some open-grown. A few snags. Rare large old stumps. Scattered canopy gaps due to windthrow. Litter intact, few/no earthworms. Likely moderately past grazed. Large old stump nearby with dense patch of Zanthoxylum surrounding it. A few lightly-used ATV trails in larger patch.

Typical of and centrally located, in ~20-acre patch of rich shrub fen along the lower reaches of Cold Creek, at the south end of Lake Plantagenet. Quaky saturatured peat (>40cm deep), no surface water. No large woody remains. Hummocks 18" tall. No surface water; water 5" deep in foot tracks. Plot ~550 feet from lake to north, ~275 feet from creek to west, ~300 feet from tamarack swamp to east. Bemidji Sand Plain.

Typical of, and centrally located in, ~20-acre patch in ~120-acre wetland south of Lova Lake. Rolling Pine River drumlin plain at the edge of the strongly-rolling St. Croix moraine. Grades to a larger and slightly less wet zone with lots of stunted Larix and Picea mariana (mostly snags). Deep (>50cm), saturated peat, moderately quaky. Low hummocks (4-12" tall).No stumps or CWD. Ericads low-statured here(stunted).

place_name: Little White Dog NW - Crow Wing River
remarks: Typical of oak-dominated, mature patches in heterogeneous, ~40-acre stand on terrace ~25 feet elevation above Crow Wing River northwest of Oylen. Plot ~500 feet from river. Trees 20-48cm dbh. A few old conifer stumps. Heavily-wormed sandy soil of the gently-rolling Nimrod drumlin plain. 5cm loamy sand A horizon over pure sand. No humus; leaf litter ~1cm. Snags occasional; CWD rather sparse. 48cm dbh red pine here. Grades to aspen-dominated patches, especially to north/northwest. Does not fit NPC classification very well.

Typical of, and centrally located in, 1/4-mile wide portion of extensive wetland complex in glacial outwash channel on gently-rolling sand plain west of Crow Wing River. Black, moist, silty organic substrate. Hummocks to 10" tall. No surface water (extended drought). Inundated in spring. Plot in larger "opening" between willow patches that cover 10-40% of wetland here. Grades to zones dominated by Carex lacustris.

Typical of, and centrally located in, ~35-acre patch in large wetland complex along glacial outwash channel west of the Crow Wing River; on nearly level sand plain south of Cottingham Park. Dark, well-decomposed, saturated peat >40cm deep, approaching mineral in concistency. No stumps or larger wood remains. No surface water (extended drought). Often more Carex lasiocarpa in adjacent areas. Borderline OPn/WMn. Grades to areas with scattered tamarack to west and northwest, shorter shrubs and open segde patches to east, tall dense willow and alder (and small wet aspen island) to northeast.

Typical of, and near northern end of, ~200 acres in broad glacial outwash channel west of the Crow Wing River; on gently-rolling sand plain south of Cottingham Park. Shallow (~10cm) highly-decomposed organic layer over organic silty mineral soil; saturated, no surface water (extended drought), inundated in spring. No CWD or larger woody remains in peat. Plot ~50m from upland margin. Shrubs (Salix spp., Betula pumila) cover 10-25% of larger wetland.

Typical of ~50 acres in large wetland complex along glacial outwash channel on nearly level sand plain west of the Crow Wing River, southwest of Cottingham Park. Deep (>40cm), partially-decomposed, saturated peat. Thick thatch. No surface water (extended drought); inundated in spring. No stumps. Scattered mature Larix in vicinity. Shrub species abundance somewhat heterogeneous, though shrub cover mostly uniformly tall and dense. Area was likely tamarack swamp in past.

One of the best remaining poor jack pine woodland patches in several county area. Plot typical of best ecological condition (~40 acres) of ~75-acre remnant patch on outwash sand along Crow Wing River south of Cottingham Park. Gently-rolling terrain, subtle southwest-facing slope. Trees mature, mostly 20-38cm dbh; ~20% mortality (jack pine budworm?), mortality patchy. No stumps. Moderate amount of CWD. ATV/OHV trails frequent in greater vicinity, though none in or very near plot.

place_name: Spearhead Lake - Miss. Headwaters Audubon Society
remarks: Typical of ~10-acre patch in rather strongly rolling sandy terrain on northeast side of Spearhead Lake. Plot captures the upper portion of a moderately steep, 50-foot, northeast-facing slope. Substrate: 1cm litter, 2cm humus, over coarse sand. Maturing stand, trees 20-50cm dbh (pines mostly 30-40cm, birch mostly 20-35cm). No stumps. CWD rather sparse. Fire scar on pine snag. Snags very rare. No pine regeneration here.

Typical of moderately large, low sand-gravel bar on banks of Crow Wing River 1/4-mile downstream from Hwy 64 bridge at Motley, just upstream from mouth of Mosquito Creek. Coarse sand and pea-sized gravel exposed by receding water levels, moist just beneath the surface. Top of sandbar 4-6 inches above present river level. Pillager Sand Plain.
This would flush with fire. In 2008 the entire CRP was burned but not the native prairie
This should be a prairie bank. Releve near east end of a set of north facing knolls that are more heavily invaded by woodies at west end, less so here, facing Cottonwood River.
This is a very odd place, just not seeing much anywhere for native grass but some of these forbs don't really seem like old field species (eg Calylophus serrulatus?). Heavy brome.

On slope. Above terrace. East of Indian Creek big seep. This community only classified to MHs because it is atypical of either MHs38 or MHs39 because Acer sacc. Ravine unusually rich in spring flora, which could be because of CCC activity (no documentation).
This area has been privately maintained by fire by a local retired teacher. The remainder of ownership is active pasture.
Wet prairie facies in far northeast corner of site - supported many Cypripedium candidum.
Best examples of prairie are on achial (spelling?) slopes.
Enormous amount of Coreopsis. This would seem to be prime habitat for prairie bush clover though none seen on this visit. Should keep on eye out for it. About as rich as these prairies are.
Degraded woodland bordering Highwater Creek.
Grazed pasture. Overall rating of tract is CD, several C rank knolls, of which this is an example. Survey at request of owner. Converted UTMs to zone 15 266049, 4928519.

Very nice annually hayed wet to wet-mesic prairie in (_blank_).    Cypripedium candidum present in unhayed areas near creek. This should be a prairie bank. Site would probably feel more like wet prairie if not mowed. Notes: Name is an informal designation. May at one time have been offered to TNC and rejected.
East of south end of old gravel pit, west-facing steep slope above stream. Variety of moisture prefs. of species in this rel. reflects steep slope gradient (eg Aster sericeus and Pycnanthemum.)
Very degraded but purpose is to characterize the forest - not presently grazed - to contrast with spring releves from grazed pasture across creek to southwest. Wormed.

Long, linear slope by river across from hunting shack. West side of river knoll. Banks are steep and eroding. The area of the site nearest trail is very poor. Notes: There is UPs23 mapped in the CRP east of the creek, but this entire area is on gravel and is UPs13d.

This stand straddles T105N R34W SESW 02 and T105N R34W NENW 11. The releve was in the latter. This is a remnant of a forest that was on the island in a drained lake (which was about 1.2 miles in diameter). Lake long drained. County Park.
On terrace, north side of Cottonwood River in privately owned portion of most important macrosite in county.

Stand almost restricted to size of a releve. This toe of forest is adjacent to an area locally known as the "Big Spring". This little pocket of sugar maple is the only naturally occurring maple presently documented in the county outside the Camden SP-Lynd area. Maple likely associated with amelioratory effect of the spring. Notes: This releve may classify as MHs49 just as readily as MHs39. I called it 39 to alert us to the island of maple.
This community gets less rich floristically the farther upstream it is from the area where large springs discharge into Cottonwood River and the higher upslope it goes.
Probably in an area that was outside the historic but drained lake bed.

Canopy suggests MHS38 but setting is very odd for it, low lying area that was once on shore of lake. Notes: Geyer (1838) reports oak, basswood, beech (unlikely) ash & hackberry w/ prickly ash in understory. Way 3, still SW of the big pond.

Slightly higher ground, extremely open stand, without leaves both the canopy and subcanopy are very parklike, shrubs very sparse, but groundlayer diversity not as rich as in lower areas. Definitely MHs38. Notes: Tree spp suggest MHs38 despite the unlikely setting.
Edge of ravine. Truly didn't see any graminoids in this plot. This releve is just beyond the area where they presently stopped cutting.

On upper Beaver Creek terrace in contrast with releve upslope on ravine slopes. Notes: This area (...?) subject to flooding (...). It looks like this riparian forest was once elm and is being replaced by boxelder & buckthorn.  Wormed. Way 60 is ~10m east of creek.
Plot is west of group camp, about 1/2 way between road and lake in effort to get into least fragmented area.
Garvin seep on a terrace at base of hill east of lower campground, north of Cottonwood River.
West facing slope in tiny remnant prairie south of south side of Garvin Park.
Notebook comment despite 10 x 10 area: "a species list does not a prairie make."
Very little real prairie remnant in this WMA. Probably would not qualify for a releve, nor the site as a site if not in DNR ownership.
Two things not seen today. Aster umbellatus and Solidago riddellii. Notes: Way 93.
Lovely sedge meadow, very clean. Notes: Way 94. NPS called is WMs83.
Much of this site does not feel "natural". This is as close as it comes to a natural community. Notes: Way 81?
Variable and patchy quality wet prairie north of Minneota. This rel is about as good as it gets in any releve sized area.
Notes: Way 42.
Hill south of and uphill of trees.
NE-facing mid-slope SW of pond right by DNR fenceline. Way 34.
One of best areas for dominance by natives.

In WPA upslope of Brockway tract not far from fence. This area feels as if it was recently burned. Vegetation is overall sparser than would be expected. Majority of WPA appears to be restoration. This area on slope native. Way 47.
Nice level A rank top of slope. Rather unusual. Appears to have perhaps been enhanced by recent fire.
Open knoll just south of oak wooded ravine east of fenceline. Prairie continues on this knoll west of fence.
Probably the best quality slope on tract. Typical dry prairie, not directly impacted by ATV trails. Belamcanda chinensis is a state record of a Eurasian cultivar, probably introduced by landowner.

Not wormed, gentle upper portion of N facing slope, west of highway 59, south of Cottonwood River. The forests in this section give off to prairie at upper slopes. Where no springs one wonders if they might once have been savannah?
No litter here but better cover of forb layer than uphill. This releve and adjacent one illustrate effect of going a short distance downhill from the open degraded prairie. W side of stream.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Typical of ~15 acres in river bend along Crow Wing River southwest of Huntersville. Mostly level terrace 2-5 feet above river level. A few old conifer stumps. Sparse coarse woody debris. Few snags. Maturing stand. Trees 20-35cm DBH (rare 50cm). Loamy silt over sand. Earthworm castings present. Plot ~20m from river. Jack pine woodland on slope above this terrace.

Mature conifer swamp. Borderline AP/FP. Typical of ~70 acres in inter-drumlin wetland. Larix 15-35(45)cm DBH. No stumps. Moderate coarse woody debris. Some windthrow. Scattered snags. Peat >30cm deep. Water 10 cm in hollows. Naturally floristically depauperate?

Mature stand, canopy interrupted due to light selective logging ~5 years ago and recent windthrow. Trees 25-45(50)cm DBH, uneven-aged. Moderate coarse woody debris. Few snags. Typical of ~30 acres on level drumlin top. Loamy soil with boulders. Thick humus. Few earthworms. Would be B- or AB-rank if not for recent selective logging and a few trails.

Typical of ~30 acres in inter-drumlin wetland complex north of Strike Lake. No stumps or old tree remains. Scattered young Larix invading. Deep saturated peat (>40cm). Water 6cm deep in foot tracks. Plot is ~100m north-northwest of releve 3927.

Center zone of inter-drumlin wetland complex north of Strike Lake. Deep saturated peat (>40cm), water to 6cm deep in foot tracks. Tall, firm hummocks (30-60cm high). No stumps or large woody remains. Low shrubs stunted (<30cm tall). Located ~100m south-southeast of releve 3926. Grades to OPn81/92, and then to FPn82.

Plot typical of a semi-connected series of openings in rich shrub fen in large inter-drumlin wetland complex north of Strike Lake. Spongy saturated deep peat (>40cm). Shallow water in foot tracks. No stumps or tree remains. Grades to areas of denser shrubs then tamarack westward, to more open fen eastward (see releve 3927).

Mature stand on ~100-acre drumlin surrounded by wetlands NW of Strike Lake. Edge of plot is ~30m from edge of wetland. Trees 20-40+cm DBH. No stumps. Occasional Pinus banksiana snags. Coarse woody debris rather sparse. No earthworm evidence observed. Loamy sand with thick humus and litter layers. Much of this drumlin on the adjacent state land (WMA) has been recently logged.

Mature stand, typical of better quality ppatches of MHc36 in ~220 acres on level drumlin top. Grades to black ash on lower ground. Trees 30-45(50)cm DBH. Straight boles. No stumps. A few snags. Coarse woody debris rather sparse. Soil is loamy with boulders, worm castings. Moderate grazing 30+ years ago. Selective logging in adjacent parts of this ~220-acre patch.

Typical of better quality forest atop drumlin. Mature uneven-aged stand. Oaks to 55cm dbh, bi-modal (15-35 and 45-55cm dbh). Occas very old stumps. Scattered coarse woody debris (mostly large oaks, due to windthrow). Snags occasional. Black loamy soil with surface boulders, lots of worm castings. Shrub layer sparse-past grazing? Good diversity but ferns too abundant.

Typical of ~20 acres in ancient oxbow of the Straight River at the inlet to Straight Lake. Mature stand. Trees 15-25(40)cm DBH. Continuous Sphagnum, hummocks to 45cm high. No stumps. Few snags. Sparse coarse woody debris. Deep (>40cm) saturated peat. No surface water. Surrounds small seepage fen which occurs in center of 20-acre basin.

Plot typifies subtle seepage discharge area of rich spruce-tamarack on west-facing slope along Toad River. Plot on gently-sloping lower / mid slope; rich conifer swamp extends ~40 feet elevation up the slope (which becomes fairly steep upslope). Marly muck substrate with CaCO3 grit. Subtle seepage flow in plot. Trees 20-40cm DBH. No stumps, scattered snags. Moderate coarse woody debris (windthrow).

Typical of larger of a series of seepage zones along Toad River. Atop and gently-sloping upper slope of 40-foot, west-facing slope. Marly muck >150cm deep, uppermost 2cm iron-oxidized. Strong artesian springs. Cold water. Seepage flows concentrated here. Grades to FPn63. Typha x glauca invading.

Typical of central portion of 1/2-acre opening in FPn63. Quaky sedge peat (over moss peat) >40cm deep; saturated, 6cm water in foot tracks; no marl in upper 40cm. Small seepage flow through plot, major seepage zones at upland margin 150m to northwest, where the seepage outflows are impounded by a beaver dam. Lobelia kalmia and Parnassia palustris added, based on August 2006 notes from this spot.

Typical of better quality portions of 120 acres on 40-foot hill south of Central. Moderately steep, upper west-facing slope. Loamy sand, stones, few worms. Mature woodland here, trees 20-45cm DBH in plot. Moderate coarse woody debris. Scattered snags. Not grazed in past 25 years. Windthrow from mid-1990's windstorm evident in places.

Typical of ~20% of a broad band of sedge fen on eastern shore of Yeager Lake. Typha glauca and Phragmites have invaded ~50% of fen, especially near lake. Plot 25m from upland, 75m from lake. No stumps or woody remains. Small trees very sparse in this zone. Quaky saturated peat >40cm deep, somewhat firmer here than elsewhere in this zone.

Maturing stand, trees 15-25cm DBH. Moderate amount of coarse woody debris, much of it fairly large and highly-decayed. Scattered very old stumps. Snags occasional. Saturated peat (>40cm deep). Microtopography: hummocks (to 35cm) and hollows. Large wetland complex along Leaf River downstream from Redeye River; several ~large patches of this community, grading to FPn63/82. Uncommon community in this part of the state.

Typical of ~60 acres on gently-rolling outwash(?) sand. Fine silty-sand. Thick moss carpet. Natural origin jack pine, trees 15-30cm DBH. Grades to mix of aspen and denser hazel (FDc23/24) in slightly lower areas. No stumps. Sparse coarse woody debris. Minor tree mortality. Scattered natural red pine in vicinity. One of highest quality (ecological condition) remnants in several county area.

place_name: Crow Wing R - Lyons Cemetery S.
remarks: Mature stand, typical of ~160 acres on terrace (drumlin?) along Crow Wing River downstream from Beaver Creek. Jack pine 20-40cm DBH, red pine to 60cm. Some dead jack pine-snags occasional. No stumps. Moderate coarse woody debris. Fire scars and charcoal present. Plot ~25ft elevation above river and ~450ft from river bank.

Typical of ~15-acre terrace in large Crow Wing River oxbow. Maturing stand (~60 years old), trees uneven-aged, 25-45cm DBH. No stumps. Soil tan sand over red/brown sand, gravel at 25cm down, hardpan at 50cm. A few old fire-scarred pine stumps. Moderate amount older and larger coarse woody debris. Tip-up mounds present. Moderate grazing in past? Litter/duff 2cm, A horizon 4cm, O horizon 15cm. Plot ~20 feet above river level.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Typical of ~20 acres in bend of Crow Wing River. On level alluvial terrace, 2-3ft above river level. Hydric soil, dark organic A horizon (25cm) above fine sand with banded iron secretions to >50cm down. Trees bimodal, a few large ones (to 60cm), mostly <20cm DBH. No stumps. Floods infrequent and short duration. Moderate amount of mostly larger coarse woody debris. No flood debris piles.

Typical of, and centrally located in, ~20-acre meadow along the Shell River south of Twin Lakes. Plot ~30m from river and within 1-2 feet above river level. Grades to narrow zones of willow near upland margins. Moderately quaky sedge peat >80cm deep. No surface water (extended drought period). Floods during spring runoff and other high water level events. Grades to Typha monoculture near the river in places. Adjacent uplands sandy.

Typical of ~120 acres on gently rolling outwash sand along the Shell River south of Twin Lakes. Fine sand with 10cm A horizon. Jack pines 15-35(40)cm DBH, minor mortality, snags occasional. No stumps. Moderate coarse woody debris, with fire scars. Grades to FDc24 with dense hazel in places. Logged in 2008 (clear-cut post releve).

Typical of, and centrally located in, ~20-acre stand in large inter-drumlin wetland complex. Deep peat (>60 cm deep), wet 10cm down (extended drought until rain yesterday), 12-24" hummocks and hollows. Uneven-aged, scattered larger trees (to 45cm DBH), most 15-25cm. Few snags. No stumps. Sparse coarse woody debris. Scattered canopy gaps due to windthrow.

Typical of ~3 acres in large inter-drumlin wetland complex. Grades to rich shrub fen (scrub tamarack and bog birch). Quaky, little-decomposed sedge peat >50cm deep; water 7cm deep, ~30cm deep in foot tracks (despite extended drought, but with moderate rain yesterday). No coarse woody debris or any woody remains. Water flow (imperceptably subtle) to south. Phragmites invading (from hydrologic alteration along gravel road 1/8-mile to north).

place_name: Mary Brown Bridge - Crow Wing River
remarks: Typical of ~15 acre floodplain meadow along Crow Wing River at Mary Brown bridge public access. Plot in center of patch, 30m from river channel. Substrate saturated, no surface water (extended drought), floods during spring runoff and other high water events. Peat 12-15cm deep, over fine grey sand (mixed with organic material). No woody remains on or in the peat. Dense thatch. Grades to areas with scattered tall Salix species.

place_name: Mary Brown Bridge South - Crow Wing River
npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Mature stand on Crow Wing River floodplain. Trees 20-40cm DBH. Level terrain with slight undulations. Shallow (7cm)organic silt over fine grey sand with iron concentrations and thin (2-3cm) buried organic horizons. Sand is more coarse at 100cm deep. No stumps. Frequent larger coarse woody debris, small CWD rather sparse. Few snags. Floods are infrequent and short duration. Little/no past grazing evidence.

Maturing stand (50-60 yrs old?) on terrace along the Leaf River. Plot ~50m from river and ~20ft above river level. Trees 20-35(45)cm DBH. No stumps. A few large old boles on ground, otherwise coarse woody debris sparse. Snags occasional. Fine sand. Very little microtopography. Few earthworms. Grades to areas with dense shrubs including Zanthoxylum.

Typical of ~80 acres on broad terrace ~20ft above and 1/4 mile south of the Leaf River. Interesting setting; community uncommon in west-central Mn. Substrate saturated, black mucky organic; low hummocks (<30cm) and shallow hollows. No stumps. Snags infrequent. Moderate amount of coarse woody debris. Trees 15-25cm DBH.

Typical of bluejoint-sedge zones in large wetland complex in glacial overflow channel just west of the Crow Wing River. Grades to willow swamp northward and westward; wetter zones nearly pure Carex lacustris. Semi-saturated, quite firm, highly decomposed sedge peat >50cm deep, no woody remains. Rootwad 15cm deep, thick thatch. Abnormally dry due to extended drought (no water in upper 40cm of peat). Plot centrally located in wetland, ~200m from nearest upland.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Mature floodplain stand in bend of Crow Wing River, debris piles in plot and elsewhere. Remains inundated for moderate duration during high water events. Microtopography of small dips and rises. No swales in plot, though swales occur in vicinity. Soil 25cm of silt over coarse sand with iron concentrations/depletions, buried organic band 32-35cm down. Plot centrally located in long bend, ~75m from river. No stumps. Moderate past grazing history?

Typical of ~25 acres in broad outer zone of 100-acre shallow basin in gently-rolling sandy drumlin plain. Grades inward to low shrub poor fen (releve 3954), then to poor black spruce (releve 3955). Deep (>50cm) slightly quaky peat, moist but no surface water. ~12" of water here on 5 June 2007 (extended drought since then). Mosses dry and shriveled. No woody remains in peat. No hummock formation.

Typical of broad zone between sedge fen (releve 3953) and poor conifer swamp (releve 3955), in shallow, 100-acre basin on gently-rolling sandy drumlin plain. Deep (>50cm), slightly quaky peat, moist but no surface water; ~8" of water here on 5 June 2007 (extended drought since). Mosses dry and shriveled. Hummocks 18-30" high. No stumps or large woody remains.

Typical of ~15 acres in center of shallow 100-acre basin on gently-rolling sandy drumlin plain. Grades outward to scrub conifer poor fen (releve 3954) then to sedge fen (releve 3953). Deep (>50cm) moist peat, no surface water (extended drought since early June). Mosses dry and crunchy. Trees 5-20cm DBH. Occasional snags, sparse coarse woody debris. No stumps. Hummocks 6-18" tall. Grades to areas with more abundant Ledum.

Mature (~80-90 years old), natural origin stand; typical of ~25 acres on nearly level sandy drumlin near the Cat River. Red pines 25-60cm DBH. Snags occasional. Fire scars on dead wood. Fine silty-sand. Thick thatch. Scattered very old stumps. Moderate amount of coarse woody debris. Moderate jack pine mortality. Good future old growth candidate; one of best of the few remaining natural-origin patches of its type I've seen in several county area.

Typical of ~8 acres in small nook of large inter-drumlin wetland complex in gently-rolling sandy drumlin plain. Moderately quaky deep peat (>70cm), saturated despite extended drought. No stumps. No coarse woody debris. Grades to a band of rich fen to west, small Larix patch to east, and elsewhere to denser, taller bog birch. Hummocks to 30" tall.

Typical of and centrally located atop low and rather narrow rise in inter-drumlin wetland. Substrate is fine sand, only a few feet above elevation of adjacent wetlands. Sand is moist ~12" down. Mature stand. Trees even-aged, 18-35cm DBH. A few very old stumps. Frequent snags, ~25% of trees dead. Much coarse woody debris. Thick moss mats. Needs fire (hasn't burned for long time). Very old trail/forest road east of plot.

Typical of ~400 acres in interdrumlin wetland complex, (low sandy drumlins). Plot 20m from outer zone which is wet meadow with dense shrubs, small Larix, and Larix snags. Deep (>50cm) moderately quaky, saturated sedge peat, no surface water (extended drought since mid June). No coarse woody debris or woody remains in peat.

Typical of better quality (ecological condition) portions of ~80-acre patch atop level sandy drumlin along Crow Wing River at Anderson's Crossing.  Plot captures areas with more open shrub layer. Mature stand. Trees 15-35cm DBH, ~10-20% dead. Sparse coarse woody debris. Few very old stumps. Moderately coarse sand >50cm deep; upper 5cm darker (some organics / litter). Grades to FDc24 with more aspen and denser shrubs on slightly lower elevations.

Typical of 80 acres on Crow Wing River floodplain at Walkin's Rapids. Heterogeneous / irregular substrate, ~24" from hummock top to hollow, hollows often large (>2m diameter), peat >40cm, upper 30cm dry (extended drought since June. Trees scattered, cover 5-10% over the ~50-acre community. No stumps. Likely was tamarack and/or ash in past (trees killed by flooding?). Floods during spring runoff and other high water events.

Typical of ~300 square meter sandbar in Crow Wing River at mouth of the Leaf River. Exposed by low flow due to extended drought.
