Sandbar is located in the middle of the river channel, and rises 8-12" above present river level. Coarse sand >50cm deep. Wet muddy silt at downstream end of sandbar (lower elevation, outside of plot).

Typical of poorest zone (~5-10 acres)in heterogenous FP, OP, AP wetland complex on outwash sand west of Crow Wing River. Moderately quaky peat >50cm deep, moist but no surface water (extended drought since June). Trees +/-stunted. No stumps or old / large coarse woody debris. This zone continues to the shore of a shallow lake ~100m to the northeast. Topographic context: Depression/Flat.

Typical of and centrally located in broad zone of tall shrubs bordering a boggy, shallow, ~35-acre lake in outwash sand west of the Crow Wing River. Moist, slightly quaky peat >50cm deep, no surface water (extended drought since mid June). No stumps or large coarse woody debris. Scattered small Larix in vicinity. Alder becomes more abundant toward upland. Plot ~75m from lakeshore, ~100m from upland.

Releve in lower drainage, in flat area. Drainage continues downslope to south from here. Many ephemeral wetlands in forest as well as poorly drained wetter areas such as this releve. Larger forest is dominated by red oak, bigtooth aspen and paper birch. Very hilly topography. Soil: Loamy clay.

Large wetland complex covering 9+ sections of land, largely rich fen but also shrub swamp and wet meadow in varying degrees of quality. Powerline cuts through NE corner near releve. Water at peat level. Peat deep, not floating, but bouncy. Hummocks medium to low. Sedge dominated.

Designated old growth red pine forest. Occasional fire scarred trees. Average red pine DBH 50cm, jack pine average 25-30cm. Topography very hilly, on the Itasca Moraine. Extent of forest is ~160 acres, but landowner to east has cut boundary of property through forest and DNR has cut on west side. No worm evidence. Soil: sandy silt loam.

Stand originating from 1959 fire. Even aged jack pine dominated. Was apparently sheared in past. Shrub layer is patchy and can be heavily overgrown by Corylus americana and Rubus species in other areas nearby which releve does not represent. Good example of FDc23 ground layer. Found Cirsium hillii in 2006, but did not find anymore in 2007.

Forest along Crow Wing River. Fire scarred stumps nearby. Releve near crest of slope. Top slope, more Pinus and Vaccinium. Old tipups and moderate coarse woody debris. Red pine ~50cm DBH. All oaks open-grown looking. Most Tilia multi-stemmed. A few dead jack pine nearby. Soil silty loam.

Small (30ac) designated old growth red pine stand. Soil fine sand. Outside plot are areas with denser fir and Corylus. Logging/ATV roads nearby. Jack pine more common elsewhere in stand. Very diverse strata; occasional stumps nearby. Fire scars. Cutting outside of O.G. stand.

Oaks somewhat open-grown. Fire scars. Rare cut stumps. Birch in canopy multistem. Jack pine ~35-40cm DBH. Red Pine ~60-65cm DBH. Top layer soil sandy loam, then sand. Forest on high "terrace" above Crow Wing River.
Even hummocks of mostly sphagnum. Occasional small cut stump. Very typical Malaxis paludosa habitat. Average Picea DBH = 15-20cm. Water at peat level. Swamp along Hennepin Creek (west side).

Releve in area slightly higher than surrounding cedar - black ash forest (WFn53). Moderate coarse woody debris. No stumps. Fire scars on surrounding cedar, soil silty-loam >5in. Tilia single stem (DBH~55cm). Aspen DBH = 40-45cm.

Releve in narrow wet forest along Necktie Creek. Water level at 3in below substrate. Soil fibric peat. Hummocks even. Sphagnum very patchy. Forest a mix between WF/FP. No stumps in plot, but elsewhere. Average cedar DBH = 30-35cm.

Diverse strata. No white pine regeneration in plot. Heavy shrub layer. Stumps rare. Fire scars. Small area near lake is best part of forest. Soil is sandy with small amount of silt. Some earthworms present in soil pit. Duff layer mostly pine needles. Good amount of coarse woody debris. Designated white pine DNR old growth. Average white pine DBH=60cm. Cutting nearby.
Fairly dry swamp. Even, medium sized hummocks of Sphagnum. Water in shallow holllows. No stumps. Releve east of Paul Bunyan State Forest ~250m. Avergage Larix DBH = 25-30cm.

Releve on small upland (~9.5ac) within larger rich fen/shrub swamp. These areas or islands typical in this part of Sand Plain - near Nimrod Drumlin field. They are often with jack pine and aspen on sandy soils. Most have been cut recently. This one is larger and still intact.  Occacional stumps. Average jack pine DBH = 15-25cm, Red pine = 45-50cm. No pine regeneration.

Releve near shoreline of Spider Lake, on peninsula that juts down from north side. Soil sandy silt, very rocky. Occasional stumps. Many large red and white pines. Average white pine DBH = 80-90cm, Red Pine = 45-55cm. Trail/road follows edge of entire peninsula. A few scattered small wet meadows nearby.

Atypical forest. Feels very mesic but there are a few errant dry species too. No stumps seen. Soil is sandy loam. Thin leaf litter. This upland is not much higher than surrounding wetland. Aspen seems even-aged. Canopy bur oaks appear open-grown. Heavy shrub-layer is patchy. Oaks DBH ~45-50cm. Forest also has mix of central and northern species.

Alnus cover ~70%. Channels and hollows filled with ~1in water. Exposed channels are very rocky. Small amount of sphagnum on hummocks. Tops of large hummocks have many drier species. Releve ~20-30m west of upland. Swamp fairly extensive ~200ac +/- running north/south. Alnus swamp averages 300m wide along upland and grades to extensive rich fen to west.

Mesic forest dominated by sugar maple, American elm, and basswood. Sugar maple dominates in all levels. Ground layer probably more diverse but site was visited later, missing the spring ephemerals. One of best spots in the small forest.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: High quality oak-basswood forest with some American elm. No sugar maple present. Canopy continuous. Shrubs patchy. Ground layer continuous and dominated by Virginia waterleaf. Several other spring ephemerals present. Slope moderately steep with a north-facing aspect.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Slightly south-facing hill top above Clear Lake. Late spring this year so few herbaceous plants visible. The soil is dark, silty loam. Average tree dbh around 40-50cm dbh. Site dominated by red oaks.
Forest dominated by black walnut. Canopy mostly continuous with basswood and ash also present. Shrub layer interrupted to continuous. Ground layer patchy to interrupted. Site has rich, moist soil.

Marsh dominated by Scirpus fluviatilis. Other species present but not nearly as dominant include: Sagittaria latifolia, Polygonum spp., and Scirpus acutus. In spring water level 6+ inches deep. Late summer no standing water, but ground spongy.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: This site is a mesic oak forest with an increasing sugar maple component. The largest trees tend to be open grown. There is a large and diverse number of seedlings and saplings. Ground layer diverse, with woody debris. Soil is soft, silty loam.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: The site is a mesic oak forest with influence of floodplain forest and wet-mesic forest species. Older trees moslty forest grown, a few large red elms present. Ground layer fairly diverse. Sugar maple is starting to dominate. Soil is soft (not-compacted), silty loam.

Occasional exposed boulders. Moderate-good coarse woody debris. Diverse strata, no stumps seen in releve area. Mature forest. This releve highlights a slightly lower spot that is common throughout with more diversity and less well-drained soil. Soil in tip-ip is very silty-loam (clay content). Soil is light brown-tan, and very smooth with just minor grit. Populus in canopy is >55cm DBH.

Gently rolling here at releve on west side of LaSalle Creek. Many low areas near here, some ephemeral pools. No cut stumps in releve area. Fire scarred elsewhere in stand. Avg. DBH for Populus tremuloides = 45-50cm.

Occ. cut stump. Soils are fine sand. Pipeline at bottom of slope. Looked for ram's head - none. 1 trail/road cuts through drainage area through the stand. Lots of downed fir. Stand has a very northerly feel.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Releve in even-aged aspen/red oak forest. Typical for this area on this upper part of the slope. Very little shrub layer. Fire scarred stumps. Scattered boulders at surface. Avg. red oak is 47-55cm DBH. Leaf litter somewhat thin. Soil is loam >5in. Mod. CWD.

Large, straight cedars. Sphag. covered med to low hummocks and other feathermosses. Occ stumps. Springs and seeps nearby - close to slope with upland. Avg DBH for cedar = 55-60cm. Mucky hollows. Not much cedar reg'n.

Tilia straight and mostly single stem. Mostly flat terrain here. Occasional charred stumps. Red oaks appear open grown. Occasional medium sized boulders exposed at surface. Moderate coarse woody debris. Shrub layer and understory fairly diverse, but northwest 300m there is a dramatic shift where there is no shrub layer and ground is dominated by Acer saccharum seedlings. Sandy loam soils here.

Occ stumps. 1939 air photos indicate this area was cut around that year. Some fire scars on tree bases and stumps. Soil is mostly pure sand. Ground covered in Pleurozium, Cladina, and Dicranum. Some jack pine mortality. Mod CWD. Canopy gaps common. Avg JP DBH = 30-35cm.

Fire scars on red pines. Average DBH for red pine = 50-55cm. Soil is sandy in the upper 7 inches. Scattered medium sized boulders at soil surface. Dramatic ridges nearby drop steeply to valley floor. This area is designated old growth red pine. 2 red pines cored nearby (not in plot) were ~100-110 years old.

Fire scarred stumps. Occasional medium sized boulders exposed at soil surface. Dense groundlayer, seems like an overgrown woodland. Soil is sandy - sandy loam. Northeast of here on same hillside - quickly changes to red pine dominated.
Releve typical of old-growth cedar-basswood forest. With Jeff Hines. Duff very thick, O-G coarse woody debris, natural gap in center of plot. Soils silt loam over straight clay, stoneless. Bt to 1 m.

This is a strip of the WMA that is a retired ROW (tracks have been pulled out). The actual rail corridor has grown up in woody plants. This releve represents a very good quality piece of the otherwise degraded strip. I would call this B rank prairie, whereas remainder of strip is D rank. Note the presence of state special concern Rattlesnake Master in this site. This species is near its westernmost present-day natural limits in this county.
Soil rocky/pebbly loam to ~1ft, then very silty-sand. Mod-high CWD. No stumps. Mod amount of leaf litter - but worm evidence. Mod sized boulders exposed at surface of soil. ATV trail nearby.

Very nice and diverse. No stumps seen. Largest red pines ~60-67cm. Some red paint on pines - designated old growth.~81m east of Movil Lake shoreline. Releve only with slight slope, but surrounding area with gentle-mod hilly terrain. Could easily classify as MHc26a.

This entire slope that stretches along NE facing is very nice - designated old growth. No stumps seen. This gently trans. to cedar swamp. Open shrub layer. Soils sandy. Continues for awhile to top of slope but then becomes young aspen. This OG stand is small, older patch surrounded by mosaic of younger age classes, some recently cut.

Soil sandy loam. Varying age classes. Lots of trails (ski/log). However there are lots of large red pines. Some areas are slightly more mesic. But overall this is pretty representative of area. Stumps (BIG!) are common. Often fire scarred. Occ. jack pine.

Low, even hummocks. Hollows w/ shallow water. Sphagnum and feathermoss dominated. Large cedars ~40-45cm DBH. Canopy patchy 60-70% cover. Quite a bit of fir in understory. Releve in typical FPn63b, but walking east, becomes less diverse closer to FPn82. Approx 150 meters east of railroad tracks.
Occ cut stumps. Some fire scarred. Old logging road. - Areas of slight disturbance - old logging? Jack Pine dying out.

Sedge mat @ edge of small pond. Water @ and slightly above peat surface. Dom by brown mosses and Mnium moss. Tamarack get larger and more frequent away from lake as well as Arethusa. Calopogon close by.

Sphagnum dom hummocks w/ occ mucky hollows - not much standing water. Quite a few dead Larix that are ~25ft tall. this habitat seemingly goes for quite a while, does not change much. Photo indicates much farther out that tall shrubs may decrease w/ Chamaedaphne increasing.

Lots of CWD - old tribal sugarbush. Heavily wormed. Loamy soil. Goldies fern goes beyond releve and into a depression leading to poor fen - sort of a drainage. But larger forest is very similar, just not as many ferns or wet forest spp.

Narrow sedge dom. mat around small interior lake. Stunted Larix gradually trans. to larger cedar swamp. Sedge mat is approx 15-30ft wide. Near here, under open canopied Larix that surrounds lake, are 100's of Calopogon. Mat is dom by sphagnum and some brown mosses. Sphagnum is >50%. Water is at peat level.
Calopogon number in the hundreds throughout this low part of swamp. Med high hummocks. Water at peat level.

Water becomes present only in middle of wetland, otherwise very dry. Heavy thatch. Small amt. of sphagnum. Somewhat transitioning from wet meadow to rich fen. Quite a bit of Spirea along edge. More wet meadow-like along edge.
Stumps occ, fire scarred. Patchy mosses. Sandy soil. No pine regeneration. Many ski/snowmobile trails throughout.
Earthworms, some stumps in plot, red pine cut long ago, conifers decline to west, deer trails through releve.

Soil is a mucky peat with much wood in it. Between stream (50m to west) and upland. Surrounding area has patchy shrub and sedge meadow communities at the 100s of meters scale. Phalaris arundinacea is in the plot and forms dense colonies in the surrounding area. Plot is near a road (Nelson Dam Road).
Standing dead willow stems w/ resprouts, somewhat hummocky. Broken dead willow branches. Releve in area of fen margin which does not key out well to OPn91.
Somewhat hummocky esp. at base of willows. Standing dead willow stems to 3 meters.

Bordering water track. Inclusion in shrub-willow dominated  area with many dead willow. Water table within 6 inches from surface. Sedge peat to 3 ft. Hemic to sapric w/ woody fragments. Charcoal fragment at surface. Occasion mod cushions.
Open-broad rich fen between larger patches of shrub fen. Water table @ surface. Uniform substrate. Hemic to 2 1/2 ft. w/ woody fragments.

Margins of Miller Creek - a braided stream flowing through peat. Adjacent to forested bog dominated by black spruce. Plot dominated by subshrubs on spongy sedge peat. Sphagnum mounds have interrupted cover with scattered graminoids and forbs.

pH=8.1 Shrubs and scatterd tamarack within 5 meters of plot. Surface spongy, sink to 10-12cm when standing in plot. Sedge peat barely decomposed to 40cm. 2 frog species adult/juvenile wood frog??, flushed 2 snipes and eastern kingbird.

Hummocks 1 1/2 - 2 ft. high. Water @ peat level in hollows. Bare spots without sphagnum has Chamaedaphne leaflitter. Not much open moss cover. Very dense shrub cover. Releve done in adjacent spot ~30m away in a wetter, bouncier spot with less dense shrub/hummocks.

Between upland and mineral island ~300-400ft from upland. Top 25cm comprised of coarse living roots and stems and leaves - sphagnum peat only top layer directly under surface layer. 25-50cm sapric partially decomposed, twigs. Lower section >50cm higher amount of roots again from Chamaedaphne? Transitioned from tall alder along upland edge. It spanned about 100ft ring.

Occ large sphagnum clumps >1-2ft. Open pools several (~4in?) deep. Soil pit shows mostly roots material ~0-25 - living woody roots and brown mosses; 25-40cm - fine sedge roots and old woody stems and roots, living rhizomes; >40-75cm - fiber and some leaves and small woody fragments. Water tan-brown. Less decomposed peat overall than releve 9180.

Water at surface of peat. Lots of thatch. Quaking mat. Moss cover very thin. Community runs along upland and then transitions to more shrub towards upland and middle of wetland. Mainly Betula.  pH = 6.1-6.2
Standing water in hollows (mucky). Hummocks 1-2ft. ~DBH Larix = 10-15cm. Adjacent to water tracks, and bog/Chamaedaphne area on other side. Tamarack swamp in area that grades to water track fen.

Subtle hummocks, water @ peat level. Slight bounce. No hollows. Expansive peatland and away from road/ditch effect. Sphagnum development occ. and outside plot (Sphagnum fuscum). Feels like mix between shrub swamp and shrubby rich fen.

Occ stumps. Typical of entire area. There are some yellow birch in upland nearby, but more in a low draw. CWD is mod. Evidence of worms. Soil very fine loam - light grey, up to 6in. Slight slope to south. Designated old growth. ATV raod runs through site.

Subtle undulations where veg has been scoured out. Releve encompasses mostly a slight rise w/ veg. Flooding has left debris in trees. Lots of Phalaris all along river. Occ stumps here. Worm evidence. Releve to document an uncommon community in North central counties.
Rolling woodland, many JP have fallen down - CWD is moderate to high. No stumps. Soil is sand. Many canopy gaps. West side of Mississippi River on high bank. Accessed from kayak up steep slope.
Fairly open shrub layer. Med to low hummocks. Moist hollows, stand H2O to 1 inch. Cedar reg'n most common in canopy gaps. Transitions quickly going NW to more FPn82. Malaxis monophyllos location.

Patches of Sphagnum fusca, esp near small interior lakes. Otherwise mostly non-sphag. Along drainage connections between lakes, Calamagrostis canadensis common. Releve done in area with more sphag and Chamaedaphne near lake edge. Occ. shallow pools. Lycopodiella is common throughout fen in patches. Fairly firm, but bouncy mat. Three small interior lakes in fen mat.
Very poor AP - close to road. But doesn't change much going west. Water at peat level. Solid sphagnum. Much more rich on east side of road. High hummocks of sphagnum.

Center of fen has higher concentration of leatherleaf and Betula but it is still present on edges - just patchier. H2O at peat level. Road divides entire wetland. Very poor on other side of road. Ditch to north on this side. Solid sphag cover but dried out and brown-yellow. Releve done more towards center.

On subtle rise (beach ridge) between ash swamp and wet meadow-shrub. 800ft north of shoreline. CWD moderate. Thin leaf litter, but good cover. Small amt of moss, some exposed soil. Some snags. On north shore of Upper Red Lake. Because of the relatively narrow area, species with affinity for wetter areas are scattered throughout from adjacent areas.

Heavy earthworm acivity throughout entire forest. High amt of CWD. Rolling terrain, nearby small stand of white pine on slope. Freq. exposed small-med boulders. No cut stumps in releve, but occ elsewhere. Areas freq w/ exposed soil, leaf litter patchy. Peninsula that extends into Kitchi Lake. Prob. high deer browsing as well.
Slight rolling terrain. Soil light-grey loamy sand in top 6in. Leaf litter moderate. Doesn't appear heavily wormed like nearby areas. CWD - mod-high. No stumps in releve.
FPn63 or FPn62. No cut stumps. Black spruces average 15-20cm dbh. Large area surrounded by much larger black ash swamp.
Shrub fen between Larix swamp and creek. A few sizable Larix trees are scattered near plot. Sphagnum in high, dry hummocks.
Between mesic hardwood upland and Nature's Lake. No Sphagnum moss observed.
Situated between creek and upland forest. Trees avg. 15cm dbh.
Situated between wet meadow shoreline of Lake Winnie and Larix-dominated conifer swamp. Part of large wetland shoreline complex. Peat wet in drought year, damp on surface. Moss on hummocks.
Open Larix featureless watertrack with Picea mariana poor swamp to SW and FP82 to NE. Many Larix have dead tops. No pools. Deer trail runs through.

Tilia and Quercus average 30-35cm dbh. Fair amount of CWD, mostly 20-25cm diameter. Soil wormed. Parts of stand nearby have very open canopy due to balsam poplar tree fall. No cut stumps observed. Shelterwood cut close by to south. Top 12 cm have organic material mixed into soil by worms, creating an A horizon. soil impenetrable below 50 cm.

Rich black spruce swamp (FPn62a or FPn82a). Trees avg 15-20cm dbh. No sign of disturbance. In middle of large cedar swamp. Quite a few uprooted trees and woody debris, both fine and coarse. Pools cover ~20%, mostly without standing water. Rich black spruce swamp extends far in most directions.
Open canopy forest on terrace above Big Fork River. No recent disturbance. Aspens 40-50cm dbh, firs 15-20cm. Mossy logs from fallen aspens.
5-acre upland island surrounded by rich tamarack swamp, black spruce bog, and shrub swamp.
Near shore of channel between 2 parts of Swan Lake. Large expanse of shore fen.
Large rich fen between upland forest with willow swamp border and Cowhorn Lake. More willows toward upland; fewer toward water.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Old flood channels cut through plot. These contain the wetter species recorded (e.g. Carex retrorsa) and are typical of this floodplain. Acer saccharinum averages 35cm dbh; Fraxinus 20cm. Mosses restricted to rotten wood.
Shrub swamp in featureless water track through very large Larix swamp (FPn82). Islands are interspersed through swamp on old dunes of the Bena Dunes LTA.

Plot chosen to represent common NPC in this slope position in Rove LTA, on talus substrate. W/in 50m of lake. No invasive plants or worms. Abundant CWD. Two very decayed cut stumps in and near corner of plot, sp. unknwon.

Plot chosen to represent burned NPC along lakeshore in Gabbro LTA. Not affected by '99 blowdown prior to July 2006 Cavite Lake fire. Previous origin date 1854. Exposed mineral soil well stabilized by liverworts, acrocarps and herb vegetation.Observed some browsing on tiny jack pine (hare?). Was FDn43c prior to 2006 fire.

Plot chosen to represent common NPC in Gabbro Bedrock Complex LTA with significant effects from '99 blowdown. Located @ top of bedrock ridge. P. banksiana blowdown most common. Some P. mariana as well. Snags and old CWD present. No exotics. Near cliff edge. Origin 1875.

Plot chosen to represent high quality NPC, common in bedrock controlled hills of Gabbro Bedrock Complex LTA. No exotics. No recent fire. Some recent blowdown of P. banksiana and P. mariana. Origin 1875.

Plot chosen to represent common expression of NPC in Gabbro Bedrock Complex LTA on terrain between bedrock controlled hills, often near wetland NPCs. Near large gram wetland formerly APn81. Part of plot includes moss- and lichen-covered sloping bedrock feature common in this LTA. No worms. Minor '99 blowdown impact. CWD common. Origin 1875.

Plot chosen to represent ecotonal community in transition from FDn32c2 to APn81. common in fine scale topo variation of LTA. Includes small dperession, also common in this NPC on level terrain. Blowdown of <=25% of canopy is also common in this LTA. Origin 1875.

Plot chosen to represent expression of this NP class in Vegetable Lakes Till Plain LTA on steep terrain. Not well described in field guide as P. banksiana is dominant to codominant. Fire origin 1936. No exotic plants or worms.

Plot chosen to represent common wetland small patch NPC of Gabbro Lake Bedrock Complex LTA. In small basin among bedrock hills. Drier hummocks common. Natural origin in 1875. No exotic plants or worms. Linked to other similar NPCs by small low gradient (intermittent?) stream.

Plot chosen to represent occasional small patch, open wetland NPC of Gabbro Lake Bedrock Complex LTA. In small basin, surrounded by APn80a1. Near low gradient drainage that links APn80 communities. Natural origin 1875. No exotic plants.

Plot chosen to represent expression of NPC not well- described in field guide i.e dominated bygraminoids vs. shrubs. Part of large wetland complex at confluence of 5 drainages. To west grades to cattail marsh. Elsewhere, APn91 and APn81.

Plot chosen to represent common NPC in Gabbro Lake Bedrock Complex LTA in level or gently sloping terrain. No exotics. Well-developed hummocks ~25-50cm. No standing water in hollows. Natural origin in 1846.

Plot chosen to represent advanced growth stage of primary forest, natural origin 1727, with some advanced regeneration of Pinus strobus. Some minor wind damage to birch crowns. No exotic plants or worms.
Plot chosen to represent natural origin NPC resulting from 1936 fire near Gordon and Cherokee Lakes. Typical of small bedrock controlled knobs and ridges, typically with shallow to bedrock soils.

Plot chosen to represent uncommon to rare NPC in Gabbro Lake Bedrock Complex LTA. Well-developed hummocks and hollows, including one ~9 sq. m pool. Little standing water in this dry year but abundant evidence of greater depths in pool @ other times. Abundant CWD all diameters and states of decay. A worm observed. Surrounding forest burned 1936. No evidence of fire observed in NPC patch with plot.

Plot chosen to represent common NPC in Gabbro Bedrock Complex LTA. Natural origin 1875. No anthropogenic disturbance. No exotic plants or worms. Moderate amount of CWD present, medium diameter. Small moist inclusion in corner of plot.

Plot chosen to represent common NPC in Gabbro Bedrock Complex LTA on bedrock controlled hills and ridges. Includes small rock outcrop NPCs. Transitions to FDn43 on north-facing slope and to east along ridge. No exotic plants or worms. Origin 1875.

Plot chosen to represent one expression of NPC type on well to excessively drained bedrock controlled features in Gabbro Bedrock Complex LTA. No exotic plants or worms. Patchy occurrence of Pleurozium schreberi.

Plot chosen to represent small patch NPC common on Gabbro Bedrock Complex LTA. Well-developed hummocks and hollows. No exotic plants or worms. Origin 1875. Common NPC in low relief terrain between bedrock controlled hills.

Plot chosen to represent richer conifer wetland NPc (FPn62) that is rare in Gabbro LTA. Located in transition between APn80 and upland forest NPC. Well-developed hummocks and hollows. Some water in small pools. No exotic plants or worms. Origin 1875.

Plot chosen to represent NPC common in Gabbro Bedrock Complex LTA. Upstream of old beaver impoundment. Well developed hummocks and narrow hollows. Relatively dry. Scattered P. mariana and L. laricina south of plot.

Plot chosen to represent matrix of large wetland complex on north shore of Dent Lake. Plot includes one large hummock and scattered small ones. Gradual transition to open water via increasing frequency of wet pools/flarks w/ abundant Rhynchospora fusca and Drosera intermedia.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC type and condition common in Wine Lake area of Gabbro Bedrock Complex LTA. Multi-age P. strobus NPCs more common in this area than elsewhere to north and east. Different landscape setting than described as typical in classification field guide.

Plot chosen to represent this NPC in common landscape setting in Gabbro Bedrock Complex LTA: a narrow band between lake and upland bedrock low cliff outcrops and upland forest. Moderate amount CWD. Hummocks moderately well-developed. No past human disturbance. Typical of conifer dominated wetlands in this LTA.

Plot chosen to represent expression of this NPC class not well-described in class field guide, but typical of Gabbro Bedrock Complex LTA at old growth stage. Origin 1875. Abundant CWD, many diameters of self-thinning P. banksiana (most) and A. balsamifera (fewer). So-facing steep slpoe to south is senescing P. banksiana (a few dead in plot).

Plot chosen to represent NPC type frequent in this landscape setting in Gabbro Bedrock Complex LTA. Compare to forest NPC of releve #9137 and same NPC type on similarly steep but north-facing slope of releve #9139. Origin 1875. Abundant CWD of Pinus banksiana and Picea mariana. These spp senescing; a few in plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC type frequent in this landscape setting in Gabbro Bedrock Complex LTA, and to contrast w/ same NPC type on similarly steep but south-facing slope of releve #9138 (origin 1875). Origin 1894. Bryophyte cover continuous in this setting. Much lower cover and richness of forbs than #9138. A few senescing Pinus banksiana and Picea mariana in plot.
Plot chosen to represent NPC type uncommon in Gabbro Lake Bedrock Complex LTA. Origin 1727. Adjacent forest burned in Sept. 2006. Moderate amount of CWD. No exotic plants or worms.

Plot chosen to represent NPC class common in Gabbro Lake Bedrock Complex LTA in advanced growth stage; origin 1729. Abundant CWD, all diameters. Betula papyrifera not coppice. Small openings w/ sparse shrubby veg are scattered throughout this NPC patch. Moose browse of nearby Pop trem spalings. P strobus seedlings common in patch.

Plot chosen to represent expression of NPC type typical in Gabbro Lake Bedrock Complex LTA. No mistletoe damage observed. All size classes of Picea mariana regen. Origin 1729 or 1936. Hummocks and hollows well-developed.

Plot chosen to capture late growth stage of NPC type. Common in Gabbro Lake Bedrock Complex LTA. Origin 1894. Typical expression in heterogeneous, low relief topog of this survey area. Large amount of CWD. Somewhat ecotonal as one corner of plot drops into edge of wet/mesic conifer swamp/mixed forest complex. Blowdown in plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC common in Gabbro Lake Bedrock Complex LTA. Origin 1894. On slope of saddle between cliff on Ross Lake shore and large forest cliff/rock outcrop w/ same NPC cover. Other areas of this NPC type w/ Thuja occidentalis in subcanopy and understory.

Plot chosen to represent expression of NPC type and growth stage common in 1936 fire area of Gabbro Lake Bedrock Complex LTA. Not well-described in NPC classification field guide. Elements of FDn32, 43, and 33.

Plot chosen to represent NPC type and growth stage originating from 1936 fire common in this area of Gabbro Lake Bedrock Complex LTA. Mature Populus tremuloides in decline. Young Pop trem scattered in understory in canopy gaps. Moderate amt of CWD mostly <=15cm dbh. Moose cow and calf observed.

Plot to represent NPC type common in this area of Gabbro Lake Bedrock Complex LTA after severe burn in Sept. 2006. This aspect of early growth stage not specifically in classification guide. Prior to fire in NPC: Populus tremuloides few, Betula papyrifera and Picea mariana co-dominant in canopy w/ scattered Pinus banksiana, Abies common in understory.

Plot chosen to represent expression of this NPC type in landscape setting typical of Rove Slate LTA. Muck among cobbles. Standing water pools appear to be infrequent. Narrow occurrence in drainage betwen flanking mesic pine forest uplands. Origin 1864. Upper end of drainage.
Wet meadow/wet prairie shrub dominated community. Poorly drained.

Stand low level upland surrounded by lowland black spruce and poor fen communities. Recent clear cut to east. No evid. of human disturbance in stand. Infrequent to occasional mistletoe in BS and browse on balsam fir. NPC subtype uncertain. Note: Eric Holmstrom assisted with this releve.

Releve represents dominant community type adjacent to Pine lake shoreline. Localized microtopography created by rocks/boulders and uprooted trees common throughout. No evidence of human disturbance in releve area - harvesting south stand. Earthworms present.

Stand in small shallow basin adjacent to mesic uplands (FDn43b), alder swamp (FPn73) and areas of transition between black spruce lowlands and fire dependent(FD) uplands (BST_CX/FPT_CX). Canopy black spruce >30ft with dense cover. Shading may account for lack of minerotrophic indicators in central stand. Cut stumps throughout (scattered). Topographic context: depression/flat.

Releve represents native plant community scattered throughout Park in small basin depressions <= 1 acre in size. Peat accumulation significant. Centrally, dominated by leatherleaf - no minerotrophic indicators. Peripherally, species common to wet meadows increase in abundance. Perhaps community in transition? Feature so small that edge effect significant.
No human disturbance noted in stand; adjacent to powerline. Mistletoe common in black spruce.

Selected as representative area of low relief upland forest. Black spruce often canopy co-dominant. Older (>50 yrs.) second-growth mix. Disturbance on mound minimal/negligible. Old logging road leads up to stand. Moderate coarse woody debris in plot.

Releve in designated old growth. Some evidence of cut stumps, maybe from salvage logging. Coarse woody debris minimal (mostly birch). Plot captures typical upland mixed forest of State Park. Balsam fir is infrequent component of Park Forest.

Releve represents birch dominated portion of NO stand. Red pine/white pine snags in area and fair bit of coarse woody debris (birch & red pine). Evidence of fire scars on cut stumps and charcoal at mineral surface. Even-aged red pine dominates canopy to N, E, & S of releve pt. Earthworms present. GL disturbance noted.

Plot representative of poor fen in small depression feature. Graminoids and low shrubs co-dominant. Richer areas of vegetation found along shoreline and in wet hollows of wetland complex. Dry mesic mixed woodlands (FDn33) surround depression.

Represents a dry sandy (more) open inclusion within a larger dry mesic FDn33 forest matrix. Species composition seems more aligned with FDn12 (vs. FDn33) but patch may not be large enough to map separately. Similar inclusions found on steep SW facing slopes throughout park; small patch NPC? Evidence of deer browsing present.

Typical of Park's steep slopes with SW aspect. Releve point represents a drier inclusion within the larger dry mesic FDN33 forest matrix. Species composition more aligned with FDn12 (vs. FDn33) but patch size is small. Cut stumps (pine) with fire scars and charcoal present at mineral surface. Litter of leaves and needles.

Releve represents drier, more open patch within dry mesic FDn33 forest matrix. Patch with altered vegetation composition and increased species diversity relative to surrounding NPC. Soil, a coarse red sand. Plot adjacent to old logging RR spur trail. Cut stumps present. Unsure of disturbance history.

Representative example of small depression wet meadow native plant community type in Park. Most are <1 acre in size and surrounded by FD upland dry mesic mixed forests. No standing water on survey date. No sphagnum present (other Park WM with variable amounts of sphagnum/peat accumulation).

Stand adjacent to extensive poor fen and small acidic lake. Stand also borders FD upland dry mesic forest. Open patches (canopy <5%) are dispersed both centrally and peripherally in the stand. Human disturbance minimal. Past beaver activity noted.

Poor fen on floating mat adjacent to small lake. Community extends throughout most of depression. Representative of APn91b stands within the Park. Richer areas of vegetation found along shoreline and in wet hollows. Adjacent upland is a FD dry mesic forest. Also bordered by stand of APn81. Remnant OHV trail bisects community.

Stand occurs on drumlin feature. Evidence of disturbance throughout feature: ground level, cut stumps (pine) remnant roads/trails, invasive species. Site relatively rich for FDn43 (silt cap?). No cedar, some yellow birch; probability key for FDn43 suggests type c, but MHn45 is also a possibility.

High quality stand surrounded by FD mesic mixed uplands. Site representative of cedar dominated portion of stand (vs. black spruce). Old winter road bisects stand but disturbance minimal. Deer and moose sign present.

Plot chosen to represent NPC type common in Rove Slate LTA. Origin 1864. No anthropogenic impacts. No exotic plants or worms. Occasional canopy gaps in NPC generally have frequent Pinus strobus regen. and recruitment.

Plot chosen to represent expression of NPC in Rove LTA 10 yrs after major blowdown event in FDn43a. Abundant large and medium dbh CWD. Plot incl. large debris pile and tip-up areas. Pinus strobus regen <= 4m common in blowdown impact patches. P. resinosa common codom in undamaged NPC (origin 1864).

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC expression in Rove Slate LTA. On steep sided peninsula in Clearwater Lk. Transitions to forest on upper slope and hill top. No exotic plants or worms.

Plot chosen to represent expression of NPC type common in Rove Slate LTA. Origin 1871. Burned snags observed near plot. These not common generally. No worms. No exotic plants. P. strobus in regen & subcan throughout patch (occasional in canopy). Rocky 'shingle' substrate w/ fine silt loam.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent small expression of NPC type in perched drainage between large hills. Includes some ecotonal areas around which drainage meanders. Plot in upper end of drainage. Tree canopy cover diminishes, forb richness decreases and tall shrub cover increases as gradient increases in drainage beyond plot boundary.

Plot chosen to represent NPC common in Rove Slate LTA canopy dominated by deciduous spp. Origin 1864 fire. Bet pap senescing. Recent Abies blowdown. Tip-up mounds x3 in plot. Pinus res and strob occasional in canopy of patch area. Thuja occidentalis subcanopy frequent in this NPC in Rove Slate LTA.

Plot chosen to represent primary forest NPC type in Rove 
Slate LTA. Origin 1681 fire. Much higher cover of Eurybia mac in this area than other releves in this NPC elsewhere in LTA. Moderate amt of CWD, mostly Abies. Large Pop trem elsewhere on ridgetop in 1681 area. Upper soil layer stony loam.

Plot chosen to represent expression of NPC type common in Rove Slate LTA on lower slopes in steep, no-facing slopes. Understory variable in cover, but <3m in height and <=30%. Tall shrubs very patchy. Some to many 1999 blowdown patches in Rove Slate LTA had this subcanopy & understory below Bet pap, Pop trem and/or Pinus spp.where hardwoods and to a lesser degree pine blew down. Origin 1864 fire.
Plot chosen to represent small patch NPC in Rove Slate LTA. Hummocks moderately well-developed. Moderate amount of medium diameter CWD.

Plot chosen to represent uncommon small patch NPC type in Rove Slate LTA. Fraxinus nig in good condition. Patch as a whole is variable in herb composition w/ some areas more rich and diverse, others dom by Glyceria stri and/or Calam can w/ few other spp. Origin 1881. Heavy moose use.

Plot chosen to represent expression of medium patch NPC type in Rove Slate LTA. Origin 1881. In patch overall, P. bank canopy variable; patch tall shrub cover. P. strob <=10m common in understory. Charred base of lrg Pinus sp decaying in plot. Transition to Pop trem and rock outcrops @ crest of ridge. Nearby P. res and strob dom, P. bank scarce or absent.

Plot chosen to represent comparatively large example of sm patch NPC type in Rove Slate LTA. Presence of B. alleg and Ulmus rub not common in small depressional/drainage occurrences. This patch assoc w/ perm stream. Likely subsurface flow all summer. Very cobbly subst.  Unveg, cobble intermittent channel crosses corner of plot.

Plot chosen to  represent common expression/condition of NPC type w/ mod loss through senescence of Pop trem from canopy where Pinus is not prominent in can or subcan, but present in underst. Origin 1881. Adjacent areas have P. strob forming broken can w/ Bet pap. Large Picea glauca & P. mari frequent.

Plot chosen to represent NPC type common on crest of ridges in Rove Slate LTA. Minor '99 blowdown impacts via large diameter CWD in plot from nearby canopy trees and large down and decayed pine snags in plot. Origin 1864 fire. Charcoal observed at transition from humus to mineral soil.

Plot chosen to represent expression of small patch NPC type in Vegetable Lakes Till Plain LTA. Occasional very old cut stumps in NPC patch. Abundant CWD, medium to large. Hummocks and hollows mod well developed. Some canopy gaps due to large Picea windthrow in plot.

Fairly representative example of this community type; more on the mesic/dry side. A Rank - No sign of human disturbance, old growth, lots of woody debris, relatively rich vegetatively. Number of down logs (mostly cedar) and yellow birch snags.

Evidence of earthworms in community. Releve to characterize a mesic hardwoods community. Young stand in general w/ one large white cedar and one large paper birch in overstory and dense understory of sugar maple.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Releve to document a mesic hardwood community. Canopy of cedar, yellow birch, heart lvd birch. Not much diversity in forb/ground layers. Wet forest to the east (outside of polygon).

Releve location most representative of the MHn45b type: Some evidence of earthworms. Certain areas quite nice- there are areas w/in total boundary of MHn45c. Certain areas with C rank. Viable stand though. Varying age difference in stand. Overall ranking B/C w/ pockets of A - B - and C.

Representative area of overall site. Higher topographic position would be MHn45c w/ transition to WFn53a grouped vs MHn45b. Mainly MHn45b in the stand. Evidence of past logging. Some worm influence (present). B to BC rank for entire stand.

Mesic hardwood community partially north (releve) of delineated stand. Sampled here for classification purposes. Earthworm evidence throughout (duff layer reduced). Small wet pools within (sensitive fern/Equisetum sp. etc). Evidence of past logging. Releve outside of delineated polygon.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Mesic hardwood community with canopy of sugar maple with cedar and yellow birch. Not much regeneration except for sugar maple. Herbaceous layer depauperate. Reduce duff layer due to earthworms. Sandwiched between wet forest to the north and MHn45a or c to the south.
Focus on this area due to the cedar; old growth with some cedars (>24 DBH). Gaps in canopy of releve; canopy far more open where cedar is less abundant with greater blowdown; no yellow birch.
Ground layer fairly open; earthworms present. Areas open outside of plot, perhaps selectively logged. Cedars in plot 16 in. DBH. Mostly sugar maple in canopy.

Fire dependent community; open canopy of balsam fir (dominant), heart-leaved birch, yellow birch, white spruce; dense shrub layer of beaked hazel. Ground cover of Lycopods, bunchberry, bluebead lily. Some trees >24" DBH. Blowdown commonly observed.
For MH key -- MHn45.  For FD key -- FDn43 - our best guess.

Southern portion of delineated stand; northern portion forested peatland. This area is fire dependent with gaps in the canopy. Canopy of white spruce, yellow birch, balsam fir, heart lvd birch; groundlayer of Lycopods/bunchberry. Shrub layer of beaked hazel & mountain maple.

Upland island of cedar; surrounded by alder swamp and fire dependent (blowdown with dense shrub growth). Large old growth cedars in this location; few >20" DBH. Most of stand surrounding releve is alder. Fir mortality nearby. Best chance for MHn45b - not sure.
Representative location within upland community in delineated stand. Interrupted canopy of fir and Betula spp. Shrub layer dense with mountain maple and hazel. Lycopods abundant.

Canopy of cedar, yellow birch, heart lvd birch; shrub layer of mountain maple and beaked hazel. Ground layer dominated by Lycopods. Overall canopy near plot is interrupted. Most similar to MHn45 but not clearly that community. Only location in stand with cedar. Evidence of historic logging/ interrupted canopy.

Interrupted canopy with heart-lvd birch, yellow birch, balsam fir, and white spruce. Dense shrub layer and goundlayer with Lycopods. Blowdown periodic. Likely mesic hardwood community. Boulders outside of plot.
Mesic hardwood or FDn43 community w/ open canopy due to blowdown. Yellow birch >24"DBH. Species poor with abundant cover from typical herbaceous species.

Mesic hardwood (?) stand with interrupted canopy (not seeing evidence of logging and few occurrences of blowdown). Mix of fir, birch species, white spruce, cedar with black ash in low-lying areas. Dense shrub layer and ground layer of Lycopods with C. borealis and C. canadensis.
Plot representative of delineated stand cedars vary in size from 9-14"; wet forest community.
Long narrow band of west facing slope prairie above corn field.

Many forbs are patchy cover representing a sort of average in the plot: Pycnanthemum virg, Astragalus can, Glycyrrhiza lepid. Downslope moister OP Vernonia fasc, Aster laterifl, Cicuta mac, Calam can, & Lythrum alatum.
Compare with EJC 1971 releve in same community.
Nice looking prairie but with no conservative spp to speak of.
Circular wet meadow between lines of trees east of powerline. Some ? in my mind if this could have been planted but it feels pretty natural.
Majority of prairie here is bromy, prairie is patchy, releve represents best there is.
Slope of hill mid to base.
Along ravine slope, S side. Releve keys either to MHs39 or MHs49 instead of MHs38, but slope position suggests this is that very mesic facies of MHs38 that grades on lower slopes to MHs49.
I wonder if sparseness of D3 is because this area is reported to be a winter deer yard? River terrace forest along Cottonwood River (north of Sarasota Springs).
About 80% of ground layer is floodwashed, bare & covered w/ woody debris.

Maple basswood forest. Level ground. Ground cover likely different two weeks ago, spring ephemerals fading. Canopy trees younger than area to east. Site appears to be regenerating from selective harvesting of past. Ground layer is diverse throughout site.

Site dominated by Carex stricta and Calamagrostis. Very little reed canary grass present here. Surrounding area is dominated by reed canary grass, however. Diversity of forbs is high. Thatch is thick.
Maple-basswood forest. Diverse age of trees. Deadfalls and limbs scattered throughout. Ground layer moderately diverse, many spring ephemerals have faded. No invasive woody species observed.

On upper mid-slope of extremely steep, east-facing, ~240-foot high slope. Typical of broad zone of scrub talus between more intact leucogranite bedrock outcrops above and xeric open lichen-covered talus below (to base of slope). Substrate a mix of talus & bedrock. Shallow highly organic colluvium between talus blocks & outcrops. Talus blocks 3"-24" diameter. 'Bare' rock covered mainly by foliose & crustose lichens, less so by mosses. Plot is at ca. 140' to 150' from base of slope, in relatively open scrub zone with 25-50% cover of Betula papyrifera and occasional Pinus banksiana & Abies balsamea. Vegetable Lekes Till Plain LTA.

Typical of ~3-acre woodland opening on large sloping (south aspect) bedrock outcrop on west side of Gasket Lake. Lower slope of extremely steep, ~240-foot, predominantly east-facing slope. Denser jack pine upslope, talus slope to south. Leucogranite bedrock, some of which is fractured into large blocks. Soil limited to isolated pockets and fractures in bedrock. Litter sparse to patchy. Jack pine 10-30cm dbh, present in sparse clumps across opening, 20% dead or dying. No evidence of recent fire.

Typical of, and centrally located in, ~5-acre basin in rugged bedrock terrain along narrow valley between Cuckoo and Cam lakes. Outlet stream dammed by beavers, water level raised ~3 feet at high level (since lowered by partial failure of dam). Standing & downed dead conifers ~10-30cm dbh scattered through basin, appear to be dead >30-40 years.  Some trees appear to have fire scars. Uneven sedgy-fibric peat >40cm deep with low hummocks & hollows; partially decomposed, probably has experienced alternating saturation & drying. Woody remains of all sizes in peat. Basin probably WF or FP before damming of outlet.

Typical of broad central zone of mud flat that occupies much of shallow western arm of Cuckoo Lake. Beaver dam at outlet partially breached, leading to drawdown. Vegetation patchy with much exposed mud. Substrate is muck with some fiber, >50cm deep & quaky. Sparse litter. Surface generally level with subtle depressions & rises. Plot is ~2-3" higher than open water of flowage channel that is located ~50 feet to southwest. A more sparsely-vegetated zone is present at subtly lower elevation closer to open water toward center of basin. Juncus brevicaudatus dominates a sublty-higher elevation zone (releve 9405) nearer to upland margin.

On mud flat in western arm of Cuckoo Lake, typical of outer zone that forms band 2-15m wide. Substrate is saturated soft brown muck w/some fiber; slightly firmer than in middle zone (releve 9404). Surface mostly level, with 5-15cm variation between open muck depressions & vegetated rises. No standing water but water appears in footprints. Beaver dam at outlet partially breached, leading to exposure of broad mud flats. Plot covers much of width of outer zone in this part of basin.

Very localized water track feature in narrow arm of small (4-acre) basin along small drainage through strongly-rolling bedrock terrain into Cone Bay, Brule Lake. Plot captures much of series of pools in wettest part of water track. Open pools cover ~70% of plot; water 15cm deep. Wet quaky peat, >50cm deep. Scattered mossy hummocks ~30cm tall. Some down logs in plot, 10-20cm diameter, moss covered. Width of basin here ca. twice the width of water track. Cedar in this part of basin somewhat stunted and more widely spaced (patchy, open canopy) likely due to the wetter conditions. Standing cedars 10-20cm dbh upstream and downstream from plot appear to be dying, perhaps indicating recent increase in water level/flow. Most of original cedar cover in broader part of basin (downgradient to east) removed by logging > 40 yrs ago. Moderate moose activity (travel corridor) in area contributes to character of vegetation somewhat?

Typical of poor fen surrounding 1/2-acre bog pond in small basin along drainage connecting Famine & South Cone lakes; rolling bedrock terrain north of Brule Lake. Edge of plot 15 meters from pond. Wetter zone with Rhynchospora fusca immediately along pond. Very wet, moderately quaky, deep peat (>50cm). Standing water up to 8cm deep. Tall hummocks (to ~30cm tall) cover 30-40% of plot. Open water covers ~20-30%. Air photos show that the plot is located in a ~5-acre area that is often flooded. Several large old (1920's-era) pine logs sunk in pool at edge of this basin (likely part of old haul route).

Plot centrally located in part of 20-acre basin characterized by stunted cedar w/some black spruce and tamarack (stunted cedar area = 4-5 acres of basin). High hummocks throughout, up to 2 feet tall. Low areas vary from wet to standing water 3cm deep. No evidence of flow in plot but sheet flow 15m to east. Sedgy fibrous peat >40cm deep. Solid to moderately quaky. Ca. 25% of trees dead. Grades southward in basin to spruce swamp.

Plot centrally located in fairly uniform ~2-acre open zone in ~20-acre basin in strongly-rolling bedrock terrain north of Brule Lake; along drainage connecting Famine & South Cone lakes. Very subtle surface flow? Low hummocks (to 15cm) and small hollows with 1-2cm water present (hollows probably mostly from moose tracks). Moderately quaking sedge peat >50cm deep. Slightly downgradient in basin from releve 9408 (which is in stunted cedar part of basin); sligltly upgradient from releve 9410 (where subtle surface flow more apparent).

Typical of a small (<1/2-acre) and localized species-rich zone in 20-acre basin in strongly-rolling bedrock terrain north of Brule Lake. Subtle surface sheet flow here where west basin of wetland narrows to join east basin. Plot ~10m from upland margin and ~10m from the loosely defined stream channel (more of a flowage) toward middle of wetland. Substrate is saturated sedge peat >50cm deep; fairly firm and level but with broad shallow depressions. Moose tracks altering the substrate here also. Plot is subtly downgradient from releves 9409, 9408 along the small drainage connecting Famine and South Cone lakes. Several old pine logs (1920's era) half-buried in east basin of this wetland indicate this drainage was used as a haul route?

Area dominated by sugar maple. Basswood, elm, and ash occasional. Canopy continuous. Subcanopy patchy with sugar maple and bitternut hickory most common. Ground layer continuous, with large dense patches of wild leek.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: The site is a mesic oak forest with Quercus rubra dominant and continuous in the canopy. Acer saccharum is abundant in the subcanopy, and is quickly taking over the forest. The ground layer was likely more diverse earlier in the spring. Soil is silty-clay loam.

The site is a small dry prairie on a sand-gravel knob. A fair amount of gopher activity on site with several fresh mounds present. A few species of more mesic prairies were observed just outside the plot. Lespedeza leptostachya is doing well at this site.
The site is a shrub dominated wet meadow. Prairie vegetation is also common throughout site. Some areas with no vegetation and with standing water up to two cm in some locations.
Maple-basswood forest on north-facing slope, above a branch above the Zumbro River. Maples younger in age, some harvesting in the past. Diverse ground layer.

The canopy is continuous, dominated by Acer saccharum, with some Tilia americana. Subcanopy is sparse with sugar maple. Shrub layer patchy with sugar maple, basswood, and elm. Ground layer is interrupted and it was fading. Ground layer was thick with leaf litter.
The site is a small prairie remnant that was formerly grazed. Some wet meadow components grade into this community such as Carex stricta. Outside of the plot, Valeriana edulis can be found.

The forest at the site of the releve is mesic oak forest. As you move east, the forest becomes dominated by sugar maple. Releve is dominated by Quercus alba, Q. rubra, and Tilia americana. Ground layer is continuous, with diverse assortment of spring ephemerals.

Lowland forest along the Straight River. The site is on a slight rise between flood channels. Early spring visit results in underdeveloped herbaceous layer. Laportea continuous. It is dominant in summer as evident by numerous stems of last year. Silver maple observed in the lower channels. Not typical of class.

The site is a high quality mesic sugar maple and red oak forest. Sugar maple is becoming more dominant on the site. There is a diverse ground cover. Buckthorn is present to the SE, however, this immediate area is free of any invasion. On lower portion of west-facing slope.

The site is a mesic oak-maple-basswood forest. Most trees are forest grown. The ground layer is continuous, and dominated by wild leek. Numerous bitternut hickory and sugar maple seedlings are present. Soil is not compacted, and is a silty clay loam.

Mesic oak-sugar maple forest. Very little basswood here. Sugar maple and bitternut hickory seedlings abundant. Ground layer dominated by wild leek. Not as diverse as other releve location in park. Canopy a little more open as well. Soil is a dark, clay loam.

Very small open patch w/ native forbs, fairly diverse. Non-native grasses (Agrostis stolonifera/gigantea & Elymus repens). Graminoids w/ dense cover. All w/ narrow to very fine leaves. Few seeds heads except for Agrostis sp (very noticeable) and a Sporobolus w/ seeds mostly enclosed in the sheath. At least one fine bladed sedge sp. Difficult to estimate cover of graminoids. Soil 'ribbons' easily to 1 inch. Fibrous roots present in upper 2 inches. Sand grains visible.

Canopy layer and seedling layer present. No mid-canopy or understory present. Seedlings abundant. Ash seedlings carpet the ground about 10-50cm tall. Duff is made up of an almost continuous layer of small sticks (~3in long & 1/8-1/2in diam.) A few leaves are present in duff layer. Small coarse woody debris present (sticks)and a few downed logs present. Few forbs and grasses. This stand of trees is in a location that was not historically forested.

Opening in larger area of taller, denser cover of cattail and broad-leaved sedges. This small patch (<1acre) is visible on the air photo. Soils are saturated muck w/ plant roots; some sedge peat may be present. There may be more Carex species present; releve done quickly. Two photos available (JRR 14 SEP 2010 #s 140, 141). Could be WMs92 or WMp73?

Unmowed patch of dry prairie on upper slope, surrounded by red cedar to each side and above. Below is mowed (for hay) grassland w/ native grasses present. Mowing done recently (within the month). Cedars are 5-15m tall. Photos JRR 2010 #s 131-132.

I chose portion of stand with less Rhamnus cathartica and less burdock. Quality of stand as a whole is quite variable. Releve plot on N-facing slope. Below is mouth of stream which empties into West Graham Lake. There is scattered coarse woody debris.

The prairie remnant is located along the active RR ROW of the DM&E RR. The confined area exhibits traits of both dry prairie and mesic prairie. Site dominated by Sorghastrum nutans and Bouteloua curtipendula. Forb tend toward more mesic species.

The site is located near Dobbins Creek. The community is mesic in nature. However floodplain species are present and the site does flood occasionally. Dominant tree species inclde Juglans nigra and Tilia americana. A patch of Phalaris arundinacea was growing in canopy opening.

npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: The site is a floodplain forest located along Rose Creek. Dominant trees include Acer saccharinum, Fraxinus pennsylvanica, and Tilia americana. Arisaema dracontium is found scattered throughout forest. Spring ephemerals were fading at this site.
Forest dominated by hickories. Oaks and elms occasional in canopy. Subcanopy also with hickories. Soil was fairly moist with some areas of standing water.
Mesic shagbark hickory forest. Canopy and subcanopy dominated by shagbark hickory. Ground layer continuous with Trillium grandiflorum and Geranium maculatum most dominant. Soil loamy clay.

The site is a mesic tallgrass prairie. It is on a gentle east-facing slope. Dominated by Andropogon gerardii and Sorghastrum nutans. A number of forbs are also present. These include: Parthenium integrifolium, Eryngium yuccifolium, and Asclepias hirtellum.

The site is a wet meadow/carr with an unusual diversity of shrubs. These include: Betula pumila, Cornus stolonifera, Salix bebbiana, S. discolor, S. candida, S. eriocephala, S. petiolaris, and Amorpha fruticosa. Ground layer dominated by Carex stricta. Phlox maculata also present.

High quality mesic prairie. Dominated by Andropogon gerardi, Schizachyrium scoparium, Spartina pectinata. Forb diversity extremely high, with large number of rare species. The site grades into wetter prairie and has a few species more typical of the wet prairie community.

West-facing slope, not much more than 10m from crest to toe. Releve overlaps adjoining wet meadow community somewhat. A diverse representation of native grasses (6 species). Few conservative forbs, but Amorpha canescens is present. Species at edge of releve from adjacent wetter NPC denoted w/ 'toe' (of slope) in species remarks.

This 'prairie' has abundant forbs, some of them conservative. However, it is very dominated by non-native cool-season grass w/ few native graminoids. Panicum virgatum & Spartina pectinata are present in the larger stand, but not present in the plot. I believe the community might respond to fire used to decrease the cool-season grasses.

Mesic prairie, diverse in native grasses and in forbs. Soil is saturated, but no standing water present. (Much recent rain). Some ant mounds present. I think there is a very gradual slope of the land to the south. Almost level though. There are probably species that I missed. Releve done in haste.

Typical of large patches of forest on low terrace along Watonwan R. On a shallow rise adjacent to channels. Some willows are dying and elms are shooting up into canopy. Much downed & well-rotted tree parts - mostly fallen willows. High density of trees. Willows are all 35-50cm dbh - no smaller ones. Is this a mid-successional phase? Also Morella (morrel fungus on site.

On low terrace along Watonwan River adjacent to flood channel. Heavy leaf litter but no duff. Numerous silver maple seeds. Trees are very large: Popu delt 70+cm dbh; silvers 80-100cm; elm & Salix 40-60cm dbh.
Better-drained part of annually-hayed meadow. On bottomlands of Chanarambie Ck. valley.
Wetter part of wet meadow that is annually hayed. On bottomlands of Chanarambie Ck. valley.
Prairie on level ground in Chanarambie Ck. valley. Annually hayed late in season. Burned in May 2006.
Marsh on bottom ravine between grazed prairie slopes. Located just upslope of impoundment. Water table above ground surface.
Prairie on level ground in broad shallow swale on bottom of Chanarambie Ck. valley. Annually hayed. Burned in May 2006.
Marsh in narrow, wet drainageway. Water table at ground surface. In broad creek valley.
Mesic to wet-mesic prairie on level ground in broad, shallow creek valley. Dense thatch present (not recently burned). Grazed or hayed in past before WMA acquisition.
In middle of ravine between dry prairie hills. Water table presently at ground surface. Last grazed in 1960s.

Small area (15 x 30m) in shallow depression in middle of Flandreau Ck. valley adjacent to creek ditch (just on W side of creek). Grades into dense Typha angustifolia to N and S. To W, grades into better-drained wet meadows. Water table presently below surface.

Meadow in long narrow zone (30 m. wide) covering bottom of ravine. Soil wet; water table below ground surface. In cattle pasture but not heavily grazed. In drainage on Bemis Moraine. Confirmed Cx emoryi i.d.: convex, tawny mouth on sheath; papery sheaths not ladder-fibrillose.

place_name: Hole in the Mountain Preserve Main
remarks: On broad, level bottomland of Flandreau Ck. valley. Huge broad veg. zone. Water table presently well below ground surface though soil is moist. Orchids abundant.
Hummocky seepage wetland on shallow toe slope on W side of Rock River valley. Water table presently below ground surface.

Did a square releve in a narrow (linear) community. A different shape would have captured it better. Wet meadow or marsh dominated by river bulrush. Very few forbs w/ very low density. Cicuta sp. was far outside plot. Half of the forbs recorded in releve were actually from adjacent, drier NPC; these marked w/ 'edge' in species remarks. More bulrush than reed canary grass, but reed canary is a significant component. Photos JRR2010 #121-122.

Plot in shallows between two small islands in Poplar Lake. Water depth in plot ca. 2-4in, down ca. 18in from seasonal high water level. Protected from waves to southwest by ridge of boulders in and emerging from water. To north of plot is smooth bedrock hump, now ca. 4-6in above water. Substrate is coarse sand with strong variation in particle size, plus some submerged bedrock (gabbro with iron content)and angular boulders. Plot covers whole patch here. Most of vegetation cover is from submerged basal rosettes, with scattered emergent flowering stalks of Eriocaulon (primarily) and Lobelia. Plot somewhat transitional between Lakeshore System and truly Aquatic. Photos here. Poplar Lake Bedrock Complex LTA.

Releve done to capture Subularia habitat, but is fairly typical of submersed aquatic rosette community on sand substrates. Plot on north side of small island and rocky spit connecting to larger island to east. In shallow water ranging from ca. 5in deep near shore to 24-30in at deepest. Substrate is coarse sand over sloping gabbro bedrock with occasional boulder. Boulders & exposed bedrock covered with algae. Some small diameter submerged branches in plot. Site protected from much of wave action that batters most of shoreline. Plot ca. 16ft from west end of releve MDL10-18 (9445) and currently separated by emerged low bedrock hump. Water level down ca. 18in from seasonal high water mark (extended drought). At deeper end community grades into Isoetes-dominated zone. Poplar Lake Bedrock Complex LTA.

place_name: South Shore Caribou Lake OG Pine
remarks: Plot in OG pine stand on upper slope & crest of ridge near south shore of Caribou Lake. Pine supercanopy patchy from blowdown & standing dead trees. Stand characterized by occasional groves of old cedar, some w/in 20-30m of plot. Stand origin = 1692 according to Heinselman map. Litter mostly needles. Dark organic humus over variable layer of gray/brown fine silty soil over bedrock. All age classes of CWD abundant. No evidence of recent fire. Two large snags in plot.

Mature forest on lower and middle slope of ridge with OG pine. Between lower edge of plot and lake is +/- level area w/ Picea mariana and Thuja & higher moss cover. 1 very old birch in center of plot, rest are younger. Opening along lower edge of plot from recent death of large old birch & balsam. 1 large well decayed birch log in plot. 1 old stump w/ nurse cedar. Litter 1-2cm. Leaves and cedar needles over 4-5cm humus over variable layer of brown silty loam w/ rock fragments over bedrock and boulders.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Mature tamarack stand with little blow down; open water 1-5% cover in hollows. Tamarack needles prevalent in PE soil layer; woody debris occasional in MP layer.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Regenerating tamarack stand with occasional old stumps present; open water (in pools ) 5-25% cover. Tamarack needles prevalent in PE soil layer; woody debris occasional in MP soil layer.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Regenerating tamarack stand with occasional old stumps present; open water (in pools) 5-25% cover. Tamarack needles prevalent in PE soil layer; woody debris occasional in MP soil layer. Many upland herbaceous plants present on hummocks in releve. Extensive tamarack mortality across stand; tamaracks being replaced by shrubs (particularly ALNUINCA). Entire stand may be considered ecotonal because of this.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Mature tamarack stand (many trees with a DBH >30cm) with blow down covering more than 10% of the area. Well formed hummocks and hollows but often not with continuous moss cover (Height of tree root hummocks 25cm); CARESTRI hummocks also prevalent in the NE portion of the releve where blow down is prevalent. Open water covers 1-5% of site.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Mature tamarack stand with occasional blowdown; open water 5-25%. blowdown less than 10% cover. Tamarack needles prevalent throughout PE soil layer; woody debris occasional in MP soil layer.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Mature tamarack stand with well developed moss hummocks and hollows. Open water 5-25% cover; many tamarack >30cm DBH. Tamarack needles prevalent throughout PE soil layer; woody debris occasional in MP layer.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Tamarack DBH 5-20 (30)cm; hummocks well developed but hollows are not. Rather, these consist of a matrix of standing water at a depth of 19cm. These areas are largely dominated by CARELACU, EQUIFLUV, and CALTPALU while other vegetation is largely restricted to the hummocks. Open water is 50-75%. Tamarack needles are prevalent throughout PE soil layer; woody debris occasional in MP layer.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Mature tamarack stand (DBH 15-20 (30)); little blowdown observed. Stand at the headwaters of a stream to the north. Open water in releve 1-5%. Tamarack needles observed in peat layer; woody debris throughout the MP soil layer.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Stand with a relatively open canopy. Extensive tamarack mortality observed. Tamarack regeneration observed north of releve. No standing water observed. Hummocks and hollows well developed. System strongly graminoid dominated; possibly ecotonal. Occasional woody debris observed to a depth of 40cm in the soil profile.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Young tamarack stand with more mature tamarack north of the releve. The hummocks and hollows are well developed. Standing water in 25-50% of the releve. Tamarack needles observed within the upper 20cm of the soil profile and woody debris observed within the upper 57 cm.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Young tamarack stand with more mature tamarack north of the releve. The hummocks and hollows are well developed. Standing water in 25-50% of the releve. Tamarack needles were observed within the upper 20cm and woody debris within the upper 57cm of the soil profile.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Mature tamarack stand (average DBH 15-25 (30)cm). Graminoids dominate the ground layer. Hummocks and hollows well developed. Standing water present over 5-25% of releve. No dead-standing tamarack within releve but occasional within stand as a whole. Woody debris observed throughout the soil profile.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Height of tree root hummocks = 23cm. Sparse standing dead trees and blow down common in releve. Moss cover is minimal. Mature tamarack stand. Releve between 5-25% open water. Tamarack needles prevalent in PE soil layer; woody debris occasional in MP soil layer. Several standing dead 25+cm DBH Larix in plot, recent blowdown near SW corner.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Mature tamarack stand sloping to the south. Average DBH 20-30cm (40cm). No blowdown or dead standing tamarack observed within the (plot?).  Hummocks and hollows poorly developed throughout. At 30cm peat soil appears to be depleted (10yr3/2 or lighter), soils at this depth appear to have some mineral content but are still organic. No standing water observed within the releve.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Maturing tamarack stand, average DBH 15-20cm (35cm). Blowdown occasional in stand (<10%). Releve includes canopy opening from an area of blowdown as well as dead-standing tamarack. Open water 1-5% throughout releve. Crustacean shells observed throughout the soil profile (<1%). Tamarack needles observed in the PE soil layer.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Mature tamarack stand (DBH 20-30cm (35)) with no blowdown in the releve and little blowdown throughout the rest of the stand. Open  water less than 1% cover. Hollows largely not pooled with water. Tamarack needles observed throughout the PE soil layer.

Plot chosen to represent common NPC expression in LTA. NPC in mid-growth stage w/ maturing Pinus. Natural origin stand. Minimal snag development. Scattered blister rust damage. Abundant CWD of various dimensions.

Plot chosen to represent NPC expression common in LTA. Somewhat rocky slope. Some CWD. Some P. banksiana in NPC w/ 'open' growth form. Some P. banksiana standing dead in NPC. Little evidence of blister rust damage or mortality.
Plot chosen to rpesprent common expression of NPC on islands in large lakes of LTA. Pinus resinosa snag outside plot. Abundant CWD of various diameters.
Plot chosen to represent expression of NPC typical of LTA. Birch and aspen snags common. Mild blister rust damage. Abundant, well-decayed CWD.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent small patch NPC occurring in narrow, gentle drains btwn ridges in LTA. Hummocks and hollows common. Abundant CWD in various stages of decay. No evidence of Fraxinus 'die-back'. Picea glauca snags outside plot.
Plot chosen to represent natural origin NPC w/ no evidence of past harvest. Little CWD. Well developed hummocks are common. No mistletoe observed.

Plot chosen to represent common NPC & growth stage of natural origin in LTA. Low 2m rock cliff in SE corner of plot. Moderate amt of CWD. Scattered wind damage to Populus nearby. North slope below here more mesic w/ higher bryo cover and spp richness, Thuja in understory. Large moss covered boulders @ surface.
Plot chosen to represent expression of NPC common in LTA but not well described in classification. Bouldery substrate. Riparian setting on steep slope. Few P. bank snags. Moderate amount of CWD.

Plot chosen to represent NPC and growth stage in '99 blowdown patch. NPC origin was Canadian Outbreak Fire. Abundant CWD. Bryos over grnd and older CWD. Betula CWD from '99 decaying. Thuja abundant in non blowdown forest as well in multiple strata. Abundant and diverse bryos and lichens.

Plot chosen to represent natural origin NPC typical in this setting in Rove LTA, and to capture maturing mid-successional NPC in LTA. P. resinosa consistently present but not co-dom in patch. Some '99 blowdown damage. Some P. strobus snags. Pit and mound micro-topog. Abund CWD. No worms.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Northeastern Bedrock)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC typical in LTA often adj. to bedrock openings. Minimal CWD. Top of E-facing cliff. Narrow, small patch NPC often occurring btwn cliff top and FDn43. Natural origin. No cut stumps. No worms. Lichens incl Cladina spp.

Plot chosen to represent small patch NPC common in area of 1996 fire. Typical in soil-bearing depressions of bedrock controlled ridges. Part of a mosaic that also includes patches of bedrock shrubland w/woody cover <25% and bedrock outcrop NPCs. Species included in these patches are Vacc myrt, Prunus pens, Alnus vir, Cornus can, Lycopodium den

Plot chosen to represent post '99 blowdown NPC. Was P. banksiana (&) P. mariana dominated canopy. Substrate is boulder garden. Abundant CWD, most on ground and in advanced decay. Remnant P. banksiana in area are pretty ragged to vigorous. A few Populus trem among blowdown trees. Few P. bank regen; excellent P mariana regen.
Plot chosen to represent common NPC in Gabbro Lake Bedrock Complex LTA on steep, shallow to bedrock sites. Rock wall <=2m & tip-up in corner of plot. Pigmented worm in humus/soil.

Plot chosen to represent NPC regenerating after harvest in mid to late 1970s. Stumps well-decayed. Could have been summer harvest or low snow cover. Little CWD. Largest stumps approx 25cm. No exotics. Openings <=100m2 not uncommon in the patch.

Plot chosen to represent an NPC uncommon in LTA. No evidence of prior harvest. Natural origin. No observable evidence of fire. Small patch w/in wetland mosaic of APn81, APn91a/b, APn90a, and APn80. Standing water likely in normal year.

Mostly level bedrock controlled woodland site with some shallow depressions, lichen moss-covered outcrops and boulders. White pine downed snag. This is not uncommon near Wine Lake on landform on all but north slopes. Foliose lichens abundant on lower branches w/out needles and interior portions up to 10m of boles. Also shield lichens common on larger conifer boles.

Plot chosen to represent fire dependent class with red maple as a major component. Seems to represent a fairly large patch of this expression in the landscape. Not uncommon in Cook County portion of LTA. Some Populus blowdown. A. rubrum and Betula multi-stemmed. CWD sparse. Not well described in classification.

South facing slope bordering Wine Lake with spruce and small white pine bordering the lakeshore (pine not in releve). Dominated by shrubs with small depressions and some small boulders at surface providing some microhabitats. Soil is very fine sand of undetermined depth. FDn33 floristically. Open or wooded? Possibly result of absence of fire.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Gently undulating location at crest of point in Wine Lake. Pinus banksiana ~6 standing dead trees. Canopy P. resinosa = age class. Plot chosen to represent NPC type and condition typical of LTA in Cook County.

Plot to represent NPC >=60 years post harvest common in LTA. Hummocks not well developed. Wet hollows present but not abundant. No sign of mistletoe. Observable stumps often >20cm diam. Alnus most abundant in small openings of broken canopy (incl in plot).

Plot chosen to represent NPC common on narrow, bedrock-controlled ridge tops. Populus dead or dying. P. strobus seedlings and saplings common in patch and surrounding area. One large erratic in plot. Moderate CWD. Natural fire origin.
Plot chosen to represent uncut NPC near same NPC harvested in 1970's. Moderate CWD.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent natural fire origin NPC with expression typical of LTA in Cook County. On stony substrate, level terrain. Moderate CWD. No worms observed.

Plot chosen to represent common NPC in LTA in Cook County in this landscape position. Soil appeared like "wormed mull" but no worms observed. This expression of No. Mesic Mixed Forest class not well described in classification. In this LTA, this NPC is typically small to medium sized patch in Woodland matrix.

Plot chosen to represent NPC of natural origin w/ scattered cut stumps (one in plot) likely of post-fire salvage origin. Large P. strobus more common to north of here. Moderate amount and size CWD. No worms observed. Some blister rust damage. Fwere large P. strobnus here than to north in smae patch.

Graminoid dominated opening with small pools with Utricularia intermedia. Adjacent to Tamarack seepage swamp community. Plot includes Carex sterilis. Plot size at 10x10m since this was collected within an opening in a forest complex.

Open wetland community dominated by bulrush and Carex pellita. Carex sterilis in plot - adjacent to tamarack seepage swamp. Official community classification is questionable without further analysis via ordination.
Fen community adjacent to a large population of Phragmites and to a ditch. Microtopography within the releve plot.
Same wetland complex as 9502 with different species present at this location. Graminoid dominated within tamarack component (tamarack seepage swamp).
Wet prairie community with a significant shrub component throughout the entire community. Adjacent to large ditch system separating this property from Larix WMA.

Community includes occassional pools. Fire scars observed on dead tamarack individuals. Carex sterilis the main graminoid in this graminoid dominated community with Potentilla fruticosa the most abundant shrub.

Open inclusion within tamarack seepage swamp. Data collected to document the habitat of Eleocharis rostellata. Pools of water present and soils organic. Pitcher plants abundant in plot. Plot size at 10x10m since this was collected within an opening in a tamarack seepage swamp.

Opening within FPw63b community type. Plot size at 10x10m since this is an opening. Plot chosen to document E. rostellata, E. quinqueflora, and R. capillacea. Tamarack abundance reduced within the opening.
