Plot to characterize a wet prairie community with calciphiles present. Soils saturated at the surface. Graminoid dominated, primarily M. richardsonis
Linear fen feature and roughly a foot lower in topography than the surrounding WPn53 habitat.
Forest on steep N-facing slope on side of Sandhill River Valley. Many dead birches. Soil is loamy sand. Chimaphila umbellata present further east in this forest.
Forests adjacent to creek. Should rightfully be surveyed in spring. (From back of form: "Lyon Co part riparian forest along Yellow Medicine just east of Bosque WMA".

South facing hill, good quality but rank forb layer. NO - I did not see either big bluestem or little bluestem. At base of hill by creek Juglans nigra and Acer saccharinum. Not grazed for 35 years, burned 2003
Not grazed for 35 years, burned 2003. Lower slope of same hill as 20030828-01.

Burned spring 2003. Bare ground 15%. This site is heavily graminoid dominated. Land use history includes repeated aerial spraying, east of gravel pit. The only native forbs in customary abundance for prairies in this area are the Verbena and the Allium.
Lower SW-facing slope.
Soil sandy. A lovely garden of Coreopsis and Amorpha.
East facing slope in saddle.

West facing side of hill in best quality area. Most of remainer of hill is dominated by brome (??) or weedy species in patches or the forbs like Artemisia are dominant. Notes: Appears to have been recently burned which may account for the open patches with Ambrosia art. Perhaps soil was exposed in burn? The only real prairie in N 1/2 of this unit in section 7.
Tiny remnant of prairie between old field and degraded woods. Woods not good enough to consider on its own merits, highgraded for oak in past.

Releve does not differentiate type of apple trees planted in natural prairie. Larger of 2 remnants. Notes: Apple orchard planted in prairie. Probably 15-20 varieties of established apple trees that should be checked for heirloom varieties before any attempt is made to restore this tiny degraded prairie with fire. Notes on 'releve typical of stand': apple trees shading out creating habitat for shade tolerant spp.

Upland more level facies of forest near head of draw gently sheltered. Most of this forest type had recently been cut at time of survey so this is a bit more on slope than desirable to typify this MHs38.
Releve intended to represent terrace situation along small tributary stream, base of slope adjacent to stream.

Attempts to represent the upland forest that has largely been recently harvested. Logging supposedly high grading for walnut but looks like they cut a lot of other large trees. So this releve is in an unharvested pocket but some of the weediness can probably be attributed to the surrounding disturbance. Notes: Much dead and down and some of it (with) girth about 30cm dbh!
At very toe of slope where terrace of tributary merges into terrace of Des Moines River. Tributary is cut 1-2 m below this level. Clearly not quite a terrace forest.

Old-growth maple-basswood. Generally open subcanopy. All size classes of trees. Some open canopy gaps. Some large dense patches of Laportea. Large rotting stumps and logs. Thick, worm-free duff. Largest A. saccharum is 63cm dbh. Many Laportea browsed.
Trees average 25cm dbh. Apparently worm-free. Canopy gap in plot increases ground cover. Dense canopy elsewhere creates very sparse ground layer. Many fir logs in plot - fewer elsewhere.

Alder swamp ~3m tall. Low hummocks. Some pols have standing water. Sphagnum and other mosses just starting to colonize edges of hollows. Appears to be on successional path beween wet meadow (along river to N) and FPn73a.

Possibly earthworm-free. Aspens average 30cm dbh. Cedars 25cm. Nice coarse woody debris, mostly fallen firs, mostly fairly recently. Canopy gap in plot, more understory vegetation than most of stand. Possibly MHn35
Open canopy due to recently fallen firs, making decent amount of CWD, but little is well-decayed. Soil is reddish loamy sand too hard to penetrate with soil probe.

Surrounding area is MH system. Here is large inclusion on shallow bedrock, running NW to SE , 50m wide. Acer, Betula, Abies average 15cm dbh. Populus average 25cm. Single Quercus ~45cm. No sign of earthworms. Soil has charcoal, one depression holds water.
South of snowmobile trail in large patch dominated by Picea mariana and Thuja occidentalis within larger Larix laricina swamp. Average dbh is 15cm, max. spruce is 25 cm. Possibly FPn63b.

Nice, old-growth hardwoods. No stumps. Lots of large CWD. Maples look like old sugarbush. Nice strata - multilayered, w/ canopy gaps. Moderate leaf litter. Several ephemeral depressions nearby w/ black ash. Nicest spot in forest. Elsewhere is dominated by multistem Tilia that is younger.

No stumps seen. Moderately high amount of CWD, occasional small pool or small flowage/creek, otherwise fairly dry-mineral soil. Feels kind of junky. Lots of Taraxacum and occasional burdock. Designated old-growth - not spectacular. Occasional rocks exposed. ~120m west of forest road.

Large red pine scattered throughout, fair amt. of CWD. Pure sandy soils. Occ cut-burned stump - old. Could potentially qualify as old-growth. Slopes NE to lowland forested complex. Avg red pine DBH ~55cm, some measured 64, 63cm.

Large wetland complex stretches into Beltrami. Occ. aspen islands. Very quaky peat. Water at peat surface. Occ clumps of Betula and Myrica and Salix but overall dom. by sedges. Occ clumps of Typha. Bryophytes minimal.

Dry even hummocks. Brown mosses under thatch. Water not visible. Fen stretches far to south. On photo, appears burned in past, OPp91 is common throughout area - maybe frequent fire is keeping Calamagrostis dominant? Has elements of fen and wet meadow. Releve is ~75m south of road, but looks similar further south away from road.

Slight rolling terrain. Occ stump, not common. Typical of area. Some birch multistem. Patchy Corylus layer. Mature forest. Most of this area of island seems to be variations of this type - sometimes slightly more towards MHc26a. Tom Huette also present for Releve (Chippewa FS Botanist).

Soil is sandy loam with some clay. Low to moderate CWD. A few old Tilia stumps, but rare. Rolling topography, <5% slope. One canopy gap filling in with diverse strata. Aspen harvest ~10 years ago approximately 80 meters SE of plot.

Releve in center of opening between ring of taller stunted Larix and Picea.Water above peat level. Sphagnum dominated. Firm mat, but fairly wet. Occ slightly higher hummocks w/ clusters of Picea and Larix. Trees only avg. 5-15ft here. Mostly 5ft.

Slight undulations in topography, 50-70m from south shore of upper Red Lake. Nice, mature forest (old-growth). Good leaf litter, mod to low amt of CWD, no canopy gaps, no stumps. Soil loamy upper strata to fine sandy/silt. Very rich.

Forest cover not consistent with topsoil, entire area lowland hardwood mix. Area just south with more Ulmus, less Abies, and solid nettle. No stumps in plot; very few in surrounding area. Moderate small diameter CWD.

Stumps occ. Occ. standing dead jack pine. Canopy gaps common. Mix of mesic hardwood spp. w/ FD spp. Red pine avg dbh=35-40cm. Jack pine ~25cm. Good amt of P strobus reg'n. sdls.  pure sandy soils below 2 in.
Medium sized hummock ~1ft high. Sphagnum dominated - no open hollows. Water at and slightly above peat level. Several down trees. Some large tamarack in canopy layer ~45cm.

Moderate amt of CWD (cedar). Slight rise, among several others along west side of Upper Red Lake. Ridges closer to lake have more Tilia and bur oak. Soil top 6 inches is fibrous, woody peat w/ sand. Mosses on down debris, mainly.

Appears somewhat wormed. Leaf litter mod. in most parts. Occ bare spots. CWD is high. Downed debris everywhere, from whole old trees to snags. A few look like elm. Many are Betula. Shade is dense. Carex is heavy in patches. Mosses cover old logs. No stumps seen anywhere on island or in plot.

Medium to low hummocks. Dense cover of Osmunda cinnomomea, which is atypical for area. Unusual swamp. Small basin on island. Sphagnum dom cover. Rare water filled hollows, but shallow saturated peat. Surrounded by upland mesic hardwoods. Avg DBH Larix = 35-40 cm, Picea = 30-35cm.

Occ fire scarred (though not cut) stumps. No cut stumps in plot or elsewhere in vicinity. Avg DBH for red pine = 50cm. Releve done in a fairly dense pocket of red pine, but looks natural. Moderately low CWD, mostly small or old deciduous trees. Birch and Pop? occ large. (some Populus up to 65cm).

Occ cut large stump. Flat. Resembles a floodplain terrace forest. CWD mod to low - just occ downed trees and light debris and snags. Leaf litter somewhat thin ~1cm - very fibrous A horizon - then ~6 in + of loamy soil. Celtis much more prevalent in canopy going NW towards lakeshore (150m). one black ash cored with DBH of 60.5cm was est. to be 103yo.
Occasional cut stump. Gently rolling topography. Mature old-growth forest. Diverse strata. Mod-low CWD. Taxus much more common to SW ~250m. Recent selective cutting to SE ~100 meters.

Low area, w/ scattered bare soil spots, much like in floodplain forests. Very large silver maple with dbh ~70cm+. Avg. 40-50cm. Rare cedar nearby ~50m. Small creek cuts through here and flows to lake. Area must be a low spot w/ clay layer beneath. A subtle rise in topography just to the north of here is much different and has no Laportea.
Base of slope in a drainage area to lake that is to the north. No standing water but saturated, mucky soils. Several yellow birch regenerating. Slightly hummocky with some tip-ups.
Bouncy mat, water at peat surface. Degraded water track due to ditches/roads. Traces of string development. ~400ft from road. Fairly dry.
Med high hummocks. Transitioning to poor fen. Water level at peat surface. Thatch covered hollows. Several dead tamarack in canopy later. Slight water track signature.
Forested margin to a more open, stunted tamarack area. Trees here are tall and canopy ~30-40% cover. Shade tolerant spp common. Tall Salix common. Hummock/Hollows moderate-low. Open pools not common.

Poor fen in swale/bog drain/saddle between two higher portions of bog ridge. Water level at peat surface. GPS point references SW corner of plot. Also, there is a metal reference tag 180 degrees az (SW) from SW plot corner, affixed to a Picea mariana. Picea is 1.1m tall and 96cm dbh.

Open water pools make up ~1/8 of plot. Water at peat surface. Hummock med-low. Bog drain. SW corner of plot marked by GPS point. Point also referenced by a metal tag on a Picea that is 2m (175 az) south of SW marked corner. Picea is 83cm tall.

Mostly low even hummocks w/ no open water or hollows. Slightly higher hummocks where Larix and Picea are. Water slightly below peat surface. Very firm substrate. On edge of transition to more graminoid dominated area. Interior of ovoid island. GPS point marks SE corner of releve. SE corner also referenced w/ metal tag on Picea that is ~2.5m tall and 52cm southwest from corner or 345 degree azimuth.

Open pools in plot ~10%. Low even hummocks. Water at peat surface, very wet and soft. Transition between bog island and rich fen. Carpet. See adjacent releve 4145 where no pools are present. Not clear if plot is in same spot as Paul's original releve 4144A.

permanent_plot_type_description: ex. metal tag on nearby tree
remarks: Hummocks - low - no open pools. adjacent to 4144a or releve 9544 (this releve is being called 4144b). Linear features that transition from bog to fen. Water at peat surface. adjacent releve #9544 has more open pools. Metal tag at NE corner ~0.5m away on 1.4m tall Larix at 350 degrees az from plot corner.
Very bouncy mat in channel. Water at peat surface. Lots of thatch, few hollows, low hummocks. Further north, clones of Cladium common. Slightly more diverse here.

String and flark releve. Several large snails and leeches in the deep pools. Releve is in mostly the flark but comprises some string. Very wet and loose. Flark seems dominated mostly by Carex lasiocarpa and Rhynchospora. Carex. chordorrhiza and C. limosa mostly in flark. Lots of algae. This is a new monitoring releve, marked permanent. Releve in both string and flark b/c very narrow and somewhat similar spp in both. Marked with pole at SW corner.

place_name: Red Lake WMA - Western Water Track
remarks: Very wet. Water ~1/2ft above surface of peat. Hummocks minimal. Some thatch. Bouncy. Upper slope of featureless water track. Marked w/ pole at SW corner. No tag.

Open pools/hollows ~10% of plot. High hummocks sphagnum dominated. Hollows w/ sphagnum and Campyllium. No mistletoe. Avg. DBH for Larix ~10cm. Small island in watertrack near head of island. Windthrow common. Releve resurveyed probably more in interior island than original. Not clear where original was. Releve marked with pole at SW corner. Metal tag 70cm from SW corner. 45cm circ. (measured w/ meter tape) 220 degrees from post to tree. GPS point marked at NW corner?

Releve in Cladium clone. Somewhat firmer on mat where Cladium  is. Bouncy. Carex livida and C. limosa only in corner, coming in on edge of clone where releve boundary nears. Water slightly above peat surface. Cladium uniformly spread across plot. See releve #9551 that is in adjacent mud pool. No old markers for #4250, so releve may not be in exact spot.

Open pools ~30% of plot. Adjacent to Cladium clone. See releve #9550. Water slightly above peat surface. No mosses. Algae in pools is heavy. Very loose, bouncy mat. Easy to break through. No tag to mark original releve. Not sure re-survey is in correct spot.

Releve plot comprises the schlenke only. Species only recorded from within schlenke margins. NOT 10m x 10m plot. Water at peat surface. Eastern post is 140 degrees from west post. 2 posts put in to define edge of schlenke. Not a traditional 10 x 10 plot. Poles 6.8m wide. Waypoint marks west post. Additional species outside schlenke relieve include Eriophorum virginicum, occasional Picea.

Occ wet hollows, shallow med-low moss covered hummocks. Some blowdown and tipups. Good amt. of cedar regeneration. Large cedars ~35cm DBH. Spruce ~30cm. Avg cedar ~25cm. Seems like very appropriate habitat for Malaxis paludosa and Cypripedium arietinum, but neither were found.
Avg dbh ~35-40cm, some occ. 45-50. Fire scarred. Occ on relatively recent stumps (last 20 yrs?). Occ CWD. (**tall killed trees**??)
Larix and cedar dense - med high hummocks of Sphagnum. Not many open pools.
East edge of bog pond. Mostly firm mat w/ occ holes in mat by beavers near edge. Stunted Larix and Picea most dense at pond edge, then becomes more scattered and poor.

Wet meadow and shrub carr adjacent to Blackduck River. Shrub area more along margin and mostly of tall Salix petiolaris. Releve done in wet meadow area. Ground moist, but no standing water. Surrounded by floodplain terrace forest along the river.
Evidence of past flooding. Forest floor mostly exposed mineral soil. High amt of CWD on ground. Very open, no shrub layer. Most herbaceous plants on fallen old logs or on tree bases.

Acer avg DBH 50-60cm, Fraxinus nigra ~45cm. Terrace forest interspersed w/ bare scour channels. Releve does not include lower channels since they have wetter spp. composition. Ground moist but not saturated. Fair amt. of CWD.

White pine - red pine forest between Main Fish Fry & West Fish Fry Ponds. Area is designated a "Unique Biological Area" by Superior NF for its "patterned ground" geology, strongly fluctuating water levels, significance  as a shorebird migration stopover(due to mudflats associated with late season draw-down of ponds) & plant diversity. Soil horizons: A, Bw1, Bw2, 2C (gravelly coarse sand). Loamy mantle glacial drift over gravelly outwash parent material. 5% slope at 200 degree aspect @ soil description.

Black spruce - jack pine woodland. Small patch on peninsula, surrounded by Main Fish Fry Pond; one of several, strongly fluctuating ponds in area. Area is designated a "Unique Biological Area" by Superior National Forest, for its "patterned ground" geology & and plant diversity. Community complex (especially mudflats area that surrounds ponds during late summer/early fall)is also a migratory stopover for shorebirds. Soil horizons: A (cobbly coarse sandy loam), BC (very gravelly loamy coarse sand), C (very gravelly coarse sand). Gravelly outwash parent material. Complex slope; short backslope on side of convex ridge: 12% on south aspect. Nearby shoreline is a pavement of cobbles and stones.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Northeastern Bedrock)
remarks: Old growth red pine - white pine woodland. Fire scars on red pine trunks. Soils with likely layer of ash from previous fire. Red pine strongly leaning. Two windthrown red pine in plot. Many exposed boulders & some exposed bedrock in plot. Rock outcrop patch adjacent.

Bedrock shrubland. Medium-sized patch. Along north-northwest facing, upper portion of ridge. Part of extensive rock outcrop & woodland complex. Herbaceous vegetation patchy within plot. Bedrock is somewhat terraced. Small amount of large, downed logs are windthrown jack pine.

Black spruce - jack pine woodland. Soil with moderate litter (3cm) & humus (3cm) with no evidence of worms. Exposed boulders are bryophyte-covered. Scattered downed logs. Topography moderately. variable (flat to knobby) over large area. Landscape heterogenous (FDn43, FRDn33, FDn32) dependent on position & soil development.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Northeastern Bedrock)
remarks: Old red pine - white pine woodland on high point above Crooked lake. Dominated by white pine. Small patches of rock outcrop. Good diversity of ages among white pine & red oak. No evidence of cutting on knob, but some cut stumps in red pine/white pine forest on surrounding slope.
Rich black spruce swamp basin, surrounding Frolic Lake and associated shrub shore fen. Surrounded by FDn32 woodlands with small patches of ROn23 bedrock shrubland. Drains to Crooked Lake.

Small patch of Northern Floodplain Forest behind shoreline on Crooked Lake. Represents regularly occurring community associated with bouldery areas near lake level. Humus layer somewhat fibrous. Downed logs wash up during flooding every year. Currently dry. State land within BWW.

Leatherleaf-Sweet Gale Shore Fen. Broad, linear patch, slightly above lakeshore elevation of Crooked Lake. Transitions from predominantly leatherleaf & sweet gale w/ scattered Sphagnum hummocks, to a mix with Alnus and nearly continous Sphagnum cover. Seasonally saturated. No discreet drainage.

Old growth lowland white cedar forest. Abundant large hummocks & hollows. Abundant, multi-layered, well-integrated, large downed logs. Bryophytes covering trunks into sub-canopy. No evidence of browse, game trails scattered No evidence of fire. Broken bedrock slopes with cedar canopy to north & west. Johnna Hyde assisted with this releve.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Old growth red pine-white pine woodland on knob of large island in Saginaga Lake. Large downed logs & small canopy gaps occasional throughout. Microtopography resulting from buried large, downed logs, rocks covered with bryophytes and occasional tip-ups. Shoreline woodlands with higher proportion of red pine in canopy.

Old growth, poor black spruce swamp. Phenology behind normal, affecting cover somewhat. Scattered downed logs. Feather mosses relegated to raised areas at base of trees. No evidence of cutting. Boundary Waters Wilderness.

Old mesic mixed forest dominated by white birch, on north-facing slope of Eagle Mt. complex. Overall homogenous landscape w/ scattered super-canopy white pine, red pine, white spruce. Occasional jack pine woodlands associated w/BR outcrops. No evidence of worms, cutting or fire. Scattered large, downed logs. Humus over boulders.

Black spruce-jack pine woodland. Small, east-facing patch on rim of Brule Mt. w/in matrix of FDn43b1. Dominated by white birch, after white spruce and balsam fir in overstory died (natural disturbance). Aspen saplings & Sorbus browsed by moose). Moderate-large downed logs (jack pine). No evidence of fire.

Black Spruce Bog (semi-treed subtype). Trees health moderately affected by Arceuthobium pusillum (mortality in canopy very light). Downed logs very light. No evidence of other disturbance. Moderate level of wildlife trails. Johnnie Hyde assisted with this releve.

Old growth upland white cedar forest in drainage valley. Some canopy blowdown (1999?). Large Pinus strobus(3), Thuja occidentalis(9) & Pinus resinosa(2) in plot. Obvious seasonal drainage with 5-25% bare ground & accumulated debris. Abundundat. Geaster("earthstar" fungi). Cedar seedlings on moss-covered logs.  Plot follows community downslope within valley.
Crystalline bedrock outcrop in woodland matrix. Scattered large boulders. Fire scar on old jack pine tip-up, among group of four jack pine tip-ups.

Black spruce - jack pine woodland, in mid-slope position on broad, SE-facing slope above North Lske. Fire scars indicate year of origin-1936. One of few areas not burned in Ham Lake Fire (2007). Scattered, patchy windthrow (balsam fir), otherwise, large, downed logs are single treefall (jack pine, aspen). Worms in soil sample. Johnna Hyde assisted with this releve.

Old growth black spruce - jack pine woodland on west-facing ridge, high above Red Rock Lake. Adjacent community, including small jack pine woodland-BR(FDn22a) and small, north-facing dry mafic cliff (CT11a). Moderate large downed logs. Scattered standing dead jack pine. Bryos over BR w/loam-filled cracks. Black-backed woodpecker sighted.

Rich black spruce swamp with white cedar & tamarack co-dominant. Adjacent mesic mixed forest & woodlands low relief, w/black spruce throughout. Very hummocky, deep hollows and short channels throughout. No evidence of Arceuthobium pusilum. Deep, well-used moose trail along edge.

Old growth white pine/red pine forest on east slope of large hill. Surface w/ abundant boulders and moderate amount of large downed logs. White pine in 3 strata, good seedling reproduction. Moose sign, but browse light-moderate. Humus w/ charcoal.

Jack pine-black spruce feathermoss forest on small island in Larch Lake. Only unburned upland patch on or adj to lake (Ham Lake Fire-2007). Island has campsite and trail along ridge. Plot w/out trails, but w/ several small cut stumps. Several downed trees (black spruce) in plot. Island w/ steep n/s-facing rocky slopes. Lisa Raetz assisted with this releve.

Old growth lowland white cedar forest. Abundant water filled pockets. Mod-abund large downed logs. Old beaver-chewed ash. No evidence of human disturbance. Occasional charred tree in surrounding area of wet forest. Lisa Raetz assisted with this releve.

Black spruce bog. Dominant community along Larch Creek. Poor conifer swamp (APn81b) & small patches of low shrub poor fen (APn91a) occur adjacent to creek. No evidence of cutting. No evidence of fire. Moose trails light within community. Boreal chickadee seen. Lisa Raetz assisted with this releve.

Lowland white cedar forest. Narrow zone along shale-bottomed, intermittent stream bed. Tall,large diameter Thuja occidentalis, Fraxinus nigra, Pinus strobus in canopy. Very large downed logs, good Thuja seedling regeneration and bryophyte cover. Patches w/ bare soil due to sometimes strong seasonal drainage & rain events. Chel Anderson & John Green (Geologist, UMD) assisted in this survey of the creek valley.

Very old black spruce-jack pine woodland on ~1/2 acre island. Canopy converting to black spruce and red pine. Entire island same comm. Perimeter w/ more JP & RP in canopy. Plot follows ridge ~15m above lake. Abundant large, downed logs(JP) w/ small areas of bare ground w/needle cover.

Remnant patch of old growth black spruce-jack pine woodland on Alpine Lake (Cavity Fire 2006). Combined with adjacent unburned FDn43 & Cedar Swamp drainage, among largest unburned patches on lake. Abundant large downed JP. No evidence of browsing. Moss depth 2-3cm. Layered shrubs. Abundant cedar regeneration.

npc_subtype_name: Jack Pine - Black Spruce - Aspen Subtype
remarks: Young black spruce - jack pine woodland from wildfire (Roy Lake Fire-1976) in previously undisturbed landscape. Community with small, scattered outcrops and scattered large, downed JP from prior growth stage. ROn12 w/in plot. Moose droppings & light browse. No evidence of worms.

Large patch old growth mesic mixed forest across broad, low hill between Grandpa and Hivernant Lakes. Scattered,large diameter JP (40cm) and Acer rubrum (30cm) outside plot and abundant large, downed logs in various stages of decay throughout. Portions of community dominated by BS or Aspen, RM, BS & BF mix. Small patches with slightly wetter soils, some sphagnum. Charcoal fragments at 18cm. Portions burned in 1976 & 2005 wildfires.

OG lowland white cedar forest. Lg. diam cedar and broad, connected hummocks among small-med cedar and lg. sat. hollows. Surr upland patch often co-dom. by lg diam cedar (w/ Taxus canadensis). Lg CWD on surf = mod. Well-dev microtopog. Abund cedar regen. Few, old cut stumps.

Poor black spruce swamp. Undulating microtopog from buried logs and sphagnum hummocks. Scatt downed logs on surf. No evidence of cutting. Labrador tea mostly <1.0m ht. & rel sparse. Diverse mix of sphag spp. Effects of Arceuthobium pusillum not obvious.

The site is a marsh dominated by Sagittaria latifolia. At the time of survey there was no standing water. Approximately 5-10% of the releve plot was bare mud. Other forbs in the plot were more abundant up from the center of the depression.

Old growth lowland white cedar forest on island. Bouldery,broken ground with temporary pools. Abundant bryophyte cover. Tree regeneration in gaps includes cedar. Island criss-crossed with beaver trails. No deer sign. Large patch of blown down cedar in center of island.

Plot represents a large, rock outcrop (ROn23a) community that is regularly repeated on the tops of steeply rolling, bedrock ridges. Overall, tree & shrub cover on outcrop is patchy (25%). Ridge is level, sloping roughly equally on all sides. Surrounded by woodlands. Ridges in linear landscape pattern.

Poor black spruce swamp. Very little Arceuthobium pusilum. Very few down trees. Old, winter trail still evident, but narrow. Community part of acid peatland complex with low shrub poor fen, graminoid poor fen, large peatland pond & scattered wooded upland islands dominated by jack pine, black spruce and other conifers.

Black spruce - jack pine woodland surrounded by acid peatland complex. Low relief, low amount of downed logs. Patchy clumps with higher density subcanopy and shrub layer of white pine, black spruce, paper birch, scattered red pine across island. State land in BWCAW.

Old growth white pine-red pine forest surrounded by old growth red pine-white pine woodland (NE Bedrock). Large, downed logs and tip-ups over long time period, create strong micro-topographic structure and substrate for white pine seedlings and abundant saplings. No evidence of fire. Lightning strike in plot. No browse, no worms. Johnna Hyde assisted with this releve.

Old growth upland white cedar forest in center of small island. Plot on crest of rocky knob above lowland white cedar forest. Community frequent across island on upper levels of rolling topography. No evidence of fire. Microtopography a combination of tree boles, bedrock below the surface and bryophyte accumulation. Johnna Hyde assisted with this releve. No evidence of fire.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Northeastern Bedrock)
remarks: Red pine - white pine woodland. Fire scars on trunks, lightning strike on red pine (still living). Charcoal in humus layer. Moderate large, downed logs. Microtopography consists primarily of feather moss covered boulders. BWCAW.

Old growth Black Spruce-Jack Pine Woodland. No evidence of recent disturbance. Large, intact patch. Large downed logs light-moderate in plot & patch (mostly single tree fall). Boulders moss-covered and just below surface. Releve representative of FDn32c in area around this section of the North Branch Cascade River.

Old upland white cedar forest. Moderate amount of med-sized downed logs. No evidence of fire. Strong microtopography due to boulders. No evidence of worms. Bottom of humus layer well-decomposed w/ good water-holding capacity. Moose browse light. Johnnie Hyde assisted with this releve.

Old growth upland white cedar forest representative of this elevational gradient. Matrix is FDn43 with significant FDn43c patches. No evidence of fire. Fairly deep humus layer. No evidence of worms. Abundant large downed logs with thick moss & seedling layer. Pinus strobus 35m ht, Thuja occidentalis 20m ht. Orientation of plot is parallel to and along elevational gradient.

Black spruce-jack pine woodland. Plot characterizes ridge lines in this area. Other portions of patch w/ larger amount of jack pine blowdown. Small patches of lichen-covered rock outcrop. Scattered, exposed boulders. Moderate large downed logs (jack pine). Topography undulating series outcrops interspersed with woodlands/forests.

Rich black spruce swamp, with Thuja occidentalis patches in canopy & high shrub layer, some areas with Picea mariana canopy & depauperate herb layer. Community influenced by both lake edge to east-northeast and 2007 Ham Lake Fire to south. Community with inclusions of Wet Forest Cedar (WFn53a) and Black Spruce-Feathermoss Woodland (FDn32c3). BWCAW. Johnna Hyde assisted with this releve.

Black Spruce Feathermoss Forest on lower bench of jack pine-black spruce forest slope adj to lake. Steepest portion of slope with abundant cedar in jack pine, black spruce, paper birch, aspen mix. FDn32c3 continues along top rim of otherwise burned area of peninsula. Orthilia secunda sampled for genetic study (Gemma Beatty, Queens University, Belfast). Johnna Hyde assisted with this releve.

Poor black spruce swamp, surrounded by uplands that were severely burned in 2007 (Ham Lake fire). No evidence of fire within community. Moderate amount of downed logs on surface. Shrubs increase toward edge. No hollows. Abundant moose trails throughout. Johnna Hyde assisted with this releve.

Crystalline bedrock outcrop above Granite River. Burned in Ham Lake Fire (2007)and Sag Corridor Fire (1995). Most veg in plot dessicated. Surrounding woodlands are young forest aspen birch with dense, mixed shrub layer. Scattered, burned, large downed logs are jack pine 20cm dbh. Young, standing jack pine is burned. Johnna Hyde assisted with this releve.

Poor tamarack - black spruce swamp. Remnant patch along Sea Gull Creek after Ham Lake Fire (2007). Portion of swamp complex clearcut in 2000. Strong edge effects (drying, increase light, wind). Moose sign throughout. Taxus canadensis abundant. No evidence of cutting or arceuthobium in community. Hollows w/ standing water.

Lowland white cedar forest along north Brule River. Linear patches repeated along river corridor. Surface very uneven, thin humus over rock, hollows and crevices very moist, likely water-filled during high water periods. All canopy Abies balsamea are dead. Lightning strike at base of Populus tremuloides.

Rich black spruce swamp. Moderate-sized patch surrounded by woodlands, burned in Ham Lake Fire (2007). Scattered tip-ups (canopy trees), abundant water-filled hollows. Moose trails light. No evidence of human disturbance. Flagging and sawn downed logs along edge suggest fire "mop-up" activity. Lisa Raetz assisted with this releve.

A somewhat wet-mesic example of FDn43b1. Topography gently undulating, with occasional saturated hollows and small areas w/Fraxinus nigra and higher bryophyte cover (incl. Sphagnum). Moderate microtopography, Large, downed logs light-moderate. Scattered small-med old stumps. No evidence of fire. Soil not obviously wormed, but 1 Dendrobaena worm in soil sample.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Red pine- white pine woodland along narrow ridge top. Large diameter downed logs (Pinus banksiana & Thuja occidentalis). Depth to BR ranges from 0-42cm. FDn43c (Upland white cedar forest) on NW slope & FDn43b1 (Aspen-Birch Forest (BF subtype)on SE slope. Light moose browse. Abundant small mammal (chipmunk) holes.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Northeastern Bedrock)
remarks: Red pine - white pine woodland above narrow channel leaving Saganaga Lake, at SW corner of American Point Peninsula. Patchy canopy of large diameter red pine w/light cover of high shrubs. Adjacent community transitional, surrounding community FDn43a. Large, downed logs are balsam fir & paper birch.

OG upland white cedar forest on mid-low hills, w/ lowland wet cedar forest betw. Soils bouldery. Downed log recruit. consistently mod. Well-dev microtopography. No evidence of cutting @ plot, but a few scatt cut stumps in broader area. Charcoal betw humus & A-horizon (@6cm).
Upper slope where apparent maple basswood canopy still prevails (N & W where land flattens oak begins to prevail). There is much bare ground in this releve. Rich MHs38 or dry MHs39.

Small isolated knoll surrounded by crops, with another knoll less than 1/8 mile west. Typical flora but somewhat unusual landscape setting as most remaining prairie in county is either associated with steep slopes of Des Moines river & tributaries or with margins of wetlands.
Typical hill prairie remnant in the middle of a corn field, TNC preserve protected upon initiative of local garden club in the late 1980s.
Level area at base of hill waypoint 59, very forby. Site is largely disturbed land, marsh & bromy uplands but has these narrow bands of wet prairie around the emergent marshes.
A sweet place for local folks easily to view prairie wildflowers right by a road. Tiny but diverse.

Very nice area of hill prairie, midslope facing wetland to the west. Some of this slope appears to be harvested for grass seed. Notes: Should learn about frequency of seed harvest. They are likely harvesting Lespedeza near here.
Ups13d at very edge of more mesic complex east of egg-shaped cattail swamp.

This community intergrades from a wet prairie to a wet meadow. It is at base of UPs13d hill with gravelly soil & experiences some seepage at downslope end. It occurs in a zone all along E side of wetland complex with an arm extending into gentle draw.

Floristically community is a sort of intergrade between UPs13 & UPs23; structurally it feels like UPs23. This community occupies lower slopes & draws between UPs13d on hill and an extensive complex of wet prairie/wet meadow/emergent marsh.

One half acre BC hill prairie (UPs13d) grading downslope and along gentle spur at east end into a mesic zone. Typical SW MN flora with invasion of wild carrot at east end. Drop of approximately 5 meters from crest to creek in a distance of approximately 30 meters. Best prairie at northwest end of knoll. Managed with fire.

D rank native prairie being shaded at south end by heavy cottonwood growth between road and former rail ROW. Probably not viable as a natural community per se, but proximity to Trimont suggests potential interpretive use and good seed source for Martin Co SWCD local ecotype project. From back of form: Graminoid layer very poor: thin and depauperate. Releve is in open area north of large clump of trees.

Abandoned rail right of way in private ownership with a fair amount of woody invasion around edges. Probably not sustainable as a native plant community because of size and shape but good seed source for Martin Co. SWCD native ecotype project. Releve is long and skinny bc of RR ROW.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Deep hollows of water ~30cm. Hummocks moss-covered. Smaller depression in larger undulating landscape. Peat 1-2 ft deep. Transitions into black ash swamp. Largest trees ~39cm. Smaller trees ~9.5cm. Dead snags and downed trees (mostly fir).
Soil very sandy, old burned stumps. Many gopher mounds (fox?/voles?). Charcoal in sand/soil.
Old cut stumps. Sig. CWD. Depth to semi-permeable layer is >100cm. Possibly FDc34b or MHc26a.
OG stand, some CWD. Pictures 76-80. some old p. birch, snags. Woodpeckers. Possibly FDc24.

Typical of ~10-acre patch of old growth cedar on bedrock terrace at base of 260-foot north-facing slope at east end of Pine Lake. Trees 35-50cm d.b.h., straight to leaning. No stumps. Much CWD. Substrate is peat- hummocks & hollows, snags rare. Lowland cedar (WFn) grading to forested cedar peatland (FPn). Rove-Slate Bedrock Complex LTA.

Typical of forest matrix this vicinity. Moderate windthrow from 1999 storm. Gentle south-facing upper slope, just below crest of ~340-foot ridge. Rocky silt. Fire scars on ridgetop pines. No stumps. Moderate amount of CWD. Aspen/birch 20-45cm d.b.h., lone pine ~60cm. Litter intact, no earthworm evidence, occasional surface boulders. Rove-Slate Bedrock Complex LTA. Plot just inside BWCAW.

Mid-slope of very steep, 340-foot, north-facing slope, rugged bedrock terrain at east end of Pine Lake. Colluvial silty soil, scattered small, moss-covered diabase outcrops. No stumps. Occasional snags. Rather sparse CWD. Trees 15-30cm d.b.h. Fire-scarred pines atop ridge. CWD becoming moderate (more abundant) downslope. Rove-Slate Bedrock Complex LTA.

Old growth upland cedar on rather narrow, level to gently sloping peninsula between Pine & McFarland Lakes. Trees mostly straight boles, 30-50cm d.b.h. Moderate amount of CWD, mostly older material. This spot mostly spared by 1999 windstorm (1999 windthrow quite prevalent nat far to the west). No stumps. Silt loam with rocks; thick litter. Low spots in plot are slightly more moist but still ~mesic (not wet). Snags occasional. Plot centrally located beween the lakes. Old growth cedar extends upslope southeastward; huge Pinus strobus become frequent here. Rove-Slate Bedrock Complex LTA.

Typical of ~5-30 foot wide zone bordering open water along ponded area (slack water) of flowage between Mulligan & Wanihigan Lakes. Area exposed in last ~5 years due to beaver dam failure that lowered water level ~3 feet. Grades to dominated by emergent plants toward water, and to more diverse graminoids toward upland. Portage trail now runs along upland margin- prior to beaver dam failure, this water body was much more navigible (canoe-friendly) and was part of canoe portion of route.

Plot 5 x 10 meters, on gently sloping sandy shore in bay of Winchell Lake. Plot includes some area of shallow water (<10cm deep). Fine sand substrate, with thin organic veneer in places. Beach exposed by seasonally ~average low water levels. Sandy shoreline habitat is quite limited in occurrence and extent on this lake and on most other Cook County Lakes. Poplar Lake Bedrock Complex LTA.

Typical of narrow to fairly broad zone of low-statured (~stunted) vegetation on shore of ~2-acre bog pond in 25-acre wetland basin south of Grassy Lake. This zone is subtly lower and wetter than the surrounding zones of more typical poor fen. Plot at water's edge on south shore of pond. Deep, quaky, saturated peat. The occasional 18" tall hummocks here are atypical of this wetter (depressional)zone. Grades to more typical low shrub poor fen, which grades further from pond to poor conifer swamp. Vegetable Lakes Till Plain LTA.

Upper slope on 60-foot, south-facing, bedrock ridge in rolling terrain south of Grassy Lake. ~10% exposed granitic bedrock (leucogranite), remainder is shallow loamy organic soil (detritus) over bedrock.  Plot accounts for ~50% of the open-canopied outcrop community here. Gentle to moderately steep south-facing slope. No stumps. Sparse CWD. Community intact other than invasive Rumex & Hieracium. Vegetable Lakes Till Plain LTA.

Typical of fairly broad wetter and subtly lower-lying areas on margin of ~5-acre pond in ~10-acre basin along drainage through rugged bedrock terrain west of Echo Lake. 1+ acres of this habitat expression. Grades to more typical Carex lasiocarpa rich fen. Saturated peat >40cm deep, shallow water (<2cm), low hummocks (<10cm tall). Vegetable Lakes Till Plain LTA.

Slightly different than nearby releve (9652) to north in same stand. Much more conifer. Very rocky soil. Occasional stumps. Young even-aged forest surrounding this small spot. Essentially flat, but subtle rolling topography.

Tilia mostly single stem and straight. Good leaf litter cover. Sandy loam soil. Occasional fir in nearby lower areas. Populus and Tilia avg 40-45cm DBH. Red oak average DBH slightly larger. Topography flat here, but subtle rolling topography elsewhere. Rocky soil deeper in soil horizon as seen in tip-up. Occasional old stumps. Occasional small to medium boulders at surface. Moderate coarse woody debris.

On drier end of forested peatland releve just south of "esker"-like formation that ends in middle of swamp, and this is where the bulk of ram's-head orchids occur. M
edium-low hummocks. Hollows not water filled - just moist. Dappled sun. Lots of coarse woody debris.

Small open fen within alder swamp. releve in semi-treed margin. High hummocks, water filled hollows and animal trails. Arethusa restricted to margin of fen, where releve is located. There are more stunted trees but becomes more sedge dominated near center (see releve 9655) and has spring fen-like qualities.

Opening in cedar swamp with spring fen-like qualities. Releve in center of sedge dominated mat. Transitions to ring of stunted Larix and Picea and then cedar swamp. Water filled hollows and tracks. Bouncy mat. See nearby releve 9654.
Soil is loamy sand. Good leaf litter cover. No pine regeneration. Average red pine DBH = 40cm. Average white pine DBH = 40-50cm. Occasional charred stumps. On west side of Rickles lake.

Average jack pine DBH = 20cm, largest = 35cm. Patchy openings. Soil sand. Wide range of jack pine sizes and age classes. Many older jack pine are dead and falling down. No stumps in releve. Solid Pluerozium and Cladina moss layer. Fair amount of jack pine regeneration.
Medium sphagnum hummocks. Water at peat surface. Poor fen ringed by stunted black spruce and tamarack. Open middle with occasional black spruce. Peat very spongy and bouncy.
Dominated mostly by sphagnum, occasion brown mosses. No hummocks. Water at peat surface. Not a floating mat, but quaky. No shrubs. Phalaris along fen edge near forest edge.
Small patches of sphagnum. Mostly brown mosses. Water at peat surface. Wet meadow perched on slope in drainage area above forested peatland below.

Low, even hummocks. Small areas of drainage, sandy deposits in discharge areas. No water flowing at this time. occasional tip-up. In canopy gaps, dense fir saplings, occasion cut stump. Average cedar DBH = 35-40cm. Upper DBH is 59cm. Forested swamp on west side of Necktie River.

Average red pine DBH = 30cm, some 55-60cm. Occasional stumps. Average DBH for Jack Pine = 25-30cm. Soil sandy loam - sand. A lot of Carex pensylvanica. Many Betula multi-stemmed. No pine regeneration. On north side of Sand River. This appears to be a somewhat overgrown woodland.
Water just below peat level. Brown mosses dominate. Bouncy but not floating. Typha and phalaris heavy along creek edge.

Native Plant Community: OPn92/OPn81. Kabekona River: Typical of veg. along river. Immediately adjacent to water is wild rice. Very wet with little to no mosses visible. Some brown mosses present, are <1%. Closer to edge of forest, becomes dense Betula pumila.
Even hummocks, occasion open mucky pools, tip-ups and coarse woody debris moderate to little. No cut stumps. Average cedar DBH: 35-40cm.

Native Plant Community: WFn55/WFs57. Sloping wet forest with drainage channels throughout. Water currently flowing through. Soils are moist and mucky. Areas nearby on slightly higher ground are loamy coarse sand. No standing water in pools. Average Fraxinus DBH = 20-30cm.

Native Plant Community: MHc26a/FDc34. West facing slope. Occasional charred stump. Low coarse wood debris. Soil loamy fine sand. Releve on crest of slope to lake in cluster of red pines. Red pine average DBH; 45-50cm, occasionally to 55cm. West side of Camp Lake.

Mostly flat terrain. Thick needle duff roughly 1 inch with soils of very fine sand. Feels almost silty. One red pine cored here with DBH of 45cm was at least 85-90 years old. Ave DBH for Red Pine = 45-50cm. Occasion stump rare. Jack pine mostly dead in area.

Nice woodland characteristics, but weedy in patches. Jack Pine 35-40cm DBH, Red Pine 40-45cm DBH. Occasional stumps. Soil is pure sand. Prairie species preset. Nice woodland characterstics. Stand cut in 2010(late winter).

Dense pine stand with occasional white pine, heavy hazel shrub layer of 60-70% cover. Designated old-growth, but does not appear "old-growth." Average red pine DBH is 25-30cm, a few are 45cm. Average white pine DBH is 45cm. A lot of needle duff. Very little moss/lichen cover. Occasional old stump. Soil is fine sandy loam.

Native plant community: AP/FPn82a. Hummocks medium to high. peat >50cm deep. less fibric than most places and very black. Water seeping in @ 30cm down. Fairly open here. Much more poor than releve 9672 nearby. Very atypical habitat for Malaxis paludosa. This ares seems somewhat transitional between acid peatland and forested peatland. Unusually heavy cover of Carex stricta. 45 Rams-head orchids found in and surrounding releve and 5 Malaxis paludosa. all found mostly on top of hummocks.

Even hummocks of sphagnum and feathermosses. Releve is inclusion within larger cedar swamp which is more open on either side and poorer. Releve encompasses entire area where Malaxis paludosa was found. 15 Malaxis paludosa found. 25 Cypripedium arietinum.

Very fine sandy loam. Somewhat thin leaf litter. Many Tilia are multi-stemed Occasional boulders at soil surface. occasional stumps, some fire scarred. Seems to be between MHc26 and MHc37. Many subtle low areas that have more wet forest affinity species in them.

Soils sand. occasional stump. Larger area (surrounding stand) of patchy quality. Average Red Pine DBH in canopy in 50-55cm. Average Jack Pine DBH: 30-35cm. Areas nearby have more fir and red maple than releve. East side of Mississippi River. Stand Cut in 2009/2010.
Wet meadow along La Salle Creek in Itasca State Park. Some water in between hollows, especially closer to creek.
Patchy sphagnum cover, about 80%. Mat firm, not bouncy. Center of fen more uniformly dominated by Chamaedaphne.

No stumps seen. Slope ~20 degrees. Community fairly typical for these east and northeast facing slopes. Nearby ravines are much more rich though, with many species with northern affinities. Good leaf litter. Did not record moss layer.

Forest approximately 60-80 years old? Dominated by even-aged canopy of red oak plus others. Moderate coarse woody debris. West face slope approximately 10-15 degrees. Occasional exposed medium-large boulders. Little to no tall shrub layer. largest oaks approximately 55-60cm DBH only occasional, more typical oak DBH is 30 cm. Leaf litter somewhat thin. Soil is sandy loam and very rocky. No stumps seen.

Canopy seems mostly even-aged. Nearby, varying stages of ages (younger) as a result of logging activities. In areas where older, such as in releve, often dominated by Populus tremuloides, Acer saccharum, and Tilia americana. Younger areas dominated by Populus tremuloides/Birch only. Undulating topography. High elevation in county on Itasca Moraine. Fire tower nearby. Scattered boulders. Stumps occasional in releve area. Average Populus tremuloides DBH = 40-42cm

Mixed pine/hardwood forest. Lots of boulders, medium to small. Occasionl stumps, but rare. Tall fire scarred killed trees. Two inches of thick needle duff, then pure fine sand - brown and powdery. Average white pine DBH: 55-60cm.
Water at peat level, bouncy mat. All brown mosses in hollows. On Birch Creek, west side.
Fen dominated by Carex lasiocarpa. Fairly wet. Some sphagnum, 40-50% cover. The rest are brown mosses. Fen rings open water in center. Upland recently harvested. Connects to Hennepin Creek.

Most Tilia straight, single stem. Litter moderate. Evidence of worms in nearby old logging trail with worm castings. Slightly rolling. No stumps seen in plot or nearby. Coarse woody debris moderate, mosses mostly on down debris.  
Soil: 0-4cm organic over, 4-6cm fibrous loam, over >6cm fine sandy silty loam w/small pebbles.

Typical of gradual to moderately steep, southeast-facing, upper slope of 200-foot ridge north of Eagle Mtn. Exposed, disintegrating granitic outcrops cover ~25% of substrate in plot. Fire scars on old trees. Jack pines 15-45cm dbh, ~25% mortality; white pines 10-35cm. Moderate amount of CWD. Bedrock is salmon-colored granitic (leucogranite) disintegrating in place, covered by lichens. Soil loamy, fairly shallow (~15cm) to bedrock. Vegetable Lakes Till Plain LTA.

Upper slope of southwest-facing, moderately steep, 60-foot ridge along Ball Club Creek. Jack pines 38-42cm dbh, ~15% mortality, lots of CWD (jack pine & balsam fir). No stumps. Thick litter and humus over very rocky brown silty clay; soil fairly shallow to bedrock. Scattered gabbro/diabase outcrops. Grades to mature aspen with black spruce and balsam fir understory atop ridge. Vegetable Lakes Till Plain LTA.

Typical of matrix forest in rolling to rugged terrain north of Eagle Mtn. Plot on moderately steep, north-facing, lower portion of 220-foot slope. No stumps. A fire-scarred pine bole nearby. Moderate amount of CWD. Thick litter, thin humus. Rocky brown clayey-silt. No worms. Small moss-covered outcrops (leocogranite) and mossy boulders in plot. No windthrow here despite rather extensive and frequent windthrow in greater area north of Eagle Mtn. Vegetable Lakes Till Plain LTA.

Typical of low-lying (wetter) microsites which constitute ~25% of ~5-acre wetland basin in fairly rugged terrain south of Globe Lake. Saturated quaky peat >40cm deep, upper 20cm fibric, hemic below. No woody remains. Closed basin (no flow through this wetland). Not sure if this fen expression is on the OP or AP side of the line. Grades to zones dominated by Carex lasiocarpa, with more Myrica and no Rhynchospora spp., Utricularia cornuta, Drosera inetrmedia, etc. Stunted cedars on outer margin of wetland. Misquah Hills in the Vegetable Lakes Till plain LTA.

Typical of fairly homogeneous ~4-acre basin in rolling bedrock terrain south of Lux Lake. Basin flooded by beaver in past. Fibric peat >40cm deep, very wet and quaking, water ~12cm deep in foot tracks, peat highly-decomposed. Large chunks of wood in peat & on surface. Alder cover is ~2-5% over entire basin. Poplar Lake Bedrock Complex LTA.

Mature stand, trees 30-45cm dbh. Moderately steep, mid-slope of ~260-foot ridge southeast of Misquah Lake, part of fairly extensive patch of aspen-birch-fir forest. North-northeast aspect. No stumps. Much CWD- mostly balsam fir & birch. Occasional old root wad (tip-up) mounds. Very rocky, grey, fine silty-clay; thick litter, no worms. Frequent moss-covered boulders. Vegetable Lakes Till Plain LTA.

Typical of ~5 acres in ~10-acre open wetland along small drainage in rolling bedrock terrain west of Vista Lake. Saturated moderately quaky peat. Shallow water in troughs between fairly tight hummocks that rise ~16 inches. Wetland periodically flooded by beaver, but this zone above (upgradient enough from) most flooding impact. Poplar Lake Bedrock Complex LTA.

Typical of narrow to fairly broad (to 15m wide) zone surrounding small (~1-acre) bog pond in rolling bedrock terrain north of Winchell Lake. Edge of plot 1m from edge of water (outside narrow band of Carex lasiocarpa along water's edge). Quaky, fibric, moss peat >60cm deep, saturated, water just below surface. Vegetation rather stunted in this zone of subtle wetter depressions and low hummocks. Plot not typical of community type, typical of yet undescribed type/subtype that often occurs on margins of bog ponds ("low-statured vegetation bog pond variant"). Poor conifer swamp surrounds the fen-pond complex. Poplar Lake Bedrock Complex LTA. This is an Ed Cushing study site.

Typical of several hundred acres of bedrock woodland in rolling terrain north of Kiskadinna Lake. Plot on crest of gradually sloping low ridge that rises ~30-50 feet above small adjacent wetlands. Mature stand; jack pines 20-30cm d.b.h., black spruce to 25cm. Few snags. Small old stumps occasional to frequent in vicinity. This is part of a large area (~550-acres) logged in ~1960's (1954-1972)and visible on 1991 NAPP photography. Soil sandy-silt, shallow to bedrock (gabbro), ~22cm deep in pit; upper 5cm organic over sandy silt, reddish at depth. Scattered surface boulders and small outcrops. Poplar Lake Bedrock Complex LTA.

Typical of much of 1/2-mile long by 1/8-mile wide bedrock-entrenched wetland basin in rolling bedrock terrain south of Finn Lake. Plot centrally located ~30m from upland margins. Saturated fibric peat >40cm deep. Trees stunted, 2-12cm dbh. Occasional snags. Hummocks rise to 30cm tall. Becomes slightly richer eastward with Menyanthes trifoliata and Platanthera clavellata. Adjacent uplands are jack pine-black spruce bedrock woodland with extensive windthrow. Poplar Lake Bedrock Complex LTA.

Typical of small patch (~5 acres) in several hundred acres of jack pine-black spruce woodland, ~90% of which was blown down in past 5-10 years. Mature stand, jack pine 20-40cm d.b.h., black spruce 10-22cm. Frequent snags. No stumps. Plot on low ridgetop and gently-sloping upper slope. Sandy-silt < ~10cm deep to gabbro bedrock. A-horizon & litter/humus ~1cm; 1-35cm reddish-brown sandy-silt; 35-40cm fine sandy clay; bedrock at ~40cm. Rather abundant CWD. Charcoal ~8cm down in soil profile. More aspen & birch than elsewhere in patch. Windthrow occasional in plot. Vaccinium angustifolium & V. myrtilloides abundant in open canopy (windthrow) areas, loaded with fruit. Poplar Lake Bedrock Complex LTA.

Mature upland cedar on moderately steep, upper, east-southeast-facing slope in fairly rugged bedrock terrain north of Swan Lake. Trees 20-45 (50)cm d.b.h., mode 30-40cm. CWD sparse to moderately abundant. Soil ~8cm, litter and humus over fine brown silt-loam, fairly shallow to bedrock. Small outcrops (gabbro) in plot. Community extends to bottom of narrow ravine and up west-facing slope (opposite side of ravine). General area lightly selectively logged (large pines) in ~1920's (General Land Company). Betula papyrifera 56cm dbh. Vegetable Lakes Till Plain LTA.

Typical of ericad-dominated peatland surrounding 1-acre pond in small (~9-acre) basin in moderately rugged bedrock terrain north of Swan Lake. Snags frequent, especially in outer zones of the basin. Appears to have been beaver-flooded in past. No stumps. Saturated deep peat; hummocks 24" tall. Vegetable Lakes Till Plain LTA.

Old growth upland cedar on gentle to rather steep north-facing slope on south side of Swan Lake. Plot on mid to upper slope, slope varies from 5-20 degrees; slope ~110 feet high. Cedars 35-70cm d.b.h., commonly 50-60cm. A few very large, old, and quite decayed pine stumps. Soil brown silt-loam, thick litter & humus. Small diabase/gabbro outcrops on upper-slope. Substrate quite spongy due to deep duff. Betula cordifolia 55cm dbh. Cedar fairly extensive patch here, extends atop ridge and down south-facing slope most of way to Tote Lake. Vegetable Lakes Till Plain LTA.

Typical of zone of low-statured vegetation immediately surrounding small (1/4-acre) bog pond in ~5-acre basin in strongly rolling bedrock terrain northwest of Swan Lake. Plot 8m x 12m, long edge parallel to pond, grades outward to poor/stunted black spruce. Saturated peat, very quaky at edge of pond. Vegetable Lakes Till plain LTA. Photos here. Lichens collected and identified by Joe Walewski.

Typical of fairly broad shoreline zone of Skinny Lake, exposed by water level that is ~12-18 inches down from spring high. Plot 8m x 12m, long side parallel to lakeshore. Shoreline zone captured by plot is ~3-8 inches above current water level. Zone is +/- level (sloping very gradually toward lake). Substrate is angular rhyolite cobbles with moist silty organics in between. This is the wetter of two lakeshore zones. Upper zone is dominated by Myrica gale. Photos here. Vegetable Lakes Till Plain LTA.

Typical of small (~5-acre) bedrock-entrenched basin along small drainage in rolling bedrock terrain south of Prune Lake. Apparently was previously poor conifer swamp which was flooded by beaver, followed by dam breaching in last few years. Deep, saturated, fibric moss peat, water at ~25cm down (drought conditions). Frequent conifer snags (stunted growth form). This plot represents a common successional stage of beaver-influenced basins along drainages in the Border Lakes Subsection of Cook County (& westward). Photos here. Poplar Lake Bedrock Complex LTA.

Typical of wetter zone in beaver-influenced sedge-alder wetland along drainage through rolling bedrock terrain southeast of Swamp Lake. Beaver dam ~150m downstream, also ~200m upstream. 35cm hemic peat over 50+cm sapric peat, becoming mucky 50+cm. Thick, dense thatch. Small wood pieces in the peat column. Corner of plot wetter- captures edge of intermittent stream/flowage channel. Grades to alder towards upland (less wet). Plot is just inside BWCAW line; uplands immediately to east have been recently logged and planted to red pine. Poplar Lake Bedrock Complex LTA.

Typical of broad zone on outer portion of wetland along small drainage in rolling bedrock terrain southwest of Caribou Lake. Beaver dam down-gradient ~150m to southeast. Grades to scrub alder then sedge meadow (C. utriculata) towards dam, to denser cedar (and less alder) towards upland. Peat ~75cm deep. Tall (20") Sphagnum hummocks. No stumps. Was likely cedar swamp in past then trees killed when flooded by beaver when dam was higher. ~5-10 acres of this zone. Large Betula bole on ground in plot. Poplar Lake Bedrock Complex LTA.

Burned in 2008. Stand origin from 1692 fire according to Bud Heinselmen. (oldest pine stand in Boundary Waters Canoe Area before burn). Many recent downed trees in plot, much 50-80+ cm DBH and also large and smaller. Large standing dead pines 50-80+cm DBH in stand surrounding plot.

Typical of one of several patches of even-aged birch which originated in 1936 (Canadian spot fires) near Vista & Gaskin Lakes. Trees mostly 15-25cm dbh. Old fire-scarred boles occas. Frequent snags. Much CWD, both Betula & Abies. Rocky silt. Frequent mossy surface boulders. Plot on gradually sloping ridgetop. Patch extends down north-facing slope to mid-slope here (downslope nearly to lakeshore in similar 1936 fire-origin patch on nearby Vista Lake). No stumps. Poplar Lake Bedrock Complex LTA.

Maturing to mature, uneven-aged patch. Fraxinus nigra 15-40cm d.b.h., Thuja 20-45cm. Few snags. No stumps. Moist, highly-decomposed organic substrate >40cm deep, 18" from hummock top to hollow. No standing water (extended drought). Typical of ~3 acres on small (~8-acre) bench in fairly rugged bedrock terrain between Parsnip, Bean, and South Bean Lakes. Vegetable Lakes Till Plain LTA.

Very shrubby facies of WMs83a clearly manifesting seepage, not a calcareous fen. (From back side of form: "This has a big peat buildup. It is neither a calcareous fen nor a forested seep, but not a typical WMs83 either. Note to self - got to go back maybe Berula here.")

Ungrazed gentle w-facing slope used by owner as native lawn west of large actively grazed pasture of apparent similar (?) type. Multiple Outside Plot (OP) species are included, from an upper slope and a lower gentle slope which grades into a wet meadow. Releve is near base of slope in prairie NE of house. Last pastured 13 yrs prior to survey, gentle WNW slope.

This releve is just S of the little bridge owner has placed along his trail so a bit unnatural setting. Thoroughness of releve was compromised by conditions of survey (haste). Must have naturally been a very nice seepage meadow. Back of form: It appears that there was active seepage in meadow at base of hill between house & road. Owner put in a culvert. The area supports a "spring" reported to "run all year". This could have once been a calc. fen but no obvious indicators in the rapid search. "Damp prairie" just upslope has clay & gravel a few inches down.
Small remnants of never plowed prairie on steep SSE facing slope, not grazed. (From back of form: "this knoll would respond to fire")

Releve on NW-facing slope of ravine. Recently grazed (woods) but recreational land at time of survey. Quite degraded. This stand marks the northern extent of public land survey mapped forests on E side of Des Moines River.
Small areas of native prairie on steep north facing slope extends S as an extremely narrow fringe on steep slope above field.
Very lovely, clean, steep dry prairie, W-facing along ravine tributary to Plum Creek. One of nicest slopes in Holly Township Macrosite. Back of form: "Soil quite dry, gravelly."
Releve done to document condition of prairie.
Releve done to characterize prairie. Grazed until 1-2 years ago. Very few forbs in terms of numbers, but a couple good species on the list. Hill mainly graminoid dominated.

Very close to Releve M-307-09-23-08-01, but together they give a little better picture of this fine slope being invaded by woodies along the N property line as is reflected in this releve nearer the fence.

This releve was done to characterize the present condition of large area that is enrolled in PTE program. It should not be used for purposes of characterizing or classification of native vegetation. Area is mapped in MCBS cover as disturbed. Entire prairie is filling in with woodies.
This prairie is enrolled in PTE and could use a burn. Releve on gentle NW-facing slope.

Releve done to characterize prairie. This would be a fine BC-rank prairie overall were it not for a pervasive invasion of wild parsnip. Also at site but out of plot: Potentilla arguta, Dalea purp, Calylophus serrul, Lithospermum can, Verbena stricta, Lithospermum incis.

Active pasture, grazed within season of survey but cattle not present at time of survey. Generally heavily graminoid dominated suggesting a history of herbicide application that affects forbs. Notes: Releve on best part of slope available at west end. NE-facing slope.
Releve on best part of slope available on east end. Heavily graminoid dominated prairie. Notes: best N-facing end near landowner fence.

This is one of the best quality privately owned sites in the county & should be a prairie bank even though it is small. Notes: Slope is very gentle. (Back of form: "Just east of ephemeral stream full of reed canary", One of the most diverse unprotected patches of prairie in the county")

Early season; heavy browse; heavily wormed; small-medium coarse woody debris present in all decay stages. Plot center 20 m from Superior Hiking Trail. NPC in minimally fragmented landscape with human disturbance history.

Early season. Coarse woody debris in all stages of decomposition. Plot center ~30 m from Taconite State Trail. Transition area from upland cedar/pine to lowland cedar/ash. Soil horizons: Oa (MUCK) over A (glaciofluvial or slope alluvium deposit parent material) over unknown (stopped by extremely stony material). Surface rocks include cobbles, stones, and boulders. Aquic soil conditions.

Plot chosen to document predominant native plant community in patch which includes state designated old growth. This is matrix native plant community of old growth. Patch includes some small woodland and rock outcrop inclusions. Natural fire origin. No stumps in plot. Few scattered elsewhere in patch. No exotic plants or worms observed.

In opening adjacent to small peatland lake. Low wet depressions amongst moderate sphagnum hummocks. Plot very dry, much of sphagnum in hollows dried up. Muck bottom hollows with dried crispy thin covering (very dry summer). peat firm, water table just below surface.

One of a series of depressions. This one ringed by Alnus incana on the south side, rocky ledge on north. Nearly pure graminoids with scattered short alder, 3-4 ft. tall. Dead and down trees laying in plot. Carex utriculata increasing in plot on east side of plot, more dominant at periphery of basin.

Small shallow depression in bedrock controlled topography; one of a series. No water present in drought year. Dead woody debris in plot from fallen tree and beaver cuttings. Basin rimmed by Carex vesicaria and other species in slightly higher and drier band (see Mike Lee's notes). Mucky soil from 8 to 14 inches.

Old growth pine stand. many trees blown down (~1999). Plot in cluster of remaining large trees. Dead and down of all sizes in plot. On slope just east of portage trail south from poplar lake. Large boulders in plot. Plot orientation 205 degrees X 35 degrees.

Alder dominated peatland with scattered and clumps of tall tamarack and black spruce trees. Plot in more open area. Adjacent to poor tamarack swamp. Hummocks (+/- 60cm) interspersed with 20% hollows. Water table just below surface in drought year.

Old growth pine and cedar along portage between Gaskin and Horseshoe lakes. Plot ~5m from trail. Several recently (<5 years) downed trees in plot, one large pine, 1 large spruce, 1 large white cedar and several smaller down and decaying logs. Ground hummocky, perhaps mainly from boles.
Prairie has been fragmented by rural water line accounting for Lotus corn. Light lavender cf Aster ericoides appears to be a cross with Aster oblongifolus.
Best quality W-facing slope of former railroad embankment and narrow adjoining prairie just south of former trestle location west side of former (railroad) track.

Apparently a wet meadow that is getting choked with cattails. Not sure how these should be classified. Cattails are so thick in this area that it is difficult to tell how representative this might be of the wetland in general. Nearly impossible to lay out a plot in this site or to get a sense of area covered. OP species included in releve to give a better sense of wetland at large between "island" and road. DO NOT USE THIS RELEVE in any form of analysis.
Highly disturbed CD rank forest, releve representative of more mesic interior of peninsula. Oaks seem to be concentrated along shore. County Park.
Quite nice prairie, but very tiny.

West-facing slope above creek. Not your typical UPs23a but nothing would key this to UPs13d. In a part of the county once with numerous lakes. Notes: Releve done to document prairie. Stand not typical of NPC type, too close to road. (Observer later over-rode classification to be UPs13d.)

Releve is in an active pasture and is quite diverse for situation. Best area is the S-facing slope facing E-W ravine. This area is unusual in this pasture, but would recover well if released from grazing. Releve done to document site.

Fairly steep and narrow W-facing slope between field and Perch Ck. wetland. North of here slopes are dominated by brome, from here south to WMA boundary they are prairie of varying quality. The amount of Echinacea on this particular hill is incredible!
Convex slope of south knoll.

Despite low forb diversity, this is a nice prairie knoll largely dominated by native grasses. Lack of conservative species drops it from BC-rank to C-rank. Releve done to document slope. Upper to middle slope position.

Rel size: This is part of an actively seeping zone some of which get a bit perilous to walk through so releve may under-represent the area. Composition varies widely from spot to spot. Active seepage zone flanks W-facing hills and appears to extend to creek. Most peaty areas overcome with reed canary. Notes: Releve done to document wetland communities.

Tiny prairie just SE of planted trees that appears not to have been planted. North of large block of restored prairie on "island" of upland in wetland matrix. Very poor. Could be old field. Releve should not be used for classification or any type of analysis. Notes: Releve done to survey site.

The area surveyed is the southern outlier of a riparian forest whose larger block is in another ownership north of creek. Stand is quite disturbed. Feeling and aspect seems more appropriate for a terrace forest but scattered large silver maples are present. Narrow floodplain with little oxbow development here. One Fraxinus with dbh >70 cm. Groundlayer appears to be wormed, dead Elm common. Notes: Releve done to characterize riparian forests.

Enter forest from field road on W side of CRP. Forest block east of creek, east of road. Much internal microtopography in this block. Bounded on east by steep, degraded MHs38 breaking into this forest that seems transitional between terrace and floodplain forest. Notes: Releve done to characterize riparian forests along Elm Creek.

Highly degraded forest was probably MHs49 in past. Formerly an island in a now drained lake. Purpose of this releve is comparison with Cottonwood Co "Mountain Lake Park", however that was a hilly island and this area is very level and too degraded. Black willow and green ash around edge of stand. Notes: Stand typical of community type: Uncertain - too low and level, too degraded to tell.
Wet prairie in a complex of wetlands. Wooded and potential old field. One of most diverse and interesting unprotected sites in County. The Cornus is amomum- has blue fruits.

Releve is in circular bowl in NWNE of the section. Community quality in the woods is poor but it is full of birds (eg. Pewee). The beautiful signature of these forests on photo is large cottonwoods. There is a circle of mulberry out of plot. DBH of some cottonwoods >1.5 meter. Notes: Releve done to characterize site. Enter site from south across a planted CRP field.

Purpose of this releve was to see if there were additional stands in county outside Timberlane County Park & Iowa Lake area that would type to MHs39. This is definitely MHs38 in a place where forests were mapped by public land survey. Notes: Some topographic variation in stand in order to fit a releve results in less than perfect classification of stand. Slope is very steep. Not a notable stand, just publicly owned, accessible, & in an historically forested area.

Degraded woods on east side of lake. Purpose of releve was to confirm community type is NOT MHs39. Mediocre forest but on east side of lake and accessible. Gentle W-facing slope to nearly flat. No sugar maple. Large silver maple OP by lake. Site is below, but this releve documents community distribution. No PLS forest mapped here.

Quite graminoid dominated open remnant of UPs13d on WNW-facing slope overlooking disturbed wetland leading into a restored formerly drained lake. Only block of prairie that has escaped significant tree planting. Notes: Releve done to characterize community.

Very poor highly disturbed band of abandoned rail ROW through crop fields. Majority has become overpowered by woody species. Releve represents about the only remaining open area big enough to use. Note long, thin releve configuration. Area may be artificially wetter than natural because RR grade was a cut rather than an elevation in this area.

Releve on lower 1/3 of slope may straddle communities. This is the slope component of a catena of forest types on steep NE-facing slope above the stream. It is adjoined just across the Co line by a nearly pure stand of mature natural Populus tremuloides (aspen), unusual in this area. Downslope it grades to disturbed MHs49. All seem to have been previously grazed. Notes: Presence of northern red oak in this relevé; very unusual in this county; first I have seen. Purpose of relevé is to “characterize unusual stand with red oak and aspen”. Stand typical of NPC? No. “Flora is very ecotonal, does not fit well even to system level of classification.” Releve is just below a fenceline on hill. (Releve possibly falls into Faribault Co. instead of Martin Co.  The GPS resolution may not be good enough to tell.)
Northernmost knob of w-facing slope. Level top is dominated by brome. Notes: Stand and releve are depauperate.
Very depauperate, but the best slope on east side of wetland south of Rd 132.
West facing slope between cornfield and wetland. Upslope of a copse of boxelder. Very narrow band of steep dry prairie on slope. Notes: Releve done to document site vegetation.
Best quality prairie on this W-facing slope is in the very thick band of Amorpha that occupies the lower third of the hill. Notes: Middle to lower slope position.

Very open canopy, and groundlayers in these floodplain forests feel very degraded to surveyor, but perhaps this is characteristic because of their frequent disturbance by flood waters? Wood thrush. Notes: Purpose of Releve: 'characterize forest'.

Very narrow N & NW-facing bank between old field and cropland, not pastured. Notes: Purpose of releve: 'characterize site'. Very tall mystery phlox-like plant; appears it will perhaps have maroon fls - too few to collect.
West-facing slope in pasture. This area known to owners as "Crocus Hill". Best diversity at site in very small steep area, not much larger than one to three releves. Very diverse forbs.

Very small bank of prairie between field and creek, but one of most significant tiny patches remaining. Arnoglossum pl and Eryngium yuc both just outside plot in more level, wet prairie transition zone between UPs13d and creek. Topography so developed and site so small that communities transition from one to another in a very short space. This releve more generally tends to dry UPs23a than UPs13d to which it classifies because of the Muhlenbergia cusp. Notes: Stand typical of NPC type and releve typical of stand = ecotonal.
West-facing slope on east side of tract south of creek. Note presence of Cassia fasciculata on OP list, very seldom seen. Gravelly soil texture.
North of creek, S-facing BC slope.
Area intergrades from wet meadow to wet prairie. Should be searched around edge in May for Cypripedium candidum. Low depression that feels like a former pond.

Equivocal vegetation, as near to prairie as could be found in this unit. Not sure if natural but density and patchiness of sage suggest could be the case, as do several historical air photos. Very poor. Notes: No soil data collected.
Battered forest on peninsula in County Park. Little understory flora, much bare soil. Least disturbed area I could find. Should have spring survey.
This releve is an actively grazed pasture and is quite high quality for that status. Notes: Releve done to characterize slope.
Flat area at top of small hill above Sunshine Lane. Exposed bedrock and boulders common. Plot just off of exposed bedrock and WFn inclusion and rock ledge. Down hill more mesic.
Releve typical of wet meadow areas dominated by forbs more so than gr- minoids.  Releve plot sampled at three times: 2 Jun, 13 Jul, 2 Sep 1987.
Releve typical of calcareous fen community in the area.  Releve conducted on 7/l5, 8/15/87. /Date and Month unknown
Releve typical of shrub-carr community in the area. Releves conducted on 6/01, 7/14, 9/01/87. /Date and Month unknown

Sub-mature northern hardwood-conifer forest dominated by Acer saccharum and Tilia. No sign of cutting. Date and Month unknown. Soil: 14 cm deep A horizon; black moist humus over 6cm B horizon; black-gray moist loam with rocks over light brown C horizon of moist loam with rocks.
