Active pasture best quality on steepest slopes. Date and month unknown.

History unknown: no stumps or weeds. Abundant lichens suggest past disturbance. No evidence of prescrib. burning N of fire break. Rolling sandy outwash. Dense forests of paper birch & JP w/scat.open /Date and Month unknown
Pitted outwash, Mgt: perscribed burning result in "brush prairie". /Date and Month unknown
Releve on Ellingson tract. Burned on 3 Jun 1974. Releve size 2000 square meters.
Releve on Nielson-Olson tract. 0 to 3% slope, well-drained with large boulders (1.1), jackrabbit (r.1). Releve size 2000 square meters.

Level, somewhat poorly drained black soil over gray clay with calcareous influence. No exotic species present in releve. Mostly level area with black somewhat poorly drained soil, 14 inches of fine silty-loam over gray gritty clay.
Mesic site on mostly level ground with slight undulation. 40 cm silty loam over sand. Site burned early spring 1986.

20-25 degree upper slope near the crest of a hill with surface boulders (5% cover). 10-15cm sandy loam over lighter colored sand-gravel mix. Releve is within area burned spring 1986. Dry mesic vegetation typical of side slopes. Hilltops have more dry prairie species (Bouteloua gracilis, Liatris cylindrica, Linum spp, Castilleja sessilifolia). This releve is an example of a glacial till hill prairie.
Old-growth northern hardwoods with patches of second growth. Hemlock in deep ravine. Yellow birch aged at approximately 164 years - 70cm DBH. Soils: well-drained coarse loamy to very fine sandy loam.
Xeric side slope of gravel kame. Dry prairie vegetation on loamy sand with gravel. Representative of the driest side slopes on the site.
Releve located at flat top of hill slope south of a small stream in woods dominated by Juglans cinerea.
Relatively intact dry prairie vegetation on gravel kame. Loamy sand over sand and gravel with occasional boulders at surface. Antelope Hills Scientific and Natural Areas.

Crest of small ridge, intact dry prairie vegetation loamy sand over gravel. Lichens common on the soil surface. Within the Alexandria Moraine Complex on Sioux gravelly sandy loam soils. Site habitat: Dry gravel prairie is restricted to crests of ridges, where gravel is at the surface or in rooting zone of plants. Areas tend to be very small. Most ridges are dominated by monotypic stands of Poa compressa with low density of forbs. Intact gravel prairie is rare.

Steep upper slope. Sioux gravelly loam soils of Alexandria Moraine. Dry to dry-mesic prairie vegetation represents the least disturbed vegetation on the site. Site dominated by dry-mesic/dry vegetation. One half inch organic layer (A horizon) over loamy sand over gravel and sand. Rooting zone of plants in gravel. Exposed gravel at surface in areas.

Dry prairie vegetation on upper slope of a glacial kame. Sand and gravel soil with large boulders at the surface.  Releve represents most intact vegetation on the site. Soil: 2-3cm organic layer over sand/gravel loam with abundant gravel within rooting zone of plants.
Nearly level site on black silt loam over gray clay loam soils. Intact mesic prairie burned spring 1986; contains calciphilic species. Site almost level terrace.

Plot represents the most intact vegetation on the site.  Dry-mesic prairie over loam soil with boulders at the surface (5% cover). Area burned spring 1986. (Releve #3). Narrow isthmus between 2 wetlands on nearly level site with <5 degree slope NW. Soil: 6-8 inches loam over gravel, frequent boulders in subsoil.
Plot represents the most intact vegetation on the site.  Dry-mesic prairie over loam soil with boulders at the surface. Releve #1.
Plot represents a transitional area between disturbed and undisturbed prairie. Loam soil with boulders at the surface. Releve #2.

Old-growth northern hardwoods, dominated by sugar maple and yellow birch. Soils gravelly sandy loam, well-drained, sampled.  Yellow birch and white cedar downslope on wetter soils. Ground layer: deadfall-15%, litter-25%, herbaceous - 60%.

Old-growth northern hardwoods dominated by sugar maple and yellow birch.  Soils gravelly sandy loam, well-drained.  Ground layer: deadfall 5%, litter 15%, herbaceous 60%.  Yellow birch and white cedar downslope.
Old-growth northern hardwoods dominated by sugar maple and yellow birch. Soils gravelly sandy loam, loamy skeletal, well-drained, sampled. Ground layer: herbaceous 85%, deadfall 10%, litter 5%.
Old-growth northern hardwoods dominated by sugar maple and yellow birch. Soils gravelly sandy loam, loamy skeletal, well-drained, sampled. Ground layer: herbaceous 85%, deadfall 10%, litter 5%.
Area formerly a black spruce/tamarack forest, apparently flooded out. Cut stumps.
Near railroad tracks, water depth 10-20 cm, open water 15%.
Very hummocky, water depth ~6 inches. Clumps of alder to the west.
Conductivity=60, water table 20 CM, floating mat-like, rained  >1" two days before, surrounding area with clumps of Typha and Salix.
Dry-mesic prairie with excessively drained soils underlain by granite bedrock. Granite outcrops interspersed. 12" of sandy loam soil underlain by sandy loam soil underlain by sandy soil with gravel.
Wet mesic prairie, on poorly to moderately drained silty clay loam, soil of the MN River outwash. Located slightly above floodplain within a glacial river channel. Previously hayed.

Slightly undulating wet to wet-mesic prairie with saline swales and a northwest to southeast oriented drainage way. Within one of the last glacial river channels, MN Valley outwash. With boulders. 18" silty loam over 1" clay.

Linear wet-mesic prairie oriented northwest to southeast; within one of the last Glacial River Warren channels. A slight southwest facing slope (<1% slope) on 3" of silt loam underlain by clay loam and clay. Plover Prairie.

Wet mesic prairie with saline depressions located on the MN River outwash and slightly above the floodplain in one of the last of the glacial river channels. Soils: 4" loam over 6" clay loam over gray clay.
Mesic blacksoil prairie, 13cm loam with some sand and clay, underlain by clay. Uncompressed litter 4-5cm. Dave Sochern (wildlife management, DNR) knowledgeable about site.
Mesic Blacksoil Prairie, nearly level, rocky.  8 cm loam, over clay. Grazed by about 20 cows and calves.
Releve on level crest of broad loess-covered upland. Soils are Seaton silt loam with a thick duff layer. Stand is a mature/old-growth forest, 120 + years.
Old growth N. hardwoods, dom. by Acer sac., Bet. lut. and Tilia amer. Largest old-growth NH stand in N. MN. Redoaks 163 yrs-58cm dbh and 157 yrs-43cm dbh.  Soils: deep silty or loamy (MN Soil Atlas).
Largest old-growth northern hardwood stand in northern MN.  Red oaks 163 years-58cm DBH, 157 years-43cm DBH. Soils: deep silty or loamy, well-drained, light (MN Soil Atlas).

Old-growth northern hardwoods dominated by Acer saccharum, Betula lutea and Tilia americana. Yellow birch aged at 177 years. Soils are silty/loamy over rock, well drained (MN Soil A) Ground layer: herbaceous 35%, deadfall 10%, and litter 65%.
Flat, broad northeast to southwest ridge. Soil: sandy loam.  Mulch layer 2-4 cm. Rocks: 3% cover.
Level MN River Terrace.  Very sandy loam to 13", then bedrock/or rock. Burned spring 1985.

Old growth northern hardwoods dominated by Acer saccharum and Betula lutea. Sugar maple aged at 176 years. Soils: deep silty or loamy, well-drained, light (MN Soil Atlas). Ground layer: herbaceous-35%, deadfall-5%, litter-65%.

Old-growth northern hardwoods in hilly topography. Largest old-growth stand extant in northern Minnesota. Red oaks aged at 163 years - 58cm DBH, 157 years - 43cm DBH. Ground layer: deadfall - 3%, litter - 3%, herbaceous - 94%. Soils are deep silty or loamy, well-drained, light colored.

Old-growth northern hardwoods dominated by Acer saccharum and Betula lutea. Ground layer: herbaceous-25%, woody-65%, deadfall-5%, litter-5%.  Soils: Deep silty or loamy, well-drained, light colored soils (MN Soil Atlas).

Old-growth northern hardwoods. Dominated by Acer saccharum, Betula lutea, and Tilia americana. Ground layer: herbaceous-30%, woody-40%, deadfall-10%, litter-20%. Soils: deep silty or loamy, well-drained, light color soil. MN Soil Atlas.

Old-growth northern hardwoods grading into black ash swamp. Soils: fine loamy, well-drained, silty clay/silty clay loam/clay.(Releve soil sample) Ground layer: deadfall-5%, litter-15%, herbaceous-80%.

Old-growth northern hardwoods grading into black ash swamp.  Soils: fine loamy, well-drained, silty clay/silty clay loam/clay. (Releve soil sample) Ground layer: deadfall-5%, litter-15%, herbaceous-80%.

Old-growth northern hardwoods grading into black ash swamp.  Soils: fine loamy, well-drained, silty clay/silty clay loam/clay. (Releve soil sample) Ground layer: deadfall-5%, litter-15%, herbaceous-80%.

Old-growth northern hardwoods, dominated by Acer saccharum, Betula lutea, and Tilia americana. Red oak aged at 192 years. Soils: silty or loamy over rock, well-drained light colored soils (MN Soil Atlas).

Old-growth northern hardwoods, dominated by Acer saccharum, Betula lutea, Tilia americana. Red oak aged at 192 years. Soils: silty or loamy over rock, well-drained light colored soils (MN Soil Atlas).

Largest old-growth northern hardwood stand in northern Minnesota.  Soils: coarse loamy, well-drained, gravelly sandy loam.  Red oak aged at 163 years-58cm DBH. Ground layer: herbaceous-50%, woody-20%, deadfall-20%, litter-10%.
This area shows interrupted canopy on aerial photo.  No C. arietinum here.  About 40 - 60m north of plantation edge.
Nearly level mesic area with slightly sandy clay loam soils over gray clay at 35 cm.
Mesic black soil prairie. Mostly level site near Ten Mile Creek. Brown sandy loam soils with some gravel and surface boulders.
Releve includes a blowdown gap, which is typical of the alternating patches of tamarack and gaps of the stand. The soil is saturated peat, but firm enough to walk on. Rare species:Polygonum arifolium

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Releve typical of mesic deciduous forest on mineral islands in Corries Swamp. Soil: Bluffton Loam.  Approximately 5 mature ginseng plants seen with seedlings nearby.
Pools in this area full of chelated iron. Area bounded immediately to North by flooded area where trees are dying.
Fair amount of deadfall producing rugged hummocks and hollows.
Not much deadfall in this area.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Releve typical of more open areas within pine groves on upper slopes and ridge crests (except S-facing). Soils are of sandy texture andare poorly developed (A1-3<7cm). Pine reproduction by gap-phase.

Releve typical of open pine groves on steep south facing slopes. Soils are sandy entisols. Pine reproduction is by gap-phase with seedlings on eroded surfaces. One individual aged at 89+ years, 75 feet.
Plot typical of flats at toe of slope of steep side-hill seep. Reticulum of 30cm deep drains with alluvial bottoms. Peat shallow and not entirely saturated.
Plot typical of vegetation with small patches of tamarack in large groundwater seep area. Soil of sedge and Sphagnum peat and saturated. Tamarack 5-25cm DBH and reproducing. Peat >1m deep over sand.

Plot typical of vegetation in old meander scars of lowest terrace of St. Croix at Williamsport. Scars filled with >1 m of sedge peat. Peat saturated by groundwater discharge. Plot 8x10m to fit channel.
Releve typical of ridges between meander scars. Large (>25") trees in plot common on north half of island, smaller trees to south. Site probably floods annually.
Releve typical of second-growth mixed-oak forest (15-25" trees). Plot has stumps and barbed wire probably logged and grazed in past. Soils are sandy loam (Doverton) with rock outcrops.
Fairly steep scarcely grazed hill in pasture. Lespedeza leptostachya somewhat damaged by herbicide drift. Enrolled in registry early 1989. 449 Lespedeza leptostachya, more potential habitat to east.
Very steep north-facing gravel hill. Pastured in winter but not summer 1114 prairie bush clover near west end of north-facing slope. Owner aware of EO, enrolled in registry early 1989.
In gently sloping area just uphill and west of family dump on south side of hill. More xeric and more disturbed than Lespedeza area.
The most highly degraded pasture visited in 1989. Some areas have Euphorbia esula. Releve from only remaining slope dominated by native prairie. Area optioned to become county park and reservoir.
South-facing hillside dominated almost exclusively by prairie grasses. Area has been optioned for County park and reservoir (Mound Creek Project). Buchloe on rocks.
Sedge meadow being invaded by shrubs.  Releve plot in open area.
Homogeneous shrub swamp. Releve located along deer trail. Shrub swamp on peaty ground - fibric peat.
Homogeneous black spruce bog, releve located at random. Forested bog. Semi-saturated fibric peat, Sphagnum and Polytricum.
Located at south eastern tip of esker ridge originating out of Rush Lake. Plot situated on top of hill in a clearing of Rhus glabra dominated old field re-generating into a sand prairie.

Numerous maple-basswood islands in a conifer swamp wetland system with an open bog. Acer saccharum DBH average 20cm, 45cm, Tilia americana DBH average 25cm, 50cm. Releve on long, thin island in west part of site. Logging but a lot of coarse woody debris.
Tamarack Bog in center of open bog on floating sphagnum mat, incomplete moat. Saturated fibric peat.
Large uniform tamarack swamp. Plot arbitrarily chosen.  Tamarack DBH about 20cm.
Plot located in open area west of property fence, along deer trail. Very dry bog with fibric peat and invading tamarack and jack pine.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mesic woodland 9 miles northeast of Twin Valley and 0.4 mile west of route 40. Releve on level ground.
Aspen woodland 6.5 miles east-northeast of Twin Valley.  Releve is on level ground.
Calcareous Fen 7 miles east-southeast of Twin Valley and 0.6 mile west of Route 40.
Mesic woodland 4 miles north-northeast of Rollag and 0.4 mile east of Route 37; about 0.2 mile north of Lake Two. Relelve on more or less flat ground.
Gravelly summit of morainic hill 16 miles southwest of Detroit Lakes.
Prairie pond margin 17 miles east of Browns Valley.
Woodland 11.5 miles southwest of Wheaton and 0.2 mile east of Route 27 .  Releve on undulating terrain.

place_name: Lac Qui Parle St. Rec. Area
remarks: Moist, sandy shore of Lac Qui Parle Lake 15 miles east of Madison.
Shrub swamp - diverse Salix.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Mixed hardwood-conifer swamp with Taxus below. On east side of north-south trending trail through swamp.

Releve located on the northeast side of a knoll in the southwest portion of the large shrub/hardwood swamp at the site. Part of the knoll was cut in the past; the releve site is undisturbed. Maple-basswood mesic forest knoll with Panax. Old dead falls (Betula papyrifera 20-30cm DBH) and oak lims (10-15cm DBH) present.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Site is at east-central border of Sherburne County, southwest of Blue Lake. Releve in transitional area between Larix and hardwood swamp. Numerous dead Larix in and near releve site. Three cut stumps in releve area.
This native community on slightly sloping terrain below beach ridge complex; a ground water discharge zone, but no active flow. Data collection abbreviated by thunderstorm, dusk.
This native community on very slightly sloping terrain some distance out from beach ridge complex, with fen zone higher up. Data collection abbreviated by thunderstorm.

Plot on nearly level part of a very low beach ridge or strand line of glacial Lake Agassiz. Very wet zone immediately behind (above) this. Lots of mulch. Slopes to west into wet-mesic and wet. Mesic black soil prairie.
Releve within 100m of small stream course in area where slightly elevated leeves support mesic prairie; wet-mesic otherwise. Area had been burned early summer. Mesic black soil prairie.
Area in which releve taken was burned early summer.  Plot just east of crest of former beach ridge, sloping very gently down to east.  Much pocket gopher activity.

Plot located in fairly homogenous saline "flat" in a matrix of rather different; Spartina pectinata - Carex species - Calamagrostis inexpansa wet prairie. ASCS airphotos suggest area where releve taken may have been plowed pre-39

Plot on crest of narrow beach ridge, abruptly sloping down to west just west of plot; more gently sloping down to east of it. Bare soil stones comprise about 15% of plot area. Burned early season 1986. Gravel prairie. Plot located in portion of the natural community that is in "A" condition. Area had been burned late spring or early summer 1986. Gravel prairie. Tympanuchus wildlife management area.
Area where releve taken had been burned early summer. Mesic black soil prairie.
Plot nearly level, just a bit southeast of local high spot. Mesic black soil prairie.
About 2/3 distance downslope from apparent high point to low (drainage way). Not mowed recently and quite thatched. Probably some influence of groundwater here. Mesic black soil prairie.
Plot close to transition to non-saline zone further west. Pretty homogeneous area sampled. Mesic black soil prairie.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Mixed oak forest dominated by Quercus alba, Quercus ellipsoidalis (both to  50cm DBH), Quercus macrocarpa, Fraxinus nigra, Tilia, and Ostrya. Good understory. Two small sink holes in limestone. Note late date: Nov.

Upland white cedar stand located on top of ridge near northeast corner of Hovland Woods. Note presence of large white pine. Dominant plants in herb layer: Aralia nudicaulis, Aster macrophyllus, and Clintonia borealis.
Old growth maple-basswood with Acer saccharum, Tilia, and Ulmus. Most oldgrowth characters. Some past selective logging. Soils: Webster and LeSueur silty loam.
Old growth Maple-Basswood forest dominated by Acer saccharum, Tilia, and Ulmus. Most old growth characteristics. Some past selective logging. Soils: Webster and LeSeur silty loam.

Closed canopy of old growth maple-basswood forest (120 years +) dominated by Acer saccharum, Tilia, and Ulmus rubra. Text book example. No cut stumps apparent. On deep Hayden loam soils. DBH of canopy trees range from 25-37 inches. Large snags and logs common throughout the forest. Complete size class distribution, no evidence of cut stumps.

Old growth maple-basswood forest dominated by Quercus rubra, Acer saccharum, Tilia and Ulmus. Many old growth features; only disturbance - removal of a few elms. On an irregular knoll with a moderately steep north-facing slope bordering an intermittent stream.
Old growth maple-basswood forest dominated by Acer saccharum. Complete canopy, some snags and down logs, all age classes of maples, patchy understory, good spring flora. Well-decayed oak stumps.
Mature maple-basswood forest (>100 years.) dominated by Acer saccharum (10-15 inch DBH) and Quercus rubra. Some old growth features, but poor spring ephemerals. Past selective logging, light grazing.

Old growth maple-basswood forest domianted by Acer saccharum and Quercus rubra. Most old growth characteristics. Disturbance limited to occassional cut stump. Serious erosion on adjacent field. 85% duff, <5% deadfall.
Old growth maple-basswood forest. The least disturbed 25 acres with most old growth features. Long history of selective logging and grazing. Hayden loam soils.
Young to old-growth maple-basswood forest dominated by Quercus rubra, Acer saccharum, and Tilia. Varied history of logging and grazing.
Old-growth maple-basswood forest domianted by Acer saccharum, Tilia, Quercus rubra and Ulmus rubra. All old growth characteristics. This portion of Diamond Lake is ranked A.
Diamond Lake Woods; exact location unknown. Moderate on St. Croix moraine. No stumps or grazing seen.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mature maple-basswood forest dominated Acer saccharum and Tilia. Tree size class distribution is incomplete; selective logging, many stumps, highly disturbed edges. Very diverse herb layer.
Releve in mesic jack pine forest on forest soils, 1 mile W of Lake Win nibigoshish. Stand age: 1928, 1931.
Releve 1 mi. N of Peysenski Lake on the Decrans farmstead. Soils are prairie origin.

Mature maple-basswood forest now dominated by Acer saccharum and Tilia (50-60% canopy coverage). Wet-mesic site. Many elms dead and dying. Lat-long from EOR; not exact location of releve. Topography nearly level.
Mature Maple-Basswood forest domianted by Ulmus and Tilia.  Heavily disturbed. By 1980 most elms at north end had died and blown down. Soil: black-gray sandy loam. 0-30 degrees slope.
Plot typical of good shrub carr; slighlty lower than wet prairie areas. Peat > 1 meter deep.
Plot typical of a rather uniform bog-birch fen.  Some standing water in pools.  pH 6.8.  Occasional, loose hummocks of Sphagnum.
Plot typical of Andropogon/Calamagrostis swales between dunes. Dry this year and burned in Spring of 1989 and 1990.
Plot typical of marsh on small island in Hoffman Lake.  Dystrophic bog lake with Dy sidiment.  Site probably exposed last year. Water pH 7.4.
Plot typical of mesic forest in steep-sided, narrow ravine. Substrate is bouldery talus.  Cool-damp, rocks cover about 5%, all moss covered.
Plot typical of drawdown area between Scirpus pungens-Typha angust. beds.  Fine sand grading to mucky sand at water's edge.
Plot typical of uniform, black spruce bog. Lots of windthrow and regeneration. Owner says salvage logged for pulp after 1940's storm. Surface water pH 3.9.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Hardwood swamp with 10-20cm DBH trees. Canopy gaps from past cutting, windthrow and dead Larix and dead elm. Sinuous mucky hollows with Poa paludigena.
Plot typical of white pine mixed with mesic hardwoods on small knolls of the Goose Creek terrace. Pines 20-45 cm.  Part of gap in plot - fairly typical. Wooden tepee to south.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Plot typical of windthrow damaged Basswood forest.  Large basswoods (40-80 cm); large ironwoods (10-20 cm) suggest past canopy damage. Lots of downed wood, some very well decomposed.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Plot typical of slight rises above surrounding wetlands. Grades to maple basswood upland forest in places. Many cut stumps and multi-stemmed basswoods. Cleared of dead wood. Stand water in tip-up craters.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Plot typical of white pine, red maple lowlands. Soil peaty, but dry this year. Large pines 30 to 70cm DBH. Several blowdowns near plot. Some stumps on plot.
Plot typical of cedar swamp just north of Norris Cabin. Some blowdowns and light gaps. Sphagnum around pools.
Plot typical of sparse tamarack swamp. Some trees very large (50-70cm), most about 30cm. Gap covers about fourth of plot. Most of site succeeding to shrub swamp. No standing water.

Releve typical of open seep within patchy canopy of black ash and yellow birch. Just east of spring rivulet, 50m west of Goose Creek floodplain. Such seeps common in narrow band at toe of slope and floodplain.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Mature northern hardwood-conifer forest dominated by Acer saccharum. Fairly undisturbed but all pines removed. Few old-growth trees. Surrounding area mostly mature aspen with northern hardwood understory. 25-50% litter layer, moderate deadfall. Three cut stumps in releve plot, appear to be white pine.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Releve was on a bluff, average 16 degrees north; but plot estimated 12 degrees north at roughly midway upslope from river. Plot has few to no stones at soil surface (silty loam) the cobbles/boulders elsewhere.
Mature Thuja stands such as this with dense shade and few canopy gaps are small, near upland knolls in Cedar Bog Lake area, and rare at CCNHA.
Plot situated on west side of Trollin Lake on moist, solid peat   just up to zone where mat floats (at the "hinge line".)  Much more Eriocaulon and Utricularia beyond plot. Should re-do pH.
A few remnants of mesic forest (with sugar maple and basswood) occur in northeast Isanti County, an area where upland forests are now mostly oak.

On south side of hardwood swamp on upland soil. Encountered this community type at sites 128, 130, 131 to the west (sec 30,32,27,26, T37N R24W) along north boundary sand plain. Associated with occasional pine.
Plot is east and upslope of a hardwood swamp. Numerous cut stumps of pine; canopy gaps. Tip-up mound with tree gone. Stumps + live pines 40-50 cm dbh.
Continuous Sphagnum mat is firm, saturated, covered with sundews. Opening roughly 50x50m, rimmed by Larix and more minerotrophic natives plus Rhamnus frangula. Cultivated fields beyond.
Level, uniform area on floodplain about 50m north of Rum River. Beyond plot to north is narrow emergent marsh in old channel and floodplain forest beyond that. Many trees single-stemmed.

Releve includes canopy gap by large diameter, senescent Quercus ellipsoidalis. Typical of old, unburned, single-stemmed dry oak forest. Owner says no cutting in over 50 years, never grazed. Natural but not pretty. Much dead debris.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Arvid Anderson says this tract was never grazed and never cut over, but windstorm of 1942 (?) brought down many big old trees and the wood was taken out. See tip-up mounds, pits, very old decay, snags, weeds rare.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Releve is on south side of small creek, south of Thuja stand and in an area of mixed swamp just west of a uniform black ash-cinnamon fern area.
Probably the best stand of white pine in Anoka and Isanti Counties. Site of Ed Cushing's class outings for releve training; Ice Lake Stand.
Unremarkable fen, but typical. Old-fields surround depression. Wet moat with Phalaris, Carex lacustris, Carex rostrata. Shrub-zone: alder, bog birch, Rhamnus frangula -- rel. minerotrophic species.
Mesic sugar maple dominated forest with white pine - very rare in Isanti County. Elsewhere at site and at other sites, white pine occurs with red oak and northern pin oak.
Low-lying, wet mesic blacksoil prairie opening surrounded by young aspen. Numerous openings throughout site. Solidago riddellii locally common elsewhere at site.
Open sedge meadow is summer-dry with tussocks 10cm, max 20cm tall. Lowland trends northwest to southeast across site but view blocked by aspen on slight rises and upland ridges.
Located in broad, peaty basin through which Cedar Creek flows. Spring to the west and creek to the east of plot. 1938 air photos suggest past mowing. Woody vegetation closing in.
A beautiful seepage area 50m west of the St. Croix river. Plot runs 20m a long small bouldery brook and 5m on either side. Symplocarpus foetid prominent in may, Carex bromoides prominent in summer.
Conifer swamp has good diversity of northern species but their abundance is low. Dense shade cast by Rhamnus frangula may be limiting reproduction of natives including Larix.
Plot typical of very uniform alder swamp. Infrequent black ash and tamarack across swamp.
Plot typical of blowout depression, more open than most seen. Site burned in 1980 or so.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Plot typical of mixed cedar swamp at toe of slope, slightly above wetlands to north. Some stumps, cedars to 40cm, plot about 50m. West of gravel road crossing wetland.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Low density stand of small sugar maples at top of ridge near northeast corner of Hovland Woods. Understory dominated by Aster mac, Clintonia, and seedlings of Acer saccharum and Acer spicatum.

South facing slope near top of southwest/northeast ridge through encampment. Forest Association property. Shallow soils. Dominated by white pines, average 1' DBH, 100 years old. Probably logged in late 1800s. Woody understory lacking.

East-facing slope near top of southwest/northeast ridge through EFA property. Shallow soils. Dominant white pine average 1' diameter, 100 years old. Woody understory lacking. Probably logged in late 1800s.

At base of southwest/northeast ridge through EFA property.  Soil: Hibbing silt loam. Five old growth (250 years) white pines. Park-like. Ground layer herbs approximately 100% cover. Selective cutting in late 1800s.
At base of southwest/northeast ridge through EFA property.  Soil: Hibbing silt loam. Six 250-years+ white pine.  Park-like. Select cutting late 1800s. Well-developed herb layer.
High quality old-growth, undisturbed. Dominated by white pines with occasional red pines. On level bench half-way up east-facing slope on north side of Encampment River gorge.

Mixed white cedar/pine stand near top of southwest/northeast ridge through EFA property. Shallow rocky soil. 500 trees/acre. Pines taller, less numerous than cedars. Cedars browsed to 8'. Very few saplings. Aster mac. dominates ground layer.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest

remarks: Along a ravine, near top of slope, that dissects edge of Minnestoa River Terrace. Sandy loam soil for 7 cm underlain by sandy clay loam with some gravel. Are not moved; too steep. Glacial till hill prairie.
Rocky ravine-dissected slopes of the Minnesota river terrace. About 1 cm of duff. 13 cm loam, then clay. Glacial till hill prairie.
Mostly level site just west of Populus deltoides and Salix interior thicket probably more dry mesic than much of this site. Loamy soils with gravel pieces. Mesic blacksoil prairie.
Surface boulders, gravel and exposed ground covers 10% of releve plot. Gravel prairie.
Near crest of hill in sandy-gravelly exposed soil on west-facing slope. History of grazing and sand/gravel excavation. Gravel prairie. 10-20% of releve plot is bare gravel.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: Young maple-basswood forest dominated by Quercus borealis, Tilia (to 30 cm), Betula papyrifera, Ostrya, and Acer saccharum. Canopy more than 75%. No evidience of disturbance. Sampled on flat of hill just south of small stream. 20-70 degree north facing slope.
Dry mesic prairie remnant on well drained sandy loam ridges bordering Sauk River outwash. Small population of Cirsium hillii on site.
Strip of remnant mesic blacksoil prairie between railroad right-of-way and township road. Goes with E.O. #30.
Degraded hill prairie south of stream.  History of aerial herbicide application. Looks good from a distance because of dominance by big bluestem, but depauperate on ground.  Accompanies EO TP#34
Degraded hill prairie east of Fairmont Sewage ponds.  Has history of aerial spraying.  Looks better from distance due to dominance by big bluestem and Sorghastrum.  Accompanies EO TP #34.

Wet prairie used as hay meadow. Owner intends to tile and drain. Dominance of grasses different to determine due to mowing 7 days previous. Not a very good releve due to conditions, but very little information available for this community in southwest Minnesota.

Heavily grazed native pasture tract connecting Prairie Sky Unit of Cottonwood River Prairies with Peterson easement. north facing slope. Population of 146 Prairie Bush Clover. Cover and abundance hard to estimate do to grazing. Soil: coarse sandy loam. Glacial till hill prairie.
North-facing slope due south of gravel pit and sils. Glacial till hill prairie.
Native prairie pasture, actively grazed; north-facing slope. Owner: Simonson. East end, just beyond Peterson's fenceline. Glacial till hill prairie.
Isolated prairie remnant on north-facing slope being invaded at base by Prunus americana. Relates to glacial till hill prairie E.O. #176.
Releve at north end of tract surrounding a patch of Eryngium. Mesic to wet mesic blacksoil prairie.
Releve on north-facing slope of large, broad drainageway into Marsh Lake. Almost no duff. Soil is sandy loam. 15 % bare ground.
Level, moist drainageway. Channel runs just south of here.  Dominated by Carex, Spartina, and Calamagrostis cf. canadensis. Clay loam (silty?). Bare ground less than 1%.  Moss covers ground surface.
Nearly level, somewhat moist site with deep loam soil. Bare ground less than 5%. Duff 1-2 cm.
7 inches of loam over sticky clay. No bare ground.  Duff is less than 1 cm.
Mostly level mesic prairie bordering Lac Qui Parle.  Clay loam soils mixed with sand and gravel.  Probably both hayed and grazed at one time.  Litter depth is less than 3 cm.
Mostly level mesic prairie bordering Lac Qui Parle. Sandy loam soils underlain by clay and gravel. Probably has haying history. Litter depth about 3 cm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Canopy was not fully leafed-out. Cover estimates are predictions but are considered to be reliable. Extent of B-rank forest uncertain; much of remainder of site is CD rank.

Old-growth white cedar forest (more than 250 years old) on wet-mesic site. Abundant down logs. Good yellow birch regeneration. Very little past cutting noted. Minnesota cedar DBH = 27.3cm, to 53.5cm. Old growth data. Northern white cedar forest.
Releve selected to include grove of large cedars (one of three encountered) in old-growth northern white cedar forest, wet-mesic site, only one cut stump(well-decayed); stand age more than 250 years.
Old-growth white cedar swamp about 210 years old. Past logging in about 1960 left many cut stumps and cut down logs. Rather brushy. Old growth data collected.
Old-growth white cedar swamp about 210 years old. Past logging in about 1960 resulted in many cut stumps and cut down logs. Releve in lowland at north edge of upland. Old growth data collected.
Plot characterized by abundant down boles and snags (see data sheet); dense deciduous leaf mulch.  Adjacent to releve 0475 (1990-01). Northern white cedar forest. Old growth data collected.

Two cut stumps in plot one cf. white pine. A few cut stumps outside of plot-cedar, yellow birch. AB condition. Abundant snags-and large boles on first floor. Moderate density of large trees. Old Growth data. Northern white cedar forest.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Northern hardwood-conifer forest dominated by 60-70 year old Quercus rubra with subcanopy of Acer saccharum. Shrub layer of varying density dominated by Corylus. Dry-mesic site on southeast-facing slope.
Old-growth upland white cedar forest(more than 187 yrs old.) Cedars concentrated in groves, in matrix dom. by Acer spic. and Betula papy.  Frequent snags and down logs.
Transcribed by Barb Delaney, October 1990 from original-Lustig plot #3. Cover/abundance here merged into height-class groups. Reliability very low. Plot data from 6/7/79 and 8/28/79.
Plot typical of meadow around Devil's Lake, encroaching onto mudflats of drying basin. Plot does not capture diversity of entire site. Minerotrophic peat, Sphagnum essentially absent.
Releve typical of red cedar-oak basalt balds. Plot near toe of southwest slope, just northeast of old green cottage. Rock outcrops approximately 30% cover.
Nearly level site on beach ridge surrounded by 2-5m bur oak trees. Looks like a tiller passed through, (or tree planter?) Bare sandy soil exposed. Extremely dry - Geum triflorum wilting.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Plot typical of mesic forest on flatter portions of steep southwest-facing slope. Most trees 30-50 cm. diameter. Soils- cumulic sandy loam. Stumps occasional on plot and in stand.  Panax present.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Plot typical of Maple-Basswood Forest on flatter topography, terrace above St. Croix. Most of plot in swale just south of east west gully. Nearly continuous canopy of sugar maple seedlings typical of entire area
Plot typical of stream bottoms white pine forest. Plot near stream where weed species are abundant. Soils loamy fine sand, alluvium. Pine and basswood blowdown on plot.
Sedge meadow occurs in broad wetland bordering cedar creek. More diverse herbs and shrubs toward upland margin. Clumps of Salix in meadow. Typha patches near creek. Same meadow as species list 9044.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Old growth maple-basswood, varying degrees of disturbance. The 80 acres southeast of adjacent scientific and natural area shows little disturbance except ruts from sugaring activity on short, irregular slopes.Northern border of the "Big Woods" region, on loamy soils of short irregular slopes with numerous marshy depressions. History of light selective cutting, and pasturing.
Old-growth white cedar-white birch-fir stand (>220 years) On gentle north facing slope. Surrounded by large white birch stands. Mesic site near Brule Lake and BWCAW.

Old-growth upland white cedar forest (> 180 years). Cedars conclusion in small groves in matrix of white birch, fir, and white spruce. Frequent stumps from cutting in late-1920's. Nearly level, mesic to wet mesic.

Large Betula grandulifera-dominated fen with black spruce swamp. Past, present ATV/snowmobile trails angle off from section line trail; creates patches dominated by Carex lasiocarpa and small forbs. Releve typical. Attractive fen with black spruce swamp.

Below house on small terrace, by dry creek bed. Hardwood-white pine immediately adjacent and upslope of plot. Canopy gap from dead trees. Much coarse woody debris, some large diameter +/- 50cm, some old snags. No cut stumps. Few boulders. Soil: Black coarse loam.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: One of many better-quality areas on north/east slopes. Trees 20-40cm DBH. Tall understory. Shady. Possibly missed a few herbs, but typical lo-div. No obvious disturb here. Trails, stumps, aspen-dominated area occasional nearby.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Plot in partial opening (dead and defoliated birch; very wet) in seepage zone with wet pools; uncommonly wet. Near base of upland. Appears undisturbed.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Plot in portion of swamp without seepage character. Firm woody peat, no open water pools; exposed organic soil in deer trail, by tip-ups. Trees 18-35cm DBH. Herb flora similar to mature Larix stand to north.
Beautiful, mature black ash swamp. Plot situated on a 0.5 wide stream with muck sides and bottom. Shady, few light-gaps. No apparent cut stumps or other disturbance.

Plot in mid-aged dry-mesic jack pine forest. Apparently past-disturbed because of relatively low diversity, much Carex pennsylvanica and Danthonis. Sandy loam to 60cm. More diverse stand in SE NW 21, more mesic.

Sedge meadow/wet meadow-graminoid subtype. Plot near upland margin of extensive shallow peatland and near meander of Buckman Creek. Organic soil >80 cm deep. Toward creek, Calamagrostis candensis appears to be dominate no forbs, shrubs.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Mature, dry-mesic oak stand in extensive, unfragmented forest of variable quality. Plot in a better area. Has a fairly large canopy gap but typical. Trees 25-40cm. No obvious stumps, trails.

Mature dry-mesic oak stand in extensive, unfragmented oak forest. Plot in better area, more diverse. Trees 34-37cm DBH. Rare, visible cut stumps. Not much coarse woody debris. Beautiful topography on St. Croix Moraine. Soil: brown silty-fine sand.
Plot in small portion (5-10 acre) of red pine-jack pine forest. Relatively diverse. Jack pine 33-35 years old; 20-22cm DBH. On sand terrace of the Crow Wing River. Rare in Morrison county.

Gravel prairie. Plot at/below crest of slope at west side of second prairie opening from Co Rd (west side sec 18). Degraded but typical of site. Some patches better, many poorer. Classic esker. Soil: silty sand-loam with small pebbles.
Sand prairie. Plot in very small prairie remnant on outwash sand west of the Ripley Esker. Interesting because so little prairie remains. This site probably too small to protect.
Rooted peat mat around 2 ha. pond. Sphagnum +/- continuous  Small pools with Utricularia. Scirpus subterm, Spargan minimum, Utric gibba in pond. Undisturbed. Peat on outwash.
Alder swamp is extensive though somewhat patchy, grading into willow swamp, emergent marsh and low rises of lowland hardwood with oak. Plot near tamaracks. Undisturbed.
Plot in narrow zone of tamarack south of pond. More diverse than Larix stand northeast of pond (less Ledum and Sphagnum than this). Larix average 15 cm DBH, max 21. No obvious disturbance.

At edge of low shrub thicket (Betula glandulifera, Salix species), northwest of small upland rise center sec 8. Plot with meadow and fen species, a few species of poor fen. Past burned? In good interdrumlin meadow.

Extensive inter-drumlin shallow peatland, mostly wet meadow, some marsh, rich fen, poor fen. Plot in meadow near upland.  Typical. No obvious disturbance. Salix discolor and Soldiago cf uliginosa outside of plot.

Plot in 5 acre area of past-grazed bur oak savanna/medium-sized oak, hazel thickets spreading with good structure/diversity. 20 acre more, but poor; overgrown with oak-aspen-hazel, or dominated by Poa.
Plot in ca. 50 by 50 m area of mesic sand prairie (savanna structure much destroyed) at margin of badly degraded old field/pasture. Site not well-searched for other remnants. On outwash.

Dry mesic prairie occurs as series of 15 - 150m squred openings in Rhus glabra/Corylus thickets along crest of Mississippi River terrace. Grazed oak savanna borders openings. Trails, road. Alluvial sand. Soil: coarse sandy-loam with pebbles.

Plot in better part of varying qualilty floodplain forest. Trees multi-stem but good herb diversity. Some areas dominated by Elymus virginicus. Here, Carex retrorsa may be >1 spp. 10 and 20 acre cuts in forest.
5 acre remnant pine-hardwood forest near crest of steep slope. Surrounding pine-oak in various stages of regeneration, poor quality. Here, white pine average 60, max 89cm DBH, red pine 30 to 62cm.

Plot in relatively mesic, older stand at site (2 red pines at 48cm, 2 white pines 50cm. Old Populus grandidentata). Pine and birch snags, fair amount coarse woody debris. 1 old cut stump 50cm. Trails not obvious. Rough terrain.

Badly degraded, past grazed bur oak savanna with dense growth of Juniperus virginana. Plot in rare, relatively-good  opening. NNE sec 13 soil is light medium-sand, recent aeolian forms; rare Hudsonia.
Wet brush prairie has tall shrub cover. Not burned recently, although upland aspen at site had burned. Uncommon community at this site; adds to site diversity.

Disturbed brush prairie in northeast 18 has old ditches, trails, cultivated field. Patchy mesic (plot) to wet. Abundance codes not very reliable, difficult to estimate vegetation cover. 5-10% litter cover.
Ca 20m by 60 m of sparse, lower-growing, relatively diverse vegetation in area of disturbed mesic prairie and wet brush prairie. Deer blinds, old trails
In area of disturbed mesic prairie and wet brush prairie of varied composition. Forb list will vary over short (20 m) distances. Disturbance to wet brush prairie unknown.
Representative of aspen woodland, although structure varies. Attractive but not special.
Plot in most diverse portion of mesic to wet-mesic brush prairie remnant.  Lumpy to flat terrain with 1-by-2m. depressions (boulders removed?).
Small, localized, semi-saline meadow with wet pools (0.5-1m squared; 1-4cm deep.) In area of extensive shrubby wet meadow. Old fences, probably past grazed.
Dry-mesic brush prairie.
Wet meadow - shrub subtype. Soil: clayey black organic over light brown sand over sand with small gravel.

Releve taken on brief visit to see Pillager District Old Growth Stand in Pills State Forest. Small stand on steep west facing slope, mature, with canopy gaps. St. Croix Moraine Complex, sandy loam. Rare old stumps.

Narrow band of oak savanna/oak woodland on 40 foot high terrace slope of Mississippi River. Plot area looks scruffy from recent oak cutting/burning, but prairie species improved. Much Poa/Rhus elsewhere.
Plot in best portion of 80-100 acre stand. Has supercanopy of pines and mature/old deciduous trees. History of windthrown and timber salvage; a few snags. Driveway; adjacent old fields; poor buffer.

In long, narrow north-south zone of relatively open, wet brush prairie or meadow;  Shrub cover to 15%. Site has been grazed in past and recently burned. No litter. Soil: Black organic over coarse sand with small pebbles.
In large opening of dense wet-mesic brush prairie; north-south narrow openings being overgrown with aspen. Plot with less dense shrubs and more herb cover than average.  Past drained, grazed?

In area of north-northwest trending zones of shrub-meadow (with small amount wet brush prairie) between broader zones of aspen. No obvious disturbance, but history unknown. Interesting patterned complex.
Plot is in better example of Betula glandulifera dominated wet brush prairie in the area, all of which appear overgrown, past drained, and have no Andropogon gerardii.
In large, apparently undisturbed rich fen opening in extensive shrub fen complex. Potentilla fruticosa usually much more uncommon.
Area of Larix swamp, black spruce swamp, and surrounded by tall Salix. Appears past-drained. Plot in moister, more diverse patch. Hummocky. Tip-ups and much debris. Stumps elsewhere.
Plot in small, shady, white cedar stand within fir swamp. Entire area is lovely: hummocky, common patchy sphagnum, much debris, including recent tip-ups, graminoid-dominated hollows.

Tamarack swamp - sphagnum subtype. Releve plot on west half of mat with 25% cover of 2m tall Larix laricina; east half of mat has continuous cover of 10m tall Larix laricina. Sphagnum cover continuous throughout. See Dan Hansen's soil profile.
Nearly continuous moss cover dominated by sphagnum, moderate relief. Dominated by 10-15m Picea mariana with very sparse Picea mariana subcanopy; Ledum groenlandicum dominant below.
Tamarack swamp - minerotrophic subtype. Windthrow damage, fallen Larix laricina every 25m in some places; understory composition is similar to alder swamp.

Black spruce swamp. Releve plot dominated by 10m tall Picea mariana, but Larix laricinia scattered thru east half of EOR. Small light gaps with open sedge/shrub fen inclusions. Common Ledum groenlandicum and Chamadaphne below.
Poor fen, shrub suptype. Continuous moss cover dominated by Sphagnum, hummocks often with 1m relief. Betula glandulifera dominates at 70-80% cover; diversity is greatest in open patches.
Nearly continuous moss cover dom by Sphagnum, mod relief up to 1 m. Betula glandulifera dom w/ diversity of ericaceous shrubs. Few scattrd Larix laricina, one 1-m Picea mariana in EOR,not near releve
Fen is disturbed by cows; path through firmer part of mat; Carex cf lacustris (or rostrata) dominates with scattered patches of Chamaedaphne calyculata; fen is quaking mat at edge of small lake.
Poor fen, shrub subtype.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Typical of mixed oak forest in this area but other areas in site 32 have abundant Betula papyrifera and/or more common Populus grandidentata.

Poor fen - sedge subtype. Thin peat layer (<6") under thick sphagnum mat (10-12"); edge of mat is 12-24" wide moat, probably created by beavers; western edge of mat dominated by Carex rostrata with common Spirea tomentosa.

Lake beach, inland mud. Approximately 70% of open water covered by Nymphaea tuberosa with Nuphar variegatum; oraganic muck substrate; releve includes zone between alder upland and water to 10 inches deep.

Feleve includes 20 meter stretch of river, 5 meters wide, to water depth of 6"; this is a small bay with a back current where plants accumulate; substrate ranges from organic muck to sand. Organic sandy much with areas of large rock.
Tamarack swamp. Some areas outside of releve were "soupy" and unstable, but primarily a patchy mat of Sphagnum.
Willow swamp or wet meadow - shrub subtype.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Aspen-birch forest. Sandy, medium texture soils; estimated 10-15% cover of fallen birch limbs; frequent birch snags; multiple stemmed birch; multi-stemmed sugar maple in subcanopy.
Soils dark sandy loam, w/ occasional dolomite bedrock outcrops; planted pines, threatened by juniper invasion in 1971. (transcribed by D. Wovcha)
Soil sandy loam over Prairie du Chien dolomite bedrock. (Transcribed by D. Wovcha.)
Soils- loamy sand; SW slope of 5 - 10 degrees
Soils thin sandy loam over Prairie du Chien dolomite. Abundant exposur es and rubble. Best bedrock bluff prairie surveyed by Cushing and Scanlon.
Probably heavily cut (for oak?) estim by 1945 (age of Acer neg). Wind- throw has kept canopy fairly open; shrubs common. Soils: silt loam underlain by red till.
Soil: sand over red till; lightly grazed prior to 1971. Rolling ridge crest.
Soils:  Edith sand over red till; little disturbed at time of releve. Red pine planted in ravine.

Soil: sandy gravel and red sand; 0-30 degree slope. Latitude and longitude are approximate: "probably an area used as gravel source for railroad. Red pine and Rhus glabra on So. At reststop 1/4 S of CR 32, over bridge.

place_name: Lake Elmo Reg Park E; MCBS #85
remarks: Soil: dark sandy loam; leaf mulch 1" deep. 0-20 deg slopes.  Most of the oaks do not appear open grown.
Soil peat, some standing water. Creek runs year-round. In center of area is ca 3 acres 100% Larix cover; in good condition. Most maples are multi-stem.
Releve typical of old-growth oak forest on upper slope and hill crest. Large (30") open-grown oaks with smaller (15") forest-grown trees of equal height. Soil sandy loam, Chetek. No cut stumps.
Soil: sandy loam. Pin oaks often multiple stemmed and young suggesting past cutting. High density of Sambucus pubens in understory. Quercus alba doing poorly. More shrubs on lower slopes. Some trash.
Soil: very fine sandy loam. Slightly rolling topog. Grazed by cattle until about 1910 and around 1940 by horses. Dead trees removed 1960. One cut stump. Old trees are well-pruned. Low wet areas.
Soil: sandy with small rocks; derived from red till.
Soil: light brown and sandy; derived from till. On moist parts of steep (30-40 degree) southeast-facing slope.
Releve includes a blowdown gap typical of forest on crest to midslope of hill. Soils: sandy w/ gravel; A1 only 5cm (Mahtomedi), an inclusion within sswd. Releve training session.

Ribbed fen located in inter beach peatland surrounded by scrub Quercus macrocarpa. Releve in drier portion of fen without pools. Much thatch. Probably beyond influence of drainage ditch. Site dry, no rain for a month.
Dense stand at base of ridge in Agassiz Beach Ridge Complex. Peat sapric approximately 15 cm. pH = 7.0.
Releve in area of faint ribbed fen pattern in interbeach peatland. Peat > 3m.
Open (rich) fen. Releve located in interbeach peatland (peat > 1m). Site very dry because of drought past 3 years. Areas surrounded by shrubs.
Shrub (rich) fen. Variable shrub covered peatland located in basin east of interbeach complex. Area burned this spring. Peat approximately 40cm, but boulder nearby.
Patch of uniform oak savanna on Dohrman Interbeach Complex in an open oak-brush type.

Located on slope of Randeen beach ridge. Few scattered large Betula papyrifera and Populus tremuloides remaining. Much large woody debris. Some openings in canopy in area around releve. No evidence of logging.
Large sedge fen with scattered Salix species, north side of road. Faint ribbed pattern. Scattered boulders. Peat approximately 40cm over sandy clay.
Large sedge meadow dissected by road.

Black spruce-tamarack swamp on Whiskey Lake peninsula of Mud Lake. Resembles bog except for large DBH (18cm). May have been impacted by past lake level changes, or wind blown dust from Red River Valley.
Large tamarack swamp north of Bemis Ridge. Peat 50 to 55cm. over clay-clay loam.
Ribbed fen in center of water track in Pine Creek Peatland. Pools present.
Very homogeneous jack pine stand (8-18 cm dbh). Several old, 5-7 cm cut stumps indicate stand may have been thinned in past. Also, many scarred stumps.  Soil = sand.
At base of Bemis Ridge, upslope of calcareous seepage fen.  pH=7.6, Cond.=257 mg/l, Alka.=3.53, Color= 0.119. Cedar approx. 300 yrs old.
WHITE-CEDAR/SUGAR MAPLE STAND ON MESIC SITE.  CANOPY GAP IN ONE CORNER.  THREE BLOWN-DOWN CEDARS IN ANOTHER CORNER.  NEARLY LEVEL SITE.
DBH (CM): LARIX-24.4,20.6  TAMARACK STAND N OF TANGNES FOREST ROAD. SHRUBBY UNDERSTORY. SHALLOW DRAINAGES FORMING MAZE THROUGHOUT. APPROX. 40% POOLS.  80% MOSS; 20% NEEDLES, MUD.  4 CM SOGGY PEAT.

DBH(CM):BS-20.8,17.5,17.3. BS STAND AT EDGE OF CUTOVER NW OF WARROAD. QUITE SHRUBBY(D4) IN PATCHES. PATCHES OF COARSE SEDGES IN STAND. LOTS OF GRAM CVR & FEW CEDARS. GRND CVR: 90% MOSS(80%BRY,20%SPH).
Palmville Peatland. Dbh(cm): Larix 22.1; BS 12.6,9.2,5.0. Stand: BS w/ few Larix to S, grades into Larix w/BS, then willow increases & grades into Larix w/few BS scattered among willow to N.
Black spruce stand north of Pine Ridge Cemetary off of Bednar Forest Road. 100% moss ground cover, mostly sphagnum. DBH (cm) spruce-11.3, 11.3; tamarack 23.6. Fruiting Geocaulon lividum collected.
DBH(cm) Spruce-18.6, 18.2; Balsam-16.5,14.6. Bryales-ground cover. Blowdown 20%. White spruce stand off of Bernard's Orchard Road.
Mixed pine-hardwood off of Roosevelt Road.  DBH(cm): aspen-12.0,15.0, 24.7; jack pine-32.5,36.7.  Center of plot is 22 m east of deer stand.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: Boreal hardwood-conifer stand west of Wabble Grade. DBH(cm): fir-17.6; aspen-13.2. Stand is mix of aspen (mostly) with small clusters of white cedar, balsam fir, and spruce; 20-30% conifer. Duff deciduous. Soil: Loam/decaying vegetation over fine light gray-brown sand.

DBH(cm): aspen-31.0; birch-18.9; black spruce-15.0. Boreal hardwood- conifer forest off River Road. Ground cover of duff. Perhaps slightly more conifer than BC-145-Riv, 20%. Soil: decaying vegetation over pale tan sand.

DBH(cm): aspen-15.3,31.5; black spruce-8.4; balsam fir-17.6.  Duff of deciduous leaves; <5% blowdown. Primarily aspen with spruce and birch. 15-20% conifer cover, less in stands to west. Decaying vegetation over gray sand over tan sand.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: DBH(cm): balsam pop-22.0,34.4; aspen-15.6. Aspen/balsam poplar stand northeast of Tanges Forest Road on powerline. Little balsam poplar, most in wet areas, at edges of small sedge wetlands or shrub swamp. Soil: sandy loam over light brown sand.

DBH(cm): balsam poplar - 17.4,11.9,19.5; aspen - 8.6; betula - 22.1. Abundance: aspen-60%, fir-15-20%, balsam poplar -15-20% and a few paper birch. Balsam poplar in small, scattered clumps; increases in moist/swamp areas. Soil: fine gray sand over fine tan sand.

Rich fen north of Polonia wildlife management area. Sea of Calamagrostis and Carex with scattered (<10%) Salix and sparse patches of Phragmites. Few apsen clones, increases to north with Salix. Phragmites sparse until west edge of section. Soil: Wet peat over moist peat over clay.
Fen north of Polonia wildlife management area. Thick hay layer. Note: Cladium near (not in) this releve, see map.
Wet prairie on Polonia wildlife management area. Patches of dense Salix opening up to sparse Salix and dense graminoids. Soil: sandy loam over coarse sand/gravel.

Cleared oak savanna? at gravel pit in extreme northwest Roseau county. Aster seri., Allium stell. Geum trif, Erig. pulc., present elsewhere at site. Representative distribution. Transition between dry open savanna and oak woodland? Soil: coarse sand/gravel over sandy loam.

Balsam poplar with ash and pockets of aspen in stand. Releve in balsam pop. Trees with leafy trunks and not very spreading canopy. DBH(cm): balsam poplar - 17.5,18., 19.8. Stand between Morehouse Forest Road and Roseau River. Soil: sandy loam over fine dark brown sand.
Black spruce swamp. This site is near the alder releve #92-29 (USFS releve #1827). No stakes.

Opening in black spruce swamp with scattered larix. 3.2 miles east on forest road road #2164. Typha dominant under denser black spruce open area surrounded by scrub black spruce 15-20feet and scattered Larix averaging 5 feet. Scheuchzeria at edge.
5.8 miles east on forest road #2164.
Black Spruce Swamp. Color slide photos #24,#25,djs.
Black Spruce Swamp.
One of densest stands of black spruce in site; scattered Larix at edge to 15m, occassional blowdown; leather-leaf and blueberries fill in light gaps.
Black spruce bog? Poor fen?
Releve is in intermediate zone between tamarack swamp and lake edge where Carex lasiocarpa dominates; parked on road 1.5 miles northeast of highway 9. Water pH=7.3 (pocket field pH meter).

70% Larix cover becomes more diverse; further south only 10-15% conifer cover in places alder dominates, cedar occasional. Near upland; ash at uplands with Bidens. Water pH=6.5 (pocket field pH meter).
Some areas of mat dominated by Chamaedaphne Calyculta, overall covers 20-30% but Carex Lasiocarpa (?) dominates overall. Water chemistry pH = 5.8-6.0.
Diverse bryophyte community - not characterized by species i.d. water chemistry pH = 7.5.
Refer to Ecological Occur Records (EOR) for remarks; water chemistry pH 7.7 (pocket pH meter in-field reading).
See ecological occurance records for remarks. Water chemistry pH = 5.7 ("pocket" pH meter reading in field).
See ecological occurrence record notes for community description. Water chemistry pH = 7.0 ("pocket" ph meter, reading in field)

Releve taken at meadow edge which is dominated by Carex oligosperma with patches of Chamaedaphne; small center island of 5-foot Larix and Chamaedaphne. Sphagnum recurvum aggreg. Dominates most of mat.
Water chemistry pH = 7.4 ("pocket" pH meter read in field).
Water chemistry pH = 7.6 ("pocket" pH meter read in field).
Water chemistry pH = 7.7 ("pocket" pH meter read in field).
Permanent plot: poles in southwest and northeast corners. Two photos: #7 and #8.
Water chemistry: 6.1. ("pocket" pH meter).
Black spruce swamp.
Ground: 70% moss covered - mostly sphagnum. 50% cover of conifer needles and cones. DBH(cm): 18.4, 18.3, 21.0. Black spruce swamp in Agassiz NWR.
Ground cover: duff of Larix needles. Small amount of moss.  Tamarack island, tamarack swamp on Agassiz NWR.

Rich fen. Ground cover: dense matted graminoid leaves. Burned aspen to 800m north of ditch (thick raspberry, aspen, balsam poplar understory) and willow common. Continuing north, area of thick Potentilla fruticosa and Salix, then open fen. Very moist peat.

Releve on fen-like spot in sea of Phragmites. Also broad wetter areas of coarse sedge. In some wetter areas Typha and Phragmites mixed. Clones of aspen/willow form islands. Some aspen burned in area. Peat over black clay over gray clay with coarse sand.

Ground cover: matted graminoid leaves. Fen with Phragmites.  Increasing Salix, weedy species (raspberry, Gerardia) to south. Coarse sedges and Typha in wetter spots. Overall 60-70% Phragmites, 30-40% fen. Moist to wet peat.

General area: Carex buxbaumii with broad patches of Phragmites and sedge/grass mixed with Phragmites. Aspen clones. Few very small wet spots with Scirpus and/or Typha. Drier patches with Cirsium, weedy species in small areas.

Uneven ground. Blow-downs common-willow branches, stems.  Ground cover: 50% moss, 50% branches, deciduous leaves. Soil moist only. Mix of aspen clones and willow swamp with tracts of Phragmites and Typha between. Soil: Moist peat over 1cm clay.
Patch of Carex in sea of Phragmites and Typha. Area little bigger than 10x10 plot. Fen in Agassiz NWR. Soil: mixture of clay coarse sand and water.

Mature aspen stand with strong understory (D3-4) of aspen.  Entire stand seems to be patches of different ages of aspen-DBH(cm)15.5, 21.2, 22.5.  North on Jacobson's Trail(MDHA) in Eckvoll Wildlife Management Area.

npc_type_name: Green Ash - Bur Oak - Elm Forest
remarks: Pocket of oak in mixed stand of green ash, balsam poplar, oak, black ash and aspen. Ground cover: deciduous leaves. Blowdown <<5%. Southeast edge of Agassiz NWR.

DBH(cm): 29.3,28.8,32.5.  Stand of large, tall aspen with well-developed shrub, herb and grass layers. Ground cover of deciduous leaf duff, covered almost completely by graminoid leaves. Abundant Rhus radicans.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: Northwest corner of Roseau County. Aspen-ash swale. Standing water up to 6" over 50-75% of plot. DBH(cm): aspen-45.0,50.4,19.9,17.6; ash-19.3,6.3,5.8. Moss - 5% ground cover.

Long island oak/aspen in wet-mesic "old field"/wet prairie just southwest of Roseau rvr Wildlife Management Area. DBH(cm): aspen-13.5,10.3,9.5; oak-9.9,7.7,9.0,13.3. Soil-top 5cm decaying plants; 10-15 gray sand; last 3 clay with pebbles.

In northwest Roseau county. Small stands of large DBH balsam pop within larger aspen stand. DBH(cm): aspen 12.2; balsam poplar-26,27.3,26.8; oak-8.6. Ash along river to south. Deciduous duff. < 5% blowdown. 1 aspen snag in plot, 25',3-4" DBH.
Small fen on Roseau River Wildlife Management Area boundary.  5-10% low willow. Grades into dense willow, then aspen/willow.

Ash stand on oxbow of Roseau River. Duff of deciduous leaves. Moss on several logs. Downed trees <5%. DBH(cm): ash-41.7,38,29.1,46; elm-6.7,7.3,7.0. Poor shrub, herb and graminoid layers; floor covered with ash seedlings.

Aspen with scattered mature white spruce. DBH(cm): aspen-14.3,15; white spruce 53.4. Dense shrub layer domianted by hazel. Sparse herb/gram layers. Duff of deciduous leaves and spruce cones. <5% downed trees. 1 aspen snag in plot.
Northwest corner of Roseau county. Aspen with very scattered Jack pine. DBH(cm): aspen-10.1,11,22.2; jack pine-44.6.

Old aspen stand with young aspen, oak, and hazel in understory. Bracken fern and Rhus radicans abundant. DBH(cm): aspen-31.1, 38.6, 35.5. Balsam poplar also seen in stand but not dominant, not patchy.
Narrow ash stand along oxbow of Roseau River. Weedier (more Xanthium and Urtica) toward opening and toward oxbow.  DBH(cm): ash-24.4,29.1; elm-9.5,4.2.
Near headquarters of Roseau River Wildlife Management Area. Island of aspen in jack pine cutover. Approximately 5% downed trees, branches. Deciduous leaf duff. DBH(cm): aspen-21.9, 12.6, 15.8.

Near headquarters of Roseau River Wildlife Management Area. Large DBH jack pine surrounded by smaller DBH jack pine with pockets of large jack pine and grading into aspen. DBH (cm) of jack pine: 31.0, 16.4, 34.0, 37.0. Soil: 5cm decaying vegetation over 5cm gray sand.

Rather uniform aspen stand with park like D4-5 layer and dense 1-3 layer of H.D. Rhus radicans abundant. DBH(cm): aspen-14.1, 12.4, 18.0 17.5. Near headquarters of Roseau River Wildlife Management Area.
Pocket of oaks in aspen stand. From north to south trail to west-scattered oaks in aspen, becoming progressively larger pockets as move east. Dense understory of hazel and juneberry in most areas.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: Aspen stand n of Bemis Hill. Very little graminoid cover. Deciduous leaf ground cover. <5% blowdown. Feathermoss and Mnium on 1 log. 1 snag 2m tall. Average DBH(cm): fir-11.5; aspen-17.5; birch-7.8; balsam poplar-19.5.

Aspen stand with small amount balsam poplar and black ash South of Swift. No spruce seen. Dense, tall shrub layer D4-5 and lots of blowdown. Deciduous leaf duff. DBH(cm): aspen-10.5,39.3,18.6,26.6 Pure aspen to east.
Small oak stand in larger stand of aspen with bam and oak northeast of Badger. DBH(cm): oak 27.9, 38.5, 11.8. Soil: thin black sandy loam.

Stand of black ash with wet soil west of Roosevelt. Lots of blowdown in area Bam and aspen around stand. Matted grass covering ground. < 5% moss cover. Open (at eye level) ash swale with strong 2-3' graminoid layer. Soil: black clayey loam with plant debris over wet gray sand with red streaks.
Aspen stand north of powerline west of Roosevelt. Mature aspen with strong D4-5 of young aspen, Amelanchier and Cornus. DBH(cm) aspen: 23.8, 20.5, 26.5. Ground cover of deciduous leaf duff.

Open, uniform jack pine stand along county road 20 southwest of Roosevelt. Low shrubs and herbs dominate understory, mosses cover forest floor. DBH(cm) jack pine: 28.5, 20.0, 26.6. Top 2cm soil decaying plant material.

Black spruce stand north of County Road 2, southwest of Roosevelt. 5% blowdown. 15% bare ground. DBH(cm): black spruce - 13.0, 20.1, 24.1. To northwest of BG-121-CO2. Rim of black spruce between aspen/BG and LB.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: North of County Road 2 southwest of Roosevelt. Pocket of mature balsam poplar(bam) includes patches of mature bam, patches of young bam (D4-5, 1-2" DBH) and areas where young is understory of old. DBH(cm) bam: 21.2, 26.6, 18.6.
Only ground cover: mounds of moss (collected) 5% of plot; covered with spruce needles. Little blowdown. Island of white spruce in bog birch, willow and aspen southwest of Badger.

Aspen stand along Morehouse road in southeast Roseau County. Relatively flat mature aspen stand with dense herbaceous layer and park like shrub layer. DBH of aspen ranged from 9-26cm (x = 18, n = 14). D 6 i had 6 snags.

Rich Fen. In Roseau River Wildlife Management Area adjacent to large area of Cladium mariscoides. Some peat burnout holes filled with water, Salix species and Scirpus acutus. Soil: 50cm of peat over silty sand to silty clay. pH=7.3.
Releve representative of rich, black spruce (13cm DBH) forest between spring fen channels in Sprague Creek Spring Fen.  Area interspersed with open seepage gaps. pH=7.0.
Balsam poplar (39-54cm DBH) with balsam fir (14-25cm DBH) on mineral island east of Minnesota Hill. Approximately 10cm of organic over sand; light gray clay below 45cm.
Typical of drier site in mosaic of upland conifer and conifer swamp. Balsam fir (16-18cm DBH), Paper birch (23-24cm DBH). 20-50cm of organic over sand over silty sand. Probably high water table.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: Balsam poplar stand on mineral island in Marvin Lake Peatland.Boulders in area. Soil: 0-5cm organic; 5-8cm silty loam; 8-30cm white loamy sand with pebbles; >30 sandy clay with strata of loamy clay; hard pan.
Old aspen stand on undulating terrain. Soil: 0-5 litter, 0-5 A horizon, 5-30 cm loamy sand; hard pan over sandy clay over loamy sand.
Large ash swamp with savanna appearance. Dense, tall herb and graminoid growth with some bare soil partly moss covered. No reproduction over .3m. Soil: 7-8 cm of muck over clay.
One of few aspen stands on eastern Roseau county with significant amount of Quercus macrocarpa. Norland Area. Soil is loamy sand.
Releve in narrow bands between jack pine and cedar swamp in Norland area. Soil is sandy clay.

Decadent stand, several dead white spruce and down balsam fir and birch. On slight sandy island surrounded by peatland.  Soil: 0-5cm duff, 5-100 very fine tan sand, very compact, boulders near surface.

Extremely brushy with fairly open birch canopy; birch appear non-vigorous with sparse crowns. Soil: 0-5 cm A Horizon; 5-25cm loamy sand with limestone pebbles; >25 cm sandy clay, clayey-sand. Rocks and boulders at surface.
Tamarack (12-17cm DBH) swamp with Spahgnum, East of Sprague  Creek between black spruce swamp and scrub fen water track.  pH 5.4.
Classic black spruce (19-26cm DBH) feather moss swamp along Sprague Creek. Nutrient-poor, pH 5.1. Peat >1m. Moss collections given to J. Janssens for ID.
Releve in well-developed flark area in northwest part of fen. Very wet after days of rain, 15cm deep. pH 7.7. Probably some disturbance by north-south drainage ditch to west. Apparently burned often.
Representative of water track on east side of Marvin Lake.  pH=6.9. Moss collections sent to J. Jannsens for ID.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: Open understory, weedy. Poorly drained site in lake plain.  Canopy complete but sparse foliage. Standing water.  Bouldery; Soil: 0-5cm muck; 5-20 cm silty loam; 20-60 cm fine sandy clay, >60 cm fine sand.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: Wet aspen-balsam poplar stand on lake plain; very lush herb cover up to 1m; Few nearly bare depressions; Soil: 0-5cm muck; >5 cm gray clay; saturated at 10 cm.
Very large aspen (40-45cm DBH) on rich site (silty clay soil). Very brushy with high species diversity. 800 feet from Warroad River.
Black spruce (10-18cm DBH, 72+ years old) Downslope of beach ridge. Graminoid dominated. Moose trail. pH ca 7.1. Moss collection given to J. Janssens.
Graminoid-dominated tamarack swamp downslope of beach ridge. Moss collections sent to J. Jannsens for ID.
Black ash (16-21cm DBH) with american elm (20cm DBH) in swamp at base of dohrman ridge. Several dead large elms. 5cm of organic over sand with 5cm of loamy sand at 35-40cm.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: Aspen (26-29cm DBH) with black ash subcanopy in wet-mesic site on lake plain near base of dohrman ridge. 5cm organic over 5-25 cm silty-clay loam over sandy to gravelly clay or clay loam.
Narrow stand of bur oak (13cm DBH) along beach ridge top in beach ridge complex northwest of Palmville peatland.
Large tamarack (38cm DBH) stand at base of beach ridge west of lost lake. A few small old cut stumps. Peat >1m.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: Dry swamp or wet lowland hardwood forest. Narrow strip at base of beach ridge adjacent to lost lake. One of few areas with large elm. Much dead and dying paper birch. Standing water in spring. 45-60cm peat/loamy sand.
Typical of open sedge area in west part of Palmville Fen.  Peat >1. m. pH=6.9. Moss collections sent to J. Janssens for ID.

npc_type_name: Green Ash - Bur Oak - Elm Forest
remarks: Mesic forest along Roseau River, South of Wannaska in old glacial clay lagoon. Aspen(16-22cm DBH), bur oak(16), green ash(15), and american elm(12-13). Stand falling apart, many dead aspen. 5cm organic over 5cm sandy loam.

Dry sand beach deposit near southwest edge of beltrami island in Roseau County. Dead and down creating gaps in canopy.  Very well-drained site. Soil: 0-2cm litter, 2-10cm A horizon, >10 cm brown orange sand.
Releve south of hayes lake. Undulating topography. DBH 22-25cm. Soil: sand-sandy loam; hard pan at 35cm.
Large tamarack (25-27cm DBH), over 100 years old in large peatland at base of sand ridge. pH 7.3. Peat about 0.5m over sand. Dry hummocks of needle litter surrounding water-filled hollows with moss.
Jack pine (15-21cm DBH) with occassional large open grown jack pine (27cm DBH) growing on sand on beach ridge deposits southwest of hayes lake state park.
Linear swamp between beach ridges off bednar road. Peat variable, 0.3 - 0.4m deep, thin clay layer over sand. pH 7.3. Adjacent releve #253 at edge of peatland.
Black spruce forest located between upland black spruce and black spruce swamp off bednar road. Apparently being paludified; only 8cm of peat over sand. Adjacent to releve #254 in middle of swamp.
Northeast of marvin lake. Very open, patchy, stunted black spruce. Undisturbed.
Small bog positioned between beltrami island beach ridges; canopy composed of black spruce and jack pine. pH 4.1-4.2.
Northeast of Marvin Lake. Undisturbed forested bog. pH ca 4.2. Black spruce (10-15cm DBH). Sphagnum hummocks large, soft, billowy, probably S. magellanicum.

Very wet, homogeneous, species-poor marsh in depression on bemis ridge. Grades into Carex lasiocarpa fen upslope. pH approximately 7.9. Water approximately 3 feet deep. Grades into open water downslope.
Dry site; soil: sand-sandy loam; DBH 22-28cm; on undulating topography on east side of bemis ridge.
Tamarack-sphagnum swamp at edge of Luxemberg Peatland. pH 6.4. Moss collections sent to J. Janssens.
Ericaceous-dominated scrub fen between swamp forest and shrub fen. Sphagnum fuscum hummocks. Scattered Larix laricina 1-3m. pH 6.0-6.1. Moss collections sent to J. Jannsens for ID.
Very rich white cedar swamp with moss carpet, few shrubs.  Numerous species of orchids and rare species. In center of bemis peatland near base of slope of bemis ridge.
Small black spruce (16-23cm DBH) stand in middle of shrub swamp. Soil underdetermined. At least 15cm duff and peat.
Poor fen in small depression on edge of sandy bemis ridge.
Black spruce/jack pine on small sphagnum island in middle of poor fen. Depression in Bemis Ridge. Peat approximately 0.5m over red brown sand. pH 4.0. Moss collections sent to J. Janssens.
Small depression on east side of bemis ridge. Peat approximately 0.75m over sand. pH 5.4.
Apparently a young tamarack swamp.  10 year old photo appears to indicate brush. Approximately 30 years (fi).
Small stand bordering balsam fir area in southeast Roseau.
Typical of large area aspen forest in southeast part of county. Soil sand. Releve on slight knoll. Scattered dead aspen snags + dead and down.
Mixed black spruce (22-28cm DBH, 50-60% cover) and jack pine (38-45cm DBH, 10-20% cover) stand near carp trail. 5cm duff over loamy sand-sandy loam. Sandy clay layer at 40-45cm and hard pan at 65cm.

Jack pine(24-30cm DBH) with black spruce(16-17cm) on peak of beach ridge running through peatland north of Bednar road. 5cm duff; sand 5-60cm; 60cm hard layer clayey sand. Water ponded on surface after heavy rain.

Black spruce(20-22cm DBH) w/25% cover large diameter jack pine(39-40cm) on 1 of series of low flat beach ridges running through peatland. 0-2cm A; 2-7 spodic?; 7-70cm red brwn sand; >70cm hard pan. Some big jack pine dying.

Black spruce(21-29cm DBH) with small crown diameters with large open grown jack pine(27-38cm) on low mineral island in peatland north of Bednar Road. Many burned stumps. 5cm duff over very fine soft red-brown sand. Hard pan at 0.6m.
Jack pine (22-29cm DBH) with scattered aspen (25-26cm DBH) along sandy ridge north of Bednar Road. Soil: 0-7cm duff, 7-12cm light gray sand (spodic?), 12-50cm sand; hard pan at approximately 50cm.
Aspen (19-22cm DBH) with jack pine (26-32cm DBH) with spruce-fir subcanopy south of Bednar Road. Soil stratified with layers of loamy sand, sand, clayey sand and coarse sand. Several dead jack pine.
Tamarack swamp between oak ridge and fen in transition zone.  Somewhat disturbed, old cut stumps. Peat > 1m.
Nearly level. In large opening; some thickets of taller shrubs within the opening. Aspen woodland patches surround opening; site is wet-mesic.
OG stand; site 18. EO rec#7994.
