Lowland hardwood forest.Some ash up to 50cm DBH. Same area as releve 0696 by NEA.
Cedars widely spaced, 6-10m between clumps making it hard to get many in one releve plot. On gentle south-facing slope of gravel ridge.

Boreal hardwood conifer forest. Southeast of Randeen Church. Enter where fir comes to road.  Releve in area with largest white spruce to 59cm DBH; fir approximately 39cm, birch 48cm. One of 4 releves in this stand, area of most mature spruce.

Boreal hardwood conifer forest. One of 4 releves from stand. Stand hard to represent because trees in mature portions so widely spaced. This area slightly downslope from most mature spruce; smaller trees so more trees per plot.
Boreal hardwood conifer forest. In facies of stand without spruce, less balsam fir, richer understory. One of 3 releves in stand.

Boreal hardwood conifer forest. One of 3 releves in stand. In area with dense fir, ground layer sparse because of heavy litter layer. 30 fir with DBH 10-25 in releve plot in E5 and many dead fir in E4. Black clayey soil.

Boreal hardwood conifer forest. Phase 2 type aspen slated for cut. Tree data (DBH's all trees in plot) Betula:19,30,32,21,19,22,26 Fraxinus:15,9,13,11,12,12,11,12,11,10,10; Ulmus:12,20 Abies:9,16,11,15 Picea:13;1 of 3 releves from stand.
Previously burned, heavily disturbed lowland aspen, part of Thief Lake Wildlife Management Area.

Superior National Forest(comp 146,stand 29/859). Old growth northern hdwds on southeast and east-facing slope. Dry site predominately sugar maple with white spruce; no yellow birch. No evidence of logging. Site probably too dry to support yellow birch.

Superior national forest (Comp. 193 Stand 9/M9) on east and southeast-facing slope. Sugar maple and yellow birch were once co-dominate in forest; selective logging removed many birch and some pine. Ground layer: herbaceous-45%, dead-15% litter-40%.

Superior national forest (Comp.193 Stand 9/M9) old growth hardwoods on east and southeast-facing slope. Sugar maple and yellow birch once co-dominate in forest; birch and some pine selectively logged. Ground layer: herbaceous-80%, dead-5%, litter-15%.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Blue Beech) Seepage Swamp
remarks: This is a narrow area between moist sandstone cliffs at the base of Queen's Bluff and Highway 61 below. Numerous seeps run through site.
Canopy trees open-grown with classic savanna form.  Infrequent snags outside of plot. Moderate amount of woody litter. Soil silt loam, mapped as Brodale Cobbly Loam.

Releve had canopy opening (gap) from fallen tree on its edge. Infrequent old rotted stumps or remains of snags. Cored trees in plot: Quercus rubra-54 cm dbh, 74 rings; Quercus rubra 87.5cm DBH, 72 rings.
Scattered woody debris, and few fallen limbs.
Narrow seep runs through plot near southeast edge. This is the north-east facing slope of Queen's Bluff, just above Highway 61 and the Mississippi River. Soil sandy loam.

Releve plot is near top of slope. Canopy trees in forest and not in releve include Populus tremuloides and Juglans nigra. Soil silt loam. Trees generally with straight trunks, forest grown. Moderate amount of woody litter on ground.
Soil silty clay loam. Several dead young Acer negundo and one dead Rhamnus cathartica. Much coarse woody debris on ground.  Canopy open-grown.
Infrequent small limestone outcrops. Heavy layer of thatch (about 2cm thick) throughout. Shrubs and small trees occur in several dense patches throughout this prairie but much is open.

Several large limestone outcrops cover 5% of plot with about 50% lichen cover. Thick thatch throughout (about 2cm).  Occasional dead Rhus glabra stems. Approximately 99 live Rhus glabra stems in plot. Mid to lower slope.
Southeast oak woodland-brushland. Canopy trees moderately open-grown. Just over ridge is a large bluff prairie (GP#2). Soil is silty clay loam. Little woody litter, no dead trees.
Dry southeast oak forest. Canopy oaks open-grown, subcanopy oaks moderately  open-grown. Moderate amount coarse woody litter. Soil silty clay loam.
Southeast dry oak forest. Occasional large stumps; forest appears to be relatively young following logging. Soil silty clay loam.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: On talus intermittent with loose silt loam. Rocks generally moss-covered. Moderate amount coarse woody litter. On slope below trail from picnic area.
Trees and brush have been cut by park staff. Lower slope with much Prunus serotina. Heavy thatch accumulation; needs burning. Few small limestone outcrops (1% cover).
Releve at base of large bluff prairie beneath and including large sandstone outcrops.  Soil is brown sand. Sparse oak forest just below releve.
Releve about 5m south of treeline at top of slope. Heavy brush cover; little Rhus mortality. High priority for burning. Thin silt loam; less than 1% limestone outcrops.
Infrequent down trees; moderate amount of coarse woody litter. Thin silt loam over limestone bedrock. Old overgrown field road runs through lower plot.
About 1% limestone bedrock cover.  Little thatch.  One small bur oak just south of plot. (about 4m tall).
Mid portion of Queen's Bluff.
Bluff prairie has been managed with fire and cutting of sumac since 1985 (?) by Parks and SNA; <1% cover rock outcrops. 50 meters south of Releve #20. King's Bluff.
50 meters north of releve #19; bluff prairie has been managed with prescribed fire and cutting of sumac by Parks and SNA since about 1985. <1% cover rock outcrops. King's Bluff.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Large Quercus rubra occur outside plot. Forest about 90 years old, on steep bluff above Lake Pepin, with hiking trail through it.
Prairie too narrow for 10 x 10m releve plot.
5% limestone outcrop cover, with lichens. Soil very well-drained loamy sand.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Plot mid-slope in older dry-mesic oak forest. Several fallen trees in plot; much coarse woody litter. On sandy loam. Hay Creek Valley, which has experienced much erosion.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Rock outcrops occasional on upper slope (about 5% of plot cover). Largest trees in releve DBH: Acer saccharum 44, 55 cm; Carya cordiformis 37 cm.
About 5% cover by limestone outcrops. Soil shallow loamy sand.

Sumac sparse, heavily browsed. Few rock outcrops top of slope. Plot represents best part of prairie (remainder with dense growth of sumac). Moderate amount of thatch. Prairie slated to be burned summer 1992.
Infrequent small limestone outcrops. Occassional dead Rhus glabra. Prairie was prescribe burned in summer, probably in 1990. North corner of plot permanently marked with fiberglass post.
Big and little bluestem of short stature. Spring burn planned 1993. Plot located about one third of the way down slope. Metal stake placed in northeast corner of site. 10m x 10m plot.
Infrequent low limestone outcrops throughout. Coarse woody debris common on forest floor. Seeps and trout run creek occur just below slope.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: On terrace above Whitewater River. Dominated by Quercus macrocarpa averaging 30cm DBH. Moderate amount coarse woody debris. Alluvial soil: loamy sand.
On outwash above cannon river floodplain. Soil is sand.  Occasional small patches of loose bare sand. Calcareous fen/sedge meadow complex below slope.

Remnant old-growth stand dominated by sugar maple (60%) and yellow birch (40%) canopy. Yellow birch over mature, canopy falling apart. Adjacent woods selectively logged. Ground layer: herbaceous-50%, dead-35%, litter-15%. Releve site picked in area where there were no stumps - this is not characteristic of stand. Site is mesic to dry, evidence of yellow birch removal.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Part of extensive, mature maple stand extending along rugged uplands. Suggested as best examples of mature hardwoods in Tofte ranger district. No yellow birch observed, otherwise similar to site 1.
Mesic prairie on narrow sandy ridge that extends into marsh.
Mesic prairie on level upland about 40 feet from shallow, wet prairie swale.
Wet prairie in shallow swale in middle of The Natural Conservancy preserve.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Riparian forest along Red Lake River. On terrace above river--not active floodplain. Live elm in center of plot with 68.5 cm DBH.
Lowland hardwood forest on better-drained, higher ground inside of bend of Red Lake River. Dominant tree multiple-stemmed Tilia americana with most DBH's 15-25 cm. Some grazing in the past.
Dry mesic prairie on subtle sandy ridge oriented north to south at the northeast corner of Pancratz Prairie north.  Appears to be virtually undisturbed.

Dry mesic prairie on well-drained, fine sandy soil 0.75 mile west of major beach ridge of Glacial Lake Agassiz in old prairie pasture. Cow pies present but otherwise looks like hasn’t been grazed this year.

Undisturbed prairie on level top of major beach ridge of Glacial Lake Agassiz. South of active gravel mine and west of old gravel mines known as "benoit pit". Soil excessively-drained, gravel soil with occasional large boulders at surface.
Typical wet prairie in low, broad swale. Was grazed over 15 years ago and has some soil compaction.

Typical wet-mesic prairie in complex mosaic with wet prairie in low, shallow swell-swale topography on very slight west facing slope about half a mile west of Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridge. Typical of large part of nature preserve.
Typical mesic prairie on top of low, shallow ridge between large areas of wet brush prairie. In interbeach zone, approximately 1/8 mile west of major beach ridge of Glacial Lake Agassiz.
Typical mesic prairie in site. Subtle but strong halophytic component. Recently burned. On level terrain in interbeach zone of Glacial Lake Agassiz.

Wet prairie in shallow swale on slightly saline soils. In mosaic with wet -mesic prairie on shallow swell-swale topography on gradual west facing slope about 1.5 miles west of major beach ridge of Glacial Lake Agassiz.
Brush prairie on slight west facing slope on west side of a beach ridge of Glacial Lake Agassiz. Influenced by groundwater seepage; calcareous soils.

Litter with bare spots(worms?). Typical forest type for upper slopes in the is area. More conifer, Abies and Picea, on flats and north slopes. Scattered large well-decayed Pinus stumps. Deer browse on shrubs. DBH range 19-30cm. No soil probe. MHn44, MHn35, or MHn46.

North slope with small terraces formed by soil slumping. Red clay soils are moist but not wet. 80%+ decayed Pinus stumps scattered throughout vicinity. Picea glauca scattered within community. Picea glauca often >20m tall. No worms. Rock creek valley. A horizon <5cm. Abies DBH range: 12-18cm. Betula papyrifera DBH range: 20-25cm. Litter of needles and deciduous leaves.

Medium sized coarse woody debris in all decay stages scattered common. Old, well-decayed Pinus stumps scattered throughout vicinity. Acer rubrum usually multi-stemmed. A horizon <5cm.
Tree DBH(cm):
Pop tremuloides: 14-30cm
Acer rubrum: 20-28cm
Abies balsamea: 20-28cm

Soils are layered with bands of sandy silt, silty clay and pebbly sand. Lots of deer browse on shrubs. Scattered piles of drift debris. Community 0.5-1.0m above today's water level of river. No litter accumulation, many bare soil spots. Edge of plot within 1-1.5m of water's edge. Litter of drift piles and last year's perennial stands.

50% of plot is exposed sand and/or rock. Long side of plot parallels river. Plot within 1m of river. Area likely to flood during most high water events. Graminoides likely undersampled. Phenologically early. Carex emoriyi lines the bank just outside of plot and slightly below it. Unable to get soil probe any deeper than ~15cm due to rock.

Seepage zone through plot, a common feature of slumpy slopes in the Nemadji River basin. Plot within areas of exposed, bare clay, very dry. Very recent slumps within community. Plot ~10m upslope from river and about 10m above(linear distance). Soil: Red clay.

Community dominates a long and relatively narrow basin between mesic hardwood forest. Purpose of releve was to capture this community type on saturated sand. The community lies on the line between two land type associations. Quite possibly this area was a shoreline of glacial lake superior. Fraxinus nigra scattered in community - especially to the south along the upland boarder. Depth of standing water 0-10cm deep.

Plot within irregularly undulating but overall flat topography. Larger landform with gentle north aspect. This area formed the edge of glacial Lake Superior. Coarse woody debris common in all decay stages. Scattered 75% + decayed Pinus stumps common throughout. Litter in low spots wet but no standing water. A horizon < 7cm. Soil: coarse brown sand. Topographic context: Crest/Upper.

Lower edge of plot within 10m of black ash swamp. Mineral soil, sand, is entirely saturated. Most Tilia multi-stemmed. Slender mature community mode DBH for all canopy species 20-30cm with scattered Populus and Acer sacc ~35cm. Slender Coarse woody debris <20% decayed scattered common. A horizon <5cm. Soil: >40cm saturated silty sand with pebbles.

Plot within 12m of Nemadji River and 5m above today's water level. The community does not appear to flood very regularly - no drift piles. Community occupies a relatively narrow flat terrace - this community type typical on this landform. Worms observed. Upper layer of soil mixed with organic and sand. Sand moist 12-20cm, wet 20cm+. A horizon <12 cm, Silty sand >60cm. Fraxinus nigra: 17-32cm, bimodal 17-22/28-32cm.

Short (4m) wide slope between terrace forest (DNR Releve 3009) and the Nemadj River. Community is variously shaded and exposed to full sun w/no not- iceable change in vegetation.  Typical community in slopes immediately adjacent to the river. Most of slope likely floods annually. Other examples of this community have near continuous (Matteuccia)? and or smilacina stellata. Carex exylis always abundant. Litter: very little to none, herbaceous material. Topographic context: Upper/middle/lower.

Many exposed rocks. Shallow to bedrock soils. Unable to get soil probe any deeper than 15cm before hitting rock/bedrock. Old cut stumps 75% decayed, scattered. A small stream flows through the community to the Moose/Toren River. Coarse woody debris, all decay stages and medium to slender in size common. Average peat depth <10cm. Soil: silty sand.
Tree DBH (cm):
Fraxinus nigra: 22-30
Fraxinus pennsylvanica: 25-30
Tilia americana: 22-28

Plot captures the more open variation of alder swamp within this large swamp. Native plant community occupies much of a large flat terrace between the Nemadji and South Fork Nemadji Rivers. Wetter variations occur with Carex lacustris dominating below. Scattered aspen/spruce islands throughout. Average peat depth <50cm.

Community is large and occupies much of a broad flat plateau between the Nemadji and South Fork Nemadji rivers. Compare with DNR releve R03-13. This plot capture an "alder forest" variation of alder swamp with this larger community. Community is drier and probably approaches wet-mesic. No standing water. Litter of deciduous leaves and graminoids.  Average peat (or humus?) depth: 2cm.

Aspen island within a large alder swamp on a high plateau between the Namadji and South Fork Nemadji Rivers. E5-7 Larix laricina scattered around periphery of island. Small (<1-5 acre) island scattered throughout the alder swamp - some with more Picea and Larix than Populus but most are Populus dominated. Slender coarse woody debris 0-25% decayed occasional. 
Tree DBH (cm):
Picea: 38
Populus: 15-25 (30)

Lower edge of plot within 2m of the South Fork Nemadji River and ~4m above today's water level. Sharp drop to river. Coarse woody debris of all sizes and decay stages common. Notable absence of graminoids. A horizon <10cm. Topographic context: lower/toe.
Tree DBH (cm):
Picea: 20-30
Populus: 15-22

Typical hardwood-conifer forest occupying a broad plateau between the Nemadji abnd South Fork Nemadji Rivers. Overall an even-aged Populus dominated forest with scattered mature Picea glauca, Abies and Pinus species. Lots of deer browse. Slender to medium coarse woody debris <50% decayed scattered common. A horizon <6cm.
Tree DBH (cm):
Populus tremuloides: 13-25
Betula papyrifera: 20
Pinus: 40
Picea: 30-36

Wet-mesic, moderately grazed (regularly pastured). Aspen suckers 2-3m high, fairly common generally, some clumps 4-5m high. A few small bur oak trees. Plot on boundary between well-drained Fram soils (fine sandy loam to clay loam) and poorly drained Percy soils (sandy clay loam to sandy loam).

In part of wildlife management area that is lightly/moderately grazed by cattle. Boulders common at surface. In extensive area predominately brush prairie, scattered small aspen groves. Parts wet. Don't use for classification.
Lightly grazed wet-mesic brush prairie (regularly pastured). Plot in opening in area of greater brush cover. Close to half-section line, but precise position along this not recorded.
Wet-mesic to mesic, based on species composition. Near woodland patch. "Opening" in very brushy area.
Plot in area a bit more open than surrounding, which has more aspen. Scattered small to medium bur oak trees. Area has savanna-like aspect.

Old growth white cedar forest on steep southeast facing slope, with exposed bedrock. Parallels cold air drainage into white cedar swamp. Located on southeast hill slope of bedrock-controlled hardwood hill. No cedar reproduction. Litter of needles with few deciduous leaves. A Horizon: 1.5cm.

Paper birch-sugar maple. Betula papyrifera co-dominant with Acer saccharum. Abundant Acer saccharum in shrub and herb layers. No evidence of cutting. Little microtopography. Worm castings in humus. Evidence of fire in surrounding birch & spruce/fir community.

Old growth lowland white cedar forest in Lake Superior watershed. Downslope of valley between Eagle Mt and Raven Ridge northern hardwoods forest. Cedar with Fraxinus nigra and Populus balsamifera canopy. Abundundant coarse woody debris. No evidence of cutting. Lutsen scientific and natural area. Litter of needles and deciduous leaves.

Lowland white cedar. Headwaters of Onion river. Abundant mucky pools, tip-up mounds, and large coarse woody debris. Surrounded by high quality mesic hardwood forest. DNR designated old growth adjacent. No evidence of cutting. Abundant cedar seedlings and bryophytes, Betula alleghaniensis seedlings/saplings. Litter of needles and deciduous leaves. 
Tree DBH(cm): 
Thuja occidentalis: 20-50 (35)
Betula papyrifera: 30-40

White cedar swamp (175 years-USFS). Basin surrounded by upland with cedar on slopes and mesic northern hardwoods on hills. Swamp edge with Taxus canadensis and good cedar regeneration throughout. Abundant windthrown coarse woody debris. Abundant water-filled hollows. Litter of needles/deciduous leaves.
Small depressional wetland surrounded by successional grasslands & for est. Wetland with well-developed floating sedge mat, broken along edge by past domestic grazing.
Steep eroded bank of the Vermillion River.

Undulating topography on large island in Mississippi River; above most flooding - no flotsam. ~15 feet above river level. Mature trees (30-50 cm), patchy leaf litter - much downed woody debris. Soil: silty alluvium.

npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: Undulating & fluted topography. Gaps in canopy, open understory with patches of shrubs. No obvious signs of flooding; ~10 ft above river. Adjacent low troughs are dominated by Acer saccharinum and more prone to flooding. Bryophytes only on dead wood.

3 arec steep sided basin with very narrow moat. Solid, stable, sphagnum mat across most of area. Carex lacustris more common around margin. Alder scattered uniformly across site. Unusual amount of Calla in Sphagnum uniformly across site. Solid peat basin.
Solid sphagnum mat. Eastern half of wetland dominated by Carex lasiocarpa and sphagnum. Floating mat on margin with no sphagnum around edge. Solid peat within center. Small basin wetland.

No floating mat but gets more so towards center of wetland; 8 inich of water above peat layer. >1 m of peat. Salix scattered in patches throughout; Typha with Phalaris invading center of 50 acre shallow basin between Big Rat and Stawberry Lakes.

Water table below surface; >1m of peat. Releve south of tamarack swamp and along Ottertail River. Along river Typha and Phragmites dominate. Margin of wetland has scattered Salix candida, serrisima, discolor, and salix gracillis. May transition to rich fen. Upland forest border consists of Quercus macrocarpa, Abies balsimifera, Betula papyrifera, and Pinus strobus.
Within ~50 acre wet meadow-calcareous fen-shrub swamp complex on east side cannon river. On saturated peat.

On saturated peat, side slope of mound. Low hummocks throughout. Peat depth >40cm. Plot in 100 square meter opening in bog birch - willow swamp. Cannon river valley, within ~50 acre wet meadow calcareous fen - shrub swamp complex on east side river.

Maturing to mature stand, trees 15-25 (30)cm DBH. Typical of 100+ acres at source of Ted Brook Creek. Few old stumps. Canopy fairly dense. Sphagnum mosses of 40-60% cover, mostly on hummocks. Phalaris is rare in stand.

Mature stand dominated by trees 35-50 cm DBH, occasional to 75cm+. Trees forest grown. Much coarse woody debris, often quite large. Scattered root mounds. Soil a deep, rich, dark, rocky loam. Gradual East-facing slope in rolling terrain on ridge top. Old stumps infrequent. Thick duff layer.

Mature stand. Trees 30-45cm (60cm) DBH; forest-grown. Plot in highest quality part of 160-acre stand on southeast side of Maple Lake. Scattered snags/coarse woody debris. No stumps. Much worm evidence. Barbed-wire in large old tree. Occasional root mounds.

5-acre basin in rolling moraine East of Rice Lake. Plot in central zone that covers 2/3 of basin. Wet slightly quaky peat >30cm deep. Shrubs fairly homogeneous. No old coarse woody debris. Nearly continuous sphagnum. 29 Oct. 2004: J. Janssens- moss data from this "mixed mire".

Typical of open portions (80%) of 10-15 acre meadow and willow swamp complex. Level sandplain, southeast of Little Rock Lake. Peat saturated, >30cm over sand. Plot in center of wetland, 15m from margin. No woody remains. Shallow old ditch 30cm to northwest does little to alter hydrology or vegetation. Slope position: depression/flat.

Mature stand on nearly level sand plain southeast of Little Rock Lake. Trees 30-50cm DBH, larger ones somewhat open-grown. Dark sandy soil, little duff. No stumps. Scattered coarse woody debris. Snags occasional. TNC Preserve for 30+ yrs. 30m from wetland, 1-2 feet above level of that wetland.

Central portion of 30-acre poor fen complex in center of larger wetland complex northwest of Thunder Lake. Plot typical of large zone with stunted Larix. Quaky saturated peat. No stumps. Few snags. Grades to areas of denser and sparser Larix zones. Depth of standing water <1cm. Margins of wetland much richer.

small 1-2 acre seepage fed meadow at base of steep, 35-foot slope along Sauk River at East end of Guernsey Lake. Quaky saturated peat, somewhat raised, with slight slope. No obvious discharged zones. 5+ ft above river which is 50cm away, through Typha wetland. Adjacent upland is cattle pasture separated by barbed wire fence. Adjacent wetland is Typha x glauca and patches of Phalaris. Lots of diffuse seepage meadows and shrub swamps at base of slopes all around this lake.

Maturing to mature stand in rolling St. Croix Moraine northesat of Big Lake. Trees 15-45cm DBH, mode 20-35cm, forest-grown. Very old and decayed stumps occasional coarse woody debris rather sparse. Few snags. Sandy-loam. Slight south slope.

Central portion of 5-acre basin in rolling forested St. Croix Moraine northesat of Big Lake. No moat. Slightly quaky saturated peat >30cm deep. Water 10-15 cm deep in foot tracks. Continuous sphagnum, hummocks low. No woody remains. Scattered small Larix and Betula papyrifera. Grades between Cares lasiocarpa and Carex utriculata as dominant sedge. Surrounded by MHc forests.
Unusual southern poor fen. Center of 5-acre basin in strongly-rolling wooded moraine S of Mound L. Quaky sedge/moss peat > 30cm deep. Grades to Carex lacustris zone. No old stumps. No moat.

Quaky saturated peat 50m from west end of Pine Island Lake. Heterogenous peatland; captures one of most common zones. Continuous sphagnum. Grades to Typha nearer lake; to areas with more alder and scattered Larix toward upland. Topographic context: depression/flat.

Typical of 30 acres of meadow in large wetland complex in broad interdrumlin wetland along Turtle Creek South of mud Lake. Deep, (>40cm) saturated sedge peat. No woody remains. No surface water. Substrate no quaky. Carex stricta in 12 inch hummocks. Plot 50m from upland. Grades to denser Salix. To north is denser Salix than typha and Phragmites near mud lake. Substrate becomes somewhat quaky North of Salix zone. Some Salix candida in Salix zone.

Typical of 20 acres of tall alder on margin of large interdrumlin wetland along Turtle Creek, south of Mud Lake. Broad zone ~100m wide. Saturated peat >30cm deep, slightly quaky. No evidence of trees in past. Grades to sedge meadow.

Typical of mature 5-acre patch in heterogenous stand on Mississippi River floodplain. Soil varies from silt to sand. Flood debris piles and worms present. Grades to terrace forest, Quercus mac/Tilia 3ft higher elevation. No stumps/no snags.

Mature stand in rather strongly-rolling St. Croix Moraine on West side of Spring Branch Creek. Trees 20-50+ cm DBH. Snags occasional. Coarse woody debris sparse. No stumps. Soil is cobbly sandy-loam, occasional boulders. Fairly level area atop small ridge.

place_name: Spring Br- L Beauty Bible Camp
remarks: Typical of sedge meadow which covers 1/4 mile wide x 1 mile long stretch of Spring Branch West of Lake Beauty. Plot 25m from upland, 50m from creek. Hummocks 30-40cm tall. Saturated sedge peat >30cm. No surface water. No woody remains.

place_name: Spring Br- L Beauty Bible Camp
remarks: Small "bay" of long, narrow wetland complex along Spring Branch Creek West of Lake Beauty. Center of wetland, typical of 5-10 acres before grading to Carex stricta dominated. Grades to Carex stricta. Quaky, saturated peat with shallow water in footprints. No Phalaris, nice upland ecotone.

Typical of better quality half of 25-acre swamp in gently-rolling terrain at edge of Clarissa Drumlin Field, southeas of Pendergast Lake. Trees 10-25cm DBH, few snags. Slightly quaky saturated peat >30cm deep. No stumps, very sparse coarse woody debris. Sphagnum continuous. Hummocks to 30cm high. Topographic context: depression/flat.

Center of half-acre basin on gently-rolling forested drumlin east of Pendergast Lake. Surrounded by mesic hardwoods. Water in plot is 6-12" deep. Feet sink 12" or more into muck. Phalaris very limited on margin, small patch.

Hummocky, gently-sloping wetland with diffuse seepage on broad terrace below 170-foot bluffs along the Cannon River. Plot 20m from upland margin. Saturated, spongy peat >40cm deep. Pooled water in footprints. Seepage rivulet in plot.

Mature (60-80 year old) stand on level drumlin top along an unnamed tributary of Moran Creek. Trees even-aged and often multi-stemmed, 20-35cm DBH. Scattered coarse woody debris. Old 1/2 decayed stumps occasional. A few snags. Rocky sandy-loam. Nice structure.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: 30-50m wide band of wet-mesic forest along trubutary to Moran Creek which cuts through broad dumlin in Clarissa Drumlin Field. Trees 20-35cm DBH, Populus to 40cm. No stumps, scattered snags, coarse wood debris sparse. Loamy soil, slight undulating substrate. Lightly past-grazed. Releve done during and after heavy rain downpour.

Central portion of 5-acre depression in forested, rolling St. Croix moraine East of Rogers Lake. Quaky saturated peat (moss and sedge) >30cm deep. Beaver moat around margin. Grades to shrub dominated margin, to areas dominated by Carex lasiocarpa. Sphagnum continuous. Vegetation is low statured. Water 4 inches deep in foot tracks. Hummocks very low.

Mature dry-mesic stand on lower portion of 80 foot knoll in forested St. Croix moraine East of Rogers Lake. Heterogenous age distribution, some large trees 45-60 DBH, many 25-35cm trees. Sandy loam. No stumps. Snags occasional. Coarse woody debris sparse. Little worm evidence.

5-acre zone on northeast arm of large basin containing Cranberry Lake. Grades to Calamagrostis canadensis toward upland margin, to dense Typha toward lake. Plot 30m from upland, 50m from Typha. Slightly spongy moist peat, no old woody remains.

Central part of 3-acre depression in rolling wooded terrain northeast of Sagatagan Lake. Very quaky mat makes a heterogenous central 2/3 of wetland, mat sinks 30cm to muck bottom. Plot captures two ill defined and poorly separated zones which intergrade. Succeeding to poor fen?

Typical of 80+ acres in extensive meadow/marsh complex along Long Prairie River North of Lake Osakis. Substrate moderately spongy peat saturated >100cm deep over sand. Forbs strangely sparse. Plot 1/4 mile south of River and 1/8 mile east of County Road 1. Flooded in spring. Water levels at near record lows. Topographic context: depression/flat.

20 acre Calamagrostis canadensis meadow in extensive meadow and marsh complex along Long Praire Ruver. Plot 30m from river (near record low flow). Calamagrostis forms 40cm hummocks in area - flooded much of summer. Peat saturated >30cm. Grades inland to Phragmites.

Typical of broad expanse of Calamagrostis canadensis in extensive wetland complex along Long Prairie River southeast of Dempsey Lake. 75m southeast of Releve 3352. Moderately spongy saturated sedge peat >30cm deep. Grades to narrow zones dominated by Carex lacustris.

Typical of somewhat limited zone(5 acres) in extensive meadow and marsh complex along Long Prairie Road SE of Dempsey Lake, 75m from lake, 75 m from Releve 3351. Quaky sedge peat, water 10cm deep in footprints. No woody remains. 25m from Phragmites/Typha. Topographic context: Depression/Flat.

Mature stand on outwash sand along Long Prairie River north of Turtle Creek. Coarse sand with 2cm duff layer. Trees forest-grown, oaks 20-40cm DBH. No stumps, coarse woody debris sparse, snags occasional.

Typical of 80 ac. of fen on West side of Dempsey Lake in large wetland complex along Long Prairie River. Grades to Calamagrostis canadensis east of lake near river. Quaky saturated peat 120cm deep over marly clay. Plot 75m from upland margin. Shrub encroaching. Mammal trap grid here. Topographic context: depression/flat. Depth of standing water <1cm.

Small, heterogenous remnant in 1850's cemetery along Co Rd 16 northeast of Browerville. Surrounded by cropland. Approximately one acre, never plowed. Gradual west-face slope just above outwash plain along Long Prairie River. Dary sandy-loam. Threat from ongoing "revival" of cemetery use.

place_name: Long Prairie R- Long Prairie N
remarks: Annually flooded mud flat along Long Prairie River in river bend at small backwater slough. Moist silt >30cm deep. Mud flat is 35cm above river today-near record low river stage. Feet sink 3-6cm in mud.

place_name: Long Prairie R- Long Prairie N
remarks: 15m x 40m zone in low area draining into backwater slough in extensive wetland complex along Long Prairie River. Saturated peat over outwash sand. Plot 50m from river, 20m from slough. Surrounded by Calamagrostis canadensis meadow. Topographic context: depression/flat.

Typical of ~80 acres in extensive wetland complex along the Long Prairie River. Moderately quaky peat >40cm deep. Grades to denser Calamagrostis canadensis meadow toward river (150m to West). Plot is 75m from upland. More fen-like than most of wetlands along river. Topographic context: depression/flat.

Middle and upper slope, moderately steep, north northwest-facing 40 foot slope. Part of 100+ acres, typical of much of stand. Lower slopes fir replaces pines. Much coarse woody debris-mostly dead fir abd jack pine (budworm). Scattered old conifer stumps, fire scars. Trees 15-38cm DBH. Thick moss carpet. FDn33a1.

Small marsh surrounded by wet meadow. Depression with ~8in of water over mucky soil. Vegetation patchy with areas of open water containing Lemna. Wet meadow has water at surface and is surrounded by old field.

Soil is mucky peat at top two inches, very sapric. Mostly moist/saturated muck soil. Part of a larger wetland adjacent to Rice Lake. Not a floating mat. Not a basin, only slight depression, poorly drained area. Releve approximately 35 feet from road.

Small, slightly depressional wet meadow, dominated by patches of swales of Carex lacustris and Carex rostrata. No floating mat. Soil of sedge peat/muck >1 meter, very fibric. Water level at or below soil surface - saturated.

Nice wet meadow, possibly in transition to rich fen? No floating mat. Water level at surface. Soil is fibric spongy peat/sedge peat. Only small patches of isolated Phragmites; Calamagrostis dominating and creating hummocky terrain.

Narrow wet meadow opening, in maple/basswood forest. Water level at surface. No floating mat. Mucky saturated soil. Depression of continuous Calamagrostis, with much Petasites sagittatus. Releve representative of whole wetland.
Trees are all straight trunked. area of rolling hills, sometimes steep. No current disturbance in this area. Canopy trees also single trunked.

Rolling hills, gentle slopes. All trees have straight trunks, none are open grown. No sign of recent disturb, most trees are single trunked. Canopy trees are 30-40cm DBH with a few maples up to 50cm DBH. Several old tip-up mounds in the releve.

Releve in center of fen which is in a depression surrounded by upland maple/basswood forest on sandy soil. Hummokcy sphagnum with a few non sphagnum marshes. Inner zone of fen is covered with Chamaedaphne. Outer zone has no Chamaedaphne but continuous Carex lacustris. Scattered paper birch in the west end end of the fen where Chamadaephane is less common and Carex lasiocarpa becomes more common. Peat deeper than probe.

Solid floating mat of sphagnum in shallow basin surrounded by upland forest. No outlet. Some beaver activity. Outer zone of Care lacustris inner zone with extensive Vaccinium macrocarpon. Releve in middle of site. Scattered Betula papyrifera across mat. Very narrow moat. No reed canary growing.

Releve in middle of basin that is shallow and surrounded by gently sloping upland forest. Typha scattered across entire area. Outer zone with abundant Carex lacustris, middle zone has less Carex lacustris and more Carex lasiocarpa. Middle zone appears to have solid peat mat, not floating; outer zone is an unstable floating mat of sedges.

Releve in middle of floating sphagnum mat. Narrow moat around edge. Out zone has more Carex lacustris, middle zone still has Carex lacustris but Carex lasiocarpa is more abundant. Thelypteris palustris abundant across entire mat. Scattered willows, some betula glad - very few. Gently slopes to upland mesic forest.  Wetland is ~7 acres.

Water in releve about 12" deep-becoming deeper towards center of site. Outer zone is all similar to releve; middle area is open water. Total area about 1 acre. Surrounded by ring of Salix in old field.

Large area in old outwash channel surrounded by narrow tamarack swamp, then upland forest. Mostly open but some are clumps of Betula glandulifera and scattered Larix larcina. Floating mat of vegetation.

Large tamarack swamp in very shallow depression. Tamarack mostly 10-20cm DBH. Very well developed hummock and hollow ground formation. No sign of any recent disturbance. Beautiful pillows of sphagnum moss.

Site within a ~160 acres of forest within a moraine west of Otter tail Lake (mostly with undeveloped shorelines). Site includes scattered wetlands. Trees mostly straight single boles. In plot down debris <5%, wind damage. Site has some past logging, but very little recent activity. Some RV trails. Paper birch very old. Range of canopy tree DBH is 30-55cm.
Very shallow basin only a few feet lower than surrounding maple/basswood forest. No floating mat. Water table below ground level. South of this area, Salix becomes more common south of the releve.

50 feet walked in from road. Low, shallow 20 acre wetland, west (and at base) of seven sisters kame. Scattered shrubs, patches of Typha invading. No floating mat. Water table at ground level. 60cm of peat on top of sandy muck - soil probe couldn't reach any clay layer. Topographic context: depression/flat.

Inner zone of 3 acre basin surrounded by upland bur oak/pin oak forest on sand. Floating mat of Sphagnum, stable and firm. This releve is in the middle of the wetland. Outer zone has no sphagnum but is still on a floating mat and has more Carex lacustris.
Outer zone of small basin (ca.3 acres) surrounded by upland bur oak/pin oak forest on floating sedge mat with some non-sphagnum moss. Middle zone is a poor fen with solid sphagnum mat.

Standing water is around 6" above the surface. Solid cover; mostly Spargnium eurycarpum across the entire marsh in low area flanked by grazed pasture. Cattle has access to the marsh but don't appear to go in there.

At west end of large shallow basin which merges into cattail marsh to the east. Tamarack swamp has pasture on the west, north and south sides. Tamaracks are small (10-20cm DBH). Apparently undisturbed, no sign of any recent logging. Nice hummock/hollow formation in the ground layer.

Small ~10 acre tamarack swamp depression. Moat around margin merging to loose sphagnum floating mat and becoming stable at center where Larix is. Ground cover dominated by Sphagnum and Vaccinium macrocarpon. No hummucks. Larix is approximately 35 feet high with average DBH of 10-20cm.

Gently rolling topography. Large exposed boulders. Occasional ephemeral wetlands nearby. No cut stumps seen. Moderate coarse woody debris. Acer saccharum look old and possibly maple sugared. Average tree DBH: Paper birch 40-50cm, Tilia 50-60cm, Quercus 50-55cm. Many Ulmus seedling, Ulmus thomasii scattered elsewhere in forest.

Very nice mixed hard-conifer swamp zone, running east-west along north side of Fittle Flat Lake. Upland border of lowland hardwoods - Tilia, Fraxinus nigra, Abies balsimifera Betula papyrifera. and Quercus macrocarpa. The releve probably captures a fraction of upland transition zone. Shallow hummocks.

Hummocks 2-3 feet high standing water in low areas. Releve done in area where Larix and Picea are, outside of this is open rich fen with upland islands of lowland hardwoods. Entire wetland is ~40-50 acres where there are other patches of Larix and Picea.

Soil sandy loam. Canopy very dense coverage. Occasional stumps. Little coarse woody debris. Red oaks (50-65 DBH). Fair amount of leaf litter. Hilly topography on White Earth moraine. Red oaks seem even aged. Currently used by ATVs. Many Acer seedlings.

Solid sphagnum mat. Releve in center of wetland where dominated by Ledum and Chameadaphne with Larix. Quickly changes toward outer rim to less ericads and more herbs such as Petasites sagittatus with denser Alnus incana and no Larix, but still with solid sphagnum.

Sphagnum hummocks one foot high - only slightly filled with water in hollows. Rich fen surrounds tamarack swamp (entire wetland ~50ac). Rich fen dominated heavily by Menyanthes and Carex lasiocarpa on floating sphagnum mat with open water channels. Dense alder swamp surrounds fen. Wetland on border or Flat Lake.
Poor fend basin on floating sphagnum mat. Surrounded by upland clearcut and newly regenerate aspen. Dominated by Chamaedaphne. Topographic context: depression/flat.

Centrally located in 5-acre+ basin in strongly rolling forested moraine between Big and Little Birch Lakes. Substrate is quaky peat 3.5m deep. Basin somewhat heterogenous - plot in "poorest" (or most acidic) portion. Jan Janssens moss transect data here also. 
pH=5.7, cond=26.1 uScm, absorb=0.32. (with Janssens & Aaseng)

Center of north end of 5-acre basin (poorest area) in rugged forested moraine between Big and Little Birch Lakes. Wet quaky peat 600cm deep. Near 7593. pH=5.2, K=23.8, abs=0.232. (with Janssens and Aaseng).
Black spruce bog with open poor fen water track to the west and rich fen to the east. Picea mariana averages 10-15 cm DBH in canopy. Does not appear raised on the aerial photo.

Band of rich fen dominated by Carex lasiocarpa and Equisetum fluviatile with very little sphagnum between black spruce bog (west) and a tamarack swamp (east) transitioning to upland. Typha becomes more abundant toward the tamarack swamp (east). Some graminoid litter.

Alder swamp averaging 2.5m tall, composed mostly of shade-tolerant wet meadow species. Surrounded by aspen forest. Soil is saturated to the surface. Pools form in my footsteps. Average peat depth >50cm. Some graminoid litter.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Black ash swamp surrounded by aspen-dominated MHn35, DBH of largest trees ~30cm. Most pools have no standing water; saturated. Has many species characteristics of WFn55a, but the canopy is not dominated by Populus balsamifera.

Short-statured alder swamp with little graminoid cover and a few short (but not stunted) conifers. Conifer swamps are in most directions (cedar and black spruce). No standing water. Sparse graminoid and alder litter.

Open black spruce-tamarack poor swamp. DBH 10-20cm. Hollows filled with sphagnum. pH 4.4. Has Gaultheria, Osmunda, and Maianthemum, which suggests APn81a, but also has Andromeda, Kalmia, Betula pumila, Chaemadaphne, and Carex pauciflora, which suggest APn81b.
Open canopy cedar swamp, DBH average 25-30cm, nearby openings are alder swamp. pH 5.8. A big old (pine?) stump. A horizon depth: 3cm. Litter of cedar needles and graminoids.
Tamarack swamp with cedar and black spruce. Nearly closed canopy. Hollows filled with non-sphagnum moss. pH 6.0, which suggests FPn82a, but species diversity is high, which suggests FPn82b.
Even aged (DBH 10-15cm) closed canopy, black spruce with a sphagnum carpet. Most pools are dry. Releve straddles entire width of polygon. Compare to releve 3471 in larger, higher-quality stand.

Some pools of water. No sphagnum. A few long-dead tree snags (short). Floating mat rich fen at edge of outflow of Mud Lake with white water lily, Sagittaria species, Potamogeton species, and etc. In other direction is fire-dependent upland. Toward upland there is greater cover of Chamaedaphne. Graminoid litter.
Open canopy black spruce bog with just under 50% canopy. DBH 10-15 cm. Situated between uplands and open peatland.

Black spruce-tamarack swamp between uplands and Mud Creek. Some pools have sphagnum; some don't, but none have standing water. DHB average 15-20cm. I couple old cut stumps, but stand does not seem disturbed. No water, even by stepping in pools.

Upland cedar forest (DBH averages 30-40 cm, max 50cm) between wet cedar forest and fire dependent upland. This patch is not much bigger than the releve plot. There are a couple old stumps that look like pine. Hit rocks with soil probe at 17cm.

Mixed ash-cedar swamp. Some pools have a bit of standing water, but most are dry. Average DBH for both ash and cedar is 30cm. Upland white cedar forest on both sides. Hit something hard with soil probe at 18cm. Sparse graminoid litter.
No pools of water; but soil is saturated. Closed canopy alder swamp ~2-2.5 m tall. Surrounded by fire dependent uplands.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Open canopy black ash at headwaters of creek tributary. Some pools have water in them, due possibly only to recent rain. Abies average 20-30 cm DBH (max 40). Many ashes have dead branches in their crowns. Aster umbellatus, Thalictrum dasycarpum, and Galium asprellum suggest WFn55 type "a." Sparse graminoid litter.

Mixed conifer deciduous with elements of both mesic hardwoods and fire-dependent forest. No evidence of earthworms. Avgerage DBH ~30cm. Large Picea glauca is ~50cm DBH. Several old, pine stumps outside plot. Some Acer saccharum nearby. Litter of leaves and needles.

Open bog with some 3-5cm DBH spruce snags. To north vegetation is similar but with ~20% cover by small black spruce (no Carex oligosperma; more Smilacina. Could fire have made this bog open? There are some logs under sphagnum. Sparse graminoid litter.

Meadow/fen with Sphagnum carpet and moat, surrounded by aspen forest. No water at the surface, but appears to be a floating mat. pH is 4.9. Soil probe brings up nothing but water, air, and Sphagnum. Sparse graminoid litter.

Cedar swamp/peatland surrounded by uplands, including esker. Pools have some water from last night's rain. Stream flows through this stand, but not near this releve. Average DBH 30-40cm, probably old-growth. At edge of esker is similar vegetation with tree canopy of black spruce and tamarack.

Upland peninsulas just above surrounding spruce bog, much lower than adjacent esker. Closed canopy, even-aged black spruce forest. Low spots have wetland vegetation, but mostly dry-mesic species. Stumps with fire scars. Average stand DBH is 20-25cm. Red pines are 35cm DBH with no fire scars. Stand is only slightly larger than plot.

More or less closed canopy black ash forest on floodplain terrace above St. Louis River. Damp spots in depressions but most without surface water Average DBH is 30cm (max 45). Terrace about 1.5m above river level. An intermittent brook runs through the plot.

Silver maple dominated forest along St. Louis River. Large depression (channel) through plot with a bit of standing water. Multi-stemmed maples; each stem average 30cm (max 50cm). Only small patch dominated by silver maples.

Native plant community on a broad relatively flat area 1/2 mile north of Mud Creek. Charcoal common in the upper 5cm of soil. Canopy pines often with dead lower branches with somewhat open grown appearance. Small and medium coarse woody debris common. 80% decayed stumps scattered. soil: silt with some pebbles and charcoal less than 10cm, boulders or bedrock at 10cm. Litter: 85% needles, 15% leaves.
Tree DBH (cm):
Pinus: 30-45
Populus: 25-30

pH=7.4. Native plant community occupies a ~100m linear corridor between forested uplands. Native plant community connected to a wet meadow bordering the west branch Knife River. No signs of disturbance. E6-6 Picea mariana scattered throughout native plant community. Adjacent uplands FDn43b1. Rossinni road ~200m west - gravel forest road. Soil: mucky sedge peat > 100cm.

Community within a water track, this area of the track less soupy and with no visible flowing water. Surface water visible within 100m to the northeast. Native plant community bordered by spruce bog and within a large acid peatland. No standing water in plot, food prints fill with water. Typha latifolia and Alnus incana >2m outside of plot, neither common in native plant community. Sparse graminoid litter.

Native plant community shrubby and forest-like, patchy areas intermingling between Thuja stands and shrubby-sapling areas. Native plant community ~100m south of the West Branch Knife River and at same elevation as its floodplain. pH=7.7. Overall community has characteristics of WFn64a and WFn53a. Sparse Thuja and graminoid litter.

Observed a small worm at humus/mineral soil interface. Fire scars on oldest coarse woody debris. Coarse woody debris common all sizes and age classes. Local area recently logged. Stand adjacent to Pine Creek with document wood turtles. Native plant community area of steep, rolling topography (esker). Deer browse and trails common. Litter of needles and leaves. Soil: Silty sand. A horizon depth: 1cm. Topographic context: upper/middle/lower.
Top of steep slope adjoining Dutch Charley Creek.
Very depauperate but solid herb layer in May. Same location as releve # 3604.
Releve in concave area of slope above terrace of tributary ravine of DesMoines. This stand shows as forest on 1938 photography. Topographic context: middle/lower.

Forest with much Abies balsimifera. just south of Rice Lake, moderate amount of coarse woody debris. Quite a bit of prickly ash in area. Forest surrounded by even denser amounts of Abies and black ash swamp. Soil is sandy loam. Lots of elm seedling.

SE facing ~25 degree slope above Elbow Lake. Soil sandy loam. Fire scars on some trees. Releve done in an opening typical along mid-upper slope. Red pine average ~50cm dbh, Jack pine ~30 DBH. No evidence of cutting, but probably will be soon, paint on many tree and already cut to northeast. Native plant community FDc24 or 23.

Fairly open jackpine woodland on dry sandy soil. Woodland is on a small circular "island" ~40ac surrounded by tamarack and black spruce swamp and Indian Creek to east. Releve on west facing slope. Top of hill and east slope dominated by more Pinus resinosa. No evidence of recent cuts. Average Pinus Resinosa DBH: 40cm, Pinus banksiana DBH: 35cm.

Mesic forest just east of Big Rat Lake. Topography mostly level-slightly rolling. Soil loamy sand/sandy loam. Occasional cut stumps. Dense Oryzopsis. No Acer saccharum(?). Seems to have some earthworm action, since closer to lake. Well to moderately well drained. Has a strange disturbed feel to it, but not a typical forest canopy and ground layer species for area. Lowland conifer swamps on all other sides (north, east, and south).

Spongy-quaky mat along Ottertail River. Water depth ~18 in above peat(peat depth >1 ft). Releve ~35m in from river. Local areas of Typha angustifolia and Phalaris along mat edge where it meets river. Unusual high water year.

Rich black spruce dominated swamp within larger tamarack dominated swamp along east side of Indian Creek. Fairly even hummocks. No deep hollows. Mucky peat >6 inches deep. Continuous sphagnum and other bryophytes except for areas under clusters of black spruce. Small black spruce DBH: ~10-20cm. Past cutting in tamarack swamp to the south. No stumps seen in releve area. 15 Malaxis paludosa found in releve plot.

Low hummocks with many upland species on dry bases of Picea. Many downed trees and tip-ups with canopy gaps. Shallow hollows with saturated muck. Sphagnum typically only on tip-up mounds in sunny areas. Low lying basin near Egg River. Patchy canopy.

Small basin spongy mat, not floating, dense sphagnum. Somewhat dry on tops of high hummocks. Supports scattered (dead & alive) Pinus banksiana. Upland of Jack/Red pine with Betula papyrifera. High sphagnum hummocks - hollows with dense Scheuchzerena. Topographic context: depression/flat.

Floating mat surrounding Cranberry Lake. Very high, dense sphagnum hummocks (2-3 feet) with water filled hollows. Scattered stunted tamaracks. Uplands of red and jack pine plus lots of recent logging close to edge of wetland.

Fairly dense, even aged (young?) black spruce forest. little to no understory. Small (~2/3 ac) path of black spruce in middle of two other small patches ~35m apart alongside Indian Creek. Upland to west in jack and red pine. Very uniform hummocks, hollows with 2.5cm of standing water. Soil is sparic peaty muck >15cm. Average black spruce DBH ~8-15cm. 7 Malaxis paludose found and 2 more in black spruce "patch" just to the northeast.
Between Balsam & Tamarack lakes. Small opening of water in center. Inner zone of swamp w/more fen qualities(where releve was done). Outer zone distinctly wet meadow-shrub swamp w/more dense A.incana

Very large, undisturbed(?) tamarack swamp (~400 acres). Jack and red pine uplands. Fairly even hummocks, patchy Sphagnum. Hollows with standing water. No disturbance seen, except for a few trails throughout. Mature conifer swamp.

Typical of 2-acre zone in center of 4-acre basin in rolling moraine north of Schafer Lake. Outer zone meadow-like. No moat. Quaky saturated peat. Larix is 2-8m tall, to 10cm DBH. 4 miles north northwest of Grey Eagle.

Rather dense canopy, trees somewhat immature. Very old stumps occasional, moss-covered, indistinct. Peat >30cm, typical hummocky, no standing water. Large wetland complex forms headwaters of Straight River. Rolling sandy uplands. Thuja occidentalis rather localized in several areas including where releve plot situated.

Typical of ~5-acre opening in 100-acre tamarack swamp northeast of One Acre Lake. Large wetland complex in rolling to rugged moraine complex (eskers nearby). Natural opening divided by narrow band of shrubs, grades outward to mature Larix swamp. Quaky sedge peat >40cm. No stumps.

Typical of mature portions of large tamarack swamp in extensive wetland complex southeast of Big Rush Lake. Uplands sandy outwash. Peat substrate, typical hummocks and hollows. Trees 15-35cm DBH. Few canopy gaps. Snags rare. No stumps. Sangs rare. Little coarse woody debris. Shallow water in hollows. "Hummocks" typically around tree bases.
Mature stand in gently rolling terrain east of Big Rush Lake. Canopy pines to 55cm DBH. Occasional jack pine snags. Frequent coarse woody debris. Fire scar present on old stump. Soil a sandy-clay?

Mature stand typical of 100+ acres in extensive wetland complex adjacent to Big Rush Lake. Larix 15-30cm DBH, Picea mariana to 10cm. Few old stumps or snags. Coarse woody debris sparse. Substrate typical hummock and hollow (shallow water). Mosses variously Sphagnum and Bryales.

Mature stand, typical of 20 acres on peninsula surrounded by rich shrub fen in large bend of creek. Trees 15-38cm DBH. Few snags or old stumps. Little coarse woody debris. Appears semi-terrestrial in places. Two Inlets moraine. Mix of Sphagnum and feathermoss carpets.

Mature, best portion of 80-acre stand. Strongly rolling moraine. Trees forest-grown, 30-50cm DBH. Scattered old stumps in places. Coarse woody debris sparse. Few snags. Ample earthworm evidence. Rocky sandy-loam.

Typical of highest quality patches of extensive tract on fairly rugged moraine east of Collet Lake. Mature stand (old-growth locally?), trees 30- 60cm DBH (mode 40-60cm). Scattered snags. coarse woody debris sparse. No stumps. Brown sandy-loam with dark 5cm humus layer. Earthworms sparse/absent. Old growth here?

Mature stand here (converted to plantation nearby). Trees 20-40cm DBH. Snags occasional. No stumps. Coarse woody debris rather sparse. Tan outwash sand. Typical of natural portions of 160-acre Blueberry River oxbow island. Little Long Lake nearby. A horizon depth: <5cm.

Typical of broad graminoid wetland zone (30m wide) on NW shore of Greenwater Lake. Plot 15m from water's edge. Substrate saturated, shallow water in places, 8cm muck over marly sedge peat containing numerous snail shells, shrub denser further from lake. Topographic context: depression/flat.

10-acres of old-growth on rolling moraine on southwest side of Greenwater Lake. Pines 45-70cm DBH, Populus to 50cm. Well-drained gravelly sand. A horizon (organic layer) depth: 3cm. Moderate duff. Few earthworms. Few old stumps. Occasional snags. Frequent coarse woody debris, often large. Fire scars present. Few old stumps. Grades to MHc37.

Center of typical homogeneous 5-acre basin in rolling forested terrain south of Greenwater Lake. Appears to be beaver-created but few disturbance indicators. Mucky substrate, water <35cm deep. Old woody remains on margins. No Phalaris.

Typical of large central zone in 40 acres of heterogeneous acid peatland. Rolling moraine between Big Basswood & Kansas Lakes. Saturated peat > 40cm deep. Continuous Sphagnum. Few snags. No stumps. Trees 1-10cm DBH. Saturated peat >40cm deep. Hummocks rise 6-12cm. Grades to zones of dense spruce. Grades outward to areas dominated by Carex lasiocarpa with frequent snags.

place_name: Bass Lk E- Little Scenic Trail
remarks: Typical of large central zone of somewhat heterogeneous poor fen in 50-acre basin in forested moraine east of Bass Lake. Quaky saturated peat > 40cm. Water is 15-25cm deep in foot tracks. No stumps or coarse woody debris. Grades to zones with more Larix. Outer zone Carex utriculata and Glyceria canadensis. Surrounding upland is young forest. Topographic context: depression/flat.

Typical of 5-acre zone in central part of 30-acre basin in rolling forested moraine south of Missouri Lake. Surrounded in basin by poor conifer swamp (APn81). Moderately quaky saturated peat. No stumps or coarse woody debris. Natural "opening." Water 8-12cm deep in foot tracks. "Poorest" wetland seen in Becker county to date.

Mature stand, 60-90 years old. Trees bimodal, Quercus macrocarpa 40-50cm DBH, forest grown; others 20-40cm. Gentle slope of narrow upland finger in wetland complex northeast of Big Rush Lake. Dark sandy-loam with thick duff layer. No worms.  Stumps, snags, and coarse woody debris sparse. Numerous old tip-up (root) mounds. Old trail (logging?) near plot. A horizon depth: 5cm.

Typical of 100+ acres on mile-long upland finger surrounded by wetlands on moraine southwest of Dinner Lake. Coarse-textured sand with small cobbles, thick moss carpets, shallow needle duff. No stumps, occasional snags. Pinus banksiana 20-30cm DBH, Pinus resinosa 15-40cm DBH. ORV trail atop "ridge."

Mature stand, typical of large wetland complex in rolling sandy moraine west of Dinner Lake. Larix to 32cm DBH, Picea mariana to 20cm DBH. Saturated peat with low hummocks and hollows. Few snags or old stumps. Scattered coarse woody debris, minor windthrow.

Typical of better quality parts of 40-acre stand in wetland complex in rolling moraine southwest of Two Inlets Lake. Maturing/mature stand. Occasional very old stumps. Scattered coarse woody debris. Few snags. Substrate peat, moderately hummocky. Hummocks generally moss covered.

Mature stand, typical of large patches on rolling moraine east of Juggler Lake. Trees 25-40cm DBH. Frequent coarse woody debris (aspen windthrow). No stumps. Few snags. Silty- -loam, one surface boulder. Part of hi-volume aspen stand on County land.

Center of 10-acre basin, forested moraine east of Juggler Lake. Quaky sedge/moss peat. Scattered stunted snags. Water 15cm deep in foot tracks. Outer zones Carex lasiocarpa or lacustris/utriculata. Narrow beaver moat.

Typical of 25 acres at north end of Straight Lake. Old fire-scarred stumps frequent; these apparently axe-hewn. Trees 20-30cm DBH, occasional to 40cm. Even-aged. Snags rare. Moderate coarse woody debris. Maturing. Sandy soil. FDn33?

High quality mature stand in rugged moraine south of Juggler Lake. Trees 30-50cm DBH. Good structure. No stumps. Frequent coarse woody debris, occasional surface boulders. Upper east-facing slope terrain undulating in plot. Worms rare/absent. Gray sandy-loam, thick humus layer. Old growth? Tree tip-up (root) mounds frequent. Topographic context: upper/middle.

Mature stand atop morainal ridge northeast of Ice Cracking Lake. Upper slope of 50-foot east facing. Lone pine 76cm DBH, Quercus rubra 35-52cm DBH, Betula papyrifera 27-58cm DBH, Acer saccharum 22-40cm DBH. Sandy loam, thick humus, few/no worms. A few very old pine stumps nearby. Large snags. Moderate coarse woody debris. Old growth?

Typical of denser-canopied parts of 50-acre stand in forested moraine south of Camp Seven Lake. Trees 15-25cm DBH. Sphagnum covers 85% of ground. No stumps, sparse coarse woody debris, few snags. Substrate typical tree base hummocks and moist hollows.

Mature stand on rolling moraine east of Many Point Lake. Trees 35-55cm DBH. Snags occasional, no stumps. Moderate coarse woody debris, lots larger pieces. Substrate with root mound microtopography. No/few worms. Litter layer intact. Some 1995 blowdown. Recent selective logging on county tax forfeit land to East.
Open area in center of large peatland basin (approx 40 acres). Stunted black spruce and tamarack scattered around. Outer ring of the basin has dense, taller tamarack and spruce. Litter of sphagnum.
In center of 5-acre basin surrounded by upland forest. Narrow moat around floating sphagnum mat. Scattered dead tamarack across mat. Mat is stable, but not particularly solid.
Jack pine are tall and straight-trunked with average DBH of around 30cm. Small stand, surrounded by regenerating Aspen. Litter of jack pine needles.
Pines are straight-trunked. No current disturbance. Medium size Pinus resinosa. (DBH 39cm, 42cm, 40cm). Litter of red pine needles.
On floating sphagnum mat on edge of small lake, closer to lake. The black spruce are more scattered and shorter. Nice hummocks of sphagnum.
Fire scars on some of the tree trunks and down timber. Canopy trees are straight-trunked with only a few twiggy side branches. Litter of oak leaves and red pine needles.
Area has recently been burnt. Trees are straight-trunked.
Old-growth forest. Lot of down, well-rotted logs in the area and tip-up mounds. Trees are straight-trunked.
Middle part of solid sphagnum mat. No Larix laricina or Picea mariana on outer zone of mat, other species are same. No moat, but zone Carex stricta, Calamagrostis canadensis. No outlet or inlet seen.
Canopy trees are often multiple trunked. All are straight trunked. Rolling topography with gentle slopes.
Jack pine present in other parts of the site. Trees are straight-trunked. Canopy trees are medium size (30-40cm dbh). Litter of red pine needles.
Floating sphagnum mat around edge of small lake, releve is about 10 meters from lake.

Approx 5-acre wetland with solid sphagnum mat, narrow moat. Vaccinium oxycoccos common in other parts of site. No apparent inlet or outlet. Aspen regeneration in surrounding upland. Gentle slope down to wetland basin.
Zone within a larger wetland basin. Rest of area has more abundant Carex lacustris and less Carex lasiocarpa.
Middle zone in larger wetland basin. Surrounding area is OPn92. Community in releve covers approximately 15 acres. Larger basin is around 100 acres and surrounds a small lake.

In middle of larger basin (approx 5 acres). Outer part of mat has abundant Carex lacustris, Alnus incana and scattered Larix laricina. Both red and green sphagnum mat solid. No apparent inlet or outlet. No moat.
Middle to upper slope, not extending to level top. Topographic context: upper/middle.

Releve concentrates on upper and near east facing slope. Distinct line of old field-like vegetation with abundant Solidago on northwest side of crest and downslope on west facing side. Too late in season for native community classification.
Waypoint 201. Probably incomplete releve because surveyor was sick while doing it. Topographic Context: upper to middle. Buckthorn at waypoint 202.
Waypoint 159. This releve is late in season and unlikely to reflect full flora of plot. Lateness of season made it difficult to estimate cover/abundance. Topographic Context, upper to middle.
North end of a long spur overlooking lake with 4 rafts of pelicans.
Lower third southwest-facing slope. Good quality- "A". Field notes say "phenomenal".
Despite the fact that this releve is higher quality than the rest of the knoll, it is still only about CD-rank. Topographic context, middle to lower.

Owner has sprayed all thistles, most of which appear to be robust Carex flodmani. Milkweed also appears sprayed, Melilotus is set back. Echinacea is marked. Tract used for seed production. Prairie treated with grass suppressant.
Plot chosen to represent NPC in LTA. Conifer-rich, espec on N & E- facing slopes incl P. strobus & Thuja elsewhere. Strong conifer com- ponent in sub/canopy. Abundant med & small CWD & snags.
Plot chosen to represent NPC of natural origin with some past high- grade harvest. Good Thuja regeneration. Large Thuja with raised bases. Abundant CWD and tip-up mounds.
Plot chosen to represent NPC common in LTA in this landscape position. Part of landscape-sized area of conifer rich uplands assoc with E-W oriented hills (bedrock & till)& narrow drains in till plain

White cedar swamp, west side of Inga Lake. Microtopography pronounced. No evidence of human disturbance. Cedar regeneration excellent. Abundant bryophyte cover. Orchids (Listera cordata, Platanthera obtusata, P. hyper) distributed throughout.

Old growth white/red pine native plant community. Occupies portion of broad plateau and adjacent northeast-facing slope. Shrubs and forbs vary from sparse-dense. No evidence of cutting. Deer stand. Few scattered white pine seedlings throughout. Soil horizons: A, Bw1, Bw2. Parent material is loamy mantle glacial drift over possibly outwash. However, could not get deeper than Bw2 to see outwash due to rock fragments.

Old-growth cedar swamp on south end Inga Lake. Scattered white pine, Betula papyrifera and Picea mariana. Microtopogy varies from hummock-hollow to flatter-drier. Cedar seedlings common. No evidence fire/human disturbance. Study plots. A horizon depth >113cm.

Mixed old forest with white pine supercanopy and large diameter mixed canopy species. Abundant fir and red maple seedlings. No evidence of cutting or browse. Moderate coarse woody debris (fir) and large buried logs. Approximately 25-50% unvegetated (litter only). Litter of needles and leaves. Soil horizons: A, Bw1, Bw2, 2BC (very gravelly LCOS). Parent material is loamy mantle glacial drift over outwash. Could not dig past 2BC horizon due to rock fragments.

Old growth white-red pine. Occasional cut stumps (20-30cm dbh). Blister rust on lower branches of white pine and scattered recent white pine blowdown. Humus layer with evidence of worms (castings). Ah horizon dark color, 5cm in depth.

Natural origin white/red pine forest with aspen and birch co-dominate. Some mortality by blister rust. Fair white pine seedling reproduction. Moderate coarse woody debris and microtopogy. No fire evidence. Large erratics. No cut stumps. Herbivory. A horizon depth >2cm. Litter of needles and leaves.
Floating to rooted graminoid bog surrounding Dime Lake. Transitions to Black spruce bog. Dime Lake with Brasenia schreberi. Sparse graminoid litter.

Black spruce bog in sphagnum creek peatland complex. Abundant hummocks and hollows. No cutting evident in plot or area, but closer to road. Deer and moose trail in adjacent poor conifer swamp. Coarse woody debris=single tree fall. Sparse graminoid litter. Picea mariana DBH: Average - 17.5cm, Max 22.5cm.

Rich black spruce swamp (basin) along Dumbbell River. Spruce grouse nest just outside plot. Arceuthobium pusillum not apparent. No evidence of cutting. Scattered coarse woody debris on surface. No surface water. Moose trails.

Cedar swamp with canopy dominated by black ash and scattered yellow birch. Associated with outlet of Hjalmer Lake. Microtopogy well developed hummocks and hollows. No evidence of human dist, deer browse, fire. Neckera abundant on ash/yellow birch. pH=5.4.

Graminoid poor fen draining surrounding forested peatlands. Native plant community with scattered hummocks surrounded by network of pools with central drainage track. No evidence of human disturbance. pH=4.4.

Low shrub bog adjacent to Driller Lake. Part of large peatland complex, Headwatrs Wehno Creek. Mistletoe has affected most of canopy and regenerate black spruce. pH=3.9. Adjacent WFn53 and upland with Betula alleghensis.

Old-growth white cedar-yellow birch. Gently rolling-hilly, assoc with Coyote Creek lowland conifer complex. Dominate by yellow birch with patches of white cedar/white spruce co-dominate. Moose sign throughout. Canopy gaps and large coarse woody debris. No evidence of cutting. Litter of leaves and needles. A horizon depth >12cm.

Representative of large, old mesic mixed hardwood/conifer forest on drumlin landform surrounded by peatlands. Portions with white cedar and black spruce. Abundant large coarse woody debris, occasional cut stumps. Well-develop litter layer, no evidence of worms. A horizon depth >6cm.

Mesic aspen-birch-fir island surrounded by forested peatlands. Increasing amount of black spruce, tamarack, white pine seedlings below crest of center of community. Scattered white pine seedlings and surface boulders throughout. Sandy-loam with high proportion of boulders. A horizon depth >5cm. Litter of deciduous leaves with some needles.

Very small (1.5ac) fen at base of slope. Moderate-high amount of shrubs on dome top, ground springy. A few small pools in northeast corner but not extensively developed. Mineral layer 3cm down, then peat. Fair amount of Phragmites on Southwest side.

Straight boles, 5% coarse woody debris, some double-stemmed red oak and basswood, some burls and frost cracks. Big-tooth at top of slope nearby, no evidence of earthworms.
Tree DBH (cm):
Quercus macrocarpa: 41
Quercus rubra (double stem): 44, 42
Tilia americana: 38 (average and max)
Acer saccharum: 27 (average), 37 (max)

Large area of floating mat around small lake, water at or above surface of mat. Some areas have dense Bog birch cover, others have more open shrub cover. Mix of Sphagnum and non sphagnum. Topographic context: depression/flat.
In small depression surrounded by dry mesic upland forest. Trees mostly 10-25cm DBH. Hummocks of Sphagnum around tree bases. Hollows between hummocks with abundant Menyanthes.

One large white pine in the plot, others scattered throughout stand. Trees are straight-trunked, mix of multi and single stems. No sign of current disturbance. Quercus rubra more abundant other parts of stand.

Small depression surrounded by upland jack/red pine forest. One area has only small scattered black spruce, tamarack and here Carex lasiocarpa is abundant. Rest of site has more abundant larger spruce/tamarack.
Small isolated depression surrounded by dry mesic upland forest. Sphagnum is very hummocky and solid. No standing water.

Trees are straight-trunked. Some areas have a heavier cover of Acer spicatum with more Lonicera canadensis. Scattered Black ash seeps along slope. Betula allegheniensis scattered around (1st time this seen in Hubbard County).
Trees are straight-trunked and single-stemmed. No sign of recent disturbance. Several tip-up mounds in the plot. Sugar maple present in other parts of the site, but overall it is not common.

Moderately high hummocks, mature canopy. No standing water, moist peat layer. Moderate-small amount of coarse woody debris. Releve in shallow/wide valley of Miss River headwaters. Canopy fairly open. ~0.5mi east of River. Tamarack/black spruce swamp extensive (+/-100ac).

Mix of large and moderate sized boulders. Trees are forest grown. Moderate coarse woody debris. Most trees single stemmed. 2cm of leaf letter (oak/maple). 2cm of humus. Rolling topography. Little-no evidence of earthworms.

Sloping black spruce swamp. Releve at toe of slope where larix and moisture is more abundant. Solid mat of Sphagnum and feathermoss create high pillows. No hummock/hollows. Water table at 10cm below peat surface. Slope is 8-10 degrees. Malaxis paludosa found at crest of slope.

Small peat-filled basin, no floating mat. Small moat with Carex lacustris and Alnus incana. Entire mat with alternating large patches of Andromeda and Chamadaphne. No standing water in hummock hollows. Basin ~3acre Fen in a nice mature MHc37 stand. On Shell Lake Moraine.
Small ~3acre peat-filled basin. No floating mat. Poor fen within a larger MHc37 mature forest on Shell Lake moraine. Center of wetland with larger sized stand of Larix. Solid Sphagnum hummocks.

Several large black ash in native plant community (40-55dbh). Open-mucky saturated hollows. Lots of coarse woody debris. Rare yellow birch in canopy-very old. Swamp ~70acre surrounded by old-growth hardwoods and red pine forest. Releve ~30m south of logging road. Swamp is linear drainage-way between two steep-sided hills. Swamp in Shell Lake moraine.

Atypical forest for region. Scattered Pinus throughout. Soil sandy loam. Corylus is patchy. Releve in area that had open shrub layer. Many mulit-stem Tilia. North of Mud Lake. Old fence runs through center. Past grazed? Probably disturbed.

West of Goose Lake on slightly rolling topography on Shell Lake moraine. Sandy loam soil. No old stumps in plot, but occasional elsewhere. Fire-scarred stumps. Slight amount of coarse woody debris. Red oak even-aged. Some oaks have open-grown look. Some tilia multi-stemmed. Average red oak DBH: ~30-50cm. Releve on upper crest of slope before dropping down to Goose Lake.

Lots of canopy gaps from downed trees. Only patches of Sphagnum on moderate hummocks. Hollows wet, but no standing water. Native plant community is a mix between balck ash and spruce swamp. Releve somewhat typical of whole swamp that is ~50ac. Adjacent to Elbow Lake.

Sedge thatch thick. Water level at peat level. Peat spongy-not floating. Pockets of Phragmites and Typha. More fen-like towards center Carex lasiocarpa becomes more dominate. Releve in wetland that is ~160acre on east of Height of Land Lake.

Extreme rolling topography, Shell Lake moraine. Large mixed conifer-hardwood forest. Areas without conifers are MHc37 nearby. Entire forest complex ~1140ac with numerous wetlands to east. Soil is loamy sand. Canopy fairly closed. Releve is pretty typical of mixed conifer-hardwood area. Diverse canopy strata. Average red pine DBH: 50-65cm, average white pine DBH: 50-80cm.

Sandy loamy soil. Red pine ~45-55cm DBH. Occassional fire scars on Red pine, Yellow paint. Dominant Abies downslope to lake. Mossy/lichen ground layer. Patchy canopy. Lots of downed Abies, young Abies filling in. Wetland complex to South with dead black ash - wet meadow. South from logging/atv trail. Heavy logging on all sides.

Large rich fen (~50ac) with only isolated patches of Phragmites. Small area near center with stunted Larix. Quaky floating mat with open pools of water. No Sphagnum, large cover of brown mosses. Many Liparis loeselii. No moat.

Canopy oaks somewhat open-grown, stunted and look even-aged. Corylus can be very dense. Occasional fire-scarred stumps. Only oldest, largest Pin oak are certain, younger could be hybrid. Soil is sandy loam. Very thin A horizon and leaf litter. Average tree DBH ~15cm. Older/larger Quercus ellipsoidalis/macrocarpa average ~30cm DBH. One pin oak to 54cm DBH.

Canopy dense, occasional cut stumps, canopy gaps. Forest similar to more southern Big Woods forests. Atypical for County. Nice diverse canopy strata. No evidence of worms, though near 2 lakes. Ginseng found nearby in old sugarbush camp. Deer browsing. Occasional Tilia multi-stemmed. Tilia average DBH ~40cm. Moderate coarse woody debris. Soil: Silty sand.

Nice cedar/black ash spruce swamp with area of Tamarack in lower area. Occasional cut stumps-mostly on east edge of swamp. Upland of Populus tremuloides on slope recently cut (last 40 yrs). Even Sphagnum/feathermoss hummocks-very dry and yellowed. In a drought. Lots of tip-ups.

Canopy 75% with filtered sun. Even hummocks, shallow hollows-filled partly with water. Currently rain. Moderate coarse woody debris. ~100m south of Hwy 26. Releve in small Picea area ~10acres within larger tamarack swamp(~170acres). 14 Malaxis paludosa counted.

Lowland hardwood forest 130m southwest of Pike Lake. Soil silt-loam. On Round Lake Sand Plain land type association(LTA). Releve done in more level, uniform area before it slopes down to lake where seepage is occurring and more black ash occurs. Worms are present, leaf litter very thin. Native plant community MHc47/MHc36.
Large rich fen has upland borders comprised of Alnus incana, Betula glandulosa, and Calamagrostis canadensis, before transitioning into Rich Fen. Sharp-shinned hawk is quartering the area.

In a Jack pine vein, represents majority of site. Shrub cover mostly beaked hazel, variable, most dense and tall under jack pine. Less so under aspen clones. Jack pine maturing, giving way to Populus tremuloides and grandidentata. All litter types.

Silty loam cap over gravel band consistently at 25cm throughout plot. Cut stumps, dead/down Pinus banksiana found near plot. On ridge top adjacent to north to south running valley to east. Recent harvests (select cuts) to the west and northwest.

Soil horizon well-drained on plot, adjacent portions of forest have water holding pools indicating either semi-permeable (impeding drainage) or sub-surface water source. Although absent in canopy, red pine and white pine were present in the past (local communication) FDc34a. Litter of leaves and needles.

Although classed as a bog, it represents the only surveyed wetland of this type in the Township. Possible minerotrophic species that were not ID'd due to lack of experience with native plant community type. It does contain bog characteristics.
No water in footprints, although Sphagnum is moist. Pastured land to west, DNR controlled lake to east. Off plot Typha.

Large boulders present about the plot, soil too dry to penetrate with probe beyond ~20 cm. Pasturing influenced this stand, livestock paths evident. Topographic context: crest/upper. Litter of leaves and grass.

Jack pine component through stand is decadent, transitions to aspen/oak/hazel brush. Many jack pine exhibit open-grown habits. No cut stumps visible. Both oak species more successful in areas where jack pine is most absent. Litter of leaves, needles and grass. Fire-dependent community in transition to aspen-oak as a result of no fire.
Some self-thinning of Aspen is occurring. Current aspen canopy is middle aged. Older wolfy trees (oaks) give clues to the stand's past structure which was more open. Litter of leaves and grass.
Plot near the intersection of 2 cross-country ski trails. Soil too dense/dry for soil probe to penetrate beyond 35 cm. All types of litter present.

Interestingly no sugar maple in a very nice MHn47. Two wet pools in area, one holds water. Two decaying pine stumps ~45 cm across. Lay of land gently rolling with a gentle slope to northeast towards Shingobee creek. Similar patches of this native plant community found throughout site 72. Litter of leaves and grass.

Cedars straight, average DBH=45cm. Black spruce average 25-30cm, one at 48cm. Slopes to northeast with occasional iron-rich springs. Soil saturated sapric mucky peat >15cm. Very little cedar/spruce regeneration. Occasional tip-ups. No stumps in releve but some fire scarred ones nearby. No sphagnum, only occasional mnium, feathermoss, and liverworts.

No standing H2O in hollows. Blk ash avg dbh=30-35cm. Soil moist-mucky sapric-hemic peat >6 in deep. Part of larger forested wetland complex. FPn63 common along creeks & lakeshore. ~200m SW of Lester L

Water at peat surface. High hummocks of Sphagnum. Carex utriculata common in patches. Spongy mat, not floating. Upland cut around fen (Picea glauca, Populus tremuloides, Pinus resinosa). Small basin fen. No kalmia, no water.

Narrow band of wet meadow on edge of Crow Wing River. Phragmites dominates other side of river. Grades to shrub swamp near upland edge. Typha angustifolia at water's edge on both sides. Peat depth >1m, Water >1ft.
Shrub swamp near Releve #3970 on Crow Wing River. No standing water. Water at peat level. Dense Carex hummocks. Shrub cover ~70%. Releve ~20 meters from river.

Very dense hummocks of Sphagnum. Very little hollow develop. Water fills holes after stepping on Sphagnum. Not floating-firm. Plot in center of open mat. Ringed by dense black spruce. CIR photo shows opening as small distinct area within black spruce.

Along south side Necktie River. Approx 120m from Cedar Swamp. Shrub swamp along forest edge. Typha angustifolia heavy in patches on north side of river. Some brown mosses. Bouncy mat, very loose near edge of river.
