On edge of opening of FPn82a. FPn82 was dry but releve in fairly wet area. This FP/AP area is adjacent to Crow Wing Lake. Has changed from very high to medium hummocks of Sphagnum. On bouncy non floating mat.
Floating mat on western side of Spider Lake. Dominated mostly by Carex lasiocarpa. Edges of mat at water's edge dom by Typha angustifolia and occasional Phragmites. All brown mosses. No Sphagnum.
Wet prairie on black, saline soils in low areas subject to groundwater seepage. Located on shallow toe slopes on West side of major beach ridge of Glacial Lake Agassiz. Carex hallii quite abundant.

This community occupies higher land in a landscape with very subtle undulations in topography.  Part of a rich fen, transition subtype. Located just east of a beach ridge of Glacial Lake Agassiz. Soil: deep cold wet dark brown coarse fibric peat >30 inches deep (end of soil probe).
Part of large, rich fen, transition section in proposed Rosewood wildlife management area. Soil: < 30 inches fibric peat.
Narrow strip of dry mesic prairie along dirt road on top of sandy beach ridge.  Possibly hayed. Soil: 0-2 inches organic  2-9 inches black sandy loam  > 9 inches brown loamy sand with pebbles.

Wet-mesic prairie on sandy upland minor strand of Glacial Lake Agassiz surrounded by seepage-influenced wet prairie. Soil: 3-15cm silty loam  15-20cm sandy clay  >20cm hard  very coarse sand/gravel (till).

Wet mesic blacksoil prairie on slightly higher land surrounded by seepage-influenced wet prairie. Numerous aspen groves present in area.  Currently is grazed. Soil: 3-15cm silty loam, 15-20cm sandy clay, >20cm hard very coarse sand/gravel(till).

Saline subtype of wet prairie located approximately 0.6 mile west of major Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridge. Soil: 0-1 inch organic, 1-6 inches black fine sandy silt loam, 6-10 inches black clayey fine sand, 10-14 inches grey-brown clayey fine sand, 14-16 inches light brown fine sand, 16-25 inches light grey brown sandy clay with gravel.

Mesic prairie on narrow sandy ridge bordered by wet prairie and emergent marshes in broad valley between two beach ridges of Glacial Lake Agassiz.  Site has been hayed in past. Soil: 0-2 inches organic, 2-7 inches black fine sandy loam, 7-12 inches black loamy sand, 12-12.5 inches coarse sand, 12.5-18 inches clayey coarse sand.

Wet prairie in swale in fine-grained mosaic of wet and wet-mesic prairie on shallow ridge/swale topography in wide valley between two Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridges. Soil: 10 cm black fine sandy clay loam over dark brown grey silty fine sand over fine greyish calcareous clay with fine sand.

Seepage fen on west edge of a Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridge. Cattails & many prairie species established on top of large hummocks. Soil very springy; peat deeper than soil probe. Many unidentified mosses. Soil: Deep, loose, spongy, fine grained, very wet/saturated, dark brown peat.
Long narrow seepage fen perched just below crest of Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridge.  In excellent condition. Soil: deep peat >1m, fine grained, very springy.
Seepage-influenced brush prairie at foot of steep slope of Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridge. Duinnick Tract. Soil: 0-7cm fine gray peat, 7-30cm firm dark gray clay with sand, +30cm hard ground layer.
Rich fen in A. Wold tract.  In wet depression bordered on west by sandy ridges from Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridge.
Oak woodland on Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridge slopes. Soil: 8 cm light brown loamy fine sand over coarse sand.
Open oak woodland on top of Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridge. Many multi and triple stemmed bur oak in plot.

Wet mesic prairie on level ground immediately west of a beach ridge of former Glacial Lake Agassiz. Soil: 2 inches organic, 2-8 inches fine black sandy loam, 8-20 inches black heavy clay loam 20+ inches heavy light gray clay.
In wet swale where Marcia Richards found 68 Platanthera praeclara. Wet prairie seepage subtype.

Wet brush prairie in swales on shallow ridge-swale topography.  Grades into mesic brush prairie on higher ground. Soil: 0-4 inches black silty clay, 4-6 inches coarse sandy clay, 6+ inches coarse sand.

Scrub oak woodland on deep sand just north of Red Lake River. Most oaks in plot are multiple-stemmed with stem diameters reaching 55 cm DBH. Soil: 0-3 inches black loamy sand, 3-30+ inches light brown fine sand.
Rich fen on Pennington-Beltrami border. Soil: deep black-brown fibric peat.

Mature aspen woodland on island surrounded by emergent marsh and rich fen.  On the border between Pennington and Beltrami counties. Several charred tree stumps present. Soil: 2 inches coarse rich organic over 1 inch black silty loam over 3+ inches light brown fine sand.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Floodplain forest on first terrace above Red Lake River in Huot wildlife management area. Grades into basswood/ash/aspen forest on steep slopes. Soil: 0-3 inches black silty loam, 3-30+ inches dark grey brown silty clay.

Wet mesic prairie on west side of Hwy 32, 6 miles south of Red Lake Falls.  On shallow ridge in swell-swale topography with wet brush prairie in swales. Soil: 0-2 inches organic  2-6 inches black sandy clay loam, 6-8 inches light brown clayey fine sand, 8+ light brown fine sand.
Wet brush prairie in swales just west of highway 30, 6 miles south of Red Lake Falls. Soil: 0-15 inches black silty clay, 15+ inches light brown wet clay.

npc_type_name: Green Ash - Bur Oak - Elm Forest
remarks: Lowland hardwood forest on sandy soil near oxbow on second terrace above Clearwater River. Soil: 0-6 inches black fine sandy loam, 6-30+ inches dark grey black fine sandy clay loam.

npc_type_name: Green Ash - Bur Oak - Elm Forest
remarks: Floodplain forest on level ground east of the Clearwater River. Releve on edge of floodplain.  Much logging above floodplain.
Rich fen (transition) shrub subtype in large, wet depression surrounded by disturbed aspen woodland and brush prairie. Soil: 20 inch fibric peat over 2 inches black sandy clay over gray clay.
Large area of rich fen surrounded by cattail marsh. Soil: very deep cold fibric peat.

Wetter phase of wet brush prairie.  Was once grazed.  (note: releve is taken from a wet brush prairie inclusion in a mesic brush prairie community). Wet-mesic and wet brush prairie with brush cover approximately 60%: predominately Betula glandulifera and several Salix species. Uplands also dominated by Andropogon geradii, Sporobolis heterolepis and Muhlenbergia richardsonis. Shifts to Spartina pectinata and Carex buxbaumii in wetter areas. In excellent condition with rich species diversity. Poa pratensis present throughout at very low level, was once grazed. Located in interbeach area of Glacial Lake Agassiz on shallow ridge/swale topography. Soil: 0-3 inches black sandy clay,  3-12 inches light brown sand, >12 inches coarse gravelly sand with large granite gravel.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Older oak/maple/basswood forest site on level ground with much leaf and decayed wood litter.  4 large downed trees showing fire damage (1975). 2 standing snags.  4 tip-ups.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Soil springy peat with many hummocks, standing water to about .4m with much tannic acid. Releve includes most of this tamarack stand.
Small old-growth stand with much coarse woody litter and several stand ing dead trees.  Quercus rubra occurs occasionally in canopy.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Selectively logged in past, but well recovered - mix of Acer saccharum, Tilia americana, Quercus rubra, Quercus alba, Fraxinus pennsylvania, Corylus cornuta, & UR dying out. Basswood most common large tree, sugar maple most common small tree.  Very diverse herb layer.
Wide variability within stand due to drainage and various facing slopes throughout.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Rocky, sandy soil. Rolling ravine with lots of tip-ups affecting microtopography. Several large, multi-tree gaps. Nursery logs and rocks common. Moss layer on rocks and logs 25-50% cover.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Sugar Maple - Basswood Forest (Cold Slope)
remarks: Some open canopy, Quercus rubra and birch. Selective cutting, evidence of burn. Rolling ravine topography, very steep and rocky with good amount of tip-up microtopography.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Oak-Basswood old-growth with Maple, Hickory, Fraxinus Pennsylvania, & Ostrya virginiana subcanopy.  Herb layer diverse - Asarum, Pamax quinquefolia. Small uncut area within larger grazed and select. cut forest area.
Taylor's Woods.
Oak and Basswood logged out - numerous cut stumps. Little or no subcanopy, understory, or herb layer. Active sugarbush operation. Lots of small coarse woody debris, few larger.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: East side younger with tons of coarse woody debris. Further west and in have savanna look with large old trees and young understory. Canopy mostly continuous though some light enters.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest

remarks: Calcareous fen in peat just north of the edge of the Chester Hills.  Very hummocky ground surface, much standing water, but ground is not very springy.  Large drainage ditches within 1/4 mile to south and east.
Typical vegetation in large calcareous fen know as Svedarsky's fen. On deep, fine-grained peat. Releve includes several small areas of exposed peat.

Large, shrub-dominated, seepage area on west-facing slope of Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridge. Very fen-like swamp. Triglochin palustris and Tofieldia glutinosa are present here. Very wet: much standing water.
Larege, level, calcareous fen-like community on deep peat. At northern toe of the Chester Hills. Grades south into large seepage-influenced shrub swamp and small rich fen-like areas.

Calcareous fen on deep, very buoyant, fine-grained peat perched near top of west-facing slope of Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridge. Numerous, sparsely-vegetated pools present. Located within heavily grazed pasture, but cattle have avoided fen.

Calcareous fen-like community on coarse, quaking peat. Surface water 1-2 feet deep and flowing toward southwest. Typical of small fen-like openings within dense shrub swamp on gradually sloping land with heavy groundwater seepage.

Small high diversity spot surrounded by disturbed areas of Salix, Cornus, Phragmites, and Phalaris. Soil thick peat. No standing water. Dominate sedge's forming hummocks. Firm, fibrous hollows. Needs fire to reduce woody species.

Good population of Cypripedium candidum. Orchid study by DNR parks in 1990 at this site. Ankle deep water between hummocks formed by Carex stricta. Hydrologic station at site. Deep organic peat soil. Same plot as releve #4088.
Brush prairie on nearly level ground at base of beach ridge. Appears to have calcareous groundwater seepage. Is located just down slope from well-developed calcareous fen. Soils very wet.

Dense shrub swamp on soils with heavy groundwater seepage. Standing water 1-2 feet deep; orange iron deposits common on groundwater surfaces. Farther north and west shrubs thin out to 50% cover, and Phragmites cover increases. Several calcareous fen-like opening on quaking peat occur throughout this community.
Undisturbed part of bog-like fen with scattered tamarack on east side of Evenmore lake. Ground is highly buoyant and is probably a floating mat. Dense carpet of several moss species.
Rich fen on deep, very buoyant, coarse, fibric peat in broad valley called the McIntosh Channel. Center of channel is most fen-like. Deep drainage ditches present.
Releve is typical of enormous fen-like swamp in middle of broad, wide valley (McIntosh Channel) on extremely wet, quaking soils. Soil is deep, coarse peat. Several deep drainage ditches present.
Narrow transition zone between large Typha marsh and wet prairie. In lowest landscape position between two Glacial lake Agassiz beach ridges. Zone reaches 40m wide.
Very level area with patchy shrubs.
Releve in area with considerable patchy Salix. Very thick litter, level, due south of gravel pit. Should be considered a seepage subtype.
Soil: 6 inches of silty black "mucky" unconsolidated peat on top of fine sandy grey clay. Water table this year about 3 inches below surface.
pH 7.8, Open area with only occasional scattered Larix. South of rice paddy, east of large deciduous clump.
Open facies of seepage fen, grandes northwets into rich fen, eastward calcareous seepage species extend under Tamarack.
Rich fen facies of wetland. Other areas have more Carex buxbaumii. Some areas have considerable Menyanthes and Phragmites.
Level, tamarack southwest of flowage, fairly open. pH:7.8.
Level, mineral soil. Visually impressive because of abundance of birch. Mixed hardwood swamp.
Tamarack swamp, seepage subtype.
Large stumps present. Level seepage tamarack.
Active seepage zone - shows as white patterned area in Tamarack. About 60% open water. Some seepage pools are open to 5m in diameter. Many deposits.
Fairly open stocked. Tamarack swamp, seepage subtype.
Level, very wet tamarack swamp with standing, oily, iron stained water in abundant pools. pH: 7.8. Apparently active seepage zone. Much downed wood and old cutting. 10-15cm DBH.
Greyer less densely packed signature in level seepage tamarack swamp. pH: 7.8. Grading West into very wet Salix/Betula zone. Tamarack swamp, seepage subtype.
Sedge subtype area, level, wet pools here and there about 1m across. Rich transition sedge fen.
Releve at seepage zone at north edge of open fen with small tamarack islands. pH 8.1.
Releve in very wet more open area. Fen with tamarack overstory. pH 8.1. Tamarack swamp, seepage subtype.
Mature conifer swamp remnants in red signature. Currently being cut, much of red signature cut winter '92-93. pH: 8.
Open tamarack east of snowmobile trail. Many stumps. Tamarack swamp seepage subtype.
Releves 4121 and 4122 side by side. pH: 8. Open facies (sedge subtype). Rich transition fen.
Releve 4121 and 4122 side by side. pH: 8. Closed facies. (shrub tamarack subtype).
Level, densely stocked tamarack in extreme southwest of section. peat to bottom of cover, highly decomposed dark brown. Fairly sunlit (about 40% sunny), much deadfall <10cm DBH, heavily hummocked.
Releve in extreme southwest corner of large calcareous fen. Fairly fine sedge peat, pretty well decomposed, rich brown.
Level. East of snowmobile trail. Southwest of mostly southerly wooded island, west of Phragmites patch. pH: 7.2.
Patterned area n of large tamarack island. Somewhat mounded microtopography, compacted peat may be 1' higher than wet areas, not spongy.
Light facies of patterned area. Apparently level, wet, spongy east of grey facies # 107-13.
Level conifer swamp peninsula extending into calcareous fen on west side.
Disturbed area obviously once part of a continuous calcareous fen but now just downflow of a rice paddy and adjacent to a ditch.
Grey signature, more open.  Facies, level area, becomes more treed westward.
Level, very wet. Somewhat superficial, hasty as dark was falling.
Rich fen (transition), shrub subtype.
Open areas in a mosaic of open and shrub fen e of aspen island.
Dry, mud-bottomed flark in a patterened fen.  pH=7.22, Ca=65.8mg/l, Kcorr=44us/cm, Abs.=0.7nm.
String (linear peat ridge) adjacent to releve #36.
Approximately 1.75 miles from county road 8 and 2 miles southwest of Bena.  Closed picea forest with continuous moss carpet rich in sphagnum.  pH=3.7, Ca=1.7 mg/l, Cond=20 us/cm, Abs=1.3 nm.
Approximately 0.3 miles west of county road 8 and 2 miles south of Bena.  Sphagnum lawn apron on lower east apron of bog.  pH=4.5, Ca=2.0 mg/l, Cond=64 uS/cm, Abs=1.5 nm.

South margin of Nett Lake, approximately 6 miles north of Silverdale. Complex of mud-bottmed pools and low hummocks/tussocks. Marly precipitate on surface and strong H2S odor. pH=7.3, Ca=82.4mg/l, Kcorr=64us/cm, Abs.=0.2nm
Three inches standing water all over.  Fair amount of birch blowdowns, not much dead elm.  Appears to have always had less elm than some areas.  West of Tharaldson's property line.

Water to two feet. pH 7.8.  Bordered to north by wet balsam popler and uphill by roadside strip of native prairie dominated by Andropogon gerardii, Sorghastrum nutans with Aster ericoides, Artemisia ludoviciana, Solidago rigida, Aster laevis, Amorpha canescens, Helianthus xlaetiflorus, and Liatrus aspera.

Soil >40 cm, perfect black loam (feels like even balance fine sand, clay and organics, very nice friable soil) over fine limonite colored golden sand, becoming fine white "sugar" sand at approximately 1 m. Soils approximately 4 cm highly organic loam (but not peat) over grey white clay which becomes whiter then yellow and brown at depth (makes sense since iron leached from layer above).

Soil >40 cm, perfect black loam (feels like even balance fine sand, clay and organics, very nice friable soil) over fine limonite colored golden sand, becoming fine white "sugar" sand at approximately 1 m. Soils approximately 4 cm highly organic loam (but not peat) over grey white clay which becomes whiter then yellow and brown at depth (makes sense since iron leached from layer above).
No forbs visible in actual pasture.  Area almost too grazed to do releve, approximately 2/3 bare mud.  Alkaline area.
Once you walk around in it you can see it is being grazed.  Grades northwest to a black area probably Scirpus acutus. No forbs visible in actual pasture.
Included in NC 125, wet prairie (nw).  Not highly hummocked.  In haste due to impending thunderstorm.
Included in nc 125, wet prairie (nw).  Highly hummocked area.
Fairly homogeneous and undisturbed.  Scattered islands of aspen and balsam poplar at south end of this continuous sedge meadow. Rich fen, transition.
Narrow zone of brush prairie on east edge of rich fen.
Releve in fen that was one of richest for bird eo's in county.  Fen has been burned annually (intentionally) for many years.
Soils only 2 cm peat over coarse grey sandy clay.  Community grades into releve 53-05 within 5 meters.
Northwest corner of big rich fen.  In an area that appears to have been once broken (on photos).
East of releve 54-08.
40 meters west of circular aspen grove.
Very narrow band small fragment calcareous fen in valley of Hill River, end of valley otherwise occupied by shrub swamp and wet meadow. Level, underlain by peat.
Wet meadow on east side of Hill River.  Rather hummocky surface.  Grey area on photo.
pH 8.1.  Bluish area on aerial photo between 2 tamarack islands.
Level, slightly higher than adjacent minertrophic shrub swamp between here and oak woodland, not on peat.
On floating peat.  Light-colored area just north of small pond.
About 20% standing water.
About 4-5" standing water. Rich fen transition sedge subtype.
Soil profile difficult to get, homogeneous black clayey loam over grey clay over fine pale brown very clean sand at 1/2 meter.
Transition community south of railroad track.  Whole area feels sparsely vegetated like it should be calcareous fen.  1" sedge peat over 1" loam over mucky steel grey clay.
South of railroad track.  Soil 12 cm loam over fine greyish white sand.
Rich fen transition section, sedge subtype.
North end of prairie, on mineral soil.
Wet prairie with seepage influence area just at east edge of area about 2' lower than adjoining mesic brush prairie to east.

In area transitional between rich fen and wet brush prairie.  Soil approximately  5 cm black muck or peaty loam over dark gray sandy clay loam, over pale yellowish-gray sandy clay.  No evident disturbance.

In small, very shallow depression. Soil approximately 5cm black, slightly fibrous peat, over 20-25cm black, fine sandy-clay loam, over yellowish silt or silty clay. Tract idle but apparently some recent grazing use.

In narrow wetland zone se side of prominent beach ridge. pH of surface water:  7.7 (pocket meter). No disturbance in immediate area. Moderately decomposed (humic) peat >.5m deep. More marsh-like south of plot.

In narrow wetland zone southeast side of prominent beach ridge, close to upland margin. Surface water pH=7.5 (pocket meter). Hemic peat >.5m deep. No disturbance in immediate area. Marshier conditions southward.

In narrow wetland zone southeast side of prominent beach ridge. Some areas marshy, some meadow-like. Surface water pH=7.0 (pocket meter). Peat depth >.5m several recent large dugouts constructed in area, no other evident disturbance.

In narrow wetland zone southeast side of prominent beach ridge, close to upland edge. Surface water pH=7.2(pocket meter). Peat depth >.5m. Several large dugouts recently constructed; no other evident disturbance.
Moderately hummocked, perhaps from past grazing.  Soil: approximately 20cm black loam silty loam, then gray loamy fine sand, then coarser brownish sand. 2nd layer approximately 30cm thick.

On better-drained "peninsula" out into rich fen. No evident disturbance. Soil: 15-20cm black silty loam over dark gray loamy fine sand, over yellow brown coarse sand. See field form for vegetation description.

Plot a phase of wet brush prairie transitional to wet meadow. No evident disturbance.  Soil: approximately 10cm black loam, then dark loamy sand, then brown to yell-brown coarse sand. See field form for vegetation description.

Plot sampled a wetter area of fen, with character transitional to a marshy meadow. Surface water pH=7.7(pocket meter). Soil: muck over black sand. Too wet, loose for good probe core. Several cm free water above surface.

Plot sampled wet prairie zone between formerly cultivated upland and rich fen to east. No evident disturbance. Soil: approximately 10cm black loam/silty, then gravel. Exposed surface boulders are occasional in prairie. See field form for vegetation description.

Substrate: hemic sedge peat, approximately 30cm deep over fine sand.  Boulders occasional on surface.  Peat surface generally encrusted with marl here. A few charred remains of willows on ground, no live willows.

No evidence of disturbance. Substrate: hemic to sapric peat approximately 30cm deep over fine sandy loam or loamy fine sand.  Marl-coated patches infrequent, small here. They become large, common at east margin of plot.  Boulders exposed at surface.
Substrate: hemic sedge peat, some fibric bands, over black, loamy, somewhat sticky mineral soil; lots of fine, gravelly material. Peat depth > 30cm.  No evident disturbance.

No evident disturbance. Soil: approximately 60cm peat over sandy loam. Peat mostly hemic, some fibric bands. Higher spots with small(<1m) Populus tremuloides, Populus balsamifera, with solidago canadensis, Rosa species etc.  To northeast Salix absent, fewer forbs, Scirpus acutus common to co-dominate.

No evident disturbance. Substrate: well-decomposed hemic sedge peat but with brown fibric bands. Depth undetermined.  Patches of white deposits (marl?) On surface common.  1 of 3 releves in close proximity.  No evident disturbance.

No evident disturbance. Substrate: hemic sedge peat, but with brown fibric bands.  Depth undetermined. [patches of white deposits (marl?) On surface common]. 1 of 3 releves closely proximal. No evident disturbance.
Substrate: hemic sedge peat, but with brown fibric bands.  Depth undetermined.  [patches of white deposits (marl?) On surface common]. 1 of 3 releves done in close proximity. No evident disturbance.

In narrow zone of seepage influence on beach-ridge slope above marsh. Shallow gravel pit along ridge crest. At 45cm subsoil is sand; profile above unrecorded. Surrounding community mainly mesic brush prairie.

Shrubby zone, transitional to shrub swamp, in huge fen. Surface water pH= 7.9(pocket meter). Soil approximately 50cm sapric to hemic peat. Mineral subsoil coarse sandy, too wet to extract probe sample. No disturbance.

Extensive shrub-free sedge lawn. Approximately 5 cm water on surface, up to 10 cm in places. pH=8.1(pocket meter). Soil aproximately 35cm hemic to sapric peat. Mineral substrate too stony for probe. No evident disturbance.

In narrow trough between narrow, very low ridges out in huge fen system. Soil: gray to yellowish-gray, fine sandy clay("soupy"); no peat. Stones common at surface. Surface water pH=8.3(pocket meter) no disturbance.

Plot typical of revegetation meander scars. 3/4" pvc on southwest and northeast corners. Approximately 40cm standing water on plot, but plants show terrestrial form. Plot outside of Carex lacustris colonies. Peat depth 19" on sand lenses. State stand #4.
Plot typical of forb-rich areas being invaded by exotics.  3/4" pipes at northeast and southwest plot corners. Peat depth 6 inches. State stand #4.

Plot typical of tall, hummocky meadow. 3/4" pipes at northwest and southeast corners. Iron flock in 6 inches standing water, obviously flowing s to creek from cedar swamp to meadow. Peat depth = 20 inches. State stand #4.
Plot typical of "upland" unburned meadow. 3/4" pipe at northwest and southeast corners. 20 cm standing water on plot.
Plot typical of wet drain.  3/4" pipe on southwest and northeast corners.  Water 50 cm deep over plot.  Unburned site.  Three inches peat over sand.
Plot typical of open meadow.  3/4" plastic pipe at northwest and southeast corners. Water standing in hollows. Peat depth > 5 feet, no sand lensing. Possible core site.
Plot typical of wiregrass meadow.  3/4" plastic pipe on north/south diagonal. Standing water in hollows.  Soils: 4-1/2 feet of peat over sand.

Gorgeous small fen dominated by Carex oligosperma.  Pine (red/jack) with aspen on surrounding upland ridge. Willow rare, mostly at edges. Ground: 6" water, matted grass/sedge, Utricularia leaves, scant sphagnum(coll). A few ATV tracks through wetland. Utricularia throughout. Soil: Saturated peat.
Area heavily hummocked (probably previously grazed).  Old fence post in plot.
Apparently undisturbed although eastward appears to have been broken in past.
About 50% bare mud as this area is heavily used by deer and moose (no cattle in this area but effect is the same).
Classic rich fen transition sedge subtype, very wet.

This is an area reported by local hunters to be a "spongy" area and by owner to be "quick sand".  May represent an area that was once calcareous fen but impacted by gravel pits upflow to east. Soil is sedge peat over muck.

D quality, highly degraded by grazing.  Soil continuous black muck to handle of corer (over  1 m), highly hummocked and overgrown by shrubs. Very sparsely vegetated and spongy underfoot.  When you stand in one place you can hear the water gurgle nearby.  Soil is muck to >1 m.

D quality, highly degraded by grazing.  Soil continuous black muck to handle of corer (over  1 m), highly hummocked and overgrown by shrubs. Very sparsely vegetated and spongy underfoot.  When you stand in one place you can hear the water gurgle nearby.
Between burned area and conifers on east.
A different facies of wet meadow nearer conifers.
Embayment at southwest end of big wetland.
Area just off upland on se side of wetland (before embayment).
At mouth of long bay on west side.
Just west of Leo Lake (some parts so wet they float).
Surface of wetland is hummocked the way they get when grazed. Not presently grazed. Level, wet area north of co. 45, rich fen facies.
Loose canopied tamarack swamp.  Much open canopy where dead elm has gone down.  Transitional between conifer swamp and shrub swamp.
Soil approximately  5 cm black loam over light gray clay loam, with sharp stones. A few boulders at surface. Community transitional to rich fen. No evident disturbance.

5-6 cm black muck over a few cm very dark gray clay loam, over pale yellowish-gray silty clay with lots of sand and sharp pebbles. Native community transitional between wet prairie and rich fen. Phalaris atypical for area.

Typical of fen, but in patch of Cadium mariscoides.  Approximately 10 cm black sapric peat over dark gray fine sand. No evident disturbance in vicinity, but separated from main part of fen by large ditch approximately 200 meters southwest.

In more typical sedge-dominated fen.  Approximately 20 cm black, sapric peat, then 10 cm black fine sandy loam, over dark gray loamy fine sand.  No evident disturbance in immediate area; separated from main part of fen by large ditch.

In small, better drained shrubby patch in sedge-dominated fen. Approximately 2 cm black sapric peat over 20-30 cm black fine sandy loam, over dark gray loamy fine sand. No evident disturbance in immediate vicinity.

Transitional between rich fen and shrubby wet meadow.  Approximately 10 cm black muck, over very dark gray loamy fine sand, over dark olive gray loamy fine sand. Slightly wetter than nearby releve. No evident disturbance.

Transitional between rich fen and shrubby wet meadow.  Approximately 10 cm black muck over very dark gray loamy fine sand, becoming orangish sand at approximately 30 cm.  Slightly drier than nearby releve. No evident disturbance.

Transitional to rich fen. Close to small upland "island" in fen. Approximately 5 cm muck over approximately  10 cm dark gray fine sandy loam, over olivaceous gray loamy fine sand.  No evident disturbance.
In slightly higher area within rich fen. Soil 3-4cm very organic rich loam (or muck) over approximately 15cm very dark brownish gray fine sandy loam over gray loamy fine sand. No evident disturbance.
Margin of slightly higher area in large rich fen.  Soil approximately 15 cm black loam over dark gray loamy fine sand over gray loamy fine sand.  No evident disturbance.

In area that is transitional between fen, meadow, wet brush prairie. Approximately 5 cm black sapric peat over approximately 20 cm very dark gray fine sandy loam over pale gray loamy fine sand. No evident disturbance.
Typical area except for presence of Cladium.  Soil approximately  45 cm black sapric peat over dark gray loamy sand.  No evident disturbance, but major ditch 150 meters southwest.

place_name: E BEACHES LAKE FEN NE  CBS # 4
remarks: Soil: 40-45 cm hemic peat over approximately 10 cm dark gray fine sand, over fine sandy loam or sandy clay loam. No evident disturbance. West releve of 2 approximately 30 meters apart.

place_name: E BEACHES LAKE FEN NE  CBS # 4
remarks: Soil: approximately 35 cm hemic peat over dark gray loamy fine sand. At approximately 1 meter is yellowish sandy clay loam. No evident disturbance. East releve of 2 approximately 30 meters apart.

Soil: Hemic peat, depth not determined.  Much of fen periodically mowed for hay. Not determined whether area sampled is mowed, but it wasn't the year before releve taken.  Area uniform, 10 x 10 meter plot no different.

Plot short distance from low ridge out into fen. Soil approximately 25 cm hemic peat over gravelly material. Much of fen periodically mowed for hay; this part not mowed year before sampling. Area uniform, 10 x 10 meter plot no different.
Approximately 10 cm black loam, then very dark gray sticky loam. Probe stopped by stones at 15 cm. Burned in 1990. Plot lower of 2 on very slight slope at foot of beach ridge. No evident disturbance.
Soil hemic peat, depth not determined. Much of fen mowed periodically for hay. Plot in area mowed previous year.  Surface slightly disturbed.

In zone of discharge at foot of beach ridge. Water, bare mud 25-50% of plot area. Hemic peat, fibric bands, 70-80 cm deep over gravelly sand. Possible disturbance by inundation behind dike of ditch spoil downslope. pH 7.7.
In zone of obvious discharge along foot of beach ridge. No bare mud, water. Hemic peat >1 m (probe limit). pH 7.7 (pocket meter). Possibly disturbed by water ponding behind ditch spoil downslope.

Soil: Approximately 12 cm black loam over very dark gray sandy clay loam, over pale gray sandy clay. Before fire in 1990 some shrubs >1.5 m. Plot higher of 2 on very slight slope at base of beach ridge.
Carex trichocarpa sedge meadow in 5-7 cm water depth from unusually wet year. Runoff & springs.
Hummocks in standing water, depth 0.25m. Seepage area at base of bluffs, alluvium of crooked creek.
Floating vegetation mat suspended on 1m deep floodwaters.

Wet meadow margin composed of wet prairie species. Lush, productive, cover >50% above 0.5 m height. Gopher mound present. Footpath/old trail bordering releve plot. 100 meters east of field station building.
Water pH=7.5 (pocket meter). Soil: hemic sedge peat, depth not determined. Boulders frequent at or just below surface. Very wet at date of sampling. No evident disturbance.
Water pH=7.4 (pocket meter). Plot in transition from fen to prairie. Soil hemic sedge peat, depth not determined. Mound of mineral soil next to plot, shrubby.
Earlier flooding killed much above-ground vegetation regrown plants small, so cover abundance values may be lower than normal. Boulders common at surface, approximately  5% of plot area.
Soil about 18 cm heavy clay loam over gravel.
Degraded by vehicle track.
Surface is dry. Soil: 6cm, highly organic (almost peaty), fine grey sand grading into clayey light grey white sand. Bottom 20cm of corer fine white sand.
Soil: 20 cm of loam over heavy grey fine sandy clay.
Species balance suggests former grazing. Surprising how little Poa.
Cobbly rough encroachment by woody vegetation, mainly grass.
Steep edges higher quality, but majority of site reflected in releve. Woody shrubs taking over. Appears formerly grazed. Clayish soils.
Rocky soil, occasional trees, some (10-20%)low shrub cover. Sandy, silty loam. Tag 32.
Dark, silty-sand loam (alluvial soil), mounded rock between, dry channels, floodplain of Beaver Creek permanent marker. Northeast corner, many fallen limbs and logs. Tag 27.
Dark sandy loam, well-drained, dense shade, channels on north border, 10 meters west of trail.

Clay-silty loam, 6" A horizon dark friable, sub horizon clay yellow, rock outcrops rare, 100% shade to ground layer, level to convex shape. Appears disturbed from past grazing or depauperite of herbs do to increased shading. Tag #24
Soil: grey yellow loess compacted = dry mesic subtype. Eroded silt loam. Seaton.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Blue Beech) Seepage Swamp
remarks: Tag 22--southwest corner. Plot 10 x 40 m. Northeast aspect. Footslope/base of dolomite-sandstone cliffs. Stake 3 ft elevation above alluvium. Muck soils--stream & alluvial well-drained soils.
Dark silty loam, b quality. Cobblestones and occasional rock outcrops. Variable slope. Parallel to road and ravine.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Silty loam with occasional rock outcrops, north aspect, 3/4 slope position. C quality, shrub layer greater in surrounding area. Fallen logs and snags occasional.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Dark friable silt loam. Dry-mesic outcrops occasional. Few cobble- stones. Midslope above parking lot (senenw17). Tag 31.
Old growth maple-basswood forest on colluvial soils, dark clay silt loam. Cobblestones (no talus). Large (10 m height) outcrops outside plot(dolomite). Many downed logs, tip-ups. Unstable substrate.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Dark silty loam with cobblestones. Rock outcrops 1m x 3m present in plot. Refer to rare features database for community description.
Releve plot on slightly elevated mound. Slopes away from west edge plot to silver maple dominated slough. Large open grown oaks with gaps nearby. Dark sandy silt loam, friable, low clay.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Dry mesic dark sandy loam (silty loam at base). Releve at foot of slope. Few rock outcrops (rare). No cobblestones. A quality old growth forest.

Footslope of bluff in hanging meander, dark silt colluvium, large Ulmus americana cresting gap. Adjacent to plot. Unique in tree size DBH, topography. Fallen limbs common. Old growth maple basswood forest.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: On east edge of north-south ravine. Considerable cobblestones and boulders. Dark silt, with high humus. Rocks and surface soil covered by moss (talus slope).
Clay silt soil, dry-mesic type. Quercus alba: 143 rings at 64 cm DBH; Quercus rubra: 96 rings at 59 cm DBH. Old growth mixed oak forest.

Convex slope to 5m wide gull, dark silty to light gray-yellow, at least 6" deep. Rare pebbles, cobblestones occasional, shading to ground 90%. Quercus rubra: 83 rings,50cm at 45m height upslope. Basal area: 200 sq ft/acre. Fallen logs common. Listed by DNR forestry as old growth.
Wind blown sand from washboard ridges due north up canyon from root river, sand loose, easily crumbles and slumps. 38 year old Quercus ellipsoidalis, 38cm at base. Open sand 15-25% of substrate.
Dry dolomite gravel, numerous cobblestones. 20% woody invasion in community.
Shale capped ridge of St. Peter sandstone with loess mantle. Edmund silt loam. Eroded.

Designated and signed old growth site in Pillsbury State Forest near Gull Lake. Photos of plot and soil. Ground: all pine needles and cones with old logs and burned stumps. Sandy humus over sand. Steep slope.

Soil: humus with sandy clay over wet brown sand. Ground cover: deciduous leaf duff. Rare moss on decaying wood. No stumps but blowdown common. Aspen DBH approximately 10". Oak wilt on leaves. Aspen stand with oak, maple, birch, basswood.

Soil: sandy humus over brown sand. Few old charred stumps. <5% blowdown. Ground: needles over feathermoss. Hunting trail through stand, little other human influence apparent. Covers top, slope, base of 1:2 hill.

Ground: moss(95% sphagnales,5% bryales), hummocky. Soil: nothing returns in sampler, but can feel going through mat of roots. Chamaedaphne the dominate shrub, Eriophorum spissum the dominate graminoid. Fills entire basin; surrounded on all sides by aspen. Surrounded by coarse sedge (Carex cf. aquatilis) in moat. Potentilla palustris also present but not in plot. Little disturbance, no stumps or trails. Wet – standing water in pools.
Soil: sandy humus over coarse (few pebbles) brownish-red sand. Ground cover of pine needles. 20% deadfall and logs/debris. Scant moss (collected).

Cover: 70% moss (90% sphagnales, 10% bryales), 10% deadfall, 15 % cedar leaves, 5% pools. Soil: peat.  Stumps very old, rotted--not appearing cut. 2 beaver-cut stumps. DBH (cm): White cedar-12.6, 11.6, 16.
Stunted black spruce and tamarack with ericaceous shrubs and cottongrass hummocks. Ground cover: Sphagnum 100% (collected). Much more black spruce than larix. Species poor. Soil: wet peat.

Species-poor wet mature black spruce stand with dense ericaceous layer and Smilacina trifolia in hollows. Sphagnum throughout. Some layering of black spruce. No larix in stand here. DBH(cm): Black Spruce-15,20,25.

Plot just on east side of outlet on southwest side of very small lake. Ground: 100% moss-covered; all Sphagnum (collected). Deadfall approximately 5%. DBH (cm): white cedar-17,12,20 balsam fir-10. Soil: wet peat, only a few inches returned in sampler.

Ground: 1 large stump; moss-covered logs with water pools between. 5% blowdown, 20% leaf litter (cedar), 75% moss (20% sphagnum, 80% bryales). Soil: peat. Representative white cedar DBH (cm):16.6,19.1,24.2.

Maple-basswood on blackduck point. Ground: all deciduous leaf duff. 5% logs and stumps- very old, well-decayed. Plot approximately flat, top of ridge. DBH (cm): Tilia americana- 27.4,17.5; Acer saccharum-50.8,23.9,37.4; Populus grandidentata-52.7. Soil: few inches loam over wet tan sandy clay.

In tall white pine forest on interior of south part of Cedar Island. Island mostly hardwood with ridge of pine/fir. Ash at north end of island. Ground cover in pine needles and deciduous leaves throughout, ~10% blowdown. Soil: few inches sandy loam over tan sand. DBH(cm): white pine-43.6, 45.1, 28.8(dead), 35.4(dead), 33.6, 40, 48.1, 57.6; Balsam fir-11.6, 11.3, 13.4; Basswood-12.9, Bur oak-33, 15.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Very decayed burned stumps in plot. Ground cover: deciduous leaf duff. 5% blow-down. Soil: sandy loam over tan sand. DBH (cm): Sugar maple-28,21.7,20.4,29,29.6,13,21,24.5,22.5,15.3; Basswood-14,16.2,31.9,19.4,22.6,25.8,28.3; Paper birch-30.3,33.

In maple basswood stand on hardwood part of Leech Lake. Laportea throughout, some shoulder high. Ground cover: deciduous leaf cover throughout. Moss(collected) rare-on logs only. 10% blowdown. Soil: 2 inch sandy loam over fine tan moist sand with slight clay component. DBH(cm); sugar maple-20,49,29; black ash-26.5,30.

Not a large cedar type--just cedar inclusion in tamarack swamp. Moss: 75% of plot; all sphagnum. <5% deadfall. Water pools-25% plot. Soil: wet peat to length of core. DBH(cm): white cedar-22.2, 5.7,15.2,11.6; black spruce-18.7,7.0,9.8,2.8; tamarack-20.6,8.4,11.4,13.5.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Oak 5-5(phase 2). Oak in superstory; maple, basswood, ironwood beneath. Open, few tall shrubs. Deciduous leaf duff throughout. Gentle relief within plot, small, low rises, shallow dips. 5-10% deadfall. Moss rare on logs(collected). 10-20 meters from vernal pool, within sight of Egg Lake. Soil: 3 cm loam over tan sand with clay component(some molding).

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Thumb island in Meadowbrook wild life management area. Ground: all deciduous leaf duff; 5-10% deadfall. Moss: almost none, little bryales on logs. Scant slope in plot, but island slopes down to surrounding marsh and swamp. Oak forest being replaced with maple-basswood. Soil: 2-3cm sandy loam over tan sand with slight clay component.

Russell property. Oak with lots of aspen, maple and birch with strong hazel understory. Ground cover: deciduous leaf duff throughout. 5-10% deadfall. Soil: 2 cm sandy loam over coarse tan sand with moderate clay component. DBH(cm): Red maple- 24.5, 16.8; Red oak - 16.1, 29.8, 28; Bur oak - 46.8; Quaking aspen - 48.2, 56.2(dd); American elm-11.3.

County forest inventory lists stand as 054. Stand is oak with birch. Plot east of Green Lake, on hill just east of road and approximately 1st corner south of public landing. Ground cover: all deciduous leaf duff, small branches. Small logs approximately 5% cover. County st.#26. Soil: 2-3 cm sandy loam over tan sand; a few pebbles towards bottom, gravel when sample is approximately 30cm. Small amount of moss on logs and tree bases.

Oak 54 type on Spider Lake road. Mix of oak, maple, birch, red pine, bigtooth aspen, white pine. On hill overlooking small wet meadow. Ground: all deciduous leaf duff. 5-10% cover dead branches, small-moderate DBH logs. Small amount of moss on decaying logs only. Soil: 2 cm sandy loam/organics over tan moist coarse sand.

Ground: 10% deadfall, 90% moss; of moss,70% bryales, 30% sphagnum. Tamarack in abundance to west--pure tamarack just west of plot; cedar mostly small DBH, none large, some 10-15 cm. pH 7.5. Soil: soppy peat to the length of sampler (~50cm). DBH(cm): Larix-13.2, 21.3; Thuja-7,6.8,11.

Releve at west edge of cedar at seeps--where tamarack begins. Ground: old moss-covered logs; hollows/seeps are approximately 1/4 plot; iron-colored water; springy ground. pH 7.8. Soil: peat >50 cm, the length of sampler. Ground cover: 20% pine needles, 80%moss; of moss 20% Sphagnum/80% Bryales.

Red pine stand with white pine; being replaced by maple basswood. Ground: pine needles. 2 moss-covered stumps, very decayed. Scant moss--only on trees, stumps (coll). <5% blowdown. Soil: 2-3 cm of loamy sand over fine tan sand the length of sampler (~50cm). DBH(cm): red pine-28,32,33.8,32; paper birch-27, 30.6; white pine-20.2; red maple-12.

Ground: needle duff and blowdown (mostly branches). Moss: scant; only on tree bases and old logs (coll). Soil: 2 cm sandy loam over fine brown sand over fine tan sand. DBH(cm): white pine-28.5, 32.8, 30.4, 16.9, 30.5; red pine-84.8, 71.8 (representative).

Soil: saturated peat. Ground cover: 5% pools, 5% logs/branches(occasional moss covered logs), 90% moss (80% sphagnum, 20% bryales). pH 7.8. DBH(cm): black spruce-13.8, 11.9, 15.3; white cedar-6.5, 13.6, 12.
Soil: saturated peat to the length of sampler (~50cm). Ground cover: 5% decaying logs, 5% pools with moss; 90% moss(90% Sphagnum, 10% Bryales). pH 7.9.

Ground cover: 5% pools, 95% moss (80% sphagnum, 20% bryales). 10% of plot with decaying logs, stumps. Soil: saturated peat most of core; dry peat last 4-5cm. pH 7.4. DBH(cm): Paper birch-8.2; White cedar-10.2, 12.8, 19.8, 7.0, 14.5, 12.6; Black spruce-9.2; Balsam fir-11.0.

Cedar swamp with Balsam Fir; Sphagnum on ground.  Leaning trees, blowdown, Usnea on fir branches. Moss: 50% Sphagnum, 50% Bryales. Soil: saturated peat to end of sampler. Gound  cover: moss over branches, logs with pool.

Larger diameter white cedar (THAN 4442) with less blowdown, shrubby layer and small trees. Some moss-covered logs and very old moss-covered stumps. Trees mostly straight. Gound cover: 20% cedar needles, 80% moss (50% Sphagnum/50% Bryales). Soil: saturated peat. DBH(cm): white cedar-31.6, 20.8, 21.2, 23.5, 23.0, 30.4; balsam fir-22.6,11.3.

Plot probably in site of ephemeral pool. Water gone now, but leaves damp, compressed. Yellow birch(mature) and few mature cedar in stand. Soil: clayey loam over light gray sand with clay component. DBH(cm): basswood-39.5; sugar maple-60, 37. Ground: bare 10%, deciduous leaf duff 90%. Moss on trees and decaying logs only.

Ground cover: all deciduous leaf duff with decaying logs (approximately 20%). Moss only on logs and bases of trees. Soil: 3-4 inches of loam over fine gray-brown sand with strong clay component. DBH(cm): yellow birch-47.5; basswood-60.5, 38, 60.5; fraxinus nigra-27.2; sugar maple-11.5,33.4 (boles op).

In stand with strong birch component, lots of that is yellow birch. Releve placed to capture yellow birch. Plot is atop a knoll. Some cedar in stand and adjacent maple basswood. In Cnf comp 88, stand 12. Ground cover: 40% blowdown – several large yellow birch logs. Deciduous leaf duff throughout, scattered Bryales on logs. Soil: few inches sandy loam over very fine tan sand with small clay component. DBH(cm): yellow birch-25.2,22,31; sugar maple-22.5.

Red pine stand along Deerfield trail. Larry Olson (Cass county land department) reports that stand is thinned approximately every 10 years. Phase 2: np57. Ground: all needle duff. Moss on stumps. <5% blowdown (branches). County st#5. Soil: 2 inches sandy loam over moderately coarse tan sand with pebbles.

Ground cover: deciduous leaf duff; 10% blowdown, partly decayed logs. Scant moss at base of trees. Birch with oak between 2 small lakes. Many birch dead or dying (sparse tops). On pine mountain forest road. Soil: 3 inches sandy loam over coarse dark sand with pebbles.
Ground cover: 5% needles, bark, 95% moss (90% sphagnum, 10% bryales). 25% logs, branches. Soil: saturated peat. pH 7.4. DBH(cm): white cedar-24, 17.8, 22.9, 6.8, 6.5, 26.8, 17.5, 17.7.

In band of cedar between black ash and tamarack.  Ground cover: 90% moss(25% sphag, 75% bryales), 10% blowdown. Few very old moss-covered stumps. Frequent empty pools. Soil: Saturated peat. DBH(cm): White cedar-23.2, 25.8, 31.6, 22, 33.6, 28.8, 29.7.

Very hummocky. 10% blowdown. No pools; no water accumulation. Usnea on black spruce. Releve in hole-in-bog scientific and natural area north of trail to lake in densest black spruce seen. Soil: no returns in sampler, saturated peat? Ground cover: 100% moss (90% Sphagnum/10% Bryales).
Farther west of 93-47; south of trail. Within sight of hole-in-bog lake. Ground cover: 100% moss (90% sphagnum, 10% bryales). Soil: saturated peat, almost nothing returns. pH: 3.8. State stand #2.

Tamarack with black spruce in understory.  Full of water courses, moss-covered logs, and Sphagnum hummocks.  Moss: 50% Sphagnum, 50% Bryales. Soil: saturated peat, only a few cm return.  pH 6.7. Moss: 50% sphagnum, 50% bryales.
Ground: Sphagnum hummocks throughout; few pools of water; < 5% blowdown.  100% moss cover--all sphagnum.  Usnea on branches. pH 3.7. Soil: Wet peat – no returns.
Ground: all Sphagnum hummocks and hollows.  Water at surface in game trails, footprints.  pH: 4.0.  DBH(cm): picea-8.1, 9.3; larix-7.3, 11.1.
Ground cover: blowdown, tipups 50%; moss 50% (50% sphagnum, 50% bryales). Soil: saturated fibrous peat. pH 7.3.
Ground cover: 70% moss. Hummocky; old moss-covered logs and stumps. Soil: saturated peat. DBH (cm): thuja-23, 12; larix-16; picea-11.

Ground: occasional stumps of burned jack pine approximately 5.9 cm DBH. Open patches of sand approximately  one foot in diameter over approximately 25% of area; rest of vegetation shoots of Andropogon gerardi. Managed prairie. See site notes for more info. Soil: sand with loam over thin medium tan sand.

Maple basswood with strong birch and oak component. Lots of Dirca and Carex pensylvanica. Maple coming up beneath. Rolling hills, gentle to steep slopes. Ground cover: 95% deciduous leaf duff; 5% dead birch branches, logs-some very decayed. Scant moss on rare bare ground. Soil: sandy loam with slight clay component over light tan sand with slight clay component.
Representative of more open part of bog on southwest end.  Very wet, relatively flat; few large Sphagnum hummocks; pH 4.2; black spruce 8-10 cm DBH; 129 years old (forest inventory).
Wet prairie facies, on mineral soil only about 100 meters north of woods.
Oak woodland at crest of south-facing slope along Middle River.
C quality mesic prairie northwest, about 1 acre in size.
Mesic prairie NW.
Mesic prairie SW?
Mesic prairie NW, B-C quality.
Robertson tract goes with EO #3. General EO quality on tract in C, this releve is better mesic prairie NW. Rich transition fen? Southwest of opening into willow carr.
Area has been burned (apparently a couple years ago), creating dead d3-4 layer.  Soil 5" black fine sandy loam over light grey fine sand. See also species list #9404.
Multi structure stand, very messy low wet aspen woodland.  Soil: A horizon 5" fine sandy loam, black; b horizon light grey fine sand.
Lowland hardwood. Interbeach area.
Black spruce swamp. On photo open area spruce are 10-12cm DBH, widely scattered, gray pattern on photo.
Very open area of tamarack swamp dominated by continuous bog birch and ericads with abundant Potentilla fruticosa.  Minerotrophic ground layer. Unusual floristic assemblage.  Post fire community?
Black spruce bog. Site directly north of midpoint of channelized section of Moose River. Very dense mat ericacious shrubs with little ground layer diversity.
Thief Lake Wildlife Management Area.
See also species list #9403. This releve is associated with black spruce swamp NC.13 which is mapped in the adjacent section as part of a complex. Thief Lake Managed Area.
Boreal hardwood conifer forest.
Much natural blowdown deadfall. Similar community both sides of bull-dozer trail. Level, low.

Oak woodland along railroad track, approximately 10 degrees northwest on 2 1/2" friable black loam over approximately 16" fine black sand underlain by fine brown sand (immediately adjoins prairie remnants on same soil and topographic position).
Area with red signature on photo, level low mixed woods on leslie torgerson land.  Selective logging about 20 or more years ago. Not stereotypic black ash swamp. This is to define boundary.

Maple stand unusual in being on 2" loamy brown forest soil over fine grey brown sand surrounded by lowland hardwoods.  Area sheep grazed 30 years ago. Light area north of here wetland impounded by beaver dam.
Open mesic prairie (probably old hay meadow).
Band of brush prairie between 2 upland forests. Open grown oak with mature aspen. Band of sinuous shape, fairly even edges--anthropogenic origin?
Mesic prairie NW.
Some question in my mind whether this is degraded native prairie or has been cultivated and allowed to go back soon after being broken.  No furrows can be felt underfoot.
Water depth 0.25m, saturated muck 0.25m. Pool fed by runoff and seepage springs on alluvium of Crooked Creek.
Emergent marsh on solid sand substrate forming delta from alluvial deposits of ravine. Water level varies due to depressions and water's edge. Organic mud over sand.

Old-growth northern hardwoods on south facing slope below and to east of tower. Adjacent and surrounding tower recently clearcut. Very few yellow birch observed this far north. Ground: herbaceous-50%, deadfall-5%, litter-50%.
Cedar beginning to close in, but prairie still in between individual trees. Average height 3m. New house built on east end of prairie. Owners want to protect prairie themselves.

Open grown white oaks indicate site overgrown woodland. Steep east facing slope with openings on crest, brushier at base. Fine textured loam. No cut stumps, no tip ups but woody debris in place, no trails. Broad spreading Quercus alba average DBH 40-45cm.

30 x 10 meter opening on south facing slope by railroad tracks. Best of several but small, being invaded by oaks and sumac. Soil coarse sand alluvium with cobbles. Bare ground 10%. Oak leaf litter. Past fire.

Edge of opening. Quercus ellipsoidalis (some dd), Rhus glabra with Populus tremuloides, Zanthoxylem above. Rank based on high presence of exotic species. 3 photos, bw--c.converse. Sandy soil with medium-size gravel evenly distributed throughout.

>600 individual Polenesia jamesii entire site. Not found under Calamovilfa. Edge of opening Quercus ellipsoidalis, Robinia pseudoacacia. Rank based on disturbance level, few exotics but low diversity, reduced forb component. Photo-1bw-c.converse. Sandy soils with medium sized gravel distributed throughout.

Remnant of what was once a much larger white pine stand. Large trees to 70cm DBH in ravine, young pines common. Standing pine snags occasional. Soil mostly sandy glacial outwash with gravel. Besseya bullii uncommon here. Surrouned by mixed hardwood forest.

Beautiful mesic stand with large Quercus rubra, Acer rubrum located on terrace of east facing slope above and 75m from Chub Lake. Trees mostly single-stemmed. Deadfall of all sizes. Quercus rubra rare elsewhere. Near property boundary. Soil is silt loam.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Sandy loam on 20m colluvium slope of flat-topped limestone mesa. Canopy Quercus rubra 40-55cm, Tilia americana 30cm DBH. Typical of much of east north-facing slopes. Rhamnus cathartica present but not too alarming. Oak leaf and scattered woody litter to 12cm.

Thin soils, scattered limestone outcrops up to 0.5m. Surrounding prairie area filling in with Junipus, Populus tremuloides above and below with Quercus macrocarpa gnarled, widely spaced in surrounding area.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: White pine relic on north and east-facing slopes on 100 foot bluff above Trout Brook in Miesville Ravine. Pines mostly near crest of slope. Young pines infrequent. Large trees to 70 cm DBH. Pasture adjacent. Slope: above crest – 12 degrees, below crest – 25 degrees. Some deadfall. Few large Pinus strobus snags in vicinity. Pinus strobus DBH: 19-60cm.
2/3 of way upslope. Limestone outcrops 5% cover--very scattered up to 1/2 m2. Gravel and boulders. Soil thin, sandy with rocks. Thatch buildup, needs a burn. Moss and lichens on rocks.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Limestone cliffs scattered along ridge. Loamy/sand soil. Recent windfall (spring '93), many large trees or branches broken off with dead brown leaves. Ground: thin oak leaf litter, moderate amount woody litter, range of sizes.
Mesic prairie on slightly saline, sandy loam soils on minor beach line a half mile west of major beach ridge of Glacial Lake Agassiz.
Wet prairie on very gradual west facing slope just west of Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridge. Appears virtually undisturbed. Brush cover quite variable and consists primarily of Betula glandulifera.
Wet prairie in shallow swale on nearly level terrain 1/4 mile west of a beach line of Glacial Lake Agassiz.  Swale oriented perpendicular to beach ridge.

Prairie dominated by halophytic species on moderate saline soils in wide zone along east edges of shallow, wet swales on very gradual west-facing flank of Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridge. Small patches of bare, black soil with white marl precipitate on surface.

Mesic prairie on nearly level soils at base of major beach ridge of Glacial Lake Agassiz. Probably has been hayed and lightly grazed in past. Grades westward into halophytic prairie zone and shallow wet prairie swales.
Wet-mesic prairie on very shallow slope west of Glacial Lake Agassiz beach ridge. In mosaic with wet prairie. Found a few individuals of Tofieldia glutinosa here.
Saline subtype of wet to mesic prairie in broad zones bordering very subtle swales on level terrain in interbeach area of Lake Agassiz lacustrine plain.
Patch of dry prairie on top of isolated, small, sandy knoll surrounded by dense aspen oak woodland and rich fen.
Rich fen on buoyant floating mat with dense moss layer. Site in excellent condition.

Wet prairie saline subtype in shallow, elongate depression with elevated soil salts. Several patches bare soils with white marl precipitate present. Just north of foot of beach ridge oriented east-west.

Releve in "A" quality portion of mesic prairie on level fine sandy loam soils. Situated close to small area of increased salinity vegetated with halophytes. On nearly level terrain at foot of east-west oriented beach ridge.
Former wet brush prairie, now overgrown with young aspen. Disturbance history not obvious, but unused for some time. Soil a sandy loam over loamy sand.
In area of wet to wet-mesic brush prairie, becoming overgrown with aspen. Several recent fires. Soil a sandy loam becoming loamy fine sand, then gravelly at approximately 25 cm.

Largest aspen 42-43cm DBH. 2 large spruce approximately 15m southwest of plot, larger 48cm DBH, >20m high. Many younger spruce in vicinity. Extensive block of forest-woodland. Spruce rare on Kittson side, more common on Roseau side.

Several snags in plot, few logs on ground. 1 recently dead tree. No signs recent fire. Soil 6-10cm dark sandy loam over fine sand. Largest trees approximately 25cm. Part of fairly large block of woodland. No evidence of grazing.

Several fallen dead trees in plot, recent to old. Charcoal on old snags; no recent fire. Approximately 10cm black, fine sandy loam over loamy fine sand. Largest trees 26-27cm DBH. Part of fairly large block woodland. No evidence of grazing.
Total woody cover  50-60%. Generally more brush here than in plot. No evidence of recent grazing disturbance. Plot on broad, low, linear upland feature trending northwest; in percy soils map unit.
Dry-mesic brush thicket, formerly savanna but growing in. On sand spit of Glacial Lake Agassiz shoreline. Soil brownish gray loamy sand over brown coarse sand.
Mesic brush thicket with scattered tree-size individuals. Mostly aspen, but a large, multiple-stemmed bur oak near plot. On sand spit of Glacial Lake Agassiz. Soil a sandy loam or loamy sand.
Mesic brush thicket with scattered tree-size individuals. On tip of old shoreline sandspit of Glacial Lake Agassiz. Soil a sandy loam or loamy sand.
Moist to wet woods dominated by mature trees. Lots of down logs, some quite large, various stages of decay. Becomes wetter east of plot. No evidence of past cutting or fire.
Within moderately large block of woodland dominated by mature aspen. Largest tree in plot: 28.5 cm DBH, most 20-25 cm. Soil a silt loam over sand. Probably mesic conditions.
More open part of mod large woodland area. Apparently wet-mesic. Soil a thin layer black sandy loam over light brown sand.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: Narrow band of black ash swamp along what appears to be seepage zone on very slight southwest slope. Soil approximately 20 cm black muck over sand. Old fence indicates past grazing. Largest ash in plot 40 cm DBH.

Mesic woodland on very slight slope, here dominated by mature aspen; fairly dense shrub layer. Part of large block of woodland with boreal forest elements. Large woody debris scarce. Soil light grayish-brown fine sand.
35% bare sand in releve; 50% leaf litter cover. Soil loamy sand with <5% gravel fraction. Prairie managed with brush cutting and burning. Hiking trails, some disturbed areas.

Loess-derived soil on ridge top above oak woodland and bluff prairie. Was cropland until about 1968.  About 30 meters west of forest edge. Dry-mesic prairie. Soil: clayey silt loam moist at present, loess-derived.
Dolomite outcrops and exposed bedrock 2% cover. Plot on lower slope of bluff prairie. Soil thin silt loam.

One of the best areas of mesic white oak forest that occurs on knolls at south end of wildlife management area. Several white oaks >50 cm DBH, formerly open-grown. Old vehicle trail. Probably past selective cutting. Typical.

Plot on west side of steep, eroded, dead-end trail. Typical, though red pine more often dominate. One large old stump. Boulders. Lumpy surface microtopography. Fairly thick needle duff. Good abundance and patterning of herbs.

Natural submature/mature mesic oak stand. Recent tip-ups and much down birch from wind on high hill. Probably best example left(and typical). Sheltered slope with oak at 40 cm DBH. Boulders in cobbly red till.

Beautiful mature mesic oak forest, trees 40-60cm DBH. Much Carex pensylvanica suggests past disturbance; good diversity overall. Presently trails and camping use. Typical of moraine; kame. Plot near swamp. See species list 940.

Mature oak forest on gravelly stagnation moraine. Plot on relatively mesic, species-rich slope. Some slopes with many tip-ups. Here, trees relatively large, 30-40cm DBH, fine canopy composition, overall flora typical.
Beautiful fen. Difficult to assess graminoid cover but Carex lasiocarpa is dominate. Forbs patchy and very small. Area typical of entire wetland, I think, and typical of this part of Morrison county.
Site actually on the beach ridge, not on the moraine. Soil landscape map not detailed enough. Area lightly grazed.

Releve from widest level area on top of hill. Because formerly pastured area not the "best" in terms of dominance by native grasses but most convenient to lay 10x10 plot in homogeneous area. Needs fire.
Site on beach ridge, not moraine. Soil landscape map not detailed enough.
Generally the low shrub layer is so dense that ground layer is sparse, mainly leaf litter. Large DBH stumps, estimated cutting >20 years ago. Releve on point between 2 cleared areas.
At least 2" black fine sandy clay loam (A) on light brown fine sandy clay.
Level, 1" black fine sandy clay loam (A) over 2" light brown fine sandy clay, sandier than at DNR releve 4676. Underlain by same fine clay as at DNR releve 4676.
Slope 20 degrees southwest at top grading to 5 degrees at bottom between mixed oak- maple at top of slope and black ash swamp at foot. Soil 5" black clay loam on dark brown heavy clay.

Soil 5" black clay loam on dark brown heavy clay. Soils in this general area are very heavy. Band of better quality community on slope of otherwise degraded hill--formerly grazed. Slope: 15-20 degrees north.
No signs of cutting--releve on flat area at southeast end of lake.

3" black clay loam over 6" light brown fine sandy clay with sand fraction becoming coarser downward. Too little dead and down. Gentle northwest facing at north end otherwise gently rolling stand. Very shaded forest floor.

Patchy quality, overall C quality due to abundant trails and small size--apparent clearance shrub layer in places. No Zanthoxylum but hard to get into area not dominated by Carex pensyvanica. Best maple stand on Maple Lake.
On round hill near center of site. Inclusion with more maple and basswood than surrounding area. Lack of D2-4 layer probably caused by heavy deer activity.
Fair amount deadfall away from road and area that has had understory cleared for campgrounds. Soil 2 1/2" black loam over 3" fine silty sand over heavy brown clay.
Not more than 100 meter south of lakeshore road, despite canopy species community feels like lowland hardwood--may be a facies of maple basswood north of ATV trail.
Grazed. Good diversity of prairie forbs, but graminoids are degraded. Actually on beach ridge, not moraine. Soil landscape map not detailed enough.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Beautiful, mature, but small forest on Fish Trap Lake. No evidence of recent cutting. Tip-up craters, coarse debris, multi-stem trees frequent due to unstable gravelly soil, typical of St. Croix moraine.

Good expansive meadow/willow swamp system; ditching to north and west might lower water table. Attempted ATV use on deer/hunter trails from knoll to knoll. Only example remaining. Rare. Most meadows converted to hayfields.

Good undisturbed vegetation in south 1/2 sec. 30 on alluvium (drained to north west). Primarily wet meadow (see releve 4688), willows and aspen rises.  A few tamarack but fen/peat development minor (though occurs in sec 31).

Releve in small 15x20m opening in overgrown savanna on sand; better than most. Along short trail connecting road to cultivated field. Cirsium hillii. Probably past grazed. Has recovery potential. Needs burn.

Narrow wet-mesic praire zone 3-5m wide between mesic prairie(disked 7/26/94) and wet meadow/willow swamp. On sandy beach or ice-push ridge parallel to mainland at edge of expansive wet mead. Rare. Should protect. Needs burn.

Releve near dry northwest edge of old-field knoll, 5-10 m from shrub/aspen margin. Good recovery from probable past cultivation. Low diversity of typical prairie species may be natural in these isolated openings.

Hastily prepared. Knoll unusual in lacking Andropogon gerardii and Poa pratensis (both occur near mainland to south and in releve 4692 nearby). Intended for comparison sake. Medium-textured sandy soil. Saw no fencelines/old posts.
Mature/old growth northerhardwood forest. No recent disturbance; good FHD.  No snags, few down logs. On hill top. DBH of 2 typical sugar maples: 35.5 and 43.2 cm. DNR forestry stand #12, NH 54.

Very narrow zone of highly productive, dense vegetation about 0.5m lower than Phalaris-dominatedridge trail. Ecotonal between higher zones (mostly destroyed wet to mesic prairie) and Calamagrostis/Carex wet meadow.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: CSA stand age 53 years. Red oak (30cm DBH, BA=100) with sugar maple (8-18cm, BA =25). Minor cutting of oak. Old pine stump. Much debris on ground. Tip-up mound. Thick leaf litter. Soil: <50cm sandy loam; >50cm loamy sand.

Fire-protected? slope on north end of island dominated by red oak (50-72cm DBH, BA=25) or basswood (30-40cm DBH, BA=100) often clumped. Also sugar maple (2-7cm DBH BA=25). Much coarse woody debris and tip-up mounds. 5cm leaf litter, Soil: sandy loam/loamy sand.
Plot in area with Carex diandra, atypical of this part of sedge meadow.

12 acre woodlot. Large trees: red oak 65cm DBH, basswood 78cm, sugar maple 20-30cm. Owner claims no grazing, but dead trees removed for firewood. Good spring flora. Dense D-layer 1.3-5m high. Much leaf litter, but patches of bare soil and boulders. Soil: 0-5cm black loam, >5 cm tan silty loam with fine sand.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: CSA stand age = 74yrs. Quercus rubra 20-52cm DBH, Populus grandidentat 48cm, Fraxinus americana 15cm, Acer saccharum 4-12cm. No disturbance in releve but high-grading of oak in stand? Dense oak leaf litter. Red-brown sandy loam with pebbles to 20cm. Releve representative of McGrath Till Plain in St. Croix state forest.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Patchy oak forest with brushy openings, stumps: high grading of oak. Aspen patches present in stand but not in releve. CSA stand age=62 years. Grazing history unknown. Soil: sandy loam.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: On peninsula in wetland. Large clumped red oak (modal DBH 36cm, BA=30) and basswood (25cm DBH, BA=40), with sugar maple (9-29cm DBH, BA=40). CSA age=74yrs. Many charred pine stumps. 0-25cm:loam. >25cm: sandy loam with pebbles. Boulders present. Upper-middle slope.
Gappy canopy. Red oak 30-50cm DBH, BA=85; Trembling aspen 36cm DBH, BA=7; Bur oak 12cm DBH; Red maple 9cm DBH. No disturbance except old pine stumps. Soil red-brown loamy sand.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: CSA stand age 63 years. Red oak 26-38cm DBH, BA=35; basswood 16-34cm DBH, BA=50. Much recent dead paper birch. Ground dominated by Amphicarpa bracteata (from past grazing? agricultural land nearby). Ground surface uneven. Soil: sandy loam.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: CSA stand age = 52 years. Red oak 23-48cm DBH, BA=80; white oak 30cm DBH BA=30; sugar maple 6-14cm DBH, BA=10. Ground uneven with tip-up mounds. No disturbance except old pine stumps. Sandy clay loam over sandy loam.
On ridge surrounded by wetlands. CSA stand age = 67 years. Red oak 25-37 cm DBH, BA=70; quaking aspen 30-42cm DBH, BA=50. Very dense overstory, sparse understory. Soil sandy loam.
Small isolated wetland in loamy sand outwash. Releve typical of sedge area with some shrubs succeeding towards poor fen. Tamarack 35m to east. Peat > 0.9m.
On small ridge between two lowlands. CSA stand age = 76 years. Red oak 15-42cm DBH, BA=80; Red maple 10-35cm DBH, BA=25. No disturbance except numerous large pine stumps. Soil loam, denser at 40cm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Representative of oak stands on undulating topography with low mesic areas and shallow hills. Canopy of large red oak, modal DBH 35cm, BA=35; subcanopy of sugar maple modal DBH 19cm, BA=50. Soil: Silt loam, very dense at 30cm. No disturbance except old pine stumps.
Representative of small cedar swamp surrounding tamarack pocket at base of steep slope along Lake Tamarack River. White cedar 13-32cm DBH, > 75 years. pH = 7.0, peat > 0.9m.
Small cedar stand in center of black ash swamp. Numerous water filled hollows. pH = 7.1, Peat > 0.9m. Balsam fir dying out in canopy but reproducing in canopy gaps. Much blowdown in area.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Mixed stand of black ash (15-25cm DBH, BA=70) with cedar (25-30cm DBH, BA=75, 120 yrs) predominate in subcanopy. Very wet with numerous pools with red brown precipitate. pH=6.3, peat>0.9m. Extensive blowdown and leaning cedar.

Mixed swamp between mineral island and ash swamp. Patchy canopy filled with black ash and balsam fir. Scattered windthrow and leaning trees. Cedar (25-38cm DBH, BA=70, 110 yr) Black ash (10-22cm DBH, BA=35). pH=6.1, peat > 1m. Shallow pools.

Extensive stagnant cedar swamp grading to ash swamp. High BA but very sparse foliage and small tree crowns. Cedar (10-20cm DBH, BA=130, 105yrs). Black ash (10-15cm DBH, BA=10). Very wet with deep pools. pH=6.4, Peat > 1m.

Black ash (17-48cm DBH, BA=45) sparse crowns, several dead; yellow birch (11-40cm DBH, BA=35). Near base of slope along abandoned terrace along St. Croix State Park. Peat > 1m. Water table below surface.

On slightly fluted alluvium next to Kettle River. Bur oak 18-60cm DBH, BA=65; basswood 17-33cm DBH, BA=70. Trees clumped. Lack of shrubs and abundant Amphicarpa bracteata may indicate past grazing. Loam with pebbly loamy sand below 10cm.
Alluvial terrace next to Kettle River. Soil:  0-10cm silt loam, impenetrable > 10cm. Bur oak (11-40cm DBH, BA = 40).

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Sugar maple < 52cm DBH, BA = 95. No disturbance. Soil: 0-40cm = light brown loam; > 40cm = dense red-brown loam with pebbles.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: No disturbance. Much coarse woody debris and dead trees (BA=25). Sugar maple modal DBH 20cm, max 52cm, BA=55; red oak and paper birch modal DBH 30cm, BA=25. Soil loam with hard layer sandy loam and pebbles at 20-40.
Representative of ridgetops in northern hardwood stand. Sugar maple dominant in depressions. Soil loam; hardpan (?) with pebbles at 40cm. Slope: crest/upper.

Releve about 50m from edge of Carex rostrata mat surrounding Black Lake. Typical of outer edge of bog with increasing scattered and stunted Black spruce southward. pH=3.9. Peat > 1m. Area burned in 1936.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Tamarack overstory but mostly black ash understory. Stand in abandoned river channel; surrounded by black ash swamp. pH=5.6; peat>1.0m.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Good size class distribution: Acer saccharum 13-50cm DBH, BA = 50; Acer rubrum 19-55cm DBH, BA = 25. Downed Betula papyrifera and Abies balsimifera. Soil loam; hardpan (?) at 40cm.

Unusual appearance, very open with few shrubs; has wet-mesic species indicating ponding or seepage along slope. Acer saccharum 10-58cm DBH, BA=60; Acer rubrum 22-55cm DBH, BA=40. Soil loam and sandy loam with hardpan at 40cm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Releve at lower end of gentle slope, 80m from swamp. No disturbance. Stand on edge of pine barren island adjacent to abandoned river channel.
Loamy sand to fine sand plateau above St. Croix River near Rock Creek. Large pin oaks (20-53cm DBH, BA=73) with smaller bur oak (9-18cm DBH, BA=13). Single jack pine snag. No signs of disturbance.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Variable, diverse, and patchy canopy; at base of slope along St. Croix River escarpment. Plot in denser canopy area. Stumps and fence in area . Oak > 100 years. Jack pine and red pine nearby. Soil: loamy sand to sand.

Typical graminoid dominated floodplain forest by lower Kettle River. Releve between river and minor channel; including tall berm at river edge and large shallow depression; slope slightly from river. Soil: 0-5cm sandy clay; 0-70cm sand with sandy layers; >70cm gray-black coarse sand.

40m strip oak savanna east side of island in St. Croix River. Level terrace 4m above river. Bordered by 7m strip mesic prairie along river. Bur oak and ironwood woods to west. Soil: 7cm black sand, 7-30cm red brown sand; >30cm brown sand with fines.
Pin oak (16-35cm DBH, BA = 55) stand in jack pine barren area. Large charred pine stumps in area. Soil: 0-4cm dark loamy sand, 4-40cm red brown loamy sand, >40cm hard pan?

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Black ash overstory (30-58cm DBH, BA=100) with diverse subcanopy. Wet hollows. Soil: peat.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Relatively dry swamp at base of slope, west side of Lost Creek Swamp. Peat > 1m. Black ash (to 43cm DBH, BA=40); yellow birch and red maple (to 54cm DBH, BA (20,25).

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Releve represents infrequent moister lower slope in Nemadji State Forest. Sugar maple and basswood to 50 cm DBH, BA= 50, 40 respectively.
Mesic site, flat area near lowland (high water table). Sugar maple up to 36 - 53 cm DBH; BA=80; Basswood up to 28 - 57 cm DBH; BA=50.
Opening in jack pine "barrens" with aspen and Comptonia encroaching from edges. Few open-grown jack pine in openings. Probable grazing history before 1930s. Burned in 1970s.
Representative of opening in "jack pine barren". Occasional scattered jack pine including seedling-saplings. Probable grazing history before 1930s. Burned in 1970s.
Typical of pure Acer saccharinum dominated canopy along west side of St. Croix River. Location uncertain.
Representative of small (about 10acre) isolated peatland. Black spruce (10-17cm DBH, BA=100). Patchy canopy. Appears fairly ombrotrphic with few scattered minerotrphic indicators.
Representative of small (15acre) peatland basin. Tamarack (6-31cm DBH, BA=45).

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Very diverse hardwood swamp along abandoned channel; dominated by black ash (17-38cm (59) DBH, BA=50) and balsam fir (20-30cm, BA=50). Many old cut stumps in area but not releve. Canopy highly variable. Peat soil.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Red pine (23-45cm DBH, BA=80) with white pine (41-65cm DBH, BA=20) on plateau above Kettle River. Stand surrounded by variable mesic hardwoods.
Richer portion of tamarack swamp. See releve #4752 for adjacent tamarack stand. Tamarack (10-20cm DBH, BA=140). Formed in peatland in abandoned river channel.

Representative of narrow weakly minerotrophic portion of tamarack swamp by edge of black spruce bog. 45m west of richer part of tamarack swamp (see releve #82). Low sphagnum hummocks, no pools. Peatland formed in abandoned river channel.

Representative of spruce-fir area in lower areas, higher water table. Much standing dead balsam fir; more dead basal area than living: soil: 2cm duff with charcoal at base; 20-30cm wet gray loamy sand; 30-50cm red brown sand.
Mature stand on wet end of Mesic with ash and marsh nearby; Canopy very diverse with largely maple understory; graminoid layer and herb layer; little coarse woody debris.

Relatively undisturbed old growth maple basswood stand on southeast hilltop, surrounded by good quality mature maple basswood which has been selectively logged to north and west; Open understory with large pit and mound relief com. Much coarse woody debris of older decay(mor

Select logged Oak/Maple basswoods woods-oak logged out. Diverse tree and herb layer with shaded and open species present-converting to Maple Basswood, no oak regeneration. Numerous other species seen greater than 2m but nearly outside plot(more)

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Supposedly old growth, but doesn't look like it; dominated by younger age classes and no really old trees. Quercus alba with Quercus rubra and Tilia americana dominant. With Carya cordiformis and Acer Sacchrum in understory with Ostrya virginiana; herb layer diverse; Fraxinus nigra present in canopy rarely(more)

Mature Oak stand; Quercus rubra and Quercus alba co-dominant; with shagbark,Tilia americana, Acer saccharum, Ostrya virginiana in understory. Diverse herb layer; all size classes of trees represented. Ribes and Rubus species prevalent.

Good quality old growth. Oak, dominated by Quercus rubra with Quercus alba, Quercus macrocarpa and shagbark hickory prevalent in understory; Zanthoxylem present and herb layer dominated by various species of Rubus and Parthenocissus, which climbs to canopy(more

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: High quality old growth. Oak dominated; canopy species of Quercus rubra with some Quercus alba and Acer saccharum just making into canopy. Understory complete Acer saccharum and Ostrya virginiana with occassional Carya cordiformis & Tilia american. Sparse herb layer by cover but diverse by species. Large coarse woody debris(more).
