Logged oak woods with old stumps and Acer negundo. Dominated by Quercus rubra, Quercus macrocarpa, Carya cordiformis, and some Betula papyrifera, Parthenocissus along with brush; Ribes, Rubus and hazel creates brushy understory with open canopy & good young sapling layer;(more)

Quercus rubra dominated with Quercus alba in canopy. Diverse subcanopy and herb layer; Corollorhiza and Panax quinquefolia seen out of plot. Subcanopy of Tilia; Carya cordiformis; Ostrya virginiana and some Quercus rubra.

Old growth black ash with understory of black ash and occasional cedar. All age classes represented. Large coarse woody debris roots above water provide most of vegetative surfaces. Diverse, yet sparse herb layer and graminiod layer-collected moss(more).

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: No standing water; interrupted ash canopy with Ulmus americana, 7 Fraxinus nigra with Fraxinus nigra understory. Rich herb, graminoid and moss layers. Much large coarse woody debris of all DC's also many decaying root boles above muck. Species ID need QC.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Old growth Ash/Lowland Hardwood stand; Fraxinus nigra making a super canopy over Fraxinus nigra and Acer rubra; no ash in sapling layer. Moss and fern diverse and abundant; Elm in seedling layer.

One of several small openings in Quercus velutina and Pinus banksiana woodland on wind-blown sand deposit. 35% exposed sand; chunks of chert common. Oaks range from seedlings to small trees in savannah openings. Jack pines local here. Talinum larege, vigorous here, flowering at 6pm.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: Mesic to dry-mesic on steep slope along Root River. Pine DBHs 35-45cm; hardwoods 20-35cm. 42cm DBH pine with 114 rings. Canopy cover 70%. Stumps occasional, snags rare. Dark sandy loam, thin A-horizon; cobbles frequent. Dolostone/Dolomite outcrops frequent.

npc_type_name: Sugar Maple - Basswood - Red Oak - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Nice small (approximately 5 acres) Maple-Basswood stand on slope above Shattuck Creek. Next to white pine-hardwood forest. Scattered downfalls and rotten logs, occasional large snags. Canopy trees 40-60cm DBH. Relatively deep, dark loam soil. Possible old-growth. Good population of Dicentra canadensis down slope. Possible old growth stand? Tree core 53cm DBH Tilia, 1.5m high = 116 years old.

npc_type_name: Sugar Maple - Basswood - Red Oak - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Mature maple basswood forest. Canopy trees 35-59cm DBH. Some maples atop slope to 75cm DBH. Subcanopy Acer, Ulmus, Ostrya, Carpinus understory. Shrub layer sparse. Soil a deep dark silt. Snags and decaying logs occasional. 59cm DBH Quercus rubra cored at 115cm high = 118 years old.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: Small stand of pines surrounded by oak forest on steep slope above creek. Canopy trees: White pines 40-70cm DBH; Quercus rubra 30-40cm; Quercus alba 35cm; Acer saccharum 30-40cm. Thick needle duff, few stumps, occasional decaying logs. Soil clay loam, rocky, with outcrops. One 51cm Pinus strobus at 103 years.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mature forest on ridge-top grading into maple basswood forest down north side of slope and dry oak forest down southwest side of slope. Large trees to 80cm DBH(modal DBH 35-55cm). Rich forb layer, frequent decaying logs of all sizes, tip-ups occasional, rich clay loam. 52cm DBH Quercus rubra cored: 98 years old.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: 5-10 acres of pine among large areas of oak and maple basswood forest. Frequent stumps. Decaying logs of many sizes common. Canopy trees-Pines 45-70cm DBH(rare 95cm); Quercus alba 40-60cm; Quercus rubra 35-45cm; Tilia 30-45cm. 53cm DBH pine=109yrs. Thick needle duff; silty clay loam.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Sugar Maple - Basswood Forest (Cold Slope)
remarks: Narrow band of northern species on steep slope above cliff. Grades into maple basswood and oak forest upslope. Scattered algific vents. Canopy patchy due to slope, slope varies from 35-50 degrees. DBH ranges 25-40cm, Pinus strobus 30-50cm; Quercus rubra 30-40cm; Quercus alba 30-40cm; Acer saccharum 25-35cm; Tilia 25-30cm. Snags frequent (especially Pinus strobus), decaying logs  of various sizes frequent. Topographic context: upper/middle.

5-acre prairie on wind-blown sand deposit 2 miles southeast of Peterson and .25 miles south of hatchery. Much of site badly degraded by past grazing. Scattered Quercus velutina. Thick thatch, deep coarse/tan sand, unexposed.

place_name: N Branch Root R- Chatfield S
npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mesic oak forest codominated by Quercus rubra, Acer saccharum, and Tilia americana. Modal DBH 35-40cm, max to 50-65cm. Soil, type varies (mildly influenced by seeps at 1150 ft. elevation) mostly silt loam with some sandy colluvium lacking organic layer. Releve typical of best parts of stand (stand=C-rank) 65cm DBH Quercus rubra at 122 rings.

On lower slope of 200-ft northwest facing ridge system along Root Road. Canopy trees modal DBH 25-30cm, max 65cm. Soil with dark A-horizon, thick thatch layer. Adjacent dry prairie also on windblown sand. 33cm DBH Quercus cf. velutina x rubra 81 rings.

Wind-blown sand deposit on lower slope of northwest facing ridge system along Middle Branch Root River. Thick thatch in most places, little open sand. Some Pinus sylvestris plantations here. Owner working to restore prairie. Some adjacent areas burning this spring. Scattered Juniperus virginiana here. Good Lanius ludovicionus spot.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Dry-mesic forest dominated by Quercus rubra and Quercus alba. Canopy height 25-30m, cover = 80%. Modal DBH 40-50cm; no large trees. Decayed stumps common, tip-ups rare, snags occasional, debris scarce. Sandy loam soil.

Dry-mesic forest domianted by Quercus ellipsoidalis (cf velutina?). Modal DBH 30-40cm, max 40-50cm. Excellent forest soil; higher percent sand in A horizon and nearly absent in lower horizon. A-horizon dark organic clay silt, < 1inch thick. B-horizon yellowish loess with some sand.

Canopy trees 25-44cm DBH, modal DBH is 30-35cm. Snags rare, no stumps, decaying wood uncommon. Sandy wind blown soil with moderate humus layer. Plot extends onto level top of ridge. Tree core: 34cm Quercus velutina = 94 rings.
Representative of better areas, which are scattered throughout large area of prairie. Substrate varied, including Jordan sandstone, Oneota outcrop, loose sand. Soil: Brodale fine sandy cobbly loam.

In swale between prairie ridges. Canopy 80%; dominated by Quercus ellipsoidalis with Quercus macrocaropa. Modal DBH 46-54cm. Soil: Deep, dark sandy loam becoming clayey at 5". Representative of high-quality savanna (?) on prairie bluff.

Dominated by Schizachyrium scoparium and Sporobolus heterolopsis. Other bunchgrasses abundant. Soil dark sandy loam with cobbles and boulders. Few outcrops. Woody vegetation 25% cover but not thick: groves of Betula papyrifera and copses of Salix humilis.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: Mature forest (although small) with Pinus strobus of 45-65cm DBH modal and max to 73cm. 51cm DBH P. strobus = 101 years. Soil dark, mostly silty sand. Allium cernuum present. Impressive stand.

Narrow stand bordered by lower-quality forest. Canopy trees 35-67cm DBH. Large decaying log (Ulmus?) and abundant tip-ups frequent. No stumps. Occasional snags. Rich deep clay-loam, alluvial. 53cm Tilia=122 years. Cutting planned.
In area with several depressions at toe of north-to northwest-facing sandy slope(?) Soil wet-mesic with dry hummocks and ant mounds.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Rich maple basswood forest on extensive 300 foot north facing slope along Rush Creek. (forest on stream terrace, slope toe, lower slope, varying from 3-35 degrees). Soil rich deep organic silt. Rich herbaceous layer. 7 EOs at site.

On NW-facing terrace ridge-spur adjacent to swale-like ravines. Canopy cover 75%. Pinus banksiana 25-42 cm DBH common, max to 49cm rare. Substrate dune-like sand with some loam, exposed on 15% of plot. Plot samples series of open savanna on this landform. Pinus banksiana at 49cm DBH: 97 rings. Quercus ellipsoidalis at 46cm DBH: 110 rings.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Soil compacted silt, no organic layer. Modal DBH 25-35cm, rare to 56cm. Occasional stumps; decaying wood of various sizes common due to past cutting. Herb layer sparse due to thin compacted soil and dense shade. Shrub layer mostly absent. Richer ground layer lower slope but small trees.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: Along Root River on Hwy 16, 3 miles southwest of Peterson. Pinus strobus dominated DNR forestry stand on north and south facing slopes, ridgetop, and valley floor. 20-50cm DBH. Occasional decaying wood, snags. Stumps uncommon. Soil silty sand. Tree core: 48cm DBH Pinus strobus = 96 years.

Open water marsh in oxbow slough fed by seeps. Entire marsh borderd by wild rice. Seepage area dominated by Carex lacustris. Drainage to southeast into Canfield Creek through wet meadow dominated by Carex trichocapa with weedy composition and other forbs (Solidago, Eupatorium, Verbena, Impatiens).

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Dry-mesic forest on narrow ridge spur. Modal DBH 20-30cm; max 30-35cm common. Larger trees cut in past. Occasional debris and tip-ups. No snags. Soil yellowish silty loam (loess). Sinkholes and some cobbles present.
Talus present in association with 5-10m high Galena dolomite cliff. Talus composed of cobbles covered with thin layer of dark silty humus. 3-4 vents present. Stones very cold (35 deg F) and dripping.

In seepage area at base of ravine. Dominated by Fraxinus nigra: typical size = 8-25cm DBH, max 45-55cm. Herb layer dominated by Symplocarpus foetidus and Laportea canadensis. Permanent stack in northwest corner. Muck soil. Stake at northwest corner of plot. Plot includes some oak forest.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
permanent_plot_type_description: ex. metal tag on nearby tree
remarks: Dry-mesic forest dominated by Quercus rubra. Local Stand. Modal DBH 35-45cm; max 50-63cm. Other stands modeal DBH 25-30cmLarge trees nearly gone - stand of Populus grandidentata. Dense shade to substrate. Soil yellow silt loam; no A-horizon, little humus, duff (20% bare ground). Various mosses hold A-horizon, lacking elsewhere. 54cm Quercus rubra = 118 years.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mature mesic oak forest dominated by Quercus rubra with abundant Quercus alba. Modal DBH = 35-45cm; max 50-60cm common. Dense shade. Soil dark clay loam, compact, little organic matter. Basal area 140 square feet. Moisture approaches dry-mesic. 56cm Quercus rubra = 115 years. Old fence.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Sugar Maple - Basswood Forest (Cold Slope)
remarks: On northwest-facing very steep slope. Wet-mesic to dry-mesic. Soil organic colluvium with cobbles and talus. Several outcrops of Galena sandstone. Located upper-mid slope, east of cliff.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Blue Beech) Seepage Swamp
remarks: Tip-ups common. Flowing spring. Wet soil, no muck. Galena limestone outcrops and rocky talus present(?). Stake at southwest corner of plot. Some barbed wire imbedded in black ash(?).

npc_type_name: Sugar Maple - Basswood - Red Oak - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: 5-acre patch of nice forest on middle of 250ft slope along Riceford Creek (most of slope young, patchy). Trees 40-65cm DBH. Lush ground layer. Much debris; several old stumps. Soil relatively thin clay loam. Considerable debris on ground apparently wind damage. Several old stumps. Rock exposures rare.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mature mesic forest on lower part of 200ft slope. Canopy trees 35-55cm DBH, some to 65cm. Scattered down trees of all sizes. Soil deep dark silty loam. Scattered dolomite outcrops. 48cm DBH Quercus rubra = 106 years.

On well-drained mound bordering slough. Quercus bicolor extends into well-drained channels. Modal DBH = 35-50cm; max of 75-97cm common throughout. Woody debris of all stages of decay. Frequent gaps. Dry sandy loam.
Canopy trees broad, spreading; DBH 40-80cm. Multiple stems. Frequent gaps; open sun to ground. Downed limbs and tip-ups common. Shrub layer almost absent. Soil well-drained clay loam, friable.

At edge of open water marsh. Tree size 40-75cm DBH. Stand of Populus deltoides to east. Thickets in southeast portion of plot are frequently scattered throughout community(?). Soil dark loamy sand, channeled, moist, mounded.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: High-quality dry-mesic forest on plateau. Modal DBH=40-55cm, max to 88cm. Succeeded to forest recently (low species diversity, open-grown trees). Soil loess with 2" dark A-horizon. 65cm Quercus velutina=85 years; 46cm Quercus alba=94 years.

Dominated by Sporobolus heterolepis with good overall diversity (although distribution of some forbs is patchy) and few weeds. Habitat diversity increased by presence of dolomitic sandstone. Woody cover < 25%.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Canopy DBH 30-54cm. No stumps; small tip-up; 1 small decaying log. Leaf litter almost continuous. Soil friable silt loam. Canopy trees marked with paint--timber sale? In Zumbro Bottoms Management Unit.

Floating mat in old channel of Zumbro River. Dominated by sedges. Mildly bouncy. Muck soil, approximately 60cm deep. Part of larger wetland complex. See also releve #4826. Needs burn management. 1/2 releves from a rich fen in Wabasha counties.

Floating mat in old channel of Zumbro River. Mat very bouncy but tough Muck soil > 50cm deep, saturated with up to 8cm of water on surface. Brown sediment on much of soil surface. See also releve 4825.

Extremely high quality black ash/northern hardwood stands shifting between dominance of Fraxinus nigra and Acer saccharum depending on almost undetectable change in moisture. Rich graminoid, herbaceous and moss diversity.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Excellent mid-age maple basswood forest with much birch and much internal topoggraphy variation much dead and down wood, and average DBH of 20cm. Representative of area east of Bagley Outwsah Plain. Soil: 1" black loam over 8" fine sandy tan clay.

Irregular patterning of black ash low areas and bur oak/basswood rises typical and included in releve. Note relatively high herb diversity. Lows not mucky; few cobbles. No cut stumps. Low terrace or St. Croix River.
Not a true releve. No plot laid out but data collected from approximately 20X20m area. Cutting (firewood?) within last 10 years just south of "plot," largest bur oak here (not in plot): 74cm DBH.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Maple basswood forest within small wetlands. Includes paper and yellow birch. Ground cover of deciduous leaf duff. Moderately uneven terrain due to well decayed logs. Several huge well-decayed stumps.

Dense shrub layer with much Acer saccharum and Ostrya virginiana reproduction. Colonies of Laportea in gaps. Several hundred Botrychium troph in several groups. Well-decayed logs common; several charred 10-12" stumps. Soil: 4 inches gray sandy clay over tan sand with clay and pebbles.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Deciduous leaf duff. Moss only on decaying logs. Occasional Betula papyrifera windthrow. Moderate coarse woody debris. Few well-decayed old stumps--old cuts. One very large (>1m across) very well-decayed stump. Soil: light gray loamy sand.

Black spruce bog with tamarack to north and south in basin. Red pine on surrounding upland. Hummocky sphagnum throughout plot. Logs common; occasional stumps, broken or cut with axe. Usnea on branches rare. Soil: 4 inches wet peat.

Surface hummocky from old stumps and logs, coarse woody debris common. One well-decayed stump 50cm in diameter.  Moss filled pools. DBHs: Thuja = 27.6, 19.2, 25.2, and 16.5cm. Abies = 8.8cm. Wet fibric peat.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: In level area near top of knoll. Selective cutting in past (oak?). One large (90cm diam) well-decayed stump; several smaller moss-covered stumps and moss-covered well-decayed logs. Deciduous leaf duff, not thick. Soil: 3 inches humus(black sandy loam) over 8 inches fine light gray sand with loam (?).

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Mature, but not old, maple-basswood forest. Occasional well-decayed, broken-off stumps with well-decayed logs. Occasional moss-covered rocks. Soil 3" sandy humus over 10" very fine light tan sand.

Black spruce swamp "inclusion" in maple-basswood forest. Nearly complete moss (mostly sphagnum) ground cover; hummocky. Few blow downs. A few standing dead spruce. Lower and middle branches bare. Soil: 8 inches sphagnum over 12 inches well-decomposed peat.
Plot in wetland dominated by Carex oligocarpa with very sparse stunted tamarack and rare bog birch. Stunted leatherleaf beneath Carex oligocarpa. Substrate = wet, poorly decomposed Sphagnum peat.

Big-tooth aspen forest on knoll with ash swale and black spruce swamp on low ground to East and West. Paper birch also scattered on upland. Thin deciduous leaf duff. Occasional blow-down. Few decaying birch logs. Soil: light gray sand over very light tan fine sand.
Occasional blowdowns--logs, branches. Stand typical of community type and releve typical of stand. Middle slope position.

Micro-relief from duff-covered decaying logs. Some small diameter old blowdowns (5% of plot). Thick duff. Soft ground. Numerous basswood seedlings. Dense canopy, open at eye level, moderate herb layer. Soil: 3 inches loam over sandy clay.
On hillside sloping to small wetland. Typed as Bi44. Pockets of Betula papyrifera in stand. Decaying birch logs; deciduous leaf duff; occasional blowdown. Soil: loamy sand over medium brown sand.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: In oak forest (typed oak 56) on state land in Meadowbrook wildlife management area. Woody debris <15cm DBH occasional. Windthrow occasional. Walked ridge to northeast; releve placed just before ridge drops off to northeast. Typical of stand. Soil: 5 cm sandy loam over 15 cm medium fine tan sand with slight clay component

In rather open oak forest on northwest-facing slope. Deciduous leaf duff, ground cover 10% coarse woody debris--mostly medium to small (3-10") DBH. Uneven ground within plot and throughout stand. Soil: 10 cm sandy loam over +15 cm medium coarse medium tan sand.

Mature red pine-jack pine stand. Few old moss-covered small (<10" diameter) stumps and some broken off high. Occasional small diameter blowdown. Few dead and senescent jack pines. Rare large well-decayed stumps. Soil: 20 cm moist medium tan medium fine sand over clay/loam compact over sand over rock/gravel.

Erythronium albidum site. Oak super canopy, sugar maple canopy. Ground cover of deciduous leaf duff. Occasional small-medium diameter coarse woody debris. Rank=A/AB. Leech Lake Tribal Land NH41. Soil: Gray loam clay with sand grading into fine clay-sand.
Releve in oak-basswood stand at top of ridge on Bear Island.  Occasional small-medium diameter coarse woody debris. Ground cover of deciduous leaf duff. Releve representative of stand. Rank = A/AB.

On slope of 2nd knoll on west side of Bear Island. Occasional coarse woody debris. 1 well-decayed log. Stand exposed to wind. Oak forest being replaced by Maple basswood forest. Rank = AB/B? Leech Lake tribal NH42. Soil: 4 inches loam over 10 inches dark gray clay with sand.

County-owned stand originating from 1959 Badoura fire. Complete ground cover of Pleurozium. Occasional small diameter blow-down and small stumps. Small stumps occasional near trail otherwise little trimming. Trees (jack pine) dense in places; various DBHs. County st.#5

On steep slope facing few degrees east of south. With red maple, red oak and paper birch in understory. Occasional decayed birch logs. Rare decayed birch stumps. Deciduous leaf duff.Wetland and base of slope, small amount of open water surrounded by graminoids. Soil: 2 inches sandy loam over 8 inches medium fine loam sand.

Pools cover approximately 50% of plot. Numerous tip-ups. White cedar seedlings rare in stand. Balsam fir on upland ridge west of cedar. Owner reported moving water in spring. Plot representative of stand. Soil: Wet peat over wet-moist peat.
Wet, with pools of knee-deep standing water. Private ownership. Substrate wet peat. Plot representative of stand.

Mixed jack pine/paper birch stand. Occasional small-medium diameter blowdown. Stand appears even aged. One old charred stump seen. Ground cover primarily deciduous leaves. Plot representative of stand. Rank=A/AB. Soil: 1 inch sandy loam over 9 inches fine tan/brown sand.

Releve in area of red pine within mixed conifer-hardwood forest. Fire scars on red pines. Gently rolling terrain. Occasional small-medium diameter coarse woody debris. Soil sandy loam over light brown sand.

Black ash forest between maple-basswood forest and poor fen. Occasional med-diameter blowdown. Moist, but no standing water. Soils black humus over light gray sandy clay. CNF Walker Dist, compartment 24, stand 31.

Stand probably has long history of maple-sugaring. Mixed ages from seedlings to large old trees. Dense Laportea throughout except where trail is maintained to cultural site. Leaf duff on forest floor. Soil: 3 inches sandy loam over 6 inches light gray-brown sandy clay over 8 inches light gray brown sandy clay over 2 inches firm light red/brown clay.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Releve just west southwest of south fork of trail. Several old windblown Betula papyrifera--mostly decayed logs and stumps. Few very old cut stumps. Very old moss-covered logs occasional. Forest floor covered with deciduous leaf duff. Representative of stand. Soil: 3 inches loam over 6 inches brown sand over 3 inches light loam sand clay composition.

Aspen-birch forest with varying amounts of birch. Ground cover of deciduous leaf duff. Occasional small-medium diameter debris. Occasional broken off tree (windthrow). Soil: 3 inches sandy loam over 6 inches light brown sand over 9 inches lighter brown fine sand.
Releve in pine (Pine Point RNA). Clusters of pine varying in density, with red maple and trembling aspen. Medium diameter coarse woody debris common. Soil 2" sandy loam over 16" fine tan sand.

On slope in large stand of mature aspen in Deep Portage Conservation Wilderness Area. Windthrown red oak; other occasional to common medium and small diameter coarse woody debris, some well decayed. One large tip-up. Thin leaf duff. Soil: 1 inch sandy loam over tan fine sand.

In cedar swamp at edge of mixed conifer (Black spruce and White cedar) swamp along Boy River between Co. 53 and Hwy 8. Floating mat of Calamagrostis canadensis, Carex lasiocarpa, and Typha between swamp and open water of river. Hummocky with pools. Wet peat 2 cones deep.

Releve in oak island (with Red pine plantation and ash swales) in Mud-Goose wildlife management area. Oaks largest diameter trees in stand. Deciduous leaf duff. Occasional very old tip-ups. No stumps in plot-rare in stand. Infrequent blowdown. Soil: 2 inches sandy loam over 8 inches dark loam sand over 10 inches fine tan sand.
Releve in very wet swamp. Deep (3-3 1/2 Ft.) pools of water cover 25-30% of plot. State stand #5. Soil: wet peat over very decomposed organic matter over silt.
Releve in white cedar swamp (upland ?) south of aspen clearcut. Cedar leaves and birch leaves as ground cover. Old well-decayed logs common. One huge well-decayed stump. Several wind-blown stumps.

Relve in maple basswood forest off CNF 2947 (285 paces N/NW on 2947; 80 paces E (70 deg.)). Plot moved slightly to include a large yellow birch. Dense D3 layer of sugar maple throughout stand. Thick layer of deciduous leaf duff. Soil: 8 inches gray sandy clay over 10 inches light gray clay with some sand.

Well decayed moss-covered logs occasional. 1 well-decayed moss-covered, charred stump. Occasional coarse woody debris, primarily birch logs/branches. Duff of red pine needles and deciduous leaves. Gentle relief in plot from old root bases, decayed logs. Soil: 1 inch sandy humus over 9 inches fine medium tan sand over 10 inches very fine light tan sand.

Shrub swamp south of black spruce with red pine and aspen-balsam fir upland surrounding. Hummocky-alder roots give support. Pools of water separated by root clumps and sphagnum hummocks. No blowdown in plot; 1 broken-off stump, 3-4" diameter. Substrate: 3 inches wet peat.

Releve in densest cedar in stand of black ash, cedar, balsam fir and aspen. Typed as cedar 54. Occasional small-medium diameter coarse woody debris. Several moss filled pools. Several well-decayed, moss covered logs. More open than rest of stand. Soil: 8 inch black sandy loam over 2 inches sandy light gray clay.

Decaying birch logs common. Some standing trees partially peeled. Patches of thin deciduous and coniferous duff. Old campsite but regrown. Releve placed to maximize birch. Comp 130, Stand 4, CNF Deer River District. Soil: 4 inches sandy loam over 20 inches fine tan sand.
Releve in Salix south of wet meadow at river edge. Salix/Betula gland/Alnus rugosa increase in density toward conifer swamp to south. Substrate = wet peat, no return in sampler.

Releve in wet meadow (Calamagrostis with scattered Salix and Phragmites islands) between oxbow and Mississippi River. Just across oxbow from metal USFS plot marker. 5" wet peat over 15" light gray fine sand.
Releve on mat, South edge of Iverson Lake. Soil: Wet peat, scant return (2 inches).
Releve in tamarack moat surrounding black spruce swamp just east of Mabel Lake. Nearly complete sphagnum cover--hummocky, wet. Soil: Only 3 cm wet, poorly decomposed sphagnum peat returned.
Releve in black spruce swamp east of Mabel Lake campground and east of releve# 94-46 (DNR# 4879). Hummocky--nearly complete sphagnum cover. Wet; water in footprints.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Deciduous leaf duff. Few broken off stumps. Occasional sugar maple - medium diameter blowdown. Few whole trees fallen. State stand 21. Soil: 2 inches humus over 2 inches gray loam sand over 12 inches very fine tan sand with little loam.

County stand #16. Ground cover of deciduous leaf duff. Occasional medium diameter coarse woody debris, including paper birch logs. Few well-decayed stumps. Undulating ground from stumps, tip-ups, logs. Soil: 3 inches sandy humus over 5 inches red medium fine sand.

Typed (by county) as NH42. Deciduous leaf duff. Mostly small-medium diameter coarse woody debris. Undulating ground from old logs, tip-ups. Carex (esp. pedunculata) growing on well-decayed logs. County stand 34. Soil: 2 inches humus/loam over 6 inches brown sand.

Plot selected as representative of unburned meadow along north side of Leech River. Approximately 40cm of peat over mineral. Aluminum posts on  northeast and southwest corners and magnet buried at center.

Plot selected to be in old hayfield on 1939 photos, but saw no obvious difference. Area was burned in 1992. Aluminum posts on northwest and southeast corners of plot. Mat floating and very wet--muskrat house on northeast corner.
Plot selected as typical of burned wet meadow. Magnet in plot center, aluminum posts on plot corners. Burned 1991, 1992, 1993. Peat depth approximately 55cm.
Plot selected as typical of floating meadow along creek, north side of Mud Lake. Aluminum posts at southeast and northwest corners. Mat very wet and treacherous, > 2m of peat and water.

Plot typical of meadows between cattails and treeline just north of access channel, east side of lake. Peat >1m. Meadow previously flooded (Calamagrostis down and matted with algae). Thatch very thick. Willows nearby. (Salix gracilis, Salix discolor and others).

Releve in black spruce/tamarack swamp with balsam fir in understory along Shingobee River. Blow-downs cover 50% of plot. Old moss-covered stumps present. Substrate = soggy decomposed peat. Average Picea DBH = approximately 20cm.

Near top of large hill in pitted, dissected outwash. Probably past grazed, long idle-no fence remains. In very slightly concave area. Carex hillii common. Old gravel test hole and knoll crest near north end of plot. Thick mulch. Active animal den (Badger?) 4m away.
Dry bur oak forest on hilly moraine. Occasional signs of past cutting, but only one stump - ca 20cm diameter at ground. Oaks often multiple- stemmed.
Thick mulch or litter. Surface very buoyant, like floating mat. Water free at surface. Substrate a soupy, root-filled muck full of tiny shells, deeper than 1 meter.
Surface bouyant, but not as much as nearby releve 9404. Not as wet. Substrate very decomposed peat/muck, deeper than 1 meter. Full of tiny shells. Surrounded by shrubbier vegetation.

Substrate moderately springy, well decomposed peat > 1m deep with shell fragments. Meadow extends south from upland, narrowing southward, becoming wetter. Clumps of Salix gracilis common in parts. Flanked with Phragmites australis and or Thypha marsh. May involve groundwater seepage.

Substrate soupy muck > 1m deep. Surface water pH=7.2. Fen becoming overgrown with shrub; in thicket with tall moderately dense shrubs in broad seep zone below Glacial Lake shoreline at margin of moraine. In pasture, cattle activity in fen minimal.
Open, nearly shrub-free meadow surrounded by wet brush prairie, thickets, some marshy areas. No signs of past grazing use.

Ground surface quite uneven; many small hollows. Occasional boulders. Some similar areas with less shrub cover. Grazed in past, probably not heavily. Plot approximately 0.5km northwest of uppermost glacial lake shore/moraine margin.

Substrate: few cm dark grey sapric peat (some fibrous material); shell fragments and marl (?); then becoming brown-gray, soupy muck with grit. Mineral base > 1m. Nearby beaver dam and pool dominate by Typha. Small channels in fen. pH=8.2-8.4.

Substrate(hand probe): dark gray well decomposed soupy muck with shell fragments deeper than probe (> 1m). Small open fen just off margin of upland, grading into seepage shrub swamp, Phragmites australis thicket.

Part of large seepage-fed wetland. Substrate very dark gray sapric peat with shell fragments. Peat depth >1m. Some scattered willow outside plot, 2-3.5m high at edge where Typha becomes dominant. Plot far from upland margin, near Phragmites-dominated zone.

Part of large seepage-fed wetland. By margin of upland island. Substrate slightly bouncy water right below surface. Very dark gray, sapric peat with shell fragments =/> 1m deep. Bog birch common at upland margin. A few Carex sterilis nearby.

Soil approximately 15cm black loam over silty clay. Burned grove with trembling aspen, balsam poplar and green ash about 30m northeast of plot; most suckers 2-3m high. Wet meadow/fen north of plot. Past grazing.
Soil fine-textured black loam over very dark gray, sticky, fine sandy clay loam. Upland area in wetland-dominated area. Conditions here wet-mesic.

Probably pastured long ago; exotic grass evidence of disturbance. Wildfire burned couple years earlier. Soil approximately 20cm black loam over dark gray fine sandy loam and fine sandy clay mixed. Wet at approximately 30cm; water table approximately 50cm. Wet-mesic conditions.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Typical of Northern Hardwoods along ridge of penninsula surrounded by conifer swamp in southeast Nemadji State Forest.
Representative of narrow band of wet-mesic Northern Hardwood forest occurring along edges of wetlands. Releve barely fits within type. Soil: humus 2in; deep A horizon, loam, mottling at 24 inches.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Representative of richer Northern Hardwood Forest in Nemadji State Forest. Organic layer 0-12 inch silt loam; 1 inch hardpan; silty clay to 50cm; gravelly loam.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Soil: silt loam with hard pan at 28 cm. Well drained. Many charred pine stumps.
Across road from rich Northern Hardwood stand. Soil silty loam; moderately well-drained. Tip-up mounds from large white spruce; many charred pine stumps.

Canopy of open-grown oaks (25% cover, 61-85 cm DBH) and forest-grown younger oaks (70% cover, 21-37 cm DBH). Narrow slope, field and highway above, lake below. Soil sand. Permanently marked metal post center plot. Largest oak with fire scar on uphill side.
Brush recently cleared; controlled burn done spring 1994. Bur oak center plot top-killed, sprouting from base. Soil sandy loam. Average tree cover in savanna 5%. Permanent metal stake center of plot.

Canopy of widely spaced, large diameter Acer saccharinum; occasional large Populus deltoides outside plot. Evidence of recent flooding. Plot is north of trail. Permanently marked by metal stake center of plot.

Frequent pools; relief from tip-ups, old logs. Ground cover 30% Sphagnum, 30% Bryales, 30% Thuja needles. 2 mature white pine just outside plot. Substrate = 20" wet peat. On Bemidji Sand Plain land type association.

Some large diameter trees (approx 70cm) with medium and small diameter pines. CNF old growth stand. On Bemidji Sand Plain Land Type Association. Soil: 8 inches med fine tan sand 10 inches light tan fine sand.

Very recent windfall--1/4 of plot. Some very large white pine with smaller diameter balsam fir, red maple, and trembling aspen. State stand 5. CSA typed as WP76. Soil: 2 inches organic/sand over 8 inches medium fine sand over 10 inches medium tan medium fine sand.

Top of knoll--includes slope to southeast. Occasional small-medium diameter coarse woody debris--some Betula papyrifera. Thick deciduous leaf duff. Rare old fire-scared stumps. State stand 20. Soil: 1 inch sandy organic over 18 inches moist medium fine tan sand.

Mature red pine plantation. Furrows. Occasional cut stumps. Ground cover primarily Pleurozia with needle duff. Occasional coarse woody debris. Waldstenia population. CNF, Walker Dist, Comp 66, Stand 18. On Itasca Moraine Land Type Association. Soil: 1 inch organic over 10 inches medium tan fine sand with pebbles.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Thick deciduous leaf duff. Occasional small-medium diameter coarse woody debris. Old tip-ups, Betula papyrifera logs, rotting stumps in stand and plot. Occasional well-decayed large diameter log. Mature stand, but not old. State stand 3. CSA typed 057. Soil: 20 inches medium and medium fine sand.

On Sand Point, which extends into Leech Lake near Walker. Releve at point between ice ridge segments on southeast edge of Point. On Itasca Moraine Land Type Association. With Carol Estes Mortenson and Steve Mortenson, LLDRM.

Releve at Botrychium mormo location (DNR EO #51) on north part of Bear Island. Thin, patchy deciduous leaf duff. Gentle relief from tip-ups, well-decayed logs. Occasional coarse woody debris. On Itasca Moraine Land Type Association.

On gentle southeast slope. Occasional well-decayed logs. Botrychium Mormo in plot (EO #26). Several decaying Betula alleghaniensis logs and other occasional coarse woody debris. Gentle relief from old tip-ups. Thick deciduous leaf duff. CNF CL Dist, Comp 83, Std 19.

On gentle southwest slope. Botrychium mormo at base of slope (DNR EO#26). Dense canopy, open below. Thick deciduous leaf duff. Occasional well-decayed logs. Moderate amount coarse woody debris. Recently downed sugar maple in plot. CNF CL Dst, Cmp 83, Std 19.
At head of gated trail running southeast of FR 2342 1.1 mile east of Sucker Bay Road. CNF, Cass Lake District, Compartment 82, Stand 29. On Guthrie Till Plain Land Type Association.

Plot on gentle slope to south, to ash swale. Occasional tip-ups, blow- down. Thin deciduous leaf duff. CNF, Cass Lake District, Compartment 83, Stand 17. On Guthrie Till Plain Land Type Association. Botrychium mormo DNR EO #26.
Thick deciduous leaf duff. Occasional old well-decayed logs in plot. Recent blowdown (1 mature basswood, 1 mature sugar maple) covering 1/3 of plot. CNF, Cass Lake District, Compartment 83, Stand 19.

Plot on gentle north slope. Relief from old tip-ups and well-decayed logs. 2 old blackened stumps in plot. Thick deciduous leaf duff. 6 Botrychium mormo plants (DNR EO #25). CNF, Cass Lake Dist, Comp 85, Stand 15. On Guthrie Till Plain Land Type Association.

Well-rotted, moss-covered logs frequent. Thin deciduous leaf duff. Dense canopy with open understory and groundlayer. Occasional small-medium diameter coarse woody debris. Botrychium mormo DNR EO #24; 8 scattered and single plants seen in plot.

Floodplain forest along Crow Wing River; boundary of plot about 5 feet from river. Frequent small and medium diameter coarse woody debris including some moss-covered logs. Soil: 2 inches wet organic over 18 inches gray-brown wet clay/sand.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Releve adjacent to oxbow about 50 yards north of Crow Wing River. Moderate amount of medium-diameter coarse woody debris. Occasional fallen snags. County Stand 3. Soil: 4 inch organic over 16 inch moist dark brown sandy silt.
Along Crow Wing River. County stand 2. Typed042. Soil: 1 inch organic over 19 inches sandy silt/loam.

Cut stumps of 55 and 58 cm diameter. Deciduous leaf duff. Occasional medium to large diameter well-decayed moss-covered logs. Dense Corylus in shrub layer. State stand 2. CSA typed 051, aged at 123 years.

Several tip-ups and nurse logs in plot. Several old medium-large diameter logs. Deciduous leaf duff. CNF, Deer River District, Compartment 201, Stand 31, typed 719. Bena Dunes & Peatlands Land Type Association.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Old growth maple/basswood forest in mesic swale between narrow ridges. Concave side slopes approaching 20% grade on each side of plot. Healthy large Juglans cineara. North aspect elevation of 1080 feet. Gently sloping gradient from dry-mesic oak to lowland hardwoods. Soil: Clay silt.

npc_type_name: Sugar Maple - Basswood - Red Oak - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: East descending, small ridge along side road about 10-15 feet above floodplain. Releve includes north aspect slope to the foot of small ridges. Heterogeneous stand. Releve includes larger trees, >45cm DBH common in canopy. West mode DBH is between 20-30cm, with larger trees missing.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Lowland hardwoods dominated by Quercus macrocarpa. Debris common from tip-ups and fallen limbs. Well Drained. Basal area:110 sq ft/acre. Silty alluvial soil-channeled.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Clayey silt, canopy 50% cover in releve, 65% overall. Horse trail in southeast corner.
North aspect, wet mesic, dark organic silt with gravel. Rock outcrop moss covered. North facing slope 60% grade. Balsam fir north east corner, Pinus strobus west of plot.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Large extent of this CD lowland hardwood forest along Canfield Creek. Basal Area: 90 Square feet/acre. Decaying elms on forest floor common. Soil a clayey silt-deep.
Algific slope. East facing with Rhamnus alnifolia, Ribes hudsonianum. Rocky cliff 50 foot with abandoned spring channel descending ridge spur. Silt loam, cold air vents, cold soil.
Dark silty-clay, organic deep. Quercus rubra, 57cm DBH at 115 rings.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Young stand with scattered large trees, much down logs and debris, mainly Ulmus. Soil a dark silt loam. Tree core: 21cmn Ulmus americana Basal area: 80-90 sq ft/acre. Debris mainly Ulmus. Crataegus crus-galli state Record??

Seepage meadow at base of terrace on broad creek valley. East aspect. Above terrace is another seepage area from base of bluff about 1140ft. Seepage meadow level with rivulels of flowing water. Plot 5x20m.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: White pine-hardwood, north aspect, large tip-ups and broken limbs. Old barbed fence near north border of plot. Side of knoll of narrow ridge spur between knolls on bluff east of River. Deep loess 12-24 inches to bedrock, 1-2 inches dark humus and duff. Dark silt layer 3 inches to yellow silt sub-horizon.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Dry-mesic oak forest, mature canopy 25-30m: Mode DBH 35-35cm, Max DBH, infrequent 50-65cm.  Dense shade to substrate ecotonal with maple/basswood forest. Narrow ridge descending. Rich organic clayey silt.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: A small (<5acre) stand of white pines, hardwoods select logged. Subcanopy closed with Acer saccharrum, super canopy 50-75% 30-35m height. Canopy 25m; 25% cover (Quercus alba/rubra). Mode DBH 15-25cm.

Mature maple/basswood with several dead Ulmus snags. Gaps filled with subcanopy Acer, substrata very open, dense shade, community similar to lowland hardwoods. Modal DBH 25-35, max 45-80 common in plot; infrequent throughout community. Abundant woody debris, substrate a dark organic clay silt.

Ecotonal due to aspect/elevation. Thin silty, organic soil with cobble and loose slabs of limestone. Mostly open grown burr oaks with Tilia in lower border of plot. Rock outcrops below level crest. Basal area 140 square feet/acre.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Dry-mesic oak forest maturing in old growth trees. Mode 25-45cm DBH. Medium size rare to infrequent >50cm DBH. Soil clayey silt mostly compacted on broad ridge with sinkholes, soil lacks humus layer, forbs depauperate. Basal area 170 square feet/acre. Sub-canopy closed, shrub layer varies from sparse to intermediate patchy never thick.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Dry mesic oak forest; canopy 20-25m height; 85% cover; snags rare to occasional. Tip-ups and downed logs common, stumps very decayed occasional. Densely shaded to substrate north aspect, bluff with ridges and swales(plot southwest aspect). Soil: grey loess silt, low humus duff patchy 15% grade. Topographic context: upper/middle.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Old growth, dry-mesic oak forest dominated by Quercus rubra, Quercus alba, Quercus velutina in area. Sangs and debris abundant, gaps frequent. Canopy 30m southeast aspect of east facing bluff ridge spur. 8% grade, dark clay silt, good horizons, thick humus and duff.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Dry mesic oak forest, dominated by old growth Quercus rubra and Quercus alba. Areas seemed selectively logged in past with areas of smaller Tilia and several multiple trunks. Tag # 64. Soil: dark grey soil to 6 inches, subsoil loess silt  friable with good humus layer and duff. Quercus alba, 65 cm at >144 rings; Quercus rubra, 55 cm at >134 rings.
5 x 20 m. plot, Gravelly silt loam compact.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mesic oak forest dominated by Quercus rubra, Mode DBH 30-40 cm, no max size DBH. Crooked boled trees, plot with 3 large tip-ups, moderate decay. Snags rare to occasional. No outcrops. Near stone building. TAG#81. Soil: organic dark friable silt with galena limestone cobble.

Centered on largest cold area. One of state's largest Chrysosplenium iowense concentrations along this 1/4 mile long algific slope. One of the largest and best occurrences of this community in Minnesota. Topographic context: middle/lower.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mature(60-80yrs) Maple/Basswood. Mode DBH 20-40cm. Infrequent max DBH to 55cm. Acer saccharum dominate with Quercus rubra increasing in abundance up slope. Moss flora diverse but scattered. Debris tips occasional. Grades to mesic Oak upslope. Soil: silt with varying talus upwards to silty clay  dark friable organic duff layer.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Dry-mesic heterogeneous oak forest dominated by Quercus rubra, Quercus alba with abundant Populus grandidentata and Acer saccharum. 90% canopy overall. Rare to occasional snags, gaps, tip-ups, old decayed stumps frequent. Abundant oak seedlings. Modal DBH 10-20cm, max size class infrequent 40-50cm;(rare >60cm). Soil: silt loess, grey high humus.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Sugar Maple - Basswood Forest (Cold Slope)
remarks: Northern hardwoods, white pine mode DBH 50-65cm; Tilia/Acer 15-25cm DBH; Abies 10-15cm DBH. No large trees in plot except one leaning outside, 40-55cm trees are common. Stream at base, steep rocky hill 10-20 yards below. Dark friable silt, mossy, some cobbles. Basal area 120 square feet per acres.

Dry to wet-mesic mesic, thickly covered with feather moss and liverworts and covered with diminutive Cystopteris bulbifera. Dry rubble borders on side with boulders platy limestone. Several cold producing vents with ice. Loose ruble and dark silty colluvium.

Mounded to level, mesic silt with gravel to wet mesic in small swales. In small alluvial valley near spring, flowing creek at east border of plot, county road at west border.  Characterized by Cespitose sedges. Indicative of past disturbance but floristically diverse. Community dissected by fence and grazed.

Excellent, slightly springy area, small hummocks mostly easy walking. Forbs evenly dispersed throughout. Realy soil, organic wet mesic saturated, not standing water. North end of community best, elsewhere thicket of bog birch. Releve next to small grove of 5-10m height aspen.

Slightly elevated ridge with depressions, gently slopes to east. Releve includes 1/2 of Bur Oak grove of 7 trees with broad spreading canopy; DBH 37-75cm. Polygon grazed fence with electric wire insulators. Patchy high quality herb flora with areas of Eurasian grasses. Canopy spread 10-15m. Soil: grey loess over gravelly glacial outwash.

Small 5-10 acre tract of mesic prairie knoll descending into Spartina-Calamogrostis swales. Releve represents the most species rich-dense area of polygon, however other portions have significant species including; Valeriana edulis and Carex annectens. Species abundant and well disperse, no weedy dominant. Soil mesic, dark silt loam.

Formerly pastured, mesic oak savanna largely dominated by Eurasion grasses, but patchy mosaic cover of native graminoids and weedy forbs. Adjacent to Cordgrass swale with prairie forbs. Older trees broad spreading, straight to crooked boles. Soil: compact silt loam.

Excellent prairie with diverse forbs abundant and well dispersed in open areas. Woody cover 60% but with several open areas. Woody cover mostly Rhus glabra. Upper slope to crest southwest aspect. Quarry across road. Soil: clayey silt with some cobbles.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Soil clay loam. Cored 2 trees: Quercus rubra (34 cm DBH 51 rings.); Quercus alba (57 cm DBH 100 rings).

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mature oak forest on top of large flat-topped hill. Little recent cutting. On deep silt loam soil with good humus layer. Apparently never grazed. One of the finest remaining stands of oak forest in county.

Calcareous fen on shallow, slightly springy mound located at approximately middle to lower slope. On shallow north-east facing slope. Probably grazed in past. In palms muck soil. Phalaris downslope from fen. One of best examples of calcareous fen left in county.
Releve typical of prairie atop well-drained, hill site is approximately 8 acres and appears undisturbed. Grades into Andropogon-dominated dry mesic prairie downslope.
Classic rich fen in very good condition, SNA quality. About 6 inches standing water at time of survey.
Opening in area that has scattered clumps of aspen. Typical of openings.
Never broken remnant of mesic prairie on Fosston Till Plain. Size 3 acres. History unknown prior to 1948, pastured 1948-1963, burned 1994. Owner seeks protection.
Potentially recoverable area, should respond to fire. Goes with est end of large community block of NC38. BC/C quality.
One of best areas in former Mentor Ranch. Very promising for management. Could be potential habitat for Platanthera praeclara.
East of area 6, East of grove along section line. North-South prairie.
Soil heavy black clay, no detectable horizons. Probably 1.5 acres of this community in area.
Within plot community is too open to call brush-prairie, but the community EO as a whole is brush-prairie.
By far the best area in this quarter.
Just southwest of line of trees that extends north-to-south. Old hay meadow.
Calcareous seepage fen perched on gentle south facing slope just north of fenceline. Community continues across fence into Becker County.
Near crest slope with stairlike pools on west side of large domed calcareous fen. About 5 major pools in plot about 1/2 mile to 1m squared. pH 8.4-8.5 Open pools constitute about 10% of area.
Northeast of shrubby dome, open lawnlike area. No standing water, no open pools. Fairly level but perched on a dome.

Model DBH 40-60cm frequent down to 25cm (canopy trees), occassionaly to 80cm DBH, rarely 100cm. Canopy trees open-grown, 1:1 height to width ratio. Snags uncommon. Tip-ups and decaying logs rare. Disturbance species uncommon. Silt loam or sandy loam soil. 76 cm DBH Quercus macrocarpa cored at approximately 120cm height, 165 years old.
Decaying logs of various sizes frequent. No stumps. No tip-ups. Canopy trees 20-40cm DBH, mode 30cm, rarely 60cm. Quercus rubra 59cm cored-122yrs. Thin layer of humus over moist light brown sand.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: Maturing mesic oak forest dominated by Quercus rubra. On 26 degree 300 foot north facing slope along Beaver Creek. Soil dark sandy loam. New logging road through lower part of slope. Core of 38 cm DBH Quercus rubra at 136 cm height.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mature maple-basswood forest on 250 foot north facing slope along Beaver Creek. Soil a deep dark clay loam. Canopy trees commonly 25-40 cm DBH, rarely 45cm. Upper slope and valley floor similar. 42cm DBH, 115cm height Quercus rubra cored = 77 years.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Sugar Maple - Basswood Forest (Cold Slope)
remarks: Mature northern hardwood/conifer forest on steep upper slope of north/northeast-facing bluff along Hemingway Creek. Sandy-loam soil. Canopy trees mostly 40-68cm DBH. Rock outcrops and decaying wood frequent. Many northern species. Soil: thin sandy loam over pure sand with frequent outcrops.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: Small stand of white pine on narrow ridge along Middle Fork Whitewater River. Mature pines to 80cm DBH. Snags occasional. Decaying wood frequent, various sizes. Thick needle duff. Compacted silty clay. Lower 1/2 of this 150 foot slope steeper supporting maple-basswood forest. Topographic context: upper/middle. Canopy trees DBH: Pinus strobus 35-80cm, mode 45-60cm; Quercus rubra 25-40cm, mode 30-35cm; Quercus alba 41cm; Tilia 25-35cm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: 200 foot slope along Middle Fork Whitewater River. Occasional dolomite outcrops. Soil a compacted silty clay. Canopy trees 25-55cm DBH, mode 30-40cm DBH. Decaying wood occasional, mostly small, no stumps, snags rare. Tree core: 36cm DBH Quercus rubra = 86 rings.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Deep north-south ravine through 200 foot south facing slope along Whitewater River. Surrounding forest much drier. Compacted silty clay with little humus. Scattered small dolomite outcrops. Decaying wood frequent, mostly small. Occasional snags. Canopy trees, Quercus rubra, 20-48cm DBH, modal DBH 30-40cm. Tree core: 46 DBH Quercus rubra = 113 rings.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Maturing forest with deep dark clay-loam soils. Medium diversity. 4 rare plants elements. Canopy trees 30-45 cm DBH. Dead falls frequent. 40cm DBH Tilia cored at 100 cm high = 107 + years old. Topographic context: lower/toe.

Plot near the southwest edge of fen in small-statured zone surrounded by Carex stricta. On saturated peat with distinct hummocks. Grazed until about 10 years ago. Prescribe burned this past spring. Up to 4 ft of peat in some areas. Two major areas of discharge with Carex sterilis. Population of Carex sterilis diffuse/occasional in rest of 3 acre meadow. Other portionsof fen variously dominated by Carex stricta, trichocarpa, prairea and mixes of these.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Bench-top terrace on upper-mid slope. Dark sandy loam.  Little evidence of disturbance. High quality mesic oak. Trees 35-50cm DBH, rare 65 cm. Larger trees marked for timber sale. Very old stumps occasional, snags rare, down woody debris occasional, all sizes. Adjacent to white pine stand. Tree cores: 63cm Quercus rubra = 98 rings; 42cm Quercus rubra = 103 rings; 37cm Quercus alba = 99 rings.

High-quality algific slope above floodplain of Beaver Creek. Very rocky slope. Prairie du Chien Formation-Oneota dolomite. 3-7m cliff above slope with little canopy cover. Ostlie, 1990. Rocks moss covered with moist cool dark organic soil between them. Releve centered on coldest area. Topographic context: middle/lower.

Small meadow at base of 40 foot east facing terrace slope along Snake Creek. Several discharge zones raised 1-2m above level of meadow. Saturated brown organic soil. Wetter areas 2-5cm standing water.

Formerly heavily grazed prairie that has been frequently burned. Artificially dense sward of Sorghastrum present. Within large savanna undergoing restoration. Dom tree species is Quercus macrocarpa. On sandy loam soil over sandstone bedrock.
Prairie on well-vegetated dune composed of excessively-drained fine sand. Located within valley just South of MN River. Releve taken in large opening among large junipers.
At transition between wet prairie and wet meadow in shallow, narrow swale. Surrounded by disturbed oak woodland. Edges are somewhat fen-like with Carex prairea and Lysimachia quad.
Wetland in shallow depression surrounded by disturbed oak woodland. Dense moss carpet(not sphagnum), at base of plants. One foot standing water below moss layer. Soft muck with methane.
Wet prairie in shallow swale surrounded by formerly grazed oak woodland.

Emergent marsh in large shallow basin surrounded by oak woodland. Degraded by past grazing. On black, stinky muck with 1.5 to 0.5 foot standing. Grades into patches dominated entirely by Typha or Scirpus fluviatilis.

Large narrow wetland in shallow swale surrounded by oak woodland disturbed by past grazing. One foot cold standing water. Soil is dark gray clay about 20 inches below surface. Dense, continuous mat of moss at water surface throughout. Grades into Carex lacustris and Scirpus cf. acutus dominated communities.
On crest of dry knoll on south facing slope. On well-drained, coarse gravelly outwash within the MN River Valley.

Mature forest on steep ravine side along small creek. Scattered trees 50-73cm DBH. Distinct soil moisture gradient from bottom to top of plot. Soil is rich black clay loam with intact humus at surface. Much leaf liter, occasional dead fall and snags. Uplands on edge of ravine, dominated by young multi-stem oaks.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Forest on level ground at edge of creek valley on loamy till on south of Minnesota River valley. Even-aged stand dominated by multi-stemmed trees with 30-40cm DBH. Much woody debris on ground (small trucks). Occasional old, rotted stumps.

Canopy impacted by elm disease. Main canopy trees approximately 40cm DBH. Much large; medium diameter woody debris in various stages of decay. Rich mesic forest ground layer. No exotics or obvious signs of disturbance. Substrate sandy alluvium, soil dark sandy loam.
On large, sloping shelf of peat. Water table is at ground surface. 4" of muck at ground surface. Soil is coarse, fibric peat at least 1m deep.

Fen on deep fibric peat. Site is well-hydrated and bouncy with much surface water between hummocks. Heavy Scirpus acutus cover in most of open areas. Most of surrounding area has fairly dense shrub cover. Located west of bike trail.

Shrub swamp on well-hydrated peat with watertable at ground surface. Lacks surface flow of water. In mosaic with calcareous fen openings. Shrub cover varied from 50-100%. No evidence of flooding, ground surface is well-vegetated and has much moss cover.
Opening dominated by low sedge species, near top of peat mound at foot of north side of Minnesota River Valley. Watertable is right at ground surface. Soil is deep, fibric peat.

Forest with super canopy of large, straight-boled Populus deltoides, DBH 35-70cm; Silver maples range 35-45cm DBH. Very high density of tree stems. Approximately 75% ground cover by coarse woody debris. In active floodplain of Minnesota River with heavy recent silt deposition. Many trees have ice scares at base.

Wet meadow on bottom lands in Minnesota River valley. Surface slightly springy. On coarse, fibric peat >1m deep. Water table at surface. In mosaic of patches. Other patches dominated by Carex lacustris or Sparganium species. Community undisturbed except for small amount of Phalaris on edges.

Wet meadow/shall marsh on ground water fed mucky-peat, north side of Minnesota River Valley. Approximately 50m from base of valley side. A couple of inches of standing water present. Leersia and Phragmites patches also occur here.

Mature forest with 40-70cm DBH tall, straight trees. Lots of small and medium coarse woody debris. Understory very open; ground and shrub layer sparse, fairly continuous. Thin litter layer. Dark silty loam with little humus. No obvious disturbance.

Mature forest dominated by Acer saccharum. Patchy subcanopy, shrub layer almost absent. Ground layer continuous and reasonably diverse. Leaf litter continuous. Soil, dark silty-loam with thick humus layer, very soft with nice organic layer. Old barbed wire. Decaying logs (elm?). On an island surround by Phalaris-dominated wetland. 81cm DBH Quercus rubra is southwest corner of plot.

Band of swamp on south and west sides of Powers Lake. On floating mat. Dense moss cover-not Sphagnum. Sphagnum present in areas as small patches. Plot is 30m south of lake edge. Grades into narrow zone around edge of lake dominated by Carex lasiocarpa.

Very mature second growth stand dominated by tall Acer saccharum (45-50cm DBH). scattered large Quercus rubra. May have been grazed a long time ago. Much deadfall throughout stand = Ulmus americana and occasional Juglans cinerea.
Undisturbed wet meadow on floating sphagnum mat. In "pot hole" surrounded by old growth big woods forest. Devoid of weeds.
Mature forest with straight boled trees reaching 65 cm DBH. On level terrace south of Rush River Heavy, moist silty soil.

Forest on shallow ridges and channels on bottom lands along Minnesota River. On moist heavy silty soils. Was flooded much of spring and early summer. Abundant woody debris including many trunks in various stages of decay.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Dominated by medium diameter (30-45cm) Acer saccharum and Tilia. Canopy with small gaps (3 medium diameter snags), although being filled in quick. Nearly continuous thin layer of leaf litter. Thin humus layer. Soil is dark silty loam with some sand. Small diameter woody debris. Small patches of moss.

Soil sand with about 10% gravel. Slope is immediately above the Zumbro River and grades to oak woodland on ridge above. About 50% of plot is open sand, stable here. Plot is 20m south of large eroded gully. Prairie ~4 acres. Lower slope with occasional Populus tremuloides, upper with occasional Quercus macrocrapa, Juniperus virginiana, and Fraxinus pennsylvanica.

Soil sandy silt loam. Dolomite outcrops occur on upper and lower slopes; plot is mid-slope. Largest pine in plot is 53cm DBH. Little to no pine regeneration; Acer saccharum and Acer rubrum seedlings/saplings common.
Large expanse of rolling sand dunes. About 20% of plot's area is bare sand, most slightly raised mole hills. Releve ~25m below crest of dune. Most of vegetation is less than 0.5m height.

Hastily prepared but good sample of the interior of north 1/2 of island. Many herbs uncommon possibly because past grazed? Canopy gaps, or large patches of Matteuccia, Sambucus, or Laportea? Large trees, and snags. Rank uncertain.
Releve in best part of 40 acre pine/hardwood forest. 50cm DBH Pinus, 45cm DBH Quercus. Tall straight trees, snags, downed logs, Charred stumps. Multi-stem Tilia. Rich soil with cobbles over granite.
Beautiful 50cm DBH red oaks and bur oaks in past grazed mesic forest. Lacks microtopography and varied subcanopy but recovery is good. Snags, downed logs. Much oak leaf litter, sparse ground layer.
Lowland hardwood (almost harddwood swamp) portion of a mesic oak forest. Wet/moist pools, complex/densely packed layers to 2m, many down trunks and limbs. Probably 5-10 more species if had more time.

Probable old-growth forest. Snags and large down wood. Good microtype. Plot near low margin where species and structure diversity is higher than the slightly higher center of maple basswood stand. Snags and large down wood. Complex species patterning.

Steep-rolling dunes at northeast end Little Rock Lake. Openings are treeless; treeless; bur oak/hazel at margins. 10-30% bare ground; 0-8% litter; and tufts of Schizachne/Panicum; Stipa, Poa pratensis in patches.

Sumac dominated opening with aspen border north of plot where slopes down to creek. Old rubbish in/by plot. Appears restorable. Dark sand on Mississippi River outwash. Prairie species spindly among abundant. Poa pratensis and woody species.

2 acre opening at east side of Zuleger Creek foot bridge is disturbed. Difficult to classify. Threatened by woody encroachment. Similar composition as dry prairie/savanna but sandy loam here more productive.

Small 30x60m wet meadow in good condition and lacking Phalaris. Surrounded by Populus tremuloides and upland shrubs, Viburnum lentago and Corylus americana. Snowmobile trail through middle of meadow. Needs burning, reroute trail.
Typical willow swamp in central portion of isolated wetland depression surrounded by Carex lacustris meadow that is mostly firm and not quaking. No Sparganium out of plot area all looks uniform.

Almost half mile band of dry barrens savanna/prairie along crest of glacial beach ridge; facing southwest. Typical Mississippi River outwash sand, well-sorted, no gravel. Pine plantation on top land, dense oaks on lower slope.

This plot plus a 3x20m corridor is extent of opening in shrub swamp (Alnus-Salix-Cornus-Carex stricta) that extends to lake; private lawn extends 100m to northeast to base of slope. On old flat lake plain, approximately 100m from old beach (dune) ridge.

3 acre patch of old forest in young disturbed, dry-mesic, low-divers oak/aspen forest. Plot on moist soil along small stream. Coarse debris; ground cover sparse. 60-80 tiny sterile Botrychium virginianum seen here; not seen elsewhere. 2 Fraxinus by trail: Fraxinus americana?

1 of 2 releves in 60-acre fen, this in central ericaceous zone. Low diversity in poor fen, releve is typical. 12 Larix to 6m. Old ditch across fen from road to north-northwest is dominated by Scirpus cyperinus.

1 of 2 releves in 60 acre fen. Plot approximately 80m from west-central margin (#5085 is in center). Dominant graminoid species patchy in rich fen but uniform in height/productivity/species composition. Old ditch across fen is dominated by Scirpus cyperinus.

Shallow basin by stream flowing north to Shakopee Lake. Formerly partly wooded swamp. Probably past-flooded by beaver. Meadow unusually dry in 1995: water level below peat surface + dense sedge thatch.

Fine 5 acre stand on clay-loam 100m from lake. Older trees and more diverse species. Snags, all sizes of coarse woody debris, tip-up pits/mounds. Litter cover 50%, well- decayed; 40% bare. Heavy deer browse. No Botrychium, despite a long search.

Former sugaring site with continued selective cutting of dead trees. Tip-up mounds. Ground cover: 5% coarse woody debris, all sizes; 65% Acer litter well-decomposed; 25% bare ground. Acer 40-90cm DBH. Stoney, clayey loam. Shady, open.

Mature dry-mesic forest typical of less-disturbed part of park. Tip-up pits/mounds common. No visible cut stumps. All Tilia multi-stemmed. Snags. Down slender birch logs. Some boulders on ridge crest. Mille Lacs Moraine.

Diverse forest near margin of upland "island" in drumlinized landscape. Tip-up mounds and finer microtopography; coarse woody debris, some well-decayed; no cut stumps. Herbs layer fairly thin. Collected Botrychium lanceolatum, matricariifolium and mormo here, 7/27/1995.
Plot on crest of highest bedrock knob along top edge of quarry face. Plot is 6x16 m; on best native vegetation on this side of County Road 55.

permanent_plot_type_description: ex. metal tag on nearby tree
remarks: Described as a wet aspen swamp. Appears to be a level area between two knolls. [Small plot size 2x2 with additional species.]

permanent_plot_type_description: ex. metal tag on nearby tree
remarks: Described as krumholz. 40% of plot is exposed rock; 95% of rock surface is covered by crustose lichens. Lichens include Cladonia rangiferina.

permanent_plot_type_description: ex. metal tag on nearby tree
remarks: Described as high impact area at edge of cliff below parking lot. Bare rock =40% of plot; gravel =20%. Parmelia? (lichen) covers 15% of rock; other crustose lichen covers 60% of rock surface.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
permanent_plot_type_description: ex. metal tag on nearby tree
remarks: Forested swamp south intersection of Hwy 61 and road to radio tower.

permanent_plot_type_description: ex. metal tag on nearby tree
remarks: Releve located on exposed talus about halfway up slope from edge of talus. Large stones (approximately 2ft in diameter) loose. Approximately 65% of plot = rock Crustose lichens cover~ 95% of rock surface.

permanent_plot_type_description: ex. metal tag on nearby tree
remarks: Paper birch forest in ravine.

permanent_plot_type_description: ex. metal tag on nearby tree
remarks: Described as young balsam fir stand; appears to have significant birch/aspen component. 15% of plot = exposed rock. Moss cover = 5-25%. Cladonia rangiferina cover < 5%.

permanent_plot_type_description: ex. metal tag on nearby tree
remarks: Paper birch forest just north of road to tower. Artemesia canadensis record nearby.

Poorly drained, thin soil over sandstone bedrock. All large aspen dead or dying; 20-25% deadfall. Succeeding to black ash. Tree cores - Fraxinus :30 years, Ulmus: 30 years. Charred wood indicates past fire.
Moist peat over bedrock, pockets of standing water. Sphagnum hummocks. Some dead aspen and birch.
Well drained, silty-loam on upland above steep southwest facing slope along Kettle River.

Very poorly drained, wet organic muck. Cattail in wetter areas. In Kettle River floodplain bordered to west by silver maple floodplain forest. Part of large sedge meadow interspersed with willow. Some of water supplied by seepage. Topographic context: depression/flat.
Moist, seasonally flooded, poorly drained, brown, sandy-clay flood plain of Kettle River. Slight rise in elevations in northeast corner of plot.
Area where releve done was burned this spring. 100m squared plot not actually laid out but approximatly 100m2 area around center. 12 inches black loam fine sand/fine sandy loam.
Very poorly drained, moist sandy loam covered by 2 feet of organic matter and with sphagnum. Bordered by Black Ash swamp, Tamarack, and Mixed hardwoods.

Somewhat excessively drained, white sand beneath narrow organic and ash layer. Stumps with fire scars. Scattered rocks. Pinus and Acer very old. Soil core would not penetrate deeper than 8". 7% deadfall.

Somewhat excessively drained, mesic sandy soil with some horizon development. Variations in vicinity include Corylus cornuta replacing Corylus americana and Betula papyrifera as co-dominant. Several rocks-covered by vegetation. 3% deadfall.
Mesic to dry,  somewhat excessively drained, sandy with some rocks and gravel. Fire scarred (charred) logs on ground but no fire scars on trees.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Mesic, excessively drained, sandy-loam, buff reddish color with some rock. Fire scars on cut stumps, 5% deadfall.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Very poorly drained organic soil, between upland ridge and St. Croix river. Dead fall 25%, much Balsam deadfall in area.

Releve's purpose to characterize relatively undisturbed aspen, but whole stand has much evidence of prior grazing. This is inclusion of higher quality than average to try to capture the fullest flora list possible.

Some oak 115 yrs old, DBH 41 cm. Releve for floristic purposes. Really recent logging road 1-2 yrs old. Plot on a slight rise. This area appears to have been previously grazed. Releve for floristic purposes.

Area includes gentle southwest and northwest facing slopes. About 70% shaded floor Approximately 1" friable A horizon over black fine sandy loam becoming more clay downward. Compacts in cover but at 10 inches. Some tip-up, fair amount dead. This area subsequently heavily damaged by windstorm in 1994.
Level, fair number of oaks are diseased. Ground layer is very rank.

Site heavily degraded by proximity of lakeshore development. Majority of site dominated by an aspen mix. No EO quality maple or priority communities remain. Releve in maple inclusion (not an EO-too small).
DBH's avgerage 20-30 cm. Area is level. Much litter. This releve intended to help understand aspen forest at edge of its range. Not an EO because NOT A PRIORITY community.

The purpose of this releve was to characterize floristic composition of aspen in this part of community. This is 2nd growth aspen, DBH's 10-30, fairly scattered from each other. Little shrub canopy. Some infrequent bur oak >60 DBH.
Just north of lake, less mature than in Dorr wildlife management area.

Purpose of releve is to characterize aspen in this township as well as possible. No EO because site is being actively logged. Up slope just west of swamp symbol on map-40x10 to keep away from logging.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: 2 1/2 to 3 inches black clay loam in A horizon on top of light tan clay. Lots of deadfall, dead and down.
Forby prairie with very parlandy aspect.
Wet prairie band - very narrow, releve a bit longer than wide. Far northeast end.
Gently rolling between aspen island and clump of Salix.
Main slope in center, west of big wetland peninsula extending north.
Smooth signature on photo. Level site at the top of the hill. Northeast end site 22.
Signature more textured on photo. Base of north facing slope adjacent to marsh.
Undulating surface-no overall slope. Degraded brush prairie.
Just east of tiny lake and north of willow clump Very forby - about 2/3 of the cover is graminoids.
West of Typha Circle, northeast of lake. Grey signature on photo.
Area looks completely dominated by Sorghastrum from a distance. Much less forby - is this a restoration?

Area includes gentle southwest facing slope <15 degree and northwest facing <5 degrees, about 70% shade. Unknown depth, friable litter about 1 inch over black fine sandy-loam, becoming clayier with depth. Very homogenous light brown fine sand at 10 inches.
Purpose of this releve is to show floristic composition of woods in this area. A very messy stand that I'd judge to be previously grazed. Hard to access whether messiness is all from past land use.

On a long thin north trending bar that may be an old ditch or fence line. Bar is about 5 meters wide. Releve longer than wide. Atypical, may not want to use in statewide analysis. Purpose of releve was to capture floristic distribution of some species of less wet conifer swamps. Atypical.
Eastern margin of wetland. Either "wet meadow" or very open willow swamp. Some scattered lone tamarack farther west.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Dominated by sugar maple with scattered paper birch and large yellow birch. Much sugar maple reproduction in all layers. Depauperate herb layer mainly of northern species. In low area. Selectively logged.
Small mature stand. Additional notes on field form.
Wet mesic prairie - entered from south. Base of slope level area between wetland and knoll to east.
The fir is very dense. Ground layer and understory are shaded and sparse, but not as depauperate in species as one might expect.

North facing slope with no sign of cutting or grazing, lots of deadfall. Note that the Aster macrophyllus in this plot is A. mac. This is somewhat unusual as the prevalent for aster in east Polk county is Aster ciliolatus. Topographic context: middle/lower.
This is a good example of aspen in this area, part of a fairly contiguous block of wooded land.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: This releve at top of hill about 30m west of road. Very nice balance of groundlayer species. Abundant and diverse fungi. Floor is predominantly litter.
Soil 2" black loam over heavy light brown clay. Fair amount deadfall < 20 cm DBH. To characterize aspen. I've been in a lot worse aspen than this. Releve west of pond.
A face of a forest that continually changes in dominance.

Very heavily shaded regenerating maple basswood stand with well developed litter layer and little ground cover other than woody species. Present regeneration looked to be about 40yrs old. Much variability and would take many releves to characterize.
Total moss cover 25-30% is mainly feather mosses. Only small proportion sphagnum. Considerable evidence of selective log Accessible to pasture but not actively grazed.
Formerly grazed (rested since around 1960) much dead and down elm 1 1/2 inch litter over heavy brown clay.

Canopy gaps from birch blowdown and dead elm, fair amount of dead and down. Typical DBH of live around 30cm. Signs of prior selective logging. > 90 deg and ferocious mosquitoes. Soil: 1 1/2 inches friable dark brown to black loam on black heavy clay, impenetrable at 7 inches.

This area appears to have occasional use by cattle, 
but there is a certain compaction that seems unnatural and no fence. Purpose of releve is floristic, not a good high quality community.
Lowland hardwoods north of old field.

Very dense tamarack and very open understory with 50-75% feather moss cover. Includes Sphagnum species, Climacium dendroides and Pleurozium schreberi. Somewhat drier tamarack than most examples in Polk County.
Soil 3" black sandy loam over 5" black clay, becoming heavier below. Not in a wetland, borders southeast shore of a woodland wetland. Wet mixed woods.
Similar canopy to releve 96-01 but less dead and down, less litter. Less structural diversity.
Very patchy canopy because of blowdown. This area is adjacent to a hayfield and may have been influenced by it. Not best example of community type, releve for floristic purposes.
Floristically interesting but this slope feels degraded. About 15% of area is bare sand. There should be some rare plants up here.
Two neighboring slopes north and northeast have considerable dominance by little bluestem. I would map prairie farther than on Wildlife Management Area map. Topographic context: upper/middle.

Level and very sunny, very rank and forby. The very large Equisetum in area is similar to very large Equisetum at Gully fen. Large for Equisetum fluviatile, needs to be checked for Equisetum telmataia.
Purpose of releve was to get a releve from Platanthera praeclara location.
Level brush praire, SW part.

Vegetation seems too uniform and number of grass species too small. Too much Argerardii. I wonder if this is a resturation that succeeded, but too much woody? Seems funny to be so dry and no Schizacrium, Muhlenbergia cuspidata or Rudbeckia? Need to check soils map, vegetation too dry for physiographic setting.
No shrubs.
Forbs and gramminoids co-dominant.
Typical swale with willow and sedge.
Open prairie at south end of field.
Dry prairie on steep southeast facing slope, all on gravel. Maybe only remaining gravel prairie in county. Area north of here is being gravel mined.

East end of western knob-crest of slope-base is shot but crest is probably not very good every other year. Lots of last years Melilotus stalks. Actually slope is all directions because releve is on crest and goes down sides a bit.
Northwest facing slope about 45 degrees midslope position, a more mesic aspect of this dry prairie.

West of Goodwin lake, pleasing but more artificial stand. Appears that oak has been selectively thinned so not a good example of natural community, but ok for ground layer floristics. About 50-60% bare litter.

This very open canopy ash swamp is characterized by open mucky pools and vegetation on hummocks and fallen logs. Cover abundance of ground layer is percent of cover on hummocks, which is about 40% of total ground cover.

Must have been grazed. Very disappointing. General scene out of releve is 100% Carex pensylvanica on groundlayer. This was best area I could find. Litter about 50% oak. Topographic context: crest/upper.

General scene mixed canopy mainly 25-30 DBH, some scattered large oak and basswood Reproduction dominated by Acer saccharum, woody species more abundant than forbs in ground layer. Solidago flexicaulis most abundant forb. Carex pensylvanica only occasional. Better litter than 94-07. The balance of tree dominance in this releve is pretty typical of the situation of co-dominance that occurs in this area.
Nearly level just west of small pond, ground layer mainly open litter. Lots of browse. Something is selectively eating Botrychium virginianum. Several large DBH birch logs about 45cm.

This is prob the "best"stand seen in Mahnomon County in 1995 field season. Less internal topography diversity and litter level than Island Lake Woods. Litter here 1.5" thick. Active sugarbush camp east of releve.

Regenerate maple with lots of open litter at top of plot, almost solid. Diversity in plot is so high because plot extends from upper midslope to foot of northwest facing hill. Fraxinus nigra is at base of hill.
Heavy shade on ground, about 95%. about 50m east of section line road. Majority of maple young: 3-12 DBH. Some very old stumps with moss. No recent cutting.
