Very aesthetically unpleasing, dominate sapling Acer saccharum, DBH 1.5-5cm. Very few big trees, almost no ground layer, solid litter dominated by oak Much dead/down, some stumps probably 5-15 years old.
80m east of road BIA compart 37, stand 3, south end 6 miles south of Highway 200. Some cutting by road. Releve sufficiently east to get out of it. Much more balanced for composition than stand 2.
Incredibly homogeneous wet meadow at northwest end of north Twin Lake. Topographic context: depression/flat.

Rather xeric woods on bouldery till elevation 1450. Most birch seen to date in a single stand in Mahn. County. Rather disturbed feeling to the stand as if formerly grazed. Betula papyrifera occasional to frequent. Releve in best part of stand.
Northeast of the traditional graveyard (terrible road). This stand was remarkable for the amount of elm in it.
Despite high cover of regenerate maple, this stand seems more floristically comparable to oak forest.
Black Ash opening around a round ephemeral pond with little vegetation because of very heavy deer use. Circular releve about 3-4m wide around a 20m  pond. Biggest ash > 55dbh, smallest about 19.
Carmen Converse has black and white photos of this plot ends at #18 slides end at 6 1.1 miles north of Mah Konce. Good acorn crop in this place this year. Very unusual.   Undulating level ground.
This is one of the Botrychium mormo releves.
AB quality Maple/basswood - open level stand S of trail.
Near boundary between Kahl and MCT on upland ridge.
Leads down to edge of ephemeral pond with ash, which is not in releve.
Very ANOMALOUS!! Mixed hardwood swamp. Dark interesting signature on photo.
Just west of a sedge meadow which is just north of a small lake Birch wetland is west of here. Low, wet site.
West side of large wetland-mostly marsh and wet meadow with some rich fen. Very heavy thatch in this area.
Not far southwest of White Earth river. Rolling topography.
Call this Oak Forest Would be B quality if not for Zanthoxylum.
Very close to fenceline, area southeast of here logged.

Acer saccharum litter only about 1" thick. No visible fungal activity Some salvage logging in past and present but real logging northwest of here. The Quercus macrocarpa is dead - created canopy gap as big as releve plot.

Releve just west of road that goes into Becker County East of White Earth Lake. Stand shows as an island in square cut over on NAPP-Regenerate hardwood, fair amount recent storm damage in D6. There is a head of a southwest flowing ephemeral stream on west side of plot. Stand is north of county line.
Conifer swamp east of Jessie Lake and south of Highway 113.
Amazing resemblance to minerotrophic portions of tamarack at Randeen Ridge/Moose River in Marshall Co!
Releve is at extreme north end of a draw, not a wetland. Odd mix of wet/lowland species. Access via logging trail and then southwest. Dark signature on photo. Great deal of bare ground.
Yew point between Hwy 4 and S Twin Lake Low, wet area just wet of lake, really defies community classification

This releve and releve 100-02 are a pair to show the change in vegetation in area. I take to be pitted outwash. This is the upslope member of the pair. Soil sandy. These releves not far west of the road. Not an EO because not priority community. Linear north-south ridges in this area, litter mainly oak. Topographic context: crest/upper.
This is a paired releve with 100-01 to show changes in linear knolls. Downslope member of pair. Much down aspen. Soil is sand. No EO, Resembles wet aspen in Marshall County south of Moose River.
Reputed to be native pine stand. On sand. Understory fairly open, looks disturbed but no fences.
Incredibly sterile stand about 80% or more bare oak litter. Very Xeric. South of lake in a flagged study area. Logging to south of here.
Purpose of releve is floristic. Stand is too highly managed (all cutting of deciduous understory) to encourage pine. Not worth an EO. Eastern most of 2 releves.

Contin conifer stand southwest of log house. Releve from crest to base of slop. Disturbed but interesting mixed conifer stand on high ground. Poor community quality because of selective present management.
Nice stand of minimum maintenance. Fair amount of internal topography variability. EW road (access via road west side Dale Danks). Stand becomes less mature westward.
Red signature of southwest side of field.
Low wet feeling area, despite elevation, just west of long NS field. Fair amount deadfall, too much Uvularia, must be formerly grazed.
Regenerate stand - old stumps were 40+ DBH mainly oak, some deadfall. Signs of salvage logging. Just north of trail southwest of EL corner.

Immature forest. Releve done to document micro site for Botrychium mormo. Very sparse open litter. Straddles ephemeral stream in low area between 2 ponds. (Cover/abundance values for forbs created during releve entry--DSW 1/22/99).
Top of long point south of Sugarbush Lake.
This releve not a good quality community, but to show floristics. Few oak forests available for releve that are not full of cattle. No EO because not good enough.
Releve collected because of abundance of narrow-leaved anemones. Hopes that they were Anemone multifida, but head shape later in season defined them as Anemone cylindrica. No trees.
This releve was done so we would have vegetation data in a mammal grid, not because it was an example of a community. It is more likely old field than prairie, despite species list.
Just west of circular wetland about 10m across west side of unit. Rather atypical floristic composition for prairies in this area.
East side of Vanose Lake.
This releve was collected "for descriptive purposes only." Rough looking area on photo west of lake in northwest part of managed area. This area needs fire.
Site is becoming shrubby but would respond nicely to fire. This prairie tax exempt.
North facing slope on knoll west of oak grove. Fairly dry prairie, but very small area by native prairie.
In MCBS mammal grid. Burned 3 years ago according to E Goodwen tribal biologist. South of old ditch.
This site is pretty disturbed feeling as a community but floristically superb. It is that the site becomes more mesic up slope. Best spring flora in county to date.

Elongate 1908 NH stand, runs EW from crest down upper slope. Toward ephemeral stream just above 1600 contour line. Supercanopy has very few trees but they are very large. Called oak forest because despite high cover D35 maple, seems like a drier site than usual.

Bouldery till soil-regenerating stand. This releve only for purposes of comparison with older stands. Ascending northwest edge of hill, rocky topography. 4 miles south of intersection on strawberry mountain road, ascending northwest edge of hill, rocky topography.
Head of Badboy Creek. Canopy is so broken that it is nearly impossible to get a representative releve.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: B quality, low species diversity. Nice structure. Parts of stand near road have had oak select logged in last few years. All these stands seem to be relatively comparable.
Called "northern hardwoods" in BIA database. C 39 S 8. despite lack of groundlayer diversity, it feels like an excellent stand.
Mixed, dry mesic hardwood and conifer stand.
This area appears not to have been mowed for hay. More structurally heterogeneous than releve 01 at same site.
This area has history of having been mowed for hay within past 60 years. Very open shrub layer, quite structurally homogeneous.

1.2 miles south of Pine Bend graveyard, east of road. Some fair patches of moss. Graminoids in this releve were not identified although they were coll. Very unreliable guess as to identity-probably shouldn't use.
This releve is in the mammal grid.
This releve is in the mammal grid.
East side of south end of wetland. Most un-diverse wet meadow I've seen. This is it for species in a 10x10 plot.

npc_type_name: Green Ash - Bur Oak - Elm Forest
Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: This is the best I can do for "riverine" forest. Stand is too variable to get any releve truly "typical" of it. Just down slope of oak south of where a road comes from gravel pit.
North of County 6 and West of County 118.
"Birch fir" community on west facing slope.
West end north side.
This is the north easternmost triangular opening in northwest of section. Established prairie needing fire. Thick clay loam block, 10cm over tough yellow clay with boulders.
Soil is loam, about 8cm black loam over course gravelly white clay. North end of opening in center of western 1/2 of section. Perhaps the clay forms a hardpan contributing to wet conditions here.
About 20 cm black fine sandy loam over 10cm gray fine sandy  clay. Underlain by grey fine sand becoming light brown below.
If this area were burned it would appear to be dominated by bluestem. Forb cover about 80%

Loamy soil. The finest and most varied unspoiled remnant of natural prairie in Hennepin County. Slope was most likely grazed in the past, but now has mild erosion. Slope has steep ravines with thickets.
Steep south facing slope with loamy course sand. Area contains natural floodplain forest along Minnesota River and prairie remnants.

300 meter square plot 12-20 degree west facing slope on loamy sand. Area includes floodplain forest on Minnesota River and prairie remnant on the steep south facing bluffs. Dry prairie-sand/gravel. --FSH

Larger plot with 0-10 degree slopes and loamy sand soil. Plot contains Poa pratensis. Disturbance history probably includes mowing in 1970 to keep encroaching shrubs down. Mount Gilboa. Very disturbed site with low diversity.
15-25 degree south and southwest facing slopes on limestone rubble and outcrop. Several letters are filed with this releve. 0.3 ha plot. Note late date, end of Oct.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: This is not really a tamarack swamp. It is an example of a low wet aspen/balsam poplar/tamarack woods that I am guessing could represent a more extensive presettlement community. Mainly all drained and farmed. Based on land survey bearing trees for the northeastern part of county.
Hummock and hollow topography
Part of a transect west of road, north of 48 through oak into conifer wetland. This area very rich with considerable blowdown.
Dry end of a transect, crest of Dohrman's ridge west of road. Graminoid layer mainly domianted by Poa pratensis. This area chosen because least dominated by Poa pratensis.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: This is middle member of a transect from crest down west slope of Dohrmans. On slope itself, between oak savanna upland and conifer lowland.
About 20% bare ground and parklike feathermoss layer with Pleurozium schreberi, Polytrichium species, Climacium dendroides, Mnium species. Seems odd in retrospect, no other sedges in releve.

Fairly dry level aspen appears to be all "gone back" agricultural land of variable age not fenced. Not a priority community. Fair amount of blowdown. Releve for purpose of understanding aspen community, Quercus macrocarpa pole to mid-age stand.
Low wet woodland west of road into excellent fen in East Park Wildlife Management Area. No EO not a priority community, this is to give an example of wet aspen woods in area.

Another alkaline area-to get enough releves of this type for community analysis. Completely dried open mud area with salt deposits. Soil 3 cm black loam grading to 2 cm fine sandy black clay to coarse grey sand.
Black fine sandy loam grading to dark fine sand over dark coarse sand. There is a ditch running through this part of prairie about 30-40 meters northeast of releve.
Woods between prairie/wetland complex and disturbed prairie/oldfield. Not priority community - no corresponding EO.
Prairie zone between edge of aspen woodland and marsh dominated by Phragmites. Soil about 25cm homogeneous heavy black clay loam grading to gray sandy clay over bright limonite colored medium sand.
On east side of sedge meadow. Mature aspen DBH >30 with dense ash understory. Deadfall everywhere. Large white pines. Releve quality may be affected by horrendous mosquitos!!
Slightly more overgrown area, slightly more degraded opening than 8901. Dry prairie, maybe oak savannah?
In area that shows as a big opening on topo map. Openings are up to 30m in diameter with open Corylus under open-grown oak. Quality of these openings varies from D to B.
Narrow band of oak woods between road and rich fen south of transmission line. Such dense corylus that ground layer is almost invisible. Soil black sandy loam about 15cm to course sand/gravel.
50m east of dry prairie. Interesting to see so much Aralia so close to prairie. Appears relatively undisturbed but terribly low species diversity.
Very small area of oak woodland where prairie species continue under oaks. Was probably maintained formerly by grazing? Just south of widest prairie opening on Marshall County side in NE07.

Largest opening that shows on photo at crest of ridge in section 7. Anomalous species composition so heavily dominated by big bluestem leaves. Wonder if being manipulated for grass seed-suspicious. May not want to use this releve for classification purposes.
"Oak opening" in oak woodland.

Releve at northeast end of big opening-same opening as releve 54-5, but seems natural. Whole area east of road is Stipa dominated and west of road is big blue dominated. Use this releve for classification purposes, not 54-5

East of influence of ditch. In open area of extensive fen that has patches of Phragmites and shrubs. Majority of fen is open-contiguous with fen on Pennington county side of line, which may also have releves.
Wetter than 36-01, between wetland and aspen. (Note that graminoid cover/abundance values were not entered on field form, but were assigned as R during data entry--DSW 1/21/99)
Very wet brush prairie.
Edge of brush prairie.
Prairie about 30-50m north of woods and narrow transition zone between woods and Salix candida. Site falls off quickly into shrubby rich fen. This is thus a transitional area.
East side of Goose lake, immediately north of public access to lake on small hill with ice contact to north and west.  Woods typical in overstory, but understory sparse. Litter thick and continuous.

Oak-ash-basswood between lakes is moderately heterogeneous with both canopy and understory patchy, though most species are represented and structure is typical. 0-1 cm litter, 5% exposed soil. Largest oak in open grown, others not.
Woods relatively undisturbed. Tip up mounds, relief<10cm, 2.1. On North facing slope is Acer saccharuma and Betula papyrifera. 2 species of caterpillar are defoliating trees, especially Tilia.
Top of kame east of Kittleson Lake. Woods open, trees widely spaced though canopy closed and understory low. Tip-up mound relief <20cm, 1.1. Caterpillars defoliating the canopy.

A 2 acre plot within a ravine with 60 degree slopes. Soil is a very sandy loam. A spring is located at the mouth of ravine along a sandstone exposure. Surrounding uplands have been grazed and old junk is present.
Releve seems to be lacking graminoids and possibly other species (compare with DNR releve #136 by JCA, which is nearby). 1 acre plot. Dark brown peat with stumps from fallen trees. See also #5536.

2 acre plot with 0-30 degree slopes and dark black loam. Parts of the ravine system that have been excluded were cut once and/or are being grazed heavily. Trees are young and are homogeneous in age structure. Note late date, end of October.

1 acre plot with 0-30 degree slopes and dark black sandy loam; grey till pm. Releve is on a wooded ridge above the Minnesota River. Adjacent areas are heavily grazed and there are fields on the upland. Ravine contains junk and cannabis, appears grazed. Note late date, end of October.
0.3 ha plot on 0-5 degree slopes on the shoulder of west side of valley. Silty loam soils are present over gelena limestone. Sinkhole present.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: 0.3 ha plot on a 10 NE slope over loess soil. Quercus ellipsoides to 22 in DBH. Other plants ID in area (outside plot) include: Solidago ulnifolia on west-facing ravine slope and Aster pronanthoid on abandoned road along ravine bed. Note late date, end of October.

npc_type_name: Sugar Maple - Basswood - Red Oak - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: 0.1 ha plot on a 15-20 degree north slope consisting of silty loam over dolomite rubble.

2 acre plot with 50-90 degree east slopes and sandy-sandy black loam soil on the St. Croix Valley wall of dolomite-limestone composition. Sugar maple basswood forest extends from upper lip of valley to the river's edge.
0.5 ha plot on 2-10 degree, east facing slope. Soil consists of deep colluvium over platteville limestone. Tilia to 31.5 inches in DBH and Acer to 20 inches. Spring seeps common.

0.5 ha plot on 0-10 degree north slope with loamy medium sand. Quercus alba to 26.8 inch DBH and Quercus ellipsoidalis to 15.5 inch DBH. Utrica, Pilea, Echinocystis, and Plantago only along trails. Goodyera fruiting abundantly. Note late date, end of October.
0.3 ha plot with 5-20 north slope. Tilia to 18 inch DBH and multi-stemmed. Acer to 16 inch DBH. Moderate logging estimated 20 years ago.
0.1 ha plot with poorly to moderately drained soils. This flat area between lakes has a moderately rich understory and good fire protection. Logging has occurred here in the past.
0.3 ha plot with this years litter on gravelly till. 10 degree slopes run northeast, north and northwest to a two degree depression.
0.1 ha plot is on a 0-5 degree northeast facing slope. Releve is roughly centered on dead birch. D5 Betula is at the north edge and Populus tremuloides is all around.
Young white pine forest (45 years old) on bedrock at edge of Superior hiking trail. 2nd growth following logging and fire. 7 old-growth cut pine stumps in plot. Many smaller pine dead.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Cool conifer woodland on Shovel Point. Dominated by Picea glauca, Picea mariana, Pinus strobus and Abies. On bedrock. Mosses and lichen dominated ground layer. Two trails through plot.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Minnesota Point)
remarks: Mature/old growth red pine forest; part of a larger stand dominated by white and red pines. Long, narrow stand on sand, just behind lake. Superior shore dunes. Relatively little human disturbance in plot.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: 8 inches dark/grey clayey silt with cobbles/gravel, friable, to yellow silt. Pine mode 50-75cm DBH; smaller sizes common. Deciduous mode 25-35cm DBH; larger trees to 45cm infrequent. Decayed limbs and tip-ups throughout-mainly pine; pine duff 2-5cm; patches of bare ground. Basal area 190 square feet. Large boulder at base, scattered small boulders in plot. Pinus strobus 72ch DBH at 102 rings.

Dark silty clay of mounded alluvium bounded by channels fed with rivulets of groundwater. Releve includes a portion of these saturated silty areas. Walnuts not leafed out at time of sample. Bright sunshine to substrate. Modal DBH 20-40cm, max size <50cm rare (Salix amygdaloides) Rank herb layer.

Mounded, channeled alluvium with ground water seeps but no rivulets. Saturated to mesic; silt loam with some sand. At north facing base of old alluvial terrace of Pine Creek. Interrupted canopy, mostly 20-30cm DBH with occasional large Salix amygdaloides or Ulmus thomasii in area. Floerkea proserpinacoides collection.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mature mesic oak forest. Dark silt loam, thin humus/duff layer; deep soils, no cobbles, clayey subsoil. Even aged stand with most trees multi-stemmed. Abundant tip-ups and broken limbs; snags. Old stumps rare to occasional.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: Mature to old growth mesic oak forest, west facing(upper-lower slope); heavy clay loam, friable, dark to 15cm depth. Subsoil clay. Rocky, gravel thin humus layer. nice profile. Open grown trees, mode 40-50cm DBH; infrequent max to 65cm (size 15-25cm common). Basal area 160 square feet per acre. Some cutting, 1 very decayed stump, many downed limbs, tip-ups, broken snags.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Dark silty-clay loam with some sand. Alluvium deposits 15cm over rock base. Crest of mound 2 feet above streambed. Edge of plot at toe of west facing slop with seepage rivulet. East border with stream and rocky shore. Mature forest 45-65cm mode DBH; decreasing in DBH as approaching stream, mode 10-25cm. Small valley with cold streambed.

Dry-mesic maple basswood; co-dominante red oak/basswood with abundant Acer. Mode DBH 25-35cm. Cirque shaped ravine; dense mulch with thick humus layer-dark and friable: silt loam with some cobblestones. Tip-ups and fallen limbs infrequent. No stumps. Galena outcrops. Quercus rubra at 79cm DBH, >198 rings to center.

Sheer cliff face prosser limestone (Galena) with colluvial soil on ledges and talus in adjacent troughs. Moss and fern cover and bare rock 25-50% cover. Canopy 50-75% cover; gap due to narrow, rocky ravine with dry streambed.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Blue Beech) Seepage Swamp
remarks: Deeply cut; small valley, narrow alluvium. Completely forested. Many seeps and springs-cummingsville limestone/galena. Swamp dominated by 10-25 cm DBH-mode. Open mud and water; 1-5% cover. Old fence.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Lowland hardwood domianted by Quercus macrocarpa. Mode DBH 35-45cm, max rare to 50 cm. Alluvial plain above stream which meanders. Channeled clay silt loam.

Canopy of tall 40-70cm diameter Acer saccharum with two large (85cm+) Quercus rubra just outside plot. Nearly continuous subcanopy of Acer. Much recent die-off of 2-5m tall saplings. Continuous leaf litter. Abundant small diameter coarse woody debris.
Old growth northern hardwood forest dominated by Acer saccharum. Releve spans slight rise typical of undulating terrain. Some coarse woody debris. No cut stumps or evidence of fire near releve.

Old growth northern hardwood forest dominated by Acer saccharum. Small ephemeral stream course in northwest corner of plot. Lots of coarse woody debris. Three cut stumps; probably Betula allegheniensis and possibly cedar.

Old growth northern hardwood forest dominated by Acer saccharum. One Betula allegheniensis stump in releve. Old growth Pinus strobus just west of releve (76 DBH) Some coarse woody debris. Acer rubrum occasional in moisture portions of community. Other areas of native community more sloped.

Mature northern hardwood forest dominated by Acer saccharum. Some parts of native community denser shrub cover. No cut stumps. Coarse woody debris present. Releve located above broad shallow drainages present within natural community.

Old growth cedar forest situated just above Temperance River on old river terrace. No cut stumps. Windthrow opening with paper birch regeneration east of plot. Low rock outcrop on north side. Coarse woody debris present.
Old growth white cedar situated midslope above Temperance River. No evidence of past fire disturbance. Releve includes corner of wet depression in canopy opening. Abundant coarse woody debris.
Hastily surveyed because of pending rain and proximity to stream; vunerable to flash flooding.
Sampled area is on crest of hill and appears more mature than downslope. Used a X-country ski trail as access. This stand should be typed for maple basswood, yellow birch (if not for maple basswood).

Betula lutea stumps, probably cut over 20 years ago. Betula papyrifera large dead fill. It appears that the mature trees aged and died. About 1 stump and 1 dead fall in an area this size. Extensive stand, typed management. Floor at 70% litter.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest

remarks: A small depressional wetland surrounded by steep, successional upland. Dense sedge tussocks at wetland edge, with open water towards the center. A road runs along the western edge of the uplands. Preliminary releve - may not be complete.

Plover Prairie Nature Conservancey Preserve. Potholes in remnant prairie/wild haylands. Lac Qui Parle Wild Fire Management Area to north along MN river. Some agriculture/grazing nearby. Bordered by roads on two sides.

Plover Prairie Nature Conservancy Reserve. Potholes in remnant prairie/wild haylands. Lac Qui Parle Wildlife Management Area to the north, along MN river. Some grazing/agriculture present. Bordered by two roads.
A small depressional wetland surrounded by successional uplands and hardwood forests along the southern edge. Well developed sedge mat, broken along wetland edge from prior grazing.
Most extensive community in site, patches of Phragmites and Typha. Grades into more extensive marsh-like signature on photo at northeast end of fen. Very dry and end of season, so not best releve.

White signature on very east side of Hangsleben tract right along fence and north of 2 small islands (Salix surrounding Spartina) that show on photo NAPP 3084-129. Vegetation continues same across fence to east.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Moderate coarse woody debris-including same yellow birch.+/- thick deciduous leaf duff. Gentle within plot, slope to the southeast. Relief from old tip-ups and decayed logs. Stand #1. Soil: 3 inch organic over 2 inch silt over 8 inch very fine silt/sand.

Old growth northern hardwoods on east-southeast facing slope. More yellow birch regeneration in this plot than usual. Selective logging for yellow birch and pine. Yellow birch was once co-dominant in this wet mesic forest.
Plot in narrow isthmus of forest betwenn lake and slough. Floodwaters leaving stagnant water on alluvial silt. Wet soil to 5cm in depth. Mode 50-85 DBH. 220 square feet per acre.
West aspect of large ridge spur, silt loam with cobbles on rock outcrops. Mode DBH 35-45cm with occasional large open grown bur oak. Frequent gaps due to topography and stand age. Varied stand age.

Swale and mounded ridges grad sloping southwest into Phlaris meadow. Moderately well drained, silt, wet mesic, compact. Mode DBH 50-70cm. Large trees >120cm occasional to rare. Woody limbs and tip-ups 1-5%, infrequent.

Dark, sandy silt alluvium, channeled moderately well-drained depressional. All size class present; mode 40-55cm DBH, max size common to 75cm. Community almost bimodal due to gaps. Large subcanopy trees 20-30cm DBH, becoming canopy in absence of larger oaks. Snags, tip-ups, and debris infrequent to occasional. Stand 10-15 feet above stream. Quercus bicolor, 55 cm DBH, 115+ rings.

Alluvial spit forming isthmus between bulrush marshes, only slightly high elev. Saturated silt with standing pools in high water. Poorly drained wet soils. Much debris, very rotted tip-ups. DBH: 15-100cm, max size 40-80cm common. Multi-stemmed trees abundant, especially large buttresses. Standing snags rare.

Bare sand 5-10% cover, several small openings. Dry barrens prairie/savanna in ravine of sand terrace of ancient meander cut into bluff (outside bend). Level terrace to north is old pasture/prairie within west facing ravine. Black oak forms well-defined canopy on north face of bluff on lower slope with sand soil. Powerline above the high-quality open prairie. Large tress border, 35-45cm DBH.

Ravine slopes of old, sandy bench terrace (plainfield sand). Most forest cut with young regrowth of black oak. Releve with larger size trees, spreading crown or crooked boles with lower dead limbs, mode DBH 10-20cm. Common max DBH 25-40cm. Several multi-stemmed trees/stumps. Many areas with thick shrub layer (saplings).

Dry to dry-mesic oak forest on upper slope of ridge spur. On unusual deposit of sand for this topographic position (silty sand/sand) with thin humus and shallow A horizon (2"). Subsoil-red sand. Canopy large spreading oaks, 40-50 cm DBH, with groves or birch. Mode DBH 15-25cm.

Dry to dry mesic; open grown bur oaks-mode 30-45cm DBH, short tress 20-25 meters height. Upper slopes with silt and cobbles. Upper slopes and narrow crest mostly dry-mesic with celtis and red elm. Buckthorn thick in some areas.

On channeled alluvium high above river bed (8-12ft), depressional, but moderately well drained. Mode DBH 20-35cm to max 35-55cm. Dead cottonwood snag in northwest corner of plot. Mostly closed canopy, abundant debris. Soil: dark grey sand silt. Large cottonwood stand outside plot.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Upland forest dominated by mature Quercus rubra. Acer saccharum common in canopy and understory. Tall shrub layer dense; dominated by Corylus and Acer saccharum. Herb layer of low diversity. South-facing ridgetop. Well-drained shallow loam soils over bedrock. Some coarse woody debris.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Upland forest dominated by Quercus rubra. Shrub layer patchy, dominated by Corylus, Abies common in understory. Herb layer depauperate, dominated by Aster mac and Clintonia. South-facing ridgetop. Well-drained loam over bedrock.

Mature forest dominated by Populus tremuloides. Abies component dead or dying from budworm damage. Tall shrub layer interrupted. Herb layer dominated by Clintonia. Abundant coarse woody debris. Some past disturbance. Rocky poorly drained soils.

Mature forest dominated by Betula papyrifera. Abies component dead/dying from budworm damage. Some Abies and Betula blowdown. Tall shrub layer interrupted, dominated by Acer spicatum. Rocky slope. Shallow well-drained soils.

Dark grey, sandy silt; 25cm to clay loam. Dry, broad alluviual channel (bounded on two sides by old terrace remnants) and creek. Super canopy mode DBH 40-50cm (max rare to 90cm); canopy mode 15-25cm. Near maple-bass forest with yellow birch. Infrequent dead limbs and elm snags. Portion of old terrace included in releve with maple basswood element.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Blue Beech) Seepage Swamp
remarks: 5x20m plot parallel to slope along stagnant pool in alluvial channel. Small, flowing rivulets, saturated mud and edges of bank. Many old, saturated fallen logs, moss and herb covered.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Alluvial terrace; level, about 10-12 feet above streambed. Dark silt loam, 7cm to yellow subsoil; friable; good humus layer 1-2cm, duff. Snags occasional outside plot. Located next to trout release post. Large black ash and black maple >35 meter tall = 35% cover. broken limbs and tip-ups common 1-5% - mature forest.

Thick duff; humus layer 1-2 cm; dark silt to yellow silt subsoil. Small, bench terrace above dry streambed; well drained. Upslope community becomes dry-mesic oak forest, abundant tip-ups/limbs. Snags frequent.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Dark, silt loam to yellowish subsoil; good humus, forms concave lateral shape. Medium sized valley nearly all foreste, some cobblestones. Convex longitudinal (upwards). 15-25cm DBH Quercus alba/Elm common.

Level bench terrace about 8' above stream bed. Sandy clay soil. Plot at butt of north facing bluff, mixed tree sizes, 10-35cm mostly. Frequent dead snags and broken decayed limbs. Some rock and gravel present in plot.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Small bench terrace about 6' above stream bed at base of south facing bluff. Old raceway channel at base of bluff; streambed just outside of plot Mode DBH 45-55cm/25-35cm DBH size common. Dark sandy silt deep >20cm depth. Large 55cm bur oak.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Maturing dry-mesic oak forest. Dark friable silt to clay/silt subsoil. Little or no humus layer. Oak duff 2-5cm thick. Most trees forest grown with straight trunks. Multiple trunked trees common; tip-ups, fallen debris occasional. Mode DBH 30-40cm, common max 45-55cm. Older trees white oaks with spreading crowns, most trees are forest grown with straight trunks. Multiple trunked trees common; tip-ups and fallen debris occassional to abundant locally.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Blue Beech) Seepage Swamp
remarks: Large upland ravine ascending northwest form creek valley. Flowing rivulet from spring. Elevated mounds 1-2' above water. Saturated to moderated well drained silt. Stagnant pools. Plot 10x40m within confines of alluvium, peaty silt. Mode DBH 25-35cm, large trees to 50cm DBH infrequent to common.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Maturing oak forest, just above old terrace before maximum gradient. Debris occasional, mode 15-30cm DBH; several multi-stem trees. Elm snags occasional; Prunus serotina snags rare

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: Thin layer of silt over bedrock on narrow ridge spur 5-25m wide crest. Above spring valley cliff and spring fed upland ravine. Dry-mesic, densely shaded. Many oaks, short, crooked boles. White pine DBH 30-65cm. Deciduous trees 25-35cm mode; max size to 50cm. Dry-mesic, densely shaded.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Small stand of lowland forest along Diamond Creek. Large down logs(Ulmus) frequent. Deep rich silt to silty - loam, alluvial, thick duff layer. Some dolomite rocks. Scattered trees with dense understory. Snags occasional. Moderate grazing >15 years ago.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Young stand overall with scattered large trees. Mult-stemmed Tilia. Highly decayed elm logs frequent, snags rare. Some cut logs. Soil: silt loam channeled alluvium, deep rich. Some cut logs.

npc_type_name: Sugar Maple - Basswood - Red Oak - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Slightly drier than average maple basswood stand. Trees large: in plot to 56cm DBH. Out of plot trees to 70cm (Quercus alba, Tilia, Quercus rubra) Snags uncommon. Tip-up mounds occasional. Highly decayed logs frequent. Stumps uncommon. Soil a somewhat compacted dark clay-loam.

npc_type_name: Sugar Maple - Basswood - Red Oak - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Rocky slope - large dolomite boulders frequent from cliffs on upper slope. Canopy trees 25-40 cm DBH mode, rare to 45 cm, scattered Pinus strobus. Trees straight boles. Recent wind damage. Downed logs frequent, all stages decay. Soil a dark silt loam - rocky.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: High quality maple basswood forest with much large Quercus rubra in canopy. Snags occasional. Tip-ups frequent. Decaying wood occasional-later stages of decay. Good understory structure, diverse flora. Mode DBH 35-45 cm, occasional to 62cm. Soil a rocky dark sandy silt loam. Topographic context: upper/middle.

npc_type_name: Sugar Maple - Basswood - Red Oak - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Rather young stand, multi-stemmed trees frequent, snags rare, decaying woody debris rare. Soil a dark, rich silty-clay.  Several rare plants, flora less diverse and drier upper slope. Dolomite outcrops occasional, small and mossy. Mode DBH 15-30cm, occasional to 42cm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mature dry-mesic stand. Grayish brown silty-clay. Snags occasional. Decaying wood occasional, mostly older. Some recent wind damage. Canopy mode DBH 35-45cm occasional to 60 cm. Core 58 cm Quercus rubra-123 rings. Topographic context: upper/middle.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: High-quality immature to mature lowland forest merging into maple basswood on slope. Seepage frequent in this section of valley. Floor dissects with several flows and dry runs. Snags occassional, decaying logs uncommon. Rich alluvial soil. Canopy trees mode DBH: 25-40cm.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Blue Beech) Seepage Swamp
remarks: Small seepage area and surrounding seepage influenced area of valley floor. At base of north facing bluff. Graded into lowland hardwoods. Open water flow areas and sedge dominated areas included. Decaying logs from logging on slope. Frequent soil wet to saturated black, organic. Canopy trees 10-30cm DBH. Topographic context: toe/depression/flat.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Ridge top gently sloping towards steep slope along Hemingway Creek. Snags uncommon, decaying woody debris small and uncommon. Trees straight. Some TSI work in vicinity. Highly decayed old stumps rare. Canopy trees 18-40cm DBH, mode 25-30cm DBH. Soil a dark silty-clay over brown clay. Topographic context: crest/upper.

npc_type_name: Sugar Maple - Basswood - Red Oak - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Mature high-quality stand with 25-55 cm DBH canopy trees, snags occasional. Large old decaying woody debris occasional. Small dolomite outcrops occasional, mossy. No stumps, scattered Pinus strobus in vicinity. Soil dark loam, no rocks. No stumps, Streptopus roseus here.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Blue Beech) Seepage Swamp
remarks: Small seepage flow along base of NNE face 220 foot slope. Nice maple basswood on slope, lowland hardwood adjacent valley floor areas. Moss covered logs. Caltha dominated in open water zone roughly 2m wide. Muck zones fringe the flow which there grade into wet lowland forest. Fraxinus nigra 28-45cm DBH. Moss-covered logs. Topographic context: toe/depression/flat.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Blue Beech) Seepage Swamp
remarks: Relatively large seepage swamp base of 220 foot, north facing slope along Hemmingway Creek. Highly diverse. Floerkea everywhere. Extensive seepage zones. One main seepage flow. Several decaying logs. Canopy trees 25-45cm DBH (Fraxinus and Betula), Pinus 25-35cm. Soil a moist to saturated organic loam over clay loam. Grades to lowland hardwood. Topographic context: toe, depression, flat.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mature to old growth stand though quite small. < 5 acres on east to northeast face. Canopy Quercus rubra 30-55cm DBH, mode DBH 38-45cm. Dark clay-loam, snags uncommon. Thick leaf layer. Grades into maple-basswood. Small, uncommon decaying woody debris. Topographic context: upper/middle.

Small low-quality stand in narrow valley between steep slopes. Canopy trees 20-42cm DBH. Tilia multiple-stemmed, decaying elm logs common.  Few snags. Soil a dark brown clay-loam. Several small drainage ruts through plot.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Blue Beech) Seepage Swamp
remarks: Narrow band of seepage along 60m length of base of northeast facing slope. Scattered small decaying logs. Caltha and impatiens dominant. Ribes americana and Glyceria also important with Fraxinus nigra. Other species along edges of seepage flow in lowland hardwood or maple basswood forest. Salix and Ulmus 25-45cm DBH.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Mature stand. Gaps due to dead elms which are occasional as logs on floor. Slight dry waterways thru plot.  Soil a deep dark brown loam. Mode 35-40cm DBH.

npc_type_name: Sugar Maple - Basswood - Red Oak - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Mature stand on northwest to northeast aspects along small ravine feeding into Beaver Creek. Canopy trees 25-50cm DBH, mode 30-45cm. Frequent scattered highly decayed stumps (oak?). Decaying woody debris occasional. Snags uncommon. Soil dark silt-loam over brown clay loam.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Sugar Maple - Basswood Forest (Cold Slope)
remarks: Steep slope above Beaver Creek, very rocky substrate, moss covered dolomite occasional highly decayed old stumps.  Decaying woody debris occasional. Some canopy cover by sub-canopy trees due to gaps. Canopy trees 20-35cm DBH, mode 25-30cm.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Blue Beech) Seepage Swamp
remarks: Heterogenous seepage swamp base of steep north face seeps -60-80m long. Vegetation varies from pole sized ash with wet mesic substrate to more open with large ash and wet or aquatic substrate. Grades to wet-mesic maple basswood on slope and lowland hardwoods on valley floor.

Very gently rolling till. Dark loam. Maturing stand. No stumps. Canopy trees 15-35cm DBH, mode 20-35cm. Frequent small surface boulders. Snags, tip-up mounds occasional. Decaying wood uncommon, small. Frequent small surface boulders (granite?).

Seepage fed area at mouth of small ravine feeding into river lake. At base of relatively steep 150 foot east-facing bluffs. Soil, black saturated organic. Several large decaying ash logs. Canopy cover varies from closed ground margins to quite open in center. Canopy trees 10-20cm DBH.

Narrow band of seepage at base of 260 foot east facing bluff along Mississippi River. Canopy variable - here intact with 15-42cm DBH trees including cover from oak forest on slope - very open in other places (disturbance). Small seepage flows common, dark saturated organic substrate with small gravel along flows.

Mature stand. Rocky soil. Trees 20-55cm DBH, mode 30-40cm. Several snags, no stumps. Decaying woody debris sparse and small. Level topography, small stand ~5 acres surrounded by clear cut and regrowth. Soil tannish gray fine silt below 2 inches thick organic root mat, rocky soil. 49cm DBH Quercus rubra - 80 rings.

Mature floodplain stand along Mississippi River at mouth of Zumbro River. Soil dark brown silt. Flooding regime somewhat intact-floods annually; 2 miles below dam. Small piles of woody debris from flooding. Small low lying areas free of vegetation.
Low poorly drained depression of alluvial silt, no standing water. Occasional beaver cut, beavers killed snags. Ecotonal. Next to stagnant slough and narrow ridge with Quercus bicolor.

Maturing stand. Canopy trees 15-60cm DBH, mode 25-35cm. Moderately well drained alluvial silt. Frequent coarse woody debris and sangs, debris piles left by infrequent (not annual) flooding. Occasional elm snags. Unchanneled alluvium.
Mature stand with canopy trees to 90cm DBH, mode 40-65cm. Trees open-grown and spreading. Little flooding debris. Alluvial silt. Immediately below lock and dam. Grazed in past?

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Immature and varied stand with scattered large trees especially, Pinus strobus, Picea glauca. This spot typical of more closed canopy areas. Upper slope areas much more open seemingly somewhat dist. Thuja to 45cm DBH. Canopy DBH in plot 15-33cm, mode 20-25cm. Small ravine up through plot. No snags here, decaying wood small and infrequent. Occasional very old stumps, nearly entirely decayed. Soil rather moist dark to reddish brown loamy clay. Topographic context: middle/lower.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Maturing stand. Canopy trees 20-50cm DBH, Quercus rubra only species over 30cm. Soil thick leaf mat over 1 1/2" dark fibric root mat layer over sandy loam, high silt content. Soil is saturated at 16 inches, standing water at 28 inches. hit rocks at 36 inches. Tip-up mounds occasional. Old stumps occasional and 90% decayed. No snags. Tree core 49cm DBH Quercus rubra-86 rings. Basal area overall 110.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Maturing stand 15-25cm DBH mode, max to 48cm rare. Old 90% decayed stumps occasional. Tip-up mounds common, snags rare. Older trees with crooked boles. Soil-thick dark root mat over sandy loam/loamy sand. Wet at 35 inches deep. No hard pan before 5 feet. Tree core: 46cm DBH Quercus rubra - 74 rings; 33cm DBH Tilia americana - 70 rings.

Best quality area of savannah encountered on TNC or SNA property. Open savannah on south-face 30'dune slope and crest surrounded by oak woodland. Also surrounded by open sand prairie. Some dead oaks due to oak wilt. Largest trees 25cm DBH, open grown. Topographic context: upper/middle/lower.

Canopy trees straight boled, non-serotinus cones. 10-45cm DBH, mode 20-30cm DBH. Much woody debris from Pinus. Dark tan sand - medium to fine grained. Almost no organic layer. 40' slope of stabilized dune. Past grazed. Several snag jack pines. Oldest jack pines with later branches to ground younger one with few lateral branches. Topographic context: upper/middle/lower.

Maturing stand some younger areas. Some large trees. Plot canopy DBH range 20-70cm, mode DBH 25-40cm, occasional max to 100cm. Acer saccharum to 65cm DBH. Scattered flooding debris, floods only relatively high water. Large decaying elm logs occasional. Few large elm snags. Old large stumps occasional. Soil dark sandy silt loam. Soil somewhat compacted, so organic layer.

Mature stand. Canopy trees 25-60cm DBH, mode 30-45cm. Represents some of better quality floodplain forest on slightly elevated area where Acer saccharinum is only occasional. Several large elm snags and large downed logs. On silt.

Mature stand. Canopy trees 25-60cm DBH, mode 30-35cm. Human impacts include campsite. Soil compacted silt loam. Only slight topographic relief. Narrow strip--island <100m wide. Stand quite variable with Carex dominated openings and denser areas.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Old-growth pine stand. Canopy trees 25-62cm DBH, mode = 35-45cm. Occasional snags of all sizes and natural canopy gaps. No stumps seen. Red pines and spruce patchy throughout stand. Some areas less dense shrubs. Frequent tip-up mounds and decaying logs.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Old growth pine stand. Canopy trees 30-64cm DBH, mode 40-55cm. Several larger snags, frequent down logs. Red pine more common elsewhere in stand as are areas of denser shrubs. Frequent tip-ups. Natural canopy gaps, no stumps. Well-drained. Black loam over tan sandy loam (loamy sand?) .

Mature stand on steep slope of narrow ridge finger. Canopy trees 30-48cm DBH. No snags, stumps. Soil: reddish brown clay-loam with rocks, 1/2" needle layer. Pines dominate here, mature stand; surrounded by young paper birch above. Topographic context: upper/middle.

Old growth stand (139 years)canopy trees 25-70cm DBH. Gray to brown loam. Moderate organic layer. Rolling ground moraine. Snags occasional. Tip-ups infrequent. Most trees straight boles, single stemmed. Coarse woody debris common. Topographic context: middle/lower. 51cm DBH Quercus rubra: 139 rings.

Mature stand, canopy trees 25-42cm DBH, mode 35cm. Soil gray-tan fine silty-sand with small rocks. Well drained. No snags or stumps. Appears even aged. Narrow upland top 3m above surrounding lowlands.

Atop large dry bedrock outcrop of Thomson formation. Upturned grawacke and slate. Nearly level top broken and cracked 30% bare rock with lichens. Slopes steeply to both south and north to forest floor 40 feet below. Opening fringed with white pine and white spruce. Thin soil.

Immature stand dominated by 15-35cm DBH trees, straight boles. Few snags. No stumps. Medium-textured brown loamy sand. Well drained. Coarse woody debris occasional and small. Most trees single-stemmed. Quercus ellipsoidalis, 67 rings.

Mature stand, canopy trees 20-50cm DBH, mode 30-40cm. No stumps. Large trees somewhat open-grown appearance; some large dead oaks. Aspect varies from north, east, south, on rolling moraine, slope level to 8 degrees. Soil dark grey to black silt-loam. Well drained. No stumps, some past grazing. 43cm DBH Quercus ellipsoidalis, 97 rings.

Rolling moraine, rich dark loam with occasional surface boulders. Snags occasional. Mature stand, canopy trees 20-50cm DBH, mode 25-35cm. No stumps. Trees forest grown, some with multiple stems. Coarse woody debris frequent. Good structure, slope from 0-6 degrees. Tree core 50c DBH Quercus rubra, 61 rings.

Small stand near road. Canopy trees 20-42cm DBH, mode 25-30cm. Many multiple-stemmed, even-aged. Soil somewhat compacted dark brown loam with small rocks. Coarse woody debris common. Some older stumps. Light and moderate past grazing, no snags. No tip-ups, no snags. Decent structure.

Mature stand canopy trees 30-60cm DBH, occasional snags to 75cm DBH-Ulmus. Coarse woody debris largely elm logs. Soil a deep black silt-loam. No stumps in plot, but occasional in stand. Many areas of stand more open canopy. Tree core: 43 cm DBH Carya cordiformis - 78 rings.
Narrow, linear lowland forest. Releve spans width of stand. Canopy gap on one side. Water channels evident. Much micro-topography and coarse woody debris. Much deer browsing evident. Mineral soils.

Conifer swamp dominated by Thuja. Much microtopography; decadent balsam. No stumps in releve, a few elsewhere in stand. Little evidence of browsing. Stand bisected by stream with beaver activity evident.

Spruce dominated stand on well-drained old river terrace approximately 11m above Temperance River. Canopy gap in one corner and two cedar stumps in releve. Ample evidence of past fire on cedar stumps and logs.
Old-growth white cedar in riparian corridor. Positioned on old river terrace 6m above Temperance River. No evidence of past fire disturbance. Two cut cedar stumps in releve. Mineral mesic soil.

Mature paper birch stand with white spruce as co-dominant and understory component. Balsam fir component dead/down. Aspen occurs singly and in small groves of large or sapling trees. Well drained. Fire evident on stumps. Coarse woody debris varies.

Mature forest dominated by Pinus strobus (max DBH 70cm). Fire origin. No evidence of prior disturbance. Shrub layer interrupted; dominated by Acer spicatum; shrubs browsed. Blister rust present. Shallow soil over rock, well drained.

Mature forest dominated by Pinus strobus. No evidence of prior disturbance. Shrub layer patchy, browsed; domianted by Corylus. Continuous herb layer. Coarse woody debris present. No evidence of fire. Well-drained soils over rock.

Mature forest dominated by Betula papyrifera. Tall shrub layer domianted by Alnus incana. Understory dominated by Diervilla. Herb layer dominated by Aster mac with abundant Calamagrostis. Well-drained soils over bedrock along shore of Lake Superior. Some coarse woody debris.

Mature forest dominated by Betula papyrifera. Understory dominated by Corylus and Acer spicatum. Herb layer with nearly continuous Aster mac. On northwest side of Carlton Peak. No evidence of past disturbance. Thin soils over bedrock. No evidence of past human disturbance.

Mature forest dominated by Betula cord and Populus tremuloides. Tall shrub layer dominated by Alnus frig and Acer spicatum. Understory domianted by Diervilla, Pteridium and Dryopteris. Dominate forbs are Aster mac and Aralia nud. Well-drained. Temperance River Valley.

Mature forest domianted by Pinus strobus, Picea species, Betula papyrifera and Abies. Tall shrub layer interrupted. Low shrubs domianted by Diervilla. Herb layer nearly continuous. Coarse woody debris common. No evidence of disturb. Shallow soil over rock.

Maturing forest dominated by Betula papyrifera, Populus tremuloides and Picea glauca. Shrub layer variable, dominated by Rubus parv. Herb layer dominated by Aster mac with Pteridium, Aralia and Maianthemum. Shallow loamy well-drained soils.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Maturing forest dominated by Betula papyrifera. Occasional Acer saccharum, Thuja and Abies. Shrub layer dominated by Corylus and Acer spicatum. Herb layer dominated by Aster macrophylla. No sign of human disturbance. Well-drained rocky sandy loams. Coarse woody debris moderate.

Mature forest dominated by Betula papyrifera. Tall shrub layer dominated by Acer spicatum. Some conifer establishment in understory. Herb layer interrupted. Rocky, shallow sandy loam over bedrock; surface appears nutrient poor. Little coarse woody debris.

Possible old-growth forest domianted by Thuja with large Betula papyrifera. Tall shrub layer interrupted, dominated by Acer spicatum. Herb layer dominated by Clintonia with Aralia, Cornus, Lycopodium, Trientalis. Moderately well-drained loam. Soil horizons: A, E, Bw1, Bw2. Excavation deeper than 55 cm impeded by rock fragment. Parent material is Superior Lobe till. Complex slopes.

Possible old-growth forest dominated by Thuja with large Betula papyrifera. Tall shrub layer dominated by Acer spicatum. Patchy herb layer domianted by Oxalis montana, Viola renifolia, Circea and Lycopodium. Moderate coarse woody debris. Rocky somewhat poorly drained loamy soils. Soil horizons: A, Bw1 (30% channers and 15% flagstones), Bw2 (15% cobbles and 25% gravel). Till parent material. Complex slopes. No redox detected above 46 cm. Drainage inferred based on slope position (lower backslope) and vegetation.

Possible old-growth upland forest dominated by Thuja and Abies. Blowdowns common. Interrupted shrub layer domianted by Acer spicatum, vertical structure impacted by browsing. Herb layer with Aralia and Aster mac. No past disturbance.

Upland forest dominated by Thuja. Minimally developed shrub layer dominated by heavily browsed Corylus. Herb layer domianted by Aster mac; poor diversity. Little coarse woody debris. No Thuja regeneration, only Picea. Well-drained slope.

Dead and dying forest of Betula papyrifera. Heavy browsing evident in shrub layer. Low diversity in herb layer; Aster macrophyllus and Pteridium dominated. Typical of Lake Terrace birch stands. Moderately well-drained shallow clay loam.

Mature forest dominated by Betula papyrifera. Shrub layer minimal, Corylus most common. Browsing evident. Aster macrophyllus dominant herb on upper/drier part. Lower moister part dominated by Calamagrostis and Rubus pubescens. Shallow soil over bedrock. Minimal coarse woody debris.
Forest on broad level ridge top mid way up north-facing side of High Island Creek Valley.

Forest on upper part of steep slope on south side of High Island Creek Valley. Nice duff layer. Little disturbed. Continuous 3-4 inch leaf litter. Several medium-large diameter partially decayed to well decayed logs. Basal ares = 90 total. Soil black loam or silt loam soils with a one inch humus layer. Canopy Acers range from 30-57cm DBH, relatively straight boled.

Mature forest on steep east northeast facing slope in ravine 1 mile west of Minnesota River Valley. Occasional snags and living american elm. Rich black loam soil with good duff and leaf layer. Frequent deadfalls, some well-rotted. Probably hi-grading in past.

Mature forest on upper part of steep slope along ravine. In dissected Des Moines lobe till near edge of Minnesota River Valley. Nice duff layer and heavy leaf cover on ground. Sandy loam soil. Located just south and upslope from trail where it passes just south of mid-slope pool.

Stand domianted primarily by straight-boled Acer saccharum 100-120 years old. On level, black silt loam near Rush River valley. Scattered gaps or snags. Frequent well-rotted dead falls. Grazed over 30 years ago and little disturbed since. Heavy clay mantle 1.5m below surface.
Mature forest on moderate north facing slope. Much leaf litter plus good humus layer. Several well-rotted deadfalls. Located just west of deep ravine.
Stand in level terrain south of Partridge creed and root river intersection. Canopy with numerous gaps due to deaths of elms. Much leaf litter and rotted deadfalls. Soil is moist black silt.

Forest in floodplain of south fork Zumbro River. On rich black silty soil. Plot is located on level terrain between recently flooded swales. Frequent elm snags and live elms in vicinity. Much coarse woody debris.
Mature stand with heavy canopy cover from 15-25m high. Much leaf litter; little duff; frequent well-rotted deadfalls. Dominant maples and oaks are 45-60cm DBH size.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: In shallow ravine in narrow strip of forest above Simpson Maderite cliff. Plot is north 5m from cliff edge and between cliff and sinkhole. Moderate leaf litter; little duff; fairly thin canopy.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Lower part of steep west facing slope in ravine along creek. Sandy loam soils with abundant pebbles formed in till.
Forest on level terrace near south branch of Rush river. Past selective cutting has left frequent gaps in canopy, as have elm death. Never grazed. On rich, moist silt loam over clay.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Steep south facing slope on north side of High Island Creek Valley. Occasional tip-ups and course woody debris on ground. On rich black loam over clay soil.

Floodplain on island in Mississippi River. Well rotted deadfalls and debris dams. Plot straddles a shallow channel that had recent flooding. Much coarse woody debris. Soil dark silty sand at surface. Other trees in canopy near plot include occasional Populus deltoides and Fraxinus pennsylvanica.

Swamp dominated by scattered tamaracks 30-40cm DBH size. On deep peat deposit in broad wetland depression along cannon river. Site burned for about 2 years in peat fire in mid-1980's. No Sphagnum seen.

Forest on bench between bluffs and Cannon River. Frequent standing dead elms. Interrupted canopy with Celtis, Fraxinus pensylvanica, Juglans nigra. In plot canopy Juglans nigra with 50 and 41cm DBHs. Occasional large down logs. Silt soil.

npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: Wells Creek floodplain, about 3/4 mile southwest of mouth. Coarse and fine woody debris abundant. Soil silt (alluvial), dry to moist.

Wells Creek floodplain, about 1/4 miles west of Lake Pepin. Occasional large down trees, moderate amount smaller size woody debris. Laportea tall, nearly continuous; other herbs beneath. Soil moist silt (alluvial).
Cannon River floodplain. Soil texture clayey silt. Plot includes low area (old river channel) with almost no herbs and slightly elevated area with patchy herb layer. Soil texture: clayey silt.

1/4 miles west of Cannon River just below steep slope; grades into floodplain forest to east. In narrow channel between slight rise on west and higher bench on east. No seeps or standing water. Sedge hummocks common. Soil organic.
Plot on crest and upper slope of dune. Occasional small patches of bare sand.
Plainfield sand. Gently rolling dune topography. Plot includes slight depression and gentle slopes. Some thatch accumulation.

Blowout (10-15m in diameter) in sand prairie. 70% open sand. 3 meter elevation difference from rim to trough. Bowl-shaped on 3 sides. Open end to west; north, south and west-facing aspects. Grades to stable sand prairie. Plainfield sand.

Plainfield sand on low rolling dunes. Portions of plot sparsely vegetated open sand, others more densely vegetated. Tallest oaks in groves. Open areas with frequent multi-stemmed oak grubs. Cored one black oak in plot, about 50-60 years old.
South-facing bluff above Whitewater River. Canopy trees somewhat open-grown. Oak DBH = 51 and 58 cm. Soil silt loam.

Mississippi River floodplain. Nearby sloughs, topography variation. Soil dry silt. Much woody debris; indicates active floodplain. Tree seedlings frequent in recently flooded part of plot where Laportea is infrequent.
Soil loamy sand. Whitewater River watershed on outwash west of Trout Creek. Occasional down trees. Little reproduction of Quercus velutina evident. Substrate Plainfield sand.
On Plainfield sand. Slope ranges from 17 degrees in upper to 27 degrees in lower part of plot. Part of large complex of barren oak savannah and jack pine barrens. East of Whitewater River.
Plainfield sand, on 25m high narrow slope east of the Whitewater River. Part of large complex of barrens oak savanna and jack pine barrens.

Narrow strip of floodplain forest between disturbed upland and crooked slough. Mississippi River floodplain. Silt soil; dry at present. Largest maples multi-stemmed; smaller single. Little coarse litter, perhaps indicating infrequent flooding.
Mississippi River terrace in Prairie Island City Park in Winona. Soil is sand with small gravel component. Topography gently undulating. Scattered trees outside plot, recently cut and re-sprouting.
Seepage streams run through plot. Part of complex of black ash swamp and seepage meadow. Separate releve in black ash swamp.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Blue Beech) Seepage Swamp
remarks: Part of complex of black ash swamp and seepage meadow. All with seepage. Soil silt (moist). Separate releve in meadow.

npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: Floodplain east of Garvin Brook, 0.5 miles from Mississippi River. Frequent large diameter snags of Populus deltoides and Ulmus. Soil silt, dry at present. Occasional large down logs. Little flooding debris.

On central portion of NE-facing slope. Area above releve with much Rubus and Ribes and dominated by smaller trees with approximately 30% Juglans nigra--probably grazed. East half of northwest fourth is within State Forest. Sampled area on mid-slope above area has many disturbance indicators, grazing?
Floating wet meadow at southeast end of Sugarbush Lake appears quite homogeneous throughout, occasional open pools and patches. Scirpus acutus east of releve. Heavy deer use.
Mix of "dry" and "wet" species is because releve plot straddles an ephemeral stream course. Plot is southeast of meadow at east end of Sugar brush lake, across trail from pole aspen.

Downhill from an old rusty boiler, east of a copse of birch blazed orange on forest trail that circles round. Between ATV trails and wet meadow. Much open litter about 1.5 inches deep. Botrychium mormo releve.

Northeast shore of Skunkn Lake, very wet meadow, feels like a floating mat. Forb cover is very little, but where open mud there are solid mats of unknown seedlings (Bidens?) and where open water solid sheets of Lemma.
South facing slope with transitional community between hardwood with much selective cutting on hill and beaver-flooded hardwood swamp.
Although releve is fairly close to road it is placed here because some of best maple seen (almost mature).
Blue green signature on phote CBM 15-19. No standing water.

Wet mesic prairie in shallow depression being invaded by Phalaris. Grazed in past and now managed with controlled burns. On rich brown soil with much sand. On sand deposit over limestone layer. On terrace within Minnesota River Valley.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Eastcentral Bedrock)
remarks: 10x10m grove of Thuja on north side of largest island in Thomson Res. Trees slender, average 25cm DBH. Very shady below. Very attractive. Dry Thuja-pine needle litter covering thin soil on bedrock. No obvious disturbance. No trails.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Eastcentral Bedrock)
remarks: 15x25m plot along narrow bedrock ridge, just east of mouth of Midway River. Vegetation very patchy: young Picea clump; Pteridium and Diervilla dense in low spot; Polypody and Arctostaphylos on rock ridge; lichen/bryophytes on old trail.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Eastcentral Bedrock)
remarks: Beautiful dry pine woodland on bedrock; largest island in Thomson Res. History of site not yet known. No trails, no human litter. Very little trampling on island. Trees appear to be about 40 years old. Plot next to Thuja plot.

Releve done here because of odd vegetation. Located on 80m wide flat area with soil between bedrock ridges. Is this meadow/woodland the result of cut over boreal (or swamp) forest? Any native meadow here?

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Eastcentral Bedrock)
remarks: Dry white/red pine woodland at west end of highest bedrock ridge east of Midway River. Rocky, much windthrow and standing dead white pine. Pines slender 15-23cm DBH. Old trails; past cutting, especially in lows between ridges.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Plot in best part of 20-acre forest. Large canopy gap adjacent to plot from cut and salvaged old dead tree; typical. Trails throughout. Also dead elm openings in black ash low spots. On Grantsburg till.

Plot in best part of small 8-acre pine-hardwood stand near lowland margin; relatively high species diversity. Stand is drier and selectively cut near road. Trillium grandiflorum not here but is nearby. No rocks; dark sandy loam.

30 acre aspen openings (aspen groves with prairie species and wet meadows) on low-relief outwash/river terrace sand. Past hayed, pastured, or cult; unsure. Plot in 10x40m opening surrounded by 6-8m tall aspen.

Plot at more species-rich end (southeast) of 5 acre old field with degraded savanna on west side and aspen opening to south. Purpose was to compare degree of disturbances here with Sand Prairie Wildlife Management Area. Old-fields.

Plot in best part of 5-8 acre, past grazed savanna. Multi-stem red and bur oaks. Fairly shrubby. Moderately low diversity of herbaceous species. One of very few natural areas left along the Elk River.

Poor quality forest (young; abundant Carex pennsylvanica) in SESE30 but releve spot has diverse canopy and herbs; some trees 30-40cm DBH, visible from road. Bouldery along small seepage through plot. Edge of McGrath till plain.
Owner doesn't think this track has prairie tax exemption (files say it does) but says there is a conservation easement on it. This is a HIGH quality area and is about 5 acres. No shrubs in releve.

Canopy of widely spaced 60-70cm diameter Acer saccharum with 30-50cm Acer, Ulmus, and Tilia filling voids. Numerous tip-up mounds and occasional large decaying logs. Dark loamy soil with thin humus and continuous thin litter. Past selectively cut for oak about 20 years ago and also basswood at some time. Dead elms removed.

Uneven-aged mature forest with occasional gaps (75% cover). Trees mostly straight boled. Continuous oak leaf litter. Some coarse woody debris but no really big logs. Occasional cut stump in stand, none in plot.

On gentle slope. Canopy of 35-65cm diameter Quercus rubra and Tilia with smaller Acer saccharum. Occasional gaps. Thin leaf litter. Moderate amount small diameter woody debris. Dark silty loam. Tip-up in plot. Occasional stump in stand.

Area of mature forest on north north east slope. Canopy dominated by tall, straight Quercus rubra. Some gaps (2 snags and 2 large logs in plot). Continuous 1" oak leaf litter. Dark sandy loam with good accumulation of organic matter. No evidence of recent disturbance.

Mature forest on gentle west northwest slope grading into shallow ravine. Canopy of 40-75cm diameter Quercus and Tilia. Several large decaying logs in plot. Thin leaf litter. Gray-brown sandy loam. Thin organic layer. Scattered tip-up mounds and hollows. Healthy ginseng population in plot, adjacent area.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: In gentle draw on north slope. Canopy of 30-65cm Acer, Quercus, Tilia and Fraxinus. Trees often crooked, forked. Several snags and decaying logs. Silty-sandy loam with good accumulation of organic mat. Continuous 1-2 inch leaf litter. Old fence at south edge.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: On gentle slope between wetland basin and steep northwest slope. Maturing canopy of 30-75cm Quercus, Tilia and Acer. Shrub and herb layers sparse. Continuous 2" leaf litter. Dark silty loam, good accumulation organic matter. Well decayed logs common. Parent material is gravelly sand.

Small area with continuous canopy of 30-65cm diameter semi-open grown Quercus macrocarpa. Continuous thin leaf litter. Brown-gray sandy loam. Large stump on edge of plot. Site somewhat junky--grazed in past?
Grazing in the past, some cut stumps. Relatively undisturbed, maple - basswood forest and abandoned farmland regenerating to forest. 10 acre site.
Logging, recreation, and vehicle use. Litter present. Some cut stumps. Relatively undisturbed maple basswood forest and abandoned farm land regenerating to forest. See also releve 6583.

Dry mesic. Burned frequently; 6 dead pin oaks within 5m of plot. Several pin oaks in plot appear to be dying. Ant mounds. 84% cover of mineral soil, 1% decaying wood, and 15% other dead organic matter (mostly acorns). In Tilman/LTER plot D/CCNHA Burn unit (old 6) 106.
0.2ha releve in basswood-oak woods. Maximum diameter canopy trees 13-23". Some stumps. Thorny shrubs common. Large deer herd reported in area. Field road and trash nearby.

0.2 ha releve in oak-basswood-sugar maple forest. Max diameter canopy trees = 15-28". Best area only slightly disturbed (grazing). Area on slope more heavily logged and grazed ( = oak-ironwood woods with open canopy).
(Diamond Creek Woods)  0.2 hectare releve. Level site.

10-acre releve in bluejoint-dominated wetland. Ditching of marsh to south lowered water table and allowed invasion of meadow by elm and ash. Level now higher and trees are dying. Railroad impedes drainage from north.
Clearwater game refuge. An uncut island in an otherwise heavily logged piece of state land.
Soil approximately 50 cm black loam over gray gravelly clay.
Undulating topography within releve, south of stream, much dead and dow.n Quite "wild" and natural aspect to this area around stream.
Down logs, other coarse woody debris ca 20% of ground surface.
0.1 ha releve on 5-10 degree southwest-facing slope. Loamy sand soil. Planted with Pinus sylvestris seedlings.
Approximately 0.3 ha releve. 0-5 degree slope on medium-fine loamy sand.

Ca 0.5 ha releve in dry mesic prairie on 0-5 degree slopes on gently dissected stoney upland. Ca. 3cm of litter. A few cow pats present. Mowed occasionally or grazed? Swales with abundant Solidago altissima.
Releve for floating mat. Releve size <0.1 ha. FSH (summer, 1995) reports site is more diverse than releve indicates, proabably because of time of year of releve.
Releve for floating mat/swamp transition. Releve size <0.1ha. FSH (summer 1995) reports site is more diverse than releve indicates, probably because of time of year of releve.
<0.1ha releve in hardwood swamp forest zone. Area grazed and compacted by cattle. FSH (summer 1995) reports site is more diverse than releve indicates, probably because of time of year of releve.

20 ha releve on rolling gravelly kame landscape. Some patches of good little bluestem on dry prairie, but much of area is infested with weedy species, especially Poa, Artemisia, Melilotus, and Solidago rigidia.
Approximately 0.2 ha releve on 0-10 degree west facing slope. Course sandy loam soil.
1 ha releve in mowed prairie on level site. Conspicuous absence of flowering stalks of Andropogon geradii and Sorgastrum nutans in some parts of the site. Litter accumualtion. (short species list)
0.1 ha releve on well-drained site. 0-2 degree slope with large exposed boulders present.
2 ha releve on level site. Continuous grass cover and good forb diversity. (Plot appears heterogeneous with some wet elements).
Approximately 0.2 ha releve on 0-10 degree west and south facing slopes. On loamy sand. Near Lake Johanna marker.
Approximately 1 ha releve in southwest corner of Roscoe Prairie 0-2 degree slope. Stoney loam.
0.2 ha releve on northwest facing slope. On south side (=grazed side or more heavily grazed side) of zig-zag fence.
0.1 ha releve on northwest-facing slope. On north side (=ungrazed or less heavily grazed side) of zig-zag fence. Seems like dry-mesic phase of mesic prairie.
0.1 ha releve on summit south-east, south, and west-facing slopes of gravel kame. Dried cattle dung prevelent.
Ca 0.2 ha releve in good-quality prairie on south-facing 15 degree slope. Iverson tract.
0.2 ha releve in an old field.
Approximately 0.2 ha releve in old field. 0-10 degree slope on crest and sides of knoll. Loamy course sand.
> 1 ha releve on east side of valley train. 0-5 degree slopes on buff silty till. Tract only lightly grazed and not mowed. (Appears to be dry-mesic prairie.)
Ca 1 ha releve in east 40 of evingston tract. 0-2 degree slopes. Few stones. Mowed every year about August. (Appears to include dry prairie.)
Ca 1 ha releve in west 40 of Ellingson tract. 0-5 degree slopes. Stone site with swales. Mowed every other year except swales. (Releve seems to include heterogeneous habitats.)
1 ha releve on level site.
1 ha releve in weedy prairie on level site. Grazing increases present and abundant, Poa pratensis. Thick litter.
Approximately .5 ha releve on moderately to poorly drained site with 0-2 degree slopes. On clayey silt. Glacial lake plain? Mowed in past. (Appears somewhat degraded.)
20 ha releve on level site. Lightly to moderately grazed within past few years. Weeds scarce. Good recovery potential. Barnes and Svea loam soil. (Some heterogeneity-questionable for analysis.)
1 ha releve on level site. Heavy litter accumulation. Many plants drying out in places, especially Apocynum and Helianthus. (List appears short for 1 ha area.)
1 ha releve on level lowland. Prairie mowed. Few weeds. (Appears to be wet-mesic. Short list for area.)

.3 ha releve on level site. Never plowed or grazed. Mowed every year. Bluegrass heads stripped (for seed?) until ca. 1960. (Liatris aspera may actually be Liatris ligulistylis. Short ca. species list.
2 ha releve in mesic prairie on level site. Site has wet prairie and cattails in low areas. Corn crib in center of prairie. Few weeds.
Releve of unknown size on slightly rolling terrain. Releve for higher parts of site; lower prairie weedier. Was once grazed (by sheep?). Inclusion of Typha in prairie. Appears to be dry-mesic.
1 ha releve on crest and upper part of 5-10 degree slopes. Old hay or corn stack spots. One corn stack still present. Weedy. Possibly dry-mesic.
0.5 ha releve on level site. Appears to be dry-mesic.
0.5 ha releve on top of bluff in intermittent stream valley.
2 ha releve on 10-20 degree N-facing bluff slope over stream. Old pasture. All plants stunted. Weedy in draws.

Releve of unknown size on hill crest and slopes of pastured prairie. Quite weedy with invaders and increasers. Liatris pycn. and Schizachyrium on crest; Sorghastrum, Solidago canadensis. and Thalictrum on lower slopes.
3 acre releve on rolling upland. Grazed in past. Grasses patchy with large stands of Stipa spartea and Schizachyrium scoparium with Bouteloua mixed in. Appears degraded.
Floating mat in 10 acre kettle hole of steep esker. Sphagnum cover continuous. Stunted Larix common. Basin surrounded by mesic forest.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Area described as A55 (aspen, 9-15" DBH, >22.5 cords/acre) on soil 13 (EXWD sand to gravel, moderate slopes). Tip-ups, old stumps, charcoal. On north side of hill, black ash below. Black bears and many deer.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Area described as A55 (aspen, 9-15", >22.5 crds/ac) on soil 6 (WD medium to fine, moderate slopes). Small upland with swamp on 3 sides. Stumps. Near new (2 year) forest road.

Area described as BF52 (balsam fir, 9-15" DBH, 7.5-12.5 cords/acre) on soil 10 (SWED coarse loamy, level to moderate slopes). Fallen fir. Patchy fir and aspen. Stumps. A few tall pines in area. Old forest roads. A horizon depth: 5cm. Litter of leaves and needles.

Area descrbed as BF52 (balsm fir, 9-15", 7.5-12.5 crds/ac) on soil 4 (SWPD minerals). Many fallen trees - firs and aspen - patchy. Stumps. A few tall pines in the area. Old forest roads. A horizon depth: 5cm.

Area described as NH42 (northern hardwoods, 5-9", 7.5-12.5 cords/acres) on soil 3 (PD mucks and minerals). Low and hummocky, only slightly higher than surrounding swamp, swales with black levees. Stumps. A horizon depth: 3cm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Area described as O54 (oak, 9-15", 17.5-22.5 cords/acre) on soil 11 (SWED coarse loamy, steep slopes). Dry island in swamp, not steep. Deer and bear. Stumps. Open and sparse. A horizon depth: 4cm. Soil: sandy loam or loamy sand.

Area described as A53 (aspen, 9-15", 12.5-17.5 cords/acre) on soil 3 (PD mucks and minerals). Dense hazel under aspen canopy (25-45cm DBH). Slope above brook. Stumps. Releve not square. A horizon depth: 8 cm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Area described as NH54 (northern hardwoods, 9-15", 17.5-22.5 crds/ac) on soil 11 (SWED coarse loamy steep). Area not steep. Deer, bear, night crawler, boulders, coarse woody debris, stumps. Opening nearby. A horizon depth: 2cm.

Area described as NH54 (northern hardwoods, 9-15", 17.5-22.5 crds/ac) on soil 4 (SWPD minerals). Hummocky with blackened leaves in low spots. Giant old stump. Uplands nearby (red and sugar maple-basswood)

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Area described as WS55 (white spruce, 9-15" DBH, >22.5 cords/acre) on soil 7 (WD medium to fine, steep slopes). Few spruce, more down slope. Snags and coarse woody debris. Aspen ~30cm DBH, birch ~25cm, spruce ~15cm. No stumps, few snags and fallen limbs. A horizon depth: 3cm. Soil silty loam or sandy loam.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Area described as A55 (aspen, 9-15" DBH, >22.5 cords/ac) on soil 5 (MW to WD medium to fine, level). No stumps. 3 big fallen aspen, conifer plant and opening nearby. Aspen DBH ~25-35cm. A horizon depth: 3cm.

Area described as A54 (aspen, 9-15", 17.5-22.5 cords/acre) on soil 12 (EX WD sandy to gravelly). Open canopy/dense hazel. Bear in raspberries. On ridge by reservoir, open nearby. Aspen DBH ~15-31cm. A horizon depth: 8cm. Litter of aspen and grass.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Area described as O54 (oak, 9-15", 17.5-22.5 cords/acre) on soil 7 (WD medium to fine, steep slopes). Upland island (approximately 10 ha) in swamp. Oak DBH 20- 47 cm, maple 18-27. Marked for logging. A horizon depth: 4 cm. Litter of needles and leaves. Hit roots or rocks at 20cm?

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Area described as O54 (oak, 9-15", 17.5-22.5 cords/acre) on soil 7 (WD medium to fine, steep slopes). Same as AIT-15 but 100m north on north slope. Oak 36- 47cm DBH, Basswood 24-28 (multi-stemmed), Maple 18-35.

Moderate coarse woody debris - including several well-decayed logs. Releve associated with soil hole IA (D Shadis). Tilia leaves diseased. Shallow layer of deciduous leaf duff. Little relief within plot. 1991 photo Ait-22-17. North of Savanna Portage Trail.
West of trail to Wolf Lake. Associated with D. Shadis soil hole IIB. Several D4-5 snags. Moderate deciduous leaf duff. Several large diameter logs - pine, paper birch. 1991 photo Ait-21-18.

South of Savanna Lake. Mixed trembling aspen, paper birch, fir on midslope. +/- depauperate ground flora. Moderate coarse woody debris. Some within-plot relief from well-decayed logs. Several charred stumps / logs. Associated with Shadis soil plot IIIC. 1991 photo Ait-20-1

Mature lowland forest dominated by slender Acer rubrum and Quercus macrocarpa. Old and large stumps occasional. Moderately slender coarse woody debris. Occasional mucky spots with black moist leaves but never standing water. Soil mottled below A-horizon to >1m, hit water at 45cm. A horizon depth: 5cm.
Tamarack swamp on mat in arm of large basin w/open water, marsh & wet meadow. Canopy trees avg 10-15cm dbh. 50% pools & 50% hummocks below. Diverse herb layer. pH = 7.5-7.6. Adjacent slopes forested.
