Unusual jack pine dominated swamp with common black spruce. 5 acre area. Fibric peat >1m depth. Standing water 1-5% cover. sphagnum carpet to 100% coverage within large wetland complex. Basal area 150 square feet/acre.

On springy floating mat in ca. 3-acre basin surrounded by gently roll- ing forested upland on till. Patches of sphagnum & feathermoss in plot pH = 4.8 - 5.3. Adjacent to zone of Carex lacustris on muc
On quaking mat in 150-acre basin in old river channel. Patchy shrub canopy w/sedge-dominated openings. Tallest shrubs senescent. pH = 8.2. Water level lowered 5+ yrs ago. Between Larix zone & Typha.

Below gravelly slope at edge of basin in old river channel. Hummocky surface. Occas pool. Saturated sedge peat. Water not strongly flowing. pH = 8.2. Borrow pit on upland: some sedimentation in basin.

On floating mat in basin in old river channel. Located between shrub swamp & Typha/Phragmites zone. Mat approx 1m thick. Undecomposed sedge peat at surface, decomposed below. pH=8.2. Dead trees nearby
Releve done to describe area along flowing rivulet in tamarack swamp. Water level in swamp affected by removal of dam ca. 5 years ago. Parts of seepage zone affected by recent gravel mining upslope.
In ca. 2-acre basin surrounded by forest on gently rolling upland. Basin strongly dominated by Carex lacustris w/occasional Typha patch. Low graminoid diversity. Muck soil. No standing water.

On floating mat in small basin. In area w/Salix & low graminoid cover. Contin moss cover w/out hummocks or pools. pH = 6.0-6.4. Most of basin dominated by Carex lacustris w/patches of Typha & Sagittar
On quaking mat in extensive basin w/much marsh & open water. Dom by graminoids w/contin sphagnum. Some hummocks, no pools. pH = 7.3 - 7.5. Surrounded by zone of Betula gland, then zone of Typha lat.
In small depression on mid-slope in rolling forested upland. Dense Carex lacustris w/few other graminoids. Mostly dry in late summer with occas pool. Approx 1m sedge peat or muck. pH = 6.4 - 6.5.
Small area of alders on solid hummocky sphagnum mat. Openings in shrub canopy w/abund Glyceria. Sphagnum saturated. pH = 4.9 - 5.3. Most of basin with fen, wet meadow. Moat at upland margin of mat.
Plot in willow swamp near margin w/wet meadow dom by Carex stricta and Calamagrostis. Solid mat w/hummocks & hollows. No standing water. pH = 8.2 - 8.5. No Phalaris.
On saturated floating sphagnum mat in ca. 2-acre basin in rolling forested upland. Mat level, w/out pools or hummocks. Plot near margin of shrub zone & wiregrass zone. pH = 5.6.

On solid mat in ca. 30-acre basin. Plot in zone dom by Carex stricta, surrounded by broad area of Carex lacustris. Mat w/C. stricta hummocks & mucky hollows. pH=7.7-7.8. Occas Salix clump outside plot
On spongy hummocky sphagnum mat in 2-acre basin in wooded upland. Occas large feathermoss hummock. pH = 4.5 (hummocks) to 5.1 (hollows). Most Scirpus in center of basin (= plot area) not fruiting.
On surface of granitic rock outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. 2.5m X 2.5m plot. Associated with releves 7737, 7738, 7739. Large exposure rising 60 feet above the Mississippi River. Peace Rock.
Margin of granite rock outcrop; exposed to full sunlight (5.8 m X 0.5 plot). Associated with releves 7736, 7738, 7739. Large outcrop rising 60 feet above Mississippi River. Peace Rock.
Fissure of granite rock outcrop; exposed to full sunlight (2.8 m X .22 m plot.) Associated with releves 7736, 7737 and 7739. Large exposure rising 60 feet above Mississippi River. Peace Rock.

Dry-mesic prairie between granite rock outcrops; exposed to full sunlight (5 m X 10 m plot). Associated with releves 7736, 7737 and 7738. Large exposure rising 60 feet above Mississippi River. Peace Rock.
On surface of granitic rock outcrop; exposed to full sunlight (2.5 m X 2.5 m plot). Associated with releves 7741, 7742  7743. Heavily past grazed. Adjacent old quarry. Watab, Peace Rock.
Margin of granite rock outcrop; exposed to full sun. Associated with releves 7740, 7742 and 7743 (4.5 m X 0.45 m plot). Heavily past-grazed. Adjacent to old quarry. Margin of 7740.

Fissure of granite rock outcrop; exposed to full sun. Past heavily grazed; adjacent to old quarry (1.5 m X 0.2 m plot). Associated with releves 7740, 7741, 7743 (min-max height and pcover values estimated).

Marginal area between rock outcrop and steep, West-facing precipice (7.5 m X 1 m plot). Past heavily grazed; adjacent old quarry. Typical margin near 7740. Associated with releves 7740, 7741 and 7742.
On surface (crest) of granitic outcrop; exposed to full sun (2.5 m X 2.5 m plot). Associated with releves 7743 and 7745. Frostview Road. Western most edge of central Minnesota outcrop area.
Fissure of granitic rock outcrop; exposed to full sun. Associated with releves 7743 and 7744 (4.5 m X 0.3 m plot). Fissure of 7744; Frostview Road.
On surface (mid slope) of granitic rock outcrop; exposed to full sun (2.5 m X 2.5 m plot.) Associated with releves 7748, 7749 & 7750. Best outcrop in central Minnesota.

Margin of granite rock outcrop; exposed to full sun. Best outcrop in central Minnesota (5.5m X 0.48m plot). Associated with releves 7747, 7749, 7750. Margin of releve 7747. (some min-max height, cover values estimated).
Fissure in granite rock outcrop; exposed to full sun. Best outcrop in central Minnesota (3.2 m X 0.22 m plot). Associated with releves 7747, 7748 and 7750. Margin of 7747.
Dry-mesic prairie between granite rock outcrops; exposed to full sun (5 m X 10 m plot). Associated with releves 7747, 7748 and 7749. Best outcrop complex in central Minnesota. Slope 0-10.
On surface of granitic rock outcrop; exposed to full sun  (2.5 m X 2.5 m plot). One of the best outcrop complexes in central Minnesota. Diverse vascular flora. Large outcrop.
On surface of granite rock outcrop; exposed to full sun (2.5 m X 2.5 m plot). On 70 foot, west-facing slope along Sauk River immediately south of Hwy 23 in Cold Spring.
Margin of granite rock outcrop; exposed to full sun. Adjacent to old quarry. Associated with releves 7754 and 7755; margin of 7754 (2.8 m X 0.45 m plot).
On surface of granitic rock outcrop; exposed to full sun. Partially quarried in past. Associated with releves 7753 and 7755 (2.5 m X 2.5 m plot).
Fissure of granite rock outcrop; exposed to full sun. Old quarry adjacent (1.8 m X 0.22 m plot). Associated with releves 7753 and 7754. Fissure of 7754.
On surface of granitic rock outcrop; exposed to full sun  (2.5 m X 2.5 m plot). Associated with releves 7757 and 7758. Graniteview Road, Waite Park. Moderate past-grazed.
Margin of granite rock outcrop; exposed to full sun. Associated with releves 7756 and 7758; margin of 7756 (3.6 m X 0.5 m plot). Graniteview Road, Waite Park. Moderate past-grazing.
Fissure of granite rock outcrop; exposed to full sun. Moderate past-grazing (2.5 m X 0.24 m plot). Associated with releves 7756 and 7757; fissure of 7756. Graniteview Road, Waite Park.
On surface of granite rock outcrop; exposed to full sun (12.5 m X 2.5 meter plot). Associated with releves 7760 and 7761. Rockville.
Margin of granite rock outcrop; exposed to full sun. Associated with releves 7759 and 7761; Margin of 7759. Rockville (6.5 m X 0.42 m plot).
Fissure of granite rock outcrop; exposed to full sun. Associated with releves 7759 and 7760; fissure of 7759 (4.4m X 0.25m plot). Rockville.

In large minerotrophic tamarack swamp complex west of St. Stephen. Canopy trees 10-20 cm DBH. Occasional small patches of Sphagnum. Peat moist, no surface water or stumps. Light past-grazing dry years. Heterogenous.
Swampy thicket on top of calcareous fen mound at foot of east-facing slope. Water at ground surface. In SWNWSW22.

Dry mesic prairie on shallow sandy soil over sandstone bedrock. In small opening surrounded by overgrown savanna. No recent fire. Known locally as the "Garden of the Gods." Bedrock approximately 1 foot below surface.
On small knob just south of creek. Well drained, sand-gravel soil with much gravel at surface derived from Buse series till. In heavily grazed pasture, but little grazing in releve.
Lower slope in shallow ravine in well-drained, sandy gravelly soil, er ratics at surface. Buse loam occurs on steep slopes on calcareous, loamy, till lacking B horizon. Past grazed, but not recently.

Site on steep-sided, rocky, gravelly sandy hills along north edge of Canby Creek Valley. In pasture but avoided by cattle. Soil is Buse loam: excessively drained loam lacking a B horizon, formed on calcareous till.
Flank of shallow mound on toe slope of east-facing hillside. Scattered small pools. Water at ground surface. SWNWSW22.
Shallow north-facing slope on side of calcareous fen mound. Large shrub-less zone. Water table at surface. Lacks open pools. On deep peat.
Open area of low sedges with abundant marly pools. Near top of large peat mound. Very well hydrated with water near surface. On deep peat.
Along drainage on edge of Prairie Coteau. Sandy loam with abundant morainic gravel (Buse loam). Mid-slope on ravine that is only 20m top to bottom. In well grazed pasture; cattle avoid steep slopes.

Shallow toeslope along drainage ditch among hills of Prairie Coteau. Mowed annually for hay. Last grazed approximately 3 years ago. Never sprayed with herbicide. Soil is black sandy loam near surface.

On shallow mound on shallow toe slope above drainageway. Saturated with cold groundwater. Hard sponge-like mineral crust with oxidized iron color at surface; coarse peat below. Much oxidized iron in surface water.

Shallow slope near top of large morainic hill. In coarse-textured soil of outwash cap. In actively grazed pasture. Soil is sandy loam near surface with well-rounded, 1-2cm granitic gravel. Small erratics at surface (sioux series).
Site straddles narrow, rocky ridge between forks of a drainage way. Small-medium sized erratics frequent at surface. At surface, soil is sandy loam. Located in actively grazed pasture.

On a subtle, shallow rise on subtly undulating terrain on broad flat valley bottomland. Calcareous, possibly slightly saline soils. Site is hayed by DNR for prairie seed. Surface soil black friable loam.
Top of ridge. Much bare, gravelly soil at surface. In lightly grazed pasture. Much angular gravel at surface. Soil appears to be formed in sandy-gravelly outwash deposits above till. .02cm A horizon.

Hayed prairie atop shallow rise. Shallowly undulating bottomland of Little Antelope Valley. Adjacent to low spots with saline soil. Moderately drained calcareous soil formed in alluvium on higher position than surrounds bottomlands.
Hayed prairie in very shallow, saline swale. In shallowly undulating bottomlands of Little Antelope Valley. In Calco silty clay loam formed in alluvium.
Wet-mesic prairie on nearly flat, shallowly undulating terrain. Never plowed due to kaolin clay layer 1-2 feet (?) below ground. Hayed annually. Typical for site. On Glacial River Warren Terrace.
On shallow rise on very shallow ridge-swale topography. Site is hayed annually. Never plowed due to kaolin clay layer 1-2 ft (?) below ground. On Glacial River Warren terrace.
Typical of several patches of low sedge areas in fen on very shallow north facing slope on south side of Glacial River Warren Valley. On very poorly drained peat.
Wet-mesic prairie on level terrain with scattered large glacial erratics on terrace within Glacial River Warren Valley.
Wet prairie in shallow depression on terrace within Glacial River Warren Valley.

Level seepage zone on lower north facing slope on edge of terrace in Minnesota River Valley. Saturated with cold groundwater. Soil is fine, black mucky peat. Portions are quite springy with groundwater seepage.
Prairie on steep south side of ridge formed by basalt dike. Shallow soils over bedrock and boulders. Occasional small areas of rock exposed at surface.
Steep west facing slope with very shallow soil layer over Morton gneiss. Soil excessively drained. Exposed rock = 10% of site. Dry prairie or rock outcrop - crystalline bedrock subtype?
Prairie on shallow soil over Morton gneiss. On upper slope of rock-cored knob on which little rock is exposed. Crystalline bedrock subtype?

In broad lowland "channel" between morton gneiss knobs. Moderate past grazing; now very lightly grazed. Hummocky ground, partly due to sedge tussocks. Sample is adjacent to lowest, wettest zone dominated by Carex lacustris. No standing water present.
Uppermost part of steep slope on ridge composed of sand and gravel deposited by Glacial River Warren. On terrace along Minnesota River.

Level top of sand/gravel ridge on terrace within glacial river Warren Valley. Probably had some disturbance in past from vehicles extracting aggregate from nearby pit. Virtually no organic soil on ground surface.
Level terrain with deep black silt-loam soil. Site hayed but never grazed. Long time since last fire--dense thatch of dead grass on ground.
In poorly-drained shallow depression. Hayed, but never grazed.
Nearly level top of small hill. Part of 1-2 acre Pioneer Cemetery 0.25 miles west of Klossner.

Small fen, rolling terrain, southwest of Richmond. Hills heavily past-grazed, wooded to east, open to west. Continuous Sphagnum cover, slightly quakey substrate, slight moat, sparse woody cover, no Larix.
Wet-mesic prairie on level terrain between railroad and HWY 19. Annual haying. Adjacent to shallow, poorly-drained wet spots.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: At lowland margin of managed northern hardwood stand (thinned 8-10 years ago). Trees 10 -35cm DBH. Red oak regeneration stems 2-6 years old. Numerous stumps. Old vehicle trails. Thin black Ah (3cm) on silt-loam. Close to water table. 3cm A horizon.

Low margin of northern hardwood forest, with greater diversity than upslope where impact of cutting is evident. Low area with microtopography, coarse woody debris of all sizes snags. Average DBH = 35cm. Thin Ah over silt loam. Only 70-120cm to water table. A few cobbles and a boulder at surface.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Submature dry-mesic forest. Slender canopy trees. Slender Populus coarse woody debris and branches. Old tip-ups and craters. On small moraine with small hummocky hills and numerous wet depressions. Occasional large boulder. Soil: sandy silt loam.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Mature forest on side of morainic ridge. Composition varies from past cutting & natural disturbance? Large old tip-ups. Occasional slumping halfway down slope. Coarse woody debris including canopy-size Betula papyrifera and Acer. Soil: sandy silt loam?

Dense Carex/Calamagrostis meadow with Salix in 100-150m wide channel. Plot 150-200m downstream of impoundment and near floating mat and flowing water. Forb abundance higher near water. Saturated sedge peat.

Narrow zone of Thuja-Acer-Tilia (max DBH 45-50cm) at upland edge on mineral soil between Fraxinus nigra swamp and cutover deciduous forest. 3-stemmed Thuja (with 2 stems cut) at least 187 years old. Plot in rare shady patch.

5x40m plot covering most of seepage area with flowing water and wet meadow species. Within typical 30-40 year old Populus tremuloides stand with Acer and abundant Carex pensylvanica. Good herb diversity; no rare Botrychiums. Silt loam.

80m long zone of Thuja between black ash swamp and Abies/Populus upland. Raised woody hummocks with Carex pedunc/Athyrium/Thuja on 80% of plot. Thuja mostly 26-31cm DBH; max = 50 and 67cm. Mucky hollows.

Ecotonal, patchy shrub swamp openings between Thuja/black ash swamp and Larix/black ash swamp. Shrubs very dense. Spongy-organic substrate with tippy woody hummucks. Old cut stumps. Some Thuja reproduction. Standing water.

Submature forest with more "northern" character than 3 miles south. Slight depressions with occasional Botrychiums. Coarse woody debris of Betula papyrifera. Past cut. Past fire. Deer trails. 2cm duff over sandy loam; charcoal at 4-5cm.
Black spruce swamp (bog-like) is very uniform, low species diversity. High hummocks. Saturated but firm peat between hummocks. Fairly easy walking. Open, airy, half-shaded. Slender downed trunks.

Between narrow zone of black ash near upland and black spruce swamp in wetland interior. Large woody hummocks with pools between. Dense shrubs and dense woody/graminoid litter with dead wood under Sphagnum. Organic woody/sphagnum peat.

Plot about 50m from Aguipegueton Point and 80m north of Lake Onamia. In opening not dominated by Salix gracilis. Almost no additional wet meadow species outside of plot except Typha and Scirpus cyperinus.
Flat wet-mesic prairie in complex of prairie, Typha, wet meadow, and shrubby areas. Soils 35cm of sandy clay loam with gravel over impermeable (with probe) layer of light brown clay with gravel.

Wet prairie grades into a shrubby area, some woody invasion occurring in plot. Moderate thatch. 20cm of black organic loam over an impenetrable (to probe) gravel layer with black loam. Several small depressions in plot.

Mesic prairie in ROW between highway 14 and railroad. Cable laid this summer - right through middle of prairie! So plot is 5x20m. Phalaris invasion is spotty, but linear plot nicks several patches. Thick litter.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Old-growth (approximately 1870's logged) pine-spruce forest. DBH mode 30-40cm, max 50cm. On sandy upland, old oxbow. Black ash and cedar swamp nearby. Logging road 40m away. Litter of leaves and needles. Releve training workshop.

Mature spruce-cedar forest with scattered white pine, on old oxbow flats. Cedars DBH 40cm, spruce 17cm, no fir. Forest patchy - managed for grouse in the 1970s? Chosen for level slope. Litter of needles and leaves.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Mature spruce forest with aspen patches and scattered white pine. Pine DBH 47cm, spruce 20-27cm, no fir. On inner curve of old oxbow. Chosen for moderate slope. Short (20m) slope. Small rotted stumps, snags. Litter of needles and leaves.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Mature spruce forest with aspen and scattered pine. Pine DBH 62cm, spruce 53cm, poplar 41cm. Inner curve old oxbow. Chosen for steep slope. Short(30m) slope. Creek, somewhat poorly drained below. Large fallen spruce. Litter of leaves, grasses, and needles.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Mature pine stand on steep sand/gravel ridge. Pine DBH 54-72cm. On outer rim of old oxbow. Chosen for soil, pine and long slope--near DNR releve #s 7956 and 7957. Sandy with boulders. Hazel glade below.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Mature spruce/birch/maple forest on steep sand/gravel ridge. Pine DBH 52cm, spruce 24cm, birch 35cm. Outer rim of old oxbow. Big (approximately 55cm) old stump (cf. 1870s). More hazel nearby. Near #s 7955, 7956. Litter of leaves and some needles.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Open spruce/pine/birch on top of narrow sand/gravel ridge. Pine DBH 22-58cm, spruce 35cm, birch 29-41cm. Outer rim of old oxbow. Patches of dense hazel. Deer trails and beds. Big old stump (cf. 1870s). Toporaphic context: flat/crest.

Scraggly open forest on east face of long ridge. Maples 9-15cm DBH, basswood 19-24cm. Twice windblown? Tip-up (25cm) dense with pebbles and cobbles. 40m from old road (ca. 1917). Swamp at base of ridge. Litter of maple and graminoid leaves.

Mature aspen stand on poorly drained flat top of 100' oxbow island. Aspen DBH 25-33cm. Scattered large (>50cm DBH) old stumps (ca. 1870s). Swamp below. Earthworms. Litter of aspen and graminoid leaves. Old homestead? Near #7960,7961,7962.

Steep south face of 100' oxbow island. All trees <30cm DBH, aspen biggest, basswood multi-stemmd. Small terrace with black ash nearby, also open glade cobbles and boulders. Swamp below. Near releve #7959,7961,79. Topographic context is upper/middle.

Mixed black ash/birch stand on steep north face of 100' oxbow island. Birch DBH 16cm, aspen 28cm. Swamp below. Scattered large (>50cm) old stumps. Cobbles and boulders. Large yellow birch snag. Near releve #795.

Patchy spruce stand on steep west face of 100' oxbow island. Swamp below. Scattered very large old stumps. Cobbles and boulders. Large spruce (47cm) with tag (R2221). Does not fit native community class very well.
Open slope of dense bracken with sparse hardwoods, chosen for showy lady slippers nearby. Blowdown? May be natural terrace. 40m east of popular trail. Across beaver pond/swamp from 99-12 (DNR# 7962).

Old-growth maple-basswood stand, spring ephemerals reported. Maples 18-50cm DBH, basswood 31-53cm, yellow birch 51cm. 100m to property line: open fields. Flaccus study site (1964). Earthworms nearby. Small pools of standing water.

Wet flat old-growth forest with temporary pools. 100m to property line, fields. Canopy patchy with more black ash to west. Big (DBH >60cm) fallen black ash. Near (within 200m?) of DNR releves 113, 114 and 115.
Flat and squishy forest. Mature end of stand--more cedar than elsewhere. Thinned for yellow birch by CCC or wind? Very near DNR releve #7967. 100m from trails.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Slightly drier area in flat, squishy forest. Mature end of stand. Generally patchy amd young: thinned by CCC? Wind? Site chosen for pines: DBH 52, 63 and 67cm. 1 dead, 2 live with lightning scars. Near #796.
Open-grown red oak and sugar maple in open matrix of mature aspen on flat ridge-top. Thinned by CCC? Big (80-100cm, waist high) old stump (ca. 1870s). Multi-stem basswood. Earthworms. Near 7966,7967.

Flat forest with temporary pools between maple basswood forest (DNR# 7964) and black ash/yellow birch (DNR# 7965). Black ash DBH and 51cm, yellow birch at 31-49cm and basswood at 31-33cm. Big fallen yellow birch (50cm). Earthworms.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Nice hardwood stand on wide ridge top. Maples DBH 12-36cm, basswood 27-40cm, paper birch 20-36cm. Occasional big old stumps. Hummocky. On terrace Sandy above. Pebbles and cobbles in tip-up mound. Very sedgy.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Sparse and tattered hardwood stand with many gaps, snags and fallen trees (mostly SW-S-SE). Near crest of ridge. Oaks DBH 30-38cm, paper birch 40cm, ash 18-23cm. More mesic in SE corner. Near powerlines. Litter of leaves and graminoids.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Old-growth? balsam fir stand on old oxbow flats. Fir DBH 22cm, spruce 45-60cm, aspen 22cm. Area patchy: fir drier, cedar wetter, spruce in between. Big fallen fir. Spruce nursery nearby. Earthworms. Litter of needles and graminoids.

Hardwood stand chosen to represent potential vegetation of ridge (i.e., without powerline, trails, blowdowns). Oaks DBH 42-63cm, maples 17-32cm, basswood 19-34cm (multi-stem). Paper birch nearby. Earthworms. Topographic context: upper/flat.

Very steep southwest face of tall (200') hardwood ridge, cut with ridges, ravines and terraces. Plot convex. Paper birch at crest, cedars at foot of hill, scattered large white pine. Deer trails, earthworms. Litter of graminoids and needles.

Cedar/black ash/balsam poplar forest in strip along base of southwest face of tall (200') steep hardwood ridge. Cedar DBH 37-56cm, black ash 19-32cm balsam poplar 28-36cm. Yellow grubs present (not worm). Litter of needles and sticks.

Steep southwest face of narrow ravine, downstream from Hemlock Ravine SNA. Red pine DBH 30-45cm, white pine 16-23cm. Cut with ridges and valleys. Plot concave. Open paper birch/bracken above. Cedar to north. Earthworm. Litter of leaves and needles.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Foot of southwest slope in steep narrow ravine, downstream from Hemlock Ravine SNA. White pine at steep upper side, balsam poplar at lower side. 1m bedrock waterfall below. Tip-up. Earthworms. Topographic context is lower/toe.

Foot of northeast slope in steep narrow ravine downstream from Hemlock Ravine SNA. Slope cut with ridges, valleys. Plot convex. Hemlock seedling at base of yellow birch at lower northwest edge. Earthworms.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Mid-slope of steep northeast face of narrow ravine downstream of Hemlock Ravine SNA. Terrace at upper edge of plot. Plot with more cedar and less birch than others at this elevation(?). Litter of birch leaves and cedar sprays.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Flat ridgetop at southwest edge of deep ravine (Hemlock Ravine SNA). Birch forest extends down upper slope. Boulders. Tip-up with sand, stones. Hummocks but no stumps. Oaks multi-stemmed. Earthworms. Sand pit nearby.

Mature to old-growth stand on ridge on northeast side of Egge Lake. Canopy trees 20-60cm DBH (mode 30cm, 40-60cm frequent). Gently rolling with undulating microtopography. Much large coarse woody debris. Occasional old conifer stump, snag, boulder. Frequent surface rocks.

Interesting area. A slight depression in otherwise dry-mesic prairie. Presence of Prenanthes, gentian, and Thalictrum is unusual for site. Area needs a spring releve. Little litter -burned last year? Soil probe won't go past 20cm, dark brown loam over loamy clay.
Dry mesic prairie on a knoll among depressions. Site hayed and grazed in past. Moderate litter. Could not probe soil.

Along ridge crest and cliff edge. Good pine reproduction. Narrow ridge-spur between small intermittent stream and middle fork Whitewater Creek. Bound by dry cliff on south aspect and grading into steep, cliffy north slope with maple-basswood forest. Sandy silt (loam? some clay?) with pebbles, boulders, and outcrop exposures on surface. Dark soil, this humus layer 1-2 inches. At least 2 snags, tip-ups and debris locally abundant. Pine DBH range: 10 ,modal 25-40, to 73cm. Deciduous DBH range: 15, modal 25-35, 40cm.

Old growth stand. Trees 30-50cm DBH. Large well-decayed pine stumps uncommon No recent stumps. Occasional snags. Fair amount coarse woody debris. Slightly hummocky or undulating substrate. Good litter and organic layer over brown clay-loam.

Beautiful old-growth mesic northern hardwood stand covering hundreds of acres in Crosby-Manitou state park. Thick maple litter over rocky brown silty loam. No stumps. Coarse woody debris of all sizes. Surface boulders. Topographic context crest/upper.

5-10 acre old growth pine relict on slight bench on upper mid portion of often steep 500 foot east facing slope above Manitou R on south side of ravine. Pines 60-100cm DBH. Cedars, spruce 25-40cm DBH. Much coarse woody debris, rocky soil. Dry-mesic, well drained.

Old growth? Upland cedar forming fairly wide band on lower portion of 230 foot south facing slope. Trees 35-75cm DBH. Scattered surface boulders. Trees mostly straight. Coarse woody debris frequent, mostly relatively recent mid size Abies. Some old Thuja logs. No stumps, snags occasional.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Immature stand. Trees 20-30cm DBH, rare 41cm. Middle to upper part of 80 foot, south facing slope in rugged terrain between Leskinen Lake and east branch Baptism River. Thin humus over brown (sandy)-loam. Charcoal present in soil, no stumps. Occasional surface boulders. Bedrock where slope steepest.

Semi-terrestrial cedar along drainage between 200' ridge to east and 300' ridge to west. Trees mostly 30-45cm DBH. A few old stumps. Few snags. Coarse woody debris common, often larger and older. Hummocky. 50m from and 5' above stream bed. Northern hardwoods upslope both east and west. Topographic context depression/flat.

Alluvial terrace approximately 20 feet above east side of Manitou River. Mature/old growth. No stumps. Occasional snags. Frequent coarse woody debris, often large, older. Two small dry channels. No flooding debris. Base of 60 foot west facing slope. Scattered large white pines occasional along river bank.

Attractive shore fen in broad valley along slack water part of Blesner Creek. Bouncy but firm mat. Saturated, no standing water. Not hummocky. No evidence of trees in past. Covers 20 acres, both sides of stream. Sphagnum rare. Grades to Carex utriculata dominated zones.

Coastal wetland between highway 61 and cobble beach berm. Wetland < 20 acres. Plot approximately 20m from beach, 50m from highway. Scattered higher areas with mature Betula papyrifera and Populus balsimifera. No stumps. Hollows moist to wet. Altered?

Broad sedge mat on northeast side Lookout Lake. Scattered stunted tamarack and black spruce. Plot in wettest micro-habitats on mat. Shallow surface water present. Grades to areas with more Myrica, Chamadaphne, Carex cf lacustris, and Carex lasiocarpa. 15m from lake edge and 20m from upland.

Mature stand along inlet stream north of Lookout Lake. Trees 20-40cm DBH, mostly somewhat leaning. No stumps. Saturated peat, no pools. Scattered coarse woody debris, mostly Picea mariana. 150 foot ridge to north and east. Candidate old growth.

Mature mixed stand on shallow black organic soil with abundant rock-boulders. Lower part of 150 foot slope above lake. Abundant snags. No stumps. Abundant coarse woody debris (especially Picea), all sizes and decay stages. Cedar swamp down slope.

In extensive (many square miles) conifer swamp complex. Slender coarse woody debris common. Blowdowns and old snags occassional. Little deer browse. Occassional old cut stump. Muck holes wet, but no standing water. Well-decomposed moss peat with abundant small woody pieces, hit log at nearly 1 meter below surface. 27.5cm DBH Larix at 116 rings.

Old-growth? Very open from 2m to subcanopy; thinning? Fire scars on old coarse woody debris and stumps. Blowdowns of all sizes occasional. Typical rolling-pitted microtopography. Most coarse woody debris newer; old coarse woody debris infrequent and mostly slender. Soil: fine sand with a touch of silt of fine grained reddish tan sand. A horizon depth: 11cm. 51cm DBH Acer saccharum >115 rings.

Mature stand with slender trees. Coarse woody debris often thick. Gaps in E4-5 scattered occasional, <5m sqaure. Old stumps common, typically larger than standing trees Sphagnum continuous on mid-high points, Mnium cover muck holes. Soil woody moss peat.

Dog hair stand. Muck holes +/- standing water. Small gaps (<5m squared) common throughout. Slender coarse woody debris common, occasionally abundant. No signs of fire. No cut stumps. Lots of Thuja and Abies regeneration. Deer browse uncommon. Soil woody peat with moss. Thin patchy litter layer of cedar needles and Ledum leaves.

Within 50m of upland. Numerous cut stumps, most 12-18cm DBH, both new (< 5 years?) and old rotted stumps. Coarse woody debris common to abundant, most moss-covered. Muck pools without standing water. Fire scars on oldest stumps, snags. Soil woody peat, moss peat. Very sparse litter layer of Thuja needles and deciduous leaves.

Within 30m of wetland and <5m above. Burn scars on older coarse woody debris. Coarse woody debris slender-medium common but not abundant; a few recent large blowdowns. Microtopography gentle with occasional large mound/deep pit. Mottles at 25cm below surface. Soil silty loam with a few small pebbles over silty clay with small pebbles and mottles. A horizon thickness: 8cm.

Plot on local high point; forest <30 above large wetlands within 100-150m. Slender and medium coarse woody debris common, recent and greatly decayed. Cut stumps occasional. No signs of fire on old or new stumps. Overall a mixed age stand or average quality but with good potential give time to fully mature. This stand has many of the structural characters of old growth. A horizon: 3cm thick. Soil is silty loam with small amount of sand over clay loam over sandy loam with clay. Mottling begins at 34cm below the surface.

Earthworms just under litter. Plot on southern tip of low peninsula approximately 50-60m wide with shrub swamp, wet meadow and emergent marsh within 10-35m of plot. Part of series in potential old growth stand and also to document worms on wildlife management area and not near a fishing lake. Old fields at north end of stand could be an old homestead and the source of worms. Very sparse Quercus litter. Many Tilia and Quercus rubra multi-stemmed but often quite large. D6 and D7 make a continuous canopy, rather shady below. 62cm DBH Quercus rubra at 100 years. Soil: 32cm silty loam with strong sand presence over 19cm silty clay. A horizon: 9cm thick.

Mottling at 20cm below surface. 1 worm found below litter. Plot <25m from shrub swamp &and nearly at same elevation. Standing water 50cm below surface. No distinct Bt horizon. Slender and medium coarse woody debris occasional. Large coarse woody debris rare - some recent. Most Tilia multi-stemmed. Mosses restricted to coarse woody debris and tree bases. A horizon: 9 cm thick.

Mottles at <35cm from surface. Worms in humus. Forest <20 feet above wetland within 250m. Coarse woody debris of all sizes and decay stages common. Large well-decayed snags occasional. Cut stumps (<5years?) occasional. No signs of fires. A horizon 3 cm thick.

Long narrow basin in middle of esker. Narrow upland ridges along north and south sides. Stunted Larix more abundant at southwest end. Rich fen/wet meadow "mote" at upland margin, 2-10m wide. Standing water in low spots. Recent heavy rains. Very little deciduous leaf litter.

Part of large wetland complex in tunnel valley. Slender coarse woody debris, mostly standing, common. No sign of disturbance: no stumps or trails. E6 trees almost always Larix. Larix below 4m rare in community. a 100 meter squared plot could have captured this commuity equally well. Very sparse litter of Ledum leaves and small twigs.

Swamp occupies tunnel valley. Plot between esker and releve #8041, approximately 40m from edge of CS and 100m from deciduous forest. Larix snags throughout (E6). Floating on thick, solid mat. Mossy hummocks, standing water in hollows. Soil is sedge peat, muck, and wood debris. Depth of standing water ranges from 10-35cm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: On broad level crest of local high point <25 feet above large wetland <100m to north. Slender-medium coarse woody debris in recens stages of decay, mostly Betula papyrifera, common-occassional. Trees bimodal: 30-33cm and 12-15cm DBH. Old stumps uncommon. No signs of fire. A horizon: 2cm thick, mottles at 22cm below mineral soil surface.

Community 100-200m wide band between maplebasswood forest and Larix swamp. Most ash >15m tall with dying tops. Open, with much sun reaching ground. No cut stumps, but few large trees. coarse woody debris and snags occasional. Mossy rises and sedgy hollows. Soils: 0-37cm soupy muck (sedges and woodies); 37-44cm mucky compressed peat with spare graminoid litter; 44-49cm mucky peat with fine sand; 49-64+cm fine-medium sand with small pebbles.

150m wide strip between ash swamp (DNR #8047) and poor fen (DNR #8049). Mossy rises and mucky hollows with shallow water and +/- graminoids. Coarse woody debris of all sizes and decay stages common. No cut stumps. D6 ash occasional throughout. Soil mucky peat with woody debris.

Approximately 100m east of Larix swamp (DNR #8048). Patches of Phragmites approximately 15m east of plot. Community varies between Alnus and Betula gland dominance. Thick floating mat, quaking but solid? Scattered D5 Betula papyrifera.

Approximately 150m from shrub swamp wetland and 15 feet above. Charcoal in humus 6cm deep. Soil mottles begin at 30cm below mineral surface. Slender-medium coarse woody debris common, most well decayed. Snags occasional. Large, often moss covered, boulders and rocks common throughout community. A slender, mature, bi-modal (30-38cm DBH and 16-23cm DBH) community. Plot chosen due to interesting canopy composition and the prevalence of Quercus rubra in such a landscape. Soil silty loam with small pebbles over silty clay loam with some sand over sandy loam. A horizon depth: 4cm.

On island surrounded by shrub swamp and wet meadow; 5-10 feet above water, within 60m of wetland edge. No stumps. Slender-medium coarse woody debris common with occasional large recent blowdown. Recent large blowdowns are usually snags instead of tip-ups. No evidence of fire. Trees +/- open-grown with many small lower branches. Canopy uniform in height. Canopy continuous, but thin allowing a lot of light below. One third to one half of canopy trees are multi-stemmed or growing from what appears to be a common underground point. Soil sand with occasional pebbles. A horizon depth: 7cm.

Charcoal in humus. Heavy worm activity. Plot within 20m of Whiskey Brook and 40m of Rum River. Plot approximately 10 feet above Rum River water level. Microtopography very sharply undulating between rich mesic terraces and small wetland pool inclusions - this is typical throughout this portion of the community. Plot capture the broad rather level terrace of a ENE slope. >90% of Tilia are multi-stemmed. A horizon: 11cm. Bare soil with a few scattered deciduous leaves.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Lower end of plot 2-5m from black ash swamp. Microtopography with gentle hummocks, hollows; deep bowls occasional. Slender and medium coarse woody debris occasional. Large coarse woody debris rare. Cut stumps occasional. Occasional recent blowdown, mostly Betula papyrifera. Much of esker crest with ATV-sized trail. Topographic context: upper/middle/lower. A horizon depth: 2cm.

Plot located 20m from small (<1m wide) stream carrying groundwater to south south east. Betula alleghaniensis, Betula papyrifera and Fraxinus pennsylvanica infrequent in canopy. Some mid to well-decayed down trees, a few snags, no cut stumps. Poa paludigena here (?). Bimodal DBH distribution: 17-22cm, upper 20 to 35cm; max 40-43cm (mostly Fraxinus nigra). 40cm DBH Fraxinus nigra at 68 years.

Wind-rowed debris. Worm activity. On broad level terrace with gentle undulations, 60-80m from Rum River. 2m above today's water level. Occasional large well-decayed coarse woody debris. Lower side of plot captures a flood channel where coarse woody debris is most abundant. Trees often moss-covered up to 1 meter above base. Creeping charlie uncommon throughout. Acer saccharinum not multi-stemmed. Plot captures the best quality floodplain forest (based on large tree presence) in this vicinity of the Rum River. Soil is 9cm dark grey alluvial silt over dark brown alluvial silt.

npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: Within 20m of west branch Rum River and 4m above water level. Wind thrown debris common. Medium coarse woody debris mostly well decayed. Large coarse woody debris rare. Multi-stemmed Acer common. Worm activity heavy. Plot 1-2m above backwater channels, about 30 meters south of plot center. Plot captures the best floodplain forest I've seen along the west branch Rum River and this is small. Worm activity heavy throughout as evidenced by lack of litter and high abundance of castings. Soil black alluvial silt over fine grain red brown sand over dark brown silt with orange mottling.

Within 400m of Mille Lacs Lake, separated from lake by either roads or beach ridges. Single and multi-stem Betula papyrifera. Occasional well-decayed stumps without associated dead fall - cutting? See also releve numbers 8064, 8065. Very little scattering of deciduous leaves.

Within 400m of Lake Mille Lacs, separated from lake by roads or beach ridges. Widely scattered Larix, Pinus banksiana and Pinus strobus in area captured by releve. Peat depth > 65cm. See also releve numbers 8063 and 8065. Very little scattering of deciduous leaves.

Lowland hardwood surrounding conifer swamp in level depression on moraine ridge. Maturing red maple with sugar, bur oak, basswood. Mode DBH 30-40cm; max 40-60cm common. Grey silt with mottles over dense reddish clay. Small coarse woody debris, abundant tip-ups, occasional snags. Pine stumps infrequent. A horizon depth: 4cm.

Mature stand on knob atop 550 foot eats facing bluff south of Encampment R. Pines commonly 35-55cm DBH. Thick needle duff over rocky shallow soil with frequent exposed bedrock. Grades to aspen-birch with spruce fir in understory. No stumps. Scattered snags. Fair coarse woody debris.

Level to gently-rolling terrain east of Crow Creek, near Superior Hiking Trail. Trees commonly 20-25cm DBH, unusual to 45cm DBH. Few snags. Occasional old stumps. Fire scars on old conifer snags. Occasional coarse woody debris mostly small and recent. Rocky clay-loam, deep litter. No bedrock exposed.

Within broad, very shallow swale. Water table is well below ground surface. Site is hayed annually at end of season; little thatch present. Never plowed due to kaolin clays beneath surface. Slightly saline soils.

Water table above ground surface between hummocks. Soil is black, fine-grained, smelly muck with white concretions. Located on slope at foot of steeper valley-side within Glacial River Warren Valley. No calcareous fen. Much groundwater seepage. A horizon depth: 25cm.
Gradual north facing toe slope on south side of Glacial River Warren Valley. Heavy thatch cover on ground. Water table is approx 1 foot below ground surface.

Small permanent wetland in deep depression on top of large Morton gneiss outcrop. Plot is in outer vegetation zone. Inner zone is all Sparganium. Site has had grazing in the past. A horizon depth: 10cm, coarse muck.

Level ground in shallow depression on terrace in Glacial River Warren Valley. Little thatch; hayed annually in late season. Soils saturated. Gradual transition from silty to clayey soil. A horizon depth: 2cm. Average peat depth: 2cm.

Located at east end of 0.25 mile long prairie on shallow slope along drainage way. On upper terrace within Glacial River Warren Valley. Sample is from better-drained portion of site. Little thatch; hayed annually in late season.

Abundant, well rounded small to large erratics on surface composed of igneous and sedim rocks. Small amount thatch present. Subsoil very different to penetrate with prob; compact and rocky. Did not find Carex species. Andropogon increases in concentration down slope and decreases upslope. Soil medium brown sandy clay loam with small gravel over light orange brown clayey sand with small gravels.
Steep slope on side of Glacial River Warren Valley. Sample is from top of slope just below the crest. Grazed many years ago. Much medium size gravel on surface. On Glacial till. Well drained.
Dry-mesic prairie on lower slope of northeast side of Glacial River Warren Valley. Appears never grazed. Much thatch. On glacial till. A horizon depth <1cm.

Formerly grazed bottomlands on former channel of Cottonwood River. Grades into Carex atherodes on wetter ground. Water table below ground surface, but soil is very moist at surface. A horizon depth 2cm black organic. Wet meadow or wet prairie?
Hayed annually late in season. Shallow depression between low, gravelly hills. Prairie Bank Site. Soil black silt loam with few white concretions over dark grey clay (loam?) with small pebbles.
Uplands on margins of shallow basin. Prairie has been hayed annually. Also has been burned recently - probably this spring. Prairie Bank Site. Soil silt loam over silty clay loam over clayey sand.

On shallowly sloping bottomland along Mound Creek. May be receiving ground water seepage? Carex stricta hummocks are tall and difficult to walk through. Within active cattle pasture. Water table presently below ground surface. Soil 4 cm A horizon of coarse peaty much over black moist silty soil with abundant marl.
Bottomlands on broad, shallow valley of Little Cottonwood River. Water table just above ground surface. Site may be hayed late in growing season? A horizon depth: 3cm.
Level lowland between very shallow uplands. Burned last year.

Near outer edge of Scirpus dominated wetland. Water gets deeper and Sparganium drops out at middle of wetland. In small pothole in shallow swale. 1.0 - 1.5 feet standing water. Soil saturated muck at surface.

Carex lasiocarpa fen on margins of ice-block lake in pitted moraine. pH 5.5. Varies from wet Carex utriculata dominated waterway depressions; floating mat with Carex lasiocarpa; sphagnum domes with Carex utriculata and Glyceria canadensis.
Sphagnum-dominated wetland with 30cm high hummocks. No standing pools. Tamarack 1-10 meters tall. Large kettle-hole wetland in Mille Lacs Moraine. Peat > 1 meter deep.

Mature aspen-oak forest. Mode DBH 25-35cm, Populus tremuloides to 42cm DBH. Open shrub layer, gently sloping. Coarse woody debris all decay stages. Clay subsoil. Depressional, mounds or hummocks. Small boulders present. Soil silt with pebbles over silty-sand/clay sand.

Mature to old growth maple-basswood forest; Mode DBH 20-30 cm; Max size 40-50+ cm abundant. Soil deep light brown clayey silt over red brown silty clay. Coarse woody debris abundant Stumps common: old, very decayed; snags infrequent to occasional. A horizon depth: 4cm.

Semi-terrestrial mixed swamp dominated by Picea mariana and Larix. Shallow hollows and .5m hummocks. Muck/moss peat to 8cm; dense gray clay with red streaks > 8cm. No standing water. Near margin with mesic forest. Soil mucky sapric moss peat over dense gray clay. pH = 4.5.

Rich forest at toe of slope on outwash terrace with occasional boulders. Mode DBH 20-30cm; max 40-60cm occasional to infrequent. Elm snags occasional to common. Large (to 50cm) logs abundant in plot. Gaps from elm loss. Tip-up mounds. Soil: dark organic over gray silt over reddish clay silt over dense cray clay with mottling.

Mature to old growth maple-basswood; 5-10 acre inclusion; in low foot slope of moraine near black ash swamp; mode DBH 30-40cm; max 50-70cm common. Snags occasional; coarse woody debris common. Stumps few, very decayed. Boulders present, soil silt with pebbles over sandy clay over clay.
Forested fen dominated by tamarack. Sapric peat 0.5m deep to dense clay with sand. Sphagnum carpets substrate; hummocky with no wet depressions. Substrate firm. Surrounded by 5m wide moat with alder.
Rich fen in abandoned channel or tunnel valley between eskers. Floating mat. Seepage? Margins of fen approaching wet meadow/emergent marsh. Thick fibrous mat of Carex diandra.
Shrub swamp with sedge openings. 60m x 30m. Releve in open sedges. Sphagnum common in shade. Ice block depression in moraine.
Poor fen in elongated swale or depression in end moraine. Bordered by Alnus with open swath of Carex utriculata and Calamagrostis with occasional forbs. pH = 4.7. Black spruce dominates nearby area.
Floating mat of fine-leaved graminoids dominated by Calamagrostis, Carex haydenii and Carex lacustris. Wet saturated pools and beaver runs. Near edge of sand moraine.

Wet meadow bordering brook. Wet-mesic soil with depressional pools and standing water. Dominated by Calamagrostis, Carex stricta and Carex lacustris; Phalaris not abundant. Small pools, mounds and old channels.

Level to hummocky peatland with sapric and woody peat >1m deep. Saturated mud and wet pools cover 10%. Standing snags and tip-ups common. Conifers 10-20cm DBH, ash 20-30cm mode, 40-50cm max. Low lying areas between fork in brook.

Releve reflects forested core of swamp/bog complex with shrub dominated and spruce and tamarack portions. Surface irregular from old blowdowns, not from hummock forming mosses. Some mistletoe. No stumps or winter road; adjacent to Cedar Lake. Average DBH = 8cm, max to 15cm. Litter of leaves and needles.
Mesic prairie near summit of moderate south facing slope, with few erratic boulders.
Northwest calcareous seepage fen. On saturated very dark brownish black to lighter brown sapric peat. Lots of manil-shell fragments, also some marly material (hand dug 20cm deep).

North plot edge ~15m from black ash swamp and < 1-2 feet above. Small moist swales scattered in community. E5-6 Abies more common outside plot. Thick duff. No worms. Coarse woody debris common-recent blowdowns. A few cut stumps 50-75% decayed. Soil saturated sand. A horizon depth: 8cm. One years worth of leaf litter.
Stunted Larix as far as the eye can see in all directions, although CIR photo does not show this detail. Plot within a large extensive peatland with scattered upland islands.

Within large peatland-floodwood bog. No cut stumps. Ground bouncy; not floating. Appears undisturbed except winter (snowmobile?) trail east of plot. Carex paupercula, Carex canescens, Eriophorum cf virginicum to north.

In large peatland-floodwood Bog. Many trails from mechanical Christmas tree shearing throughout community. Plot in patch free of shearing. Southwest/northeast trail just northwest of plot for access to northwest/southeast pipeline bisecting bog.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Long narrow beach ridge northeast side of Lake Mille Lacs. Most D6 Quercus macrocarpa open-grown. Plot at east tip of ridge with wet meadow within 10-15m on 3 sides. No evidence of worms. No sign of fire, but vegetation more open in past. Humus and A horizon together equal 16cm. Soil humus-leached sand over reddish brown sand to 85cm+. Topographic context: crest/upper/middle.

Worms. No litter accumulation. Observed worms while burying magnet. Very little coarse woody debris-most Betula papyrifera. Woodland? Soils to be completed by ECS contractor at a later date. Topographic context upper/middle.

Many D7 Fraxinus nigra with dead branches at 15+ meters. Basin between 2 railroad grades. Just south of plot: younger, even-aged black ash swamps. No worms seen; castings present. Blowdowns and Fraxinus nigra snags. East to west flowage and rock outcrops north of plot.

Local high point on east to west rock outcrop. Plot in narrow vegetation patch between steep south facing bedrock slope and ledge to north. No cut stumps or signs of fire. Soils shallow organic to deep ~40cm clay/silt pockets.

Small bedrock exposers (boulders?) scattered throughout community. Many rocks covered with hummus with flora similar to dry bedrock forest community. Lowest depression with water ankle deep. Many depressions without water. Litter of graminoids, leaves, and herbaceous material.

Huge peatland basin. Plot within .5 mile of ditches north, south, and east. Scattered snags and larger coarse woody debris; few root tip-ups. Open water pools rare. Bouyant; not floating. More deciduous shrubs outside plot. Wood in peat.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Placed to capture oak/birch expression of oak community. Upslope from Tettegouche Lake. Presence of earthworms in bare-soil patches-lack of humus layer.
Placed to sample hardwood expression on upper slope- eventually drains into adjacent wetland. Undulating pit-mound topography. Downed trees have created canopy gaps.

One yellow birch stump cut at DBH. Placed to sample hardwood expression in valley area. Some yellow birch have near 50cm DBH. Large fallen trees have created canopy gaps and undulating terrain. Large woody debris.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Only small woody debris; placed to capture oak common on top of feature-located adjacent to ridge overlooking Lax Lake at highest point of the hill. Surrounding this small oak component is more aspen dominated forest. Undulating terrain due to rocks.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Generally flat terrain. Releve placed midslope to capture aspen-birch community along east-facing downslope. Medium to small woody debris. Majority of dominant crowns equal height.

Placed in flats of sect. 19 to capture rich yellow birch/maple comm. Upslope from wetter ash/cedar comm. Large and small woody debris of old fallen yellow birch. A few canopy gaps. Slightly undulating terrain.

Placed on flats above east facing slope which is north/northwest of Nipisiquit Lake. Large downed woody debris/young maple have bullseye cankers; patches of bare ground with blocky texture/no humus layer (earthworms). Topographic context: crest/flat.

Placed in upland cedar comm surrounded by Northern hardwood community. Both large and small woody debris-large old fallen cedar have created canopy gaps and undulating topography. Indistinct humus layer, but no earthworms. Litter mainly deciduous, some cedar.

Some small and medium sized and few large woody debris from fallen trees. Placed at base of Mt. Trudee feature to capture rich hardwood community with Dicentra groundcover (although too late in season to see Dicentra).

Old growth northern hardwoods on broad ridge south of Benson Lake. Some large and small coarse woody debris from fallen birch and maple; Canopy gaps. Slightly undulating terrain. Some small sugar maple with bullseye cankers. Topographic context: middle/flat.

Placed to capture Betula cordifolia component in Upland Cedar community. Located near shore of Manitou River; large downed woody debris of birch and cedar creating canopy gaps also. Litter is deciduous mixed with coniferous.

Both large (downed cedar and yellow birch logs) and small coarse woody debris. Plot south of Yellow Birch Trail, west of Manitou River, to capture cedar community. No humus layer, but no earthworms present in crumbly soil. Litter deciduous mixed with coniferous.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Undulating terrain, very few scattered mid-sized woody debris. Some downed and/or dying with birch have created canopy gaps. Leaves of some herbs seem chlorotic. Some bare spots of soil. Releve placed to capture paper birch stand. Ground flora/soil seems like starting from primary succession.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Placed to capture oak community located upslope from Tettegouche Lake. Earthworms present in soil / no humus layer / patches of bare ground. Some small and large coarse woody debris of birches have created small canopy gaps.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Releve placed to capture northern maple-basswood forest community. Few scattered medium downed trees/coarse woody debris which created only small canopy gaps Some maple with bullseye canker. Earthworms present-bare soil. Upper/middle.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Placed to capture northern maple-basswood forest community located East of Moose Mountain Ridge; small and medium corase woody debris which created open canopy patches. Earthworms, no humus layer, and bare patches of ground.

On ridge of Moose Mountain to capture red oak woodland on shallow rocky soil; few scattered small and medium coarse woody debris; open canopy patches due to exposed rock areas; earthworms present with lack of humus layer. Topographic context: crest/upper.

Placed to capture poplar and fir forest. Located downslope from Moose Mountain Ridge, upslope from Lester River. Lack of humus layer and small earthworms present in soil. Litter deciduous mixed with some coniferous.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Releve placed to investigate yellow signature on IR photo, plus include possible yellow birch component. Both large and small coarse woody debris including much balsam fir blowdown. Located near Lester River.

Placed to capture sugar maple community on this summit; scattered large and small coarse woody debris, but no resulting canopy gaps nor undulating terrain. Many bare soil patches and no humus layer-earthworms may be present.

Placed to capture maple-basswood community also large associated yellow birch (1-2' DBH). Large coarse woody debris, large pits along gently undulating terrain; no humus layer, earthworms present, bare soil patches.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Placed to capture black ash/white spruced floodplain community. Does not include adjacent creek bed. Some medium coarse woody debris. Litter deciduous mixed with some coniferous.

Placed to capture red oak woodland near rocky summit of Ely's Peak. Very near groomed ski trails. Much of plot is exposed rock. Some small and medium coarse woody debris. Topographic context: crest/upper.

Placed to capture old growth maple-basswood near Ely's Peak. Average canopy dominants have 1-1.5' DBH. Humus layer absent, many bare soil patches; large and small coarse woody debris; undulating terrain.

Placed to capture black ash-sugar maple comm. Includes small gravelly creek which represents community type in this area. Very little coarse woody debris. Adjacent area is either water logged soil or too far upland.

Placed to capture oak woodland on Barden's Peak. Placed southwest from summit to avoid ski trail dist. Mixed deciduous composition representative of this type in this area. Large, medium, and small coarse woody debris. Rocky and undulating terrain.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Very few small-med sized coarse woody debris; placed to capture red oaks. Maple common on this east-facing slope. No humus layer/bare soil patches, some mid-aged maples have bullseye canker. Located off Skyline Drive.
Placed within black ash swamp which is from one of the largest wetland patches in north end of Magney-Snively LSA. Soils very mucky. Extremely thick under and mid story. Near snowmobile/ski trials.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Located adjacent to ATV trail, but no sign of recent human disturbance. Open area of this stand 2 chains west of this plot looks like birch were selectively cut out. Placed to capture paper birch community. Near highly disturbed area located in Hasty Brook near (just north) a large wetland complex.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Placed to capture sugar maple community on this Brookston Morain; located in Hasty Brook LSA in between wetland complexes. Small and medium coarse woody debris, closed canopy, some pit-mound topography. Near ATV trail, but releve relatively undisturbed. Topographic context: middle/flat.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Placed to capture red maple component of wet forested maple community on this Brookston Moraine. Located just south and upslope of a small wetland. Some small and medium coarse woody debris, slightly undulating terrain.

Placed to capture black spruce comm. Exact location determined by Chel Anderson. Slopes (drains?) down to Nester Creek. Conifers fairly even distribution and even aged. Large and small coarse woody debris have created small canopy gaps. Topographic context: middle/flat. Litter coniferous mixed with some deciduous.

Placed to capture both fir and shrub dominated understory patches. Chel Anderson pre-designated plot center. Large coarse woody debris scattered especially within dense patches of 2m high fir. Very blocky humus. Litter deciduous mixed with some coniferous.

Placed to capture hardwood community not domianted by birch or cedar. Located on upper portion of hill near Richey Lake. Large, medium, and small coarse woody debris, has created pit mound topography. Many roots in humus layer (many maple seedlings)

Placed to capture conifer dominated forest on lower slopes near Richey Lake, but not below the 1750' contour. Does not include adjacent open patches of blowndown fir and spruce, but includes large coarse woody debris from blowdown. Litter coniferous mixed with some deciduous.

Placed to characterize coniferous community, I suspect to include large white pine (1.5' DBH). Plot center predesignated by Chel Anderson. Located NNW of Bally Creek. Large and small coarse woody debris (Blowndown spruce and fir). Litter coniferous mixed with some deciduous.
Prairie on Glacial River Warren bottomlands. Hayed annually late in season. In outermost zone of wetland communities on margin of lake.
On level bottomlands of Glacial River Warren Valley. Located just West of lake. Hayed late in season.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Upper part of gradual to moderately steep southeast-facing, 70 foot slope above Paccini Lake. Fairly rugged terrain. 50 feet above lake. Soil rocky loam, scattered surface boulders, bedrock exposed on knobs upslope. No stumps. Immature stand, trees multi-stemmed. Paper birch DBH 15-35cm, Sugar maple DBH 10-20cm.

Heterogeneous wetland complex along Sawmill Creek. Below Forest Ecology Building at Wolf Ridge ELC. Spongy, moist, organic substrate, no surface water present except in small channel. Scattered trees.

Small strip of fen along drainage ravine in fairly rugged terrain. Several upwelling zones and slow-moving channel. 2-3 acre opening. Tamarack-cedar swamp up gradient in broader ravine. Small pools in plot.
Five-acre stand of mature trees (33-56cm DBH) on upper slopes and top of ridge along Superior Hiking Trail. Frequent exposed bedrock and boulders-diabase. Several old charred snags. Soil very rocky.

Post fire, naturally regenerated native plant community with remnant of previous NPC. Typical slope position and aspect of remnant natural pine stands in land type association. Within climatic influence of Lake Superior. No cutting evident. Matrix forest is mixed aspen, birch, spruce, and fir. Exposed bedrock within 100 meters up and across slope.

Shrub dominated wetland behind Lake Superior gravel beach line. Seasonally saturated and at higher lake levels. No evidence of anthropomorphic disturbance. Wind throw of scattered mature trees. These coastal shrub swamp of limited extent.

Typical mature northern hardwood native plant community of upper south facing slopes of bedrock controlled hills within 3 miles of Lake Superior in eastern-most portion of North Shore Till Plain. Evidence of prior use as 'sugar bush'. No worms observed in soil sample. A horizon depth: 7cm. Soil: silty and sandy loams over clay loams.

Typical band of old growth cedar forest of middle and lower slopes of bedrock controlled hills within 3 miles of Lake Superior on lake clay soil in eastern most portion of north shore Till Plain. Subsurface flow. Small drain nearby.

Typical of old growth (+130 year) Acer dominated forest on level terrain on top of bedrock controlled hill. Extensive community approximately 550 acres. No stumps observed. 85cm white pine snag in releve, 2 nearby. Acer saccharum average DBH 26.5cm, max to 55cm. A horizon: 2cm.

Describes band of mix forest on steep north and west facing slopes 1500-1700 feet of bedrock controlled hill whose top and south facing slopes are dominated by Acer saccharum. Pinus strobus observed elsewhere in community. No evidence of cutting. Average Thuja DBH 35cm. Litter of deciduous leaf and coniferous needle.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Plot located to describe rich black ash on mineral soil terraces. Just above small brook to south. Site clearly gets surface water from hillside to North. Semi-terrestrial. No worms observed. Litter of herbaceous skiff. A horizon depth: 33cm.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Releve to describe wet-mesic boreal hardwood conifer forest on heavy soils. Uniform second-growth forest. Water filled soil pit to 25". Two non-pigmented worms observed. A horizon depth: 12cm.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Releve to describe lowland ash forest on bench above the Brule River. Community sloping from toe of long slope to approximately 5 feet above the river. Bouldery with clayey/mucky holes. Everything large and luxuriant. No worms observed. A horizon depth: 42cm. Litter of this years herbaceous.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Post-disturbance. Pinus strobus show evidence of fire. No evidence of cutting in or near releve. Early successional community transition, back to Acer dominated community. Too late for ephemerals. No worms observed.

Located to describe matrix forest community on northwest facing slopes of bedrock controlled hills near Lake Superior, and within influence of lake clay soils. Red and unpigmented worms observed under coarse woody debris. May account for low herb diversity. No stumps observed.

Located to describe forested swamp native community within larger wetland complex of gramminoid, shrub, and forested wetlands. May be influenced by beaver activity along stream within 1/4 mile. Few old stumps. Blowdown? Natural regeneration.

Reprsentative of flarks in ribbed fen perched near top of bedrock controlled ridge of North Shore Highlands. Adjacent to string of tamarack and black spruce 2-4m high. Headwaters of Fall River. Large peat complex. pH=4.8, cond=27.0, abs= .420.

Representative of ericaid dominated portion of small peatland in oval basin in bedrock controlled hills of North Shore Till Plain. Peat more decomposed than normal. Evidence of cutting and fire. pH=3.9, cond=6.0, abs=.64.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Located to describe natural regeneration/succession of post fire native community of small bedrock controlled hill of North Shore Till Plain, 5 miles from Lake Superior. No stumps, some elsewhere. Charred Pinus strobus snags. No worms.

Within the releve is a small area of standing water, approximately 2 to 3 percent of releve. This has been an unusually wet summer. Presence of black ash suggests this site is a relatively wet patch in this stand. A horizon depth: 3cm.

Lake Superior Shore; 10-15m from water. Between bedrock beach and forest. Typical of open patches in patchy native community that includes patches with more shrubs and trees. Abundant goose browsing and trampling. Abundant ants.

Plot is near crest of rounded hill, nearly level here. Adjacent parts of stand on variable slopes in rolling hills. Mature to old-growth fores.t no cut stumps, no browse line, no obvious worm activity here. Core taken from 60.8cm DBH Betula alleghaniensis, age >160 years. Litter of leaves and twigs. Bumpy and hummocky ground surface. A horizon depth: 9cm. Several trees over 20cm have fire scars.

Cobble shore within 10m of Lake Superior; rocks are angular cobble, soil is shallow between rocks. Shrubs and sedges are codominant, no trees. Area receives some seepage from upslope, small areas are wet. Litter of graminoid leaves, driftwood. A Horizon >5cm (sandy loam?).

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Minnesota Point)
remarks: Pine forest in low spot between dune ridges near Lake Superior, on soils with a black organic horizon at the surface. Lots of coarse woody debris. There is a two-track sand trail about 10m southwest of releve. A horizon depth: 20cm.

Conifer wood just inland from open cobble and bedrock Lake Superior shore on small triangular peninsula. Small stand in good condition. Foot trail northwest corner of plot. Lots of coarse woody debris. 5cm A horizon of silty loam. Litter of needles and wood.

Lake Superior rocky shore, most of plot is rock outcrop with about 5% soil patches in crevices 6 to 20cm deep. Lichens are dominant ground cover. No trees or shrubs. About 25m in from Lake Superior, exposed only to storm waves. Graminoid leaf litter.
Large peatland north northeast of Mud Lake with a few snowmobile trails. Many stems of black spruce and tamarack about 9.6 to 9.8cm DBH. pH = 3.7.

Lake Superior rocky shore approximatley 15-20m from lake. Releve is typical of dry, exposed bedrock midway between lake and upland woods;exposed to spray from large waves and winter ice scour. Gull nest nearby.

Large open bog mat southwest of Bog Lake with scattered, stunted tamarack and black spruce. Hummock and hollow topography of sphagnum mat. >100 stems of black spruce and tamarack under 10cm. pH = 3.9 of water in hollows. Minimal litter of sedge leaves.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Minnesota Point)
remarks: Pine forest on gently rolling old sand dune, in a swale or hollow with slight slope to northeast. This area burned a few years ago – a ground fire leaving a few charred stumps and fire scars. Some old rusty trash here. Litter of needles and leaves.

Juniper shrubland on stabilized dune between red pine-white pine dune forest to southwest, and beachgrass dune grassland to northeast toward Lake Superior beach. Shrubland on upper slope of dune near the crest. Litter of driftwood, grass leaves, and human litter. A horizon 0-1cm under mosses.

Low shrubland on back side of dune between Lake Superior and Saint Louis estuary/harbor, old blowout gradually being stabilized by grasses, herbs, dwarf shrubs, mosses and lichens. Litter of sparse leaves and twigs. Exposed soil: 45%.
Submerged/floating-leaved marsh south of indian point campground in the St. Louis River estuary. Water is about 0.9 to 1.0m deep.

Emergent marsh on north side of island south of Indian Point Campground in the St. Louis River estuary. Water is about 0.2 m deep. Island may be dredge spoils, with natural succession to marsh. Soil silty much over more fibrous muck (mucky peat).

Low shrubland on disturbed dune; soil is sand with some gravel mixed in. Very gently sloping upper slope of low dune between airport runway and gravel road, near crest of low dune. Litter of leaf and shrub stems.

Dune grassland on gently rolling (nearly level) sand dune closest to Lake Superior Beach. First vegetated zone inland from open sand beach. Grades inland into juniper/bearberry shrubland, then pine woods. Litter of leaves and grasses.

Submerged/floating-leaved marsh on east side of Kilchlis Meadow in St. Louis River estuary. Water ~0.5m deep. pH 8.3. Vegetation zone about 15 to 20 meters wide between open river channel and emergent marsh on island. Soil mucky clay >50cm.

Emergent marsh on east side of Kilchlis Meadow in St Louis River estuary. Water 3 to 15cm deep. pH 8.5. Vegetation zone about 5-7m wide along east side of island, grading to east into submerged/floating-leaved marsh. Litter of leaves and stems.

Dune grassland adjacent to open sand beach on slope facing Lake Superior, most exposed part of vegetated dune. Releve extends upslope to near crest of 1st dune. No adjacent shrubland/woodland-all grassy.

Dune grassland in shallow depression between 1st dune crest closest to open sand beach on Lake Superior and 2nd dune crest inland with shrubland and open woodland vegetation. Gently rolling, nearly level dune surface. Litter of grass leaves.

Juniper shrubland on crest of 2nd dune ridge inland from open sand beach on Lake Superior shore. This is a relatively stabilized dune area, possibly an old blowout--has a concave shape. Litter of leaves, branches, and twigs.

Shrubby cobble shore at upper edge of +/- permanent rock pool. Plot in low area receiving drainage/seepage from rocks and woods upslope. Rocks are large cobble to boulder size, on gentle concave slope. Litter of leaves and driftwood.

Was savanna at settlement. Dom by open-grown Quercus macrocarpa. Dry-mesic forest herb layer, no prairie species seen. Scattered large multi-stemmed formerly open-grown Ostrya. Probably logged, grazed in past. On soil formed in Glacial Till. Scattered erratics present.
Dry-mesic hardwood forest. Zanthoxylum largely confined to northeast corner. Side of large kettle hole. Site with history of selective logging. Canopy trees +/- young, many with multiple stems.

East-aspect, middle slope, well-drained. Open grown mature oaks scattered throughout. Few understory (not well developed) oaks and seedlings. Shrub layer dominated by Zanthozylum americana and Rhamnus cathartica. Outwash-formeded soil.

Low area surrounded by drier slopes. Most canopy trees - Acer negundo, with a few small-medium size Quercus macrocarpa. Ahrub layer is thin and scattered. An soil formed in outwash. Lower slope, somewhat poorly drained.

Red pine woodland on summit of narrow rocky knob/ridge. Several large red pine (DBH 30.9-48.3cm) just outside of plot on north side of ridge crest, also some white pine north of releve. Loam soil, excessively drained. A horizon: 8cm. Litter of leaves, needles, and grasses.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Floodplain forest in narrow floodplain zone between St. Louis River cobble shore and steep ridge with mixed pine-hardwood forest. Just downstream from dam, flood regime altered. Includes open vernal ponds, typical of stand. Black ash and basswood canopy. Litter of leaves and twigs. A horizon depth: 9cm (4-10).

White cedar swamp in old oxbow area of St. Louis River. Nearly level area below steep, incised sandy ridge. Mucky well decayed organic soil, with small patches of standing water at base of trees, a drier patch of oxbow area. Silty sand or silty clay in another spot. A horizon depth (mucky): 12cm.

Open mesic northern hardwoods at crest of slope above steep ravine of tributary to Red River. Area burned or grazed? (Some dandelions present) Red oak, bigtooth aspen and ironwood in canopy. Clayey soils. Litter of grass and oak leaves.

Basswood-red oak-black ash-maple forest on nearly flat interfluve between creeks to represent "boreal hardwoods". White spruce just outside plot is only conifer seen in area. 7cm A horizon of organic clayey loam.

Mesic hardwoods on middle of slope to creek, near 2 tall pines select to represent "boreal hardwoods". Few conifers on slope, dense shrubs with Corylus dominant. Evidence of fire and bear disturbance. Well-drained, steep slope. A horizon depth: 10cm. Topographic context: middle/lower.
Alder swamp along a small, sandy bottom stream with very tall, mature alders (mostly 4-10m tall). Clayey silt over silty clay soils. Somewhat poorly-drained. A horizon depth: 5cm.
Sedge and grass-dominated beaver meadow with lots of old logs buried under sedges. Lots of stumps. Mottled clay soil, poorly-drained. A horizon depth: 10cm. Liter of leaves, sedges, and grasses.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Mature black ash swamp with some balsam poplar. Evidence of fire about 90 years ago, possible 1913 Cloquet fire? Saturated soil at lower corner of plot. Soil is oxidized at roots, charcoal present. Seasonally flooded. Litter of leaves, old logs, and graminoids.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Northern hardwood forest with scattered large red and white pines & a few smaller white spruce. At crest of slope above steep ravine. Paper birch snags. Parts of stand have more pine and hazlenut, others more oak, maple, and less pine. A horizon depth: 10cm. Clayey sand or sandy clay. Quercus rubra DBH up to 29.3cm, Acer saccharum DBH <30cm, Pinus resinosa DBH: 47.5cm, 45.2cm.

Northern white cedar swamp with mossy hummocks and mucky pools. Lots of old coarse woody debris-probably old-growth? Approx 20% standing water, 25-30% mucky peat soil. 0-2cm humus on hummocks under moss.

Black ash-cedar-alder swamp with sedgy/grassy groundlayer in narrow wet depression between rocky ridges. Ground surface of scattered mossy rocks and cobble, mucky wet pools, rotting logs. Nice, but hard to walk. A horizon depth: 3cm. Litter of leaves, twigs, and wood.

Nice, old stand of white cedar on gentle north northwest-facing slope above wetlands. Below very steep slope with several small springs/streams. Groundlayer is predominantly ferns and fern allies. Silty clay soil. A horizon depth: 2cm. Litter of sedge and cedar leaves. Thuja DBH to 56.5cm common.

White cedar-black ash swamp in old oxbow area of St.Louis River, nearly level area below steep,incised sandy ridge. In wetter patch of oxbow. ~20% of releve has water-filled depressions, mossy elsewhere. Litter of mostly mosses, a few leaves. A horizon depth: 2cm. Mostly decomposed peat.

Plot sited to represent small-patch native plant community common in Northshore Highlands in small gently sloping drains or shallow depressions. Surface (small streams) and subsurface water flow evident. Abundant coarse woody debris.

Mature/old-growth stand at mesic end of the type. Grades to wet-mesic in ravine downslope, to northern hardwoods upslope, plot 300 feet above Manitou River - west side. Scattered large coarse woody debris, a few well-decayed stumps. Betula alleghanienses. Canopy Thuja 40-65cm DBH, Betula alleghanienses 45-75cm.

Typical of 3/4 mile long and 1/8 mile wide basin in rugged terrain west of Manitou River Cascades. Grades to Thuja along margins of wetland. Trees mostly 7-20cm DBH, no stumps. Swamp along narrow bedrock hollow. Soil saturated peat.

40-acre basin surrounded by steep 200' slopes of bedrock-controlled terrain. Varies from semi-terrestrial cedar at margins to swamp in center. Occasional old stumps. Much coarse woody debris. Slight stream in plot. Few pools.

50-acre inclusion in large northern hardwood stand. Lower mid-slope of 300' east facing slope; steeper upslope. Mature stand, trees 25-45cm DBH. Occasional snags, frequent coarse woody debris. Scattered old stumps. Near slight moist drain in plot.

Wet ash-cedar along slight drainage atop broad ridge east of Manitou River. In extensive old-growth northern hardwood complex. Varies from moist to wet. Trees 20-65cm DBH, cedars leaning. No stumps. Much coarse woody debris. Mix of wet troughs and drier raised areas. Grades to cedar-yellow birch to northwest. Shallow organic soils.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Mature stand on ridge west side of hare lake. Trees 30-45cm DBH. No stumps. Little coarse woody debris. Snags occasional. Scattered surface rocks/boulders. Grades to paper birch downslope toward lake. Thick duff layer.
Mature stand on broad terrace east side Caribou River south of North Shore State Trail. Trees 18-35 (42)cm DBH. Coarse woody debris occasional. No stumps. Appears natural, high quality for type.

Mature/maturing stand in level to gently-rolling terrain northwest of moose lake. Trees 15-30cm DBH, Acer and Betula often multi-stemmed. Little coarse woody debris, a few very decayed stumps. Soil horizons: A, E, Bw1, Bw2, 2BC. Excavation deeper than 80 cm impeded by cobbles. Parent material is glacial grift over lodgment till.

Maturing to mature stand on level, narrow finger of land between cedar swamps on north side of Moose Lake. Pinus 38-51cm DBH, Picea 20-35cm, Thuja 10-18cm. No stumps. Little coarse woody debris. Pinus rare in surrounding area.

Mature stand in broad cedar/spruce wetland complex northeast of Moose Lake. Tree 15-42cm DBH, often leaning. Uneven substrate with 30% wet troughs. No moving water. Coarse woody debris occasional. Few snags. A few very old stumps.

Trees 16-30cm DBH; straight, tall. Ground fairly level but moderately hummocky, covered by sphagnum. Frequent coarse woody debris. No cut stumps. Deep peat, part of larger peatland that grades to cedar and/or alder on north side of Moose Lake.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Semi-terrestrial stand in small pocket along slight drainage through northern hardwoods in rolling terrain 80 feet above east side of Caribou River. Fraxinus 15-48cm DBH. Trees buttress-looted. No stumps or snags. Little coarse woody debris.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
