remarks: Upper slope of steep 320 foot east facing ridge north of railroad tunnel. Localized stand extends 100 feet downslope. Quercus rubra 20-38cm DBH, Acer saccharum 10-35cm. No stumps. Fire scars present. Soil shallow to bedrock. Oaks defoliated 80% by tent caterpillars.

Mature, rather even-aged stand mid way up gradual (here) to moderate-steep, southeast-facing, 450 foot slope above l superior and highway 61 west of Caribou River. Frequent old fire-scarred pine stumps. Frequent moist seeps. Frequent snags and coarse woody debris. Frequent seeps/wet spots. Trees 15-35 (40)cm DBH. Buttress rooted. Canopy denser upslope.

Crest of gradual to moderately-steep, 450foot slope above highway 61 and Lake Superior west of Caribou River. Ridgetop along superior hiking trail. Mature stand. Fire -scarred old conifer stumps occasional. Grades to paper birch-balsam fir. Little coarse woody debris. Few snags. Soil rocky clay-loam.

Mature stand on gradual northwest-facing slope near ridge-top. Trees buttress rooted, 20-55cm DBH; largest are Thuja, Picea glauca and Betula cord. Thuja straight. Some coarse woody debris, windthrow, occasional snags. No surface water.

30 acres of open bog surrounded by much larger black spruce bog in drainage through rolling terrain between caribou road and county road seven. No surface water. No coarse woody debris. No stumps. Continuous sphagnum. Deep peat. Trail to east.

Mature 50 acre stand along river. Varies from cedar to cedar-spruce mix. Thuja 15-35cm DBH, straight to leaning. A few old stumps. Occasional coarse woody debris. 50m inland and 1m above river. Hummocky, infrequent small pools. Slope position: depression/flat.

Broad sedge fen surr small unnamed lake west of crooked l. Scattered stunted Larix and Picea mariana. Plot 40 feet from lake edge. Vegetation low-statured. Grades outward to zone with old snags then Picea-Larix bog. Peat.

Mature stand along Blesner Creek and County Road 7 at Blesner Lake Road. 5-10 acres between creek and road. Trees 12-30cm DBH. No stumps or snags. Infrequent coarse woody debris. Substrate mildly hummocky. Grades richer with alder/forbs.

Maturing stand on lower portion of fairly steep, 200-foot, northwest-facing slope above North Shore State Trail, just east of valley draining Kowalski Lake. Natural origin? Small pile of small diameter old conifer logs.

Maturing stand on moderately steep upper portion of 150 foot slope along North Shore State Trail east of Manitou River.  Acer: 8-28cm DBH. Often multi-stemmed betua 20-35cm DBH. No stumps, coarse woody debris sparse. Soil shallow, rocky loam. Trees rather short. Part of isolated, 40 acre stand.

Level ground just above level of black spruce swamp in narrow valley btwn 40-100 foot hills in rugged terrain west of Manitou River, along middle trail. Deep ravine just to southeast. Mature stand. Frequent coarse woody debris. No stumps. Stand small in extent due to setting. ECS soils plot here.

Very steep upper portion of 350 foot east facing slope above the Manitou River, below cedar ridge trail. Mature stand, Thuja 15-35cm DBH, rooted in thin soil amongst exposed bedrock and large talus blocks. No stumps. Extends above crest where less steep. Much coarse woody debris. Talus/bedrock.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Paper birch succeeding to sugar maple. Maturing stand rather even-aged many trees multi-stemmed, betula 18-30cm DBH, Acer 10-22cm. No stumps, coarse woody debris sparse. Fairly rugged terrain along matt willis trail south of Benson Lake. One very old conifer stump. Soil is rocky clay-loam.

Fairly broad mat on west side of balsam l. Zone of low-statured shrubs 15 feet from waters edge. No coarse woody debris. No stumps. No surface water. Mildly hummocky. Grades to wetter Carex lasiocarpa zone-releve 8505.

Fairly broad mat on west side of balsam l. Plot 30 feet from waters edge on spongy mat,wetter than nearby releve 8504. Slightly hummocky with shallow water in troughs. No stumps. Grades inland to cedar.

Open bog forming broad zone on west side of egge l. Plot 30 feet from waters edge on southwest side of lake. Mat quite firm here, hummocky. Rather dryish, no surface water. No old stumps. Scattered small snags present. Grades inland to denser stunted spruce. Sphagnum continuous on hummocks, less so in troughs.

Broad sedge mat surrounding Doyle Lake. Localized area of low-statured vegetation 10 feet from waters edge. South west side of lake. Mat very spongy here-feet sink 6-12 inches. Grades to firmer Carex lasiocarpa-dominated zone.

Broad sedge mat surrounding Doyle Lake. Semi-treed bog on northwest side of lake, 75 feet from waters edge. Grades to poor (shore) fen (releve 8507). Which dominates most of mat- alder in some spots. No stumps. Few small snags. No surface water. Mat here quite firm, moderately hummocky.

Mature cedar in fairly broad wetland in rolling terrain along upper reaches of creek. Thuja 15-38cm DBH, straight to slightly leaning. Scattered very decayed stumps. Much coarse woody debris. No surface water in troughs. ECS soils plot here.

Mature stand in shallow depression in rolling terrain east of Beaver Forest road and north of Hockamin Creek. Fraxinus 10-40cm DBH, Thuja 25-40cm. Few old cedar stumps. Coarse woody debris sparse, snags occasional. Water in troughs. ECS soils plot here.

Maturing/mature wet cedar along upper reaches of Hockamin Creek. Broad, subtle, lower portion of 150 foot southeast-facing slope. 10 feet above stream level and 200 yards from it. Trees 15-40cm DBH. Scattered old Thuja stumps. Grades to Alder. ECS soils plot here.

Plot in densest white spruce I've seen in North Shore Highlands. Native origin? Upper portion of steep southeast-facing, 350 foot slope above l superior and 1/2 mile inland. Upslope from power line above hwy 61. Picea 20-35cm DBH. Coarse woody debris sparse. Heavy deer browse, old pine stumps fire scarred in vicinity. ECS soils plot here.

Semi-terrestrial alder (possibly a result of past beaver activity?) Along Manitou River between county road 7 and "the cascades". "Floodplain" 2-3 feet above river and 100 feet from it. Wet-mesic mineral sandy-loam. Part of large Alnus-Thuja-Picea "wetland" complex along river.

Maturing stand atop narrow ridge 40 feet above Hockamin Creek. Trees 12-35cm DBH, mode 15-20cm. Very old conifer stump in plot which includes the ridgetop and gradual, upper, south-facing slope. Coarse woody debris sparse. Few snags. ECS soils plot here.

Mature stand on lower portion of 150 foot, north-facing slope along Hockamin Creek. Trees 15-42cm DBH. Coarse woody debris rather sparse, mostly Aibes. Plot 30 feet above creek. Soil rocky with scattered small to large boulders.

Mature stand along Hockamin Creek 1/2 mile southwest of mouth of Hefflefinger Creek plot ~10feet above stream level and 1/8 mile from it. No standing water. Trees 15-35cm DBH, scattered snags.Sparse coarse woody debris. No stumps. Substrate moderately hummocky.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Maturing/mature stand atop bedrock ridge southeast side Thunderbird Lake. Grades to paper birch on south-face slope nearby. Trees often multi-stemmed with few large boles. A few very old stumps. Snags rare. Coarse woody debris sparse. Acer saccharum DBH 5-30(38)cm, Acer rubrum DBH 6-18cm, Betula 18-43cm DBH, Pinus strobus 68cm DBH. Fairly shallow to bedrock, loamy soil.

Large forested wetland in rolling terrain south of Shoepack Lake. 200 acres of cedar, 40 acres spruce. Thuja 10-35cm DBH, mostly straight. A few old conifer stumps. Coarse woody debris occasional. Sphagnum and feathermosses abundant.

Maturing northern hardwoods with red oak atop narrow ridge in rugged terrain east of Manitou River. Oaks local in forest and on rock outcrops atop south facing slope 50m away. Very old fire-scarred pine stumps. Few snags, scattered coarse woody debris. Quercus rubra DBH 20-48cm; Acer saccharum DBH 15-45cm.

Small depression along subtle drainage feature atop ridge west of Benson Lake. No stumps. A few snags including Betula alleghaniensis. Canopy patchy, sparse. Coarse woody debris occasional. Sphagnum covers 80% of plot. Peat > 25cm deep.

Mid to upper portion of moderate-steep, 70 foot, northeast to northwest-facing slope above small wetland. Rolling terrain along superior hiking trail southwest of Benson Lake. Small bedrock outcrops exposures. Loamy rocky soil. Scattered coarse woody debirs, including large old conifer boles, a few old pine and cedar stumps. Thuja: 15-25(40)cm DBH, Betula cord 20-40cm DBH, Betula alleghaniensis 25-35cm DBH, Picea glauca DBH 42cm, Pinus strobus DBH 61cm.

Mixed stand, somewhat heterogeneous. Along gentle drainage in rugged terrain south of Benson Lake. Substrate moist/wet peat, no standing water. Snags and old conifer stumps. Grades outward(upland) to cedar-yellow birch. Fraxinus 5-15cm DBH, Thuja 20-40cm, Betula 30-45cm.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Plot depicts semi-terrestrial hardwood native plant community typical of shallow depressions, lower and toe slopes embedded within matrix forest occurring on soils with significant lake clay influence. Litter of herb and leaf. Native plant community is Northern Wet-Mesic Black Ash(MHn62?).
Rich transition sedge fen. Approximately 35cm well decomposed sedge peat over sandy clay loam. Plot estimated, not actually measured out.
Soil approximately 10cm black loam over dark gray clay loam. Lots of coarse fragments. Becoming lighter, mottled. Larger gravel. Grades to wet brush prairie towards woods margin.

Soil approximately 10cm dark brown-gray loamy fine sand over light greyish-brown fine sand. Well decayed charred remnants of medium-size aspen, plot in open are a surrounded by aspen-bur oak woodland.
In extensive mosaic of wet brush prairie and dense thickets of aspen suckers. Seems slightly depauperate, but no past disturbance evident. Plot estimated, not actually delineated. Next to PR91-05.

In extensive mosaic of wet brush prairie and dense thickets of aspen suckers. Seems slightly depauperate but no past disturbance history apparent. Plot estimated, not actually delineated. Next to PR91-04.

Mesic brush prairie, sand-gravel subtype. Open area on sandy soil. Airphoto shows linear pattern suggesting past clearing, plowing. Low # of graminoid species consistent with distrubance. Plot area estimated to be 100m squared.

Mesic brush prairie, sand-gravel subtype. Open area on sandy soil. Airphoto shows linear pattern suggesting clearing, plowing in past. Low number graminoid species consistent with disturbance. Plot area estimated to be 100m squared.

Shallow, south southeast-trending depression; meadow intergrades with wet brush prairie. No Spartina in wettest parts. No evident disturbance. Burned in wildfire fall '89 or spring '90. Cornus stolonifera occasional outside plot.

Site was sheared several years earlier, little damage evident. Burned by wildfire fall '89 or spring '90. Intricate mosaic with shrubby wet meadow. Two types intergrade. Sometimes wet-mesic. Plot boundary paced.

Site was sheared several years earlier, but little damage evident. Burned by wildfire in fall '89 or spring'90. Intricate mosaic with wet brush prairie. Calamagrostis canadensis dominant in wettest places. Plot paced.
Long, narrow linear wet meadow, flanked by aspen woods. Not obviously degraded, though couple of exotics common. Boulders frequent at surface.
On long north facing slope on Plainfield sand. Some portions of white pine forest to west more mesic and mossy, without Chimaphila and Lycopodium. Adjacent to dry oak savanna. In Whitewater Valley.

White cedar-black ash swamp with hummocky ground. A few old cut stumps present. Good condition, upland to north recently logged. A horizon >50cm. Litter of leaves and coarse woody debris. Thuja DBH 20-40cm, Fraxinus nigra DBH 15-40cm, Betula DBH 45-50cm.

place_name: Fond du Lac to North Bay
npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Black ash dominated floodplain forest in the estuary of the St. Louis River at North Bay. Active floodplain-floods every year. Southwest edge of releve is within 3-5m of emergent marsh on river shore.
Wetland depression of about 5 acres with vegetation mostly on peat over mineral soil. Not a floating mat. Water depths 12" after recent rain. Salix gracilis a feature of central portion of wetland

Mississippi River Floodplain, 100m north of river. Topography slightly undulating, plot adjacent to old channel. Woody debris common. Canopy Acer mostly ~25cm DBH, multi-stemmed. Several snags in plot.

place_name: Fond du Lac to North Bay
npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Narrow zone of black ash-willow floodplain forest on sandspit in St. Louis River estuary, at upper edge of marsh and shrub swamp complex in embayment formed by spit. About 2 miles downstream from lowest dam. Sandy loam soil. A horizon depth: 5cm. Litter of twigs and leaves. Fraxinus nigra DBH 20-30cm, Salix amgydaloides DBH 40-50cm; max to 90cm.

Floating Sphagnum mat with no obvious sign of disturbance. Dominated by Carex lasiocarpa and Thelypteris palustris. Lots of Vaccinium. Releve in middle of fen about 30m from edge. In kettle hole with road running along south edge. Soil sphagnum mat over peat.

Dominated by Sorghastrum nutans and Andropogon gerardii. Very little Bromus inermus. Poa compresa throughout. Lower areas dominated by Spartina pectinata. Liatris pyncnostachya and Helianthus max are dominant forbs. Home construct. Silty loam <42cm, clay with gravel >42cm. A horizon depth: 4cm.
Part floating sphagnum mat, part Carex stricta hummocks. Outer part of fen ~15 m from edge. In kettle hole, very poorly drained. Road running along south edge.

Floating sphagnum mat up to 2 feet deep. Releve in middle of mat.Outer part of mat much thinner and does not support weight. Carex lacustris dominant with Thelypteris palustris. No Vaccinium. A few holes, not disturb, road along north edge.
Water table about 6 inches above ground surface. Old cattle fencing-former pasture. Black fine-grained peaty muck soil, depth at least 2 feet.

Releve done south of middle section of fen. Lot of Drosera rotundifolia. No sign of disturbance. No real concentric zones; northern, middle and southern sections do vary slightly in species composition. No Vaccinium.

Coarse sphagnum peat. In small basin. Releve 30m from edge of mat. Tracks through mat (deer and snowmobile?). Some dead areas of sphagnum - result of runoff from surrounding lawns? Houses around basin could increase run-off. Thin mat-spongy with holes.

On terrace of gentle north-facing slope. West side of seegage area. Some invasion by Phalaris, more possible. Lots of Equisetum. Marly on soil surface; peaty, mucky, sandy deeper. Large boulder outside plot.
Terrace on middle of slope with gentle slope. Long narrow zone following contour of slope. Marly on surface; mucky peat to ~24 inches, then sandy clay.

Mosaic of patches dominated by different sedge species. Area domianted by Carex lasiocarpra. No sign of disturbance. Part of a large area of wet meadow. Soils: 20" organic peat, 6" lite gray gravelly clay sand, sandy gravel.

Dry mesic prairie at top of slope, has 4 species of Liatris. Liatris pycnostachya found nearby. Poa pratensis is dominant grass, good diversity. Silty sand soil <10 cm, rocky soil deeper. Exposed granite <1%. Waypoint 1A. A horizon depth: 10cm. Soil: silty sand over rocky soil.

Well-drained dry mesic prairie with excellent species diversity. Both Poa and Brome present, not much of either. High abundance of forbs, especial Zizia aptera. Black fine sandy loam <10cm, light brown loamy sand.

South facing slope of east to west running esker. At base of slope. Solidago canadensis is dominant and Rhus glabra encroaching. Field road along top of esker. Open to grazing, does not appear disturbed by cattle. Soil sandy loam and silty sand with gravel. A horizon depth: 8cm.

Relatively open, compared to rest of site. On hilltop. Lot of Rhus and quite a few junipers (on hillsides). Would be very good quality with management (burn and brush cutting). Fine sand over sand with pebble soil. A horizon depth: 10cm.

Dominated by Carex lasiocarpa, some Carex stricta. Shrubs scattered throughout. In other parts of area, purple loostrife is growing and may pose a threat, but this area is free of loostrife at the moment.

Small area of prairie on flat land, moderately-drained. Hayfield to south. Shrubs/cattails to west, north, and east. Heavy dominated by Sporobolus. Poa and Brome here not as dominant. Dark loam with sand <48cm and sand with gravel soils >48.

Poorly-drained. Dominated by Carex stricta with a few scattered willows and dogwood. Lot of Impatiens cap under the stricta. 20m to north cattails. Muck soil <10cm, sandy clay <67cm, coarse sand with small pebbles >67cm. A horizon depth: 2cm.

Post-mature northern hardwood forest  dominated by Acer saccharum, with Betula papyrifera. Mode DBH 30-40cm; max size common throughout 40-60cm DBH. Moraine knoll with eskers and outwash channels nearby. Silt over clay, bouldery. Subsurface water >12cm. A horizon depth: 3cm.

Rich mesic mixed forest domianted by Populus tremuloides with Thuja abies and Picea glauca. Mode DBH 30-40cm; max 40-60cm. Locally abundant in stand. Lower-mid slope. Terrace or ridge of moraine with silty mesic moderately drained. Occasional boulders, abundant coarse woody debris.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Wet-mesic forest on terrace 15 feet above Gooseberry River, below gradual slope. Trees 15-35cm DBH. Earthworms present, leaf litter lacking. Soils compacted clay/silt with slight undulations. Logs present (Populus balsamifera), many recently fallen, some snags standing.

Clump of mesic to wet-mesic cedar in area of scattered cedar clumps surrounded by open Alnus/Betula papyrifera/Fraxinus nigra. Cedars 20-45cm DBH. Cedars are straight to somewhat leaning with buttress roots. Sparse coarse woody debris. Browse line at 2.5m. Cedar regeneration limited to seedlings.

Upstream from mouth of Gooseberry River, at Lake Superior level. Influenced by seiche. Channels of water formed by seiche movements penetrating the stand at the upper reach of seiche. Soil appears scoured as in a floodplain forest. Many openings in alder canopy dominated by Calamagrostis canadensis and Thalictrum dasycarpum.

Cedar-dominated forest just below crest of slope above Gooseberry River. Cedars 20-40cm DBH. Seep and small draw within plot, heading downslope. Cedar regeneration limited to seedlings. Some cedars are buttress-rooted, but most have straight trunks. A horizon depth: 14cm.

Narrow bedrock shrubland between Lake Superior Cliff and birch forestr. On east side of Gold Rock Point, mostly low shrubs with some taller Alnus, Sorbus and Betula. Disturbance mostly from wind and ice from Lake Superior.

Alder swamp in floodplain of stream just above Lake Superior, just north of Gold Rock Point. A stagnant side channel runs through releve. Alder dominated - 5-15cm DBH, old trunks leaning. There is one large rotten log, soil is bare, obviously flooded sometimes (debris), earthworms present. A bit of beaver damage to some alder trunks.
East side of hill on Gold Rock Point, at base of slope, and just inland from Lakeshore shrubland. Just northwest of releve 8589. Soil clay-loam, very shallow to bedrock (~5cm).

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Wet-mesic Fraxinus nigra/Populus balsamifera forest on terrace above Gooseberry River. Heavy earthworm presence, only a thin smattering of leaves and stems over bare soil. Fraxinus to 30cm DBH, Thuja 30-40cm. A horizon depth: 4cm.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Mesic soil with large earthworm presence. Aspens are 10-30cm DBH. Only a few stems cover the bare soil. Releve is at top of hill, but soil is not well-drained. Some big old stumps, but few logs. A horizon depth: 6cm.
White spruce dominated forest, DBH 20-35cm. Western border of park in northern-most part of conifer-dominated forest. Clay-loam soils fairly shallow to bedrock. Mixed conifer and deciduous litter.

Atop a ridge where many birches have died of disease, leaving a shrub-dominated community. Lots of down birch logs. Area likely logged and severely burned in early 1900's. Rocky soil shallow to bedrock. Pine stumps. A horizon depth 10cm. Litter of grass with deciduous leaves.

Birch forest 50m inland and about 20m above Lake Superior. Birches 20-30 cm DBH, some broken or top-killed due to disease or ice damage. Corylus and Acer spicatum browsed heavily and have large subcanopies. A few birch logs. Corundum point heads off to southeast. Litter of grass and some deciduous leaves.

Clifftop shrubland above Lake Superior, with lots of bare bedrock. Many human trails. Heavy deer browse. Sorbus and Amelanchier dominant. Shallow soil is organic down to bedrock, 0-50cm deep. Corundum point. A horizon depth: 20cm. Litter of old stems.

Betula/Sorbus forest with open canopy due to disease/ice damage. Shallow soil with high organic content. Some trees broken, standing birch snags. A few old stumps. Betula 15-25cm DBH. Corundum point. A horizon: 7cm. Trail through releve plot.

Wet-mesic swamp with an alder opening. Lots of down logs, all stages of decay. Very little cedar regeneration over a few cm tall. Spruces 15-45cm DBH, cedars 15-25cm DBH. Evidence of deer browsing. Deer trail. Ground spongy with lots of moss. Most trees buttressed. Deer trail passes through.

Young (15-30cm DBH) spruce-dominated forest with open canopy and a few rock out-crops. Shallow soil, lots of organic matter. Few logs. Deer browsing signs. Some old cut stumps. 30 meters above talus slope. A horizon depth: 4cm. Mixed conifer and birch leaf litter.

Open birch scrub with Corylus-dominated shrub layer. Shallow, reddish organic- rich soil over bedrock. 8 planted Pinus strobus, <1m tall in plot with cages for deer protection. Only a few logs. Birch trees are 20-30cm DBH. A horizon depth: 8cm. Litter of grass and leaves.

Betula papyrifera/Populus balsimifera forest on steep slope. Thin layer of newly fallen leaves over previous bare soil with lots of earthworm casting. Fair amount of fallen logs. Small gully on one side of releve. Old stumps. Trees are 20-30cm DBH.

Betula papyrifera forest on steep slope with lots of loose rocks on soil. A horizon depth: 10cm. Very few logs. Trees are 15-25cm DBH. Shallow soil with organic matter over rocks. Beaver damage at lower end. In some places it is a bare rocky slope (rocks about 1 dm diameter). Heavy deer browse.

Mixed Picea glauca and Betula papyrifera. Stand with Picea up to 25cm DBH. Betula up to 30cm. Several old pine stumps with fire scars. There are gaps in the canopy. A few logs, but not many. Mixed litter of conifer and birch leaves.

Pinus banksiana on bedrock within 1 mile of Lake Superior. Natural regeneration from wild fire circa 1920. Releve captures area of native plant community with densest cover of Pinus. Sparsely vegetated openings embedded within the forest.

Plot located to capture shrub-dominated native plant communit adjacent to perennial low-gradient streams. Seasonally flooded. 2 large Ulmus species snags and 3 saplings in plot. Poorly-drained, deciduous leaf litter.

Chosen to sample intermittent stream bed of regularly flooded side channel of Flute Reed River. Dry on 7/23/2001. Main channel flowing with no vascular species. Raised shrub dominate island separates channels.

Selected to sample vegetation of intermittent stream bed of Flute Reed River. Water flowing through 25% of bed on 7/23/01, pooled in much of remainder of channel. 1-20cm deep, moderate gradient. High water, floods >area.

Chosen to describe moderate rich fen (pH 6.9) in basin of North Shore Ecological Classification System. Adjacent lake with pH 7.8. Shrub cover variable, in zone with mid-range shrub cover. Scattered stumps from harvest. Historic fire.

On floating mat on middle of small kettle hole basin. Plants growing in continuous moss layer. Mat is firm, but springy. Water at surface of moss layer. Small moat on edges. Forest surrounds all sides. Coarse peat.

Fen-like seepage zone. At midslope on north edge of low ridge. Water table near surface. Site not very springy. Some very small, wet open areas. Marly peat at surface, peaty muck <50cm, sandy clay deeper.
6 inches standing water between hummocks. In large, shallow wetland basin. Soil is peaty muck, fine-grained, black < 25cm. Grayish, silty muck with gray streaks > 25cm.
On upper part of south facing slope. Difficult to tell if any grazing in past. A few large glacial erratics at surface. Not able to get soil probe below about 4-6 inches, kept hitting rocks.
Open seepage zone on shallow southwest facing slope. About 15% of plot consists of bare, exposed peat under shallow groundwater pools. Much marl on peat surfaces.

On upper part of steep slope on side of huge esker. Grazed at time of survey. Cow pies cover about 0.5 square meters of plot. Not able to penetrate ground with soil probe. Sandy loam <2cm, gravelly sand >2cm.

Water table at ground surface. 1 patch in a mosaic of patches dominated by different graminoids. In wet meadow zone, just east of large Typha marsh. In former glacial river channel. 0.25 mile east of large esker. Coarse peat over fine-grained mucky peat.

In zone of wet prairie and wet meadow. On low, level terrain on bottom land within former glacial river channel. Approximately 0.25 miles east of large esker. Past grazing. Water table below surface. Scattered small-medium shrubs. Extensive Typha angustifolia marsh to West. A horizon depth: 2cm. Black silty loam over coarse sand with small gravel.

Prairie on steep southwest-facing slope on knob known as "badger hill".  Site has been managed with controlled burns. Probably grazed before acquired as park. No glacial erratics present on hill. Soil appears to be formed in sandy outwash with small size gravel.

Between wet prairie and sedge dominated mixed emergent marsh. Downslope of large hill to east. Appears groundwater infiltrated. Gray clay component. Litter of sedge leaves. Soil sedge peat muck over silty clay loam.
Standing water between Carex stricta clumps. Very slight slope. No peat, heavy saturated black clay with grey clay at 30cm.

Wet mesic prairie within a complex of wet prairie, wet mesic prairie, wet meadow and Typha marsh. Andropogon main dominant. Good species balance. Likely hayed in past, due to a weedy haybale spot. Now moderate thatch. Soil calcareous silty clay loam.

Wet prairie within a complex of wet prairie, wet prairie seepage subtype wet mesic prairie, wet meadow and marsh. Excellent microsite variability, slight presence of Agrostis. Rhamnus a serious future threat. Soil calcareous silty clay loam.
10-15 degrees west-facing slope-narrow band of oak between prairie and wetland. Very messy but owner reports not grazed in last 26 years. Quercus macrocarpa DBH 25-40.
East facing slope of prairie knoll. Loamy soils with gravel fragments.
This is a Lespedeza site just released from grazing this year. It has been grazed at least since the mid-1980's. A heavy season long grazing it is in the process of acquisition by SNA. Soils coarse

Level site with much internal hummock microtopography pH 7.2. Microtopography reflected in species list, no way to avoid it and still be in this signature on photo-do not use for native plant community classification.
Last grazed in 1998. North facing slope south of impoundment, mid slope, convex hillside. Among best quality areas in this go. This is in record #28980.
Rotationally grazed pasture. Releve during period of active grazing which affects cover/abundance of forbs. Midslope on south-facing slope just above lightly wooded ravine. Corresponds to EO #28976.
Releve is late in season. Earlier notes from prairie in general report more species. Grazed by horses.
Active pasture but slopes are characterized by releve, BC because of Poa, Brome and timothy, Tragopogon, etc. Fairly weedy releve.
Active pasture, steep slopes in best condition releve on south side of concavity at head of very small draw prairie wraps around draw.
Lake Superior rocky shore on east side of stoney point. Upper portion of exposed bedrock shore 10m from lake, with lichens abundant on rocks, shrubs and herbs in rock crevices. Diabase bedrock.

Rocky shore of Lake Superior north of Shovel point. High, narrow ledge about 10m wide between lake shore cliff and spruce-fir forest. Level ledges about 10m above lake, with low vertical rock face (1m). Rhyolite.
Upper slope of high, rocky knob on Lake Superior shore at gold rock point. Open rocky area includes an oval wooded patch of black spruce. Granite bedrock.
Upper slope of high, rocky knob on Lake Superior shore at Gold Rock Point. Open rocky area between linear patches of balsam fir/black spruce woods. Granite bedrock. A horizon depth: 2cm.

Black spruce-feather moss forest on upper, northwest-facing slope; high rocky knob on Lake Superior Shore at Gold rock point. Dense stand of stunted, small DBH black spruce. Granite bedrock. Soil texture duff only, 0-8cm over bedrock.
Lake Superior rocky shore near top of cliff on point of land north of gold rock point. Open rocky shore with dense cover of lichens, scattered herbs, shrubs in rock crevices. Diabase bedrock.
Lake Superior cobble/pebble beach, upper beach ridge washed only by storm waves. Open low shrubland, with sparse cover of shrubs. Rhyolite cobble/pebbles.
Lake Superior rocky shore with rock pool on point of land north of Gold Rock Point. Small perched meadow at edges of rock pool, with sedges and shrubs, plus shallow mossy depression. Diabase bedrock.

Lake Superior rocky shore, summit of small, rocky point south of long, curving pebble beach and north of small cove. Bedrock covered with crustose lichens, a few mosses, herbs sparse in crevices, basalt bedrock.
Exposed rocky summit of Palisade Head along Lake Superior shore, ca 0.15 mi inland from lake and 330 feet above lake level. Open rocky woodland, scattered stunted trees. Rhyolite bedrock.

Steep, rocky south-facing slope of Palisade Head along lake superior shore, ca 180m inland from lake, 280 feet above lake level. Open slope with rocky ledges and low vertical faces south of summit. Rhyolite bedrock.

Lake Superior rocky shore with rock pools and perched meadows in "rock garden" area near campground of Temperance River State Park. Pools in shallow bedrock depressions hold seepage water. Basalt bedrock. 10cm A horizon of organic muck/peat for 10% of plot, 90% exposed rock. (Plot size 2.5m x 10m).

Lake Superior rocky shore with rock pools and small, shrubby meadow in "rock garden" area near campground of Temperance River State Park. Shallow bedrock depression holds seepage water. Basalt bedrock. 18cm A horizon of muck.
High rocky slope of Corundum Point along Lake Superior Shore. Rocky summit area includes many small exposed rock areas within a shrubby woodland. Bedrock is anorthosite with glacial striations.

Cobble/boulder shore of Lake Superior, north of Gold Rock Point just above lake level.  Rocks covered with lichens, wet gravel between rocks has patches of herbs and shrubs. Diabase and glacial drift rocks. Sparse litter of grass or sedge leaves.
Rocky shore of Lake Superior north of Crystal Bay in Tettegouche State Park. Lower slope of bedrock shore, ca 4m above lake level at tip of triangular peninsula. Few vascular plants. Basalt bedrock.

Steep rocky shore of Lake Superior north of Crystal Bay in Tettegouche State Park. Middle slope of bedrock shore ca 10m above lake level, includes small seepage area/rock pools, mostly dry rocks. Basalt.

Boreal conifer forest on Shovel Point along Lake Superior shore in Tettegouche State Park. Forested lower slope of rocky peninsula, foot trails nearby. Mix of spruce-pine-fir. Rhyolite bedrock. A horizon depth: 6cm.

Krummholz boreal conifer woods above cliff on north side of shovel point along Lake Superior shore. Wooded, steep rocky slope near old trails. Stunted trees and many low shrubs. Rhyolite bedrock. Soil 16cm humus over rock. Litter of leaves and twigs.
Gravel and sand beach on Lake Superior shore of flood bay; shrubby upper beach ridge zone between open beach and marsh. Glacial drift and basalt sand/gravel. Sparse litter of leaves and driftwood.
Rocky shore of lake superior n of shovel point in Tettegouche State Park. Shrubby krummholz area near crest of rocky knob 6m above lake level, with patches of lichen-covered rocks. Rhyolite bedrock.

Summit of rocky knob near Lake Superior shore in Judge cr Magney State Park. Open rocky patch in open rocky woodland, near crest of knob about 38m above lake level. Ferromonzodiorite bedrock. A horizon depth: 10cm.

Upper slope of rocky knob near Lake Superior shore in Judge cr Magney State Park, near crest of knob. Wooded patch with stunted fir and spruce in open rocky woodland. Ferromonzodiorite bedrock. Litter of leaf and needles. A horizon depth: <30cm.

Shrubby wet cobble shore of Lake Superior northeast of horseshoe bay in Grand Portage State Forest. Large cobbles and boulders just above lake level with moist sandy humus between rocks. Diabase bedrock. 12cm A horizon of sandy humus. Spare litter of leaf and coarse woody debris.

Spruce-fir-aspen-birch on rocky bluff along Lake Superior shore on the south side of horseshoe bay in Grand Portage State Forest. Few shrubs, scattered herbs with patches lichens and mosses. Diabase bedrock. Litter of leaves and needles. Charcoal and abundant coarse woody debris.

Rocky shore of Lake Superior in butterwort cliffs Scientific and Natural Area within Cascade River State Park. Upper slope of exposed bedrock shore with broad ledges and low vertical face. Many lichens few herbs basalt bedrock.

Spruce-fir-pine-cedar forest on gently sloping rocky ridge near shore of Lake Superior north of Shovel Point in Tettegouche State Park. Groundcover of mosses/lichens on shallow duff over Rhyolite bedrock. A horizon depth: 3cm. Litter of needles, leaves, and coarse woody debris.

Rocky shore of Lake Superior at south end of lighthouse in two harbors. Uppermost zone of exposed bedrock near small path from Sonju Trail. Mostly well-drained with a few small rock pools. Basalt bedrock.
Rocky shore of Lake Superior near picnic tables at picnic flow in gooseberry falls state park. Heavily used area with several small temporary rock pools, mostly well-drained. Basalt bedrock.

Rocky shore of Lake Superior near picnic tables at picnic flow in Gooseberry Falls State Park. Grassy mat next to one large/several small rock pools filled by seepage. Trampled area. Basalt bedrock. 30cm A horizon of sandy humus.

Rocky shore of Lake Superior on southeast side of artist point in Grand Marais. Upper zone of exposed bedrock with large rock pool filled by seepage. Small boggy meadow along pool, lichens on dry basal bedrock. 34cm humus/A horizon over bedrock (average 10cm), covers 20-25% of plot. Patchy leaf litter. Exposed rock: 35% dry/above water and 20% under water. Plot size 2.5 x 10.
Rocky shore of Lake Superior on southeast side of artist point in Grand Marais. Gently sloping exposed bedrock at end of foot trail, heavily used area. Few herbs, crustose lichens. Basalt.

Large mesic prairie on broad ridge top surrounded by oak forest on slopes below. Last burned 5/04/01. Releve better than surrounding (c rank) prairie, which has more Solidago canadensis. Managed with tree and brush cuts, fire.
Ditches around perimeter of Wildlife Management Area and across middle and ends, but no obvious impact to fen. Plot estimated-not measured.
Wet-mesic brush prairie, excellent condition, in mosaic with wet brush prairie. Occasional boulders at surface. Plot estimated, not measured
Soil about 6 inches black clay loam over yellowish-gray sticky clay loam. Intergrading with wet mesic prairie. In regularly hayed area,with reduced shrub component. Plot estimated; not measured.

Not Hayed. In fine-grain mosaic with wet-mesic brush prairie (see DNR 8721). Soil: about 4 inches black clay loam over dark sandy clay loam to fine gravel at about 8-9 inches. Plot estimated; not measured.

Wet mesic, shrubs sparse; not hayed. In small-grained mosaic with wet brush prairie (see DNR 8720). Soil: about 5 inches black loam over light gray sandy clay, dense small gravel at about 14 in. Plot only estimated.
In fine-grained mosaic of wet and wet mesic brush prairie, mostly the former(see DNR 8724 for the wet-mesic type). Possibly hayed in the past. Plot estimated, not measured.

Wet-mesic brush prairie with suppressed shrub component from hay mowing. Soil: black sandy clay loam over dark brown fine sandy clay loam over mottled light gray fine sandy clay loam. Plot not measured, estimated.
In fine-grained mosaic of wet and wet-mesic brush prairie, former predinating. See releve DNR 8722 for wet-brush prairie here. Possibly hayed in the past. Plot not measured, only estimated.

In fine-grained mosaic of wet and wet-mesic brush-prairie, 1st predominate. This plot in an area grading to wet-meadow. See DNR Releve 8722 for typical wet brush-prairie here. Possibly hayed in past. Plot estimated.

Represents best drained part-most of prairie here is wet. Heavy accumulation of litter/mulch. Needs burning. On private land just beyond Wildlife Management Boudary. Plot only approximate, not measured and marked.
In 15-20 acre opening in mosaic of wet and wet-mesic aspen woodland and brush prairie. No recent disturbance apparent. May have been kept open by hay in past. No plot actually measured/marked.

In 15-20 acre opening in mosaic of wet and wet-mesic. Aspen woodland and brush prairie. Old trail across west edge of plot only evident disturbance. May have been hayed in past. Plot size only est. Prairie is wet-mesic.

Sandy slope in "sand coulee" which is a northwest to southeast trending valley that feeds to Zumbro river. Barbed wire near plot edges indicates past grazing. Adjacent areas more brushy (sumac, black locust, small oaks). Dark sand.

Rich hardwoods dominated by yellow birch (DBH 55-75cm) and sugar maple (DBH 15-25cm). Decayed snags with debris mounds of old wood. Boulders infrequent. Rich organic silt with earthworms. Snags, locally common. Terrace of Pine Creek. Soil dark silt.

Conifer woodland on outwash terrace in bend of Cloquet river dominated by white pine with white spruce, paper birch and quaking aspen. Excessively drained silty sand. Thick pine duff. Pine DBH 35-45cm. Coarse woody debris 5-15%. Thick Abies understory. Ground mounded and pitted. Soil silty sand.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Wet-mesic Fraxinus nigra forest in shallow depression on terrace about 3m above Cloquet River Bed. Moderately drained organic silt over clay and sand. Surround by sedge dominated low area. Abies 5-15cm, Fraxinus nigra 15-25cm, Picea glauca 15-25cm.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Dry-mesic, mixed forest on well-drained berms of Cloquet River. Dominated by paper birch, black ash, white spruce with white pine scattered. Pine DBH 35-55 cm. Birch DBH 25-35cm.  Sand and unsorted gravel with depressions. Coarse woody debris 5-10%, snags infrequent.

Black gabbro opening on ride spur (total area: 5-10m x 100m). Massive bedrock, 2m tall, flat with drainageways, cracks and rubble 25% bare rock exposed. Lichens and moss on remainder. Small shrubs and stunted trees on shallow soil and edges.

Mixed mesic forest dominated by paper birch (DBH 25-35cm), red maple (15-25 cm), white spruce and white cedar (45-55cm). Open canopy dense shrub layer. Bouldery substrate of ravine at large bedrock ridge. Coarse woody debris common, snags occasional. Dark organic silt.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: White pine-hardwoods on rock outcrops, mid slope of ravine. south facing aspect. Pine DBH 50-90cm. Rocky, bouldery substrate and gabbro outcrop. Tip-ups and down logs infrequent.

Rich, mesic forest dominated by sugar maple with white spruce and paper birch. Typical DBH 15-25cm; max DBH common 35-45cm (mostly open grown crowns). Many old decayed pine stumps. Ridged crest on till with large tip-up mounds and hollows. Mull humus. No worms.

White cedar swamp. Old-growth dominated by Thuja occidentalis. DBH 15-35cm. Hummock and hollow microtopography. Dense shade. Wet depression. Tip-ups and coarse woody debris common. Stand next to recent clear cut. Sphagnum dominant substrate. Water-logged hollows 15%.

Hardwood forest, terrace/ravine of ridge. Open woodland dominated by paper birch (15-25cm DBH) with quaking aspen (25-35cm DBH). Abies (15-25cm) common to abundant. Tip-up and blowdown <20%. All stages of decay. Hummock and hollow microtopography.
Wet meadow bordering bear lake. Half floating mat/half open pools. With firm bottom <75cm depth. Soil organic muck.

Mixed forest dominated by red pine (35-45cm DBH) on narrow rim of kettle hole of esker/stagnation moraine. 50% grade on southwest and northeast aspects. Rim crest <5m width. Coarse sand and gravel, thick pine duff. With Abies (DBH 15-25cm).
Poor fen at edge of esker and bordering black spruce deep hummocks (35cm height above water tracks).
Tamarack/black spruce fen. Firm substrate. Low area of tunnel valley near esker. Larix DBH 15-35cm. Picea mariana DBH 5-15cm.

Mixed pine forest with white pine and red pine (pine DBH 35-55cm) on  gentle 10-20% slope. Dark silty loam with gravel, earthworms. Thick pine duff. Aspen snags infrequent. Down logs and limbs common. Hummock and hollow microtopography. All stages of coarse woody debris decay.

Mixed conifer hardwoods dominated by white pine (45-55cm DBH) white spruce (35-45cm) with quaking aspen and paper birch (25-35cm), red maple (15-25cm DBH). Level to rolling crest. Sand-gravel unsorted. Coarse woody debris, old logs, and tip-ups very decayed. Topographic context crest/upper.
Black spruce fen dominated by Picea mariana (DBH 15-25cm). Deep sphagnum hummocks. Hollows dry. Coarse woody debris common, tip-ups. All stages of decay. In large basin of glacial outwash.

Mesic hardwoods on north facing ridge on level bench terrace with exposed gabbro, lower slope. Dominated by sugar maple, paper birch, white spruce and red maple with black ash. Spruce DBH 25-45cm, Acer saccharum 15-35cm, Acer rubrum 5-15cm. Plot adjacent to white cedar swamp.
Wet meadow dom by lake sedge. Oval shaped depression w/in large black ash swamp. Standing water in center w/depth to 25cm. Open water 15%. pH 5.8. Surrounding matrix black spruce fen in outwash basin
Brush swamp with tamarack dominated by Alnus and Carex stricta with diverse shrubs. Transition to poor fen/swamp. Thuja DBH 15-25cm, Picea mariana 5-15cm, Larix 15-25cm pH 6.9. Large outwash basin.
Wet meadow/rich fen dominated by Carex stricta with Carex brunescens densely covered with low shrubs. Shallow basin with firm substrate on terrace adjacent to wide-meander of Cloquet River. pH 7.5.
Sand meadow at edge rich fen beneath overhanging boughs of red pine (50-70cm DBH). Free of shrubs, grassy slope. Brown silty sand. Moderately well drained to moist with mounds of cobbles.
Wet meadow/emergent marsh, along brook with braided channels. Open water 10-15%.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Floodplain forest on low-lying terrace on inside bend at base of rapids of Cloquet River. Moist sand. Level <1m  above stream. Bare sand 15-25%. Coarse woody debris common. Occasional large boulder outside plot. DBH 5-15cm.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Floodplain forest on high terrace in drainageway with moderately-well drained sand to moist with depressions dominated by Acer saccharinum 25-45cm DBH. Multiple stems. Dense herb layer. Coarse woody debris 15% - common.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Silver maple floodplain forest on narrow strip along Cloquet River where joined by small drain receiving water from nearby shrub swamp. DBH 25-35cm max 35-45cm common. Alluvial sand and silt. Undulating to level with channels. Coarse woody debris <5%.
River bank sand bar on northside of Cloquet River. Bare sand above high water mark on inside bend of river. 50% bare sand. Graminods, forbs and adventive shrubs.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Open silver maple forest on high terraces of Cloquet River with low depressions and berms. Somewhat poorly drained to well-drained. Mode DBH 15-25cm, max DBH 35-45cm, rare to infrequent. Half of plot on berm.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Lowland forest with black ash on inside meander (north bank) of Cloquet River. Low depressions surrounded by berms of sand, especially along east bank. DBH 15-25cm. Coarse woody debris common.
Sand bar in main channel of Cloquet River on spit separation, back water slough from river. Stagnant water 15-20%.
Jack pine forest on level terrace of Cloquet River. Sand outwash jack pine DBH 15-35 (45)cm. Even-aged stand. Coarse woody debris common, <20%. Black spruce and balsam fir in equal abundance.

Dry conifer-birch forest on rocky soil. Level to hummocky with large boulders to 1m diameter. Coarse woody debris moderate to common from tip-ups/blowdowns. Spruce DBH 15-25cm, birch 15-25cm, Quaking aspen 25-35cm. Dark loam, no worms.

Jack Pine woodland included within larger and denser forest. Large open-grown Pinus banksiana with spreading crowns. Mode DBH 15-25cm nearly devoid of tall shrubs. Low ericaceous shrubs abundant. Mostly level. Plot typical of scattered openings. Populus DBH 5-15cm, Picea DBH 5-15cm (25cm rare). On terrace of Cloquet River. Soil coarse sand and gravel.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Silver Maple forest with black ash on sand terrace of Cloquet River. Sand and gravel with large boulders, ridges and raceway channels. Moderatey well-drained. Coarse woody debris moderate. Undudulating slope(0-15%). High berm along river. Rich diversity. Acer DBH 15-35cm.

White cedar swamp dominated by mature Thuja. Much of stand has wind blown trees. Coarse woody debris abundant. Thuja mode DBH 35-45cm. Lower areas in the stand are dominated by young Thuja to 15cm and 5m crown height. Black ash graminoid swamps on stand margins. pH 6.7.

Poor fen bordering small pond near esker. Water table higher evident by pine snags (45cm DBH). Zones of rich fen dominated by Carex utriculata to poor fen dominated by Sphagnum and Carex lasiocarpa. Graminoids increase abundance away from pool. pH 5.5.

pH-8 mixed coniferous swamp with Thuja and Populus balsamifera 50-100m north of Marion lake in a hummock depression with 5-10% cover of shallow pools (pH=8 measured). Numerous tip-ups/windfalls ~5-20% cover.

Shrub swamp dominated by Myrica on level terrace 5m wide bordering Marion Lake. Southeast aspect. Base of balsam/cedar slope. Abrupt 1/2m rise from lake shore. Well-drained mineral soil over boulders (which line shore). Intersected by animal trails to lake. Well drained, moist organic.

Ridge along moraine (?) apparently large in extent, parallel Cloquet River. Earthworm castings evident. Well-drained soils (silty  sand over unsorted gravel). Several tip-ups, wind damage and stumps with charcoal. <5% downed logs. Decayed stumps, logging probable. Slight depressions. DBH range for Pinus resinosa 35-55cm for Betula papyrifera. A horizon depth: 2-3cm.
Backwater of West Branch of Cloquet River.  Muddy bottom pH 8.2.

Dry-mesic forest dominated by Betula papyrifera (DBH 15-25cm) and Abies balsamea (DBH 5- 15cm). Oval shaped knoll with few boulders. Silt and gravel. Mixed with earthworms. Level to 5 degree. East aspect. Moraine feature amid large bog complex.
Black spruce bog. Dense growth of Picea mariana (<15cm DBH) thick sphagnum with few pools <1%.

Wet meadow or rich fen on mineral soil between arms of upland moraine. Surrounding forest Quaking aspen and dry-mesic paper birch and white spruce. Releve within channel 25m x 1150m and joins larger poor fen complex. Mineral/muck soil.
Backwater slough of Cloquet River. Rich fen and shallow emergent marsh with adjacent open water. Mud bottom, plot shape 1 x 100m area. Floating mat at waters edge including submergent aquatic plants.
Rich fen floating mat on lost lake. Quaking vegetation mat dominated by sedges and deciduous shrubs. Bordered by a narrow band of stunted Larix and Picea mariana on north side of lake.

Birch woodland with scattered red pine on moraine ridge between lake and tamarack fen. Coarse unsorted sand on ridge bearing south. Level crest (about 5m) to 30degrees. Slope east and west aspects. Diverse shrub layer. Saddle knolls and depressions. Coarse sand soil. Coarse woody debris, tip-ups <5%. Pinus resinosa DBH 25-45cm, Pinus strobus DBH 52cm.

Tamarack on poor fen complex of level flats between lake and brook. Scatted Larix to 15cm DBH, 3-15m tall. Thick shrub cover with Myrica gale. Open areas bog-like with Carex chordorhiza. Hummocks - no open pools, peat moss covers all.

Mesic conifer forest over bedrock, cobbles and boulders. Thinly covered by soil. Silty sand, fine-grained. Large boulders <4m diameter in plot. Pine duff 3cm. White pine 45-65cm DBH. Thuja 10-30 (65cm). Rock saddles but no depressions. Coarse woody debris 1-5%.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Narrow band of floodplain forest on both sides rocky, raceway channel of Cloquet River below rapids. Mostly on low, bouldery/cobbly terrace near channel.

Mixed forest dominated by Pinus strobus (DBH 45-85cm), Pinus resinosa (35-55cm), Betula papyrifera (25-40cm) with a dense subcanopy of Abies. Pine sapling and most forbs within small openings. On spit between bays of lake. Silt over sand and gravel. Coarse woody debris 25%.
Black ash swamp-level, wet-mesic, minerotrophic. No standing water. Ash 25-45cm DBH, Thuja 35-45cm, Acer rubrum 25-35cm with multiple trunks. Scattered boulders. Muck-silt.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Late summer releve in mesic hardwoods dominated by paper birch (DBH 25-45cm) and sugar maple (15-35cm). Occasional groves of basswood (35-45cm) with scattered white pine. Silty soil with earthworms. No duff and humus. Pitted moraine - steep depressions, irregular aspects. Coarse woody debris 15%, wind blown, tip-ups and broken limbs.
Large forested fen dominated by Picea mariana (DBH 15-25cm) and Larix (15- 35cm DBH). Dense sphagnum carpet. Open canopy areas dense with Alnus, Salix and Ledum. Sphagnum and sedge peat.
Rich fen-shrub swamp dominated by Chamaedaphne, Betula glandulifera on firm sedge peat near brook.

Percent cover of canopy species varies-always Acer saccharum dominant. No worms. Scattered red dead and down, some large (occasional stump-old). Wood frogs, Black T. Green, ovenbird, review. Tent caterpillars chewed shrubs, now is seasonal recovery. Seasonal ponds. High quality. Litter of leaves and twigs. Soil rich, moist organic black layer.
Swamp variable, % Alnus/Abies/Thuja mixed ages with D and D - No obvious stumps. Litter of needles and twigs.
Possible old cut area. Very brushy. D and D birch/fir. Large scattered super-canopy white spruce. Scattered white spruce super canopy. Litter of leaf, sticks, and needles. Rocky, gritty loam.
Remnant patch of clustered old white pine. White pine otherwise few and scattered in area. Worms not apparent. D and D - charcoal in duff. Litter of leaves, twigs, and needles.

Topograpy rolling-species variable. D and D ~primarily birch fir-old stumps but cutting on stump not apparent. Worm curds. Taxus short=browsed ~10"- charcoal (stumps possibly pine). Litter of leaves, sticks, and twigs.
Rolling, hummocky swamp-mistletoe prevalent in spruce: deformity and +/- snow drop. Maybe attributed to Larix dominance in canopy. Very low forbs and graminoids.

Mixed emergent marsh in Weaver Bottoms area of Mississippi River, about 80m northeast of USFWS observation deck. Wades to Phragmites dominated-marsh to east. Level microtopography. 50% cover leaf litter, with Sparganium dominated litter species.

Part of large emergent marsh-shrub swamp complex in Mississippi River flood plain. About 100m east of railroad tracks. About 25% with no emergent vegetation. Much herbivory from muskrats. 2-12 cm standing water. Rivulets throughout complex. <5% litter cover of Scirpus fluviatilis.
Area being selectively logged (red oaks). Gently rolling landscape. Forest surrounded by wetlands, lakes and old field. One of only a few sites with Trillium nivale in Douglas County.

Unusual to see a forest in this area with a canopy dominated by sugar maple. Many of the maples are large with DBH over 50cm. Herbaceous layer is much sparser in this part of the tract where maples dominate.
Typical mesic forest of this part of the state. Most of the basswood in the plot and in the stand are multi-stemmed. Undulating terrain with gentle slopes. Dark loam over loamy clay.
Dry prairie on ice contact deposit (crevasse fill). Typical diversity of species for this site. No bare soil. Area not grazed, but is burned on a regular cycle. A horizon depth: 10cm.
On ice contact deposit - some bare soil and scattered small rocks. Are a not grazed but is burned on a regular cycle. A horizon depth: 5cm.

Hummocks of Sphagnum with Carex interior and Carex disperma. Tamaracks growing on these hummocks. Shallow pools between hummocks. The whole area on a firm and stable sphagnum mat. Coarse sphagnum peat over organic.

Floating Sphagnum mat with hummocks of Carex prairea. Mat is stable without holes. Area grades into area with taller tamaracks that form an almost complete canopy (see releve 8831). Coarse peat over organic.

Dry prairie on ice contact feature that runs east to west (crevasse fill). Area is lightly grazed on a rotational basis (currently ungrazed). Part of a large area of prairie that is being managed with rotational grazing.

Area lightly grazed within a larger area of prairie that is grazed on a rotational basis. On an ice contact feature (crevasse fill) ridge running northwest/southeast. Small patches of bare ground, to rocky to get soil probe. Topographic context is upper/middle.

On dry ridge running east/west (ice contact features; probably an ice crevasse fill). Bare patches of soil throughout with some exposed rock. Very little thatch build up, area is burned period, but not this year.
On ridge running east to west - an ice contact feature (ice crevasse fill). Area not grazed but burned occasionally (not this spring). Some thatch built up.

Area becomes shrub swamp just south of the releve with an old fence line separating the two communities. Area probably hayed in the past? Horses currently have access to fen, but don't appear to spend much time there - mostly in the upland prairie.

On gently sloping south facing terrace, cut into south facing slope. Upwelling water seeping out of slope. Calcareous fen area merges into a rich fen, seepage community along rest of the terrace. Some game trails through the area.
On east/west running ridge. Prairie is high quality along the entire ridge. Area burned this spring. Calcareous loam till.

30x120m wetland oriented east-west, surrounded by well drained dry sand gravel prairie hills (20 degree slopes). In the spring, wetland center standing water(to 1m), now very wet, but only pockets of standing water. 5 meter ring wetland contains Scirpus cyperinus, Eleocharis and Carex stricta. Beyond this strip, another strip that has been heavily grazed(Trifolium repens).

Northwest/Southeast running ridge-crevasse fill ice contact deposit. Currently lightly grazed. Sandy loam with gravel and small cobbles average about 4cm. Forb abundance seems lower than in other parts of the tract. Litter of litte bluestem leaves.

Standing water above ground surface between Carex stricta hummocks. Site not very springy. Soil appears to be sedge peat in top 1/2m situated in gravelly outwash land form. Many gravel pits on uplands near by. Some groundwater seepage. Soil fine grain peat.

Water table below ground surface. Part of broad seepage zone at foot of gravelly hill. Soil fairly coarse peat with whitish specks that appear to be marl. Small, active flowing rivulets of cold spring water present.

Seepage wetland on toe slope along Sucker Creek. Water table above ground surface. Site is quite springy. Iron oxide colors in water-no marl seen. Releve is in the most calcareous fen-like part of this wetland. Soil fibric coarse peat.

Mature stand atop 150 foot ridge/knoll on west side of county road 3 north of London Crossing. Acer saccharum DBH 15-30cm, Tilia americana DBH 20-38cm,l Tilia marked with blue paint. Coarse woody debris sparse. One old pine stump, no recent stumps. Rocky, loamy soil. Tilia mostly multi-stemmed. Bedrock(diabase?) exposed at crest of north-facing slope. Logging road 1/2 mile to South.

Typical of large expanse of old growth on ridge south of Stony Creek. Plot on upper portion of gradual east facing slope near crest. Trees 20-65cm DBH. Frequent recent wind damage. Tip-ups and decaying boles frequent. Occasional old pine stumps, some fire-scarred. Good structure and age diversity. Rocky, loamy soil. Snags occasional.

Old growth in rolling terrain west of county road 2 southeast of Thomas Lake. Trees 30-75 cm DBH, good age structure. Rocky loamy soil. Scattered coarse woody debris, recent wind- falls. Snags occasional. Scattered large old pine stumps. Tent caterpillars on maples.

Mesic old growth cedar/yellow birch on gradual lower slopes of 20foot ridge rising from swamps between county road 2 and mining railroad. Grades to old growth sugar maple atop ridge. Trees 30-70cm DBH. Rocky loamy soil. Occasional large old pine stumps. Frequent snags and coarse woody debris. Tip-up mound micro-topography.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Typifies higher quality patches of community atop rugged diabase ridge above Milepost 7 tailings ponds. Trees commonly 25-40cm DBH, occasional to 60cm. Snags occasional. Large old conifer stumps rare. Rocky loamy soil. Occasional coarse woody debris. Little earthworm evidence. Old growth here? Grades to patches where Betula papyrifera is co-dominant in canopy. Tent caterpillars on oaks.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Dry-mesic stand in rather shallow rocky loamy soil over bedrock atop rugged diabase ridge above Milepost 7 tailings ponds. Trees short, large oaks somewhat open-grown to 35cm DBH. Tent caterpillars defoliating oaks.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Maturing to mature, dry-mesic, even-aged stand upper portions of 180 foot bedrock ridge-northern most "nester bluff". Most trees 15-25cm DBH, but occasionally to 50cm. Rocky sandy-loam. Few snags. Fire scars on stumps. Much logging in vicinity. Fairly large patch surrounded by much recent clear cut logging.

Typifies best portions of large patch of old growth between county road 2 and railroad northeast of Stewart. Near top of gradual slope of broad ridge. Trees frequent 50-65cm DBH. Old fire-scarred conifer stumps occasional. Loamy soil, rather shallow to bedrock. Tip-up mounds frequent. Light earthworm activity. Thick leaf litter. Good structure and age diversity. Scattered coarse woody debris, including large old boles. Grades to cedar-yellow birch in low areas.

Mature wet-mesic stand. Outer portion of large conifer wetland complex forming headwaters of Encampment River along county road 2. Trees 15-40cm DBH (mode 20-25cm). Few old stumps. Moderate coarse woody debris. Shallow water in troughs, hummocks dryish. Sphagnum species in lower areas.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Mature stand, upper midslope of mod steep, 150foot-southwest facing slope above North Shore State Trail southwest of London Crossing. Trees 25-44cm DBH. Many oak mult-stemmed. Old fire-scar conifer stumps. Small basalt outcrops in plot. Some recent selective logging downslope out of plot to east. Rocky loam soil.

Typical of large patch of mature to old growth maple on gently-rolling terrain west of London Crossing. Rocky loamy soil, fairly shallow to bedrock. Trees 15-65cm DBH. Old stumps uncommon. Good structural diversity. Occasional coarse woody debris, snags.

Designated old growth spruce. Mature(?) stand atop 1/5 mile wide x 3/4 mile long plateau between fault-line canyons in extremely rugged terrain south of Glen Avon Falls. Soil shallow to bedrock, outcrops frequent. Pines occasional. Coarse woody debris sparse. Few snags. Rock outcrops dry, moss-covered, frequent in stand but rarely very large.

Mature stand on extremely steep midslope of 400foot ridge above Beaver River at Glen Avon Falls. Trees 15-40cm DBH, mode 25cm. Few snags. Coarse woody debris sparse. No stumps. Old fire-scarred coarse woody debris on adjacent cliff. Much exposed bedrock. Naturally depauperate type. Exposed bedrock is 50-75% moss covered. Bedrock outcrops mostly vertical exposure 2-8 feet tall. Litter of needles and leaves.

Typical of 60 acre stand in basin east of county road 2 north of Two Harbors. Canopy patchy to interrupted, trees to 30cm DBH. Picea mariana nowhere common. Continuous sphagnum carpet, hummocks. Snags rare, no stumps, little coarse woody debris. No standing water.

Old growth-typifies older patches in 200 acre stand between county roads 2 and 3 North of Two Harbors. Gentle slope of 150 foot ridge. Rocky, loamy soil. Trees 25-60cm DBH. Snags occasional, no stumps. Tip-up mounds common here. Fire-scarred cedar stumps down slope.

10 acre atop 80 foot granite knob along Chapins Creek. Exposed rock including lichen-dominated areas: 90%, soil 10%. Tree cover patchy to dense. Scattered old small conifer stumps. Herbs more diverse in shallow soil. Trees short. Bedrock is much-fractured.

Plot characterizes wettest low lying areas in 5 acre basin north of Crosscut Lake. Wettest areas cover 1/5 of fen, grades to higher hummocks, some in plot. Surrounding terrain rolling, gravelly. Sphagnum on hummocks. No old stumps or snags.

Typifies most of 10 acre fen on east side of Crosscut Lake. Spongy mat, saturated peat. Grades to ericaceous; Chamaedaphne-dominated outer zones. Sphagnum restricted to higher hummocks. Shallow pools occur along wildlife trail. No old stumps.

Rather narrow zone between wet-mesic/mesic (upland) prairie and wet meadow/marsh. Deep moist highly organic black soil. Grades to wet-mesic prairie just 2 feet higher elevation. Never grazed/plowed. Calcareous till along Sedan Brook.

Typifies low-lying wettest areas in 10 acre sedge-ericad fen otherwise dominated by Carex utriculata and Chamaedaphne. Wettest areas cover 1/5 of fen. No Larix or Picea in fen. Several low hummocks in plot. Surrounding rolling uplands intact forest.

Typical of wetter low-statured vegetation in lowest lying areas of broad fen surrounding 5 acre bog lake in 15 acre basin north of Spur Lake. Saturated peat, slightly spongy, many hummocks in plot which is 15m from west side of lake.

5m from water's edge on 30m wide floating mat on north side of Spur Lake. No stumps. Grades to areas dominated by Carex lasiocarpa eastward, by ericads then black spruce inland, by cattails to west. Vegetation low-statured. Saturated peat, low hummocks, water in troughs.

Wettest, low-lying areas of 8-acre poor fen surrounding 2-acre bog lake in small basin south of Moose Lake. Wettest micro-habitat covers about 1 acre. Plot 30m from southeast side of lake. Spongy saturated peat. Several hummocks in plot. No surface water.

Old growth localized on upper slope of extremely steep, 300f00t, west facing slope above upper Sawmill Creek North of Sect 13 cliffs. Large trees 40-65cm DBH. No stumps, snags occasional, moderate coarse woody debris. Shallow rocky loam soil.

Mature mesic stand covering 30 acres on moderate to steep, southeast-facing slope 300 feet above Lake Superior on southwest side of Beaver Bay. Soil shallow to bedrock. Outcrops 50 feet upslope. Trees 20-70cm DBH. Stumps rare. Several snags, some coarse woody debris.

place_name: Little Net R old growth cedar
remarks: Designated old growth stand in drainage of Little Net River southeast of Holyoke. 60 acre swamp. Shallow peat. Few old cut stumps. Few snags. Scattered coarse woody debris. Mosses carpet ground. Trees 15-40cm DBH. Scattered wet depression.
Chamaedaphne zone in center of wetland. On firm, floating Sphagnum mat with vigorous pillows of Sphagnum.
In outer part of Carex lasiocarpa zone on solid sphagnum mat. At margin of wetland in small basin.

On top of broad ridge. Soil is very loose sand. Pin oaks reach 45-55 cm DBH. Lots of dead falls. Never grazed. In geomorphic area mapped as supraglacial drift, site appears to have sandy outwash/ice contact deposit.
Prairie on level terrain between plowed fields. Unplowed because heavy clay subsoil causes seasonal ponding.
On heavy, black gummy silt loam soil. On level terrain with frequent, shallow depressions. At end of warm, wet summer.
Forest on low peninsula extending into Cedar Lake. Elms reach 50-60 cm DBH.

Top of ridge; gentle northwest slope. Hummocky, wet. B-B ranch. Prairie bank. Also between ridge and gravel road ~1/2 mile east: Salix candida, Cornus stolon. Salix eriocephala, Solidago riddellii, Aster ericiodes, etc.
Sandpiper Prairie Scientific and Natural Area. See also plant list PL 99-10.

Glacial Ridge plot north of pile of 3-4 boulders northeast 1/4 of section between rock pile and willow/aspen/balsam poplar stand to north. Location selected to capture forb diversity. Uneven ground-past disturbance, but level overall.
On Glacial Ridge Project (TNC). Between two short +/- EW ridges in north 1/4 of section adjacent (crossing) fence east side. Some introduced species not dominant.
Glacial Ridge Project (The Nature Conservancy). Dry prairie at east end of narrow gravelly ridge crossed by north-south fenceline dividing section.

Wet prairie in Glacial Ridge Project (The Nature Conservancy). Cypripedium candidum habitat (11 plants seen) adjacent to Dugdale Wildlife Management Area between old road/borrow pit and seep zone. With Jason Ekstein, The Nature Conservancy.
Unusual species assemblage. Open band between shrub-dominated wetter bands. Grading to wet brush prairie. Disturbed by past grazing? drainage? Needs fire. Don't use for classification work.

Unusual species assemblage, many meadow species. Disturbed looking-past graze? drying? Becomes shrubbier to south as peat depth decreases. Peat here at least 60cm, probably about 75cm. Plot estimated, not measured.
Fen on flank of large mound at toe slope of sandy/gravelly hill. On east side of small lake.
On large fen on floating peat mat.
Sloping fen just south of north edge of section. On deep, saturated, marly peat. A few, small open pools present. Southward, grades into shrub swamp-seepage subtype.

On saturated mound of peat containing abundant marl concretions. Scattered, small, minimally vegetated pools. Surrounded by dense Scirpus acutus/Larix/Betula pumila wetland with much Carex prairea. At foot of gravelly hill. In pasture.
On upper slope of mound - upslope from large areas of bare, marly pools in calcareous fen. Top of mound has heavy Typha, Phragmites and tall shrub cover.
In middle of open, low sedge zone with frequent small areas of bare, marl-coated peat at surface. On flank of peat mound. Water table presently at ground surface.
In middle of large wetland on floating mat. Very springy. Surrounded by dense tamarack swamp. Heavy Typha invasion. No other disturbance detectable. Very remote. Continuous non-sphagnum moss cover.
Swamp with mid sized Larix and many old fallen trees. Most plants rooted in moss on tops of tree roots or logs. Frequent marshy pools between mossy areas. No stumps seen.
Mature forest on well-drained sandy soil. No evidence of recent logging or grazing.
On very buoyant, floating sedge mat. In open wetland surrounded by dense tamarack swamp. On deep, fibric peat. Occurs as small inclusions within rich fen.
On dense solid sphagnum - plot in center of wetland - in small, steep-sided basin. Very little moat on edges.
Dominated by mature open-grown Quercus macrocarpa. with thin but continuous canopy. Protected from disturbance for several decades.
Swamp in small creek valley. Canopy trees are mostly 20-30cm DBH. Heavy moss cover throughout, half of which is Sphagnum. Very moist with small pools.
Spruce-fir zone on edge of large tamarack swamp. Heavy moss cover throughout. Orchids very scarce.
In huge area of meadows on bottom lands of Leaf River. Very hummocky. Dense thatch of dead graminoid vegetation. Water table right at ground surface.
Plot in band of open fen bordered by shrub zone dominated by Betula glandulifera. Just west of tamarack swamp. In patterned peatland. Water table above ground. On fibric peat.
In extensive wet meadow along Leaf River. Plot is in open meadow between clumps of 2-4m tall Salix gracilis. Occasional Larix laricina also in area. Water table right at surface.
Large open, tree-less area, between bands of tamarack. On E edge of large tamarack swamp. Water table approx 1 ft above substrate. Very cold groundwater. Deep fibric peat with minimal decomposition.
Larix reaches 15-20cm DBH; most smaller. Much standing water between trees. mossy hummocks at bases of trees have different flora from pools between trees. Past logging. Phalaris rare here.

Swamp in Wing River Lake basin. Mosaic of several moss species present including some patches (~20% cover) of Sphagnum. Ground fairly firm. Water table below surface. Some small muck pools between roots. Abundant well-rotted deadfalls.
Floating sedge mat in channel linking South Lemmerhirt Lake with Wing River Lake. Water table just above mat surface.
Isolated spruce stand surrounded by dense tamarack swamp. In large basin that drains into Cat Creek. Heavy moss cover mostly Sphagnum. Malaxis unifolia is confined to non-Sphagnum mosses.

Level meadow in broad valley of Wing River. Water table at ground surface. Soil is black, fine-grained, calcareous peat - no marl concretions seen. Site has been hayed in past, but not last year (too much thatch).

Dentaria is more abundant here than other parts of the site. Some cut stumps in the area but these are scatted and uncommon. The presence of both Dentaria and Trillium grandiflorum is not typical for the region. This is the only site I've seen where they both occur.
The bur oaks are mostly open grown although the lower branches have long since been lost. The basswoods are multiple trunked. No signs of current disturbance.
Bur oaks are open grown, single trunked. Aspen are mostly large and straight trunked. Area is rolling with valley and ridges.

Several down trees in the area, no cut stumps or evidence of past or recent past grazing. Acquired by DNR in 1960s-part of former farm, so likely was grazed long ago. Most of canopy-single stemmed and straight trunked.
Down logs common. Sugar maple saplings filling small canopy gap. Area in ownership of DNR since 1930s. Several dead paper birch in and around plot.
Mostly single stemmed oaks-other parts of this site have small aspen clones. Oaks somewhat open grown and medium size (~30 DBH). 15cm A horizon of sand loam.
Hummocky sphagnum with small pools between hummocks. Most sphagnum is on tree roots. Area grades into upland aspen/oak community. Fair amount of down trees, rotten. Organic muck soil.
Low lying but slightly higher than the lowest area, some small pools, but mostly continuous hummocks of moss. To the south, this area becomes dominated by tamaracks. Coarse moss peat soil.

In the middle of a 5 acre poor fen in a basin surrounded by upland forest. East half has dense head high Betula glandulifera with more herbs e.g., Thelypteris palustrus., Onoclea, Potentilla palustris. Sphagnum mat is firm and stable.

Carex lasiocarpa dominates across the entire basin. Shallow depression surrounded by upland forest on sandy soil. Parts of the wetland have more abundant low-growing Betula glandulifera. Sphagnum hummocks scattered across the wetland. Soil coarse non-sphagnum peat.

Solid floating mat with hummocks of mostly non-sphagnum mosses(some sphagnum) around tree bases. Shallow pools between hummocks. A few cut stumps but mostly undisturbed. Most larger tamaracks have ~30cm DBH. Moving north, the swamp becomes dominated by balsam fir. Soil coarse peat over muck.

Floating Sphagnum mat with mounds of non-sphagnum peat. Open moat around the edge. In basin surrounded by Quercus macrocarpa woods. Mat is unstable around the edge becoming more stable in the middle. Some small dead trees scattered around, trembling aspen. Coarse peat soil.

Mostly north facing slope of a prairie complex managed by rotational grazing (~ 2 week grazing intervals) so releve site shows evidence of some preferential grazing (Stipa spartea not grazed; Boutelona curtipenda yes). Very close to large Cirsium Hillii population of more than forty plants, releve has a few basal rosettes. Litter nearly absent. Soil silty sand with small gravel.
Site is grazed on rotational basis. This area appears ungrazed this summer. Surface boulders scattered around the releve plot (granite with the occasional limestone).
Area is lightly grazed on a rotational basis. Lots of rocks and larger boulders at the surface.
On ice contact feature (kame). Not currently grazed. Very few (if any) exposed glacial erratics. Gravelly loam with coarse sand.

Inner part of large wetland surrounding open water. Moving further from the open water, towards the edge of the wetland, tamaracks become much more abundant, but they are never very tall. Entire wetland on floating mat of rich sphagnum. Coarse peat soils.

Middle zone of a large wetland basin on non sphagnum floating mat with abundant hummocks of sphagnum. Further towards the center of the wetland shrubs decrease and the community is more open rich fen surrounding a small open water lake.
Large basin with floating sedge mat surrounding small area of open water. Standing water present between tussocks of Carex prairea. Water is cold. Coarse sedge peat soil.

Area was burned this spring. Not currently grazed and has not been disturbed for several years. Scattered boulders and larger rocks. Slopes down to more degraded draw. Rolling landscape, open with little shrub or tree cover. Sandy soil with gravel and scattered boulders.

Gently rolling with shallow depressions and low rounded hills, almost flat. Land was privately owned until 1991. Lots of cut stumps. Many of the basswood are multi-stemmed. Tip-up mounds common. 20cm A horizon.

Open area (~300 square miles) surrounded by cattails. Gently sloping dome. Releve is on the side of the dome. Center of dome a small open area surrounded by a zone of willows. Center is marly (crunchy underfoot). Coarse mossy peat soil.

On top of a hill. No recent disturbance. Several down trees in the vicinity. Aspens are grouped together (which is typical of the site) while the oaks are spread throughout the site. Oaks are medium size (20-40cm DBH). Fine silty sand soil. A horizon depth 10cm.

Pin oaks are even aged and mostly medium size (20-30cm DBH). Most of them are single trunked. Some parts of the site outside the releve have more bur oak in the canopy. No current disturbance except some ATV trails.

Maturing to mature stand (trees 20-45cm DBH). Quercus rubra occasionally multi-stem. Rolling terrain east side Higgins Long Lake. Light past grazed. Much coarse woody debris. Rocky sandy-loam, thick duff layer, few earthworms. Grades more dry-mesic and dominated by Quercus ellipsoidalis, much of 1000 acre stand.

Mature stand on 30 foot, north northeast-facing slope in moderately rugged terrain southeast of Mound Lake. Trees 30-50cm DBH. Oaks mostly single-stemmed, forest-grown. Coarse woody debris sparse. Sandy-loam, few worms. Light selective logging 10-20 years ago. Light past grazing, long ago? Stand considerable more mesic than most of surrounding terrain.

Perched seep with two seepage flows, on gradual south-facing slope in rolling moraine northwest of Nellies Lake. No canopy above seep. Deep, saturated peat, raised between seepage flows. Small moss-covered coarse woody debris in plot. No stumps. Rolling wooded moraine. Organic peat soil.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Mature mesic oak on 30 foot, northeast-facing slope in rolling St. Croix Moraine southwest of Lincoln. A few acres high quality adjacent to young regeneration. Trees 35-70cm DBH. No stumps. Coarse woody debris sparse. Sandy-loam, thick duff. Few worms. Good woody structure. Quercus rubra DBH 45-60cm. Slightly smaller trees atop slope.

Center of mature, 5-acre stand in 20-acre basin in rolling St. Croix Moraine southwest of Lincoln. Trees 15-35cm DBH. Continuous sphagnum. Peat is slightly quaky. Grades outward to poor shrub fen. No stumps.

Typical of dense canopy, spruce-dominated areas of 50-acre conifer swamp in large wetland complex on sandy outwash southwest of Motley. Trees 5-20cm DBH. Continuous sphagnum. Flora more diverse where Larix occurs.

Maturing stand with occasional large trees (40-55cm DBH). 20-35cm trees are dominant. No stumps. Sparse coarse woody debris. Dark sandy-loam, rather heavy worm evidence. Mid-slope of 50 foot, northwest facing slope above Mons Lake.

One of more diverse upland forests in county. Mature stand, trees 25- 35cm DBH, occasional 45-65cm. No stumps. Several snags. Moderate coarse woody debris. Tip-up mounds. Dark, sandy-loam, few worms. Pinus strobus to 110cm. Rolling terrain northeast of Lake Beauty.

Typical of denser portions of large stand along drainage which forms headwaters of Little Swan River, northeast of Lake Beauty. Mature stand, trees 15- 30cm DBH. No stumps. Peat-wet troughs and mesic hummocks.

Typical of 150-foot wide by .5-mile long zone in drainage forming head-waters of Little Swan River, northeast of Lake Beauty. Saturated sedge peat, ice at 25cm deep. Shallow water in depressions. Grades to tamarack swamp. No sphagnum. Some areas with much more Typha.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Mature stand in fairly rugged terrain east of Coal Lake. Trees 25-55cm DBH. Good structure. No stumps. Scattered snags and coarse woody debris. Rocky sandy-loam. Gradually sloping area above steeper, 100foot, southwest-facing slope. Trees larger here than most of stand.

Mature stand, trees 25-60cm DBH, approximately 80 years, uneven-aged, forest-grown. Upper, 40-foot, northwest-facing slope-rolling moraine northeast of Bunker Lake. Coarse sandy soil. Several snags. Occasional coarse woody debris. Canopy thin. Good structure. Range of DBH 30-60cm, mode 40cm. 6cm A horizon of sandy loam.

Dry-mesic stand atop level hill in fairly rugged terrain northeast of Higgins Long Lake. Mature stand, trees 20-45cm DBH, forest-grown, many multi-stem. No stumps. Snags occasional. Dark sandy-loam with little duff layer. Many trees multi-stemmed. Canopy thin but nearly continuous. Moderate past grazed. Sparse coarse woody debris. Trees forest-grown, uneven-aged.

Typical of sedge-dominated areas in patterned fen complex in large inter drumlin wetland northeast of Clarissa. Very quaky, saturated sedge peat >45cm deep. No sphagnum. Patterning: strings of short Betula glandulifera. Brown mosses on low hummocks and elsewhere.
