Shrub-dominated zone where patterning less evident than in adjacent portions of large patterned fen complex in inter-drumlin wetland northeast of Clarissa. Plot 75m from east edge of wetland. Wet quaky peat >45cm deep. Shallow standing water.

Typical of wiregrass lawns (flarks) between strings of stunted shrubs in large patterned fen in inter-drumlin wetland northeast of Clarissa. Quaky peat >45cm deep, water 30cm deep. This flark is 60m X 40m wide between shrub "strings." No sphagnum. No hummocks.

Shrub-domianted area on margin of large patterned fen in inter-drumlin wetland northeast of Clarissa. Very quaky peat >45cm deep. Low hummocks, shallow water to 30cm deep. No sphagnum. Open wiregrass lawn to southwest. Denser and taller shrubs to north and east.

Mature stand filling much of 30-acre depression in moderately ruggged terrain northwest of Bunker Lake. Trees 15-40cm DBH. Few snags. No stumps. Sparse coarse woody debris. Peat substrate is mix of wet mossy troughs and mesic hummocks. Plot centrally located in stand. Thick needle litter on hummocks. Nice ecotonal transition to upland. Few exotics/invaders.

Typical of least wet zone in heterogeneous wetland along county road 11 south of Iona Wildlife Management Area. Slightly quaky peat >45cm deep (ice at 45cm). Vegetation somewhat patterned locally. Grades to shrubbier and more open zones. Few mosses, no sphagnum in plot. Inter-drumlin wetland.

Wettest zone of heterogeneous inter-drumlin wetland along county road 11 south of Iona Wildlife Management Area. Quaky sedge peat >45cm deep (ice at 45cm). No moss. Knee-deep water (recent heavy rains). Plot is 20m from old fence. Grades to zones of shrubs to south, and Typha to west.

Typical of shrub-domianted zone in inter-drumlin wetland along county road 11 south of Iona wildlife management area. Moderately quaky peat >45cm deep. Shallow water between hummocks. Shrubs become taller just to west. Sphagnum is common to south and west of plot.

Flark (sedge lawn) of patterned fen in large wetland complex north side of Burleene wildlife management area. Flark 25m X 100m, one of several. Strings domianted by Betula glandulifera and scattered Larix. Quaky peat >45cm deep. No sphagnum. Water 30cm deep. Grades to tamarack and shrub swamp.

String (shrub finger) of patterned rich fen in large wetland complex north side Burleene wildlife management area. String runs perpendicular to flow, north into Eagle Creek. Quaky saturated peat >45cm deep. Shallow water, raised hummocks with fine sedges occasional. Grades to tamarack swamp, wiregrass lawns.

place_name: Crow Wing R - Lois Lake Bed NE
remarks: Maturing stand on sandy outwash on terrace along Crow Wing R east of Staples. Pinus banksiana: 18-32cm DBH, appearing even-aged. Few snags. No stumps. Rather sparse coarse woody debris. Canopy heterogenous in 40 acre stand.

Central zone of 10-acre depression atop nearly level drumlin east of the Partridge River. Slightly quaky peat. Sphagnum and Polytrichum mosses carpet substrate and form 30cm high hummocks. No stumps or snags. No surface water. Grades to zone of dense young Larix and denser Chamaedaphne.

Mature stand on nearly level drumlin top east of the Partridge River. Oaks 35-60cm DBH, somewhat open-grown, especially larger trees. Canopy thin. Snags infrequent. Old stumps occasional. Rocky, sandy-loam. A few trails in stand outside plot. Rocky sandy loam soils.

Represents one of several zones in 30-acre poor fen complex atop broad drumlin east of Partridge River. Quaky floating mat, saturated peat >45cm, firmer and less wet than other zones. Continuous sphagnum, low hummocks. No stumps. Scattered small Larix snags. Grades to zone with more Carex utriculata and wetter, also to denser and taller Larix.

One of wettest of several zones in 30-acre poor fen complex atop broad drumlin east of Partridge River. Quaky peat mat, water 30cm deep. Zone is localized in 2 acre area. Continuous sphagnum. No stumps. Scattered stunted and dead Larix. No stumps.

Mature stand in inter-drumlin wetland northeast of Eagle Bend. Larix commonly 25-38cm DBH. Deep peat (>12 feet beneath nearby road). Surface water not common. Small ditch 100m to east. Snags and old stumps occasional.

Typical of 60 percent of 150-acre wetland in sandy outwash plain southwest of Motley. Grades to poor black spruce swamp in central portion of wetland. No stumps or old decaying wood. Slightly quaky peat. Plot 75m from edge of spruce stand.

Plot in 20-acre zone of 150-acre rich shrub fen and black spruce wetland on sandy outwash southwest of Motley. Continuous sphagnum, hummocks to 40cm high. Frequent coarse woody debris: fire-scarred old trunks from 1980 fire. Grades to closed canopy spruce 30m away. No stumps. Shallow water between hummocks. Slightly quaky peat. Topographic context: depression/flat.

Typical of 3-acre zone center of shallow 10-acre depression in sandy outwash southwest of Motley. Slightly quaky peat. Stunted Pinus banksiana here. Outer zone dominated by Carex utriculata. Area burned in 1980 fire. Upland is jack pine-pin oak-aspen. 6-12 inches water between hummocks which are 12-18 inches high and cover 80 percent of substrate. Continuous sphagnum carpet.

Typical of 15-acre in east end of larger wetland that is mostly dominated by alder and alder/tamarack. Slightly quaky peat >45cm deep. No stumps. Water between hummocks. Rolling, forested St. Croix moraine south east of Big Lake. Larix DBH 5-15cm.

Typical of 15 acres covering southeast arm of large Alder-dominated wetland. Wooded St. Croix Moraine. Vegetation low-statured. Several small stunted snags. No stumps. Saturated peat >45cm deep. Hummocks 30cm high. Centrally located in fen. Outer zone with taller Betula glandulifera, Alnus incana, also Carex utriculata.

Maturing stand with occasional large trees (45-60cm DBH, somewhat open-grown). Rolling St. Croix Moraine southwest of Big Lake. Fine sandy-loam. Root mounds occasional. Snags occasional. Old stumps rare. Sparse coarse woody debris. Much of stand lower quality. Patches of aspen are frequent. Stand overall is C rank.

Mature stand. Moderately steep, 130 feet, upper east-facing slope of morainal ridge west of Mons Lake. Trees forest-grown, 30-55cm DBH, mode 43cm. Sandy-loam. Occasional boulders, coarse woody debris, snags, and old stumps. Earthworms common. Grades to areas dominated by patches of Populus.

Mature stand on slight mid-slope terrace on 100 foot east facing slope of morainal ridge northwest of Mons Lake. Trees 25-50cm DBH, mode 38cm. Snags and coarse woody debris occasional. Few stumps. Uncompacted loamy soil with many earthworms. Plot includes portions of slope above and below terrace.

2-acre+ wetland basin in rugged forested moraine south of Mound Lake. Organic muck 15cm deep over mineral soil. Substrate saturated but no surface water despite very wet summer. No Phalaris or other exotics.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: 60-80 year old stand in nearly level area atop steep-sided, 100 foot knoll in strongly-rolling St. Croix moraine east of Rice Lake. Rather even-aged, trees 30-40cm DBH. No stumps. Few snags. Moderate coarse woody debris. Sandy-loam, thick litter layer. Adjacent north-facing slope with much erosion. ATV trail near plot.

Central portion of 8-acre basin in forested moraine east of Rice Lake. Moderately quaky peat, no surface water. Fen heterogenous-some zones domianted by Carex lacustris, some zones with more Chamaedaphne-some with much less.

60-80 years old. Gentle southwest-facing slope on moraine north of Mound Lake. Red oak often multi-stemmed, 25-40cm DBH, rather even-aged. Few snags. Moderate coarse woody debris. Stumps rare. Grades to areas dominated by Populus grandidentat or Acer saccharum. Sandy-loam. Down slope from small wet meadow.

Very quaky floating mat forms 10-30m wide zone around 3 acres of open water, plot 3m from water. Sandy outwash southeast of Staples. Brown mosses carpet substrate. Water knee-deep in plot. Grades to unusual poor tamarack swamp. Grades to dense tamarack.

Center of mature, 60-acre stand in inter-drumlin wetland east of Bertha. Larix: 15-30cm DBH, mode 20cm. No stumps. Scattered windfall. Sphagnum hummocks cover much of peat substrate. No standing water.

Typical of broad zone adjacent to 40-acre tamarack stand in inter-drumlin wetland east of Bertha. Moderately quaky peat >45cm. Zone is homogeneous 10+ acres. No stumps or snags. Larix denser and taller to west.

Broad zone of sparse small tamarack on north side of Mud Lake. Center of 150m wide quaky mat. 40m from dense, mature tamarack. Peat >45cm deep. No stumps, snags, or decaying wood. Sandy outwash south of Motley. Topographic context: depression/flat.

Mature stand on drumlin between Jacobson Lake and Moran Creek southwest of Staples. Trees 25-50cm DBH, mode 38cm. No stumps, few snags. Moderate coarse woody debris. Rocky, silty-loam, with tip-up mounds. Occasional red/pin oak hybrids.

Center of 10-acre inter-drumlin wetland southwest of Jacobson Lake. Typifies 70% of wetland. Outer zone is 20-30m wide and captured by Releve 8995. Quaky peat >100cm deep, some decayed wood-formerly Larix? Shrubs rather low-statured.

Very decomposed sedge peat >1m deep. 20-30m wide meadow zone surrounds poor fen (releve 8994). Tall sedge hummocks. Inter-drumlin wetland southwest of Jacobson Lake. (with R. Dana, N. Aaseng, D. Wovcha, E. Rowe.

Mature stand. Localized area of sugar maple on gradual, lower, 10 foot, northeast-facing slope; rolling moraine southeast of Stump Lake. Loamy soil, non-compacted. No worms. Adjacent to ephemeral stream. No stumps. Few snags. Moderate coarse woody debris. Duff layer intact. Inclusion in larger patch of mesic to dry-mesic hardwoods (oak).

Typical of 10-acre depression in rolling moraine southeast of Thunder Lake. Larix to 30cm DBH, Pinus strobus to 35cm. Sphagnum forms hummocks. Peat saturated peat. Few snags. No stumps. Sparse coarse woody debris. Grades to zone of shorter trees, more open with abundant Carex lasiocarpa and limosa.

Combined releve data from May 5th and July 7th (see Nancy for details) Near bottom of north-slope. Seedlings-oak, maple, basswood, Prunus. Dwarf trout lily colony site. Soil is sandy loam. Sparse ground layer.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: +/- thin deciduous leaf duff. Moderate coarse woody debris. Within-plot relief from well-rotted logs. +/- open maple basswood forest with few red oak in supercanopy and rare to occasional paper and yellow birch in canopy. Soil: 2.5 inches organic over 11 inches light tan silt/fine sand with pebbles. Stand #15.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Shallow deciduous leaf duff. Within plot relief from well-decayed logs, old tip-ups. Moderate coarse woody debris. 3" organic over tan silt.

Example of the ambient pervasive, ubiquitous woods in this part of the county. Nothing spectacular as to the type or quality. Fraxinus nigra and Viburnum trilobum is small plowage on northwest side of plot.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Very heterogeneous. Typed as ash, but not dominated by it. Large canopy trees are mix of bur oak, basswood, silver maple, green ash and rarely black ash. Soil: muck in low areas and fine silty loam on rises. Substrate: heavy, grey silt with clay. Muck in low laying areas, A horizon: ten cm of fine silty loam over grey silt with clay. Undulating topography.

Northwest quadrent of study area. Northern hardwoods forest on moist, level terrace of Swarta Plain. Shaded moist soil. Natural drainage may have been disrupted by ash pond on eastern edge of stand. Soil: 2-11cm moist black loam rich in organic matter, 16-56cm moist brown silty loam.

Southwest quadrant of study area. Pathology plot releve on 20 degree, south facing, moderately drained slope on edge of ash pond. Sunny to densely shaded. Soil: 0-12cm moist dark brown sandy clay; 12-24 cm moist black loam; 24-30cm moist dark grey loam; 30-67cm dry to moist sandy clay.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Typical of narrow zone of fluted shallow channels along this area of St. Croix River with mixed tree canopy with a diversity of size classes. Much course woody debris.

Rolling topography. Typical mesic deciduous forest, but releve shows better than average diversity. Sparse shrub layer. Panax quinquefolia nearby. Fraxinus = F. pennsylvanica with some F. cf americana.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Rolling topography. Plot near crest; large, frequent, old tip-up mounds/pits up to 2x5m. Little or no coarse woody debris. Canopy with typical narrow crowns, but here lacks Acer subcanopy.

Rolling terrain. Irregular microtopography from many tip-up pits/mounds. No large course woody debris. Much bare ground below herbs; leaf litter sparse unclear why. Loamy soil to 20 cm then hardpan. Boulders.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Topography is not smoothly rounded; plot on irregular crest. Microtopogy relief is slight. Trees seem to snap if damaged, not tip. No cut stumps. Unclear why D4-5 is sparse and sapling at 2m is dense.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Mesic forest on gently rolling terrain. Much shallow microtopogy (tip-up mounds/pits). Old pine stumps. No coarse debris. Frost cracks on trees. Leaf litter dense though not thick. No white pine or yellow birch.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Plot is 10m from St. Croix and 1-3m above water level on low ridged terrain (old levees/channels) on sand. Very thin organic layer. Thicker organic (over silt) in lows. Some piles of flood debris. Lowland hardwood on rises. Litted down wood, no snags. Acer all multi-stemmed, average stem DBH = 25-35cm.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Plot is 8-10m east of river edge under larger silver maples on peninsula (Average 35-40cm DBH; range 25-50). Relatively diverse compared to low spots with large clumps of Carex lupulina and Carex tuckermanii, or areas that flood. Soil: red/brown silty sand.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Eastcentral Bedrock)
remarks: Dry pine woodland on thin soil over large, irregular blocks of bedrock at base of gentle 6-degree slope. Red pine in 2 sizes: 40-46cm DBH (max=55, OP) others 15-20cm DBH. Deciduous all <15cm. Charcoal on old stumps.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Eastcentral Bedrock)
remarks: 10x40m plot on sandstone ledge between 8m cliff and toe of northwest-facing slope; thin soil. Red pines 20-35cm DBH. Fire scars on decayed stumps. This vegetation type is rare. Below cliff: moister. Upslope: dry mixed forest.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: 10x40m plot along seepage stream bordered by 2m high rock walls. Water emerges from sandstone ledge by plot; sandy bottom, good flow. Up channel, water is stagnant. Trees slender 15-25cm DBH; max 40cm DBH.

On east facing mesic talus slope 5m above Wolf Creek. Thin soil on large mossy blocks of sandstone. Canopy trees 10-25cm DBH, a few 30cm. Slope varies from 25-35 degrees. Topographic context: middle/lower.
Plot in small 20x40m opening in oak-pine woodland on solid bedrock surface with little to no soil except at edges/low spots. Rare.

80 acre shrubby meadow/rich fen on south side of large bog mat. Litter cover 10% lying on hummocks and over wet pools (5-10cm deep). Some dead wood. Other zones more open Spha-erioph with less Typha or woodies.

Plot at water edge, slightly quaking, firm except for small channels with water, Utricularia intermedia and muck. Only one species of Sphagnum. Not much litter this year (still green); looks vigorous. Grades into Carex rostra.

Walked southeast from canoe at open-water channel to releve site: from poor fen to progressively taller, coarser, more forb and alder rich area along the narrow 8-10m wide shrubby channel. Saw 1 orchid.

Plot at northeast edge of upland forest. 20m from black ash margin of large spruce swamp. Low lying, much microtopogy, tip-up mounds, occasional cobbles, occasional pine? Stumps. Upslope more red oak in canopy and less diverse.
Plot on crest of large old dune (or sand capped hill?). Dry crests have better sand prairie character; lower areas dominated by Poa. Site history uncertain: past grazed/cultivated?
Plot on flat, former lake bed of Little Rock Lake. Site history unknown - past cultivation or grazing?
Overgrown dry oak savanna is located at the edge of cultivated field on slopes down to wetland. Releve in 30x30m opening along old fence-line. Formally grazed. A few gopher mounds. Spp list 9519.

Formerly a dry sand/gravel savanna, but tree removal and digging long ago to create river crossing led to barrens aspect. Few native species here. Linaria cana present. Ground: 8% bare, <1% lichen, 20% Selaginella.
Went in to this wet meadow looking for wet prairie. None. Uniform throughout except >75% cover Salix grac in one half. Grazing-increasers are not freq. Maybe missed some graminoids; late season.

Extremely rare remnant of dry prairie on Mississippi River north of St. Cloud. Plot on steep bluff; 2 acre praire on topland also. Fewer native species than sites in Sherbourne County. Soil slumps/animal burrows/many weed.

Formerly grazed/disturbed rock outcrops with old piles of farm rubbish. Generally dominated by aggressive weeds but also many natives and lovely 5-12m tall open-grown Quercus macrocarpa. Vegetative cover in plot approximately 80%.

Example of disturbed mesic forest. Dominated by multi-stem Tilia; lacks sub-canopy and woody seedlings. Laportea abundant throughout. Plot in relatively diverse area. No down logs or snags. Little microtopography.
Releve converted from plot data. Black spruce: 140 yrs old, 17.5m, 8-14cm DBH. Peat 1.4m. pH=5.6.
Releve converted from plot data. Small peatland between Hay and Dinner Creek.
Releve converted from plot data pH=4.1
Releve converted from plot data. Appears to be off main portion of raised bog, probably transition with swamp forest. X-mas cutting lane on topography.
Releve converted from plot data. Directly downslope from a burned jack pine stand. 68 years old. pH 4.7.
Releve converted from plot data. 5 miles east of Big Fork River. At toe of large raised bog.
Releve converted from plot data. East side of Red Lake between ridges. 54 years old. 1.1 m
Releve converted from plot data
Releve converted from plot data. 95 years.
Releve converted from plot data
Releve converted from plot data.
Releve converted from plot data
Releve converted from plot data. Located at edge of peatland near Lake of Woods.
Releve converted from plot data. Peatland at base of "beach" ridge complex.
Releve converted from plot data. Small peatland at base of "beach" ridge. 84 years. pH 6.5.
Releve converted from plot data. pH = 5.6.
Gramminoids and forbs about equal in co-dominance. Slope between burned aspen and Thypha/Phragmites.

Similar to jack pine forest sampled north of this site. Numerous jack pine seedlings from human intervention and opening of canopy. Some prairie species present but needs burn. Fine yellow-brown sand, slightly dark in upper 10cm. This litter layer of primarily needles. Paper birch canopy trees cored, 24cm DBH - 43 years; 35cm DBH - 49 years; 19cm DBH - 36 years; 25cm DBH - 42 years.
Immediately adjacent to and south of small stream level to slopes of 20 degrees by stream. Grades southward into aspen stand. Much dead and down.

Mature red pine with basswood in subcanopy. Selectively logged 5-15 years ago with many well-decayed cut stumps of medium to small. Sub-canopy of hardwood species (from 3-10cm DBH) likely generated after logging. Stand possibly planted. Three cored red pines, 43cm DBH - 83 years; 50cm DBH - 85  years; 37cm DBH - 89 years. Soil: 1 inch pine needle litter over 2 cm of dark soil with organic matter (A horizon), over 30cm of medium grain sandy, over 20 cm of medium grain very loose sand; stopped by roots or rocks.

Gently rolling topography, sandy soil-fen bare exposed sand spots. Many dense packets of shrubs dominated by oak corpses, grades to oak woodland-brushland to northeast, several snags present. Pin oaks fairly large, bur oaks small. Breeding bird point count location.
4 mile south of Pine Bend graveyard, east side of road. One of few remaining uncut remnants of apparently natural, old stands. Releve in area with fairly broken canopy.
Very homogeneous, undiverse area that shows on photo as northwest smooth grey area. Open.
Only the best timber was removed from parcel 33(9), so a few large oaks remain. Maple and ironwood have become the principle regenerators in the parcel since logging ended in 1958.
1979 intern survey that is not considered 100% reliable. In permanent plot HA-1 in NE corner of preserve. Resurveyed by Bob Steinauer et al in 1988 (See releve 5687).

Scattered ant and gopher mounds. Burned frequently for the past 25 years. Releve located on level top of dune hill small mounds. Resurvey of 1979 intern study (see DNRrel#7080). (TNC) macroplot code = USMNSSALIS01.02. NE corner of plot is 43m S & 52m W of NE corner of preserve. 3/4" galv conduit at 4 plot corners & NE conduit marked with aluminum tag #617.
Foldahl Cemetery Prairie, the unmown rear part. Only slightly larger than a releve. Majority of remnant mowed - still priarie. Only dry prairie on beach ridge in county.

Dry upland site, hilly and uneven. Few burned pine stumps. Betula papyrifera 60 years. 1 inch litter of leaves and twigs. Soil: 4 inches light brown sandy loam with much organic matter over 2 inches tan colored sandy loam over reddish light brown loamy fine sand, containing many rock fragments.

47 year old stand. Thin litter of leaves and twigs. Soil: 5 inches dark brown loamy sand with much organic matter over 1 inch grey fine sand over reddish brown fine sand containing many rock fragments. Dry soil, many fibrous roots in A horizon, larger ones scattered throughout the A and B horizons.

Medium moist site on slight slope in rolling terrain. Basswood 122 years. Spares litter of leaves, grass, and twigs. 6 inches dark brown loam over 3 inches brown sandy clay loam over reddish brown sand, containing a litter clay and a few rocks. Roots throughout the A and B horizon.

27 year old aspen stand in middle of low terrain. Moist site. No disturbance. Sparse litter of leaves and twigs. Soil: 1 inch black sandy loam with concentrated roots over 2 inches grey loamy fine sand over reddish brown clayey medium sand with sparse gravel.

Dry upland site in rolling topography. 60 year old red oak. Thick mat of leaves and twigs - 2" thick. No disturbance. Soil: 3 inches black loam containing a large amount of organic matter over 5 inches light greyish brown loamy sand over reddish brown sand containing very few rock fragments. Root distributed throughout the A and upper B horizons - fairly thick.

68 year old oak. Several large pine stumps present. Scarce and well incorporated litter layer. Soil: 3 inches dark brownish black loamy clay over two inches dark brown clay over reddish brown pure clay. Very dry site.

Aspen 28 years in rolling topography. Several dead and down aspen. No evidence of fire and logging. Soil: 3 inches dark brown sandy loam over 2 inches brown sandy clay loam over light reddish brown sandy clay with rock fragments. Thin litter layer of dead grass, leaves, and twigs.

Unevenly level site; ridged-giving appearance of plantation. Water from recent rain collected in low spots. Stand 32 years. One fourth inch litter of mostly pine needles. Soil: brown coarse sand on top of sandy gravel, many large rocks. Gravel at a depth of 6 inches mixed with sand. Very dry soil.
36 years old aspen stand on flat site with slight depressions. Many logged aspen stumps, show signs of fire. Soil: fine sandy loam, thin litter.

Level ridge top with broken topography on bedrock. Many dry outcrops with wet depressions. Aspen in depressions have rotten centers. Succession is heading toward maple. Soil: dark brown sandy loam. Litter layer a quarter of an inch thick with patches of moss.

Upland site in gently rolling area. Dry site with healthy jack pine. Understory has much grass and moss with sporadic patches of hazel. No jack pine reproduction. Half inch thick litter of needles, grass and moss. Soil: 5 inches black fine sandy loam over brown sand.

58 year old stand on medium dry site. Pine stumps nearby. Soil: 5" fine sandy loam; 1" fine sand-fairly rocky. Reproduction: aspen, sugar maple, and Abies. Birch declining. Thin, well decomposed litter of leaves and twigs. Soil: 5 inches fine sandy loam over 1 inch grey loamy fine sand over reddish brown loamy sand, fairly rocks; roots throughout.

Populus tremuloides - 35 years old. Several white pine stumps. Very small wood lot/shelter belt. Moderately dry site. Soil: 3 inches black loamy mull over 2 inches dark brown sandy clay loam over reddish brown sandy loam, with many small rocks. Many fibrous roots in A and upper b horizon. Thin litter of grass and leaves, incorporated into upper A horizon organic matter.
32 year old stand. No site disturbance. Thin litter of mostly leaves. Soil: 8 inches sandy loam over light brown fine loamy sand, rocky soil throughout. Water table very shallow.

Paper birch 50 years. Populus grandidentata 73 years. Few fire scarred pine stumps. Rolling topography. Thin litter layer of twigs and mostly leaves. Soil: 3 inches black loamy sand over 10 inches reddish brown loamy sand with pockets of black loamy sand over light reddish brown gravelly sand. Mandy roots throughout A horizon.

Lowland site. No disturbance. Thin litter layer of leaves, twigs, and ferns. Soil: 6 inches of dark brown clayey loam over 2 inches brown sandy clay loam over reddish brown loamy sand with much gravel. Medium wet soil. Many roots in A horizon.

Betula papyrifera 66 years old. No disturbance. Depression in plot holds water from recent rain. Birch production from stumps only. Thin litter layer of leaves and twigs. Soil: 8 inches dark brown sandy loam over loamy sand with much rock and gravel at 10 inches.

Lowland site in fairly low and flat area. Very moist site. Very healthy cedar stand. No hazel and braken. 1 inch litter layer, but variable thickness; composed of needles and twigs. Soil: Organic peat with water table at 6 inches; contains many chunks of decaying wood and dense roots in the upper few inches. Very wet soil.

Extremely wet lowland site in rolling area. Flat site. Very healthy black spruce stand in a boggy area. 3-4 inch layer of sphagnum moss on top of an undifferentiated peat soil. Water table at 6 inches depth. Extremely wet soil. Roots not very dense.

Fairly healthy pure aspen stand in lowland of rolling terrain. Medium moist site. No signs of past disturbance. Very thin litter layer composed of leaves and grass. Soil: 5 inches black loam over 6 inches greying fine loamy sand over 19 inches grey very fine sand/silt over reddish brown sandy clay containing many rock fragments. Medium moist soil, numerous roots in A horizon.

Rolling terrain. Fire scarred pine stumps. 70 year old pop. grand. 50 years old Betula papyrifera. One fourth inch think litter layer composed of leaves and small twigs. Soil: 4 inches black loam over 2 inches dark brown loam over brown sandy loam with much gravel, rock at 18 inches. Medium dry soil, dense roots in A horizon.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: 82 years old. Sloping upland in hilly area. Medium dry site. Maple reproduction is very thick, very little hazel. No braken fern. One fourth inch litter layer composed of leaves and twigs. Soil: 6 inches dark brown to black loam over 2 inches light brown loam over light brown sandy loam with much gravel. Gravel and large rock stop probe at 15 inches. Medium dry soil.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Upland site in rolling terrain. Medium moist. Very tight crown cover and only a small amount of understory vegetation. Several large white pine stumps around the plot, some have large birch trees growing on top of them. Medium healthy maple-basswood stand. Reproduction mostly sugar maple and covers 50% of the plot. One quarter in litter layer composed on leaves and twigs. Many fibrous roots in upper 3 inches of soil. Several small rocks in band C horizons.

Upland site in the midst of an extensive low area - medium moist. One fourth inch litter composed of leaves, grass, and twigs. Soil: 5 inches dark brown loam over 6 inches light greyish brown silt over reddish grey brown pure clay grading into sandy clay. Dense fibrous roots in A horizon, small stones numbers at 3.5 feet down. Medium moist soil.

Upland site in gentle rolling area. Young aspen in fair to poor health medium moist site. One fourth inch litter composed of grass and twigs. Soil: 4 inches dark brown clayey loam over 2 inches light brown loamy clay over 10 inches light brown fine sandy clay over reddish brown gravelly sand.

Lowland site in gently rolling area. Poor aspen stand. Medium moist site - wet part of the year. Many large moss covered rocks on and around the plot. Many small dead trees, creating much slash. No signs of past disturbance. Reproduction is quaking aspen and some balsam poplar. About one half inch litter of twigs, sticks, grass, and a few leaves. Soil: 5 inches dark brown loamy clay containing many roots over 18 inches light reddish brown sandy loam over brown sandy loam; rocks scattered throughout.

Stand cut 20-40 years ago; fairly open, look drier site. Side of small ridge, gently rolling area. Aspen not vigorous; old ski trail 5' wide on east side of plot. Soil good example of Duluth (504) in all characteristics - quite moist. 87% litter cover, 2% moss cover, 1% rock cover, 2% bare ground, 3% grass cover, and 5% slash.
2 story stand. Soil: fine sandy loam over light olive brown loam. Thick solom. 2% rock cover, 10% slash, 86% litter, and 2% grass.

Jack Pine 58-77 years (?). Upland site in rolling area, medium to very dry. No sign of past disturbance. Much Abies reproduction. 1 inch litter layer of needles and twigs. Soil: 2 inches dark brown loamy sand over 4 inches brown sand over light reddish brown sand. No rocks present. Roots throughout the A and upper B horizons.

Very wet lowland site in fairly flat area. No signs of past fire or other disturbance. No bracken fern or hazel. Very thin litter layer and quickly incorporated into the upper soil. Soil: 5 inches black clayey organic matter over brown loamy clay with much organic matter. Water table at 8 inches down.

Upland site in hilly area-almost pure birch. Medium dry.  No sign of past disturbance. Half inch litter layer composed of stems, twigs, and leaves. Soil: 4 inches dark brown sandy loam over 2 inches brown sandy loam containing many rock fragments, over reddish brown sandy loam containing 25% rock fragments and many large rocks. Medium dry soil. Roots distributed throughout the A and upper B horizons.

Lowland site in fairly level area. Poor aspen stand with some clumps of paper birch. Many large canopy openings. One fourth inch litter layer composed of leaves and twigs. Soil: 4 inches dark brown loam over 2 inches dark brown sandy loam over reddish brown sandy loam with slight gravel. Roots mostly in upper layers of soil, well distributed and dense. Above average moisture.

Plot 29 years old. Appears undisturbed. Soil: 15 cm gray loamy sand cap over  reddish brown loamy sand and 25cm over sandy loam at 30cm. Course fragments. 80% plot has mounds. 96% litter cover, 2% grass cover, 1% rock cover, and 1% slash.
Stand 27 years old. Appears damp, shrubs patchy. Soil: 510(Amcek) with Royce.

Medium moist site in rolling terrain. 50 year old Sugar maple. Half inch litter layer composed of leaves, grass, and twigs. Soil: 4 inches black sandy loam over 3 inches grey loamy sand over reddish brown sandy loam. Medium moist soil. Roots numerous throughout A and upper B.

Lowland site in rolling topography. Basswood 114 years old and sugar maple 76 yrs, (64 cm DBH). Rock at surface. Thin litter layer made up of leaves and twigs. Soil: 1 inch black sandy loam filled with fibrous root systems over 3 inches grey fine sand over light brown fine sandy loam.
This area would respond beautifully to fire.
Grades into area completely dominated by Spartina, although fair amount Poa distribution of natives is good-would respond well to fire (better than Mentor Ranch "comparable" areas).
On "island" of mesic prairie visable in rich fen on photo NAPP 3084-129.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: 10% fallen logs - some in advanced stages of decay. +/- thin layer of deciduous leaf duff. Abundant Carex pensylvanica. Stand #3. Soil: 3" organic over 8" silt, fine light tan sand. Loon lake candidate.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Within plot relief from old tip-ups and well decayed logs. Thick decd. leaf duff 5-10% of plot with coarse woody debris +/- open stand; 1-2 m layer nearly absent. Stand 1.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: ~10% coarse woody debris. +/- thick deciduous leaf duff. Stand 5. 1" organic over 6" light grey-brown silt and fine sand.
Releve established to document goat prairie vegetation prior to being managed/burned. South and east edges have sumac encroaching.
Plot lies mainly on flat top and down south-facing slope.

Old growth northern hardwoods on east/southeast facing slope. More yellow birch regeneration observed in this stand than usual. Selective logging for yellow birch and pine. Yellow birch was once co-dominant in this wet mesic forest.
Large treed cedar swamp stand with more or less continuous bryophyte cover, including Sphagnum clones. No open water at this time, but pits dug filled quickly.

Small uncut area in selectively-logged stand. Rollin terrain east side of Little Birch Lake. Trees 25-40cm DBH. Tip-up mounds frequent. Few snags. Soil: Brown sandy-loam, 2" organic layer, small rocks, surface boulders occasional. Some smaller coarse woody debris. Selectively logged most of stand 3-5 years ago.

Maturing stand surrounded by wetland and development in southwest side of St. Cloud. Trees straight boles 15-30cm DBH, often multi-stemmed. Few snags. Little coarse woody debris. Well-drained dark sandy loam with small rocks.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Mature stand canopy trees to 70 cm DBH, bimodal 50-70cm and 30-35cm. Uneven aged. No past grazing and very selective logging according to owner-in family since settlement. Gently rolling terrain. Rich black loam. Frequent snags. Much coarse woody debris. No stumps.

Northern hardwoods and surrounding tower, recently clear cut. Private land to east of tower has been used as sugar brush. Continuous maple canopy. Very few yellow birch trees this far north. Ground layer: herbaceous-45%, deadfall-5%, litter-50%.
Dry prairie vegetation on excessively drained gravelly soils, glacial stores at the surface, vegetation undisturbed.
Clay loam soil.
Numerous stumps result of beaver dams. Wetter area down slope with more Carex lacustris. Soil: 15 cm of muck over clayey sand to sandy clay.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Old growth pine with canopy gaps and much coarse woody debris. 2cm of duff with much pine litter. No fire scars on trees. Large DBH old growth stand with large gaps, good for white pine regeneration.

Bedrock ridge with scrub oak forest along slope. Plot barely fits. Soil: Bedrock with some silty loam in cracks. Represents oak end of scrub conifer woodland type. On very steep slope, plot adjacent to woodland.
White cedar stand in black ash swamp between upland and black spruce bog. Hemic peat > 1m. pH = 6.7, spec. cond = 82, absorb. =.600.
Strip of tamarack between alder swamp and leatherleaf bog. Peat > 1m. Hemic, with a small upper cap of fibric peat. pH= 4.1; spec. cond. =30 Absorb = 0.720.
Releve represents pine bedrock outcrops in a matrix of aspen forest (complex). ~4 degree slope on shoulder of crest. Up to 4cm of silty loam over bedrock.
Taller jack pine, red pine, white pine surrounding plot. Greenstone bedrock ridge.
Small stand near wetland and lake. Much down jack pine. Soil average 8 cm (3-24cm) silt loam over bedrock (schist). Occasional holes in the canopy.
Located adjacent to cattail mat at edge of lake. Drainage running through plot with open water (Potamogeton, Utricularia). Floating mat= 50 cm deep.
Occasional black ash. Very unhealthy looking-dead tops; succeeding toward shrub swamp. More black ash along margins of the wetland.
Most tamarack 8m, a few up to 20m. Fibic peat 64cm over dense gleyed clay.
Stand also contains large openings in jack pine cover with oak remaining and more junipers. Along ridge adjacent to Rainy Lake. Soil: average 8cm, silt loam.
Equisetum fluviatile very abundant but makes up little cover, perhaps under represented by the cover value. Water depth 6-8 in standing. Fibric peat >1m. Layer of sphagnum between sedge peat.

Surrounded by steep ledges of schist. Some minerotrophic indicators (Alder) at margin of basin. Hummock/hollow complex well developed. margins of peatland with half meter of peat over silty loam with coarse sand. Center of peatland with much deeper peat(probably site of old pond). Site saturated. Peat > 1m. pH= 4.3; Sp. cond.= 32; Absorb.= .980.
Openings common in stand and dominated by Alnus. Hummock hollow complex fairly well developed. Standing water in hollows common. Many deep holes. Sapric peat >1m. pH = 4.3, S.C=27, Abs.=.610
Hummock/hollow complex highly developed. Fibric peat >1m. Grades into cattails toward lake edge; more shrubs inland.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Stand relatively small, surrounded by +/- upland aspen and L.B. 5cm high on silt loam over heavy clay. Redoximorphic features present at 8cm in clay indicating fluctuating water table near surface. Many wet aspen typed stands in area are mostly upland aspen with pockets of wet areas. Ash looks like green ash, one possible black seedling found.
Stand located along Rat Root River. Typha rooted in substrate in 3 feet of water.
Water 1-1.5 m deep. Stand just south of Skunk Island in East Black Bay. Bulrush dense, but canoeable.
Water 1-1.5 m deep. Much of surface of water covered with dead Zizania leaves. Located just east of Skunk Island in Black Bay. Wild rice marsh.

Stand contains areas of dense Abies and areas of bedrock colonized by moss and lichens. Inclusions of more dense aspen also present. Soil: 0- 25cm, 25-30cm sandy loam over bedrock. Spruce budworm damage to many Abies trees.

Soil: 3 inches black sandy loam over 1.5 inches thick sandy clay over reddish brown sandy loam down to 1.5 meters. Very little reproduction, one red maple and a few aspen. Medium moist site, sandy level sandy upland. Originated from disturbance - fire? Very sloe to a wet area. 90 year old branchy red pine.

Many stumps indicate red pine logged and birch was left (48-62 years), birch and aspen have filled in. Soil: medium textured sand with slight amount of loam; pebbles increase >2.5 feet. Very thin litter layer.

No evidence of disturbance but 60 yards from road ditch. Soil 4" moss; 2" decomposed peat over loamy clay. Fat boggy area - much sphagnum moss, very wet. History: no evidence of logging, fire, or other disturbances. Very healthy looking, reproduction by layering in black spruce.

83 year old red and white pine in rough rocky rugged site over-looking St. Louis River. A few pine stumps present. Half inch litter layer. Soil: 5 in of dark brown loam on bedrock and containing concentration of roots. Many rock outcrops present.

Populus grandidentata 53 years. Hill top rising out of flat plain. Dry site, but water in depressions from recent rain. Probably small woodlot. Fourth inch litter of grass and leaves. Soil: 3 inches dark brown loam containing much organic matter over 3 inches brown clay loam over reddish brown clay loam with many large rocks.

Level area on top of hill. Stand of over mature(?) aspen, but 40 years old? No apparent signs of past disturbance. Secession is headed toward a maple-oak stand, very litter aspen reproduction. Very thick hazel understory - up to 10 feet. Fourth inch litter of mostly leaves and a few twigs. Soil: 2 inches dark brown sandy clay loam with many roots over 2 inches light reddish brown sandy clay loam; slightly rocky.

Red pine=62 years, Jack pine=49 years old. Uneven in gently rolling terrain. Site is dry. Very little pine reproduction, balsam fir and white spruce are reproducing well and will take over the stand. Corylus cornuta is think, up to 8 feet high and completely defoliated by tent caterpillars. 2 inch thick pine needle litter. Soil: 2 inches light brown loamy sand over 4 inches mottled dark and light brown color over reddish brown loamy sand with numerous rock fragments.

55 year old stand. One inch thick needle cover. Many pine stumps. Probably heavily managed. Moving toward white spruce, balsam fir, and paper birch. Very little red pine reproduction. Slightly sloping site in fairly level topography. Hazel is moderate density and up to seven feet high. Stand of puree red pine. Soil: 3 inches dark brown loamy sand over reddish brown sand.

32 year old aspen stand in hilly area. Site near wet depression. Many pine stumps. A few decayed pine logs and many dead aspen. A large amount of slash on the ground. Reproduction is scarce and mostly in the form of aspen, balsam fir and american elm. One fourth inch litter layer of mostly leaves and a few twigs. Soil: 2" brownish black loamy sand over 2" grey fine sand over brown sand with a few small rock fragments. Roots spread evenly throughout A horizon.

33 year old aspen stand. Medium dry site with many rocks and rock outcrops. Many pine stumps present that are baddly scorches. Fairly flat site in flat area, uneven due to the presence of rocks. Much middle ages aspen, not in good shape. many dead standing and down aspen. Reproduction is mainly red oak and trembling aspen. Fourth inch litter of leaves and twigs. Soil: 6-8" of dark brown clay loam over bedrock. Many roots concentrated into top soil and evenly distributed.

Flat site in bottomlands near lake, moist site. Largely sugar maple over story with a little ash, basswood, and birch mized in. Reproduction is mostly by sugar maple; but also balsam fir, red oak, ash, and basswood. many large, well rotted, fire scorches white pine stumps are present. Most maples are rotten in the center. Almost no hazel. Very thin litter of leaves and twigs. Soil: 4 inches dark brown to black fine sandy clay loam over 3 inches brown clayey fine sandy loam over reddish brown loamy fine sand with little clay. Very few rocks.

Flat moist site in level lowland terrain. Moist ground surface, but no standing water in low pockets after much fairly recent rain. Reproduction is mostly balsam poplar and black ash. A few well decomposed logs and stumps but no sign of past disturbance. Wet site, no hazel or bracken fern. Half inch thick litter composed of wood, bark, leaves, and grass. Soil: 3 inches dark brown loam with much organic matter and many large root over 3 inches black loam with many fibrous roots over light brown clayish loamy sand with a few roots. Moist soil but no sign of water table at one foot.

Basswood 71 years. Sugar maple 48 years. Uneven but unsloping site in level terrain. A few large rocks distributed throughout the plot. Two 25cm DBH sugar maple logs hollow and well rotted. One cut sugar maple stump and two burned pine sumps. some maples with fire scars. Little hazel and up to 4 feet high. Almost no bracken fern. Medium moist site. Reproduction numerous and mixed between sugar maple, basswood, balsam fir, red oak, and ash. Thin litter layer quickly incorporated into A horizon, composed of leaves and grass. Soil: 4 inches dark brown crumb mull, loam over 3 inches dark brown fine sandy loam over rock brown fine sandy loam.

18 year old aspen. Level lowland site, moist. Composed of dense very young aspen, a few rotted cut aspen logs and stumps. Many dead standing aspen of all ages. Reproduction is scarce - mainly green ash. Moist site. Haze is not very dense, up to 5 feet high. Almost no bracken fern present. Gently rolling topography. Thin litter of leaves, sticks and grass. Soil: 3 inches black loam containing much organic matter over 2 inches grey sandy loam over reddish brown clayey sand. Roots throughout A horizon, no rocks.

Slightly sloping site in gently rolling area. Thick mat of pine needles on floor. Medium dry site. A few rotten pine stumps present. No sign of fire scars. Reproduction is mainly white pine, balsam fir, and paper birch. Hazels and brackens both medium dense. Three fourths inch litter of pine needles on top of mineral soil. Soil: 2 inches sandy loam containing much organic matter over 2 inches brown loamy sand over light brown sand with a few small rock fragments.

Level lowland site in hilly terrain. Overstory is 90% defoliated by caterpillars. Many dead and dying trees. Aspen 34 years. Fairly dry site surrounded by several, low pockets. Reproduction scarce, mostly aspen and balsam fir. Hazel thick, up to 7 feet. Very thin litter layer of twigs and grass. Soil: 6 inches dark brown to black sandy loam over 3 inches light brown sand over reddish brown clayey sand over clay. Water table at two and a half feet, roots evenly distributed down to water table.

Level upland in hilly area, very moist. No disturbance. Populus balsimifera = 51 years old. Floor with dense needle cover and some moss. Regeneration composed mainly of spruce, balsam fir, and a little balsam poplar. No hazel and no bracken fern. 1/5 inch litter layer composed of twigs, needles, and leaves. Soil: 2 inches black sandy clay loam over 2 inches grey loamy clay sand over 4 inches browning clayey sand containing pockets of clay. Increasing clay below. No rocks or pebbles. Roots very close to surface.

Dry sloping site. A few over mature aspen. Paper birch (50 years). No disturbance. Two medium sized birch of the ground and a few small stumps. A handfull of over-mature aspen present. No signs of a past disturbance. Sugar maple is reproducing bets, also red oak is reproducing well. Secession toward maple forest. Hazel is medium thick. One inch litter of leaves and twigs. Soil: 3 inches black loamy sand over 1.5 inches grey clayey sand over reddish brown fine sand with a little clay and loam. A few rock fragments present, roots sparse and scattered throughout.

Medium dry upland in hilly area. Balsam fir taking over site from over mature paper birch. Many large white pine stumps, fire scorches. Many of the older live trees are fire scared at base. Many dead standing and downed balsam fir, the ones standing are infested with wood bores. Reproduction by mostly balsam fir and maple. No hazel or bracken fern. Half inch litter layer of twigs, needles, and leaves. Soil: 4 inches black loam with much organic matter over 4 inches grey loamy sand over reddish brown loamy fine sand with several pebbles. Many fibrous roots in A horizon.

Steep hill side in a hilly area. Medium dry site. Many large white pine stumps, fire scared and scattered throughout the plot. Many dead standing and down balsam fir - a few aspen. Much slash. White pine and white spruce numerous on outskirts of the stand. Mass soil movement is a problem in this area where not forested. Reproduction is mainly balsam fir with a little quaking aspen. One fourth inch litter layer composed of grass, needles, and leaves. Soil: 3 inches brownish-black loamy clay over 2 inches dark brown clay over light brown clay. Roots mostly confined to A horizon. No rock fragments present.

Dr site in rolling topography. Jack pine plantation in very good condition. Most trees are about 6 feet apart and have very few low branches. Reproduction is composed of mostly balsam fir with a little red pine and white spruce. No bracken fern. Hazel sparse, up to 3 meters high. One inch thick litter layer composed of needles and twigs. Soil: 2 inch thick dark brown sand with a bit or incorporated organic matter over reddish brown fine sand with a few small rock fragments. Very dry soil. Roots well distributed through A and B horizons.

A level upland site in a gently rolling area. Medium dry site, well drained. Very healthy stand of red pine. Thin mat of pine needles covering the ground. The stand has been thinned, several low stumps on the plot and numerous small diameter slash on plot. Reproduction is in the form of white pine, balsam fir with a little white spruce and trembling aspen. Hazel is thick and up to 6 feet high. One half inch litter layer composed of needles. Soil: 4 inches dark brown and reddish brown sandy loam over reddish-grey brown loamy sand containing many rocks. Several large root throughout the A and B horizons.

Upland site in rolling terrain. Healthy sugar maple stand with havey crown cover and very few shrubs. Grass is very dense over much of the plot. Two dead balsam fir trees on the plot. A few stumps around the plot but no signs of a past disturbance. Reproduction is very numerous. Thin litter layer of leaves, twigs, and grass. Soil: 4 inches dark brown loam over 2 inches dark brown and reddish brown sandy loam over reddish brown sandy loam containing many rocks. Moist dry soil. Many thick roots in A and upper B horizons.

Very close to road. Lowland site in rolling terrain. Extremely wet site. Very healthy larch stand with ground surface covered by sphagnum moss. No sign of a past disturbance. Reproduction is numerous and composed mainly of black spruce. Litter layer is 4 inches of living and dead sphagnum moss. Soil is peat with many touch roots in the upper six inches. Water table is at 8 inches.

Lowland site in fairly flat area. Moist site. Healthy stand of white cedar. Has almost two completely different moisture environments - the highs spots around trees and stumps are very dry and the many low pockets in between are extremely dry. The diffing of the ditch along the road may have changed the environment by lowering the water table. Reproduction is very sparse. Litter layer of moss, needles, and twigs. Water table at 6 inches. Many roots in upper few inches.

Upland site in slightly rolling area. Medium dry site - well drained. Balsam fir stand in poor health - spruce budworm is killing some of the trees. A few very old aspen on the site, many fire scared stumps and decayed logs on and around the plot. Slash is heavy. Thick needle cover on the ground and litter shrubs and ground vegetation. Reproduction is scarce. 1.5 inch litter layer of needles with twigs and leaves on top. Soil: 1 inch black loam with much organic matter over 1.5 inches greyish reddish brown sandy loam over reddish brown sandy loam. Roots scattered throughout A and B horizons. No rock present.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Location uncertain. Upland site in rolling terrain. Medium dry site. Sugar maple stand in below average health. A few very large red oak tree nearby (one is 108.6 cm DBH). Thick crown cover and thick shrub and herb layers. Broad grass carpet on the plot. No sign of past disturbance. Litter slash on the plot. Reproduction is heavy and composed mainly of sugar maple with a litter bit of red oak and balsam fir. Thin litter layer of leaves and grass. Soil: 8 inches dark brown to black sandy loam over dark brown sandy loam over reddish brown gravely sand with many rock fragments and small stones. Many roots in A horizon.

Upland site on a steep slope in a hilly area. Medium dry rod oak stand in poor health, the tops have died back on almost all of the large trees. Grass covers most of the ground. A curing line of tall grass runs though the plot, it appears to be a drainage or an old road. A few well rotted pine stumps near the plot. Reproduction is heavy and composed or maple and green ash. Thin litter of leaves and grass. Soil: 6 inches dark brown loam over 2 inches dark brown silty loam over reddish brown silty loam. No rocks, several roots in A and upper B horizons.

Upland site on a very steeps slope in a hilly area. Dry site. Birch stand in medium health - a few aspen and oak mixed in. A few small pine stumps on and around the plot. Few birch in clumps. Shrubs are not very heavy - herb ground cover is heavy. Reproduction is mostly aspen under the canopy openings. Thin litter layer of twigs and grass. Soil: 5 inches dark brown loamy clay over reddish brown clayey loam. Root are concentrated mostly in the A and upper B horizons, many rocks - especially in the A horizon.

Upland site in a hilly areas. Medium moist site. Stand of balsam poplar in good health. Many well decayed and fire scared pine stumps on and around the plot. Reproduction is numerous and composed mainly of balsam poplar. Thin litter layer of leaves. Soil: 6 inches black loam over 4 inches brown loamy clay over reddish brown loamy clay. Roots distributed throughout A and B horizons. No rocks present.
The lowest quality site sampled this summer! Appears to have been grazed, cut, then left alone for the last several years.
Nearly level somewhat poorly drained soils with numerous poorly drained depressions. Wet mesic prairie and wet prairie. Area burned 4/93, area formally grazed and hayed.
Sampled area on top of circular knob in undisturbed area.
These plants were not keyed. Used names provided by EO. Top of knoll, due south of entry road-driest homogeneous area without sweet clover, just north of pond.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Blue Beech) Seepage Swamp
remarks: Dark wet mesic to saturated silt with high organic content. Overall slope 70% grade, but nearly level on small bench terrace at ravine side. Dry narrow ridge crest above releve with Betula papyrifera, but maple basswood on side slopes. Mode DBH 5-15, largest trees from 5-25% cover in community to 50cm DBH. Much of plot canopy is from adjacent maple basswood forest, with a gap. Seepage forms regulate flow over talus near base of plot center.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: Dark sandy silt with cobbles and some boulders of super steep slope beneath 10-20m height dolomite cliff. Mode DBH 35-45cm with larger trees to 55cm: rare to occasional. Ostrua large 15-25cm DBH. Occasional boulder, few tip-ups/limbs.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Medium sized alluvial plain; mounded draining away from stream toward north northwest - facing bluff with old channel at base. Mode 20-30 cm DBH with common large DBH tree; 40-55cm DBH: Tilia, Celtis, Acer. Tip-ups and limbs common (1-5%). Soil: dark silt loam with some sand. Deep humus layer.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: Dark sandy silt loam, compact, thin, pine duff (except in depression/ledges of steep slope. Scattered boulders. Pine DBH 15-65 cm; Deciduous DBH mode 25-35 cm, occasional max to 45cm. Slope undulates from ridge to concave swales: perpendicular to slope. Areas of cobblestone accumulations/talus. Sandstone/dolomite outcrops - two tiers - New richmond/Willow creek shakopee. Tip-ups, down limbs occasional.

Sandy silt dark friable deep duff and thick humus. Bur oak dominate. Crooked open grown trees. Mode DBH 25-35 cm. Larger trees to 55cm occasional to rare. Plot at the west edge of old road (overgrown). Approximately 4-8 feet above stream bed.

Dark clay silt loam dark/black to 3-4". Sub-horizon yellow brown, more clayey(?) with modules. Undulating Iowan surface (oak subsection). Dominant Quercus alba, mode DBH 40-50cm, frequent max size to 65cm DBH. Debris infrequent and snags occasional.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Mature dry mesic oak forest on side of long ridge with little relief, gently sloping to level. Silty sand with top soil dark to 1.5 inches below yellow sand with silt. Thick mulch/duff layer and 1/4-1/2 inch humus layer. Abundant debris, limbs and tip-ups all stages of decay. Mode DBH 30-40cm, common max to 70cm DBH; 70-100 years.

Silty sand, 3" to yellow sandy subsoil, dark-grey topsoil with unsorted gravel (occasional). Canopy 80% open to substrate with shrubby thicket in patches. Black cherry dominates this portion but becomes common to occasional in the north transect. Mode 25-35cm DBH, max to 50cm occasional.
Ridge crest between ravines of old bench terrace of plainfield sand. Short, open grown trees with dead lower branches. Mode 35-45 cm. Several smaller girth; rarely any larger. Transitional.

Upper slope near crest of southwest descending ridge spur with narrow crest. Broad crowns, crooked boles, short crown height, dark silt with cobble and infrequent rock out crops. Mode DBH 25-45cm, max occasional to 55cm (in vicinity). Portions resemble oak woodland.

Dry plainfield sand of old bench terrace. Narrow ridge between ravines Plot includes portion of crest and upper slope. Pines reproducing in open canopy. Past grazing likely although plot was isolated.

Plot at base of Jordon sandstone cliff capped with oneota. Large gaps in canopy from dead snags of pine. Apex of long narrow ridge spur between valleys. Sand with colluvial silt and heavy pine duff. Aspect varies from west to north to east, community extends to crest of dry cliff. Pine DBH mode 35-45cm, max to 80cm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Dry mesic silt, A horizon 1-1.5 inches, to yellow brown, thin humus and duff. Excellent forest soil profile. Crest of wide, convoluted ridge spur with steep slope. Very diverse canopy with several age class. Mode: 45-65cm DBH; smaller DBH common; woody debris. Abundant small tip-ups, limbs, all stages of decay. Snags rare (Ulmus). Scattered broad canopy white oaks occasional to infrequent. Canopy gaps rare.
Dry to dry-mesic oak forest. Large, broad spreading open-grown trees. Rocky silt with small boulders. Thin humus and duff. Oneota rock outcrops to 1 meter high. Sub-canopy 5-15m high missing.

Narrow band of dry oak forest at crest of large ridge spur with prairie on south aspect and dry-mesic oak below plot on northwest-west aspect. Broad bur oak and walnut with birch on edges. Silt with some cobbles. Clear demarcation between prairie and forest due to aspect. Mode DBH: Juglans/Quercus macrocarpa; 30-40cm, Birch; 15-25cm. Tipups/broken limbs common.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: 5-10% logs, some well-decayed. +/- thin deciduous leaf duff. Old tip-ups common. Tiny Botrychium (cf. virg.) trophophores common.
A few cut stumps in plot-occasional in stand. One burned stump in plot. 10% coarse woody debris. Thick deciduous leaf duff. Stant #27.
Thick needle duff. Few cut stumps. Minor within plot relief. Stand #14. 1.5" organic over 9" medium fine medium brown sand.
Needle duff. Plot location selected for dense, tall red pine. 10% coarse woody debris. Few well-rotted stumps. Stand #41. Old foot holds nailed on red pine at plot edge.
Stand #19. Along Prairie river.

Moderate coarse woody debris - including moss-covered logs. Moderate within plot relief. Stand #17. Plot placed on ridge. Stand is a mix of red pine on ridges and high knolls and aspen lower and black ash lowest.

Thin deciduous leaf duff. Moderate to abundant coarse woody debris within  plot relief due to old tip-ups. Stand #6. Stand selectively cut and thoroughly X-crossed with new and old forest trails to access wood. Recently cut stumps. Soils: 2 inches organic over 10 inches medium fine light tan sand.

Needle duff. Coarse woody debris moderate to abundant. Stand #6. Plot placed at apparent highest point on island and placed to capture white pine. Soil: 2 inches organic over 2 inches grey clayey sand and pebbles over over 11 inches gray medium coarse sand.
Stand "#9". Full of large water-filled pools- covering "1/2" the plot. Iron colored water. Nicer cedar south of plot-less ash, alder, some paper birch.

Red pine needle duff over Pleurozium mats. Occasional well-decayed stumps. Sparse coarse woody debris. Stand #5. Typed as NP59. Occasional paper birch and infrequent white pine. 3" sandy organic over 7" orange-tan med. coarse sand.

Duff of needles and cones. Light to mod coarse woody. Slight slope to south southwest. Moderate within-plot relief. Infrequent well-rotted stumps. Plot placed to capture white pine in northwest corner of exclosure. Soil: 1 inch organic over 12 inches fine gray-brown over fine medium tan sand.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Flood plain forest dominated by silver maple. Sandy ridges with silty low areas. Maples on sandy ridges. Coarse woody debris common -large diameter logs. Shallow wet matted deciduous leaf duff. Stand #5. Soil: one inch sandy organic over 9 inches gray brown fine sand.
Moderate coarse woody debris. Thin deciduous leaf duff. Stand #3. Plot on slight knoll between black ash and conifer swamp. Sand one inch organic over 8 inches light medium tan wet sandy silt.
Thick deciduous leaf duff. Stand #5. Plot placed at the highest point on knoll. 3" organic over 12" light tan silt. No graminoid layer in plot. Knoll known locally as Unnecessary Mountain.
Thick deciduous leaf duff. Sparse coarse woody debris. Slight within-plot relief. Stand # 14. 2"organic over 7" light tan silt.
Sphagnum hummocks throughout. Occasional coarse woody debris. Stand #5. Wet peat-only few cm returned. Very species poor.
Sphagnum hummocks throughout. Rare coarse woody debris. Wet peat. Rare plant releve - Plantanthera clavellata.
Abundant coarse woody debris. Duff sparse. 3" organic over 10" clay - some silt?

Coarse woody debris frequent. Nurse logs common. Few large, old well-decayed stumps. Standing water throughout and some pools. Soil: three inches organic over 2 inches silt (?) over 6 inches light gray clay.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Relief from small ephemeral pools - now dry. Thin matted deciduous leaf duff. 10% coarse woody debris. Few large-diameter old cut stumps-now moss covered in plot Along Prairie River.
Thick spongy decid leaf duff. CWD common. Extensive wind throw adjac. to plot on north side of knoll. Moss covered logs & well-decayed, duff covered logs occasional. Yellow and paper birch.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Thick decid leaf duff. Mod CWD - incl. 1 windthrown aspen. Within plot relief from well-decayed logs.  2" organic over 8" very fine lt tan sand with silt. Stand #7.
Water-filled depressions common. Betula allgh.reproduction. Most cedar leaning. Moderate coarse woody debris. Relief from sphagnum hummock, fallen logs, and tip-ups. Stand #6.  Wet peat.

Moderately thick deciduous and needle leaf duff. Moderate coarse woody debris. On steep slope to south. 2" organic over 6" light tan sand with silt and small pebbles. Plot not typical of stand-placed to capture pine.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Thick deciduous leaf duff. Several large rocks exposed. Moderate coarse woody debris. Several well decayed logs. Within plot relief from decaying, duff-covered logs and old tip-ups. Thick 3-4" organic layer over dark tan fine sand and pebbles. Stand #3.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Thick deciduous leaf duff. Occasional well-decayed logs-some paper birch. A few old tip-ups. Few well-decayed stumps. Stand #3. 3" organic over 5" silt.
Very wet black ash swamp - full of pools. Stand #6.
Thick deciduous leaf duff. Moderate coarse woody debris. Abundant Acer saccharum reproductive but not in 1-2m height class. Stand #2. 2" organic over grey brown silt.
Black ash swamp south of SPSP  jct. #7. Soil: 4" organic and 6" wet gray silt/sand.
Marked within plot and within stand relief. Coarse woody debris abundant. Few inches of organic over sand. Primarily Betula papyrifera. Topographic context: crest/upper.
Moderate coarse woody debris. Thin deciduous leaf duff.
Thick deciduous leaf duff. Within-plot relief from moss-covered and well decayed logs, tip-ups. Stand #2. 3" organic over 5" light gray-brown sandy silt.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Thick deciduous leaf duff. Coarse woody debris moderately abundany. Primarily paper birch. No cut stumps. Relief from tip-ups, well decayed logs. 1" organic over 7" very fine light grey-tan sand.
Thin deciduous leaf duff. Sparse to moderate coarse woody debris.
Shallow deciduous leaf duff. Coarse woody debris moderate to common. 1" organic over 3" grey silt over 5" very fine sand/silt. Stand #2. Mature aspen forest being replaced by maple/oak.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Thick deciduous leaf duff. Moderate coarse woody debris - nice. Betula papyrifera slight. Within plot relief from well decayed logs.
Very wet tamarack swamp. Full of moss-covered logs and pools.
Thin deciduous leaf duff. Moderate coarse woody debris including moss covered logs. 1" organic over 9" fine, tan sand.
Black ash swamp, northeast corner of SPSP, north of Savanna River ditch. 2" organic over 8" grey clay.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Scant deciduous leaf duff. 1 charred stump in plot.  Occasional coarse woody debris, most moss-covered. 2 inches organic over 8 inches grey clay.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Moderate deciduous leaf duff. Moderate abundant coarse woody debris.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Thin deciduous leaf duff. Moderate coarse woody debris including paper birch. No cut stumps. Within plot relief from old tip-ups and well decayed logs.
Thin deciduous and needle leaf duff. Moderate coarse woody debris, occasional moss covered. 3.5" organic light tan silt.

Soil plot on side slope(middle), general plot rolling gently. Hearty aspen. light crown cover-dogwood and hazel 7' high. Thalictrum dasycarpum 6' high; Osmunda claytonii 4 1/2 inches high. Age= 38 years. Ferns thick, forbs below. Soil: 10 cm loam cap over reddish coarse loamy sand with 25-50% gravel at 43cm over argillic (slightly mottled) at 55cm. 97% litter cover, 1% bare ground, 1% rock, 1% slash.

Soil: 13cm loam cap over fine grey brown sand with red brown tonging (30cm) over agrillic at 35cm (grey color). 5-10 course fragments. Hazel 8'. Herbs distinctly 2 layers, Aralia on top moderate Rubus below. Site uniformly flat. Age = 36 years. Ground cover: 2% slash, 1% bare ground, 1% rock, 1% moss, 92% litter, 3% grass.

Soil-10cm loamy cap over a fine sandy loam. 5-10% course fragments. Hazel 9'tall. Somewhat open aspen stand, a few standing dead trees. Stand age = 28 years. Ground cover: 77% litter, 1% rock, 5% slash, 15% grass.

Appears undisturbed. Young aspen (27 years.). Most heavy cover of impatiens seen so far. Plot appears moist. Soil: 10cm loam over 20cm fine sandy loam over red brown loam sand with 5-10% course debris. Ground cover: 1% rock, 1% slash, 95% litter, 1% moss, 2% grass.

Undisturbed site appears moist - area generally very flat. Aspen appears healthy except 2 larger ones, which are breaking down. Stand age = 29 years. Soil: 10-15cm fine sandy loam cap over red brown loamy sand. Ground cover: 2% moss, 1% rock, 2% grass, 8% slash, 87% litter.

Flat topography. Very tall aspen, two story stand. General health of aspen is good. Black ash present. Soil: loam (25cm)/sandy loam. Water seeping at 45cm. 5 to 10% coarse fragments throughout. Ground cover: 1% rock, 3% slash, 95% litter.

Plot uniformly flat, no bracken. Hazel sparse 7'. Aspen = 40 years. Undisturbed site. Soil 10cm of loamy sand cap over gray loamy sand and red/brown course sand. Water table at 40 cm. Ground cover: 1% slash, 99% litter.

Hazel 8'-9'; plot slopes down to creek. Surrounding area rolling. Some standing water - no ferns. Several aspen have rotten centers (38 years). Soil: loam cap (5cm) over loamy clay (10-15cm) over red clay. Ground cover: 3% water, 95% litter, 2% slash.

Location uncertain. Surrounding area is flat. Stand age = 38 years. Plot appears moist. Shrubs average 7'-8'. Soil:10 cm loam over dark black clay. No course fragments >60% clay. Water table: 40cm. Ground cover: 3% slash, 97% litter.

Hazel 8-10' bracken 2.5-3'; Aspen = 40 years. Plot uniformly flat, area surrounding rolling. Drainage ditch 1/2 mile wide, running east to west through  south 1/3 of plot. No standing or flowing water - moist. Soil: 10cm loamy sand cap over 30cm coarse sand over 10cm silt. Ground cover: 94% litter, 3% slash, 1% moss, 2% bare soil.

Hazel thick 7', bracken 3'. Microsite gently rolling. No fir on plot but it is on adjoining area. Plot is dry and well drained. Age= 44 years. Soil: 10 cm loam cap over brown fine loamy sand with <10% coarse fragments over reddish loamy sand with <10% coarse fragments.

Surrounding area gently rolling to flat- plot microtopography flat. Healthy 35 year old aspen. Sugar maple sapling understory.  5-6' hazel, 1-1.5' bracken. Both sparse. Fairly undisturbed- moist site. Soil: 10 cm loam cap over find sandy loam over coarse sandy loam. Ground cover: 95% litter, 1% slash, 3% mineral, 1% moss.

Hazel 6' chewed by caterpllirs. Bracken  to 4'. Flat microsite. Surrounding area flat, site dry and well drained. Appears to be 15-20% sugar maple below bushy area. Soil: 10cm loam cap over brownish sandy loam (40cm) over reddish brown sand with 10-15% coarse fragments. Ground cover: 2% slash, 98% litter.

Hazel 10' tall, extremely thick, no bracken. Ferns 3-3.5. Much mineral soil, little slash and low litter. Undisturbed site. Plot flat. Aspen healthy.  Plot appears very moist. Stand age = 42 years. Soil: 10 cm loam cap over sandy loam (40cm) with 5% coarse fragments over light brown fine clay loam. Ground cover: 3% slash, 45% soil, 50% litter, 2% rock.

Hazel 10" tall, very thick bracken 3'. Surrounding area flat. Large amount of exposed mineral soil. Plot appears moist. Loam cap over brownish loamy sand, over brown sand. Age=45 years. Soil: 10cm loam cap over brownish loamy sand (10cm) over coarse sand. Ground cover: 3% slash, 66% litter, 30% soil, 1% rock.

Extensively thick hazel 8-10'. Bracken sparse 1.5-2'. Healthy aspen. Surrounding area gently rolling. Soil: high amount of under-decomposed matter over loam over sandy loam. Stand age = 50 years. Ground cover: 96% litter, 4% slash.

Hazel 6', no bracken. 2 story stand; age=40 year.; Abies below. Soil: 10 cm of grayish brown medium sand over 20cm of brown medium sand over 35 cm of brown course sand. Ground cover: 1% moss, 97% litter, 2% slash.

Extremely thick hazel 8' bracken sparse 2'.  Surrounding area rolling. Mineral soil exposed. Some slight runoff. Healthy tall aspen. Soil: 10cm loam cap over fine brown sand over fine silt. Age=41 years. Ground cover: 5% rock, 5% litter, 74% slash, 15% mineral rock, 1% moss.

Slight drainage ditch on southside of plot; mottles in soil. Hazel 6'. Rolling microsite, flat surrounding area. Larger aspen does not look healthy; age=43 years. Open area with no shrubs. Ground cover: 1% slash, 99% litter.

Rich diversity of species in plot. Hardwood stand coming below aspen overstory. Moist site. Healthy aspen. Hazel 8-10', no bracken. aspen = 37 years; balsam fir = 57 years. Ground cover: 1% slash, 99% litter.

Surrounding area flat. Hazel 5', bracken 2-3'. Thick shrub and fern layer, moist and undisturbed site. Tall aspen. Soil has 50% large (baseball size) course fragments. Stand age= 40 years. Ground cover: 1% rock, 96% litter, 3% slash.

Surrounding area rolling. Plot on mid-slope and is flat. Healthy looking aspen. Bracken 2'. No hazel. Balsam understory. 3 standing dead aspen Larger and older aspen not vigorous. Age= 63 years. Ground cover: 98% litter, 2% slash.

General topography surrounding area gently rolling. Farmer selectively cut aspen 10-15 years ago. 5 aspen snags, others appear healthy. Soil: 5-7 cm loam cap over 20 cm of fine sandy loam over clay. Ground cover: 2% slash, 1% mineral soil, 2% moss, 95% litter.

Understory of maple-fir spruce-birch with shrubs forming a thick layer Aspen healthy looking. Area gently rolling, plot flat. Undisturbed. Age=51 years. Ground cover: 97% litter, 2% slash, 1% bare soil.

Hardwood, all age stand. Red oak = 77 years. old. Flat microtopography surrounding area flat. Rock pile on south side of plot, 2 square meters. Soil: loam cap over brown loam with 5-10% course fragments (30-35) over reddish brown loamy sand. Ground cover: 1% mineral, 4% rock, 2% slash, 93% litter.

Surrounding area to west rolling to east steep. Plot uniformly flat. All age maple basswood stand, (Sugar Maple=85 years.) sparse shrubs, no bracken. Heavy ferns and grass. Soil: loam (15cm)/silt(20cm)/silt and clay.  Ground cover: 1% moss, 3% slash, 1% rock, 95% litter, 1% soil.

Flat microtopography. Healthy looking jack pine stand (80 yrs). Surrounding area flat. Thick needle layer on forest floor. Soil: 5cm loam cap over coarse red brown sand. 1% coarse fragments. Ground cover: 45% moss, 1% slash, 54% litter.

10cm loam cap over sandy loam (20cm) over loamy sand (50cm) becoming gradually gravelly red/brown sand with 25-40% gravel. Stand rather open, flat except 2 mounds and 2 old rotten large stumps. Age= 37 years. Ground cover: 2% rock, 1% mineral soil, 3% slash, 73% litter, 20% grass.

Soil: 10cm loam cap over light brown fine loam and sandy loam with some reddish brown mottling over reddish brown clay and loam. Stand age=42 years. Ground cover: 2% slash, 10% grass, 2% rock, 86% litter.

Young (32 years.) healthy stand with 10% Acer rubrum saplings in understory. Area flat to slightly rolling. Soil: sandy loam over clay; no mottles. Very moist soil. Ground cover: 6% slash, 1% grass, 1% soil, 2% moss, 90% litter.

Very low and wet; 1' to water table, generally flat topography, rocky and some water puddles. Hypoxylon on older stems, young and in good shape. Age= 31 years. Ground cover: 3% rock, 1% mineral, 1% water, 25 slash, 93% litter.

Plot microtopography uniformily flat. Heavier tree cover and grass, light herb and shrub. Age= 35 years. Soil: sandy loam over coarse sand with coarse fragments; water table begins at 35-40cm. Ground cover: 1% slash, 1% rock, 96% litter, 1% moss, 1% soil.
Hazel 6-7', no bracken present. Dead balsam fir. Topography generally flat. Dead standing aspen, some hypoxylon on aspen. Slight fir and maple understory. Age=31 years.

Young stand (32 years.) with some scattered older trees (48 yrs.) Surrounding area appears to be an old river bed, gently rolling. Moist sand with mottles. Stand is long and narrow. Ground cover: 15% slash, 2% rock, 1% soil, 1% moss, 81% litter.

Stand = 40 years. Elm and black ash in understory, rather open stand. Hazel 9-10' tall. Flat topography, aspen not real healthy. Small east-west creek. Age=40 years. Soil: loam cap 10cm/mottled fine sandy loam/clay loam. Ground cover: 2% grass, 97% litter, 2% slash, 1% rock.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Mature deciduous forest with canopy dominated by Betula papyrifera with lesser amounts of Tilia and Acer saccharum. 30% of Betula >10cm DBH are dead. Tall shrub layer nearly absent. Rich understory very old cut stumps. Sandy loam. Ground cover 55% leaf litter.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Mature forest dominated by betula papyrifera and populus tremuloides. Some Abies in sub-canopy. Tall shrub layer dense; dominated by Corylus. One Pinus strobus snag. Some Populus tremuloides down. No evidence of past disturbance. Herb layer dominated by Aster mac. and Aralia nud. In slight depression on top of knoll.
Area heavily invaded by oak, recently cut with much slash left in place.
Part of larger sand prairie that is planted to pines.
Sand prairie, some brush invasion.
Steep slope much gravel and sand.
25% bare ground, little litter.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Closed canopy red oak forest with tall straight forest grown boles--sub old growth in character. Herb and graminoid layer sparse, but with uniform distribution of many species. Carya cordiformis in subcanopy. Much microtopography, possibly from old tip-ups. Thick leaf litter. 3cm dark A-horizon/fine sandy loam with occasional gravel.

On 60m wide esker ridge with wetland on both sides. Sub-mature oak dominated forest with areas of large diameter red pine and big tooth aspen (residuals/regeneration after historic logging?). Burned yearly in past? Subject to windthrow. On sand with silt. 2 cm well developed A horizon with organic matter. Large boulders and glacial erratics common. Tree core Quercus rubra: 40 cm DBH  - 73 years; 36cm DBH - 73+ years; 40cm DBH - 71+ years. Topographic context: crest/upper.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Mix black ash, bur oak, and trembling aspen forming interrupted canopy with little to no subcanopy, but dense low sapling layer of ash. Understory dominated by a mix of sedges and ostridge fern. Large amounts of coarse woody debris, covered with moss. Cored 4 canopy trees; 36cm DBH bur oak - 93+ years, 40cm DBH bur oak - 92+ years, 47cm DBH basswood -76+ years, 37cm DBH black ash - 66+ years.

Matrix of sub-mature to mature aspen/birch forest with oak and red pine occasional and red maple subcanopy. Lots of micro topography and well-decayed coarse woody debris. Historically logged? 1cm dark well developed A-horizon over brown medium-coarse sand. Cored 3 canopy trees; 28cm DBH red oak - 60+ years, 33cm DBH big toothed aspen - 56+ years.

Young-mature dry pin oak forest. Short canopy and numerous dead lower limbs indicate previously open condition, though canopy is approaching closure. Paper birch and jack pine secondary species. Jack pine dying back. Dense shrub layer to 2m. Very few cut stumps. Notable fruiting bodies of many fungi species. 2cm A-horizon over fine yellow brown sand. Cored pin oaks; 23cm DBH - 68+ years, 23cm DBH - 65+ years, 28cm DBH - 60+ years.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Small but high quality mature to sub-old growth maple/basswood stand with all size classes. Low volume of coarse woody debris overall, but several large natural downfalls. Nice herb layer. 3cm A-horizon of silt loam with lots of roots and organic matter/fine silt loam with rocks. Thin but continuous leaf litter. County to log? Three core: 34cm DBH Quercus rubra - 57+ years; 38cm DBH Acer saccharum - 178+ years; 43cm Tillia americana - 62+ years. Topographic context: upper/middle.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Sub old growth; dominated by red oak and sugar maple with maple in understory. Closest to old growth I've seen in county. Large volume of coarse woody debris and large well-decayed logs, snags. Charcoal on old snag. Continuous leaf litter. 2cm A-horizon, dark well developed with much organic matter/silt-loam with clay. Tree cores: 30cm DBH Quercus rubra - 64+ years; 42cm DBH Quercus rubra - 73+years; 33cm DBH Acer saccharum - 80+ years.
