Dominated by 25-35cm DBH (average) Quercus ellipsoidalis with Betula papyrifera secondary in canopy. Trees 25-35cm DBH with smaller size classes also. Herb layer a mix of open and closed canopy species but dominated by hog peanut and aster macro, good old growth potential. Thin oak leaf litter. Soil: top 3cm dark brown color/30cm fine yellow-brown sand/30cm coarser yellow-brown sand. Cored trees; 24cm DBH pin oak - 57+ years, 30cm DBH pine oak - 68+ years, 27cm DBH pin oak - 69+ years.

Mature red and jack pine surrounded by "30cm+" quaking aspen. Pin oak and paper birch in understory with hazel and diverse mix of shrub and herb species. Many pines with fire scars on north-northwest sides. Several large well-decayed stumps, apparently cut. Topographic context: toe/depression. Thin litter of leaves and needles. Soil: 10cm well-developed dark A-horizon/fine yellow-brown sand. Tree cores - Red pine: 28cm DBH - 94+ years, 24cm DBH - 48+ years, 26cm DBH - 45+ years; Jack pine: 32cm DBH - 51+ years, 27cm DBH - 55+ years, 22cm DBH - 53+ years.

Mature aspen-oak forest with occasional red pine. Undulating topography. Patchy canopy and understory. Some old well-decayed cut stumps. Reasonable mature stand which should succeed nicely to old growth if not logged. Large amounts of small diameter coarse woody debris. 1cm leaf litter. Soil: 5cm dark A-horizon/fine loose sand and rock. Two cored canopy trees: 51cm DBH red pine - 82+ years, 26cm DBH red oak - 83+ years.
Juniper dominant on St. Peter outcrops along road, but common in sampled area. East side of the fence on sample hill is grazed, west side (sampled) apparently not.

Northwest of trail which leads from Mulry's south gate to southeast corner of Sugarbush Lake. At this point trail is orientated at 30 degrees east of north. Releve in a level basin like area west of downed Tilia on southwest side of plot and large birch on northeast of plot. Botrychium mormo in plot.
Small meadow in woods south of southeast end of Sugarbush Lake, shrub cover varies. Releve in shrub zone.
Top of small rise, very old stumps. Heavy equiptment working East of plot.
Koch tract (DeMaster) west of circular small pond.

This birch inclusion is on slope between maple basswood stand on north shore of Sugarbush Lake. Unusual for a birch slope, because is devoid of fir. Despite no Quercus canopy considerable Quercus rubra litter in plot. Topographic context: upper/middle/lower.

Bare litter floor ~85%, litter predominately Quercus rubra. Heavily shaded and dominated by oak layer, may account for the sparse groundlayer. Canopy and sub-canopy attractive. Deer browse. Several animal holes about 8-10 cm in diameter. Releve is in a draw, predominant slope of plot is 4 degrees trending northwest, but south side of plot is a steeper north facing slope of 15-20 degrees.

This releve is from southwest side of trail on gently west facing slope of Kidney shaped wetland. Just southwest of where aspen is currently ranked out along trail an represents good forest on both sides of trail in this area. On a level hill. Ground about 100% shaded because of heavy D4 layer Litter all oak-ground mainly bare litter.

West side of Ostrum tract in unpastured area between field and wetland. Mediocre woods, part of macrosite. Groundlayer mainly bare litter of 50% Quercus rubra and 50% Acer saccharum. Releve about 40m South of road.

Majority of tract appears to have been logged (maybe in the 60's). Stump sprouting to beautiful regenerating Northern hardwoods. Releve northeast of a north-south trending draw, west facing slope, east of wet meadow.
All along the edge of this meadow the shoreline forest has abundant birch, aspen, ash, and elm.
On an isthmus between small lake and wetland. Trail passes to west of releve.
On narrow linear northeast trending point that extends into south side of Wakefield Lake.

Hill on southeast side of Skunk Lake-level near crest. About 80% of the ground layer is bare litter about 2" thick with lots of club fungi. Not as rich groundlayer as stand is on the northeast side of lake.
Iron stained water with an "oily" look. Ash cover is about 50%, the remainder of canopy is just open except for the single birch.

Northeast of Dinasaur Ridge Trail near junction with main trail. Similar to forest east of oak savanna, except that forest has lots of Amphricarpa, Cornus racemosa, and walnut. Topographic context: upper/middle.
Plot located 30m north of edge of open water at northeast end of Fish lake. On floating mat of course peat. Much standing water. Shrubs are stunted. High cover by non-sphagnum mosses.

Part of mosaic of fen-like and wet meadow-like patches on deep fibric peat with much groundwater input. At foot of valley side slopes on west side on Minnesota River Valley. Plot is ~40m east of Hwy 169.
One of several kinds of patches in fen/meadow mosaic on coarse, springy peat. Located ~300m east of Hwy 169. At 1 foot of steep slope on west side of Minnesota River Valley.

Part of mosaic of seepage-influenced wet meadow/shallow marsh communities at foot of east side of Minnesota River valley. Water table is just above surface. Soil is peaty muck. Surrounded by patches dominated by Phagmites, Typha, and Acorus.
Low sedge opening surrounded by Scirpus acutus/Carex prairea community On fine peat with marl on terrace at foot of east side of Minnesota River valley. Cold water at ground surface.

Fen-like zone on very shallow toe slope approximately 300m west of bottom of steep west facing side of Minnesota River valley. Soil is wet, fine grained peaty muck that has small white concretions, no odor. Not bouncy. On edge of well-developed calcareous fen.
Part of mosaic of seepage-influenced wetlands on deep peat deposit on shallow toe slopes on east side of Minnesota River valley.

Seepage wetland on very shallow terrace on lowermost toe of east side of Minnesota River valley. Plot is ~200m west of county road 23. Water table at ground surface. Soil at top is course, saturated peat. Did not see marl concretions. Slightly bouncy ground.
Plot is in center of small kettle hole wetland on floating sphagnum mat. Surrounded by mature oak woodland/forest. Poorly-developed example of poor fen. May be suffering from nutrient inputs?

Small patch of prairie on rocky knoll surrounded by formerly plowed land. Large granitic erratics and sandstone fragments at ground surface. Located just north of small pond. On terrace of Minnesota River valley. Other parts of terrace are being mined for limestone. Within Unimin's Prairie Conservation Area.
Dry mesic prairie typical of most of site. On shallowly undulating topography. On dark brown sandy loam soil over dry sand layer above limestone bedrock on terrace within Minnesota River Valley.

Small area of dry prairie on subtle, shallow knoll ~30m west of road. On rich dark brown soil with much sand. Glacial erratics at soil surface. On terrace within Minnesota River valley. Grazed in past, now managed with controlled burns.
Emergent marsh in bottom lands along Cannon River. Plot is north of river, 20m east of county line. Plot is typical of ca 5 acre patch near road. Rest of wetland is dominated by Typha.
Patch in mosaic of fen/meadow/marsh complex on fibric peat at foot of west side of Minnesota River valley. Water table is just above substrate surface.

Releve is in marginal area of wet meadow where there was a sufficiently large area west of moat, so may not represent interior of wetland. If anomalous in analysis, drop it. Area burned several years ago.
On level upland west of Tamarack bog. Open litter about 20% of ground- about 1" thick and dominated by oak leaves. Not grazed in at last 2 decades, but formally grazed.

This releve is just east of a forest trail on a topographic bench. No apparent stumps, but dirth of oak and maple in favor of birch and Tilia suggests former logging. Tilia not multi-stemmed. Probably formerly grazed.

Species composition suggests this is better typed as a poor fen than an open sphagnum bog because eriaceous species are scattered and low cover. Surface is generally smooth and even. Community now rare.
This is the level, flat top of same stand as releve 6459, which was on slope. This portion looks like formerly grazed (but not in the last 25 years). Stand looks hardwood on photo.

This releve is interesting because it is an example of a site where we know the disturbance history: grazed in 1946-1956, oak cut in the 50's. Aspen was cut in 1990, from number of stumps, appears once co-dominant.
Very rich aspen-birch just southeast of an ash swamp inundated by beaver. Releve is from base to near crest of slope but not on the flat top. Black ash is at border of wetland.
Top of long point south of Sugarbush lake, forest floor feels disturbed but lots of Dirca and fantastic canopy. Very abundant songbirds of several types.

High-quality old-growth forest. Logged approximately 100 years ago according to owner and large residual pines occasional throughout. Heterogeneous. Abundant coarse woody debris, snags. 1cm litter of pine needles and leaves. Soil: 2cm dark A-horizon with organic matter/fine sand (top 10 cm dark, 30cm+ light). Tree core: 58cm DBH red pine - 155+ years; 40cm DBH big toothed aspen - 65+ years; 28 cm DBH white pine - 66+ years.

Much relief due to well-decayed logs and tip-ups. Large amounts of coarse woody debris, representative of canopy species and in all decay classes. Thick deciduous leaf duff. Soil: 10cm dark A-horizon with extensive roots and organic matter/yellow brown medium fine sand.

Small area of closed canopy and sparse shrubs compared with surrounding forest. Die-off of large aspen has produced large (>30cm) snags and coarse woody debris. Soil: 5cm dark A-horizon with organic matter/fine sand, clay and loam/sandy loam at "30cm+" root material throughout to 30cm. Tree cores: 47cm DBH Quercus rubra - 70+ years; 35cm DBH Quercus macrocarpa - 83+ years; 22cm DBH Acer rubrum - 40+ years; 21cm Tillia americana - 50+ years.

Plot on reletively broad (50m) terrace of the Nemadji River, 10m from the bank. 15x25m plot situated on elongate rises (1m high). Next to a 10x6m shaded wet pool, no pools in plot. No organic layer. No coarse woody debris.
Scatter hazel 6 feet tall, no bracken. Two story stand with balsam fir and mountain maple. Generally flat topography. Developed wood road on south end of plot.
Soil-no pit dug, visually confirmed RRW. Flat, rocky, water standing, thin mineral layer. Mixture of balsam pop, black ash, aspen, paper birch. Aspen (48 years.) vigorous, surrounding area flat.
Hazel 6-7', bracken 3' tall, stand one story with few elm, basswood, and sugar maple below, microsite flat, surrounding area generally flat, overall stand is young (59 years.)
Aspen vigorous, healthy, tall - plot microtopography uniform flat ex-hole 1m2 around large boulder. Surrounding area gently rolling, appears to be a moist site. Stand 41 years old.
Kitchen middens 10% of the plot; plot flat otherwise. Aspen healthy- hazel 7'- bracken 1.5', surrounding area flat, small amount of balsam fir in the understory. Stand age = 39 yrs.
Unusually open stand, hazel patchy 6' very low shrub layer. Flat, microsite flat, trees healthy. Stand age= 38 years.

Plot uniformly flat- SE 1/4 wet with flowing water - soil very wet but site is not apparently wet throughout the season. Plot undisturbed but understory sparse. Aspen (41 years.) healthy. History unknown. Water table at 30cm.
Plot uniformly flat. 2 large boulders (1 m3). Unusually sparse. Heavy waist high shrub and fern cover. Two cut stumps. Aspen (50 years old) does not look vigorous. Stand hit by tent caterpillars.

Plot not located on topo or photos, presumed destroyed by development. Little Corylus, bracken. Aspen healthy (42 years) Standing water, fairly open stand; very flat microsite. Plot appears undisturbed. Water table at 40cm.
Very dense hazel 8' to 9' tall, thick fern cover, but little bracken. Microsite and surround. area very flat. Sparse overstory, but no cut stumps. Some white pine in area. Stand age = 45 years.

Very little hazel or bracken. Aspen (41 yrs.) does not appear healthy. Large amount of standing water over the flat topography. Some bog species present. Standing dead trees. Appears wet most of the year.
Old balsam stump. Many blown down trees. Sparse hazel and bracken. Site dry and undisturbed.
Surrounding area flat, as is plot. Sparse shrub layer. Timber thinned some years ago, but now there is no sign of disturbance, except a few stumps. Stand age 55 years.
Old growth, undisturbed stand, old fire scars present.
Open jack pine stand with little blowdown. Flat microsite and flat surrounding area. Hazel extremely thick.
Heavy hazel cover, light bracken. Kitchen middens 15% of plot, some erosions off top of middens.
Surrounding area gently rolling. Plot on upper side of slope. Undisturbed. Very sparse hazel, no bracken. Considerable balsam blowdown and breakage surrounding plot. Age = 57 years.
Stand borders clear cut. Birch appears healthy, balsam blow-down, old fire scarred pine. Stand age= 49 years.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Plot microtopogrphy -humpy, on hilltop. Kitchen middens on 5% of plot. All age; 76 years. Pit stopped at rock at 50 cm.; moist, rocky. Extremely sparse herb and shrub cover.
Flat microtopography, surrounding area flat. Dense crown cover, abundant. Acer saccharum reproduction. Stand age = 80 years.
Stand age = 54 years. Soil unusually dry; midslope; Duluth very fine sand loam.

Anomalous wind damaged stand origin 1899. Stand was falling apart before 1995 wind storm and biggest tress got knocked down by storm. On sand. Enormous canopy gaps and big domino effect, perhaps because of soils. Releve purpose was to get on sandy soil. No pit, sand over clay?

Funny stand, beautiful signature on photo, lovely canopy, but floor feels formerly grazed. Very strange location for this case. Should check history of area. Southwest side of curve south of Bass Lake.
Core of Calcareous seepage fen surrounded by open circular zone of active upwelling. Perhaps this is a later sucessional stage?

This is a very small wet seepage area on a slope north of Spring Creek and south of a hill prairie. It may represent a degradation of a calcareous fen or it may be an incipient seep, not active enough to be a calcareous fen.
About 300m northwest of field in area where smooth grey signature on photo runs continuously both east and south. Undulating.
No shrubs. The Utricularia is in open pools. Very undiverse.
Transitional zone between mesic prairie and rich fen. (Includes some mesic to dry-mesic and many wet species.)
West of railroad tracks.

In Salix candida zone of rich fen/sedge meadow/emergent marsh complex east of railroad track. This releve does not represent any of our standard communities -- an oddball. Topographic context: depression/flat.
This knoll shows on topo map - west of railroad track.

Typical of better forests on hilly moraine; probably 70-80 years since last cut; multi-stem Tilia; dead/down is only Populus grand; large old tip-up mounds/pits. Trees here 30-45cm DBH; productive soil.
Large calcareous seepage fen, this releve in shrubby lower area. Tiny blue leafhoppers in the Lobelia kalmii. pH 8.2
Yes, this is all there is in a 20x20 plot. Picea 5-15cm DBH are 12 to 18 inches apart, very dense. Dry barren floor.

Releve just beyond edge of a selective cut. Difficult to find unaffect area. Predominately maple litter is only about 1 inch thick. Much of logging here appears to be wind storm salvage. Despite ecotonal geographic location, floristically characteristic of community type in this part of state. Dead Quercus macrocarpa has created a canopy gap as bi as a releve plot. Tree is outside plot but picked up by prism because of it's large size.

Low wet aspen east side of Harstad or west side of Templeton tract north of trail that shows on photo. Difficult to estimate cover and abundance of graminoids. A messy transitional lowland forest community. Interface of LLWL and LLWD.
Releve in sadder of hill. Fox den in plot.
A wonderfully diverse little area with a juxtaposition of species characteristic of wet and dry prairies. Owner says never been broken. Probably 2 acres at most.
No shrubs.
West of DNR parking lot, north of wetland on county line, east of wetland, west of road.
West of road, pretty level, slightly westerly slope.
Survey by Wendt and Converse called this BC, too much Poa now and Lythrum salicaria bad at the site. Site now C to D. Re-evaluation of 1986 site.

Between grove and very NENENE33. Contrast this releve with sec 28, which is poor quality. This location has better gramminoid dominance, few forbs, few weeds except on mounds and recently burned edge of grove.
A bit more forby than one would hope- unclear whether this is a natural tendency to forbiness.
Transitional zone between sandy upland and tamarack swamp. Taxus canadensis in this zone.
Releves in this swamp are at interface of geomorphic units 11 and 47. This releve may actually be on Itasca moraine (11) as discharge areas are downstream to the west.
Loose red/brown signature on photo CBM 19-2, red on NAPP 3099-13. Openly stocked, sunny tamarack, almost no shrub layer, open pools. Appears flooded. 2/3 of Larix dead.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Just west of old NS trail. About 1 inch loamy clay over 9 inches heavy black clay. Signs of old logging.
Southeast end labeled "demonstration woodland" east of north-south trail. Regenerating stand.
Very undiverse. Groundlayer mainly oak litter and Uvularia. This is one of the more oak dominated areas on hunting club property.
Strange area on slope between sandy pine upland and shrub swamp meadow wetland (purported former conifer swamp). Wet site but on sandy soil with black A horizon.
100 meters south of releve 62-01. Pretty tacky woods, but releve to get sense of floristics on prairie soils of Alexandria moraine.
Ground is about 85% bare litter. On photo this area has a grey signature and is about 30-40 meters wide on ground. All vegetation in bad shape because of blight and insect damage.
Nearly all the oak in county is grazed. One of few publicly owned stands in what should be the oak savanna zone of county. Disappointing. Large stumps each 1 foot DBH with sprouts 25cm.
Biggest nuts on hazelnuts in the county. Grazed and firewood cutting in past. More recently, less selective firewood cutting southeast of this releve.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: On same point as releve 6527 but on a bench on east side. Feels like an overgrown channel or a piece of floodplain that has an island of Tilia between here and the river. Grazed and firewood cutting in past.
On point of land on a big bend in river with steep 10 foot banks. Grazed and firewood cutting in the past.
Fair amount of bare litter. Riparian forest along Wild Rice River. Entire area previously grazed and incidentally harvested for firewood. Plot smells of bear.
Without the planted spruce thisn would be a fine, but tiny prairie remnent, B quality, one of the few hill prairies in county. Incursions by renter, who is plowing whatever is possible.
Very aesthetically pleasing open structured with wet meadow dominated by Carex lacustris and Carex aquiatilis in center with Salix gracilis scattered.

Beautiful 10ac oak forest grades downslope to maple-basswood forest total 30 acres. Past cutting but trees now 25-42cm DBH. Stand is exposed along a road; plot is 5m from edge. Herbs senescing, cover is low.

Mesic forest at toe of slope and at edge of small wet forested depress. Has a few large old sugar maple and many different-age oaks. One cut stump: oak? Herb list similar to upslope but cover and abundance is greater here.

Quick releve to describe the broad zone of cut-over forest along the backslopes of the development's roads. Plot divided into two 4m x 50m bands on opposite sides of the road. Disturbed land, not a natural community type.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Important stretch of undeveloped shore on Whitefish Lake. Plot is 30m from steep 3m drop to water. Peninsula past disturbed, old trail through plot. Tilia 22cm, Quercus rubra 50cm DBH. Canopy species vary, cover 75%.

Possibly old-growth forest at south-southeast shore of Whitefish Lake. Odd irregularly pitted upland; much microtopography; very old trail to northeast? Past disturbed but not clear cut; some trees >80cm DBH. Very attractive.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Wanted to get hardwood forest releve but had few leads - this from Steve Wilson. Stand is small (ca 40 acres) but mature, probably past selective cutting. Exact location uncertain; scenic view to south from Hwy 135.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Plot is 150m upslope from Kettle River on mini terrace with small moist seepage and temporary pools in rocky tip-up pits. Thin canopy and tall shrub is typical. Natural? Past-cut, grazed? Much windthrow.

Plot alongside trail on narrow crest, highest elevation. Trees 30-45cm DBH; old Betula papyrifera at 55cm. Old down logs. Tip-ups large and continuous with low spots with swamp species just outside plot. Snags; old and new windthrow.

Plot is in lowland ecotone between wet meadow and disturbed upland forest. Botrychiums mostly restricted to this zone. Botrychium matric >80 & B.lanc >25 in plot. Many tip-up mounds/pits. Trees 18-28cm DBH.

Attractive mostly uniform wet meadow; Calamagrostis co-dominant in places. Sedge thatch 10-20cm thick with water below. Disturbed areas dominated by Polygonum sagittatum. Nice margins with occasional tall forbs.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Slightly better area (ca. 10 acres; trees 25-38cm DBH) in a large monotonous past-cut C/BC rank forest with many trails. Herb diversity low through-out, better near wetlands. Plot with good microtopography; some down logs.

Lowland hardwoods at this site are common as narrow zones at upland margins. Plot in unusually large 60m x 80m stand on rise in small conifer swamp. Trees slender. Lacks dead wood. Betula alleghaniensis present.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Interesting lowland hardwood along Snake River: typical species, but large bedrock blocks create uneven surface and limit tree size/density. Rocky grottos less woody, more mossy. Quercus rubra, Tilia and Betula papyrifera by river.
Disturbed wet meadow at edge of old field; past cultivated and/or grazed. Wanted to document non-riverine meadow species, but this site is too disturbed to be of much use. Silty lake plain soil.
Expansive lowland hardwood forest appears to be past grazed but is recovering well. Trees 25-35cm DBH. Not much coarse woody debris. Moist low spots are occasional (ca. 1m to 4m sq).

Dense willow swamp between silver maple floodplain forest and wet meadow along Rice River. 1 mile northeast of Rice Lake on downstream side of dam. Dense thatch of Calamagrostis. Appears to be subject to drawdown.

Attractive floodplain forest with southern characteristics; dominated by 20-45cm DBH silver maples. Very open below; microtopography mostly flat; some old down trunks; plot by wet meadow ca. 60-80m from river.

Mature hardwood forest (trees 20-40cm DBH) with old cut stumps. Has conifer associates in groundlayer but lacks white pine. Scattered Thuja in low areas. Tip-up mounds and other microtopography; downed logs.

Mature cedar swamp with only a few cut stumps (more by road). Plot in cedar dominated area but at east side of stand near mixed conifer-hardwood swamp and therefore herbs and shrubs more diverse than center of stand.

10x40m plot between a disturbed maple-basswood forest and narrow alder zone along south shore of Kettle Lake. Brushy woodland structure. Aspen, basswood, and ash cut by beaver. Note Botrychium cf lanc.

Plot in a 120m wide channel between forested uplands; appears to receive surface flowage and groundwater seepage. Grades to mixed conifer swamp. Plot on southeast of old trail. Downed logs; standing water.

Typical mid-age (60 year) forest dominated by multi-stem, 22-32cm DBH, Quercus rubra/ Tilia; Populus grandidentata in patches and Populus tremuloides marginal. Acer understory. Fire scars on east and south side of trunks. Many tip-up mounds. Lacks shrub layer.

Relatively large area of lowland hardwood. Canopy species variable from place to place, but not obviously; all trees straight and slender (10-25cm DBH). A few Tilia and 30cm. Lacks shrub layer; not much dead wood.

Plot in small 5-acre, less disturbed forest on steep slope amid recent northern hardwood and aspen cuts. Multi-stemmed Tilia 15-25cm DBH and dead Betula alleghaniensis at 48cm. 8m above small pond. Boulders. Abies in shrub layer.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Example of past-grazed lowland hardwood along the Snake River with dead cf. Ulmus americana at 50cm DBH. In old meander of channel, about 40m wide. Moist organic layer on silty sand (?); not rocky. About 60m from river.

Plot in mature mesic forest 80m south-southwest of 1994(?) clear cut. 2m east of old trail. Trees mostly 30-35cm DBH; max = Acer and Tilia at 55cm. Dead Juglans cinerea at 30cm. Dense leaf litter. A few boulders.

Good example of lowland-hardwood canopy dominated by Quercus macrocarpa, Tilia, and Fraxinus nigra. Site was visited as field-check of lowland hardwood-classification/satellite data. Mostly past-grazed. Plot in best area. Stumps. 1.3 miles east of Ernst Pool.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Releve typical of moderate-low diversity, post-fire/past-cut forest. Trees slender, straight, 20-30cm DBH. Birch snags and debris; fire scars. Acer subcanopy; sparse shrubs/forbs. At edge of McGrath till.

Beautiful, locally moist, species rich, 5 acre portion of "120+" acre C/BC rank oak forest. On mini-terrace near small ravines on northwest side of Rhine Lake. Boulders; irregular microtopgraphy with Botrychium in lows; fire scars on south side.

Odd forest of multi-stem Tilia with occasional Quercus rubra; mostly 20-30cm DBH. Acer subcanopy; shrub density variable. Forest +/- open and airy. Tip-up mounds and pits through-out, but not much coarse woody debris. Fire? Dry lake wind effects?

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Beautiful, straight, tall black ash supercanopy (trees 45-52cm DBH) above large old yellow birch. Shady below. Snags, tip-ups, tilted and down wood. Mucky pools (0.5-3m squared) are dryish this year. Plot is 30-40m from upland.

Ecotonal community type occurs as a narrow zone at lowland margins of oak forest; this example just large enough to sample (between two wet-lands). Tip-up mounds and pits. Large down trunks-(Populus grandidentata)?

On lower slope of gravelly knob. Continuous canopy of 25-40cm Acer and Tilia. 1 large diameter (58cm) Acer snag. 1 large diameter well-decayed pine stump. Numerous tip-up mounds. Dense Acer reproduction and low herb cover. Sandy loam over gravelly sand. Thin leaf litter.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: On upper slope of gravely knob. Supercanpy of 65-75cm Pinus strobus over canopy of 25-30cm Acer saccharum and Tilia. Large Betula in vicinity. Large decaying pine log down center of plot. Tip-up mounds. Continuous 1-2 inch needle and leaf duff. Silty/sandy soil. Fire scar on one pine.

On steep north facing slope above wetland kettle. Continuous canopy of 20-45cm diameter Thuja. Large birch logs down in stand. 1 very large well-decayed stump in plot. Thin but continuous litter of cedar leaves and twigs. Dark silty soil with much organic matter. Deer trail through plot. Occasional moss cover on boulders and stones.

In pine grove on slope of bedrock hill with pine groves and open areas with exposed rock. Canopy trees 15-45cm diameter; largest ones open grown. Fire scars on trees. No cut stumps. 2 large pines down in plot. Thin soil over bedrock. Abundant mosses.
In plot 4,1 of 1ha permanent plot. 1-2 degree northwest-facing slope. Dead wood cover = 1.1. 0-1cm litter layer of last year's leaves and wood. A horizon = silt loam. Site moderately well drained.
In plot 2.2 of 1 ha permanent plot 1-2 degree south facing slope. Litter absent. Dead wood = 1.1. Standing dead trees (Acer saccharum, Ostrya) "=+.1." A horizon = silty loam.
On 0-5 degree north facing slope. Well drained. Approximately 15 year old downed logs of cf Acer saccharum and cf Quercus.
20 degree east southeast facing slope. Litter is this years leaves and wood (logs and stumps = 2.2). Soil well-drained loam.
Nearly all the tamarack in this stand are being debarked by an insect.
Almost on county line Marshall/Roseau Counties, east of a small lake, right next to ditch. Hard to judge whether to call wet meadow or shrub swamp.
Pole aspen 15-20cm DBH, open and dry, on fine sandy soil. Disturbed regeneration stand, probably re-invaded pasture.
Southwest of stunted aspen/birch heath.
Birch heath, very monotonous and homogeneous, weird area.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: Circled back southeast toward section line road. Very young (probably a result from fire), difficult to judge whether this is aspen forest regeneration or shrub swamp.
Lowland aspen, open canopy. Soil a bit friable, unconsolidated forest peat to at least 40 cm.
One of the oddest communities I've ever been in. Appears to be a tamarack swamp in which aspen has replaced the tamarack. Maybe after a fire, but the peat not burned out.
Structurally diverse, but floristically un-interesting. Southwest of small pond.
Mid-age aspen with open D3 and continuous ericaceous understory. NW of releve 05. Soil: brown unconsolidated course, decomposed woody peat to at least 40cm.
Very open ericaceous heath, so thick that scarcely anything else grows here.
White area on photo. Burned over area with much dead down apsen - DBH 15-20 cm.
Choked with ericads, no physical space for anything else to grow.

Mature spruce barred ground layer probably result of deer/moose yarding 25% dry litter. About 200m northeast of releve 175-14. Extent of conifers not large enough to account for extent of red signature on photo.
Small circular bog just west of Hwy 54. Mature spruce DBH >10cm. Very sparse ground cover, 100% dry moss, very depauperate.
Releve size is 100 rather than 400 because the tamarack area is not 400 square meters and the canopy is extremely open. Not sure how to classify this area. Some open pools with charcoal.
About 30-40% bare litter in ground layer.
Small wetland, probably impacted by two roads. Soil: muck, water table 9cm, sp cond = 192. Ecological group 3
Small wetland. Soil muck, 10 cm to water table; sp. cond = 204. Ecological group 1.
Soil muck, 5cm to water table; sp. cond =243, pH=6.5 Ecological group 3.
Small wetland near road and Otter Creek. Soil muck, 18cm to water table; sp cond = 432, pH= 5.9. Ecological group 2.
Soil muck, 3 cm to water table, sp cond=158. Location uncertain.
Large peatland adjacent to lake. Soil muck over sand, 43 cm to water table, sp cond =161; ecological group 1. Location questionable, no wetland on topo map.
At head of King Creek; road up slope, possible impact? Soil muck, 36cm to water table; sp cond =71. Ecological group 3.
Large wetland adjacent to Park Lake. Soil muck, 37cm to water table. Sp cond. = 345. Ecological group 1. Location in doubt.
Soil muck, 22cm to water table, sp. cond =159. Ecological group = 2. Location uncertain.
Off highwat 210. Soil muck, 30cm to water table, sp, cond, =218. Ecological group 1. Same as releve 5722?
Soil muck over loam, 53cm to water table; sp. cond. = 272. Ecological group 1. Location may be slightly off.
Very small wetland. Soil muck over loamy sand, 76 cm to water table; sp. cond. =217. Ecological group 1.
Soil:muck over sandy loam, 33 cm to water table; sp. cond. =254. Small strip along Gillespie Brook.
Soil muck, 37cm to water table; sp. cond. = 215, pH=6.0. Ecological group 3.
Large wetland adjacent to road. Soil: muck over sandy clay loam, 84cm to water table, sp. cond. =433; pH= 6.8. Ecological group 1.
Soil: muck over sandy loam, 12cm to water table, sp. cond. =168. Ecological group 3. Location uncertain; no wetland on topo, slightly sloping.
Soil: muck over sandy clay loam, 82 cm to water table; sp. cond. =249, pH=5.9. Ecological group 2. Location uncertain, no wetland on topo, slightly sloping.
Soil: muck over clay; 84cm to water table; sp. cond. =645; pH=5.7. Ecological group 2. Location questionable. No wetland on topo map.
Large peatland, no ditches. Soil muck; 29 cm to water table, sp. cond. =128, pH=5.7. Ecological group 3.
Soil muck, 6.5 cm of water table; sp. cond. =119. Ecological group 3.
Soil muck, water at surface; sp. cond. =181, pH=6.2. Ecological group 2. Small wetland along stream?
Soil muck, water at surface, sp cond = 103, pH=5.8 Ecological group 2.

Native prairie on west facing slope of Des Moines River Valley. Used as pasture. Degraded in valley with steep northwest and southeast slopes B-C quality, very large population of Lespedeza leptostachya A quality.
Sample area marked on soil map, on mesic Nicollet soil, south of permanent stakes marking Habernaria.
Area has been cut long time ago- biggest stump: cedar 38" at cut about 18" above ground.
Exact location not known, but the old growth northern hardwoods is on a south facing slope below and east of the Hovland Lookout Tower. Ground cover: litter 35%, deadfall 5%, herbaceous 60%.
Southwest facing slope - midslope dry/drymesic soil with stones at the surface.
Dry mesic prairie on gently sloping, well drained, deep dark colored solis on the Big Stone Moraine. Area has history of haying.
Low flat terrace adjacent to Big Stone Lake on deep poorly drained dark colored soils. Mesic to wet prairie. Associated with seeps, area hayed occasionally. Grazed in the past.
Well drained silty clay loam soils over Souix Quartzite bedrock. Area burned in April 1983. Nearly level site with prairie ranging from dry to wet-mesic.
Annually mowed dry-mesic to wet-mesic prairie on Germantown clay loam soils with areas of Sioux Quartzite outcrops.
Lightly grazed prairie on Germantown clay loam soils with extensive Sioux quartzite rock outcrops. Level to gently sloping mesic to dry mesic quartzite prairie and quarzite outcrop communities.

Annually mowed prairie on Germantown clay loam soils with shallow depth to bedrock (Souix quartzite). Dry mesic to mesic prairie on level land. Portions of area drilled with red clover. Area lightly grazed.

Dry-mesic prairie on west northwest-facing mid to upper slope. Part of series of grazed hill prairies along Chanarambie Creek, which cuts through Bemis Moraine. Small prairie remnant with much lighter past grazing.
Dry to mesic prairie on Ihlen soils wih extensive areas of Souix Quartzite outcrops. Mesic soil over bedrock; area burned fall 1981, 10 to 15 acres of undisturbed prairie in area.
5-10 degree southwest facing slope. Well drained loamy silt, dark grey. Leaf litter (this years). Decayed wood 2.1, approximately 25 years old. No specific map location.

On 0-5 degree north-facing gently rolling site in southeast part of woods. Leaf layer 5cm. A horizon = 10cm fine sandy loam, dark grey, grading to medium to light brown grey. Abundant earthworm casts on surface.

Approximately 20m south and 20m east of permanent plot stake 0,5 in southeast part of woods. 0-2 degree south facing slope. Rotting wood =2.2. O-horizon absent. Soil cf. lester series, B-horizon=loamy sand.
Located ca 60m southeast of permanent plot stake 0,5 in southeast part of woods. Slope = 1-2 NE. Rotting wood =2.1. O horizon absent.
In plot 3,4 of 1 ha permanent plot. 0-2 south facing slope. approximately 2cm? this year's leaf litter over mineral soil, sand loam A horizon. Downed wood (Acer branch) cover=1.1.
In plot 0,4 of 1 ha permanent plot 0-3 degree south facing slope 3-4cm of this year's leaves over mineral soil. Sandy loam, A horizon >15cm. Well drained.
In plot 0,4 of 1 ha permanent plot. On 0-5 NW-facing slope. Well- drained. One wind-fall hollow, wood common on forest floor.
In plot 4,4 of 1 ha permanent plot. On 0-5 east facing slope. Moderately well drained. Litter layer this fall's leaves only. One large red oak.
In plot 3,4 of 1 ha permanent plots. 1-2 degree southwest-facing slope. Well drained.

In plot 4,0 of the 1 ha permanent plot. 2-5 degree northwest-facing slope. Well drained. Soil= OL/OF/15cm A/ sandy loam. Dead wood=1.1. 102cm diameter Quercus rubra and 56cm diameter Acer Saccharum in plot.
I plot 1,2 of 1ha permanent plot. 0-2 S facing slope. Dead branches and boles of Ostrya, Acer Saccharum, and Quercus rubra.
In plot 3,0 of 1 ha permanent plot. 2-3 degree northwest-facing slope. 1-5% cover down wood (Acer saccharum). Organic layer this year's leaves only. A-horizon = 15cm thick.
5-10 southeast facing slope (steeper in the southeast corner of plot.) Exact location not known.
In plot 4,0 of 1 ha permanent plot. 1 standing dead Acer saccharum in D7 layer. Largest Acer = 80.1 cm diameter.
5 degree southeast facing slope. Litter is this year's leaves only. Dead wood= 1.1. Racoon scat.
Exact location not known.
Between trail and creek near 1 ha permanent plot. 5% north facing slope. Well drained.
On top of knoll due southeast of location marker 12 on Wolsfield Woods SNA map. Level to slightly sloping. Quercus rubra <71cm diam, Acer saccharum <40cm, Tilia <44cm.
In parts of plots 3,0 and 4,0 of 1 ha permanent plot. Down wood, 1.1.
Resurvey of 1979 the nature conservancy intern (Lustvig) survey. (See releve #6665). Xeric. Gopher and ant mounds. Burned periodically for the past 25 years.

Xeric. Mineral soil 98% ground cover. Ant and gopher mounds; burned fall 1987. Prunus virgiana would have been tall shrub last year--fire knocked it back to herbaceous level. 50% of canopy is Quercus ellipsoidalis. Plot is 72m south of Anoka Elec Coop powerline (pole #11667) and 13m south of sedge swale. Metal conduit at 4(?) corners; aluminum tag (#619) on conduit at NE corner. "Nearly on top of" surveyor plot# USMNSSALLI01.01 (DNRrel#5685) from 7Jul1988.

54 year Populus grandidentata with open-ground red pine 67 years old. Large pine stumps. Many tip up mounds. Soil: 10-12" loam cap over gravelly sand. Ground cover: litter - 93%, moss - 2%, slash - 5%.
50 year old aspen stand. Loam over gravelly sand. Ground cover: litter - 91%, rocks - 2%, slash - 5%.
66 year old aspen. Ground cover: litter - 95%, moss - 2%, slash - 3%.
Abnormal open look. 64 year old Populus grandidentata. Excessive hypoxylon canker. (Soil pit data on original.). Ground cover: litter - 75%, moss - 1%, slash - 4%.
Two story stand. 47 year old. Esker: gravel loam (10cm) over gravelly sandy loam. Ground cover: litter - 90%, moss - 2%, slash - 5%, rock - 3%.
Young stand (31 years.). Soil: Omega sand. Ground cover: litter - 90%, slash - 10%.

Soil: wetter variant of 510 Ameck (Mora variant). Young stand (29 years). No evidence of logging. Small (14") ditch runs through plot. Ground cover: litter - 90%, moss - 1%, slash - 3%, grass - 5%, rock - 1%.
45 year old stand. Soil: 10" loam over coarse loamy sand. Ground cover: litter - 76%, slash - 7%, grass - 10%, rocks - 5%.
Stand age= 40 yrs. Soil: 510(Ameek) looks moist. Small 6" ditch runs through plot. Ground cover: litter - 85%, moss - 2%, slash - 5%, grass - 5%, rock - 2%, bare ground - 1%.
Young stand, 29 years old. Ground cover: litter - 86%, slash - 10%, grass - 2%, rocks - 1%, mineral - 1%.
44 year old stand on top of knoll; intermediate moist site. Pine stumps with fire scars.
Seasonally inundated pond. At present soil saturated. Soil is muck. Slopes slightly toward middle of basin which has some standing water Surrounded by floodplain forest.
Soil muck. Plot is on east edge of Spring Banks Lake, in narrow zone (~15m), west of floodplain forest. Soil saturated. Small stream just S of the plot.
Frequent old stumps. Canopy of multiple-stemmed  silver maple, dbh 31- 59cm, Soil alluvial (silt). Vermillion River floodplain. Woody debris from flooding common.

Releve generated for entire tract? Max caonpy dominants 25-39", although average considerably smaller. Dense Laportea in ground layer with other species restricted to marginal areas. Very little litter. Some logging.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Releve of unknown size in 12 acre stand. Max diameter canopy trees = 20-36 inches, some open grown. Site with 0-5 degree slopes. Silty loam soil (cf. hayden). Stumps > 5 years old. Windthrown logs.

Releve of unknown size in 25-acre stand. Max diameter canopy trees = 22 to 48". 0-10 degree slopes. Sandy loam. Leaf litter absent in much of stand, but much twig and branch litter. North half with thin leaf litter, greater diversity other herbs and smaller trees.
0.5 ha releve in 10-acre stand. Max diameter canopy tree = 22 to 34".  0-10 slope, mostly east and north facing. On silty loam till. Some stumps (>10 years old). Litter mostly this years.
0.1 ha releve in basswood-elm forest in south facing ravine with ca. 10 degree slopes. Tilia to 37" diameter; Ulmus to 33" diameter.
0-3 slope, well-drained. Silty loam soil. Down wood. Diamond Creek Woods.
Basswood-elm forest on north facing ravine slope. Max diameter canopy trees = 18". Basswood multi-stemmed.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: 5-acre releve in least disturbed part of woods. On gently sloping upland and northeast facing slope. Quercus rubra to 25" diameter. On grey till. Fire scars on trees indicate at least 2 ground fires in 40 years.
Diamond Creek Woods. 0.5 hectare releve. 0-5 slope. on cf Hayden soil over till.  12" x 20" puff ball in woods!

0.8 ha releve (includes vernal pool). Max diameter canopy trees = 20-44". 0-10 degree slopes, mostly north east and west facing. Soil = 18" black silty loam over yellow brown silty clay loam. Large > 80 year old Acer. Quercus stumps present.
On 0-5 east facing site, well drained. 3-5cm this years litter, 1-2cm old litter. Soil loam, friable, dry. No browsing noted. Windthrow isolated and rare. Taylor's Woods.

Odd shaped releve 10x5 to keep in community type. Soil profile poorly defined (may have been churned by hooves in past - but): 10cm somewhat peaty black loam over 5cm black clay over coarse grey sand. Half of surface of releve is bare mud.
Large homogeneous rich ren in north central part of tract.
Island at north end of rich fen in MN DNR Releve #6721 (58-02).

Heavily hummocked, formerly grazed, burned in last 5 years (wild fire). Heavily compacted black clay loam won't give a core. Disappointing-base of ridge-expected calcareous seepage zone because of nearby ditch.

Done on the same field trip as DNR # 266. On 0-2 degree north facing slope, well drained. Tip-up mounds and downed trees present. This year's leaf litter = 2.5cm; old litter patchy <1cm. A horizon 8 cm loam, B horizon to 20+cm, silty loam.  Soil dry.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: East of Newfolden fen.
East of Newfolden fen. Much litter.
Recently burned area just north of section line.

Overgrown prairie in graveyard on east side of Beaulieu, dating from turn of century, last used in world war two. Small area, releve extends from top of knoll to area adjacent to wetland. Not a CBS site. Releve purpose to garner potential list of flora in patative oak savanna zone of county.

Oak fores (overgrown woodland?) along west flank of beach ridge between gravel pit and brush prairie. Very narrow band of woodland just wide enough for releve plot. Disturbed, grazed formerly cut. Fine sandy black loam over gravel.

Aspen unevenly distributed, DBH mostly 10-15cm, up to 25cm. Stand burned recently: dead Corylus tops to 2m common-sprouting. Down logs well-decayed, up to 20cm DBH, mostly oak. Plot not measured out but area sampled is ca 400 square meters.

Soil probe: approximately 15cm dark brownish-gray loamy sand over orange-brown sand. Some Betula glandulifera, but not in plot. In places aspen saplings. Up to 5m common. No evidence of past disturbance, except Poa pratensis.
Oak generally not as common as in plot. A few charred aspen snags. Large woodland "island" in vast rich fen. No disturbance other than fire.
Soil probe: dark grayish black loamy sand, approximately 8cm, then pale yellowish gray moderate fine sand. No signs of past cutting or grazing. Charring on down logs, snags.

Soil approximately 10cm black loamy sand, then pale yellowish gray moderate fine sand. Apart from mature aspen, no clear layers. Generally densest at 2-3m. Large aspen logs in varying stages of decay are moderately common. Charcoal on snags and logs.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: Number of small to medium elm logs on ground and snags. Mature birch widely scattered, no juveniles. Black ash localized to what appears to be a seepage zone in very gentle slope.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: Several down logs, well rotted (one large birch) to recent. One large aspen snag. Soil dark gray silty loam over brown gray sand (hand probe). Apparent seep zone in 3 sec block of aspen. Not typical of this large block.
Plot size only approximate. Part of 3-section block of aspen woodland forest on sandy soils.
Plot only approximate. Large, mostly well-decayed down logs common. Part of plot very wet.
Sample area approximately 400 square meters. Open, brushy spot in 3 section block of aspen forest-woodland. Soil probe: Dark grey sand over light colored sand.

Plot not actually measured out, but area sampled approximately 400 square meters. In 3-section block of aspen forest-woodland. Thin, black organic-rich layer over sand. No signs of cutting, grazing. Wetter than #6743.

Plot not actually measured out but area sampled approx 400 square meters. In 3-section block of aspen forest-woodland. Soil gray sand over yellowish to orange sand(hand probe). No signs of cutting or grazing. No recent fire.
Plot not actually marked out, area sampled approximately 400 square meters. Plot in high area; boulders at surface, vegetation brush-prairie transition to woodland.
Plot not marked out-area sampled approximatley 400 square meters. Plot ungrazed but may have some grazing history. Nearby area fenced, grazed; exotic grasses much more prominent in grazed area.
Releve boundary not actually marked, but area sampled approximately 400 square meters.
Plot not actually marked out, but area sampled approximately 400 square meters. No evidence of past cutting or grazing.
Plot not actually measured out, but area sampled approximately 400 square meters. In somewhat poorly drained area close to river, behind slightly higher levee. No evident human disturbance.
Stand is very small and transected by an ATV trail, community grades northeast into alder swamp. Upslope communities have been cleared for field between here and remnant aspen/oak.
Wind damaged stand, don't know how to rank. Aspen sustained greatest wind damage. Pole elm unscathed. This stand is on sand. Canopy cover was reduced from I to P by storm and aspen from 3 to 1.
This releve is an attempt to get into natural vegetation at interface of Bagley outwash and Alexandria moraine (very difficult because nearly all OW cut and converted to plantation).
On a knob. Excellent signature on photo, but disappointing on ground.
On Bagly outwash plain, south of McCraney Lake.
Top of hill north of kidney shaped lake and south of snowmobile turn, north of Sucker Lake.

Island in a tamarack swamp. One of few stands actually called oak in CSA. Probably so mesic because very little elevation above surrounding tamarack swamp. Ground layer feels grazed. Presence of Xanthoxylum strange.
There is a considerable area that is this species poor, could not find a better placement to get a richer releve.
On slender ridge.
Dominated by Spartina, less forby than the WMA. Inactive pasture.
Despite the longer list of prairie forbs, Poa is the dominant grass.
Just east of eastern most circular feature right along fenceline.
This is the "Waubun prairie" of Itasca Biological Station fame, but its quality is no better than most Mahnomen County prairies. West side.
This is a beautiful level fen-lower in elevation than surrounding prairie, but too dry, extensive area with islands of Salix bebbiana and Betula glandulosa.
Mature sugar maple- this should be an old growth candidate or replacement stand. Exceptional maturity, wonderful photo signature. Grant-in- aid snowmobile trail. 60% open litter- stand 2 NH 54.
Distinctive sulfer odor on ground. pH 6.9
Hasty releve on account of stirring up a hornet's nest!
South of creek not for S of ditchline, south of a low emergent marsh. In open area NE of highest part of wetland, about 15m S of creek. Transitional comm between wer pr seepage subtype & calc fen.
Very fine A ranked oak, good oak signature on photo. No stumps although recent selective logging of Aspen in mixed stand southwest of here.
Tribal biologists are managing with intermittent fire.
.3 miles north of county gravel pit, appears to have been previously grazed. Not an ideal stand, but difficult to find hardwood on Bagley outwash in this area.
Seepage area west of tracks this may be an eastern transitional outlier of the Wanbun calcareous fen. No open pools.
Wet prairie between aspen and burned oak. Releve has a small inclusion of wetter area.
Unsurpasses A rank steep hill, but no bare ground. This hill discontin uous from the others, which probably accounts for higher rank.
Grazed south-facing slope.
Steep south facing slope that is actually grazed from time to time. Area used for off-road motorcycle races in late 40s through early 1960's.
Grey green smooth signature on map, actually grazed and still excellent quality. Clearly dominated by native grasses.
West facing hill, bottom slope. As nice a grazed prairie as I've ever seen anywhere. There are cowpies in here and it is still this good.
Grey signature on photo north and west of county gravel pit. Top of gentle northwest facing slope of actively grazed prairie pasture.
Flat area west of hill by powerline trail-very recoverable area.
Releve in flat break between hills where powerline turns south to show condition of degraded prairie/ active pasture.  This area shows fine red linear strips on aerial photo.
This releve for getting data from Plantanthera monitoring plots. Location permanently marked by orchid baseline.
4 inches standing water (after week of rain).
Seepage zone at interface of rich fen and prairie. Long skinny releve 5x20 to match distribution of community.
Opening in aspen woodland, 50% forb cover, area being burned 5% bare ground. Releve reflects what happens when fire is used in established aspen in aspen parkland area.
Being burned for commercial prairie seed harvest. It has been burned hard two years in a row.
Oak woodland in east side of prairie-wetland complex. 1m tall shrub layer. Has appearance of savanna, but probably from former grazing? Wildfire in last 10 years.
More Dirca in this stand than in most maple basswood stands, generally indicates a rich site. Topographic context: upper/middle.

This is a very small fen dome with bot birch and Potentilla. Hummocked. It is very small and a very distinctive mound that looks disturbed from a distance. Hummocked - may have been disturbed in past but not in owners memory.
BIA compartment 31 stand 6. Lowland hardwood inclusion along an intermittent stream. Entire releve area subject to surface sheet flow of water on day of visit. Not anomalous releve shape.
BIA compartment 31, stand 6. Max DBH of Quercus rubra is 62cm, Populus tremuloides to 45. Much dead and down large birch ~30cm DBH, wood has decayed. Stand year of origin recorded as 1902 (BIA).

This releve represents the type of situation in which birch becomes abundant in these mixed mesic hardwood forests. It should not be used in ordinations of the vegetation as a whole. BIA comp 31, stand 6.
Natural boreal hardwood conifer. Fir zone on northeast-facing slope, typical position for fir dominated in these otherwise hardwood forests. Fair amount of blowdown elm and fir.
Too degraded for an EO.

Total stand size may be 2 acres. I think this is a pine stand of natural origin. Right by Clearwater county line. Interior of stand dark, dry shaded by heavy Acer saccharum. Species concentrated at east edge of stand. Average pine DBH 40-50cm.
Releve in and around a swale about 10x20 because ephemeral pond swale is that small. This is an ephemeral pond inclusion in a northern hardwood stand.
Open oak, probably from logging, forest with disturbed canopy (?) rather than woodland. Average DBH 25-35cm. Because of proximity to stream this may be heavily degraded gallery forest.

Heavily disturbed woodlot adjacent to Sand Hill River. Formerly grazed with heavy resulting Xanthoxylum. Releve represents best area. Releve in area not presently being logged but much present and past selective logging.
Very small area, probabaly 1-2 acres at most of less degraded area within a CD rank matrix with too much Carex pensylvanica and Xanthoxylum.
Edge of ephemeral pond - Releve is about 10m wide and 20m long.
Red shoulder hawk area near Goodwin Lake. Ground cover mainly bare litter ~ mixed maple and oak. Near a small pond. Max DBH Tilia ca 50cm, Betula ca 40m Acer ca 30, Populus ca 45cm.
Releve in orchid monitoring plot. No releve permanent marker, but plot is permanently marked. Releve is standard size around plot.
Outlier of Mentor Ranch not surveyed in 1994. Platanthera praeclara found in this tract by Ross Heir in 1996, Upland sand piper, 1995.
Very small area of too forby wet prairie/fen in an area otherwise completely overpowered by cattails.
Pretty heavily grazed-for comparison with immediately adjacent ungrazed releve.
Very homogeneous rich fen south and east of old feedlot area where the yellow rails are. Almost a turf of Carex sartwelli. Topographic context: depression/flat.
North of an area dominated by Typha. Homogeneous rich fen.
Northeast end site 22. Top of hill on level pennisula. Rough signature on photo south of emergent marsh. Feels like a "restoration" not a natural community.
Not sure if highly degraded priarie or old field. Just south of tallest clump of aspen. Probably prairie. Very forby.
This brushy area is not degraded prairie it is a nice example of brush prairie.
Somewhat circular wet brush prairie - southeast from field and then east through dense willow. This 0E of the willow. Soil: black clay loam over fine lighter colored sand at about .25 m.

Soil about 5 cm loam over grey clay turning to whitish yellow clay at depth of probe handle. Extensive area of circular wet brush prairie; like a lawn of Sporobolus not more than 30m south of that releve.
About 5 cm sandy peat overlying grey fine sand.

npc_type_name: Green Ash - Bur Oak - Elm Forest

remarks: Whole area so heavily shaded by Corylus that there is very little ground cover (ca 35%) The rest is bare litter. Opening on topography is solid Corylus.
Brushy area between open fen and oaks.
Open rich fen north of road across from extensive fen on south.
This prairie-like area appears to be disturbed (by management) and is probably not an example of a natural community. Not a very good releve - not well placed on ground.
Probably an old field - at least manipulated in some way- very rough area. Feels like brush prairie that was broken one time and allowed to succeed back?
Very disturbed ambiance in this area.
About 75% open litter and moss cover. No D3-4 layer at all. Heavily used by ungulates and very dry feeling.
Very structurally choppy stand. Hummock and hollow microtopography. Very wet.
Narrow band of Ooak between trail and wetlands to west. West of small field.
Black signature on NAPP photo west of old field. Very open aspect almost like a floodplain forest, some areas with no tall shrub layer. DBH of some trees to 40 cm.
Sphagnum majus pools in W internal water track. Sinuous linear hummocks. Water table at surface. Bryophytes >90%, lichens <5%; vascular plants >80%; water <10%.
Eastern internal tract; water filled hollows; high sphagnum hummocks with  ???    many of which are dead. Water <10%, vascular plants >90%, lichens <5%, bryophytes >70%.
Sphagnum- Carex oligosperma lawn; near western crest; continuous Sphagnum lawn; isolated pocket of spruce. Bryophytes 100%; lichens.
Burned by wildfire spring 1990. Plot is narrow zone of dry savanna/ scrub on broad, well-defined glacial lake beach ridge. No disturbance away from highway, sampled area only approximate.
In narrow shrubby zone at beach ridge base, just below zone of dense, large tamarack. Pocket meter pH: 7.7-7.9 in pools. Thin muck over fine sand. Sampled area approximate, no disturbance.
Mesic site, much recent aspen mortality. Much charring of snags, down logs (small). Sandy loam soil; stones topped probe at approximately 10 cm. Sample area only approximate.
Wet/wet-mesic site. Much recent aspen mortality. Few larger down logs. Well-decayed, much charring. Sandy loam soil; stones stopped probe at approximately 10 cm. Sample area approximate.
On broad, level beach ridge crest. Dry brush prairie becoming woodland thicket. Ungrazed at time; but grazed in past (last year most recent). Sampled area only approximate.
On broad, level beach ridge crest. Ungrazed at time, but grazed in past (last year most recent). Sampled area only approximate. Plot in most open part of stand.
On very gently convex crest of beach ridge of Glacial Lake Aggassiz, close to west (lake) side of broad beach ridge. Black loamy sand approximately 6 inches thick. Gravel at 8-9 inches.

Brushy oak savanna just off beach ridge crest (Hwy 11 along crest). Prairie species - lead plant, porcupine grass, prairie dropseed, sand reed grass- are concentrated near upper edge of plot, near highway.
Old cut stumps to south, but not in immediate area sampled. coarse woody debris ca 10% of ground surface. Wildlife openings cut elsewhere in woods.
Burned in wildfire spring or previous fall; shrub height reduced. Not grazed. No evidence of cutting. Woodland patch in wet to wet-mesic brush prairie matrix.
Large continuous woodland north side of Two Rivers. Soil probe: sandy loam, stony at 15cm. Charcoal on some snags. Lots of coarse woody debris, but no really old logs. No sign of cutting.
Soil is sand or loamy sand. Occassioanl well-decayed aspen logs on ground. In extensive block of aspen woodland/forest north of Two Rivers. Plot in slightly convex area. No signs of disturbance.

In large block woodland/forest north of Two Rivers. Plot in young aspen; widely scattered mature trees still standing. Old logs on ground. Few old stumps up to 1.5m high, well charred. Black sandy loam.
In large block of aspen woodland/forest north of Two Rivers. Plot in mesic area. Lots of large down logs. Mature trees common. Soil dark gray fine sand over lighter fine sand. No signs of cutting.

In large block aspen woodland/forest. North of Two Rivers. Plot in wet-mesic area. Large down logs occasional. Mature trees common. Soil dark gray, silty fine sand over lighter fine sand. No signs of cutting.
Woodland ecotone between prairie and large wetland. Burned in 1989. A few large decayed logs on ground. No signs of cutting. Soil is sand.
Part of large block of aspen woodland/forest. Burned in wildfire '89, but no tree mortality. Small down logs common, no large ones. Lots of charred wood. No signs of cutting.
Small upland "island" in wetland. Soil loam or fine sandy loam over course sand. Several dead trees down near plot. No signs of disturbance except exotic herbs.

Large patch of woods. Down logs, poles common, various stages of decay. Soil probe: 10cm dark gray sandy loam over pale gray fine sand. No signs of grazing, cutting. Some areas here with dense tall hazel layer.

Sampled area only approx. Mature jack pine super-canopy over young aspen woodland. Pines dying; reproduction only in nearby agric areas. Soil very sandy. Stand at west limit of jack pine in Minnesota.
In the densest pine signature (red) possible.
Managed (formerly hayed) dry-mesic to mesic prairie on Germantown clay loam with extensive areas of Sioux Quartzite outcrops. Well-drained level to gently sloping site. Burned May 1983.
Releve compiled from 2 transects through Cornus-Rhus and Carex stricta - Phalaris zones of swamp. See report of September 2, 1985. Very long species list probably not useful for analysis.
0.4 ha releve on disturbed prairie (dominated by Poa pratensis). On course loamy sand on 5-20 degree east facing slope.
Distrubed prairie currently being grazed by dairy herd. On course loamy sand. Well-drained rolling crest.
Releve in Nerstrand woods, parcel 5 ca 20m? South southwest of fence at northeast corner of parcel 5, section 9.

In Nerstrand Woods, Sec 16, lot 23 of Harriet Mason, northeast corner of lot. Approximately 15m south of road. Level site, loamy silt soil. Some small diam woody debris. some cut stumps. 2x4m pit with concrete chunks nearby.
In Nerstrand Woods State Park, sec 9 lot 23, west of Hidden Falls.
In Nerstrand Woods, sec 9, woodlot #1. On 8% east facing slope. Soil: A horizon = silty loam. This falls litter only. Approximately 30 year old Acer saccharum stumps (cov = "+.1").
In Nerstrand Woods sec 9, lot 13N, level, moderately well-drained site
In Nerstrand Woods. Harriet Mason's lot 4. 3-4 degree north facing slope. Well drained. Tip-up mounds = 1.1. Acer saccharum stumps = r.1

In Nerstrand Woods, west side of Fawn Trail along creek below falls. Area clearcut approximately 1938. Well drained 1-2 cm litter on silt loam. Down wood (branches, small trees)= 1.1. Stumps ="+.1" (Acer saccharum, Quercus).
In Nerstrand Woods, west of ravine west of picnic area. 1-2 degree north facing slope, moderately well-drained. 0-1 cm litter on alfisol on loess. No stumps. 1 clump of dead oak, fallen.
Approximatley 0-2ha releve on 0-10 degree slopes and knolls. Silty loam mollisol over till. Not mowed or grazed this year.
Lightly grazed (17 cattle/50 acres) dry-mesic prairie on upper north facing slopes (>25%). Droughty Buse loam soils with rocks on the surface. On Bemic moraine in Prairie Coteau landscape.
Ca. 1ha releve on 0-5 degree slopes. Moderately to poorly drained site. Bromus inermis becoming abundant in southern part of site.
Size of releve unknown. On 0-2 degree slopes on very fine sand loam mollisol over outwash. Abundant Poa pratensis and (cover 3) Solidago canadensis (cover 3).
Releve of unknown size on 30-45 degree west-facing slope above creek.

Ca 0.01ha releve on level to gently sloping site near wetland. Area has been sprayed with herbicide, especially near road where damage is evident in Solidago. Spraying was probably for thistle control.

Releve of unknown size on level terrain near edge of cattail marsh. Used as pasture, but not recently prior to 1971. Burned every spring to prevent encroachment by trees and shrubs. Best in county in 1971.

16 square meter releve on south end of Lakeville-soil ridge, just south of gravel pit. West facing 10-20 degree slope. Gravel soil. On formerly cultivated land-prairie species with abundant Poa compressa.
Down logs "+.1"; tip-up mounds r.1; exposed boulders (ground level)"+.1."

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Bohall trail, crest of 1600' knoll, south of Snail Lake, southeast of Vulture's nest. Down logs (Populus, Pinus)1.1. Stumps and snags.
Campground stand. Sandy loam till, top of the hill. Moderately well-drained, rolling moraine. Charcoal in soil. Resurvey of 6936 and 6937.
Bohall trail in north edge of plot, just west of Buell's line between fir-spruce and maple-basswood. 0-2 degree slope, top of knoll. 1-4cm A horizon.
Inside Mary Lake exclosure, center, just south of hare fence. Pinus strobus bent by 1977 snow "+.2."  Blister-rust on Pinus strobus. Red pine with 3 fire scars. Resurvey attached to form.

east side of Tamarack Lake, 40 miles south of South Tamarac access road. 0-1 degree slope southwest, moderate drainage. tip-up mounds "+.1", relief to 0.3m. Estimated "50+" years old. Exposed boulders "+.1" on tip-ups. Fairly homogeneous.

About 50m south of Two Spot Trail, 200m east of Dead Beaver Lake. Tip-up mounds "+.1", relief 0.5m. Charred Pinus snags to 2m "+.1." Cut and charred stumps "+.1." Diameter to 45cm. Soil very dry, hard. Two cored trees - 23cm DHB Quercus borealis, 50 rings; 30.1cm DBH Populus grandidentata, 63 rings.
Twin Island Lake Stand, 50m from road. Tip-up mounds "+.1", relief 0.7m.

1m west of Novy. Area is rolling moraine; forest has been cut over and burned estimated 40 years ago. Pinus strobus >50 years, cut and charred stumps. 750 years old. Tip-up mounds "+.1." Exposed boulders. Max relief .8m.
About 60m in from east shore of west arm of Lake Itasca, opposite Boutwell creek. Small grove of Ostrya, ca 0.06 ha. Fairly homogeneous. Old tip-ups 2.1 dead wood 1.1, 2 deer trails.
Lake George pine stand. Unknown location, not mapped, Nice releve however. Decided to enter. Gave lat long to the center of lake George.
South west of Snail Lake 4 cm O horizon, A horizon - 2cm sandy loam, E horizon 6-8cm of sandy loam, B1 to 15cm sandy loam, and B2 mottled, silty loam till.
Bohall trail, east of Buell's line, mapped location an estimate. O horizon 3cm; A horizon 2cm; 8cm E horizon, 15cm B1.
Just east of Bear Paw campground. Sandy loam soil, exposed boulders "+.1"; tip-up mounds r.1 (relief 0.7m).
Well drained, large tip-up mound 1m relief, boulders "+.1." Betula, Tilia, Quercus, and other logs 1.1. 1cm of litter over sandy loam till.

Point opposite Schoolcraft Island. Moderately drained stand on medium sand. Tip-up mounds 2.1 relief <0.4m. Down logs 2.1, well rotted. Vegetation on point outside plot - heterogeneous. Much wind damage. Openings created by Betula blowdowns.
Ca. 25cm east of Deer Park Trail, between Myrtle Lake and Deer Park Lake. Microrelief 20cm, moderately drained. Deadfalls 1.1, estimated origin of Populus tremuloides (N=1)  1886.
Standing dead snags (Populus) "+.1." Down logs (Populus) "+.1"; cut stumps (Pinus, dbh <30cm) charred "+.1." Tip-up mounds 1.1. Relief 20m.
Tip-up mounds 1.1; relief 0.7m; logs rotted 1.1. 225m south of drive on trail; 20m east of trail. West of Lake Mary.
Down logs 1.1 (birch and aspen). Tip-ups "+.1", relief 4m. Exposed boulder "+.1" (ground level).

About 50m north of CL77-4; west of Lake Mary. Populus snags and logs, many remaining tops dying. 1 in 10 aspen in area are dead this summer. Most trunks heavily cracked. Soil: Loamy fine sand, friable; over sand loam till, stoney, friable; stones increase below 15cm.
Same stand as 5814-752. Moderately well-drained, low tip-up mounds common, down logs also common. Stumps: Pinus resinosa R.1; Populus tremuloides "+.1"; Tilia americana R.1.
Resurvey of releve 5814-751 (DNR #6936) one year later.
Well-drained plot with tip-up mounds "+.1"; relief 2m. 1956(?) blowdown of Abies and Betula 1.1. East end of Bohall Trial, west shore of Lake Itasca. Soil moist to 30cm.
Flat, poorly drained beside beaver worn ditch near tip of Snail Lake. Lake shore on organic soil to mineral soil. Open area with full sun.
Well-drained plot, tip-up mounds and deadfalls "+.1", Betula. 1cm litter.
Old tip-up mounds "+.1", Well drained top of slope.
Wilderness area immediately north of Bohall Trail. Location estimated.
Bear paw point - central ridge. Not mapped because location unknown, entered because location accurate to section.
0-5 degree slope. Moderately well-drained, knoll tip; tip-up mounds 1.1, down logs.
Bohall Trail ecotone stand -- south of trail. Location estimated. Sugar maple seedlings, about 100m west of releve over north of trail.
0.2 ha releve, moss peat hollows 1.1, relief 4 dm.

Releve of unknown size in 8 acre prairie on 3-15 degree west and northwest facing slopes. On sandy loam to gravelly loamy coarse sand. Draws draining adjacent cornfield have Agropyron, Bromus, and Helianthus.
0.5 ha releve in railroad prairie, includes well to poorly drained prairie. Fairly heterogeneous, but abundant Poa. Prairie also present NE10 and SE 3. RR since abandoned and cultivated (LAB 1999).
0.5 ha releve. Site reported to have been mowed previous year.
0.04 ha releve. Site with ca 2 dm relief. Mowed previous year.

Approximately 1 ha releve. Soil = mollisol on loam to 35cm, stoney beneath. Not mowed previous year. Wet area to the west avoided, it had Hordeum jubatum 2.3, Muhlenbergia asperifolia 3.3, Dist stri "+.2", and where disturbed Spartea.

This releve is located in a sand blowout, much of which is an approximately 25 degree mostly south to southwest-facing slope; there is a slight leve area to slight depression at the base of the blowout. The site still has some open sand, but the level areas have lichens. The sand on the slopes has not stabilized. The site is part of a complex of sand-based topography (much of it dunes). The releve occupied 25% of the blowout itself. Vertical distance from the base of the blowout to the ridge on the north edge is about 7 meters. Resurvey of 1979 releve #1 by SNA to study the Agassiz Dunes Preserve, representative of "aspen woods."

The releve occupies a site on the crest of a low, stabilized sand dune.  Within the boundaries several slope exposures exist, most of which face north to northeast; part of the releve is on the crest of the stabilized dune and that surface is nearly level; slope angle with the releve is probably not more than about 5 degrees; the site is part of a complex of sand dune and sand based topogrpahy.

The releve occupies a site which is only very gently undulating with some very minor microrelief differences. The site is mostly stabilized surface which consists of very sandy parent material which is part of a complex of sand dune and sadn0based topography. The topography surrounding the releve is also very gently undulating to nearly level in places.
The releve is located in a site which is nearly level and surrounded by nearly level topography with some scattered shallow depressions; the parent material is sand deposited.

The releve is located on a nearly level site surrounded by nearly level topography; soil parent material is and. Numerous bur oak seedlings established on the forest floor - 1995. The site in which releve #5 is located lies immediately southwest of the much more complex sand-dune topography.

The releve is located on a site which occupies a south to southeast-facing slope of an old stabilized sand-dune which is of relatively low height; surrounding topography i more complex with a fairly large, mostly stabilized dune to the east of the plot and topography to the northwest;a large, shallow depression lies to the east and south ot the releve although the southeast corner of the releve lies within this gentle depression. Soil parent material is sand.

The releve is located in a partially stabilized sand blowout; the releve itself includes the nearly level base of the blowout as well as portions of southwest, south, and southeast facing slopes; the slope angle is approximately 20 degrees but varies with exposure and slope position; the site still has some open sand although much of the more level topography at the base of the blowout supports a lichen cover; the slopes are still not completely stabilized although there is very little active dune movement; the site is part of a complex of sand-based topography. The releve occupies about 30% of the blowout itself. Vertical distance from the base of the blowout to the top of the slopes on the north edge is about 7 meters.
Plot in nearly level area slightly higher than surrounding prairie. Transitional between wet and mesic prairie. Very heavy litter accumulation estimation difficult.

Low, large swale slightly lower than surrounding area of mesic to wet-mesic. This releve is located on the beach complex of glacial prairie. Very heavy litter accumulation on this releve and a lot of grass and sedge cover made it difficult to separate species and estimate cover.
Plot in nearly flat to slightly depressional area. Very heavy litter accumulation in 1995. Several cottonwood trees west of plot nearly blown into releve.
Plot in area transitional between wet and mesic prairie. Soil a course sandy loam according to the 1980 report. Heavy litter accumulation made estimation difficult.
Plot flat to gently sloping with about 10-15cm microrelief. This area burned in Spring 1995: vegetation is lush and grasses average 1-2 meters tall.
Nearly level plot on low beach ridge.
Releve is in shallow depression on slight west facing slope of glacial lake shoreline. Transitional between mesic and wet mesic prairie. Soil: black clay loam.
Plot in gentle west facing glacial lake shoreline feature, on sandy, well drained soil.
Plot in shallow depression near base of low beach ridge. Heavy litter accumulation suppressing flowering.
Plot on upper slope of wave-cut glacial lake shoreline, on sandy, well drained soil. In formerly cultivated field, grazed for a time after.

Area of releve plowed in 1930 and grazed very heavily prior to it's acquisition by the TNC in the 1970s. Plot in upper slope below lake shoreline escarpment, on sandy soil. In filed cult. Originally dry or dry-mesic.
This area burned spring 1995. Plot in level area within glacial lake Shoreline complex. Soil sand and small rocks.
Plot in large swale and dry-mesic prairie. Much species change and aspen height increased from 1-3 meters.
Plot in swale within wet-mesic prairie. Some species changes noted and willow more common and taller. Willow seems to be displacing prairie. Soil: poorly drained fine sand and silt.
This releve occupies a nearly level site on a low ridge within the shoreline complex of glacial lake Agassiz. Soil is mapped as belonging to the Sioux series.
Releve located on a flat low ridge within glacial lake shoreline complex. Plot is within Lohnes soil series.
Releve located in slight depression with nearly flat to minor microrelief within glacial lake shoreline complex.
This releve is on a flat area with some microrelief, within glacial lake shoreline complex. Soil mapping unit is Lohones series.
The plot is located on a flat portion of the Agassiz beach complex, although there is some microrelief.
This releve is located in an area last cultivated in 1970. Mesic conditions. Located on an old field. Site nearly level with slight slope to southwest.
Plot in flat to slightly depressed area in glacial lake shoreline complex. Soil mapping unit is divide series.
Releve located on beach complex of Glacial lake Agassiz. Soil mapping unit is Divide series.

Plot in old-field area, near top of high ridge, on sandy soil. Area previously cultivated. This area burned in spring of 1995. The site is very well-drained do to soil texture and topographic position.
Plot near crest of high ridge; on sandy soil. This area was burned in spring of 1995.
Plot located on level area in "saddle" of high ridge, on sandy soil.

Plot in level patch of woodland (<10 acres) on northwest end of high ridge. Dry-mesic conditions. A number of large trees burned down in July 1995 storm. Aspen woodland surrounded by prairie and pasture and some cropland.

This releve is located on the crest of a low hill (old, stabilized dune?) surrounded by mostly gently rolling topography. Site slopes very gently to north. Resurvey of Releve#7080 done in 1979. Marked with 1m tall conduit in each corner. Metal tag (HA-1) attached to conduit in NW corner & metal tag (#617) attached to conduit in NE corner.
Releve located neat crest of low sand hill surrounded by gently rolling topography (old dunes).

The releve occupies a site near the crest of a low hill with gently rolling micro-relief. Variable slopes. Resurvey of 1979 releve. All 4 corners marked with 1m tall metal conduit. Conduit on NW corner marked with metal tag "HA-3".

Plot within area of stabilized sand dunes. About 3m relief. The releve occupies an area which is mostly level (to sligtly depressed) on the south edge to an anoub 10 degree slopeo n the north edge (unstable dune face). Slope exposure varies from south to southeast.
Plot in old blowout w/in stabilized sand-dune formation. Plot includes level bottom of blowout and gentle side slope. Bare sand occupies 25-50 percent of plot. Variable slopes.

Releve is in a slight depression in the previously cultivated, nearly level 30% of the preserve. Releve is in an old field. It is less well-drained, than most of the field area. Bare sand with some mosses 5-25% of plot.
Plot in level, not very well-drained site, within area burned in Fall 1994. Prairie is wet-mesic.
This releve is located on a level not well-drained site with some minor micro-relief due to small mammal activity.
Plot in level area in old beach complex of glacial lake. Litter accumulation in 1995 was suppressing flowering.

Plot in slight depression within nearly level area; about 25 cm standing water in 7m diameter central depression. Only one corner marked of 1979 plot found, made northeast corner of this plot, but probably southeast or southwest.
Plot nearly level in mostly level prairie area. In part of site burned Spring 1995, resulting in very vigorous growth and flowering activity.

Aspen woodland or aspen openings. Plot in level area within mostly level glacial lake shoreline complex. Many downed trees from fire within the last few years. Regrowth average 2 meters high, 1.5" DBH.
Releve in slight depression within flat area. Hummocky microrelief (15-20cm). Appears to be a seepage area, but not a fen. Some standing water between hummocks.
Plot in nearly level to gently depressed site. Some pronounced hummocky microrelief deeper swale. Some standing water present.
Plot in nearly level prairie. Wet mesic phase of mesic prairie. Accumulation of litter seems to be suppressing flowering activity.
Releve is located in a nearly level area. Moderate litter accumulation.
Plot in very slight depression in level area. May have been grazed in the past. Wet mesic prairie. Heavy litter accumulation seems to be suppressing flowering.

Releve is in previously cultivated area. "Potential" vegetation would probably be mesic prairie. Topography nearly level with some minor micro relief due to small mammal activity. Area burned in spring 1995.
Nearly level wet-mesic phase of mesic prairie. Area burned this spring (95); vegetation in beautiful condition. Many fruiting grasses >1m.
Plot in slight depression below low beach ridge. Slightly hummocky substrate moist, spongy, but no standing water. Moose trails across plot; moose bedded in plot. Wet prairie/shrub swamp.
Plot in shallow swale within nearly level area. Substrate moist to wet but not standing water when releve done.

Aspen woodland. Releve in nearly level to gently sloping upland area, mesic conditions. Apparently burned within the last five years; aspen suckers dominated the area. Prairie invaded by dog-hair aspen.
Plot in nearly level, mostly upland area, mesic conditions. Cultivated in the past, but native component enough to classify as degraded prairie.

Plot is nearly level to slightly depressed area. Old hay piles noted in 1980 still present. Evidence of disturbance present. Heavy litter present, many be suppressing native species. Very productive site.
