Plot on level to slightly sloping area between upland prairie and wet meadow. Heavy litter accumulation may be suppressing native species.
Plot in nearly level area. Soil mapping unit Rockwell series. Heavy litter accumulation present may be suppressing native species.

Heavy accumulation of litter, except where the willow is most dense. There is also some downed Salix stems. Could be wet meadow or wet prairie. The wet prairie or meadow has been maintained by fire/grazing/mowing in past.
Plot in nearly level area. Soil mapping unit: rockwell series. Heavy accumulation of litter present may be suppressing natives. Wet mesic phase of mesic prairie.
Releve in slight depression below and 100 meters west of low glacial lake beach ride. Heavy litter accumulation present, may be suppressing natives.
Plot in level to slightly depressed area. Wet prairie or wet phase of mesic prairie.
Releve mostly level with a slight depression. Surrounded by slightly higher prairie. Area slightly alkaline.
Plot in slight depression with minor micro relief in level site. No standing water present. Very heavy litter accumulation, may be suppressing natives.

Plot level with minor microrelief, in larger level area. Heavy litter accumulation, may be suppressing natives. Plot located by TNC as the perm-marked 1980 plot (rel#4) but that was in SWSW12. Many differences in species lists. Wet-mesic phase of mesic prairie or wet saline prairie.
Prairie near midslope on very low rise, in mostly level to slightly rolling terrain. Soil silty clay loam with some sand. Heavy litter accumulation may be suppressing natives.
Plot in low prairie swale surrounded by higher wet-mesic prairie. At time of this survey water table just below surface. Soils reported as in Parnell Series. Soil: silt and clay packed with rhizomes.
Plot in level spot between low swale and higher mesic prairie. Moderate litter accumulation. Prairie is wet-mesic.
Plot in large swale that crosses preserve north to south. Woody vegetation seems to have increased. Soils reported as in the Parnell series. Soil: silty clay loam with some sand.
Releve of unknown size in weedy prairie on level site. (Appears to be very degraded prairie.)
Scattered stumps on all sides of hill, but infrequently on top of hill (~15 acres). Recently logged. No evidence of conifer charcoal. No grey layer in soil (E horizon). See releve 7077.
Langly Hill, Superior National Forest and private holding. Old growth of northern hardwoods with scattered super canopy. Selective logging. See also releve 7076.

Numerous low swales and depressions throughout tract dominated by Phleum pratense and red clover. Meliotus, Agropyron, and Poa are abundant in places. Vigor of vegetation much reduced by annual mowing.

South of Wolf Lake in Savanna Portage State Park. Hummocky sphagnum. Few broken stumps . Occasional tip-ups. 1" standing water in depressions. Ca. 5-12 cm DBH Picea. pH 4.3, Cond. 14.1, Absorb. 0.392. Stand 5.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Near Wolf Lake Savanna. Port State Park. Stand full of blowdown (50% of stand). On gentle slope north to black spruce swamp. State stand 4. Photo 20-18. Bird list. Soil 1 and a half in organic/sand over 8 inches moist medium coarse red-tan sand.

Marked relief in plot from moss-covered logs and tip-ups. Moderate coarse woody debris. Vaccinium myrtilloides, Quercus rubra (outside plot) and Betula papyrifera on drier tip-ups. Several broken stumps outside plot. pH 5.4, Cond 25.4, Absorb .367. Wet peat. North of Wolf Lake.

Mix of white cedar and black ash east of "Junction 7" maple-basswood knob in Savanna Portage State Park. Cond = 156.9, Absorb = 0.276. Full of exposed roots and tip-ups. Stand 9; photo 22-17. Moss id: Jan Janssens.

Battle Island in Big Sandy Lake, part of Savanna Portage State Park. Plot at top of narrow ridge with edges sloping off gently. Rare old cut stumps. Few beaver-cut stumps. Infested with poison ivy. Sandy soil.

Black ash east of "Junction 7" maple-basswood knob in Savanna Portage State Park. All height classes black ash. Logs and tip-ups common. Stand something between black ash swamp and lowland hardwood. Soil: 8 inches fibric peat over rock. Stand 14. Cond = 132.1, Absorb = 0.398. Moss id by Jan Janssens.

East of west Savanna River in Savanna Portage State Park. Frequent blowdowns. Old moss-covered logs and tip-ups common. Occasional very old cut stumps. Most lower branches dead. Some multi-stemmed Abies. Deer trail through plot. Bird list. Stand 8.

Well-decayed high cut stumps common. Dead lower branches. Most trees with leaves clustered at top. Needle duff. Blowdowns +/- common. Moderate within plot relief. State stand 10. See D. Shadis soil data.

Poor fen east of west Savanna River. State stand 13. Photo 20-22. Calopogon tuberosus, Scheuzenia palustris, Carex pauciflora, and Sarracenia purpurea in open area northeast of plot. Carex chordorhiza interior to moat surrounding fen.

Burned spring 1997. Scattered dead Salix and Alnus. Savanna Portate trail (board-walk) passes through this stand in Savanna Portage State Park. Scattered dead ash at perimeter of wet meadow. Carex stools throughout. Occasional old logs.

Conifer swamp north of spruce-fir forest. Mix of black spruce and tamarack. Patches where tamarack dominates (including canopy tamarack); other patches black spruce dominates. Hummocky, occasional coarse woody debris. State stand 3.
Wet meadow east of Prairie River Flowage in Savanna Portage State Park. Floating mat of coarse sedges with patches of Typha lat. and scattered D1-3 Salix and Alnus. State stand 6. Photo 19-23.

Upland island along Prairie River Flowage. Savanna Portage State Park. Occasional coarse woody debris. Patches of forest on high ground, interspersed with coarse sedges and Salix in low areas. State stand 4. Photo 19-23.

At base of esker extending north of Savanna Portage State Park head quarters. Stream running through plot. Occasional sedge hummocks. Moderate coarse woody debris--rotting logs. State stand 27. Photo 20-20. Soil: wet fine grained peat.

Approximately 150 square meter patch along west side of rail road on edge of overgrown Quercus macrocarpa savanna. On deep, moist, sandy loam. Occasional large glacial erratics at surface. Site has had a fire within last few years.

High quality Larix swamp on coarse peat with abundant coarse woody debris. Canopy patchy, nearly all Larix. Alnus rugosa and Betula alleghaniensis dominate understory. Not dominated by Sphagnum. Graminoids notably sparse throughout. Soil: Coarse woody peat to 40+ cm. No signs of mineral soil.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: B-rank black ash swamp on course, woody peat with muck at water table. Patchy canopy of Fraxinus nigra with abundant understory of Alnus and Fraxinus. Coarse woody debris abundant and forbs abundant in a patchy moss layer. Soil: Coarse peat with 50% woody debris and 20% muck.

B-ranked wet meadow grading into Salix swamp with infrequent paper birch inclusions on sandy silt mottled clay soils. Slightly above water table. Coarse graminoid mix with patches of Solidago, Aster, and Rubus idaeus. Possible historic disturbance.

High quality rich fen, "Salix sav." on Lake Ogechi. Continuous G layer of wire type Carex. Very diverse Salix community. Easy walking thick floating mat with few large tussucks. Soils peat/muck to 40cm. 6 inch standing water in pockets.

B-ranked emergent marsh floating mat dominated by Typha latifolia. Mat > 40cm thick. Non-woody coarse peat. Diverse forb layer, moderate coverage. Graminoids abundant for community. Typical of north Ogechie shore and channel. Soil: Floating mat >40cm, coarse non-woody peat.

Community on mucky peat >40cm. No open water, but very juicy. Continuous sphagnum. Coarse woody debris infrequent both above and below moss layer. Snags infrequent; no cut stumps found. Earthen dam/trail bridge to northeast alters hydrology(?). Topographic context: depression/flat.

Mature black spruce bog in Mille Lacs State Park. Canopy interrupted to patchy. Shrub layer dominated by Ledum. Sphagnum continuous throughout. Appears undisturbed with abundant tip-ups and coarse woody debris. Yellow birch frequent. Soil a coarse fibrous peat to 40+cm.

Coarse woody debris, stumps (from blowdowns not cutting), snags frequent. Good quality black spruce swamp in Mille Lacs Wildlife Management Area. Canopy interrupted with few open patches. Shrub layer very abundant and dominated by Ledum. Graminoid and forb layers sparse yet typical. Soils coarse peat and muck >40cm (coarse peat with muck: 0-10cm; muck with coarse peat: 10-40cm).
In "200+" acre wetland complex. Plot, 150m north of grassy trail, captures typical quality for community. Area rooted to slightly floating. Soils 40cm coarse peat with muck. See also releve #7209.

B rank alder swamp inside a black ash fringe. Betula papyrifera and Picea individuals occasional. Larix/Picea inclusions common. Quality in question due to Phalaris abundance and Urtica presence. At water table. Coarse peat with 30% muck.

Typha patch within large sedge meadow complex. Small patches of Alnus also present in complex. Area burned every 5 years; last burned spring 1995. Soils are coarse peat to 20cm grading to peaty muck on a mostly rooted, non-floating mat. See also #7202.

Typical wet meadow of lower quality. Dominants include Phalaris, Calamagrostis Carex lasiocarpa. Sugar maple a thick to very thin floating mat to rooted. No new threats to site expected. Forb presence and diversity low. Releve with standing water below detritus and tussucks about 6 inches deep.
Typical shrub swamp Betula/Alnus subtype along Rum River just past lake Ogechie outlet in MLK State Park. Area is peat, but EM is mostly floating. Area undisturbed; microtopography full of tussocks.

Tamarack swamp with black spruce nearly as common. Forbs nearly non-existent. Healthy, near continuous, graminoid layer dominated by Carex species. Soils coarse peat. Part of large complex grading into poor fen shrub subtype. Standing water just below Sphagnum mat. No snags. Very little coarse woody debris.
Plot captures periphery of "600+" acre conifer-dominated wetland complex Moss layer sphagnum-dominated, not continuous. Stunted Larix scattered throughout community. Coarse peat. Ericaceous common.

Standing water over most of plot. Water level manipulated, maybe causing death of Fraxinus and Picea within complex. Soils unretrievable to 40cm. Typha presence and abundance curious. Standing water over most of plot.

Small isolated basin. Standing water <20cm deep in bowls of microtopography. Coarse peat to "40+cm". Site at/slightly above water table. Coarse woody debris abundant. Area appears undisturbed but is within 20m of gravel road. High abundance of Carex. Coarse woody debris abundant, mostly Picea mariana.

Burned shrub community within large wet meadow complex typical of area. Thick healthy regeneration of dominant woody species, Salix, Cornus, and Alnus. Most shrubs at and above 2m dead but with sprouts at bases. Soils unrecoverable to 40cm, coarse peat to 20cm. See also #7217.

Typical wet meadow for this area. See also releve #7216. Site burned spring 1997 and likely to be burned every 5 years to control shrubs. Area predominantly wet meadow with patches of shrubs and Typha. Soils unretrievable with 40cm core, coarse peat to 20cm.
Releve community between maple basswood forest and Alder swamp. Frequent cut stumps. Overstory with Frequent gaps. Soil saturated peaty/muck to "40+" cm. No standing water.

Tamarack swamp ESE of northeast corner of Olsen Field surrounded by extensive alder swamp. Saturated peat to "40+" cm. Sphagnum nearly continuous, coarse woody debris plentiful above and below moss layer. Many old tip-ups.
Wet meadow floating mat (>30cm thick) very typical of Dinosaur Island. Community burned in 1993. No ditches. Potential impacts include winter logging trails. Plot within "1000+" acre wetland complex.

Maple-basswood forest on well-drained silty-loam with 4 inch thick A horizon. No evidence of recent logging. All trees single stemmed. Fire scars on some stumps; none on trees. Diverse ground layer. Releve on level crest of slight hill. Tip-ups common. Continuous canopy without major gaps.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Northern hardwood forest on crest and southeast upper slope within a series of east-west troughs and crests. Inclines unusually steep for area. Soils: reddish silty sand. Coarse woody debris, rocks, boulders, tip-ups common. Recent logging in vicinity.

A-B rank wet meadow at water table on mucky, non-woody peat. Tall tussucks with standing water between. Coarse graminoid mix dominated by Calamagrostis and Carex stricta. Forb diversity influenced by proximity to open water. Moss very sparse.

Typical Alder/Betula swamp for Ogechi Lake. A-B rank site at water table on mucky, non-woody peat. Mature tall tussocks with +/- standing water between. Diverse, sparse forb layer. Continuous graminoid player dominated by Carex stricta and Calamoagrostis.

East of west Savanna River in Savanna Portage State Park. Blowdown common. Occasional logs. Dead lower branches. Some multi-stem trees. Patchy open ground upslope with cones, twigs, and feather mosses. Occasional well-decayed stumps. Broad range of DBH.

Near West Savanna River in Savanna Portage State Park. Within stand relief due to tip-ups and logs. Standing water in pools. Occasional multi-stemmed Fraxinus. All age class of Fraxinus; stand heavily dominated by Fraxinus. Stand 22. Soil: 1 inch wet organic over 8 inches clayey silt grading to clay.

Lowland hardwood forest southeast of "Junction 7" maple basswood knob in Savanna Portage State Park. Occasional blowdown and rotting logs. Within-plot relief from well-rotted logs and tip-ups. Occasional multi-stemmed red maple. State stand 8. Shallow deciduous leaf duff. Soil 3 inches organic over 8 inches sandy gray tan silt.
Wetland east northeast of Savanna Portage State Park headquarters. Stand 11. Upland species on old stumps and logs.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Old growth deciduous forest dominated by Acer saccharum and rubrum; Betula alleghaniensis and Quercua rubra smaller components. Sub canopy dominated by Acer saccharum and Ostrya. Floristic diversity and richness low, too late for ephemerals. No disturbance. Coarse woody debris present.

Old growth deciduous forest dominated by Acer saccharum and rubrum. Occasional mature Picea glauca. Floristic diversity and richness fair. Abundant coarse woody debris, stumps of Betula alleghaniensis and conifers elsewhere. Too late for ephemerals.

Old growth deciduous forest dominated by Acer saccharum, less Acer rubrum. Pinus strobus snag 94cm. Floristically rich and diverse, cover varies. Adoxa mosh E.O. Large coarse woody debris present. Area previously high graded.

Maturing deciduous forest dominated by Acer saccharum, Acer and Betula alleghaniensis. Old growth individuals. Fire and selective harvest origin. Floristically poor. Top of drumlin, poorly drained, rocky, moist shallow depressions.

Conifer swamp forest dominated by 90 year old Picea mariana. P. Mariana in sub canopy with Abies. Scattered Betula papyrifera in canopy. Alnus incana dominates minimal understory. Ground cover mix of graminoids and forbs; rich and diverse. Continuous multi-species bryophyte cover, not deep. Shallow depressions, rock outcrop.

Deciduous forest dominated by senescent Populus tremuloides. Probable timber harvest origin. Subcanopy dominated by Acer rubrum and Popululus tremuloides. Understory mixed saplings. Little conifer. Continuous ground cover dominated by Aster mac, Pteridium aquilinium, and Calamagrostis canadensis.

Natural origin, old growth conifer forest dominated by Thuja on wet-mesic site grading to swamp. Betula alleghaniensis and papyrifera also in canopy. Understory mostly open patches of Acer spicatum and Corylus cornuta. Ground cover variable. Continuous moss cover. Rock outcrop. Abundant coarse woody debris.

Deciduous forest dominated by old growth Acer saccharum and Tilia. Smaller components of Betula alleghaniensis and Quercus rubra. Spring ephemeral unknown due to season. No disturbance, fire protected among knobs on high ridge.

Small mixed forest dominated by old growth Pinus strobus and Populus grandidentata. Subcanopy dominated by Acer rubrum and few Betula papyrifera. Tall shrub layer, moderately dense Corylus. Herb layer not well-developed. Small stand, more disturbed and early successional elsewhere.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Fire origin 90 year second growth conifer forest dominated by Pinus resinosa with Pinus strobus. Some old growth pine. Acer saccharum dominates subcanopy and understory. Herb layer species poor and sparse cover. Top and crest of steep well-drained slope. No stumps. Trail nearby.

Fire origin deciduous forest dominated by Betula papyrifera in senescence. Tilia and Acer rubrum also in canopy components. Acer rubrum dominates subcanopy and understory. Shrubs of moderate density; uniform cover of herbs and graminoids. Well-drained. Succeeding to northern hardwood. Thin to no soil over boulder garden common throughout.

Natural origin conifer forest dominated by Pinus resinosa; lesser component of Pinus strobus. Weak subcanopy of Betula papyrifera. Understory shrubs sparse. Moderately dense Abies <2.5m. Ground layer dominated by herbs, cover sparse. Pinus strobus regeneration. Upland perched between swamps. Soil horizons and exact textures: A, Bw, 2C (FSL). Densic till not observed but expected at greater depth. Some surface stones present. Parent material: glacial drift over subglacial till.

Post fire origin deciduous forest domianted by Populus grandidentat about 60 years old. Subcanopy Acer rubrum, some Betula papyrifera. Understory domianted by Acer spicatum and hazel. Rocky, well drained. Ground layer diverse.

Mixed coniferous forest domianted by Pinus resinosa and strobus with subcanopy of Betula papyrifera and Acer rubrum. Some Abies and Picea. Shrub layer sparse. Pinus about 100 years: few stumps. Coarse woody debris present. Fire scars.

Conifer swamp dominated by "70+" year old Thuja, some old growth trees. Occasional Picea mariana. Minimal shrub cover. Some sapling Fraxinus nigra. Numberous wet depressions in hummocky deep moss cover. Natural origin.

Coniferous forest dominated by old growth Pinus strobus. Mixed understory of Betula alleghaniensis and papyrifera; scatttered Thuja, Abies, and Picea glauca. Patchy shrub layer domianted by Acer spicatum and Corylus cornuta. Ground layer needle covered, patchy cover of herbs. Fire scars. Coarse woody debris.

Conifer swamp forest dominated by Thuja occidentalis. Patchy canopy cover. Tall shrub layer density variable, dominated by Alnus incana. Deep bryophyte cover continuous; hummocks and pool microtopography. Coarse woody debris present. Moist to wet.

Natural origin conifer forest dominated by Pinus strobus >90 years. Subcanopy Betula papyrifera, Picea maiana and Abies. Tall shrub layer generally  dense Corylus cornuta in patches. Herbs dominated by Aster mac. No evidence of disturbance. Abundant coarse woody debris.

Aspen-birch forest spruce fir subtype. Canopy dominated by Populus tremuloides and Betula papyrifera. Much Abies budworm mortality and blow-down. Abies regeneration present, also Populus regeneration in openings. Herb cover continuous.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Deciduous forest dominated by young and maturing Acer saccharum. Post fire regeneration; portion of larger northern hardwood community. A few old growth Acer still present. Understory open. Shrub layer sparse. Little coarse woody debris.

Sixty year old, fire origin conifer forest dominated by dense Picea mariana. Occasional Pinus banksiana, also scattered Populus tremuloides and Betula papyrifera. Understory open. Ground layer is continuous thin layer of feather moss. Herb cover patchy. Aster mac. and Cornus canadensis most frequent.

Boreal-hardwood conifer forest dominated by old growth Thuja; some Betula papyrifera in canopy. "200+" year old super canopy of Pinus strobus. Patchy understory of Acer spicatum. Ground cover patchy depending on light. Abies in canopy and subcanopy dead, still present in understory. Thuja stumps observed, no evidence of fire.

70 year old deciduous forest dominated by Populus tremuloides and Betula papyrifera. Understory of Abies, Picea mariana and Thuja. Budworm mortality and blowdown common. Fairly open understory domianted by Acer spictatum. Herb layer dominated by Clintonia borealis and Aralis nudicaulus. Probable post fire salvage of conifers.

Conifer swamp dominated by Thuja, including old growth and regeneration. Understory patchy Alnus. Much microtopography with continuous bryophyte carpet and patchy herb cover of moderate species richness. No sign of disturbance. Abundant coarse woody debris.

Mature stand on 30 acre hardwood island amongst large tamarack swamp. Canopy trees 20-40cm DBH (rare 48cm), straight boles, few snags, no stumps. Occasional coarse woody debris. Soil brown sandy-loam. Thick organic layer, surface boulders occasional.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mature stand on "terrace" below 120 foot northeast-facing slope adjacent to marsh. Canopy trees tall and straight 25-52cm DBH; mode 35-45cm. Snags uncommon. A few stumps in vicinity. Deep, black loam. Coarse woody debris sparse.

Rather steep north face slope of 80 foo. gravelly esker. Dark loam soil. Maturing stand, canopy trees 25-40cm DBH. No stumps or tip-ups, few snags. Occasional coarse woody debris, mostly larger. Grades to mesic oak.

Mature stand on gently-rolling terrain. Trees straight-boled. Few snags. Stumps rare. Occasional coarse woody debris. Light past grazed? Soil 2" dark sandy loam over brown silt-loam. Best and most mesic area seen in this site. Canopy trees 25-50 cm DBH.

Sandy loam soils with gravel, occasional boulders. At top of one knoll in a series of hill prairies south of the Sauk River. Area generally open exposure with many invasive woody plants nearby; thick mostly graminoid duff. Area in need of fire.

Level wet-mesic prairie with past haying history. Black loam soils with gravel. Good soil texture, little compaction. Bordered on north by Sedan brook, south by Phragmites; east by willows and red-osier dogwood.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: County owned floodplain forest along Mississippi River. Chin high Matteuccia throughout-covering cut and blowdown logs. Occasional cut stumps. Silver maple hanging over river. Laportea patches adjacent.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Maple-Basswood forest north of Twin Lakes Road. Shallow deciduous leaf duff. Moderate open ground layer. Several large, decayed conifer stumps near plot. Only slight within-plot relief. Silt cap. Soil: 1 1/2 inch organic over gray silt over light tan silt.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Maple-basswood forest north of Twin Lakes Road. Plot placed on southeast-facing slope. Soil: 2 inches organic over silty loam becoming sandy.
On silt-capped ridge extending from Hay Lk into Savanna Portage State Park. All age classes Acer. Thick Deciduous leaf duff. Within plot relief from old tip-ups and decaying logs.

Plot placed to capture yellow birch-in matrix of maple-basswood forest. On silt-capped ridge south of Hay Lake. Moderately-thick deciduous leaf duff. Moderate coarse woody debris, including yellow birch.

Hardwood forest on moraine northwest of Remote Lake. Moderate coarse woody debris - mostly birch (~2 to 6" DBH) with occasional moss covered logs. Gentle within plot relief from old tip-ups and decaying logs. Stand full of depressions and knolls. Thick deciduous leaf duff. Soil: 2 inches organic over 7 inches loamy sand over 1 inch medium tan fine sand.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: County-owned floodplain forest along Willow River, north of Palisade. Plot near river. About 25% of plot with dense D4 Fraxinus nigra. ~20% of plot without ground cover. Acer saccharinum present, but not major canopy species.
Lots of bare maple litter.
Pocket of nice ungrazed wet meadow at south end of wetland complex that grades northward into remnent calcareous fen.
100m releve is long and skinny - represents transition between grazed pasture and wetland. Pasture is highly degraded prairie. Releve should not be used in classification analysis.

Woodland with patchy matrix of shrubs and tall grasses in understory. Occasional well-decayed cut stump. Soil: 15cm dark brown sandy loam with high organic matter/2cm charcoal/5cm dark brown sandy loam/light sandy loam. Tree cores: 46cm DBH Quercus macrocarpa-53+years; 47cm DBH Quercus macrocarpa-94+years; 20 cm DBH Quercus macrocarpa-60+ years; 37cm DBH Quercus rubra-9+ years; 6 cm DBH Acer rubrum - 43+ years.

Perched, circular, actively upwelling fen on otherwise 5% slope, just S of flowing well. This releve is long and linear in a circle of open active seepage that surrounds a brushy central core. Ground is 10-15% bare mud.

Narrow strip of possible old growth ash with yellow birch on edges. No standing water, but depressions appear seasonally inundated. Diverse moss, sedge, wood and herb layer on raised hummocks and roots. Soil to 50cm = uniform dark "muck" with organic mater. Tree cores: Fraxinus nigra, 31cm DBH-114+ years; 41cm DBH 101+years, 45cm DBH 168+ years. Topographic context: depression/flat.

Old growth-mature mesic forest with sparse subcanopy, shrub, seedling layers. Herb layer dominated by bracken fern. Graminoid layer nearly absent. Few old stumps. 3cm needle litter/2cm dark brown A-horizon/30cm medium brown sand loam/30cm light brown-yellow sandy loam. Will succeed to white pine/red oak if left to go. Tree core: Pinus strobus; 47cm DBH-83 years+, 47cm DBH-82 years+, 50cm DBH-82 years+.

Old growth/sub-old growth homogeneous bog. Extensive sphagnum mat with occasional hummock of of other species. Sparse ericaceous shrubs and ubiquitous Maianthemum canadensis. No evident disturbance. Cored 3 large spruce: 20cm DBH - 120+, 23cm DBH 63+, 24cm DBH 93+ years.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: High-quality old growth ash stand surrounded half by wetland and half by clear cuts. Abundant Mitella nuda. Open wallows with little vegetation = 25-50% cover. Most vegetation on raised roots and coarse woody debris. 2 ash cored: 28cm = "176+" and 36cm = "186+ years."

Floating mat of sedges and mosses with occasional clusters of shrubs. 2-4m moat, with duckweed and clumps of sedges and mosses, and flow channels around edges. Eriophorum and Typhya not in releve, but noteable in community.

Matrix of 2nd growth red oak and maple-basswood. Tall cut stumps throughout with occasional very large well-decayed conifer stumps. Central and southern portion of stand dominated by red oak and northern portion co-dominated by Tilia, red and sugar maples, and red oak in mostly closed canopy throughout. Soil: 3cm well-developed dark A-horizon/yellow-biege fine silt. 3 red oaks cored at ca. 80 years.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: High-quality mature red oak forest. Few snags or coarse woody debris. Several small wetlands in stand. Thick oak leaf litter/2cm dark A-horizon/fine light orange brown sand with some silt. Tree core: Quercus rubra; 39cm DBH-64+ years, 35cm DBH-66+ years, 42cm DBH-63+ years. Topographic context: crest/flat.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Young mature oak forest with mostly closed canopy and pole sized subcanopy of basswood and sugar maple with occasional green ash. 3 canopy trees cored at 35cm DBH at 58+ years, 27cm DBH 62+ years and 32cm DBH at 60+ years. On very hilly terrain with steep slopes and network of drainages. Low areas mostly similar in composition to slopes and crests.
Wet meadow at Grayling Marsh Wildlife Management Area. Typha encroaching. Sedge mat over sedge peat.
Floodplain forest along Willow River. Laportea throughout. 1/10th of plot in old oxbow-mudflat with Acer saccharinum seedlings. 15 inches dark brown loamy silt, no organic.
Old MB forest S of Hedbom For Rd. Yel birch & wht cedar in stand, but not in plot. Also in stand: Adiat peda, Caul thal, B. lanceolatum, B. mormo, B. Matr, & B. diss. Thick decid. lf duff.
Old maple-basswood forest north of powerline. Frequent well-decayed logs and old tip-ups. Tiny ephemeral pools, occasional Betula papyrifera in stand increases to north and west. Sandy soil.
Conifer swamp on South side of smallest of Twin Lakes in Rice Lake NWR. Occasional ~4" diameter coarse woody debris. Sphagnum hummocks continuous. Wet peat: 3 inches sedge peat, fibric in returns.
McGregor Marsh SNA. Salix with dead stems and suckering in stand. Reportedly burned (arson?) spring 1997. Also in stand, but not in plot Triadenum fraseri, Thelypteris palustis. Floating mat.

Wet meadow in Grayling Marsh wildlife management area. Extensive Calamagrostis canadensis with patches of Carex lacustris in wetter areas. D34 Salix out of plot at edge of wet meadow and rare within community.
East of Hwy. 65, north of McGregor. No satnding water, wet peat collected. Hummocky sphagnum.
Wet meadow along Rice River in Rice Lake NWR. 10 inches wet sedge peat.
Wet meadow along Rice River in Rice Lake NWR. Wet sedge peat.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Near south edge of Twin Lake West. Plot on north slope of narrow ridge. Moderate coarse woody debris, primarily Betula papyrifera logs and Ostrya. Most tress single-stemmed. State stand 11. Thick deciduous leaf duff. 2-3 inches organic layer over 2-3 inches silt loam.
Wet meadow at south edge of West Twin Lake. Scattered Typha and small patches of Phragmites out of plot closer to open water. Hummocky. Floating mat at the north end of plot

East of Moose River Flowage in Moose-Willow wildlife management area. Mix of white cedar and black ash. Full of moss-covered tree roots and logs. Pools with only a film of standing water. About half of cedars are leaning. State stand 8.

East of Moose River Flowage in Moose-Willow wildlife management area. Areas in stand with more aspen than in plot- especially to southeast where stand grades into aspen forest. Soil: 2 inches organic over sandy silt.

Part of extensive conifer swamp west of Mississippi River.  Hummocky sphagnum throughout. Tops of highest hummocks dried. Also in stand, not in plot: Carex oligosperma, Scirpus palustris. Mosses to Jan J.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: South side of large upland island at north edge of Mandy Lake in Rice Lake NWR. Sandy soil. Fraxinus, Tilia, Quercus multiple stemmed. Thin deciduous leaf duff. Soil 3 inches organic over 7 inches very fine medium tan sand.
Soli: fine sand.

Relatively open canopy. Understory patchy and heterogeneous. Some areas with dense moss mats. Thin needle litter. 1st 10cm soil slightly darker/fine yellow-brown sand to 1m. Average canopy trees ca. 30 years. Topographic context: crest/upper.

Large bedrock bald with clumps of Vaccinium angustifolium, Diervilla, Selaginella and Cladina lichens. Recent organic soil in large 5x6m clump is 20-40 cm thick. Cover 10% shrub, 4% forb, 8% graminoid, 20% moss, 58% rock/crustose lichen.
Alder swamp between 2 large rock outcrops along Leveaux bike trail. Typical. Seems intact despite logging/grazing and therefore young aspen/birch stands on mineral soil between outcrops.
Releve in small peaty depression on mini-terrace at base of slope; seepage just off to side of plot. Hiking trail on opposite side toward river. Firm black peat, not much muck. History unknown.

Very small patch of upland white cedar on mid-slope. No obvious seepage in plot, but rivulet below plot along base of slope. No Thuja reproduction. Surrounding deciduous forest young, past cut, probably grazed.
Series of 3 releves across typical meadow/fen mat in large wetland system adjacent to Ann Lake. Peat is loose, footing is difficult; soupy sink into water over 0.5m in places.
Unusual forested slope with moist soil but no obvious seepage. Canopy very heterogeneous. Gaps. Trees not large. Past cutting or unstable substrate? High species diversity. 200m from Kettle River.

Series of 3 releves. This plot is transitional between wet meadow and rich fen, typical of this wetland system (vegetation types not distinct). History unknown. Water level manipulations? Ann Lake WMA.

Cobble-boulder beach on St. Louis River at mouth of Crystal Creek. Plot includes band of annual plants on pockets of silty-sand at high water line. Remaining 80% of plot dominated by Spartina/Carex stricta/Calamagrostis canadensis.

Sphagnum continuous at 80%. Hummocky on woody or sedgy clumps. Very uneven, not like well-developed cushiony hummocks in a poor fen/bog. Numerous narrow wet hollows. Much Carex rostrata/Calamagrostis litter.

Dense shady dry Thuja stand lacking conifer regeneration. Microtopography uneven-rocks, roots, but substrate fairly uniform: thin dry Thuja litter over thin organic soil. Very small stand. History unknown.

Small white cedar swamp on fairly heterogeneous microtopography of primarily moist muck, but also down logs, mucky wet hollows, cedar roots; bedrock ledge 1-2m high around plot. Plants patchy. Adjacent to railroad and gravel pit.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Very shady even-aged black ash swamp, trees 10-18cm DBH; average 13cm. Many wet mucky pools 0.5m deep. Vegetation on raised woody hummocks. Very few black ash seedlings. History unknown.

Disturbed, past-cut area transitional between hardwood and tamarack swamp. Now, tall shrub swamp with much coarse woody debris over wet pools but seems to have been peatier than releve #7456 and will succeed to Larix.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Groundlayer typical of mesic hardwood forest on well-drained irregular moraine knobs and ridges. Canopy quality good: older, less birch, aspen. To be thinned. Good vegetation sequences from ridges to swamp.

Mature black ash swamp with lowland hardwood and wet/wet-mesic northern hardwood on 3 sides.; wetter swamp beyond (see releve     ). Tall straight trees, Carex, Brome, and high species diversity make this zone distinctive.

Wet swamp in +/- channel between lowland hardwood rises that extend out from upland. Farther out, narrow zone of deciduous/coniferous swamp then large black spruce swamp. Microtopography is soupy matrix with coarse woody debris and tree base rises.

Incomplete releve. Done to record woody structure for draft class of TM satellite data. Possibly past-cut black spruce patch. No abrupt zonation/border. Sphagnum hummocks low, firm; possibly compacted.

Broad expanse of wet meadow and shrub swamp near the origin of the Chelsey Brook channel. These wetlands continuous with conifer swamp (headwaters). Phalaris in meadow in winter trails and winter logging landing.

Shrub zone between upland and wet meadow along Chelsey Brook. Here, woody-sedge peat is very hummocky; a small rivulet with Calla flows through plot. Beyond plot, scattered old down logs, some were tamarack; some from winter logging.

Alder swamp with a few tamarack occupies a 5 acre wet mucky depression. Surrounded by clear-cutting, now 10 year old aspen. Wetland seems intact tho more lowland/wetland buffer is desirable for species refugia.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Typical older patch (40? and 80? year old classes) of mesic hardwood forest. Max DBH: Acer = 50cm, Tilia = 45cm; average = 30cm. Poss fire scars on west side. Single stems. Almost no coarse woody debris. On scenic ridge. Adjacent logging.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Typical older patch of mesic hardwood forest with fine tall oaks mostly 35-44cm DBH though many long-curved; occasional fire scar on North. Acer slender. Shady sparse herbs, much leaf litter. Logging trails nearby. No coarse woody debris.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Plot +/- level at mid-elevation between DNR releve #7466 and 7468. Microtopogy with dips and irregular small rises. Some rocks at surface. Typical thinned stand to create single-stem oak. Minor impact. Young Botrychium near plot.
On flat "200+" acre low-lying knoll in large wetland system. Unusual. Isolated. Disturbed by past and current logging, but ground layer seems seems intact. Conifers rare. Snags and down logs common.

Releve +/- same as BCD 96-14 (DNR# 6556). Done here for training; high overall species divers on low-lying uplands, wet depressions and swamps. Potential Botrychium habitat here and in SW SW 12--more search needed.

Wet-mesic margin of hardwood forest (see DNR releve # 6556 and 7469?). Slight 1-3m square rises; dips do not hold water. No rocks at surface. Silty loam with mottles at 20-30cm and silty-clayey at 40cm. Past cut. Max DBH 30-40cm.

Typical mesic hardwood on irregular moraine topography 1 mile southwest of Lake Mille Lacs. Plot +/- level, mid-elevation between max/min. Occasional boulders and tip-up mounds. Populus grandidentata snags/down logs 30cm DBH. Acer 10-28cm, Quercus 22-35cm.
Releve in 15 acre peaty depression subject to drying and sun from adjacent upland logging. Peat firm, no water in footprints.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Typical moderate-low diversity, past-cut hardwood stand near crest. Plot in portion of stand with more oak and less aspen/birch. Estimated age: 60 years.
Mostly disturbed wet mesic prairie located between lobes of cattail marsh. Disturbance by grazing? likely. Clay loam soils probably saturated in spring.

Slightly more upland level site within a brush (willow) prairie and marsh complex. Loamy soils probably saturated in wet years. Past grazing probable-abundant Fragaria and Achillea; also seedling Melilotus.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: White cedar swamp 25-50% depression with water. Cedar 20-30cm, black ash 10-20 cm, paper birch 10-20cm. Tip-ups abundant.
Tamarack 10-35cm DBH, saturated soil floating mats of mounded sphagnum. Narrow band between large stand of Thuja occidentalis and Picea mariana. pH=4.3 (JAJ).
Bog like. Typical DBH 8-15 cm.
Bog like tamarack swamp with black spruce understory substrate firm and dry with mossy hummocks and depressions. Typical DBH 5-13cm; max size infrequent to 20-30cm DBH (Janssen calls poor fen).

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: White cedar/mixed hardwoods, Dry mesic/mesic organic silt with depressions 15-25%: white cedar DBH 40-65cm; black ash 30-40cm DBH, white spruce 20-30cm DBH. Old growth.
Black spruce bog, hummocks and depressions - wet-mesic. Typical DBH 4-10 max 11-16cm common; possible tending toward Poor fen with minerotropic moss species - Janssen calls poor fen.

Mixed mire or bog island of wet meadow with Sphagnum hummocks and swamp depression. Canopy thickly dominated by tamarack. Typical DBH 10-20cm; frequent tip-ups mounds and debris or loess. Depressions 25-50%, wet saturated organic matter.
Forested fen with sphagnum hummocks firm depressions covering 5-25% area. Peat <5cm to sand. Typical DBH 30cm which are infrequent in area.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Heterogeneous 50 acre stand. Recovering from several past selective logging episodes. Many stumps. Patches of Populus grandidentata and Populus tremuloides in canopy. Loam soil. Represents mesic end of forest spectrum in this part of stats. Lots of Populus sangs and decaying Populus logs.

Maturing stand on strongly rolling terrain south of Avon. Rich sandy-loam. A few snags. Stumps rare. Scattered surface boulders. Occasional coarse woody debris. Many trees multi-stemmed. Canopy trees 25-38cm DBH. One of best mesic stands in Avon Hills and all of Stearns county. Topographic context: crest/upper/middle.

Floating mat surrounding shallow marly lake grade to minerotrophic tamarack swamp. Continuous sphagnum cover. Phenology of spring ~2 weeks ahead of average. Little standing (ankle-deep) water. 15m from lake edge.

Phenology 2 weeks ahead this spring. 20 acre spongy floating mat surrounded by strips of wooded, 20 foot hillsides. Mat with continuous Sphagnum cover except for large Polytrichum hummocks. No surface water.
Narrow fen on bouncy substrate along water tract draining thru extensive Tamarack swamp complex. No sphagnum. Much wetter than surrounding Tamarack swamp. Hummocks well developed.
Fairly firm sedge mat surrounded by marsh along Kolling Creek. 10-20 acres of ("fen") similar habitat. Phenology "2+" weeks advanced this year. Large wetland complex west of Richmond.

Best area of 100 acre mediocre oak stand on hilly terrain 2 miles south of St. Stephen. Soil dark brown sandy loam >8" deep. Likely moderate past grazed. No snags, or stumps. Coarse woody debris occasional. Trees 20-45cm DBH, occasional multi-stemmed.
Multi-stemmed trees 25-35cm DBH. Deep loamy soil. Level terrain. Natural firebreak from George Lake on the west. Noted by original land surveyors, used by pioneers for firewood and posts.

Even-aged appearing stand on gradual to strongly rolling terrain northwest of Avon. Is northern extent of Avon Hills. Coarse brown sandy-gravel soil > 2ft deep. Well drained. Trees 25-40cm DBH, mode 30cm. Trees often multi-stemmed, few snags. Large stand. Abundant coarse woody debris.

With R. Dana. Highly decomposed marly peat > 1/2 meter deep with lots of shell fragments. Saturated to surface, no standing water. Mid-point of slight slope just above the creek. Immediately upslope is shrubby. Had some past cattle grazing. Two ditches partially drain this 50 acre fen.

Slightly-bouncy peat saturated to surface, marly, to depth > 1/2 meter 25m from head of 2m deep ditch with flowing water Which defines current boundary/edge of this large fen complex. Slightly springy substrate. Possibly this variant of the 50 acre fen complex related to the ditching. With R. Dana.

Strange patch of mesic prairie with better prairie both up and down slope on slight gradient along Sedan Br. Soil moderately well-drained loam with 12" A  horizon over brown coarse sandy-loam. 1-3 inches of litter built-up. Not hayed in past few years. (with R. Dana)

Annually hayed. Plot in transitional band from mesic prairie to Carex lacustris meadow. Wet prairie? Soil saturated and slightly springy, marly, organic. Shallow wetland depression along Co. Rd. 137 in Waite Park.

Forested bog. 20 acre wetland all this community type. Continuous Sphagnum cover. Mature stand, trees 10-28cm DBH; mode 15cm. No coarse woody debris or standing water. Sapric peat, well decomposed, > 1 meter deep. Stand surrounded by gravelly wooded upland moraine.

Poor Fen? Three acre depression atop 60 foot wooded hill. Floating mat with continuous Sphagnum cover all except margins. Several inter grading zones encompassed by plot. No Larix here. Much Vaccinium dead or dying.

6 acre depression in steep, strongly-rolling, gravelly wooded terrain. Spongy floating mat with continuous Sphagnum cover. Shallow water in part of plot. Narrow surrounding moat. Plot also visited 7 May, 1998.

Fen meadow. 12 acre depression amongst strongly rolling wooded hills west of Clearwater Lake. Plot centrally located in depression where substrate is bouncy but sturdy. No Sphagnum. Few shrubs. Peat saturated but no open water.

Poor Fen? Floating mat in 20 acre depression surrounded by rolling wooded terrain west of Clearwater Lake. Sphagnum continuous except around margins. Small central, open water section. No moat. Few shrubs, no Larix. Lythrum salicaria present as scattered plants and two large marginal patches.

Poor fen? Floating sphagnum mat in 15 acre depression surrounded by rather steep 30-50 ft hills of an esker. Spongy mat. Peat saturated to surface, but no surface water. No trees. Scattered shrubby areas. Scattered Typha patches. NO open water. No ericaceous plants. No moat.

Poor fen/bog? Subtle water track feature bisecting rather large forested bog dominated by Picea mariana. On southwest side of Ludwig unit. Plot centrally-located in low-statured vegetation near downstream end of drainage feature. Peat saturated but no surface water.

Dry barrens/sand-gravel prairie. 3-4 acre sand prairie on mod to steep slope of 40 ft terrace along the Clearwater River at Hwy 75 bridge. Soil a tan medium to fine textured sand with small gravel particles (5-10% gravel). 20% bare sand. Several ATV trails.

Mesic (sand-gravel) prairie? 3-5 acres of prairie in ROW between highway 75 and old railroad. Silty loam A horizon over sand in outwash terrace 1/2 mile south of the Mississippi River and immediately east of Plum Creek. Grades to wet-mesic and wet with Spartina and Betula gladulifera near creek. Well drained.

Linear wet meadow complex along drainageway through oak/aspen woodland. Wettest central zone dominated by Carex lacustris, Plot located in a portion of less wet outer zone. 0-4" water between hummocks after recent heavy rains. 15m from woods edge, 15m from Carex lacustris zone.

Poor fen. Floating mat in long, narrow depression amongst rather strongly-rolling wooded sandy terrain. Mat bouncy, with continuous Sphagnum (all but edges), forms hummocks. Troughs wet but no standing water. Few small, scattered trees; Pinus strobus, Larix, and Betula papyrifera.

Lowland hardwood. Heterogeneous stand along Keene Creek. varying from lowland hardwood with black ash to northern hardwood with scattered conifers. Soil well to moderately well drained silty loam. Good litter layer. Few snags. Tip-up mounds occasional. Some old stumps. Trees 15-40cm DBH; bimodal 25-35cm and 15-20xcm. Some moist hollows but no surface water.

Within oxbow on Mississippi River northeast of Aitkin County Park near Jacobson. One old oxbow in plot and several within stand. Carex alopec. and Carex lasiocarpa in old oxbow. Coarse woody debris common. Acer abundant near River. Wide range of DBH for both canopy species; Fraxinus nigra and Acer Saccharinum.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Stand bisected by Splith and forest road. North of 200 east of Hill City. Many white pine seedlings in stand. Within-plot relief marked due to decomposing logs, tip-ups. Several yellow birch logs. Moderate coarse woody debris. Occasional ash swales and seasonal ponds. Occasional groups on white pine, otherwise white pine scattered.
Location selected for butternut. Forest dominated by red oak (super canopy). Moderate coarse woody debirs including paper birch logs. Juglans in canopy, sub-canopy, and as saplings.
Rice Lake NWR. Wet meadow along ditch leading from lake. Dominated by Calamagrostis canadensis. Scattered Salix. Hummocky. Standing water. Sedge peat.

Floodplain forest along Willow River in Roberts-Wikstrom wildlife management area northeast of Palisade. Floodwaters have only recently receded. Wet, matted leaves, coarse woody debris; much exposed wet soil. Narrow floodplain dominated by silver maple. Phalaris on river bank.

On Rice River in Kimberly wildlife management area. Floodplain on bend of Rice River. About "1/2" plot with sparse to dense Polygonum; about "1/4" of plot bare "with wet" matted leaves and silver maple samaras. Range of silver maple DBH's.
Hellickson WPA (USFWS). Pothole landscape dotted with tiny Typha or Scirpus filled or ringed wetlands. Occasional Carex-filled drainages between.
Hellickson WPA, USFWS. Pothole landscape--dotted with tiny Typha or Scirpus filled or ringed wetlands. Occasional Carex-filled drainages between.
Wet meadow along Rice River in Kimberly wildlife management area. On well-decomposed sedge peat, at least 33cm deep.
Silver maple dominated floodplain forest on bank of Rice River in Kimberly wildlife management area. Silver maple samaras and seedlings common. ~50% of plot open, wet bare mineral soil.

Maturing even-aged mesic oak forest. Crowns 30m tall, cover 90%, DBH 25-35cm, matured sized <50cm DBH rare. Stagnation moraine narrow ridge to undulating swales and depressions with sedge meadows and tamarack swamp at or near base of slope. Soil: A horizon to 5cm, silty loam with clay pan at or >46cm. Subsoil with small pebbles. Scattered erratics through forest. Snags rare to occasional, debris and tip-ups occasional. 35cm DBH Quercus rubra at 77 rings.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Oak forest on the crest and upper slope of a local high point on pitted terminal moraine. Soils: sandy loam. Canopy dominated by Quercus species. Note occurrence of Quercus Alba. Forbs low in abundance and diversity. Carex pennsylvanica very common but rarely abundant. Soil: 0-5 cm A horizon; 5-50+cm sandy loam with no pebbles or rocks. One cored Quercus alba at 100 years old. Topographic context: upper/middle.

Good quality tamarack swamp on "90+" cm fibris peat. Largest trees 60-65 years old. Diverse forb and shrub layers. No standing water in community. Blow downs and snags frequent. Possible exotics, otherwise no threats. Soil: 0-60cm fibric peat, 60-90cm fibric mucky peat. Core of largest Larix: 60-65 years.

EM/SS inclusion within black ash swamp polygon. Peat depth >1m. Diverse forb layer. No signs of disturbance except other footprints. Average (typical?) quality: BC. Shrub community becomes dominate to the west northwest. Mostly Carex litter with herbaceous leaves. Soil: mucky sedge peat to 43 cm, over fibric compacted saturated sedge peat >100cm.

Mid-quality black ash swamp with strong Abies balsamifera and Acer spicatum presence. Soils: peat to ~25cm grading into mottled clay. Standing water to 3cm deep. Many blowdowns and a few cut stumps; diameter 45-50cm. Litter of leaves and needles. Average peat depth 25cm. 49cm DBH Ash core at 150 years.

Mature stand of slender 25-35cm DBH Thuja; uniform within plot but somewhat patchy throughout stand; canopy gaps with much Abies and Acer spicatum. Moderate coarse woody debris; occasional old stumps. Plot adjacent to old vehicle trail. Average Thuja DBH range 25-35cm. Microtopography fairly uniform, 30cm variation from woody rises to moist but firm low spots. Average peat depth: 100cm.

Dense shrub swamp with a poor fen character; E45 Larix single-to-patchy throughout this floating mat community. Matted shrubs suggest snowmobile trail running east to west just south of the plot. Graminoid dominated understory. Soil: floating mat of sedge peat with thickness of .5-1 meters. Average peat depth: 100m.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Mature black ash swamp with slender canopy trees and slender +/- sparse sub-canopy. Shrub layer not dense, easy to see through community. Moderate amount of small, slender coarse woody debris. 1/2 plot mucky pools, 1/2 woody rise.

Mature slender patchy canopy of Abies balsamifera, Populus tremuloides and Acer rubrum. Slender to medium coarse woody debris abundant. Tip-ups, snags and broken stumps frequent Local topography with many small knolls with mesic/saturated forests and wetland between. Litter of leaves and needles.  Soils are a coarse sand/gravel with abundant small to large pebbles/rocks that block soil probe at 20cm. Topographic context: crest-lower.

Poor fen with open-to-patchy canopy of Picea, Larix, and frequent, but not abundant Pinus. Most canopy trees have 12-18cm DBH with infrequent 30+cm DBH Larix. No cut stumps; few tip-ups. Slender coarse woody debris common, but not abundant. Soil: sphagnum moss peat to 1+ meter. No open water pockets but foot prints immediately fill with water.

Poor fen dominated by gramminoids and Sphagnum moss. Situated on the border between Picea/Larix. Poor fen and Populus/Betula upland. Dredged channel within 150m of plot. Not floating. Easy walking/few tussocks. Average peat depth: 60cm. Soil: sedge peat over sandy gley/clay with mottles.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Slender to medium mature oak forest with frequent Fraxinus, Tilia, and Populus in canopy. Slender-large coarse woody debris, tip-up mounds, old and new, common. Rolling topography with low spots, tending towards wet-mesic. Small patches of Populus grandidentata occasional. No cut stumps observed. Soil: Sandy silt with occasional pebbles. A horizon depth: 6cm. Litter of leaves and twigs. Topographic context: crest/upper.

Mixed-aged wet mesic forest situated between upland oak forest and black ash swamp within 50m of the Camp Lake shore. coarse woody debris of all sizes common. No cut stumps but multi-stemmed canopy trees common. A horizon depth: 7cm. Soil: silty sand with light brown mottles over sandy clay with mottles.

A long skinny poor fen open subtype dominated by graminoids and Sphagnum. Occasional short Larix and Pinus strobus throughout with small Larix patch on south end. Rich fen edge all around dominated by course gramminoid and patches of Alunus and Betula glandulifera. No signs of disturbance except for two unusual stumps on fence posts. Litter of graminoids and leaves.

Wet mesic forest with patchy Tilia canopy a rather sparse shrub layer and notable sparse spots in litter and herb layer. A few burnt stumps and occasional stumps. Coarse woody debris of all sizes common but not abundant. Tip-up common. Multi-stemmed Tilia. Worms present in A horizon.

Mature oak forest with an open understory and notable bare understory, herb and gram layers. Cut stumps occasional to common throughout. Coarse woody debris of all sizes common. Plot typical of crest and upper slope for this ridge. A horizon depth: 4cm. Soil: sandy silt with large pebbles, could not probe past 33cm.

A rather slender mixed deciduous forest on a steep slope with occasional large boulders and frequent rocks. Large coarse woody debris infrequent, slender coarse woody debris common. Rather dense, continuous canopy when D7 and D46 are combined, resulting in rather sparse understory communities. A horizon depth: 4cm. Soil: sand and small pebbles with a minor amount of silt.

A mature but slender northern hardwood forest. Past disturbance evidenced by multi-stem Tilia and uncommon large coarse woody debris. Slender to medium coarse woody debris and old tip-up mounds common; stumps infrequent. Rather open below d45. Soil: sandy loam over loam over clay over loam.

Typical mid to upper slope oak forest within the "ridge complexes" associated with this end moraine top. Large coarse woody debris absent; small-medium coarse woody debris common. Fire scars on older cut (?) stumps. Mode canopy DBH for community is 32cm. Soil: sandy loam over loam over clay over loam.

Plot rather ecotonal between lowland hardwood and mesic. Most Betula in stand DD/DY. Slender coarse woody debris common. Recent large blowdowns, mostly Populus, common. Very large tip-up mounds common. No cut stumps, no fire scars. Tilia and multi-stemmed.

Fire scars on old stumps. No cut stumps. Slender coarse woody debris common. Recent medium to large blowdowns occasional. Old tip-up mounds common. Plot parallels hiking trail to within 5m. Topography with steep slopes for area. Upper to middle slope. Litter of leaves/twigs.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Occasional fire scars. Stumps infrequent and heavily decayed. No standing water. High-water marks ~50cm above muck bowls. Slender coarse woody debris abundant. Moss restricted to tree terraces.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Canopy trees slender. Occasional large tip-up mounds. Large coarse woody debris nearly absent, medium coarse woody debris common, slender coarse woody debris uncommon. Occasional burn scars on old stumps. No cut stumps observed. Upper to middle slope. Litter of leaves and twigs.

Very open below continuous canopy. Slender to medium coarse woody debris common to patchy abundant. Tip-up mounds infrequent. Fire scars on older coarse woody debris. No cut stumps found. Mature E7 Pinus strobus in community but rare. Litter of leaves and twigs.

Rich, slender oak forest occupying narrow trough at slope base. Medium coarse woody debris common-abundant. Quercus rubra snags occasional. Microtopography level with few tip-ups. No cut stumps; fire scars on old stumps occasional. Excellent Botrychium habitat. Litter of leaves and twigs.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Mature forest on a crest of a ridge complex. Medium coarse woody debris abundant. Most blowdowns without tip-ups. Old tip-up mounds common. Old stumps with fire scars. Possible "previous pine" site. d45 snags common throughout.

Mature northern hardwood forest very open and sparse below 5m; typical of this east to northeast mid-slope. Slender coarse woody debris common, but never abundant. Many recent slender blow downs throughout. Tip-up mounds occasional. Most Tilia multi-stemmed. Few old stumps throughout, older one with fire scars. Middle-lower slope.

Slender mixed deciduous forest with frequent but never common Pinus strobus. Medium coarse woody debris common. Old tip-up  mounds frequent, but stumps uncommon. Deciduous trees rather even aged and often multi-stemmed. Fire scars on older stumps. Releve chosen to capture a community with healthy white pine. Lower to toe slope.

Releve captures typical community in vicinity. Large old pine stumps with fire scars occasional. Slender and medium coarse woody debris common but never abundant. Tip-up mounds infrequent. Middle to lower slope.

Community with stunted Larix and Picea most below 5m. Releve characterizes conifer portion of large poor fen. Snags occasional; coarse woody debris nearly absent. No signs of disturbance. Moderate forb browse. No standing water.

Plot includes soupy/mucky "holes" with graminoids and sundew and submerged Sphagnum but little else. Most of plot is sphagnum carpet with very short graminoids. Typical of open areas in large poor fen complex. Beautiful muck pockets with cool to cold water - springs? No obvious wellings.

Dense alder swamp with no standing water and without deep muck holes. Community undisturbed although old field 100 m west. Community varies between Alnus and Salix dominance with Alnus most abundant. Much slender coarse woody debris below.

Northern hardwood forest with multi-stemmed Tilia common. Medium coarse woody debris common; tip-ups common with a few (rare) large, deep (0.5m) bowls. Canopy patchy, rarely continuous. Occassional continuous patches of Carex pensylvanica and also occasional thick shrub patches. No cut stumps observed, but obviously a disturbance history, burn scars on older coarse woody debris.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Slender mature black ash swamp with Larix scattered throughout and grades to SS in patches. Rather dry with no standing water and only moist muck. Slender coarse woody debris common. Shrubby overall. 0.5 m from tree bases to muck. Releve typical of forested wetland in site.

Slender mature northern hardwood forest with previous pine characteristics. Slender to medium coarse woody debris common; tip-ups common. Fire scars on old stumps. Old barbed wire in corner of plot but no noticeable change in vegetation.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Mature mixed-deciduous. Forest typical for site and with a less-dominate previous pine feel than 7649. Large tip-ups occasional, fire scars on older large stumps. Recent large Populus grandidentata blow-downs occasional. Rather shrubby throughout. Topographic position: crest/upper.

Mature slender wet-mesic forest representative of lower forest in site. Medium-large coarse woody debris common; sometimes abundant. Mixed age and species canopy. Burn scars on old stumps, most Betula and Populus DY. Shrubby throughout with some very thin patches. Soil: loam A horizon, over sandy loam over loam

Rather low diversity shrub swamp dominated by Salix and Carex lacustris. Plot typical of basin. Community with frequent but small open patches with same graminoid cover, but no Salix. No standing water. Rather easy to walk through.

A rather monotypic wet meadow/rich fen throughout. Releve in small contained depression surrounded by upland forest. No shrubs >2m throughout; shrubs rare. No standing water, not floating. No hummocks. Easy walking.

Typical forest for site. Thick D4 layer, patchy oak canopy and rather sun-loving forb layer. Large tip-up mounds common, medium-large coarse woody debris common throughout. Fire scars on old coarse woody debris.

Typical emergent marsh fringe for Black Bass Lake. Community floating to <5m of water's edge then firm >5m in. Appears undisturbed except for beaver runs and water holes. Grades into shrub swamp and wet meadow toward west upland.

A mature northern hardwood forest with a strong maple basswood feel overall very open below; D4 layer almost absent. Slender medium coarse woody debris common, much of it Betula papyrifera. Shallow tip-up mounds frequent. No cut stumps observed but nearly all Tilia multi-stemmed. Litter of oak leaves and twigs. Topographic context: upper/middle.

High quality rich fen grading into poor fen with patchy emergent marsh. Community with frequent beaver channels. Water ankle deep. Community not floating and without edge moat typical of wetlands with beaver activity.

Open poor fen appears undisturbed and quite mature with a very thick layer of Sphagnum and Chamadaphne above water table. Forbs entirely absent. Releve typical of western arrowhead of large wetland complex. Many graminoids scenessing and without fruit or flowers.

Mature Pines scattered over skinny deciduous understory. Fire scars on old Pine stumps. Slender to medium coarse woody debris common. Shallow tip-up mounds common. Recent blowdowns occasional. Overall a young forest with scattered large red and whit pine. Occasional Pinus strobus seedlings throughout. Litter of needles and leaves.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Slender mostly multi-stemmed, Quercus rubra and Betula papyrifera, forest typical of much of this site. Medium-large coarse woody debris common; microtopography with abundant low crests and troughs proving diverse micro-habitats. Overall 50-60 years old. Recovering from logging? Litter of leaves and twigs. Worms present. Many pebbles and cobbles present in soil.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: B(C)-rank oak forest typical of the shrubbier oak forests hereabouts. Canopy Betula papyrifera and Populus grandidentata just outside plot. Medium large coarse woody debirs common. Microtopogy undulating with out large tip-up mounds. Compare to 7662 on north slope.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: B-rank. Extremely sparse and open below D5. Typical of pure oak stand north northwest of here within SE 1/4 4. Slender to medium coarse woody debris common and mostly Betula and Populus. Small areas of black duff, but no worm casting. Compare to 7661. Topographic context: upper/middle.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Mature mixed age stand with canopy Populus grandidentata and Betula papyrifera in community. Old stumps with fire scars. Medium to large coarse woody debris common (some decayed). Most tip-up mounds moss-covered. Scattered exposed rocks common. No worm casting patches. Worms in A horizon.

Young slender stand with occasional cut stumps and fire scars on old stumps. Medium coarse woody debris common, but never abundant. Small depressions with seasonal flooding common. Old tip-up mounds common. Bi-modal DBH 33-35cm & 22-25cm. Ground layer has survived history of disturbance very well.

Mature, mixed-aged stand with all sizes of coarse woody debris common, but never abundant. Old stumps with fire scars. Small bare patches in groundlayer with worm casts. Overall a moderate slender community. Old and new tip-ups occasional. Middle to lower slope.

Mature oak forest rather sparse and open below continuous canopy from 4-5m above. Community on a small gently sloping upland "island" between black ash swamp and shrub swamp. Medium coarse woody debirs very common, most from tip-ups. Worms present in A horizon, litter of leaves and twigs.

Mixed age, mixed deciduous mesic forest transitioning from Populus to Quercus or maple basswood dominated. Medium coarse woody debris common; old tip-up mounds common. d4-6 Betula and Quercus snags occasional throughout. Plot on an undulating and rolling local high point. Slope crest to upper. Heavy evidence of worm activity.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Mixed deciduous forest with mixed age and size structure. Tip-up mounds abundant. Medium coarse woody debris abundant, occasional recent large coarse woody debirs. Slight "previous pine" feel. Fire scars on older coarse woody debirs. Overall a younger forest than area. Slope crest/upper. Soil dry and rocky sandy loam.

Slender stand rather sparse below 1m, but rather shrubby above 1m. Large old stumps common; all with fire scars. Old large tip-up mounds common. Plot within 5m of EM/OW edge yet mesic. Slender medium coarse woody debris common.

Open poor fen with scattered low Larix dominated by Sphagnum, Carex and Camadaphne. No open water, feels like a very thick mat when walking. Very pretty. This plot in first zone out from center as shown on airphoto.

Mature stand with continuous cover from 5m and above. Local topography undulating with plot on higher ground. Slender to medium coarse woody debris common. Fire scars on older debris. Bryophytes absent even on tree bases. Old tip-up mounds common.

A rather open D4 coverage with groundlayer very similar to emergent marsh/wet meadow to west. Larix and BA snags 5-15m, occasional to common throughout. No standing water but moist soil. Mosses restricted to lowest areas/bowls.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Mature stand abutting the EM fringe of Shakopee Lake. Rather shrubby. Slender-medium coarse woody debris common; very large coarse woody debris rare. Most Tilia multi-stemmed with many large DBH trees throughout. Bryophytes restricted to tree bases. Slope middle to lower.
Uneven-aged stand. Some gaps from elm die-off, now mostly filled in. Rich herb layer. Ground soft w/good humus. Black silty/clayey loam. Does not appear grazed. Moderate amount of woody debris.

Gently sloping upland near river. Tall somewhat gappy canopy of 40-60 cm Acer & Tilia. Abundant cwd, some well decayed. Tip-up mounds & hol- lows. Silty loam w/snd. Affectd by elm disease. Never grzed
Old-growth forest on gently sloping upland near river. Uneven-aged canopy. Open understory w/patchy shrub & herb layers. Old well-decayed logs. Silty A, clayey B horizon. Some cutting. Grazed in 30s

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Small area of mature oak forest w/in larger forest characterized by large open-grown oaks & maples w/younger & early successional trees filling voids. Cont thin litter. Dark silty loam.

Mesic forest on slope adj to wetland. Canopy trees 30-50cm dbh. Some cutting (mainly dead trees) "+" gaps from elm disease. Cont 1-2" litter. Some humus. Dark silty loam w/gravel below. Occas Acer snag.
Small area of mature forest on slope above lake terrace. Canopy trees 25-70cm dbh. Occas gap from elm disease. Rich herb layer. Cont 1" lit- ter. Rich humus. Dark silty loam. Well-decayed large logs.
Mature forest on level upland. Canopy trees 30-70cm dbh. Moist site adj to ephemeral pool. Rich herb layer. Thin cont leaf litter. Dark silty/clayey loam. Decaying logs & recent small snag in plot

Tamarack swamp on quaking mat in part of 80-acre wetland basin adj to lake. Patchy canopy of 10-25cm dbh trees. Cont sphagnum & abund Calo- pogon below. No disturbance in stand but hwy runs thru basin
Stand of 5-10cm dbh Larix on hummocky floating sphagnum mat in small basin surrounded by rolling forested upland. pH = 3.9-4.1 in hollows, 3.6 on hummocks. Circled by open area w/wiregrass, bog birch

Center of long wetland complex domianted by Carex lasiocarpa and C. oligosperma. Sphagnum varies from absent to complete coverage with hummocks. Tamarack and bog birch stunted. Water pools <5% area. Hummocks 1-3m diameter.

Black spruce swamp with tamarack. Crowns 5-10m tall, mode DBH 10-20cm, max DHB occasional to 30cm. Large kettle bog complex between sand moraine ridges. Large, deep, well drained hummocks dominated 50-75% of area. Depressions with Sphagnum and water to 1cm depth, saturated peat beneath. Next to shrub swamp dominated by bog birch.

Black spruce in large Sphagnum bog in kettle-hole depressions between moraine ridges. large (0.7m tall) hummocks. Overall depressions 50-75% spruce crowns 10-15 m tall, mode DBH 10-20cm max size 30cm.
Mature tamarack swamp, mixed size class, mode DBH 15-25cm; max common to 41cm. Dry late season without rain. Hummocks >75%, depressions without water. Seems more like white cedar swamp.
Rich mature forest on midslope "terrace". Limited selective logging in the past. No past grazing. Floor has thick leaf litter and very nice soft organic duff. Season is 2 weeks ahead of schedule.

place_name: Swan Lake WMA: North Star Unit
remarks: In flat bottomland along Swan Lake outlet. Soil is moist black silt. Even-aged, youngish forest with thin canopy.

Even-aged stand of approximately 50-80 years old, trees with high species diversity. In cove, on heavy, moist, black silty soil. Typical site on river valley sides within Glacial Lake Minnesota basin. This season early.

Mature forest with tall, straight trees, and very open under canopy. Acer average 35-40cm DBH and goes up to 56cm. Dense litter layer. Nice duff layer. Black silt loam soil. In very shallow depression on level upland.
A horizon a perfect black loam, depth 18-20 inches, B slightly lighter brown. Deep loam. With NP Sather.
Just upslope from a ravine dominated by bur oak, heading up into Craetagus and scattered bur oak grubs. Burned in spring. Some light grazing disturbance during winter. Grazing history.

Burned in spring, pastured by ponies last winter, previous history of grazing. Just above a distinctive gravel layer. Soil here is stoney. Just below upper slope down to midslope. Bare ground 10-15%. Upper to middle slope.

Characteristic of open peatland to slightly shrub covered area along east to west axis of Lake Superior rocky beachline behind beach ridge. Open graminoid area to east, conifer swamp to north. pH=6.4, cond=196.2, Abs=.225.
Typical of more open area of linear wetland just north of Lake Superior beach. Area north is cedar/tamarack scrub swamp; area west contains more shrub. pH.=6.9, Cond=73.1 Absorb 0.196 Peat >1 m

Thick canopy for community type with open patches dominated by Betula papyrifera and allegenioensis. B layer patchy, Ledum and blueberry dominate. Forbs unusually sparse. Continuous Sphagnum on "40+cm" mucky peat. Soil is organic peat to 40cm+ with much woody content and sphagnum and herbaceous remains.

High to mid quality floating mat cattail marsh along northwest shore of Lake Shakopee. Dominated by Typha x glauca and T. latifolia. Typical forb coverage and diversity and higher graminoid diversity than typical. Mat .5-1m thick.

Represents largest, most diverse Minerotrophic Tamarack Swamp in ecological region. Trees 15-30 cm DBH. Substrate of pronounced hummocks and wet depressions. Peat 3-5 feet deep. No Sphagnum here. (M. Lee).

Lowland hardwood forest. Wooded slope with Fraxinus nigra, Ulmus America, and Acer negundo. Island grazed from early to mid 1900s. Much of island non-forested in 1939 photo. Very poorly drained alluvial soils. Data also 6/8/79.

Lowland hardwood forest. Wooded floodplain with Tilia, Ulmus americana, and Acer negundo. Island grazed from early to mid 1900s. Much of the island nonforested in 1939 photo. Very poorly drained alluvial soils. Data also 6/8/79.

Lowland hardwood forest. Wooded floodplain island with Tilia, Celtis and Acer negundo. Sparse canopy of box elders tapped for syrup at 1920. Grazed annually from 1920-69. 1939 photo shows scattered trees. Very poorly drained alluvium.

npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: Floodplain forest on island in MS River. Sparse canopy of Acer saccharinum, A. negundo and Fraxinus pennsylvanica. Open below with continuous Laportea. Grazed 1900-49. Dense trees in 1939 photo. Very poorly drained alluvium.

npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: Floodplain forest on island in MS River. Sparse canopy of Acer saccharinum, Fraxinus pennsylvanica, Acer negundo and Ulmus americana. Open below with abundant Laportea and Glechoma. Grazed from 1900-49. Very poorly drained alluvium.

A disturbed wet meadow (shrub subtype?) in railroad ROW. Grades into very disturbed wet prairie (mainly Poa pratensis). Exotic grasses and bird's foot trefoil invading. Not sure about willows, but I have not seen this type of woody invasion in railroad in this part of state. See also railroad Survey 153.
Lowest quality site I have surveyed for this project. Area rank with Laportea. Butternut and elm dyinh. Many downed trees - natural and selective. No sedges. See spring releve #8232.
Summer plot of spring releve #8233. Large sugar maple down just west of plot since the spring and more light is going to come into plot. No graminoids and little litter.
See spring releve 8234. Very rank area on floodplain. Canopy primarily red elm - disease will change area. Numerous deer trails. Debris in northwest corner. No sugar maple.
Summer plot of spring releve #8235. Much woody debris on this land between channel of Prairie Creek old channel. Old barbed wire fence through plot.
Summer plot of spring releve #8236. Area has experienced continued erosion from recent rains. Little litter.
Summer plot of spring releve #8237. Area has diverse woody flora, but relatively few herbaceous species. Ground moist and there is little litter. Some erosion from recent rains.
See spring releve #8238. Community unlike other dwarf trout lilly releves as it has very few shrubs/tree reproduction. un-diverse ground layer. Butternut and elm dying. Erosion.
Summer plot of spring releve #8239. Area atypical of preserve as there is a large gap from fallen Box elder. Also fewer D4 trees - open. Canopy just over 50% coverage.

This is a summer releve of #8240. Butternut and red elm dying. Very large green ash at top of hill. Sedges primarily along numerous deer trails. Erosion serious problem. Moss covers ~5% of plot. Little litter. Lots of centipeds.
Summer releve of 8241. Area where dwarf trout lilly common now has few herb species. 5-10m tree layer missing. Floodplain area rank with weedy species and sedges.

This area will look much different in several years. The canopy is dying red elm and butternut. Odd species due to eroded areas that flank the plot. Moss covers 75% of plot. No sugar maple. See spring releve 8242. Topographic context: upper/middle/lower.
Releve in jack pine mixed with red oak and aspen, just north of Host- age Lake. Plot flat, soils Nymore Series and collected for Oak Ridge soils project.
Open stand of jack pine between Bonnie Lake and Bass Lake.  Stand mixed with some big red pines, red oak, birch, and aspen. The releve is on level ground, soils are Menahga, possibly dune sand.
Releve on transition between poorly drained and better drained soils (see remarks on original releve sheet) Releve size: 2000 square miles (see also a releve by R. Darling, 7 Sep 1971).
The site has been burned at least once. Releve size 2 hectares.

West to northwest facing midslope; fairly even topography with silty clay loam over clay soils with gravel. Area is managed by prescribed burning; portion containing releve site burned within last five years. Glacial hill till prairie.

Nearly level, very moist site, slightly hummocky site with 6-8 inches somewhat poorly drained black silt-loam over yellow clay soils. Surrounded by thickets of Populus spp., Betula pumila, Salix spp. or Cornus stolonifera. Site is large wetland/aspen parkland complex. Many shrub/aspen thickets or groves interspersed by Phragmites/Typha wetlands and wet-mesic (calcareous) prairie.

Releve within wet to wet-mesic transition vegetation found on nearly flat, poorly drained clay loam soils. Site burned in spring 1986. Level, poorly drained black clay loam soils dominated by wet and wet-mesic prairie vegetation. Releve representative of wet to wet-mesic transition.

Lower slope due east. Mesic vegetation. Burned in spring 1986. Loamy clay soil over clay. Releve plot representative of lower slopes dominated by natives but low diversity and density of native forbs.

Very dry, slightly convex site near top of 15 degree southwest facing slope. Soils, Buse-Sioux complex; 1-2 inches silt loam over sand and gravel. Releve is of the driest prairie on site. Very few exotic species. Site appears to be most typical of Great Plains grassland structure. Prairie has not been recently burned. Grazed up to 1979, then part of prairie tax credit program.
Releve in open bunchgrass community found on excessively drained gravelly crest of beach ridge.
Releve in open bunch grass community found on excessively drained gravely crest of a beach ridge.
Level crest of beach ridge with 2 inches of loam sand over sand and gravel. Sioux sandy loam. Grazed within the last several years, not presently grazed. Located southeast of excavated gravel area.

Releve in open, xeric bunchgrass community found on excessively drained crest on beach ridges. Area burned (hot fire) in spring 1985. Possible reason for low species diversity? On sioux loamy coarse sand.

Releve located on one of a series of moderately grazed morainic hills located east of a large wetland/shrub carr complex of barnesville wildlife management area. Langhei barnes loam soils. Soil: 3 inches silt loam over fine silty (clay) sand. Plot 5-10 degrees mostly north facing slope. Clumps of vegetation interspersed with small areas of bare ground having gravel at the surface. Releve encompasses transition from hill crest to case of lower slope.

Releve located on steep 20-25 degree east facing upper slope of one of a series of gravelly moranic hills overlooking Lake Christina. Plants are clumped in some areas with bare ground and some surface gravel between plants.
Releve located on east to southeast facing 30 degree slope of one of a series of gravel hillsides (upper midslope) which border Lake Christina. Lichens and mosses present on surface gravel.
