RELEVE IN OPEN BUNCHGRASS COMMUNITY FOUND ON EXCESSIVELY DRAINED, GRAVELLY CREST OF BEACH RIDGE. SIOUX LOAMY COARSE SAND SOIL (12-14" SANDY LOAM OVER SAND & SMALL GRAVEL). BOULDERS COVER <5%.

Releve located on one of a series of moderately grazed moranic hills located east of a large wetland complex in Barnesville wildlife management area. Soil: 1-12 inches loam over stones and cobbles with medium sized stones and small pebbles near surface.

Releve located on one of a series of moderately grazed moranic hills of Sioux loamy coarse sand soils east of a large wetland complex of Barnesville wildlife management area. Prairie intact on hill tops and side slopes.

Small, less than one acre prairie fen on terrace between drier prairie knolls and wet prairie.  Just to the east of Barnesville wildlife management area. Found on Markey muck - very poorly drained, strongly calcareous soils. Carex sterils, Lobelia kalmi, Picea glauca.

Old-growth Northern hardwoods dominated by Acer saccharum mixed with 2nd growth northern hardwoods. Acer saccharum short in stature and many frost cracks. Soils: coarse gravelly loam, well-drained. Ground layer: herb-30%,deadfall-10%,litter-60%. Overstory is open because of deadfall. Three old maple snags and large paper birch. Continuous cover of Acer seedlings, herb layer is depauperate. Scattered stumps found throughout, but no evidence of logging.

Old-growth northern hardwoods dominated by Acer saccharum. Black Ash aged at 105 years. Ground layer: herb-75%, deadfall-5%, litter-20%. Soils: well-drained coarse loamy, fine sandy loam (Releve soil sample).
Releve site is representative of the prairie of the side slopes. 10 cm of silt loam over 15 cm gravelly light-colored clay loam. Area was burned in the spring 1986.
Releve within mesic prairie area on deep, poorly drained Vallers loam. Mesic areas interspersed with wet prairie and swales and depressions dominated by Typha. Black loam over clay loam.

Level, poorly drained loam with saline groundwater influence bordered on east by extensive wetland complex. Saline prairie dominated by Schizachyrium scoparium, Sporobolus, asper. East grading into tallgrass prairie west. Barnesville Wildlife Management Area.
Moderately saline area on Deerwood muck (very poorly drained calcareous). Characteristic low diversity and density of forbs. Dominated by Schizachyrium scoparium and Sporobolus asper.
Releve in hyper-saline area adjacent to stream course. Area sparsely vegetated; low stature of vegetation. Forbs in low abundance and diversity. Adjacent to Anna Gronseth Prairie.
Mesic se facing 10-15 degree mid-slope. Well-drained loamy soils with clay at 8-10 cm.  Occassional glacial erratics on surface; moderate deadfall, snags, but no evidence of cutting or grazing.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Located in mostly level bottom of a ravine. Slight N slope. Ground is undulating because of tip-ups and rotted deadfalls. Deadfalls on ground cover less than 5%. Two photos taken.

Gentle 2-3% south-facing slope. Mesic site with deep leaf litter layer, 25% cover. Large logs on forest floor. All characteristics of old growth forest sugar maple, basswood and yellow birch. One remnant charred stump, well decayed. Moderated dead fall, no large logs.
Near roadside willow, west side of road 50 m.
Near willow, east side of road.
Water Table 0-1 CM
Onwer said beaver dam has flooded area for past 3 years, previously cut for hay.
Water table = 0 cm. Disturbed poor fen, dried out by adjacent road ditches. Bird habitat study.
Water table = 0 cm. See releve 0061, part of bird habitat study.
Water table= 0 cm.
American bittern nesting site. Water table =5 cm.

Conductivity = 90. Water Depth: 10 cm.
Conductivity = 230, water table just below surface much dead Carex in hollows, short shrub area adjacent to tall shrub area surrounding central wet open area.
Water table at surface ground matted with much dead Carex rostrata.
Water table 10-40 cm, large patches of open water.
Conductivity=47, appears to have been burned over (1969 photo).
Conductivity = 39, water table 0-5cm, very hummocky.

Releve plot is on southeast slope of limestone ridge, just below grazed top and just above weedy toe of slope. Soil is < .3m deep and with limestone flags (Brodale). L 1 a present.  Presence list, 9004.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Toe to middle-slope of northwest face of gravelly ridge dominated by white pine. Stand of virgin pine, sugar maple, red oak, yellow. birch. ca. 1894. No stumps, old-fence, recreational trails. Single fire scars.
Old-growth northern hardwoods dominated by sugar maple.  Soils fine-sandy loam, well-drained, sampled.  Black ash aged at 105 years. Deadfall 15%, litter 45%, herb 40%.
Releve typical of sand prairie on upper slopes. Bur oaks small and scattered. Soil is light-colored sands with some gravel, severely eroded in spots. Exotic weeds common on eroded surfaces. PNA-78.

Old-growth northern hardwoods with patches of second growth. Dominated by Acer saccharum, Betula lutea and Tilia americana. Eastern hemlock in deep ravine. Yellow birch approx age 164 years-70cm DBH. Soils: deep silty or loamy, MN Soil Atlas.

Nearly level mesic prairie, high quality, surrounded by degraded prairie. Good forb composition. Threatened by Melilotus alba and brome encrochment from adjacent degraded prairie. Many surface boulders.

Old-growth northern hardwoods. Soils: silty or loamy over rock, well drained light-colored soils (MN Soil Atlas).  Red oak aged at 192 years. Ground layer: herbaceous-30%, woody-60%, deadfall-5%, litter-5%.
Releve in mature forest on mesic soils, with large boles on forest floor and occasional snags.  Representative of least disturbed maple-basswood sites.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Releve located on uneven, hummocky ground created by old tip-up mounds. Representative of least disturbed maple-basswood sites.  Photos: 21, 20, 19.  Relatively flat, < 4% slope to SW.
Releve located on nearly level, slightly hummocky silty clay soils with 6 inches of organic matter. Representative of least disturbed sites dominated by wet-mesic species.

Old-growth northern hardwoods, dominated by Acer saccharum, mixed with second growth northern hardwoods. Sugar maple-short in stature and many frost cracks. Releve soil sample. Ground layer: herbaceous-10%, woody-70%, deadfall-10%, litter-10%.
Shape of releve limited by extent of community, moatside community just north of bearing tree, extends 20m to east and west, width of community only 10m between water and mat.
Open floating mat on south side of lake, similar community on northeast side of lake.
Open tamarack spruce community, southwest end of lake.

Releve size is extent vegetation type where clustered bur reed occurs. Landward side moat 12m long (e-w), 8m wide (n-s). 7 dominant species, each occupy ca. 1/7 total plant cover, open water 50% of area.
Releve is directly uphill of clustered bur reed location in a facies with more continuous shrub layer than the area a few meters west. Disturbed area, logged in 1927.
Releve taken on slightly convex rise. Zone clearly marked by presence of Stipa spartea. Represents true mesic phase here. Currently used as hay meadow. Soils: silty clay loam, clay loam.
Represents a wet-mesic type of vegetation.  Currently used as a hay meadow.  Soils: silty clay loam, clay loam.
Slight swell or rise, better drained than surrounding area.  Long history of haying, so generally low stature of vegetation.  No litter. Soils: fine textured black loam - slightly sticky.

Level low "flat" north of previous releve (8703) by ca. 25 yards. General height of sward ca. 2 dm. This plot fairly typical of the shorter grass, wet mesic-more diverse than some. Soils: dark fine textured loam.
Water table =15cm, previously higher this summer; very wet with deep holes in spots.
Water table = 10-15 cm some dead Carex thatch with patches of decomposed vegetation.
Water table = 0-1 cm, area very seem very distrubed, apparently dried out by roa d ditch.
Releve typical of wet meadows in area. Releve conducted on Jul 15 and Aug 31, 1987.
Releve typical of wet meadows in the area. Releves conducted on 7/l5 and 8/31/87.
Releve conducted in community transitional between wet meadow and calcareous fen. Releves conducted on 6/02,7/13 and 9/01/87.
Releve typical of calcareous fen communities in the area. Releves conducted on 6/01, 7/13, 9/01/87.
releve typical of calcareous fen community in the area. Releve conducted on 7/15, 8/31/87.
Releve typical of calcareous fen community in area. Releve conducted on 6/01,7/13,9/01/1987.
Releve typical of shrub-carr communities in the area. Releve conducted on 7/l5, 8/28/87.
Releve typical of sand delta communities in the area.

Releve on crest to midslope. Typical of mixed jack pine and black oak savanna containing elements of both jack pine woodland and open barrens. Soils are sand with chert as an inclusion (20% bare sand).
Plot typical of oak forest on crest of hill. Some stumps on plot probably selective cutting of oak. Some old fencing nearby, probably grazed in distant past.

Plot typical of large diameter (40-65cm) red and white oak forest on knoll southeast of stream. Understory reproduction good - american elm, basswood, sugar maple. No obvious logging or grazing. Plot of forest-grown trees.

Releve typical of bog-birch carr on Sphagnum/wire grass mat. Sphagnum hummocks well developed, 3-4dm. Example of depauperate flora of bogs in southern Minnesota. Tamarack grove in center of bog. Peat inclusion.

Releve typical of quaking sphagnum mat. Sphagnum hummocks well-developed 4-5dm. Example of depauperate flora of acid bogs in southern Minnesota. Northwest end of bog flooded by beaver. Peat inclusion.
Typical of alder swamp with sphagnum mat. Alder clump bases 30-40cm above ground. Scattered red maples 5 inch diameter.
Tamarack variable in age 10-20cm diameter. Tamarack cut over in part - several stumps. Sphagnum mat variable with nearly all Chamaedaphne cover to sedge cover.
Releve typical of small prairie just below overlook. Cut juniper logs and charcoal suggest past management. Thin sandy loam over bedrock with cobbles on surface. Glenn-Lewin site 087.
Highly degraded overgrazed pasture dominated by exotics with a few native species on quartzite outcrops.  Buchloe on outcrops.
Best Prairie Remnant on Red Rock Ridge. In Prairie Tax Credit and Registry. Owner aware of Lespedeza leptostachya EO.
Mesic portion of prairie, just above Quartzite outcrops near center of north side of tract. Best remnant on Red Rock Ridge. Owner aware of EO (Lespedeza leptostachya), in PTC and Registry.
Difficult to tell whether this area has been broken in past, dominated by old field vegetation, recently disturbed by earth moving equipment. Buchloe at edges of rocks.
Releve in burned unit of tract about 50 meters north and 50 meters east of sw corner.
Mainly degraded pasture, area with native species about 40 m south of Preserve boundary, Bouteloua spp. very visible here in fall, Buchloe dactyloides on rocks, searched unsuccessfully for L.lepto.
In burned portion of tract about 80 meters west of Preserve fenceline near top of hill. No Lespedeza located within area of this releve late r in summer.
Midslope in west part of unburned unit of Preserve.
Tiny remnant with prairie species, severely invaded by shrubs in east facing draw on south side of creek.
Remnant of prairie vegetation on north-facing slope, very nice, would be interesting to see adjoining flat area to south without grazing. This area is south of the stream.
Near top of hill in north unit of pasture used by Kosell. Grazed but less degraded than expected in this area.
In flat area just S of fence between N and S units of pasture used by Kosell. Buchloe, Schedonnardus on nearby rocks.
In managed area in center of parking circle.  Area was burned in May, 1986. Lespedeza leptostachy and hybrid Lespedeza x capitata present.
Prairie never broken, not grazed for years. Homestead in same family as at settlement.  In Prairie Tax Credit. Owner aware of need to burn and has requested burn from area wildlife manager.
This releve in pastured area where prairie species visible near top of hill near northeast part of actual pasture. This is not area where Lespedeza leptostachya subsequently found.
On steeper NE-facing slope, still in actual pasture, but area similar to area where Lespedeza leptostachya subsequently found, should be searched more carefully.
Releve on west and northwest-facing slopes of small isolated hill Spring aspect excellent. Revisited and less impressive in Sept. Too steep to have been disturbed. Good wet-mesic spot just east.
Small prairie remnant in ravine. Needs burning. Buchloe and Scheddonardus on quartzite bedrocks in valley. In prairie tax credit, owner is interested in burning.
Releve in nearly flat area at crest of hill, west end active pasture, heavily grazed in 1988. Spring quality of this prairie was best this year. Bush clover is at base of n-facing slope east end.
Ungrazed prairie remnant north of pasture fence. Releve is on north- west facing slope near road. Bush clover on W, N and E facing slopes (E-facing downhill of rock pile). Wildfire here June 1988.
Releve near top of west-facing slope at southeast end of prairie, about 30 m north of section line. In PTC. Grazed by 180 head cattle until 6 years ago. Bad mulch buildup here. Needs fire.
Dry Sand Praire north of Bunker Hills County Park. Has history of grazing but regeneration is good. Releve is on level ground. Oenothera rhombipetala collected.
Very homogeneous tamarack swamp west of Cedar Drive and North of Cedar Creek.

Sand prairie, relatively long undisturbed. Has an extensive lichen mat. Releve is on level ground. Oenothera rhombipetala, Aristida tuberculosa, and Hieracium longipilum collected. Very extensive lichen/moss mat.
Dry prairie on east-facing slope of morainic hill, 16 miles southwest of Detroit Lakes.
Sandy beach of Artichoke lake 10.5 miles north of Correll and 0.1 mile east of Route 25.
Floodplain Forest 6 miles north-northeast of Bellingham; Lac Qui Parle WMA.  Releve on level ground.
Releve in sand prairie opening within overgrown oak sand savanna and on north side of very large, disturbed blowout.
Large, fairly typical tamarack swamp.  Quite uniform throughout.

Sand savanna - Calamovilfa dominated. Releve located just east of the highest dune hill at the site. Vegetation was typical of that on dune slopes and crests in the northern port ion of the site. Gopher mounds present. Ground cover: 35% litter with lichens and bryophytes, 15% bare ground, 30% graminoid cover, and 20% herbaceous cover.
Relatively thick ground cover in this part of savanna, south of center of site.  The southernmost of the two releve locations. Soils: loamy fine sand. 6-12% slopes. 10% litter cover.

Relatively sparse ground cover in this portion of the savanna, north of center. Disturbed sand adjacent to releve.  Northernmost of the two releves at this site. Soil: Loamy fine sand. 6-12% slopes. Ground cover: 28% graminoid, 12% herbaceous, 50% litter, and 10% bare.
In northcentral area of large swamp-complex southwest of West Twin Lake. Along east side of north-south trending trail through swamp. A few dead paper birch and tamarack in shrub swamp.

Releve is located east of Lower Birch Lake in a "wire-grass" meadow of Carex lasiocarpa with Sphagnum below. Releve is "bog" because of continuous Sphagnum, but grades into sedge meadow or shrub swamp.
Releve located in south-central portion of the savanna just north of large shallow sedge meadow. On nearly level site, no trees in plot. 15m x 15m plot. Gopher mounds present. Fall burn in 1987.

Site is owned by Minneapolis Girl Scout Council. The only good natural community is white oak forest on the west and northwest of Stone Lake. This is one of two very similar releves in forest; has prickly ash.

Site is owned by Minneapolis Girl Scout Council. The only good natural community is white oak forest west and northwest of Stone Lake. One of 2 releves in forest; apparently better shrub and herb layer.
The community is intermediate between conifer swamp and forested bog. Canopy is solid Larix. Soil is organic, well-decomposed, not boggy. Sphagnum is hummocky, continuous. Diversity is low.
Releve collected about 30 meters west of County 5, small population of vegetative Polemonium occidentale here, uncharacteristic of major Polemonium habitat in this swamp.
Releve from area of old growth cedar about 20 meters west of County 5 near south end of wetland. No Polemonium occidentale within releve area."Forestry" data is old-growth data.
Releve from about 350 meters west of County 5. Go west into swamp half way between phone pole 237 and the pole just north of it. "Forestry" data are old growth.
Releve from heart of blooming population Polemonium occidentale about 300 meters west of County 5. 93 blooming Polemonium occidentale in releve plot.
Releve in area that shows as a distinct white opening on aerial photo, north of stream but southeast of area with obvious strip cutting. This is wettest area with large Polemonium population.

Mature Maple-Basswood Forest dominated by Tilia, Ulmus americana, Ulmus rubra, and Quercus borealis. Long history of selective cutting. Incomplete size class distribution, no large down boles, dense herb layer.

Mature to old growth maple-basswood forest dominated by Acer saccharum , Tilia and Quercus borealis. portion with old growth features. Moderate to heavy past selective logging; none now. Sparse deadfall, 50% leaf mulch, no exposed soil.
Releve on level outwash sands. Forest soils O-A-A/B, 0-2.5-9-15cm. Dominant age class 1935(36).
Releve on level outwash 1/4 mi. S of Co rd. 11. Soils moderately dark O-A-B-C, 0-2-11-17cm. Dominant age class 1944.
Releve SW of railroad and NE of Mississippi river. Plot on level out- wash, soils moderately dark O-A-B, 0-3-6-?. Dominant age classes: 1928 and 1941.
Releve approximately 1.5 miles N of Decker Lake. Forest soils, O-A-B1-B2-C, 0-3-8-11-15cm. Stand age variable: 1913, 1917, 1922.
Releve about 1 mile S of Sylvia Lake. Forest soils: O-A-A/B-B-C, 0-1-5-6-9cm. Dominant age class 1943(39).
Approximately 2 miles east of Pinewood. Forest soils: O-A-B1-B2-C, 0-1.5-6-15-30cm. Dominant age class: 1924.
Releve about 1.25 miles NW of Scribner. Forest soils. Dominant age class 1924.
Releve about 0.5 mile W of Wolf Lake. Forest soils. Dominant age class variable: 1917, 1920, 1922, 1939, 1941.
Releve just NW of fire tower. Forest soils. Dominant age classes: 1926(27), 1917.
Releve approximately 1.25 miles S of Shell Lake. Forest soils. Dominant age class: 1938(39).
Releve 0.25 mile W of Lower Twin Lake, just NW of Co. Rd. 21. Forest soils. Age class variable: 1937, 1941, 1946, 1953.
Releve appx 0.25 mile S of Co. Rd. 7. Prairie soils. Age classes: 1917, 1920, 1933.
Releve about 2 miles SE of Osage. Prairie soils. Age classed variable: 1915, 1917, 1942, 1949, 1950.
Releve just N of Blueberry Lake. Prairie soils. Age classes variable: 1911, 1921, 1925, 1937, 1941, 1946, and younger.
Releve in undisturbed school 40 just east of Moran Lake. Prairie soils Age classes variable: 1902, 1910 (red pine), 1913, 1914.
Releve 0.5 mile east of Dorset. Prairie soils. Age classes: 1908, 1907
Releve just south of the Straight river. Prairie soils? Stand age: 1919, 1921, 1953.
Releve 0.5 mile E of Mud Lake. Forest soils. Stand age variable: 1909, 1918, 1941.

Releve 0.5 mile SE of Hwy. 371, just south of Brainerd. Prairie soils. Stand age: 1932?, 1934, 1934.
Prairie soils. Stand age var: 1897, 1932.
Releve 0.5 mile west of lower Twin Lake. Forest soils mapped but appear to be transitional. Stand age: 1927, 1927, 1930.
Releve 1.5 miles SE of lower Twin Lake. Prairie soils. Stand age var: 1938, 1940, 1948.
Releve about 1 mile E of Moran Lake in senescent woodlot. Prairie soils. Stand age: 1925,1943?,1946.
Releve 0.5 mile E of Moran Lake in senescent jack pine woodlot. Prairie soils. Stand age: 1928, 1936, 1936, 1939.
Scenecent jack pine woodlot 0.5 miles SE of Dorset. Prairie soils. Stand age: 1901, 1906, 1909. West of Wentzel's Pond.
Releve on NW shore of 7th Crow Wing Lake. Prairie soils but mapped as forest. Stand age: 1930, 1938?, 1947.
Releve 0.25 mile S of Co. Rd. 44. Forest soils. Stand age variable: 1919, 1924, 1929. Lake Minnie site.
Releve 0.25 mile NE of Brown Lake. Forest soils. Stand age: 1925, 1928, 1928. Lake Minnie site.
Releve appx. 1.5 mile S of Shell River Bridge, Co Rd. 24. Prairie soils. Stand age: 1922, 1922, 1923.
Releve in dry jack pine forest 1 mile W of Lake Minnie. Forest soils. Stand age 1930, 1930.
Releve 3.5 mile NE of Wilton, just east of Big John Pond. Forest soil. Stand age: 1933, 1938?.
Relve 3 mile N of Wilton near Big John Pond. Forest soils. Stand age: 1928(33).
Releve 2 mile N of Wilton, near Big John Pond. Forest soils. Stand age: 1933, 1931, 1936.

Releve 3.5 mile north of Wilton, near Big John Pond. Forest soils. Stand age: 1928, 1930. Plot typical of dry pine forest. Trees 20-50cm DBH. Lots of dead branches and litter on ground. Lots of cut pine stumps.
Releve 1.5 mile N of Scribner, near Big John Pond. Forest soils. Stand age: 1927, 1925.
Dry jack pine forest on prairie soils, 1 mile south of the Mississippi River. Stand age: 1923, 1928.
Releve on forest soils, just west of Bonnie Lake. Stand age: 1917, 1927. Site for Hostage Lake.
Releve in dry jack pine forest on forest soils, just S of Pine River and north of County Road 11. Stand age: 1937, 1941.
Releve in dry jack pine forest just east of road to camping area, betw een Co. Rd. 11 and Pine river. Forest soils. Stand age: 1921, 1941.
Releve 0.25 m. west of Co. Rd. 11. Forest soils. Stand age: 1919, 1924 , 1931.
Plot in mixed jack pine/hardwood stand, 0.5 mi. W of Co. Rd. 3. Forest soils. Stand age: 1914, 1918, 1926.
Releve in dry jackpine forest, 1 mile NE of Dolney Lake. Forest soils mapped, but looks like prairie transition. Stand age 1914,1932.
Releve located north of Lake George, on forest soils. Site collected for mossed by Jan Janssens.
Releve in mesic jack pine forest about 1/4 mile N of Peysenski Lake. Prairie soils with alfic horizon. Photos of Jim from tree.
Releve 0.5 mile N of the Badoura Nursery. Forest soils.
Releve 1.2 miles E of Dorset, just S of the Heartland Trail. Mesic jack pine forest on prairie soils.
Releve 1 mile west of Straight Lake. Senescent jack pine woodlot on prairie soils. Shrub cover very dense with little on floor.
Releve 1 mile west of Straight Lake in senescent Jack Pine woodlot. Prairie soils.

Releve just W of Straight Lake. Stand of senescent jack pine on prairie soils.
Releve 1.5 miles SW of Tripp Lake. Plot in dry jack pine forest on forest soils. Immediately adjacent to the 1976 Badoura fire.
Releve 1 mile E. of Bladder Lake.  Dry jack pine forest on forest soils.
Releve 1 mile E. of Lake Minnie, between Alcolhol Creek and the Schoolcraft River.
Releve is 0.5 mile W. of Hubbard Lake, on forest soils.
Releve is 0.5 mile W. of Co. Rd. 11.  Dry jack pine forest on forest soils.
Plot typical of dry ridge top. Plot partially includes Arenaria rock on plots west side. Soil thin loess, residuum on flaggy bedrock surface.

Mature Maple-Basswood forest dominated by Quercus (oldest to 90 years), Acer saccharum, and Tilia. Best areas with complete range of tree size classes, large down boles, open understory, past logging.
Mature to old-growth maple-basswood forest domianted by Acer saccharum (to 57 cm), Ulmus americana (to 114 cm), Ulmus rubra, and Tilia. Past grazing. Probably destroyed by Highway 14 bypass.
Mature Maple-Basswood Forest dominated by Acer saccharum, Tilia, Ulmus americana, and Ulmus rubra. Elms dying in 1980.  Some selective logging.
Mature Maple-Basswood forest dominated by Tilia, Ulmus, and Quercus borealis (Quercus rubra). On north-facing slope.  Long history of selective cutting.

DSW 22May2018: releve moved to approximate location of grid square 0,0 in 1ha permanent plot based on JCA and EJC sketches and maps from 21Apr79 (copy of sketches attached to DNR releve 6645 field form).

Mature forest (60 years old) on dry mesic slope. Grazing and selective cutting ended about 50 years. Betula papyrifera. Large decaying stumps present. Gently undulating terrain. Sandy loam over sand/gravel. 1 inch A horizon.
Maple-Basswood forest with old growth features.  "Lots" of nice maples at this site not represented by releve.  Dry to dry mesic site. 1/2" humus over 14" C-layer of sandy loam. High site.

Maple-Basswood forest. Little evidence of disturbance, except some stumps. Releve in draw; includes 6 degrees north-facing and 8 degrees south facing slopes. Silt-loam over sandy loam, 0-6 inch A horizon. Low site.
Plot typical of wet prairie area between wet-mesic prairie to north and wetlands to south. Soils clayey, about 30 cm of black, oxygenated clay loam over lighter colored saturated clay.
Plot typical of dry pine forest. Trees 20-50 cm.  Lots of dead branches and litter on ground.  Lots of cut pine stumps.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Plot typical of upper knoll and knoll top. Releve boundaries are one of Taber Allison's grid cells. Tip-up mounds common.
Plot typical of Tamarack swamp in old channels, lower terrace of St. Croix. Topography hummocky, sedge-filled depressions, trees cause hummocks (mossy). Minerotrophic except some Sphagnum.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Plot typical of moderate open areas of forest. Stumps present from timber salvage. Taken too early for many plants.
Plot typical of upper slopes, gentler grade with no rocks. Plot burned last year, cover values slightly adjusted up.
NA
30m west of plot is a hardwood swamp. The upland has probably been grazed but not for at least 50 years. 1938 aerial photos show more open woodland structure.
Large diameter trees are very attractive. Past cutting is evident. Herb diversity and abundance very low in dense shade of young Acer saccharum.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Situated on an esker-like ridge of relatively coarse sandy loam with small gravel. Site has been grazed not long in the past but is a better example of oak forest than other degraded sites.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Mixed Hardwood Swamp with some White Pine.

Plot is along north side of vehicle trail in a conspicuous patch of Hudsonia up face of small dune. Quercus ellipsoidalis and Quercus macrocarpa in groves. Adjacent areas grazed and cut in past. Gopher mounds present. 30% litter cover, 20% bare sand.
Tall, mature alders, very shady below. 3cm max standing water on firm woody peat (muck also in hollows).
Low-rolling upland savanna with wetland sedge meadows. Bur oaks are small to medium sized, short single stems. Similar today to structure in 1939 photos.
Along yamaha fenceline, west side County property at edge of highest dune, the surface of which is totally denuded but ATV use. Several old ATV tracks across plot.

Plot located within boardwalk loop. Patchy cover: Larix and Picea in southern third, more open beyond. Did not walk on mat: species must be visible in plot from boardwalk. Searched for herbs within 2m.
Plot typical of logged pin oak  ridge at crest. Multiple stemmed pin oaks, 20-30 cm. Old trail through plot.
Plot typical of most of area, which has been thinned and burned. Plot includes open sand areas, which are only occasional on site. Soil: fine loamy sand.
Plot typical of dry oak forest with large diameter (50-80cm) pin oaks. Plot in canopy, but much of site with lots of windthrow and brushy openings.
South-southeast facing sand prairie opening on southwest side of Lake Ann. Quercus ellipsoidalis and Q. macrocarpa in groves in troughs and north facing slopes of this dune field.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Plot typical of mesic forest, well above swamp to east, includes part of gap-typical of stand with some wind damage. Some dead black ash. Soils with some cobbles at surface.
Nearly level dry-mesic prairie with sandy loam over sandy clay-loam soils.
Nearly level mesic black soil prairie with haying history.  Black loam soil.
Nearly level wet-mesic site with sand/clay/loam soil. Mesic black soil prairie.
Level;  Good duff layer.
Plot typical of aspen forest, slightly elevated above rich fen to north.
Within the glacial meltwater channel system of Glacial River. Warren. Soils are 6 inches silt-loam over clay. Wet blacksoil prairie.
Within the old glacial river channel on nearly level poorly drained silty clay loam soils to 16 inches. Mesic blacksoil prairie. Bare ground <5%.
Cirsium hillii collected. Glacial till hill prairie.

Degraded glacial till hill prairie remnant no greater than 5 acres on north slope of ravine near head of Little Cottonwood River Prairie between field and creek. Releve in north facing concavity where Lespedeza leptostachya found.
Highly degraded gravel hill prairie.  North-facing slope.  Very dry.
"Improved" native pasture southeast of Sanborn sewage ponds, about 50-60 meters west of county line. Prairie improves west of here. Map dot should go with glacial till hill prairie occurrence #170.
Native pasture southeast of Sanborn sewage ponds. North-facing slope about 130 meters west of county line. Higher quality than pasture east of here. Glacial till hill prairie occurrence #170.

Releve from least diverse slope facing east in smaller remnant of prairie west of ravine. Larger part east of ravine richer in species composition on slope. Level top of hill dominated by native grasses. Grazed 4-5 years ago. Releve about 50m downhill from field.
Isolated and heavily brush-invaded mesic prairie remnant in lower midslope of north-facing slope. Relates to glacial till hill prairie EO #176.

Releve represents the best quality remnant in a heavily grazed and degraded native pasture. Approximately 150 acres native pasture of which approximately 30 acres are prairie remnants. Glacial till hill prairie E.O.#18
North-facing, ungrazed prairie remnant less than 10 acres in size on south side of ravine leading to Des Moines River.  Remnant being invaded by Plum. East end of same ravine is active pasture.
North-facing slope of hill. Part of 50 acre (est.) prairie.  Not grazed for 25-30 years. No Poa in releve plot. Part of Glacial till hill prairie E.O. #182.
Releve on north facing slope northwest of creek. Slope of 30 degrees notable due to absence of Brome or Poa. Not grazed in 25-30 years. Part of 50 acre prairie; glacial till hill prairie E.O. #182.

Top of slope west, less than 5 degrees. Edge of Minnesota River Valley terrace-area dissected by drainage channel. Duff less than 1cm. Sandy loam. Annually hayed portion of prairie. Bare ground 5%. Element: Astragalus lotiflorus. Glacial till hill prairie.
Represents drier portion of prairie; probably quite closely underlain by bedrock(?). 2-3" loam soil over stony loam. Litter layer 3-4cm. Bare ground less than 1 %. Mesic black soil prairie.
Releve collected about 200 meters north of road, very homogeneous area. Forested bog.
Forested bog.
Identified as Old Growth Cedar in Phase II inventory. Tree DBH data available.

Soil is sandy loam, very well drained. Approximately 10% exposed rock cover, including small outcrops and loose gravel to cobble-size rocks. Prairie outside releve includes more sumac, scattered trees. Bluff prairie.
Soil is sandy loam with approximately 5 percent cover by rock outcrops. Bluff prairie.
Heavy thatch layer. Soil silt loam, with approximately 5 percent cover of rock outcrops. Representative of site.
Soil is sandy loam. Approximately 20% of surface consists of limestone rock outcrop, partially covered with crustose lichens. North edge of plot is at top of bluff.
Soil sandy loam. Numerous loose pieces of rock, together with areas of exposed intact bedrock, cover about 15% of surface.
Soil is sandy loam, with many small, exposed limestone outcrops. Evidence of past burning in charred tree stump outside releve and sparse thatch layer. Bluff prairie.
Soil is sandy loam. Approximately 5 % rock outcrop. Releve typical of prairie around and below releve. Slope above with more Poa pratensis, Andropogon gerardii, Sorghastrum nutans.
Releve is on nearly flat ridge top, and is representative of the area. Juniperus communis occurs infrequently outside releve. Approximately 35 % cover of exposed rock.  Bluff prairie.

Sandy loam. Releve includes half of this bluff prairie. Underlying bedrock is sandstone. Brush and trees are encroaching from all sides. Medium to heavy thatch layer. Brush and trees encroaching from edges. Large Quercus macrocarpa on prairie edge.

Sandy loam to sand; approximately 20% exposed rock outcrop, boulders, and loose talus. Releve about 1/3 of the way down from top of slope, in area including more rock outcrop than lower part of slope. Rocks covered by crustose lichens, about 50% cover.
Old-growth white cedar swamp forest about 250 years old dominated by Thuja. Patchy canopy, relatively few large snags. Occasional well-decayed log. Past selective logging.
Superior national forest. District-Comp 329-Stand 48. Old Growth Forest data collected.

Mature lowland white cedar conifer swamp with Fraxinus nigra in every height class. Scattered large Betula lutea clumps very impressive. Much decayed dead-fall. Canopy openings filling with ash. Old windthrows in sample area.
Stand is punctuated with upland islands with red pine. Highly variable stand.  Plot laid out to represent variability of shrub cover and species composition within appparent "Old Growth" area.
Transcribed by Barb Delaney, October 1990 from original- Lustig plot #2. Cover/abundance here merged into height class groups. Cover/abundance seems reasonable--visited 1989.
Typical of shrub swamp north of ditch and road and south of Linwood Lake. Plot positioned to reflect apex cover of shrubs vs. Care lacustris sedge meadow.  Soils-- minerotrophic sedge peat.
Releve plot typical of open bog, being invaded by tamarack.  Bog apparently raised-well developed moat. Sphagnum cover continuous, many species. Fibric peat, saturated.
Fairly dry lowland cedar south of Middle Creek. Chippewa National Forest, Marcell district, compartment 120, stands 42 and 9. White Cedar Swamp.
Hummock and hollow microtopography with iron-stained water in hollows. 13 cedars of 8-24" DBH and 5 black ash of 3-7" DBH in releve plot. 24 acre stand just west of Rt 6, aged 112 years by USFS.
East of REleve 0492. Seems more acid with Sphagnum understory, fewer pools. Trees from 6-8" DBH. Aged 112 years. About 70 m. W of Co. 6.
Mixed conifer swamp northeast of Marcell, west of Johnson Lake. Lowland with fairly open canopy. 13 acre stand, aged 90 years old by USFS.

Mixed conifer stand east of Marcell, east of Carpic Lake.  Dense shrub layer of Alnus and Abies with much deadfall. Very thin canopy. Moat-like area at north end. 7 acre stand aged by USFS at 88 years.

Heterogeneous stand, typed cedar by USFS; variable canopy, some areas dominated by alder, ash and fir on sandy soil.  Lots of open area with aspen litter only about 50% ground cover. Aged 92 years by USFS.
Typed Cedar by USFS, but considerable aspen and fir. 11 acre stand aged 70 years by USFS.
Dry "upland" cedar, tall straight trees. Releve in area typed "tamarack", but actually more an open alder swamp.

Dry cedar type with tall straight boles, little potential habitat for special plants. Part of compartment is typed tamarack and is actually alder; part is typed cedar. Tall shrub layer missing. 15 acre stand, aged 90 years by USFS.

Typed by USFS as "Mixed Swamp Conifer", but dominated by cedar; a "cedar-feather moss" forest. Little green orchid well-distributed throughout; "100+" plants. Ground-layer hummock and hollow dominated by feather mosses. Cedar 2-16" DBH.

Heavily stocked with cedar 1.5 m tall, small diameter. Heavy stocking E3 mixed conifers. Releve has interrupted canopy with opening appropriate for Palemonium. East of clearcut on end of EW spit (esker?). Aged 54 years, USFS.
About 20 meters west of logging road and 100 meters south of clearcut. D2-3 layer present only where sheltered by dead trees.

Remnant white cedar with dry, highly disturbed understory. Total area of stand: 1 chain east to west by 5 chains north to south. Too much edge effect to be considered a community. On flat bench between hill and lake.
Cedar swamp grading uphill to upland cedar with Acer rubrum Tilia americana understory. Approximately 8 acre cedar on south side of Forest Road 2206.
Exact location in question. Stand structure and composition heterogeneous. Difficult to get representative sample. Northeast of young overgrown clearcut. Not sure if federal or state land.
White cedar swamp west of Rt 38, between 38 and south arm of North Star Lake.

Old-growth red pine forest; moderate fire in June 1988-all pines with fire-scorched bole base. Balsam understory killed. 1/2 to 1/4" to mineral soil. 80% needle cover. Southwest 1/2 of plot on steeper slope.

OldGrowth red pine forest; moderate fire in June 1988. All pine fire-scorched; lots of down balsam saps and small trees; ground cover is needles. Many rocks and boulders. Old growth data for this and adjacent plot.

Old-growth white cedar swamp( >140 years) domianted by Thuja with lesser amounts of Betula papyrifera and Fraxinus nigra.  Heavy logging in mid-1920's; succeeding to Black Ash Swamp. Releve at south end of swamp.

Nearly pure old-growth white cedar stand (>200 years) on 30-60 degree north to northeast-facing slope. Little understory. No human disturbance. Scattered large rocks. Releve located near upper edge of stand.

Bryophytes > 90. Lichens >5. Vascular plants >90. Water table 27cm below surface. Near crest of raised bog. Picea mariana stand >30 feet. Good growth-not excessive clumping. Moist, well-growing hummocks of Sphagnum.

Bryophytes >90. Lichens >5. Vascular plants >90. Black Spruce stand, crest of bog. Shaded with well-spaced spruce -single stem; little or no clumping. Near 2nd crest,just east of opening. Vigorous moist Sphagnum hummocks.

Bryophytes >15%. Lichens >10%. Vascular plants >90%. Water sample 311. East flank of bog. Sphagnum pools with high Sphagnum tussocks. Scattered dwarf Picea and Larix on hummocks. Scattered dead snags.
Open, midslope, firm tussocks, soft bottom, shallow pools, dead tree stump. (Species: 2 bryophytes, 0 lichens, >90 vascular plants).
Patterned fen. Vascular plants 80-90. Bryophytes >5 if any. Lichens 0. Water 5.
String.
Flark, west of raised bog; soft mud bottom with standing water; between strings with Larix.  Bryophytes <20%, lichens 0%, vascular plants 80%, water 20%.

Boreal rich sedge fen. South end water track. Flarks; ridges diffuse; not well-developed. Carex exilis and Scirpus cespitosus throughout. Bryophytes <15%, lichens <5%, some on bare tussock hummocks, vascular plants >90%, water <10%.
Boreal rich sedge fen. Near releve 196--Cladium clone. Firm; water table near surface. Substrate mostly dead Cladium shoots. Bryophytes <40-30%, lichens <5%, vascular plants 100%, water.
Boreal rich sedge fen. Flark in upslope portion of water tract; wet flarks; well-defined strings. Bryophytes <10%, lichens <5%, vascular plants 90%, water 10%.
Plot on crest of rise in area of dry-mesic prairie. In relatively diverse portion of site, weedy in swales. On sandy loam with gopher mounds, boulder.
Small 10-by-30m wet meadow opening rimmed by Betula glandulifera and Populus tremuloides. In area of extensive wet meadow. Old fence line, probably past grazed.
Plot on railroad or hwy right-of-way on east side of small ditch. Much small gravel at surface. Mesic and dry-mesic species. Disturbed but attractive, visible. In Strathcona.
Plot in small area of relatively dense Larix. Rough hummock-hollow topography, 0.3m relief, dry now in hollows, not spongy. Many tip-ups and large canopy gaps with tall Salix bebbiana.
Site typical of oak savanna on Plainfield sand soil. Elements=Talinum rugospermum, Tephrosia virginiana.

Soils shallow to moderately deep silty loam on dolomite that is bare in places. (Transcribed by D. Wovcha)
45 degree NW-facing slope within ravine.  Soils dark loam; possibly lightly grazed on slope; grazed on hill above. Sheet erosion has  made horizontal ripples in soil. (Transcribed by D. Wovcha).
Soils thin (<20 inch) sandy loam over sandstone bedrock. Site has long history of disturbance. Cover/abund codes not all reliable; transcribed by B.Delaney
Interbeach rich fen.  Peat > 3 feet deep.  pH=7.5
Dense jack pine on grayish sugar sand. DBH ranges from 8 to 17cm (3 to 7 inches).
Shrub/rich fen. Located downslope of tamarack forest fingers in large water track apparently spring-fed. pH=7.3 Transitional between boreal peatlands and prairie wetland.

Rich fen. Releve in western part of water track, drier with shrub cover, diffuse string pattern. Subject to periodic fires. Transitional between boreal and nonboreal peatland type. Surface dry, some small hummocks.
Stand along base of Lake Agassiz Beach Ridge. Typical staghorn cedar appearance. Sparse understory, much litter with patches of graminoids. Scattered hollows dry during drought year.
Releve located in open part of ribbed fen near outlet to East Branch of Warroad River. Releve #0687 is scrub fen of same area. pH = 6.6.
Releve located on shrub rib of shrub fen on downslope portion of peatland near outlet to East Branch of Warroad River. pH = 6.6
Located in wetland/peatland bordering Lake of the Woods. Moss collections given to J. Janssens for ID.
Open (rich) fen. Releve located on peatland surrounding Lake of the Woods. Water table at surface, buoyant spongy peat surface. Dense thatch on ground oriented ESE.
Rich shrub fen. Releve located on wetland/peatland on west shore of Lake of the Woods.
Releve in peatland bordering Lake of the Woods. Area patchy with varying dominant grasses and sedges. Water at surface. Much dead thatch litter.
Tamarack swamp. East side of Pine Creek Peatland adjacent to Minnesota Hill. Diverse vascular and bryophyte flora. Few cut stumps.
Mesic site on plateau above Roseau River in Hayes Lake State Park. Few cut stumps. Charred wood. Stand age is 63 years.
Jack pine (19-27cm) on sandy beach deposit on edge of Marvin Lake. Peatland complex. Dense stand with scattered openings. Few cut stumps. Loamy sand over sand with gravel lenses. Moss ID by JAJ.
Burned over black spruce bog (?), located between Sprague Creek and sedge fen water track. Black spruce (3-4cm) regenerating, on large Sphagnum hummocks. pH = 4.3 to 4.4.
Partially open jack pine stand on slight rise on Bemis Ridge Beach deposit. Sandy soil. Stand age 69 years.

Very dense canopy of white cedar (DBH = 28-32cm) on slight slope (>1 degree) at edge of mineral upland in Sprague Creek Peatland. Peat variable, .2-.7m over sand or silty clay. Nearly devoid of understory.
Partly open white cedar swamp downslope of Gun Club upland, Sprague Creek Peatland. More than 1 meter of peat. pH = 7.5.
Black spruce swamp with tamarack on east side of Sprague Creek water track. Peat more than 1 meter. pH = 6.2 to 6.3. Stand age is 70 years.
Sedge fen in large Sprague Creek Water Track dissected by ditches. pH = 6.9. Peat > 1 meter. Moss collections given to J. Janssens for ID.

Small jack pine(48cm DBH) stand on slight rise surrounded by wetland in Bemis Ridge Area. Many dead snags and downed trees. High water table. Soil: 0-4cm duff; 4-10cm white sand; >10cm red brown sand; hard pan at 50cm. Stand age is 70 years.
Calcareous seepage fen. Stand age is 108 years.

Black spruce (16-20cm DBH) stand in a rich cedar-spruce swamp at base of Bemis Ridge. Moss carpet flat with few very low hummocks. Almost no understory vegetation structure. Soil: peat 28cm over silt and sandy clay. Stand age is 102 years.
Sedge fen on east side of Palmville Peatland near Salix and Populus islands. Appears to be near eastern limit of transition subtype. pH = 7.2.
Small tamarack (20ft tall, 12-13cm DBH), very dense stand. This area drier, more compact peat than adjacent tamarack stands. Near Canadian border. pH = 6.4.
Narrow strip of black ash (17-27cm) along small stream cutting into Bemis Ridge. Patchy canopy, blowdowns; 65cm of peat over sand. Some disturbance, roads, cut stumps in area. Stand age is 98 years.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Floodplain at base of steep slope on Warroad River. Dense canopy but many large dead elm (55cm DBH). Very dry site, 30cm of silt over sand. Much bare ground; depauperate flora. Stand age 83 years.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Level bench above Roseau River. Fraxinus nigra and Fraxinus pennsylvanica 11-42cm DBH. Relatively dry site. Dense forb layer but not very diverse. Stand age 63 years.
Large, widely scattered red pine, 50cm DBH, in jack pine stand (23 to 27cm DBH) on Bemis Ridge. Red pine about 125 years old. Soil sandy with 5cm duff layer. Stand age is 69 years.

Very dense Picea mariana stand (20-43cm DBH). Much dead (naturally thinned) spruce and balsam fir. 5cm of organic layer over 5-40cm of loamy sand with gravel over sandy clay with gravel. Apparent upland with high water table. Stand age is 48 years.
Picea mariana (16-20 cm dbh), Populus tremuloides (28cm), and Abies balsamea (25 cm) on slight rise. Very old cut stumps (pine?) Soil is fine sand.
Very tall (14 m) and dense stand of black spruce, 15-25 cm dbh in Salol Peatland.
Burned black spruce bog, with Picea mariana regeneration. Few scattered taller tamarack (10 m). Very high hummocks of Sphagnum moss.
Releve in same area as releve #0725 but less dense Picea mariana (36-38 cm dbh) canopy and sphagnum-dominated ground cover.
Burned bog, formerly covered with black spruce.  Few remnants remain; Much black spruce regeneration occuring.
Picea mariana/ Thuja occidentalis stand in a rich cedar swamp at base of Bemis Ridge. pH=7.63, cond.= 171, Color= 0.208.
Site typical of openings in oak savanna on Plainfield sand. Several dead oaks on side of plot, possible due to oak wilt. Elements=] Lycaeides melissa samuelis, Tephrosia virginiana.
OLD-GROWTH WHITE CEDAR FOREST (>190 YRS). SITE WET-MESIC BUT MERGES INTO DRY-MESIC ON NW-FACING SLOPE.  NO CUT STUMPS.  PLOT CORNER 5 M FROM LAKE SHORE.  SUPERIOR NF COMP #70, STAND #15.

OLD-GROWTH WHITE CEDAR SWAMP.  NEARLY PURE CEDAR W/OCC. BL. SPRUCE AND BALSAM IN CANOPY.  SMALL DIAM TREES. CANOPY COVER 50%. FREQ HUMMOCKS, POOLS, & SM DIAM DOWN LOGS. NO CUT STUMPS. SUP NF CO243 ST1
OLD-GROWTH UPLAND WHITE CEDAR FOREST DOMINATED BY LARGE DBH THUJA (MN DBH=40.8 CM) W/LESSER AMOUNTS OF WHITE BIRCH.  NO CUT STUMPS.
Relatively good condition oak savanna adjacent to gravel pit, east of Strathcona. Prairie interspersion with native grasses (almost all Stipa and big bluestem); lower species richness in herbs.
Open "fen" area near black spruce swamp at Lake Lucille.

Aspen stand north of Roosevelt. Mostly Populus tremuloides, some huge. Significant ash understory. Some blowdowns but walking not difficult. Eastern character to stand species list. 10% blowdowns in plot, most in 1 pile. Soil: sandy loam over fine sand or silty sand.
Black spruce (11-16cm DBH)/cedar (11-12cm DBH) swamp along Canadian Border. Swamp forest dissected by seepage tracks. Numerous connected pools filled with submerged herbs and mosses. pH=7.2.
Sparse stagnant tamarack and black spruce in large water track east of Hwy 310 in Sprague Creek Peatland. Water track probably impacted by ditches. pH=6.5.
Sparse stagnant spruce and tamarack area upstream of spring fen channels at Sprague Creek Peatland SNA. pH=7.5.
Representative of open tamarack (16-22cm DBH) with scattered black spruce (24cm DBH) in Sprague Creek Fen Area. Incipient water tracks in area. Peat > 1m. pH=7.2 Great Gray Owl nest nearby.
Fairly open tamarack swamp near transition with black spruce; on west site of Pine Creek Water Track. Peat > 1m; pH=7.1.

Superior national forest. Extensive area of old growth northern hardwood; yellow birch and pine removed. Site converted from mixed stand to primarily maple. Average maple DBH is 30cm; scattered old growth maple in 50cm DBH range. Ground cover: herbaceous: 35%, deadfall: 25%, litter: 40%.

Superior national forest. Old growth northern hardwoods on south/southeast-facing slope. Stand located inside loop of recreation hiking trail. Ground layer: herbaceous-34%, deadfall-10%, litter-55%. One 54cm DBH Picea glauca cored at 125 years old.

Old-growth northern hardwoods on south/southeast-facing slope. Stand located inside loop of recreation hiking trail. Approximately 40 acres. Ground layer percentages: woody-15%, deadfall-5%, herbaceous-5%, litter-75%.
Releve on upper slope; prairie becomes steeper (50%) below.  Heavy growth of Physocarpos and Rhus glabra throughout. Less than 1% rock outcrop in releve.
Overgrown woodland; larger trees with fire scars on upslope side. Canopy trees moderately open-grown. Probably grazed in past (old fence top of slope). Silt loam. Frequent small dead oaks.
Remnant old-growth stand. Abundant yellow birch snags. Regeneration dominated by sugar maple. Adjacent woods have been selectively logged. Ground layer: herbaceous-50%  deadfall-35%, litter-15%.

Old growth northern hardwoods, parts of area undisturbed, other areas have been selectively cut for conifers. Continuous sugar maple canopy with some paper birch and white spruce. Ground cover: herbaceous-25%, dead-10%, litter-5% woody-75%.

Small open water pools common; water 10-20cm deep, soupy muck to 75 +cm. Many E1-2 Abies balsamea dead. No cut stumps observed. Canopy Fraxinus nigra often with 25-50(+)% moss covering lower half of tree. Coarse woody debris common in all sizes and decay stages. 
Tree DBH (cm):
Fraxinus nigra: 27-40(45), 15-22, <50
Thuja occidentalis: 15-20cm

Tip-ups common. Canopy Larix widely scattered through out community. Community is rather small, surrounded by Alder swamp and connected to other small to medium sized peatlands in an otherwise upland landscape. Peat may not be much deeper than 60cm because it took six probes in different locations to get the probe to sink 60cm, otherwise it hit something hard at ~40cm which felt like a rich or hard soil. Soil: moss/mucky peat > 60cm
Picea mariana DBH: 10-14cm

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks:
Small scattered pools with ~3cm of standing water, otherwise no standing water in community. Coarse woody debris scattered common. Scattered 70%+ decayed stumps throughout community. Community within a larger upland landscape in mesic hardwood forests. Rocky soils. Soil: pebbly sand and rock with gravel. A horizon <8cm. 
Tree DBH (cm):
Betula alleghaniensis: 49
Fraxinus nigra: 18-28, 35-40
Picea glauca: 36
Populus balsimifera: 20-26

Community occupies a long narrow terrace between mesic/wet-mesic hardwood-conifer forest and the wet meadow fringe of Sullivan Creek. 2-3 cm standing water in low spots, but most of community without standing water can get quite dry on the surface. Soil: Rocky sand and gravel, saturated to >60cm. A horizon < 7cm. Litter of needles, twigs, very little deciduous leaves.

Many large rocks and boulders at surface and below. No standing water in community but likely holds water in the spring. Coarse woody debris, slender-medium in all decay stages, common. Scattered 75%+ decayed Pinus stumps scattered throughout community. Soils: Coarse sand with rocks. A horizon depth: 16cm (worms). Soil: coarse sand with rocks.

Worms make distinguishing between humus and A horizon difficult. Combine the two reach ~10cm before pure mineral soil begins. Charcoal common in the A/humus layer. Recent blowdown scattered common throughout community. Community occupying a +/- esker along Sullivan creek. Soil: sand with pebbles. Litter of needles and leaves.
Tree DBH (cm):
Betula papyrifera: 15-26cm
Abies balsimifera: 10-18cm

Mature mixed-age forest with good structural diversity. No worms observed. Thick, spongy duff. Coarse woody debris of all decay stages scattered throughout. Old cf. Pinus stumps 75% decayed scattered. Community marked for logging. Microtopography undisturbed with bowls and mounds. Topographic context: crest/flat. Stand probably >100 years old. Litter of leaves and twigs. A horizon <25cm. Soil: silty loam with fine sand.

Thick floating mat on the edge of Stroud Lake. Native plant community of releve ~20m wide surrounded by conifer swamp. This releve captures an area that is more floristicly rich than much of the floating mat community, other areas predominatley Carex lasiocarpa, Sphagnum and Thelypterus palustris.
No standing water. Community occupies an isolated basin. Larix widely scattered, nearly absent, within community. Coarse woody debris common, all decay stages.

Mixed hardwood-conifer swamp within a wetland basin affected by beaver dams and +/- connected to Twin Lakes. Community in good condition with no cut stumps, new or old, observed. Note Botrychium simplex found on a high point of the microtopography. 
Tree DBH (cm):
Fraxinus nigra: 20-35
Betula allegheniensis: 42
Thuja occidentalis: 20-30
Abies balsimea: 33

Plot on a level terrace upslope from the Moosehorn River. Exposed bedrock common in this vicinity. Low spots between bedrock with 5-15cm of humus, otherwise no mineral soil found with soil probe, bedrock and/or large rocks encountered at 5-15cm below surface repeatedly. Species +/- hydophydic restricted to low swales. Malaxis uniflora growing out of moss covered bedrock. Possible history of logging/grazing. 
Tree DBH (cm):
Populus tremuloides: 20-30cm
Acer rubrum: 10-20cm

Worm castings observed, only one year's worth of litter. Most Acer rubrum multi-stemmed. Coarse woody debris widely scattered and mostly <10% decayed. Exposed boulders common throughout vicinity. Old cf. hardwood? stumps (75% decayed) scattered. Overall a rather open community. No recent cut stumps observed. A horizon: 5cm. Soil: sandy loam or loamy sand.

No standing water in low spots on this date. Repeated soil probes hit rocks at 10-40cm below the surface. Exposed and moss/vegetation covered boulders common throughout community. Large old conifer stumps (>75% decayed) scattered. Coarse woody debris mostly <25% decayed, scattered common. Soil: sandy loam or loamy sand. 
Tree DBH (cm) range:
Fraxinus nigra: 20-30cm
Acer rubra: 20-30cm

Plot captures the predominate native plant community within a 3-5 acre contained basin. Compare to releve 3031. The outside plot (OP) species within the releve include species < 2m away from plot edge. Smaller areas within basin with continuous patches of Scheuchzerir, Carex limosa or Carex chordorrhiza. Sparse litter of graminoids and leaves.

Compare to DNR Releve 3030, this native plant community on ~10m border around most of the same basin. On opposite side of basin within an area dominated by Carex limosa and Carex chordirhiza there is a ~70 square meter patch that is matted down by numerous cf. deer. Soil: Sedge peat with muck. Sparse litter of graminoids and leaves.

Rocks, roots and hard soil prevented soil probe >30 cm deep. Charcoal in the Ah horizon, no burn scars on standing trees. Stumps 70% + decayed scattered throughout. Native plant community matches Marschner's interpretation and is likely a good example of pre-settlement vegetation with history of logging. Rolling topography. Plot with 2 small knoles and a trough below, all similar flora. Litter is 80% needles and 20% leaves. A horizon depth: <7cm. 
Tree DBH (cm):
Pinus strobus: 33-48
Betula papyrifera: 18-28
Pinus resinosa: 30-40

No standing water in community. Native plant community within a larger wetland complex dominated by black ash swamp. This wetland complex contains a small flowage that joins Boulder Creek to the southwest. Scattered areas with cut stumps ~50% decayed coarse woody debris common in all sizes and decay stages. Average peat depth ~20cm. Soil: Mucky peat over sandy silt with possible gray clay content.

Low spots with 0-2cm of standing water. Soils saturated. Native plant community dominates large wetland basin which also contains northern white cedar swamp. See DNR Releve 3033. Scattered areas with cut stumps 25-50% decayed. Coarse woody debris mostly smaller. Small stream flow out of native plant community to Boulder Creek to the southwest. Soil: mucky beat of sandy silt with possible clay content and rocks and pebbles. 
Modal Fraxinus nigra DBH: 18-30cm.

Shallow organic soils +/- covering boulders. Unable to get soil probe any deeper than 10cm without hitting rock. Plot <100m from the St. Louis River and <5m above. Intermittent stream through plot with bouldery bed. St. Louis river hereabouts very bouldery. Slender open forest community. Could not get soil probe past 10cm. Sparse litter of graminoids and leaves.
Fraxinus nigra DBH: 20-30cm (35).

Long narrow zone between Alnus incana-lined upland border and poor fen scrub tamarack. Community may be ecotonal but it is a distinct vegetation pattern than either native plant community adjacent to it. Sphagnum covers hummocks with mucky hollows in between mostly graminoid and Typha dominated. Typha throughout in patches and scattered individuals. Soil: Sedge, Moss, Mucky peat.

Predominate native plant community in a ~4 acre basin connected by narrow channels to acid peatlands to the south. Compare to DNR Releve 3036, this plot ~20 Typha presence suggests water level fluctuations. Drivable trail and likely beaver activity ~half mile south southwest. Community on a thick bouncy mat (is it a mat or a thick layer of Chamaedaphne roots?) Deer trail dissecting plot account for the species more typical of a richer or wetter community. Good four toed salamander habitat along the South upland border of community - Alnus with sphagnum covered hummocks and leaf covered much in between. Soil: mossy, mucky peat.

Compare with Releve 3036 and 3037, this the best quality. No beaver impacts or Typha angustifolia in this basin. Native plant community with variations between this releve and patches dominated by Carex rostrata with no pitcher plants. Adjacent to an esker-like ridge.

Plot borders Mouse Lake. This native plant community occupies a 5-20m band around 90% of the lake, the rest with black spruce swamp to water's edge. Outside plot species all at waters edge. Larix widely scattered within community. Deer trail through plot.

Many E6-6 Picea mariana with witches broom widely scattered DD in vicinity of plot. No cut stumps observed. Community surrounds most of Mouse Lake. Compare with DNR Releve 3039. Coarse woody debris common in all decay stages. Picea marina DBH (cm): 13-16, max 19.

CSA age = 100+ years. Tree distribution appears natural. Coarse woody debris scattered common with recent blowdowns. Scattered <1 acre canopy openings and with similar forb and graminoid vegetation as plot areas with lots of deer browse. Most Pinus strobus <1m appears browsed. Lots of deer trails. Saw a doe and buck on the forest road just North of here. Slope position: crest/upper/ulat (rolling). A horizon depth: <11cm. Soil: silty sand over sand with small pebbles and gravel. 
Tree DBH (cm):
Pinus resinosa: (38) 40-45 (49)
Pinus strobus: (35) 40-48 (52)

Native plant community on a broad ~ flat terrace in the Nemadji River basin. Small open patches scattered common throughout with open Fraxinus nigra canopy and graminoids dominated below. Slight rises in topography up a more mesic flora. Scattered E7-7 Pinus strobus in vicinity. No signs of fire. Coarse woody debris of all sized and decay stages scattered common. Many Fraxinus nigra DY and DD scattered throughout, often in patches. Litter of graminoids and leaves. Soil: red clay. A horizon depth: <7cm.

Soils thin organic and alluvial over/between boulders. Native plant community north of the St. Louis River between black ash swamp and fire dependent forest. Scattered coarse woody debris of all sizes and decay stages common-some recent blowdowns. Fire scars in adjacent uplands. Native plant community is done dry on this date. Topograohic context: middle/lower. Scattered stumps >75% decays with fire scars. Ecotonal? 
Tree DBH (cm):
Populus tremuloides: 30-32cm / 20-25cm
Abies balsimea: 10-15cm

Native plant community between Wolf Lake and an upland island surrounded by mostly acid wet-lands. Blowdown and coarse woody debris common. Patches of heavy deer browse throughout. Adjacent upland island with a lot of blowdown. Sphagnum mostly dry on this date. Scattered exposed boulders in this native plant community. Litter some sparse needles and ericaceous leaves. Interesting soil profile with sand layered with peat over peat to 60cm+. 
Tree DBH (cm):
Picea mariana: 15-22
Larix laricina: 20-22

Stand adjacent to the west side of Wolf Lake. Worms! Patches of blowdowns scattered in vicinity throughout the stand. Snags throughout the community. Coarse woody debris of all sizes and decay stages common. No signs of fire. Widely scattered 70%+ decayed stumps. Soil: silty sand. A horizon: <11cm.
From airphotos, this may have been hayed in past. Plot boundary estimated, not measured. Species composition suggests transition between wet-mesic and wet.

Yellowbirch old - some hollow/conke. No obvious fire scars. Occasional white pine - large. Cut to north - quite a bit of this type appears to be cut in Isabella area, very little to no surface boulders. Early season, may have missed later emerging species. Litter of leaves and twigs.

Percent canopy varies in > area. Ass. dead and down. No Thuja. Suspect Betula papyrifera and Betula cord in community. No obvious stumps. No obvious worms or fire scars. Yellow birch large, in > area. Very fine texture soil (not gritty) mixture with rock. Litter of leaves and twigs.

Old yellow birch mix; adjacent areas have more open canopy and a higher percent brush. No obvious human disturbance in plot but past cutting likely in some adjacent areas. Uncertain what all happened in this > area. Community type seemingly threatened in this general area due to heavy cutting. Litter of leafs and twigs. Several surface boulders. Soil: smooth very fine dark with few worms.

Assorted dead and down and snags of ass. conifer. Few, scattered old charred snags. No stumps - portions of adjacent forest/stands are cut. Area of rolling topography on flat/crest. Litter of needles/bark/twigs/cones.

Jack pine is falling out; numerous snag/dead and down - fir appearing to become more dominant. No obvious stump or fire scars. White pine scattered. Yellow gold mychorrhiza in fine duff. Jack pine is falling out of stand. Numerous snag/dead and down - fir likely becoming more dominate.  Litter of needles, twigs, and bark.

Exposed moss/lichen dominated bedrock outcrop with pockets of shallow soil above cliff/talus. > area more treed with mixed woodland. Charcoal. Good view. A horizon >7cm. Average depth to bedrock 0-14+ inches.
White pine in shallow soil at uppermost elevation of feature. No exposed bedrock. Charred wood. No stumps. Worms present. A horizon depth: 1cm. Litter of needles, twigs, and bark.

Jack pine on rocky-cobbly sandy loam. Assorted dead and down, standing dead (jack pine, black spruce, balsam fir). Some trees uprooted-some snagged. No obvious fire scar. Abundant yellow-gold mychorrhiza. Homestead Lake down slope to north. Jack pine follows ridge to south west to south east with Betula papyrifera/Populus tremuloids/Abies. Litter of needles, twigs, leaves, and bark.

Plot chosen to represent northern example of native plant community. No evidence of anthropogenic disturbance. Late sample date for some spring ephemerals. Wet-mesic swales with Fraxinus nigra. Picea abd Thuja also present in native plant community. Black throated blue warbler heard. Soil: rocky loam.

Plot selected to reflect typical natural fire origin native plant community on deep, rocky till. No anthropogenic disturbance. Scattered burned snags still standing. Approximate age 95 years. Burned snags from native plant community origin fire still scattered through.

Plot chosen to represent natural origin native plant community. No anthropogenic disturbance. Near '99 blowdown patches. Bud worm mortality in understory Abies. Soil: Rocky loam. Litter of needle/leaf.

Plot selected to represent native plant community on floating and stranded mat margin of small lake. Plot spans water's edge to forest edge. Evidence of past beaver occupation of lake. No anthropogenic disturbance of native plant community or surrounding forest.

DNR old growth. Plot selected to represent native plant community of natural origin common on uplands in the land type association. Abundant coarse woody debris. Some damage and mortality from blister rust. (FDn43a). Soil: Rocky sandy loam.

Plot representative of conditions in common senescing fire-dependent native plant community. Standing dead and down Pinus banksiana and Pinus mariana. Also budworm killed Abies. Plot chosen to represent high quality, natural origin native plant community, undisturbed since fire of origin. No cut stumps. No worms. Charred snags, cat faces on supercanopy. Litter of needle and some leaves.

Small depressional wetland surrounded by rolling pasture. Wetland rece ives runoff from adjacent cattle farm. The wetland has a diverse emerg ent community.
Small depressional wetland surrounded by abandoned pasture. Wetland ha s an emergent edge. Center of  wetland is open water, with abundant su bmersed aquatics.
Small depressional wetland surrounded by forest. Wetland is deep and s teep-sided with a narrow emergent fringe of Phalaris arundinacea & Sag ittaria rigida.
Small depressional wetland surrounded by industrial/office development & urban parkland. Site receives increased stormwater runoff from adja cent impervious surfaces.
Small depressional wetland mostly surrounded by forest, except on N. e dge (agric. land). Farm road runs through wetland. Wetland has dense T ypha angustifolia perimeter.
Small depressional wetland surrounded by successional grasslands & for est along S. edge. Well developed sedge mat broken along edge, from pa st domestic grazing.
Small depressional wetland surrounded by steep, successional grassland s. Dense sedge tussocks form edge of wetland, grading to emergent stan ds of Typha latifolia & Sagi. Lati., & open water.
Small depressional wetland surrounded by a recent residential developm ent. Site receives stormwater runoff from adjacent impervious surfaces . Annuals predominate vegetation.
Small depressional wetland with significant urban stormwater input. Su rrounded by roads, lawn, & parking lots. Fringe of emergent veg. with sparse woody patches surrounds open water.
Very wide portion of floodplain of Minn. River with many stagnant pool s in oxbow channels. Abandoned agri. fields are present within the flo odplain & area dom. by willow shrubs.
Very wide portion of floodplain of Minn. River with many stagnant pool s in oxbow channels. Abandoned agri. fields are present within the flo odplain & area dom. by willow shrubs.
Floodplain site along the Vermillion River with steep banks (~5m high) at river's edge. Some silver maple dead.
Small (3 ac.) basin. Buoyant mat, peat >30 cm. Water ~ 10cm deep. Sphagnum starting to form in middle of basin. Outer edge more species poor, but has more Lemna.
~400 m2 patch between cattail bordered lake and Carex lasiocarpa dominated interior. Bouncy mats of highly decomposed peat. Located just north of boardwalk. Odd inclusion dominated by Sparganium.
Loose patchy mat in center of small wetland basin surrounded by open water. Water ~75cm deep, mucky bottom. Mat can support very little weight. Wetland dissected by road.

npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: Small island with fluted topography. Terrace above most flooding. Alluvial variable - sandy to silty. Moderate downed woody debris.
Small opening in cattail dominated wetland. Peat is springy. Heavy thatch. Water just below surface.
Large cattail dominated wetland with openings. Open water in spots, generally <15 cm deep.
Large uniform cattail dominated wetland. Typha thick and tall. Water 20-25 cm deep.
Small shallow depression in wet prairie. Interbeach wetland. Dense cover. Adjacent to small Typha-marsh. Water 10-15cm deep. Mucky peat 75cm with shells over silty clay.
Mosaic in wet prairie. Water table at surface. Saline subtype. Clayey silt over clay. Soil wet to surface.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Patchy canopy, variable; between levee & first terrace along Buffalo River. Large dead elms in area. Basswood variable up to 55cm; multiple stems. 3m above & 15m from river. No agricultural siltation. Deer browsed. Sandy loam over fine sand. Surface slightly undulating.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Undulating terrace >50m from river; low channel to rear. Large dead elms (~1m DBH). Trees leaning, sending new tops. Matteucia patch. Much deer browsing/trampling in area. Dark clayey silt (60cm) over sand.

Variable shallow basin wetland in prairie; adjacent to marsh with patches of open water. Muskrat activity-cause invasion of Phalaris? Dead Salix and snages indicate recent rise in water table. Water depth 10-15cm. 10cm muck over sand.

Behind beach ridge that impedes surface flow. Water near surface. 5-10 cm of muck over thin layer of clayey sand over very coarse sand. Much thatch. Soil: 5-10cm much over mineral over clayey sand over coarse (calcareous?) sand. Average peat depth: 5cm.

Small bulrush stand off point of 28 acre pond between open water and cattails. Water dark brown; 20-40cm deep. Stand monotypic but more diverse in shallow water. Gray clay mostly firm bottom but soft in places. Depth of standing water: 40cm.
Small (<1 acre) basin surrounded by prairie. Releve represents Typha dominated center of basin. Adjacent to releve 8286. Gap in canopy with water to depth of .5m. Organic mucky bottom.
Small (<1 acre) basin surrounded by prairie. Releve represents outer ring of bulrush/cattail surrounding Typha center (Releve 3285). Mucky bottom under 40cm of water.
Small (~1 acre) basin surrounded by prairie. Water depth 30-40cm. Approximately 10 cm of muck over gray clay. Releve represents interior; adjacent to releve 3288.
Small (~1 acre) basin surrounded by prairie. Water depth ~30 cm. Mucky over gray clay. Releve represents mixed cattail bulrush area surrounding interior (releve 3287).
Opening in shrubby zone (Salix discolor and gracilis). Seepage water from beach ridges drains through area. Hollows with 3-4 cm of water; some hummocks above water. Soil: gray fine sandy clay.

On saturated hummocky peat between the cannon river and bluffs, down-slope from calcareous fen, on east side river. Well-developed hummocks Within ~50 acre wet meadow-calcareous fen shrub swamp complex.

Marsh ~3-4 acres. Pothole surrounded by mesic prairie and some cropland on hills ~20 ft high. In lowest part of basin. No open water. Moist silt loam; some silt apparently eroded in from croplands. Iowa Nature Preserve.

Toe of slope, grading to bulrush marsh below and mesic prairie above. Wet prairie occupies about 1 acre. On moist deep loam, on edge of pot-hole. Iowa State Nature Preserve. NPC code added by Dustin Graham.
Sedge meadow forms ~20 M zone around pothole (pond). Grades to narrow zone emergent marsh next to pond, and to wet prairie and then dry prairie upslope. Iowa State Nature Preserve (36 acres).

South side of Hall's Lake. 2-3 acre area surrounded by narrow-leaf cattail-dominated marsh, areas of Carex lacustris and other areas of Phalaris. 30m from mature oak forest. One of largest Sparganium areas seen.

npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: Straight River floodplain, on east side. Frequent oxbows, channels and ponds. Piles of woody flood debris common. Much bare soil. High water year ( flooded in June). Worm castings abundant. Deep silt.
Releve in one of few areas free of reed canary.
Substrate black, very well-decomposed peat, saturated to surface, >1m deep. Not quaking. Plot markers left, plot rechecked 4 July 04, 22 Aug 04. Typical of less shrubby parts of wetland.

Distinctive long, narrow zone dominated by Carex lacustris, sparse shrubs. Very wet (some surface water in hollows); quaking. Substrate very well decomposed peat, black, >1m deep. Revisited 04 Jul, 22 Aug 4.
Black, very well-decomposed peat, >1m deep. Saturated to surface, but no standing water. Revisited 22 Aug 04.

Water up to 15cm in parts; moss hummocks above water. Substrate black silty clay loam to 1m (length of probe). Southwest corner of plot at margin where changes from marsh to meadow, Scolochloa > Typha.

Soil dark silty clay loam becoming slightly grayer with depth. At approximately 75cm A layer pale gray coarse sand full of water. Dark gray clay loam below. Free water at approximately 50cm. Narrow zone between marsh, wet prairie.

Soil: 15-20cm black silty clay loam, some fine sand. Becoming medium dark brownish-gray, same texture. At approximately 50cm dense, heavy clay, drier than above. Similar deeper depression with >Lysmachia Hybrid, Polygonum amphibium.

Narrow transition zone between wet prairie and large Typha angustifolia marsh in channel of early outlet of Glacial Lake Agassiz. Appears regularly mowed and depauperate. Do not use for classification.
Trans zone between wet prairie and large marsh in old channel of early outlet of Glacial Lake Agassiz. Not burned or mowed. Soil black silty clay loam, becoming dark gray. To depth of probe (ca. 1m).
Soil; deep black, fine-textured loam, moist, not wet, as deep as probe (ca 1m). Typha denser in some other parts of slough; many dead stems from previous year in plot area.
In narrow transition zone between prairie and drawdown. Soil black sticky loam wet. Some gravel, then grayer colored at ca. 50cm. Round, well-defined pothole in disintegration moraine.
Marginal zone of small depression in distintegration moraine, trans between prairie and marshy meadow.
Marshy meadow towards central part of small closed depression in disintegration moraine. Surrounded by shallow meadow ring, then upland prairie. Water ca. 40cm deep.
Shallow meadow in small closed depression in disintegration moraine, surrounded by mesic prairie. No marshy center.

Surrounding upland dry to mesic prairie. Had been grazed earlier in season, but no sign of grazing disturbance in plot. Scattered Typha cf. angustifolia, both Scirpus acutus and validus in wetland. Water ca 45 cm deep.
Representative of small inclusions in Scolochloa meadow, in shallow depression in hummocky moraine. Surrounded by upland prairie, road crosses one end. No standing water when data collected.

Plot representative of vegetation dominating depression; occasional small patches within sparser cover of Carex atherodes, more species-rich. In hummocky moraine. Upland around is native prairie. No water on surface.
Soil very sticky silty clay, some whitish mineral material in top few cm. At ca 0.5 m. Becomes yellowish-brown, same texture. Borders slough dominated by Typha cf. angustifolia, Eleocharis palustris.

Small area amidst more diverse, forby meadow. Most forbs here towards margin. This area barely large enough to contain the plot. Substrate saturated well-decomposed peat, springy, free water in hollows.

Typical of 50 acres in rolling sandy moraine at headwaters of Straight River. Plot edge is 20m from upland margin. Trees 15-30cm DBH. Typical peat hummock and pool substrate. Upland is sandy. No stumps, few snags, little coarse woody debris. South of Mallord Lake. Topographic context: depression/flat.

Typical of 20-acre stand in large wetland complex in rolling sandy terrain along the headwaters of the Straight River. Substrate with very low hummocks and thick root mat; wet peat >30cm deep. Stand appears rather even-aged. No stumps. Few snags.

Open zone of broad wetland on northeast side of Little Flat Lake. Plot 1/8 mile from lake. Quaky sedge peat >50cm deep, no coarse woody debris. No Sphagnum. Grades inland to Betula gland; to Phragmites toward lake. Depth of standing water <1cm. Topographic context depression/flat.

Typical of 5-acre basin in rolling forested moraine. No moat. Substrate is quaky peat >30cm deep. Sphagnum nearly continuous but not forming hummocks in most places. East side of Co Rd 135 NE of Duck Lake.

1-2 acre basin in rolling mesic hardwood terrain on West side of Tamarack Lake. Very quaky mat not strong enough to support my weight. Center of basin mat 2 feet above muck bottom. Plot is centrally located in Basin. Basin zoned, heterogenous.

place_name: Pickerel L Ponds WMA- Irish L
remarks: Center of heterogenous 4-acre basin in strongly-rolling forested terrain on north side of Irish Lake. Moderately quaky saturated peat >40cm. Polytrichum hummocks 60cm high. No old stumps or coarse woody debris. Beaver moat on margin.
