Water depth in plot approximately 0.5m. Plot ca 15m east of edge of open water center of slough. Emergent diversity increases towards slough margin to west. Do not use for classification.
In part of slough not taken over by Typha angustifolia. Phragmites is native North American strain. Slough surrounded by native prairie.
No free water on surface; soil moist to wet but not saturated at surface. Narrow margin of Spartina, Calamagrostis canadensis, Apocynum sibiricum. Wet-mesic prairie surrounds. No moss.
Water up to 5+ cm deep, but many low hummocks above water. Narrow, shallow part of slough in native prairie.
Level area at foot of very gentle slope. Seepage influence evident on slope. Substrate in plot firm, a few cm water. Invaded by typha angustifolia.

In shallow slough that deepens to east, joins stream channel. Very small channel runs through just east of plot. Substrate in plot saturated at surface, few cm water in low spots surrounded by wet prairie.
In broad, level bottom of glacial meltwater gorge. Substrate slightly springy, organic muck, unknown depth. Saturated to surface, but no free water. Plot in area not dominated by Typha angustifolia.

In broad, level bottom of glacial meltwater gorge. Substrate slightly springy organic muck. Unknown depth, top few cm orangish-brown. Saturated but no free water on surface. Typha angustifolia dominated surrounding area.

Groundwater seep/flow zone, marly pools with Chara. Flanked by zone of taller vegetation, no pools: Muhlenbergia glomerata, Scirpus pungens, Rhynchospora capillacea, Viola nephrophylla, Parnassia glauca, moss. Only slightly springy.
Small, nearly level area in bottom of incised creek valley. Springy seep zones dominated by Carex aquatilis present. Plot in firm area, water trickling through. Upland native prairie.

Wet meadow border of emergent marsh (releve 3421) basin. Saturated peat muck >1 meter. Basin surrounded by old field. Water level at surface here, whereas standing water depth in adjacent marsh is ~6-8 is above mucky surface of marsh.

Very shallow basin surrounded by maple/basswood forest close to edge of lake, but separated by narrow upland. Upland area is only a few feet higher than wetland. No floating mat, water is below ground level. Scattered Fraxinus nigra around the edge of the basin. Some cat tails invading from the north.

Straight trunked trees, mostly single stemmed (some of the Tilia have multiple trunks). Trees are mostly medium to large (30-40cm DBH). Tip-up mounds common. No sign of recent grazing or logging. MHc26 or 37?

Large narrow old outwash channel, about 1/4-1/2 miles wide and about 2 mile long. North 1/2 cattail marsh, then halfway down there is a man made dam and wetland changes to wet meadow, shrub swamp. Floating mat, sinks to knee depth. Open pools here and there. Scattered tamarack further down.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Fraxinus-Acer forest on banks of Two Rivers in Lake Bronson State Park. Sand deposits. 25% bare ground. Some vegetation deposited in rows and small clams shells in area . Old oxbows within and just outside releve.

Probably old oxbow. Vegetation matted from water earlier in season. Moderate moss covered coarse woody debris - branches and 15-25cm DBH logs. Cornus, Vitis, and Clematis on river bank.  Bur oak dominated forest upland with Pteridium aquilinum, Corylus americana, Smilacina stellata, and Toxicodendron radicans.

Large Typha marsh just northwest of Thief Lake, east of County highway 49. Occasional small patches of Phragmites especially along ditch and adjacent to distant small islands of Salix/Populus. Scattered standing water within tracks. Moderate moss covered surface.

Marsh just south of Nereson Wildlife Management Area. Water >2 feet deep. Open water ~25%, and occasional patches of Typha latifolia, Typha angustifolia, and Scirpus acutis. Matrix of Carex lasiocarpa and Equisetum fluviatile.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: No cut stumps; occasional beaver chew of ash; ~1% standing water in plot in wet depression/drains. Diverse vegetation. Trees appear healthy. Site likely gets flushed when Stony River runs high. Litter of leaves and twigs. Soil horizons: A, AB, Bg1, Bg2, 2Cg (GRV LCOS). Glaciofluvial over outwash parent material. Excavation beyond 60 cm in 2Cg impeded by rocks and saturated sloughing. Iron depletions and concentrations begin at 25 cm and saturated soil begins at 51 cm below surface when sampled on 5/19/2021. Places this at boundary between SPD and PD drainage.

No stump, surface cobble moss covered. > area variable in species. Percent canopy cover - Picea maria 100%. Dead and down-moderate mostly jack pine, percent aspen/paper birch also variable. Local areas more surface cobble. No fire scars. Adjacent area toward stream has more open undersotry and forb layer - more near surface rock and higher percent Pleurozium. Litter of leaves, twigs, and sticks.
Dead and down; tip-ups; no obvious stump; canopy gaps. Occasional moss covered surface boulder. Duff and mychorrhiza. Litter of needles, cones, twigs and leaves.

Open wetland approximately 3dh from open water. Much of > area with higher percent stunted black spruce (all <25% canopy) and higher percent Betula pumila and Alder - likely periodically beaver flooded. Releve represents most wet and less woody portion of wetland. Litter of sparse Carex leaves.

Open peatland with scatter stunted tamarack and black spruce. Portions of surrounding areas more wet/dry puddled with higher plant diversity. Areas (local) of peat quite floating. Edges of open peatland with increasing percent black spurce and Chamaedaphne calyculata.
Shore fen of small bog pond. Area selected avoided adjacent hummock inclusions of higher percent ericads - Picea maria etc. Plot size: 12 x 8.3 = 99.6.
Releve focused on non hummock-flats of area. Abundance on fen species. Much dryer than last year. Wetter areas without sphagnum. Weak flarks but many peat bottom pools! Mixed fen!
Southwest of Great Gray Island - Open Trichophorum fen. Hummocky with Trichophorum; scattered Sphagnum/Picea glaua /Chamadaphne calyculata hummocks. Mixed fen!

Wet fen. West northwest of Great Gray Island. No obvious pattern but wet pools, pattern more distinct on photo. Occasional sphagnum/stunted black spruce/Chamdaphne calyculata hummocks <5%. Association TES.

Subtle depressional areas in more open wetland/peatland, >30% Carex dominated all sterile. Ericads primarily on hummocks and not part of releve. Hummock-dense Chamadaphne calyculata, Sphagnum/dicranum; wetter - more central areas versus edge zone. Litter of carex and forb leaves.

Releve captures the dryer - ericaceous dominated zone of peatland. Peatland by FD - mixed pine/aspen/paper birch forest. Some areas to the south ericaceous/sphagnum with <5% Carex and forb mix of Carex lasiocarpa and Carex olig. - Carex lasiocarpa established to be dominant (much sterile material). Litter of Carex and Chamadaphne leaves.

Sedge meadow. Some portions with little or no Carex lasiocarpa and higher percent Carex utriculata/vesicaria.  wetter to south with Typha patch and higher percent Equisetum (~8"+ deep). Succeeding to fen.

Patchy raised center of peatland between County Road three and gravel road. Cut-over for fence posts. Floating mat in center not sampled. Reticulate with deep, mucky trails. Road impeded drainage, getting richer. Soil: Fibric peat.
Grazed natural stand of red pine 60 years. About 30" medium sand over double silty clay bands perching water with bright mottles over very coarse sand. Well-drained.
Releve to characterize aspen inclusion in NE corner of stand #2. High water table, thistledew series. Keys to FDn45 but atypical soils.
Releve to describe Jack Pine type. Stand mostly FDn12, but areas with 2 silty bands key to FDn33. With Tim Russ and Dan Hanson.
Releve typical of dry-mesic pine forest on gravelly stagnation moraine. Soils are stony, loamy sand till.
Releve demonstration in St. Louis County. Dry-mesic pine. Releve on biophysical plot 678, point 1.
Demonstration releve in St. Louis County. Typical MHn44 on edge of Glacial Lake Agassiz.
Beautiful hardwood stand. With Jason Johnson Training site for Hill City. No worms and very thick duff. Topographic context: upper/flat.
Releve to describe net hardwood stand. Land surface big rock lag (15% exposed rock) probably water washed prairie river: lake plain nearby.
Releve to describe old-growth stand near aerial seedlings of Jim Kelly. Soils sandy, cobbly loam.
Releve typical of mixed pine forest on crest. Pine stumps common with up to 4 fire scars. Soils somewhat excessively drained, straight LFS, probably a dune.

Worms prominent, small patches of exposed soil, less than one years litter only. Deer browse common. Small blowdown patches and frequent canopy gaps in surrounding forest. Community occupies an island (~29 acres) in Knife Lake. no cut sumps observed. Good site index evidence by tree size. Small and medium well-decayed Coarse Woody Debris common, recent layer of coarse woody debris common. Mature birch in community are mostly dying, previously more imported. Soil: 8cm silty with organic and worms over silt.

Present-day young forest was probably cut or burned a few decades ago. Deer trails numerous & browse is evident. No large down logs, just small woody debris. Avergage tree DBH 20-30cm though some Tilia a little larger. Sandy soil without well-developed organic layer. Moisture availability is evident only based on species composition (dry year).

A beautiful deciduous forest with relatively large (30-45cm DBH), tall trees. Situated on a steep, northeast-facing slope on very sandy soil (easy to see at the base of tip-ups). Surprising to me that the ground layer contains so many rich forest species and so few dry forest of woodland species. Suggests that the slope has not been influence much by logging or fire. The ground layer plants are small and sparse. Dry leaf litter is the dominant feature. Large and small dead branches. Tip-ups and snapped trunks.

The tall trees, bur oak and basswood, create about 75% canopy cover. There is abundant Carpinus and Ostrya which suggests past disturbance to the forest canopy, probably logging, but there are no cut stumps or large down dead trees. The landscape position is appropirate for lowlland ahrdwood or wet-mesic forest. Well-drained sandy soil. On low terrace of the St. Croix River.

Typical willow swamp dominated by slender willow with speckled alder in patches. Dense and difficult to walk through shrub clumps. After 4 weeks of drought, peat is still moist and between clumps there is wet muck. The peat is fairly compact, though, so it definitely feels like the water level has dropped some.

A little example of a wetland that has some "boggy" vegetation with sphagnum mosses, only about four such places at Wild River State Park. This is a small circular basin with a soupy "moat" at the margin and a central peaty mat. The plot was located under well-grown alder clumps on the peat. This alder swamp is the sort that grades into tamarack swamp in east-central Minnesota as opposed to alders that grow at the margin of sedge fens on shallow black soil. Here, forbs are abundant rather than graminoids. Surrounding forest, woods and fields show grazing, fencelines, brushy areas of prickly ash, buckthorn, and tatarian honeysuckle, lack of diverse ground layer under dry-mesic red maple forest canopy, low forb diversity, and abundant Pennsylvania sedge at the wetland margin.

This prairie slope by Dry Creek is one of the best remaining examples in the Upper St. Croix Valley of a complete assemblage of native, dry prairie species on sandy terraces and outwash near the St. Croix River (as opposed to the Anoka Sandplain outwash). Complete assemblages are exceedingly rare in Chisago County. Land was heavily grazed and cultivated in the past. Small, predictable, assemblages of dry sand prairies are good at recolonizing old fields, especially nutrient-poor, sandy fields and roadsides. In contrast, the relatively intact example has a high species diversity and includes some less-common species. Current management here includes removing encroaching woody plants and monitoring certain desirable species. This is a very valuable remnant.

This mesic forest is similar to those occurring on the 30-60 foot high terrace slope throughout the park except it has red maple rather than sugar maple as a canopy co-dominant with red oak and basswood. The vegetation on this slope is patchy, drier areas in canopy gaps have white oak trees and some trees that look more like northern pin oak (Querces ellipsoidalis) than red oak. There is a good amount of dead wood on the ground, all sizes. The soil is sandy loam, loose, and tip-up mounds are common. Interrupted fern is abundant at the toe of the slope. Below, further out on the low terrace near wetland margins here, the oak-basswood-maple canopy in not continuous and shrubs (hazel and Rubus spp.) are common. Shadier patches on the lowland have only a moderately good variety of mesic forest herbs. Virginia grapefern (Botrychium virginianum) was found in this area in 2001, no rare Botrychium ferns.

This oak forest on the topland above the shady, mesic forest slope, has the characteristic tree species of the topland: red oak, bur oak, and white oak. Sugar maple or red maple are nearly absent in this plot but they do occur in the vicinity but they are noticeable patchy. Oak reproduction is typically nearly absent. Some red oak trees here have features of norther pin oak but they are lumped with red oak as presumed hybrids because they don't show all the northern pin oak features. In and near this plot, the canopy trees are slender, straight, mostly single-stemmed, and averaging 25-35cm diameter(DBH), with a few red oaks at 40cm DBH. The number of ground layer species is larger than appears at first glance in the field because there are only a few individuals of each species and they are not distributed evenly. Forbs are withered because of mid-summer drought and their total cover estimate is 25-50%; that might be 50-75% under more favorable conditions.

This plot is the largest opening (with prairie species) in a rectangular area of brushy savanna within a larger area of dry oak woodland/dry oak forest. At present, the prairie species diversity is not high. This plot and the next plot (2001-18) together illustrate the compositional shift from savanna to shady woodland. Additional prairie species not found in the rectangular area occur in the adjacent old field to the north, those prairie species are somewhat weedy or are tolerant of droughty conditions. (Poa, Danthonia, Artemisia campestris, Hieracium longifilum, and abundant little bluestem.

This woodland plot has a composition that is typical of dry oak forest as well as dry oak woodland on droughty, sandy soil on the topland in the park. The dominant oaks here are called red oaks, but have characteristics of northern pin oak (hard to distinguish hybrids). This White spruce seedling from mature, planted trees.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Species-rich forest in fine condition despite the small total acreage along Dry Creek and cutting and grazing associated with past farm use. Plant species occurring in this area not often found elsewhere in park. Erosion and deepening of a horse trail through area threatens stand.

Loss of oak canopy because of oak wilt in a part of a fairly uniform and level dry (or somewhat dry-mesic) oak forest. This plot was well-exposed to sun at the ground layer all growing season. There are a good variety of non-prairie species here, and suggest that fires have shifted the canopy from forest to woodland.

This plot is located west of station 6 on the paved bike trail, about 35 meters in from trail. Dry-mesic oak forest seems to have been more open in the past. Old tip-up craters and mounds. There are also fairly large-diameter, oak trunks on the forest floor in the last stages of decay. Large amount of leaf litter.

Mesic oak savanna that grades into woodland (brushier areas dominated by shrubs and trees). This plot characterized the portion having the least amount of woody brush and a ground layer dominated by prairie species. Savanna and woodland here is situated on about 10 ac. of flat terrace along Dry Creek about 1/2 mile west of St. Croix. Valley slops of Dry Creek that rose ~50feet from this terrace, also a combination of savanna and woodland.

Small remnant of maple-basswood forest on a northeast-facing slope 0.2 to 0.5 miles south of the park entrance. The plot is situated at the crest on east side of the gravel road. Different soil type (siltier) that throughout most of the park where it is sandy (760-850 feet elevation). Subtle difference in plant species composition compared to mesic forest on shady terrace slopes in the park(showy orchis, rattlesnake fern, and grapefern). This is a small but significant rich maple-basswood forest.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: St. Croix River terrace, slightly undulating with low moist areas (low areas between leveessuch as this plot), slight rises (old depositional levves;see plot 2001-26), and deeper, old, abandoned channels. This floodplain is not active every year but this year, 2001, the St. Croix had a prolonged, high-water period in the spring. This plot are is flooded and the patterning of plants was typical of active floodplain rather than black ash swamp. Litter mostly twigs and sticks. This area has had some major disturbance historically because of logging, grazing, and the river crossing at Never's Dam site. Old barbed wire. Rhamnus cathartica is a threat.

This is a wonderfully diverse alder swamp, having a wide variety of shrubs, forbs & sedges. There are many subtle microhabitats - narrow deer trails, a patch of sphagnum moss, a raised hummock with black ash sapling, a wet pool of mucky water, shady-mossy below arching alder canopy, slight opening with dense, low shrubs. Resembles alder swamp despite the mixed shrub swamp and rich fen influences. Hard to find a uniform 10x10 plot. Saw no Rhamnus frangula. Moss cover (including sphagnum clumps): 1-5%. Muck: 1-5%. Litter (dead sedges, forbs, twigs):10%.

This plot is on a slight rise on the floodplain along the St. Croix River. The terrace is slightly undulating with low moist areas, slight rises and deeper, old abandoned channels. This floodplain is occasionally active. 2001 water was particularly high. This plot does not show evidence of flooding. There is old barbed wire just to the west of the plot, evidence of the history of disturbance. There is little micro-topography on the ground although south of the plot there are some tree tip-up mounds and down dead trunks. Despite the maple canopy, this plot is more like disturbed, lowland hardwood forests in the park than maple-basswood forests.

This plot is located in a slight depression on a broad, fairly flat, sandy, mid-elevation terrace (850 foot elevation) at the park. Surrounding the plot is old field vegetation. Because the swale is small it contains a variety of upland and wetland plants nearly side by side and therefore the species list is quite long. Gopher mounds present which provide micro-habitats for weedy species.

This is not a typical floodplain forest. This forest is situated at the toe of a northeast-facing, mesic forest slope, it is a narrow band about 40-50m wide between the toe-of-slope and the St. Croix River. There was unusually high water in spring 2001 and there are new bands of depositional sand here. Herbaceous perennial plants were buried in places and have re-grown during 2001. There is beaver activity that creates some canopy openings.

Mesic forest on the steep, northeast-facing slope overlooking the St. Croix River. It is just a narrow strip. The variety of species found here was good. Much dead/down wood, old decaying trunks, and old tip-up mounds. Two notes worthy species preset, bladdernut and wahoo or burning bush, both have been heavily browsed.

This dry oak woodland is situated on a broad flat terrace of post-glacial St. Croix River (at 850 foot elevation) the variety of shrubs and the presence of species such as blueberry, native honeysuckles, Pyrola, and Oryzopsis racemosa suggest that there may be a  history of white pine-hardwood or maybe jack pine woodland on these sandy St. Croix River terraces.

This scenic but narrow band of mesic forest is on the slopes and crest of a large ravine overlooking the St. Croix River. Plot is at the crest of a slope, about 50m away from the gravel road/park boundary. There are cut stumps and trees are fairly slender averaging 15-30cm DBH. Tree reproduction (subcanopy) at this time is sugar maple and bitternut hickory. Heavy deer browse.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Very steep, very small patch of white pine-hardwood forest above the Sunrise River. Cut white pine stumps on plot topland. Natural erosion from sand/gravel road is a threat to site. High-quality natural community and scenic area.

Nice example of floodplain along the Sunrise River that experiences natural flooding. Plot is about 30m from the river. Area dominated by silver maple and has slight linear rises. (old depositional features; levees). There are a lot of dead tree trunks and limbs. Rhamnus cathartica frequent in area but absent in plot.

This portion of the St. Croix River Floodplain was under water for an unusually long time during the spring of 2001. There are large, new piles of dead, woody debris. Below the herbaceous goundlayer, there is exposed silty-sandy soil.

This plot is on a slight terrace above the general level of the floodplain. The canopy trees are not large in diameter (20-30cm DBH). Dominate grass is Elymus virginicus. Few old/large trees, history of disturbance? There is a lot of down, dead, woody debris here.
Dry-mesic forest here is typical of this large area of unfragmented oak forest. The plot is situated to the east of an island-like rise. This plot is at roughly 810 feet.

Surprisingly nice little savanna opening because it is far from other prairie remnants. Plot basically encompasses the opening. It is surrounded by bur oaks and red oak/northern pin oak hybrids at about 2-5m in height. On the south side of the opening there are even a few jack pines at about 5m in height.

A lovely little sphagnum-tamarack wetland that is the only of it's kind at Wild River State Park. There are several species of sphagnum. Plot is situated near the west end of the little basin and grades into a margin of alders and sedges.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: One of a number of patches of black ash swamp on the lowland terrain. Late in the season for representative percent-cover. Substrate of moist, black, organic soil. Bur oak is a canopy co-dominant. Buckthorn is a serious threat, common along the trails.

Typical lowland hardwood forest within about 100m of the St. Croix River on broad, non-active floodplain. Lot of large and small dead down wood. There are cobbles and boulders in the silty-sandy matrix. Buckthorn is common.
Plot chosen to represent natural origin native plant community; undisturbed; on boulder/ cobble substrate with small pockets of sandy loam soil. Blister rust mortality <1%; damage approx. 40%.
Plot chosen to represent typical Pinus banksiana dominated community after harvest and planting, without fire.
Plot chosen to document this native plant community in Laurentian Highlands subsection on timber frear till plain (Le03). Abundant spruce stumps - old high grade harvest.

County Forest Road ~100m east 0.5 square miles. Open water pools infrequent. Native plant community occupies small basin connected to other small wetlands. pH=5.7, good quality native plant community, no signs of local disturbance. Surrounding landscape with heavy forest management. Sparse graminoid litter and Larix needles.

Scattered 75%+ decreased stumps. Native plant community occupies a relatively flat area between small wetland basins. Pinus resinos and P. strobus common within native plant community  to the west, most of NPC herabouts without pine component. Snags occassional/common throughout. Blowdown to the east. No soil probe. Sparse deciduous leaf and herbaceous litter.
Tree DBH (cm):
Abies balsimifera: 42 (max)
Picea mariana: 39 (max and mode)
Betula papyrifera - mode: 20-22
Populus tremuloides - mode: 25-32

Designated DNR old-growth stand. Minimal/no worms, spongy duff layer. Shallow isolated pools with moderate standing water or wet, mucky common throughout native plant community. Scattered areas with cut stumps ~50% decayed. Coarse woody debris of all sizes and classes scattered patchy common. 
Tree DBH (cm):
Betula alleghaniensis: 40-50
Acer saccharium: 33-43
Tilia americana: 32-38

No standing water. Shallow peat and mossy peat with twigs and needles (~14cm) over saturated sandy silt soils. Soil probe repeatedly hit rocks and hard-packed mineral soil. A little bit of mistletoe throughout, not heavy. Coarse woody debris common. Native plant community lies within 1/4 miles of and <10 feet above Cloquet river. pH: 5.3. Tip-ups expose rocky sandy silt mineral soil at ~10-15cm below the moss surface. Modal Picea DBH: 14-21cm.

Patches of heavy moose browse throughout native plant community, shrubs within plot moderately browsed. 80% decayed stumps scattered occassional, cut? Betula often in clumps or multi-stemmed. Moss-covered rocks at surface common. Coarse woody debris patchy common. Thuja occidentalis occurs within native plant community, but not characteristic of overall NPC here. Soil: 10 cm black organic w/some minerals over sandy silt loam > 30cm. Mineral soil saturated at ~15cm below the surface. Sparse litter of leaves and needles. 
Modal Tree DBH (cm):
Abies: 12-23
Betula: 18-35
Picea: 13-20

pH=5.3. Native plant community occupies an isolated basin 1/2 mile southeast and about 30 feet above St. Louis River. Basin surrounded by gently sloping uplands. Native plant community appears undisturbed, no trails (except deer and moose). No cut stumps. Coarse woody debris common. Sparse litter of graminoid, twigs, and needles.

Worms observed in Ah soil horizon. Fire scars on older coarse woody debris and snags. Coarse woody debris all sizes and decay stages occasional/common. Pinus strobus scattered patchy within native plant community. Picea mariana dominated throughout. Deer browse. Dry soil. A horizon/humus layer: 10cm.

pH=7.2. Native plant community part of larger wetland complex drains to St. Louis River, half mile southwest. Many tip-ups and leaning trees. No cut stumps observed. Overall rather slender (DBH mode=18-30). Native plant community with many small shrubby canopy openings. Standing water in low spots of microtopography. Sparse litter of graminoid, twigs, and leaves.
pH=4.2. 0.25m southeast of the Cloquet River. Native plant community on a broad ~flat landscape with northern fire dependent(FDn) forests with extensive interconnected wetlands.

Native plant community borders Cloquet River. No standing water in plot. Soils moist sandy silt with oragnic soils. NPC site ~1m above today's river level. This example of Alder swamp may not fit well into FPn73a. NPC occupies narrow, flat terrace along Cloquest River. No drifted debris observed but NPC obviously flooded. Moss mostly restricted to moss. Sparse litter of graminoid and twigs.

pH=4.8-5.0. No standing water but soils are saturated. Native plant community occupies a large area within an inside bend of St. Louis River. Very thick mat. Adjacent NPC, FDn43 & APn81. No signs of disturbance. Stunted Larix and Betula papyrifera within NPC. Sparse litter of graminoid and Chamadaphne leaves.

Native plant community a small 15-acre patch along St. Louis River. NPC surrounded by FPn73a & APn91. NPC doesn't appear influenced by surface flooding although NPC's north edge is ~20m from River. pH=4.2-4.6 No mistletoe and no stumps observed. Very little wind toss. Sparse litter of graminoid and twigs. 
Tree DBH (cm):
Picea: max 27.6, mode 9-13
Larix: max 22.5, mode: 4-6

Flat terrace along south side of small flowage between east and west Pike Lakes. Moss restricted to rocks & wood. Hollows with flowing water. Stream 10m north of plot. Coarse woody debris common/abundant, mostly Betula papyrifera and lesser Thuja. Adjacent uplands are FDn (fire dependent). Soil: Organic over rocky silt. Sparse litter of Thuja needles, leaves, and twigs. Thuja occidentalis DBH (cm)- mode 23-26, max 36.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Upper slope above the west end of East Pike Lake. Fire scars on older coarse woody debris. Small and medium CWD common, large CWD rare outside of an area of heavy blowdown 100m northeast. Rocks are typically moss-covered, otherwise moss is absent. Sparse litter of needles, leaves, and twigs. Soil: brown/tan sandy silt with loess and pebbles.

20m wide wetland on downstream side of an active and old beaver dam on the SW side of Gogebic Lake. The same native plant community fringes the pool behind the dam. Moderate standing water in hollows, dry surface soil common. Continuous Carex lasiocarpa at lakeshore.

Native plant community not wet at surface but soils are saturated. NPC lies at the upper end of a small ~125m wide catchment that feeds into the flowage between Rocky Lake and Johnson Falls. Coarse woody debris common, canopy gaps with Alnus, Betula, and Abies.

D4-5 Acer saccharum occasionally in Native plant community. Coarse woody debris medium-large common. Pinus strobus often with forked trunk. Snags occasional. Patchy deer browse. 
Tree DBH (cm):
Pinus strobus: 30-50+
Betula papyrifera: 25-30+
Abies: 18-20
Populus: 22-29
Pinus Resinosa: 35-42

This Native plant community marked by a darker colored CIR photo signature. Wet, mucky hollows occupy 75% of the ground with Chamaedaphne and Sphagnum hummocks <1 m square each covering 25% total. pH=4.3.
pH=4.1. Thick floating mat bordering a bog lake. Plot edge 1m from water's edge.
Coarse woody debris occasional. Mistletoe in vicinity. Native plant community within a large wetland complex between drumlins. pH=3.5.
pH=4.7. Peat greater than 1m deep. Native plant community part of a large wetland complex. Trees widely spaced. Muddy hollows with standing water 1cm deep. Coarse woody debris occasional/common.

pH=5.9-6.0. Native plant community part of the extensive 100 mile swamp complex. Existing mine <0.5 miles north, proposed mine ~1.0 mile southeast. Adajcent uplands are fire dependent(FDn). Plot 1/4 mile southwest of Mud Lake.

pH=3.5-3.6. Native plant community part of the extensive 100 mile swamp complex. Existing mine less than 0.5 miles north, proposed mine ~1.0 mile southeast. Adjacent uplands are fire dependent(FDn). Plot 0.25 mile southwest of Mud Lake.

Mucky hollows Bryales-covered, saturated without standing water. Peaks typically with Sphagnum. Coarse woody debris occasional. Small native plant community patch between ~20-year old aspen and black spruce bog. No pH taken.
pH=4.4. Plot on south side of a bog lake. Floating mat with variable thickness. Lake with 90% open water, 10% floating and emergent vegetation.
pH=3.5. A small native plant community occurrence surrounding a bog lake and nearly surrounded by young forest and clear-cuts. No standing water.
pH=4.2(1). Native plant community borders a ~75m x 4m open water pool within an extensive black spruce bog. Snowmobile trail ~15m north with summer ATV use.
pH=4.1(0). Poor fen fringe of Launa Lake, east side of lake. Lake with history of beaver daming at outlet. Wild rice common in shallow water.
No pH taken. No standing water, soils saturated. Plot within 15m of Dent Lake shoreline. Native plant community continues to shoreline with greater species diversity at water's edge.

pH=5.4. Plot edge at water's edge. Native plant community between Dent Lake to east and mixed conifer swamp dominated by Thuja to the west. On a thick +/- broken mat with numerous beaver trails crossing to swamp. Nymphaea odorata in water.

No standing water. Water pooled 18" below Sphagnum surface. Old logging trails in native plant community, no cut stumps observed within plot but overall native plant community  is rather open. pH=5.8. Thuja dominates to the east, closer to the shore (WFn53). Larix DBH: 15-20cm, 35cm max.

pH=5.6. Platanthera clavellata observed sporadically to north within Native plant community. Native plant community within a moderate-large acid peatland complex between drumlins. Dent Lake 0.25 miles southeast, uplands 1/8 mile west.
pH=4.0. Native plant community occupies a small basin with a narrow connection to a linear acid peatland complex between eskers. Drumlinized landscape. Plot taken at eastern side of the basin.

No standing water in native plant community, pH of a 30m x 10m open water pool=6.2. Pool surrounded by native plant community. Plot between pool and Partridge River. No moss or woodies with in plot/NPC. Patches of Salix species, Spirea alba, and Cornus stolonifera within NPC. Plot between shrub community and railroad grade.

pH=5.6(7). +/- 1.0cm standing water. Soils saturated. Active railroad bisects Native plant community east/west w/most of native plant community north of tracks. NPC part of large wetland complex extending north and south and draining to Partridge River. Compare to DNR releve 3581.
Native plant community part of large APn and FPn complex that drains to the Partridge River. Active railroad 100m south. Adjacent uplands FDn. Compare to DNR Releve #3580.

pH=5.9. Plot 10m from water's edge of a small bog lake. Vegetation trampled and on a broken mat between plot and water's edge. E3-4 snags common in vicinity. Plot at the north side of a small bog lake.

pH=5.5. Occasional 2-3cm deep pools a footprint in size, otherwise no standing water. Saturated peat soils. Picea/Alnus 10-15m wide band between this native plant community and FDn43 upland to the southeast.

Coarse woody debris all ages and decay stages common. Many recent blowdowns. Plot on higher point of island surrounded by swamp and Partridge River, 5-10 feet above today's water level. No signs of flooding. E6-6 Picea mariana, Picea glauca, and Abies balsimifera more common at island edge.

Hollows moist, moderately moss (weft) covered. No standing water. Scattered canopy gaps with Thuja, Abies and/or Fraxinus, Alnus filling in. 75% decay cut stumps occasional within native plant community. Coarse woody debris of all sizes and decay stages common. NPC lacks a consistent large tree component.

Worms absent/minimal. 75% decayed cut stumps in plot and vicinity (cf. Pinus). Native plant community on slight broad depression within a gently sloped/flat landform. Canopy Picea glauca uncommon in native plant community. Coarse woody debris small-medium all decay stages common, large well-decayed occasional.
NPC on an esker. +/- fire scars on oldest stumps. CWD, usually Abies bals, common, slender <25% decayed. Canopy Pinus strobus occas in NPC, patches of canopy Pop trem occasional in NPC. AciA conifer

No worms observed but presence seems likely. Duff ~spongy. Picea glauca often DD in vicinity. 75%+ decayed stumps scattered common. Areas of heavier Acer saccharum +/- Thuja occidentalis within Native plant community. Coarse woody debris all sizes and decay stages common. Topographic context: middle/lower.
Tree DBH (cm):
Acer saccharum: 25-35
Bet allegheniensis: 45-55
Bet papyrifera: 20-28
Thuja occidentalis: 18-30
Very well developed cover of spring ephemerals. Mid-slope.
Somewhat less carpeted with spring wildflowers than the slope immediately to north. Cornus is mainly browsed off and just leafing so hard to guess species.
North facing slope of a long ravine leading to DesMoines River.
Releve in level forest west of lookout. Parthenosissus just budding.
Level forest. Upper/middle slope.
Maple litter layer. Releve is across trail, due N of deer stand. Best example in county with respect to community quality.

Northwest facing slope, draw behind cemetery. Dutch Charley Creek is transparent, sandy bottom in the area around 10-12 meter wide, present depth approaches a foot. This releve is on slope.
Tree DBH (cm)
Tilia: 25-50
Ulmus: 10-15
Quercus: 50-100
Level releve on a "terrace" above river. It is likely that this terrace was a presettlement floodplain into which Dutch Charley Creek has eroded a deeper channel.
Lower slope of north facing hill just above picnic ground restroom facilities.
Fair amount of open, disturbed soil, on terrace just north of stream south of outhouse on north side of stream.

The amount of publicly owned forest in this park is tiny, probably = to 3 or 4 side by side releves, purpose of releve was to capture floristic distribution of spring flora in the County. Highly disturbed site, not intended as an example of a quality community. Releve is in best possible quality area. Majority of park has a solid shrub layer of Rhamnus.
Repeat releve for comparison of spring and summer aspects and flora. Same general area as 05-06-97-01 (couldn't get summer GPS points).

Probably the spring ephemerals had higher cover. Was rained out for most of month of May. Small rivulet enters ravine just east of plot and is bounded below to east by a seepy area. Topographic context: lower/toe.
Plot size controlled by extent of seep 20m east to west and 10 north to south on lower part of slope. Open discharge on surface at least 5%.
Lovely block of oak woods, clean aspect without buckthorn. Topographic context: upper/middle.
Stand typical of community. Level of invasion of buckthorn not typical of natural condition but reflective by actual condition of most of these riparian woods.

Releve on upper terrace south of Highwater Creek. Mature oaks and ash widely spaced 4-6 meters apart. Rhamnus scattered. Probably more species under the solid cover of Laportea. Should have a spring releve. 
Tree DBH (cm):
Quercus macrocarpa: 40-65
Frax pennsylvanica: 40-60
No litter and at this season about 70% bare ground. To see at this time of year you wouldn't guess the spring aspect. Same location as releve #3596 done in April. Slope: 30% E of N 35 degrees.
Releve at base of bowl in a cove like setting, coming down a gentle concave north facing slope.

Floodplain terrace. Appears there is a lower, more frequent flooded terrace full of dead elm and Laportea. This one is only slightly higher, maybe 8" -1ft at most. Nearly all trees DBH between 14-24cm. Topographic context: lower/flat. Tree DBH (cm): (Mainly between 14-24cm)
Celtis: 26, 24
Ulmus: mostly dead, average 26
Carya: mainly dead, similar size to elm
Juglans: 30, 40, 25

Very well stocked plot on slope of ravine. Majority of tract is more highly dist. than plot. Base of one of the oaks looks like exposed by worms. Ravine full of deadfall. Forest floor about 50% bare at this time of year.
Terrace on west side of DesMoines River, fairly level.
Terrace between deerstand and sharp bank of DesMoines River
NA
NA
No perm marker - releve typical.
This is a prairie bush clover site new in 2005. You can look up the legal for it to get 1/4 1/4 section.
Areas of this park are heavily infested with garlic mustard. This releve was consciously placed as far as possible from the infestation.

Near crest of west facing down slope. Several large WS windtoss No apparent cut stumps. Lush lycopods. Soil: shallow sitly loam to rock or w/scattered rocks and boulders. Sparse litter of leaves and twigs.

Shallow hollows and slightly raised hummocks. Exposed roots over bouldery subsurface. No stump. Dead and down firs. Moss covered rock, seasonal wet holes. Litter of leaves and twigs. Soils: peaty/organic.
Scattered canopies and rocky ground creating moss covered, patchy Ledum/Sphagnum and charcoal in lower duff - no fire scar. Sparse litter of leaves and twigs.

FDn43 or WFn64 in a wet draw within MHn35. Draw only ~50m wide. Wettest part, including releve, has pools of water. Rocks are covered with moss. Heavy earthworm infestation. Litter of leaves and graminoid.
Tamarack swamp between railroad, aspen forest, and rich cedar swamp. Pools of water cover ~10%. pH ~6.2.  1 large rock. Average DBH is 15-20cm.
Alder swamp in swale within aspen-birch-spruce-fir forest that opens into a larger forested and open peatland complex. pH ~6.0. Shallow pools cover ~20%. Sparse litter of leaves and graminoid.
Wet cedar forest with gaps. Shallow pools cover ~20%. Surrounded by alder swamp and aspen-fir-spruce forest. Trees average 30cm DBH. Max cedar is a leaning 45cm.
Wet meadow near mouth of Stone Creek into St. Louis River. Adjacent veg. is shrub shore fen semi-floating mat.
Black ash swamp. Flooded near road, but here it appears undisturbed. Average DBH 10". Pools cover ~40% of area, but do not have standing water now. Upland near by is young aspen FDn43b.

Soil earthworm worked. Shallow pools are dry and have been for a while. Pools cover approximately 20% of area. A bear has ripped moss off some rocks in pools. Diameters skewed. Some ash 45cm, most trees average 20cm. A horizon depth: 23cm.

FDn43 or MHn45b native plant community class. Heavy earthworm infestation. A few old cedar stumps. Cedars average 14" DBU. Max yellow birch is 45cm (maybe 50). Red maples average 10". Both MH and FD forests on this drumlin.

Paper birch and tamarack swamp with open canopy and a complete cover of alder in open areas (WFn64?). Pools cover about 10-20% of area, but are dry now. About 30% tree cover. Average DBH 15". A Horizon depth: >50cm.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Community class WFn55a. Small pools are dry. This is a small patch of wet forest intermixed with FDn43b downslope from a hill of mesic hardwood forest. A horizon depth 10cm.

OPn92 native plant community  along St. Louis River. On inland side, poor fen with scattered tamarack and islands of jack pine-dominated FDn43. About 50% graminoid cover and 50% short shrub layer. A few old tree stumps up to 15cm DBH. Dry now, but standing water a month ago.
Rich shrub fen on shore of small lake. Inland is acid peatland community dominated by Myrica gale, with significant sedge cover. My feet are dry, but would not have been a month ago.

WFn64a native plant community. Dry pools cover ~40%. Below 20cm is an unpenetrable layer of wet gravel and rock. Jack pine and tamarack average 30cm DBH, black ash averages 15cm. About 20m from upland. Gravel road separates this from a pure black ash forest, with flooding near road and young tamaracks regenerating. Litter of deciduous leaves and graminoids.

Upland, just above adjacent alder swamp and conifer swamp. Trees average 20 cm DBH (max 30cm), even aged, probably natural origin (no cut stumps). Dry now, but low spots are probably wet sometimes. A horizon depth: 3cm. Average peat depth >60cm.
Transitional upland black spruce forest between FDn43b and FPn62. Trees average 20cm DBH. Shallow soil over rocks. Rocks above soil surface are moss-covered.
OPn92 native plant community on shore of Round Lake. Some areas have significant Typha latifolia, suggesting lake level fluctuations. A few old dead tree trunks.
Patch of shrub shore fen within a graminoid rich fen on shore of Seven Beaver Lake.
Situated between rich fen and forested bog. Trees average 10cm DBH. APn81 or APn80 community.
Poor black spruce swamp (APn81) in narrow band running southwest-northeast between fire-dependent upland forests. Average DBH 12-15cm.

Slopes down to small creek. Some small patches of Phalaris arundinacea Some small scattered openings nearby with springs (emergent zones). Iron rich water. Soil: sphagnum peat: 0-10cm, marly:10-44cm+.

Slopes down to shrub swamp, then large wild rice bed (Lower Rice Lake). Scattered small springs and seeps around site. Some areas with more tamarack, other areas with more Black spruce, overall tamarack is more common.
Hummocks of Sphagnum across the entire site. Slopes down to Boutwell Creek. Can hear water running under the Sphagnum.
Level area by creek, has an old fieldy look, but owners insist it was never plowed. Dominant forbs in single species patches.
Very close to edge of ravine, just west and upslope. Owner refers to hill as "Dinosaur ridge". 50 Prairie bush clover in a 5m diameter circle, slightly lengthened north to south.
On point between Juniper patches, crest of knob, east of pines. This site is being overwhelmed by Juniperus horizontalis. Releve placed to minimize this situation. Topographic context: crest/flat.

On slight southwest slope. Site known for years by botanists as "Creeping Juniper Ridge". Appears to be overtaken by Juniperis horizontalis, but does not appear to be much more dense than in 1979 visit.
Level degraded area west of large stash of rocks and heavy metal.
Slope on east side of former pasture. Level area to west is degraded and cool season dominated.
Releve adjacent to road. Topographic Context, Mid to Lower
Below the stash of heavy metal.
Just downslope of junk pile.
N-NE facing slope on NE rather level outlier of prairie bank.
NE-facing slope, SE end of rock pile. Topographic Context, Middle to Lower
Convex area of slope. Owner's wife accompanied surveyor.
Concave area of slope. [NOTE: 11 duplicate species; not original form in files.] Note from NPS document: "west facing slope above creek".  Owner's wife accompanied surveyor.
Southeast-facing slope due east of radio tower, north of fence. There are vehicle tracks all over this prairie.
Top of hill northeast of radio tower, level to gentle top slope. Needs burn.
Much bare ground. soil texture: gravelly.
Northwest of tower buildings on west to southwest-facing slope. Slope dominated by big bluestem. Soil texture: gravelly.
Releve too far upslope to have captured Lespedeza population reconfirmed in 2004.
Very nice northwest-facing slope grades into gentler north-facing slope. Quality declines near ravine. Releve on longest part of slope.
Very steep north-facing slope right against east fenceline.
Releve on southwest-facing slope at east end of prairie north of stream, east of steeply eroded ravine. Very depauperate, fair amount of bare ground on this slope.
Difficult to assess cover, this area is presently fairly heavily grazed. Releve in best possible area. Upper portion of slope pounded, lower portion somewhat more lightly grazed.
Waypoint 87.
Downhill and west of old gravel works. 20 Lespedeza leptostachya associated with this releve.
Hasty and undoubtedly imcomplete releve conducted with an onlooker for the purpose of illustrating how disturbed an area can support Lespedeza leptostachya. Over 80 plants. Waypt 123
Releve on a very steep east facing bank of creek with considerable woody invasives. Good species list, but poor quality. "Lookout Hill". Topographic context: upper/middle/lower/toe.
More level part of rolling prairie. Slope: 3-10% south southwest. Topographic context: upper/middle.
Prairie continues on slope of hill. Near pine plantation. Much previously good prairie in 1980's has been destroyed by plantation. Topographic context: upper/middle/lower.
Waypoint 149
NA
This releve is only slightly downhill of two 2003 releves, but includes the Lespedeza.
Upper slope, west facing, slightly to the north of the meadow.
Wet brush prairie being evaluated for Land Owner Incentive Program(LIP) woody plant removal. Approximately 8 acres not presently overpowered by woody invasion. Most of prairie invaded by woodies.
Releve associated with Prairie bush clover, fairly rank and steep slope near ravine being overtaken by woody species.
Wet prairie north of road in area that supports Cypripedium candidum.
Nearly level wet-mesic prairie.
Wet prairie in area that supports Cypripedium candidum.
Slightly rolling area west of seepage.
This area seems more like wet prairie than as mapped by wildlife management area cover.
Selected to represent somewhat patterned area of large rich fen. pH~ 6.1. May reflect flooding impact from RR ROW. Scatt graminoid & Sphag hummocks, irregular pools & tracks. Drosera anglica nearby.
Plot chosen to capture typical representation of peatland NPC of natural origins with some mistletoe infection and mortality.
Plot chosen to represent high quality NPC in large peatland complex of forested & graminoid wetlands in large basin among low hills. Other NPC in complex incl: Spruce bog, Open bog, Poor fen. pH 4.1
Natural origin stand. Old growth conditions. Abundant CWD-all sizes & states of decay. Scatt, well-decayed stumps various sizes of Thuja- yg trees deer browsed. Shallow wet much pools common. pH 6.5
Plot chosen to reflect transitional NPC between lowland & upland White Cedar forest. Scattered old stumps. Abundant CWD of all sizes. See DNR releve 3762 for adjacent wet forest.
Plot chosen to represent NPC as it occurs on long, narrow esker island in large patterned peatland. Plot spans width of esker & NPC. Scatt decaying stumps<= 10-inch diameter of cut Pinus resinosa.
Plot chosen to represent NPC class on landform common in LU subsect. Gently sloping upland terrain between swamps. Heavy fir regen, espec in canopy gaps & under birch. Not well represented in NPCkey
Plot selected to represent NPC common in this landscape of low, but influential relief. Occurring in drains poorly defined by topography usually with a variety of other shrub & graminoid wetlands.
Natural origin stand. No evidence of past management. Abundant CWD, mostly Betula papyrifera. Some blister rust damage of Pinus strobus, but little mortality.
Plot chosen to represent NPC with abundant advance regeneration of conifers in mesic mixed forest class. Natural origin stand. Pinus strobus regeneration common.
Natural origin stand with no evidence of past management. Comparitive- ly little microtopography of scattered hummocks and few hollows.
Plot chosen to reflect toe slope setting & common NPC in Frear sites. Fir budworm mortality extensive, most blown down. Older aspen & birch senescing. Sprouting trees common in open canopy areas.

Steep slope above creek. Plot selected to avoid areas historically heavily grazed. Representative of surrounding area. Basswood with multiple stems, not open grown. Topographic context: upper/middle/lower.

Earthworms common. Much deer browse. Much coarse woody debris. Concave, mid-slope of 100-foot, northeast-facing slope along Des Moines River. DBH 35-50cm. Caulophyllum unusually abundant. Silty clay-loam. Along >1 mile of slopes.

npc_subtype_name: Jack Pine - Black Spruce - Aspen Subtype
remarks: Old-growth jack pine/black spruce riparian forest along Little Isabella River. Flat, but broken terrain with tip-ups and dry-saturated hollows. Abundant coarse woody debris. Scattered large vegetation, boulders. No cutting. Clint borealis. Deer browsed. Sparse litter of needles/leaves/twigs.

Wet sand-seasonal wetland basin. Hydrological and vegetative gradient from surrounding upland conifers to ponded center of basin (depth 0.25m). Soil: Silty sand, large-small boulders throughout. No OHV use or other human disturbance. Wolf and deer tracks.
Mesic mixed forest with hardwood and conifer co-dominant. No evidence of fire or cutting. Slopes east toward open peatland complex. Old forest.

N-facing white pine/red pine forested slope of glacial erratics (Anorthositic gabbro). Fire scars at base of trees (0.3-2.0m). White pine 35-40 years old common, abundant seedlings. Small cut stumps of white pine. Soil revisit resulted in no soil description - unable to penetrate boulders 3-8 ft in size. This is a rubbly backslope.

Natural origin white-red pine old growth. White pine in patches within native plant community. Very little conifer regeneration (except fir). Greater area with patchy blowdown from 1999 windstorm. Evidence of windthrow (hummocks) and coarse woody debris. A horizon depth <4cm. Litter of needles and leaves.

One of few large patches of high quality, natural origin, old-growth white pine/red pine forest in area. Composition and structure very diverse. Moderate coarse woody debris, microtopogy. No evidence of blister rust. Herbivory light. Soil with worm castings. Soil: loam balled as in worm castings. A horizon depth >10cm. Litter of needles with some leaves. UPDATE soil - horizons: A, Bw1, Bw2, Bw3, 2C (very fine SL), 3C. Parent material is loamy drift over glaciofluvial over friable (ablation/supraglacial) till. Excavation below 3C impeded by rocks at 110 cm.

Large patch natural origin white pine/red pine. Rolling and bouldery with very fine sand-loam soils. Abundant large coarse woody debris, some blister rust, patchy White pine seedlings. Cone crop good in 2003. Adjacent area pine clear cut, regenerate Aspen/Birch => edge effects. Litter of needles/leaves. A horizon depth >5cm.
High quality rich fen adjacent to Shamrock Lake. Grades into tamarack swamp. Pools and water tracks interspersed. Few scattered hummocks. Beaver channels (east edge).

Graminoid poor fen surrounded open water basin. Fen with several species of orchids and rare plants. Area impacted by recreational use. Trails through fen and along waters edge results in pooling. Impacts to orchids unknown.

Old-growth white-red pine forest. Scattered old, small diameter cut stumps. Canopy with mixed amount of aspen and birch. Charcoal in soil. Scattered tall snags with fire scars. Low amount of large coarse woody debris. Slopes gently to west. Soil: Fine sandy loam with charcoal. Litter of leaves, needles, twigs, cones, and bark. A horizon depth >10cm.

Old-growth white/red pine forest in Dragon cRNA(USFS). Regenerate of white pine and white spruce associated with moderately abundant large coarse woody debris. Aspen often co-dominate in patches. No evidence of cutting or fires. Low deer browse. Sandy loam with small cobbles. Litter of needles and leaves.

White pine-red pine forest with multi-storied canopy. Terrain rolling with scattered boulders. Low browse. No evidence of worms, cutting or fire. Abundant large coarse woody debris. Adjacent to large forested peatlands to south and east. Litter of needles with small amount of leaves.

Moderately well-drained wet cedar forest on drumlin. Community is heterogeneous with mesic mixed forest. Previously high-graded with spruce and other species removed. Soils sandy-loam with no evidence of gleying.

Moderately well-drained mesic mixed forest on drumlin with low relief relative to surrounding peatlands. Native plant community heterogeneous, with patches of lowland and white cedar. Spruce and other species cut. No gleying. Canopy with Betula cordifolia.

White pine, black spruce, heart-leaved birch, paper birch and tamarack in canopy atypical of FDn43. On drumlin (low relief) surrounded by peatlands. Soils sandy-loam with clay hardpan (30cm). Season saturated, no gleying.

Old jack pine-balck spruce on rolling bouldery bedrock adjacent to Norway Lake. Soils with charcoal frags. Moderate-abundant large coarse woody debris and exposed rock with lichens and bryophytes. Sparse subcanopy. Good reference for FDn32c native plant community. A horizon depth >5cm.
Graminoid poor fen (ph=4.7) with +/- broad shore. Fen adjacent to Ova Lake. Shore fen with several rare species and Lycopodium inundatum.

Graminoid rich fen (water track). Water tracks range from pools-networks-linear. Surrounded by poor conifer swamp. Upland island in center dominated by Picea mariana. Headwaters of Bald Eagle Creek. pH=5.5. Sparse graminoid thatch.

Rich black spruce swamp with canopy ranging from pure black spruce to mix of tamarack, black spruce and patchy alder. Native plant community with scattered large patches of FDn32. Abundant hummock and hollows. Occasional cut stumps(cedar). No fire evidence. Variable surf water.

place_name: Crow Wing River - Knob Hill S
remarks: Typical of 3-acre, slightly wetter inclusion in 120-acre rich conifer swamp along the Crow Wing River south of Knob Hill. Trees 5-22cm DBH. Few snags. Substrate moderately hummocky, slightly wetter than adjacent FPn82b. Little coarse woody debris. Seepage stream near plot. ~100m to river.

Spring-fed 3-acre opening in 20-acre tamarack-black spruce swamp at north end of Straight Lake. Scattered small pools. Seepage flow to lake 50m to the southeast of plot. Wetter areas with low-statured vegetation. Quaky saturated peat. No stumps. Surrounded by 40-foot slopes. Jan Janssens recorded bryophytes along a 30-meter transect through the relevé plot (Janssens site 2551, 20 June 2007)- these species added by MDL.

Typical of ~80 acres in extensive inter-drumlin complex 6 miles NE of Nimrod. Snags common, mostly in understory. No stumps. Moderate coarse woody debris. More Picea mariana in some areas. Plot east of north/south-running winter tail, near county line.

Typical of 80 acres between Hwy 71 and old B-N railroad grade south of Menahga. Mature stand, Larix to 41cm DBH, Picea mariana to 28cm+, Abies to 20cm. Water in hollows. No stumps. Snags frequent. Coarse woody debris rather sparse.

Typical of ~30 acres in large conifer swamp complex south of Menahga. Deep peat; shallow water in hollows. Sparse coarse woody debris. Few snags or old stumps. Canopy slightly more open than releve #3814 (1/4 mile to northwest).

Typical of broad zone on south side of Mud Lake, also north side of lake. Basin surrounded by forested eskers. Plot 20m from lake, 25m from upland (Larix snags frequent toward uplant). No stumps. Quaky saturated peat. Hummocks to 40cm high. Water 4-8cm deep in foot prints. No surface water. 100m from releve #3817.

Southeast side Mud Lake. 20m from lake, 20m from upland (esker). Trees stunted, few snags. Quaky, saturated peat; no surface water. Typical of 10-acre area in much larger peatland. 100m from releve #3816.

40+ acres of mature forest on and adjacent to esker, east side of Mud Lake. Level to undulating terrain. Fine sandy-loam; humus intact. Trees 35-55cm DBH. Few old pine stumps. Snags occasional. Much large coarse woody debris. one of the nicest mature aspen stands in Becker County. Old trail just outside plot to north.

Typical of Jack pine/bur oak areas (grades to aspen) on ground moraine west of Big Basswood Lake. Pinus banksiana mature, to 40+cm DBH. Oaks frequently multi-stemmed to 30cm. Coarse woody debris sparse. Snags frequent. Soil is tan loamy sand with gravel. Topographic context: crest/upper.

Typical of 50 acres on peninsula between old stream channels feeding west end of Blueberry Lake. Tan sandy-loam >25cm deep. Very old conifer stumps frequent; fire scars. Scattered coarse woody debris. Trees 24-40cm+. Even aged stand. Ground layer very sparse except in canopy gaps. 
Tree DBH:
Populus 25-45+cm DBH
Abies to 30cm DBH
Picea to 35cm DBH

Typical of best quality of 160-acres north of County line road. 600-acre conifer swamp forms headwaters of Cat Creek. Mature stand, trees 15-35cm DBH. Few snags. No stumps. Peat >40cm deep. Depressions are wet, standing water <1cm.

Typical of 40 acres. Plot 50m from upland, 30m from small pond, center of fen. Moderately quaky peat >40cm deep. A few scattered, stunted Larix and Picea mariana in parts of fen. Upland is rolling moraine, with young aspen of various ages.

Typical of 120+ acres in forested moraine north of Coon Lake. Mature stand, trees 15-35cm DBH. Windfall frequent in places. Peat >40cm deep. Typical hummock/hollow substrate. No stumps. Snags occasional. Scattered coarse woody debris. South of forest road.

Center of ~8-acre poor fen filling basin in rolling moraine. SW margin of basin: 30-ft esker. Moderately quaky peat. Trees stunted, some dead. No stumps or large snags. No moat, water level unaltered. No beaver currently. Water 7.5cm in foot prints. Carex lacustris more abundant in outer zone, some outer areas dominated by Carex utriculata or Carex lasiocarpa.

Typical of 200+ acres northeast of Bad Medicine Lake. Level ridgetop in rolling moraine. Mature stand. Pines to 48cm DBH, mode is25-35cm. Moderate coarse woody debris. Snags occasional. No stumps. Litter/humus intact, 4 cm deep over tan fine sandy-silt.

Typical of 100 acres (fragmented by logging) on east side of Bad Medicine Lake. Pines 40-50+cm DBH, oak/aspen 25-40+cm; mature stand. Low ridgetop in rolling moraine. Few snags. No stumps. Moderate coarse woody debris. Root mounds common. Tan sandy-silt. Pines scattered in stand.

Maturing stand, 60 yrs here, often younger elsewhere. Upper portion of gradual north facing upper slope in gently rolling terrain. Occasional old stumps. Few snags. Sparse coarse woody debris. Trees 25-40cm DBH. Little worm evidence. Humus 2-3cm. Soil is gray to tan fine loamy-silt. Shrub layer unusually open here, patchy elsewhere where aspen more abundant in canopy.

Typical of 120 acres along Crow Wing River south of Knob Hill. Mature stand. Trees 15-40cm DBH. Old stumps infrequent. Sparse coarse woody debris, some windfall. Peat, hummocks/hollows 20-40cm high/low. Hollows dry; extended drought.

place_name: Two Inlets Trail - Small Lk N
remarks: Center of 3-acre poor fen surrounded by stunted and dead Larix swamp in wetland north of Small Lake. Despite drought, water level in wetland raised by beaver, least impact in poor fen zone. Peat >40cm deep, fairly quaky. Hummocks low, vegetation stunted. Drought year. Water 15cm deep in  footprints. Topographic context: depression/flat.

place_name: Indian Ck Rd - Coleman Lk SW
remarks: Typical of 120+ acres on rugged moraine SW of Coleman Lake. Middle and upper part of 50-ft SE-facing slope. Mature stand. Pines scattered, to 75cm DBH, fire scars on large pine. No stumps. Fine textured loamy-sand. Thick litter/duff, few worms. Topographic context: upper/middle.

One of one of the largest and best quality patches of this woodland type in Becker County. Mature stand, jack pine to 20-44cm DBH, red pine 46cm, 0aks 5-15cm. Sparse coarse woody debris. No stumps. Snags occasional. Silty-sand; outwash south of Straight River. Soil: silty-sand.
Trees are straight-trunked and mostly single-stemmed. Biggest trees (Birch) are 30-40cm DBH. Few scattered Pinus resinosa in the surrounding area.
Most canopy jack pines are around 30cm DBH. All are straight-trunked. Hazel is in thickets separated by small openings where the graminoids dominate. Litter of needles and leaves.

Canopy size red oak are mostly multi-stemmed. No cut stumps. Canopy boles are 30-40cm DBH. Vaccinium angustifolium seen nearby, but not in site. Surrounding area is gently rolling hills. Soil probe won't go >10cm.

place_name: Audubon Center of the N Woods
remarks: Lot of tip-up mounds. Pastured until 1968. Trees have straight trunks. No current disturbance. Past cutting of pines in late 1800's. Hinckley fire in 1894. Aspen cutting in 1950's.

Scattered fire-scarred stumps, a few cut. Most canopy trees are 20-30cm DBH. Scattered smaller trees. Most cedars are straight-trunked, few have upward-curving boles. Few downed small spruce and cedar.

Northern hardwoods designated old growth ~45 acres. All trees forest grown. Nice diverse strata, rolling terrain. Releve on high flat area. Surrounded by wet meadow & black ash swamp. Soil loamy/silty sand. Rocky soil seen at base of tip-ups. ATV trail runs through center of forest. Nice coarse woody debris. Good leaf litter. Scattered red pines and white pines in canopy. A horizon depth: 5cm.

Located at base of 2 gradual slopes; no evidence of earthworms. Many sugar maples have broken leaders and contorted upper branches, straight boles, some multi-stemmed. Cut cedar stumps common, little coarse woody debris. A horizon depth: 7cm.
Presence of Typha may indicate road or powerline caused water level fluctuations. Tamaracks average 20 cm DBH. Hummocky.
Beaver-influenced meadow. This end is a little higher and has grown up with alders. Toward upland edge is alder swamp. One old tree stump.
Ashes average 30 cm DBH. Extensive mucky pools are still moist even after drought. Sparse graminoid litter.
Charcoal in upper soil. Several large cut pine stumps from decades ago. Pines average 61cm DBH. Litter of needles and leaves.
Extensive area surrounded by mesic hardwoods. Hummocks formed by Carex stricta. One old tree stump. Litter of alder and graminoid.
Aspens average 25 cm DBH. Cedars 25-35cm. Soil is inpenetrably dry. Earthworms present. Pine-dominated forest to north, WFn53 to east, shrub fen to south. A horizon depth: 5cm.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Just above creek, surrounded by fire-dependent upland with significant cedar component. Soil so dry it is impenetrable with soil probe below 20 cm. Ashes average 25cm DBH (max 40), cedars 40cm. Earthworms. No pools even when wet. Ash and graminoid litter. A horizon depth: 5cm.
A couple acres along creek, with adjacent lowland ash and cedar and some upland cedar. Hummocky.
Spruces average 15cm DBH. Tallest 10-15 meters tall. Just above Mississippi River floodplain.
Near where Hwy crosses tributary to White Oak Lake in broad floodplain of Mississippi River. Mix of graminoid and shrub meadows. Litter is graminoid and willow leaves.

Red pines avg 40cm DBH. Birch and oak 20-30cm. Charred stump observed. Most birches have peeled bark for crafts, still look healthy except for one off plot. Oaks may be hybrids of Quercus ellipsoidalis. A horizon: 3cm.
Trees average 10-15 cm DBH. Triangular area a few times larger than releve between highway and APn81a.
Trees average 5-10 cm DBH. Presence of Typha and many dead and partly dead tree stems indicates change in water level, but did not change community type. About 25% canopy cover.
Birches average 20cm DBH. Firs 15cm. A few old rotten stumps. Newer birch logs. Planted red pine (old) nearby. A horizon: 5cm. Hard layer hit is 22cm, may not be bedrock.
Acid black spruce. Basin surrounded by mesic hardwoods. Trees average 15 cm DBH. 75% canopy cover.
Small pools are dry. Young fire-dependent upland forest about 30 meters east. Cedars average 25cm DBH. Firs average 10-15cm. Pools occupy 10-20% of area.

Just barely uphill from cedar swamp (20m north). This stand continues south. Transitional between swamp and upland. Not large, but large enough to stand alone. Spruce 20-25cm, firs 10-15cm, birches 10-15cm. Litter of needles and leaves. A horizon depth: 5cm.

Worms present. Cedars average 30cm DBH. Numerous fir logs on ground. Red pine nearby. Stand is only twice as wide as plot-at north end. To south stand is more open and shrubby. A horizon: 6cm. Soil probe can only penetrate to 20cm.

Heavily wormed. Charred stumps. Cedars average 20cm DBH. Birches 30cm. Spruces 35cm. Several mossy logs. This stand is quite large. Contains some Pinus resinosa. A horizon depth: 9cm. Sparse litter of needles and leaves.

Depression within MHn47. Native plant community FPN62 or FPn63. Spruce averages 20cm DBH, Yellow birch less. Stand is only 2-3 X size of releve, but very distinct from adjacent vegetation. Adjacent part of basin is WFn53 and beyond that WFn64a.

Part of ash swamp has significant yellow birch. Adjacent to MHn35. Stumps present, but don't appear cut. Yellow birch max 45cm DBH. Ash averages 20-25cm. Many wet depressions, but only a few small pools. Earthworms present. Litter of graminoid and deciduous leaves.
Plot typical of very open mixed aspen type. Sandstone boulders cover 20% of surface and are moss covered. Worm activity common. Soils with small rocks.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Plot typical of wet, broken canopy mixed aspen on flat topography abov the Kettle river. This stand disturbed - lots of buckthorn. Soils rocky at surface, somewhat poorly drained silt.

Plot typical of slight rises in wet aspen cover type. This site much less disturbed than S1+S2. Soil deep silts, moderately well drained to somewhat poorly. No stones on surface. Litter of leaves and twigs.

Plot typical of mesic forest on flatter slopes above river gorge. Rich herb layer. Soils silt over saturated gravel, well-drained. Nice forest-grown trees. Water in ground layer 104-142cm. 2.5cm litter of leaves and twigs.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Eastcentral Bedrock)
remarks: Rock ledge/terrace complex with scattered, stunted red pine. Bedrock ledges with this type to Sphagnum/Ledum mats in pools between ledges. No soil sample, sandstone bedrock.

Plot typical of drier knolls in slightly rolling topography. Stand of aspen and birch succeeding to red oak. Soils moderately well-drained silt loam over clay loam (18"). 1/2cm litter of leaves and twigs. Water seeping into pit at eleven inches.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Plot typical of hardwoods on steep rocky slope above Kettle river. Fenceline nearby, possibly grazed. Microrelief is hummocky - cradle knoll.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Old river channel at base of slope, euic system. Typical black ash swamp between upland and alluvial levees.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Eastcentral Bedrock)
remarks: Plot typical of red pine rock ledges above creek gorge. Soils sand over bedrock to exposed bedrock. Litter of red pine needles and oak leaves.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Plot typical of dry mesic hardwoods succeeding to sugar maple and basswood forest. Red oaks to 38cm. Dry cradles in tip-ups. Soils are well-drained silty loam 40" over clay loam. 10cm A horizon.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Plot typical of young aspen/oak stands on thin soils, droughty. Many tip-ups with dry cradles. Soils shallow over sandstone bedrock with loamy sand to sandy loam texture, excessively drained. Litter of leaves and twigs.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Plot typical of second-growth mesic hardwood forest. Tip-up mounds and occasional large rocks on surface. Soils are heavy silt loam, well-drained. Succeeding to sugar maple and green ash. Surface cobbles: 1-2%. Worm activity common.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Eastcentral Bedrock)
remarks: Plot typical of mixed red and white pine on dry, rocky slopes above Kettle river. Site approaching barrens. Sandstone boulders across the surface and moss covered. Double fire scars on older red pine.

Plot typical of wet aspen forest. Several wetland taxa present. Heavy clayey soils, somewhat poorly drained. Lots of birch in stand but not on the plot. Site nearly level with shallow small depressions.

Stand typical of aspen/birch covertype succeeding to mesic hardwoods. Large tip-ups on plot. Soils well-drained silt loam over sand. Large diameter basswood scattered in stand. Topographic context: upper to middle.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Plot typical of drier hardwoods on rocky slope. Only moss cover is on rocks. Site possibly grazed, unusual amount of sprouting on bases of red maple and red oak.

Plot typical of drier ridgetop hardwoods in area of slightly rolling topography (10' relief), with wet forest or sedge bottoms. Soils are well-drained sand loam. Large diameter red oak and bigtooth aspen. ~1cm litter and leaves and twigs. Abundant charcoal in A1 horizon.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Eastcentral Bedrock)
remarks: Plot typical of mixed pine and hardwoods on vary shallow soil over bedrock. Large tip-ups across plot. Charcoal present beneath duff.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Plot typical of wet depressions dominated by aspen. Standing water in tip-up cradles perched over dry till. Loam textured soils, which are poorly drained.

Plot typical of hardwoods on higher knolls above wet swales (10') of relief. Large tip-ups and Vaccinium suggest former cover of pine? Soils well-drained loam over clay loam. Thin litter of leaves and twigs.

Plot typical of red oak (20-30 cm) and aspen on long NE slope. Some rocks on surface. Soils well-drained, loam over gravelly loam. Gravel layer at 72 inches. Lots of tip-up mounds. 1cm litter of leaves and twigs. Topographic context: middle to lower.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Plot typical of comparatively mesic stands of large red oak (30-45cm) with sugar maple nearing canopy. Very shady and open beneath. Soils well-drained sandy loam over clay loam. Large tip-ups, some rocks. ~1cm litter of leaves and twigs over ~1cm organic matter, charcoal in litter. Topographic context: upper to middle.

Plot typical of second-growth aspen/birch/hardwoods succeeding to red maple/oak communities. Soils with perched water table, otherwise well-drained loamy sand over clay loam till. ~1/2cm litter of leaves and twigs. Some charcoal present, many worms.
Plot typical of black ash seep with skunk cabbage. Seeps coming off hill well above the river. Soils saturated muck. Very high quality natural area.

Plot typical of gradual rocky slope with bigtooth aspen cover, successional to mesic hardwoods. Big tip-ups with dry cradles. Soils are well-drained loams, mixed with cobbles and shallow (47") to bedrock. Sparse litter of leaves and twigs.

Plot typical of knolls in rolling topography with scattered red and white pine. Tip-up cradles moist but not standing water. Soils are well-drained silt loam over sandy loam. ~1/2cm litter of leaves and twigs. Heavy worm activity.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Eastcentral Bedrock)
remarks: Plot typical of red pine on rock terraces; numerous large boulders on plot. Soils are sandy loam between rocks, very shallow and excessively drained. Several cut stumps on plot.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Mixed oak forest with some hickory, basswood and green ash in canopy with lush diverse herb layer and understory composed primarily of saplings.
Virtually no disturbance history, though 2 old roads with some cutting alongside. Dense understory of elm and box elder, with lower layers of prickly ash, Prunus and Cornus.
Selectively logged for oak around 1980. Areas of canopy taken over by Populus balsamifera and Prunus serotina.
NA
NA
Old-growth, amazingly brush free. Oak in understory and east end with largest, oldest trees. Saw yellow lady slipper.
Mature, almost completely Quercus rubra, though some Quercus alba (both with seedlings). Diverse herb layer, understory dominated by PS & PV, Corylus, Lonicera, Ulmus, & Ribes.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Dominated by Quercus alba, Quercus rubra, and some walnut. Releve on high, flat area of stand Herb layer very diverse.
Open canopy, brushy and prickly understory. Very diverse herb & tree layer composition. Very disturbed - several large Quercus rubra, the rest a younger understory. Plot oriented diagonally to north.

Selectively cut, especially Quercus rubra - now dominated by Acer saccharium,Fraxinus pennsylvanica, Corylus cornuta, and Acer nigra with nearly closed canopy. Herb layer dominated by Laportea canadensis - sores with thick humus layer and fairly loose.
Interior portion of Willow River Fen. Representative of sedge dominated area in Typha/Carex mosaic. Peat >1m. pH:6.3.
Near edge of water track, approximately 20m from black spruce bog. Abrupt transition from bog to poor fen. pH:5.4; peat >1m. Typical of fen area between bog and Typha dominated fen.
Small fen; evidence of occurrence trees in the past, tamarack sangs (5cm DBH), paper birch stump (6cm DBH). pH:5.9. Poor fen area to north near stunted tamarack.
Releve representative of non-typha dominated portion of vast sedge meadow. Water at surface, brown colored. pH = 6.9.
Typical of Carex lasiocarpa dominated area in mostly wet meadow wetland on north side of Bear Hill. pH = 6.4.
NA
Pool (flark) in water track south of ovoid islands.  pH=6.5, cond.=44umho, Ca=5.9mg/l, Abs.=0.3.
Pool (flark) in water track south of ovoid islands.  pH=6.0, cond.=42umho, Ca=5.8mg/l, Abs.=0.4
Pool (flark) in water track between ovoid islands.  pH=6.2, cond.=67umho, Ca=12.0mg/l, Abs.=0.7
Pool (flark) in water track east of Waskish Road (Hwy. 72).  pH=6.2, cond.=55umho,Ca=10.1mg/l, Abs.=0.3  Upstream of ditch but close; may be impacted?
