Releve along top of dry ridge. Jack pine (17-21 cm DBH, 45-50 years), red oak (12-24 cm DBH). Soil: red brown sand.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Super canopy of large black ash(25-38 cm DBH) being replaced by yellow birch (9-14 cm), elm(10-31 cm) and red maple(7,26 cm). Very wet mucky pools interspersed throughout; peat >1m; pH=6.6. Many large down logs. Scattered white pines in areas.

Undulating alluvium along kettle river. Dominants include basswood (27-56 cm DBH), bur oak (34-45 cm) and black ash (18-45 cm). Many large downed logs, some highly decayed. Soft A horizon. More soil info. Soil: 0-15 cm loam over 15-25 cm sandy loam over 25-50 cm fine hard packed loam.

2 size classes of jack pine (26-32, 13-18 cm DBH), crowns small, but basal area indicates higher dominance. Soil: 5cm black A, some leaching just below; red brown sand with pebbles, some fines at top, decrease with depth.
Patterned fen adjacent to raised bog; 300 m north of county road 8. pH=4.94, Ca=3.61mg/l, Cond=26 umhos, Abs=1.2 nm.
Patterned fen adjacent to raised bog; 30 m south of county road 8. pH=4.60, Ca=3.82 mg/l, Cond=23 umhos, Abs=1.06 nm.
East of hwy 89 and north of Moose River. This is the shrub swamp that is visible from highway 89.
Boreal hardwood-conifer forest. Tiny remnant stand.
Plot long canoe transect through wild rice bed in bend in river and stream coming in from east.
NA
Old field site. Acer negundo and Ulmus pumila more prevalent between county road 2 ditch and 200m into field south.
Prairie restoration site, unit 12, in Myre Big Island State Park.
Old field.

Well-drained slope on hilly portion of sugar hills moraine complex. Moist soil with occasional falling and rotting trees. Occasional stones on surface overgrown with moss. No signs of disturbance. Soil: 0-3cm rich litter of aspen, maple, and sedge leaves; 3-9cm moist black loam; 9-17cm moist, yellow to olive silty loam.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Moist soil with rocks on surface and fallen trees. Fire-scarred stumps. Soil: 0-2 cm rich litter of oak, maple leaves, twigs, and charcoal. 2-6 cm black loam, 6-9 cm black brown loam; 9-20 cm yellow loam.

Conifer swamp in poorly-drained depression. Partly-sunny,very moist carpet of sphagnum moss. Selective cutting of white cedar and occasional trails. Soil: 1-4cm moist, green unhumified sphagnum moss, 4-50cm very moist black humified peat; water table 10cm below surface.

Alder thicket along drainage depression. Partly-sunny, moist hummocks at base of alders alternating with water-filled depressions. Soil: 1-4cm green, unhumified moss from hummock; 4-16 cm wet black, humidified peat with wood. Water table 4 cm below surface hummock.

Open conifer swamp in poorly-drained depression. Sunny moist sphagnum hummocks and wetter depressions occasionally with standing water. Water table 4cm below surface of hummock. Very wet, black, humified peat.
NA
NA
Picea island on floating bog. Kettle depression in moraine. Moist hummocks in very small dense stand. Water table at surface. Sphagnum peat.
Floating bog with occasional picea trees. Kettle depression. Sunny, moist sphagnum hummocks alternating with wetter holllows. Signs of beaver activity. Water table near surface. Sphagnum peat.
Edge of floating bog facing open water. Kettle depression. Sunny, very wet hollows. Common signs of beaver activity. Water table at surface. Sphagnum peat.
Floating bog in kettle depression. Sunny, wet sphagnum mat with occasional hummocks. Water table at surface. Sphagnum peat.

Pioneer hardwoods stand on moderately drained gently rolling portion of Aitken Lacustrine Plain. Shaded, dry-moist soil with fallen trees on ground. Little signs of disturbance. 0-3 cm leaf litter, 3-13 cm black-brown loam, 13-24 cm grey-brown loam, 24-51 cm light grey, silty clay with stones.

Northern hardwood forest on gently rolling portion of Swarta Plain. Shaded, moist soil with occasional fallen trees. Very large white pine (97cm DBH) and sugar maple (76cm DBH) occasionally present. Little sign of disturbance. 0-3cm leaf litter, 3-8cm black moist loam, 8-17cm gray-black moist loam, 17-52cm brown olive silty loam.
Chamaedaphne bog in poorly-drained depression. Sunny, moist sphagnum hummocks and wetter depressions. Water table very close to surface. Sphagnum peat.
Chamaedaphne bog with conifer trees in poorly-drained depression. Sunny, moist, very high sphagnum hummocks and very wet hollows. Water table very close to surface.  Sphagnum peat.
Alder thicket at edge of large conifer swamp in poorly-drained depression. Moist hummocks at base of alders and wet depressions with standing water. Water table at surface. Peat black humified.

Orchid releve in small opening of black spruce swamp. Partly sunny. Clearing may be due to recent cutting. Water 14 cm below hollow surface. 0-7cm moist green-brown, unhumified moss peat; 7-41cm wet, dark brown to black humified peat.

Picea swamp in poorly-drained depression. Densely shaded, moist hummocks and hollows with partial moss cover. Water table 15cm below surface of hollow. Soil: 0-3cm dry-moist, brown moss, 3-5cm moist black humified peat.
Chamaedaphne bog in small, poorly-drained depression. Moist sphagnum hummocks and hollows. Small trail crosses southern portion bog. Water table just below surface. Wet unhumified peat.

Thuja swamp at bottom of northwest facing, poorly-drained slope with surf seepage. Shaded, moist, hummocks at base of trees and fallen logs, wetter hollows. Cedar stumps common. Soil: 0-3cm green, unhumified moss with Thuja leaves, 3-41cm black wet humified peat. Water table 12cm below surface of hummocks.

Fraxinus-Thuja swamp on wet poorly-drained floodplain of Prairie River. Partly sunny, moist hummocks at base of trees and fallen logs, very wet depressions. Signs of Thuja logging. Water table at surface of hollow. Black humified peat.

Fraxinus-Thuja swamp on wet, poorly-drained floodplain of Prairie River. Wet-moist, hummocks at base of trees, depressions with standing water. No signs of cutting. Water table at surface. Soil: 0-3cm moss with sparse Thuja litter; 3-25cm black humified peat.

On wet-moist, poorly-drained floodplain of Prairie River. Moist moss-covered hummocks at base of trees; wetter depressions with standing water. Occasional signs of cutting in stand, not in releve. Soil: 0-4cm green unhumified moss with surface litter, 4-35cm very wet black humified peat.
Edge of floating bog facing small pond in poorly-drained depressions; floating mud around edge of pond. Water level at surface. Sphagnum peat with rootlets of sedge and ericaceous shrubs.

Pioneer hardwoods stand on level, moderately drained portion moraine. Dry-moist soil. Fallen trees common in stand but little signs human disturbance. Soil: 0-3cm leaf litter; 3-7cm dry-moist, dark brown clayey loam; 7-56cm dry-moist, olive to light grey loamy sand with stones.

Red pine stand on well-drained slope in depression. Partly sunny, dry soil; occasional fire-scarred stumps. Soil: 1-2cm needle litter; 2-6cm dry, black to grey sandy loam; 6-31 dry, yellow sand with occasional stones; 31-53 gravel.

Red pine stand at crest of well-drained slope. Sunny, dry soil; fire-scarred stumps and occasional standing dead trees. Soil: 0-3cm needle litter; 3-7cm dry, dark brown to black, loamy sand; 7-56cm yellow brown sand with small stones.

Mixed conifer-hardwood stand on moderately-drained aitkin lacustrine plain. Stand open, possibly disturbed. Dense shade in Abies thickets. Soil: 0-2cm litter, 2-17cm dry-moist loam, 17-51cm dry sandy loam. Orchid releve.

Alder thicket with occasional conifers in poorly-drained depression. Shaded, moist, moss-covered hummocks at base of alders and wetter depressions. Water table 8cm below surface of hummock. Soil: 0-2cm moist, green unhumified moss; 2-21cm very wet, brown to black, humified peat.

Poorly-drained depression. Partly-shaded moist, Sphagnum hummocks and wetter depressions. No signs disturbance except small trail outside plot. Soil: 0-4cm green to light brown, unhumified moss, 4-30cm wet dark brown to black humified peat.

Pioneer hardwood stand on nearly level, moist terrace. Partly shaded, moist soil. Natural opening caused by fallen trees common. Soil: 2-6cm moist black silty loam, 6-11cm dry-moist grey brown silty loam, 11-65cm dry-moist grey silty clay.

Meadow on nearly-level poorly-drained lake shore. Wet-moist Calamagrostis tussocks and wetter depressions. Water table 4cm below surface of tussock. Soil: 0-3cm wet-moist brown dead bases of graminoids, 3-25 cm very wet black partially humified sedge peat.
Nearly level poorly-drained lake shore. Soil: 0-2 cm phragmites shoots; 2-6 cm dark brown, partially humified phragmites peat; 6-39 cm black humified peat.

Carex atheroides meadow on nearly level poorly-drained lake shore. Tussocks and occasional wetter depressions. Soil: 0-3cm litter of sedge shoots; 3-11cm dark brown to black partially partially humified peat; 11-33cm black humified peat with occasional fragments.
Phragmites sedge meadow on poorly-drained lake shore. Soil: 0-3 cm phragmites shoots, 3-30 cm wet-moist to very wet, partially humified herbaceous peat. Aitkin lacustrine plain.

Shaded moist soil. No signs disturbance. 0-2cm leaf litter, 2-14cm moist, black, clayey loam; 14-20cm moist, grey to black clayey loam with stones; 20-78cm dry to moist, light brown, clayey loam with stones. Marcell moraine.
Floating mat in depression. Very wet sedge tussocks and depressions. Water table at surface. Wet, partially humified peat. Nashwauk-warba moraine complex.

Partly sunny, partially moss-covered soil. Trees arranged in rows suggestive of plantation. Moderately drained soil: 0-2cm moist green moss and needle litter; 2-6cm moist black loam; 6-11cm moist light grey sand loam; 11-72cm moist sand.
NA

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: On moderately drained point bar of Mississippi River floodplain. Point bar with meader scrolls of depressions and ridges. Flotsam and other signs periodic flooding. Scattered signs of timber cutting outside plot. Soil: 0-2cm sparse litter; 2-65cm complex no distinct horizons, interbedded yellow-orange sand in light grey silty loam.

Partly sunny, moist sphagnum hummocks and wetter depressions. No signs of disturbance. Soil: 0-4cm green to brown unhumified sphagnum peat; 4-12cm brown, relatively unhumified peat;  12-43cm very wet dark humified peat.

Carex vesicaria meadow in poorly-drained depression on point bar meander scrolls along Prairie River floodplain. Very moist soil; probably flooded during high water. Complex soil profile; sand interbedded in silty clay.

Floodplain forest on moderately-drained point bar with meander scrolls along Prairie River. Nearly level terrace with slight relief produced by alter depressions with slight ridges. Soil: 0-2cm sparse leaf litter; 1-13cm dark brown sandy loam; 13-18cm yellow sandy loam; 18-52cm dark grey silty clay.

Partly sunny, dry-moist, partially moss-covered soil. Stand intersected by power line and unpaved roads. Soil moderately-drained; 0-2cm needle litter; soil: 2-17cm dry-moist black sandy loam; 17-22cm dry moist dark brown loamy sand; 22-72cm light yellow dry-moist loamy sand.

Pathology plot in fragment of northern hardwood forest. Extensive signs of disturbance from humans and burrowing animals. Soil moderately drained; 0-2cm sparse leaf litter; 2-12cm moist black loamy sand; 12-23cm light brown to brown loamy sand with black mottling; 23-74cm light grey-yellow sand.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Floodplain forest on moderately drained point bar with depressions and rises. Flotsam common. Very little signs of disturbance. Soil: 0-2cm sparse leaf litter; 2-15cm moist light brown loam over 12-35cm yellow to light brown clayey loam; 35-50cm light grey yellow fine sand.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Floodplain forest on moderately drained terrace with ridges and depressions. Subject to seasonal flooding, tree scars. Soil profile complex with indistinct horizons. Sparse leaf litter on moist, dark brown to black clayey loam interbedded with light gray to yellow sand.

Alnus thicket in poorly-drained depression in plain. Shaded, moist hummocks at base of alders and wetter hollows with standing water. Water table at surface. very wet dark brown to black humified peat.
Rock outcrop community on well-drained slope. Very shallow, consisting of moss and organic matter; bare rock. Herbaceous cover 5% on rock surfaces and 100% in pockets with deeper soil.

Pioneer hardwoods stand on moderately drained terrace. Partly sunny to densely shaded, moist soil. Natural openings in stand caused by fallen trees. Soil: 0-2cm aspen leaf litter; 2-7cm black loam; 7-10cm dark grey loam; 10-68cm yellow to light grey fine sand with stones.

Control plot on well-drained terrace of Prairie River plain. Partly sunny, dry-moist soil, partially covered with moss. 0-2cm sparse needle litter; 2-4cm black loam; 4-75cm light yellow to gray fine sand with many stones.

Control plot in Scenic State Park, Chamaedaphne bog. Sunny, moist sphagnum hummocks and wetter hollow. Water table 10cm below surface. Moist to wet, relatively unhumified sphagnum peat with rootlets of sedges and ericaceous shrubs.

Pioneer hardwoods on well-drained slope. Dry soil with large rocks and fallen logs on surface. No signs of human disturbance. Soil: 0-3cm leaf litter; 3-12cm black sandy loam; 12-17cm light grey loamy sand with stones; 17-22cm yellow fine sand; 22-62 light grey loamy sand.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Northern hardwoods on moderately-drained slope. Shaded, moist soil with fallen and rotting trees on surface. 0-3cm leaf litter; 3-7cm black loam; 7-10cm dark grey loam; 10-65cm light brown, clayey loam with stones.

Fraxinus-thuja swamp in poorly-drained depression near White Oak Lake. Shaded, moist peat with fallen trees on surface. Occasional signs cedar cutting outside releve. 0-2cm leaf litter; 2-28cm dark to reddish brown humified peat over 28-33cm sandy clay with peat over 33-65cm light grey-yellow silty clay.

npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: Frequent dead and dying elms, very open understory. Relatively young forest, regenerated post-logging (frequent stumps). Small amount coarse woody litter. Populus deltoides 61 cm DBH, Acer saccarinum 48 cm DBH. Grades to emergent marsh to east, highway 61 to west, McCarthy Lake to north.
Litter approx 3 cm thick. Silt loam. Moderate amount coarse woody material on forest floor. On bluff above tributary to Snake Creek. Quercus rubra to 59 cm DBH.
Ridge top. Relatively undisturbed area--some selective cutting. Slope: 5-10% N.

Unusually species rich area in northern hardwood strip along escarpment in park. Very moist from sub-surface flow from black ash swamp upslope. Tilia 35-57cm DBH. Soil 5-7cm of black silty loam over rock or dense red-brown sandy loam.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: On very subtle crest. Red oak 30-50cm DBH, BA=70; Red maple patchy, 15-25cm DBH, BA=35; basswood 10cm DBH; Paper birch dead, 37cm DBH. Soil: 0-50cm red-brown loamy sand; >50cm with pebbles. Unusually sandy for this landform. Water table high.

CSA stand age = 67 years. Red oak 20-33cm DBH, BA=70; aspen 28-42cm DBH, BA=50. Undulating topography with small wetland depressions. Paper birch rapidly dying (10+ snags). 0-40cm silt loam; >40cm dense sandier silt.

Maple-basswood stand on Langby, fine sandy loam, a well-drained soil characterized by northern hardwoods. Stand may have been cleared of underbrush in 1960's for a scenic vista. Several 4ft white pine stumps.

White pine stand on Snellman-Sugarbush. Stand has subcanopy of white pine saps. Fine sandy loam; soil is well-drained and supports northern hardwoods. Located at boundary of Lengby FSL on east side of Lake Itasca.
Old growth red pine stand on Snellman-Sugarbush. Fine sandy loam on east side of Lake Itasca excessively well-drained, very steep slope.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Maple-basswood forest southeast of Bearpaw campground, north of lakeshore and behind mound (human origin?). Lacking forbs and shrubs; much earthworm activity.
Old growth maple/basswood with elm dying out; thick sapling layer of sugar maple and many red elm seedlings; Herb layer sparse but much Bothrychium virg. & Poss. B. mult CWD dom. by Elm.

Mature maple forest with occasional basswoods; very thick seedling and saplings layer up to 3m, mostly sugar maple with ironwood, red elm and occasional basswood. Little to no herb or graminoid layer-moss covered logs, but sparse coarse woody debris.

Closed canopy old growth maple basswood forest-sugar maple and basswood in all size and age classes; large old coarse woody debris; high incidence of rot indicators in both species; dense ironwood and sugar maple seedling layer; several small ash inclusions in stand.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Recently select cut northern hardwood managed stand; some areas of close canopy-other very large gaps, 50m in diameter for each. Dominated by sugar maple, basswood, and yellow birch with occasional ash inclusions; numerous brush piles and cut pie in coarse woody debris(more

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Selectively logged and possibly pastured long ago. Mature maple/basswood with some red oak and bitternut hickory; Ostrya subcanopy and sugar maple dominant seeding layer/ sedge layer dominant to herbaceous.

Dicentra cuc? found by landowner,also Carex careyana, Dryopteris gold on flat area north of plot. (C.C. & T.A.); coarse woody debris large with many advanced D.C. [several misidentified species on original form- M Lee].

Sandy soil; mature Quercus rubra with Betula payrifera and Ostrya virginiana to hazel understory occasional. Tilia americana and Acer rubra with Acer rubra in seedling layer; Hog peanut and Carex pennsylvanica herb and graminoid layer; old roads and old shack-stumps-obviously a used area in the past.

Interrupted canopy due to much gap phase activity; numerous large, old tip up mounds and pits-decay class 5; Numerous snags and large coarse woody debris; continuous sapling layer dominated by 3cm Acer saccharum, Celtis occidentalis, Cornus alternifolia, (more)
Fairly recently logged Red Oak stand with some Quercus rubra canopy trees left and dense sapling layer=2-10m with wide variety of species. Diverse herb layer. 2 Panax quinquifolia off plot.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Managed Maple/Basswood stand with Quercus rubra component. Old White pine and Quercus rubra stumps; Betula papyrifera snags, occasional Populus grandidentata, but mostly Acer saccharum in short young canopy and sapling layer. Deedling, herb, and graminoid layers sparse; coarse woody debris consists of tops, (more)

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Candidate old growth Oak with super canopy or Quercus rubra but largely Maple/Basswood with canopy and subcanopy of Acer saccharum with occasional Tilia americana. Scattered large coarse woody debris; several large gaps with BA. Seedling layer of Acer saccharum and Ostrya virginiana with sparse herb and graminoid layer-beautiful site. Windstorm 7/95.

25% standing in water; most vegetation on logs at bases of trees with exception of grasses; log looking-all age classes in trees and much large coarse woody debris in varying decay states; complex canopy structure.

Fraxinus nigra dominated with Acer saccharum, Ulmus americana, and Tilia americana. Little subcanopy or sapling layer. Head high Laportea; diverse fern, sedge, and spring ephemerals. Some areas with more open canopy where elms have died. Mucky soil with water.

Wet area ranging from mucky to 6" of water, hummocky; Tall canopy of Fraxinus nigra with little subcanopy, but healthy sapling/seedling layers. Patchy shrub layers; patchy areas dominated by herb and sedge.
Mature Ash with Fraxinus nigra and Fraxinus pennsylvanica dominant; Acer rubra and Fraxinus nigra subcanopy. Very diverse herb and graminoid layer; Betula papyrifera snags.

Called old growth, but very small trees. Mixed Fraxinus nigra, Populus and Betula papyrifera with areas with Fir & Cedar, some Quercus macrocarpa (one sow and 2 cubs 20m from me!). Diverse herb and graminoid layer; lots of large coarse woody debris.

Representative of Carex stricta dominated area. Soil wet-mesic silt, loam with much organic matter. No hummocks. Other areas dominated by Carex lacustris and Glyceria striata. Phalaris arundinacea colonies along margins with old fields.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks: Dry-mesic 5 acre old-growth forest. Modal DBH = 40-60cm; max to 86cm common. Soil silt loam over Galena limestone (exposed outcrop in gully). Tree trunks appear to have bell-shaped distribution of sizes. Cored trees: 53cm Quercus alba > 117 years; 37cm Ulmus rubra = 78 years; 67cm Quercus rubra = 93 years; 66cm Quercus rubra = 114 years.

Some old stumps, nice stand continues eastward, grades southward and northward into mixed stand with more aspen/oak. Ranked B because ground layer not diverse for A-rank. Typical of hardwoods west of Bagley Outwash Plaines. Visited in 1995. Maple basswood forest north central section.

On county land just southeast of Sanborn Lake. Some taller Betula papyrifera and Pinus banksiana to northwest of plot. Moat with Carex, Iris versicolor, Calamagrostic canadensis, and Scirpus around fen. Hummocky. Carex oligosperma fruits on 1-2 plants near plot. Soil: wet peat, litter return; 2 samples.

Maple basswood forest in northernmost "hardwood point" on northwest Leech Lake. Cabins on point. Rel on state land west of fork and south of road. Dense canopy of Acer; no Acer or Tilia seedlings but Acer present as D4-5. Broad patches of Laportea. Soil: 7 inches fine light tan loamy sand over 10 inches fine light brown sand.
Fen surrounded by aspen-birch with red pine. Very uniform throughout. Sink ankle deep. Substrate = 5 inches peat over very fine tan sand.

Dense, tall red pine stand with hardwood understory. Occasional decaying logs, some moss covered. 1 moss-covered cut stump in plot. Hummocky from windthrow. Moderate amount of medium and small diameter woody debris. Rank = AB/B. Soil: 1 inch sandy loam over 7 inches grey fine dry sand.

Plot selected as typical of burned meadow. Aluminun posts on northwest and southwest corners. South side of Leech River, approximately 40cm of humified peat over sand. Burned '91, '92, '93. Magnet at plot center.
Small oval depression in moraine, close to large wetland in glacial drainage channel. On peat > 1m deep (well decomposed, nearly black). Plot approximately 5m out from upland margin. No open water.

Firm springy peat>1m deep. Fen begins and upland contact. Plot approximately 3m from upland edge. Peat gray-black, highly decomposed, soupy, some brown, more fibrous. Some areas dominated by Phragmites australis or Typha species, other areas shrubby.
On saturated peat just downslope from calcareous seepage fen to the east and near Gun Club Lake to the west, in the Minnesota River valley. Phragmites has been increasing in recent years.
On saturated muck. Part of large variable emergent marsh downslope from calcareous seepage fen to the east and near Gun Club Lake to the west. Phragmites has been increasing in recent years.
Plot is on edge of Gun Club Lake in the Minnesota River Valley. Soil deep fibrous peat. Hummocks are saturated, with standing water between them. Large patches of Phragmites occur nearby.
Soil saturated muck, 3 cm standing water between hummocks. Grades into emergent marsh at toe of slope. Plot just west of large Phragmites clone and large willow clumps.

Occasional moss covered stumps (45-55mm in diameter) and moss covered logs (some cut ends). Windthrown branches and trees common in plot following recent storms. Deciduous leaf duff. On Guthrie Till Plain Land Type Association. Soil: 2 inches organic over 2 inches gray sand over 6 inches very fine medium tan sand over 10 inches light tan sand with pebbles.
Thin deciduous leaf duff. Small-medium diameter recent blowdown common in plot. Botrychium mormo population present (DNR EO #49). On Aitkin Lake Plain.

At location of CNF Botrychium mormo collection #1001. 6 Botrychium mormo observed in plot (DNR EO #42); not searched. Deciduous leaf duff. Occasional coarse woody debris. Nurse logs with Carex pedunc frequent. CNF Blackduck Dst, Cmp 59, St 46.

Occasional tip-ups and nurse logs growing primarily Carex pensylvanica. Deciduous leaf duff. Botrychium mormo in plot, not searchd. DNR Botrychium mormo EO #41; CNF. Botrychium mormo occsional. #1002/3. CNF Blackduck District, Comp. 49, Stands 4, 7.

Deciduous leaf duff. Occasional tip-ups and nurse logs growing mainly Carex pedunculata. Occasional large diameter coarse woody debris. CNF Botrychium mormo occasional #1009 & DNR EO #37; 1 plant seen in brief search. CNF Blackduck Dis, Cmp 96, Std 35.

Frequent blowdowns. Abundant coarse woody debris. 2 dead elms outside plot. Thin deciduous duff. Black ash swamp near southwest corner of plot. CNF Botrychium mormo occasional #1008, DNR EO #36; 5 plants found in brief search. CNF Blackdck Dist, Comp 97, Std.

Occasional tip-ups and nurse logs growing. Carex pedunculata and Luzula acuminata. Occasional coarse woody debris- primarily Betula papyrifera. Thick deciduous leaf duff. CNF Botrychium mormo occsional. #1014, DNR Botrychium mormo EO #38. CNF Blackduck Dist, Comp 276, Stand 15.

Frequent blowdowns and coarse woody debris.  Occasional moss-covered logs and stumps. Thuja and Fraxinus/Acer rubra/Tilia inclusion in aspen forest with paper birch. Opening south/southeast of plot. CNF Botrychium mormo occasional. #1013, DNR EO #39. Blkdck Dst, Cmp 276, Std 33.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Thick deciduous leaf duff. Occasional tip-ups. Downed mature aspen on plot. Plot slopes 4% northeast and 4% southwest; on crest of gentle knoll. Acer saccharum seedlings/saplings abundant. CNF Botrychium mormo occasional #1007, DNR EO#45. Blackduck Dst, Cmp 179, Stand 11.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Betula alleghaniensis, Abies balsimifera and Betula papyrifera logs in plot. 1 large-diameter well-decayed stump. Several well-decayed nurse logs with Carex pedunculata. Thick deciduous leaf duff. Botrychium mormo EO #32--1 plant relocated. CNF ML Dist, Cmp 125 Std 22.

On gentle east/northeast slope. Occasional rotting paper birch and other logs. Relief from well-covered logs, tip-ups. Dense canopy, very open beneath. Releve in area of Botrychium mormo occasional #29 but none found. CNF DR Dst, Cmp 86, Stand 13.

Bluff prairie on a upper flank of narrow rocky ridge (N-S) north of White River on well-drained, rocky soils just below limestone outcrops. Site is virtually undisturbed. Releve in deeper soils than other parts of the prairie on ridge (where Andropogon is absent).

On deep floating sphagnum mat approximately 30m south and 20m east of Lake. Tamaracks gradually increase in cover with increasing disturbance from lake. Sphagnum drops out in dense tamarack cover. Very wet, very bouncy surface. Tamarack swamp with scatter trees, 8-13cm DBH. Continuous hummocky Sphagnum mat.

Forest on steep slope on sandy-loam soil over gravelly,  bouldery till. Medium sized boulders at surface. Larger trees not seen. Even-aged forest with dominants averaging 35-45 cm DBH. Larger trees not seen.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Plot may be on till island outwash. Tip-up mounds. Soil: loamy sand with hard pan at 24". Well drained. ECS plot#11

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Old growth red maple stand in Ludwig unit. Till over lake sediments? Soil: fine sandy loam over silty clay; hard pan at 12". Well drained.
Small stand in northern hardwood area. Soil: 0-10" very fine sandy loam over sandy loam, hard pan at 12". Well drained. ESC plot #13. Tree tip up mounds.
Slight "outwash" ridge between wetlands. Soil loamy sand (0-34") over sand; 6" spodic horizon; much charcoal. Moderately well-drained. ECS plot #14.
Appears as uniform wiregrass fen. Chamaedaphne not conspicuous, but patches are frequent nearby. Part of large 80-acre shallow fen on southwest side of Fish Lake at CCHNA. Anoka Sand Plain.
Dry, excessively drained thin clayey soil over basalt bedrock. Fire scars on old stumps. 5% exposed rock, 10% exposed rubble soil. Bur oak Savanna.  No deadfall.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Poorly drained, wet organic soil. 3% deadfall. Water table close to surface and visible in depressions. Probably spring-fed; still moist though it's a dry year.
Poorly drained, moist organic soil. Sphagnum ground cover. Topographic context: depression/flat. [Location moved to be in WM polygon.]

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Eastcentral Bedrock)
remarks: Xeric, excessively drained. 90% substrate is exposed sandstone bedrock. Vegetation rooted in deep crevices of much fractured, blocky surface. Lichens and mosses on exposed rock. Trees only in deep crevices. Fire scares on stumps and deadfalls. Water in deep crevices. Organic sandy-loam present in crevice and elsewhere occasionally.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Eastcentral Bedrock)
remarks: Well-drained thin soil over bedrock, dry sandy-loam. Some bedrock exposed. Fire scars on stumps and deadfalls. Deadfalls 10%.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Mesic, well-drained loamy sand on "levee" in floodplain of Kettle River. Rarely floods.

Wet-mesic prairie. Soil 6-8cm dark blackish brown sandy loam over fine sand. Plot is on boundary between soil landscape unit above and a SSPD unit, which is in interbeach area of Agassiz Lacustrine Plain.
Seems like a terrace on slope-aspen above, black ash below. Loamy sand beneath thick organic layers, mesic, 5% dead fall.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Poorly drained, mucky organic soil, moss on deadfalls. Ground very hummocky. Fraxinus nigra seedlings numerous. Canopy very open. Cedars old(?) 7% dead fall.
Poorly drained, wet silt alluvium along St. Croix River 17% deadfall.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Varying from wet to mesic organic alluvial soil, no rocks.
Very poorly drained, wet organic soil, hummocky, somewhat bowl-like depression. No rocks. Water table near surface. 15% deadfall.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Very poorly drained, wet organic soil 2ft deep. Hummocky. Below steep, south facing slope. 7% deadfall.
Wet organic layer over wet sand. Very poorly drained. Sphagnum covered ground. Edge which borders Alder swamp and Aspen forest. 5% deadfall, some charred stumps in vicinity (pine).
Somewhat excessively drained, mesic, sandy-loam. In vicinity density of Acer rubrum, Quercus rubra, and Betula Papyrifera is higher.
Rich fen, low diversity.
Weird mix of "dry" and "wet" prairie species. Seems fairly characteristic of these forby prairies in this area.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Small stand on hilltop. Basswood seedlings common. Canopy fairly open but shrub/ground layers poorly developed. Old charred deadfalls but no charred stumps. Additional notes on field form.
Overgrown savannah (Oak woodland-brushland?). Sandy soil, more open to east, shrubs to west Breeding Bird Point Count loction. Trees small except for a few large Pin Oak.
Bur and pin oaks are small in surrounding area. Brushier to west, Aspen clone in northeast. Soil sand, some bare sand areas. Breeding Bird Point count location.
Sand; good example of a savannah, shrubs thick to South. Ground cover somewhat thin. Breeding Bird Count location.
Sorghastrum down in graminoid layer, low spot to west explains aspen presence. More overgrown to north. Not many big trees, but many shrubs. Prime savannah. Breeding Bird Point count location.

Mesic/moist soil, good duff layer. Snags frequent, less lady fern to north. Mixed-age subcanopy, many young ash. Prickly ash making comeback. Managed with prescribed burns. Breeding Bird Point count location.
Oak woodland(?) Grades to more heavily shaded forest to north. Snags frequent, young trees common, very prominent shrub layer. Breeding Bird Point count location.

Moist/mesic rich soil, snags occasional. Ferns abundant. BBPC location Canopy trees young except for scattered larger Pin oaks Grades into aspen to west, wetland to south, formerly grazed? Ferns abundant. Breeding Bird Point count location.
Very thick shrub layer. Some dead standing birch and deadfalls. Grades into open wetland to west. Breeding Bird Point count location.
Prairie overrun with leafy spurge. Sandy loam soil. Releve on valley-side below 900 foot terrace; south of senic overlook across 169 from Flying Cloud Airport. 0.2 ha plot.

2-5 slopes on silt loam over calcareous till. Not mowed this year; probably last year, not burned. Only scattered patches of good prairie, most is weedy with other good patches to the west. Probably a mostly dry-mesic prairie.

Soil is well to poorly drained on silty clay loam, over 1m of clayey silt. Releve is southwest of minnesota highway 22 over rairoad tracks. Strip is variable in quality, especially near crossing. Roadside mowed. 0.2 ha plot.

8000+ meter squared plot. Dry prairie covering dolomite, silty loam soil. Lightly grazed, but in fine condition. Plot is mostly weedy. EOR for this area is typed at mesic prairie. Note late date: November.

Large 0.2 ha plot. Poorly drained soil on clay loam. Historical lake bed receives drainage from nearby cultivated fields. Moist soil prevents plowing, but area is mowed irregularly. Site has both mesic to wet mesic or wet prairie.
1000 meters square plot. Moderate to poorly drained soil on silty clay loam lake bed. Partially wet-mesic or wet prairie and partially dry mesic or dry prairie. -- FSH
Oversized plot (2 ha) contains a wide range of species and possible community types and therefore may not be useful for classification. Site contains many exotics, very weedy. --FSH

Large, 2 acre, plot with flat topography; dry soil consists mainly of red sand with pebbles to large rocks(till).  Prairie species, especially Andropogon gerardi, are moving into the field from railroad track and replacing Bromus.

2 Acres. Light sandy soil covers a 0-25 slope of dolomite blocks and is exposed occasionally. Glacial till fills in lowlands. Prairie lacks Juniperus virginiana. Hills grazed before 1957. White pine planted.

1 acre plot containing dolomite mounds underlain by nearly pure quartz sand. Sand is exposed by roadcut. Slopes 0-40 degress southeast. Mound #4 has planted pine. 5 was grazed until 1954 and current year.

2 acre plot with thin sandy soil over thin dolomite layer and underlain by St. Peter sandstone. 10-20 degree slope. Area has been grazed in the past, many old Juniperus virginiana. Best prairie begins at roadside and extends back.

10-30 degree south-facing slope on loess over dolomite outcrop. Trees and shrubs are only at edges of prairie.  County is interested in acquiring for a park. In 1994 FSH could not locate this prairie. Note late date, end of Oct.
Mature maple basswood forest, very dense Botrychium mormo population.
Mature maple basswood forest with scattered birch, elm, and balsam fir. Scattered Botryichium mormo.
Mature maple basswood forest with scattered birch, balsam fir, and Botrychium mormo.
Young, recently cut, maple basswood forest. Dense strand of small trees and scattered Botrychium mormo with some dense patches.
Mature maple basswood forest with scattered birch and balsam fir. Scattered Botrychium mormo. 10 deg slope, west aspect; plot 3 meters from base of lower slope.

Old Corduroy Road All Rotted. Typed as T1. Soil horizons: A, Bw1, Bw2, 2C (very gravelly coarse sand). Parent material is suspected to be glaciofluvial (or aeolian mantle?) over outwash.
Center of section 36. West side of Big Sandy Lake; west of MN Hwy 65 at Wayside Park. White pine stumps +.1 and tip-up mounds 1.1.

1 acre plot on a 10-15 degree slope covered with a red sandy till with small pebbles. The dry soil is almost absent because of erosion, probably caused by past grazing. Grasses dominate cover with rich variety.
Across from Conn's cottage on the east side of Pomm de Terre Lake.
Sugar Point. Hardwood stumps, well rotted, +.1.  Tree density low because of selective logging. Across road from releve # 5487 (CS57781).
On Sugar Point in Leech Lake. Low density; well rotted hardwood stumps +.1. Tree density appears low because of selective logging. Bare ground 3.3. L 0-1cm, silt loam. Rapid releve.
Itasca moraine, medium stony sand. E3 Pinus have been planted in east to west furrows, trees 10-12 years old.
Plot 40m east of roadside edge of the woods. Level sand plain. Jack pine, 52 years - 28 DBH. No stumps; gopher mounds +.1. Soil: reddish brown, medium sand, stoneless. 11cm/flcm/Al 2cm/A-Bcm/B17cm+

Releve ~50m north of road; ca. 10m east of fence line in rather homogeneous stand. Hummocks 0.1-0.5m high, hollows saturated, but no standing water. Woody peat. Releve rapid, based on sight identifications.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Dark black-brown loam with gentle topography. Recreation uses include snowmobiles and motorcycles. Vegetation on ridges is therefore, poor. The oak basswood forest has good age distribution. Rich herb layer located along swamp. 2 open water areas. 2 acre plot.

2 acre plot with peat to muck soil type and generally flat topography. Birch swampland has some thickets and is spring fed. Swamps were drained in the past and vegetation reflects. Future development is possible, owners surrounding area wish to sell.
4 acre plot on sandy loam soil on low wet to mesic hills. A good oak stand with an unusual southern stand of aspen. No junk is present. Multi-stemmed oaks indicate possible logging or fire in past.

80 acre plot that is fairly homogeneous in composition. Elm and Populus grandidentata are more prevelent in the east half and more oak, red maple, and aspen in the west half. This gently sloping area is well drained and has been selectively logged in the past.

1 acre plot on dark brown loamy soil with 2" mulch layer. Area has slightly rolling topography. Some of the oaks and many basswood are multi-stemmed. 2 logging roads enter area apparently to remove dead logs.

B. Delany(1996): Releve is typical of forests on St. Croix moraine on south side of lake. Alex: Past logging, fires, and recent grazing resulted in a patchy dry-mesic stands. Compare with releve #0658 (1991). Note late date: November.

1 acre plot with black-brown silty loam soil and 0-10 degree rolling hills. This is an elm basswood stand that appears fairly young with several multi-stemmed trees. Laportea and Elymus dominate understory. No shrub layer.

80 acre plot with part reddish brown sand and part yellow-brown till soil. A previous attempt to drain the bogs had no appreciable effect. Grazing inferred from an absence of intermediate maples and impoverished ground cover.
0.5 ha plot with 2-10 north facing slopes on silty loam soil. Area is being heavily grazed by cattle. Note lack of saplings and seedlings; gaps are being filled in by weeds.
No location info beyond "East Shore of Geneva Lake" maybe in section 17, 20, or 30. Mapped in 30. 0.1 ha plot with 0-2 slope with medium to poorly drained soil.
No site location; is most likely located on wooded pennisula in Albert Lea Lake. 1 ha plot with 0-5 slopes. Note late date: November.
0.2 ha plot with 5-30 degree slopes. Ravine topography is deeply eroded; estiamte 2-3 m cut below pre-settlement level. Banks are steep, cut into loam mollic alluvium. See also DNR releve #5508.
0.2 ha plot with 0-2 deg slopes on alluvial floodplain of Cottonwood River. See also: DNR releve 5507.
0.1 ha plot with 0-20 degree slopes in the north and east facing ravines. Bottoms of ravine have alluvial and silt loam till. Attached to releve is an interpretive program from Camden State Park.
0.3 ha plot with 0-2 deg slopes. This stand is used as a source of firewood for only the heirs of W. Ward. The presence of stumps (+.1) indicate logging activity approximately 10 years ago.
Releve located on 3-5 degree slope east of Mays Lake. Some (+.1) stumps and downed tree tops (est. 15-20 years old) and shallow tip-up mounds (+.1). Deer trails also cross area.

npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: 2 acre plot with silty clay loam soil. Area has floodplain topography with ridges and channels from high water. Some of the trees are very old. Willows are near the water followed by cottonwood and elm. Note late date: November.
1 ha. plot with fine reddish sand. Releve is old field >20 years old. Pocket gopher mounds (1.2).

2 acre plot. Soil is loam on red till parent material. Oak, elm and maple forest may have been logged for sugar maple, since many are multi-stemmed. Disturbances include construction of a road and the potential for a housing development.

Southside of road on slope down to lake 1269.  The woods were cut in approximately 1950, but now have a rich understory. There is no evidence of grazing. Soil is well drained loamy till. Rapid releve.
0.3 ha plot with 0-5 degree slopes on upland interfluve. Quercus alba to 21 inch DBH and Populus to 18 inch DBH.  Moderate logging estimated more than 20 years ago.
Coarse sandy gravel covers the 25-30 degree slope of prominent kame. See releve form for additional communities surrounding the releve. Releve was done rapidly.
0.1 ha plot with 0-5 degree slope on flat Lake George outwash plain. East facing slope to closed depression. Soil is well drained and is very dry.
Medium sand soil on outwash plain.
Unknown plot size. Area appears to be recovering from grazing that occurred over 20 years ago. There are Ulmus stumps (r.1) scattered within plot. White-tailed deer were spotted.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: 0.2 ha plot with 0-5 degree slopes on silty loam soil. Forest is a red oak and white oak mix with a partially open canopy due to past logging. Understory was dominated by impatiens, but they seem patchy perhaps due to past disturbance patters. See releve form for additional outside plants and other information.
Plot size unknown; slope estimated from quad map. Ulmus forest on floodplain of north fork of the Whitewater River. Soil is silty clay loam alluvium. River has cut below bulk of floodplain.

Soil is dark to black silty loam with grey till parent material. 1 acre plot with 0-10 degree slopes. One of the oldest forests in the county. There are few multi-stemmed trees and few signs of disturbance. Appears to be 3 cut trees. Understory has probably not been grazed.
1 acre plot unstable water-logged mat of roots and leaves. Soil is very black and organic (peat). Area is a flat outwash plain. Disturbance includes hunting, grazing, transmission and pipe line.

Plot size unknown. 0-30 north slopes are dissected by ravines. The oak-basswood forest is on the upper terrace of MN Valley. Xanthoxylum, other shrubs, and rusted fence indicate past grazing. Note late date, end of October.
0.2 ha plot with 0-10 north facing slope. Ulmus to 34 inch DBH, Tilia to 16 inch DBH. Luxuriant flowering on Erythronium and Mitella.
Releve located on the west side of paved road on peninsula of Pelican lake. Woodlot. Slope in plot ranges from 5-15 degrees northeast. Rapid releve.
Releve is located on the east side of paved road on peninsula on Pelican Lake. Woodlot. Slope in the plot is 0-5 degrees south southeast. Rapid releve.
Small woodlot approximatley 2 km from the prairie/forest border. Releve is on a level, well-drained hilltop. Roadcut 0.5 km away shows coarse gravelly sand.
Plot is on 0-1 degree moderately drained slope with 0.5cm L/fine sandy loam. Releve has stumps (+) and one large Ulmus americana cut recently. Gaps from selective cutting common elsewhere.
Releve is on 6 degree northeast facing slope with well-drained soil.
Old-growth white pine forest (pine ~26m tall). No recent disturbance. Canopy and sub-canopy include white spruce, paper birch, balsam fir, and quaking aspen. Dates from 1855-56 fire.

Although 1934 map had a dominant oak overstory, it is now primarily maple with a few large oak trees. No regeneration of oak. Selective removal of fire wood and a 1961 logging event to remove dead timber. Past grazing and logging roads also.

Parcel 7(16) has been partially cut irregularly throughout settlement history, but never heavily. Most recent removal of oak was in 1953. Maples are now replacing oak as dominant plants. Logging was attempted in 1961, but DNR would not allow access to land.

Parcel 10(9) was partially cut for many years. The rolling slopes may have been subject to erosion as timber was cleared away. Presently few oaks remain and no regeneration is occurring. Maples poised to rapture dominance.

Parcel 14(9) was clearcut is 1940. Sheep grazing began in 1942 and continued for several years. Now canopy is very open with tangled understory of shrubs, saplings, grasses, and weeds.

Parcel 17(9) was clear cut in 1940 and used for sheep pasture 1938-1944. Presently the canopy is open with an understory of shrubs and saplings and a ground cover of grasses and weeds.

Parcel 22(9) was partially cleared for personal use. Oak was primarily cut, but basswood also. Currently maple & basswood create overstory w/ understoy of maple and Ostrya.
Parcel 18(9) was surrounded by clearcut plots, but it was only selectively cut w/sm patches of clearing. Now canopy is fairly open and some oak regeneration has occurred.

Parcel 22(9) was partially cleared for personal use. Oak was primarily cut, but basswood also. Now maple and basswood create overstory, with an understory of maple and ironwood. Sandstone erosion into creek.

Parcel 23(9) was partially cut until 1954. Most of oak on the parcel has been removed. Maple and basswood are now overstory species with an understory of maple and basswood. Sandstone erosion into creek.

Parcel 24(9) was a partially cut woodlot until acquired by state in 1942. Although lightly cut and never grazed, oak on parcel has steadily declined and no regeneration is occurring. Maple and ironwood are overstory species.

Parcel 7(16) has been recently cut moderately irregularly, but not heavily. Most recent was the oak harvest in 1953. Maple is replacing oack in overstory dominance.
Only the best timber was removed from parcel 33(9), so a few large oaks remain. Maple and ironwood have become the principle regenerators in the parcel since logging ended in 1958.

Parcel 35(9) was selectively cut from the 1860's through 1956 and occasionally until 1977. Currently has a few small oak with many maples reproducing. A Forestry demonstration area was established in 1984.

Parcel32(9) was a good stand until 1938 when timber was cleared and area was used for loading logs. Sheep grazing followed for several years. Now patchy canopy overlooks dense shrub layer with a ground cover of forbs, grasses, and weeds.
Parcel 22(9) was partially cut for personal use. Oak was primarily cut but some basswood also. Now maple and basswood create overstory with an understory of maple and ironwood.

Parcel 46(9) had its north slope and south bluff cleared in 1940, followed by sheep grazing until 1945. These activities greatly changed the vegetation structure. Now the open canopy is supported by a tangle of of shrubs, saplings, weeds and grasses.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Tofte district ranger suggested this stand as the best of maple in area. Portion typed as maple-basswood is an extensive stand. Ground cover sparse, at 50% litter. No yellow birch found.

Obviously disturbed-recently cut stumps and Xanthoxylum. Compare with ice lake stand. The overstory is mainly white pine, paper birch, and basswood. Forb and shrub layer is mix of northern and southern species, but dominated by Amphicarpa bracteata.
Pony grazing in spring. Unplowed prairie with much aspen and several oaks invading from surrounding slopes. No woody species taller than 1 meter.

Area sampled is deciduous with white pine protruding from canopy. Slope is 10-15 degrees north northwest. West of here is a purer area of white pine, which I judged to be planted, but did not examine.
Wet prairie complex at Anna Gronseth Nature Conservancy Preserve. Prairie cordgrass and canada blue joint dominate. Ragweed, thistle, and crabgrass only at the edges. (Species i.d. not reliable.)
Remnant/old field prairie with a wet swale and potholes throughout. Bordered by two roads. Preliminary releve - may not be complete.
Remnant/old field prairie with wet swales and potholes throughout. Agriculture surrounds with roads on two sides. Note: Myriophyllum heterophyllum not in MNTAXA.
Wet prairie of grasses and sedges at Bluestem Prairie Nature Conservancy preserve. Drier areas have more upland tallgrass prairies species.

Bedrock woodland dominated by Quercus ellipsoidalis. Soil 0-8 cm deep. Frequent old cut and burned pine stumps. 35% cover oak leaf litter. Large oak in plot = 19cm DBH, approx 45+ years old. Post-logging community.
