1988 resurvey of a 1979 intern survey. See DNRrel#5686. Gently rolling sand dunes support mostly oak savana on dry sand. 60+ years of grazing ended in 1960 and burning began immediately. Good savanna structure - old, but stunted trees scattered with good grass below. Metal conduit with tag at NW corner. NW corner 51.6m south (162degrees) from Anoka Power Co. utility pole #11667 and 39m from largest bur oak south of small swale on other side of firebreak.
Burned periodically. Note late date: November.

Medium dry site. 48 and 23 year old aspen. Rotting fire scarred aspen stumps. Additional information on field form. Sparse litter of grass and leaves. Soil: 3 inches dark brown loamy clay over 1 inch dark brown clay containing a few pockets or coarse sand over reddish brown clay.

Typical of pure birch stand in large sandy esker (?) deposit. Stand 74 years old (CSA). Scattered red pine and burnt pine stumps. No disturbance noted. Soil: loamy coarse sand, rock, boulders at surface.
Mixed red pine-aspen stand (64 years old-CSA). Some disturbance-cut red pine stumps and very little coarse woody debris, may be from salvage logging. Soil: loamy coarse sand, pebbles, and rock >25cm.
Stand typical of pure big-toothed aspen stand on large sandy esker area. Stand age 73 years (CSA). Soil: loamy coarse tan orange/brown sand. Paper birch is prevalent in surrounding area.

Representative of boreal hardwood-conifer with conifer just below canopy. Much dead and down aspen and fir. Several large old white pine stumps in area. Grading to wetland to northeast. Soil: spodic horizon to 10cm, over red/brown loamy fine sand.
Small remnant of jack pine on sandy plain. No disturbance seen. Soil: soft, loamy fine sand, tan; hit rocks and pebbles >55 cm.

Typical of BHC with white spruce major dominant. Aralia nudicaulis/balsam fir or Aster mac/white spruce dominated areas. Much dead and down. Soil:0-30cm of loamy fine to sandy loam; 30-50 loamy clay; >50cm clayey sand; impenetrable over 60cm.
Represents driest site in the area. Steep southwest slope. Jack pine dying (50% of basal area). Becoming a woodland? Soil: red brown coarse sand.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Red and white pine stand on well-drained sandy soil of Crow Wing Outwash Plain.
Plot includes 15 foot cliff on east side. Moderately well drained. Soil: 8-18 cm of sandy clay loam over bedrock. Dead and down conifers.
Crest of bedrock ridge on Dryweed Island. Canopy variable, very open bedrock to closed canopy jack pine. Soil mostly bedrock (Ely Greenstone) with ~2cm of silty loam in cracks and depressions.
Stand includes entire slope to base. Much dead balsam fir. Succeeding to upland white cedar. Soil: 3-7 cm of silt loam over bedrock.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Northeastern Bedrock)
remarks: Along bedrock ridge on Dryweed Island. Topography broken. Large canopy gaps. Soil: bedrock(Greenstone) with 0-10cm of silt in cracks and depressions. <10% rock outcrop (boulders).
Bedrock ridge with exposed bedrock (schist). Soil: 0-24 cm of silt loam with pebbles. Burned pine stump. Location near former cabin site. Site may have been impacted by human activities in the past.
Located on short slope with wet depression at base and more open ridge at top. Soil: Clayey loam.
Scattered white pine in overstory in area surrounding plot. Forest cover fairly patchy/many openings. Soil: 8-32cm to hard clay pan. 4cm A horizon.

Surrounding area has scattered Salix, Alnus incana, Spireae, white spruce. Area farther north more dominated by Carex, less blue joint, more shrubs. Many herb species colonizing fallen logs. Water at surface but little standing water. 6-8cm of fibric peat over dark clay.

Polygon containing more pure stands of pine (red and white) and areas of more concentrated aspen/birch. Openings in canopy common. Soil: 0-9 cm of sandy loam over bedrock. Beaver disturbance (downed aspen) present.
Some areas of bedrock (with lichens and mosses) present in plots. Jack pine scattered in stand. Populus tremuloides present in scarce amounts. Soil: 0-4cm (some areas 24cm max) over bedrock.

May receive runoff from slope to the southeast. Soil > 10 cm over bedrock. Occasional openings present (fallen aspen). Some patches with less conifers present. Soil: silty loam over coarse sand over heavy clay over bedrock.
Plot transitional between tall dense bog birch toward lake edge and shorter, sparser area more inland. Well decomposed sedge peat >1m. "Shore fen."
Slightly upslope of black ash swamp. ~5cm of silty loam over 5cm dense clay. Some areas are 3-5cm of fibric peat over clay. Peaty hummocks. Wet mesic.
Appears to be impacted by beaver dam; fairly wet, 5cm of standing water in pockets. Slightly hummocky terrain. Soil ~60cm of mucky peat over clay.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Soil: 5-21cm of sandy loam over bedrock. Island on slight slope going toward lake. Occasional bedrock outcrops.
Open bog along highway 212 next to Michigan Peat Operations. Has since been destroyed.  pH = 3.9, Abs. = .775, Spec. cond. = 13.

Flat upland site in fairly level area. Dry site. Very healthy red pine stand with a few white and jack pine mixed in. White pines are dying from white pine blister rust - 4 dead standing on the plot. Very thick needle cover on the ground, 2 inches thick. No sign of a past disturbance. Reproduction is almost non existent - mainly red maple with a couple aspen seedlings. Hazel medium thick. Soil: 3 inches black sandy loam mixed with brown sandy loam over reddish brown loamy sand changing to reddish brown sand and containing numerous small rock fragments at 14 inches. Dry well drained soil, large roots throughout A and B horizons.

Upland site in gently rolling area. Medium dry site. Medium healthy stand of quaking aspen. Aspen leaves devastated by leaf minors. No sign of past disturbance, several small dead standing and down aspen on the plot. Much slash. Thin but consistent grass cover on the ground. Reproduction is mainly aspen with some red maple. Hazel very heavy. Thin litter layer composed of leaves and grass with a few twigs. Soil: 4 inches black loam over 2 inches brown loamy sand over reddish brown fine sandy loam. A few small rock fragments in the B horizon. Many roots in the A horizon and extending into the B. Medium dry soil.

Upland hilltop in a gently rolling area. Medium dry site. Healthy birch stand, containing a few old aspen. A few rocks scattered around the plot. Ground is very uneven as if some holes were dug before the trees started to grow. Reproduction is almost nonexistent because of the heavy shrub cover - aspen, birch and red maple. Near the plot is a low pocket which ponds water during the wet season. Hazel is extremely dense. Thin litter layer of leaves and twigs. Soil: 1 inch black loam over 4 inches grey sandy loam over reddish brown fine sandy loam. No rocks present. Numerous roots in A and upper B horizons.

Mature forest dominated by Betula papyrifera and Populus tremuloides. Some Abies in canopy and subcanopy. Tall shrub layer patchy, dominated by Corylus. Herb layer dominated by Aster mac, Pteridium, and Lycopodium clav. Well-drained site.

Old-growth Pinus strobus and Thuja scatterd in a mix of Betula papyrifera and dense Acer spicatum and Corylus. Herb layer dominated by Aster mac. No cut stumps observed, coarse woody debris present, mostly Abies blowdown. Mesic to dry-mesic site.

Mature forest dominated by Populus tremuloides and Betula papyrifera. Tall shrub layer interrupted, domianted by Acer spicatum. Lower shrub layer dominated by Corylus and Diervilla. Herb layer dominated by Aster mac and Pteridium. Mesic rocky site, bouldery mineral soils.

Mature forest dominate by Populus tremuloides and Betula papyrifera. Interrupted tall shrub layer dominated by Salix humilis. Patchy low shrub layer dominated by Diervilla and Corylus. Herb layer dominated by Aster mac and Pteridium. Well-drained rocky soil.

Mature swamp forest dominated by Fraxinus nigra. Scattered Abies in canopy and subcanopy. Tall shrub layer nearly continuous; dominated by Alnus incana and Acer spicatum. Rich herb layer. Floor with wet depressions, root mounds.

Mature forest dominated by Populus tremuloides. Pinus and Picea prominent in canopy, Abies and Picea in understory. Tall shrub layer patchy. Herb layer nearly continuous. Rocky, well drained. No evidence of past cutting.

Mature forest dominated by Populus tremuloides and a mix of conifers (Pinus and Picea). Tall shrub layer patchy. Shrubs dominated by Corylus. Herb layer dominated by Aster mac. No stumps or fire scars. Rocky shallow well-drained thin soils.

Mature forest domianted by Populus tremuloides. Betula papyrifera and Abies dominate subcanopy. Interrupted shrub layer domianted by Corylus. Continuous herb layer dominated by Aster mac, Lycopodium annotinum and Clintonia. Natural origin stand on more mesic site than most sites in this subsection.

Mature forest dominated by Picea glauca. Abies prominent in subcanopy. Pinus strobus, Pinus resinosa, Thuja and Picea also present. Tall shrub layer domianted by Corylus. Low shrubs domianted by Diervilla. Poorly drained loam. Coarse woody debris abundant.

Maturing Fraxinus nigra swamp. Betula alleg frequent in understory. Tall shrub layer dominated by Acer spic. Herb layer moderately rich with some weedy species. Evidence of past fire. Abundant coarse woody debris. Poorly drained organic soil.

Old-growth forest dominated by Thuja. Located in seep area transitional to to mixed conifer swamp. Tall shrub layer dominated by Acer spicatum and Alnus incana. Ferns common in herb layer. A few old stumps. Coarse woody debris present.
Plot located in pitted topography area south of Red Lake. Most of area on slope with small depressions. Old fire scars and red pine with charcoal on bark. Soils dune sand with dark A1--old prairie.

Plot typical of 2nd growth mesic forest on Ponemah Point. Most trees are coppice growth. Some white pine in stand + scattered large tip-ups. On old wave-cut terrace, medium-coarse sand with round pebbles. Dark surface soil.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Species area plot in moderate quality sugar maple/basswood stand on tamarack lowlands. Soils - surface 34 inches deep over thin layer of cobbles over sand and gravel.

Plot typical of remnant pine stand-small intact groves-some charred stumps. White Pine size varies - 24cm, 57cm, 54cm, 47cm. Red Pine smaller - 43,43,36cm. Soils-surface 10" aeolean/lacustrine/sand and gravel. Very grey E layer and 2 inches.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Plot typical of lowland hardwood forest on elevated (non-flooding) old levees. Soil VFSL, LVFS; alluvium; moderately well drained.
Releve to describe silver maple floodplain forest - Found only on active levees immediately adjacent to Mississippi river. This seasons alluvium obvious.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Plot typical of black ash-basswood forests on low, abandoned levees. Some swales with sedge cover-not included by design, but integral part of system. Soil stratified alluvium, SL, L, SiL, CL, well drained. 52" to chroma.

Plot typical of BF where cedar is mixed with paper birch and aspen. Few tip-ups, some stump(old), some fire scars, charcoal abundant. Stony till surface over SiCL lacustrine(?). Demo plot. Topographic context: upper mid.

Plot typical of old lowland hardwood forest succeeding to Spruce/Fir. Stand originally black ash and american elm-elms now dead and poor reproduction of both on 1st levee, but better to south on interior levees.

Plot typical of lowland hardwood forest, well above river and with little riparian influence. Large old, ice-scarred bur oaks on 1st level are the only old trees. Stand brushy and in poor condition. Worm activity?
Plot typical of low swamp--mixed black ash, cedar, white spruce. Not typical of cedar groves on mineral rises. Woody fragments mostly intact.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Immature stand locally mature in plot, canopy trees 20-35cm DBH. Tip-up mounds frequent. Few snags. Decaying woody debris frequent, small. Stumps infrequent. Thick leaf litter and humus layer, thick root mat. Tan loam with rocks 2 inches down. Small wet depressions frequent under canopy. Occasional boulders.

Patchy, variable stand many openings. Soil reddish clay-rather moist. Many dead Abies and decaying logs-moss covered. Canopy trees 15-25cm DBH. Old natural stumps occasional, very decayed. Along Nemadji River. Topographic context: upper/middle.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Mature stand (80-100 years) canopy trees 25-50cm DBH, mode 30-40cm. Occasional snags, recent wind damage. No stumps, coarse woody debris sparse and small. Well to moderately well drained. Soil 1 1/2" organic layer over 2" gray loam over tan/brown loam with small rocks. Grades to ash swamp.

Maturing stand dominated by 25-40cm DBH trees. Many of Tilia multiple stemmed. Relatively narrow band of Low hardwoods between maple-basswood and black ash swamp. Dense understory. Occasional coarse woody debris, no stumps. Tree bases raised. Moist soil with small rocks. SOil thick (3 inches) root mat black organic layer over moist tan loam with many small rocks, large rocks beneath frequently can't dig below 6 inches.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Immature stand canopy trees 20-45cm DBH, mode 20-30cm. No snags. Gently rolling ground moraine atop slight ridge slopes both north and south. Occasional very old stumps. Sparse coarse woody debris-small. Soil rocky, thick organic mat over tan loam. Tip-ups frequent.

Maturing stand canopy trees 20-45cm DBH, mode 25-40cm. Few snags. Frequent stumps 1/2 decayed. Weedy? Some areas with much Lycopodiums in herb layer. All appears grazed moderately in past. Soil dark brown sandy loam, no A horizon. Few snags. Many trees multi-stemmed. Basal area: 120.

Rich mature stand on esker. Little coarse woody debris. Surface boulders, rich dark organic layer 2" over dark gray silt loam. Few big old pine stumps, tip-up mounds occasional-often shallow. Grades to lowland hardwood. Large 80% decayed pine stump in vicinity. Botrychium mormo in vicinity. Good size class distribution in canopy and decent understory structure. Topographic context: crest/upper.

Mat stand (CSA 120+years) canopy trees 30-55cm DBH, mode 30-40cm. Moderate past grazing pressure(?). Occasional 20-40 year old stumps of oak. Soil dark sandy loam 6" over light tan loam, well drained. Few snags. Tip-up mounds frequent. Sparse coarse woody debris.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Immature stand canopy trees 20-40cm DBH. Scattered old stumps 70% decay. Snags rare, coarse woody debris uncommon.  Well-drained. Soil: 2" organic layer over reddish clay-densely compacted.

Mat stand on gentle upland rise. Grades to cedar swamp and hardwood conifer. Some areas much more shrub-acer spicatum. Small drainage through stand. Occasional 95% decayed stumps. Very open understory. Occasional boulders. Soil: 3 inch moist dark organic root mat over moist brown loam with small rocks. no wet pool sin releve plot.

Mature stand on island of upland surrounded by ash swamp. Snags occasional. Canopy trees 20-55cm DBH, bimodal 20-35cm and 40-50cm. Little coarse woody debris. Frequent large pine stumps, 80% decay. Rolling ground moraine with occasional surface boulders. Soil: 2 inch root mat organic layer over 2-6 inches grey silt loam with rocks over tan loam with rocks. Thick leaf litter.

Mature stand on small, narrow upland island. No snags. Coarse woody debris sparse. Canopy trees 25-55cm DBH, mode 35-40cm. Stumps common-90% decayed(oak and pine?) Topography rolling all aspects, slope varies, level to 10 degrees. Well drained coarse grey loamy sand subsoil, 2 inches organic over coarse gray loamy sand.

Surrounding uplands with prominant fire scars. Scattered tip-ups. Occasional snags. Trees 5-20cm DBH, mode 10-15cm. 40% pools and moss-less area 60% ground moss-covered logs and hummocks, often sphagnum.

Crest of long narrow ridge surrounded by forested wetland. Mature stand canopy trees 30-65cm DBH, mode 45cm. No snags. Small 80% decayed stumps frequent with fire scars. Soil: 1 inch needle duff over powdery coarse gray silty sand. Very well-drained.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Maturing even-aged stand surrounded by recent clear-cuts. Few snags. Frequent oak(?) stumps 80% decayed, fire scars. Tip up mounds common. Canopy trees 20-40cm DBH, mode 25-30cm. Soil compacted, 1.5 inch litter layer over rocky tan loamy silt, well drained. Tree core: 38cm DBH Quercus rubra-69 rings. Recent wind damage occasional. Occasional surface boulders.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Mature stand (120+ years), canopy trees 25-55cm DBH, mode 30-40cm. Few snags. Old stumps (75-95% decayed) frequent, tip-up mounds frequent. Coarse woody debris occasional. Soil with occasional large surface boulders, moderately well drained. Thick organic/leaf layer very rocky. Tree core: 35cm DBH Quercus rubra - 62 rings. Topographic context: upper/crest.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Mature stand though very open canopy. Snags common, no cut stumps. Canopy trees 25-35cm DBH. Soil rocky with frequent bedrock exposure. Much coarse woody debris. Heavy deer browse most of island. Well drained. TIlia in vicinity to 50cm DBH.

Mature pines 40-70cm DBH distributed through plot. Few snags. Well drained. Steep slope of 50' esker. Rocky soil with surface boulders.Thick needle duff. Small stand, localized. Frequent small coarse woody debris, largely Abies and Betula. Thick needle duff, well drained. Topographic context: upper/middle/lower.

Mature stand on approximately 20 acre upland surrounded by bog/swamp. Snags occasional. Flat crest of island center. Canopy trees 25-55cm DBH, mode 35-45cm. Many tip-up mounds. No stumps. Coarse woody debris occasional-all sizes. Soil: 3 inch organic layer over rocky brown loam, surface boulders. Tree core: 51cm DBH Quercus rubra - 93 rings.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Mature stand (>120 years) on 15 acre upland island surrounded by ash swamp. Few snags. Canopy trees 20-45cm DBH, mode 30-35cm. Few very old stumps. Tip-up mounds common. Woody debris sparse and small. Soil thick leaf and organic layer over light brown sandy loam.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Mature stand,canopy trees 25-55cm DBH, mode 30-40cm. Occasional snags. Tip-up mounds frequent. No stumps. Coarse woody debris sparse and small. Soil thick leaf and organic layer over brown sandy loam with few surface boulders. Tree core: 55cm DBH Quercus rubra - 78 rings.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Mature dry-mesic stand (100-120 years), canopy trees 20-45cm DBH, mode 25-35cm. Snags occasional. Stumps occasional, most 95% decayed. Coarse woody debris sparse. Tip ups frequent. Gently rolling moraine, plot located on high area. Soil compacted tannish-gray silt-loam, few surface boulders. Appears moderately grazed in past.

Rolling moraine. Plot encompasses more mesic aspects of this stand. Situated on gradual slope between two hills. Immature to mature stand. Canopy trees 24-45cm DBH, mode 30-35cm. Many twisted boles. Mod past grazing. Woody debris common. Soil a brown loamy sand under 1 1/2 inch organic layer.

Mature forest dominated by Pinus resinosa. No evidence of disturbance. No Pinus resinosa regeneration; few Pinus strobus. Shrub layer interrupted, browsed; dominated by Corylus. Continuous herb layer. Coarse woody debris present. Shallow soils in rocky terrain.

Mostly maturing forest dominated by Picea and Abies with scattered individual and groups of mature Pinus resinosa. Often dense shrub layer dominated by Corylus. Continuous herb layer. No evidence of past disturbance. Little coarse woody debris.

Mature forest dominated by Populus tremuloides and Betula papyrifera. Interrupted tall shrub layer with Corylus and Acer spicatum. Continous herb layer dominated by Aster macrophylla, Aralia nudicaulis and patches of Calamagrostis canadensis. Shallow loamy soil over bedrock, well-drained. Coarse woody debris moderate.

Maturing wetland forest dominated by Fraxinus nigra. Nearly continuous tall shrub layer dominated by Alnus incana. Rich herb layer, dominated by Aster species and Caltha pal. No evidence of past disturbance. Saturated organic soils. Part of complex.

Mature forest domianted by Pinus resinosa with scattered mature Pinus strobus. Advanced regeneration of Pinus strobus. Interrupted tall shrub layer with Alnus, Populus and Betula papyrifera. Low shrubs diverse. Rocky well-drained site. Coarse woody debris common.

Mature forest dominated by Pinus resinosa with scattered Pinus strobus, Picea species and Populus tremuloides. Abies prominent in subcanopy. Interrupted tall shrub layer Herb layer dominated by Aster mac and Pteridium. Well-drained loams in rolling terrain above Stoney River.

Mature coniferous forest dominated by Pinus resinosa with occasional Pinus strobus. Pinus strobus, Picea comprise subcanopy with occasional Betula papyrifera. Pinus strobus regeneration present. Shrub layer dominated by Corylus. Moderate coarse woody debris. Moderately well drained.

Mature forest dominated by Pinus strobus with Pinus resinosa and Pinus banksiana. Abies in understory. Scattered large Populus tremuloides. Interrupted tall shrub layer, dominated by Corylus. Rocky well-drained soil. Coarse woody debris and blister rust evident.

Mature forest dominated by Pinus resinosa with some Pinus strobus and Pinus banksiana. Interrupted tall shrub layer dominated by Corylus. Herb layer domianted by Aralia, Aster mac and Clintonia. Rocky well-drained soils. No sign of past human disturbance.

Mature forest dominated by Pinus resinosa with some Pinus strobus. Abies and Pinus strobus in subcanopy. Tall shrub layer interrupted; domianted by Acer spicatum with Corylus. Moderate amount coarse woody debris. Rocky well drained soil. Coarse woody debris moderate.

Mature forest dominated by Pinus strobus; Pinus resinosa dominates other parts of area. Tall shrub layer patchy, dense. Low shrubs nearly continuous; dominated by Corylus. Advanced regeneration of Pinus species. Coarse woody debris present. Gentle slope, well-drained soils.

Mature forest domianted by Pinus resinosa; Pinus strobus dominant elsewhere in area. Tall shrub layer dense; dominated by Corylus. Low shrubs dominated by Vacciniums. Advanced regeneration of Pinus strobus. Flat, well-drained top of knoll. Coarse woody debris present.

Mature forest dominated by Betula papyrifera. Shrub layer sparse, dominated by Corylus and Diervilla. Scattered Abies in understory. Herb layer dominated by Aster mac and Carex species. Coarse woody debris present. Well-drained rocky mineral soils.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: In Rice County Wilderness Park on steep slope on east side of Cannon River. Soil sand. Coarse woody litter 5-10% cover. Red oak seedlings frequent, but few saplings.

npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: In Rice County Wilderness Park. 1/4 mile west of Cannon River. Lowland Hardwood Forest occupies narrow band between steep slopes and floodplain forest. About 15% coarse woody litter cover. Soil loamy sand.

Bluff in state park above Mississippi River. Occasional old snags. Plot just east of constructed trail, wooden steps. Soil sandy loam. Moderate amount of coarse woody debris. Quercus rubra all sizes present.
Transcribed 7/6/96 by R Dana from K Wendt's original field form. A couple of older specific epithets changed to be in accordance with present. Conducted for benefit of a TV program.
Mature forest on steep, bouldery slope; wet depression 20m below. Most of Warren hill now cut/thinned except this small 10ac stand, (east side; DBH 18-55cm). On hilly Mille Lacs Moraine.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Forest doesn't appear as mesic or diverse as list sug's. Past burned: charcoal abd hot spot with sparse vegetation. A few open-grown oaks 35-50cm DBH; other trees 10-28cm. Water table near surface. Dry lake breeze seems to affect stand.

Fairly distinct 2-acre patch of Carex rostrata near edge of upland island. At upper end of a narrow flowage across 1000-acre poor fen/forested bog. On watershed divide between Aitkin Lake Plain and Kettle River system.
2x50m plot along narrow surface flowage in 1000 acre bog/fen system. Quaking mat, deer trails. Distinct from adjacent, hummocky ericaceous-Eriophorum spissum mat.

Uncertain native community types for remaining pine woodlands on this outwash. Abundant Carex pennsylvanica and Oryzopsis suggests past grazed; was past cut. Frequent dying jack pine; red pines 30-35cm. Few adult or sapling oak.

Small (10ac?) area of mature oak forest; grades into lowland hardwood. Down logs, snags, wet pools to one side (now dryish), some rocks. Trees 35-45cm DBH. West of parking lot just north of gravel pit on esker.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Typical past disturbed oak fores on dry southwest slope on esker. Plot is 20m from wetland. Species are patchy, especially forbs and shrubs. Old dead Betula papyrifera; 45cm DBH Populus grandidentata snag. Trees 25-35cm. Has recovery potential.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Lowland forest on black organic soil, some rocks, lowspots moist/firm. Large spreading bur oak at 36cm DBH; oak/ash usually more slender/straight. Plot on stream bottom land next to upland margin.

Mature mesic forest on north facing slope. Tall Acer subcanopy; open below Sparse, well-spaced herbs and low woodies over continuous leaf litter. Other areas more shrubby but same moderate-low diverse herbs. Along esker system. Rocks and gravel, especially in small gully. Some coarse woody debris

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: A few 2-5 acre areas of northern hardwoods on knolls or bordering areas of lowland hardwoods. Occasional cut stumps, canopy only partly mature. Plot on low edge of knoll; partial canopy gap. Carex pensylvanica is less dense here.

Plot in upper relatively level portion of 15-20% N facing slope. Many large maples in tract and many ephemeral pools in low areas (none in releve) ~5% cover of coarse woody debris. Stump and fence present in tract although not in releve.

Plot in very mesic, low level area. Many large elm, black ash, and Tilia trees in vicinity of plot. Soil with good organic mater accumulation. 10" A horizon and definite B+ at 10-18". Stumps present, although not in releve. Fenece present in tract.

Tall healthy aspen (46 years) with understory of sugar/mountain maple, and birch. Site appears moist. Surrounding area rolling. Old large burned stump. Soil 10cm loam cap over 20cm loam with reddish mottles over reddish clay.
Soil: muck over loam, 67cm to water table, sp.. cond. =359, pH =6.2. Ecological group 1. Wetland split by road.
Dry mesic. Burned regularly. Gopher and ant mounds. 99% cover of other dead organic matter.

Original canopy removed - bur oak? Canopy now consists of middle aged pin oak sprouts, which fire is killing. Ground layer is free of weeds, but brushy, low forb diversity. Improper management, burned regularly.
Old fire scars on bur oaks. 96% cover of other dead organic matter, 3% decaying wood, 1% mineral soil.
Missing entities from oak savanna, some blowout disturbance; burned fall 1987. A few ant and gopher mounds. 95% cover of mineral soil, 5% cover of other dead organic matter.

Part of 40 acre patch of woodland. Many younger bur oak present, some in canopy. Good condition/quality, but canopy dominance is wrong. Patches of disturbed ground present. Burned frequently in the past 25 years.

Ground layer is disturbed in large patches. Fire unit #11: burned only 3 times in 24 years. Low shrub layer is dense in large patches. Lower and middle slope of small hill. Ground layer diversity seems typical for type. 98% cover of other dead organic matter, 1% cover decaying wood, 1% cover of decaying wood.

Dry mesic. Burned. 3 dead pin oaks in plot-2. Others appear to be near dead. Many trees around plot also appear to be dying. Small ant mounds. 98% cover of other dead organic matter, 1% cover decaying wood, 1% cover of decaying wood.

44 year old stand in uneven site on top of small rise. No disturbance. Many large rocks on surface. Location uncertain- near hospital. Soil: 4" loamy sand over gravelly sand. Thin litter of leaves and twigs.

Medium moist site on a dry soil. A few small pine and aspen stumps. No disturbance. Soil: 2 inch litter layer of needles and moss, 3 inches black loam with much organic matter over grey fine sand over reddish brown fine sand. Dry soil but moist site. Many roots distributed in A and upper B horizons.

1-acre releve in mature oak forest on rolling terrain. Quercus ellipsoidalis to 22 inch diameter; Quercus macrocarpa and Quercus alba to 16"; Betula to 13". Diverse herb layer with some northern species. On Edith sand. No recent disturbance.

Canopy of large (15"-47" max diameter) Celtis, Ulmus, Tilia, Populus, etc. Divrse herb layer with spring ephemerals. Spotty cutting. Elms dying. Some exotics. Silt loam to sandy alluvium. Scour and fill channel.
0.5 ha releve in ravine in oak forest on north side of high ridge. Total area of woods = ca 10 acres on Superior lobe. Sand and medium gravel.
Releve generalized or entire 8 acre tract. Somewhat variable in quality, but all second growth.
5 acre releve. Site with <5 degree slope; aspect unknown. Some cutting. Ground disturbed.
Releve generalized for entire 7-acre patch of woods. Acer saccharum to 22.5 " DBH, Tilia to 19.5", Quercus rubra to 27", Ulmus to 50" (at marsh margin). Site with <5 degree slope. Cutting.

Releve generalized for 15-acre stand. Quercus rubra to 33.5" DBH, Acer saccharum to 20.5", Tilia to 29.5", Ulmus americana to 29.5", Quercus alba to 21.5". Some cutting. Paths. Site with <5 degree slope.
Releve generalized for 9 acre stand. Acer saccharum to 24" DBH, Quercus rubra to 27", Tilia to 31", Ulmus rubra to 19". Site with <5 degree slope. Stumps, wood pile.
0.1 ha releve. Salix nigra to 19" diameter. Appears typical of depauperate floodplain forest along lower Minnesota River.

5-acre releve in "virgin" oak-maple forest on rolling Des Moines Lobe till. Max diameter canopy trees = 25"-37". Lacks sapling class--probably grazed until < 15 years ago. Fire-scarred Ostrya, Quercus and Acer.
Cut stumps (cf. Pinus strobus) present, to 40cm DBH. Soil: O horizon <1cm over loamy medium sand.
Small area of savanna (1 acre) at edge of bur oak forest on gravelly river terrace. Becoming overrun by sumac (75% cover). Probably grazed. Sandy soil.
Survey not reliable and should not be used in analysis. See DNR #6996 for more accurate survey of the same plot.
Survey not considered reliable. See DNR #6995 for more accurate survey of the same plot.
Survey not considered reliable. See DNR #6999 for more accurate survey of the same plot.

Seepy head of draw below old cabin. Plot includes seep and extends a bit up sides of draw. Northeast side of draw previously grazed? West side appears undisturbed. Some open mud (fine sandy) in active seep area.

Releve on small wooded knoll rising 2 meters above surrounding swamp. Woods appear young and disturbed: canopy dominated by Ostrya and ground layer by Carex cf. pensylvanica. Mineral soil, 0-2cm litter. Prob anomalous.
Generalized 15-acre releve on disturbed (heavily grazed in past) prairie. Dominated by Poa pratensis with Agropyron repens and Solidago canadensis on course loamy sand. Strongly rolling 0-30 slope.

Ca. 0.1ha releve on floating peat mat in small basin. Described as raised bog. Sphagnum present (25-50% cover), but appears to be minerotrophic. 3-4m wide moat. Surrounded by hardwoods. Note late date, end of Oct.

Ca. 0.5ha releve in Carex lacustris/Typha latifolia marsh. Dense stands of Phragmites in deepest portions; Calamagrostis co-dominant with Carex in shallow water. Lythrum salicaria abundant in west end. Edges of marsh disturbed by residences.
0.5 ha releve in dry prairie on 0-20 degree slopes on rolling gravel moraine with high lime content.
1 ha releve on 0-10 degree slopes on north-south trending ridge of silty clay loam over till.
0.05 ha releve in dry prairie on crest of gravel ridge. 0-15 degree slopes. On Dovre moraine with high limestone content.
0.5 ha releve on dry-mesic prairie on north east flank of drainage way through rolling kame and till moraine. Loam and loamy course sand. cf. Barnes soil type. Prairie mowed.
0.3 ha releve on 0-10 degree slopes on ridgetop of strongly rolling moraine. Silt loam over gravel. Cow pies abundant from previous year but not this year. Boulder pines from adjacent fields.
0.2 ha releve on 5 degree south facing slope.
> 1ha releve in heavily grazed prairie on strongly rolling moraine. Stoney of Barnes soil. Poa pratensis dominant (cover = 5).
0.1ha releve on 0-10 degree slopes on rolling upland. Most of prairie accidentally burned in fall 1969. Part of prairie mowed in late summer 1970. Several diverse wetland potholes within prairie.
1 ha releve on level to gentle slopes on moraine. Most of prairie accidentally burned in fall 1969. Part of prairie mowed in late summer 1970. Several divers wetland potholes within prairie.

1 ha releve on 0-10 degree slopes on rolling moraine. Probably not grazed within 10 years (not felled off from adjacent cultivated fields. Mowed irregularly. Litter thick. Areas near cult field and road weedy.
1 ha releve on 6-10 degree north facing slope. Loam over buff till (cf. Barnes).

Approximately 2ha releve on rolling 5-15 degree slopes. Stony loam over till. Not especially weedy, but has low diversity, especially of forbs, treated with herbicide? Mowed last year, but litter moderate.
0.5 ha releve on 3-5 degree west facing slope. Tractor tracks all over--used as access to field above slope and as turning lane during cultivation. Area below slope highly disturbed.
Approximately 0.5ha releve on 0-15 degree slopes (all aspects). Stony silt loam till. Moderately grazed in past, mowed trails. Planted with green ash seedlings.
0.1 ha releve on 30-40 degree south facing slope on silt loam till.
0.5 ha releve. 0-5 degree slopes. Well drained, on loamy sand. Area was burned recently (probably spring 1971). Grasses are dark green with vigorous growth. Note abundance of Poa, and cf. Amorpha.
Approximately 1ha releve on 0-20 degree north west facing ravine slope. Mowed, but apparently not grazed. High forb diversity. Silt loam over till.
Ca. 0.5ha releve on 0-5 degree slope. Mowed; no evidence of grazing. Abundant Poa (cover=3). Described by EJC as weedy (notes 31 August 1977). Site reported destroyed by N. Sather in 2008.

Ca. 0.5 ha releve on 0-2% slope adjacent to lowland along stream. Mowed: no evidence of grazing. Abundant Phleum pratense (cover =4). Described by EJC as weedy (notes, 31 Aug 1977. Site destroyed (NPS 2008).
0.2ha releve in strip of prairie between marsh and wheat field. 0-2 degree slope on silty loam mollisol. Described by EJC as in good condition. Some portions of area mowed, plowed, or ditched.
0.5 acre releve in ca. 2 acre prairie bisected by road. Used as pasture but not recently, prior to 1971. Burned every spring to prevent encroachment by trees and shrubs. Black peaty (or clayey) loam.
1ha releve in disturbed wet-mesic prairie. Solid Andropogon gerardi. Low diversity. Heavy Melilotus and Fragaria invasion. Willow species uneven. Several cattail marsh inclusions.
1/2 acre releve in ca 25 acre willow swamp at south end of Big Swan Lake. Areas above water table hummocky. Bisected by transmission line.
Knoll 0-5 degree slopes, location estimated.
0.4 ha releve on 3-6 degree north and south-facing slopes.
1 acre releve in oak forest on south facing 30-45 degree slope. On calcareous gray till. Either community is de-pauperate or list is incomplete. Note late date, end of October.
1 acre releve in mesic oak forest on north facing 30-45 degree ravine slope on calcareous gray till. Species list is incomplete. Note late date, end of October.
1 acre releve apparently in oak grove within savanna landscape (No prairie species in releve, but prairie openings are present at site). Nearly level topography. Light brown to gray sandy soil.
Ca 0.5 ha releve on 0-10 degree slopes. Regularly mowed. Adjacent to wet prairie on level alluvial terrace. (Releve seems to include wet and mesic elements).
Ca 10 acre releve on north and east facing 0-10 degree slopes. On stony gray till. Regularly mowed. Adjacent to wet prairie on level alluvial terrace.
ca 60 acre releve on level alluvial terrace, poorly drained. Regularly mowed. (Releve seems de-pauperate.)
Ca. 2 ha releve on poorly drained alluvial terrace. Regularly mowed. Releve incomplete because of falling darkness. (Appears to be poor-quality prairie).
1 ha releve on bluff over drainage channel. Gravel substrate.
>1 ha releve on 0-10 degree slopes on rolling gravelly, stoney moraine. Not hayed or grazed in >20 years. Has been burned. (Releve seems to include mesic prairie as well.)
1 ha releve in lush wet prairie on level site. Soil is hummucky with holes or troughs about 1 foot deep. Area surrounded by sheep fence. Hummocky surface caused by grazing?

1 ha releve on level site. Panicum present mostly between areas with Schizachyrium scoparium and areas with Spartina. Mowed every year after Labor day for 40+ years. (species and soil map indicate probably wet saline prairie).
1 ha releve on level site. Burned within past few years. Fences indicates past grazing, but almost no weeds. Appears depauperate. Possibly wet saline prairie. Questionable for analysis.
Releve of unknown size on level site. Thick litter accumulation. Weedy. (Appears to be wet-mesic, but is heterogeneous. Questionable for analysis.)
1 ha releve on driest portions of low level site with wet prairie and cattail marsh inclusions. Thick litter. Vegetation tall. (Releve appears heterogeneous. Questionable for analysis.)
2 ha releve on level site. Mowed last year-hay piles still in field. Owner reportedly mows every year in late summer. Everything short and very weedy with Poa and Melilotus. (Appears wet-mesic.)
10 acre releve on nearly level site with some wet depressions.

0.5 ha releve on slight south to north slope. Unusually tall growth of all plants and unusually large proportion of forbs. Some low (seepage?) areas with many weedy species (Releve appears heterogeneous).
0.2 ha releve on level site. Prairie has weedy patches especially along road used as access to wheat field to north. Adjacent to cattail marsh.
Releve of unknown size in level low-lying prairie. Appears to include both wet and wet-mesic prairie. Questionable for analysis.
Releve of unknown size in 2 acre prairie. 0-20 degree slopes on knoll sloping in all directions. Releve appears to include dry prairie. On stony, silty clay loam over gray till. Litter from 0-5cm.

1979 survey of The Nature Conservancy property. Original form indicates plot was visited 15June, 30July, and 14Sept in 1979(?). In permanent plot marked with with 1m tall conduit in each corner. Metal tag (HA-1) attached to conduit in NW corner & metal tag (#617) attached to conduit in NE corner. Not considered reliable and should not be used in analysis. See DNR #6987 for a resurvey of the same plot.
Survey not considered reliable and should not be used in analysis. See DNR #6988 for more accurate survey of the same plot.

1979 survey of The Nature Conservancy property, not considered reliable and should not be used for analysis. See DNR Releve #6991 for resurvey of same plot. Height classes in this releve do not appear accurate.

There was evidence that the bare sand is shifting as some plants were found half buried in sand. Survey not considered reliable and shouldn't be used in analysis. See DNR #6954 for accurate survey of the same plot.
Survey not considered reliable and shouldn't be used in analysis. See DNR releve #6955 for accurate survey of the same plot.

Survey is not considered reliable and should not be used in analysis. Survey was also conducted on 4 July 1979.

Survey not considered reliable. Releve was also done on 22 August 1979. See DNR #6976 for a more accurate survey of the same plot.

Survey not considered reliable & should not be used in analysis. Survey also done on 22 August 1979. See DNR #6975 for reliable survey of same plot.
Near lakeshore; old beaver activity; young Thuja grazed by deer; some parts of polygon disturbed (human?) and more open; Soil: 2cm A horizon, 3-4 of strong E horizon, hardpan at 15cm
Pin oak polygon nearby. Lake on one side. Exposed bedrock in a few places. Bedrock 0-5 cm in most places.
Hummock/hollow complex no standing water in hollows (dry year). Soil: saturated peat.
No bur oak present. Exposed bedrock and loose boulders. 3 cm average soil depth. Deepest soil 10cm in one location. Schist.
Adjacent to shallow marsh and lake shore. Many burned stumps. deep saturated peat; hummock hollow well developed.
1-2cm soil over bedrock, soil to 10 cm in some places. Some dead standing white pine. Many white pine seedlings. Schist.
Water 10-15cm below surface, part of large peatland. Lake Aggasiz lake bottom.
Soil thin, very rocky, exposed bedrock and boulders. Abundant pine needle litter. Some fire scarred trees; granitic felsic surficial geology. Rocky southwest facing slope (boulders and outcrop).
Part of pattern (incipient string) in large peatland; fairly wet, some standing water; upwelling of water; surrounded by black spruce bog; hummock/hollows present.
Soil depth 1-2cm; area previously burned, polygon (but not plot) has dead standing burned trees. Upland brush type. rocky, granitic surficial geology. Rocky, no trees in plot.
Deep peat on edge of large peatland adjacent to upland, grades out into black spruce woodland type.
Soil grey, granitic surficial geology.

Soil depth 5-8 cm; a lot of coarse woody debris; areas of bedrock outcrop; some large white pine and trembling aspen in area; almost all fir dead from budworm(?); many rocks throughout plot, schist. 5cm A horizon, 13cm B; dusty red fine sandy loam. Average soil depth is 5-8cm.
South end of plot is crest of hill. Survey taken towards north on slope. Granitic-felsic surficial geology, most areas appear schist.
soil: 6cm dark A horizon over dense hardpan of coarse sand and clay. (some areas within polygon A is deeper over deep clay; mineral soil, no hummock-hollows; dead Ulmus americana in plot.
much blowdown; dead standing fir and dead and dying black spruce, schist surficial geology.
Average water depth: 1m deep. Wild rice cover more sparse than usual; small clumps of Scirpus cf validus and clumps of Typha in polygon. Area permanently flooded.
Old beaver meadow? East end has dead standing timber (from flooding?). Soil grey.
Floating mat in bay; water 1m deep below mat; parts of polygon without much sedge component (almost all typha) muck over clay. Area permanently flooded.
Pines patchy throughout polygon; other areas have more balsam/aspen/birch. Granitic-felsic surficial geology.

Soil 5-8cm deep; very rocky; a lot of red maple seedlings; most fir dead (budworm?); some coarse woody debris (fir mostly); polygon surrounded by aspen birch forest; areas with less fir and more aspen. Many glacial erratics, very rocky; granite on schist. Many red maple seedlings.

In between BSF and BSL; dry end of BSL; 60% Sphagnum, 40% Pleurozium (top of hummocks); mapped as BSF; confined basin; BSL without labrador tea. Soil about 8cm fibric peat over deep (>1m) of sapric peat.
Area permanently flooded.
Standing water .5-1m deep; adjacent to bay (open water) and leather-leaf shore fen. Some hummocks with Scirpus and Calamagrostis canadensis. Area permanently flooded.
Woodland phys; 50% Picea, 50% Larix; deep peat; well developed hummock and hollows; bordered by leatherleaf bog and black spruce alder swamp.
Patchy distribution; complex: some areas with Scirpus validus (50% Scirpus 50 % Typha). Area permanently flooded.
Fairly open canopy for this type; some cedar trees partly uprooted, leaning; well developed hummocks and hollows.
Deep organic matter. Beaver activity. Seasonally/temporarily flooded site.
Type somewhere between shore fen and dogwood willow swamp on shore of Tom Cod Bay.
Ash mainly in lower portion of polygon, upper portion is mixed ash and cedar (60:40). Seasonally flooded site. Downhill of Aspen.

Plot and polygon very variable: part typical of type and part like a black spruce bog with Sphagnum, Carex trisperma etc. Parts are fairly open with more white pine in overstory and fir in understory (saplings). Soil to south; feather moss, 2-10cm fairly saturated rocky loam soil. Soil to north; 10cm fibric peat over clay and hardpan of coarse sand and clay.
Plot between deep marsh and beaver impoundment and Fraxinus nigra swamp standing dead Thuja occidentalis surrounding plot. Dry season, evidence of water having been higher.

Fairly rocky; soil a classic spodosol 5cm A horizon and up to 20cm leached E horizon mixed with B horizon. Soil shallow (8cm) in some spots. Very little moss cover for type. A lot of coarse woody debris.
Soil depth 3-15 cm (3cm A over 3cm E horizon), B horizon fine sandy loam. Mapped as pin oak but predominately Ostrya virginiana and Acer rubrum. Schist with granitic-felsic inclusion.
Not a complex. Jack pine, aspen and birch mixed in this stand. Spruce may include black spruce (difficult to id tall trees). Small organic layer, 6cm E horizon, 6+cm B horizon, soil to 20cm deep.
Soil 3cm over bedrock; flat in plot but polygon rolling topography near Cruiser Lake very dry season.
West end of large beaver meadow, grades into sedge meadow hummocks/hollows present (low) deep peat.
Exposed bedrock present, near top of crest of hill. Schist. Soil: reddish silty-sand.
Old beaver meadow. Some area dominated by Carex rostrata. Sphagnum throughout. Floating mat in places. Small patches of leatherleaf throughout polygon, gets more minerotrophic by areas of open water.
Semi-floating mat, 5cm thick. Site saturated.
Aspen fairly large for type. Ridge top, open bedrock in places, lower areas with Corylus and aspen. Soil depth ranges 0cm-12cm.
Mosiac of leather leaf and sedges (Eriophorum and Carex limosa). Patchy distribution of leather leaf.
Much open bedrock and loose rock, some coarse woody debris (downed jack pine). Soil 4cm over bedrock; 12cm at deepest.
Cut-over stumps of white pine, previous burn (very old). Soil is 2cm over bedrock, some places with 5cm soil. Steep hillside.

Small polygon between upland; some standing dead birch; hummock hollow topography with sphagnum; soil 8cm sapric peat over coarse sand--ground water discharge area (?) and/or receiving water from upland.
Active beaver lodge in center of polygon. Cover estimates made from shore over entire polygon interior lake. Area permanently flooded.
Near crest of hill some small boulders (granitic-felsic).
Small low area (bowl) surrounded by upland parts of polygon with leatherleaf deep sedge peat.
Bulrush marsh surrounded by Phragmites and pond weed polygons. Area permanently flooded.
Part of large patterned peatland deep peat some minerotrophic species, plus Carex lasiocarpa and Betula pumila.
Surrounded by bulrush marsh.
Some standing water deep sedge peat; water track of large peatland most trees under 5cm DBH, some dead.
2-4cm soil over bedrock some bedrock exposed few small openings in dense shrub; granitic felsic gneiss.
Most willows 2-5 m tall polygon in low area connected to Daley Bay. Soil: saturated muck.
Soil only in crevices, 1cm thick with fibrous organic matter. Exposed bedrock covered with lichens and mosses. Granitic-felsic surficial geology.
Parts of stand with more aspen. Drought may have killed many forbs. Soils 6 cm over bedrock; a lot of open bedrock.
Previously cut over (very old). Soil probably saturated under normal conditions (very dry year). Soil in low spots slightly moist.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Northeastern Bedrock)
remarks: Mostly bare rock, some spots with soil 5cm (15cm in cracks) Low area in southeast corner of releve with deep (>50cm) silty clay and muck, these pockets common in polygon. Some areas of polygon with jack pine more prevalent.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: 8cm sandy loam over a hardpan. 1 Betula papyrifera snag. Seasonally flooded.
Soil 7cm (at most) over bedrock; polygon a mix of dense oak (70% cover) and sparse rock ridges, releve includes both; lichens and mosses found mostly on rock ridges.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Rock outcrops. Granitic surficial geology. Upper 1/3 10% slope; lower 2/3 3-4% slope.
Estimated from shore inland (not on big lake) north end of Wolf Pond.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Some exposed bedrock and boulders. Granitic-felsic. Previously burned (white pine stumps).
Polygon is BSF on bedrock, some areas of open bedrock like pine woodland; part of plot open bedrock; evidence of fire in soil(charcoal pieces); soils at most 7cm deep.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Northeastern Bedrock)
remarks: Exposed bedrock 5% of plot. Granitic felsic. Thin red/yellow soil.
Water 1.1m deep; mapped as wild rice marsh; scattered clumps of Typha angustifolia outside plot; ring of Typha towards land; about 15% open water; isolated bay. Permanently flooded.
Tall shrub layer competing for light-almost as tall as Fraxinus nigra understory. Dense brush layer. Granitic-felsic gneiss. Soil yellow tan silty sand.
White pine throughout polygon; some area with less Carex rostrata and more Carex are oligisperma; bordered by deep marsh and leather leaf bog; deep peat.
Water 1.2m deep; bulrush occurs in patches about 20X20m. Permanently flooded.
Hillside, some exposed bedrock. Granitic-felsic surficial geology. Soil is light color fine textured sandy loam.

7cm silty loam over deep clay; old beaver meadow; some hummock/hollow development; thick thatch layer may explain lack of species diversity; down stream end of beaver meadow. Seasonally flooded. Topographic context: depression/flat.
2-3cm soil over bedrock some bedrock. Exposed granitic-felsic gneiss. Plot on hillside.
Granite bedrock; soil only present under clumps of jack pine, up to 20cm silty loam; Corydalis and Aralia hispida in area; stand includes some wet, bog-like areas.
Top of steep hill. Surficial geology of granite-felsic and schist.
Some coarse woody debris; parts of stand with continuous feather moss cover; clumps of fir common (fir subtype); soil: 10-18cm deep over rock.
Soil gleyed blue colored clay. Semi-permanently flooded area.

Water depth 1.6m, more dense cover than many wild rice marshes. [Note] UTM on form places plot in 67N 17W SESE03, which Norm says is more likely than SWNE07. Note: current lat is 48 18 38, which is 10' deep water on topography.
Rooted mat, soil gray color.

Soil 21cm peat over clay; hummock/hollows well developed; parts of polygon more open with Fraxinus nigra and Alnus incana coming up; fairly young stand (?) - trees relatively small DBH. Area saturated.
Rooted cattail mat, 75cm water depth.
Water depth 30cm (standing water); deep sedge peat; fairly species rich for type; thatch layer thick; more species rich as approaches lake edge (Typha) mat becomes more floating, thinner.
High hummocks of Sphagnum fuscum, very few hollows plot south of Ash River Trail.
Water depth 77cm, clay bottom part of polygon with 100% cover, part with 30% cover.
2cm soil over bedrock, up to 15 cm in places; yellow-brown color. Previous fire evident (very old). Boulders present; granitic felsic gneiss.
Stand grading into more open canopy, releve may be more open than others of type; just north of ash river road; deep peat.
Soil reddish sandy loam at most 10cm deep, many boulders and rocks on surface ground layer of oak leaves and moss, some coarse woody debris. Granitic felsic gneiss and schist.
Fairly isolated from shore, surrounded by upland (aspen birch forest) and shallow marsh; deep peat.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: 2-8 cm soil over bedrock. Rock outcrops present in polygon. Old cabin nearby. Granitic-felsic gneiss surficial geology.

25cm peat over clay; surrounded by upland (WRPA); low hummocks; spruce varies widely in height, canopy anything over 2m, some as tall as 25m, some standing dead spruce; rock outcrops in polygon. Topographic context: depression/flat.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: May be saturated in non-drought year; soil fine textured, grey color. Seasonally flooded.
Water depth 50cm. Soil thin layer of muck over clay, solid bottom. Isolated area in Daley Bay. Some areas with more Typha, some with more Carex. Permanently flooded.
Rocky polygon. 1-2cm soil over bedrock; up to 8cm in places. Granitic-felsic surficial geology.
Fairly open canopy, many layers (if "subcanopy" included, % cover is a bout 75%); located between white cedar tamarack and tamarack fen; deep peat.
Hillside facing west-southwest. 2-4cm soil over bedrock; 6 cm in places. Granitic felsic surficial geology. On peninsula.
Deep peat; more tamarack than white cedar; canopy multi-layered ranges 5-2 0m; some tall Picea mariana emergent;  grades into tamarack swamp; very shrubby; some downed trees.
Soil to 10cm deep. Upland brush.
Deep peat fairly open canopy for this type; fairly wet-water in hollows; in large peatland.
Water 1m deep. Plants growing in rock crevices (?) underwater, patchy distribution of Phragmites. Rock substrate. Area permanently saturated.
Deep peat stand fairly mineral rich for type? Standing water in hollows; spruce dense for this type.
South facing hillside. Granitic-felsic and schist boulders.  Island. Fine sandy loam.
Trees short, stunted, canopy open; spruce and larch somewhat emergent from cedar; very shrubby;  grades into area where trees even more wide evenly spaced and more stunted; deep peat.
Small polygon. 20cm soil on top of bedrock. Fraxinus nigra stand present uphill away from lake. Seasonally flooded.

Ash canopy with cedar subcanopy; well developed hummocks/hollows; nearly all vegetation on hummocks and dead trees. Standing water in hollows (probably in non-drought year); deep peat; Picea glauca and fir in area.
Dense shrub layer; fairly open canopy-woodland type; part of large peatland; some areas with more cedar and tamarack; deep peat. Hummocks and hollow present.
Soils mostly > 10cm deep, occasional granite rocks on surface. Downslope from jack pine woodland.
About 50cm standing water.
Hummocks and hollows from old downed cedar. Soil black, fine textured. Area saturated.
Water depth 75cm. Soil is about 10cm peat over clay. In Daley Bay, sheltered from waves, adjacent to willow swamp and shore. Area permanently flooded.
Water 1m deep. Large open lake. Area saturated/permanently flooded.
Incipient water track in large peatland; large, wide polygon (water not narrowly channelled); most tamarack under 2m tall, gnarled, with dead limbs and trunks; deep peat.
Beaver impoundment. Clumps of vegetation on floating logs (Dulichum, Triadenum, Calamagrostis canadensis). Area saturated.
Not a completely closed canopy (cover of spruce low for type); small polygon; adjacent to spruce woodland type; cover of Care pauciflora greater than others of type; deep peat.
Dense hazel; upland brush type. Near beaver impoundment, tracks through brush; probably beaver caused type.
Water depth 1m. Old beaver pond in Indian Creek; some places with far fewer plant (too deep?); polygon very variable in that regard. Area permanently flooded.
Fairly open canopy more cedar here throughout polygon than is typical - more minerotrophic? Deep peat.
Some areas with shorter bog birch, less dense; occasional black spruce and larch 5m tall; adjacent to leather leaf bog and shore fen; deep peat.
1cm soil (mostly organic material) over bedrock; up to 10 cm in places. Soil dark gray color. Granitic-felsic gneiss.
Tall dense bog birch, much like BBSF, though not shoreline situation; polygon rings LL bog, alder swamp on upland side; fairly mineral rich; thatch layer from Carex heavy in places; deep peat.
Soil gleyed.

Low area surrounded by upland and BSAS; some standing dead trees; alder dense, little light to forest floor = lack of herb/grasses? Sphagnum layer not well developed; 7cm peat over 10cm loam over clay. Area saturated.
Fair amount of coarse woody debris (oak and jack pine). Litter layer of oak and maple leaves. Soil: 5cm O horizon, 2cm A horizon, 5cm E leached horizon.

100m2 plot within JPL polygon; sparse vegetation type; fallen jack pine in releve; vegetation in small depressions in rock; granite bedrock; living jack pine (15-20m tall) in area but none within 20X20 meters around relve plot.

Sphagnum cover unique for type; adjacent to leatherleaf bog in old beaver meadow; fairly large polygon. Sphagnum peat >16 inches; suggests that Carex lacustris is invading over sphagnum. Some standing dead trees. Area saturated.
Carex cover low compared to others fairly open for type; adjacent to SPF and BSW hummock/hollows not well developed; deep peat.
Fewer, larger trees than #7358; some holes in canopy from fallen trees; cover of Carex chordorhiza. Hummock and hollows more well developed; deep peat.
Very large polygon; releve in center; spruce over 5m mostly dying; fairly wet; hummocks and hollows poorly developed; cover of Care pauciflora continuous; deep peat.

Areas with less bog birch and more willow, resembles BF type; not directly adjacent to shore, mat not floating; less leather leaf than other BBSF; willows below bog birch; bog birch growing on hummocks.
Many dead willow shrubs; graminoid hummocks well developed; some areas of polygon with greater cover of leather leaf; bordered by shore fen and shallow marsh; deep sedge peat.
Complex. Jack pine blowdowns abundant. A few standing dead jack pine. Southwest facing slope. Granitic-felsic gneiss. Southwest facing hillside.
Most tamarack dead or dying; not as wet as VOYA-91 SPF; less mineral rich? Carex livida present but rare in polygon. Directly adjacent to LBC with spruce. Deep peat.
Extremely dry due to drought. Many Acer rubrum clumped. Granitic gneiss. Soil red-yellow color. On hill landform.
Series of 3 releves. This plot typical of transitional characteristics between wet meadow and fen. History unknown. Water level manipulations? Ann Lake Wildlife Management Area.

Oak forest occupying half of terrace escarpment between jack pine and black ash swamp. Well drained red-brown coarse sand. A-layer 5cm. max DBH 40cm, typical DBH 35cm. Quercus ellipsoidalis 39.5cm 80 years. Multi-stemmed common. Some open grown trees with dead lower branches, frequent gaps, fallen oak logs and a few sangs, pine stumps. Releve edge 80m south of road.

Within old oxbow loop at south end. Releve series of small ridges and channels. Sandy silt with dark organic layer. typical DBH 20-30cm; max DBH 30-45cm common. Plot well drained. Elsewhere is polygon, scattered white pine, paper birch, northern pin oak, and Tilia. 27cm DBH Quercus macrocarpa - 55 rings; 66cm DBH Quercus macrocarpa 210 rings. Worms present in soil.

Medium sand with organic silt in top 3" at crest of mound between meanders of sand creek. Canopy 50-75%; crowns 15-20m tall; typical jack pine DBH 20-30cm; oak DBH: 20-30cm; max 45cm. Infrequent snags, tip-ups occasional, debris common. Tree cores: Pinus banksiana 34cm DBH-31 rings; 47cm DBH Quercus ellipsoidalis-58 rings. Topography is level to slightly mounded in plot center. Litter of leaves, needles, and twigs.

On ancient island of outwash channel. Releve on level terrace of knoll alternating mounds and depressions about 0.75m relief. Sandy silt with unsorted gravel on mounds; depressions sandy-clay silt with bare ground but no standing water. Moderately well drained. Substrate moderate to densely shaded. Typical DBH 15-25cm; max 35-45cm common. Tree Cores: 32cm Quercus macrocarpa - 75 rings.

Silty-fine sand, rich humus with dark organic material in topsoil. Lower slope of well-drained knoll with tip-up mounds occasional; stumps infrequent (white pine). Canopy typical DBH 25-35cm; no max DBH. Area pouched with depressions, mounds and boulders. Abundant tip-ups and broken limbs, snags occasional.
Dark clayey silt with unsorted gravel, A horizon 3-4" depth.
Open woodland on elongated knolls. Medium sand, humus layer 3-4cm thick, organic layer 4cm to pure sand. Birch DBH 10-25cm.
Mature aspen typical DBH 25-40cm. Ridge spur at lower slope of knoll. Medium sand, humus 2-3cm, silty organic 2-3cm, area with some ridges a channels. Paper birch 7-48cm.
Bryophyte data collected by Jan Janssens.
Wet meadow or intermediate fen. Bryophyte data by J.Janssens.
Releve bisected by deer trail where it is rich with bryophytes. Peat > 40cm deep. Wet meadow (Sedge Fen). Intermediate fen. Bryophyte data by J.Janssens. pH=4.7; Cond= 20.3; Abs.=0.495.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Saturated mud 15-25% cover; abundant woody debris: tip-ups, down limbs; snags occasional to infrequent; canopy gaps occasional. No standing water, perhaps ecotonal with mixed hardwood swamp. Typical DBH 25-35cm; max DBH 40cm infrequent.

Black ash with open canopy and understory with broad leaved sedges dominating substrate. Alder swamps and wet meadows nearby. Releve 25% cover of wet depressions, sedge hummocks 5-25%; Carex lacustris dominate 25-50%. Rich moss flora.

Dominated by Carex lacustris with blue-joint grass, Wooly bulrush. Riverulets of flowing water. Firm mineral soil and gravel. Occasional glacial erratics. Bare wet muck 1-5% cover between hummocks. Organic silt <0.5m on sand.

Black ash swamp amid larger alder swamp. Soupy muck 5-25% cover; elevated mounds. Snags and tip-ups occasional. Woody peat to 45cm depth. Sedge peat to 90cm. >90cm blond peat. Black ash DBH 15-35cm typical.
Carex lacustris meadow with sedge peat over sand. Sphagnum subsecundum present. Meadow like transitional fen. Linear wetland channel between forested ridges. Opens to north into tamarack swamp.

Fine organic silt thinly covering unsorted glacial stones, cobbles and boulders. Deep humus and litter, debris infrequent to uncommon snags occasional. Nearly level terrace with shallow depressions which are moderately well-drained, not supporting standing water. Most trees at or near 20m height. Typical DBH 20-40cm. Bare ground 10-15% with moss 25-50%.

At foot slope of gently sloping terrace; abrupt edge of mixed hardwood swamp. Oaks on ridge. Organic silty sand to 3.5", deep coarse sand to 1m depth. Largest trees in ecotone. Red oak 18-73cm DBH. Central mesic oak forest. Worms in A horizon. Rock at 68 inches, water table at 43 inches. Litter of stems to leaves and dried sedges.

Level with depressions; coarse red sand; silty organic layer 1-2". Typical pine DBH 35-45cm; max size 50-60cm infrequent. Red pine 80 years. Tree tip-ups scattered. Litter of leaves, needles, and twigs.

Level to gently sloping area at crest of large ridge. Deep coarse sand with humus 1-2.5". Typical DBH jack pine 15-20cm. The shrub 2-5m layer is 1-5% cover. Area varies in shrub thickness and near absence of prairie grasses. This releve less common. Basal area 100-190. Litter of moss, leaves, needles, and twigs.
crest of knoll sloping on all sides. Aspen forest on sinuous ridges and swales. Dark A-horizon 2-3". Coarse red sand. Debris common. Moss covered logs 1-5% cover. Aspen typical DBH 25-35cm.

Terrace ridge between channels. Level with depressions and hummocks at bases of trees and shrubs. Tip-ups, woody debris 5-25%. 3-9" of dark clay silt over boulders and cobbles. Dry depressions 25-50% cover. Thick pine needle duff.

Pines on crest and upper slopes of ridge spur of terrace between rivers. Red pine DBH 40-50cm common, 60-70cm DBH occasional. Red medium-fine sand, A-horizon 3-5cm of silty sand. Pine duff 1-2cm. Depressions and mounds; elsewhere level.

Well drained level, but with depressions. Silty sand 5-7cm over rock. Depressions with rock base, scattered boulders, unsorted sand/pebbles. Oak DBH mode 20-30cm; occasional max DBH 30-40cm, gaps frequent with tip-ups, aspen snags. Debris 5-10%. Open grown.

In old well-drained channel typical of this undulating land form of out wash. Soil 2-10cm of fine sandy silt with some areas of clay over cobble stones. Occasional boulders. Aspen typical DBH 10-20cm; green ash 5-15cm DBH.

Lowland hardwoods near St. Croix River. Mode DBH 15-25cm; max DBH 25-40 cm infrequent to common. Level with depressions and mounds. Well drained silty loam 2-10cm to reddish brown silty sand with pebbles. Charcoal 5cm depth; humus 1-4cm depth. Large Populus sangs, all sangs infrequent to common. 1-5% debris - fall trunks limbs. 5-10% bare ground. Landform with occasional large boulders and frequent swales. Releve characteristic of dryer end of scale. Moist areas with black ash grading into Alder thicket and Carex lacustris meadow.

Dry-mesic well drained, slight depressions, mounds and boulders. Small area maple basswood forest on lower slope of middle ridge. Soil silty sand. Organic layer 5-10cm depth. Medium sand with silt to 25cm depth, then rock/cobbles. Typical DBH 25-35cm; max DBH (red and bur oak) to 45cm occasional. Debris 5-10%, dry material.

Releve dominated by large quaking aspen with red oak enclosing sub-canopy. Aspen mode DBH 40-50cm. No max. sub-canopy 10-15cm with red maple. Level terrace becoming wet-mesic in north plot. Debris 5-10% cover, tip-ups limb outside plot, occasionally dominated by paper birch. Soils: slight depressions and mounds on nearly level terrace - 20 feet below ridge crest. Soil silty sand, 3-7cm organic material. Humus 2-4cm thick (in depressions). Otherwise is medium grained red sand. Charcoal observed at 3cm depth. 45.5 cm Red oak; 78 rings to center.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: High ridge over bear creek, undulating to gently sloping to the north. Debris 5-25% cover. Silty sand 3-7cm, medium coarse sand. Mature mesic oak forest, red oak DBH 25-55cm. Standing water at 5.5 feet.

level to slightly sloping due to small ridges and knolls. landscape has shallow relief. Typical pine DBH 15-20cm with frequent max to 25cm. Rich deep organic silt in sand to 7cm depth. Tip-ups and limbs frequent. Debris <1% cover. Moss covered ground in places. Moss covered ground in some places. Litter of leaves, needles and twigs.

Channeled floodplain on modern alluvium forming small terraces with standing pools. Releve a combination of poorly drained areas with drier banks. Mud bare ground 25-50% cover. Mode DBH 40-50cm, >60cm DBH common. Tip-ups and debris 5-25% cover. 1 inch organic layer.

Dominated by red maple and quaking aspen. Crowns 20m tall. Mode DBH 10-20cm; max DBH <35cm infrequent Land undulating mounds and depressions. Tip-ups occasional. Rocky with thin layer of silt and humus. Tip-ups occasional. Soil unconsolidated boulders, cobbles, and pebbles with organic silt and silty subsoil. Bare ground with depressions 20-25%, woody debris 1-5%.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Terrace crest level to gently sloping southeast. Mounds and depressions 2-3' relief. Boulders and pebbles covered 7-10cm of organic loam and sand. Mode DBH 25-35cm, rare max DBH to 40cm. Red oak and red maple <20cm.

Old growth. Soil 10-20cm organic silt (peat at base) medium sized sand subsoil. Releve at edge of black ash swamp. Releve on toe of terrace slope (20-30 feet in height). 7% grade than 20% grade. Maple basswood also on upper slope between edge and swamp. Debris 1-5%, tip-ups occasional; snags occasional to uncommon. Sugar maple 20-40cm DBH; basswood 16-54 cm DBH.

Releve inclusion within northern hardwoods. Level to gently sloping eastward. Boulders and cobbles. Soil a dark loam (sandy) to 7cm depth. Subsoil of clayey sand to medium grained sand. Low mounds and depressions. Mostly immature but with maturing trees forming scattered stands throughout. Bimodal DBH; 15-25cm with scattered inclusions of 25-55cm DBH: Bur oak, basswood, red maple. Debris <1%.

Soil: 2-5cm organic silty sand; subsoil red medium sand. Shallow rolling ridges or knolls on large upland ridges. Pine cover characteristic for this portion of stand but density increases towards road - gaps frequent. Red pine mode 40-50cm DBH; no max. Paper birch 15-25cm DBH. Northern pin oak 10-20cm DBH. Abundant snags; thick duff layer and debris.

Prairie openings amid open grown oaks on level crest of basalt ridge at center of island in St. Croix river. Soil 2-20cm deep over bedrock; silt and pebbles. Dark A-horizon to 10cm. Tree DBH 8-35cm, bur oak 31cm DBH - largest. Heavy browse on shrubs. Occasional piles of exposed basalt boulders.

Aspen woodland with scattered oak and prairie openings surrounded by hazels. Soil silty sand (dark) 5-8cm deep to coarse red sand. Typical aspen DBH 10-20cm, scattered oak 25-35cm DBH. Multi-stemmed; open grown. Litter of leaves, twigs, and sedges.

Soil 2-8cm organic silty sand over coarse red sand. Pine mode 15-25cm DB, typical DBH northern pin oak 20-30cm. Canopy open with uniform spacing. No large trees. Level to rolling with small knolls. Debris 5-10% cover, snags occasional.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Area described as NH53 (northern hardwoods, 9-15" DBH, 12.5-17.5 crds/ac) on soil 10 (SWED coarse loamy, level to moderate slope). Upland island (~9ha) in ash swamp. Deer, large old stumps, large red pine 20m DBH OP. A horizon depth: 5cm.

Area described as BI54 (birch, 9-15" DBH, 17.5-22.5 cords/acre) on soil 4 (SW PD minerals). Hummocky, low spots damp, soil on low side thick and black. Near (100m) new logging road. Multi-stem maple and basswood. A horizon depth: 2cm.

Area described as A55 (aspen, 9-15" DBH, >22.5 cords/acre) on soil 12 (EXWD sandy to gravelly, level). Between logging road (30m) and wetland (20m). Stumps, multi-stem red maple. Aspen DBH 30-48cm. A horizon depth: 3cm.

Area described as A55 (aspen, 9-15" DBH, >22.5 cords/acre) on soil 13 (EXWD sand to gravel, moderate slope). On long, narrow slope (40x700m) between aspen and swamp. Large fallen fir and aspen. Fir 26-36cm DBH. A horizon depth: 3cm. Litter of leaves and needles. Topographic context is whole slope.

Area described as BI54 (birch, 9-15", 17.5-22.5 cords/acre) on soil 14 (EXWD sand to gravel, steep). Hilly, hummocky, large old burned stumps. Deer (U.g. bitten), bear. Aspen DBH 33-47cm. Slope spans slope or crest to toe. A horizon depth: 8cm. Topographic context is whole slope.

Area described as BI54 (birch, 9-15" DBH, 17.5-22.5 cords/acre) on soil 14 (EXWD sand to gravel, steep). Same as AIT-21 but 50m west on shallower south slope. Aspen 36-41cm DBH, birch 19-25cm. Slope spans crest to toe.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Area described as BI44 (birch, 5-9", 17.5-22.5 cords/acre) on soil 11 (SWED coarse loamy steep). Stumps. Hill being mined for gravel. Large fir stumps, sparse woody debris, leaves brown and holey, earthworms? A horizon depth: 7cm. Litter of leaves and graminoids.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Area described as BI44 (birch, 5-9", 17.5-22.5 crds/ac) on soil 9 (complex mixed texture, steep). Big stumps, tip-ups, boulders. Swamp nearby (200m); tall red pine and old logging trail nearby.
Area described as A46 (aspen, 5-9" DBH, >27.5 cords/acre) on soil 12 (EXWD sand to gravel, level). Area not EXWD. Small wetland 20m east. Old logging trail nearby. Stumps (cedar?). Moose tracks.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Area described as A56 (aspen, 9-15" DBH, >27.5 cords/acre) on soil 8 (complex mixed texture, moderate slopes). Small (6 ha.), low (10') upland island. Beaver. Aspen clearcut nearby. Old logging road. Stumps. A horizon depth: 3cm. Litter of needles and leaves.

Area described as A53 (aspen, 9-15" DBH, 12.5-17.5 cords/acre) on soil 6 (WD medium to fine, moderate slopes). Hummocky, ash-grey soil, multi-stem basswood, oak leaves, holey. Small ash swamp and fir nearby. Old logging road.

Area described as NH55 (northern hardwoods, 9-15" DBH, >22.5 cords/acre) on soil 9 (complex mixed texture, steep slopes). Stumps, old gas can, basswood clumps, large sugar maple (61cm DBH) and aspen (56cm). Most 20-30cm DBH. A horizon: 3cm.

Area described as NH54 (northern hardwoods, 9-15" DBH, 17.5-22.5 cords/acre) on soil 5 (MW to WD medium to fine, level). Deer bed and browse. Cut-over 60-70 years ago. (Dan and Joe). Near ash draw (30m) and swamp. A horizon depth: 2cm.

Area described as NH54 (northern hardwoods, 9-15" DBH, 17.5-22.5 cords/arec) on soil 4 (SWPD minerals). Stumps, deer, old logging road. Small (200m^2) cattail/reed opening nearby (20m). A Horizon depth: 3cm.

Area described as A53 (aspen, 9-15" DBH, 12.5-17.5 cords/acre) on soil 7 (WD medium to fine, steep). Big old stumps, tip-ups, a few fallen trees, deer, old logging road. Fir forest grading into aspen/northern hardwood. A horizon depth >10cm. Litter of leaves and needles.

Area described as WP42 (white pine, 5-9" DBH, 7.5-12.5 cords/acre) on soil 14 (EXWD sand to gravel, steep). Steep but not sandy. Open-grown dead pine nearby. New logging road and pothole wetland nearby, deer, duff. A horizon depth: 3cm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Area described as NH42 (northern hardwoods, 5-9" DBH, 7.5-12.5 cords/acre) on soil 5 (MW to WD medium to fine, level). Sandy, not fine. Big (90cm DBH) stumps, pine seedlings, swamp and new logging road nearby. A horizon depth: 10cm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Area described as NH53 (northern hardwoods, 9-15" DBH, 12.5-17.5 cords/acre) on soil 6 (MW to WD medium to fine, moderate slopes). Big (90cm DBH) old and small (30cm) young (fir) stumps. Swamp nearby. Old logging trail. A horizon depth: 3cm. Soil: silty sand.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Area described as A55 (aspen, 9-15" DBH, >27.5 cords/acre) on soil 7 (MW to WD medium to fine, steep). Big old and small young stumps. Steep and irregular Oak DBH 32-34cm, aspen ~35cm. Fallen fir and birch. A horizon depth: 3cm. Soil: Silty sand.

Area described as A58 (aspen, 9-15" DBH, ?? cords/acre) on soil 13 (EXWD sand to gravel, moderate slope). Stumps, deer, no bear. Pine seedlings in fir to north. Red pine to south 3-layer canopy: Populus grandidentata, Pinus resinosa, Acer rubrum, Abies balsamea. A horizon depth: 4cm. Litter of leaves and aspen. Soil of silty sand.

Area described as BF53 (balsam fir, 9-15" DBH, 12.5-17.5 cords/acre) on soil 13 (EXWD sand to gravel, moderate slopes). Big old burned stumps. Swamp and new logging road nearby. 2 Lycopodium species 5m OP. A horizon depth: 3cm. Litter of leaves and needles.
Black spruce present but small cover (though many dying, stunted trees ). Grades into tamarack forest and BST types. Deep peat. Along north-south entrance trail.
70:30 Cedar:Tamarack. Tamarack trees larger, but fewer. Much like an o pen cedar swamp. On edge of large peatland. Standing water in hollows. Deep peat.

Aspen mixed with birch nearby in stand. Just down slope from jack pine woodland with bedrock. Soil coarse sandy loam or clay loam, red. Duff layer 2 cm, leaves about 60% cover. Soil at least 10cm deep.
Rocky slope above cedar swamp. Toeslope. Uncommon type in park but locally common. Soil spodosol, leached E horizon. Coarse sandy loam, rocky, up to 15 cm deep. Evidence of fire and charcoal in soil.
Some parts of stand very rocky with less aspen. Soil >10cm silty loam. White cedar/aspen.

Stand is clumps of cedar and aspen/birch, not well mixed. Very shrubby for cedar. Shrubs in canopy openings. Mosses on logs, rocks, and trunks. Soil fine sandy loam >10cm deep. Leached horizon, rocky, but not a lot of surficial rocks. White cedar/aspen. Ontario, Canada.

Completely closed canopy, very little understory. Slight hummocks and hollows. Much coarse woody debris. Soil: 4cm organic layer - undecomposed needles/leaves. 14cm peat? high organic content, some silt loam. Clay hardpan at 18cm. White cedar/aspen.
Adjacent to lake-isolated bay. Not a floating mat. Fairly thick thatch layer. Standing water 5cm below surface (low water year, probably usu ally well above surface). Deep sedge peat.

Drought has killed many forbs. Forb data probably incomplete. (saw trilliums etc. here earlier in year) Near Lake Kabetogama on island. Some dead standing elm. Soils sandy loam, deep to 15cm; not rocky. Little horizon development

Widely spaced, tall spruce trees with subcanopy of fir and aspen/birch. Very rocky. Much coarse woody debris. Many fir dying (spruce budworm?). Soil shallow 3cm over rock, up to 15cm. 2cm O horizon, 1cm A horizon, 3+ cm B horizon; fine sandy loam.
Slope above bay. Much coarse woody debris. Very rocky. Tall spruce presumably black, though white spruce seedlings found. Soil thin 2-5 cm. 2 cm organic material over 2 cm fine sandy loam over rock.
Floating mat of peat over 0.5 - 1.0m water. Plants rooted in mat. Acorus marsh isolated bay between water lilies and cattail marsh. Peat over clay.
Part of large peatland. Larix emergent, borderline enough for white cedar tamarack type. Deep peat
Slope above beaver pond. Soil somewhat rocky. 15+ cm sandy loam. 2cm O horizon, 2cm A horizon, 4+cm reddish B horizon.
Long eastern arm of Daley Bay. Slow moving water, no wave action. Clay substrate. Part of polygon in.25m water. Grading into a small Carex rostrata marsh. H3 fibric peat over clay.
Old maple basswood forest northeast of Pancake Lake. Moderately thick deciduous leaf duff. Straight single Tilia boles. Moderate coarse woody debris. Gentle within-plot relief.
Fire scars on some Pinus in vicinity. Plot is upslope from Moss Lake. Variable forest matrix of Pinus/Betula and Populus. Litter of needles and leaves. A horizon depth: 2cm.

Soils with charcoal-assorted wood incorporated in organic layer > 14 cm. over fine gray-brown silty with sand grit in cobbles. A horizon depth: 8cm. Litter of needles and leaves. Topographic context: upper/middle.
Deep organics- moss cover.
Black spruce/tamarack swamp - primarily moss substrate - few forbs, etc.
Few dead and down Abies. Soil brown cinnamon color - fine texture with angular rock/sand. Charcoal present -no fire scars observed. Litter of needles and leaves. Topographic context: upper/middle.
Some charcoal in soils - no stump/trunk scars observed. A horizon depth: 10cm. Litter of needles and aspen.
Loamy sand; shallow, intermixed with cobble/boulder/rock. Fire scars on old stumps. Litter of pine needles and bark.
