Ericaceous/sedge/sphagnum mat between pond and lowland conifer forest.
Betula cordifolia appears in the community, but not in releve. Soils = several cm to 13+ cm humus, with exposed rock (talus).
Peat > 12", still fibrous at that depth (water level below 12"). Plot Plot approximately 2 chains north of river - bounded by river and graminoid/ericaceous.

Saturated peat, >12" deep. Water level about 10" below surface. Plot in area to east of gale/ericaceous releve (DNR# 7693). Bounded by river to south, Fraxinus nigra to north and Thuja farther to east. A horizon depth: 2cm.
Ground cover moss, with varying degrees of decomposing moss, etc. to at least 12" below. Sparse litter of Thuja needles and light deciduous leaves.

Forest mosaic includes boreal hardwood-conifer forest and pine mixed. Soils: silty loam mixed with lots of rocks/cobble. Releve on southwest side of portage. Forest mosaic includes boreal hardwood conifer forest and pine mixes. A horizon depth: 2.5cm, litter of needles and leaves.
Sedge peat soils - graminoid wetland adjacent to bay and boreal hardwood conifer forest.
Soil is fine textured but amongst lots of cobble/cobble/cobble. Many downed Abies in area. Litter of leaves and twigs.
Fire scars present. Fire went through this area; change in vegetation is obvious on photo and in landscape. Litter of leaves, twigs and needles.
This community is part of a complex which includes shrub swamp and areas of concentrated Thuja. Some down Picea mariana. Geocaulum lividum in fruit (collected).

Site is forested talus - adjacent area to west is more open talus; above is cliff (20'-intermittent). At base of slope is Deer Lake. 2 burned cut pine stumps (old, 16" diameter). Numerous bryophyte/lichen collected. Litter of leaves needles and twigs.

Tamarack stand in large wetland meadow. Larix in several strata. Substrate sunny. Sphagnum forms carpet with large hummocks to 0.5m tall, deep fibric peat. Moss floats on standing water which is 10cm, but with depressions to 50cm. Meadow dominated by Carex urtriculata and Carex lasiocarpa.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Isolated stand of Thuja in black ash swamp. Peat shallow over sand under-laid by thick band of gray clay. Pebbles and boulders present. Level with hummocks and depressions. Immature black ash. Logged forest to the south. Many surrounding ares with drumlins dominated by Acer saccharum. Much fallen debris. A horizon depth: 3cm. Average peat depth: 5cm.

Tamarack marsh in drumlin field. Shallow peat to organic soil or clay? Heavy brush; hummocks >76%. Dry pools due to late summer drought. Mode DBH 15-25cm heterogeneous. Stand with all age classes. Surrounded by Alder thicket. Wetland between drumlins.
In a shallow, muddy depression on rock outcrop surface; exposed to full sun (1.5 m X 1.5 m plot). Associated with releves 7744 and 7745. Frostview Road.
Carex lasiocarpa and Sphagnum in bog or poor fen between eskers. Moss forms low lying hummocks about 2m diameter. Carex in standing water to 25cm depth. Shrubs stunted <10cm tall.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Lowland hardwoods on channeled silty alluvial terrace, 3-5m elevation above Mississippi River. Releve at toe of higher terrace in depression. Immature to mature forest; mode DBH 20-30cm, max DBH 40-50 cm (silver maple). Closed canopy adjacent to floodplain forest margin and well drained ridges with mesic trees. Tip-ups and downed logs occasional.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Soil dark silt to clay subsoil. Mode DBH 20-30cm; occasional max DBH 35-60cm (bur oak, tilia). Outside bend of Mississippi river. Many raceway channels, terrace ridges 5-10m above water's edge. Grades to maple basswood forest. Tip-ups and downed trees common, all stages of decay. 33cm DBH Quercus macrocarpa at 79 rings.

Sandy silt to silty sand with gravel and boulders. Mature aspen forest on crest of moraine ridge with ice block depressions. Aspen mode DBH 35-45cm. Releve on saddle ridge between depressions. Slope both east and west. Depressional soil with high silt. Thick acer subcanopy. Some areas of stand with larger aspens. A horizon depth: 4cm.

Wet meadow on terrace of Little Pine River. Open canopy at edge of black ash swamp. Alluvial silts 1-2m above stream bed, mixed with wet organic muck. Releve includes two small gullies. North facing, southbank.

Wet prairie/mesic oak savanna. Former pasture with low grazing intensity. Burned annually for 40 years. Low swale and sandy ridges. 30 acres along brook. Alluvial silts and clay over sand, season floods. Forb content high. Large abundance of wet prairie species in open areas.

Sapric peat or muck and loam. Poorly drained, often hummocky with Carex stricta, and Carex lasiocarpa dominated large areas. Forb diversity and abundance low. Species listed are frequent to well dispersed. Area 2-3 square mile wet meadow bordered by willow thicket/aspen.

Fibric sedge peat. Springy floating mat. Large bog or poor fen dominated by Carex lasiocarpa on level to saturated wet depressions. Wet areas 10-25%. Raised sphagnum domes dominated by Chamaedaphne and Sphagnum species. Bog with no lagg but bordered by wet meadow.

Dark silty sand over sand. Mature white pine on slope of kettle bog including toe. Heavy pine duff, mixed age classes. Large pines open grown. Pine DBH mode 20-30cm, max DBH 30-50cm common in plot. Burnt dead boles with charcoal. Basal area 125. A horizon depth: 2cm. Tree cores: 31cm DBH PInus storbus-58 rings; 44cm DBH Pinus resinosa-88 rings; 37cm DBH Pinus strobus-74 rings.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Dark silty coarse sand to coarse sand with pebbles. Mature red oak forest mode DBH 30-40cm; max DBH <50cm infrequent. Moraine with small depressions and scattered boulders. Canopy gaps infrequent; abundant downed logs from understory. Basal area 150 square feet/acre. A horizon depth: 1cm. 40cm DBH Quercus rubra at 69 rings. 38.5cm DBH Quercus ellipsoidalis at 63 rings.
Mixed emergent marsh. Floating mat in shallow lake. Releve 100m along water's edge.

Fine sandy silt to fine sand and pebbles. Mature red pine mode DBH 40-50 cm, even aged stand. North-face of moraine between kettle bogs. Releve has mesic aspect with dry crest. Surface pocked with depressions of fine silt and sandd, low organic material. Few tip-ups and snags-deciduous trees immature. Red maples - deciduous mode 10-20cm DBH. A horizon depth: 3cm. Pinus resinosa tree core: 46cm DBH - 77 rings, 89cm DBH - 89 rings.
Dark silty sand to sand. Immature trees, crowns 20m tall, mode 10-20cm DBH, max 20-30cm DBH. Tip-ups and debris abundant. A horizon depth: 1cm.
Wet meadow in arm of kettle bog between moraines near Stewart Lake. Soil: muck and sedge peat over wet organic sand.

Alluvial silts and sand to coarse sand. Open canopy with mixed age class, no understory or shrub layer. Alluvial flats on bend of Mississippi River. Flooding scars evident on trunks. Mode DBH 20-30cm; max 40-70cm DBH. 6cm A horizon of fibrous organic material and some decomposed branches.

Silty sand over gray to fine red sand. Mature lowland hardwoods on old terrace of Mississippi River with undulating sand and depressions. Generally sloping away from bank. Mode DBH 30-40cm; max DBH 50-70cm common. Several Tilia with multi-stems; ground layer abundant. Old channel depressions; paper birch in tip-ups no longer in canopy. A horizon: 2cm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Dark silt and fine sand over light colored fine sand. Narrow island in Mississippi River inside oxbow meander. Narrow ridge crest with closed canopy pine stands. Oak woodland and some prairie openings. Floodplain forest on lower slopes. Sand outwash with terraces. Mixed age pine. Deciduous mode DBH 20-30cm, max size rare. Litter of needles and leaves.

Light gray sand, fine. Mesic maturing mixed pine. Pine mode DBH 30-40cm. Deciduous mode DBH 20-30cm. Crest of narrow island. Releve 10x40m. Nearby is permanent campsite - few old stumps very decayed. A horizon depth: 1cm. Soil light grey sand over red white fine sand.

Brushy opening on crest of narrow meander island, 50 foot relief bordered by steep sides. Part of a continuum along ridge at different elevations. Opening maintained by beaver cutting of small trees and brush. Seedling layer nearly absent, grasses thinly scattered beneath forbs. Fine silty sand over unsorted sand and gravel. Hard clay pan layer about 18-22cm depth. Plot 10x40m area. A horizon: 2cm.

Dark silty sand to medium-fine sand subsoil. Mesic jack pine forest on outwash. Mature pine mode DBH 15-25cm, crowns 15m tall, much woody debris. Frequent canopy gaps. Soil dark silty sand over fine medium sand. A horizon depth: 1cm.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Alluvial sandy silt (gray) over fine sand. Maturing uneven aged silver maple floodplain, 10 feet above normal late summer flow of Mississippi River. Plot 5x80 includes mounds and raceway channel. High water flow 1 to 2 feet above highest point. Debris common. Mode DBH 30-40cm, max size 40-60cm occasional. Plot is lowest of three terraces.

Silty sand over fine sand. Mature aspen forest crowns 25m tall, mode DBH 30-40cm; max size rare. On 4th terrace of Mississippi. Trees with shelf fungi. Several down trees and thick brush from open canopy. A horizon 1cm.

Dark silty sand over medium sand. Sand moraine on west bank of Mississippi River. Dominated by Quercus ellipsoidalis. Crowns 10-15m tall, mode DBH 20-30cm. Several stands of Populus grandidentata and Betula papyrifera with scattered red pine. 28cm DBH Quercus ellipsoidalis-84 rings.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Dark silty sand, medium-fine. Maturing even-aged stand dominated by red oak crowns 20-25m tall, mode DBH 20-30cm, max DBH rare, mostly aspen. Sand and gravel of drumlin between sedge meadow and tamarack complex. Much debris and tip-ups. surface undulating, pocked with depressions and mounds. Basal area 170. A horizon: 2cm.

On low ground between hills in Altamont Moraine, Prairie Coteau. Parent material: calcareous till; mineral soil 3cm below surface. Watertable at surface. Past grazing. Site 0.5 miles west of Minnesota/South Dakota border and .4 miles south of Gary. 3 cm mineral south; 3 cm A horizon.

Much disturbed by wind. Sparse standing 80-90cm DBH trees and snags/coarse woody debris. Dense shrubs and tree reproduction. On low peninsula in wetland complex--prone to disturbance? Large tip-up mounds. Ice-push topography. Patchy litter and humus layers.

Mature wet-mesic northern hardwood forest on lake terrace at base of 1-2m slope. Gaps from wind damage. Deer trails. Flat microtopography. Relatively dense forbs. Upper terrace with maple basswood and northern hardwood, logging trails. Botrychium habitat.

In linear shrub swamp-wet meadow complex between beach/ice-push ridges on northeast side Mille Lacs. Openings in Salix gracil patches are +/- rich fen, more so than Carex lacustris/Calamagrostis/Typha patches. Alder local, not throughout.

Patchy oak, birch, and Tilia canopy with sugar maple and Tilia sub-canopy. No stumps. Moderate coarse woody debris, moss on trunks. Few large tip-ups, undulating microtopogy. Soil layer relatively undisturbed, few worms. Charcoal in organic layer. Litter of leaves and twigs.

Fairly open maple-basswood forest with "springy" soil. Many large tip-ups and large boulders. Much maple reproduction. Moderate coarse woody debris including several birch trees. Plot on a crest of small slope. A fairly large depression to the east, but no standing water.

Canopy of balsam fir and aspen. In the stand the sub-canopy contains occasional ash and bur oak. Some old stumps(+). Some fir dying. Stand also has wet depressions, worm disturbance. Rolling topography. Worms present in A horizon.

Even-aged aspen stand with scattered oak and Tilia. Thick duff with charcoal. No stumps, several tip-ups (1 large in middle). Coarse woody debris, especially birch. Abies scattered throughout stand. Sedges common on tip-ups.

An oak-birch forest, which is succeeding into maple basswood. Selective cutting of oak in past (stumps = +). Charcoal in duff. Some coarse woody debris, boulders at surface. Band of oak on upper slope, lower slope younger maple basswood. ONe large worm found on surface.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Maple basswood forest on northwest-facing slope of small hill. Canopy predominately maple with Tilia. Large red and white pines occasional. Stand was sugar bush. Well-decayed stumps occasional. Thick duff, charcoal. Much sugar maple reproduction.

Dying jack pine forest on large hill surrounded by Larix/black spruce swamp. Sand substrate with moderate thick pine duff. Some wind damage (aspen still alive). Blown over jack pine. Well-decayed stumps (cut?) covered with moss and lichens. Sandy soil with mottles starting at 44 inches, a few rocks at 1-2 inches and at 32 inches.

Fairly open red pine canopy on outwash. Plot thick with hazel. Fairly thin litter with some exposed mineral soil. Small boulders scattered throughout. Very well decayed stumps (cut). Some wind damage, down trees scattered. Soil: sand over clay sand with many rocks and a gravel layer at 18 inches.

East of Big Rush Lake on slight slope. Stand has been grazed, much Carex pensylvanica. Prickly ash abundant. Microtopoy is undulating. Younger mixed stand, predominately oak. Multi-stemmed Tilia and oak. Thin litter over mineral soil, mottles at 30 inches. One large bur oak dying. Soil: sand over loamy sand over sandy over clay sand, 4 inch O horizon and 2 inch A horizon.

Jack pine forest ~100m from county road. A few cut stumps, most well-decayed. Some wind thrown trees and tip-ups. Several ant mounds. Undulating microtopogy. Small worms. Charcoal in litter. Large colony of Corallrhiza. One inch A horizon.

Mixed stand of balsam fir, jack pine, paper birch, and aspen. Scattered stumps: some cut; others of wind thrown origin. Multi-stemmed birch. Some tip-ups and down trees. Undulating microtopogy. Small pond nearby. Litter of leaves and needles.

Jack pine forest on a sandy ridge between clearcut and black spruce swamp. Possible stand origin was cutting. Very well decayed stumps and no charcoal in litter. Approximately 50 years old. Moderate needle litter. Large clumps of Abies in canopy gaps. Jack pine somewhat healthy. Litter of needles and twigs. 2 inch O horizon and 1 inch A horizon.

Relatively open, dying jack pine stand with many shrubs. Much charcoal in litter (thick). Windthrown trees cross plot. Few well-decayed cut stumps and tip-up mounds. A water impeding layer at bottom of soil pit. Litter of leaves and needles, evidence of charcoal.

65 year old plantation on outwash; done to complete township quota. Recent and decayed coarse woody debris common. Dense shrub layer with several tall bur oak. Trough like microtopography. No large slash piles evident. Much deer browse. Litter of needles and twigs, thick A horizon.

Red pine forest with patches of aspen. Well-developed shrub-layer with very few well-decayed stumps. Tip-up mounds occasional. Very little wind-damage. Thick litter layer, coarse woody debris common. Soil with mottles at 4.5 feet.

Mature aspen stand with scattered conifers. Carpet of Carex pensylvanica, but lacks other grazing indicators, such as prickly shrubs and exotics. Some aspen dying and large coarse woody debris common. Soil with mottles at 4.5 feet.
Very mature jack pine stand. Several downed jack pine throughout plot. Tip-up mounds (one recent) occasional. Moderate to thin litter. Plot narrower and longer to avoid depression and large gap.

Open-grown red and bur oak on level ground. Scattered red pine throughout. Thin litter, worms. Surrounding area recently logged, but once (1993) large continuous stand. Some very old tip-ups, no stumps. Little coarse woody debris. Soil gravely and coarse from 28" to 53."

Mature maple basswood forest with good maple regeneration. No stumps in stand, rather many fallen logs and broken trees. Thick litter. Old tip-up mounds. Trails common in stand (ATV or snowmobile). Used as sugar bush. Soil with mottles in very thick bands as depth increases.

Mature maple basswood forest with much reproduction of sugar maple, elm, and ash. No stumps, many downed logs and several broken snags. Coarse woody debris common. 2 inch very dark, rich A/O horizon. Soil with mottles starting at 2.5 feet.

Mature white pine stand with occasional red pine. Some decayed stumps, but many fallen trees and broken-off stumps. Probably selectively logged in past. Stand map ages at 109 years old. Near village of Elbow Lake. Moderate duff/needle layer. Heavy rock layer at about three feet.

Predominantly aspen over story with scattered sugar maple. Area used as sugar bush by White Earth Band and has forest road leading to it. Down logs occasional. Rich site. Populus 18-29cm DBH, Acer 10-14, Tilia 10-18. Impermeable gravel layer at 3 feet.
White Earth HCP. Moderate coarse woody debris. Several large oaks with boles just outside plot, branches providing canopy in plot. Soil data collected by Jim Barott.
White Earth HCP. Soil data collected by Jim Barott.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: White Earth HCP. Coarse woody debris sparse. Occasional nurse logs. Basswood and ash seeds common on ground. Soil data collected by Jim Barott.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: White Earth HCP. Much of D(1-3)i due to Acer seedlings. Very dense canopy. Occasional nurse logs. Moderate coarse woody debris. Soil data collected by Jim Barott.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: White Earth HCP. Supercanopy red oak, paper birch, basswood. Deciduous leaf duff. Occasional coarse woody debris; paper birch, red oak, mod decayed logs, occasional well decayed nurse logs. Soil data collected by Jim Barott.
White Earth HCP. White pine inclusion in maple-basswood forest. Soil data collected by Jim Barott.
White Earth HCP. Moderate coarse woody debris. Occasional bare soil. Outwash. Soils info collected by Kellie Wolf. Soil with mottles at 2.5 feet.
White Earth HCP. Coarse woody debris common. Moderately thick deciduous leaf duff. Soil with mottles starting at 2.5 feet. Soil data collected by Kellie Wolf.

Coarse woody debris common, including large diameter Ostrya. Moderate thick deciduous leaf duff. Equisetum throughout stand. One well-decayed stump outside plot. Outwash. White Earth HCP. Soils info collected by Kellie Wolf. Find sand soil with mottles starting at 2.5 feet.
White Earth HCP. Moderate coarse woody debris. Soil data collected by Jim Barott.
White Earth HCP. Few well-decayed, moss-covered stumps in plot. Soil data collected by Jim Barott.
White Earth HCP. Occasional old tip-up mounds. Moderate coarse woody debris. Soil data collected by Jim Barott.

White Earth HCP. Moderate coarse woody debris. Old tip-ups. Quercus rubra DBH 18-30cm, Acer rubrum DBH 8-14cm, Acer saccharinum DBH 6-19cm, Populus tremuloides DBH 7-8cm. Outwash. Soils info collected by Jim Barott.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: White Earth HCP. Scant-moderate coarse woody debris. Gently undulating microtopography. Tip-up mounds nearby. On till. Well drained. >5'to water table table. Tilia 8-25cm, Quercus macrocarpa 23cm, Acer sac 7-23cm. Soils by Jim Barott. Magnet buried in northwest corner.
White Earth HCP. Moderate coarse woody debris. Soil data collected by Jim Barott. Soils sand to loamy sand/sandy loam.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Much of site has dead elm in canopy and it is riddled with skid roads. Releve away from both, higher quality than stand as a whole. Quercus macrocarpa DBH 11-24cm, Tilia americana 5-25cm, Acer saccharum 20-27cm, Ulmum 18cm. Thick A horizon. Plenty of worms.
This place is heavily used by bears. Scattered, torn trees, and it reeks of bear. Populus DBH 18-34cm, Ulmus 9cm, Quercus macrocarpa 39cm. 8 inch A horizon, two worms present.

Large distances between trees. Most pine regeneration under snow in normal winter. No aspen in plot. Betula DBH 39-85cm, Pinus banksiana 36-100cm, Pinus strobus 158cm, Pinus resinosa 65-170cm. Low cover of Pinus banksiana as most are dead. 2 inch A horizon.

Has a disturbed feel in understory that I can't put my finger on. Perhaps the dirth of species diversity in herb layer is because of heavy D1-3 cover? Not a high quality stand, but a dirth to sample in this township. 3 inch O horizon, hit rocks at 53."

The understory groundlayer is so heavily dominated by maple seedlings that there is little space for much else. Along Buckboard Road. 13 species of basidomycetes. Old white pine 30 meters south of plot. Releve is south of road. Some wind damage. 3 inch O horizon, 1 inch A horizon; no worms observed.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: East side of Height of Land Road south of Island Lake. Not as rich an understory as expected. Some nice dead and dying birch all under 7cm--why? Lots of bare litter. Acer DBH 11-34cm, Tilia 11-31, Populus 55, Quercus 35. Three inch O horizon, 1 inch A horizon.

Species data look good, but no litter. K Wolf says no evidence of worms. Plot east of tribal stand boundaries on map based on powerline ROW used as access. Formerly burned. Acer DBH 11-33cm, Tilia 14-66cm.

Thin litter layer. K. Wolf says no worms. Huge Botrychium virginianum. Stand is east of route 133 about 200m north of curve in road. Ostrya DBH 13cm, Tilia DBH 10-25cm, Acer saccharum DBH 10-42cm. D3-4 very dense. Soil is loam over very fine sandy loam with mottles at depth.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Very choppy canopy. Fairly steep, rocky site. Sloping south to north shore of St. Clair Lake. Dry feel to site. Abundance of prickly ash suggests former grazing. Quercus macrocarpa DBH 13-40cm, Quecurs rubra DBH 21-36cm, Betula papyrifera 20-25cm.

Charcoal in silty soil with worms. Pop tremuloides DBH 11-22cm, Abies balsimifera DBH 10-17cm, Picea glauca DBH 49cm, Betula papyrifera DBH 10-17, Ulmus americana DBH 17cm, Quercus macrocarpa DBH 15cm. Worms and charcoal present in 3 inch A horizon. Litter of leaves and needles.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Beautiful area, SNA quality, neither logged nor blown down. Groundlayer mainly oak litter about 1" thick, more depauprte than canopy and structure would suggest. J Barot says maybe some worms, but not lots. Charcoal present in A and O horizon, coarse loamy till. Hit rock at 53 inches.

There are orange flags in some of these trees. This stand appears to be a small remnant of the original stand.  Pinus resinosa DBH 27-45cm, Populus tremuloides DBH 14-38cm, Prunus serotina DBH 18cm. Litter of leaves and needles, 2 inch A horizon.

Red pine on Anchor Hill Road. If plantation, red and white pine must have been planted in equal numbers, not in rows. Many dogwoods with tree-like growth form. Acer saccharum in D5 and Acer rubrum in D1-2. Pines to 40 and 50cm DBH max. Lots of charcoal present in O horizon, no worms.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Tilia americana DBH 10-38cm, Acer saccharum DBH 43, Populus tremuloides DBH 10-16, Ulmus americana DBH 17, Prunus serotina DBH 14.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest

remarks: Red pine/aspen.

In distinctive band of forb rich prairie surrounded by forb poor. Water table at approximately 30 cm. Pitted microtopography. A medium boulder in plot. Not burned in at least 3 years. Moderate litter accumulation. Mapped location only approximate. Soil approximately 11cm black organic muck over silty clay loam to 50cm over silty clay.

Wet-mesic prairie between upland and lowland area. The west side of plot near old field (restored). Slightly bumpy microtopography approximately 10cm. At least 1 year since burn, no more than 3. Silty clay loam soil.
Prairie has not been burned in 1, maybe 2 years, not much thatch accumulation. Soil black clay-loam to > 45 cm.

Dry mesic prairie on south facing slope. Prairie narrow and bordered by agricultural fields; exotics a problem, especially at edges. Moderate thatch, 2-3 years since burn. Few gopher mounds. Moderate to well-drained soils. Soil a sandy loam with gravel and boulders.
Mesic prairie in CP Railroad Row. Releve plot 5x20 to avoid ditches and balast. Gopher mounds occasional. Few exotics in plot, but Phalaris dominates ditch. Few sedges.

Transition between mesic prairie and shrubby area. Plot inadvertantly strattles fire line; south half burned this spring, north half burned 1 or 2 years ago. 18 cm black sandy clay loam over silty sand. Poorly drained (wet sand).
Band of wet meadow between Typha swamp and shrubby area. Water table at surface, mucky substrate - organic and falls out of probe. Uneven tussock-like microtopographyy.

Shrub subtype of wet meadow (see rel #7910) between Typha swamp and aspen thicket. Water table near surface, but no puddles. Burnt stumps occasional, but thatch thick fire approximately 3+ years ago? Soils muck/organic.

Despite reports saying wetland area relative undisturbed, I found it to be disturbed, overabundance of Helianthus grosseserratus, Poa pratensis and small patches of reed canary give site disturbed feel. Plot located in better area. Thick thatch. Water table at approximately 75cm.

Wetter area than releve #7912 with different sedge dominants. Water table closer to surface and microtopography much more tussock-like. Forb component strongly dominated by Helianthus grosseserratus and Eutrochium maculatum, which is typical for site. Water table at 65cm or so. Soil clay loam over loamy clay.

Mesic (dry-mesic?) prairie on gentle slope to Typha marsh. Prairie hayed in the past (for approximately 100 years) and has a timothy presence. Gopher mounds common in site and plot. Thatch moderate, 1-2 years since burn. Friable soils. Soil silty loam over clay loam over sandy clay with mottles.

Wet prairie has approximately 100 years of haying (see SNA file). Wetter area in general a bit forby. This plot typical of the band around Typha marsh. Thick to moderate thatch, burned 2-3 years ago. Few sedges present. 50-60cm dark clay loam over sandy clay with mottles.

Third releve at Lundblad to document community of wet depression in upland (away from Typha marsh) in northeast corner, which may not have been hayed as often. Moderate thatch. Fewer forbs than #7615, nicer. Soil silty clay loam over loamy clay.
Wet prairie in large depression in rolling hill complex surrounded by mesic to dry prairie. Plot: thick thatch, several years since last burn. Gopher mounds occasional.

Dry mesic prairie on west southwest facing slope, just west of small lake. Soil gravelly, some scattered boulders. Little thatch. Gopher mounds occassional. Soil: difficult to probe, 6cm dark brown loam over sandy loam.

Sedge dominated area in a complex of Typha and Phalaris. Some of sedge meadow dominated by Helianthus gross, this area is not. Soils so wet, fall out of probe. Organic. Tussocky, water table at surface.

Forb and sedge dominated community between sedge meadow and broamy lower slope of hill. Few native grasses. Two different orchids. Water table at 70cm. Silty clay muck, over 60cm of heavy clay with silt and sand. A horizon depth: 10cm.

Wet meadow surrounding Typha swamp in northwest corner of wildlife management area. No standing water, but ground is wet. Fairly thick thatch, at least 2 years since last burn. Carex lanuginosa more common than in releve #7919.

Prairie calcareous seepage fen. Springy bulge on west facing slope of wide shallow valley contained in wildlife management area. Upslope from releve is a small patch of Typha, below is a slight depression with standing water and marl. Soil is muck with sand, falls out of probe. Probe stops at 75cm. Fairly thick thatch, puddles have duckweed.

Releve typical of area between Typha marsh and sedge meadow at site. 4-6cm of standing water. Clay containing layer approximately 50cm below surface. Having little experience in this type of community I do not know if actually represents mixed emergent area or not.

Typical of band of wet meadow between Typha area and more disturbed upland. Like other southern wet meadows, this one has large areas of Helianthus grosseserratus--releve placed to capture. Very thick thatch, has not been burned in several years. Soil 5cm organic over black clay loam over black loamy clay, water table at 20cm.

Releve typical of band surrounding slight depressions on the fairly flat wildlife management area. Site apparently has history of grazing and haying (EOR) and this may account for strong Helianthus grosseserratus and Poa pratensis component. Soil silty clay loam over loamy clay.

Wet prairie dominated by Spartina and Andropogon gerardii. Area burned every spring and combined every fall. With Todd and Sara Hawbaker. Soil 20cm clay loam over 40cm loamy clay over brown mottling clay.

Area dominated by Panicum virgatum, sedges, and Andropogon gerardii with component of Liatris pycnostachya. Soil 20cm of black clay loam over 40cm loamy clay over light brown sandy clay. Burned this spring, combined for seed every fall.

A somewhat overgrown calacareous fen on west facing slope below Lespedeza(bush clover) monitoring grid. Fen is being encroached from all sides: Phalaris and shrubs. At 50cm heavy clay/sand impeding layer; above rather viscous layer of clay, sand, organic matter and water.
Species-rich dry prairie on hills overlooking Des Moines River. Relatively thick thatch and last years stems, several years since last fire. Soils: sandy loam with gravel - could not probe farther.

Odd-overgrown fen on west facing hillside along the Des Moines River. Releve requested by NPS. Plot elongated to avoid margins. Standing water at surface-hummocky sandy clay with organic matter, gets thicker with depth. Plot size is 6.6 x 15.

Small kidney-shaped fen on south southwest facing slope along Des Moines River. 75% graminoid cover. Some areas have moderately-sized marly pools with rank water. Edges are being encroached by exotics, shrubs, and Typha.

A rather depauperate fen on toe slope of exotic-covered hills. Grades from slender band of wet meadow (also in draws) to a Typha marsh. Marly pools occasional. Many deer trails cross wetland complex. Sandy/gravel confining layer at 45cm.

Flat wet meadow at the foot hills of the Yellow Bank Hills. Grades into a Typha marsh, and uphill into a forb dominated area. Very thick thatch. 15cm of organic loam, clay content increases until 50cm, which is black clay.

A somewhat disturbed wet prairie community at base of Yellow Bank Hills. Over dominance of Aster ericoides, Aster lanceolatum, Solidago canadensis, and presence of exotic grass point to disturbance in past. Thick thatch, needs burn. Soil black sandy loam over tan sand with mottles over clayey sand impeding layer.
Wet-mesic prairie in a gentle depression in Glynn Prairie complex. Moderate litter, at least 1-2 years since burn. Somewhat species poor, grazing history. Soil probe stopped at 20cm.

Mesic prairie on the shoulder of a southwest-facing slope. Drier than #7937 and also more disturbed site. Prairie has haying history. Moderate thatch; approximately 2 years since last burn. Soil dark brown loam, probe stops at 20cm.
Ungrazed dry prairie fragment along bend in road through preserve. Some exotic invasion, especially in the draws of hills. Relatively thin litter - burned last year.

Dry-mesic prairie in relatively undisturbed area of Blue Mounds State Park. Area has light grazing history. Releve farther upland with somewhat different forb composition than #6644. Area burned this spring.

D. Hagamen called this "very good" but I would call it fair or possibily good for RR survey. ROW quite disturbed and dominated by exotic grasses. Little litter-burned recently? Herbicide damage, especially compass plants.

Small, but incredibly diverse mesic prairie on west-facing slope. Thin litter, probably burned last year. Few exotics, but abundance of Helianthus rigida indicates some past disturbance. Not many insects. Could not probe soil.
Small prairie remnant at an intersection with railroad tracks. Old field adjacent. Thick litter. Remainder of ROW Phalaris. Railroad ROW survey 19. County now owns Nobles-Rock RR ROW.

A wet-mesic prairie in railroad and highway ROW dominated by native grasses, but there are exotics and red clover. Railroad land much more forb rich than DOT because of mowing. Thin litter. Many beetles and lepidoptera species.

Small piece of wet or wet-mesic prairie along an otherwise disturbed railroad ROW. Hagamen called this a "very good"; again I would call it fair-except for this tiny section. 5x20m plot. RR survey #91.
Area between wet-mesic uplands and wet meadow lowlands. Sedge component probably more diverse and abundant, spring releves needed. Thick litter. Impenetrable layer of grey clay/sand at 75cm.
Mesic prairie 75m east of the wet prairie releve (#7948). Somewhat rapid releve because of impeding storm (no soils).  On crest of gentle slope. Moderate to thick litter.
Wet-mesic prairie in railroad ROW-probably the nicest active stretch in area. Moderate litter layer. Tractor tire tracks through the center of the prairie.

Paper birch forest on northeast face of tall hardwood ridge. Pebbles, cobbles in tip-ups in plot and on ridgetop (tip-ups birch, lying south southeast). Note fir and pine seedlings. Ridgetop very sedgy. Fairly far from trail.
Prairie has a significant component of Poa pratensis and is in need of a burn. Disturbance increasers common.
Dry prairie on the shoulder slope of the west facing valley of Big Stone Lake. Burned this spring. Grey loamy substrate with gravel and rocks. Topographic context crest/upper.
Mesic prairie amongst cornfield, lake, and disturbed areas. Prairie needs a burn, very thick litter. Exotics occasional. Gopher mounds. Soil is grey loam.

Diverse wet-mesic prairie in ROW along highway 56 and old railroad bed. Area somewhat shrubby/overgrown (?) and it was difficult to determine coverage. 6cm organic mud over 20cm of mottled grey sandy clay over 30cm coarse white sand with mottles over orange sandy clay. A horizon depth: 6cm

Broad strip of alder between semi-terrestrial black ash on both sides. Drains imperceptibly to northwest. Water to several inches in troughs. Sphagnum scattered, only on high hummocks. No stumps or fire evident. Surrounding communities ground cover is much more dominated by sphagnum than here. Larix laricina and Picea mariana DBH approximately 10cm or smaller. Soil: undecomposed peat.

Mature aspen with spruce and fir understory. Canopy trees are 20-30cm DBH. Fair amount coarse woody debris, but mostly smaller stuff. No stumps. Scattered boulders. Relatively inaccessible stand, east of Greenwood Lake. Few if any trails visible on photo. Grades to black spruce with sphagnum. Soil silty sand.
Mesic prairie in the southern portion of Cartney wildlife management area. On a very gentle slope toward a small creek. Thin litter, probably burned last year.

Mesic prairie in abandoned railroad ROW. Diverse area (burned this year). Some places rank with Ambrosia trifida and disturbance increasers, such as Solidago canadensis. Releve in higher quality area in this section - did not look at much of Scientific and Natural Area since all entrances are are rand with woodies and urtica.
Mesic prairie on flat active railroad ROW between tracks and ditch of highway 218. Thick litter and much herbicide damage. See also railroad ROW survey #495.
A somewhat rank area in the north part of Scientific and Natural Area. Somewhat thick litter-burned 2-3 years ago.

Plot typical of mesic boreal on ridges; located specifically to include ridge and has northeast aspect as well. Out with Aitkin county - Mark Jacobs, John Almendinger, and Bruce Carlson. Signifigant blowdown from 95 in stand. Charred stumps. A horizon: 5cm.

Specifically placed in transition between northern harwdoods and semi-terrestrial ash. Out with Aitkin county - Mark Jacobs, John Almendinger, and Bruce Carlson. At 2m higher than water table in adjacent ash swamp, 2 chroma grey mottles at BC (saturated).

Out with Bob-Aitkin county; 3-4 old stumps, = pine? (1930's type map says this is conifer) Presence of decaying logs, large blowdown tree. Half of plants are northern hardwood, other half of plants are dry mesic pine/oak forest. Early 60's cut pine?

Between 2 small Calamagrostis wetlands (to east and west). Many dead fir logs (natural mortality). Stand may have resulted from some type of disturbance. Hunter trail running along releve border with few cut stumps. Out with Bob, Aitkin county. Deciduous litter with a mix of conifer. Humus is a fungal mat.

Is within a narrow jack pine strip - road on one side, clear cut on the other. Picked this site because Aitkin county wanted it done. Small coarse woody debris - not very abundant. Out with Dan and Joe - Aitkin county. Litter mostly needles.

Can also be dry-mesic pine. Placed to capture half open conifer, half less dense understory/more deciduous component overstory (typical of entire stand). 53 inch DBH red pine. Some cut pine stumps. Earthworms in mineral layer. Out with Dan and Joe - Aitkin county.

Located on ridge to sample on predetermined soil type. Blown-down with pine branches, large diameter blowdown with pine and balsam snags-patchy disturbance. Plot located northeast of beaver dam-wetland areas. Moss collected. Litter a mix of hardwood and conifer.

Represents surrounding aspen type-avoided spot of stand with no aspen. Coarse woody debris of balsam branches. Found red back salamanders. Out with Mark Jacobs and Dan of Aitkin County. Not familiar with moss species taxonomy. Soil is 16cm sand over 20+cm sand with orange and black mottles. A horizon: 3cm.

Stand near forest road. Picked by Aitkin county to represent aspen type. Several large aspen ~40-50 years old. Large limbs of aspen and one balsam snag on ground, otherwise small coarse woody debris throughout releve. A horizon: 6cm. Soil: gray sandy silt over sandy silt with orange mottles.

Northwest side of forest road, area chosen by Aitkin county. North corner of releve has blowdown fir, South corner near black spruce blowdown - both recent (green). Pit-mound topography. Also could be mesic oak type. No human disturbance. Thin litter of mostly leaves with some needles. A horizon: 4cm. Soil: 3cm grey sand over orange sand.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Typical of surrounding hardwood stand. Earthworms present. Many tip-up mounds often where birch grow. No cut/burned stumps. Out with Bob-Aitkin county. Could be Dry Pine type. Moderate amount small coarse woody debris. Logged 60-70 years ago. A horizon: 4cm. Soil rocky, orange sand.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Once was burned in 1918 Cloquet fire, many downed logs, large coarse woody debris. Some blowdown has opened small gaps throughout stand. Many large downed rotted birch and red oak logs. Located east of pine plantation. A horizon: 3.5cm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Much pit-mound topography, many old logs have created mounds. Large trees have succumbed to windfall in last year, but are still semi-standing and alive. Parts of site have shallow bedrock layer <10cm from surface. Difficult to penetrate 10-20cm - rocky/hard layer. Soil light brown clay sand, forming when wet. A horizon depth: 5cm. 69cm DBH Betula alleghaniensis.

Near beaver dam, near recently thinned hardwood stand. Charcoal and burnt big pine stumps (when red pine originated). Stand approximately 90 years old. Downed aspen logs, medium sized coarse woody debris. Could also be hardwood type. With Dan and Joe - Aitkin county. Mixed litter. Soil coarse tan sand >20cm. A horizon depth: 3cm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Entire releve on top of glacial deposit ridge running northwest-southwest and grading into swamps on either side (so releve also has northwest aspect). East of a recently thinned hardwood stand. Many pits-mounds. Gravel layer and 20cm. Soil coarse silty sand. A horizon depth: 2.5cm.

Along same ridge as #8022, lower slope class. Burnt pine stumps present. Downed birch logs throughout plot (clinker conk), also down fir logs. Tiny earthworms. Could also be mesic oak. With Dan and Joe - Aitkin county. Mixed litter. Soil: gray sand over coarse sand. A horizon depth: 1cm.

Burnt stumps. Most pine in releve = 40 years. Some pine in surrounding stand have burn scars, maybe approximately 100 years old. Some downed balsam in plot medium-sized coarse woody debris. Could also be mesic oak type. Out with Aitkin county. Litter of pine needles with some deciduous. Soil: 3cm dark tan sand over 4cm light tan sand over orange tan sand.

Presence of large burnt pine stumps in surrounding stand. Charcoal layer in soil. Downed balsam - due to old age and rot. Small branches = coarse woody debris. Mixed litter. Soil light tan coarse sand over orange tan coarse sand. A horizon depth: 1cm.

Presence of small diameter cut stumps present, and old downed logs with moss. Typical of surrounding stand that has open patchy spots. South of wetland. Presence of Armillaria root rot. Soil coarse orange sand with few small orange mottles and slight clay component. A horizon depth: 1cm.

Much balsam fir blowdown in stand, standing dying balsam fir in plot. 1 blowdown white pine. Blowdown=patchy areas. Soil has gravelly air pockets at >5 cm. At top of slope that heads downhill north-northeast. At south-southeast of gravel pit. SOil very coarse sand with gravel. A horizon depth: 1.5cm.

Typical of surrounding hardwood stand. North of wetland, south of pine plantation. "Messy" due to much old blowdown aspen, thick understory, patchy open areas of blowdown. Edges seem disturbed near management; narrow strip. A horizon depth: 1.5cm.

Releve part of series capturing patterns on CIR 10-16-92. E4 Larix slightly more abundant throughout than releve shows. Numerous deer and bear (?) trails. Not floating. Standing water in footprints only. Soil is sedge and moss peat.

Plot captures 30-40m band between alder swamp and Larix swamp. On thick mat. Plot within 30m of upland and 20m of Larix swamp. Purpose was to capture fen dominated by graminoids rather than ericaceous shrubs.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Worms below litter and in humus. Plot <15m from swamp inclusion. Scattered old stumps with fire scars. Slender-medium coarse woody debris common. Some recent windthrow. Microtopography varies between rather open/sparse low spots and rather densely covered high and mid points. More Acer saccharum throughout than plot shows, but is never the dominant tree. Soil wet to 1m+ after heavy rain. A horizon depth: 4cm.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Within basin including Larix and Thuja patches and shrub swamp. No cut stumps. Numerous large blowdowns near plot, mostly Thuja, some ash. Muck holes often >50cm, with standing water. Bimodal DBHs: 35-45cm and 22-30cm. Soil is woody peat and muck.

20-acre Thuja swamp surrounded by shrub swamp, tamarack swamp, black ash and lowland hardwood. Rare community type for Mille Lacs Uplands. Scattered cut Thuja stumps throughout. Coarse woody debris common-abundant with all decay stages. Muck holes firm. Ditch 1/4 mile west in same basin.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Plot 40 feet above wetlands, approximatley 150m to north, west, and east. Scattered recent cut stumps northeast of plot. Many recent D6-7 Betula papyrifera and Populus tremuloides blowdowns. No signs of fire. Well-decayed coarse woody debris rare throughout. Hollows with water after heavy rains. Soil: silt loam with fine sand over sandy loam. A horizon depth: 1cm.

Within 40m of wetland and <5 feet above. Small island surrounded by black ash swamp and wet meadow. Plot at perimeter of island, slightly higher than interior which has rich mesic maple basswood. Plot captures outside perimeter. No sign of fire. Occasional old cut stumps. Slender to medium coarse woody debris common, recent large blowdowns occasional. soil loamy sand with few pebbles. A horizon depth: 5cm.

On level terrace <3 feet below high point of stand. Wetland species found only in occasionally wet low spots. Stand within 200m and <20 feet above conifer and open water wetlands. Scattered open-grown red oak in vicinity of the plot and west towards the OW. Slender-medium coarse woody debris common with all decay stages represented. Large coarse woody debris restricted to recent blowdowns of primarily Populus tremuloides and Betula papyrifera. Soil fine to medium reddish brown sand. A horizon depth: 8cm. Topographic context: upper/flat.

On broad level plain between 2 flowages, <10 feet above water. Slender trees wtih occasional open-grown Quercus macrocarpa. Slender-medium coarse woody debris common. Recent blowdowns occasional/abundant. Large old pine stumps with fire scars. Worm activity throughout entire community. Soil a very fine light silt with orange mottles over clay loam with orange mottles over sandy clay loam. A horizon depth: 4cm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: On small knoll and upper-mid slope to north, west, and south. Rolling terrain typical of community. Fire scars on older coarse woody debris and stumps. Cut pine stumps occasional. Acer saccharum seedlings patchy to continuous. Large coarse woody debris uncommon. Microtopography variable with shallow and deep bowls and with frequent, small ephemeral wetlands. Soil grey, soft loess (silt) over very soft rusty brown and tan loess/silt. Litter of 65% needles and 35% leaves.

Plot within 400m of Lake Mille Lacs. Largest Larix and Picea appear open grown. Recent cutting in northwest corner of stand, associated with deer hunting stand. On peat >70cm. Varies between pure stand of Pinus banksiana and Picea mariana and the mixed community capture in this plot.

Part of series capturing dominant patterns on CIR 10-16-92. Thick floating mat. Standing water only in footprints. Thin sphagnum carpet throughout, much covered by graminoid litter. Easy walking for community type. Sparse litter of Carex and Eriophorum.

Within 100m of wetland and <15 feet above. Medium and slender coarse woody debris. Stumps +/- burn scars. Multi-aged stand. Tornado passed through area ~100m south of plot ~2 years ago. A horizon depth: 5cm.
Releve done to characterize later-successional lowlnd hardwood-conifer forest. With Aitkin Co. foresters and Jessica Wahlquist. Numerous winter-cut stumps, mostly cedar. Mosses restricted to wood.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Releve typical of mesic stand of red-oak. With Aitkin county Forestry and Jessica Wahlquist. Stand recently thinned.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Basswood Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Plot typical of semiterrestrial Black Ash. With Aitkin Co. Foresters. Plot positioned in drain between two upland white cedar groves.
Releve typical of jack pine areas on Hay Point. North Hill City DNR & history may include old-filed/pasture, but now notice regular charcoal abundance.
Typical of declining jack pine on Hay Point. Possibly old-field recolonized by jack pine. Sand w/ standing water approx 32".

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Releve typical of 1st non-flooding terrace of Lowland Hardwoods. Silty alluvial soils with standing water at 48" -no recent flooding. Duff removed by earthworms.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Typical of first non-flooding terrace w/ Lowland Hardwoods. Small channel in plot. Plot NNW of Forestry Station bar, Jacobsen. Soils banded silty/sandy loam alluvium w/ standing water at 50".
Plot typical of MDL Rich Hardwood forest. With Aitkin Co. staff. Photos. No worm activity. Very homogeneous plot.
Releve typical of N. Hardwoods on rises in matrix of lowland hardwood forests. Dense ??  & Cl Bt, standing water aoubt 6" in tip-up holes, but dry below pan. Worms infrequent.
Releve typical of black ash drains in water coming across dense hardpan of surrounding rises. Deer stand w/ lanes just W of plot about 100 yds. Soils silty/gravelly/clay-banded. Worms removd duff

Small area, but since this comm on sand is not well represented on the Rove study area it was sampled. Older trees and marked to be harvested. Site hit by the July 4th storm and since harvested/salvaged(?). A horizon: 6+cm. Litter of needles, sticks, and leaves.

Slope is basically boulders and rock covered with mosses and/or organics. Approximately 8 cm of organics, duff, and litter to dark brown sandy loam with boulders and rock. Litter of needles, leaves, and pine bark. Pine older-mostly all living. Several downed Pinus/Abies.

Betula papyrifera DBH 14-27cm, Picea mariana DBH 14-20cm, Abies balsimifera DBH 8 and 20cm, Thuja DBH 7-16cm. Soil rusty brown fine loam, lots of charcoal present. Litter of leaves, needles, and twigs. Slope is rock, cobble, forested, and cover with moss and organics intermixed between boulder/rock to varying depths.
Site near clifftop in greater area of mixed Pinus/Populus/Betula. Soil is sandy loam between broken rock and bedrock. Litter of needles and leaves. Topographic context: crest/upper.

Variety of white pine with partial dead upper branches/tops; assorted dead Abies; small patch of unvegetated cobble. Soil is brown gray loam with very little sand. Litter of leaves and needles. Populus tremuloides DBH 19-31cm, Abies balsimifera DBH 19-22cm, Betula papyrifera DBH 11-24cm, Pinus strobus DBH 28-84cm.

Thuja swamp intermixed with Picea mariana/Abies balsamea. Some areas with more open Picea - lots of Carex gynocrates (locally abundant). A horizon depth 15cm of sapric peat. Litter of cedar leaves/needles/twigs.
Shrub/Carex wetland between stream and Larix/spruce swamp. Standing water: ankle deep. Depth of organics unknown. Litter of leaves and twigs.
Basically shallow soils over bedrock. South facing. Site stands out on photos. Pinus resinosa DBH 24-39cm, Picea glauca DBH 10-21cm, Pinus banksiana DBH 24-30cm.

Surface partially buried, scattered rock/boulders. Soils under varying depths of litter and organic chocolate brown loam. Litter of needles, cones, and branches. Pinus strobus DBH 41-70cm, Thuja occidentalis DBH 40cm, Pinus resinosa DBH 50-66cm.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Rock outcrop with/o shallow soils. Crest of south facing slope. Several large white pine blown over from recent windstorm. Golden fungus fingers abundant (Clavariadelphus ligula?) beneath Red pine. Some limited charcoal in soil, no fire scars on trees. Litter of needles and cones.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Organic decaying branches with gold mychor. South facing slope with exposed rock common; shallow organic and mineral to rock. Some charcoal present. Scattered larger trees down in stand due to storm damage, 4 July 1999. Litter of pine needles and branches.

Soils-fair litter/organics depth over misc rocks; organics with gold mycorrhizae. No obvious charcoal in soil. Plot 75-100 yards from lake on north shore. Possible Suillus pictus fungi on site! Litter of needles, sticks, and pine bark.

Charcoal in organic layer at approximately 4 cm. Mycorrhizae in organics-mineral soil fine. Some conifer windtoss-exposing bedrock. Areas outside plot more brushy. Pinus resinosa DBH 19-39cm, Pinus strobus DBH 33-46cm. Litter of pine needles and pine bark.
Black spruce swamp - swamp with wind toss as a result of July 4th storm. Wind toss variable. Very sparse litter of small sticks.
Shrub/graminoid swamp. Betula glandulifera common in swamp but uncommon in Rove Land Type Association. Organic soil. Litter of graminoids, sticks, and leaves.

Thuja swamp. Moderate amount downed trees (not recent). Sphagnum with moderately dense vegetation. Very little litter and humus. Litter of leaves and a few twigs. +/- deep peat. Scattered balsam long dead. Depth of standing water 0-14cm.

Red oak dominated mesic forest on moraine ridge. Oak mode DBH 25-40cm. No max size. Diverse canopy with gap phase species. Coarse woody debris common, tip-ups and limbs. Level to slightly undulating with well drained depressions. Boulders common. Stand typical of dense oak stand. Soil is gray silt with pebbles over clayey red silt; rock/boulder layer at >35cm. Topographic context: crest/upper.
Mostly level poorly drained site dominated by Carex lasiocarpa and Salix gracilis. Peat soils near surface (no soil sampled).
Sandy loam soil.
Soil: approximately 7 cm medium dark brownsh gray fine sand, turning light yellowish brown fine sand. On very slightly convex surface in gently undulating part of sand blanket.

Soil: approximately 4 cm dark blackish-brown loamy sand over medium dark brownish-gray loamy sand. At approximately 10 cm pure, fine sand, orange-brown. Plot seems grading towards mesic conditions. Alnus incana occasional.
Small depressional wetland surrounded by aspen woods. Close to being shrub swamp.
Mesic brush prairie (sand gravel). Sandy loam, or loamy sand. Very stony. Tree-size bur oak 5-7 m high, widely scattered. Grazed previous year.
Soil sandy loam, apparently calcareous based on vegetation. Probably grazed in past. Wet-mesic conditions.
Rich fen. Very thick, spongy "duff" (?) layer, then approximately 20cm sapric peat, but with brown fibrous material in parts, over dark blackish sand.

Rich fen. Area with shrub component. Approximately 20 cm sapric peat dark brownish-black, quite a bit of fibrous stuff. Under this 5 or so cm dark, blackish sand, then yellowish-brown sand. No spongy duff layer.
Rich fen. Central area, shrub-free. Approximately 35cm decomposed peat, lots of brownish fibrous stuff, below this medium dark brownish gray sand.
NA
Burned in wildfire Spring 90 or Fall 89. In intricate mosaic with wet brush prairie. Plot not actually measured out, but estimated by pacing.
Burned in wildfire Spring 90 or Fall 89. In intricate mosaic with wet- mesic brush prairie. Plot not actually measured out, but estimated by pacing.
In clearly delineated level band trending northwest. Flanked by denser brush on higher ground. Burned in spring.
Rounded crest of dune form.
In small area of dune-forms, on lower dune slope next to aspen-brush swale.
Soil loamy sand or sandy loam; boulders exposed at surface. Gently undulating topography (outwash?). Releve plot size approximate; not actually marked out. In open prairie surrounded by woods.

Soil loamy sand or sandy loam with stones. Gently undulating topography (outwash?). Releve plot size approximate, not actually marked out. Releve in small open savanna area, surrounded by advancing aspen.
Heavy thatch; numerous pools of water several cm deep; pH=7. Soil: several cm black sandy loam, over dark gray sandy loam, over light gray sandy loam, turning yellowish; slightly sticky.
Soil: Approximately 10 cm black loam over light gray sandy clay loam, some gravel; becoming yellow. Saturated at surface. Wet-mesic brush prairie.
Mostly level area on sand; some small dunes (well-developed dunes just a bit northwest). Probably grazed in past.

Releve to show dry cliff/bedrock knob community on top edge of ledge rock. Forest on top is jack pine/black spruce. Approximately 50% exposed rock with lichen/moss cover where partially shaded. Trees stunted.
Rich sedge fen. Saturated sapric peat, approximately 30 cm thick, over dark gray sand. Gravel at about 50 cm. In relatively shrub-free zone. Scattered small dead Salix shrubs (fire?).

Rich shrub fen. Some free water on surface. Substrate soupy muck, fibrous at surface and then again further down, approximately 33 cm thick, over dark brownish-gray sand. Surface water pH=7.4. In shrubbier part of fen. Plot area only approximate.
Extensive swamp on muck--seepage influenced. Substrate very black sapric peat, with some marl (?). Plot not actually measured out.

Level area on broad beach ridge(Glacial Lake Agassiz) just east of slightly higher, gently convex crest. Soil: 10-12 inches black loamy sand, then several inches dark brown loamy coarse sand, then previous with gravel.
Narrow meadow at base of beach ridge. Substrate black sapric peat at least 60cm thick. Three ponds excavated in meadow just south of releve. Plot not actually marked out.
Small open area on crest of glacial lake beach ridge with bur oak margins. Soil loamy coarse sand, much gravel at 20cm.

Lightly grazed pasture idle at time. Soil: sandy loam, dark brownish-black becoming dark gray; at 30cm, lighter yellowish gray sandy loam. One of 3 releves close together; transitional between wet-mesic and wet.

Lightly grazed pasture, idle at time. Soil: approximately 6cm very dark loam, then dark brownish gray loam. At approximately 15 cm, dark gray sandy clay loam over yellowish gray sandy clay loam. 1 of 3 plots to capture subtle variability.

Lightly grazed pasture, idle at time. Hummocky within plot. Soil: 5 cm very dark brownish black loam, then dark gray sandy clay loam; abrupt change at approximately 30cm to coarse yellowish sand. 1 of 3 plots to capture variation.
Wet-mesic. Evidence of recent light grazing. Burned (wildfire) past spring or fall. Gopher mounds suggest sandy loam soil. Plot area estimated; not measured out.
Wet-mesic; evidence of recent light grazing. Burned in wildfire past spring or previous fall. Plot area estimated, not actually measured out.

Ground water discharge zone at base of glacial lake beach ridge; 5-7cm free water (flowing) on surface. Peat (muck) depth >0.6m (length of soil probe). State ditch forms lower body of seepage zone. Plot area estimated.

Ground-water discharge zone at base of glacial lake beach ridge: 7-10cm free water on surface. In area where flow ponded by state ditch spoil below seep zone. Peat (muck) > 0.6m (length of soil probe). Plot area estimated.
Low flat in small prairie remnant. Soil approximately 8 cm black loam. Under this very dark brownish gray fine sandy loam or loamy fine sand, slightly sticky; blocky structure.
Small high quality prairie remnant on lower-most shoreline of glacial lake Agassiz. A number of small boulders at surface.
Nearly level, slightly convex area in small remnant of beach ridge prairie. Evidence of long ago grazing (fallen down fence).
Nearly level, slightly concave area in small remnant of beach ridge prairie. Evidence of long-ago grazing (fallen down fence).
Dry prairie opening on Juniperus virginiana wooded hillside.
Rich deciduous woodland bordering the Minnesota River. On top of shaded rock outcrops.
Rock outcrop on the surface of west facing, steep-sloped, granite gneiss boulder; in shade. Shade subtype? (2.5m x 2.5m plot).
On surface of granite gneiss outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. (2.5m x 2.5m plot).
On surface of south facing, steep-sloped granitic boulder; in shade. (2.5m x 2.5m plot).
Dry prairie opening on Juniperus virginiana wooded hillside and strewn with boulders.
Flat, mesic prairie.
On surface of granite gneiss outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. (2.5m x 2.5m plot).
Dry prairie on summit of moderate, east-facing, gravelly slope.
On surface of rock outcrop; in full sunlight. (2.5m x 2.5m plot)
Dry prairie opening on moderate, southwest-facing Juniperus virginiana wooded slope and strewn with granite boulders.
Dry prairie on moderate, northwest-facing, gravelly slope.
Mesic prairie on edge of Pomme de Terre Valley.
On surface of a nearly vertical, east-facing granitic boulder in dry-mesic prairie. (2.5m x 2.5m plot).
On surface of granite gneiss outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. 1 of 2 microhabitats sampled at this location. (2.5m x 2.5m plot).
Fissure on granite gneiss outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. #2 of 2 microhabitats sampled at this location. (3m x 0.2m plot). (fissure of GAW97-42).
Mesic prairie on moderate east-facing slope.
On surface of granite gneiss outcrop; in full sunlight. #1 of 2 microhabitats sampled at this location. (2.5m x 2.5m plot).
In fissure of granite gneiss outcrop; in full sunlight. #2 of 2 microhabitats sampled on this location. (4.8m x 0.25m plot). (fissure of GAW 97-46).
Dry, rocky prairie on top of ridge formed by basalt dike.
In dry-mesic prairie between rock outcrops; in full sunlight. (10m x 10m plot) On shallow soils over Morton gneiss outcrop.
In floodplain forest bordering the Minnesota River.
On surface of granite gneiss outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. (2.5m x 2.5m plot).
On surface of granite gneiss outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. (2.5m x 2.5m plot).
On surface of quartzite outcrop; exposed to full sunlight.  (2.5m x 2.5m plot).
On surface of Jordan Sandstone outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. 1st of 3 microhabitats sampled at this location. (plot size 2.5m x 2.5m = 6.25 square meters).

Margin of Jordan Sandstone outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. 2nd of 3 microhabitats sampled at this location. On shallow soil over sandstone (margin of GAW 98-04). (Plot size is 4.2m x .6m = 2.5 square meters).
In mesic prairie on shallow soil over sandstone between rock outcrop exposures; in full sunlight. 3rd of 3 microhabitats sampled at this location.
On surface of quartzite outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. (2.5m x 2.5m plot = 6.25 square meters).
On surface of quartzite outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. 1st of 2 microhabitats sampled at this location. (2.5m x 2.5m plot = 6.25 square meters).

In fissure of quartzite outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. 2nd of 2 microhabitats sampled at this location. In shallow soil over quartzite (fissure of GAW 99-02). (Plot size 2.7m by .26m = .7 square meters).
Summit of south facing terrace, on rock surface of quartzite outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. 1st of 2 microhabitats sampled at this site. (2.5m x 2.5m plot = 6.25 square meters).

Summit of southfacing terrace, in fissure of quartzite outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. 2nd of 2 microhabitats sampled at this location. (fissure of GAW 99-04) In shallow soil over quartzite. (plot size 3.8m x .21m = .8 square meters).
On surface of quartzite outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. 1st of 2 microhabitats sampled at this location. (2.5m x 2.5m plot = 6.25 square meters).

In fissure of quartzite outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. 2nd of 2 microhabitats sampled at this location. In shallow soil over quartzite (fissure of GAW 99-06) (Plot location 4.2m x .22m = .9 square meters).
On surface of quartzite outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. 1 of 3 microhabitats sampled at this location. (2.5m x 2.5m plot = 6.25 square meters).
In shallow soil along fissure of quartzite outcrop; exposed to full sunlight. 2nd of 3 microhabitats sampled at this location. (fissure of GAW 99-08) (Plot size 4.2m x .22m = .9 square meters).
In shallow soil over rock margin of quartzite exposure; exposed to full sunlight. 3rd of 3 microhabitats sampled at this location. (margin of GAW 99-08). Plot size: 5m x .6m = 3 square meters.
Dry prairie on moderate, southwest-facing slope; with some gravelly spots.
In wet-mesic prairie strip, adjacent to railroad tracks, in slight depression. Focus on Agalinus auriculata habitat.
Carex stricta dominated stand in wetland complex. Soil is decayed sedge material.
Carex trichocarpa dominated stand in wetland complex. Soil is decayed sedge material.
Carex stricta dominated stand in wetland complex. Soil is decayed sedge material.
Bullrush/cattail dominated stand in wetland complex.
Phragmites stand in wetland complex.
Spartina/sedge dominated stand in wet meadow. On terrace in Glacial River Warren Valley.
Sedge dominated stand in moist meadow. On terrace in Glacial River Warren Valley. Soil is decayed sedge material.
In mesic prairie strip, adjacent to railroad tracks. Purpose of releve is to describe Agalinus habitat.
On black muck as deep as I could dig by hand (8 inches) saturated to surface. Mapped location only very approximate.
Small shallow marsh in narrow slough, flanked by wet prairie. Most of upland cropped. Soil black muck 3-4 in deep, over black silty clay loam. Wet, but no surface water. Burned spring 99.
Releve is just E of the Northernmost part of the fullest curve of river & midpoint in releve is ~4-5m north of river @ its northernmost point.
Releve contains at least 6 dwarf trout lily colonies. Releve on toe slope and floodplain of tributary of Prairie Creek. Dark loamy soil with limestone. Some silt from floods. Summer releve #8245.
Releve between corners D&E and 4 and 5 of the DTL monitoring grid at RBNC. On east side of river, the area is shrubby and full of exotics. Ground flat with some micro-relief. See summer releve #8246.

On floodplain east of Prairie Creek. Plot centered on DTL colony north of fence. Large multi-stem Tilia and dense sapling layer. Soil loamy and silty with pieces of limestone. Much coarse woody debris. See summer releve #8247

Plot mid-slope in monitoring grid at NBWSP. There is much exposed soil and erosion. Litter layer relatively thin. Ground lumpy poss resulting from mammals. Some coarse woody debris. See summer releve #8248.

Population on west side of trail - many more than 8 plants reported in Ecological Occurrence Records. Dwarf trout lillies found on midslope to silted floodplain. Tributary channel to Prairie Creek. At toe slope coarse woody debirs, Phalaris. See releve #8249.

Hundreds of dwarf trout lillies in a draw, a very healthy population. Much erosion and coarse woody debris, including trees. Releve captures two large colonies. Steep slopes. Releve half in draw. See summer releve #8250.

Area where clones are stable to recovering. On the south-side of river and east side of tributary. Large tree fall adjacent to rocky stream bank. Heavy deer browse. Sparse litter, earthworms. See also #8251.
At least two colonies on mid to toe steep north facing slope. Large green ash and aspen at top of hill (above releve). Deer trails causing much erosion and browse. See Releve #8252.

Dwarf trout lilly (#16) common, but not dense along toe of gentle north facing slope and adj flood plain. Much erosion on slope. Recent treefall pinned several red elms down. Deer browse and exotics. See summer releve #8253.

Approximately 20 dwarf trout lilly on mid to toe slope on steep north facing slope between erosion area and old motor bike trail. Some lilies in trail. Moss covers ~25% of plot. Open species along eroded area. See releve #8254.
There are no Asarum canadense, Hepatica, or Claytonia virginica in plot.
Floating mat with no soil development, only organic material substrate of Thelypteris palustris and moss. Mucky peat at 16". Cold water. Onoclea sensibilis elsewhere, but not in releve.
North shore sugar maple forest at headwaters of Onion River. Dissected drainages, intermittent streams in repeating pattern throughout which is variation represented by this releve. Very wet soils.

Much large downed woody debris. Mesic spruce forest with spruce budworm-killed snags and blowdown. Selected to represent diversity of ground flora prior to natural disturbance and vegetation response to blowdown.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Possibly old growth. Open understory-large canopy gaps. On hill surrounded by wetlands-not likely impacted by management-except old logging road on north side. No earthworms-litter/humus intact. With Lawson Gerdes.
Possibly old growth. >30 contiguous acres, but more extensive in patches throughout conifer-shrub swamp. Large diameter cedar (>2ft.). In some spots water table at ground level.

Gently undulating terrain. Large and small downed woody debris. Vegetation reflects higher water table. Adjacent to areas impacted by human disturbance with cut aspen and planted white spruce-avoided areas for releve. Litter mostly hardwood some coniferous.
Represents riparian forest community in the Onion River watershed in transition zone down to river. Some large downed woody debris. Litter a mix of deciduous and coniferous.
Represents lowland conifer wetland complex in Barker Creek drainage near Frisk Lake. Water table at ground level-some areas of stagnant/standing water have algae growing.

Represents forested wetlands of Barker Creek watershed, but isolated from Barker Creek drainage system. Water table at ground level. Many downed logs and roots covered with Sphagnum. Topographic context: middle/flat.

Burned ~4 years ago. Some large oaks, Pinus serotina removed from plot; canopy now 40%. Adjacent to area cleared by hydro-ax, where canopy's now 20%. Few Zanthoxylum indicate probable grazing in past.
Road ditch right of way adjacent to railroad right of way. 17 Agalinis auriculata. Soil black loam. Wet mesic prairie remnant.
Wet mesic prairie depression along County Road 54.

place_name: Sherburn ROW I&M Rail Link LCC
remarks: Wet mesic prairie remnant on moderate slope between highway and railroad right-of-way along Martin Co 26. Topsoil removed to depth of 3" in 1999 exposing stony yellow clay.

Native grasses dominate 150 square meters of remnant,low diversity. Remainder is weedy, dominated by Quercus macropcarpa, Juniperus virginiana, Ostrya virginiana. High quality oak forest below bluff, more degraded above.

Diverse native graminoids dominate. Bromus, Poa have significant presence. Surrounding forest encroaching but tree/shrub cover in remnant is low. Nearby Zanthoxylum, L. tatarica indicate past grazing.
High quality mesic prairie between degraded calcerous seepage fen and degraded wet meadow. Soil core shows uniform dark clay loam down 20cm. Shrub cover higher than rest of prairie. Probably burned.

Earthworm castings throughout plot. Downed butternut (dead of canker) outside plot. Narrow corridor of rich bottomland forest in maple-basswood matrix. Associated community: mixed hardwood swamp, wet meadow.

Snag in plot. Coarse woody debris ~5% cover. In strip of rich bottomland forest downslope from maple-basswood forest to east, small stand mesic oak forest to west. Early stage garlic mustard invasion threatened.

Stand has prominent microrelief but little coarse woody debris. Equal size mixed hardwood swamp south of plot. Both part of narrow band of deciduous forest stretching 1.5 miles southwest-northeast. Degraded wetlands to east.

Site logged ca. once in past 60 years ago; thinned more recently. In 400+ acre Neds-Mud-Deer Lake natural area-mosaic of upland oak forest, lowland forest, wetlands. Dumping, paintball, litter, OHV activity.
In Neds-Deer-Mud Lake NA (upland oak forest, lowland forest, wetlands). Gaps in plot from 3-4 dead elms (typical of stand). Coarse wood debris is prominent. Possible grazing, raptor nest. Ant mound.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Area's been grazed. Oak forest and small maple-basswood stand to north. Small sand-gravel prairies in white-pine hardwood forest. Communities grading to mixed hardwood swamp and seepage fen near St. Croix River.

A horizon indistinguishable from soil #1. Plot at south end of band of black ash seepage swamp on west side of Lake Alice. It's downslope from maple-basswood forest (not mapped by MCBS) east of band's North e

Band of lowland hardwood forest east of Linwood Lake, upslope from narrow mixed emergent marsh. Marsh and wet meadow also in forest. White pine hardwood forest south of lake--small part adjacent to LH forest.

Soil gravelly; hard to insert probe. Pinus strobus density > than surrounding area. Stand along stream feeding into St. Croix River. Stands of white pine-hardwood forest in maple-basswood forest along river.

Stand along stream feeding into St. Croix River; among several white pine hardwood stands in linear band of maple-basswood forest along river for miles. Upland forests grade to floodplain forest and wetland.

Plot located to describe forested portion of larg undisturbed peatland, set among low hills of till plain. Headwaters of Mud Creek. Large population of Rubus chamaemorus. pH= 4.1 Spec. Cond.= 18, Absorb.= .800.
1 acre of linear wet meadow/rich fen swale meanders through shrub swamp. Deep organic soils. Historic ditches 100 meters away (now fallow). Recent wildfires have increased abundance of rare species.

Sedge meadow band between oak/aspen forest and Carex lasiocarpa-dominated rich fen. Inundated in spring. Saturated through most of growing season. Woodland was grazed to wetland (old B-wire fence at edge).
Marsh inundated for most of growing season; now drawn down. Avoided exposed muck. Mud flat 30 meters away. Dominated by Scirpus validus and S. smithii. Few openings for mudflat annuals to establish.

Very open marsh dominated by Scirpus smithii (and Typha angustifolia in places). Basin mostly drawn down in mid-Sept. Mudflat annual cover at its highest. Surrounded by oak forest with residential buildings.

Marsh on backwater pool of Rum River. Water level low (late season). Dominated by Scirpus fluviatilis. Between open water/unconsolidated bottom aquatic system and second growth silver maple floodplain forest.

Marsh on deep, saturated, sapric organic soil. Original CBS polygon be coming dominated by cattail. Exposed mudflat drawn down in late summer --15 meters to west. Releve in highest quality part of community.

Saturated emergent marsh between wet meadow and Scirpus fluviatilis-dominated emergent marsh. Areas inundated 3-4cm in August. Likely entirely inundated in spring. Higher diversity than River bullrush stands.

Marsh dominated by Scirpus fluviatilis on seasonally inundated silt loam with high organic material. Drawn down in August; soils saturated to surface. River bullrush stands less diverse than other openings.
Saturated wet meadow zone between oak savanna upland and semi-permanently flooded River bullrush-dominated emergent marsh. Community has features of wet meadow and emergent marsh.

Marsh between ditched/widened Rice Creek and expansive blue-joint-dominated wet meadow. Typha becoming more abundant. Area likely wet meadow before creek channelization; 10-30m band along creek is wetter.

Wet meadow/rich fen transition between oak/aspen woods and Carex lasiocarpa /D. arundinacea meadow. Isanti sand; 12cm organic/sand horizon. ORV disturbance (east edge) creates exposed sites for rare species.

High cover of low-growing deciduous shrubs. No recent disturbance. Dense grass/shrub layer shades out forbs and rare sand plain species. Likely grazed in past. Soil: Isanti on Lino/Isanti/Seeleyville continuum.

Poor fen surrounded by 2nd growth oak/apsen forest. 3-10m wide ring of Typha angustifolia around edge. Dominated by Carex oligosperma, Eriophorum angustifolium , Chamaedaphne calyculata. Sphagnum hummocks. Pronounced depression.

Shallow depression surrounded by 2nd growth oak/aspen forest. northwest corner of basin has higher coverage (5-25%) of Typha (cloned). Pronounced hummocks of Carex stricta and Sphagnum throughout basin.

Marsh on edge of large wetland complex between lowland hardwood forest and cattail marsh. Saturated sapric-organic soils. Drawn down in August but likely inundated 18-24cm in spring. Dense moss hummocks.

Forest along Minnesota River. Canopy: silver maple, american elm, green ash, cottonwood. Pronounced ridge and channels. Appears to flood each spring. Herb layer: native species and exotic agr. weeds. Many snags/logs.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: Hardwood swamp in 10-50m wide zone between dry oak forest and alder swamp. Frequent hummocks. Most trees <25cm DBH. Occasional down large to small trees. Soil moist, not saturated. Unusually dry year.
Part of 40 acre wetland complex. This area dominated by Carex lasiocarpa; ecotone between shrubby fen and cattail marsh. Sedge hummocks frequent.

Part of 40 acre wetland complex disturbed by ditches. Other parts of complex cattail marsh, Carex lasiocarpa-dominated fens, and aspen clumps. Plot location chosen for rare plant species concentration.

East shore of Island along side channel in St. Croix River. Grades to floodplain forest top of slope. Narrow mudflat zone along shore with Eleocharis, Leersia, other graminoids. Down trees in river and along shore.

Large island in St. Croix River. Plot has raised linear feature and parts of linear sloughs on both sides. Little woody litter. Occasional large snags outside plot. Island has emergent marsh to west, wet prairie to east.

Soil saturated. Water line on vegetation at ~40cm indicates flood level. Marshy point of island in protected bay in St. Croix River. Grades to floodplain forest. Little vegetation zonation except Eleocharis on edge.
5 acre poor fen grading to wet meadow then lake to south and upland forest to north. Hummocks of sphagnum moss. On peat >1m deep. Just north and west of boardwalk. Soil saturated.

Boardwalk runs through plot. Grades to wet meadow and marsh to south and west, up land forest to north and east. Plot with ~100 square meter patch Chamaedaphne grading to Carex lasiocarpa on edges. Soil saturated.

About 1m wide sand beach; north side of small lake. Along lake, soil saturated, dominated by Sagittaria, Scirpus validus, Eleocharis. Soil dry inland; grades to Carex lasiocarpa then aspen/oak/willow forest. Burned in last year.

~5 acre wetland. Plot central; dominated by Chamaedaphne; grades to Carex lasiocarpa edges. Saturated-moist Sphagnum hummocks on peat >1m deep. Disturbed uplands north, south, and west. Wetland/lake east. ORV tracks outside plot.

Narrow zone between oak woodland/aspen edge and wet meadow/shrub swamp. Cornus stolonifera patches common outside plot. Sedge hummocks common. Much of litter is sedge leaes attached to plants. Needs burning.

Several down Populus and Quercus. ellipsoidalis in/around plot. Many Q. ellipsoidalis are multi-stemmed. Plot within 100+ acre oak woodland with granite outcrops, wet meadow, and aspen woodland inclusions.

Shore of Chub Lake; bottom is muck over sand. On southwest shore near outlet to Chub Creek. Fragmented floating mat. Part of wetland complex on south shore that includes emergent marsh, wet meadow, and shrub swamp.
Plot within 100+ acre marsh adjacent to west side of Shields Lake. Plot adjacent to stream. Moist (not saturated) fibric peat. Grades to cat tail marsh (described in additional releve) to North.

Plot within 100+ acre marsh adjacent to West side of Shields Lake, just north of stream. Saturated fibric peat. Grades to mixed emergent marsh to south, toward stream (described in additional releve).
Basin between 2 knolls. Plot by mudflat and open water, below gravel road. Soil saturated. 700+ acre wetland-upland complex by Shields and Mud Lake. Water edge 8cm muck over clay.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
