remarks: Occasional dead black ash snags and down trees. Occassional low hummocks at tree bases. >1 m deep peat. Soil moist. Most canopy trees <30cm DBH. Grades to oak forest to north, tamarack swamp to east. ~30m from paved road.

In 4 acre prairie that includes disturbed edges of Phalaris, trees, and shrubs. Has had brush cutting and prescribed burning. Last burned ~4-5 years ago. See also releve 0338 in another portion of prairie.

40 acre oak savanna surrounded by new housing and Interstate. Most of stand degraded; dense oaks with forest understory interspersed with open savanna. Prob past grazed. Occasional bare sand next to gopher hole.

1 of several prairie openings on south-facing slope, surrounded by tall Quercus macrocarpa and Juniperus virginiana. Cobbles and exposed bedrock frequent. Most prairie openings < 150 square meters. Little thatch.

Marsh on south side of Ned's Lake. Grades to sedge meadow, then oak forest to north. Marsh surrounds Ned's Lake on all sides. Part of cooperatively managed natural area including oak forest, lakes, and wetland.

Many hummocks present. Soil saturated. 50m from mixed hardwood swamp. Part of extensive shrub swamp northeast of Deer Lake; part of large cooperatively managed natural area with oak forest, lakes, wetlands.
Site mix of upland oak forest and wetlands. Plot with canopy gaps from dead pin oak and birch. Coarse woody debris ~5% cover.
Saturated peat; no standing water. Peat-filled depression surrounded by upland oak woods. Part of large cooperatively managed natural area including oak forest, lakes, and wetlands.
Grazed in past, shallow A horizon (15cm), moderate litter accumulation, ice decay moraine.
Sloping seepage fen at base of prairie complex. Southeast of gravel pit. Soup muck, highly decomposed.

Long, shallow depression with saline characteristics. 25m wide. Periodically harvested for seed. Woody species rare, compostition varies somewhat with patches of Calamagrostis canadensis. Needs fire. Soil silty muck over dark clay layer over light clay with gravel.

Harvested periodically for seed, former hay prairie. Ranges from dry-mesic to wet-mesic prairie. Soil black silty clay with gravel at 45-50cm (over lake bed?). No mole mounds in plot but some outside of it. Mostly flat, some micro relief. Burned spring 1999. Sorghastrum cone near plot center.

In prescribed burn program. ON a slight rise (.4-.5m) but typical of these slight elevational gains. Burned spring 2000. Numerous ant mounds toward periphery. North of crop field, (good-longer) buffer in other directions.

In prescribed burn program. Former hay prairie. Spring 2000 burn. Shallow depression, part of variable microtopography. Soil to 55cm sandy silty black,a s gets to 55cm then color changes to gray brown with a high sand content. Outside of plot is a large patch of Apocynum to north and a large Maybe 10-15% open ground post burn, see some seedlings and expansion.

Grazed in past- patches of grazing increasers. Cypripedium candidum scattered across site. Cypripedium population with plot 12. On very subtle rise. Rank due to abundance of Poa and exotic forbs. Needs burn badly. Low apparent reproduction from NWSGs. Layer of silt to 40cm then layer of graying clay to 75cm, then layer of brown sandy clay to length of probe.
In burn program. Former pasture. 2 exposed rocks, formerly grazed.
Burned spring 2000. Moderate slope. 20% bare ground. Loam with sand and gravel component, black on surface than tan.
Burned in spring 2000. Steep northwest-facing slope. Some erosion in past, but now more or less regenerated. Rocks and gravel on surface.

Releve 2 of 2 in this wetland. Aproximately 20m from lake. Assorted wet pockets with decreasing %-0 moss; hummocks with moss. Intermittent channels from wetland/lake adjacent with Spar min/Utricularia. Few, scattered Picea/Betula dead snags

Open wetland between lake and upland (Acer saccharum mix; birch mix); several patches of snags; intermittent small channels and water pockets near shore. Plot approx 10m from lake. Carex missed due to lateness of season. (1/2 releves in this wetland). Litter of shrub leaves, graminoid debris, and dead moss.

Area adjacent to recreation impacts (bare bedrock). Plot with several foot paths. Stunted birch on shallow soils over bedrocks. Betula with some deadtops and mortality, many multi-stemmed. Barren ant mounds. Presence of worms and charcoal. Litter of sticks and leaves.
Remnant area of older trees. Several ski/hiking trails bisect comm. Ash wetland downslope; Paper birch mix upslope. Some Picea glauca dead and down. Worms present. Goshawk landed on yellow birch!

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Shallow soil over rock fragments; old fencing occasional. No stumps. Community varies from almost open understory to one of dense Abies. Community grades into birch/aspen. Some old dead and down - similar in sizes below. Some hiking trails running north and south along upper slope. Few old boards and nails.
Birch community N. facing slope of > cliff feature- continues to top of topography- NOT at cliff base. Surface of ~30% cobble boulder (moss/ lichen covered). Scattered standing/snagged & d&d Betula.

Wetland complex varies in canopy closure; some areas also have +/- Larix overstory (scattered). Beaver influenced (some chew and likely flooding over time. Some dead and downed; primarily Betula. Organic soils > 3 feet deep.

No worms observed; deer trail through plot. No obvious sign of fire or cutting. Other similar elevation slope may have >% Thuja-however this patchy pattern reoccurs. Site south of Gravel Pit. Few dead and down Abies. Litter of leaves and sticks. Soil 5cm organic over sandy loam over silt loam.

Swamp is mixed and patchy with Thuja. Releve represents the black spruce swamp elements although it varies too with openess and shrub density. Some areas with > shrub density; < SD; > Thuja % (Thuja pocketed). Moose trails.

Plot corner ~3m from pond edge. Open bog surrounds pond. Black spruce (few Pinus strobus/Betula cord) rims open bog. North side of pond has spruce cut. Cypripedium acaule only orchid observed in adjacent spruce.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Paper birch enters community down slope. Several red pigmented worms observed in lower litter. An assortment of oak and maple are several trunked at base. Charcoal and unpigmented worms present below organic. Soil: Gritty brown sandy loam with rocks. Litter of leaves, catkins, and acorn caps.

Community is variable in canopy cover % having occasional small open patches; areas of all Thuja, but much of what was viewed had some sub-canopy Fraxinus. Water pocketed. Moose droppings. Litter of needles, twigs, leaves, and dried Carex.

Balsam fir-balsam poplar-black ash-white spruce forest on level terrace ~9 foot above current river level, 40% of releve includes toe slope. Litter of leaves and fine coarse woody debris. A horizon depth: 12cm; humus layer incorporated.

For I.C.C. field exercise with Beth Jacqmain. South edge of plot nearly in black ash drain. Soils silty with very strong Bt and hardpan. Heavily infested with worms. Cut sugar maple stumps on plot, nearly decomposed.
Plot straddles shallowly sloping depression in deep kettle hole. Site is former woodlot with history of selective logging. Consists mainly of mature multi-stemmed Tilia. A horizon depth: 2cm.

Former woodlot, past selective logging with lots of multi-stem trees. Lower end of area runs into flat terrace. Canopy part defoliated by caterpillars. On north facing slope just south of round lake. Sandy silt-loam <25cm, sandy clay with gravel >25. A horizon: 9cm.

Soils sandy, silty loam (<72cm). Leaf litter and humus depth= 2cm. In State Park. Included in burn unit. In kettle. Very limited shrub layer. Small depression on edge. Sandy silty loam over greater proportion of sand and clay.

NNE-aspect, middle slope. Litter and humus depth=1cm. Sandy, silty loam soils <35cm, clayey sand deeper. Moderately drained. Within prescribed burn unit. Multi-stemmed basswood, no low shrub layer. A horizon depth: 35cm.

Well-moderately drained. Part of prescribed burn unit. Limited oak reproduction. On verge of becoming forest-woodland structure with mesic ground flora. Oaks mostly stunted, open-grown. Sandy, silty loam and sandy clay. A horizon depth: 10cm.
Unusual example of a maple-basswood forest in this part of Pope County. Earthworms present. In slight depression. A horizon depth: 19cm. Topographic context: middle and depression.

Upper slope, sandy clay with loam soils. Most canopy trees in plot multi-stemmed. Old barbed wire fence just to north. On a broad terrace on a small hill. 1-5% of plot covered by woody debris (>7cm DBH). Topographic context: upper/flat.
Middle slope, sandy black loam soils (<10cm), sandy tan clay (>10cm). Centered on shallow drainage. Part of Tilia blow over in southeast corner of plot. Most Tilia, Fraxinus multiple-stemmed.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Oaks dominant at this upper slope/cliff topographic zone. Farther upslope oak decreases and becomes maple basswood forest. Rocky slope/cliff-like downslope. Asstd dead and dying, nothing large. Nightcrawlers, castings observed. Charcoal present.

Cedar swamp but not bryophyte/Sphagnum lush. Seasonal water pockets ~5%. Deer droppings. Dead and dying cedar/fir. Cedar regeneration poor. Gaps with shrubs/Fraxinus/Acer saccharum (less). Occasional dead standing Betula and Abies.

Ass. snags and coarse woody debris primarily Populus tremuloides. Plot represents islands of higher percent Populus tremuloides in matrix of similar community with a lower percent aspen &and higher percent Alnus. Creek downslope. Aspen dead and dying = 38.7cm DBH. Caterpillars reduced canopy to ca.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Earthworms. Charcoal. Few Abies/spruce snags and few dead and dying (low). Density of spruce variable. Several scattered Pinus strobus. Picea DBH 17-52cm.

Broader community varies in percent of Populus balsimifera and Thuja, with some areas wetter than others. Occasional stumps, some cut (unknown and old cedar). Moderate dead and dying with Populus balsimifera falling out of overstory. Acer slope and upland to west. Worms present.
Abundant Acer saccharum seedlings. Dead and dying Thuja, birch. Old yellow birch snags. Large cedar with old saw cut (live, standing). No obvious stumps. Night crawlers present.

Broader comm varies in percent cover--areas of more ash, more Thuja, etc. Occasional deer droppings. Scattered old/decayed Thuja stumps. Occasional dead and dying Thuja/Abies. Approximately 7% periodically pooled with water (tip-up hollows).

Black ash dominated portion of mixed ash/Thuja/birch wetland. To south southwest is beaver-flooded area; +/- dead Thuja along drainage. Several old very rotted "cut" cedar stumps at plot corner. Pools 5-10%.

Greater wetland varies in percent species cover of cedar, ash, and birch. Seasonally flooded hollows approximately 5-10% cover. Dead/down/snags of Abies and birch. Overstory in > wetland appears scattered, patchy, or clumped.

Scattered birch overstory-dead, dying. About one third standing, one third have signs of dead branching, and one third okay. Rocky substrate. Surrounding area varies with higher percent brush, Populus balsimifera, percent Calamagrostis canadensis continues. Northern hardwoods upslope to west. High water table.

Portions of wetland more mixed, higher occurrence of ash on edges. Occasional dead and down Thuja/fir. < Moderately water pocketed. No obvious signs of human disturbance or deer droppings observed. Litter of leaves, twigs, and cones.

Dead and down (old decayed mostly) spruce, scattered. Hummock and hollow (hollows "pooled") about 8-10% of plot. No sign of human disturbance. Organic soils. Stick enters ground to >100cm. Organic soil. 0-6cm patchy litter of mostly cedar needles with some sticks.

Spruce +/- supercanopy in areas (taller trees). Very old conifer stump with deer droppings. Site has very nice spruce concentration, other than old stump and ski trail. No obvious signs of human disturbance.

Deer droppings. Dead/down/standing fir and cedar. Very little hummock/hollow expression. Some "G" category missed due to late season. Black spruce dominant to west. Litter of cedar needles, twigs, and deciduous leaves.

Forested talus on upper part of steep 300 foot slope below 30-80 foot cliffs on north side of Leveaux mountain. Narrow zone (15-60ft wide) above open talus zone. Talus pieces 4-12 inches diameter. Moss cover 30-60%, lichen cover 10%. Open (sunny) talus below this zone.

Dense cedar on very steep upper portion of 300 foot northwest-facing slope crest of Leveaux Mountain. Much exposed rock-both boulders and bedrock. No stumps or snags. Scattered coarse woody debris. Immediately below superior hiking trail. Moss cover 40-60%.

Large basin intersected by highway 65, releve east of road 100+ meters. Some stumps near road, old barbed wire fence but no grazing evidence. Mostly sphagnum-covered hummocks with depressions, very wet with only one small pool of standing water. Patchy canopy, with some patches receiving full sunlight. Tip-ups of evergreens over 10m in height quite frequent. Thuja DBH average 13cm, Larix DBH to 24cm, Picea mariana DBH to 26cm.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Worms. Area floods with calm water. No windrowed debris. Litter +/- absent. Community occupies level terrace along north side of Bear River. Larger community with patchy canopy, open areas dominated by d4-5 corylus species or graminoids. Microtopography rolling with frequent swales that are not dry but appear to frequently pool with water. Moss most abundant on tree bases. Soil Silt over silty sand over sand.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Heavy worm activity. Plot about 100m north north-west of Link Lake. Small stand of mature forest with pole-sized Populus species and Acer saccharum to north and west. Snags and coarse woody debris of all decay stages and sizes scattered. Lowest end of plot >5m above the poor fen to the east. Very sparse leaf litter, much bare soil. Topographic context: crest, upper, middle. Could not get probe past 15cm.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Worms seen, castings abundant. Community grades to black ash swamp to the north and west; releve captures a similar ground flora with a  mixed canopy of old-growth (assumed) Pinus strobus-widely scattered, but all 100+cm DBH. Highway 1 – 100m south, old logging trail 50m to east. Sparse litter of leaves and needles, bare soil. Soil worm-influenced sand and loam over silty sand (loess?).

Wetland fringe of small (<1 acre) open water pool within large conifer swamp complex. Moss sparse. Much of ground covered by graminoid litter. Sphagnum patchy. Buoyant, but not floating. Community 10-20m wide from waters edge to conifer swamp.
Low spots of microtopography with ankle deep moss covered water. High points rather dry. No sphagnum species observed in a continuous moss carpet.

Community within a large peatland complex. See DNR releves 8527 and 8528 from same area. Scattered cut stumps to south, but none observed in plot. Community similar to north and south. Moss covered hummocks, a few scattered bouts of standing water.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Worms present, not heavy. Plot 100m southwest of Long Lake. Many Tilia and Acer with dead branches. Coarse woody debris of all sizes and decay stages scattered to common throughout. High-quality forest stand on county land near SNA. Humus layer in this case refers to the black soil layer on the top of pure mineral soil, this layer appears to be a mix of humus and mineral soil and assumed to be the worm influenced zone. Topographic context: upper/middle.

No standing water or mucky bowls on this date. Recent and old large coarse woody debris present. Scattered patches of pole-sized Fraxinus nigra. Largest trees widely spaced. No cut stumps. Moss abundant on lowest 1m of ash trunks. Soil muck over moss and woody peat. Sparse twig and graminoid litter.
Best quality is nearest road sloping ~2 degrees toward backslope. Typical forby mix of "wet" and "dry" species of Mahnomen County prairie.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Releve to describe wet-mesic hardwood community for Paul Dubuqe. Pass Project for white pine restoration. Soils are sand cap of ~22in over hard pan of sandy clay loam. Standing water at 37in perched above soil saturated at 60 inches.

Dead Lake Wildlife Management Area. Rich mesic forest dominated by Tilia americana and Acer saccharinum. Duff layer thin to moderate depth + open at 1-2 level. Moderate coarse woody debris. Likely grazed and/or disturbed by earth worms.

Tamarack canopy 50% cover; 10m tall, even-aged 5-20cm DBH. Level outwash plain associated with lake depression in stagnation moraine flooded by Stony River. Sphagnum 80% cover, hummocky. Standing water almost absent - present in subsurface. pH=6.7.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Dominated by Betula papyrifera with Abies and Acer rubrum. Heterogeneous open canopy. Level to gently sloping. Lower slope of moraine esker. Deep humus over clay, scattered boulders. Slight depression-no water. Coarse woody debris common. A horizon depth: 1cm.

Dom by Sphagnum, Rhynchospora alba with Xyris mont. One of 3 releves(1/3). Floating mat and submergent vegetation along open water. In center of fen, water covers plants >50%. Rills and floating mats shallow <20m, pH=5.9.

Poor fen dominated by small sphagnum hummocks between open water and upland esker. One of 3 releves. Plot includes beaver trails with standing water. Peat firm >1m deep. pH in hummock = 4.4, 4.9 in Xyris water of beaver run. Water 1-5%.

Forested poor fen-inclusion of conifers on rise within Sphagnum/Carex oligocarpa domianted fen complex within depression of moraine. Linear east-west oval shaped rise. Hummocks to water <2m depth(relief). Dominated by Pinus banksiana, Pinus strobus 15-25cm DBH. Picea mariana 10-20cm DBH.

Forested poor fen with edge of Oberg Lake domianted by Picea mariana. Mode DBH 5-15cm. Sphagnum densely covers area. Shallow hummocks. No standing water. Cut stumps partially decayed are common. pH 4.3.

Ericaceous fen on Sphagnum bordering Oberg Lake and transitory to forested poor fen. Dominated by Chamadaphne, roots extend into water's edge(pH=7.8). pH plot interior = 5.0. Stunted conifers. Spruce releve 20m west.
Rich fen dominated by Carex utriculata and Carex Lacustris. Large meadow along waterway in moraine. Low water, late-season drought. pH 5.8.

Maple-basswood forest. Domianted by Acer saccharum with Quercus rubra, Tilia. Mode DBH 25-35cm. Former sugar site. Low moraine with depressions. Silty sand over unsorted till. Clay within 75cm. Stumps common, very decayed.

Black ash wet mesic forest in low drainage at base of moraine outwash plain draining Little Pine Lake. Dominated by Fraxinus nigra, moderately drained during drought. Dark organic muck. Level to slightly mounded. Distinct layering in herbaceous layer. Snags common. Coarse woody debris common to abundant. Thuja 75cm DBH outside plot.

Aspen-birch forest dominated by Acer saccharum, Betula papyrifera and Populus tremuloides. Moraine knoll, with many small depressions. Semi-terrestrial swamp nearby. Crest with deep, fine sand to >75cm. Mode DBH 15-25cm, max size to 50cm infrequent. Immature coarse woody debris common, broken branches. Tip-ups, fallen snags. Standing snags infrequent. Silty sand over fine sand.

Dry-mesic prairie dominated by Andropogon and Sorghastrum, but brome common. Shrub on knoll of stagnation moraine best on east aspect decond. Ice block depression with rich fen-floating mat. Quaking aspen on lower slopes with prairie herb layer. Silty sand over unsorted till and gravel.

Mesic savanna dominated by Andropogon and Sorghastrum with scattered large bur oak and groves of Populus tremuloides. Bifuicated opening on rolling crest of stagnation moraine. Loamy sand with unsorted gravel, well-drained. Bur oak 40-50cm DBH in plot, broad crowns. Adjacent aspen with prairie.

Rove Formation, senescent Pinus banksiana ~75 years. Native plant community of Disporum trachy. Top and upper south facing slope of bedrock controlled hill. Border Route Trail nearby. Plot located to describe Disporum trachycarpum habitat.

Located to describe habitat of Nabokov's blue in Border Lakes Ecological Classification System. Scattered tree harvest circa 40's-50's shown by well-decayed stumps/slash. Largest Picea and Larix 75-85 years. Native plant community island within 90's clearcut.

Located to describe Nabokov's blue habitat in Border Lakes Ecological Classification System. Scattered tree harvest circa 40's-50's shown by decayed stumps/slash. Largest Picea and Larix 75-85 years. Native plant community is island within clearcut of 90's.
Located to describe streamside northern alder swamp in Superior National Forest. Likely regular flooding. No standing water during very dry period. Large boulders at surface not uncommon.
Dominated by Sphagnum with Carex oligosperma. Near edge of Morris Lake. With stunted Larix. Low mat zone with low hummocks. Firm peat. pH=4.0

On lake border surrounded by conifer swamp. Chamadaphne forms thickets on sphagnum hummocks. Firm peat and suspended vegetation. Various creeks drain conifers swamps through thicket. pH=4.3 collected in fen, pH=7.3 Lake.

On Sphagnum domianted rim of open water within larger fen dominated by Carex oligosperma. Hummock and hollow microtopography. Low mat zone dominated by Rhynchospora alba. Low tracks of water, pH=4.7. Xyris montana in low tracks.
Large fen with low mat zone in water tracts and few hummocks. Ericaceous plants 1-5% surrounding Picea mariana 1-5% cover. pH=4.4. Releve near edge of pond.
Rich fen-floating mat in small 0.5 acre ice block depression in stagnation moraine. pH=7.6
Poor fen dominated by Carex lasiocarpa, Carex utricularia with Carex lacustris at margins in moat. No sphagnum. Typha sparse. pH=6.0.

Wet-mesic prairie with inclusions of wet meadow. Former hay field on level plain of Hay Creek. Dominated by Carex stricta, but Phalaris arundinacea common. Shrubs <1%, mineral soil. Bordered by cultivated field and wet meadow.
Conifer swamp or forested Poor fen dominated by Larix and Picea mariana. Outwash and pitted moraine near Lake Emily. On St. Louis sublobe. Deep peat >1m, deep hummocks and hollows with water.

Bordering open water pond in larger forested fen/poor fen complex. Releve floating mat with beaver tracks. Sphagnum hummocks of with low tracts dominated by Carex lasiocarpa. Open water 15%. Substrate tremulous.

In outwash channel of St. Louis moraine. Carex lasiocarpa and Carex oligosperma dominates margins of beaver pond. Sphagnum forms low hummocks. Larix is scattered throughout fen. Beaver mud flats with annual plants at pond margin.
Wet meadow dominated by Calamagrostis candensis in narrow channel draining lakes within St. Louis moraine. On wet sand with seeps from side slopes. Wet drain from seep into creek. 2 X 10 meter area.
Dominated by Carex stricta and Calamagrostis canadensis. Outside meander of drainage valley thru stagnation moraine. Footslope toe ancient alluvial plain of creek into Nokassippi River. Mineral soil.
On floating mat with shallow sphagnum < 1m. Low hummocks of sphagnum. Fen separated from main lake by narrow spit with pines.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest
remarks: Dry-mesic oak forest on slopes, knolls of moraine hills with scattered white and red pine nearby. Sand-gravel, steep side slopes of ice block depression. ATV trail nearby.
Oval-shaped, ice block depression of Mille Lacs end moraine. Dom by sphagnum hummock and hollow microtopography. LAGG 5-10 meters wide with Alnus. pH=5.0-note early date.
Wet meadow or rich fen on floating mat at edge of lake. pH=7.3. Early collection data with good graminoid abundance.
In large wet meadow patch. Part of large wetland with other patches dominatedd by Lythrum salicaria or Typha angustifolia. Water table presently just below surface. On Mud Creek valley bottoms.
Fen in wetland zone between two ridges of gravelly outwash. To west it grades into heavy Typha angustifolia cover. Continuous layer of non-sphagnum moss.
Water table presently 6 inches below ground surface (very dry year). Releve is in zone between tamarack swamp and areas of heavy Typha/Phragmites cover. Coarse peat soil.

Along Poplar River. Upstream of campsite east side. Cut stumps numerous. Good regeneration. No roads/trails. Frequent hummocks/hollows. No mistletoe. Seperate from river by band of shrubs. Perched? Lake Agnes pcrna.

Shrub meadow between Caribou Creek and Poplar River. Large patch within wetland complex of Thuja and Picea swamps and linear graminoid community. Dissected by beaver runs. Possible type site for animal surveys. UTMS converted from NAD27(Field Wpt) to NAD83.

Thuja swamp between Poplar River and Caribou Creek. Hydro flux/windthrow dominate. Cedar appears more open-grown (low branches), and extremely water-stressed. Distinct hummocks/tussocks/hollows create uneven microtopog. Good type site for bryophyte sampling. pH 5.7. Field Wpt in NAD27,corrected to NAD83.

Rich black spruce swamp representative of wetlands in 6-mile creek drainage. Old, moss covered stumps from past selective logging (30-45cm diameter). Ground surface broken, water-filled hollows, sphagnum hummocks. Sparse patchy litter of needles, branches and leaves. Field Wpt in NAD27. Corrected to NAD83.

Northern cedar swamp wetland complex includes rich spruce, black ash and alder. Headwater wetlands of Onio River surrouned by northern mesic hardwood forest. Occasional large coarse woody debris, abundant smaller coarse woody debris and water-filled pockets. pH 6.1. Litter of conifer needles and deciduous leaves. Field wpt in NAD27, corrected to NAD83.

Aspen-birch spruce-fir mesic mixed forest dominated by Populus tremuloides (30-40) 60cm DBH with scattered Picea glauca in canopy. Saddle between northern hardwood knolls and between drainages. Low-moderate coarse woody debris. No evidence of fire. Soil: silt with gravel and cobble. A horizon depth: 3cm. Field wpt in NAD27, corrected to NAD83.
Dry mesic hill prairie near crest of hill 15 degree, southwest facing slope on coarse gravelly, sandy soils.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Releve is almost on county line west of the road 1/2 mile south of Schantzen Lake, but the road winds a few hundred feet east of county line. Past windstorm releve in area that escaped storm intact area just barely larger than size of releve.
Flat top looks like oldfield. Releve on prairie north-facing slope. Heavily invaded by woodies, needs burn. Owned by belmont church very small remnant prairie.
Best prairie is on slopes of ravines.
Heavily grazed fairly steep east facing slope, upper midslope. About 90% bare ground. Compare with releve 2001-06 which is relatively ungrazedfacies of same canopy type. This is north of 28975.

This portion is on slope between 2 fairly steep ravines and does not appear to be grazed at present time. Midslope. Dominance of oak increases upslope of basswood downslope compare with releve 2001-05.

East of river. This prairie is grazed from bean harvest until bean planting every year since mid 60's, previously harvested for wild hay it is in excellent condition. Grazing regimes don't need change.
Representative of prairie in this ownership, record 29109 last grazed 1999, on slope just south of stream, similar community continues east along slope to road.
This releve is associated with dry prairie southwest hill subtype 29056 but includes Lespedeza leptostachya record #29054. It represents the eastern edge of the prairie.
Releve is right in heart of concentrated Besseya population and with respect to this species uncharacteristic of prairie as a whole.
Upper midslope of west facing spur east of des moines river.
Second ravine south of shelter, up ravine just far enough to lay a releve plot on north-facing side of ravine fully on the slope.
Level to barely west sloping at head of y of ravine.
Pastured, west-facing slope. Red-shouldered hawk calling nearby. Midslope bare ground 35%.
Northeast facing head of draw about 30m west of fenceline near head of steep ravine. Fairly open woods, but cool and moist only spot with moss. A rank really nice.
Terrace slightly above floodplain at base of high quality spur.
About 25% bare. Flood cleaned ground - in floodplain.
On peninsula in Iowa Lake, interior of peninsula. This is a wonderful stand.

Small species list is partly a function of patchy clonal nature of vegetation in this park. Other areas have Erythronium albidum, Uvularia grandiflora. Several releves are needed to characterize site.

Releve to characterize wet measic boreal hardwood conifer forest for B.R.D.F. Summit Stop #1. Classic coarse over impermeable. About 20" mottling in sand above lacustrine. Small remnant patch-cut to north.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Releve typical of old-growth mesic hardwoods, just southwest of Irvin Lake, across the road. Field trip for U of M extension. Good humus layer without worms, worms abundant across road. Mosses absent on ground. 1cm A horizon. Soil 15cm silt mantle over FSL till.

Mixed forest dominated by white pine (mode DBH 25-35cm; max DBH 35-45cm frequent). Selectively logged with understory removed. Scattered red pine (35-45cm). Level to rolling near small esker. Silt loam and unsorted gravel. Worms. Stumps frequent.

Poor fen with linear pool (pH 6.4) in kettle-hole depression near Cloquet River bridge on Langley Road. USFS firm sedge peat, deep, hummocky with a few pools. Releve in 3 distinct zones: Open water, Calamagrostis, Chamaedaphne.

Jack pine forest on outwash terrace ridge with unsorted sand and gravel. Level to slightly hummocky. Pine mode DBH 10-25cm with occasional max 35cm DBH. Well-drained, densely moss covered. Slight organic silt <1cm. Coarse woody debris 5-10%. USFS near Langley Road.

Mixed conifer swamp in low area between drumlins. Patchy canopy of Thuja, Picea mariana and Larix. Poorly drained muck and peat. Hummocks and pools ratio, 70/30. Many tip-ups. Thuja DBH 15-25cm, Picea/Larix DBH 10-20cm, pH 7.8.

Mixed forest dominated by Abies balsamea (DBH 35-45cm), Betula papyrifera (10-35cm), Picea glauca/Abies (10-35cm). Lower slope of drumlin near swamp. Microtopography with slight mounds and depressions. Moderately well drained loam over unsorted silt and gravel. Boulders <1%. No earthworms.
Poor fen on floating mat at edge of Woodcock Lake with Beaver runs. Firm peat, sedge peat and sod. Shallow pools <5%. Hummocks to 0.5m height. Scrub tamarack and Chamaedaphne. pH 5.7.

Poor fen dominated by low mat of Rhyncospora and Eriophorum. Slight rises and flarks (with green sphagnum). Large flats devoid of woody plants. Floating mat pH. Scattered low shrubs of Chamaedaphne developing into mounds of peat.

Many multi-stemmed trees. Populus and Betula more common within community than releve shows. Suspect minor worm presence. Soils appear undisturbed from past logging. Lots of deer browse. Coarse woody debris +/- lacking. Large coarse woody debris absent, small and medium occasional. cf Pinus species stumps, 75% decayed in community.

Low points of micortopography with wet flora and open water, high points with mesic flora. Large 85% decayed stump(cf.Thuja)in plot. No recent cut stumps observed. With open water. Rocks and boulders common at the surface. Little coarse woody debris. More Populus tremuloides just outside of plot. Litter of leaves and conifer needles.

Small worms beneath last year's litter. Lower side of plot with shallow pools of water. 5" rainfall 2 days ago. Large, medium and small coarse woody debris, decayed <40% common. E7-8 Pinus strobus scattered in community. D7-7 Betula alleganiensis widely scattered.

Long ridge on west side of Thistledew Lake. Scattered openings with Populus and Abies blowdowns throughout comm. Tilia more common throughout community than plot suggests. Deer browse, at times heavy. Worms suspected but not seen.

Coarse woody debris sparse. South of Wolf Lake. ~0.5 miles. Scattered mature red pines throughout. Scattered dense D4-4 patches with same species as releve. E5-6 snags occasional as are recent E6-6 dead falls. Unsure about stand origin.

2 inches standing water in low points; otherwise soil is saturated. Scattered cut stumps throughout, 50%+ decayed-coarse woody debris, mostly older and moss covered, common throughout community. Most Tilia multistem. Scattered Thuja patches throughout community.

Abies and Picea blowdown common throughout community. Rolling end-moraine topography. West side of Erskin Lake. Scattered cut stumps ~50% decayed, cf. Pinus and Thuja occidentalis. Coniferous coarse woody debris of all decay stages common throughout. Litter of coniferous needles and deciduous leaves. See releve #8798. Soil sand with organic leaching over light brown fine grained sand. Topographic context: crest/upper.
3 acre patch bordering Erskin Lake on West side surrounding uplands sand-capped end moraine till. See DNR releve 8797. Microtopography with sphagnum covered hummocks and +/- open water low points.

Broad gently sloped lake-washed topography. North of Bass lake. Plot ~200m from shoreline. Cut stumps >60% decayed about 30 cm DBH, scattered throughout stand. Near clearcut to the west with E7-7 Pinus left standing. Litter of leaves and needles. A horizon depth: 10cm, dark organic. Fine grained tan sand.

Roll topography with scattered depressional, isolated wetlands. Plot captures characteristic low knoll and its upper slopes to the east and west. Clonal patches of Populus tremuloides dominate this stand. Plot is more divrese canopy, typical between Populus clones. A horizon depth: 8cm black organic with worms. Coarse sand with small pebbles.

Plot within 30m of Day Creek. Community about 100-200m wide along a 1/4 mile stretch of the creek. Scattered Salix patches throughout. Scattered Alnus incana patches along transition to black ash swamp. Beaver activity in area. Tussocks to 50cm tall.

Saturated soil, community on a terrace within 200m of day creek. Dominance of Fraxinus nigra, Thuja occidentalis, Abies blasamea and Alnus incana, variable in patches. Plot captures an average dominance of all tree species and a higher dominance of Alnus Incana. Very spare deciduous litter.

Community within the interior of basin bordering east side of O'leary Lake. Scattered patches dominated by Carex oligosperma, Chamaedaphne calyculata or Scheuchzeria palustris throughout. Scattered 1-3m Larix and Picea, many dead near upland edge. Sparse scattered graminoid litter.

Compare to 8803 for a contrast of the two wetland native plant community classes occupying the basin bordering east side of O'Leary Lake. Picea DBH range = 7-15 cm. No cut stumps. Picea appears healthy. No mistletoe observed.

Worm cast common. Scattered cut deciduous stumps, 50% decayed east of plot. Plot about 200m south of Bear River about about 50feet above. Populus canopy even-aged. Plot captures representative of the more mature deciduous forest in township. Scattered, mature red pine and white spruce.

Community has a "savanna-like" distribution and spacing of canopy trees. Plot captures cedar swamp at mouth of south flow from bog-lake about 300m north. Low points mucky with +/- open water. Flow is difficult to follow.

10-20m wide rich fen edge of bog lake. Plot within 2m of water's edge. Community on a thick floating mat. Lake within a large white cedar swamp. Plot captures typical community surrounding the lake. Polemonium in flower.

Represents drier end of the forest communities in this vicinity. No worms. No fire scars. Scattered cut stumps >75% decayed, cf. Pinus species. Slender-medium coarse woody debris common in community. D3-4 Corylus cornuta near continuous throughout community. Litter of needles and deciduous leaves. Coarse reddish dry sand.

No worms. Fire scars on older stumps and coarse woody debris. Compare to 8808, same landform, different canopy. Plot captures typical mixed canopy forest in this area. Slender-medium coarse woody debris common throughout community. Scattered decayed cut stumps, >75% decayed throughout community. Litter of deciduous leaves and coniferous needles.

Isolated basin surrounded by fire-dependent asp/birch-pine forest on sand. Community likely burned in past thus accounting for jack pine presence. Low points of microtopography appear to have had open water until recently. Community <50m north of Beatrice Lake.

CCSA age=149 years. Scattered blowdown patches. Unique air photo signature for area, maybe due to high amounts of Alnus incana between conifer trees. Recent cut in swamp to the south. No cut stumps observed in area of plot.

Appears to worm-free community on a gently sloped, near level topography adjacent to a large conifer swamp. Fire scars on older coarse woody debris. Small-medium coarse woody debris in all decay stages common. Large coarse woody debris of all decay stages scattered.

Mineral soil(sand) saturated for entire length of core. Humus layer drier not saturated. DNR old growth candidate. Community within a larger thuja occidentalis swamp and borders Townline Lake. Scattered blowdowns. No cut stumps. no fire scars. Litter of half needles and half leaves.

Gentle transition from upland to lowland. No exposed bedrock. No standing water. Diverse DBH in canopy(19-43cm). Coarse woody debris-all sizes and decay stages occasional. Snags occasional. Scattered areas within community dominated by graminoid ground layer and small DBH trees, and a more open canopy. Patchy leaf litter.
Within very large marsh-rich fen-shrub swamp complex. About 50m east of railroad tracks, which are just below highway 61. Level microtopography. Standing water varies from 2-5cm depth.

Phragmites dominated marsh in Weaver Bottoms area of Mississippi River, about 100m northeast of USFWS observation deck. Grades to Acorus-Sagittaria marsh to west, shrub swamp and river to east. Saturated muck, areas with 4cm standing water.
In emergent marsh-shrub swamp complex in Mississippi River floodplain, about 40m East of railroad tracks. Saturated muck, no standing water, a few low hummocks. 10% litter cover of Scirpus.

Typifies low-lying wettest areas that cover 1/3 of 8-10 acre fen in small basin in gravelly rolling terrain northeast of Dumbell Lake. Grades to patches dominated by Carex oligosperma and patches of ericaceous shrubs. No Picea or Larix taller than 1m.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Maturing stand (60-80 years) on narrow plateau between South Fork Nemadji River and tributary ravine west of highway 23. Pine 40-50cm DBH, spruce and aspen 10-30cm. No stumps, few snags, sparse coarse woody debris. Plot in densest pine on ridge, grades to aspen birch.
Releve to document wetland following plugging of Brown's Lake ditch in spring of 1999. Andromeda glaucophylla in community, not in plot. Soil probe: decomposed peat. Plot southeast of ditch plug.
Releve to document wetland following plugging of Brown's Lake ditch in spring 99. Plot southeast of ditch plug.
Releve to document wetland following plugging of Brown's Lake ditch. Plot northeast of ditch plug.
Releve to document wetland following plugging of Brown's Lake ditch. Potentilla palustris in community, not in plot. Plot northeast of ditch plug.
Wet prairie in wet mesic-dry prairie complex. Northwest area of Glacial Ridge Project.
Glacial Ridge project (The Nature Conservancy). Dry-mesic prairie, about equidistant between gate in north-south fence and west-edge of woodlot.

Cedar swamp at base of ridge with springs north of LaSalle Lake. Hummocky from old tip-ups and moss covered roots. Some very rotted cut stumps. White cedar DBH from 34.3-67.0 cm. Sphagnales 50%, Bryales 50%.
At one of series of springs on ridge above and to the south of the Leaf River in northeastern Ottertail City. Gentle slope to northwest. Skunk cabbage common. With Phil Goeden. Peaty soil at seep.

Wet prairie dominated by narrow and medium-leaved graminoids, east edge of Glacial Ridge Project. Salix ~5% in interior of community. Fenceline passing through and bordered by ditch. With Jason Ekstein, The Nature Conservancy.

Lego Property near 5m. point on Leech Lake. Moderate coarse woody debris. Shallow duff, occasional patches of bare ground. On northeast slope to small wetland adjacent to plot. Graminoids absent from plot. Wormed?
Smokey Hills State Forest, on unusually thin, tall shrub layer. Can see right through stand. Very sparse ground layer as well. Mainly oak litter.
Level to rolling.

Species composition changes top to base of slope; cover of following species is greatest at base: Gymnocarpium, Cornus alternifolia, Mitella, Cireaea, Equisetum, Rubus pubescens. Just north and downslope of releve #8923.
Level top of slope, south side of road, south of clearcut across road, just south and upslope of releve 8922.

Low dunes. In wildlife refuge, frequently control-burned. Widely scattered open-grown taller bur oaks, frequent low oaks. Bare sand cover ~25%. Surrounded by matrix of burned woodland/savanna. Almost no litter.
Soil dark colored sand. Oak woodland burned repeatedly by refuge managers. Tall Quercus elipsoidales with lower layer Quercus macrocarpa all with burn scars and fire-damaged branches.
Crest and upper slow of low dunes. North edge grades to woodland. <10% open sand. No recent fire. No coarse woody debris.
East facing slope of low dune. Grades to oak savanna to East (10 m away). Approximately 10% cover by coarse woody debris. Oaks with open-grown form. Occasional old oak stumps, well-decayed.

Numerous standing dead oaks just North of plot (oak wilt and/ or fire). Gently sloping stable dune in preserve managed with prescribed fire. Approximately 10% cover coarse woody debris. 1 foot (?) trail runs through plot <5% cover bare soil, mostly from gopher mounds.

Flat to gentle west-facing slope. NE corner approximately 10 m from small sedge meadow. South and West edges grade to old field, now open prairie (~10m away). Plot part of long-term burning research area. Largest Quercus with burn scars on base of trunks. ~10% cover coarse woody debris. Occasional standing dead saplings and shrubs.

Plot approximately 10m from field road. Burned in large controlled burn, Spring 2008 (this year). Most shrubs burned to ground now coppicing. Some oak wilt in adjacent Quercus ellipsoidalis. Approximately 10% coarse woody litter cover.
Plot includes animal study area (open), grading to more wooded edge (bur oaks and planted pines). Some wet prairie character in lower parts. Past disturbance (grazing, pines, portions plowed?).

Coarse woody litter. Woodland grades to oak savanna in other parts of preserve. Most trees with open grown forms. Occasional small openings with prairie species (<10m diameter) in otherwise fairly dense woodland.
Slightly undulating dunes, exposed sand in very small patches. Very little litter.

South-facing low dune with scattered clumps of Quercus macrocarpa, Quercus ellipsoidalis, and planted Pinus banksiana. About 5% cover of bare sand. No coarse woody debris, very sparse leaf litter (most oak). May have been partially dug many years ago.

Low dune system: aspect here West and North. Mostly open; scattered small clumps of Quercus and Juniperus trees. <5% coarse woody debris. Frequent small patches of open sand. Stumps of large Quercus ellipsoidalis from trees that died of oak wilt were removed.
Openings have been restored via fire mgt. (every 3-5yrs) and timber removal. Gently rolling terrain in former Glacial Lake Grantsburg. Many prairie spp of Great Plains origin, "dry mesic prairie"
Pitted sandy outwash plain. Managed by county as a fire break. Burnett County.
Plot was selected for savanna/open woodland structure. Unknown management history. Very dry, due more to aspect than soil. Mid-slope. No fire recently.
Creek in vicinity of site; relatively isolated from roads & other pote nital land use effects. Two beaver dams impound approx. 40% of the sit e; a spillway is located upstream.
River has large, straightened channel with very broad riparian wetland . Dredge spoil from channel deposited on channel banks
River has large, straightened channel with very broad riparian wetland . Dredge spoil from channel deposited on channel banks
Recently tilled; walnut plantation along river; altered hydrology, fre q. disturbance & heavy pesticide use. Historically a floodplain forest .
Recently tilled; walnut plantation along river; altered hydrology, fre q. disturbance & heavy pesticide use. Historically a floodplain forest .
Part of site is early successional forest along river recently cleared for highway construction.Surrounding area is intact floodplain forest .
Part of site is early successional forest along river recently cleared for highway construction.Surrounding area is intact floodplain forest .
Intact floodplain forest along river,
Intact floodplain forest along river,
Remnant along the river in Hastings; highly disturbed. Control structu res reduce frequency of floodplain inundation. Bank stabilized with ri p rap.
Remnant along the river in Hastings; highly disturbed. Control structu res reduce frequency of floodplain inundation. Bank stabilized with ri p rap.
Releve conducted in community transitional between wet meadow and calcareous fen. Releves conducted on 6/01,7/13 and 9/02/87.
Releve typical of shrub-carr communities in the area. Releve conducted on 6/01, 7/14, 9/01/87.
Releve typical of shrub-carr habitat in the area. Releve conducted on 7/15, 8/31/87.
Releve typical of lowland hardwood forest communities in the area. Releves conducted on 6/02, 7/14, 9/02/87.
Releve typical of lowland hardwood forest communities in the area. Releve conducted on 6/02, 7/14, 9/02/87.
Releve typical of sand delta communities in the area. Releve conducted on 10/03/87.
Consult Dr. Jan Janssens for additional plot info in PARADOX system. Vascular plant and moss collections with Janssens, DUPS at Deer River. - Month unknown

Fairly flat site in a level area. The large maples are not good, but basswoods okay.  Heavy sugar maple reproduction. Date unknown. Half inch litter of leaves with some small twigs. Soil: 4 inches very dark brown loam over 3 inches brown loam over light reddish brown sandy loam with much gravel. Roots distributed throughout A and upper B horizons.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: +/- thick deciduous leaf duff. Infrequent coarse woody debris, a few well decayed, medium-large diameter logs. Stand 8. Rolling topography; plot on the top of knoll. Date unknown. Soil: 2 inch organic over 6 inch silty/clayey sand with pebbles.
Soil muck, water at surface; sp. cond. = 214; pH=5.7. Ecological group 2. Date unknown

This tract had been grazed. This is the 2nd growing season without grazing (owner said tenant had overgrazed pasture so now he is letting it rest). Overall, native grasses are diverse and some conservative forbs are present. However, forbs are patchy and sparse (as can be seen in this releve). Releve on an upper slope. Lower slopes are more mesic.

Sedge meadow is diverse with sedges. Baltic rush is visually prominent because of its height & color of fruiting heads. No shrubs present at all. Heavy rain the previous day (several inches); water at the soil surface or perhaps 1-2cm above the surface, but below the thatch. Microtopography is somewhat hummocky, but not markedly so. Violets and ragwort in bloom. Setting is a basin in a 160-acre pasture w/ sedge meadow in shallow draws/swales leading down to basin. There is probably some groundwater seepage. The basin extends east onto the neighbor's property but is surrounded by cropfield on that side. Soils-from NRCS Soil Mapper- Parnell silty clay loam.

Very dry and sandy. Few old pine stumps nearby, well decomposed. No sign of fire. Nearly level site in rolling area. Reproduction mainly balsam fir and aspen with a little read and white pine and paper birch. Data from Sloan, John p. 1981. Aspen site productivity classification in Carlton County, Minnesota. M.S. Thesis University of Minnesota.
Over mature poor aspen site. Moderate amount of clover suggests possible old field. 90% defoliated by tent caterpillar. Soil: clay with few rocks. Most roots confined to A horizon (6").
No evidence of worms observed. Undulating microrelief with large and small tip-up mounds.
Plot center area appears to be in a slight depression. Undulating microrelief with some small tip-up mounds. No evidence of works, but very dry out. Herbs fading fast. Very uniform lady fern.

Few small tip-up mounds, gently sloping. Conditions very dry at survey. Plot 15m from edge of large sedge meadow/wetland. North half of plot looks a lot like classic maple basswood, south half is variable. Corylus americana and Corylus cornuta are about 50:50.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Plot in very mixed forest. Almost nothing about knee high. Long gradual slopes. Undulating with small to medium tip-up mounds. Decaying trees on ground are common. No evidence of worms.
Site is right no edge or normal wetland. Also on the edge of a small depression. Gently undulating microrelief. Upper 2 inches of soil more poorly drained than lower 3 inches. 2 worms found in soil.
Topographic context is lower midslope. Looks more poorly drained in upper 3 inches than in lower 2 inches. Undulating microrelief.Plot farthest east in a Tilia clump. No evidence of worms.

Site on edge of maple basswood upland and fern filled ash lowland. Nearly level microrelief, few small tip-up mounds. Seems more poorly drained in the upper horizons. 1 goblin fern seen. No evidence of worms observed.
Undulating microrelief with few large tip-up mounds. No evidence of worms. Site contains bare patches of exposed soil (o layer).

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Microrelief undulating with large and small tip-up mounds. Plot is a small closed depression with stones at surface. Complex slopes. 1 small worm observed.

Site encompasses most of slope from ridge top to small drainage. very large some drying aspen form top of canopy in suppressed sub-canopy of pure maple. Possible worm site? Evidence of worms and worm castings. Very little organic matter on floor and much exposed soil. In some places the mineral soil is exposed in other places is still last years leaf fall. Bright mottles due to subsurface lateral flow.

Stand in gently rolling terrain. 50/50 sugar maple and basswood with some aspen and birch. Site is an open spot in carex carpet just about 1 m diameter, center of plot is 75-80% bare duff. Stands of carex, oak fern, wild ginger ring corners end edges of plot. Gently undulating microrelief, a few small tip-up mounds. Worms in O/A soil layer, it looks like this layer is in transition from organic to mineral.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Complex slopes. Mottles and gleyed colors could be due to texture(silty) and lateral movement of water in BC horizon. Undulating microrelief with few small tip-up mounds. No evidence of worms, soil is dry in upper 15 inches.

Plot north-south. South east 1/2 is hill side, northwest 1/2 is valley floor, at transition from slope to valley. 22cm DBH basswood 6 m from center of plot, flagged. Plot is at edge of a drainage way(swale) that goes in a swamp. At least 8 individuals all on slope. A few species very obviously only in stream channel and not associated with slope. Stream channel has mossy logs with many species of moss and liverwort. Undulating microrelief, a number of trees have fallen over. Looks like burned out at the midslope position. No worms observed.

Canopy almost pure maple, but a few basswood and white cedar. No shrub layer. Northwest corner of plot much higher with more saplings. A lot of leaf litter. Microrelief near level with few old tip-up mounds and some scattered blowdown. No evidence of worms. Lots of Carex pennsylvanica and sugar maple seedlings. Botrychium mormo. all over site.

Plot side north-west and east-west. Corners marked with red fabric flagging. Check exact spot indicated from previous Botrychium mormo. sighting including under duff, none found. Undulating microrelief with some tip-up mounds. Soil is moist.

Very diverse hill prairie that seems too 'rich' for UPs13d. Lower mid-slope; a fairly gentle slope. Diverse in grasses and forbs. Species list for the ~4acre prairie patch plot sits in would be much longer. Soil seems to be a light colored sandy loam w/ small stones (~1cm diam or less) scattered on top. Plot more mesic lower on slope; somewhat drier species are present higher on slope. Most of plot more mesic. Maybe this should be considered an 'Ecotonal' plot. Not sure.

Prairie on gentle WNW facing slope. A tree planting is within 100m to SE of plot. This area was harvested for prairie seed by Wildlife for a number of years. Wildlife Division intends to manage entire site as prairie with fire. The only exotic forbs noted were Melilotus spp, and Cirsium arvense. High diversity of native forbs present. Soil seems to be a moist loam. Large ditch of channelized river runs along W side of WMA & has unknown impact on hydrology of releve here.

Open low 'prairie' dominated by Carex sp.,Poa pratensis, & Agrostis sp. Some conservative forbs present. Wildlife maps area as 'mesic prairie' but typical warm season grasses are largely absent. Big bluestem was present in plot. Soil seems like moist loamy clay. Soil type was not thoroughly evaluated. No shrubs in plot.

Releve is in A-quality portion of wet brush prairie at base of western slope of a Glacial Lake Agassiz Beach Ridge. This is typical of brush prairies that occur at the feet of beach ridges in Polk County.

Gravel-cobble beach shoreline at Main Fish Fry Pond. NPC maintained by fluctuating water levels and seeps. Pond one of several in area. Surrounding upland forest is black spruce-jack pine woodland, white pine-red pine forest or young forest (aspen). pH of pond 8.6 (seeps pH 7.1). Some invasives and increasers. ATV use.

Old-growth upland cedar island, west side of Perent Lake. Bouldery, broken ground. Mostly level. Abundant bryophyte cover. Large patch in center blown down in 1999. Gaps dominated by Acer spic, Betula, Abies, Thuja. Island criss-crossed by beaver trails with small birch taken. No deer sign. Good cedar reproduction. Taxus canadensis patches.

Rich black spruce swamp adjacent to protected bay of Perent Lake. Tip-ups, moss-covered logs common. Peat depth >110 cm. Geocaulon lividum found within community, but outside of plot. No anthropogenic disturbance or fire.

place_name: Western Water Track - Red Lake WMA
remarks: Scrub tamarack/bog birch fen along southern flark of the Western water track. Some dead and down tamarack, almost all living trees with dead tops. Overall canopy <25% cover. Paired with #9778 to the north which has a sparser canopy. Some alder in area, rare.

place_name: Western Water Track - Red Lake Peatland
remarks: Sparse scrub tamarack (1-3" dbh) along southern flark of Western water track. Appears to represent slightly wetter drainage through sphagnum dominated shrub fen continuum. Paired with slightly drier releve to the south. Low flat peat-bottom hollow at water level.

place_name: Western Water Track - Red Lake WMA
remarks: Unmarked hurried releve while waiting for helicopter. Western water track just north of scrub tamarack/bog birch. Very subtle flark pattern. Photos.

place_name: Lake Bronson State Park, Prairie Monitoring Releve
remarks: Graminoid dominated with fair forb diversity. Area burned in past few years. Graminoid diversity low, mainly big blue stem and prairie dropseed. Notes: Very little leaf litter. Photo taken by OTGockman looking NE. Plot marked with spike with 2 washers in SW corner.

place_name: Vegoe Prairie Bank, Prairie Monitoring Releve
permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Dry to mesic prairie on mid to lower slope of rolling ridge. Typical of entire tract except it has no smooth brome, which is prevalent elsewhere. There is smooth brome in adjacent swale and lower slope <2m away. Notes: Photo taken south boundary to north. Moved transect from original given GPS point because it was in western snowberry & smooth brome which was not representative of tract.

place_name: New Prairie WPA, Prairie Monitoring Releve
permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Crest and upper slope of dry prairie on open ridge. SW corner of plot has open, gravelly area. Few widely scattered boulders across gently rolling ridgetop. Bromus inermis appears to be invading plant community - top of ridge is scattered to dense smooth brome. Notes: Tried to overlap similar plant community as old releve 8839. GPS point for that plot took us to the north-facing slope of the ridge, but the old data sheet described a SW-facing crest, so we moved the plot within 25m to SW-facing slope that appeared to have similar community. Photo taken from NE corner toward SW corner.
Poor Quality Releve. A horizon depth: 5 inches.

Poor Quality Releve. Mature multi-aged forest with small canopy openings and hummocky topography. Much coarse woody debris (all sizes), much of it well-decomposed. +/- Fire. Multi-Stemmed Tilia on island in sedge wetland. A horizon depth: 9cm.
Poor quality releve and no spp. cover. Recent wind disturbance adjacent to plot. A horizon depth: 4cm.
Poor quality releve.
Poor quality releve.
Poor quality releve. Native Plant Community, Oak/Aspen/Maple. Topographic context is Middle/Lower.

Native Plant Community: Maple Basswood Forest, East Central. Mature forest recovering from fire/logging disturbance. Site is relatively low/flat area with scattered cut pine stumps. Mesic soil. hummock topography. Much evidence of windthrow. water table not present. Located in Mille Lacs moraine complex. Percent tree cover; Acer saccharum: 60%, Quercus rub 25%, Tilia am: 15%.

Native plant community: maple basswood forest, East Central. Plot located in Mille Lacs Moraine complex. Plot hummocky, on slightly raised knoll. Remnant charred pine stumps in plot. Site is drier and flat. Poor A horizon. Oak dominated area - height < 75 feet. Water table not present. Drier, less diverse than releve #4629. Tree cover; red oak: 75%, Sugar Maple: 25%.

Most of plot in same topographic position - exception is east corner subplot. Some hummocks present (5%). Area drainage is poor to very poor. Uneven aged stand. Area is mesic and relatively low/flat. Canopy 72 feet high. Tree Cover; Sugar maple: 90%, Basswood: 7%, American elm: 3%. Maple Basswood Forest, East Central.

Dominated by sugar maple and scattered mature yellow birch. Numerous white pine stumps present in advance decay. One red pine sump. mature woods with scatter old-growth sugar maple. Hummocky. Moderate deadfall. Tree cover; Acer saccharum: 75%, Tilia americana: 20%, Betula all.: 5%. Maple-Basswood Forest, East Central.

Hummocks, relatively flat. Dominated by sugar maple, basswood, and yellow birch. Cut pine stumps in advanced decay. Tree Cover; Yellow Birch: 50%, Basswood: 30%, Sugar Maple: 7%, Red Oak: 7%.Maple Basswood Forest - East Central.

Cut white pine stumps in plot charred and well-decayed. Pine stumps rare but occasional throughout maple-basswood forest. Low wet mesic site, flat. plot uniform throughout. Sparse-moderated deadfall. Few large lows in advanced staged of decay. Tree Cover; Sugar maple: 90%, Basswood: 10%. Maple Basswood Forest, East Central. Vegetation compiled from 6 7m X 7m subplots. Site/General data compiled from old field note cards and releve data sheets.

Relatively flat, mesic site dominated by maple-basswood, with occasional bur oak, red oak, and ash. Cut pine stumps. Tree cover; Sugar Maple: 50%, Ironwood: 18%, Basswood: 8%, Bur Oak: 8%, Black ash: 8%, Red oak: 8%. Maple Basswood Forest, East Central.

Site dominated by invasive grasses
Fresh small mammal burrowing activity
About 20% of the site is open sand, with lots of burrowing activity. The plot also has some small pines from the nearby plantation.
This site is on a slope with about 75% open sand and moss. Roughly 1/3 of plot in brome field, the other section high quality dry prairie.
About 20% of the site is open sand. Some small burrows present.
White pine plantation on a nice dry prairie.
Pine and spruce has been planted on this site. It has patchy open sand with burrows and mounds.
About 25% of the plot is open sand.
About 25% of the site is open sand.
About 20% of the site is patchy open sand.
This site has small scattered patches of open sand. Very little litter.
Site may have been partially planted. This site has about 20% open sand and there are small mammal burrows and mounds.

Plot chosen to represent common aquatic native plant community of low gradient streams with organic substrate in Ely-Knife bedrock LTA. Located below short boulder bed, steeper gradient stream segment. Diversity and abundance of aquatic species diminishes with distance from inlet. Floating leaved species = 20-25%. Abundant algae covering submerged vegetation and in floculant masses on surface. Depth of substrate variable, deep to minimal to bedrock. Water depth = 1 meter, substrate = mix of organic and fine mineral. High % of fine organic. A couple species with inflorescence above water.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Northeastern Bedrock)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent natural origin native plant community common in Ely Knife Bedrock LTA in this setting. Minor '99 blowdown impact. Low to moderate coarse woody debris. Origin 1921 fire. Charcoal near surface. Transition to FDn43a on top of ridge - lies between releve location and recent burn to East. No past harvest. No evidence of earthworms observed.

Plot selected to represent small patch native plant community in Ely Knife Bedrock Complex LTA. Within matrix of fire dependent native plant communities burned in '07 prescribed fire with severe '99 blowdown impacts. Plot with blowdown of largest canopy trees in '00. Well-decayed coarse woody debris abundant. Shallow depressions with evidence of standing water pools = 50% of plot. Moss covered tree bases and decaying wood substrate for most plants. No past harvest. No evidence of earthworms observed.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Northeastern Bedrock)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent small patch native plant community (within FDn43b1 matrix) common in land type association. This patch with wind throw of Pinus banksiana - 1, Pinus strobus - 5, and Picea glauca - 3. Native plant community common on cliff tops and upper, steep slopes; various aspects. No past harvest. No evidence of earthworms observed.

Plot chosen to represent native plant community and condition common in this area and in transitional growth stage. Canopy trees senescing and canopy discontinuous. Transitional growth stage, FDN43b1 moving to FDn43a. Abundant coarse woody debris of large Populus tremuloides, different stages of decay. Not part of '1999 blowdown. Tall shrubs typical <2.5m. No past harvest. No evidence of earthworms observed.

Plot chosen to represent rich peatland native plant community expression unusual in Gabbro Bedrock Complex land type association. Hummocks and wet hollows well-developed. Pools and short water channels common. Small water tacks, water movement in at least one. Part of peatland complex that includes FPn63a and APn81a along south side of Polly Lake. (Burned post-releve in Sept. 2011 Pagami Creek fire, natural ignition). No past harvest.

Plot chosen to represent native plant community and condition common in land type association on tops and slopes of large b.rock-controlled landforms in gentle terrain. Decadent canopy species here and some recent windthrow. Transitional growth stage. Located in patch with evidence of scattered harvest (1940s or 50s?).  One possible cut stump in plot. Pinus banksiana most likely target species of harvest. No evidence of worms observed.

Plot chosen to represent natural origin small patch native plant community common in this portion of land type association. Two low rock walls within plot(2m and 8m long; <2m high; P. virginianum habitat) Coarse woody debris, all sizes, abundant. No evidence of worms observed. No past harvest. Fire origin. Island in Fraser Lake. Flat areas above slope with small wet depressions within Thuja - dominated uplands.

Plot chosen to represent native plant community common in land type association, eleven years after catastrophic blowdown event (1999). Abundant coarse woody debris of Picea mariana, Pinus banksiana, Populus tremuloides. No evidence of worms observed. Shallow to bedrock soils. Persistence of previous native plant community type appears likely. No past harvest.

Plot chosen to represent natural origin native plant community, common in land type association. Picea mariana layering evident. Open understory. Hummocks mostly low, some moderately high. Hollows few and with out pools. No mistletoe observed. This is a small patch NPC within mesic forest and woodland matrix. No past harvest.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent native plant community of natural origin, common in land type association in scoured bedrock terrain. No evidence of worms observed. On bedrock controlled feature on peninsula of Alworth Lake. Burned snags in plot. Small bedrock glade runs length of plot; common occurrence in this woodland native plant community. Low to moderate coarse woody debris. No past harvest.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot to represent Native Plant Community common in this area and setting. Natural fire origin, post light impact of 1999 blowdown event. Bedrock outcrops within plot. Topography within plot variable with narrow draws in between outcrops. Abundant coarse woody debris. Some charred wood still evident. Identified as FDn32 vs. 43 due to scoured bedrock setting. No past harvest. No evidence of worms observed.
Old-growth red-pine stand (OG IS SW-27). In Soudan State park. Area has several erratics and gaps, releve reflects. Stand is on top of pine dominated ridge near lake Vermillion.
In southern part of old-growth pine at Lost 40 Scientific and Natural Area. Releve typical of stand/community on state ownership. Stand continues onto US Forest Service land to South.

npc_subtype_name: Jack Pine - Black Spruce - Aspen Subtype
remarks: Releve is in low area next to a bay on small lake. Adjoining forest is a jack pine-black spruce woodland with many rocks. Plants were more akin to those in jack pine stand, but soil was very different. The soil and proximity to the lake bay may account for differences in plant species between the two stands.

Northern shrub shore fen with high cover of Betula pumila. Large patch peatland complex. Large, high sphagnum hummocks. Community grades from treed to open (along river). Downed logs likely buried under sphagnum with occasional standing dead. No evidence of disturbance, browsing or wildlife trails. Emily Peters (UMN) assisted with this releve. Postscript: Releve fell within Pagami Creek Fire (August,2011).

Jack Pine-Black Spruce Woodland "island" within poor conifer swamp.  Old, cut stumps provide evidence of past logging (Heinselman disturbance history data estimates 50-90 ybp). Occasional, very large erratics. Distribution of large, downed logs are light-moderate, with one large, downed log in plot. Knob to west (~3m higher in elevation)is dominated by jack pine.  Micro-topography is flatter than expected for this community. Emily Peters (UMN) assisted with this releve plot.

Black Spruce-Feathermoss Woodland on northwest-facing slope above Isabella River. Abundant medium-sized downed logs.  Exposed boulders on surface. Abundant micro-habitat for seedling reproduction (old stumps, tip-ups, broken ground). Bryophyte cover nearly contiguous. Patchy sphagnum. No evidence of anthropogenic disturbance. White pine seedlings scattered throughout community. Emily Peters (UMN) assisted with this releve.

Low Shrub Poor Fen adjacent and parallel to Isabella River.  This community occurs in small and large patches, in a repeating pattern, for the length of the river.  Community is often adjacent to narrow Black Spruce-Jack Pine Woodland (FDn32c) patches. Margin along river often with tall, moderately dense, shrub layer (e.g. Alnus incana, Fraxinus nigra). Emily Peters (UMN) assisted with this releve.

Upland White Cedar Forest. North end of island that was partially burned in June 2011. Moderate abundance of large downed logs throughout (incl. Abies balsamea, Thuja occidentalis, Betula papyrifera).Bryophytes common throughout. Large fire scar on white birch canopy tree. Several, very large erratics. No charcoal in soil. No evidence of browsing. Plot on crest of low hill in middle of small peninsula, at south end of large island. Maryann Smith assisted with this releve. Postscript: Releve fell within the Pagami Creek Fire (August 2011).

Black Spruce-Jack Pine Woodland. Moderate, medium-sized downed logs, a few tip-ups. No evidence of fire or browsing. Charcoal fragments just below moss layer.  Minimal mineral soil development. Adjacent to linear, Crystalline Bedrock Outcrop (ROn12b). Maryann Smith assisted with this releve. Postscript:  Releve fell within Pagami Creek fire (August 2011).

Low Shrub Bog (APn90a). Scattered, stunted Picea mariana (2-3m ht),and  occasional, mostly dead, Larix laricina (periodic inundation). Smaller, live individuals (0.5-1m ht.)scattered on higher hummocks. Overall, hummocks are low. Edge of community complex transitions from Northern Spruce Bog (Semi-treed subtype)(APn80a2) to Low Shrub Bog. Bog pond ~100m to east.

Old growth, White Pine-Red Pine Forest. Moderate, large, downed logs. Large (~64cm dbh), fire scarred , white pine snag (~3m ht). Natural origin @1864 (Heinselman). Canopy dominated by white pine (with paper birch). Bedrock outcrop scattered throughout community. White cedar co-dominant in portions of community. Deer pellets in plot. Large, downed logs in various states of decay (long time scale) comprised of roughly equal number of large diameter white pine, paper birch and (smaller diameter) balsam fir. Charcoal in upper soil layer. Soil "ribbon" >5cm. No evidence of worms.  Ann Schwaller (USFS-SNF) assisted with this releve.

Graminoid Rich Fen (Water Track).  Surrounding, semi-treed areas are Rich Tamarack Swamp (FPn81a); with portions where water accumulates, creating lags and pools with Iris lacustris and Carex lacustris. Arceuthobium pusillum common on black spruce shrub layer, with much of canopy black spruce affected. Moose (deer) trails from adjacent uplands to fen and through water track. Sphagnum cover 25-50%.  Ann Schwaller (USFS-SNF) assisted with this releve.

Small, linear island in Gabbro Lake.  Several tree and shrub species (Betula papyrifera, Thuja occidentalis, Pinus resinosa) stunted by wind (krummholz). Entire island with gravelly substrate over bedrock. Additionally, shore with low-medium amount of cobble. Unusual rock or charcoal fragment in soil profile (obsidian-like).  Minor use of shore by canoeists. Scattered, downed logs low but large. Some beaver-chewed stems (Betula papyrifera). Shoreline zone is inland lakeshore community (LKi). Ann Schwaller (USFS-SNF) assisted with this releve.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Old Growth Red Pine-White Pine Woodland at top of 10m high x 100 m long cliff wall along South Kawishiwi River. Fire scars on canopy red pine. Large, downed logs in various stages of decay, scattered throughout (red pine, white pine). Medium-small, downed logs common. White Pine-Red Pine Forest (FDn43a) and Crystalline Bedrock Outcrop (ROn12b) adjacent. Large, linear patch a complex of all three communities. Charcoal at top of mineral soil layer. No evidence of worms or browse.

Old growth Lowland Wet Cedar Forest. Drainage between shallow-to-bedrock uplands. Beaver influenced, with short, scattered dams between cedar at lower end. Community transitions to upland cedar along edges. Peat depth ranges from 25-131cm. Cedar on raised hummocks above peat. Scattered exposed boulders. Hollows are currently saturated, but seasonally pooled. Beaver chewed Fraxinus nigra (all sizes) common. Deer and moose droppings in plot.

Old Growth White Pine-Red Pine Forest. Abundant, large, downed logs. White pine seedlings common in small gaps and tip-ups. Dominated by conifers. Multi-storied white pine in canopy, sub-canopy and high shrub layers. Minimal browsing by deer. Community common in uplands and on ridges around several small, poor conifer swamps in area. No evidence of worms. Large downed logs in all decay classes, many older logs associated with tip-up mounds. Deciduous shrub layer (aspen, birch, balsam fir, Lonicera canadensis) browsed. White pine not browsed. Abundant white pine cones from last year (2010) on ground.Soils with charcoal at top of mineral layer (E-horizon ~1 cm in depth).
Native Plant Community: Jack Pine Forest. Gently rolling topography. Moss 5-10m thick.
Native Plant Community: Mesic Deciduous Forest.
Edge of Mulligan Lake water track. Shrub Swamp.
Calcareous fen community dominated by Carex sterilis with limited shrub cover.

A graminoid dominated opening surrounded by FPw63b with no obvious areas of exposed peat. The plot includes several rare plants as well as R. alba (extremely infrequent at this WMA). Phragmites is abundant outside of the plot.

Open Stipa dominated prairie on a W-facing hill. This last remaining reasonable quality unprotected UPs13d on east side of Des Moines River between Christiana & Belmont Bridges is actually within statutory boundaries of Kilen Woods State Park. Prairie is filling in with woodies; needs fire.
Releve on slope downslope of a Sioux Quartzite erratic boulder in level bromy top. Problems with green ash invasion in all concave portions of slope prairies.

One of a series of releves purposed to document the condition of a series of W-facing knolls S of Kilen Bridge on east side of Des Moines River. Site has many C rank UPs13d hills, little for cons. spp., but all native or being invaded by woodies.

Strongly convex SW-facing slope east of Des Moines River S of Kilen Bridge. Long spur of prairie extends almost from top to base of hill above new bridge. One of a series of releves to characterize knolls of prairie, that is within statutory boundary of KWSP.

Red shouldered hawk in this stand. Mediocre woods probably reflects history of grazing but should be surveyed in spring as this is the 'tired' time of year for wds of this kind in Des Moines River Valley.
North-facing slope 7-10m wide between 2 ravines not far from old homesite up ravine from Des Moines River. Notes: Stand is depauperate.
Small very lush mesic prairie east of wetland and NW of open water body.
Community exhibits seepage characteristics, but not a fen. Drainage class: Very Poorly Drained, discharge area. Topographic Context: Upper/Middle.

Releve in area with high concentration of prairie bush clover, upper mid slopes facing road west of large draw, east of parking area. Typical quality and PBC habitat. Topographic Context: Upper/Middle.

This prairie is grazed by tethered horses. This is typical of an area in which the horses were tethered last spring. Part of old MCBS Site #1, but split off because different ownership protection strategies.
Prairie in spring - grazed draw, east side of N-S ravine. Formerly part of site 1, but split off because different ownerships have different protection strategies.

One of several lovely open very small calcareous fens with obvious discharge zones. Releve may be more like 64 + meters squared as each of these patches is pretty small and releve confined to actual fen. The only example of a sedge I was able to recognize as Carex hystericina was one plant with old head. The cover may be low. Narrow leaf sedge could be either interior or sterilis. Fairly hard to tell from lvs but aspect right.
This is a lovely stand right in the middle of town!

North facing slope of steep east-opening ravine along Des Moines River north of canoe campground. This is very close to an area visited by Mike Lee et. al. earlier this month. Mike collected Athryrium in this draw. Unknown could be Thaspium barbinode. Too immature to ID.

On main terrace of Des Moines river. Understory (herbaceous) suggests FFs57, but canopy MHs49. Probably formerly a floodplain, but river has cut over a meter below the level now. Surface soils silty alluvium. Some wet standing pools.

Releve on convex ENE facing spur. Parts of forest floor feel wormed. Notes: Yes, this forest has maple and basswood. Ravine mainly owned by coop elevator. Leads down to gravel pit across road from Riverside Park.
This stand on both sides of ravine is the northern-most extent of the Jackson area maple forests. Pastured (site is grazed). Steeper slopes are higher quality.

This W-facing slope is best part of forested pasture to get least disturbed releve. This stand and the S-facing one across the ravine are the northernmost of the Jackson maple forests, which only go this far north on east side of river. Gentler part of slope. Notes: Releve Typical of Stand: Pastured. Stand typical of Community Type: Ecotonal MHs39 and MHs38 at N extent of maple.

Northernmost stand of MHs39 for sure in county with sugar maple in canopy. South facing slope of ravine east of Des Moines River. Dearth of canopy oak not result of present logging but Des Moines Valley reported to have been highgraded for oak in last 40 years. Releve just upslope of property line fence. Notes: Stand Typical of Community Type: Herbaceous layer tends toward MHs38 but sugar maple in all woody layers.

Terrace is transected by a sheep fence - this area is west of fence. Spring ephemerals are on slightly higher areas & flat areas are dom bare ground & Glechoma or Hydrophyllum or, closer to river, reed canary. Some trees submerged by high water. Notes: Topographic Context: Toe/Depression/Flat.

NW corner - CRP - Sect 35 Petersburg: Majority of site is CRP. This an effort to find some lurking native prairie. Must have experienced repeated herbicide. Depauperate. Notes: this is the site by Iowa border S&E of all the other Petersburg sites accessed through gravel pit rd. Releve in remnant in CRP site.

Purpose of this releve was to characterize portions of prairies in NW unit of otherwise high quality site. This area is both drier and less high quality than anything native in main N unit or SE unit. This is near a spent gravel pit which may explain why it is so dry.

Germantown 2 large complex visible from highway is almost entirely all planted. Releve reflects small remnant of native prairie in the NE facing corner on steep slope. Notes: Hardly any native prairie present in tract (mainly CRP). Topographic Context: Upper/Middle. Purpose of Releve: Document if any of large site is native.
