Surveyed this area because original MN Nat Hist Survey report for Cottonwood county cites a peat survey in last quarter of 19th century that said there was peat on this property. Hoped for calcareous fen but all seepage areas are WMs83 similar to this one west of homesite and visible from county rd. Peat deposit persists. Margins are hummocked. Releve in best area.

This releve is on flank of slope, s & w of releve in heart of wet meadow. This releve is clearly ON slope south of pond portion of wetland. Visible from road. Peat on this terrace is quite remarkable.

This releve is in an actively grazed pasture, fairly closely cropped, so difficult to assess cover of some plants. Very good considering ambient use. Notes: Purpose of Releve: Document Besseya habitat.

Steep north facing actively grazed slope of ravine. Heavily grazed. Difficult to determine cover of grasses. Note presence of both Astragalus missouriense (25 plants, 3 in fruit) and Besseya bullii (over 100 plants) in this releve.

Heavily grazed pasture dominated by native grasses, but with many weedy species.However note also presence of Astragalus crassicarpus and Besseya bullii. Grazed to a height of 1-2 inches. Cattle were here 1 week ago.
Active pasture, cattle were here five days ago. Grazed to 1-2 inches at present, which probably affects estimate of cover and releve quality. Releve on upper gentle slope.

Steep north facing slope of a bank facing creek. Only the slopes support native prairie. Rank based partly on extremely small size of site. Fragmented by a small impoundment. Total prairie at site only about one acre.

South facing slope of ravine trib to Des Moines River. In actively grazed pasture. Ordinarily I would not do a releve in an area like this. It is to document the degraded internal condition of slopes in draws that are less steep and do not face Des Moines River.

Degraded north facing WMs83 seepage zone that occupies terrace flanks and circles on slopes at similar elevations through most of the tributary ravines in this pasture. In active pasture but cattle appear mainly to stay out of these if they are not forced in. This is not a calcareous fen. Best example near S end of this pasture complex. Peat not measured, but notes say "not springy."

Prairie Bank. East facing steep slopes above Des Moines River just outside Windom. Despite dominance of brome, note Besseya bullii in plot and Lespedeza leptostacha just out of plot. They are just far enough apart that one can't lay out a standard releve that includes both.

Steep north facing slope east end of WMA. Lower third of slope below releve may have been planted and mainly failed. Volunteer woodies in draw include Celtis occidentalis, Vitis riparis, and Prunus americana. Don't understand ecological reason for presence of Aster novae-angliae and Silphium perfoliatum.
Top of very steep NNE facing slope (west of planted prairie). This is either very mesic UPs13d or very dry UPs23a. Equivocal setting for so mesic a flora.

Forb abundance is high but brome is so heavy it is difficult to assess cover of native grasses. If Amorpha and Phlox are a measure of community rank this slope is AB, if brome dominance it would be CD. There must be some seepage, indicated by patches of Spartina on slope.
Steep east facing slope about 30% dominated by native grasses, would respond to fire. Low forb biodiversity despite better potential of graminoid recovery.
Very pretty long prairie slope just north of deerstand. Completely dominated by natives. Ranked B because of lack of conservative species. Among the best slopes in Holly township.
Prairie Bank reputed to be best part of tract. Seed was harvested here for restorations on the north side of the creek.
This is actually the best of this tract. Phlox, Amorpha, slightly longer list of natives.
South facing slope of knoll, across a fence from slopes on the east which are largely dominated by non-native cool seasons with half the native forbs north of Plum Creek.
"Moderate slope woods. Canopy open trees about 5 m apart. Many deer trails (lead to spring) N facing slope. Probably has spring flora now dormant for the year"
Native grasses plentiful. If burned, this would probably be dominated by big bluestem. Rank might be AB if not for the young ash.

On dunes, on open slope above sedge meadow. Scattered bur oaks upper to top of slope, more open below; grades to more trees lower slope, below releve plot. Much open sand, very little thatch. Many pocket gopher mounds, frequent deer tracks. One old tree stump NE corner of plot.

Low dunes. Clumps of oaks on north and south edges of plot, interior open. Shallow blowout in NE corner of plot. About 10 percent cover of open sand in plot. Several large cedar stumps in plot. Landscape matrix is composed of groves of oaks among open prairie areas.

Nearly flat topography, on dark brown sand. Recently burned. Large charred branch on ground in plot. Signed "Oak Savanna Restoration Area." 5% cover open sand from burn. Most woody vegetation sprouted from base of burned plants, except tallest trees in plot. Grades to woodland/overgrown savanna. Plot part of restored area, ~5 acres. Canopy trees all Quercus ellipsoidalis.

Open bog surrounding open water, floating. Near stand of Tamarack. pH:4.6-5.4. Releve within large poor fen/conifer fen complex. On ground moraine of Superior Lake Wisconsin glaciation. Peat depth >1m.
pH 4.9. Continuous cover of sphagnum species many >.5m above water table. Bog/extremely poor fen.

Bimodal 17-22cm DBH, 27-32cm DBH. Worm castings common in surface. Plot center within 30m of wetland edge and only slightly above. Old stumps with fire scars. Large well decayed coarse woody debris occasional; slender to medium/moderate decay common. Undulating microtopographcy with bare bouls and graminoid covered higher areas. Very large well decayed pine stumps common throughout uplands.
>6 feet water table depth.

Centered on largest cold area. One of state's largest Chrysosplenium iowense concentrations along this 1/4 mile long algific slope. One of the largest and best occurrences of this community in Minnesota.

Representative of small rock outcrop features in Mesabi Range. Typically surrounded by larger bedrock shrubland native plant community. Minimal soil development along level ledges and crevices. Some evidence of recreational foot traffic. Alternative NPC: ROn23a.

Seemingly drier inclusion on periphery of mesic mixed forest. Ground layer variable; portions dominated by moss and lichen cover. Vegetation shift result of NPC transition or edaphic conditions created by 90+ years under jack pine? May be better described as jack pine dominated FDn43? Canopy openings common where jack pine and paper birch have died back. Spruce budworm activity widespread. No human disturbance noted. Alternative NPC: FDn43. Mineral soil horizons and exact textures: A (FSL), Bw1 (FSL), Bw2 (LFS), C1 (FS), C2 (COS). Parent material: eolian over outwash.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Associated with bedrock outcrop and cliff feature. Representative of small pine dominated woodlands on bedrock knobs/ridges in BL subsection of state park. Old cut stumps with fire scars and burned snags present.

Mature stand; no human disturbance noted. Small canopy openings frequent throughout. Deeper peat; shallow pools common. Diversity is high; >45 species. Stand appears to integrate with northern cedar swamp.

Floating mat complex adjacent to lake; includes both rich and acidic peatland native plant communities. Releve describes rich fen dominated by Typha and fine-leaved graminoids. Standing water depth ranges from 1-2 feet. Alternative NPC: OPn81.

Ridgetop woodland dominated by stunted oak; along transition from rock outcrop feature to the northern mesic hardwood (MHn) matrix. Exposed bedrock and fire scars present. Contains elements of both fire dependent(FD) and mesic hardwood(MH) systems; may be better described as MHn35 on bedrock recovering from fire. Associated with "rock knobs" in Mesabi Range Land Type Association. Alternative NPC: MHn35.

Low level area; bisected by stream flowage. Older large diameter cedar present (living and down logs). No human disturbance noted. Water table 12 cm from surface. Evidence of moose activity, but browse minimal. Indicators for both native plant community class types a/b are present. Alternative NPC: WFn53b.

Large peatland drain. Plot located in representative area; standing water and Carex lasiocarpa cover increases in portions of water track complex. Large scattered clumps of Andromeda common. Deep peat.
High quality cedar swamp; representative of native plant community in park. Located on periphery of basin. No human disturbance noted.

Small inclusion surrounded by shrub poor fen. Site minimally impacted by recent beaver disturbance along shoreline. Wet hollows present. Sphagnum magellanicum is dominant moss in pools. Carex lasiocarpa abundant throughout peatland complex.
Evidence of mistletoe in plot and throughout stand. Highest hummocks approximately 36cm in height.

High, near continuous "mound" of Sphagnum fuscum; invading tree bases. Larger opening in forested bog may be result of fire disturbance? Some coarse woody debris present. Standing water only observed around open tree bases in "pits."

place_name: Bear Head Lake State Park/Spruce Lake Complex
remarks: Apparent change in local hydrology. Standing dead tamarack throughout stand. May be result of past beaver activity further to northwest. Species list comparable to releves further south in peatland.

Low level upland site. Plot located in older part of stand where large diameter Thuja preset. Also includes significant canopy gap created by downed Thuja and birch; dominated by dense shrub layer. Charcoal on soil surface. Evidence of earthworms and heavy browse pressure. No moss in ground layer.

Periphery of large peatland complex. Patchy high hummocks dominated by dense shrub layer. Deep mucky hollows with minimal vegetation; dominated by brown mosses and minerotrophic sphagnum species. Standing water level low, mid-August. Soil saturated peat/mucky peat near surface.
Representative of featureless water track native plant community for large peatlands of Nashwauk Uplands subsection. Depth of standing water is variable. Deep peat.

Representative of forested native plant community dominating large peatland features of subsection. Canopy cover and dominance varies. Plot located in area of higher canopy cover dominated by black spruce.

Water track with subtle flark development. Plot centered in pool, but includes portion of adjacent peat ridges. Pool character consistent; approximately 5cm standing water. Hummocks in string more variable; typically >20cm height.

Level lake plain, northwest side of Fourth lake, a few feet above lake level. Saturated soil: ~12 cm highly-decomposed organic over very fine grey sand, no rocks or boulders. No surfave water. Trees bi-modal sized: 20-42cm DBH occasional, 5-20cm DBH common. Moderate amount of coarse woody debris. No stumps. Earthworms present.

Typical of ~200 acres on west / northwest side of Kemptons Lake. Patchy canopy, cedars to overly large, 15-30cm DBH, most leaning. Many cedars with partial die-back. A few snags. No stumps. Poorly-decomposed peat >35cm deep. Icy cold water, saturated to just beneath level of the hollows. Grades to areas with some Fraxinus nigra. Ely-Knife bedrock complex LTA.

Typical of aquatic marsh community in large, fairly sheltered bay in eastern arm of Wood Lake. Water approximately 60cm deep in plot, more or less typical water level for this time of year. Decent water clarity, bottom clearly visible. Substrate is deep (200 cm+) silty organic (gyttja). Plot approximately 20 meters from shore. Community present in water to 150cm deep though species composition and abundance changes somewhat with greater water depth. Ely-Knife Bedrock Land Type Association. Strongly rolling bedrock terrain; bedrock is somewhat calcareous.

Beaver-impacted rich fen in approximately 20-acre basin along the creek that connects Wood and Hula Lakes. Large beaver dam raises the water level in wetland approximately 4-5 feet. Community is somewhat transitional due to flooding. Plot centrally located in area with patchy shrub cover, approximately 30 meters from upland and approximately 75 meters from stream channel. Approximately 1/3 of shrubs are dead. No old snags or large coarse woody debris except along upland margin. Quaky deep peat. Grades to zone of more pure Carex lasiocarpa (~monoculture) nearer stream. Ely-Knife Bedrock Land Type Association. Strongly rolling bedrock terrain; bedrock is somewhat calcareous.

Upper slope of extremely steep, ~90-foot bedrock ridge on southwest shore of Hula Lake. Plot covers a significant portion of a very steep south-southeast facing bedrock exposure. In some spots the community is talus-like as the bedrock is disintegrating in place (and moving a short distance down slope to lay in shallow lens atop the clastic / volcanic [dacitic/andesitic tuff/breccia] bedrock). Very little soil development in plot. Most of the rock is lichen-covered. Scattered Pinus strobus on the slope in vicinity, but no evidence of pines in past (no stumps or large coarse woody debris) in or very near the plot. Ely-Knife Bedrock Complex LTA.

Along lower reaches of Madden Creek approximately 1/2-mile upstream from Wood Lake. Typical of and centrally located in approximately 20-50 meter wide zone (~5-10 acres here) between creek and poor black spruce swamp. Deep, firm, saturated peat with frequent old wood remnants. Small coarse woody debris (old conifer remains) frequent. No stumps. Grades shoreward (north) through zone of stunted spruce / shore fen then denser taller spruce in poor conifer swamp. Plot ~25 meters from stream channel and ~35 meters from stunted spruce zone. Compare to south side of creek where conditions appear richer (releve 9921). Ely-Knife Bedrock Complex LTA.

Along lower reaches of Madden Creek approximately 1/2-mile upstream from Wood Lake. Typical of and centrally located in broad zone (~10-20 acres here) on south side of the creek. Tall Carex stricta hummocks (to ~60 cm). Wet troughs between hummocks, occasionally with up to 3 cm standing water. Deep, highly fibric sedge peat with frequent, small, old wood remnants. No stumps. Plot center is ~20 meters from stream channel. Grades through zone of conifer snags (~60 meters from stream) to live tamarack swamp southward. Compare to north side of creek where conditions appear poorer (releve 9920). Ely-Knife Bedrock Complex LTA.

Typical of fairly large outcrop complex on ridge in rugged terrain northeast of Hawks Nest Lake. Rock is salmon-colored leucogranite, exposed rock makes up ~20% of plot. Soil elsewhere is shallow, <15cm deep, loamy organic / detritis. Several old conifer stumps nearby. No invasive Hieracium species here. Trout Lake Bedrock Complex LTA (near edge of Ely-Knife Bedrock Complex).

Typical of ~10 acres on middle and upper south-facing slope of 120-foot bedrock ridge above west end of Vera Lake. Plot on broad mid-slope terrace; slope much steeper above/below. Dark sandy-loam soil, fairly shallow to bedrock. Occasional small gritstone/argillite/greywacke outcrops. Oaks small and open-grown. Much coarse woody debris from 1999 windstorm. Mostly Pinus banksiana and Populus tremuloides blown down in 1999, few of these taller tress (over 5(8)m tall) remain in vicinity. Soil shallow over bedrock. Ely-Knife Bedrock Complex LTA.

Typical of small (~2 acres) sheltered cover along south shore of Vera Lake. Early vegetational stage of bay in-fill process. Deep organic silty substrate >100cm deep. Much old buried wood (beaver lodge) as well. Remnants of old beaver lodge nearby. Plot near shore in water ~35cm deep. Native plant community: submersed/floating leaved aquatic. Ely-Knife Bedrock Complex LTA.

Typical of fairly broad, very gradually sloping shoreline zone exposed by water levels that are down ~80cm due to drought. Edge of plot is 1 meter from waters edge. Sorted silty sand over sand. Organics in upper 7cm. Plot covers most of exposed shore zone here. Boulders nearby. Shoreward edge of plot is approximately 12cm above present water level; lakeward edge of plot just above present water level. Trout Lake Bedrock Complex LTA.

Typical of large patch of mature, aspen-dominated mesic forest on rolling bedrock terrain southwest of Jackfish Lake. Stand origin 1921 (Heinselmann). Red, white and jack pines sporadic in larger patch, jack pines mostly dead. Old stumps uncommon. Big-tooth aspen +/- even aged, 30-48cm DBH; pines 40-50cm. Snags occasional. Moose droppings in plot. Soil: 10cm grey silty sand with stones over orange silty sand with stones (iron precipitate).

Typical of wetter and subtly lower-lying micro-sites in broad poor fen zone surrounding Webfoot Lake. Edge of plot  ~8 meters from lake on north shore. Deep peat, somewhat drier than normal due to drought. Fen plants are noticably stunted in these wetter microsites, not so in more typical poor fen settings elsewhere here. Fen grades to poor black spruce swamp approximately 30-50 meters from lake.

Typical of several zones of large but subtle depressions in broad poor fen on west side of Webfoot Lake. Slightly wetter than adjacent fen. Deep, quaky, wet peat; likely drier than normal due to drought. This wetter, lower zone extends from near lake margin to ~30m inland where poor black spruce swamp begins. Plants noticably stunted in these wetter zones compared to those in typical poor fen here. Sphagnum carpets mostly absent in wettest spots. Plot center is approximately 12m from edge of lake.

Typical of mature/old growth pine atop 70-foot granitic ridge between Webfoot and Tick lakes. Pines to 60cm DBH, mode 45-55cm. Edge of plot 10m from crest of steep north-facing slope. No stumps. Moderate amount of coarse woody debris. Occasional boulders. Rocky silty sand: 15cm humus, fine silty sand below. Stand origin 1921 (Heinselman) though likely an "island" of older forest in large 1921 patch that was partially logged in early 1900s. 75cm DBH Pinus strobus to west of plot.

Typical of dry bedrock (granitic) woodland on ridge top and upper portion of 150-foot slope along the Jackfish River. Jack pines 20-40cm DBH, most alive; black spruce 8-20cm. Outcrops frequent, boulders occasional. A few snags. No stumps. Moderate coarse woody debris. Stand origin 1894 (Heinselmann). Blueberries more abundant in canopy gaps nearby (outside plot). Thick carpets of Pleurozium schreberi with frequent Dicranum and occasional Cladina. Soil is organic sandy-silt.

Typical of old growth pine (stand origin 1759- Heinselmann) surrounding Sauna Lake. Plot in one of the denser patches of the 65-100cm DBH (mode ~85cm) pines remaining here. No stumps. Moderate amount of coarse woody debris- mostly Abies. Low granitic (leucogranite) outcrops in plot. Lower edge of plot approximately 15m from lake. Very fine sandy-loam over very fine rocky, silty-sand over bedrock. Charcoal at 3-8cm down. Slope height ~25 feet, length ~50 feet. Trout Lake Bedrock Complex LTA.

Typical of large patch of mature black spruce-feathermoss woodland atop granitic ridge north of Sauna Lake. Stand origin 1894 (Heinselmann). Picea mariana 5-35cm DBH, Pinus banksiana (uncommon) 25-35cm. Moderate amount of coarse woody debris. No stumps. Occasional snags. Very fine sandy-loam over very fine sandy-silt, shallow to bedrock (<15cm), charcoal at surface. Trout Lake Bedrock Complex LTA.

On north side of Clearwater River upstream from lakes 1 and 2 by Bagley. Some off plot cattail, but none in plot. Located on inner swing of river meander. Some small woody debris. Cattails forming dense stands below beaver dams in area; but growing only occasionally in this meadow. This plot is typical of the best quality of this type ~30 acres, many willows are dead, small dense patches of Carex lacustris, Carex aquatilis and some off plot Aster puniceus.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Terrace forest with strong graminoid/herbaceous cover. Composed mostly of black ash and silver maple. First silver maple sighted along river (start point was Clearwater Lake). Some exposed alluvium but otherwise vegetated. Adjacent uplands are grazed and contain prickly ash. This area represents a low, off-river elevation that is not similar to the next highest elevation, ~WFn53 ash dominated. High amounts of coarse woody debris. Soils are deep organic/alluvium.

Open rich fen dominated by Rynchospora fusca and Carex oligosperma with scattered clumps of Myrica gale. Flat with standing water in foot prints. Part of a 10-12 acres wetland flowing east towards Middle Cone Lake (not typical of class - MDL).
Plot is a transition from dense alder to open water with an area of stunted tamarack between this plot and the open water. Very spongy and wet, typical throughout plot.

Plot taken in an open area, nearby are Alnus incana and Salix discolor. This plot is representative of the low-wetland swales in the vicinity. High quality, with only a small patch of reed canary grass. Other wet areas closer to the camp 4 road have Typha latifolia/angustifolia and consequently are of lower quality.

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: Mature are of forest as the result of a fire skip in the 20 year old landscape. High amounts of coarse woody debris here compared to the burned area in plot 811-(1).

npc_type_name: Lowland Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Forest
remarks: Young, diverse stand, flat terrain, somewhat mucky moss on all tree bases. This area was entirely burned approximately 20 years prior. There is one large log in the plot with charcoal.
Alder on west edge of lake is typical of the entire western shore. Standing water in some low pools.
A quality rich fen dominated by Carex lasiocarpa with some small open water pools with Utricularia intermedia and Menyanthes trifoliata.
Wet forest with standing water in pools over 20% of plot. Hummocks with bryophytes - Plagiomnium.

This plot is located on an area of high ground adjacent to the Clearwater River and surrounded on the west, north, and east by low conifer swamp. It's a sandy alluvial island that doesn't classify out well as FDc23 or FDc24.

Moderate coarse woody debris, transitioning fire dependent stand with jack pine declining; red pine inclusions with some encroachment from balsam fir. Predominantly moss on the ground layer, little development in the shrub layer - no fire scars visible - dry sandy ridge in a larger wetland dominated area.

npc_type_name: Green Ash - Bur Oak - Elm Forest
remarks: No worm evidence, topography with only minor elevation change. Between dryer aspen/oak areas and wetter aspen/ash zones. Similar to another, relatively nearby releve in Beltrami County recorded by Erika Rowe.

Small poor fen surrounded by mixed hardwood conifer forest. Releve taken in center, more tamarack and Carex lacustris near fen edges. A road with a cattail filled ditch runs along 1 side. 15 acres total. Small depression on till plain.

Uncommon patch of mature, large red and white pine. Hardwood forest matrix (perhaps glimpse of what region looked like in past). Bordered on all sides by clearcuts or roads. Recommended to county forestry as high conservation value forest. Topography is rolling. Plot appears to be on s-curve. Large coarse woody debris is conifer. 24-30 inch red pine diameter.

Representative plot of larger area, much of which has been recently harvested. Terrain is rolling till. Duff layer is only one season thick, so worms are present. Coarse woody debris is low. Top of slope, 8% azimuth grade. 25cm hit pebbles.

Gradually sloping towards the Clearwater River, multiple slopes on plot, no stumps, some standing dead trees. Plot on upper alluviual sand along the Clearwater River. Loamy sand without signs of redox - somewhat grey matrix with organic material present.
Deep sedge peat saturated with shallow water featureless water tract.

Low upland plot with large, healthy examples of all species. Little elevation gain from surrounding wet forest. Moderate to low amounts of coarse woody debris. One very large bur oak ~ 3 feet DBH. No evidence of cut stumps. One large basswood at 2.5 feet DBH. Generally flat, soils with high organic content. Duff 1-2 inches think, no worms.

Fen mat community dominated by Carex lasiocarpa with shrub component of Betula pumila and Andromeda glaucophylla. Generally species poor, no surface water, but saturated. Much wetter and likely inundated earlier in the year.

Water track feature dominated by Rhynchospora alba. Small linear pools present and include one listed species, Rhynchospora fusca; in small linear flows. Carex livida easy to pick out. Some open (shallow 1-2 inches) water, void of vegetation.

Aced peatland (open), vegetative pattern at this location differs from surrounding areas (although same community), far less graminoid cover than remainder of the community in the immediate vicinity, sphagnum carpet. pH range from 6.5-10.

Open peatland community of Betula pumila and graminoids, hummocks with feather mosses and other bryophyte specks. Forb diversity low with Rubus arcticus common on the moss hummocks. No surface water observed.

Rich fen community in the western water tracks. This is an extensive community dominated by Rhynchospora alba with sundews in exposed muck along with Utricularia cornuta. Common forbs include Sarracenia purpurea and Menyanthes trifolia.
Peat soils - graminoid. Releve to characterize a rich fen community. 4-6 inches of water over mat surface at time of documentation.
Releve to characterize a spring fen with Carex exilis as the dominant with pockets of Cladium mariscoides and Rhynchospora fusca. Mix of Sphagnum and graminoid fibric peat.

Birch and jack pines dying or dead: stand is <80 years. Last burned and logged near turn of century - cut stumps. Best area in the stand. Closest representative of pine forest. Soil: Entisol with no visible charcoal - probably prairie in the past.

Coarse woody debris moderate to high, near bottom steep slope about 30 degrees. One rare, large, stump. The steep slope continues towards shoreline where it becomes a steep, ~100ft ridge top. Upslope, bur oak becomes dominant with Celtis. Menispermum is also common outside plot. Only on this ridge, mostly the sides that are east facing (more protected) have Celtis. Have not seen this community elsewhere.
Occasional stumps, ground heavy with Dicentra. Leaf litter and coarse woody debris moderate. Rolling topography, slopes slightly to south and southwest, about 2 degrees? Not far from FDn33a.

One white cedar measured 14in DBH, tree core was also taken and was 130 years old (60ft teall). Soil is fibric peat. Hollow development minimal. Area surrounded by very wet ash swamp to the west and north.

Wet meadow opening. Area varies between sedge dominated and shrub dominated. Part of a larger mosaic of lowland rises with aspen and cedar and wet meadows and black ash swamps south of Mahnomen Creek.
Bog drain on south side of large raised forested bog. Open pools about 1 x 2 feet and sometimes 3 x 5ft. Very wet. Water at peat surface.

Aspen, mineral island in peatland complex near Mulligan lake Peatland. Varies from wet-mesic at margin of island to more mesic in the interior. Releve in wetter area. Water seeping in small soil pit at about 6 inches down. Aspen are often growing on slightly elevated mounds. Coarse woody debris is mostly small DBH. Soils are pure, fine sand. Slightly oxidized. Moose pellets nearby. Soil is 1.2cm litter over 1.2cm humus, with an A horizon from from 2.4cm to 3cm over sand.
Water flowing through/under hummocks. Hummocks medium size, hollows occasional. Hummocks covered mainly with Pleurozium and Sphagnum.

Mat is firm, not floating where releve was done, which was closer to forest. However, species are similar throughout, with the exception of Platanthera dillatta. Nearby, Betula is about 4 feet high and forms dense margin around forested swamp. Water level in releve is about 6 inches above peat surface. Thatch heavy. Brown mosses only. Swans and other duck species are common on lake.

Releve done more in shrubby area closer to mineral island. But this is fairly typical of fen here. Although there are more open (less shrubby) areas throughout that have more Thelypteris palustris instead. Moss cover is about 75%. pH is 7.7. Bouncy mat. Water is slightly above peat surface.

Fire scars on black ash of 38cm DBH? Pools 3-8 inches deep common, very wet. Not much vegetation growing in pools. Coarse woody debris is low, some fine material. This community is a long east-west running subtle ridge of largely black ash. Slightly higher areas have aspen. Surrounded by massive Larix swamp. Average canopy black ash DBH: 30cm; average subcanopy black ash DBH: 15.

Very bouncy mat. No distinct pools with marl deposits, just Sphagnum hollows. Water at peat surface. Many plants still just in early development. Cladium mariscoides flowers just starting to open or develop. Arethusa bulbosa scattered throughout. Winter road travels through fen. Tracks are evident. Very shrubby to north (outside releve). With Potentilla fruticosa common. Lots of thatch, and areas where Schoenoplectus acutus is very dense.

Old growth red pine (old growth forestry stand - Red Lake State Forest). Appears to have been thinned a while ago - very open understory and cut stumps are common. But ground layer is nice and in good shape. No evidence of disturbance otherwise. Good pine regeneration. Realized after doing plot that I am in a clearing that has been thinned of shrubs because of deer stand. Areas nearby have much more hazel. Broad-leaved evergreens are benefiting from the opening. Cutting and pine plantations surround this stand. Cored: average canopy red pine at 44cm DBH, 93 years old. Soil profile: 1/2cm of needle litter of 1 cm humus; 2 to 2.5cm sandy loam over brown sand >2.5cm.

Water at peat level. Betula shrub level is fairly consistant, but with occasional areas more open with lots of Iris. Documenting shrubbiness and ditch/road impacts. Sphagnum mostly on raised hummocks with Betula. Location in NW corner.

Water at peat level. No Sphagnum. Large fen complex with several small upland islands, large patches of Phragmites outside plot common. Although close to boundary, vegetation seems uniform throughout. Very bouncy peat.

Water at peat level. Not a bouncy mat - very firm. Very different from north side of road. Although close to road, vegetation is uniform throughout. Believe that this side is burned frequently. Fen complex in this area of releve has little to no Phragmites or Typha anywhere.

Medium high hummocks of Sphagnum/feather mosses. Hollows small and minimal with no standing water. Occasional cut stump, but very old. Small DBH of Larix and Cedar about 10-20cm. Occasion hollows with shallow water.

Soil moist muck. No standing water in hollows. Cedar regeneration on occasional rotten log, but not common. Releve representative of larger mosaic of WFn53 and WFn55 and open wet meadow area that is surrounded by peatland complex.

Water level slightly below peat level. Appears to be transitioning to rich fen, as there are more concentrations of Sphagnum near center of wetland. and releve includes typical amount that is patchy throughout.
Water at peat surface, sedge peat; semi-bouncy. Areas near by with more Betula. Releve in more sedge dominated area. Good diversity of bryophytes. No Sphagnum. Scattered Larix from 5-20ft nearby.

Some Sphagnum. See associated releve # 9979, in adjacent open area. This releve documenting area with more tamaracks. Small hummocks about 1/2 ft high. Minimal microtopography, even where there are large, mature tamaracks.

Interior of forest island. Coarse woody debris medium, mostly fine-medium; not many large down or rotten trees. Two canopy Fraxinus look cut, but they are both laying next to stumps. Moose pellets (last years?). Soil to 6 inches is fine loam with some clay. Picea glauca large in canopy, ~60-70cm. A couple of the Fraxinus are ~40-50cm, but most Fraxinus in canopy is ~20-30cm.

Water pH is about 6.8. Drosera anglica only in NE pools of plot. Seems like majority of Eleocharis pauciflora in SW corner. Marly pools with about 40% cover. Graminoid cover at about 50% Difficult to determine. Corners of plot at 70 degrees, PVC pipe in SW corner. Very shaky loose mat. Water at peat surface. Chara species common in marly pools. This releve, as opposed to releve #9983, documents pools with less Scirpus acutus.

Eleocharis rostellata plot. Almost in center of plot is one Picea mariana about 10ft tall, one Larix about 5 feet tall and two cedars about 4ft tall. E. rostellata dominates about 2/3 of plot. Marly pool near SE corner and only comprises about 5% of plot. SW corner marked, corners at 45 degrees.

Not typical of surrounding area but still a large area that's distinct. Keep encountering this type and not clear what community it is. It is semi-open and semi-poor. High hummocks, hollows dry. Moss is dried out - no rain for a while. Lots of cedar regeneration. Many young cedar tipped over. Cedar and spruce mostly small DBH.

Moss mainly on bases of trees and downed woody debris. Not a thick layer of leaf litter, but humus layer is 2-3 inches thick. Very subtle topography, quickly changes nearby to wetter vegetation. Releve in more dry area. Appears to be a natural origin aspen stand. Oak in canopy look very old. Aspen are about 60-75 years old with several young ones coming in. No cut stumps. Occasional medium sized boulders at surface. Soil is light gray loam/silt (?) in upper 6 inches. Island surrounded by rich fen.

Previously burned, possibly annually. Surface is moist, but no standing water. Firm substrate. Phragmites common throughout, but not in plot area. Occasional clumps of shrubs including Betula pumila and Salix. Aboout 200 ft west of ditch/road. no Sphagnum.
Water below peat surface. Firm mat. Fen dissected by road. Willows dominate margins. Shrubs minimal, further away from road. Native plant community is OPn92a or OPn91b.

Water slightly at or below peat surface. Releve to document fen on east side of road (upslope). west side of road - more shrubby and OPn92-like. This side more OPn91-like. Native plant community is OPn91a or OPn92b. Mosses mostly brown mosses (campyllium??).

Occasional old cut stump. Average canopy tree DBH 15-20cm, but occasional larger DBH <= 30cm. Minimal hollow microtopography, no standing water in hollows. Part of a larger tamarack swamp south of Mulligan Lake. Community could be a mix of FPn81/82.

Releve in drier aspen/cedar areas typical of larger area. Possible old decayed stump in plot. Occasional areas of low spots where no vegetation, and probably ephemeral pools in spring. Light gray soil - silty fine sand to about 6 inches. Fine-medium coarse woody debris common. Occasional old tip-up. Native plant community is WFn53b or MHn44/45.

Ground moist, not bouncy. Water level below peat surface. Thatch fairly thick. No hummock/hollow topography. Fire scars on some shrubs. Small patches of Phragmites throughout. Releve indicative of entire fen. Ground mineral soil.

Releve done in moderately shrubby area. May not have represented all Carex due to late season. Several large boulders emerge at surface. Soil is moist, but not saturated. Fire scars on willows and coarse woody debris. Areas of bare soil, various mosses are patchy. Nearby area with scattered tall (20-40 ft) aspen, appear mostly cut. Patches of Phragmites nearby, but not a lot.
Soil is moist but not saturated. Releve represents more sedge dominated area. Releve nearby (9992) is on slight rise with aspen. Occasional Betula nearby.

Youngish aspen woodland. Disturbed feeling with fair amount of invasives. However, this is typical for many aspen woodlands of this type in this region. Canopy aspen appear to be around 50 years old. Native plant community is either FDw44b or FDw34b.
Thick thatch, no Sphagnum, and very little moss cover.

Wet meadow with occasional shrubs, mostly around edges of wetland. They consist largely of Salix petiolaris or discolor. This releve is documenting the wet meadow without the shrubs, which is dominant in middle area. Wetland currently dry. Lots of Cirsium arvense here, some spots with heavier amount, which is why it is ranked BC. Forest surrounding this wetland is junk. It is full of Phalaris and other weeds; dominated by Fraxinus, Populus tremuloides, and Populus balsamifera.

Releve represents a graminoid dominated opening, surrounded by tall willows. Nearby, there are small upland rises with aspen. No standing water. Dense thatch. Ground is moist, but not saturated. Larger swamp is dominated by areas mostly of tall willows, however there are areas, such as this releve, that are slightly different in species diversity and are large enough to be mapped as something else like wet meadow.
Releve represents a more shrubbier aspect than releve 9997. Tall scattered aspen nearby. Areas of tall willow more dense in some areas outside releve. Moist hummocky ground.

place_name: Lake of the Woods State Forest
remarks: Large area of bedrock outcrop. Cladina and Crustose lichens. Several jack pine regenerating. In nearby shady areas, Sphagnum is common and so is Picea mariana. Pink-hued granite is dominant rock exposed. Extensive carpets of Polytrichum and Pluerozium common. This community is relatively small, about 5 ac. surrounded by FDn22a; which transitions to mesic-wet hardwoods.

place_name: Lake of the Woods State Forest
remarks: Canopy open with lots of aspen tip-ups. Loamy soil with lots of boulders. Several large dead jack pine. Adjacent to wetter aspen. Trying to capture drier jack-pine woodland.
Very little shrub layer. Leaf litter thin, but present. Rolling topography subtle. Tilia often multi-stemmed. Coarse woody debris is low.
Med-high hummocks, water at peat surface. Hollows not very common, when present they have Utricularia. Scattered dead Larix at about 5 feet tall.

Releve away from water's edge about 15m, where it is more representative of sedge dominated fen here. Drosera anglica is common closer to water as well as Scheuchzeria. Lots of game trails to water. Swan nest nearby. This west side of water is much less shrubby as well as less Larix. Water at peat surface.

Low even hummocks, little to no microtopography. Areas of Scheuchzeria dominant. More Betula scattered here than at releve upslope. See releve number A006, which was placed south of here. Stunted Larix outside plot, but only occasional. Water at peat surface.  These releves are documenting vegetation on the hydrological gradient of Sphagnum lawn.

Low to medium hummocks. Little hollow development. Water table at peat surface. Near Paul's equipment. Releve documented vegetation upslope on expansive Sphagnum lawn. Related releve was done downslope of here - see releve #A005. NE corner of plot marked with PVC pipe.

High sphagnum fuscum dominated hummocks about 2 feet high. Mistletoe present and fairly widespread, already some mortality in 2-20m range. Also some blister rust affecting needles or spruce. Water table at about 6cm below peat. Occasional moist hollows. 4 corners marked with PCVC pipe.This is to resurvey old glaser releve #4165. Releve marked on middle of north line, south of old Glaser E/W transect (old trees cut at 2 ft above peat). Metal tag at NE corner on Larix. Tree marked at about 0.7m from ground; tag 103 degrees azimuth from stake to tree. Water sample taken by P. Glaser.

Releve at edge of water track on east side approximately 50 yards from edge of raised bog island. One small patch of Sphagnum entering plot otherwise very little moss cover. Water at and slightly above peat surface. Andromeda appearing just as short sprigs growing uniformly throughout. Sphagnum hummocks with Larix about 6 ft tall nearby - 4.7m SE corner. Plot marked at old PVC pipes from original Glaser plot (#4137). Old releve #4165 is marked in interior of Spruce east of this releve in raised bog.
Area of seepage wetland complex; gently rolling prairie. This is the best part of this little prairie edge.
Most clearcut oak signature in site, perhaps in county. Brownish - red signature on CBM series photo. However sufficient maple that this is a former sugarbush  (old buckets all over).

Second growth forest. ~25 years old. Cut stumps moss-covered. Intact ground layer. Canopy P. banksiana starting to DY/DD. Slender recent CWD common. Larger (20cm + dbh) CWD moss-covered common. Gravel pis in vicinity. Recent timber harvests in adjacent forests. Soil drainage class: excessively well - well drained.

Fire scars on older stumps. Cut stumps common, 25%-50% decayed. Worms present. CWD small-medium common <25% decayed, +/- moss covered. Grassy trail <20 m from plot edge. WFn55 <5 m from plot edge and at nearly the same elevation. Ground layer intact - assumed winter harvest. Some recent blowdown (Populus trem). L1-1 estimated with CWD mosses and soil surface moss, doesn't include vertical structures with moss. Purpose of releve = training site.

Plot used for Kooch County ECS training site. CWD common, lacking large CWD. Wormed. DBH of Pop. trem. 12-15" average. Abies 3"-4" average. Within a broad, generally flat till plain within close proximity to the Kooch Peatland LTA. CWD variously moss-covered. Fire scars on stumps in near vicinity outside of plot. Soil drainage class is "Somewhat poorly to Poorly."

Topographic context: middle-lower. JP and Picea mariana +/- open grown. Scattered lichen-covered bedrock with/in NPC, one 4 square meter example in plot. No cut stumps observed in plot but 75% decayed stumps to W, S, and SW within same NPC. Old CWD observed without burn scars. Plot typical of JP dominated areas within matrix forest. Most observed stumps appeared natural with associated deadfall.
Topographic context: Middle-Lower. Cut stumps ~50% decayed, lichen-covered bark, cf Pinus banksiana. Similar to BWC R10-01 on same date - here more of a forest, less woodland. Canopy dbh 5-7".
Moss restricted to rocks. Ground layer with leaf litter feels ~ spongy. Scattered tip-ups common of all species. No fire scars observed. Cut stumps 80% decayed. Plot ~ 70m from lakeshore.
A lot of jack pine blowdown in vicinity. Many standing JP DD or DY.

Additional surveyor: Kevin Bergstrand. Cut stumps throughout stand. Last harvest recorded from 1980. Canopy gaps occasional throughout. Surrounding stands either pine plantations or WF cedar. Fire scars on oldest snag - none as younger CWD. Tip ups uncommon. No invasive plants observed within stand. Overall +/- pit and mount microtopography. 

Notes: ~110 basal area - Kevin estimated visually. Litter type = needles and leaves. Humus type = fungal mat.

70 acre island in Rainy River. Plot captures the most common NPC this being one of three ground layer variations. Compare to DNR Releves ___ and ___. CWD common of all sizes with patchy windrowing of slender CWD from flooding. No cut stumps in plot but widely scattered fairly recent cut stumps and downed. No soil probe - soils estimated by hand digging. 

Notes: All dbhs (max, min, mode) from Acer saccharinum except one Frax pens. NPC fits with FFn57 description although it shares some FFn67 characteristics such as a silver maple dominated canopy. But, 9+" of rain fell here in last 30 days - a near record for area, and stand shows no signs of being recently flooded. No ice scars on trees observed.

Compare to R10-06 - this plot ~ 1 foot higher in elevation than R10-06. CWD common in all sizes and decay stages. No cut stumps in plot but are widely scattered throughout NPC. Plot within 10 m of WMn. Area received near record rainfall in July 2010 (9+") yet no signs in plot of recent flooding. No ice scars on trees. Windrowed debris not as evident as R10-06. Soil data was taken from Releve #A018 (R10-06).

Notes: Core taken from 19" Frax. nigra.

Plot occupies canopy gap commonly scattered in NPC. Microtopography with hollows and stages, pits holding water. Recent heavy rains. Cedar patchy in NPC. Adjacent intact canopy with Smilax ground layer. NPC occupies large basin in large island on Lake Vermilion. CWD of all sizes occasional to common. All decay classes of CWD. No cut stumps observed.

Plot on Pine Island on Lake Vermilion, near (5-10 m) from the slope (same NPC). Moose and deer browse on Acer spicatum. Cut stumps were decayed (75 So.)(?), scattered. No fire scars observed. CWD is common, especially Betula papyrifera. Abies balsamea blow-down common in area. Fir and spruce dying or dead. Assumed worms based on thin litter layer. 

Notes: other large blowdown in NPC (basswood and Populus).

NPC occupies highest elevation on the island. No cut stumps observed, past logging assumed given aspen size. CWD uncommon. Assumed worms based on little duff and hard soil. NPC is minor component on island. Lies on high point between FFn57a and WMn. No standing water. Min, max, and mode tree DBH data is for Populus tremuloides only.

Plot chosen to represent small patch native plant community frequently occurring on east shore and small islands of Birch Lake. Often linear in shape on crest and slopes to lake. Occasionally with Pinus resinosa dominant. No evidence of past harvest. Charcoal at surface. Patch of blowdown (Pinus banksiana, P. mariana, Abies balsamea) as south end of releve native plant community. No evidence of worms observed.

Plot chosen to represent a native plant community typical on exposed bedrock with little to no soil accumulation. This native plant community on island in Denley Creek Channel. No past human disturbance. No evidence of worms. Location 3-4m above water channel. Vertical rock wall to water not included in plot. NW aspect of island is FDn32.

Plot chosen to represent native plant community common in land type association. AB rank only because of small size. Natural origin. Charred snags near plot. Betula papyrifera occasional elsewhere in this patch of native plant community. No evidence of worms observed. Moderate amount of coarse woody debris in various states of decay.

Plot chosen to represent part of forested wetland complex surrounding small isolated pond in basin among bedrock-controlled hills. Channel flow obvious but low and diffuse. Hummock and hollow micro topography. Sphagnum and feather mosses abundant on coarse woody debris and tree bases. Pools common but most moist versus standing water. AB rank for small size.

Plot chosen to represent high quality natural origin native plant community in this setting in Ely Knife Bedrock Complex Land Type Association. Moderate coarse woody debris in various states of decay. Pinus strobus seedlings and saplings common to abundant in releve and in FDn32 and FDn43 native plant communities in area. No evidence of worms observed.

Plot chosen to represent (comparatively intact) native plant community common in this land type association in this setting, elsewhere heavily impacted by '99 blowdown and prescribed fires. This is remnant of patch with more damage elsewhere. AB rank for size. No evidence of worms observed. Plot with five Pinus banksiana blown down.

Plot chosen to represent natural fire (Fraser Lake 1976) origin forest patch. Micro topography is high associated with pits, mounds, rock outcrops and small shallow bedrock depressions which may perch water. Moderate coarse woody debris. No evidence of worms observed. Patch canopy ranges from 100%-10% in exposed bedrock areas. No density dependence mortality in Pinus banksiana yet. FDn43 dominated by Pinus banksiana common in land type association but not well-described in native plant community classification.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent natural fire origin native plant community common in this setting in this land type association. Many similar native plant communities in this area impacted by recent prescribed burns. Plot includes low south facing rock wall about 8m long. Moderate amount of coarse woody debris from 1999 or later. No evidence of worms observed. On slope below plot, scattered very decayed cut stumps.

Plot chosen to represent small patch native plant community in this land type association. Pools of standing water common. Thuja and Fraxinus coarse woody debris common, average 20cm DBH in varying decay classes. Mosses, especially Sphagnum growing on upturned roots, decaying coarse woody debris, and tree boles. No past human disturbance. AB rank due to size.

Plot chosen to represent rich wooded wetland expression in this land type association. Small patch native plant community. Plot in area of old canopy blowdown with conifer recruitment in progress. Other parts of this basin native plant community have dense cover of Betula pumila; bedrock outcrop shoals; >50% canopy of mature Picea and Larix. Occasional water filled hollows throughout. No past human disturbance evident.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent native plant community common in this setting in this area of land type association. Natural fire origin. Southeast corner of plot is steep bedrock outcrop slope. To north on top of ridge slope is FDn43a - common pattern on these bed rock controlled features. Moderate amount of coarse woody debris in various sizes and stages of decay. No evidence of earthworms. Dead and dying mature Populus tremuloides and Betula papyrifera common in vicinity. A few Pinus strobus in plot with dead tops.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent native plant community common in this area of land type association. Natural fire origin. Pinus strobus < or = 37cm DBH. Soil > or = 15cm but only in small depressions in bedrock substrate. Little coarse woody debris present. No evidence of earthworms.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent native plant community expression on bedrock-controlled features common in this area of land type association. Natural fire origin. Plot includes two broken vertical walls </= 6m high. Lichens cover exposed bedrock. Thuja present nearby in this native plant community. Large coarse woody debris present but infrequent. Small DBH coarse woody debris common. Plot includes both crest and upper slope. Slope ranges from 0-100 degrees. No evidence of earthworms. No anthropogenic disturbance. Soil in pockets, </= 15cm deep.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent vegetation resulting from 1950-60s harvest in FDn pine native plant communities. Stumps widely dispersed and very decayed. Part of large area of conifer harvest. No non-natives observed in plot or general area. Large erratic near by. Pinus resinosa, 25cm DBH cored at 50-60 years. Source of regeneration natural and/or artificial seeding. Not planted. Minimally constructed access routes do not fragment patch.

Plot chosen to represent matrix native plant community originating after 1936 fire and associated with soil profile documented by NRCS ecological site description program. Large Thuja burned in 1936 observed in plot; some salvage of these. Moderate to large coarse woody debris. Worm castings observed, no middens. Soil layers two and three with high silt; 1-3% cobbles also present in soil layers 2-4. At 43cm high color (3%), low chroma (5%); coarse loamy rainy till series - unnamed at this time.

Plot with unknown origin, furrows about 45cm wide as long as 15-20m. Treefall gaps common. Soil mineral horizon designations: A, Bw1, Bw2, Bw3, E&Bt (sand with loamy sand lamellae). Parent material: outwash.

Community position between OPn92 and APn81. Shape is linear width 20-30m south to north. Outside of plot are scattered black spruce about 11cm DBH. Notes: dug 60cm pit but no water reached. 28cm depth where peat changes to hemic. Substrate becomes muckier and darker brown with depth.

Plot placed to avoid shrub clumps. Area as whole seems transitional between wet meadow and rich fen as if water fluctuations/oscillations determine which community it resembles most. Sphagnum appears stranded as water rises/falls. Zonation of communities heterogeneous. Patches of Phragmites common closest to water. Pit dug down to 20cm. Brown fibric peat. Releve located within matrix of rich fen, shrub shore fen, and near shore wet meadow. Distance from water to APn81 is about 50m. Releve community is patchy throughout this 50m width as there are also circular patches of Myrica gale and larger patches of Chamaedaphne calyculata.

One of the larger ROn12 seen in state surrounded by Pinus banksiana, P. resinosa, P. strobus, and Acer rubrum. Of the 98% bedrock, 35% is completely bare rock without growth of plants, lichens, or moss.

npc_subtype_name: Jack Pine - Black Spruce - Aspen Subtype
remarks: Coarse woody debris of Pinus banksiana common, stimulating origin of Betula papyrifera. Slope variable with steep rock benches. Beaver activity seen on small diameter trees, high percentage of rock below 10cm from surface. Plot on slope of bedrock island with exposed bedrock/outcrop areas. Coarse woody debris common. Stand with variable slope and rock benches 10-15 degrees. Area surrounding releve with more aspen in canopy. Sparse litter of birch leaves and needles present. Carex with red base, clump forming. Carex with no red base has 5mm wide leaves.

Aquatic vegetation survey. F1-3 vegetation category is interrupted to continuous 70-80%. Note: heights of anything other than submerged or floating begin at water level surface. Releve plot bounded by shrub shore fen, closest distance is about 15 meters. Past water depth of 60cm lies >140cm muck (Gyeta substrate - sediment algae, well-decomposed organics suspended).

Charcoal detected in soil. Bedrock benches common. Irregular topography. Large pines in vicinity. Stand is uneven age aspen stand. Aspen are falling in older size classes, but regenerating in younger classes. Litter of leaves and needles present. Surrounding area outside of releve with heterogeneous canopy; majority is large red and white pines, balsam fir, aspen, and birch. Gaps are common with thick Corylus cornuta outside of plot.

Zone of Carex lasiocarpa bounded by Muskeg Creek and Chamaedaphne shrub zone to west just before hitting APn81 black spruce peatland. Width of sampled zone is about 10 m wide hence the 5x20m plot. To south is zone of Carex utriculata. Pockets of deeper water (~20m) present with Utricularia spp. Sedge and grasses occur as tussocks. Of the two OPn92 graminoid expressions (ie Carex lasiocarpa and Carex utriculata), the former is dominant. Stand is close to Muskeg creek and shrub shore fen to west. Typha angustifolia invading surrounding areas, in small patches.

Plot situated midslope above drainage where black ash occurs and between crest of slope where canopy gets more open, more white pine appears and shrub layer is heavier. Both Populus grandidentata and P. tremuloides occur together with latter more downslope. Large boulders occur throughout plot. Earthworms present in soil: 1(low) rapid assessment rank.

Plot has abundant hollows where water was present above soil surface earlier in the year and few plants were growing at time of survey. Trees growing on mounds above hollows (30cm). Larger context of plot is basin/drainage of surrounding uplands. Coarse woody debris present of ash and yellow birch. 6cm of fibrous root layer.

Survey of south facing slopes as entered from road on west side of section. South-facing knolls support southern dry hill prairie on the convex slopes with woody invasion coming up the intervening ravines. Steep slope with oak at base. Adjacent to overgrazed native pasture.
BC rank slope east of ravine before reaching group of planted spruce.
Northeastern most slope of tract.

Releve from a long northeast facing spur above walnut planting. Distinguished by the presence of Coreopsis palmata and Phlox pilosa, which tend to push it more toward a mesic prairie classification. Graminoid component is dominated by Sporobolus heterolepis. The cover abundance of woody species represent only the releve area, everywhere else the cover of sumac is heavy except for adjacent northeast-facing knoll.

Releve represents a marginal northwest facing knoll, CD-rank. The cover-abundance of woody species is only for opening in which the releve was placed. Adjacent level top of knoll dominated by smooth brome, with occasional prairie species.

These 2 releves are hayed and appear to rival every prairie bank looked at in Lyon county. South facing downslope between 2 trees on fence line. This should be a prairie bank; west side of Jerry Towne, North of Cottonwood River. Accompanied by releve A055.
Note presence of both Phlox and Coreopsis in this releve. Gentle, broad west facing slope maintained by haying. Accompanied by releve A054.

WMs83 tending toward calcareous fen at base of slope and edge of wetland complex, with audible hydrological discharge. Conservatively not identified as a calcareous fen, but some people would call it one; little peat buildup, bounce, or typical odor-very small extent.
Releve on slope above spring, south facing slope of spur. Topographic context: upper/middle.
This releve is on a slope that was recently grazed (all summer) and dry. Cattle were removed only two weeks ago. Steep southwest slope. Topographic context: upper/middle.
North facing slope. Topographic context: upper/middle.

Northwest facing knoll, near crest, northwest of Balaton Sewage Ponds. Characteristic of best portion of very narrow band of prairie slope between field and wetland complex to north. Adjoins C rank native pasture on steep slopes on same hill to south.
One of the best quality active pastures in county at time of survey. First ravine north of highway 14, west of Balaton. Topographic context: upper/middle.

Steep south facing slope dominated by little bluestem overlooking Plum Creek. Lower slopes below releve heavily invaded by Rhus glabra, plum, Symphoricarpos alba, Rhamnus cathartica, and brome dominant on level top of hill. Topographic context: upper/middle.

Steep northwest facing slope, graminoid dominated, diverse prairie. Slope just east of mouth of ravine that extends into a field to the south (ravine is also prairie). Topographic context: upper/middle.
Southwest facing prairie slope visible from road on west side of section when driving north. Very heavy dominance by Solidago canadensis. Long slow slope. Topographic context: upper/middle.
CD rank Ups13d, not very diverse, but no weed problems. Depauperate.

Jack pine-black spruce woodland with small patches of ROn12. Exposed rock generally covered by Pleurozium schreberi and lichen. Standing snags but little coarse woody debris. On saddle between Bruin Lake and spruce-tamarack acid peatland to the east. Some evidence of spruce budworm. Charcoal at mineral soil-humus interface.

These woods will look tired and degraded in the fall because the heavy dominance by spring ephemerals will leave much bare ground. Later in season Juglans cinera nut on ground, but could not find tree; convex higher slope with very little litter. Wormed and appears to have been pastured.

Stunted, Picea mariana-dominated conifer swamp on south side of Acorn Lake. Typical of extensive peatland complex surrounding lake. Plot approaching transition to lakeshore poor fen (see MDL12-7). Largest trees 8-10cm DBH. Deep peat, >30cm.

Wide range of tree diameters- largest recorded. Low hummocks, mostly moss-covered. Dry at this time. Deciduous shrubs and most of herbaceous layer generally confined to under small canopy gaps. 0.3m tall stumps (small diameter) sparse adjacent to and in plot. Decayed- fall apart easily. Many small diameter trees of each species. About 20% are larger diameter like those measured. Cedar regeneration present.

Younger stand, trees ~10-14cm DBH max, most under 10. Hummocky - no standing water at this time, although hollows appear to have held standing water recently. No cut stumps except perhaps one very old one. Boreal chickadee calling.

Large diameter (14-16in) ash forest with abundant coarse woody debris. Moderate level of deer browse, understory relatively open. Forest floor with moss and root hummocks; no standing water, but patches of litter-covered soil appear to have held water earlier. Some 2-4 inch diameter ash, but very few smaller. Tip-ups and other diverse microsites in and near plot. Earthworms present.

Releve in large OP/FPn73 areas north of western water track. Eventually this area grades into APn81 or FPn71. Logging nearby. This large shrub-fen has varying degrees of scattered Larix and Picea throughout; and varying degrees of Alnus and Betula pumila. Dry, although currently in severe drought.

Wet meadow follows Hansen Creek. Mostly there isn't much Typha angustifolia or Phalaris near here. In this spot, pretty good quality. More so west of here near road and old impoundment and upstream closer to Beaver dam. Meandering channel, low right now.

Soil is sandy loam >= 5 inches. Carpets of Carex sprengellii in patches. Lots of deer browse. This forest is similar to other narrow strips of forest nearby, along these sandy beach ridges. Some other areas have Viburnum lentago, however, this area does not.
No stumps seen. Some jack pine mortality (~5% in canopy). No jack pine regeneration. Coarse woody debris light-medium. Gently rolling terrain. Overall community size >20 acres? Soil is sand.

Cut stumps throughout. However, very large red pines present (ave. 60-75 cm DBH). Blue paint on them. Strange pit nearby, ~4ft deep 10x10 ft wide. Slightly rolling terrain. Mineral island surrounded by vast Larix peatland forest. Could be BC rank - seems slightly disturbed despite large white pines. Soil is light fine sand.

The oldest aspen and oaks are open grown. Canopy gaps common. Can go from dense shade to sunny opening. Soil is sandy loam, top layer 2-4 inches then moist, grey sand. Only 1 years worth of leaf litter. Worms seen. Coarse woody debris low, although there are a couple of large aspen snags. Transitions to terrace forest down-slope that follows north branch of rapid river. Quercus in canopy ~25-30cm DBH, occasionally really old open grown ones are 45-50cm; aspens are about the same. Native plant community could by MHw36 or FDw24b.

Peat very bouncy/buoyant. This wetland seems to be straddling the WMn82-OPn81 line, Native plant community could be WMn82b? Areas of heavy Typha and Phragmites, but areas without those spp. is good quality; such as here at releve. Water slightly above peat. Several sedges and grasses not yet blooming so difficult to tell what some of them are.

Lots of downed trees/coarse woody debris - mostly fir. Slight rise and subtle depressions with more Rhododendron. Releve in more solid upland. Occasional rare stump. Native plant community could be FDn32c2 or FDn43b1.

Even terrain of mosses. Minimal hollow/hummock development. Lots of browsed yew in plot and nearby. Releve represents large cedar band that appears to be drier than surrounding swamp and maybe on slight rise of mineral soil. This is evident on airphotos where cedars are taller and forms small NE/SW ridge through larger open canopied cedar swamp. Occasional old stumps of cedar. Occasional very large cedar; quite a range of DBH's. Some cedar regeneration. Native plant community could be FPn63c or FDn43c.

Occasional cut stumps, fire scarred. Large red pine (63cm) has fire scars up to about 5ft. Average black spruce in 20-30cm. Lots of downed trees, especially on margin - fir and spruce. Several large old jack pines dead and on ground. Several large old jack pines on margin (40-45cm), living. Soil in upper 6-8 inches is fine light grey sand. Native plant community could be FDn33c, FDn32d or FDn32c2.

Moderate coarse woody debris - occasional cut stumps (fire scared). A few dead jack pine snags. Releve on a crest between larger open APn91 and small depressions. Average jack pine DBH: 25-30cm; average red pine DBH: 35cm. Soils fine brown sand.

Medium hummocks, about 1-3ft high. Hollows are moss filled. Cutting going on in this community not far. Releve to document what this native plant community is that is being cut. Average DBH for spruce is 10-15cm.

Mature aspen woodland. Not a great time to do releve as ground layer species are dried up and brown. Under a severe drought currently. Probably missing some sedges and grasses as a result. Aspen are large and several aspen snags present. Canopy gaps common. Coarse woody debris is moderate to high. No stumps seen. Nicer aspen woodland seen in area; although small. Invasives are not bad. Average aspen DBH in canopy is 30-35cm, but several reach between 35-48cm. Soils are moderately wormed. Soil is sandy clay loam or sandy loam. Very gritty with a lot of little pebbles. mosses mostly on tree trunks.

Stand cut sometime around 1940's? No stumps evident, but recent photos show maybe more Larix in old strip cuts. North, about 50m, gets slightly smaller DBH Picea. Moss hummocks are patchy in some areas. Even terrain, no hollows. Average black spruce DBH 15-20cm; average tamarack DBH is 20-25cm.

Fair amount of thatch. Plot just outside margin of Cladium clone, to measure expansion of clone in future. Does it enter the plot in future years? Plot not exactly in old P. Glaser releve 0537 spot. Water slightly above peat surface. Small pools <= 2X2ft. Cladium is 1m beyond NW corner. Cladium is 8m from NE corner beyond(174 azimuth from NE to SW corner). Old plot has Drosera linearis and no Pagonia, could not located any D. linearis. NW corner of plot boundary (where Cladium touches) does not have a pole. Marked SW corner.

Mud pool in center of plot, about 30% cover. Occasional circular mound of Sphagnum cf sect. Sphagnum with Kalmia. Paul Glaser noted that plot seems drier with more Xyris than original plot. Rhyncosporus alba slightly more than R. fusca. Old Glaser releve 4233.

Evidence of old Christmas tree cutting, only occasional. High hummocks of Sphagnum from 2-3 ft. West side of plot more open. Mistletoe present in plot, airphotos show this. Old P. Glaser releve 4237, metal tag at southwest corner at pole on 15ft tall Picea.

Very firm mat. No standing water, level below peat surface, but surface is moist. Phragmites more abundant outside plot. Patchy. Releve is likely not marking original locations of P. Glasers releve #4229.

Picea circular island next to Paul's instruments. Eastern edge more forested (shadier) than rest. Center of plot dense Rhodedendron. Hummocky, lots of down spruce trees under Sphagnum. Paul G. thinks that there is more Smilacina and Larix than original plot, releve #4164. Mistletoe present.

SW corner marked and has more mud-openings. NE quarter of plot is Rhynchospora fusca. Water at peat level; bouncy. No bryophytes. Mud pools make up about 10% of plot. Releve adjacent to Picea island releve 4164. Original P. Glasers releves 4135/4136; not sure which one this releve represents - one was wetter.

Hummockes about 2-3 ft high; occasional hollows - no standing water, but at hollow level. Some downed trees, coarse woody debris moderate. Edges of plot just within tear drop margin. Old P. Glaser releve #4230. Plot location is entered from NW corner (400683/5334490), SW corner is UTM 5334488/400699.

A forested peatland with a tamarack and black spruce canopy. Dense shrub layer of Aldera nd leatherleaf. Shallows (?), pools with primarily Calla palustris. Open pools throughout with Calla and Potentilla palustris.

An upland island surrounded by forested peatland. Canopy is interrupted and includes Pinus strobus, Thuja occidentalis, and Abies balsamea. Trees in canopy and subcanopy are of uneven age. White pines are the largest and tallest of the grove. Down balsam fir on the island. Not much diversity. Litter of leaves and needles present.

A wet forest community with a canopy of cedar/black ash. Small micro-depression/pools which one likely inundated center in the year. Cedar and balsam fir are more prevalent in the shrub layer than black ash. Canopy 75-100% cover. Moss cover at the bore of the trees(non sphagnum species). Borders a mesic hardwood transition to the northwest.
Open fen community dominated by graminoid cover. Shrub layer almost absent with exception of Betula pumila. Releve typical of area, dominated by Rhynchospora alba.

Open fen community domianted by graminoid cover. Limited shrub cover, almost absent with exception of Betula pumila. Releve typical of area; Rhynchospora alba most prevalent graminoid. Historic ditching attempt near releve location. That area is now narrow with vegetation filling in(?) the linear pools.

Acid peatland community with a black spruce canopy (up to 15m). Canopy closed at sampling location, but opens up south of the plot. Sphagnum cover is almost continuous. Species poor, willows and Rubus idaeus located in a tip-up depression.

This relevé seems relatively atypical for the site. The surrounding areas have a higher forb cover with Helianthus spp. being the most abundant forbs. This particular relevé area may have experienced some form of anthropogenic disturbance in the past which has shifted the species composition.

This relevé represents a narrow community band that is perhaps ecotonal in nature. The community appears to be a calcareous fen dominated by Carex sterilis. Other calciphiles are present though never very abundant.

This relevé represents an area just down slope of a calcareous fen system. The community shifts away from dominance by Carex sterilis and towards a more diverse assemblage of forbs and grasses. Well-formed tussocks are present throughout.

This relevé documents a wet prairie community which is located just north of a calcareous fen community. This community is located along approximately the same topographic contour as the fen. Site is located at the base of a beach ridge.

This relevé documents a calcareous feature located at the base of a large beach ridge which runs NE to SW. Overall this area has an intact flora however this fen is not particularly different from the surrounding area in regards to stature and species assemblage. This relevé includes a diversity of calciphiles with Carex sterilis being the most abundant, adjacent areas include additional calciphiles such as Triglochin palustris.
This relevé is located in the center of a narrow opening within a stand of aspen. This relevé is relatively representative of the overall community however adjacent areas have more Salix spp.

This relevé documents a calcareous fen feature within a larger wetland complex at the base of a series of beach ridges. Overall this area is dominated by graminoids (mostly Carex sterilis) with a diverse assemblage of calciphiles.
This relevé documents a narrow community in the middle of a series of beach ridges. Overall this community is dominated by graminoids with a good assemblage of forbs.

This relevé represents a wet graminoid dominated community just down slope from a calcareous area (possibly calcareous fen). Though some calciphiles are present in this relevé these are far scarcer than the area up slope.
Marsh community located to the west of Frenchman’s Bluff. The area is dominated by Typha which may be a sign of altered hydrology. Overall this area is very species poor.

Open shrubby fen with stunted Larix and Thuja, surrounded by rich Larix swamp. This open community narrows to the southwest where water funnels into flowing pools. Water-filled trails cross fen in all directions, apparently created by deer, not water movement. They cover less than 5% of plot.
Shagnum lawn with some higher patches, some lower. Higher dominated by Carex oligosperma, lower by Rhynchospora alba. Probably influenced by lake level as managed by Minnesota Power.

Sphagnum lawn downstream of water track which has dissipated and emptied into this large open fen. No pools, and hummocks are very low. Probably influenced by lake level as managed by Minnesota Power.
Pools dominated by Carex limosa, Sphagnum lawn by Rhyncospora alba. Water is funneled here from southwest where the water track is narrower than here.

In fen water track coming from west along southside of open black spruce bog and flowing northeast from here. To south of here is Sphagnum lawn poor fen without Rhynchospora alba (APn91b), similar to Releve A112.

Floating mat lakeshore fen. Poor conifer swamp to north, sparse Zizania in lake to south. This community is in a band about 10m wide along lakeshore. Adjacent to north is APn91a with higher Sphagnum hummocks.

Pine forest on slope above open fen. No blowdown here, but some nearby forests have very open canopy. Decent amount of coarse woody debris, but mostly birch (and one fir), no large pine logs. Several birch and white pine snags in plot. Max red pine is 56cm; max white pine is 43cm. Average canopy trees are 35-40cm; birches are 20-25cm.

Young jack pine forest regrowing after older trees killed by fire. Some jack pine snags still standing, most fallen. Some dense young pine, some openings. Average pine is 10cm DBH, max is 15cm. Downed pines average 30-35cm. Possibly FDn32. Sandy loam just a few cm thick over apparent bedrock.

Stand straddles edge of patch of younger Acer rubrum, Betula papyrifera, and Populus tremuloides and patch of older Thuja and Betula alleghaniensis. Lots of coarse woody debris, mostly old Betula alleghaniensis logs. Old rotten pine stump with no corresponding log. Earthworms rank 5. Freshly fallen leaves on mineral soil. Moss on rocks and logs. Soil dry and impenetrable, appears to be moderately well drained.

Cedar dominated area with depressions that may hold water in spring. Lots of coarse woody debris, mostly cedar logs. Several old pine stumps with no corresponding logs. Earthworm rank is 5. Freshly fallen leaves over bare mineral soil. Moss on rocks and roots. Soil dry and hard, but appears to be moderately well drained or somewhat poorly drained.

Acer saccharum and Tilia americana dominated forest with some old pine stumps with no corresponding logs. Soil appears worm-free. No A-horizon to speak of. Appears to be 80-100 years old,with scattered older trees. Appears to be well drained MHn45b or MHn47a.

This is a linear feature associated with a small beach ridge with fens species (C. sterilis, R. capillacea, and E. quinqueflora). The relevé location includes a small flark-like feature. The community signature on the aerial photo is distinctive.
This is a graminoid dominated linear feature that includes several small flark components with R. capillacea. Shrub growth is generally stunted and the forb diversity is low.
This is a small calcareous fen feature associated with a minor beach ridge. The community is graminoid dominated with stunted shrubs. The relevé plot includes R. capillacea. and C. sterilis.

This relevé is located on the edge of the community boundary and adjacent to a wet prairie community. This particular community is graminoid dominated and species poor. Non-native cattails appear to be spreading.
This is a wet meadow community, graminoid rich and dominated by Carex pellita and a sparse shrub layer. Two individual plants of Carex sterilis were observed in the sample plot.
This is a wet prairie community dominated by graminoids with limited shrub cover.
This is a calcareous fen feature associated with a beach ridge. This particular location experienced fire earlier in the year and cattails appear less abundant in comparison to the surrounding area.

This is a calcareous fen feature with marl pools and associated with a beach ridge. The community at this location is dominated by Andropogon gerardii, Parnassia glauca, and Triglochin martima. This area experienced fire this past year and the shrub growth was limited as a result.
A wet prairie community dominated by graminoids and located at the base of a beach ridge. Shrubs are very sparse in the sample plot. Sonchus arvensis was observed commonly within the community.
This is a degraded calcareous fen feature with non-native cattails moving in. The plot location has the least amount of cattails within this area.
This is a calcareous fen feature; high quality in terms of vegetative diversity, rare species, and lacks disturbance.
This is a graminoid dominated community with dense cover of shrubs including willows, red-osier dogwood, and bog birch. A railroad is present to the east.
A small calcareous fen adjacent to a rail line and next to an encroaching patch of cattails. Shrub cover is minimal.
A calcareous fen community dominated by Carex sterilis on well-formed tussocks. Cattails appear to be moving in from west of the railroad. This fen was likely divided by the railroad.
A graminoid dominated community with significant shrub cover and hummocky throughout.
A calcareous fen opening dominated by Carex lasiocarpa with stunted shrub layer of Betula pumila. Plot includes Primula mistassinica and Carex sterilis.
This is a plot to characterize an ecotonal divide with Carex sterilis; graminoid dominated. West of a prairie restoration.
This is a wet prairie community dominated by Andropogon gergardii and late season composites. This area had been mowed and brushed earlier in the year. Sand mine nearby.
This is a calcareous fen community with a linear feature. The area is currently grazed by cattle. Pockets within are entirely dominated by Carex sterilis. Areas also with heavy/dense shrub cover.

Releve revisit of #4466, SW corner of plot marked with 1/2 galvinized conduit pipe. Cardinal directions from SW corner (plot layout). Site selectively logged in 2009 due to 2008 wind storm event. Soil is loamy sand over reddish brown sand.
Releve revisit of #4464; SW corner of plot marked with 1/2 inch galvanized conduit pipe. Cardinal direction plot layout. Site logged, timber salvaged in 2009 after 2008 windstorm.
Releve revisit of #4740. Site was logged/wood salved in 2009 due to 2008 windstorm event. Plot layout in cardinal directions from SW corner (pipe).

Releve revisit of original releve #4739. Plot SW corner marked with 1/2 inch galvanized conduit pipe. Cardinal directions used to layout plot starting in SW corner. Since 1994, site has experienced repeated prescribed burns. Cirsium hillii site.
Loamy sand over sand. Releve revisit of #4465. Site was logged - wood salvage in 2009 due to 2008 windstorm. Plot layout in cardinal directions from SW corner.
Margin of calcareous fen with shrub layer heavily dominated by Potentilla frusticosa. This appears to extend all the way to a band of Phragmites near the property line. Scattered tamarack.
Part of a seepage wetland complex developed on peat. Brushy fen areas with a lone tamarack merges into a transition zone with cattails and rises near property line to Phragmites.

Rich fen transitional area in seepage fen complex. This is the transitional edge at the toe of very gentle slope grading between prairie and fen. Not certain in classification whether prairie or fen. Releve should not be used for classification.

Old jack pine-black spruce woodland. Abundant, large downed logs (Pinus banksiana and some Picea mariana) in all stages of decay. No evidence of cutting. Plot in same NPC as University of MN bird plot (Ed Zlonis, Gerry Niemi). Plot placed adjacent to exact GPS coordinates for bird plot, to capture central concept of NPC and limit edge effects.
