Occasional large boulders on surface. Black-backed woodpecker feeding along trunk of Pinus banksiana. Charcoal evident at 4cm (bottom of humus layer). No evidence of worms. Bedrock outcrops are occasional along low ridge that is running parallel to the Little Isabella River.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Old growth red pine-white pine woodland. Plot is representative of a large, heterogenous landscape complex interspersed with FDn33a, small patches of ROn12 and areas of FDn43a/b1. Generally low-relief topography with bedrock close to the surface and low areas that accumulate and hold water for periods during the growing season. Balsam fir is not a dominant component and mostly with buds killed, presumably by spruce budworm. Community complex is predominantly coniferous and dominated by black spruce with jack pine on ridges and white pine throughout. Good black spruce and white pine regeneration. No evidence of worms or fire.  Deer sign light. Nancy Schultz assisted with releve.

Old Growth white pine-red pine forest (FDn43a). Approximately 1/3 of plot tending toward FDn32a. Canopy closer to 20m ht. with scattered individuals >10m ht.. Light browsing by deer (scat in plot). Charcoal at top of mineral soil layer. Scattered large downed logs (red pine and white pine recruited from canopy). Little-used illegal campsite along west portion of community (outside plot) with some evidence of cutting for campfire wood, but no compaction or non-native invasive species).

Rich black spruce swamp (FPn62a).  Well-developed micro-topography. Abundant hummocks and hollows. Regular recruitment of downed logs from canopy. No evidence of cutting, herbivory (browse) or Arceuthobium pusillum. Little-used wildlife trail, especially around the perimeter, along the edge of community.  Seedlings sparse (Piea mariana, Pinus strobus, Acer rubrum).  No evidence of fire.

Black spruce-feathermoss woodland. Community is variable between FDn32c1-c3.Abundant large downed logs in all stages of decay. Many large diameter Pinus banksiana down throughout patch. Herbivory (on aspen) and deer sign (scat)is light, with a minimal use wildlife trail. No graminoids were observed in plot or portions community traversed. Plot represents a somewhat variable community, with varying amounts of Picea banksiana, Populus tremuloides and Picea mariana in the canopy & scattered Betula papyrifera. Topography with rocky knobs and wetter hollows. No evidence of fire or worms.

Poor black spruce swamp (APn81a). Well-developed micro-topography (hummocks & hollows). Light recruitment of large, downed logs. Mild effects of Arceuthobium pussilum in canopy. Some portions of community patch are less treed, with higher cover of Rhododendron groenlandicum. Fairly fresh moose scat in plot.

White Pine-Red Pine Forest (FDn43a). Gray, leached horizon in soil (Site occupied by conifers for a long period). No evidence of worms.  Light browse, no scat. Ridge above plot is shallow to bedrock.  Moderate amount of large, downed logs. Micro-topography primarily from rock on or close to surface.

Aquatic releve at outlet of Bald Eagle Creek. Water depth 0.5-1.0 meters.Substrate organic, but bottom somewhat solid and shallow to bedrock. Nymphaea leibergii scattered throughout channel from this point to rock barrier at creek mouth. Creek channel ~20 meters across (open portion). Nearshore aquatic communities composed of Carex lasiocarpa, C. utriculata, Eleocharis palustris, Sagittaria latifolia. Nymphaea leibergii more abundant at mouth, where organics are less well-developed (flow?). Nymphaea cf. leibergii also at broad mouth of August Creek nearby.

Large, northern shrub shore fen/rich fen basin complex (OPn81a/OPn92a) with small, linear open pond. Andromeda glaucaphylla and Chamadaphne calyculata exhibiting die back (presumably from low water levels due to drought). Many linear channels within the community (perpendicular to the Isabella River). Low hummocks associated with Alnus incana and Betula pumila patches.  Beaver sighted and abundant sign (channels, chewed saplings). Increasing cover of Alnus incana and Salix petiolaris closer to river.

Large, northern shrub shore fen/rich fen basin complex (OPn81a/OPn92a) with small, linear open pond. Andromeda glaucaphylla and Chamadaphne calyculata exhibiting die back (presumably from low water levels due to drought). Many linear channels within the community complex (perpendicular to the Isabella River). Low hummocks associated with Alnus incana and Betula pumila patches.  Beaver sighted and abundant sign (channels, chewed saplings). Increasing cover of Alnus incana and Salix petiolaris closer to river.

Aquatic releve. Representative sample of the composition and relative abundance of aquatic vegetation with the Little Isabella River from BWCAW Entry Point #75 (Little Isabella River) to confluence with Isabella River.

Large black spruce bog adjacent to John Lake.  Much of adjacent lake edge is shore fen. Actively used moose trail (fresh scat)through bog to lake. Black spruce, especially in lower height stratas, with some evidence of spruce needle rust infection (cf. Chrysomyxa ledi / cf. C. ledicola) (yellow powder on needles).  Effects on tree viability unknown. Light cover of downed logs with dbh of canopy tree (~8cm). Moss hummocks overall  between 10-15 cm up to 40 cm (around tree boles).

White Pine-Red Pine Forest (FDn43a). Fire-scarred trees, snags and large downed logs scattered in plot and community. Evidence of cutting in the past. Evidence of dieback of Abies balsamea and Picea glauca (drought, lack of snow, deep frost 2011?). Pinus strobus (Populus tremuloides, Betula papyrifera)seedlings and saplings moderately browsed by deer.Micro-topography moderately well-developed. some areas with dense Abies balsamea and Acer rubrum pole-sized trees. Boulders on surface common. Community as a whole with about equal proportion Pinus resinosa and Pinus strobus in the canopy (in clumps). Upper 4 cm of mineral soil strongly leached (gray). Johnnie Hyde assisted with releve.

Northern Mesic Mixed Forest burned in Pagami Creek Fire (September 2011). Fire severity light to moderate. Soil surface is comprised of ash mixed with mineral soil for ~2 cm. Small patches of unburned herbaceous vegetation, with most of surface humus consumed. Scorch height ~7-10 meters. Clonal patch of aspen in canopy skipped by fire. Large white pine (95 cm dbh) charred at base and roots with ~25% of branches killed by fire. Adjacent large, white pine with <5% of branches burned. Post fire dead-fall covers ~25-50%. Post fire needle-drop 75-100% cover. Johnnie Hyde assisted with releve.

Floodplain forest along the South Kawishiwi River, with a mixed canopy of bur oak, green ash and silver maple. Seasonally flooded (water occasionally held back by Birch Lake Dam ~0.5 miles upstream). Roots of canopy trees are exposed and above soil surface. Many herb seedlings (annuals). Community occurs in narrow, linear patches along shorelines of mainland and islands, and  larger patches in low-lying areas along this stretch of river (between dam and White Iron Lake). Deep humus. Mineral soil (CL) with very few gravelly coarse fragments.

White pine-red pine forest (FDn43a). Canopy red pine with forked main trunks common throughout area (1 in plot w/fork at 10 meter height). Large downed logs mostly jack pine. Evidence of browsing on low shrub layer. Abundant fungi (club fungi & polypores). Old fire scar on large downed logs. Deer pellets in plot. No evidence of worms. Slope ranges from 0-20 degrees (ave. 10 degrees). Rock outcrop patch in plot. Down logs moderate, in all stages of decay (standing dead, recently downed, integrated into soil, etc.). Charcoal at 3 cm below humus. Daina Antanaitis assisted with releve.

npc_subtype_name: Jack Pine - Black Spruce - Aspen Subtype
remarks: Black Spruce-Jack Pine Woodland (Jack Pine-Black Spruce-Aspen Subtype).  Plot representative of high fire severity (both canopy and ground) within the FDn32c3 community in the Pagami Creek Fire area(September 2011). Moderate large, downed logs(burned), mostly recruited post-fire. Occasional tip-up mounds exposing bare soil. Litter layer composed of charred woody fragments and ash.  One individual each of Circium arvense and Leucanthemum vulgare located within community but far from plot. Profuse jack pine regeneration (seedlings) in plot and throughout community. Canopy aspen is dead but often not scorched above start of crown. Aspen suckers <5% cover but profuse number of stems. Daina Antanaitis assisted with plot.

Upland white cedar forest. Moderate amount of downed logs in all stages of decay (most logs on surface are Populus tremuloides with some Picea mariana). Micro-topography well-developed. Somewhat small patch, but without strong edge-effect. Abundant cedar regeneration (seedling-sized).  Many of the canopy trees are small diameter for height of tree. No evidence of fire or worms. Daina Antanaitis assisted with plot.

Small, graminoid poor fen (basin) adjacent to peatland pond Narrow band of shrub shore fen along edge of pond. Network of drainage-ways between shrub shore fen and graminoid poor fen. Moose trails. Surrounding uplands are black spruce-jack pine woodlands edge rapidly transitioning to mesic mixed forest with scattered white pine, jack pine, black spruce and paper birch. Hollows saturated with water at surface. Daina Antanaitis assisted with this plot.

Aspen-Birch Forest (Balsam Fir Subtype). Patch with varying amount of Pinus banksiana and Picea mariana in canopy overall. Small canopy clones of Populus tremuloides scattered throughout. Betula papyrifera canopy scattered in even distribution thoughout. Shrubs moderately browsed. Scattered small bedrock outcrops. Scattered moose scat. Abundant large, downed logs (mostly Populus tremuloides and Pinus banksiana). Abies balsamea moderate to occasionally heavy in shrub layer. Humus and mineral soils densely packed. No evidence of worms. Litter layer deep (5cm). No evidence of fire (no charcoal, no fire-scars). Soil powdery dry. Scattered standing dead canopy Pinus banksiana. Daina Antanaitis assisted with plot.

Aspen-birch Forest (balsam fir subtype, burned in the Pagami Creek Fire (2011). Some of canopy birch with concentrated sprouting.Large, downed logs sparse. Scattered small diameter downed logs. Funaria hygrometrica and Marchantia polymorpha are unusually sparse relative to other upland communities visited within the fire. Populus tremuloides (suckers) outside plot. A few canopy Betula papyrifera outside plot still alive, but dying. No evidence of worms. Fire severity high in both canopy and ground layer. Bare soil/ash ~5%.  Eric Ogdahl assisted with this plot.

White Cedar Swamp. Abundant hummocks and saturated hollows. No evidence of large-scale disturbance (anthropogenic or natural). Abundant cedar regeneration (seedlings & adventitious). Scattered old tip-ups and medium-large downed logs in various stages of decay. Micro-topography highly variable due to hummocks, hollows and tip-ups. Goodyera tesselata and Platanthera huronensis occur within the larger community patch, mostly in drier areas with larger trees (dbh & height), thinner organic (peat) layer, less sphagnum and sparser ground flora (WFn53a inclusions). Eric Ogdahl assisted with plot.

Bryo Transect AE2; Releve AE-RI OPn91a rich fen, far from ditch, moderately dense vegetation. Firm, shallow peat dominated by Betula pumila and Sali spp. with Carex matrix cover. Amorphous mixture of shrubs with few large gaps. Small mats of Sphagnum squarrosum with Drosera rotundifolia (area 1x1 m). Evergreens .3-5m tall - 1-5% cover; ever green seedlings 1-5%; tall deciduous shrubs 5-25%; mid-level shrubs(.5-2m) 50-75%;sub-shrubs 1-5%; grass and sedges 75-100%; forbs 1-5% and moss 75-100% cover.

Releve AE-R2 OPn91a; Releve just east of north-south ditch. Releve is typical vegetation. Shallow peat (actually appears to be OPn92 dominated by dense bog birch and willows). Tall shrubs 5-25% cover; mid-level shrubs 75-100% cover; sub-shrubs 25-50%; grass and sedges 50-75%; forbs 1-5%; and moss 50-75% cover.

2012 Bryo Transect AW1; Releve AW-R1 OPn91a rich fen, far from ditch, moderately dense vegetation. Amorphous water track fen dominated by bog birch and Carex species. Evergreen saplings <1% cover; mid-level shrubs (.5-2m) 50-75%; subshrubs 25-50%; grass and sedges 75-100% cover; forbs <1%.

2012 AW 100m Transect; Releve AW-R2 OPn91a. Releve includes ditch berm, resulting in conversion of OPn91 to WMn82a. Tall shrubs 50-75% cover; mid-level (.5-2m) shrubs 25-50%; subshrubs 5-25%; grasses and sedges 50-75%; forbs 5-25%; moss 25-50% cover.

Releve BE-R1 OPn91b2. Dense willow thickets developed from ditched OPn91. High shrub hummocks (20-30cm tall). Hollows with lake sedge. Salix hybrid with S. sericema and S. petiolaris. Tall shrubs 75-100% cover; mid-level shrubs (.5-2m) 25-50%; subshrubs 1-5%; grass and sedge 25-50%; forbs <1%; moss 25-50% cover.

Releve BE-R2 OPn91b2. Water track fen. Flark dominated by Carex lasiocarpa, Carex chordorrhize and Care prairea with springy vegetation mat and 10 cm water when depressed. Mid-level shrubs (.5-2m) <1% cover, subshrubs <1%; grass and sedges 75-100%; forbs 1-5% and moss 5-25% cover.

Releve BE-R3, OPn91b2. Water track fen - string; dominated by willows (including putative hybrid between Salix petiolaris and Salix sericema). Moss hummocks 10cm tall; deep sedge thatch. Mid-level shrubs (.5-2) 50-75% cover; subshrubs 5-25%; grass and sedge 50-75%; forbs 50-75%; moss 25-50% cover.

Bryo Transect BW1; Releve BW-R1 OPn91b2 rich fen, flark. Water track fen - flark dominated by Carex lasiocarpa and Carex prairea. Adjacent strings rather amorphous. Mid-level shrubs (.5-2m) 1-5% cover; subshrubs 1-5%; grass and sedges 75-100%; forbs 1-5%; and moss 50-75% cover.

Releve BW-R2 OPn91b2. Plot 4m x100m in area. Plot arcs along curve of Fen-string formed by tall bog birch and Phragmites. Substrate firm, bounded by flarks of Carex lasiocarpa. Shrub root hummocks with 20cm relief (tall). Mid-level shrubs 25-50% cover; subshrubs 5-25%; grass and sedges 50-75%; forbs 25-50%; moss 50-75% cover.

Releve BW-R3 OPn91b2. Roadside of winter road (west side). Degraded into shrub car (WMn82a) from water track fen (opn91). Tall shrubs 25-50% cover; mid-level shrubs (.5-2m) 50-75%; forbs 5-25%; moss (no data).

Releve CN-R1 OPn91b2. Waypoint at NE corner of Releve. Featureless water track fen. Some standing water. Photos from SE corner. Mid-level shrubs (.5-2m) 1-5% cover; subshrubs 5-25%; grass and sedges 75-100% cover; forbs 1-5%; moss 25-50% cover.

Ditch degraded OPn91 becoming wet meadow-shrub carr (WMn82a) dominated by tall Salix bebbii and Salix petiolaris. Tall shrubs 25-50%; mid-level(.5-2m) shrubs 75-100% cover; sub-shrubs 5-25%; grass and sedges 50-75%; forbs 1-5%; moss 5-25%.

Bryo Transect CS1; Releve CS-R1 OPn91a. Featureless water track fen. Releve plot less than 100m from ditch. Dominated by Carex lasiocarpa and Carex prairea. Salix 25-50% cover. Extensive moss cover in low carpets between sedge hummocks. Well transect. Herbs on shrub hummocks (roots). Mod-level shurbs (.5-2m) 25-50% cover; subshrubs 25-50%; grass and sedges 75-100%; forbs 1-5% and Moss 75-100% cover.

Releve CS-R2 OPn91a. Waypoints in NE corner of plot. Lines in N-W and E-W directions. Water track fen directly impacted by ditch parallel to plot. Beaver activity noted. Tall shrubs 50-75% cover;mid-level shrubs (.5-2m) 25-50%; sub-shrubs 1-5%; grass and sedges 50-75%; forbs <1%; moss 5-25% cover.

Releve DN-R1 OPn91b2. Ditch bank within degraded OPn91 water track fen. Tall shrubs 50-75% cover; mid-level shrubs (.5-2m) 25-50%; seedlings 5-25%; moss 5-25% cover; grass and sedges 50-75%; forbs 5-25% cover.
Releve DN-R2, OPn91b2. Water track fen - string. Tall shrubs <1% cover; mid-level shrubs (.5-2m) 50-75%; woody subshrubs 5-25%; grass and sedges 50-75% and forbs 25-50%; moss 50-75% cover.
Releve DN-R3 OPn91b2. Water track fen - flark. Mid-level shrubs (.5-2m) 1-5% cover; subshrubs 1-5%; grass and sedges 75-100%; forbs 5-25%; evergreen saplings <1%; and moss 50-75% cover.

Featureless water track fen. Plot heterogeneous mixture of tall willows and sedge openings. Unconsolidated shrubs cover without pattern. Vegetation mat springy. Tall shrubs 5-25% cover; mid-level (.5-2m) shrubs 5=25-50%; subshrubs 5-25%; grasses and sedges 75-100%; forbs 1-5%; and moss <1% cover.
Releve DS-R2 OPn91a. Degraded water track fen (OPn91) becoming wet meadow (WMn82a). Tall shrubs <1% cover; mid-level (.5-2m) shrubs 5-25%; grass and sedges 75-100%; forbs <1% cover.

Very old Aspen-Birch Forest (Balsam Fir Subtype). Plot lies behind ridge on west side of Little Isabella River in association with UMD bird research plot (Ed Zlonis, Gerry Niemi). Lightly scattered old, cut stumps (cf. Pinus banksiana). Scattered, well-decayed downed logs include large diameter Betula papyrifera (39 cm).  Abundant downed logs on surface include Picea mariana, Betula papyrifera, Abies balamea (27 cm). Shrubs are lightly browsed. Grouse scat in plot. One large, dead Populus tremuloides (53 cm) broken off at base and lying on the surface. Worms are likely, but no direct evidence. No charcoal observed in soil. Phenology is still set back ~1-2 weeks. Katie Winkler (UMD) assisted with plot.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Representative of red oak-dominated areas, within broader northern mesic hardwood forest or mixed forest community.  Soil is heavily wormed as evidenced by abundant castings, and only previous year's leaf litter present. Five worms observed in soil sample (IERAT Rank=4). Charcoal fragments in mineral soil at 10cm. Scattered, downed logs recruited from canopy. Micro-topography relatively flat. Plot and slope overall with abundant boulders on the surface. Numerous acorns on the ground in the plot. Downslope, the shrub layer much denser (Corylus cornuta, Quercus rubra, Acer spicatum)and scattered, large-diameter aspen often broken off at ~5m ht. Not specifically delineated as a blowdown patch in the 1999 blowdown GIS layer (Superior NF), but scattered blowdown patches were delineated in the area. No obvious fire scars in plot or broader area. Jenna M. Pollard assisted with releve.

Fire scar seen on dead red pine snag. Naturally occurring old stumps present, some charred. This suggests that this was the fire that originated stand, and no severe fire has occurred since. Crest with open understory of Juniperus communis. Not much coarse woody debris on ground of stand. There are some tip-ups in the mid- to recent decay class woody debris, suggesting canopy break up and senescence just beginning. Charcoal found in soil pit at 18 cm below surface. Soil pH taken (mineral horizon) and estimated to be 5.75.

Ground cover composition plus loamy soil suggests FDn43a NPC, even though jack pine is the overstory dominant. Old jack-pine dominated stand that has not been burned lately since stand origin. Canopy is breaking up through natural mortality. Lots of coarse woody debris and snags, many of large Abies balsamea. Charcoal faintly detected on downed Pinus banksiana tip up. Moose signs with scat and snapped twigs of Acer spicatum and Cornus rugosa. Rolling terrain, some low spots outside of plot with pools of water between boulder crevices. Heavy, cobble layer below 20 cm.

npc_subtype_name: Jack Pine - Black Spruce - Aspen Subtype
remarks: Black soil A-horizon thicker than expected from mor humus due to probable earthworm mixing. Worms dug up during soil description and likely are adding mineral soil to mor humus transforming it to a wormed mull of sorts. Soil pH test of A-horizon 4.5. Soil drainage actually somewhat excessively. Litter includes leaves in addition to needles. No real tall deciduous shrub layer. NPC rank AB because of long ago logging presumed. Several stems seen browsed. Hummocky landscape with Pleurozium-covered mounds and logs. Natural coarse woody debris on forest floor. No recent fire activity. More recent cutting occurred directly south of this plot/stand.

npc_subtype_name: Jack Pine - Black Spruce - Aspen Subtype
remarks: Areas of more open canopy due to tree fall and more hazelnut shrub layer. No recent logging. Mounds with Pleurozium growing on it. Tree regeneration mainly balsam fir. Rank A because no recent anthropogenic disturbance. Windthrow and senescence naturally occurring in canopy of jack pine. Stand would benefit from a burn. Soil pH of top layer (A) is 4.5; bottom layer (E?) is 4.0. Litter layer composed of both needles and leaves.

No cutting within plot observed. Surrounding communities include a very open-canopy, dense hazelnut understory stand with overstory of reserve white spruce, white pine, paper birch, and sparse cedar after cutting.  This occurs to the east of the plot.  To the west is a lowland WFn53 cedar community. Within plot, the white pine forms a supercanopy above cedar. Lower mineral soil horizons are trending to a sandy clay loam but not quite; it is still coarse in texture and well drained sandy loam is dominant texture.  Soil pH in all three horizons 4.5.

Majority of stand is FDn43c with inclusions of WFn53a. Rocks near soil surface. Recent cutting absent. Some black spruce on way into releve afflicted with dwarf mistletoe. Not much browsing and cedar regeneration suggests so. Soil pit dug up only gravel coarse fragments but community has cobbles and stones too. Mineral soil layer described is khaki brown, some iron precipitates but not enough to deem prolonged soil saturation of water. Soil pH is 4.0-4.5. Evidence of downhill, intermittent stream flow within plot (seepage), but dry during sampling. Natural tree fall and coarse woody debris.

No recent cutting. Elsewhere in community, there is evidence of dwarf mistletoe-caused mortality and witch's broom growth on black spruce. Rank B because of proximity to the The Grade, mistletoe infestation, and small community size. Depth of water in soil pit is 23 cm below sphagnum surface hollow. pH taken in a surface pool situated in sphagnum hollow. Very little surface litter - labrador tea leaves. A linear bedrock intrusion occurs in swamp with FDn32c2 mini-community. Closer to upland, community becomes more FPn62a, slightly drier and more occurrence of Pleurozium and Dicranum species with less labrador tea and Sphagnum.

Hummocks and hollows abundant. Decaying stumps of long-ago cut cedars seen. Dug soil pit in hollow but with some surface sphagnum growing. Sphagnum thickness at pit was 5 cm. Very cold water. Within community, canopy cover is variable. Plot and community borders a black spruce swamp (FPn62a) to the east. Coarse woody debris due to windthrow observed. This community appears transitional to a WFn53a community as well; certain species are indicative of such as is neutral water pH.

Rank B because of small area, and surrounding areas likely logged. Litter thickness and deposition only on base of trees and not on sphagnum, sedge mounds, or pools. Cutting of cedar occurred nearby surrounding stand and plot. Soil profile mostly mucky peat (hemic) dark brown color with woody pieces, roots, and fibers; approaching sapric muck with greater depth with blacker color and greasier feel.

Most of the dead spruce are small-diameter understory stems shaded out. Old stumps visible in later stages of decay. Litter includes birch leaves and spruce needles. Soil substrate below fibric peat is mucky peat (hemic) but is almost to a greasy sapric muck. Depth to water table in soil pit is 24 cm below surface. Soil pit dug in low sphagnum flat between high mounds of sphagnum. Standing water only within game trails; these trails criss-cross the community.

Bedrock not reached when digging soil pit, but it is exposed farther upslope (north). Soil becomes thinner upslope but with more exposed rocks/boulders. 2 cm of topsoil sandy loam is mostly organic mixed with some mineral soil - black, shallow A-horizon. Below is a light gray layer. No cutting observed. Shrub component unevenly dense; some areas thick, others bare.

The plot exhibits typical extensive "woodland-savanna-shrubland intermediary" that is in between the upslope releve (ROn12, MDL13-5) and forest condition on lower slope where bedrock is deeper below surface. This plot represents a common condition of the bedrock controlled landscape, and the heterogeneity of the plot itself is also common. Aspen and jack pine snags common. Lichen cover intact - no trampling. Coarse woody debris consists of larger jack pine. Exposed rock mostly on vertical faces of benches. 15% of plot is exposed rock with lichen and 5% is truly exposed rock with no lichen. Boulders on top of bedrock and loose rock piles (talus-like) aggregated at base of bedrock benches. Boulder erratics disintegrating. Fire scars seen on trees upslope (north of plot). NOTE: slope is averaged but varies from 1-2 degrees on bench flats to near vertical on bench faces. Most of substrate is 2 to 5 degrees; taken across plot, however, is recorded at 14 degrees.

Soil is coarse but loamy and with decent water holding capacity. Cobbles and boulders near surface. Soil pH in both layers is ~4.5 Stand is quite close to road, but large trees with natural coarse woody debris present. Intact needle litter layer. No pine regeneration, however. Understory very shaded. Moss-covered boulders common outside of plot. Rank B due to proximity to road, small size, and long ago past cutting.

Plot occurs within larger peatland that includes FPn63a to the south and southwest and a transitional zone that is FPn62a but includes FPn63a species. Rank AB because cut stumps from long ago observed. These stumps have since rotted away. Typical hummocky topography and natural tip-ups and coarse woody debris. Water table 26 cm below surface. Sparse leatherleaf litter, patchy.

Other parts of stand are on more exposed bedrock with more sun and less canopy cover than plot location. This community is a woodland area within exposed bedrock matrix but also contains low wet spots with sphagnum patches with Carex trisperma in hollows of boulders. Within plot is a narrow, linear wet drainage. Soil pit dug in patch of Pleurozium schreberi and accounts for thick humus layer. Though sandy clay loam soil likely perches up water, it also drains rapidly due to shallowness. Therefore it is difficult to give this a drainage class. Parts of plot are on bare rock as well which would be excessively drained. No mottling seen so water doesn't stay near surface long. Fungal mycelia throughout humus layer. Soil pH = 4.0.

Rocky substrate though no exposed bedrock. Most rocks covered with moss. Abundance of coarse to medium fine roots in upper 20 cm of soil. Many large cobbles occur at 15 cm below surface. Soil pH ~4.5. Moose scat seen. No recent stand cutting. Natural windthrow and coarse woody debris.

Treefall common with cedar vegetatively layering. Tip-up cedars common with 1 meter tall root mounds. Hummocks and hollows common. Pools of water still present. Humus layer only on tree bases (2 cm). Soil pit was dug in a hollow. Lots of decomposing wood in pit. Water temperature was 12.6 degrees Celsius. No strong browse pressure evident; a bit on alder.

Very wet conditions with most of the bladderworts and sundews submerged. There are different zones of shrubbier myrtle/leatherleaf islands around the plot. Whether they constitute different communities is unlikely but the plot is in Rhychospora alba-dominated pools with fewer shrub islands than surrounding. Fibric peat below water surface. Game trails seen criss-crossing community. Because releve plot was located in a wet pool, total sphagnum cover under the water could not be ascertained. Sphagnum was only seen on hummocks.

Exposed boulders common. Though only two understory cedar in plot, cedar is common, though infrequent, throughout stand. No obvious recent cutting observed in the plot, but nearby. Natural coarse woody debris on floor. 20 cm wide cobbles dug out of soil pit. Depth to bedrock not reached but many large cobbles near surface just below humus layer. Heavy deer browse. Sparse cedar needles form litter layer.

40 cm moss hummocks when on coarse woody debris; 17 cm when on soil surface. Pools of water mostly dry; when present, 4 cm. Litter depth mostly <1 cm and consists of both needles and leaves. Soil pit contained some decomposing wood but not much. Soil more on the mucky side of mucky peat. Large cedars likely cut in the past. Natural coarse woody debris present. Lots of cedar exhibiting tip-ups and layering vegetatively. Heavy deer browse.

Lots of cobbles within 7 cm of surface in soil pit are flat sheets; many coarse roots. Horizon is cocoa-brown. Deer browse evident but numerous white pine seedlings seen. No white pine saplings however. Browse is heavy on the maples, especial mountain maple. Stand to the north flattens out into cedar-aspen dominated with fewer exposed rocks. Rank AB because of cutting in nearby stand virtually no pine/cedar regeneration. Surrounding stand seen with Oxalis and Dactylis glomerata; DNR wildlife cut understory maple and fir to give more sunlight to forest floor.

Past cutting of cedar seen surrounding stand. Stand as a whole with wet pools in the spring (vernal ponds) especially in between exposed rocks and boulders where wet species occur. Rank B because of past logging and surrounding. Soil pit with 3 mineral horizons of different coarseness; A-horizon (pH 4.5) mixed with humus; second horizon (pH 5.0) lighter in color beige; third (pH 5.5) rusty iron color with many pebbles (coarse sand texture). Some iron precipitates seen at the second horizon suggesting seasonal higher water table. Stones also occur in soil pit. Litter also includes cedar needles. Wetter species seen along rocky drainages that likely experience water flow in spring.

No type within FDn22 is described well enough to fit this releve plot. Rank C due to power line, evidence of past logging, proximity to clearcuts to the east and west, and possible understory cutting for possible shooting lanes (outside of plot). Topography with some slight rock benches. Wet species occur in rock crevices and drainages that perch water. At lower slope, more balsam fir, aspen, maple, white spruce. Good oak regeneration and decent for white pine. Exposed rock covered with moss and lichen. Oak browse seen but acorn production also good on older trees. Natural coarse woody debris and snags present. Soil: very thin humus layer and very patchy fine roots are present. Drainage is somewhat excessively drained. Worm class is approaching 3 with some bare mineral soil. FDn22 plot is in matrix with ROn23. Charcoal and fire scars observed.

Black spruce-Jack Pine Woodland burned in Pagami Creek fire (2011). Fire severity high (both ground and canopy). Abundant medium-sized downed logs recruited since fire. Phenology set back ~2 weeks (late green-up). Near an old town site "Forest Center", a Tomahawk Timber Company town site between mid-1940s-1960s. No evidence of logging, but portions of NPC may have had some cutting during that era. Rayma Cooley and Louis Hilgemann (Iowa State University) assisted with releve for training purposes.

Rich Black Spruce Swamp. Microtopography with abundant hummock & hollow, scattered tip-up mounds,coarse woody debris in varying stages of decay.  Picea mariana saplings with some die-back.  Pleruosium schreberi with some die-back. Wildlife trail with light use (deer pellets outside plot).  Hyla crucifera in plot. Tending to a drier site overall, then wet. No strong evidence of Arceuthobium pusillum (possibly Picaea mariana saplings with die-back). Ruby-crowned kinglet singing. Jenna Pollard assisted with releve.

White Pine-Red Pine Forest. USFS prescribed burn (2005). Scattered large downed logs (red pine aspen). Fire scars 0.5m (1.0)m height on the Populus tremuloides (dead snages) and Pinus resinosa (Live canopy trees). Outcrop ledge (~1.5m height) runs ~15m along edge (outside plot).Small Rock Outcrop (ROn12b) community just outside plot. Several dead Populus tremuloides (Canopy) snags in plot (killed by fire). Moose scat inside and outside of plot. Soil upper horizon (to 10cm) very leached (grey). No charcoal detected in humus or mineral soil. Appears to have been a surface fire in this area. Segments pieces of smaller, charred trees occur on the surface. Larger community patch has inclusions of FDn32a and ROn12b. Jenna Pollard assisted with this plot.

Black Spruce-Jack Pine Woodland, Black Spruce, Feathermoss subtype. Abundant large down logs in various stages of decay, plus tip-ups, results in a high degree of microtopography. Logs with abundant bryophyte cover. No evidence of worms. No  evidence of fire. Heinelman year of origin - 1894. Jenna Pollard assisted with this releve.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Old Red Pine-White Pine Woodland with evidence of recent moderate ground fire. USFS prescribed burn 2005. Moose browse on Betula papyrifera, Populus grandidentata, Acer rubrum and Salix humilis. Large, down logs moderate to heavy throughout community (mostly Pinus banksiana, some Pinus resinosa). Excellent regeneration of Pinus resinosa, Pinus strobus, Pinus banksiana and Picea mariana throughout community patch. Humus (5cm) includes 2-3cm ash/charcoal.  Leeched mineral soil from 0-5 cm depth. Average height of fire scars 1-2m on live trees. Many canopy Pinus banksiana (25-30cm dbh) were torched by fire and are dead. No evidence of worms. Jenna Pollard assisted with releve.

Black Spruce Bog - Treed subtype. Large down logs light-moderate from canopy, in varying stages of decay. Highly varied microtopography. No evidence of Arceuthobium pucillum. No wildlife trails observed. Breeding passerines abundant. No evidence of anthropogenic disturbance. Jenna Pollard assisted with this releve.

Graminoid Poor Fen (water track) Featureless subtype (APn91c1). Large peatland complex. Releve conducted in small patch of stunted cedar (otherwise scattered black spruce throughout) portion of fen. Network of intermittent water tracks throughout. Water tracks with predominantly graminoid species, including Carex exilis. Fen has characteristic ribbed pattern in at least 3 distinct areas. Community transitions  to Poor Fen/Wet Meadow downstream (west) of plot(toward Little Pony River). Jenna Pollard assisted with releve.

Old growth white cedar swamp. Community varies from mostly saturated, with strong microtopography (hummocks & hollows), and scattered cedar and alder, to somewhat dry, with larger diameter cedar and black spruce. No obvious Arceuthobium pusillum damage. Browse very light. No evidence of cutting. Winter road runs through north half of patch. Canopy cover variable. GPS coordinate taken at NW corner of plot.
Stand consists predominantly of wet brush prairie. Big blue stem is rare to absent elsewhere in the stand. Plot is in close to moderate proximity to wet mesic aspen forest boundary.
Releve is situated in wet mesic prairie. Thatch cover is thick at 10 to 15 inches. Asclepias cf speciosa is very young and resembles Asclepias ovalifolia.
Mesic upland prairie on flat to east of north-south running depression of wet prairie. Same general location as 2008 releve (#7984). See 2008 notes.

Mesic prairie adjacent to Typha march. Releve itself is flat but part of a very gradual slope down to marsh. Site has very abundant big bluestem and forbs and releve is similar. Timothy is present but has apparently decreased since 1999 sample. Gopher mounds common. Helianthus pauciflorum/rigida is very abundant across entire site; very large colonies. Small wren, possibly sedge wren, seen at site in morning.
A wet prairie community with shrub components of bog birch and willows; generally less than three feet in height. In management zone for grazing.
Burned within last year. Releve documents a portion of dry prairie on a NW facing hillside. The site is dominated by grasses with a fairly diverse forb component.
Ecotone between upland grassland/savanna and wetland grassland.

permanent_plot_type_description: ex. metal tag on nearby tree
remarks: The releve area is less grazed then most of this pasture; it appears to have barely been touched this year. Cows came off about 3 weeks ago, owner stocks at a low rate and rotates his herd. Top of beach ridge, ridge drops off at the west edge of the releve.
Well developed flarks in water track adjacent to ovoid bog island. Open pools 2-4 cm deep.  Much Carex lasiocarpa.
Isolated bedrock island in middle of peatland. More than 15 ft. above peatland. Much blow down. Walking releve that extends to the SE.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Old growth red pine with gaps being filled by balsam fir, trembling aspen, and white pine. Dead and down balsam fir. some tip up mounds. Drier pine towards shore, aspen increasing away from shore. Old gas cans in plot.

Linear wetland drainage in bedrock controlled topography. Plot represents lower portion of stand with conifers. Microtopography slightly undulating. Very dry. Represented upper portion of stand with balsam fir.

Stand Typical of NPC: No--doesn't fit classification well. 

Remarks: Typical of broad but rather localized zones dominated by T. alpinum in fairly large fen (rich to poor) on west end of Slumber Lake. Grades to areas with more Myrica + Carex rostrata, and further away to poor graminoid fen + spruce bog. Deep saturated peat, moderately quaky, with shallow water in depressions between 6-12" tall hummocks. Richer zone here ~40x60 meters. No old stumps or woody remains. Plot ~50 meters from lake.

Remarks: Typical of much of broad and rather large zone (8 acres) of open fen on west end of Slumber Lake. Quite quaky deep saturated peat. Plot center ~35 meters from lake. Low Sphagnum hummocks, to 8" tall. Shallow water in foot tracks. No old stumps or large woody remains. Stunted spruce and tamarack (E1-4)cover ~1-5% of this zone(though none in plot). Grades to richer zone at releve MDL12-1 to the North, and to poor black spruce and spruce bog toward upland to the Northwest, Southwest, South. 

Notes: 
- Stunted conifers (E1-14) average ~1-5% cover in this zone, though none actually in plot. 
- Ericoids mostly quite stunted/low-statured (B1-2). 
- Photos of plot + community zone.

Remarks: Typical of ~3 acres of low-statured vegetation in broad zone of poor fen on north shore of Slumber Lake. Subtle depressional microsites cover ~60% of the plot; low hummocks (2-8" high) cover 40% of plot. Plot positioned to capture the subtle depressional habitat which is fairly extensive here. No stumps or old CWD. Plot located ~60 meters from the lake, and ~70 meters from poor spruce swamp / spruce bog to the north and east that borders the upland. Stunted spruce and tamarack (E 1-4) cover up to 5% of this zone.

Notes: Photos of plot w/ Jeff for scale. 
- Stunted conifers (E1-4) typically ~5% cover this zone.
- Pale yellow caterpillars (these rather small) quite abundant on Scheuchzeria palustris leaves.

Remarks: Typical of broad zone bordering the southwest shore of Muskeg Lake. Plot ~100 meters from the lake in the general vicinity of a small inlet flowage (Muskeg Creek). Scattered old conifer snags (Picea mariana, Larix) may indicate past water level fluctuations (beaver flooding?). Substrate is deep peat. Microtopography of tall hummocks and deep hollows, ~36" from top to bottom. Shallow water in hollows. Grades to areas with young Larix (4-15 meters tall), then to young black ash (southward toward upland), grades westward to black spruce bog.

Typical of ~120-acre patch of cedar swamp south of Mud Lake, east of Fall Lake. Plot centrally located in patch. Canopy quite ragged due to July 4, 1999 wind storm; much large CWD, many snags. Live trees leaning in all directions. Cedars 20-42 cm DBH, mostly 20-30 cm. No stumps. Very hummocky peat substrate, typically 18-24" from hummock to hollow. Shallow water in many hollows. Taxus is heavily browsed.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Typical of better quality (more mature) portions of a 40-acre patch of ash on the east side of Muskeg Creek, in broad depressional valley between bedrock ridges. Trees in plot (5)10-38(40+) cm DBH. No stumps. Occasional old remains of large Picea mariana/Larix. Moderate CWD. Snags occasional. Substrate of hummocks + hollows, 12-16" top to bottom. Shallow water in hollows. Peat > 45cm deep, fibric with fair bit organic content. Patch somewhat impacted by July 4, 1999 windstorm.

Remarks: Typical of a fairly narrow zone (3-15 meters wide) on the southwest shore of Acorn Lake, a 14-acre bog lake in large peatland (mostly black spruce bog) north of Wind Lake. Very wet and quite quaky peat. Edge of plot 2 meters from water's edge.  Vegetation very low-statured this zone. Hummocks are low, to 6" high, and cover ~1/3 of the plot. Grades to narrow zone of poor conifer swamp then semi-treed bog away from lake.

Notes: photos taken of plot, zone, lake. 
- Courtney did releve (CKK-001) in semi-treed bog southwest of the lake (50 meters to SSW of MDL12-7)

Remarks: Typical of ~15-20 acres of oak woodland on crest and steep southerly slopes of 120-foot bedrock ridge at the northwest end of Wind Lake, above portage trail to Wind Bay, Basswood Lake. Plot includes part of upper slope and crest. Extensive July 4, 1999 windthrow, abundant CWD. Many trees snapped off or uprooted. Oaks 25-35cm DBH. No stumps. Occasional small bedrock outcrops. Abundant surface rocks, bedrock-derived. Soil is quite rocky silt, quite shallow to the metamorphic schist bedrock (soil mostly <6 inches deep). Slope varies from 5-10 degrees, southerly aspect.

Notes: Courtney took photos of releve/npc.

Remarks: Typical of tamarack-dominated areas in heterogeneous tamrack-cedar swamp east of an 8-acre bog pond south of Washte Lake. Larix mature, 20-40cm DBH, many trees >30cm. No stumps. Snags uncommon. Moderate windthrow in the patch, less so directly in plot. Substrate microtopography of hummocks + hollows, 18-30" top to bottom. Fibric peat >40cm deep. Water in hole at 15cm down. Possibly better fit for WFn53b- Lowland "Cedar"? Grades northward to patches of mature cedar with trees to 60+cm DBH.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks:
Remarks: Typical of broad zone of ash on outer margin of 30-acre black spruce bog east of Wind Bay, Basswood Lake. Uneven-aged, trees 15-42cm DBH. No stumps. Few snags. CWD rather sparse. Substrate of mesic hummocks and moist hollows, 12-18" top to bottom. Peat >30cm deep. Peatland occurs along small creek flowage into Wind Bay. Plot located ~250 meters south of the creek. 

Notes: 
Courtney identified many of the mosses. 
Moose dung in plot (no dung moss).

Remarks: Typical of, and centrally located in, broad zone of shrub shore fen along a small creek (boggy flowage) east of Wind Bay, Basswood Lake. Plot ~45 meters from the creek; not far from a small and subtle upland rise covered by immature Pinus banksiana. Subtrate is fibric peat with twig-sized woody remains. Water at 5cm deep in dug hole. Grades nearer to the creek to a similar zone but without bog birch. 

Notes: 
No photos taken. 
Small Pinus banksiana are associated with the low "upland" rise as well as occurring in the nearby portions of the shore fen peatland.

Remarks: Typical of ash-dominated zones in fairly narrow, bedrock-entrenched drainage between Found and Juggler Lakes. Canopy trees 20-45cm DBH, mode ~30-35cm. No stumps. Moderate CWD, including large and very old boles. Swamp was mostly missed by July 4, 1999 windstorm that flattened uplands in vicinity. Substrate of low hummocks and shallow hollows, with iron-stained water up to several inches deep in hollows. Peat >40cm deep, saturated; 0-9" deep fibric peat, becoming more decomposed and mucky at 12" deep. Grades to areas with more cedar (to northeast) or to alder swamp (to southwest). 

Releve-Wide DBH Statistics: 
Min: 20  
Max: 45  
Median: 32  
[no individual DBH measurements given]

Remarks: Plot captures much of one of the larger openings in 5-acre outcrop complex atop 100-foot bedrock knob overlooking Juggler Lake; near highest point on the hill. Exposed bedrock (includes lichen-encrusted) ~33%, rest of ground is mix of rocks exfoliated in place and very shallow detrital organics over the granitic bedrock. Several old fire-scarred cut stumps in vicinity of plot. No invasive hawkweeds here. Grades to areas with sparse patches of pines, and to dry cliff on south face of the steep-sided knob. 

Notes: 
Plot includes crest + uppermost slope. 
Photos taken of plot + surroundings.

Remarks: Typical of, and centrally located in, 14-acre patch of spruce bog that nearly fills a bedrock-entrenched basin northwest of Prairie Portage; on inner part of peninsula separating Inlet Bay from Bayley Bay, Basswood Lake. Deep fibric peat, >40cm deep, moist. Hummocks to 18" high. Sparse CWD. Snags uncommon. No stumps. Scattered Larix on outer margins of the patch where it grades to ash + alder, with white cedar very local in some spots. 

Notes: 
Jason took photos of the plot.

Remarks: Typical of a large patch of red pine-dominated forest on the eastern end of Washington Island, a large island in Basswood Lake. Patch likely planted or at least manipulated by Cliff Ahlgren through early work at Quetico (Hubachek) Wilderness Research Center. Trees 20-40cm DBH. Highly decayed old stumps occasional, possibly cut, some with fire scars. Snags rare. Sparse CWD. Gravelly sand substrate: 3cm moder duff; A-horizon is light brown fine silty-sand with significant gravel component. At 10" deep color change to orange begins (redox). Frequent stones in soil profile in addition to gravel-sized pieces. Thick moss carpets. Small aluminum tags on trees immediately east of plot. Larger trees OP upslope, where forest appears more natural. 

Releve-Wide DBG Statistics: 
Min: 20  
Max: 40  
Median: 30

place_name: Basswood Lake, Washington Island North - BWCAW
remarks:
Remarks: Plot typical of, and centrally located atop, 2.5-acre island north of Washington Island, Basswood Lake. Mature to old growth native-origin stand. Large pine snags frequent. No stumps. CWD rather sparse, but some large old boles. No rock outcrops. Substrate: 10cm duff, mostly needles; silty-loam to 28+cm deep, no redox. Scattered large surface boulders. 

Notes: Photos taken of plot, also of the island from the lake.

Remarks: Typical of Carex rostrata-dominated zone in broad, 18-acre poor fen on west end of Manomin Lake. Plot is ~60 meters from lake, 50 meters from poor conifer swamp/spruce bog, and 15 meters from zone dominated by Eriophorum virginicum (see releve A250). Deep quaky saturated peat; water in foot tracks. Hummock to hollow microtopograhy, ~16 inches from top to bottom. No stumps. This zone ~2 acres. 

Notes: Photos taken of plot and setting / surroundings.

Typical of the main zone in a broad expanse (18-acres) of poor fen on west end of Manomin Lake. Plot located ~50 meters from the lake, and ~100 meters from stunted spruce bog to the west. Deep peat. Grades to slightly richer(?) areas (see nearby releve A249).

Aquatic / shallow lacustrine marsh. Plot in small shallow cove in the back (south end) of Rice Bay, Basswood Lake. Water ~3 feet deep. Substrate is deep silty-muck. Plot ~centered in 30x50-meter zone, ~25 meters from shore, near the landing of the portage to Manomin Lake (small creek from Manomin Lake enters Rice Bay here). Water depth in this zone varies from 18-48 inches. Height strata for F, H, and G start at surface of water; also for S but values are negative. Releve done in a bit of a hurry.

Typical of, and centrally located in, 25-acre patch of black spruce bog adjacent to the west shore of Back Bay, Basswood Lake. Trees 8-20cm DBH, no stumps. Few snags. CWD sparse. Deep saturated peat; water table ~20cm below surface. Tall hummocks, these 23-46cm tall, mode ~30cm. Peat is fibric upper 30cm, below 30cm more hemic with more sedge remains. Continuous moss cover: 80% Sphagnum spp,, 20% Pleurozium schreberi. Grades in places to poor conifer swamp with Myrica & Betula pumila. ~60 acres total of APn80/81 in immediate vicinity here adjacent to Back Bay's western shore. Releve-wide DBH: min. 7, max. 20, median 13. Dan took photos of plot center and at corners.

Typical of fairly broad zone of ash & cedar on the margin of a rather large black spruce bog on the west side of Back Bay, Basswood Lake. Trees 15-35cm DBH. Cedars straight to leaning. No stumps. CWD rather sparse. Deep peat (>40cm), upper 25cm fibric, below 35cm much finer, hemic. Water at 15cm deep in dug hole. Microtopography of hummocks and hollows, 24-30" top to bottom. Hollows likely were shallow pools earlier in season. Releve-wide DBH: min. 15, max. 35. Dan took photos of plot, from center in all directions.

place_name: Jackfish Bay NE, Basswood Lake - BWCAW
remarks: FDn22a- Jack Pine Bedrock Woodland or ROn12- Rock Outcrop? Upper east-facing, moderately steep slope of a 60-foot high bedrock ridge on peninsula in the northeast end of Jackfish Bay, Basswood Lake. Slope varies from 5-20 degrees. 30-40% of plot substrate is exposed bedrock (biotite schist- Vermillion Granite Complex), rounded and lightly-fractured. Snags occasional in and near plot. No stumps. Soil restricted to shallow pockets in subtle bedrock hollows. Community extends from lakeshore to the top of the ridge. No invasive hawkweed present! Grades to denser pine atop ridge. Dan took photos of plot: four corners toward center and panoramic from upper edge toward the lake.

place_name: Jackfish Bay NE, Basswood Lake - BWCAW
remarks: Plot on the gently-sloping crest of a 60-foot high granitic ridge in the northeast end of Jackfish Bay, Basswood Lake. Steep south-facing slope and lake shore immediately below (downslope). Pines mature, mostly 40-53cm DBH. Scattered old fire-scarred stumps (natural?), scattered snags. Moderate CWD, mostly larger pine boles and limbs. Moss-covered outcrops cover 5% of plot. Soil is brown fine sandy-silt with stones, 20cm deep in soil pit. No earthworm evidence in plot (however earthworms are present downslope- noticed walking into stand from lake on lower moister area near campsite.). Photos taken (by Dan)around periphery toward center, not specifically at corners or midpoints. Scruffy community is difficult to photograph.

Typical of, and centrally located in, 35-acre patch of black spruce bog along the west side of the lower reaches of Muskeg Creek. Trees to 15cm DBH. No stumps, snags rare. CWD sparse. Spruces moderately stunted, +/- mop-top. Deep peat: upper 20cm fibric, below 20cm hemic. Water at 25cm deep in dug pit. Hummocks 12-24" tall (Sphagnum fuscum even taller). Grades toward creek to poor spruce swamp with Myrica gale, then shrub shore fen, then rich sedge fen. Releve-Wide DBH Statistics: Min: 3cm, Max: 15cm, Median: 8cm.

Remarks: Typical of Carex utriculata-dominated zones in fairly extensive ~linear peatland complex bordering the lower reaches of Muskeg Creek. Edge of plot is ~1 meter from creek. Quaky wet sedge peat >50cm deep. Shallow water between sedge hummocks. This zone was much wetter in July (2012) when Jeff and I were nearby (on opposite side of creek). Grades to more extensive patches dominated by Carex lasiocarpa (see releve JL-030-2012) in the same creek-side zone. Farther from the creek the vegetation grades to shrub shore fen then black spruce bog.  

Notes: 
Photos taken of plot, creek, setting...

Remarks: Typical of broad zone of shrub shore fen bordering lower reaches of Muskeg Creek. Plot ~30 meters from the creek, ~60 meters from black spruce bog to the southwest. Substrate is deep peat, 0-5cm deep is root mat, 5-50+ cm deep hemic peat, water in dug pit at 27cm deep. Hummocks ~18" tall. Grades to rich sedge fen and sedge meadow immediately adjacent to creek.

Remarks: Submerged aquatic community in small sheltered bay between Pipestone and Jackfish Bays, Basswood Lake. Plot ~25 meters from shore. Water depth ~30 inches. Substrate is moderately firm silty organics. The adjacent lakeshore here is Calamagrostis canadensis meadow, grading to shrub shore fen.  

Notes: Dan took photos of plot, setting...

Remarks: Typical of rather large areas of heavily-wormed forest on broad rolling ridge between Pipestone and Jackfish Bays, Basswood Lake. Mature forest, trees 25-42cm dbh. Snags infrequent. No stumps. Moderate CWD. Plot on mid to upper slope. Slope ranges from 2-6 degrees; aspect is northeast. Substrate: no litter, ~5cm wormed A-horizon, stony coarse loamy sand >10cm deep. Small granitic outcrops atop the ridge (OP); a small low outcrop (under canopy) not far west of plot (OP).  

Notes: 
Dan took photos of plot.

Remarks: Typical of shoreline mud flat community along Sauk River at end of Sauk Landing Road (canoe access); inside of river bend. Broad, mostly level mud flat comprised of deep moist silt (dry at surface). Current is fairly slack here. Mud flat is presently ~30" above river level (mid/late summer drought). Mud surface with a cracked crust. Shaded by adjacent floodplain forest on terrace 1-3 feet higher in elevation.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Oak - Sugar Maple Forest
remarks:
Remarks: Typical of best portion of old growth native white pine-hardwoods on upper mid portion of an extremely steep 220-ft, west-facing bluff along the lower reaches of Shattuck Ck. Pines 50-65cm DBH. No stumps. Snags infreq. CWD sparse to moderate. Past grazing effects are minor due to steepness of slope. Dolomitic colluvial silty-loam with moderate earthworm evidence. Outcrops (dolomite) rare this vicinity. Moderate amount of needle litter. 

Notes: 
- No photos taken. 
- Condition rank grades to BC-rank (and even C-rank) where past grazing pressure had more lasting effects in general vicinity (less steep slopes). 
- Earthworms are more abundant in adjacent oak-basswood forest to south.

Remarks: Typical of, and centrally located in, 22-acre patch of black spruce bog along the lower reaches of Spawn Creek. Trees mostly 10-20cm DBH. Snags are infrequent. No stumps. Trees somewhat mop-top in form. Deep peat. Continuous Sphagnum cover. Hummocks 6-16 inches tall. Grades to poor conifer swamp then black ash on margin of the patch. Little evidence of recent moose activity.

Notes: 
- No photos taken. 
- Grades to poor conifer swamp near zone of black ash on outer margins of the bog patch. 
- Moose trails lightly used. No dung seen.

Remarks: Typical of broad and fairly extensive zones of shrub shore fen along the lower reaches of Spawn Creek. Plot ~40 meters from the creek, ~80 meters from the upland (jack pine bedrock woodland). Deep wet peat, upper 23cm fibric, below 23cm mucky peat. Fairly tall hummocks (12-24" high). No standing water, but 2-4" deep in foot tracks. Floods in spring and other high water level (in creek/lake) events. 

Notes: - Photos taken of plot, setting, shore fen zone.

Remarks: Plot captures pine woodland in shallow silty-sand over granite bedrock on moderately steep mid-slope of 150-foot ridge above Jackfish Bay, Basswood Lake. Even-aged patch, trees 25-35 cm DBH. Occasional snags. No stumps. CWD rather sparse. Though several large decayed boles present. Soil is shallow + rocky sandy silt, mostly less than 10 cm over granite bedrock; small outcrops in plot. Thick moss carpets. Grades to even-aged aspen to the west; pines are rather localized here near exposed bedrock. Small, broken, dry cliffs occur not far upslope (OP). 

Notes: 
- No photos taken.

Remarks: Typical of a large (400-sq. meter) opening in large outcrop complex atop an 80-foot granite ridge on the north shore of Jackfish Bay, Basswood Lake. Exposed rock covers 80% of the plot (includes Cladina-covered rock). Frequent crevices and fractures present; outcrop surface is irregular, with lots of small voids where shall accumulations of "soil" (and moisture) occur. Soil pockets (detrital organics) never deeper than 3cm in plot. No cut stumps. One very old fire-scarred snag in plot. No invasive hawkweeds. Grades to jack pine savanna/shrubland/woodland-see releve JL-198-213 (Jeff Lee plot). 

Notes: 
- Photos taken of plot and setting.

Remarks: Typical of richer jack pine-black spruce woodlands in this vicinity. Plot on lower portion of gradual west-facing slope of a 60-foot bedrock ridge along small drainage north of Jackfish Bay, Basswood Lake. Mature even-aged patch; jack pines 25-35cm DBH, others 10-25cm DBH. Stand origin 1921 (Heinselman). No stumps. Scattered snags. Moderate CWD, mostly jack pine boles--all decay stages. Sandy loam over coarse sand; granitic bedrock mostly within 50cm of surface, scattered small outcrops. Litter includes both needles and leaves. Thick humus. Soil pit down to 59cm in deeper soil pocket; hardpan at 59 cm, not bedrock.

Notes: 
Photos taken of plot (rather poor quality images).
Tree Diameters: Basal area measurements are presented in lieu of DBH (see paper data sheet).

place_name: Pipestone Bay SW, Basswood Lake - BWCAW
remarks: Remarks: Typical of 10- to 30-meter wide zone along the shore of a large bay in the southwest end of Pipestone Bay, Basswood Lake. Water depth ~20 inches; water level has risen considerably due to recent heavy rains. Substrate is firm (silty-clay?). This zone grades lakeward (toward lake) to broader zone of Scirpus acutus, and inland to wet meadow dominated by Carex utriculata, C. vesicaria, and Calamagrostis canadensis; then to willow-dogwood shrub swamp before transition to upland (aspen-birch-fir here).

place_name: United States Point, Basswood Lake - BWCAW
remarks:
Remarks: Typical of ~5-acre patch on gently sloping lower portion of northwest-facing 100-foot bedrock ridge, on the inner portion of United States Point, Basswood Lake. Plot 25 meters from the lake. Jack pines mostly 20-33cm DBH; mature, starting to "fall apart". Stand origin 1921 (Heinselmann). Occasional snags. No stumps. Moderate CWD. Exposed lichen-covered granite bedrock ~10% of plot; elsewhere shallow silty-loam (<15cm deep). Frequent surface boulders. Bedrock surface fairly uniform, rounded. 

Notes: 
- Dan took photos of plot, setting...

place_name: United States Point, Basswood Lake - BWCAW
remarks:
Remarks: Mature patch on gently sloping lower east-facing slope of 140-foot bedrock ridge on the inner portion of United States Point, Basswood Lake. Trees 25-38cm DBH. Moderate windthrow ~5-10 years ago- several resulting snapped off snags. No stumps. Moderate CWD (several large aspen boles). Soil is very rocky sandy-silt; thick litter and humus. Occasional small surface boulders. No outcrops in plot. Several old-growth white pines not far from plot- (~20-30 meters from center of plot), these 80 and 88cm DBH. Red and white pines (including some large ones) become common upslope where bedrock is frequently at/near surface.
 

Notes: 
- Dan took photos (+ video?) of plot.

Remark: Plot situated to capture non-outcrop expression of ~20-acre oak-pine woodland-outcrop complex on broad granitic ridge along the Basswood River. Nearly level bedrock terrace here, sunny outcrops both upslope and downslope, not far from plot. Pines mature; scattered very old fire-scared stumps pine stumps in vicinity. Occasional large pine snags. Stand-origin 1921 (Heinselmann). Soil silty, often shallow to granitic bedrock (>20cm deep in center of plot). Moderate earthworm abundance. Occasional surface boulders. Litter consists of both leaves and needles. Patches of Sphagnum are occasional in subtle depressions atop the ridge (in otherwise dy-mesic woodland groundlayer). 

Notes: 
- Dan took photos of plot. 
- Dan lost sunglasses in plot! 
- Plot on East/West lines between sections 18 & 19. 
- Earthworm rapid assessment score 3?

Ownership: State of MN--School Trust--BWCAW

place_name: United States Point, Basswood Lake - BWCAW
remarks:
Remarks: Typical of ~5 acres of mature jack pine-black spruce-feathermoss woodland atop a narrow, 80-foot high bedrock ridge at the tip of United States Point, Basswood Lake. Plot on fairly level bedrock crest. Scattered granitic outcrops frequent near the plot. Jack pines mostly 20-30cm DBH, black spruce 15-25cm. Much CWD, much of it due to July 4, 1999 windthrow. No stumps. Snags infrequent. Thick humus. Very rocky tan fine sandy silt, >25 cm deep in slight bedrock hollow (likely <30cm to bedrock throughout plot, often shallower). 

Notes: 
- Dan took photos of plot/setting. 
- Stepped on ground hornet nest beneath old decaying tree bole. No stings suffered.

place_name: United States Point, Basswood Lake - BWCAW
remarks:
Remarks: Typical of fairly extensive oak zones on broad bedrock ridgetop on the inner portion of United States Point, Basswood Lake. Pines 22-67cm DBH, oaks 7-20cm, occasional snags. No stumps. Moderate CWD. Mature stand. Stand origin 1921 (Heinselmann). Soil a rocky (stony) fine silt-loam, >20cm deep over the granitic bedrock in most areas; small outcrops in/near plot. Frequent surface boulders. Apparently no earthworms present. 2cm litter (needles and leaves), 3cm humus. Fire-scars on old snags in vicinity. 

Notes: Dan took photos of plot and vicinity.

place_name: United States Point, Basswood Lake - BWCAW
remarks:
Remarks: Typical of ~ 12-acre patch of bedrock pine woodland on extremely steep northwest-facing slope of 220-foot high bedrock ridge on the shore of United States Point, Basswood Lake. Plot on mid slope. Mature, +/- even-aged, fire-origin patch. Fire scars on old conifer snags. No stumps. Granitic outcrops frequent. Soil is a tan fine silt, very rocky, 22cm deep in soil pit (likely the deepest soil pocket in the plot, shallower elsewhere). No earthworm evidence. Surface rocks are common, these are mostly broken pieces of the granitic bedrock. Thick moss carpets; lichens on exposed rock. 

Notes: 
- Dan took photos & video of plot, including the process of conducting the releve.

Remarks: Typical of mature jack pine-black spruce on shallow soil over granitic bedrock, forming a major component of the matrix forest patchwork in rolling bedrock terrace southwest of Basswood Falls. Plot on gently-sloping lower slope of 60-foot high granitic ridge. Trees mature; occasional snags; CWD common-lots of jack pine boles. Scattered old fire-scarred cut stumps in vicinity. Heinselmann stand origin 1921- "partially cut-over 1898-1921". Thick humus over 5cm of grey sandy-silt, over 15-25cm of tan silty sand. No evidence of earthworms. Depth to bedrock in soil pit is >21 cm. Small granitic outcrops are occasional. Frequent surface boulders. Grades to areas with more aspen. 

Notes: 
- Dan Wovcha took photos.

Plot chosen to represent high quality, natural origin (1988/1759/1681)NPC common in this setting within Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Understory regenerating in are of plot location following low intensity fire in 1988. Charring of mature tree boles common. Low to moderate amount of medium size CWD, well to moderately well decayed. No evidence of earthworms observed. North end of burned patch with 10% cover of mature trees and abundant Pinus strobus saplings (4-6m). No anthropogenic disturbance.

Plot chosen to represent high quality natural origin community common in this setting within Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Abundant CWD all sizes and stages of decay. No evidence of earthworms observed, no evidence of anthropogenic disturbance.

Plot chosen to represent one aspect of wetland/peatland complex in Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Headwater depression perched among ridges of FDn43 mesic mixed forest. No anthropogenic disturbance. Adjacent communities are APn81, MRn83 and WMn82, the latter two without strongly defined boundaries. No evidence of recent beaver activity in or near releve.

Plot chosen to represent natural origin (1894) community, common within this setting in Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Not well-described in NPC classification i.e. Pinus banksiana is dominant canopy spp. otherwise FDn43 floristics. Pinus banksiana and Abies blow-down is frequent within patch beyond releve. No evidence of anthropogenic disturbance. No evidence of worms observed. Abundant CWD.

Plot chosen to represent high quality natural origin (1894)community common in this setting in the Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Largest Pinus resinosa with fire scarred boles. Low to moderate CWD. One old, very decayed possibly cut stump observed. No evidence of worms observed. Tall shrubs patchy within NPC patch. Transitions to FDn32a (red/wt pine woodland) on steep west-facing slope above Dahlgren River.

Plot chosen to represent natural origin community in riparian setting in Lac La Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Adjacent NPCs are wet black ash forest to the west, lowland whites cedar forest to the east, and red pine forest and mesic mixed forest to the northwest. Bryophytes common on CWD and tree bases. Occasional large DBH Pinus (one fire scarred). Abundant CWD in all stages of decay. Thuja regeneration on CWD nurse logs. NPC patch has occasional brushy patches in canopy openings. Exotic earthworm middens common.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent high quality natural origin (1864/1759/1681) NPC common in steep bedrock lakeshore setting in the Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. 1-3m high nearly vertical, moss-covered rock wall runs across slope of plot. Exposed rock estimate does not include this wall. No anthropogenic disturbance. Minimal CWD. Adjacent to Agnes Lake and white pine/res pine forest (FDn43a).

Plot chosen to represent high-quality NPC common in steep, bedrock-controlled ridge settings in the Lac la Croix Bedrock LTA. Plot includes near level partially shaded 'terraces'. Pinus banksiana deformed and stunted; a few dead outside of plot. Plot is situated along the top of 5m vertical wall with about 75% cover of foliose lichens. Bryophytes are acrocarp spp. No anthropogenic disturbance. Plot includes some large boulders. Adjacent to dry-mesic Pinus banksiana/Picea mariana woodland (FDn33).

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent high quality NPC of natural origin(1681/1759) common on crests and upper bedrock controlled, south-facing slopes. Minimal course woody debris and no fire scars were observed. No anthropogenic disturbance or evidence of earthworms were observed.

Plot chosen to represent riparian native plant community in Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Canopy ash appear healthy with no dieback. Plot includes a large tip-up wad. CWD amount is low. Silty clay muck substrate. Yery gradual slope; drains to Agnes Lake. Conditions may be wetter than typical due to heavy rain event during the previous day. Location is from NW corner of plot. No anthropogenic disturbance.

Plot chosen to document native plant community (NPC)from area of element occurrence record from 1971. Plot location from SE corner of plot. represents high quality natural origin (1776) NPC, common in these settings in the Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Canopy openings in one corner of plot which boosts forb cover. CWD low and in various stages of decay. Moderate sized erratic nearby. No anthropogenic disturbance. Moss principally on rocks and CWD. Slope of plot 7 degrees but situated on flatter terrace of ridge.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality natural origin (1864) native plant community in riparian setting of Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Positioned as band between upland and poor black spruce swamp (APn81a). Hummocks and moist hollows without standing water present. Moderate amount of CWD in various stages of decay. small area of northern cedar swamp adjacent to the east end.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality natural origin native plant community (NPC) of Lac la Croix Bedrock LTA. Medium-sized patch NPC positioned between upland and a large peatland complex. Highly variable micro-topography of small, drier, slightly elevated areas between dominant wet/wet-mesic draws with mucky hollows. Saturated logs are common. Moderate presence of CWD. Plot location recorded from SE corner.

place_name: Boulder Bay Lac la Croix E
remarks: Plot chosen to represent high-quality natural origin (1894) native plant community common in these settings in Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Large erratic within plot. Abundant CWD mostly from Pinus banksiana. No antrhropogenic disturbance observed in plot on NPC patch.

place_name: Boulder Bay Lac la Croix E
remarks: Plot chosen to represent quality origin (1894) NPC common in these settings in the Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Soil only in small bedrock depressions some of these depressions water-holding, with Sphagnum cover. There is little presence of CWD. All bedrock at surface is covered by lichens. No anthropogenic disturbance observed.

place_name: Boulder Bay Lac la Croix E
remarks: Plot chosen to represent shoreline native plant community (NPC) of Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA not well described in NPC classification. Variable flooding/ draw down regime depending on season/ annual/ multi-year water levels. NPC is narrow band which extends, 3-4m inland from water line to wooded upland. Plot does not include slope in standing water. Evidence of wave wash. Collection 2319 nearby.

Plot chosen to represent small patch, natural origin native plant community (NPC) of Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Few standing water pools. Minimal CWD. NPC patch at top of first order stream which flows to the lake. Stream channel with Fraxinus nigra part of canopy.

Plot chosen to represent very old growth stage of natural origin (1681) native plant community (NPC) with significant recreation-related exotic earthworm impacts in Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Island location with campsite. Medium size patch in which some Pinus resinosa from 1681 are still present in the canopy. Abundant CWD and two large P. resinosa are in the plot. Depth of humus is quite variable, but mostly minimal to absent (earthworm impact) with 4cm maximum under large P. strobus. Red pine-White pine woodland (Canadian shield) adjacent on ridge top.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality natural origin (1759) native plant community common in this setting in the Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. The oldest Pinus resinosa are senescent. No anthropogenic disturbance. There is abundant CWD in all sizes and states of decay. Part of fire-dependent woodlands and mesic mixed forest complex on large bedrock-controlled feature.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality natural origin (1894) native plant community (NPC) of bedrock controlled ridges in Lac la Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Plot includes glade and rock outcrop area. One of numerous small patch woodlands and rock outcrop NPCs occurring at fine scale.  Woodland glades developing under widely scattered senescent Pinus banksiana of the oldest cohort. Multi-aged P. strobus emerging as next dominant conifer canopy sp.. Exposed bedrock lichen-covered with bryophyte patches. Glades with cover of lichens/mosses (especially Pleurozium schreberi, dense Vaccinium spp., Quercus seedlings.

Plot chosen to represent expression of natural origin native plant community (NPC) class not well described in classification but not uncommon in these settings in the Lac la Criox Bedrock LTA. Coarse woody debris minimal. NPC patch follows crest of ridge. This location with less Corylus cornuta then typical in other parts of patch. Dense C. cornuta in other areas of patch. Other areas of patch also have stones/rocks more evident at the surface.

Plot chosen to represent one expression of (circa 1900) native plant community common in this topographical setting in bedrock controlled landscape of small to medium sized woodlands and wetlands; heterogeneous at fine scale. Adjacent to small Alnus dominated wetland; ecotonal influence in forb and graminoid species. Cut stumps nearby are likely Pinus banksiana. No cut stumps in plot but may have decayed; NPC patch plot represents may be harvest origin in all or part.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality natural origin (1895) native plant community (NPC) occurring on a large bedrock-controlled feature, surrounded by channels of the Stony River. No anthropogenic disturbance is evident. Patch is part of heterogeneous mosaic of NPCs on this feature. Low to moderate amount of CWD.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent high-quality natural origin (1854) native plant community common in these settings on Gabbro Bedrock Complex LTA. Microtopography of bedrock-controlled landform creates small mesic/wet-mesic pockets; one of these is within this releve. Low to moderate amounts of CWD are present. No anthropogenic disturbance is evident.

Narrow(somewhat linear) stand occupying shallow depression on landscape; integrates with Northern Wet Cedar Forest. Wet pools with minimal vegetation common. Understory vegetation of plot clustered along tree bases and roots. Late season releve.
Sphagnum relatively level and near continuous in plot; wet hollows infrequent. Evidence of mistletoe noted throughout stand. Late season releve.

Representative of matrix npc in the Border Lakes portion of Park. Stones and cobble common. Aspen and B fir cwd moderate in plot. B fir defoliation by Spruce budworm. Fire scars noted on snags. Nice humus layer; no evidence of earthworms. 1ERAT Rank = 1

Releve representative of small patch npc of Giants Range on high bedrock knobs; this example dom. by JP. Soils are shallow and exposed bedrock present. Surrounding matrix mesic mixed Forest/ mesic Hardwood Forest. Evidence of older cut stumps in area. Fire scars evident.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: "Valley" between bedrock knobs. Rep. example of Mesic Hardwood forest on the Giants Range landscape. Spp. diversity often low and with indicators for both the MHn and FDn systems. Stones and cobble common; sometimes creating wetter microsites. Large old Pine stumps scattered in stand. Earthworms present: lacking intact humus layer, no middens.  IERAT Rank 4.

High quality older stand with no apparent human distrb. Lrg. white Pine scattered throughout. Likely receives heavy use in winter from deer (moose?). Moist depressions but no standing water mid-Aug. Stopped by coarse frag. close to surface. Spp. indicators for both types in npc class.

Upland Cedar npc occupying low level landscape position near base of slope. Plot soil profile stopped by coarse frag. just below surface. Paludification of stand further west near peatland transition; scattered rocky depressions with mucky peat and sphagnum present. Drainage is either mod. well or somewhat poor.
Lagg of large peatland complex. Narrow npc with variable width. Old winter road follows/bisects npc; becomes dominated by graminoids in remnant track.
Extensive water track; dominant vegetation shifts along feature (compare to releve further south). One deeper hollow present in plot. Standing water level ranges from 3-8 cm.
NPC surrounds narrow tributary of Grassy Lk. Experiences periodic inundation. Has likely been influenced by changes in hydrology related to beaver activity. Moss hummocks <18 cm in height.

Small stand bordering narrow drainage. Level lawn; Sphagnum spp. and moss hummocks absent. Standing water levels relatively consistent across plot.  No evid. of recent hydrologic change, however evid. of past beaver activity in area is present. Unique npc for park.

Vermilion Moraine, close to Subsection boundary. Cobble and stones abundant. Stopped by coarse frag at 15 cm. Charcoal (including lrg. pieces) common in humus layer. Earthworms likely. CWD moderate. Disturb. minimal, but old stumps noted.

Mature example of scattrd MHn patches on upland knob features near Lake Vermilion shoreline (often S/SW aspects). Ostrya locally abundant in these stands. Earthworms present- surface mixing extensive in plot. Could not determine depth of humus. Cobble and stones common. Past land use history unknown.

High quality example of small patch npc. No sign of human disturbance. Npc tends to occupy transition area between uplands and poor conifer swamps (in park). Scattered canopy openings present; CWD moderate.

Releve representative of confusing npc of lower landscape position in Giants Range area. Stopped by coarse fragments at 74 cm; may have dense till underneath. Redox features first noted at ~15 cm. Plot includes somewhat poorly drained "rubbly aquepts" common on this landscape. No bryophytes on soil substrate. Soils work done by NRCS (Jeff Kroll).

Smaller basin in bedrock controlled landscape. Stand apparently receives greater inputs relative to adjacent npc's of feature (poor conifer swamps). Canopy cover variable but typically greater than 50%. Canopy gaps frequent w/ appropriate CWD of canopy trees. Evidence of mistletoe on BSpruce in stand and noted beaver chewed B. alleghaniensis OP. Shallow pools present among high sphag hummocks. NPC determination uncertain; forested peatland seems best fit at this stage. Canopy B. alleghaniensis diameters range from 10-30 cm (dbh). UTM = NW plot corner.

Older stand on island in Lk Vermilion; no obvious sign of human distrb. Canopy gaps common and large diameter P. Birch and Cedar CWD present. Plot contains portion of canopy gap. Understory densely shrubby under C openings; conifer regen minimal. High levels of browse noted. Upper soil layer mocha brown followed by a tan brown layer. @ 42 cm, soil exhibits precipitate of iron but no gray matrix. Mottling suggests water transport and possible heavier soil or bedrock @ > 50 cm. Cobble and gravel common. UTM = NW plot corner.

Old growth; large decomposing logs common. Recent canopy Abies CWD. Large stand occupying lower to mid topographic position of upland feature. Conifer component variable in stand; some patches of dense Thuja present. NPC determ. uncertain; does not fit well in classification 2.0. Soil to 54 cm is mostly gray E very gravelly sand. At 54 cm, strong orange mottling present and substrate is compacted sandy clay. Soil is noticeably more moist starting at 40 cm, but no redox features detected until reach densely compacted layer. UTM = NW plot corner.
Open wetland complex at the headwaters of the Bear River. Plot captures veg in area with greater peat accumulation and lower species diversity relative to adjacent npc's. Too dry for pH reading.
Mature stand with small, scattered canopy gaps. Low wet hollows with brown mosses common throughout stand (though no standing water in plot on releve date). UTM = SW plot corner.

Representative of small patch woodland npc on shallow soils/exposed bedrock knobs of Giants Range (Mesabi Range LTA). Plot located on bedrock bench between steep bedrock exposures (ROn/CTn). Stand integrates with FDn33 where soil depths increase. Evidence of cut stumps and recreational foot traffic. Late season releve; some graminoids could not be identified. UTM = NW plot corner.

Mature example of small patch npc in Mesabi Range LTA. Typically occurs on mid/upper slopes and level tops/terraces in areas of mod to shallow soils relative to matrix npc; often adjacent to even drier woodlands or rock outcrop npc's on exposed bedrock. Plot located +/- midslope on relatively level terrace of ridge feature; rocky but no exposed bedrock. Charcoal present. Stopped by coarse fragments (bedrock?) at 8 cm. UTM = SW plot corner.
