Large stand occupying upper/middle slope. Canopy cover variable; large gaps present where canopy birch is dying back. Releve located in area w/ relatively intact canopy. Jack Pine and Red Pine present in stand but infrequent. Rocky till but no exposed bedrock; stopped at 12 cm by dense layer of cobble/stones (or bedrock?). Late season releve. UTM = NW plot corner.

Small patch npc, somewhat ecotonal in nature. Intermed. landscape position, occupies shallow, gradually sloping "valley" between bedrock ridges. Some wetter, rubbly inclusions present; eventually grades into wet cedar forest downslope. Multiple soil pits attempted, typically stopped by coarse frag in upper 5 cm. Cobble and stones volume is high with mix of rock types. Charcoal observed in upper profile. Npc determination uncertain; best guess based on ground data from stand. UTM = SE plot corner.

Small patch npc on bedrock feature. To some extent, integrates with Dry Bedrock woodland and contains small inclusions of bedrock outcrop (ROn12b). Stand may be better described as FDn22 with inclusions of ROn? Exposed rock in plot with near continuous cover of lichens.

High quality old growth; No sign of human disturbance. Stand along subsection/section boundary, on glacial lake Agassiz lacustrine deposits. Upper soils either very fine sandy loam or loam; stopped by roots at 18 cm. Deer browse prevalent; conifer regen is minimal. CWD appropriate for age of stand. Large size earthworm castings present but no middens observed. BA-1 and BA-2 noted on data sheet. *Images taken from NE corner of plot.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Located on subtle slope near edge of Glacial Lake Agassiz. Microtopography abundant with lower mucky depressions and drier mounds common. Low spots often with moss and sparse vegetation but no standing water on date sampled. Humus = muck humus. UTM = SW plot corner.

Mature example of small patch npc on Pike-Sandy River Sand Plain LTA. Canopy gaps & lrg. diameter Populus coarse woody debris and snags present in stand. Scattered cobble/ stones/ boulders common. Ground nesting birds present. UTM = SW plot corner. Soil horizons: A, Bw1, Bw2. Parent material: drift. Excavation deeper than 90 cm impeded by rock fragments.

In swale southwest of low, NW-to-SE-running glacial beach ridge. Open wetland between wet cedar forest to northeast and tamarack-dominated forested peatland (harvested 14 years ago) to the southwest.  Tamarack mortality common and visible in every direction. A few Salix and Betula pumila shrubs in wetland outside plot.

Tamarack forested peatland between 2 low, narrow glacial beach ridges dominated by wet cedar forest. Tamarack healthy here, unlike many nearby areas. Blowdown rare. Tamarack 4-8 inches dbh. Sphagnum hummocks to at least 1 m tall maximum.

Very uniform stand, assume even-aged- was aged at 62 in 1980 according to forest inventory. Trees range from 2-6 inches dbh. Continuous cover of well-defined moss hummocks of moderate height. No standing water, hollows are moss-covered as well. Old stumps, but unsure if cut or of natural origin. Peat saturated below 18 cm.

Slight hollows with standing water. Dense shrubs over head-height. According to historic PLS notes, this area was "heavily timbered cedar, spruce, and tamarack", so assume this extensive shrubland likely originated from anthropogenic factors such as cutting, swamping and/or burning.

Very uniform, open (beneath closed canopy) stand- likely due to deer use, hence lower rank. Farms to south. Isolated stand is surrounded by open wetlands which according to historic PLS notes were formerly densely forested peatland. Tree trunks and roots create microtopography (not mosses). Water 2 in. below mucky surface of hollows. No visible stumps, blowdown occasional. Thuja dbh 5-14".

Stand is amidst extensive lowland conifer clearcuts (much of which converted to Salix shrubland) and Larix mortality. Dying Larix and blowdown more common outside plot. Shrubs and graminoids most abundant under dead Larix canopy gaps. No recent stumps visible. Picea mariana 3-11" dbh.

Roughly circular open wetland amid intermingled Larix- and Salix-dominated wetlands. Deeper water in northern half outside plot- possibly a source of upwelling with flow to southeast, based on aerial imagery. Three distinct islands of Larix on southern edge of open wetland. Salix maccalliana collected 75 m southeast of releve.

Releve encompasses small crest of bedrock and upper east-facing slope adjacent to forest. Releve placed on east side of outcrop because it is less disturbed (fewer invasives, less-trampled lichen). Moderately heavy deer browsing. A few 5-8 m Quercus macrocarpa to west of plot.

Releve in eastern third of wet forest where larger dbh Thujas (15-20 in.) are found. Significant microtopography (root hollows, horizontal trunks), moreso outside plot. Thuja under 3m tall absent except as seedlings. Some coarse woody debris, not much blowdown. Some old, jagged stumps. No standing water at this time- hollows mossy or sedgey.

Representative of large pools near OP-AP boundary. Surrounded by stunted Larix laricina and Picea mariana with Phragmites and Typha. Distinct pools present for 800 meters running north to south along this transition. Also a series ~700 m west, with black spruce "islands" and less distinct pools between.
Occasional mucky pools with standing water. Head (north end) of island wetter, pools more frequent. Plot on the most well-defined of a small group of treed islands surrounded by strings and flarks.

Soil disturbance in past (mounds). No recent cut stumps, possibly older small ones. Some CWD, not much. Blowdown rare here and in stand. Standing dead Pinus banksiana outside plot. Stand looks thinned to north (trails, open areas) but not here.
Larix mostly alive here though lots of larch beetle in area. Most standing dead trees are Picea mariana. Very few mucky pools and almost no standing water. Trees ~6 inches dbh or less.
Several trees recently blown down in plot- mostly smaller-dbh Thuja and Abies. Herbaceous layer sparse. Appears similar to numerous other tiny upland islands in very wet forested peatland matrix.

Plot encompasses drier, Thuja-dominated patch and Sphagnum-Picea-Larix-dominated patch. Deer browse and droppings evident. Larger Thujas 8-10" dbh, Picea to 6", Larix and Abies to 8". Blowdown and CWD rare and small. Pools dry though had water previously. Water 10" below peat/muck surface.

Standing water minimal, though muck is saturated. This shrubby zone is between forested peatland and to west and narrow zone of wet meadow adjacent to creek to east. Dead and stressed Larix scattered directly west. "Brown mosses" dominate and form hummocks.
Plot captures wetter part of open acid peatland. Peat slightly quaky and saturated. Bottom of pools wet- other formerly wet pools nearby are dry at surface.

Maximum Picea mariana dbh ~4", majority 1-3". Larix occasional and more stunted, ~2" dbh. No wet hollows, hummocks well-developed. Near circular mistletoe opening but away from heavy infestation; trees lightly infested, few "brooms".

Plot occupies wetter, slightly more hummocky area, which is typical of ~50% of these 40 acres. South edge of plot is drier- drier area continues south. Canopy gap in center has great Alnus cover than under closed canopy. Deer trails evident. CWD to 10" dbh common. Wetter areas of plot have Carex-(non-Sphagnum)moss hummocks ~15 cm tall. Dry between hummocks but probably seasonally wet.

Recent blowdown SW of releve along forest-gravel pit edge, and along powerline right-of-way to south. Blowdown occasional in interior of forest. Betula papyrifera clumps more common near right-of-way. Pinus banksiana to 13" dbh in plot. Small opening of unknown origin in NW corner of plot.
Larix 2-6" dbh- 5-10% mortality in plot which increases toward the northwest. Brown fungus at base of dead trees, but probably secondary invader. Trees have very narrow and sparse crowns.

Regenerating 13-year-old clearcut with 6" dbh slash and stumps common. Populus, Betula saplings visibly stressed and dying and unlikely to persist, but lowland conifer regen appears healthy.  Vaccinium oxycoccos and V. vitis-idaea fruiting abundantly, likely due to high light levels.
A more accurate description of context would be a saddle lower that the crest of a hill and above the base.

Red pine-white pine woodland. Large, moss-covered boulders, some with associated wet hollows. Patch with scattered jack pine throughout canopy (some dying).NPC has composition of both FDn43a and FDn32c. Downed logs mostly Picea mariana canopy trees. Black-throated blue warbler male, singing just outside plot (within NPC patch). White pine seedlings abundant (>>20 in plot). Only conifer seedling in plot (no balsam fir seedlings). Thick litter and humus. No evidence of worms. No charcoal.Soil very thin w/ nearly continuous boulder cover. Very coarse sand to nearly gravelly, with a few cobbles and some loam. Very leached (grey). Site likely long occupied by conifers.  Regina Flanigan assisted with releve.

Old red pine-white pine woodland. Scattered cut stumps (likely white pine) with average dbh ~34cm. Bedrock outcrop within and adjacent, and scattered throughout landscape patch. White pine and red pine canopy in clumps and patchy throughout. Cover of white pine and red pine within plot +/- average for larger landscape. Large, downed logs light. Die-back of white pine mostly in 2-5m height class. More white pine and red pine than typical in the 0.1-10m height range. Plot fairly representative of landscape patch. No evidence of browse. Bear scat in plot. Abundant charcoal in humus layer. No evidence of worms.

Mature white pine-red pine forest. Large downed logs are light-moderate (mostly large Populus tremuloides). No evidence of logging. Very old downed logs and lichen-covered residual tip-ups create micro-topography. No evidence of browsing by deer or hare. Northwest-facing slope dominated by Populus tremuloides and Betula papyrifera with Abies balsamea and Populus grandidentata. Charred snags broken off low. Small amount of charcoal in soil.  NPC likely fire origin (vs. planted).

Rock Outcrop within Black Spruce-Jack Pine woodland. The MBS Astrid Site as a whole has several ROn23a/FDn32c complexes such as this. Most are small and wooded.  Moose sign (scat, prints, browse) in area. Amelanchier in plot is browsed. Scattered large boulders and broken rock.  Rock Outcrop extends SE/NW a minimum of 50m in each direction from plot. Scattered downed logs on surface.

Old White Pine-Red Pine Woodland. Boulders and bedrock close to the surface. No evidence of prior cutting. Downed logs moderate on surface, creating micro-topography below the surface. Surrounding native plant communities are White Pine-Red Pine Forest and Woodlands of same high quality. No evidence of worms. Small amount of charcoal fragments in humus layer. Pine warbler singing in area of plot.

Graminoid Rich Fen, Flark Subtype. Large, high quality fen complex with braided water tracks throughout core area of fen. Some tracks with linear string/flark pattern, especially in the western leg and southern portion of the fen. Many rare species populations occur within the fen complex, with Platanthera clavalata and Platanthera lacera distributed throughout the core area. Birds singing: 3 LeConte's sparrow (two with visual id), Savanna Sparrow, Lincoln's Sparrow and Palm warbler. Many Bog copper butterflies observed.

Graminoid bog with open pond.  Drains northesast to peatland adjacent to Gull lake. Peatland drains water from adjacent, steep uplands, especially on west side  (ROn and east-facing dry cliff). Open bog transitions to treed bog on south side. Drainage creates deep, relatively sterile channel. Depth of peat reflects dense root network under sphagnum.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Northeastern Bedrock)
remarks: Old growth red pine-white pine woodland complex on top and along west-facing slope of long knob above Boot Lake. Plot taken in center with bedrock outcrop (ROn12) and jack pine woodland (FDn22a) surrounding and on slope. Predominance of red pine-white pine woodland (FDn22b) in patch is rare in this chain of lakes and in the site as a whole. This patch is one of the largest woodland/rock outcrop complexes in the area.  A unique patch. No worms, No evidence of fire,no charcoal in soils sample. No evidence of prior logging. Fungi diversity high (a good year for fungi in general).  Jenna Pollard assisted with releve.

Poor conifer swamp within large peatland complex, including OPn81 (Northern Shrub Shore Fen), APn91b (Graminoid Poor Fen (Basin)), APn81b2 (Poor Tamarack-Black Spruce Swamp (Tamarack subtype)) and APn81a(Poor Black Spruce Swamp)communities. Arceuthobium pusilum present in patch, but minimal on lower branches. Animal trails in patch, but no direct evidence of moose. Island within peatland complex is FDn32c2 (Black Spruce-Jack Pine Woodland). Very few downed logs on surface. Abundant spittle bug activity. Jenna Pollard assisted with releve.

Poor Black Spruce Swamp. No Arceuthobium pusilum damage evident. Wildlife trails. Deer droppings. Scattered downed logs on surface. Variable hummock height. One area within plot, previously occupied by larger trees, is dry, with surface logs and Sphagnum encroaching over Pleurosium schreberi. NPC between peatland pond and upland. Eric Ogdahl assisted with releve.

Northern Dry-Mesic Mixed Woodland dominated by Quercus rubra. Situated on high ridge above large, poor conifer swamp. Large, very old stumps occur, with red oak and white pine growing from center.  Possibly cut, but no direct evidence. Fair to moderate microtopography. Coarse woody debris is light. Litter is comprised of leaves and needles dominated by last years' leaves.  Patch within the Superior National Forest-Birch Bay Unique Biological Area. Eric Ogdahl assisted with releve.

In middle of narrow seepage zone on toe of North facing slope. zone is about 20 m wide by about 1/4 mile long. The water table is at the surface with cold groundwater below the surface. Uppermost soil layer has some marl speckles but very little marl seen overall. Much RCG above and below. Eriophorum occupies only about 60m of the seepage zone at its West end.

Young Aspen-Birch, Spruce-Fir Forest regenerating from clearcut. Plot conducted for NLEB study (USFS SNF, MNDNR, CRTC & UMN, 2014) and is centered around F12E roost tree. Brad Smith (Bio-Tech, Superior NF-Kaw RD) assisted with releve. Canopy closure homogenous at roost tree and througout plot. Residual cut stumps (~25-35 cm dbh) throughout. Community is missiing species (e.g. white pine) and size class/age class diversity. Moderate level of large, downed logs on the ground. Balsam fir infested with spruce budworm (especially large trees). Fair amount of microtopography resulting from buried wood and rocky terrain. No evidence of fire.

Old Aspen-Birch, Spruce-Fir Forest. Plot conducted for NLEB study (USFS SNF, MNDNR, CRTC & UMN, 2014) and is centered around F12A roost tree. Brad Smith (Bio-Tech, Superior NF-Kaw RD) assisted with releve.Deer pellets in plot. Canopy aspen dying out over time. Large, down logs in plot light-moderate. Canopy gap at roost tree ~5m X 10m diameter. No evidence of fire.

Aspen-Birch, Spruce-Fir Forest. Plot conducted for NLEB study (USFS SNF, MNDNR, CRTC & UMN, 2014) and is centered around F12D roost tree. Brad Smith (Bio-Tech, Superior NF-Kaw RD) assisted with releve. Balsam fir dying (abundant lichen cover on many) presumably from spruce budworm. Plot with low deciduous shrub cover. Relatively low species and age class diversity for the NPC. Large down logs light and fairly flat microtopography (except for boulders at surface). No other evidence of logging. No evidence of fire. Abbreviated plot data due to limited time.

Old Aspen-Birch, Spruce-Fir Forest. Plot conducted for NLEB study (USFS SNF, MNDNR, CRTC & UMN, 2014) with roost tree of F05C & F06B at NW corner and roost tree of F04B at NE corner. Brad Smith (Bio-Tech, Superior NF-Kaw RD) assisted with releve. No evidence of recent logging. Aspen and Acer spicatum browsed. Abundance of large down logs is moderate and in all stages of decay. One White Pine (subcanopy) within 20m of plot.

Old Aspen-Birch, Spruce-Fir Forest. Plot conducted for NLEB study (USFS SNF, MNDNR, CRTC & UMN, 2014) and is centered around F05B roost tree. Brad Smith (Bio-Tech, Superior NF-Kaw RD) assisted with releve. Plot encompasses small drainage/valley (may be seasonally moist) with slopes to either side (E/W). Scattered canopy white pine adjacent to plot. Large, old white pine stumps in area around plot. Moderate amount of large, down logs in all stages of decay. Canopy aspen with very healthy crowns. Charcoal between mineral soil and humus layer.

Old Aspen-Birch, Spruce-Fir Forest. Plot conducted for NLEB study (USFS SNF, MNDNR, CRTC & UMN, 2014) and is centered around single roost tree of F04A & F05A. Roost tree is large dimaeter, very decomposed, dead snag (likely white pine (8-10m ht and 57 cm dbh).  White pine scattered in the canopy adjacent to the plot. Gap in canopy to ENE is ~20m X 10m in diameter. Large, down logs are light-moderate (mostly balsam fir). Brad Smith (Bio-Tech, Superior NF-Kaw RD) assisted with releve.

Old Aspen-Birch, Spruce-Fir Forest. Plot conducted for NLEB study (USFS SNF, MNDNR, CRTC & UMN, 2014) and is centered around F10A & F11A roost tree. Brad Smith (Bio-Tech, Superior NF-Kaw RD) assisted with releve. No charcoal in soil. No other evidence of fire or recent logging. Large, down logs are predominantly aspen and balsam fir that have been more recently recruited to the forest floor. Microtopography mostly due to boulders on the surface.

Northern Wet-Mesic Boreal Hardwood-Conifer (Aspen-Birch-Red Maple) Forest. Plot conducted for NLEB study (USFS SNF, MNDNR, CRTC & UMN, 2014) and is centered around F10B roost tree . Brad Smith (Bio-Tech, Superior NF-Kaw RD) assisted with releve. Very bouldery surface, with standing water common in rock crevices. No evidence of fire. No evidence of prior logging. Little used trail runs (E/W) along border of plot.

Very old, White Pine-Red Pine Forest. Plot conducted for NLEB study (USFS SNF, MNDNR, CRTC & UMN, 2014), with F07B roost tree (aspen) in southeast corner of plot. Brad Smith (Bio-Tech, Superior NF-Kaw RD) assisted with releve. Abundant large down logs (shite pine, aspen, balsam fir), recently recruited to the forest floor. Old porcupine chews on large red pine in forest outside plot. No evidence of logging. Microtopography is fairly well-developed. Areas devoid of ground flora (~25%) due to woody debris and needle cover. Upper 3 cm of mineral soil is gleyed. Deer pellets in plot.

Rich Black Spruce Swamp. Plot conducted for NLEB study (USFS SNF, MNDNR, CRTC & UMN, 2014) and is centered around F07A roost tree (Populus tremuloides,28cm dbh). Brad Smith (Bio-Tech, Superior NF-Kaw RD) assisted with releve. Plot on broad bench, upslope from Hill Creek. Scattered cut stumps. Well-developed microtopography. Moderate levels of large down logs in various stages of decay. Fairly continuous boulder layer below 18cm of peat (0-4cm=Fibric, 4-17cm=Hemic, 17-18=Sapric).

No obvious recent cutting or fire. Moderately open understory. Plot situated in larger matrix of FDn43b1. Natural downed woody debris present. Exposed boulders/rocks common though not abundant. Very thin humus layer and no real mineral soil over the shallow bedrock. Organic matter in humus very moist due to recent multi-day rains and perching effect of bedrock; also causes Sphagnum moss patches. Deer browse evident. Cut stumps long decaying.

Drainage channel artificially dug up encircling stand near road (75 cm deep, 3 m wide). Also, obvious cutting of large cedar occurred long ago. Still some cedar seen, but most are dying or exist as snags. Drier species, like bunchberry, are limited to downed logs and high tree bases. Lots of downed trees.

Severe blowdown has affected the stand; much of stand is very open in terms of canopy. Some areas within stand with more black spruce and tamarack, appearing more FPn63. Flora points to WFn53, despite wet conditions suggesting FPn63. Pools common - perhaps just an abnormally wet snow and rain year during the winter and spring, respectively.

Surrounding stand is clearcut; releve in higher quality spot. Areas of north slope seepage of Sphagnum occurrence also seen. Cutting undoubtedly occurred in stand, but nothing recent in releve. Some odd animal disturbance on topsoil/litter layer observed throughout stand; litter cleared away exposing humus in small patches approximately 10 x 10 cm; animal rutting/scraping? Soil with some Oe left. Water table present or perching effect by bedrock at 33 cm below surface. No redox features in soil. Wet spring year of 2014 may have caused high water. Stump sprouting in maples and birches seen, but not in oak. Heavy deer browse. Unsure about drainage class.

Stand is intermixed with ROn23a openings. Exposed rock common. No recent cutting. Fire scars not seen. Natural coarse woody debris and snags through natural mortality. Soil layer with 4 cm black, minimally fibrous humus that is well incorporated to result in dark black color and leaves residue when rubbed; likely worked by earthworms. Top mineral horizon is muted dark gray-brown; bottom horizon orange-brown. Oaks appear to have been here for awhile and no mor humus identifiable. Water table from a wet spring at 36 cm below surface, yet no mottling or redox seen. Texture is difficult to discern due to saturated soil. Shallow soil causes frequent tip-ups with odd patches of exposed organic soil seen devoid of litter - oval patches 40 x 70 cm (animal scraping/rutting?). Topo context on top of hill (crest) of this releve is actually more favorable for moisture due to deeper drift than is slope leading to plot from west. The slope appears to be FDn22 with large boulders present.

Lots of cedar tree fall. Rank BC, due to road/rairoad nearby and stand with reed canary grass. Pools still wet at time of survey. Pit and mounds common. Highly layered understory. Dead balsam fir saplings common. Soil pit 6 cm of fine root organic layer in muck. Soil texture oddly mucky where pit was dug with very few fibers seen though color is more consistent with hemic (mucky peat) and is black-tan.

Drainage with high slopes to each side where FDn43 occur. Logging sale nearby. Heavy deer browse plus some weed species. Close to ATV trail and also cut area downgrades quality. Ground felt "spongy" with standing water. Releve is not typical of stand because it exists as a small inclusion (as most MHn46 do in this landscape) within matrix of FDn43 and MHn44; it occurs only in small drainages. Gleyed soil begins immediately at first mineral soil horizon below the 2 cm litter and 8 cm humus. Therefore it keys to poorly drained, but vegetatively, it seems more somewhat poorly drained. Standing pools of water 2 cm deep, but soil pit had water at 24 cm below surface. No mottling seen, just gray matrix. The Munsell class for the top horizon is 10YR 4/2.

Charred wood seen around stand but no recent cutting observed; however, it was cut in the past. Exposed rock benches common as are boulders. Top 7 cm E soil layer leached gray (pH 4.0). Bottom layer orange with iron deposition (pH 4.0). Fine roots present and no evidence of soil saturation. General soil texture more aptly described as gravelly loam. Drainage class feels more somewhat excessively but keys to well. Natural coarse woody debris present. Much of boulders on slide slope bench originating from settling, presumably. Many boulders present, but plants growing on them so they don't count towards exposed rock percentage.

Seepage and stream drainage to WMn82b to the NW seen in stand. No cutting evident. Natural blowdown and coarse woody debris. Wet pockets are springy and to the NW grades into WFn53 slightly before reaching WMn82b. Soil pit: Water reached 45 cm below surface. Soil drainage keys to poorly but feels more like somewhat poorly. A moder horizon 12 cm thick from surface to first mineral horizon which is gleyed with redoximorphic precipitates of iron; clay texture perches water. No coarse fragments. Deer browse evident. Ranking due to proximity to cut areas and finding of heal-all in ground cover.

Natural windthrow, no sign of dwarf mistletoe damage on spruce. Pools mostly absent. Most canopy trees at or slightly above 10 m height. Soil pit dug in pool. Thick fibric peat anchoring roots followed by hemic underlayer. Possible water movement underground from the nearby creek to the west?

Heavy deer browse. Windthrow is prominent; much of peninsula is very open in canopy and with moderately thick understory of mountain maple or balsam fir. Past cutting evident with old decaying stumps. Likely very large trees taken out possibly even cedar. Charring seen on birch bark and rock. Sandy loam textures throughout with lots of cobbles. Top mineral horizon black (pH 4.5), middle horizon gray (pH 4.5), bottom horizon orange-tan (pH 5.0). No redoximorphic features. Soil felt moist but not saturated after previous day's thunderstorm. How much this burns being a peninsula unknown.

Soil drainage keys to poorly but feels more like somewhat poorly. Iron precipitates seen throughout gray matrix. Fine roots present. Worm category between 2 and 3. An 'A' soil horizon exists and thoroughly studded with worm castings. Water seepage seen at bottom of soil pit. 'A'-horizon pH 6.5-7.0. Clay horizon below pH 6.5-7.0. Litter composed of both cedar needles and aspen leaves about equally. Deer browse heavy and natural tip-ups occur. Little, moist micro-depressions common. Drainage keys to poorly, but it seems closer to somewhat poorly drained.

No recent cutting within stand though surrounding has been cut. No fire scars evident. Large boulder erratics and large cobbles occur. Road runs through native plant community. Nice humus Oa layer with abundant fine roots and fungal mycelium. Charcoal seen in upper 7 cm and within humus layer. Some moistness starting at third mineral horizon, but no visible wetness; there is some cohesion of soil particles - a stickiness. pH of all 3 horizons 4.0-4.25.  Upper horizon: black-brown; middle horizon: dark brown; third horizon: tan brown. Sphagnum present in rocky hollows.

Aspect is at 134 degrees recorded along sloping ridgeline; however, the land abruptly slopes perpendicular (SW to NE) down to the open peatland. Moose scat seen in several spots about 5-10 years old (est.). Plot occurs on crest surrounded by open peatland. Though not recorded in plot, trembling aspen and black spruce occur closer to the edge of outcrop. Interesting to see some characteristic wet species. Exposed rock is 30% without counting lichen cover, but about 70% if lichen covered rock included.

Standing water in patchy pools and muck flats. No recent cutting. No stumps seen. Cedar-dominated forest near to the southwest. Black ash community situated next to cedar community and WMn82b near river. Browse activity evident. Absence of black ash seedlings seems odd. Old cut cedar stumps seen while walking to releve location.
Road and clearcut near plot. Many hummocks and pools; mucky and moist at this point in season. No soil layer data taken due to time limitation (needed to make my helicopter pick-up point).

Beaver created wetland. Some sphagnum moss and mat closer to center (southwest of plot) where open water exists. Sphagnum is common and mat is unconsolidated, though surface water depth does not appear deep.

Much of would-be exposed rock is moss covered. Upper soil horizon is black with pH 4.0; lower soil horizon brown with pH 4.0. Soil drainage keys to being well drained, but it feels drier than that. Site situated near rock outcrop. Lots of benches and perching of water for sphagnum moss growth. No fire scars seen. Deer browse pressure strong. Logging occurs in nearby stand. No recent cut stumps within plot. Good black spruce and balsam fir regeneration.

Trash seen and a natural blowdown occurs farther inland to the north. Large remnant white pines occur but suffer wind breakage. Charred bark on a large red maple but no other fire evidence. Leaf litter mostly just previous' growing season. Top mineral soil horizon is a black 'A' with pH 5.0. Second horizon is a light brown 'B' with pH 4.0 and approaching a loamy sand. Landscape has many boulders present covered with moss. Classification problematic: MHn35a is best guess but species lists scores give slight advantage to MHn46, which seems too wet for this site and landscape position.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Base of large rock feature to the east serves as a source for water drainage into this wet site; no standing water at time of survey. Humus layer has very abundant fine roots. Top mineral soil horizon is a black 'A'. The second horizon is gray and with pH 5.5. No recent cutting seen. Heavy deer browse seen on mountain maple seedlings/saplings.

Stand situated next to shrub shore fen. No recent cutting seen. Stand is dry but moist at time of survey. Tree base hummocks common and hollows interspersed between. Heavy litter of tamarack needles. Fine roots mainly in upper 15 cm of soil. Top organic horizon is black with pH of 6.0; bottom organic horizon is brown with pH of 7.0. Water measured at 25 cm below ground surface in soil pit. pH of surface water was recorded at an earlier time period (July 8, 2014) during previous visit. Classification between FPn82a and FPn82b uncertain; species indicators point to latter, but low pH surface water and relatively low species diversity point to former.

Active harvesting nearby to the east, south, southwest less than 200 m; no recent cutting in this stand however. Appears to have some mistletoe damage on the spruce. Deer browse evident. Water is 13 cm below soil surface. Large sphagnum hummocks and hollows. Not too many windthrown coarse woody debris. Stand appears to transition to APn81a on south and west edges. Surface water pH recorded during earlier visit (June 24, 2014).

Plot located at the base of rock bench to the south that leads to a crest. There is a rock bench riser at the north end of the plot, rising up 0.5 m where Pleurozium schreberi and white pine seedlings are covering. Plot with lots of natural blowdown. No evidence of recent cutting or fire. No dwarf mistletoe detected in adjacent spruce peatland to the northwest. Soil pit dug to 40 cm below surface until a firm sloping rock; not sure if this is bedrock; substrate near rock is rather fine. Upper Oa/Oe layer has fungal mycelia and is loose/unconsolidated. It is mixed with some mineral soil to make a very thin 'A' layer (pH 4.5). Underneath is a very cinnamon brown layer on top of rock which makes up the majority of the mineral soil (pH 5.0). Pit was dug in small hollow without cobbles. Lots of lichen-covered snags and downed woody debris. Drainage class more accurately somewhat excessively drained.

Some parts of NPC with low Sphagnum spots. Glacial erratic boulder seen. Rock benches present but of low relief. Stand surrounded by recent clearcuts to the SW. Lots of natural coarse woody debris especially balsam fir. Deciduous trees occupy subcanopy layer at D6-6. Deer scat common. Long ago cut stumps but no recent burns or fire scars on jack pine, though a 20 cm dbh red maple shows a possible lightning strike. Soil consists mostly of a humus layer on top of bedrock and very little mineral soil; not enough to test for texture or determine drainage class. Humus thickness ranges from 5 to 11 cm. Fungal mycelia and fine roots in upper 2 cm and binding humus together. Most of rock is covered by Pleurozium schreberi.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: No cutting seen. Natural abundant coarse woody debris. Fire scarring prominent on a snag. Boulders common on surface. Humus layer with abundant fungal mycelia and fine roots. Very difficult to find a place to dig soil pit that didn't hit boulder. Soil profile consists of an ashy gray horizon below humus, followed by dark brown, then medium brown layers. All three tested at pH 4.0. Coarse fragments are cobbles at 35-60% plus stones at >90%. Needle litter have not been burned in a long time. Deer browse evident on red maple. Most of rock is moss covered.

Aspen-Birch Spruce-Fir Forest. Plot conducted for NLEB study (USFS SNF, MNDNR, CRTC & UMN, 2014)and is centered around F12B roost tree (Populus tremuloides, 34cm dbh). Residual patch between large,regenerating cut-over area and peatland. Moderate amount of downed logs. Deer pellets in plot. White spruce, balsam fir and white birch are dying. Brad Smith and Helen Becker (Superior NF-Kaw RD) collected vegetation and soils data within plot.

White Pine - Red Pine Forest. Plot conducted for NLEB study (USFS SNF, MNDNR, CRTC & UMN, 2014) and is centered around F06A roost tree (Populus tremuloides, 33 cm dbh). Large down logs, in all stages of decay, cover ~10% of plot. No occurrence of cut stumps. Balsam fir appears healthy. Year of origin 1913.Brad Smith and Helen Becker (Superior NF-Kaw RD) collected vegetation and soils data within plot. REVISED   soil - horizons: A, Bw1, Bw2 (fine SL), Bw3 (fine SL), 2C (gravelly COS). Parent material is loamy mantle glacial drift over gravelly outwash.

Aspen-Birch Spruce-Fir Forest. Plot conducted for NLEB study(USFS SNF, MNDNR, CRTC & UMN, 2014)and is centered around F12C roost tree. Roost tree (Populus grandidentata, 32 cm dbh) in middle of fir thicket. Very little vegetation on forest floor. Brad Smith and Helen Becker (Superior NF-Kaw RD) collected vegetation and soils data within plot.
Large, patchy Northern Crystalline Bedrock Outcrop (ROn12b)/Woodland Complex with releve plot sample area within ROn12b. Moose and deer droppings in plot.

White cedar-yellow birch forest. Plot in slightly lower portion of "saddle" (+/- drainage-way) between uplands (mostly woodlands). Abundant white pine, yellow birch and red oak seedlings. Moderate amount of large, down logs (yellow birch) with recent recruitment of logs fewer and of smaller diameter (black spruce, balsam fir). Fir scar on large white pine just outside plot. No charcoal in soils. No evidence of worms. Mineral soil gleyed from 0-6cm. Photo interpretation of larger landscape, shows the occurrence of many large patches with potential to include MHn45b. These patches occur on mid slopes among RP/WP woodlands in the surrounding rugged terrain. Plot within Superior NF, Birch Bay Unique Biological Area.

Rich Black Spruce Swamp (Basin). Large patch for Border Lakes subsection. Large boulder on surface at corner of plot. Canopy cover approximately 50% with subcanopy and high shrub layer approximately 25-50% cover.

Acid peatland system dominated by black spruce with a canopy of 50-75%, some shrub cover with Betula pumila and Alnus incana; mainly small shrubs (Lab tea). Bryophyte cover 90%; mostly sphagnum. Forbs and graminoids sparse.
Acid peatland dominated by black spruce with low shrub cover ranging between 75-100% and mainly Labrador tea. Bryophyte cover roughly 95% (Sphagnum).

Acid peatland with canopy of black spruce and tamarack; tall shrubs mainly dwarf birch <25% and low shrub layer mostly Labrador tea with cover of 75-100%. Not much diversity and bryophyte cover at nearly 100%. Somewhat transitional but still APn81.
Acid peatland community of tamarack and black spruce with limited shrub cover of deciduous species but greater than 50%. Labrador tea canopy 50-75% and almost continuous bryophyte cover.

Forested peatland dominated by cedar. Some Abies balsamea in the canopy. Mixture of sphagnum and brown mosses. Dense and continuous canopy but the canopy is no more than 10m in height. No cedar regeneration observed in plot.
Forested peatland system with an interrupted canopy of white cedar with balsam fir and alder in the understory. Moss cover near continuous with mainly sphagnum and periodic brown mosses.

Close to FPn71. Peatland system mainly black spruce with infrequent tamarack in the canopy. Canopy interrupted. Spruce to 15m in height. Labrador tea dense in the low shrub layer and considerate amount of V. vitis-idaea. Typically species poor but a few pockets that added diversity.
Acid peatland community dominated by black spruce less than 15m in height with near continuous byrophyte cover (Sphagnum) and low shrubs >75% with labrador tea.

Forested peatland; interrupted canopy of mostly tamarack, small cedar and alder/dwarf birch. Shallow pools with Calla palustrisand Carex lacustris. Inundated pools at the time of survey; trees on hummocks.

Forested peatland comprised mostly of white cedar, fairly dense but includes black spruce and balsam fir. Most of the bryophyte cover is feather mosses (50-75%). Mixed aged cedar and not much diversity in the understory/ground layer. Close to FPn63 but species depauperate. Possibly transitional but closest to FPn63.
Forested peatland comprised of white cedar with infrequent tamarack and balsam fir. Moss cover nearing 90%. Mix of sphagnum and brown mosses.

Alder community with occasional tree species (white cedar and paper birch) and few balsam balsam fir. Small pools with water at the time of the visit. Peat above mineral soil. Graminoid cover primarily Carex lacustris.

Peatland community of mixed composition of white cedar, alder, balsam fir, tamarack; varying height (open canopy). Transitional community with shallow pools and brown mosses; Sphagnum primarily absent.

Acid peatland with stunted tamarack with few black spruce – all less than 10m. Low shrub dominated by Labrador tea and nearly continuous cover of Sphagnum. Carex chordorrhiza the most common sedge in plot.
Acid peatland community dominated by stunted black spruce (<10m) and fairly species poor and nearly continuous cover of Sphagnum. Carex pauciflora very abundant.

Acid peatland community dominated by a canopy of black spruce, some nearing 15’ in height. System is species poor. Mainly Sphagnum with brown mosses. Missing several typical species for this community type. Eriopphorum angustifolium observed.
Forested peatland comprised of tamarack with some cedar. Not much in the shrub layer (tall growth). Mix of brown mosses and Sphagnum.

Forested peatland, primarily tamarack with black spruce and white cedar in the understory. Labrador tea prevalent in the ground layer. Bryophyte cover is a mix of Sphagnum species and brown mosses at nearly continuous cover.

Young tamarack stand (managed). Logged in part 15-20 years (trees fairly young). Tree growth dense with limited floral diversity. Limited bryophyte cover, mainly brown mosses. Small pools present but dry at the time of survey.

Forested peatland of tamarack, fairly uniform and dense. Existing pools lacking water at the time of survey. Limited bryophyte cover and not much in terms of diversity and abundance other than tamarack and alder.

Forested peatland of cedar and tamarack with limited shrub cover and ericacads noticeably missing or very sparse. Community resembles an FPn63 but with limited ericaceous cover, limited shrub cover, and very few graminoids.

Forested peatland (tamarack swamp). Mostly tamarack, limited amounts of balsam fir, black spruce, and white cedar. Bryophyte cover nearing 90%, mostly brown mosses. Redosier quite prevelant and ericaceous cover absent.

Acid peatland system consisting of black spruce with tamarack. Nearly continuous bryophyte cover, mainly Sphagnum. Very limited graminoid cover as well as a limited herbaceous layer. Ericaceous cover great.
Acid peatland community mostly comprised of black spruce (less than 30m in height). Bryophyte cover near continuous, mostly Sphagnum. Species poor.

Forested peatland; cedar swamp with tamarack; bryophyte cover is greater than 75% cover and primarily Sphagnum but includes brown mosses. Shallow pools still inundated at the time of survey. Mainly cedar in the lower height classes rather than tamarack.

A forested peatland, primarily tamarack in the overstory and black spruce/white cedar in the understory. Almost continuous bryophyte cover but a mix of Sphagnum and brown mosses; shallow pools with partial inundation and includes Calla palustris.
Forested peatland; cedar swamp with greater than 50% bryophyte cover. Balsam fir in various height classes. A limited amount of ericaceous cover and very few sedges.
Forested peatland dominated by white cedar with balsam fir. Uneven in terms of age. Mainly feather mosses with Sphagnum in the low patches.
Acid peatland with continuous cover of stunted black spruce averaging 3-4 meters. Occasional tamarack and Labrador tea very prominent throughout. Sphagnum cover nearing 100%.

Acid peatland comprised of stunted black spruce and dense ericaceous cover. Dwarf mistletoe present but not drastically impacting the black spruce. Leather leaf concentrated where black spruce dissipates.
Acid peatland of stunted black spruce (interrupted); occasional tamarack; Carex oligosperma quite prevalent and ericaceous cover varying density.
Acid peatland; black spruce and interrupted cover; mix of ericaceous and graminoid cover. Representative of the APn80 community type.
Acid peatland of stunted black spruce; reduced forb and ericaceous cover and Carex trisperma quite prevalent.

Peatland community of black spruce and tamarack; adjacent to elevated area with alternative composition but the releve is more representative of the greater area. Open areas consisting of bog birch and Carex lacustris with minerotrophic input. Ericaceous cover is patchy.
Forested peatland, mainly tamarack with white cedar and black spruce (uneven in age). Bryophyte cover nearly continuous and Labrador tea the most prevelant ericad.
Forested peatland of mostly tamarack with black spruce almost continuous bryophyte cover and limited ericaceous cover.
No hollow development. Flat mossy terrain. Moderate amount of smaller CWD. Occasional old, cut stumps but very decayed. FIM indicates this is a 158 yo cedar stand. Avg. cedar ~21-30cm DBH.

Fire scarred snags (approx 20ft tall). Occasional old stumps. Typical of this area of jack pine mixed with black spruce and semi-wet sands. Some other areas nearby however are solid black spruce with pockets of sphagnum. But this spot is indicative of vegetation in larger area. Sometimes areas grade to more FDn12 with more jack pine, but only on slightly higher rises. Lots of downed spruce.

Small, narrow upland bordering expansive swamp to north and road to south. Large fire scars on snags. Fire scars on red pine ~15ft high. Little to no pine regn. Lots of downed large trees around. Mainly fir and spruce. CWD high. Lots of old rotting logs. Possibly old cut stumps, but so old it's difficult to tell. A few dead cedar and jack pine that used to be in canopy and subcanopy. DNR designated old growth stand.

Black spruce dominated area which is different than nearby FPn63c. This area is fairly large and distinguishable on air photo as different. maybe due to past logging? Tree canopy is fairly open and there is significant amount of cedar regn here. Some downed trees.

Maybe some very old moss covered stumps present but not positive. Occasional hollows with water, ~1-2in deep. Hollows typically 3x3ft wide. Otherwise ground layer flat and even, with mostly dry hollows ~2ft deep. Geocaulon mostly scattered along edges with more sun.

Small subtle rise, which is similar to other isolated nearby areas on sand with perched water table. Lots of CWD and downed trees. Under canopy gaps, drier. Ground layer diverse with mix of upland and wetland species. The subtle rise in topography seems to host slightly more upland species and more aspen in canopy, compared with nearby areas. Rich loamy soil here with clay ~8in below. Lots of Carex capillaris and seems to prefer shady areas.
Fire scars on woody stems of old, dead shrubs. No standing water. Thick thatch. Very little bryophytes. southeast of beach ridge that runs nw-se.
Narrow linear feature which is part of a larger east-west flowage. Water at peat level. No hummocks of peat. Very little thatch.

Previously WFn53, but burned in 2012 North Minnie Fire resulting in a change to wet meadow community. No living cedar left. All top layer of peat is burned off and substrate now just exposed quaky, muck with soot. Close to ditch road.

Somewhat younger appearing forest. Younger to south. Releve represents this large tamarack swamp despite variations in the ages. The species haven't changed much except for amounts. Old stumps here. Lots of dense cedar regn. Canopy gaps create mossy openings with more diversity. Otherwise dense and patchy moss.
Designated old growth red pine forest. Fairly diverse so not FDn12. Fire scars on red pines. Tall fire killed snags (red pine). Red pines ~47-53cm DBH at upper end. Most are 25-30cm.

Deep hollows, water filled (recently rained). Water ~6in deep. Hollows 2-3ft deep. This is a denser version of adjacent area that is much more open but has similar character. Adjacent area has more Thuja and Alnus inshrub layer. There are lots of trees down. A few old stumps are present.

Several downed aspen and fir in plot. In canopy gaps, lots of fir sapling. Some mistletoe on spruce in upper canopy. Occ old stumps, some cedar stumps. Soil is wet sand. It is light grey in color and moist. Very fine. No clay. Area is on a slight rise above cedar/black spruce/tamarack swamp.
Black spruce upland on oxidized fine sand. Lots of fir CWD. Possible occasional old stump. Lots of downed fir. Dense fir saplings in canopy gaps. Several old large jack pine snags.

No cut stumps seen here. This is a designated old growth balsam fir stand. Nice structure of an older senesced forest. Lots of canopy gaps with dense Acer spicatum and corylus. What seems older than the fir, is the white pine in stand.

Releve represents mostly a small canopy gap where an old aspen came down. Most of the herbaceous spp. were here in opening. Beyond here, forest is pretty dense coverage of cedar and aspen without much ground diversity. Significant amount of small and large CWD, even in forest. Lots of mossy old trees decaying on floor. Old cut stumps, but mossy and very decayed. Several large, tall straight aspen.

Notable flow through pools, iron deposits-algae in pools(bright orange). Hollows~3x3 ft, sometimes more or less. hummocks 1-2 ft high. 1-3 inches of water or more in hollows. In deeper ones there is more. Hollows patchy. Cut stumps occasional.

Hummocks and hollows small - water filled. Occasional tamarack in canopy throughout stand, but rare. Old cut stumps scattered. Occasional dead tamarack. one large spruce tip-up in plot has exposed a large pool of muck and water where the abundance of Glyceria and Viola cf. mackloskii are growing in abundance.
Many hummocks, 1-2ft high, water filled hollows minimal and small. Larix dead due to larch beetle. Much more extensive mortality to south, where tamarack is more dominate.

This is a resurvey of Paul Glaser releve #4204. Dense cover of Phragmites. Not sure if this is the exact location of Glaser's original plot. Tried to find area nearby flark which had similar spp as releve. Fairly diverse, more so than original? Hummocks less than or equal to 28 cm, hollows below water approx 20 cm.

Tall strata of stunted, top-killed spruce. One deep hollow-like pool where Fissidens, Hypnum and Drepanocladus are found. Hummocks around 0.5m high. Hollows water filled. Hummocks dominated by mostly S. magellanica but but some with abundant with S. Fuscum. Hollows just small openings around 0.3 x 0.3 m, but channels connect them occasionally. Close to Glaser's plot 4200(OPN91b2). His plot was not as shrubby.

Plot not in exact spot as Glaser's- missing Betula pumila in plot. nor is this a dry mud bottom pool as Glaser's plot was described. This has been a very wet year though. Water around 2 inches above peat level. Mosses submerged and lots are dead but mostly alive in surrounding, slightly firmer peat. Located between two linear stands of Phragmites. No bearing trees. Poles placed in SW and NE corners of plot. GPS point in SW corner.

Water is around 15 cm above peat level. Small hummocks (2 x 1 ft) with sphagnum and Ericads. S subsecundum surr. Also stretches to North west corner. Slightly higher hummocks with S. fuscum on West and North side of plot. Scattered dead, stunted tamarack around poll, but none in plot. Mosses, except for Scorpidium, are clustered mostly on the West side near hummocks.Bearing tree is a tamarack, 6.75m from SW Pole; 20 degrees from SW pole and 1.9cm DBH.

PH 5.1. Internal water track. Water level high in pools with half of plot pool-like. hummocks 12-15 cm high. South side Sphagnum lawn, West corner has large Rynochospora hummock. low hummock/lawns of S. papillosum.

Larix ringing wetland almost all dead- some smaller-dbh ones still alive. Fairly uniform and low-diversity wetland that is similar to a few widely scattered wetlands in the area, between low glacial beach ridges and within a matrix of forested peatland and wet cedar forest.

Stand aged at 117 in 1981 according to FIM forest inventory layer. Typical of cedar-dominated transitional zone between upland and large peatland basin. Widespread, severe Larix mortality to the north and east. Water below soil surface painfully cold. Abies regen more common on east side of plot where canopy's thinner. Blowdown and CWD common. Distinct tree-derived microtopography.

Plot ~120 meters north of painted trees- forested peatland to south and older upland forest may be harvested in the near future. This basin currently intact and relatively diverse. It becomes more stunted and Larix-dominated to the north and east of this plot. Some old, small stumps of uncertain origin are present in plot.

Older mesic hardwood stand of apparent age (based on tree diameters) that is greater than average for mesic hardwoods in this area. Within painted harvest boundary that extends into forested peatland to north. Microtopography is common in southern part of plot, with water from recent rains in small depressions of unknown origin. Some CWD, no recent stumps. Update: clearcut as of June 2015.

Plot is slightly more open (has fewer trees) than surrounding area, though dryness is average. Does not contain pools, which are scattered throughout open portion of peatland. No disturbance evident near plot. Near-surface peat saturated from recent rain.

Many water-filled hollows between drier tree bases and distinct sedge- and shrub-dominated hummocks. FIM forest inventory layer indicates an age of 90. No visible stumps. Some recent blowdown, perhaps because this is a wetter site with tall hummocks. Single Malaxis paludosa found within releve after plot delineation and initiation of data collection.

Plot contains a wet depression over bedrock, a few stumps, and some fallen snags. Abies is dying as is Pinus banksiana to a lesser degree. Pinus strobus is more common in pockets off the plot. Pinus banksiana regeneration scarce and heavily browsed.

Contains very small, subtle rise and canopy gap with deciduous trees in it. Hollows shallow, green and moss-covered. Frequent coarse woody debris. Peat with fibrous chunks of wood to 14", water present 6" below soil surface.

Larix stressed and stunted, with many dead. Pools of water between non-Sphagnum hummocks at base of trees. No apparent stumps. Larix 2-3" dbh. This area transitional between open acid peatland to north and forested rich peatland to south.

Stand 140+ years old according to FIM forest inventory. Plot in narrower portion of basin that drains surrounding rocky uplands; wetter and more stunted to south. "Supercanopy" of sparse Picea mariana. Thuja shorter but larger dbh. Upland clearcut on private land 150m west. Some blowdown and CWD, and no recent stumps.

Stand aged at over 160 years old in FIM forest inventory. Continuous, rolling carpet of Sphagnum- no water-filled hollows nor taller, drier hummocks. Occasional CWD, moreso off plot. No visible stumps. Gray Jay family and numerous game trails observed.

Small, discrete peatland basin with minerotrophic influences partly from adjacent steep bedrock outcrops to north. Moderately hummocky with damp hollows and little to no standing water. Occasional fallen trees. Fibrous, saturated peat.

On slope between bedrock rise to north and forested peatland to south. Large snags and coarse woody debris common. Canopy gap on east side of plot- young Abies growing thickly beneath. Populus tremuloides regen sparse and chlorotic. Soil is thick humus and thin sandy loam over bedrock.

Relatively dry Thuja forest- no standing water nor tall hummocks, though shallow hollows are saturated. Old stumps visible. Blowdown and CWD uncommon. Moss and vascular plant cover patchy- heavier under canopy gaps, sparse under shade of mature Thujas.

Plot between lowland conifer clearcut 200 meters west and regenerating mesic hardwoods 70 meters east. Deer trails evident and Menyanthes leaves browsed. Some blowdown. Hollows saturated but no standing water.

Wet forest near the southern edge of a large forested peatland. Very dense woody vegetation- thick Abies understory dying out. Ground very uneven, but from tree roots and trunks rather than deep moss layer. Pools between mossy tree trunks either saturated or with up to 2 cm standing water.

Fraxinus not exceptionally large, but stand aged over 100 years in FIM forest inventory. Hollows between tree roots are saturated but no standing water present at this time. Water present 4" below soil surface, and abundant wood chunks and fragments are distributed throughout mucky soil to at least 14".

Extremely uniform but unique small peatland, ringed by a distinct band of Betula papyrifera which transitions to wet forest. Small, moss-covered stumps present- unsure whether from cutting or blowdown, which is quite common. No water or bare peat visible- entirely moss-covered, mostly Pleurozium schreberi. Chunky peat to at least 14"- damp from 4-10", waterlogged below 10".

Plot encompasses very gently north-facing bedrock outcrop with closed-canopy, damp Picea mariana depression at its base. Blowdown relatively uncommon and trees generally dense in area. A few small, old stumps apparent. Picea mariana confined to depression and not mixed with other trees.

Forested peatland with lowland conifer clearcuts ~300 meters to north, in a matrix of regenerating aspen-dominated uplands. Picea mariana mostly "mop-top" and exhibiting orange needle rust. Blowdown uncommon. No standing water. Most hollows are mossy and water is present 4" beneath surface of peat in hollows.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Northeastern Bedrock)
remarks: Bedrock rise surrounded by regenerating hardwoods and harvest trails. Relatively level plot, with less exposed rock than nearby areas. Rock visible here is mainly broken chunks. Canopy gap in southeast corner. Scattered larger red pine with many smaller. No recent stumps visible. Paired with nearby Releve CKK 14-022, which is topographically similar but has charcoal on and near the soil surface, and its vegetation is much more open. This plot lacks those characteristics and does not appear to have burned as recently.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Northeastern Bedrock)
remarks: Bedrock rise amidst regenerating hardwoods and harvest trails, with forested peatland to ~300 m north. Charred, old stumps and charcoal at and near soil surface. Paired with nearby Releve CKK 14-021, which is topographically similar but lacks charcoal, and its vegetation is much denser. This plot appears to have burned more recently.

Thuja 100+ years old west of the inland end of Tilson Bay. Fairly open and shrubby for mature wet Thuja forest- perhaps periodic inundation stunts the trees. Hollows damp with no standing water, but cold water within one inch of peat/muck surface. (Rainy Lake and its bays very flooded this year.) Moderate amounts of coarse woody debris. Fibrous peat to 14".

Linear forested peatland surrounded by wet forest west of the inland end of Tilson Bay (which is very flooded this year). Stand quite uniform. FIM forest inventory indicates age of 75. Coarse woody debris scattered and small. Hollows mossy with no standing water. Vegetation here does not appear stressed as does Fraxinus forest to north. Water 6" below peat surface.
Steep undulating slope along Sturgeon River. Nature of slope & aspect variable in plot (typical for slope). Old stump noted in vicinity. Fire scars present as well as charcoal @ soil surface.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Shallow sandy loam soils over bedrock. Woodlands and forest intermixed on landform, plot w/ indicators for both FDn32 and FDn43. Mature N.O. stand w/ evid. of selective harvest/thinnning over time. Humus and mineral soil highly intermixed by earthworms. Charcoal bits present.
Lowland along Rice River. No evid. of human disturbance. Indicators for both the a&b npc "types"  present. Stand integrates with wet cedar forest along periphery. Additional surveyor: Eric Holmstrom

Floating mat along Big Rice Lake and outlet to Rice River. Shrub dom areas and graminoid dom areas both present in stand. Plot representative of shrub dominated portion. Standing water present in plot hollows.
Periphery of large peatland complex, associated with water track feature.
Releve representative of water track feature. Contrast w/ associated npc, Releve # A497.
Releve captures npc on slightly higher/deeper peat bordering water track feature. Contrast w/ releve in WT, # A496.
Small peatland basin. Relatively level sphagnum "lawn". Shallow wet hollows abundant. Shrub component increases along periphery of basin.

Younger woodland, likely artificial regeneration (? origin). Spp diversity, composition and structure different from nearby JP/RP plantations. Old stumps w/ fire scars present. Soil horizons and exact textures: A, Bw1, Bw2, 2Bt (with clay films on all ped surfaces), 3C (COS). Parent material: outwash/beach deposits over glaciofluvial over outwash.

Laurentian divide along Giant's Range. Rocky till with cobbles and stones prevalent. Evid of med. to high earthworm impact (Rank 4-5). Stumps w/ fire scars observed. Additional surveyor: Donald Galloway.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Attempt to capture small patch npc on narrow terraces along Sturgeon River. Often near base of steep slopes (toe). Somewhat transitional in nature. Shallow depressions common but no standing water on 8/13. Portions of stand appear younger--unk disturb. Noted layer of debris deposit. Earthworms present. Terrace Forest?

Releve representative of small patch npc on narrow terraces at the base of steep slopes along Sturgeon River. Wet-mesic w/ shallow depressions but no standing water on date. Somewhat transitional in nature. Modified plot size. NPC uncertain.

Small, somewhat transitional/ecotonal npc surrounding lower, ephemerally wet forest inclusions. Evid. of earthworm activity. Setting w/ increased moisture & richness relative to matrix. Rocky till with cobbles and stones abundant. Additional surveyor: Christina Anderson.
Periphery of large peatland complex. Shallow wet hollows frequent. Setting slightly elevated relative to Releve # A505.

Dominated by spp. characteristic of wet hollows. Intermediate in nature and spp. composition b/w basin and water track poor fen. Appears to be influenced, to some extent, by water inflow from adjacent water track feature.

Small patch npc/forest inclusion in mesic hardwood (MHn35) matrix where Thuja frequency increases and understory vegetation shifts. Rocky till along slope. Microtopography present. Additional surveyor: Eric Holmstrom.
Area of high relief relative to landscape. Landform may be a kame? Older growth forest. Earthworms present -> impact moderate to high.

Older growth upland cedar. Microtopography abundant. Bryophyte list incomplete. Soil horizons: A, E, Ex (fragipan characteristics and ferric concentrations), B/E (with ferric concentrations and clay films) [B/E = glossic horizon: degradation and redistribution of clays within an otherwise argillic horizon], Bt (with ferric concentrations, clay films, and sand or silt skeletons), C (with iron depletions and ferric concentrations). Soil excavation deeper than 100 cm impeded by rock fragments. Very bouldery surface. Parent material: ablation till over lodgment till.
Releve representative of large stands in peatland complex. Evid of past management and heavy deer/moose activity. Standing water minimal; where present, depths range from 3-10 cm. Moss cover > 95%.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Bedrock knob with shallow soils. Small inclusions of exposed bedrock present. Plot representative of vegetation on crest and level top. Abies in stand dead or dying from spruce budworm impacts.

Low relief upland rise within large peatland setting. HQ natural origin JP woodland on deep sandy soil. Stand canopy composition variable; primarily dominated by JPine with minor components of B spruce, RPine, Bfir, and Aspen. Canopy JP reaching maturity. Fire scars present. Indicators for both FDn32d and FDn12. No evidence of earthworms.
Plot representative of large, level, graminoid dominated poor fen feature (Basin). Shallow wet hollows common (1-5 cm water depth). Deeper wet depressions (depths > 5 cm) present but infrequent.

HQ example of mature JP woodland on deep loamy sand. Plot representative of NPC on steep slopes in area. Appears to be natural origin from stand replacing fire. PB CWD and snags occasional. Patches of exposed sand present. Some patches of ground covered with diverse mix of bryophytes.

HQ mature JP/BS woodland on deep fine loamy sand. Setting is low relief upland rise within large peatland complex. Local water table may be near surface in spring. Scattered canopy gaps common in stand (tree fall).

Shallow soils over dense layer of stones and cobbles (stopped at 7 cm). Moss covered rock fragments abundant. Plot located on crest; terrain with gradual slope to E, S & W from plot center. Abundant windfall, tip-ups, and CWD. Moderate level of deer browse.

Moderate undulating landscape. Rep. of upland matrix NPC. Somewhat "drier" feel upslope but no shift in NPC. Large diameter WP/RP scattered in stand. No evidence of worms. Browse level moderate. Late season releve; some graminoids could not be identified. Soil remarks: Red mottles common 30-54 cm (soils are FSL). At 54-101 cm fine sandy loam becomes more compacted and both red and gray mottles are common. 99-101 cm is semi-permeable layer of dense compacted till. Very sandy below 101 cm; mottles infrequent. Charcoal noted. Detailed soils work done by J. Barott (SNF) and R. Holmstrom on 9/30/13.
NPC occupies long, somewhat linear depressions on undulating landscape. Late season releve: no standing water on date. Moss layer is patchy. Disturbance history unknown.

Rep. of small patch NPC occupying zone between MHn forest on level top and areas of exposed bedrock (ROn/FDn22 complex). Soils relatively shallow, stopped by Rock at 10 cm. Evidence of old cut stumps and snags with fire scars. Dead/Dying PB prevalent; patchy canopy gaps common. Earthworm IERAR = 5, heavy impact.

Mature example of dry-mesic mixed woodland with increased confifer component in canopy (contrast w/ releve #A518). Soils shallow, close to bedrock. Scattered surface cobble and stones common. Evidence of worms extensive. IERAR 4/5.

Rep. of small patch NPC on areas of exposed bedrock. Highly integrated with associated bedrock woodlands. Shallow soil accummulation in bedrock cracks and depressions. Crustose and foliose lichens cover 25-50% plot. Steep slope with E aspect.
Shallow soils over bedrock. Areas of exposed bedrock primarily covered with bryophytes. Fire scabs noted. Late season releve.

Older cut stumps with fire scars. Charcoal noted at soil surface. Evidence of past GL disturbance; shallow furrows/ruts(?) bisect stand (no uniform direction). Earthworms present. Plot located on relatively level site with gradual slope to S/SW.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot representative of mature woodland along south aspect slope. Small patches of exposed bedrock common. Evidence of older cut stumps with fire scars prevalent on slope. White Pine snags noted. UTM = NE plot corner.

Small island in Lake Vermillion. Plot representative of narrow woodland NPC (small patch) on shallow soils/bedrock close to shoreline. Charcoal noted. Stand integrates with other woodland NPCs as move inland. Older Jack pine present in stand; primarily dead or dying. JP snag (OP) w/ 45.2 cm dbh. Evidence of recreational use along shoreline. Bird list available. Additional surveyor: Norma Malinowski. UTM = SE plot corner.

Old growth forest: snags, CWD, and structure appropriate for growth stage. Stand with large but patchy canopy gaps. Plot located in portion with relatively intact canopy. No obvious sign of human disturbance. Additional surveyor: Jennifer Hammer. UTM = NE plot corner.
Deeper soil deposit; bedrock far from surface. Site with dramatic topography. Pines present in stand but sparse. Observed old cut stumps along slope. Fire scars present. UTM = NW plot corner.

Releve representative of stunted oak woodlands on upper slopes and level tops of large bedrock features. Shallow soils with small inclusions of exposed bedrock. Old cut stumps with fire scars present. WP regen. common in understory. UTM = SW plot corner.

Small patch NPC on bedrock knob near Lake Vermilion shoreline. Mature example. CWD and snags common. No obvious sign of human disturbance. Browse moderate. Indicators for both a and b NPC "Types" present. UTM = SW plot corner.
Water-filled depressions/pools common. Mature example but lacking large diameter CWD. Disturbance history unknown. UTM = SW plot corner.

Plot located on gradual slope near subsection boundary. Thin soils over densely packed layer of cobbles and stones. Stopped by coarse frag. @ 13 cm. Recent spruce budworm disturbance; large amounts of balsam fir (and black spruce) CWD (newly fallen). UTM = NW plot corner.

NPC uncertain. Ecotonal? Likely on upland/wetland transition. May tend toward WFn53. Older growth forest with minimal evidence of human disturbance. Large diameter CWD in plot. Pools/wet depressions and muck/peat absent. Additional surveyor: Chris Lintula. UTM = SE plot corner.

Wet hollows common with standing water, depths 1-5 cm. Evidence that pools held deeper water earlier in the season. No sign of human disturbance in area of plot. Additional surveyor: Norma Malinowski. UTM = NE plot corner.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Plot located on subtle slope along periphery (near shore) of Glacial Lake Agassiz. Microtopography abundant but no standing water on date. Surface mixing of muck and muck humus by earthworms, hard to discern actual depth of M humus. HQ mature example of NPC. Basal areas 1 & 2 noted on datasheet. UTM = NW plot corner.

Even-aged natural origin stand with fire scars on cut stumps and snags. Charcoal noted on soil surface. Plot located just upslope from area of exposed bedrock along shoreline (Lost Lake). Soils still relatively shallow in plot, stopped by rock at 11 cm. Indicators for both FDn43 and FDn32. Additional surveyor: Kelly Beaster. UTM = NW plot corner.
Small patch NPC occupying portion of linear depression. Stand associated with other rich forested peatland communities. No evidence of human disturbance. Plant diversity is low. UTM = NE plot corner.

Large complex of highly integrated oak woodland and rock outcrop communities. Plot representative of open bedrock NPC component. See Releve #A538 for example of woodland component. Patches of shallow soil, very find sandy loam. Additional surveyor: Eric Holmstrom. UTM = NE plot corner.
Evidence of mistletoe. Patchy canopy openings common. No standing water. UTM = plot center.

Woodland dominated by stunted scrubby red oak. Scattered pine in supercanopy. No exposed bedrock in plot, but scattered stones and boulders cover ~ 15%. Old cut stumps noted in stand but infrequent. Basal areas 1 and 2 noted on datasheet. Additional surveyor: Eric Holmstrom. UTM = SE plot corner.

Undulating landscape. Plot located in mid-topographic position in area where terrain is moderate and soils are deeper (stopped by coarse fragments at 18 cm). Mature stand, large diameter Aspen and P. Birch CWD and snags frequent. Evidence of human disturbance minimal/absent. UTM = SE plot corner.

Occupies floating mat near narrow channel that drains to Lake Vermilion. Influenced by oscillations in lake levels; early season 2014 with above average water levels in Lake Vermilion. Microtopography highly variable with high hummocks and deep hollows. Additional surveyor: Norma Malinowski. UTM = SW plot corner.

Lowland associated with narrow drainage to Lake Vermilion. Stand may be influenced by oscillations in lake levels. Deep wet hollows and high hummocks present. Evidence of variable water levels in plot/stand. UTM = NE plot corner.

Steep bedrock ridge above Lake Vermilion shoreline. Portion of lake with greatest expanse of water; high exposure to wind and wave action along this shoreline. Woodlands occupy "benches" on ridge and areas of feature where topography is more gradual. Old scattered stumps noted. UTM = SE plot corner.

NPC occupies upper slopes and level tops above Sturgeon River/Dark River and associated Terrace Forest complex. Obs. more complete soil profile to west of plot along slumped bank: 0-76 cm loamy sand with underlying layer of thick clay (76->86 cm). Redox features noted around 70 cm. Plot located on relatively level site with gradual rise to both the E and W. Mature forest w/ scattered canopy gaps and large diameter CWD. UTM = SE plot corner.

Releve is located in an acid peatland community which is dominated by Larix and Picea in the canopy. Lower woody layers are sparse, but inclde Alnus and small Picea. The low shrub layer is dominated by fairly dense Rhododendron with some Betula pumila mixed in. The graminoid and forb layers are sparse but moss cover is near 100% consisting of Sphagnum with some brown mosses mixed in. Arceuthobium is very abundant in this area and has lead to some Picea mortality.

This releve is located in an acid peatland community dominated by tall Picea with some Larix and Thuja. There are very few trees in the subcanopy. The low shrub layer is sparse to moderately dense with Rhododendron, Chamaedaphne, and Betula pumila. The forb layer is sparse but the graminoid layer is fairly dense with Carex stricta. The moss layer is nearly continuous with Sphagnum. During field surveys the water seemed unusually high.

Releve is located in a wet forest community on the transition between a mesic cedar stand to the northwest and an alder swamp to the southeast. The area has a canopy of Fraxinus nigra and Betula papyrifera. There is a high shrub layer of Alnus and young Fraxinus nigra and a low shrub layer of young Populus balsamifera and Alnus. The ground layer is dominated by Rubus pubescens, Carex stricta, Maianthemum canadense, and various other graminoids.

Releve is located in an acid peatland dominated by stunted Larix with some stunted Picea. Some young Picea are present in the low shrub layer but over all this stratum is dominated by Betula pumila and Rhododendron. The ground layer is fairly diverse but appears to be dominated by forbs. The moss layer is approximately 95% but almost entirely Sphagnum.

This releve is located in an acid peatland community dominated by tall Picea which are evenly spaced giving the area an open feel. The shrub layer is short statured and dominated by Rhododendron. Only true bog species are present. Moss cover is continuous and is roughly 50% Sphagnum and 50% Plerozium, Dicranum, and feather mosses. The area is relatively dry likely due to the presence of a ditch along the road to the west.

Releve is located in an acid peatland community with a tall canopy of Picea. There is very little in the subcanopy and the "tall shrub" layer giving the area a "park-like" appearance. The short shrub layer is very dense with Rhododendron and other ericacious plants. Only true bog species are present. The moss layer is approximately 90% Sphagnum with some Plerozium making up the rest. No standing water present.

Typical of better quality portions of a small (~1 acre) seepage meadow along Diamond Creek. On rather narrow valley bottom near the base of a steep, 250-foot, north-facing bluff. Seepage influence is subtle in most of meadow. Moist to quite wet (saturated) silty muck; a small swale (flowage) through middle of meadow is included in plot. Disturbance history includes grazing (pre 1970?) and ATV damage (1994) though neither seems to have had lasting effects on the heart of the meadow (where plot is located).

Typical of mature, natural-origin woodland on northeast side of Purvis Lake. Tree diameters range from 24-26cm DBH, mode ~40-45cm. Soil is silty-sand with numerous small angular stones. No outcrops in plot (small granitic [tonalite] exposures ~ 100 meters to south near lakeshore. No stumps. Few snags. CWD rather sparse, highly-decayed large old boles occasional. Thick litter and humus. A horizon dark, 2-3cm deep.

Typical of areas of denser pine in fairly extensive natural-origin patch south of Purvis Lake. Mature to old growth, originating from slash fires ~1910-1920. Pines mostly 40-50cm DBH. Stand +/- even-aged here. Snags infrequent. Fire scars present on old snags in vicinity. Sparse CWD, occasional old large decaying boles. Occasional old root mounds. Level to gently sloping setting. Soil is coarse gravelly sand. Upper 8cm is loamy-sand. Moose droppings in plot (2-3 yrs old?)

Typical of rather broad zone (20-40 meters wide) bordering a small (~1 acre) bog pond in fairly large peatland southwest of Twin Lakes. Plot typifies the depressional, low-statured vegetation habitat zone here but includes several Sphagnum hummocks which are typicaly minor inclusions in this zone. Edge of plot is ~5 meters from the pond. Saturated peat >40cm deep. Water is ankle-deep in foot tracks. Grades outward to stunted spruce bog (APn90).

Typical of mature ~100-year-old patch along road (to Bear Head Lake State Park) north of Eagles Nest Lake #3. Level to gently-rolling terrain south of Pickerel Lake. Natural-origin from slash fires 1910-1920. Trees mostly 40-60cm DBH, rare to 72cm. Several old fire-scarred stumps in plot. No snags. Sparse CWD. Soil is tan loamy-sand with stones, 10cm deep A-horizon. Low rock outcrops (Ely greenstone) ~ 50 meters to north of plot. Trees painted for sale to north (on Co. Tax Forfeit land). Larger patch is a mix of ownership with scattered houses/cabins.

Typical of large patch of mature (to old growth) natural-origin pine (~1910) forest on rolling terrain southwest of Purvis Lake. North side of plot is not far from (top of) a steep, 70-foot, north-facing slope. Pines mostly 44-61cm DBH. Occasional snags. No stumps. CWD rather sparse. Slope in plot varies from 0-5 degrees, aspect is southeast. Soil is rocky fine tan sand with a shallow loamy A-horizon. An old fire-scarred snag is present in plot.

5- x 20-meter plot captures the more open aspects of a large outcrop complex atop 120-foot granitic knob on east side of Fourtown Lake. Plot located above crest of extremely steep south-facing slope; vertical outcrops downslope. Grades to bedrock shrubland with no trees atop the ridge (several feet higher elevation). Slope varies from 0-10 degrees, southwest aspect. One fire-scarred snag present in plot. Exposed rock covers ~1/3 of plot, remainder is very shallow silty-detrital soil over bedrock and along bedrock crevices.

Typical of broad zones in poor sedge fen complex recovering from long past flooding (early 1900's, logging-related; along stream/flowage between Fourtown and Horse Lakes). Old conifer snags on upland margin eastward, these all cut at ~6-8 feet above current wetland elevation (reflects the past flooding elevation). Grades to larger zones dominated by Carex utriculata; and to low shrub poor fen and poor scrub conifer swamp westward (up-gradient) in this peatland. Sphagnum hummocks 8-12" tall, these cover ~20% of plot, rest of plot is low Sphagnum carpets. Deep saturated peat, fairly firm; no large woody remains in peat here.

Typical of fairly extensive patch of oak-pine woodland on bedrock ridge and upper portion of 120-foot, south-facing slope above Mudro Lake. Plot on level ridgetop. Granitic outcrops near plot, and frequent in larger oak patch (~60 acres). Pines mostly 25-40cm DBH, often occurring in small clumps. Oaks mostly 10-15cm, scraggly with dead lower branches. A few old cut stumps in vicinity. Snags uncommon. CWD rather sparse. Silty soil with rocks, fairly shallow to bedrock (mostly greater than 25 cm deep). Dan W. took photos of plot and vicinity.

Typical of large patch of old growth upland cedar on fairly large peninsula (50 acres) on northeast side of Fourtown Lake. Upland cedar covers entire peninsula. Thuja mostly 25-45cm DBH. Scattered large red and white pines, these 60-80cm+ DBH, many dead. No stumps. Snags infrequent. CWD rather sparse. Low, moss-covered granitic outcrops in plot, on crest of a low ridge. Very thick humus. Grey silt with occasional stones; charcoal at ~9cm (just below humus). Occasional small mossy boulders. Small moss-covered granitic outcrops present, these cover ~5% of plot. Grades to somewhat more diverse ground layer along moist drains. Dan Wovcha took photos.

2.5- x 10-meter plot captures most of the lakeshore zone here, on small low bedrock island in Fourtown Lake. Shallow silty gravel amongst boulders; on low, very gently sloping granitic shelf that is currently 1-3 inches above lake level (which is down ~16 inches from the early season high mark). Gravel varies from 1-15 cm deep over bedrock. Borders a narrow zone of Myrica gale then Alnus incana-Calamagrostis canadensis inland. Plot wraps around a small point. Both Dan and Mike took photos. Dan also has GoPro video of site.

Typical of fairly broad zone bordering the Moosecamp River flowage north of Fourtown Lake. Meadow borders the river for most of its length (~2.5 miles). This zone is likely flooded in spring, currently no surface water. Substrate is firm, moist, mucky-organic mineral soil; water at 25cm deep in soil pit. Edge of plot is 10 meters from the river, similar distance from opposite edge of plot to upland ecotone. Grades to zones with more Carex lacustris. Calamagrostis canadensis forms hummocks ~30-40cm tall.  Beaver dams encountered periodically along the flowage, but no beaver flooding effects are apparent here. Both Dan and Mike took photos of plot and setting.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Typical of patches of mature pine-dominated woodland on broad bedrock ridge 4 miles west of Ash Lake. Similar patches not far to north are designated old growth (stand ages: 132-153 years.) A few old stumps in general vicinity. Snags occasional. CWD sparse. Soil very shallow to granitic bedrock, <10 cm deep in several soil pits. Occasional surface rocks and small boulders. Moss carpets nearly continuous over bedrock, rocks, and shallow soil. Thick humus. Gently undulating microtopography. Hard frost several days before data were collected.
