Water at peat level. No sphagnum, and little other mosses to speak of. Lots of thatch. Surrounded by Cedar/Black Spruce swamp and small cutover upland of white pine. This fen is one of several rich-fen openings in this area.

Cedar swamp with occ large tamarack & occasional Paper Birch. Community is between FPn63 and Wet forest (WFn53). Hollows occasional, shallow, and intermittent. Bryophytes are mostly feather mosses. Lots of Cedar seedlings on old logs & hummocks. Hollws are mucky- no standing water. Adjacent to small wet meadow opening within larger lowland swamp.

Plot chosen to represent high quality natural origin NPC frequent in this portion of Gabbro Lake bedrock complex LTA. No evidence of anthropogenic disturbance observed. Abundant CWD of various diameters. Exposed bedrock within 30 meters of plot. Observed pockets of pure fine and coarse sand. Abundant CWD, small to moderate size. Very coarse loamy sand at >100 cm. Exposed bedrock within 30 m.

Plot chosen to represent NPC not well described in classification. No clear evidence of anthropogenic disturbance but in a location with potential past harvest, grazing. Same character in 1930's aerial imagery, i.e. open areas w/ scattered large trees. Large birch w/ open grown growth form, i.e. 4-8 meter high boles and broad, many- branched canopy. Located within broad dissected till-filled basin between bedrock hills. Fine sandy loam; Superior Till parent material. Total veg cover ~95%

Plot chosen to represent NPC not well described in classification. Some mottles throughout soil profile SLC 100-150 very fine, pressured till parent material is water deposited alluvium/colluvium mantle over pressured fine till. Water perched above pressured fine till @75 cm about 10 meters from point profiled above.

Plot chosen to represent expression of NPC typical of LTA in which mesic mixed forest occurs in small to (medium?) sized patches within a woodland matrix. No cut stumps or other anthropogenic disturbance. Bouldery substrate w/fine sandy loam between; surface irregular. Low to mod CWD less than or equal to 20 cm dbh. Dendrobaena sp. only earthworm observed; no middens. Very bird rich.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality example of natural origin. NPC common in Lac Lacroix Bedrock Complex LTA. No evidence of anthropogenic disturbance or non-native spp observed. Moderate amt of CWD. Exposed bedrock typically lichen-covered. Scattered stones and boulders on surface. Browsing evident on Acer rubrum. No non-natives in flora. Moose scat.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Northeastern Bedrock)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent high quality natural origin expression of NPC common in this setting in Lac Lacroix Bedrock Complex LTA. No anthropogenic disturbance observed. Charred tree base in plot. Plot to represent older growth stage of NPC. Pinus and Quercus older?/larger than to East near Lake Jeanette.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent high-quality NPC @ old growth stage common in this setting & in Lac Lacroix Bedrock Complex LTA. A few very-decayed sm-dbh (~15 cm @ base) cut stumps near plot. No cut stumps in plot. Large ROn12b community nearby.
Plot to represent high-quality, natural origin NPC common in this setting and in LLB Complex LTA. Part of high-quality, nat orign. complex of woodland NPCs on this landform. No anthro dist.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Northeastern Bedrock)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent high-quality, natural origin NPC in common landscape setting in this area of the Lac Lacroix Bedrock Complex LTA. Part of high-quality woodland comlex on this landform. Pinus strobus dominated (FDn22b)- not often observed to date in other portions of the LTA.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality natural origin NPC in typical setting in Lac Lacroix Bedrock Complex LTA. No anthropogenic disturbance observed. Nearby fire-scarred P. strobus snag w/dbh larger than those in plot. Other pines w/out fire scars. Abundant CWD, all sizes. Very fine sandy loam w/abundant grey mottling down to compacted reddish loam. Medium-sized erratic nearby.

Comments re: "Stand not typical of NPC": Pinus banksiana dominant canopy conifer. Comments re "Releve not Typical of Stand": typical of one area of rare plant habitat in this NPC, canopy mostly intact. Remarks: Plot chosen to represent one area of Prosartes trachycarpa habitat where canopy is comparatively intact, providing at least moderate shade to herb layer.

Plot chosen to represent NPC uncommon in Lac Lacroix Bedrock Complex LTA. Patch @ edge of larger APn81a. Standing water pools common in this wet spring/summer. Hummocks medium height, highest associated w/ tree bases; Sphagnum spp. dominant cover. CWD common and typically <15 cm dbh. No anthropogenic disturbance observed. Some blowdown. Standing water pools typically ~5 cm deep.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality, natural origin NPC common in this setting and Lac Lacroix Bedrock Complex LTA. No anthropogenic disturbances observed. Surface irregular, soil in pockets, variable depths. Most exposed rock moss/herb covered. No cut stumps observed, no worms. Moderate amount of CWD, mid-size dbh.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality natural origin NPC occurring in small patches in drainages of Lac Lacroix Bedrock Complex LTA. Evidence of pools (~30% of plot) common but no standing water on this date. Bryophyte spp many; a few IDed (see strata). Only absent from pool bottoms. Herbs and graminoids mostly on tree/shrub bases. CWD abundant, sm to lrg dbh. No anthropogenic disturbance. Fraxinus nigra vigorous no snags or dead tops. Muck over peat. Transitions to WFn55 to NE. Patch as a whole may be variable.
Plot chosen to represent high-quality natural origin small patch NPC w/in woodland matrix. On moderate to steep slopes above Vermilion R. Moderate amt of CWD sm to large dbh.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality natural origin community w/in wet forest complex in Lac Lacroix Bedrock Complex LTA. This NPC type uncommon in LTA. Occurs as small patch w/in WFn55 patch. Abundant large dbh CWD. Highly variable microtopography of tree base hummocks and wet hollows. Pools evident (early to mid-season, no standing water on this date. Wet forest complex in very gently sloping drainage.
Plot chosen to represent high-quality natural origin plant community uncommon in Gabbro Bedrock Complex LTA.Hummocks and hollows common. CWD infrequent.

Plot chosen to represent one expression of vegetation associated with vernal/ephemeral pool w/in MHn45c, w/water holding capacity into July and beyond at least in some years. Highly irregular boundary; some adjacent ecotonal habitat; other portions of this depression have different floristic composition. Except canopy layer (E7) plot data is from pool area and CWD and shrub bases w/in pool area. Deepest muck 17cm; typically 12cm. Angular and rounded cobble common at and above surface. Muck over rock substrate. Some standing water on this date, 5cm or less. A few large boulders. Abundant med to large CWD. In shade of Acer saccharum. Note: In the dry spring of 2015 this area was moist but had little standing water.

Vernal wetland located in mesic-hardwood forest. Releve placed to capture major band of vegetation between lowest spot of exposed soil and mesic forest edge. Ground dominated by Pilea pumila and an assortment of graminoids. Area held water longer into season than normal.

Larger vernal wetland located within mesic-hardwood forest. Releve placed in vegetative band between forest edge and open mud flat (lowest area of wetland). Some canopy cover from Fraxinus pennsylvanica. Dominated by Pilea pumila, Boehmeria cylindrica, and Leersia. Area held water longer into year than normal.

Vernal wetland located in mesic-hardwood forest. Releve placed to capture major band of vegetation between lowest spot of exposed soil and mesic forest edge. No trees in plot, but hose outside of plot provide cover. Phalaris arundinacea invading on edge.

Releve is located on one of higher open knobs in the north section of this pasture on an area with little soil development (bare sand gravel exposed). Native grasses being very sparse on the uplands of this site, but with good forb diversity and cover. Small cedar trees (1-2m) are sparsely distributed on these sites. Collected as example of Grazed prairie (Dairy).

This pasture lacking much of the native grass component. There are some grazing lawns present outside releve area but there are no animals currently. Overall, the area has add odd mix of grazing increaser and Decreaser species with prairie clover, silky aster, and prairie turnip common and prairie smoke very abundant across site. Releve collected as example of grazed Prairie. Talked to landowner who said the site had been horse pasture through much of its history.

Pools cover about 30% of surface and about 30% of pool surface is covered by mosses. Cedars average 15 cm dbh, many leaning over. Phenologically still early, many plants still emerging. Some very old cut stumps. 

wypt 041 in NW corner

Canopy ashes range from 15 to 30 cm dbh. This basin is mostly WFn53 of mixed cedar and ash, but the two ends are ash dominated. Hummocks mostly formed from long fallen logs, most with moss cover. Pools cover about 60% of plot. Phenologically still early, many plants still emerging. One Large fallen tree in plot, several dead ashes in canopy.

[Remarks from other fields:]
Notes: Wypt 51 in SW corner

Pools occupy about 30% of plot, some pools have moss cover. Many cedars are reclining. Average dbh is 20-25 cm. Surrounded by wet forest types. Phenologically still early, many plants still emerging. 

wypt 54 in SE corner

Rich fen shoreline of Strand Lake. Most of shoreline does not have Sphagnum but this area does (>30x50m). Hardwood forest to northwest.

[Remarks from other fields:]
Notes: Wypt 124. close to lake edge

Wide fen between upland and lake, lake bed covered by dense stand of Equisetum fluviatile.

[Remarks from other fields:]
Notes: Wypt 129 -close to edge of lake

On sandy plain above St. Louis River. 1948 air photo shows open pine canopy. Forestry records indicate natural stand origin. Floodplain forest is far way but still contributing some seeds here. P. resinosa average 40 cm dbh (max 50 cm). P. banksiana smaller. Possibly FDn33 or FDn32. Also observed in stand: Epigaea repens, Comptonia peregrina, Salix humilis, Arctostaphylos uva-ursi, and Diphasiastrum digitatum.

NW corner of plot is wypt 143.

Open acid peatland surrounded by P. mariana bog. No minerotrophs present, suggesting open bog, but on Forestry CIR air photo flark and string patterns are evident. Pattern not noticeable on ground. pH measured at 4.3, but I'm not completely confident in the meter (+/- 0.3). Possibly APn91c

Mature floodplain forest about 2m above current, low river level probably floods most years. Scour channels apparent though plot. A. saccharinum 4-18" Q. macrocarpa 6-8". Some large Acer logs. 2 old cut maple stumps.

[Remarks from other fields:]
Soil information--Litter Type: Leaves and Grass
Notes: Wypt 286 @ center of plot. Some floodplain forest along this river are lower, closer to the river level and flood for longer durations.

Rolling topography, sandy inclusion in a peat and clay landscape. Lots of charcoal in upper soil. Decent CWD (mostly birch and fir), but no large logs. Areas to north have been thinned recently, but not here. Pinus resinosa 25-45 cm dbh, Betula papyrifera 15-30 cm, Acer rubrum 10-15 cm.

[Remarks from other fields:]
Notes: Wypt 330 NE corner of releve

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: This part of forest is older than most of the rest, with a few older trees left standing during last cutting 60-70 years ago. Aspens average 30 cm dbh, red maple 15-35 cm, sugar maple and basswood 15-30 cm. More sugar maple here than other parts of forest and fewer indicators of MHn44 (due to age?). Only sign of earthworms is a 1 cm A-horizon of soil of Dendrobaena castings below the thick humus layer. Presence of Matteuccia and Gymnocarpium is unusual for this forest.

Terrace above St. Louis River, currently 4-5 m above river, floods rarely. Series of +/- level rises and channels form undulating pattern. A few 15-20 cm logs on the ground. Some small trees and shrubs cut by beavers. Soils very fine sand or very fine loamy sand.

Waypoint 373 at center of plot

Rolling topography pitted with vernal pools. Good amount of coarse woody debris, mostly fallen jack pine. Deer trail passes through plot. Red pines have been planted in parts of this forest. In this area the trees look natural, but possibly planted. Some mesic species present may have seeded in from nearby pools. Canopy suggests FDn32, ground layer FDn43. Former gravel pit is about 60m to west.

[Remarks from other fields:]
Notes: wypt. 37 near center of plot.

Part of a series of wet-mesic uplands between the West Swan River to north and large peatlands to south. Water table is very high. Most surrounding uplands have been recently clearcut. Fair amount of CWD, mostly fallen Abies balsamea same age as canopy trees. Soil profile not altered by worms, and no worm castings observed, but worm sign seen near river. Worms possibly =2. Trees avg 25cm dbh.

After heavy rain, water covers ~70% of surface. Appears to be young stand that has succeeded from FPn73. this rich swamp is situated between Picea mariana dominated swamp to west and upland island to east. Some root tip-ups and leaning trunks in plot. pH reading error estimated to be 0.3.

Picea mariana swamp surrounded on 3 sides by FPn63. A few trees killed by dwarf mistletoe. Some areas of open canopy nearby due to mistletoe mortality. Deer/moose trails pass through. A small basin of mixed rich and poor conifer swamp. Water sample with pH reading error estimated to be 0.3.

Pools cover 15-20%. Many cedar trunks are straight, not curved. Deer browse and pellets in plot- used as winter yard. One very old cut cedar stump near plot. Pools about half-covered with Rhizomnium. In small basin dominated by Thuja. Water sample.

Pools cover about 40% of plot. Most cedar trunks are relatively straight at the base, only a few curved. Peat appears sapric, but less than 1/3 escapes between fingers when squeezed. In a mosaic of FPn63, WFn53, and WFn64 at east end of large minerotrophic forested peatland. Mosses recorded only from ground, not trunks or stumps.

Some tamarack mortality around plot from insect damage. Large tip up mound. Pools cover about 15% of plot. Example of rich Picea mariana-dominated swamp. Adjacent to FPn63 in small peatland basin. Wypt 111 near center of plot. Water sample collected, but I'm not confident in the pH reading of 8.0, but it is certainly high nonetheless.

Situated in broad area between upland and creek with wide meadows. Many fallen Abies balsamea logs. Plools cover about 40% of plot, moist but without standing water after wet spring. Mosses from stumps and trunks not collected.

Open water track in large peatland complex. Numerous dead Larix stems 2-3 m tall. Pools are not in any pattern. Pools cover approx. 30% of plot, with no moss cover. Water sample taken to office for pH measurement, but I do not trust the reading of 6.2.

Open transitional fen in middle of extensive stunted Larix swamp, presumably due to subsurface water flow. Water sample read 6.7, but I do not trust this reading. 5.5 is more likely. Numerous dead Larix stems 3-4 m tall. A small ditch ends about 200 m southwest, coming from west. It's now full of peat. Larix on dredge spoils a few meters wide are taller. Powerline and railroad bed cross peatland to south and west.

Interior of large acid peatland with large areas of sparse stunted trees that do not appear to be water tracks. Some areas with significant Carex oligosperma cover, but not here. Hummocks cover about 80% of plot, hollows (Sphagnum-filled) about 20%. Water sample with pH reading error estimated to be 0.3.

Interior of large acid peatland with large areas of sparse stunted trees that do not appear to be water tracks. To south, C. lasiocarpa transitions to C. oligosperma. Possibly APn91b. Water sample taken for measurement at office, pH reading error estimated to be 0.3.

Large area of open canopy of stunted trees surrounding water track and surrounded by denser forested peatland. Old, grown-in trail about 100m away, possibly for Xmas tree cutting. Hollows (without standing water) cover about 25% of plot. Spruces have a rust fungus on needles. Water sample collected for office measurement, pH reading error estimated to be 0.3.
Large open rich fen water track within larger forested peatland. Water sample collected for office measurement, pH reading error estimated to be 0.3.

Water track draining large acid peatland, originating from pond near center. Hollows with some standing water cover about 40%. To northwest the track is wetter with more Typha. Water sample taken to office for measurement, pH reading error estimated to be 0.3. Possibly OPn91. SNA designated by Legislature, but managed by St. Louis County.
Poor fen alongside water track in large peatland. Hollows (Sphagnum-filled) cover about 20% of plot. Water sample taken, pH reading error estimated to be 0.3.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Mesic forest on terrace above Floodwood River as it passes through the Wawina Peatland. Good amount of course woody debris in form of logs of Tilia, Populus tremuloides and Betula papyrifera. No sign of cut stumps.

Short statured Larix swamp in a "peninsula" surrounded by even shorter statured swamp. Plot chosen to be representative of the taller Larix to the east. Within a very large peatland complex. Hollows mostly moss-covered, both Sphagnum and Pleurocarps. Hollows about 20% of plot. Possibly FPn81. Water sample taken, pH reading error estimated to be 0.3.

Some fallen logs, but fewer than would be expected from an undisturbed forest. Uneven aged forest with some scattered very large trees, but understory is more open than it would be if undisturbed. Logs include Abies balsamea. Humus thickness varies from 0 to 1 cm. TREE BASAL AREA DATA: A. saccharum- BA1: 11; BA2: 11; Tilia a.- BA1: 6; BA2: 9; Thuja o.- BA1: 0; BA2: 2

In narrow swale about 3x releve width between sandy uplands. Adjacent to wet meadow along small creek, but appears not to be influenced by creek. There are a few scattered Fraxinus and Betula papyrifera trees, but not in plot. Hollows cover about 80% of plot, hummocks 20%. Former channel of St. Louis River. Mosses collected/ID only from hummocks & hollows, not from wood surfaces. Many Carex have lost identifying characters.

Large swamp dominated by Fraxinus nigra, some places with denser shrub layer than here and some places with more and deeper water cover. Some large Fraxinus have recently fallen, creating CWD, but not in plot. Most trees have some degree of canopy dieback. Very little hummock-hollow topography. Designated old growth ash stand; water sample collected. BASAL AREA DATA: F. nigra- BA1: 10; F. nigra- BA2: 11; U. americana- BA2: 2

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Grades at top of slope to overgrown savanna. Notably sparse ground layer. Small amount of coarse woody litter. Adjacent to dog park so dogs run loose here often. Base of plot is next to wide trail. In Mississippi National River and Recreational Area.
East slope of main hill WMA extends east of here. Steep bank.
Because of all the amorpha it is obvious from road that this is natural vegetation. Prairie confined to west facing slopes, heavily dotted with Amorpha. Hill just south of pine plantation.

Although the knoll is mapped by Wildlife as prairie, it is dominated by brome. Releve is on east flank and it's unclear whether this is still in the native prairie or is in the restoration, or a zone where the two may mix. Saddle of western hill. Slope position: lower to middle.
Only location on field form says "30 meters north of pines."
Characterizes what can be found in the cattail marshes

Notes say "Between waypoints 105 and 106" and "from way 105 to dense willow I see no evidence of it not being natural." but also "odd assemblage, wonder if attempted prairie planting in too wet a spot. Reminds me of Wirock WMA."

Native prairie remnant on east side of WPA SW of parking area. Amorpha more abundant than is typical. In narrow  certain to be prairie with a 10 m buffer between here and road. Probably native throughout knoll to west but restoration boundary uncertain elsewhere. Would be B rank from sp. list if not for dirth of graminoids and over abundance of brome

place_name: Clinton Falls Dwarf Trout Lily SNA
remarks: Terrace forest dominated by Acer saccharinum, Celtis occidentalis, Tilia americana. Erythronium propullans dominates the herb layer. Releve placed to document long-tem flooding impacts along river. Vitis riparia vine dbh 9 cm. Metal stake is located in southwest corner of plot.

place_name: Clinton Falls Dwarf Trout Lily SNA
remarks: Terrace forest dominated by Tilia americana, Celtis occidentalis, Ulmus spp., Acer saccharinum. Erythronium propullans common. Debris dams and woody invasive removal debris present. Several wind damaged trees. Releve placed to document long-term flooding impacts along river. Permanent marker in northwest corner of plot.

place_name: Clinton Falls Dwarf Trout Lily SNA
remarks: Terrace forest dominated by Tilia americana, Ulmus spp., Celtis occidentalis. Herb layer dominated by Erythronium propullans. Releve placed to document long-term flooding impacts along river. Placed within highest quality area on point. Northeast corner near basswood clump.

One of the nicest small remnants surveyed in the county; adjoined by crop fields; neither grazed nor burned, but owners use it as a place to dump rocks. Not sure if enough acreage remains for Prairie Tax Exemption.

Apparently a former savanna, oaks are mature (DBH > 60-70 cm) and open grown, widely scattered. Prairie below is depauperate. Just above trail with SSw bearing. Extremely steep. Just upslope of very active seeps along Indan Creek. Uncertain of ranking as this is the first time I've really seen a bona fide example of this community and have some concerns it may be restoration.

To fit a releve of standard size into this narrow ravine and small remnant of good prairie it was necessary to include the entire slope from top to bottom, which accounts for the long species list and bimodal mix of dry prairie and wet species.
Prairie barely elevated between neighboring wetlands, mainly surrounded by restorations.
Edge of wetland, dry at time of visit, and highly hummocked (reason for low rank of community)
Exquisite meadow with leafy spurge coming right down to it on the west side!
extremely gentle slope in area mapped by WMA as dry prairie, but floristically extremely poor, probably D rank because so depauperate for such a site.
Could hardly find a single native species of grass in an area the size of a standard releve. Dominated by Poa and Brome
Wouthern-most slope west of lake, this area is nice the best mix of native grasses and forbs in SE7 portion of this site.
Plot is on a very bouldery hill very close to informal trail
Soil is gravelly reddish brown at surface. Releve is actually SSW facing

Southeastern end of this prairie north of road, but similar praie with steeper slopes appears to continue south of road in land owned by gravel pit. this set of slopes is the only remaining dry sand-gravel prairie located & surveyed by MBS in Lyon Co in 2006
Slight higher qualith lower slope than majority of NW facing prairie. Prairies to east infested with leafy spurge.
Releve on very very gentle rise between wetlands, too gentle to have real aspect and slope
Very near corner of S WMA at mouth of ravine
Approach to spur east of draw and south of wetland. No really conservative species. Apparently managed by mowing. Unclear if this is to conrol weedy species or is bringing them in.
East facing slope west of draw south of wetland
West facing slope east of wetland, one of best slopes observed on this visit, notebook says "at least B rank"

Forby wet meadow in putative seepage zone in wetland just N or where a trail comes to a dam like structure. Unclear whether this is entirely natural or whether it is partially an artifact of this structure.
Location is just a little lower than "midslope" on a fine-sandy rust colored soil.
Example of convex slope facing small draw. South of large wetland
Wet prairie on west side of site not far east of road, very rich.
Releve is on "knoll in far SW corner". This area is mapped as wet prairie, but I obviously thought it was more mesic from field notes. releve ranked slightly downward because of presence of weeds.
Grazed native prairie on the south end of a plowed U, west side, west facing slope above wetland, near CRP. Species list reflects grazing.
Could not find sideoats or little bluestem in a standard size releve on this slope. Quality of slopes degenerates going north. The Carduus has been treated and  is dead.
SW face of spur. Nodding Echinacia suggests slope may have been sprayed. Lookslike badly affects Ratibida but not Liatris. Very few Carduus to begin with.
Barely grazed slope, appears better than S facing slopes were.
Nice knoll. Prairie wraps all around it to fence line
Quality improves on slope in this area. Gazed pasture but apparently presently rested.

For an example of a very heavily grazed pasture that made it difficult to identify much that was too grazed down. This releve should never be used for classification. Apparently the first pasture used in season for last two years.
steep south facing slope in actively grazed pasture with very few native forb species persisting. Head of ravine of first pasture used in spring for last two seasons.
This is where the owner told me there were the "best flowers". Spur southeast of fen. Cattle not into this pasture until July in recent years.

Classic calcareous fen with lawn of Rhynchospora capillacea, located on NW facing slope in active pasture. Nearby fence diverts cattle from moving through this area, whereas other parts of same community are trampled. Marl deposits and Chara.
Steep convex slope in "home" pasture. Higher quality than less rugged and more extensive areas of pasture. Cattle not put into this pasture before July in recent years.
Releve placed to avoid planted trees in parts of this very good prairie ravine
North facing slope of ravine in fair quality, dominated by native grasses but no conservative forbs.
Steep narrow prairie slope dominated by natives. Although in the big picture this is not "upper" slope, within the Prairie Bank it is.
Very steep very narrow prairie slope facing stream above dam. this site is a prairie bank, but the remnants of prairie in this loop of stream are confined to steepest slopes

Releve is on upper slope at interface of native prairie slope and restoration. Is area with best native grass component on slope between two gentle draws and includes their edges. Aspects of species list make one wonder if this is actually "restored."  Perhaps interseeded?

Large shrub swamp between hardwood swamp and floodplain levee along St. Croix River. Some open patches in shrub cover are dominated by graminoids. surface with hummocky clumps (Carex). Peat substrate of unknown depth. No standing water in drought year.

Rolling topography with pockets of wetlands. Much dead and down Populus tremuloides & Abies balsamea. Several windthrow tree. Bog to the east. Large white pine? stumps in area.
WPt 019.
Sparse canopy (small thin crowns) most have fungus. Alot of coarse woody debris. Large boulders scattered. Ave dbh = 15- 40 cm dbh Fraxinus nigra.
Small stand between black spruce swamp and tamarack swamp. Broad shallow depression saturated with dead tamarack and paper birch. NPC at NW edge of its range.

Flat area with wetland nearby. Representative of jack pine with more spruce-fir. Several Jack pine snags. Fine sand light colored to 35 cm, iron colored below; difficult to get probe below 40 cm. Fine sand.
Adjacent to black ash. Very tall alder (up tp 20 ft.) with scattered openings.

Usual rich conifer swamp fo this oart of state. Located at base of Kettle River terrace. Close to interstate 35. Seepage peatland. Water in hollows ~ 25 cm deep. Fair amount of dead & downed spruce and paper birch.

Mixed pockets of Larix & Picea- quickly,& subtly grades to wet sand upland, FDn33c. Hummocks <= 12 in high dominated mainly by Sphagnum magellanicum around tree bases. Hollows very soupy with Sphagnum angustifolium primary moss. Peat ~30 cm over mucky/organic material (10 cm) then wet sand. Small area overall that releve represents. pH=4.5.

Spring fen channel, in area of slight opening.Area opens here a bit wider near head of spring fen. Adjacent are stunted black spruce trees w/ occasional Larix. Edges at channel have more Phragmites & Betula pumila. NE corner has small marly pool. Permanently marked SW corner w/ 5 ft pipe & NE corner w/ small 2 ft pipe. Notes: Using a Davis Peat Sampler, we were able to ascertain that the peat depth down to mineral soil (very gleyed clay) was ~3m in depth. MOSS NOTE: Drepanocladus aduncus- (falcate version) occ small raised flat hummocks & on higher hummocks w/ Sarracenia & Larix

Water at surface of mucky sedge peat. Taller Larix invading. Surrounded by Larix swamp. Peat depth ~1 m. to mineral (clay) soil. Lots of tall shrubs throughout- borderline shrub swamp. Indicative of several openings that range from circular upwellings to linear striations - all openings w/in larger tamarack swamp.

Area of bare soil- these areas dom by tiny Frax nigra seedlings. Most areas though dominated by thick thatch of Poa. Just on other side of berm that is along river. Releve in depression, then slopes up to Black Ash swamp ~5 ft slope. Most mosses on tree trunk bases & dead wood. CWD is comprised of lots of fine sticks to medium-sized boles that are down. Soil in upper 2 inches is loamy sand. Frax pen are largest trees. core taken: dates to ~1932. Ulmus dying, DBH 42 cm.

Stand represents a sparser canopied black ash dominated area. Water table below surface, soil on top 3 inches is organic w/ some sand (minor), >4 in clay soil mixed w organic. Grnd layer resembles wet meadow. Adjacent to river separated by berm.

Soil drainage class is somewhat excessively. Litter is primarily leaves with some needles. Humus consists of Oe and Oa in fungal mat. Top mineral horizon cocoa brown pH 5.5. Bottom horizon much coarser and lighter tan pH 5.0. Gravel pit along access forest service road 610 signifies really coarse soil. No fire or recent cutting seen within stand, though cutting occurs surrounding plus road runs through NPC. Overall, natural windthrow coarse woody debris and snags common, causing nice microtopography. Deer browse seen on red maple seedlings and saplings.

Plot located in more mesic conditions (drainage) compared to surrounding woodland. Creek flow from upper WFn55 from the north within 2m of plot location. Parts of plot with boulder voids where water collects. No recent cutting. Some deer browse. No fire evidence. Lots of boulders upon which white pine and other trees have grown. Some boulders on surface, many moss covered. Naturally occurring coarse woody debris. Soil pit dug in wet saddle - may skew actual drainage; more moderately well drained where majority of plot sits. Standing water only in hollows. Seepage seen 40 cm below surface. Soil - first horizon, pH 4.5 gray, dark brown; second horizon, pH 4.5 cocoa brown; third horizon, pH 5.0 gleyed on upslope side, tan where seepage has not reduced soil, cemented sandy loam.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Many moss-covered boulders on surface. Natural windthrow and coarse woody debris; Very old decayed large stumps seen. Windthrow gaps common with higher light infiltration. Deer browse pressure high. No signs of wildfire in a long time, though charcoal detected just above E-horizon and mixed with humus. Charcoal quite prevalent and mixed with organic and mineral soil. Dug to bedrock. Leached E-horizon gray (pH 4.0) and below resides a solid brown horizon (pH 4.5) just above bedrock. Sphagnum moss depression formed due to white pine tip up. Much of ground surface covered by needle litter and not plants.

Plot situated on slope where upper and lower flats are more poorly drained and exhibit WFn55 character. The plot is within 50 m of logging clearcut to the west. Stand with natural snags and coarse woody debris. Heavy deer browse though seedlings seen germinating on coarse woody debris. Pools and wet spots localized to drainages/channels running downslope and spaces among boulders. Fine roots in thick humus layer. Strangely, no gleying; seepage seen at pit bottom. Soil is moist and started to exhibit pooling at the bottom after 3 days of previous storms. Soil is surprisingly coarse but water flow must keep this continuously moist. Soil drainage keys to well but feels more moderately well. Top horizon black 'A' (pH 4.5) and bottom horizon above rock muted brown (pH 4.5). Bedrock likely not reached but rock prevented further digging past 33 cm.

No recent cutting. Many multi-stemmed silver maples. Reed canary grass on river levee to the east 60m of plot. Natural coarse woody debris and snags present throughout stand. Soil pit dug and hit water at 26 cm below surface, though one surface pool measured at 2 cm. A 3cm fine root layer occurs beneath litter, almost appearing as an Oe humus layer with the root mat binding silt loam mineral soil. Majority of profile a gray matrix silt loam but with slight orange specks of mottling. Thick roots all through soil pit.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Stand mapped as old growth by Superior NF. Natural snags and coarse woody debris. Deer browse high. No recent fire activity but decaying/burnt stump seen. Decent white pine sapling regeneration under canopy openings. Upper soil horizon black (pH 4.0) and with charcoal; black mineral soil likely due to incorporation of charcoal. Soil feels moist after heavy weekend rains. Very coarse sandy loam soil. Heavy root system encountered during soil pit excavation. Some large boulders encountered throughout stand.

Moose dung seen; no deer browse evidence, nice regeneration of knee-high cedar. No cutting evidence but some stumps noticeable. Soil layer below 44 cm and to depth of pit is black muck but mixed with est. 10-15% gritty sand particles - possibly contributing to slight nutrient enrichment. Hemic layer above filled with partially decomposed roots and wood not present in muck layer. Water in pit at 30 cm below surface; some sparse above-surface pools present. Black spruce density greater than cedar in canopy but cover similar. Overall regeneration of cedar better than that of black spruce.

Plot situated among FDn22 and FDn32 nearby with short-stature Pinus strobus and Quercus rubra on the plot's perimeter. Plot exhibits full sunlight. Many ants occupy plot. Plot surveyed a bit too late in season. Exposed rock 60% if including lichen-covered; 25% if counting truly exposed. Litter layer <1 cm, mostly none.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Part of stand marked for logging soon. Naturally occurring coarse woody debris and snags. Moderate-high deer browse impact on vegetation. No hydrologic impairments. Water 20 cm below surface. Litter layer <1 cm. Root mat in upper 5 cm of first soil horizon, combined with a mucky organic with underlying clay mineral horizon. All soil layers jet black.

Standing water only occurs in pools within hollows; mostly no standing water. Surface water pH measured twice at 4.3 and 4.8 readings at two different locations. Fibric peat in upper 10 cm followed by hemic peat. Dark brown, very abundant roots and decayed wood pieces in large chunks.

Oak species identification uncertain. Sun leaves are lobed deeply suggesting Q. ellipsoidalis, while lower shade leaves and seedlings appear more like Q. rubra. Stand likely pine dominated in past. Abundant collar sprouting from oaks when top-killed by wind. Naturally occurring coarse woody debris and snags. Moderate deer browse impact. Odd patches of bare soil with charcoal on surface. Charcoal also seen under humus layer and likely contributes to black color just below humus. Humus type almost a fibrous mor, but lower amorphous black color does exist. Top mineral horizon tan; bottom brown. Soil pH 4.5 for both horizons; coarse sandy loam. No recent cutting. Exposed rock common. Mid-slope NPC with more P. resinosa, P. banksiana, P. strobus, and Populus grandidentata; exposed rock faces with Heuchera richardsonii, Toxicodendron rydbergii, Juniperus communis, Dichanthelium xanthophysum, and Cardamine parviflora.

Dwarf mistletoe detected in stand with resulting black spruce mortality. Very cold water in soil pit; measured at 13 degrees Celsius. Some deer browse impact. Standing water only present in patchy pools. Surface water pH measured at two different locations.
Plot close to private boardwalk 80 m SSE. No standing water present.

Water found at 26 cm below surface. 4 cm of litter plus humus-like decaying leaves of past years before reaching hemic peat layer that is dark brown. No thick roots encountered in pit. Plot surrounded by wild rice beds near river and forested peatlands to the west.

Old stumps seen and have since been completely mossed over and spongy. Stump sprouts seen on some trees like paper birches. In soil pit, lots of decayed soft wood comprising hemic peat. Most of the fine roots found in upper 6 cm. Water found at 32 cm below surface. Litter confined to tree bases.

Wild rice marsh along Vermilion River. Open parts with more Brasenia schreberi, Nymphaea odorata, Potamogeton spp., Sagittaria rigida, Pontederia cordata occur in patches. Boat traffic can be a disruption along edges. Very soft sediment unconsolidated - gray brown slimy. Height of emergents measured from waterline as 0 cm. Floating treated as 0 cm. Submergent estimated as height above bottom substrate equal to 0 cm (i.e., since water depth is 84 cm, submergent heights ranged from 0 to 84 cm).

Plot purposely placed at toe slope transition from FDn32 to MHn44 drainage. Some cutting long ago with rotting stumps. Stand exhibits natural coarse woody debris and snags. No fire evidence but lightning scar on red maple. Deer browse moderate heavy. Humus with bottom blackish leaving residue when rubbed. Top mineral horizon is strikingly 'marly' white concretion of sandy clay loam and dry-brittle (pH 5.0). Lower horizon is tan and smoother in texture clay loam with very angular blocky soil structure (pH 4.5). Drainage uncertain. Feels moderately well drained as there is no mottling evidence within 34 cm; however, the muted colors of the top two horizons suggests saturation-induced reduction.

Heavy deer browse impact. No cutting or other anthropogenic disturbances other than old paint/chemical can seen in plot. Bare root/soil patches due to flooding or ice scour. Root mat 8 cm thick with crumb-like soil aggregates. Orange mottling 15 cm below surface. Three distinct horizons. First horizon crumbly dry aggregates bounded at the top by roots in dark gray color (pH 4.5); texture is almost a silt loam. Second horizon and start of semi-permeable layer is black-brown (pH 4.5). Last horizon is heavily mottled gray-tan (pH 4.5). Note: difficult to distinguish between black and green ash seedlings/saplings.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Part of plot is in a little flat saddle where some wet-mesic species occur; overstory becomes more dominated by trembling aspen - possibly FDn43. Majority of plot on shallow soil FDn32a. Slope is steepest at 301 degrees but the local crest top also slopes gently to the south. Fungal mycelia througout humus layer. First horizon appears to be leached 'E' that is gray-white (pH 4.0). Second horizon 'B' that is lightly orange-tan (pH 4.5). Last horizon khaki tan (pH 4.5). Roots and cobbles hindered digging deeper. Thick needle layer hasn't been burned in a long time; no evidence of recent fire.

No recent cutting; old growth possibly. Natural canopy breakup through wind disturbance - coarse woody debris and snags prevalent within stand. Nurse logs available for observed yellow birch germination. No recent fire. Some parts of stand with heavily wormed bare soil, especially SW part. Worm castings and middens very evident in some patches. At least two different species of worms seen. Deer browse especially heavy on mountain maple. Soil drainage keyed to somewhat poorly, but feels more moderately well. Subtle orange mottles at 34 cm below surface. Fine plant roots and humus present in soil but Oe/Oa made up of mostly needles and not deciduous litter. Litter depth 0.5 cm. No gray matrix but subtle mottling seen at 34 cm. Soil pH 4.5 among all horizons. First horizon black, second leached gray, third tan brown, fourth cemented and khaki colored.

No recent cutting seen. Not many snags or coarse woody debris seen. Plot purposely placed with cedar overstory component but majority of stand generally without cedar. Water found 17 cm below surface. Top organic layer is almost muck and is darker black and greasier than the bottom organic layer which has more whole wood pieces and is more hemic brown-black. Many graminoids appear lax or flattened from early-season high water. Wildlife trail runs through plot and is muckier, wetter, more compacted. NPC Type uncertain; has attributes of both FPn82a and FPn82b. Would lean towards latter.

Drainage class estimated. Possible redox features below 48 cm. Soil profile with abundant roots, medium-coarse on top horizon. Charcoal flakes in upper horizon which may contribute to chocolate brown color (pH 4.0). Iron flecks in lower horizon in beige matrix - not assumed to be mottling, however (pH 4.5). Abundant snags and coarse woody debris. Canopy break up and large trees suggests old growth condition. No cut stumps. Abundant large canopy gaps due to tree fall. Varying decay classes of logs. Some pit and mound topography. Strong deer browse pressure on Corylus. Exposed boulders present.

Nice fungal mycelia throughout humus. Bedrock hit at 10 cm below surface. Stand is rocky with boulders on surface. Foot trail within 10 m of plot on west boundary. Many multi-stemmed red maples in understory and overstory. A few cut logs seen; appears to be small-diameter balsam fir. Lone mineral horizon with recorded pH of 4.0. Forgot to record aspect and slope percent in the field; aspect derived from LIDAR contours. Slope was on toe; therefore, at most, slope percent is 3%.

Plot occupies a narrow zone between bedrock-controlled fire dependent community upslope and wet forest WFn55/64 plus near-river community downslope. Abundant deer browse on mountain maple. Good amount of heavily decayed coarse woody debris, but no large snags - only some top-killed understory trees. Soil drainage keys to poorly, but it is more appropriate somewhat poorly. Top 'A' soil horizon mixed with organic humus and black. Second horizon mottled (pH 4.75). At 28 cm, gray matrix dominates without mottling (pH 4.5).

Plot located in saddle; surrounding native plant community FDn32. Rockier knobs to the north and southwest. Saddle gradient generally about 3%. Slopes leading up to woodlands range from 8% on the low slope to 50% on the midslopes. No cut stumps but lots of old, large fallen trees snapped at the base, mostly pines and up to 48 cm in diameter. Large coarse woody debris greatly decayed. Snags of white spruce abundant or about to die. Soil drainage class estimated. Top black 'A' horizon (pH 6.5), middle white-gray 'E' (pH 5.5), and bottom gray-brown with tinge of orange but no mottling (pH 4.5). Mottling expected at deeper depths. Classification favors MHn44 due to ground layer; however,  overstory composition and proximity to fire-dependent communities leads me to retain FDn43 call.

Community changes to FDn43b1 downslope. Depth to bedrock not reached but stones are very shallow and abundant. Naturally occurring coarse woody debris common, mostly aspen. Wind-snapped aspen snags also common. Large red pine observed to the east of plot 15 m. Lots of bigtooth aspen suckering. Very stony/cobbly soil; cobbles present with stones in both horizons. Mostly a black-gray 'A' horizon but a copper brown 'B' horizon resides below. Soil pH 5.0. Soil is wormed with abundant castings. No Oa layer but still some fine roots present; no middens found.

Plot chosen to rep new NPC; veg assoc w/small, "ephemeral pool", "vernal pool","temporary pool" in mesic sugar maple forest (MHn45c) setting. Plot area equal to the max water-filled area. Vascular plants mostly emergent from pool margin and/or small raised areas of mineral soil or decaying, saturated CWD. Callitriche only sp growing as aquatic. Pool is densely shaded by adjacent canopy A. saccharum. Set in slight depression of one of several terraces on S-facing slope. Connected by first order stream to other pools below during spring and high precip events, most if not all of these draw down before July. Three med to large saturated tree boles (B. papy, A. sacc) in various states of decay are nurseries for Sorbus, R. idaeus, Pica glauca in addition to forbs/grams seen on margin. Cobbles/stones common in plot & surrounding forest substrate.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality, natural origin wet forest NPC associated with north central Lac La Croix Bedrock Complex LTA, in settings influenced by Lake Agassiz including this one: area of level terrain between upland ridge and lake. This WFn expression is not well-documented or described in NPC classification 2.0. This expression more spp rich and structurally complex than narrow bands of WFn-like NPC associated with lake shores - with direct lake water influence - in this LTA. This setting behind band of rocky shore community and ecotonal zone. Soil observed may be clay loam vs slit clay loam.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality, fire-dependent NPC, natural origin in 1894, in one typical setting in Lac La Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. A few recent P. mariana blowdown across one corner of plot. Moderate amount of CWD. No mistletoe observed. Substrate moist, grey to red shift.

Plot chosen to represent one expression of veg development continuum of possible new NPC, boulder pavement NPC. Standing water pools occas visible btwn angular boulders/stones; most interstitial spaces are moist organics above any pool, and are primary substrate for vascular plants. Crustose and fruiticose lichens ubiquitous on exposed rocks. More continuous cover of veg mat and complex veg structure i.e. more advanced dev stage of same NPC at margins.Only one of the coll lichen spp was on the MNTaxa list. Others IDed = Cladonia mitis, Lepraria cf neglecta, Umbilicaria deusta, Umbilicaria muhlenbergii, Xanthoparmelia stenophylla.This plot/expression in the middle of the NPC continuum, which ranges from well-exposed stones and boulders w/+/-cryptogram cover to boulder, stones w/bryo/org mat cover w/conifer or mixed coni/deci dom canopy.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality, natural origin (1864) NPC in one typical setting w/in the Lac La Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Abundant mod to large CWD and Populus trem snags. Old growth stage w/broken canopy as P. trem are senescent. No charcoal observed in limited search. Many bryo spp on logs and rocks. Small (less than 1.5 m wide) intermittent stream channel runs through plot. Spp in stream channel and on adjacent rock outcrop were not included in the spp list. Percent of exposed rock does not include stream channel or outcrop.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality, natural origin (1987) fire-dependent community on island in Lac La Croix, 28 years post-fire. Previous origin dates for island veg 1759 and 1681 per Heinselman. Two large pit/mound elements. Moderate amount of large CWD, typically with charred roots, branches and one side of bole. Well-decayed charred stumps (not cut). Acer and Betula are not coppice. A few beaver cut Populus stumps. Pleurozium schreberi on small areas of exposed rock. FDn43c patch nearby. UTM = SE corner of plot.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality, natural origin MHn community in advanced growth stage, not well-described in classification 2.0. In small valley between bedrock-controlled features. Within upland patch burned in 1988. Cobble/stone stream channel less ~1 meter wide runs through plot. Located upslope from WFn55 and downslope from beaver infl stream segment, (both low gradient), plot in steeper gradient. B. alleg up to 40cm dbh from canopy. Spp assoc w/stream bed not included in plot spp composition. Exposed rock of strambed not incl in % exposed rock. UTM = mid-point of SE side

Plot chosen to represent high-quality community not well described in NPC classification 2.0. This plot in typical setting for this NPC in Lac LA Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Water moving thru slowly west via multiple sm channels connecting pools. 30% of plot area is muck-bottom pools w/standing water. Located in narrow, low gradient drain of no more than 6% slope overall. Some portions including plot less than that. Btwn bedrock controlled hills along low-gradient segment of stream btwn higher gradient segments. Abundant evidence of iron-fixing bacteria in pools and channels.UTM=NW corner of plot

Plot chosen to represent high-quality, natural origin community in typical setting in the LAc La Croix Brock Complex LTA. Soil present only in isolated pockets. Bryo-covered bedrock is dominant substrate. Litter layer minimal and discontinuous. Humus depth varies from 0-3cm. Most expose brock is lichen-covered. Origin of NPC in 1875 (Heinselman). CWD present but minimal.UTM = plot center.

Plot chosen to represent natural origin (1875) high-quality community. Canopy Pop trem and Pinus bank CWD abundant. Boulders at surface, tops exposed; irregular microtopography. Sandy loam soil at least 18 cm deep in pockets, grey in upper horizon. UTM = center of plot.

Plot chosen to represent one expression of veg development at late end of continuum of possible "boulder pavement" NPC. Sphagnum and other mosses cover boulder substrate. Standing water in pools btwn boulders occasionally visible. Small area of drier conditions dev @ tree bases. All spp listed grow from Sphag, a subset of these also grow in drier organic substrate of drier area.Some P. bank and P. mari DD w/in plot. Peat depth variable, up to 15cm. Abundant CWD.UTM=plot center

Plot chosen to represent high-quality community of bedrock lakeshore found in Lac La Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Not well-described in classification 2.0. Plot in area with evidence of temporary standing water from precip and/or higher lake levels. Approx. 18cm above mapped lake elevation. Setting is depression of variable depth (0-40+cm) in bedrock of small peninsula of island. At least 4 spp of mosses,one or two of which are liverworts.UTM = SW corner of plot

Plot chosen to represent high-quality community found on lakeshore not well-documented/described in classification 2.2. On narrow neck of long peninsula. Located above wave wash/ice push zone and below woodland on adjacent crest of slope. About 1/2 of plot exposed gravel/sand w/some veg or bedrock exposed but exposed vs covered by veg mat/roots. Crustose lichens abundant on exposed brock and cobbles. Zero to at least 13 cm to brock. Stones and cobbles 7-54cm diameter numerous over brock in mosaic w/veg mat patches. UTM=plot center.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality exmple of this NPC in northwestern Lac La Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Upslope and adjacent to WFn55. Abundant CWD of many diameters. Bryophyte cover high on CWD. Within FDn43 and/or 33 matrix with natural origin date of 1864.UTM = plot center.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality fire-dependent community in typical setting in Lac La Croix Bedrock Complex LTA. Micro-photography variable; not level; bedrock very close to surface; thin soil typical. Some lower oak branches dead from suppression. Large CWD infrequent. Low to moderate amount of small dbh CWD. Mature Pinus strobus outside plot on level terrain of ridge top in FDn33a. Avg depth to bedrock estimated. UTM = plot center.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality fire-dependent community of natural origin (1759 (Heinselman)or earlier). No charcoal found. Humus is up to 20cm deep under large supercanopy Pinus strobus. Abundant Taxus canadensis extends far beyond plot to at least one hectare. Plot in patch in fire-protected setting on island in Lac La Croix i.e. WFn community on two sides and lake on two. Heavy needle litter over most of plot. High degree of pit and mound microtopography. Two 84cm dbh P.strobus 30+m tall w/out fire scars. Lass than 1% exposed rock.UTM=NW corner of plot.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality natural origin community on Sand Island in Lac La Croix. Pools (dry on this date) are 50-75% of the plot area. Leafy liverworts abundant on pool bottoms. Bryophytes(Sphagnum and leafy liverworts) abundant including on Fraxinus boles. CWD, all diameters, is abundant, some saturated. Some portions of WFn patch outside plot with higher frequency of Betula alleghaniensis and Taxus canadensis.UTM = plot center
Mesic prairie dominated by Andropgon gerardii and Panicum virgatum. Site has long history of haying.  The releve plot is near the prairie boundary, adjacent to crop field.
Early season releve in EWR- owned portion of Lost Lake Peatland SNA. Taken in transition between upland FPn system and alder swamp. A lot of recent rain; very wet.

Wet cedar forest typical of SNA and stands to the south. Structure and CWD common to old cedar forests. Most species not bloomed yet. Ground broken with many shallow pools. Sphagnum or moss covered most surfaces. Some tip-ups and recent blow down.

CWD large to small, common, all decay stage. Deer browse common. Depressions hold water seasonally. 1/8mi to St. Louis river. No signs of flooding. Scattered snags common. No fire scars of cut stumps observed. Possibly wormed.

Notes: BWC wypt. 0148.

Soils, litter type: "leaves, needles"

Local high point. Scattered, thinly covered bedrock. Small to med. CWD common - all decay stages. Sm-med. snags scattered and common. Super canopy conifers scattered throughout. No cut stumps or fire scars observed. West of St. Louis River (~1/4 mi.) Deer browse common. Seemingly worm free.

BWC wpt # 147
Early season releve. Upland portion of Lost Lake Peatland SNA, south of Lost Lake and west of the entrance road. Some blowdown and gaps, likely caused by spruce budworm outbreaks.

Old Red Pine - White Pine Woodland on shallow soils. Patch encompasses most of the NW/SE running hill above Nigh Creek. Large, coarse woody debris is light - moderate. Widely scattered stumps (unsure if cut or not). Two large, white pine snags in plot (7m & 14m heights). Scattered boulders on surface (small-medium). No charcoal in soil. No fire scars. Small bedrock knob to west is FDn22a.

Black Spruce Woodland. Well developed microtopography. Moderate, large down logs on surface and buried under moss. Soils shallow to bedrock, with patchy, thin peat development under sphagnum in low spots. Approximately 50% of canopy black spruce is dying (likely as a result of spruce budworm). No evidence of Arceuthobium pusillum. White pine seedlings scattered throughout. Healthy Populus tremuloides (~14cm dbh) scattered throughout. Scattered wet hollows (unvegetated). Small bedrock openings nearby. White pine regeneration may survive beyond black spruce canopy.

Bedrock Shrubland above Pauline Lake. Small patches of the NPC occur regularly along the ridges surrounding the lake and throughout the Astrid MBS Site. Most tree species with multiple stems and are stunted/shrubby. Cedar waxwings stopped over twice during releve sampling.

Black spruce bog. Well-developed microtopography. Fairly diverse moss layer, with moss species co-dominant. Arceuthobium pusilum light. No strong evidence of spruce budworm. Large, downed logs moderate-sized as expected, and well integrated into moss and peat layers.Diameters of standing trees range from 10-23cm, with multi-layered regeneration. No evidence of fire. Scattered Larix laricina within NPC. Beckie Prange (UMN) assisted with releve.

White Pine-Red Pine Forest. Moderate amount of large downed logs, and fairly well-developed microtopography. Scattered snags and natural (not cut) stumps are low to the ground and add to microtopography. Scattered, medium-large boulders in plot. Canopy of NPC patch (as in plot)is a fairly co-dominant mix of Pinus strobus and Pinus resinosa of various diameters. Pines are also fairly well represented in the subcanopy/shrub layers (light-moderate). Dead trees are broken off low to ground. Noted 1 large cut stump in plot. No evidence of fire (no fire scars or charcoal in soils). Top 2 cm of mineral soil is gleyed.

Somewhat atypical Poor Black Spruce Swamp, with occasional jack pine in the canopy and a fair number of large, dead and down jack pine logs (mostly ~22cm dbh)on the surface. No evidence of fire. Microtopography is well developed, with abundant downed logs on the surface. Hit rock at 26cm in two places when getting peat depth. This patch is a higher quality example of the NPC along the Range River, between Low and Range Lakes. Canopy jack pine is dying or dead in many areas along the river in this stretch. Riparian corridor may have experienced significant change in hydrology. Many high snags along the river and in surrounding NPCs suggest that canopy trees snapped off in wind event (1999 blowdown?).  The landscape inland of the riparian corridor experienced large-scale logging ~20-50 years ago. Surrounding woodlands often contain dense Alnus viridis. Shore fen with sometimes dense Alnus incana. Beckie Prange (UMN)assisted with this releve.

Graminoid Poor Fen Basin adjacent to peatland pond. No graminoid lawns. Adjacent Poor Black Spruce Swamp (APn81a)is moderately impacted by Arceuthobium pusilum. No obvious drainageways, although north extension and south boundary extend nearly to lake shore. Abundant, lightly used, wildlife trails in surrounding poor black spruce swamp. Jenna Pollard assisted with this releve.

Low Shrub Poor Fen. Small patch between steep, sandy-gravelly-bouldery Red Pine-White Pine Woodland ridges, that experienced a prescribed burn (underburn) in 2005. Canopy sparse. Fen is very dry. Peat is likely shallow. Canopy and seedling layer of fen, with both peatland and upland tree species (e.g white pine). Jenna Pollard assisted with this releve.

Red Pine-White Pine Woodland on south-facing slope of sandy-gravelly-bouldery ridge.This NPC patch is representative of the other ridges in this concentrated area of rugged topography. Area was part of the 1999 blowdown and underwent a patchy prescribed burn (underburn) in 2005. Heinselman's BWCAW disturbance maps indicate that the area was largely cut over @1900.White pine/red pine regeneration is moderate. There is a moderate-abundant amount of large downed logs (resulting from 1999 blowdown, where Rx burn skipped. Jenna Pollard assisted with releve.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Red Pine-White Pine Woodland. Charcoal fragments at the base of the humus layer (just above mineral soil). Heinselman map indicates that landscape was "largely cut over" @1900. May have regenerated from post-logging era fire. Coarse fragments are flat (~2cm thick/7cm diam)and break easily (contain quartz). No fire scars on standing trees or stumps. Microtopography fairly well-developed. Large downed logs moderate. Jenna Pollard assisted with this releve.

Aspen-Birch Spruce-Fir Forest. Plot was a fairly rapid assessment to capture condition of forest between Little Trout Lake and North Arm of Trout Lake, and more generally, the matrix forest in the Trout Lake Site. No soils data or tree diameters collected. Moose sign along portage in this area, otherwise deer sign predominates. Pre-blowdown canopy was primarily Populus tremuloides, Populus grandidentata, Picea glauca, Betula papyrifera (~18cm dbh). Jenna Pollard assisted with this releve.

Black Spruce Bog. Very large, homogenous NPC. No evidence of cutting. Well-developed microtopography. Very few large, down logs on the surface. Canopy trees overall uniform in dhb from 6-12cm dbh. Minor amounts of Arceuthobium pusilum evidence/damage. Small group of boreal chickadees (4-5), plus 1 kinglet, were observed within plot. Wildlife trails (likely moose) occasional. Eric Ogdahl assisted with this releve.

Poor Black Spruce Swamp. Appears to be transitioning slowly to upland conifer composition. Higher cover of upland conifer species (also in higher height class) than usually found in acid peatlands. Wildlife trails occasional throughout. Black spruce and tamarack appear mildly stressed, with dead needles throughout tree.White pine also stressed a bit with shorter needles. Leatherleaf has died in patches with denser canopy cover (mostly bare ground with needle cover 1-2 cm deep). Deer pellets in dense canopy areas. Eric Ogdahl assisted with releve.

Red Pine-White Pine Woodland. Community very densely shrubby, with trees and shrubs mostly under 10m height. Many areas within patch with little canopy in the 10-20m height class. Some Acer spicatum in the 5-6 cm dbh range.  Portage trail bisects plot, but is narrow, with very little edge effect. Shallow to bedrock. No charcoal. Many fine roots in humus. Multiple years' leaves on surface. Eric Ogdahl assisted with releve.

Red Pine-White Woodland. Island with high quality example of woodland condition prior to early logging (@1900). Moderate amount of large downed logs. Pine warbler singing in plot. NPC as a whole , needle covered, with little herbaceous cover. Other patches with dense shrub layer. Charcoal at top of mineral layer. Humus layer very deep (~21cm). No evidence of cutting. White pine canopy tree (larger dbh) with lightning strike. NPC of this type and quality is rare in the area. Eric Ogdahl assisted with releve.

Red Pine-White Pine Woodland (old growth). Moderate large down logs and microtopography.Charcoal remnants on downed logs. No evidence of cutting. Rotted stumps with their associated downed logs are evident. Boulders at surface are infrequent. White pine seedlings are common. High numbers of Epigea repens than expected (<5% cover). Needle-covered ground 25-50%. Red squirrel holes fairly common. Charcoal fragments at top of mineral soils layer. No evidence of worms. Deep loamy sand.

Low Shrub Poor Fen. Adjacent to small peatland pond. Embedded in a mostly upland landscape. Narrow band of graminoid shore fen along southern shoreline. NPC is somewhat atypical in that it includes many, evenly distributed white pine saplings, mostly ~2m height. Katie Frerker (SNF) assisted with releve.

White Pine-Red Pine Forest.  NPC likely planted (CCC) or recovered naturally from turn-of-century logging. Scattered cut stumps suggest more recent thinning. Light to moderate microtopogrophy. Light-moderate large, down logs, with some recent recruitment (large dbh white pine). High potential for recovery/restoration of old growth characteristics. Deer pellets in patch. Deer browsing on Acer spicatum. No evidence of worms. Charcoal in soil at humus/mineral soil boundary. Katie Frerker (SNF) assisted with releve.
