Typical of the most diverse zone (~1 acre) in a 10-acre seepage meadow complex along Rush Creek. Gradual slope on fairly broad valley bottomland between steep 320-foot bluffs. Elevation changes ~3 feet (higher) to north near the base of the south-facing bluff, and +4 feet lower southward. Wet (saturated) and moderately quaky mucky organics over clay. Thick thatch over the muck. Grades to zones dominated by Carex trichocarpa and areas with less herbaceous diversity. Several springs and seepage outflow streams occur in the larger wet meadow complex. Adjacent ownership to west is heavily grazed.

Atop level to gently undulating 50-foot high bedrock ridge above the eastern portion of Ojibway Lake. Part of a mature 10-acre patch of pine-dominated woodland. Trees +/- even-aged, mostly 30-42cm DBH occasionally to 48cm. Snags uncommon. No cut stumps. Fairly shallow (~25cm) silty loamy soil over basaltic (greenstone) bedrock. Edge of plot 15 meters from top of a steep, 50-foot, south-facing shoreline slope. Some very old metal (junk) present in plot. Old stone fire-ring near edge of plot.

Typical of a larger opening in sparse- to patchy-canopied jack pine woodland atop a 150-foot high bedrock knoll between Saturday and Sunday Bays, Crooked Lake. Plot is located at the highest point of the knoll, not far from the top of a steep southeasterly-facing slope. 70% of plot is exposed, rounded, little-fractured granite; shallow detrital soil (<5 cm deep) elsewhere. Lichens cover ~85% of the exposed bedrock, mosses cover ~10%. No invasive hawkweeds! Grades to denser jack pine-white pine woodland with few (or no) outcrops on gradual to moderately steep north- to west-facing upper slopes. Photos of plot taken by Dan and I. Sorbus is moose-browsed; old moose pellets in plot (~2-3 yrs old?)

Typical of, and centrally located in, a ~2.5-acre zone of rich sedge fen in the back of a small bay and at the mouth of a small drainage into Saturday Bay, Crooked Lake. This is the wettest zone of a ~35-acre peatland here; grades to shrub shore fen, then to poor fen and stunted spruce-tamrack poor conifer swamp. Plot ~25 meters both from the lake and from the shrub shore fen zone. Deep sedge peat, fibric, saturated, >40 cm deep. This zone is flooded earlier in the season (annually). Circular patches of Chamaedaphne occur sporadically in parts of this zone. Dan took photos of plot and vicinity.

Plot captures the +/- level top of a small, low, bedrock island in Saturday Bay, Crooked Lake. The granite islet is ~1/4-acre in size and rises ~4 feet above lake level. Substrate in plot varies from bare bedrock to several inches of detrital organic soil over rock. One small boulder occurs in plot. Plot captures the zone just above most wave action. Grades to slightly lower zones (nearer to lake level) with Myrica gale at the water's edge, then Carex vesicaria and C. lasiocarpa in shallow water (littoral zone). A few small trees occur on the islet. Photos taken by Dan and I. This is one of only ~six places where I've seen Vaccinium macrocarpon in a bedrock lakeshore setting to date (only observed on Basswood, Crooked, and Iron Lakes).

place_name: Saturday Bay South, Crooked Lake - BWCAW
remarks: Typical of rather extensive floating-leaved - emergent marsh along the lowermost one mile reach of Sinneeg Creek, on the southeast side of Saturday Bay, Crooked Lake. Along a slack-water flowage that is at the elevation of Saturday Bay. Plot captures the zone between the more open central "channel" and a somewhat narrower zone of Eleocharis palustris toward the upland. Water depth in the plot is ~24 inches. Soft unconsolidated organic substrate ~3-8 inches deep, over firm muck/clay. Water level down ~12 inches from early season high. A fairly narrow sedge meadow dominated by Carex utriculata and C. lasiocarpa borders the upland on the edge of the flowage here (immediately "inland" of the Eleocharis palustris zone). Dan took photos of plot and setting. (Height strata are measured from surface of the lake.)

place_name: Saturday Bay South, Crooked Lake - BWCAW
remarks: Typical of the dominant zone in a fairly large (10-acre) beaver meadow along a small drainage south of Saturday Bay, Crooked Lake. Plot more or less centrally located in a somewhat linear wetland, ~30 meters from eastern upland and ~70 meters from western upland. Widely scattered young Larix occurs throughout the meadow. Quite quaky saturated peat, ankle-deep water in foot tracks. Grades to a zone dominated by Calamagrostis candensis (covers 15% of the meadow). Dan took photos of the plot and setting.

place_name: Saturday Bay South / Bungee Creek - BWCAW
remarks: Plot includes the top and gradual upper slopes of a low, rounded bedrock knoll along the lower reaches of Bunggee Creek, south of Saturday Bay, Crooked Lake. Slope varies from level to 3 degrees, all compass aspects are present in the plot. Trees mature; Pinus banksiana 20-38cm DBH, mode 25-30cm; Picea mariana to 28cm. No stumps. Few snags. Lots of CWD- large boles frequent. Soil: 2cm litter, 5cm humus; rocky sandy-silt to 25+cm deep. Granitic bedrock at ~30cm deep, 1% of plot is exposed, moss-covered bedrock. Occasional surface boulders present.

place_name: Saturday Bay South, Crooked Lake - BWCAW
remarks: Typical of ~1/2-acre zone near a tiny (0.05-acre) bog pond in 60-acre peatland south of Sunday Bay, Crooked Lake. Plot centrally located in zone, ~16 meters from north end of the pond, ~15 meters from edge of this zone elsewhere. Deep and rather firm saturated peat. Ankle deep water in foot tracks. Ericads in plot are low-statured. Grades outward to spruce bog (releve A788 done ~90 meters to the southwest), and to graminoid fen nearer the pond (releves A943, A944). Photos taken of plot, adjacent zones, setting, etc. by Dan Wovcha.

place_name: Sunday Bay South, Crooked Lake - BWCAW
remarks: Typical of ~90% of this 60-acre peatland in large bedrock hollow south of Sunday Bay, Crooked Lake. Trees somewhat stunted, 4-12cm DBH, mode ~7cm. Snags uncommon. No stumps. CWD rather sparse. Deep peat, firm. Plot located ~75 meters from a tiny bog pond and ~90 meters from the nearest upland margin (to south-southwest). Grades to poor fen near the pond (see releves A787, A944, A943).

place_name: Sunday Bay South, Crooked Lake - BWCAW
remarks: Typical of a large patch of mature conifer woodland on bedrock ridge south of Sunday Bay, Crooked Lake. Frequent snags (mostly large jack pine), frequent large CWD- all decay stages. No stumps. Never logged. Stand origin 1894 (Heinselmann). Slope varies from level to ~6 degrees, aspect south-southeast. Soil 2cm litter (needles and leaves), 4cm humus, very fine (sandy-) silt >30cm deep, few stones, well-sorted. Upper 2cm grey, below 2cm orangish-tan. ~10cm from top of leaf litter to mineral soil. No exposed bedrock in or near plot. Dan Wovcha took photos of plot and vicinity.

Typical of shallow-to-bedrock expression of a heterogeneous, several hundred-acre patch of jack pine-black spruce woodland on broad bedrock ridge between Friday and Saturday Bays, Crooked Lake. Mature stand, origin 1894 (Heinselmann). Never logged. Lots of CWD- representative of canopy trees. 25% of plot is exposed granite or bedrock covered by thick moss carpets. Elsewhere soil up to ~30cm deep. Occasional surface boulders. Soil is (very fine sandy-) silt. Thick humus. Tree tally and diameters stored in old growth database (see forest age plot #2 data). A 48cm DBH Populus tremuloides just outside plot. This releve was done in same spot as plot #2 (1/15-acre) of a six plot series of forest age / old growth plots in this patch of FDn32c. This plot has low species richness compared to other plots this FDn32c patch. Releves A791, A792, A793 are also located at forest age plots in this patch. Dan Wovcha took photos.

Typical of richer areas in a heterogeneous, several hundred-acre patch of mature jack pine-black spruce woodland on broad bedrock ridge between Friday and Saturday Bays, Crooked Lake. Stand origin 1894 (Heinselmann). Primary forest (never logged). Lots of CWD- typical of canopy species, all decay stages. Tree tally, DBH, and age data stored in old growth database. (Fine sandy-) silt with stones. ~1cm of litter (needles and leaves). 5-6cm of humus. Small Sphagnum colony in shallow depression- similar small Sphagnum patches are sporadic in larger upland patch. Releve A791 corresponds to plot #3 of forest age / old growth methodology (six forest age plots done in this NPC patch). Species richenss is intermediate here compared to 3 other releves done this FDn32c patch (A790, A792, A793). Dan Wovcha took photos of plot.

Typical of richest zones in a heterogeneous several hundred-acre patch of jack pine-black spruce woodland on broad bedrock ridge between Friday and Saturday Bays, Crooked Lake. Plot on gradual, lower-mid-slope, southeast aspect. Primary forest, never logged. Stand origin: 1894 (Heinselmann). Lots of large CWD. Fine sandy-silt with stones; thick humus. 1cm of litter (needles and leaves). 4cm of humus. Age, tree tally, DBH, and CWD data stored in the old growth database (plot #4). Small granitic outcrops nearby (upslope). Small colonies of Sphagnum sporadic in small hollows and moister spots throughout the larger FDn32c patch. Releve A792 corresponds to plot #4 of six plots done for forest age / old growth methodology. Three other releves were done in this FDn32c patch (A790, A791, A793). This releve has the highest species richness of the four releves done in this FDn32c patch. Dan Wovcha took photos here.

Typical of low species richness zones near bedrock outcrops in a heterogeneous several hundred-acre patch of primary forest (black spruce-jack pine woodland) on broad ridge between Friday and Saturday Bays, Crooked Lake. Never logged. Stand origin 1894 (Heinselmann). Tree tally, DBH, age, and CWD data stored in old growth database (plot #6 of six old growth methodology plots this patch). Frequent CWD, large boles. Occasional snags. Thick moss here over stony sandy silt and granitic bedrock which is exposed in plot (1% of plot). Litter (needles and leaves) is very sparse and patchy. Thick humus. Large chunks of charcoal at surface of mineral soil. Species richness is the lowest of four releves done in this FDn32c patch (other releves this patch are A790, A791, A792).

Plot captures much of a relatively narrow zone of old growth (primary forest) ash bordering the back of a deep bay in Sunday Bay, Crooked Lake. Ash trees 40-55cm DBH, buttress-rooted. Elevation is 1-2 feet above lake level, just above the early season high mark, appears to be flooded by wave action in spring. Upland rises gently to south where vegetation quickly grades to FDn32/43. Substrate is moist to wet grey clay (with sand/gravel particles); ~3cm deep mucky cap, 3cm deep humus. Water in soil pit at 12cm deep. Long sides of plot are parallel to the lake shore. Setting is at the mouth of an ephemeral drainage, near the landing of the old, overgrown (essentially lost) portage trail to Sunday Lake. Several photos of plot taken (low light conditions).

Typical of a fairly large zone (1.5 acres) of subtle depressional graminoid fen in broad poor fen on the southeastern shore of Ritual Lake. Plot ~50 meters from the lake and 30 meters from the upland, in zone that is wetter than the surrounding poor fen. Deep quaky saturated peat; water 8 cm deep in foot tracks. Vegetation is quite low-statured (stunted). Plot includes a few low Sphagnum hummocks which are more characteristic of the much broader surrounding poor fen. No old woody remains of any size on surface or in soil pit. Mike took photos of the plot and setting.

place_name: Michaelson Farm WMA - Bend in the River Park
remarks: Typical of a small (~1/2-acre) alluvial marsh along a small backwater flowage (slough) on the Mississippi River floodplain south of Rice. River is +/- free-flowing this reach. Marsh is ~16 meters wide and parallels the +/- linear flowage for 50+ meters; a somewhat narrower marsh zone occurs on the opposite side of the narrow seepage-enhanced flowage. Substrate is deep saturated silty-muck; upper 15-20 cm is peaty-muck. Ankle-deep water present in foot tracks. Grades to a narrower and wetter zone of Zizania palustris and Scirpus validus at the edge of the flowage channel; and to floodplain forest on slightly higher elevation nearby. No invasive plants here! Photos of plot and setting taken.

place_name: Michaelson Farm WMA - Bend in the River Park
remarks: Typical of higher quality areas in 40-acre patch of floodplain forest along +/- free-flowing stretch of the Mississippi River south of Rice. Plot placed on highest ground here between small backwater sloughs (flood channels). Mature patch, uneven-aged; trees 40-60cm DBH (75cm nearby). CWD rather sparse. No flooding debris piles here. Moist organic clayey-silt. Plot inundated in spring,  <2 feet above present elevation of nearby river. Recent buckthorn removal this general area includes some buckthorn cutting in plot.

Plot encompasses much of what is a somewhat ecotonal wet aspen zone on small upland rise in large wetland complex, on outwash plain. Plot is subtly higher elevation (<6 inches) than the adjacent sedge meadow (5 meters from outer edge of plot.) Inland edge of plot near a 12-inch elevation rise that supports pin oak-aspen woodland (FDs37). Soil is moist sand with shallow darker surface horizon. Very little litter or humus. Stand is uneven-aged, bi-modal; trees 8-42 cm DBH, two cohorts: 35-42cm and 8-20cm. Similar "ecotonal" zones in vicinity grade to basswood and oak on higher elevation rises. Wet aspen forest (WFs55) is much less common in this vicinity (MBS Site 280) than the NPC mapping suggests.

Typical of, and centrally located on, a fairly large sandbar on the downstream end of Graham's Island, along a free flowing reach of the Mississippi River. Setting is ~12-18 inches above the present river level; the entire sandbar is inundated in spring and during other high water periods. Level to gently sloping fine sand substrate. Heavy use by Canada geese here (some plants, including Eleocharis intermedia, cropped very low). The current river level has recently risen 2-3 inches due to recent rains (sandbar vegetation extends into shallow water at the edge of the river- these plants were above river level until recently). (I visited this same spot on 8 September 2005 and at that time the river level was ~16 inches lower than it is currently.) Photos taken of plot and setting.

Typical of wetter zones of aspen-dominated woodland in large sedge meadow complex, on level outwash west of Phibrook. Uneven-aged; several age classes, largest cohort 36-41cm DBH, these infrequent. Modal size is 20-25cm DBH. No stumps. Snags infrequent. CWD rather sparse. Medium-textured deep sand, moist to surface; upper 10 cm with slight organic component, grey and mottled with iron-colored bands below 10cm deep. Slightly higher elevation zones (few inches) with abundant Cornus racemosa and Carex pensylvanica. Phalaris arundinacea is patchy and sporadic, sometimes forming the dominant cover in this setting.

Typical of a rather large (65-acre) and mostly level island in a large peatland complex on gently rolling outwash plain. Fairly mature patch; uneven-aged, trees mostly 25-42 cm DBH, largest 48+ cm. Few snags. No cut stumps. Rather sparse CWD. Plot margins are 40-50 meters from surrounding wetland. Plot is 2-3 feet higher elevation than wetland. Earthworm castings common; earthworm assessment score = 4.  Thin litter. Upper 15 cm is wormed silt over sandy-silt; no stones. Photos taken of plot and vicinity.

Typical of somewhat heterogeneous and rather broad ecotonal zone on the margin of a small (2-acre), low, upland rise in large peatland complex. Bimodal tree size-class distribution, 36-42cm and 8-18cm DBH. Occasional snags. No cut stumps. Sparse CWD. Plot covers much of the rather limited wet aspen zone here. Elevation is within a few inches (<5") of adjacent sedge meadow. Soil moist to the surface; upper 15cm is dark organic silty-loam, below 15cm is grey sand. Grades to oak-basswood with a few inches higher elevation nearby.

Exposed gravel-cobble bar along the Mississippi River opposite the downstream end of McDougall Island. Substrate is small rounded cobbles 1/4 - 4 inches in diameter (mostly 1/2 - 2 inches), moist to surface; below surface is coarse sand and gravel. Plot varies from 3-5 inches above the present river level; entire bar is inundated in spring/summer. Plot slopes very gently toward river (to the southeast). Adjacent river segment is shallow riffles here, moderate current. Free-flowing reach 1.5 miles downstream of the Blanchard dam. Narrow zone of floodplain forest occurs on the adjacent riverbank. Photos taken of plot and setting.

place_name: Royalton Sportsman's Landing NE, Mississippi River
remarks:
Plot captures the +/- level to gently undulating top of a fairly extensive cobble bar/beach along the east bank of the Mississippi River between McDougall Island and Sportsman's Club landing. Setting is 8-12 inches above the present river level; entire bar is inundated in spring. Free-flowing river reach 2 miles downstream from the Blanchard dam. Substrate is rounded cobbles mostly 1-5(8) inches in diameter at surface of ground, just below the surface is moist coarse sand. River here has a light current; this cobble-gravel bar complex occurs on the outside portion of a river bend, and near the downstream end of that bend. Photos taken of plot and setting.

Notes:  
 -- Photos of plot + vicinity / setting.  
 -- Plot is higher, drier, exposed longer and with larger cobbles compared to A803 1/2 mile upstream.

General Soil Texture: Cobble (not an option). Likewise for soil layer 1.

Typical of a broad cobble/gravel bar (~2 acres) on the upstream end of an 8-acre floodplain island in the Mississippi River. Plot centrally located on bar, in setting 8-12 inches above the present river level. Free flowing river reach, moderate current here. Substrate is rounded cobbles mostly 0.5-2 inches (0.25-5 inches) in diameter; dry at the surface, just below the surface is moist coarse sandy-gravel and cobbles. Heavy use by Canada geese here. Photos taken of plot and setting/vicinity.

6x9-meter plot covers most of a small mudflat zone here; does not extend onto the adjacent small sand bar which is at a slightly higher elevation. Plot setting is 2-5 inches above the present river level (inundated earlier in the season) in a small, shallow side channel amongst a series of islands and braided channels in the free-flowing Mississippi River north of the Camp Ripley cantonment area. Substrate is deep moist silt, becoming rather shallow over sand on the edges of the plot. This spot is the largest patch of river shore encountered in a several mile stretch of the river in the Camp Ripley Cantonment Area vicinity. Grades to (a small) sand bar and to (a small) backwater marsh. Photos taken of plot and setting.

Centrally located on rather extensive (~1.5-acre) cobble bar along the western bank of the Mississippi River, at Beaver Islands, St. Cloud. Level setting 3-6 inches above the present river level; entire bar is inundated earlier in the season. Free-flowing reach of river, one mile downstream from 10th Street South dam. Substrate surface is rounded cobbles 0.5-6 inches in diameter (mostly 1-3 inches). Moist coarse sand just below the surface in matrix with cobbles/gravel. Water level has risen 2-3 inches recently. Exposed substrate (bare cobbles) covers ~50% of the plot. Photos taken of plot and setting.

Plot captures lower terrace of a large, two-tierd sand bar along free-flowing Zumbro River in Zumbro Bottoms forestry unit. Level setting 4-6 inches above the present water level, lower bar is inundated earlier in season (upper bar only inundated during major flood events). Moderate river current here; plot located on inside of river bend, on downstream portion of bar. Substrate is deep, moist, coarse sand with thin silty cap and frequent pea-gravel cobbles at surface. ~35% of plot is bare (unvegetated) substrate. The upper terrace of the bar is 3-8 ft above the river, and is dominated by dense Salix interior; degraded floodplain forest further inland. Photos taken of plot and setting (near dusk).

Plot captures downstream end of a fairly large (1/2-acre, 75 meters long, x 18 meters wide) sand-cobble bar in the Zumbro River at Zumbro Falls Woods SNA. Level setting 3-6 inches above river level, the entire bare is inundated earlier in the season. Free-flowing river here. Deep moist sand, fairly coarse, with thin lens of silt over much of the plot. Bare substrate covers ~55% of plot. Upstream portion of this low bar is cobble substrate (cobbles to 2 inches diameter). Exposed bare is even larger in drier years (connects to river bank and large sand bar complex just upstream on 2011 air photos). Photos taken of plot and setting.

place_name: Vinegar Ridge - Root River Trail Bridge
remarks: Plot captures the upstream end of a fairly large (3/4-acre) sand bar in the free-flowing Root River, not far downstream from the Root River State Trail bridge at the Vinegar Ridge forestry unit. Level setting 6 inches above the present river level; entire bar is inundated earlier in the season. Deep, moist, fine to moderately coarse sand. Subtle microtopographic undulations occur in plot. Bare sand covers 45% of plot. Grades to slightly higher zone (a few inches higher elevation) dominated by small Salix interior- this higher zone is weedier. Significantly higher sand bar zones occur on the adjacent river bank (inner portion of river bend)- these are covered by dense stands of tall Salix interior. Photos taken of plot and setting. Metallic blue-black beetles quite abundant here, congregating on vegetation in the plot.

Typical of denser portion of ~8-acre patch of oaks atop 120-foot bedrock ridge near the west end of Jackfish Bay, Basswood Lake. Pines mature, 30-45cm DBH; largest oaks ~25cm. No stumps. CWD rather sparse. Rocky loamy soil is shallow to the granitic bedrock, mostly <25cm deep. Occasional surface rocks and boulders. Exposed bedrock within 20 meters of plot (southward); in exposed bedrock zones the vegetation is more of a savanna, with less dense oaks and fewer pines. Grades to a fairly extensive rock outcrop community further southward, toward the top of a steep cliff-crested slope.

Notes:  
 -- No exposed bedrock in plot but rock outcrops occur within 20 meters of the plot.  
 -- Grades to bedrock savanna + rock outcrop southward / southeastward toward top of steep cliffy slope.

Soil almost pure fine sand, gray on top layer, yellowish below, but barely holds in a ball when wet. Deer browsing of Pteridium & Aralia, but little on Corylus. Island in peatland. Pinus and Abies snags present. CWD decent from fallen Abies. Largest pine is OP. Other parts of island have less Populus and more canopy gaps. Draft condition ranking form completed. Counts from tree basal area plots 1 and 2: P. resinosa(2,2), P. tremuloides (8,8), P. strobus (1,2), A. balsamea (4,0), A. rubrum (1,0).

Rich swamp between upland and large acid peatland. Pools cover about 30% of plot. Surface water sample collected, pH reading error estimated to be 0.2. Counts of tree basal area plots 1 and 2: L. laricina (8,7), L. laricina DEAD (1,0), P. mariana (4,1).

Fine sand with high water table. Close by is wet forest transition to large acid peatland. No cut stumps observed but this must have been logged or there would be more large logs. Dominated by even-aged aspen about 20 cm dbh. Single massive white pine in plot. Decent CWD, but no large logs. No large snags. Used condition ranking form. Counts from tree basal area plots 1 and 2: P. tremuloides (9,4), A. rubrum (1,2), F. pensylvanica (1,0), P. tremuloides DEAD (0,1), B. papyrifera DEAD (0,1), Q. macrocarpa (0,1), A. balsamea (0,1), P. strobus (1,0)

Cedar and ash forest on deep sapric peat between upland and creek. Many canopy  gaps due to past blowdown. Old cut cedar stumps observed in nearby cedar swamp, but not here. Pools cover about 40% of area and most have leaf litter cover. Currently, no standing water, deer browse level relatively high. Draft condition ranking worksheet completed. Counts from basal area plots 1 & 2: F. nigra (4,1), T. occidentalis (3,9), B. papyrifera (2,2), B. papyrifera DEAD (3,1), A. balsamea (1,0).

Large island surrounded by cedar swamp. Mature forest lacking large trees, but no old cut stumps observed. An old large pit/mound in plot. Plenty of CWD from fallen fir, birch, and cedar. Some parts of island have open canopy with fallen fir and birch and more blueberry than plot. High deer browse. Designated old growth. Draft condition ranking worksheet completed and included here. Counts of basal areas 1 & 2: B. papyrifera (4,9), T. occidentalis (5,3), P. tremuloides (1,1), A balsamea (1,0), P. glauca (1,0), P. mariana (1,0).

Probed several holes, and one had loamy sand at 55 cm instead of clay. Black spruce nearby has many low, spreading branches, suggesting this may have been open pasture at one time. Road may also influence hydrology. Soil does not feel compacted. Alders growing on slight mounds. No standing water. Cornus is browsed. Mosses mostly on logs.

Transition zone about 5 m wide between upland pine forest and graminoid lakeshore. Clearly flooded by lake occasionally. Essentially no soil. Instead a thin layer of well-decomposed humus over loose rocks. Scrubby due partly to beaver-harvesting of small ashes. Scattered layer ashes up to 30 cm dbh. this transitional community is in a band around entire bay. EFP wypt 013 at northeast end of linear releve.

Island burned around late 1980s. This band about 30 m wide on SW shore is heavily dominated by jack pine. Lakeshore is 5 m away. To N jack pine becomes evenly mixed with paper birch. Most trunks from previous forest burned away, but there are a few logs, some charred, some rotten and don't appear charred. Top 3 cm of soil is leached gray. There are a few beaver-cut birch samplings. Many young pines have died through self-thinning. One larger snag standing. Purpose of releve = disturbance ecology. EFP wypt 025 at southwest corner of plot.

place_name: Lady Boot Bay, Lac La Croix
remarks: Downed logs mostly small fir and spruce (up to 30 cm dbh), but other parts of this stand have large pine logs. Also, 1 birch log. Litter is a mix of needles and leaves. Old growth. EFP wypt 035 near center of plot.

Wide central water track in large peatland with poor spruce swamp to north and bands of open Larix swamp to south alternating with narrower open water tracks. Many "pools" between hummocks are covered with very tall Sphagnum angustifolium, which makes hummocks look nearly continuous. Parts of water track have more pools and Typha, part more hummocks and C. chordorhiza. Plot straddles both. pH reading error estimated to be 0.2. I thought this was APn91c until taking the pH. EFP wypt 043 near center of plot.

To south the shrub layer (primarily Betula pumila) thins out. Edge of large peatland - this portion has open, canopy of stunted Larix. Here Larix are mostly 8-12 cm dbh and 5-8 m tall and top-dead. pH reading error estimated to be 0.2. Ownership = state forest - swamp trust. EFP wypt 044 near center of plot.

Ownership = State Forest - Swamp Trust. Part of large rich fen surrounding Steamboat Bay of Leech Lake, between small creek and upland. Fringe of Larix is expanding into fen. Across creek are abandoned wild rice paddies. Highway 371 and paved rail trail cut through ~100 m southwest. Water sample collected from footprint an stored unfrozen for a few days. pH reading error estimated to be 0.2. EFP wypt 046 in southwest corner of plot.

Skid trail nearby is full of central floristic spp - sparse in the plot. One old ut stump (P. banksiana?) in plot has fire charring. Cornus and Amelanchier stems significantly browsed, but light on Corylus. Litter is mixed birch leaves and pine needles; birch predominates. Humus is conifer origin. A few fallen canopy pines, but no older logs. Scattered red pine reserved during last cut are now ~ 50 cm dbh. Includes condition ranking form. Counts of tree basal area plots 1 and 2: B. papyrifera (9,0), P. resinosa (5,2), P. banksiana (5,3), P. banksiana DEAD (3,3). EFP wypt 048 near plot center.

Some birches and firs are dead or recently fallen, but no large logs. No legacy trees or snags. Road to nearby boat landing passes about 20 m away. Pine plantation is about 50 m away. One jack pine log. More earthworms near road in process of removing duff from plot. Condition ranking form included in files. Counts from tree basal area plots 1 and 2: P. resinosa (1,0), A. balsamea (4,1), B. papyrifera (5,4), B. papyrifera DEAD (2,1), P. glauca (0,1), A rubrum (0,1). EFP wypt 054 near plots center.

Plot includes one of many small open bedrock outcrops in community. See some old stumps with charring. To northwest is pine-dominated FDn22a and FDn33a similar to across the river. Quercus rubra/ellipsoidalis have leaf sinuses and dead lower branches like ellipsoidalis, but acorn caps look closer to rubra. Conditional ranking form included in documents. Counts from tree basal area plots 1 and 2: P. resinosa (2,0), P. strobus (3,0), Q. macrocarpa (2,1), Q. rubra (0,3), A rubrum (0,1).

Poor fen water track through middle of large acid peatland dominated by open Larix swamp. Track starts at group of islands with sandy soil. No patterning. Sphagnum hummocks nearly continuous. Hollows cover <5%. Larix are stunted and most have very short needles and appear to possibly be dying. pH reading error estimated to be 0.2. EFP wypt 087 at southwest corner of plot.

Small patch of deciduous forest within large area planted with red pine and jack pine. Grades into MHn44 toward peatland to south but here appears above influence of water table. Some logs, but less than expected. Condition ranking form included in documents. Counts from tree basal area plots 1 and 2: A. balsamea (2,0), P. grandidentata (4,0), B. papyrifera (6,7).

About 1 m or less above Big Fork River. Low area with a large silver maple and lots of C. lupulinus cover part of plot. Grades uphill to southeast into apparent MHn35. Fewer large trees and snags than expected but there are many rotten logs on ground - moss covered. There are 1 or 2 old cut stumps at edge of plot. Condition ranking form included in attached documents. Counts from tree basal area plots 1 and 2: F. nigra (5,7), F. pensylvanica (1,2), A. negundo (1,0), A saccharinum (0,2).

About 50 cm above current level of big fork river. Logs present at various stages of decay. Appears to flood every year. Condition ranking form included in attached documents. Counts from tree basal area plots 1 and 2: A. saccharinum (7,4), F. nigra (3,0), Q. macrocarpa (1,0), F. pensylvanica (1,3), F. pensylvanica DEAD (0,2). EFP wypt 92 is near center of plot.

Stand has less tree mortality than typical for stand. Water level controlled by Pancake Lake. It appears to be higher than in recent past, killing many canopy trees, which now stand as snags. Hummocks are old mossy logs and stumps, covering about 30% of plot, the rest pools, now saturated but no standing water. Logs at various stages of decay. Just south of plot it grades through transition of WFn64a to upland. Most ashes in plot have canopy dieback. Condition ranking form included in attached documents. Tree basal area count (1 plot possibly missing): U. americana (4), F. nigra (12), F. nigra DEAD (1). EFP wypt 093 near plot center.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Appears to grade to south into MHn46 and then mesic upland. Heavily used ATV trail between plot and lake. Many ashes with canopy dieback, few outright snags. Some logs but less than expected. Old ATV trail passes through plot. EFP wypt 094 near center of plot.

Open fen water track with significant cover of stunted Larix. High hummocks cover about 80% of plot with small hollows between them. Track passes through open Picea mariana bog. pH reading error estimated to be 0.2. EFP wypt 096 near center of plot.

Open canopy Larix in poor water track, grading into APn91c1 down-track and into APn80a to the side of the track. Larix more stunted than typical for NPC. pH reading error estimated to be 0.2. EFP wypt 097 near center of plot.

Old Growth ID: LH-RP-1. Soil color cocoa, pH 5.5. Clean cut sections of red pine tree trunks in stand. CWD - large downed quaking aspen, paper birch, red pine, white spruce. Ash swamp near plot (< 50 meters from edge). Old cut stumps in various states of decay, some well-decayed. Large Pinus strobus measured outside of plot: 55 cm and 61 cm. Birds heard during survey: red breasted nuthatch, broad winged hawk, blue jay, black capped chickadee.

Nice native hillside within Coteau landscape. Non native species are not abundant here compared to other areas elsewhere on site.

Exposed Rock: 1-2%, some exposed gravel

Low prairie with abundant forbs. Some invasion from red top (Agrosts gigantea). Site is nearly level with no dominant aspect.  

UTM Accuracy: submeter.

Original releve states upper slopes on SW hillside. GPS marker was near edge of Lake on toeslope. Moved point to 10m N on upper slopes of hillside. GPS point at SW corner. Photo at SE corner. Matches description of old releve to current plot: gravelly area present in SW corner, boulders scattered across rolling hillside.  

Notes:  
Brome and symocc appear to be invading this area.

UTM Accuracy: submeter.

Nice native hillside with good forb diversity compared to surrounding prairie. Bearing from NW corner is 100 degrees. Stand is typical of hillside, but considerably more diverse from flat grassland located to northeast.  

UTM Accuracy: submeter.

Upland mesic prairie surrounded by a scattering of cattail marshes. Plot is nearly level with a slight slope to the southwest.  

UTM Accuracy: submeter.  GPS point in SW corner of plot.

Low quality mesic prairie vegetation. Mainly dominated by non-native brome grass. Leafy spurge documented within the releve plot and throughout the plant community. Lack of management has resulted in the encroachment of cedar trees and green ash. Soils are loamy, moderately well drained. Typical of Storden-Clarion Loam soil type. Additional surveyor: Amy Husveth.
Planted and restored southern mesic prairie. Little bluestem common, as well as stiff goldenrod. Loamy soils, medium texture.
Southern Terrace Forest. Silver maple with cottonwood, american elm, green ash. Understory species are typical of low quality disturbed forest.Additional surveyor: Amy Husveth.
Area not classified as native plant community type.
Moderate quality example of upland dry prairie. Soils contain gravel and area well drained. SW facing knoll, typical of plant community type.
Well sorted, dry sandy soils. Bur oak common, along with green ash, ironwood, common buckthorn.
Mesic hardwood forest dominated by bur oak, basswood, ironwood, hackberry. Overall low diversity in herbaceous understory. Soils are loess, wind deposited silts. Well drained.
Floodplain forest dominated by cottonwood, green ash, hackberry, boxelder, american elm. Additional surveyor: Amy L. Husveth.

Fire dependent oak woodland. Open grown oaks present within the releve. Abundant oak and hackberry, basswood, hickory present. Buckthorn dominated shrub layer. Soils are degraded. Some native herbaceous understory observed. Soils are sandy loam. Clarion Storden complex. Additional surveyor: Amy L. Husveth.

Well drained loam soils on 25-50% SW facing slopes. Supports dry hill prairie species. Short in stature. Herbaceous layer dominated by native prairie grasses with few forbs intermixed. Limited weedy species present.

Low quality terrace forest along. Subject to infrequent flooding. Canopy trees typical of riparian forest. Somewhat poorly drained, sandy loam soils. Flat topography along the Cottonwood River. Soils are disturbed and lacking in organic layer. Dominated by early successional herbaceous species. Additional surveyor: Amy L. Husveth.

Somewhat poorly drained sandy loam soils. Flooded with some frequency. Soils are disturbed. Herbaceous vegetation dominated by early successional native species and weed species. Garlic mustard detected within the releve plot and common in the area. Additional surveyor: Amy L. Husveth.

Mesic Maple Basswood Forest with bur oak, sugar maple, black walnut, hackberry and green ash common. Understory herbaceous vegetation essentially due to lack of forest soils, organic material. Mineral soils exposed. Well-drained soils on relatively ssteep slopes. Loam soils, typical of Clarion-Terril Loam Soils. Additional surveyor: Amy L. Husveth.

Low quality wet to mesic hardwood forest. Adjacent to Cottonwood River. Sandy, loamy, silty soil surface with stratified layers below. Soils typical of Kalmarville Sandy Loam. Herbaceous understory generally dominated by aggressive, native, early successional species. Additional surveyor: Amy L. Husveth.

Poorly drained, clay loam soils. Oshawa Silty Clay Loam soils. Saturated condition. Fed by groundwater lateral flow. Supports common wet meadow species. Reed canary grass common. Carex stricta hummocks also common. Additional surveyor: Amy L. Husveth.

Poorly drained loam soils on 2% slopes. Typical of Clarion Loam soil complex. Bluejoint and prairie cordgrass common in the releve plot. Moderate forb diversity typical of wet prairie vegetation. Additional surveyor: Amy L. Husveth.
D-quality - lacking forest organic soil horizon (duff) due to earthworms. Additional surveyor: Amy L. Husveth.

Silty soils on the surface with stratified silt, sand, gravel below. Quality is a D rank plant community. Severely earthworm impacted. Bare ground is commonly exposed due to earthworm activity. Organic forest soils are lacking. Tree regeneration is minimal. Additional surveyor: Amy L. Husveth.
Sandy gravel soils. Supporting stand of willow species. Herbaceous understory diverse, but dominated by aggressive early successional native species. Additional surveyor: Amy L. Husveth.

place_name: MN Valley Rec. Area - Lawrence Unit
remarks: Carex laeviconica swale on terrace at intermediate elevation above river. Between slough mudflats and floodplain forests.

place_name: MN Valley Rec. Area - Lawrence Unit
remarks: Wet meadow dominated by Carex laeviconica and Reed Canary grass with 50% cover of sandbar willow. Within raceway slough channel surrounded by floodplain forest.

Mature oak, maple and basswood trees.  Also hickory present. Understory sparse, earthworm activity noted. Soil silty loam, typical of Grays series. Earth worm impacted, heavy deer browse, soils lacking, hemic layer (organics) lacking silty parent soil exposed, little to no forest regeneration observed.

place_name: MN Valley Rec. Area - Lawrence Unit
remarks: Mesic hardwoods dominated by infrequent bur oak with large trunks and spreading canopy branches with maturing basswood enclosing canopy. Oak DBH 16-32"; basswood DBH 6-14". Glacial River Warren Terrace with 5-10% boulders. Soil is mollisol with deep A horizon. Mesic forest forbs with rich diversity.

place_name: MN Valley Rec. Area - Lawrence Unit
remarks: Oak woodland dominated by open grown, craggy bur oak. DBH 6-16". Crowns 10-15 m tall; deep mollic A horizon. Recent park management in nearby old pasture. Glacial stones 1-5% cover; mesic, deep organic soil. Trees with epicormic branches that are very common. Broad spreading crowns, crooked trunks. Forbs a mixture of prairie and woodland species.

C-Quality Bulrush Marsh.  Dominated by river bulrush.  Presense of reed canary grass noted. Moderate diversity of native species in the herbaceous layer.  Soils are typical of Glencoe clay loams, poorly drained.  Clay soils.
C-quality ranked wet meadow.  Water ponded over poorly drained histosols. Vegetation dominated by lake sedge and bluejoint.  Native forbs interspersed throughout the releve.

place_name: MN Valley Rec. Area - Lawrence Unit
remarks: Emergent marsh in small basin of floodplain with 5 cm of standing water.

npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: D-quality green ash and boxelder floodplain forest.  Buckthorn and tartarian honeysuckle noted. Native forbs and grasses present, species are common and typical of disturbed forest area. Soils are poorly drained clay loams, typical of Glencoe soil complex.  Degraded lowland.  Hardwood forest around landscape depression.

place_name: MN Valley Rec. Area - Lawrence Unit
remarks: Small basin or swale with emergent marsh on toe slope of valley bluff. Surface water 5 cm depth. Possible seepage from lower slope at base.

place_name: MN Valley Rec. Area - Thompson Ferry Unit
npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: Floodplain forest on high terrace of MN River next to raceway slough channels with WMn82 meadow shrub carr. North third of plot on escarpment dominated by silver maple. Terrace rise is dominated by red elm (DBH 14") and Kentucky Coffee Tree (DBH 1-14"). Alluvial soils are well-drained and periodic flooded, area dissected with many channels and small ravines.

C-Quality Mesic Hardwood Forest.  Mature Bur Oak, Green Ash, American Elm, Hackberry, Black Cherry present within the plot.  Shrub layer moderatly diverse, includes common buckthorn. Earthworm impacts noted, mineral soils exposed.  Herbaceous layer dominated by native species, typical of distrubed forest systems.  Soils are well drained.  Loam soils, typical of Lester soil series. Approx. 7 inches of black loam over olive colored loam.

D-Quality mixed cattail marsh.  Located in inland depression along Albert Lea Lake. Cattail and reed canary grass common.  Soils are poorly drained histosols.  6 inches of water over soils at point of releve. Farmed, degraded, species poor.  Non-native cattail dominated.

Young stand, plot taken after salvage logging after July 2011 blowdown event. Plot placed using cardinal directions. Staked at SW corner. Near Matthew Laury Trail, west side, about 200 yards south of 2011-2012 logging landing. 1/2" Conduit stake placed at SW corner of plot.
Low terrace associated with Little Fork River. Fine, silty/silty clay deposits (well sorted). Snail shells present on forest floor. CWD moderate. WP 33 averaged at SW plot corner.
Raised bog in large peatland complex. Deep peat. Additional surveyor: Norma Malinowski. UTM=NE plot corner.
Plot representative of the open npc associated w/ periphery of raised spruce bog. Deep peat with relatively level surface. Additional surveyor: Norma Malinowski. UTM = SE plot corner.

NPC classification uncertain, may be best described as wet forest (WFn55 or WFn53?). Microtopography abundant. Higher mounds with > 8 cm of muck humus. Some shallow hollows with standing water on 6/27. Mucky peat present in upper soil profile. Evidence of old cut stumps. Lacking large diameter CWD and snags. UTM = SE plot corner.

Additional surveyor: Shelby Curry. NPC classification uncertain, may be best described as mesic hardwood system. Old growth forest with canopy gaps and large diameter CWD and snags common. Thick humus layer. Fine sandy loam in upper profile, well to mod well drained. Standing dead Abies likely due to SBW. UTM = SE plot corner.

NPC classification uncertain, may be best described as wet forest (WFn55 or WFn53?). Microtopography abundant with drier rises and low mucky hollows. Standing water largely absent from hollows on 7/16. Mature stand with evidence of old cut stumps. Drier mounds with muck humus, hard to discern due to earthworm activity. WT @ depth of 18 cm. UTM = SW plot corner.

Plot representative of npc on low level terraces associated with Sturgeon River. Evidence of flooding in 2014 (above average water levels in June/July 2014). No CWD and minimal to no humus present. Very fine sand/silt alluvium > 25 cm.

NPC System uncertain. Plot representative of stand on subtle slope in lower topographic setting (upland) between FDn matrix and wetlands near shore. Plot contains canopy gap. Large diameter aspen and white spruce (>50 cm dbh) CWD present. Mod well/somewhat poorly drained. Did not observe mucky hollows or wet depressions in stand. No evid of charcoal on soil surface. UTM = NW plot corner.

NPC occupies the more level/gradual "benches" of slope where soil accumulation exceeds that of adjacent woodlands. Large aspen and JP CWD in plot (JP CWD diameter = 35cm). No exposed bedrock. Scattered stones and cobble common. UTM = SW plot corner.

Releve representative of low, level upland forest (mature) along periphery of large peatland. Near subsection border. Canopy gaps common in stand; plot located in area w/ relatively intact canopy. Tip ups and microtopography present. Mod well/somewhat poorly drained. Upper profile very fine sandy loam (powdery residue and no coarse frag). @~20 cm, seems more like fine sandy clay loam. Some red mottles noted. No obvious sign of earthworms. UTM = SW plot corner.
Additional surveyor: Norma Malinowski. Hummock height widely variable, average 40 cm. height. No pools or standing water on 8/18. UTM = NW plot corner.
Small, low rise upland within large peatland complex. Legacy snags and CWD rare in stand. Earthworms present, but impact appears minimal. UTM = NE plot corner.

Steep slope along Little Fork River. Mature stand. Canopy gaps frequent; aspen and ash regeneration prevalent. Large diameter CWD and snags common. Humus organics and mineral top soil highly intermixed. Slope variable across plot. UTM = SE plot corner.

Relatively level setting, shallow valley straddled by two upland knob features of higher relief. Slight slope to east. Soils are fine/very fine sandy loam (upper 45 cm). Redox features noted between 25-45 cm depth. Soil noticeably more moist @ 45 cm. Small rocky depressions scattered in stand/plot, often wetter microsites/inclusions (rubbly aquepts?). Older growth forest; canopy gaps and large diameter CWD and snags common. UTM = SW plot corner.
Plot taken after salvage logging after 2011 blowdown event. Metal conduit stake on SW corner.

Intermediate landscape position. Soil profile: 0-36 cm SL/Fine SL no coarse fragments. At 36 cm hit dense layer with increased clay component (peds present). Sandy clay loam or sandy clay. Mottles present at/> 36 cm. Old scattered stumps noted in stand but infrequent to rare. Large diameter CWD and snags present. UTM = SW corner of plot.

Releve representative of alder dominated npc with tree cover (trees taller than 4m) less than 25 percent. Tree components in stand include black ash, red maple, and tamarack. Pools of standing water present in plot. UTM = plot center.

Diverse structure- CWD, openings are common. No evidence of cutting. Completely saturated just below surface of hollows - water sort of stinky ... iron smell? Less Picea mariana in plot than whole stand. On a long, gradual, north-facing slope that drains to Rice Lake.
No evidence recent disturbance (stumps, invasives). Moderate mortality of small dbh conifers. CWD common in various stages of decay. BA-1 data included on datasheet.

Uniformly shrubby basin southeast of Mallard Lake, bisected by powerline right-of-way. This and other wetlands (including forested acid peatland) in area invaded moderately to heavily by fruiting Frangula alnus.
No stumps apparent. Water 3" below lowest soil surface. Smooth muck with no fibers or chunks to 12". Wetland located in ancient channel of Mississippi River.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Humus to 3 cm, charcoal 3-5 cm, loamy sand below. CWD from blowdown common, no obviously cut stumps. Canopy gap along east edge of plot.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Trees smaller dbh but unsure why. Moderate amount of CWD. Plot on slight rise that slopes to west to small tributary of Beaver Brook.

Varying sizes CWD common. Less exposed bedrock and more tree regeneration (both deciduous and coniferous) than bedrock exposure as a whole. Most of this bedrock rise is dominated by deciduous trees, except the most elevated portions.

A few tall Larix exceed denser Picea mariana. Very dry at present. Deep peat to 18" below hollows. Peat damp, but water does not appear in 18" excavated hole. Picea 2-7" dbh. Larix 6-7" dbh. No visible cut stumps. Aged at 115 years old in FIM. Clearcuts 120 meters west.

Browse evident- assume mostly deer but moose tracks nearby. Jagged, decayed, moss-covered stumps present. NE half of plot drier than SW, which has bare, formerly saturated hollows. Trees mature but not that large. A couple leaners but no blowdown. CWD moderate. Many boulders from ~ 8 inches deep downward.

Three pits of soil disturbance in plot of unknown origin, gravel pit 170 meters west. Area to SW somewhat recently thinned. Plot contains shallow drainage that runs to pond below. Browse and mortality obvious in sparse shrub layer. Various sizes CWD common.

Beaver-influenced peatland, totally saturated just below surface. Light-colored Sphagnum and plant remains, mostly undecomposed to 14" deep- dark, fibrous peat below that. A few wet depressions are dominated by semi-aquatic Sphagnum.
Unique structure. Very open but blowdown uncommon off plot. Dense patches with only small trees.

Most of plot dry or mucky - one pool with standing water in north end. Trees confined to/create elevated spots. Some CWD. A couple old stumps but look like naturally fallen trees. Data for basal-areas 1 and 2 can be found on attached datasheet.

Diverse structure - clumps of mature trees, gaps w/ dense Thuja regen. Some blowdown and leaning trees. Moderately tall hummocks, very little standing water. No cut stumps visible. Some Larix dying in plot, some dead outside. Oozing knotholes with orange-brown shelf fungus. Waterlogged dark blackish-brown peat to 15" with wood chunks. Data for basal areas 1 and 2 are provided on attached datasheet.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: North-facing edge of bedrock knob. Appears wind and lightning impacted. Charred 15 ft Pinus stump just outside plot. Includes relatively deep depression. Blowdown and CWD, some charred. Data for basal areas 1 and 2 available on attached datasheet.

Low spot (subtle) in center, slopes gently upward on E and W sides. Area has been harvested previously, and part currently marked. Larger trees outside plot on higher spots. Abundant Sphaerid (fingernail) clams on top of soil, indicating early season standing water. Basal areas 1 and 2 data on attached form.

Some mature Thujas have dead tops (last 1-2 m). Many diagonal tree trunks, blowdown in plot and elsewhere. Wet here compared to most lowland conifer at this time. Peaty muck black brown to 12" then finer muck 12-18". Basal areas 1 and 2 data provided on attached datasheet.

Plot occupies subtle rise - Pinus b. more dominant off rise. Extremely large dbh Pinus r. between here and highway- many blown down. Blowdown common in stand but less common in plot. No obvious charcoal in soil. Some Abies pushed over by bough cutters. Basal areas 1 and 2 are provided on attached datasheet.

Loamy sand over red sand. This releve redo was conducted at a site that was not affected by 2008 or 2011 blowdown events, and did not have any salvage logging operations. Site is richer than other FDc25 sites in park to the east. 1/2" conduit stake place in SW corner of plot.

Remarks: CWD minimal -- a few moss-covered logs. Wet depressions w/ standing water. Heavy rain last night. Occasional moss-covered boulders. ~100m south of Crooked Lake. Near edge of FDn aspen forest. Dead branches on Fraxinus and Ulmus common. Frax pens in vicinity. Photos taken by DSW.  

NPC Code = MHn46? WFn55?

Plot on floating mat at margin of lake. Community is fairly extensive on west side of lake. Plot ca. 20 m from edge of water. No pools in plot, but present nearby. Peat of moss origin. Adjacent upland is FDn forest. Photos taken by DSW.
High relief, a more well-drained feature of landscape. Upper soil layer (0-> 18 cm) very fine sandy loam/loam. Worms present. Mature example, but lacking snags and CWD. Evidence of cut stumps common.

Plot within designated old growth stand SW-162. Natural stumps and fallen trees, well decayed. A deer trail or possibly old, overgrown ATV trail cuts through southern half of plot. Old growth white pine with balsam understory and open patches. Plot area at relatively high, flat position compared to stand overall, which gradually slopes toward reservoir. Did not see evidence of cut stumps in stand. Red pine with 58.5 cm DBH out of plot. Birds heard during survey: Blackburnian warbler, red eyed vireo, oven bird, veery, cedar waxwing, northern parula, Nashville warbler, American robin, bluejay, red breasted nuthatch, black capped chickadee, evening grosbeak (while walking out from stand). Heard leopard frog. UTM coordinates for NE corner of plot. Entered elevation from 2' Lidar contours.

UTM coordinates were not recorded correctly, but are within 100m of reported location. Plot within old growth stand SW-112. Old growth red pine forest with areas of dense balsam understory and more open areas with hazel. Releve reflects this mix. Plot placed in approximately half covering dense balsam and half in more open area with hazel and bracken fern. From web soil survey, Alden lake/Pequayan soils - sandy loams, well-moderately well drained. Gently rolling topography. Hummocky forest floor from old deadfalls and stumps decaying under litter with pits from old root systems. Birds heard during survey: hermit thrush, blackburnian warbler, pine warbler, ovenbird, Nashville warbler, American robin, eastern wood peewee, bluejay, brown creeper, red eyed vireo, magnolia warbler, broad-winged hawk, red breasted nuthatch, black throated green warbler, northern parula, common yellowthroat, blue headed vireo, veery, pileated woodpecker, white throated sparrow (in the distance).

Designated old growth white pine stand (EH-73) on steep terrain. Patches of balsam understory interspersed with canopy gaps dominated by mountain maple. Lots of CWD including fallen paper birch and cedar. Some disturbance through stand (not plot): ATV/hiking trails, Clearwater Rd., some recently cut trees on edge of trail. Large "leafy" lichens on downed trees. Birds heard during survey: blackburnian warbler, swainson's thrush, black throated green warbler, magnolia warbler, red breasted nuthatch, winter wren, black capped chickadee, white throated sparrow, Nashville warbler, black and white warbler. UTM coordinates for NE corner of plot. Elevation entered from 2' lidar contours.

Designated old growth stand OG3-07. Leaves of canopy basswoods defoliated by tent caterpillars. Huge fallen yellow birch in plot (79 cm dbh). Hummocky areas from root pits. Some well-decayed and more recent woody debris. Deer herbivory on some herbs. Few well-rotted stumps. Occasional large white spruce in stand (not plot). Acer saccharum with dbh 56.5 and 38.5 outside plot. Nearby areas within stand have more continuous Carex pensylvanica carpet suggesting earthworm invasion that is more severe than rank assigned to releve plot. Understory open and consisting of small maples. Structure of releve representative of nearby surrounding stand, but ground layer flora may be somewhat more diverse than that observed in the northeast 1/3 of the old growth stand overall. Stand classified as MHn47, but could also possibly be MHn45 or MHn35. Birds heard during survey: eastern wood peewee, oven bird, red eyed vireo, least flycatcher, American goldfinch, American robin, pileated woodpecker.

permanent_plot_type_description: ex. metal tag on nearby tree
remarks: Plot located at point 89 of Aitkin County bird survey study within the treatment group. SW corner of plot is a basswood with blue paint marking bird point count. Veery or hermit thrush nest just outside of plot. Second nest in two large maples that have fallen across the plot. Yellow birch in understory outside of plot. Coarse woody debris - branches on forest floor. Hummocky forest floor in very gently rolling terrain. Some canopy gaps (not in plot) in otherwise near continuous maple-basswood canopy. On till plain of Superior lobe with soils with loamy till parent material and fine sandy loam soils according to web soil survey and geomorphology of MN GIS layer. Birds heard during survey: eastern wood peewee, veery, broad winged hawk. Entered elevation from lidar 2' contours.

Plot located at northwestern-most bird point count (point 916) in Aitkin County bird study control. Plot slopes gently to the north, but is perched on the crest of a hill that slopes more steeply on the west and especially east sides. Rolling terrain with hummocky forest floor and occasional wet (ephemeral ponds?) inclusions between forest road and plot. Large dead, fallen, decaying maple lying across eastern edge of plot. On ice contact sedimentary association of Superior lobe with soils with loamy till and sandy and gravelly outwash parent material (from web soil survey). Birds heard during survey: red eyed vireo, white breasted nuthatch, least flycatcher. NPC could also be keyed to MHn35 due to presence of a couple of Lathyrus ochroleucus plants, but chose MHn47 because of relative abundance of species associated with rich forests. Saw tiny orange frog during survey. Entered elevation from 2' lidar contours.

Plot within designated old growth stand DC-4. Plot represents variation within stand, which alternates between a canopy of pure black ash to a mixed canopy of black ash, paper birch, and an occasional balsam. One particularly large tree within plot, otherwise tree sizes representative of stand. Several small diameter black ash and poplar snags. Numerous fallen trees (poplar?) at various states of decay in plot. Lots of smaller coarse woody debris. Birds heard during survey: red breasted nuthatch, common raven, blue jay, American goldfinch, black capped chickadee, blue headed vireo. Entered elevation from 2' lidar contours.

Designated old growth red pine stand DC-3. Foot path from NE Grade on W side of stand. Larger (ATV?) trail cuts through eastern tip of stand. Trees marked for harvest(?) on E edge of trail and old tree stand near UTM 568114, 5231841. Stand has rolling, fairly steep terrain with mature red and some white pine on ridges; sparse to very thick balsam understory. Some openings in 'valleys' with large balsam, paper birch, a few large quaking aspen, occasional white cedar. Plot representative of areas in stand dominated by red pine. Pines in plot are some of the older/larger within stand. Understory of balsam moderately dense, but not so dense as in areas with younger pines. UTM coordinates for plot are for NE corner of plot. Logging will occur ~100 m from the plot on the very edge of the stand. Some cut, decaying stumps at edge of stand and near plot. Occasional trash 20-30+ years old throughout the stand. Occasional dwarf mistletoe on balsam. Earthworm assessment rank 1 or 2.

Plot within designated old growth stand DC-2. Old growth red pine on ridges of relatively high elevation and on slopes. Balsam understory, dense in patches with openings from past blowdown. Plot reflects this mix. Lots of CWD, large downed trees (spp: white pine, balsam, quaking aspen, paper birch, white spruce) and snags. Occasional paper birch, aspen, spruce. Lowland ash and cedar swamps in depressions between ridges (but not near this plot). Plot is ~60% open blowdown 40% dense balsam understory. Some invasives in plot, probably due to close proximity to CR 4. Deer scat in plot, may transport seeds. Doubtful that this is indicative of quality of stand overall. Stand is large and mostly away from road - did not have time to scout majority of stand. Earthworm rapid assessment rank 1 or 2. Birds heard during survey: bluejay, common raven, red breasted nuthatch, northern waterthrush, broad winged hawk, American robin, pine warbler. Entered elevation from 2' lidar contours.

Plot selected to represent forested portion of rich water track feature. Contains high Sphagnum hummocks and deep hollows. Most hollows with deep standing water (ave. depth ~50 cm); Water table at or near peat surface.

Releve representative of level terrace along Kettle River (north). Stand with subtle levee near river and abundant microtopography. Plot straddles heterogeneity of stand, contains portion of narrow shallow trough (no obvious pool development). No evidence of recent flooding in stand.

Stand not typical of NPC - hypothesis: it succeeded from barrens oak savanna. Permanent marker magnet buried at NE corner and marked by pink flag. Canopy trees open grown to moderately open-grown. Young white pines have seeded in from nearby planted pines. In Sand Dunes State Forest, in area designated "Immediate Restoration Site #2." Very small amount of coarse woody litter. Releve collected for baseline monitoring. Basal area 1 provided on attached datasheet.

npc_type_name: Silver Maple - Green Ash - Cottonwood Terrace Forest
remarks: Terrace forest near the shore of Sturgeon Lake, which is connected to the Mississippi River. Canopy dominance by bur oak unusual for this type. Bur oaks are large diameter with open-grown forms; other canopy species similar in diameter. Little coarse woody litter.

Location source: Air photo + Topo map. Additional surveyor: Dave Arras. Canopy white spruce scattered within NPC. Dense patches of Abies balsamea scattered throughout. Low ash swales scattered in NPC. Snags uncommon. CWD small to medium size occasional, new to well-decayed. Large CWD absent. Worms assumed due to lack of leaf litter and bare soil. ATV trails within NPC. Patches of blow down scattered <1 acre each. Quercus macrocarpa within stand.
Plot 0.2 miles north of Sunday Lake. Beaver channels through plot. NPC with no standing water. Soil moist, NPC within FDn forest matrix. Litter type = leaves and grass.
Vegetation group: Lakeshore. Sunday Lake north shore inner vegetation zone +/- present between upland shoreline and outer veg zone captured by DNR Releve. NPC ~3-4 m wide at most.
NPC common on north shore of Sunday Lake in ~60 cm of water. NPC ~15 m wide and variously extends to bedrock or forest shoreline or to the vegetation zone captured by DNR Releve.

NPC 3 m from open water pool - the second vegetation zone out from water's edge. Black spruce AP surrounding. NPC ~ 3 m wide surrounding half of open water pool. Adjacent and parallel to DNR Releve A944. No standing water. Foot prints fill with ankle deep water.

NPC bordering 20 m x 5 m open water pool. Broken peat mat. Shallow open water patches interspersed with Sphagnum patches. NPC continues to water's edge. NPC within larger black spruce acid peatland. Next vegetation zone away from open water captured by DNR Releve A943. A787 captures next zone outward (low shrub poor fen). Dan Wovcha has photos.

DD Pop. trem and Quercus rubra snags patchy scattered. Plot between two bedrock openings. Oaks are open-grown. Apparently, no worms. Pine stumps scattered throughout. Several oaks are multi-stemmed. Stumps are well-decayed, all the same height and without signs of associated dead falls - assumed cut stumps. Historical logging camp(s) in vicinity. Dan Wovcha has photos. General soil texture: Silty Loam. Additional moss species on rocks and wood.
large white pines in stand near high point in peninsula. Basal areas 1 and 2 available on attached datasheet.

Peat mat along ~10 acre peatland lake in granite bedrock controlled topography. Peat firm, continues low rolling mat of sphagnum, only two small hummocks of Sphagnum fuscum. Hummocks increase in size away from lake toward black spruce forest. 3 acres.

Narrow 0.5 acre patch between open bog and 10 acre pond. Peat very loose and squishy and hummocks only 7-10 cm. Tops dry, hollows saturated Sphagnum. Sharp boundary between open bog where surface is ~ 10 cm higher and finer peat.

Fairly open black spruce stand in small (100 acre) peatland adjacent to pond. Plot in denser part. Water table just below hollows. Mostly low hummocks (7-10 cm) except for occasional 0.5 m hummock of Sphagnum fuscum.
Plot just into vast tamarack swamp of Agassiz Lake Plain.

Burned in fall 2011 by Pagami Creek fire in an area with vegetation characteristic of fire dependent NPCs. High burn severity, 0 tree survival. 8-10 downed trees half paper birch, half balsam fir similar size to standing. ~25% of cover open rock and boulders. ~100 m N of Island River. Surveyed for birds 2012-2016. E. Zlonis curator of bird data. Birds heard during survey: hairy woodpecker, eastern phoebe, gray jay, American goldfinch. Many grasshoppers, dragonflies: meadowhawks and darners. UTM coordinates mark plot corner at largest standing balsam fir. 135 degrees southeast to next corner, NE to third corner, etc.
Found earthworms when digging. Soil layer 1: Color = 10 yr 2/1. Soil layer 2: Color = 10 yr 6/3. Permanent marker type: rebar/magnet.
Mineral soil with organic material worked into it. Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/1. Soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 7/3. Permanent marker: rebar/magnet.
Grassy opening in ash/oak forest. General soil type: loam - sand. Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/1. Soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 6/3. Litter type: Leaves and grass. Permanent marker: magnet/rebar.
Lots of slash, no worms present or castings (contrary to info in soil tab. Aspect: WSW. Permanent marker: magnet/rebar. Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/1. Soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 46.
Lots of blowdown, trees planted. Permanent marker: magnet/rebar. Litter type: leaves and needles. Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/1; layer 2 color: 10 yr 6/2; layer 3: 10 yr 4/4.
Dark soil to about 6 cm, sandy underneath that. Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/1. Soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 4/6. Permanent marker: magnet/rebar.

Recently clearcut and planted to Pinus strobus. Planted trees were bud-capped last season and are now 1-2.5' tall. A few oaks and maples were left standing. Plot is on edge of old stumps and a little slash on plot. Soil layer 2: 1-2 cm rocks throughout this layer. Start color contrast from top layer to this. Soil layer 1 color: 7.5 yr/3/1; soil layer 2 color: 10 yr/5/3. Permanent marker notes: Magnet, orange (faded) flagging on 5" AC5A 18.0' @ 190', rebar with orange paint on top. Litter type: leaves and grass.

Fraxinus nigra stand 6"-14" DBH w/ 2" Betula papyrifera. 0 leaf litter + bare soil exposed. IRAT 5.  Permanent marker notes: magnet + yellow plastic stake. Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/2; soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 5/3.

Some ash trees have been girdled in plot and surrounding area. Litter type=leaves and grass. Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/1. Layer 2 color: 10 yr 6/2. Permanent marker type: magnet [no location reported - e.g. plot corner, plot center].
In ash forest, at songbird call-point. Litter type: leaves and sedges. Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/1; soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 6/2. Permanent marker type: magnet.

Deep ruts, just N of plot. Original round, yellow corner stakes at N and E corners. Pink flagging at center, pink flagging and triangular corner stakes at corners. *Plots on this transect are oriented diagonally. Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/1; Soil layer 2 color: 5 yr 7/1. Permanent marker type: magnet.
Permanent marker: magnet. Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/2. Soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 6/2. Deep ruts through S portion of plot parallel to azimuth.
Permanent marker: magnet. Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/2. Soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 4/1. Large tip-up in SE corner of plot.
Trail runs approx. N/S through center point. Permanent marker type: magnet. Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/2. Soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 6/2.
Permanent marker type: magnet. Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/2. Soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 6/3. Litter type: leaves and grass.
Permanent marker type: magnet. Litter type: leaves and grass. Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 3/1. Soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 6/.
Soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 4/3. Litter type: leaves and grass.
Soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 6/2. Litter type: grass and moss. Humus type: muck.
Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/1. Soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 6/2. Permanent marker type: magnet.
Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/1. Soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 6/3. Seasonal wetland just W of plot. Permanent marker type: magnet.
Soil layer 1 color: 10 yr 2/2. Soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 6/2. Permanent marker type: magnet.
Soil layer 1 color: 7.5 yr 3/2. Soil layer 2 color: 10 yr 7/2. Permanent marker type: magnet.

Mesic forest East of Lake Katrina. On stony, upland slope. Includes plant species data from Oct 5, 1977 surveyed by Dyhr and surveyed May 19, 1978 by Dorio. Walking Relevé. Many Acer saccharum seedlings observed during Spring survey. Approximate extent of plot is 9.5 acres.

Upland slopes. Most of Acer saccharum 12-inches or less, only a few larger. Although other D6 species are infrequent, most are 20-inches or better. Almost all D2-3 vegetation are not more than waist-high, and mostly below the knee. There are only a few very old stumps, that indicate any cutting of trees in the past. Walking releve. Surveyed on Sept 8, 1977 by Dyhr & May 18, 1978 by Dorio. Approximate area of plot is 4.5 acres.

Upland, gently sloped. This releve characterized by it's location. The canopy and shrub layers are variable throughout, ie; patches of D4 Acer saccharum, and extensive area of D2 Acer saccharum, pockets of Elm (some with Dutch Elm disease), others already removed. These were consolidated into the Releve since surrounding Releves distinguish it's boundaries fairly precisely. Note: there is one very large 6-8 inch diameter granite boulder on the SW end. Walking releve. Surveyed on Sept 8, 1977 by Dyhr & By Dorio on 5/18/78.

Upland slope and base of slopes near intermittent creek. Some old stumps, but very few. Occasional windfallen logs. Woody plants, D3-5 almost non-existent. Wide open understory. D3-4 plants slong S edge (alongside wet meadow) almost exclusively. Walking releve. Surveyed on 9/6/77 by Dyhr & on 5/18/78 by Dorio. Wood peewee seen in plot.

Very gently sloped uplands. Some diseased Elm removed on E edge. Characterized by continuous canopy dominated by Acer saccharum. D3 & D2 only patchy. D6 Quercus and Ulmus mostly on E & W edges. D4-5 practically absent. There are scattered windfalls and branches and only a few stumps and a continuous leaf mulch layer. As noted in 1st paragraph: Several very large Ulmus Americana on NE & N edges, 40-48 inch dbh. Walking releve. Surveyed on Sept 2, 1977 by Dyhr and on May 18, 1978 by Dorio. Approximate area of plot, 3.3 acres.

Upland slopes, cut logs-moss covered. This releve characterized by a mixed species canopy. The canopy has large gaps, under which D4-5 species predominate. Overall the variability in the strata throughout the Releve visually distinguishes this area, ie small areas look like #372, with patches of D4-5 sapling trees. Some logs, which were cut and are now moss-covered, are lying on the ground. A fenceline remains here (N-S). Walking releve. Approximate area of plot is 1.5 acres. Surveyed on 9/2/77 by Dyhr and by Dorio on 5/18/78(?).

S-facing slope. Boulders, stumps, 4-foot shrub edges. Characterized by predominance of Acer saccharum in canopy, wide open 5-50 foot strata and dense shrub and sapling layer at 4-5 feet. Most A. saccharum range from 10-20-inch with a few larger ones. Tilia, Quercus, and Ulmus are large trees (20-40 inch dbh. The southern edge is the meandered shore of L. Katrina. Here D4-5 species are dense, but only on that narrow strip. Only a few old stumps visible. This particular releve has so diseased elms removed, but log skidder went through here to #371. Along this path D2-3 species damaged. A few large granite boulders occur on the soil surface (2-4 foot diameter. Walking releve. Surveyed on 9/2/77 by Dyhr and on 5/18/78 by Dorio. The cover abundance value for Dicentra cucullaria is probably not indicative of it's true cover/abundance because it's dying back. Approximate area of plot is 1.9 acres.

Upland slopes. Characterized by D4 shrub layer and diverse canopy. Most Laportea Canadensis in north part of Releve. Many Acer saccharum seedlings. Walking releve. Surveyed by Dyhr on 9/1/77 and by Dorio on 5/18/78. Approximate area of plot is 1.6 acres.

E-facing slope. Note the lack of Sambucus as compared to #364. This is a narrow strip of Maple-Basswood. Canopy interrupted and dense D4-5 saplings along edges. Lots of leaf litter. This is a walking releve. Approximate area of plot is 1.2 acres. Surveyed on 9/1/77 by Dyhr and on 5/11/78 by Dorio.

Nearly level uplands. At least 6-10 seedling and young plants that could not be identified. This is a walking releve. Approximate area of plot is 5.8 acres. Surveyed on 9/1/77 by Dyhr and on 5/16/78 by Dorio.

Large old tree stumps. Large rocks in the ravine.West slope most diverse species. Surveyed on 7/29/77 by Hertz and on 5/17/78 by Dorio. This is a walking releve. Approximate area of plot is 7.5 acres.

place_name: Baker- E of Half Moon Lake
remarks: Numerous old tree stumps (dbh=15-30"). Elm almost non-existent on W 2/3 of releve. Dbh of A. saccharum appears to decline in E 1/3. Lots of leaf litter. This is a walking releve. Approximate area of plot is 34.5 acres.

Most herbaceous and seedling ground cover restricted to eastern 1/2 where there is also greatest density of A. saccharum. W 1/2 is influenced by upland shrub along fenceline. Lacks herbaceous and seedlings. West graduates into Intermediate Upland Forest. Large rocks on surface. Most diversity on lowest slopes. This is a walking releve. Approximate area of plot is 0.5 acres. Surveyed on 7/29/77 by Hertz and on 5/18/78 by Dorio.

Banks and adjacent uplands of intermittent stream. Characterized by D6 canopy, mostly A. saccharum in central area, Ulmus Americana on E end, and Ulmus-Fraxinus on W level. This is the same ravine as in #299 & 300, but here it resembles a larger intermittent stream bed. The forest resembles a stream bed to floodplain-type forest. An aspen clone (50" diameter occurs on the S edge of Relevé and is expanding into adjacent grassland. Canopy trees range from 8-20" dbh. Mostly 12" or less. The south bank and uplands contained the most diversity especially Thalictrum dioicum, Anemone quinquefolia, and cf Lathyrus ochroleucus. This is a walking Relevé. Approximate area of plot is 2.3 acres. Surveyed on 7/29/77 by Dyhr and on 5/18/78 by Dorio.

place_name: Baker-N of Cartway along Co Rd 19
remarks: Upland, rolling, some small depressions. Two woodcock flushed along NW side, along pasture fence line. Two fox squirrels also observed. This is a walking Relevé. Approximate area of plot is 17.6 acres. Surveyed on 6/16/77 & 10/27/77 by Dyhr.

Large D6 Acer saccharum dominate here with very little shrub layer except for scattered colonies of mostly Ostrya and some Acer saccharum. NE edge- Acer saccharum (D6) gradates into D4 saplings. Fraxinus and Ulmus mostly restricted to outer boundaries. This is a walking Relevé. Approximate area is 2.4 acres. Surveyed by Hertz on 7/22/77 by Hertz and on 5/19/78 by Dorio.

place_name: Baker-N slope, N of Half Moon Lake
remarks: Steep, sloping terrain. Little intermediate-sized growth here. Mostly consisting of taller trees and small saplings and large number of seedlings. This is a walking Relevé. Approximate area of plot is 9.7 acres. No spring survey recorded for this site.
Located on hill. Mowed trail borders this Relevé on east end. This is a walking Relevé. Approximate area is 4.0 acres. No spring survey at this site recorded.

Stream flowing westerly. Water flowing west from ~24-inch culvert under road. Small minnows in stream. Boundaries are not exact due to poor map. Mowed trail passes through near western boundary (culvert under it) running N-S and swings east near northern boundary. This is a walking Relevé. Approximate area of plot is 10.6 acres. No spring survey done at site.
South-facing slope. This is a walking Relevé. Approximate area of plot is 0.2 acres. No spring survey done at this site.
South-facing slope. About dozen beehives on north edge in small clearing. This is a walking releve. Approximate area is 1.3 acres. No spring survey done at this site.
No supplemental notes recorded. This is a walking releve. Approximate area of plot is 13.7 acres. No spring survey done at this site.

Locate on hill and slopes. Observed old metal thing in plot-looks like a peaked top of some kind of grain storage bin. This is a walking Relevé. Approximate area of plot is 19.6 acres. No record of spring survey done at this site.
Located in a ravine sloping north. This is a walking releve. Approximate area of plot is 1.0 acre. No spring survey recorded for this site.
Located on NE-facing slope. This is a walking releve. Approximate area of plot is 0.1 acres. No spring survey recorded for this site.

place_name: Lake Rebecca- E of L. Rebecca
remarks: Located on N-facing slope. Large rocks. Ends at former opening on East. This is a walking Relevé. Approximate area of plot is 1.4 acres. No spring survey recorded at this site.

place_name: Lake Rebecca- S of Lake Rebecca
remarks: Plot has large rocks. Southern boundary is a deep ditch. Approximate area of plot is 1.5 acres. This is a walking releve.

Plot has logged stumps. Characterized by D4-5 Carya, Acer saccharum, and Ostrya. North boundary is a steep ditch. Water entering through culvert from across the highway. This water flows into marsh known as Relevé #121. Horse trail runs from E to W. Approximate area of plot is 19.7 acres. This is a walking Relevé.

place_name: Lake Rebecca- S of Roy Lake
remarks: Plot is upland, slopes and hilltop. Mixed-age class canopy with mature trees (12-30") scattered and numerous small diameter (6-12") D6 trees throughout. Species distribution variable, generally not very homogenous, except characterized by continuous canopy, sparse to patchy understory and numerous species of herbaceous groundcover plants. Approximate area of plot is 8.3 acres. This is a walking Relevé.

place_name: Lake Rebecca- W of Lake Rebecca
remarks: Plot on slopes and moist flats. Forty-five species of herbaceous plants. Cuscuta will be eliminated by bike trail. Approximate area of plot is 3.3 acres. This is a walking Relevé.

place_name: Lake Rebecca- S of Lake Rebecca
remarks: Logged stumps in plot. Characterized by D4-5 Acer saccharum and Xantho americanum. Ends where shrub layer is almost non-existent. Also 5.5 Laportea canadensis is abundant. Approximate area of plot is 5.7 acres. This is a walking Relevé.

place_name: Lake Rebecca- South of Lake Rebecca
remarks: Logged stumps in plot. Large rocks. This Relevé is dominated by Tilia americana and Carya cordiformis in the D5 layer. Also it is dominated by Prunus virginiana in all shrub layers. Approximate area of plot is 3.1 acres. This is a walking Relevé.

On N-facing slope. Large rocks and junk pile. This Relevé is an isolated stand that borders a sedge meadow on W and brome grass field on N, E, & S. Approximate area of plot is 0.4 acres. This is a walking Relevé.
No written comments recorded on form. This is a walking releve. Approximate area of plot is 3.8 acres.
No comments recorded on form. Area of this plot is 6.2 acres, determined by T. Dyhr on 4/77. This is a walking releve.

place_name: Elm Creek Park- Bordering Co Rd
remarks: Site includes area, a small basin on W side which is more open with fewer trees. This is a walking releve. Area of plot is 5.9 acres, determined by T. Dyhr on 4/77.
Area of plot is 8.8 acres, determined by T. Dyhr on 4/77. This is a walking releve.

place_name: Elm Creek- Diamond Creek Crosses Road
