remarks: Located a slope up form the creek. Area of plot is 2.2 acres, determined by T. Dyhr in 4/77. This is a walking releve.

place_name: Elm Creek- North side of Diamond Creek
remarks: Plot has organic soil. The difference in the percent seedlings and saplings in #010 & 008 are blended in this compartment. Area of plot is 7.0 acres, determined by T. Dyhr in 4/77. This is a walking releve.
This releve is park-like in appearance. A road cut runs through this releve N-S. Plot located on North & West slopes. Approximate area of plot is 9.3 acres. This is a walking releve.

Plot located on upland slopes and hilltops. Characterized by mature Q. rubra and Acer saccharum with scattered mature Ostrya; a very open understory (D2-4). Oak wilt is active on SE end (see #653 where oak wilt has wiped out the canopy) and could pose a serious problem on W 2/3 of this area, if not arrested. Most A. saccharum on E edge. Surveyed by Dyhr on Sept 20, 1977. Herbaceous monitoring only done on May 24, 1978 by Dorio. Approximate area of plot is 5.0 acres. This is a walking Relevé.

Located on upland slopes. Characterized by diverse canopy of mature trees and abundant D4, D5 vegetation. There are not many large trees, most are ~12" dbh or less, but there are a few larger. Cut stumps are numerous. These are well-rotted, but intact. This Relevé is not that much different from adjacent ones. There seems to be no real distinct blocks in this whole forested area. Changes are very subtle, i.e.; in density of canopy trees and understory density. Choice of these Relevés has been somewhat arbitrary. Several well-used deer trails here. There are numerous chipmunks and squirrels. This is a very large Relevé. Approximate area of plot is 6.6 acres. Surveyed by Dyhr on 9/14/77 & 5/24/78 (herbaceous survey only). This is a walking Relevé.

Located on upland slopes. Characterized by predominance of A. saccharum in canopy and only a patchy understory. Many places the understory is open and parklike. There are numerous cut stumps, well-aged and rotted, but still intact. Cut logs were seen occasionally, never taken out. One pile of old logs was encountered. Surveyed by Dyhr on 9/13/77 & 5/24/78 (herbaceous survey only). Scarlet tanager and Cuckoo seen in plot in May 78. Approximate area of plot is 7.7 acres. This is a walking Relevé. Additional notes on D6-7c layer: most of bigger trees obviously cut out years ago, ie; stumps present yet.

West 1/2 dominated by Elm and Tilia with only an occasional D6 A. saccharum, but 25-50% of area with D4-5 A. saccharum. Approximately the East 1/3 and SE 1/4 is characterized by D6 A. saccharum, which continues down E slope of large N-S ravine. Many old tree stumps from previous logging. Surveyed by Hertz on 9/20/77 and Dyhr & Dorio on 5/25/78 (herbaceous monitoring only). Approximate area of plot is 32.4 acres. This is a walking Relevé.

Very steep N-facing slope adjacent to intermittent stream bed. Most ground cover absent with little detritus. Bare soil characterized by steep slope. Bounded by stream bed (N), field (S), change in understory on W and change in cover on E. Surveyed on 8/22/70 by Dyhr and on 5/25/78 by Dorio (herbaceous monitoring only, Morel mushrooms observed). On south side of ravine. Approximate area of plot is 1.3 acres. This is a walking releve.

On E-facing slope. Area is characterized by dense D4-5 component. Mature trees don't form continuous canopy. Vegetation nearly absent on ground and litter layer absent or thin on E end. Note relative absence of mature maple, but saplings common, suggesting an upcoming change in the canopy. Diseased elms removed just recently. Plot bounded by old driveway on E, meadow on S, and field on N. West boundary arbitrary. Relevé #353 changes to a stand with less dense D4-5 species. Windfall logs frequent, and some old cut stumps present. Within this Relevé area there is one very small, closed basin with no canopy. Urtica gracilis, Polygonum sagittatum, Cirsium arvense, Lappula echinata, Arctium lappa are the major species there. Approximate area of plot is 7.4 acres. Surveyed by Dyhr both on 8/24/77 & 5/25/78. Spring survey for herbaceous species only. Swainson's thrush observed in plot. This is a walking Relevé. NPC type noted as "Intermediate Upland Forest- Basswood 2f".

West boundary is where Juniperus begin. A few D3-4 Acer saccharum scattered throughout and the remainder are seedlings, along with dense H2 ground cover. Surveyed by Hertz on 10 August 1977 & by Dorio on 22 May 1978 (herbaceous survey only). Morel mushrooms observed in plot. Water in creek. Three to five species of forbs unidentifiable. Approximate area of plot is 1.6 acres. This is a walking releve.
On E-facing steep slope. Between road and grassland. Approximate area of plot is 1.9 acres. This is a walking releve.

Upland slope with deep ravine cut in (20-30' vertical drop in W end). Only on W end is Laportea not continuous. Some large elms removed (STDC) on W edge. Approximate area of plot is 16.9 acres. This is a walking Relevé.

Nearly level with small, poorly drained depressional areas. Typical Mesic Forest understory, i.e.; very open, D3 & D4 barely present. Abundant Acer saccharum, with D3-4 A. saccharum & Tilia on edges and where canopy gaps occur. Should be checked in Spring.  Approximate area of plot is 5.0 acres. This is a walking Relevé.

On upland, hilltop and steep adjacent slopes. This area is surrounded by emergent aquatic bog except the S edge which is an old fence line. Numerous old cut stumps and rarity of large diameter trees are evidence of extensive cutting here. There are a few large diameter Tilia and Ulmus though. Also, STDC work was done here during 1976-1977. Some diseased wood was burned on N tip just last week. Younger D5 trees are relatively dense on NW 1/3, otherwise they are not abundant. Approximate area of plot is 21.1 acres. Surveyed on 18 Oct 1977 by Dyhr and on 23 May 1978 by Dorio. This is a walking Relevé.
Surveyed by Hertz on 12 Oct 1977 & by Dorio on 23 May 1978 (herbaceous layer only) - 2 forb species unidentifiable. Approximate area of plot is 22.0 acres. This is a walking Relevé.

On steep slopes. NPC type listed as "Intermediate Upland Forest". Characterized by pole-size trees, especially Carya, which have reached canopy height, and topography, i.e., slope adjacent to marsh. Approximate area of plot is 1.4 acres. This is a walking Relevé.

Red pine plantation with scattered jack pine, paper birch, and bur oak; hazel abundant in mid story, furrowed micro topography. Yellow stakes at corners of plot. Bearing trees to locate plot listed on "ECS transect/plot relocation sheet".

Furrowed regenerating pine-oak stand. Overstory of sparce mature red pines and pin/bur oak. Understory of pine and oak saplings. Some jack pine. Overgrown logging road west of plot. Unable to find original releve plot. Plot re-established. Field notes from 1999 call plot "lost". Hazelnuts w/ disease.

Original releve not found; plot re-established @ UTM location. Few tall red pines; jack pine, paper birch, and bur oak also present in canopy; dense hazel understory; hummucky & furrowed microtopography.

Furrowed red pine plantation. Young trees ~2-6" dbh. Canopy mixed red pine, jack pine, quaking aspen. Cherry, hazelnut, bur oak understory. Old logging road SW of plot. Unable to relocate original releve established in 1988, plot re-established at UTM location w/ 280 degree diagonal.

See also ECS transect/plot relocation sheet. Releve not typical of stand: at edge of red pine plantation and aspen regen. Plot re-established near site of old releve 1273 plot when no evidence of old plot was found-; followed hummocky microtopography; slope varies from 4-8% and is N-facing; stand has been cut within last 20 yrs.

See also ECS transect/plot relocation sheet. Mature red pine stand with bur oak/red maple understory. Shrub layer open. Northern 1/4 of stand sloping to the north, the rest +/- flat crest. Past thinning: living trees painted yellow.

See also ECS transect/plot relocation sheet. Middle-aged red pine stand w/red oak, bur oak, and red maple sub canopy; abundant hazel cover; no evidence of old plot found, plot re-established at UTM location.

See also ECS transect/plot relocation sheet. Mid-aged furrowed red pine plantation w/red oak understory and +/- open shrub layer. Original plot not found, plot re-established at UTM location with a 60 degree diagonal.

See also ECS transect/plot relocation sheet. Marker type: rebar at center, yellow corner stakes. Young regenerating stand with Populus tremuloides. Quercus macrocarpa overstory. Red pine forest to the NW, marshy area to the SE. Plot sits on the crest and northern slope of hummock. Center relocated, corners re-established in a diamond pattern with a diagonal of 178 degrees.

See also ECS transect/plot relocation sheet. Young regenerating red pine stand w/ some bur oak and abundant hazel, center magnet relocated, but no corners found; plot re-established w/ diagonal bearing of 178 degrees.

See also ECS transect/plot relocation sheet. Very nice mature red pine stand with red maple, red oak, paper birch midstory and open understory. Area +/- level with hummocks throughout. Center magnet near the base of young ash tree.

See also ECS transect/plot relocation sheet. Red pine-white pine stand. Recent skid trail passes through north-west half of plot. Center marker near the base of ~8"dbh white pine tree. Roughly half of plot has been recently disturbed (w/in the last 5 years), remaining plot was previously thinned (+/- 15 years).
See also ECS transect/plot relocation sheet. Plot in close proximity to cut, and thinning has occurred in plot within last ~15 years.

See also ECS transect/plot relocation sheet. Mature red pine stand with red maple, white pine, paper birch midstory. Diverse ground cover. Plot center SW of tagged ~30" dbh red pine (bird plot 84??). Red pine tip up in center of plot going E-W. Surface of plot very uneven with many hummocks and depressions. Unable to locate original releve plot, plot re-established.

See also ECS Transect/plot relocation sheet. Red pine canopy, paper birch & red maple subcanopy. Charcoal on red pine and ground suggest fire within ~last 15 years; abundant red maple regen. Metal tag on paper birch near plot center; yellow corner stakes.
See also ECS Transect/plot relocation sheet. Mature red pine stand w/ scattered White pine, Red Oak & Paper birch in subcanopy.
See also ECS Transect/plot relocation sheet. Yellow stakes in corners of plot.
See also ECS Transect/plot relocation sheet. Any factor affecting the vegetation- windfall, fire, disease, logging. Plot windthrown, red pine top in center, 3" red oak at plot center.
See also ECS Transect/plot relocation sheet. Overstory of mature red pine; paper birch and bur oak subcanopy; abundant hazel.

See also ECS Transect/plot relocation sheet. Releve- lower quality- regenerating cut area. Regenerating red pine stand. Sparse overstory of mature red pine ~10-22 dbh. Understory dense hazelnut. Young red oak ~15' just east of the plot, logging road just south of plot. Some scattered rotten and burnt stumps in area.

A peat apron feature with an interrupted canopy of tamarack with occasional black ash; shrub layer is minimal with red osier; ground layer primarily graminoids (Carex aquatilis) but includes Carex sterilis and Carex prairea. Associated with Deep Lake. Well-developed hummocks observed. Strong carbonate layer with 30 inches of peat; evidence of remnant flark (21-26").
Calcareous fen feature sloping into a basin; graminoid dominated with Eleocharis rostellata and Carex sterilis. Exposed marl pools with U. intermedia.

A small calcareous fen pocket dominated by graminoids including Carex sterilis and surrounded by Wet Meadow (WM). C. sterilis is abundant on the perimter of the feature. WM portion with surface water (C. aquatilis/C. pellita. Transitions to a poor fen dominated by C. lasiocarpa.

Peatland system of stunted black spruce (<5m) with occasional cedar and tamarack; linear feature bordered by taller conifer cover. Graminoid cover mainly T. cespirosum; Betula pumila. Patterned Peatlands. Photo 3164.

Forested peatland/tamarack swamp; canopy interrupted with dead individuals (still upright), but mortality not recent. Down woody debris common throughout with sphagnum and small open pools. Photo 3333. Calla in pool pockets.

Releve collected to document the shift in community structure and composition in relation to Rel #B080. Canopy of tamarack and black spruce; limited shrub cover. Mainly brown mosses/feather mosses. Diversity poor.

Forested peatland; tamarack canopy and appears uniform in size and continuous (12-15m). Very limited understory/shrub component. Limited black spruce generally less than 2.5m and infrequent white cedar (which increases in cover/dominant to the south of the releve plot. Includes shallow (small) pools with Menyanthes and Calla palustris. 3363

Releve to represent wet prairie that was grazed in the past but has had a number of years to recover. Outside of releve is a large area of similar vegetation as well as some areas of wet meadow affinity and small areas of degraded aspen upland.

Releve located on top of an over-washed beach ridge. The area was more open in historical photography, but scattered trees were present. This area is one of the driest portions of the community and spruce trees are less common here than to the east. Andropogon is strongly dominant through the entire area.

Oak woodland located on beach ridge.This releve represents the majority of this area which is strongly dominated by bur oak. The area included in this releve is more open at the east end, which captures the variation in canopy cover that is typical in this area. A low cover of CWD is present and no past cutting is obvious. At a broader scale this community contains many aspen clones that have been recently cut, these areas are not represented in the releve.

In flark of poor fen water track. Placed to capture part of flark with little/no Rhychospora fusca and solid carpet of Sphagnum. Plot covers nearly entire width of flark, with Carex lasiocarpa possibly expanding from higher hummocks in string to north. One small pool with standing water <1 sq meter. There is C. oligosperma nearby, but in plot it all appears to be C. lasiocarpa. Water sample collected, but reading of 3.36 is not possible. EFP waypoint 095 at plot center. Not in exact location of Rel 4189. PVC pipes at southwest and northeast corners, w/ tag #80 at SW, tag #81 at NE.

In flark of poor fen water track. Rectangular shape chosen to avoid strings to north and south. Northeast corner of plot is at edge of string. Placement made to capture part of flark with little Sphagnum cover and lots of Rhynchospora fusca. Standing water throughout most of plot - in a wet year. Water sample gave a questionable reading. EFP waypoint 096 at plot center. Not in exact location of Rel 4188. PVC pipes at NW & NE corners of plot (5m N-S, 20m E-W). NW pipe has tag #82, NE w/ tag #83. 3m tall, 5cm dbh Larix w/ tag #84 is 110cm @ 50degrees from NE corner

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Plot centered at hemlock #1. Old gully runs through center of plot, but appears long-stabilized with large Picea glauca growing in it, though upper end dominated by young trees. Two old cut Thuja stumps in plot, and one Pinus strobus. Acer spicatum has been browsed. Tsuga seedlings on P strobus stump and nearby. Several large conifer logs, well-decayed. Basal Area Measurement counts at prism plots 1&2; T canadensis(L) 1,0; P glauca(L) 2,2; A balsamea(L) 5,4; B alleghaniensis(L) 3,3; T occidentalis(L) 1,4. EFP waypoint 098 is at center of plot where hemlock tree #1 has metal tag. Mosses counted only when growing on soil. Soil core done outside gully.

Open mudslide with most recent movement in June 2012. Upper slope lost a lot of soil with small eroding rivulet channels showing continuing erosion. Lower portion of plot had significant deposition in addition to some deep eroding channels. One small portion of original topsoil at bottom corner, possibly slid from above. Plot N-S-E-W w/ southwest corner at top. Cobbles scattered over soil surface. Directly west from southwest corner it is 7.5m to edge of bluff where water flows from small swale and another 17.5m directly west to 25cm dbh Thuja near road. EFP waypoint 118 at plot center.

Plot is N-S-E-W on open mudslide with most recent large movement in June 2012, with small eroding rivulets showing continuing erosion. Southwest corner is 4m directly north of 40cm dbh Thuja still standing in middle of slide. Loose cobbles and gravel cover ~25% of surface. EFP waypoint 188 at plot center.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Plot w/ 4 tagged hemlock trees just above narrow open creek corridor. Mudslides most recently moved in June 2012 are on both sides of plot, which is enclosed in a mesh deer exclosure. Some very old rotten logs, but little recent CWD. Deer browsing on maple during time fence was down (after mudslide). One cut pine stump, still maintaining complete shape. Larger Pinus strobus (>60cm) OP. Plot is irregular shape, approx. 350 sq meters, filling lower part of deer exclosure bounded on NW & SE sides by mudslides. Upper boundary of plot is delimited by a line starting at a 15cm dbh Picea glauca that is 6.5m uphill along eastern fenceline from hemlock #5 and heading due west to western fenceline. Basal Area Measurement counts at prism plots 1&2: T canadensis(L) 1,0; T americana(L) 0,2; T occidentalis(L) 20,9; P strobus(L) 1,2; A balsamea(L) 0,1. Measured plot sides: E side 24.5m, N side 15 (25?)m, W side 15m, S side 21m.

Relatively even-aged Fraxinus with a few old large trees and some small too. Pools cover 80% of area, but are dry now. Deeper portions (30%) are covered in cf Drepanocladus moss (and others). Some fallen trunks/branches up to 20cm dbh, but no larger logs. Winter road nearby - probably logged a long time ago. Platanthera has been browsed. Basal Area Measurement counts from prism plots 1&2: F nigra(L) 17,9; B papyrifera(L) 0,1; B papyrifera(D) 0,2. EFP waypoint 128 near plot center.

Pools cover ~40% of plot, dry now, mostly moss-covered. Painted section line runs through plot just north of center. Lots of logs of fallen Abies and Picea. A few very old mossy stumps possibly were cut. Basal Area Measurement counts from prism plots 1&2: T occidentalis(L) 11,19; P mariana(L) 2,1; P balsamifera(L) 1,0; B papyrifera(L) 1,0; A balsamea(L) 0,4; A balsamea(D) 0,3. EFP waypoint 133 near plot center.

Picea mariana dominated area of larger Thuja swamp. Just to northeast is small area of blowdown. No Thuja stumps observed here, but there are many closer to Young's Bay. Only a few small Picea logs. Moss-covered hollows cover ~40% of plot. No standing water. Some Picea mortality due to mistletoe. Thuja regeneration appears unbrowsed. Basal Area Measurement counts for prism plots 1&2: P mariana(D) 3,2; P mariana(L) 10,11; T occoidentalis(L) 1,10. EFP waypoint 140 is near plot center.

Forests on this "island" of sandy soil vary with depth to groundwater, with mosaic of wet Thuja, wet Fraxinus, and paludifying Populus-Picea mariana. Releve represents driest end of spectrum. Picea is larger here than nearby, where canopy has opened by fallen Picea and Abies, but Thuja is smaller here, probably due to dryness. Lots of fallen Abies in plot, but no large logs. One granite rock. May be FDn43b, but moss carpet suggests FDn32. Basal Area Measurement counts for prism plots 1&2: P glauca(L) 3,5; A balsamea(L) 4,3; B papyrifera(L) 2,2; A balsamea(D) 0,1; T occidentalis(L) 0,4. EFP waypoint 168 is near plot center. Mosses recorded from ground only, not logs.

Lower part of June 2012 mudslide where it removed soil between 2 Tsuga trees. Patch of Cornus in center of plot where less soil was removed. Eroding gully ~30cm deep and 30cm wide runs through plot. Upper part of slode is steeper with sparser vegetation. Tsuga tree #9 with metal tag marks northwest corner of N-S-E-W plot, with west side downhill. EFP waypoint 190 marks Tsuga #9.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Intermittent creek runs through old growth mixed conifer-hardwood down to main creek. There has been some soil slumping near intermittent creek in past, but not during June 2012 event. CWD of all sizes and decay classes. Basal Area Measurement counts at prism plots 1&2: P strobus(L) 3,0; P strobus(D) 0,1; B alleghaniensis(L) 1,1; P glauca(L) 2,0; T occidentalis(L) 2,0; Q rubra(L) 1,0; A saccharum(L) 0,1; B papyrifera(L) 0,6; A rubrum(L) 0,2.  74cm Pinus strobus near bottom of slope is at EFP waypoint 173, southwest corner of N-S-E-W plot. A 76cm P strobus sits at northwest corner.

Some fallen Betula and Populus of various sizes. Old, seldom-used ATV trail passes outside northeast corner of plot. On slight rise with wetlands on most sides and wet Populus transition zones. There has been deer browse in past few years, but very little in past year. Soil at 46cm deep in impenetrable to soil probe. Wet from recent rain to that depth. Magnet buried 34cm deep at plot center. Basal Area Measurement counts at plots 1&2: Picea mariana(L) 3,0; P glauca(D) 1,0; P tremuloides(L) 4,5; Abies(L) 2,1.

Within large area of wet-mesic Populus tremuloides forest, mostly 15-20cm dbh average, but patches like this a little larger. Heavily used deer trails converge in plot. Trails and other depressions have standing water after recent heavy rain. Soil surface is wet, but below it is dry and becomes impenetrable to soil probe at 55cm. Magnet buried 35cm deep. Basal Area Measurements for plots 1&2: P tremuoides(L) 6,6; Abies(D) 1,0; Acer rubrum(L) 1,2; Fraxinus nigra(L) 0,1; P tremuloides(D) 0,1

On rise surrounded by wet forest + wetlands. Upslope of plot is drier w/ more Pleurozium + Linnaea + many P. strobus + resinosa. 1 large P resinosa log OP. Lots of mossy P tremuloides logs. Dense layer of Abies ~5-7m tall dead, presumably budworm, but layer ~10m tall alive. Eurybia browsed. Dendrobaena seen in leaf litter. Charcoal at surface of soil. Top 3cm leached gray. Lycopus and other wetland plants are scattered sparsely throughout. Dead Abies stems not measured, but basal area counts of 5 and 8. Moss recorded from rocks and soil, but not wood.

Plot fairly flat but slopes to the NW outside of plot and locally slopes south and is near FDn22 rock outcrop. Old cut stumps visible, coarse woody debris and snags present. Good microtopography from moss-covered woody debris. Deer scat and browse common. Lack of recent fire and little pine regeneration; higher amounts of canopy red pine outside of plot. Witches broom seen on 10 m tall balsam fir. Dried up wet hollows with labrador tea punctuate the plot. Drainage is somewhat excessively; bedrock depth unknown but rocky impasse occurred at 55 cm. Charcoal was seen in humus layer - fire history may have caused humus to change from mor to moder. Horizon description with depth: 'E' coarse loamy sand, black-gray; 'Bs' coarse loamy sand to coarse sand, bright orange; 'BC' or 'C' moist coarse sand, muted gray. Pooling occurred at bottom of pit, possibly due to recent rain events.

Slope is near 0%; barely NW aspect. Context is on an upper slope flat with undulating topography. An interesting spot that gradually slopes up from FPn62a to the east. Much of stand is low gradient, barely upland forest with high water table and/or bedrock close to surface causing ponding in early spring. Landform is bouldery but no exposed ROn/FDn22 typical of bedrock complexes. It has a feel of a black spruce poor conifer swamp with sparse needle/leaf litter layer. Mineral soil horizon 'A' black-brown with high organic component; fine roots common. Texture is gritty. A nearby tip-up did show deeper soil with cobbles, 15-35% volume, and more color development in a B-horizon sandy loam. Another tip-up shows stones and may be reason for impeded digging. Plot with good coarse woody debris and snags. Abundant deer scat though low browse impact - perhaps a place for winter cover. Tree diameters small to medium, cutting has occurred in past but nothing recently.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Decent coarse woody debris plus some snapped off trunks. Logging and roads nearby to the northeast. Deer browse commonly seen. Very few standing pools - surface mostly dry. Water was detected 21 cm below surface. Middens present and litter occurs in sparse patches. First soil horizon black and highly wormed with abundant castings and very few fine roots. Second horizon gray with orange mottles starting at 15 cm. Soil below depth of soil pit likely silty clay.

Surrounding matrix communities of ROn23, ROn12, and FDn22. Farther south, turns to FDn22. Percentage of truly exposed rock is 5%, but 30% when including crustose lichen growing on surface. Rocks wet after previous night's thunderstorm. Coarse woody debris and snags common, but no evidence of recent fire. Significant deer browse. None of the Asteraceae spp. even close to flowering at time of survey.

Deer browse moderate but higher to the north in WFn53 cedar swamp. Standing water measured in pools; water at bottom of soil pit was very cold. Tip-ups and downed woody debris common. No cutting evident.

Mostly flooded at time of survey though patches of dry mucky spots exist among pools. Therefore, worm presence/impact cannot be discerned and soil description difficult (texture estimated). Plot situated in FFn67a with some risers/berms caused by differential flood deposits and treefall; no terrace FFn57 seen in stand. Park-like canopy trees with very little shrub stratum. Abundant coarse woody debris and slight windrowing. No cut stumps present. Moderate amounts of deer browse. Groundcover plants concentrated on downed logs.

place_name: Rat Root Lake West Water Track
remarks: Small pools scattered throughout plot/stand. Depth of standing water ranges from 4-10 cm; pH 5.5-5.6. Plot located in incipient water track with higher pH than transitional APn91 and APn81 surrounding. Tall Sphagnum hummocks (up to 55 cm) present, but for the most part, flat hollows of inundated pools make up 10-15% of plot.

Within-plot slope generally gentle, but slope off of island knob to adjacent MHn44 25-100%. Nearby cutting especially on lower slopes; some hummocks may be very old cedar stumps from long ago logging. No fire in long time as evident by dog hair balsam fir. High deer browse with very little cedar regeneration. Medium diameter snags and coarse woody debris, mostly of cedar. Thick humus layer with good fine roots with underlying black A-horizon sandy loam (almost sandy clay loam), pH 4.0-4.25. Vaccinium myrtilloides cover greater than V. angustifolium.

Stand has experienced harvesting of some pines but stumps are moderately decayed and soft; appears some cedar cut but most are dying naturally now as evident by large cedar coarse woody debris. Past fire likely facilitated pine dominance. Foot trail skirts western plot boundary by one meter; hunting blinds nearby. Eastern boundary a low swale with wet-mesic species. There are large patches of thick duff and no groundcover species. Fine roots present in black Oa humus. Semi-permeable layer does not exhibit mottling, just a consistent dull tan, muted orange color. Third horizon bordering on a sandy clay loam. Soil horizon color and pH by depth: black, 5.5; brown-tan, 6.5; tan-orange 5.5.

Slope is short; plot spans both upper and middle slopes. Plot located between exposed rock outcrop to the east and low slope flat of MHn44 to the west. Snags and coarse woody debris abundant; stumps throughout stand. A few boulders punctuate landscape. Plot was shoehorned in to capture FDn43, but some wetter species occurred nonetheless. Charcoal ring 8 cm below surface and beneath thick humus layer (though as thin as 2 cm in places). Fine roots throughout humus. No real A-horizon but mineral black soil does exist as thin band above charcoal. Soil pH of mineral horizons in descending depth (5.0, 5.0, 5.5). Third horizon also has cobbles at a volume of 60-90% in addition to gravel. Soil color in descending depth (tan, tan orange, rust orange). Texture is barely a coarse loamy sand; could be straight sand. Soil felt moist at bottom of pit.

Plot within a water track but still fairly acidic and nutrient poor. Good condition with no threats and natural flowing hydrology. Other parts of water track exhibit incipient string-flark pattern but has yet to be organized, and flora doesn't reflect a highly minerotrophic water chemistry. Other parts of water track with Menyanthes trifoliata, Carex limosa, and Betula pumila.

Within designated old growth stand, but plot doesn't seem to exhibit old growth characteristics. Plot straddles both middle and lower slopes - MHn44c downslope and FDn32a upslope. Boulders present upslope. Plot located in ecotonal NPC, FDn43a best guess. Steepest slope 14% but grades to 3-4% on low slope. Coarse woody debris present but no large logs or those of old decay class. No large snags. Stumps seen in stand but not in plot. Soil pit dug to 59 cm below humus and soil was very wet, possibly due to heavy rain the night before survey. Pooling at bottom of pit was 11 cm deep. Needle litter patchy. Charcoal mixed in with humus - dark black humus appearing more moder than mor. First mineral horizon very uniform putty brown-tan color and where all cobbles occur. Despite wetness, no mottling or gray matrix detected. However, soil texture becomes heavier with depth suggesting possible semi-permeable layer below excavated pit. Moderately well drained may be more appropriate.

Wildlife trail runs through plot. Some moderate browsing seen on bog birch. Native plant community shows both FPn62a and Fpn71a attributes. A few old stumps occur, likely of natural mortality; no evidence of logging. Water at bottom of soil pit was uncomfortably cold. Standing water pools sparse at time of survey.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Topographic context mostly flat but there is some slight sloping due to flood deposition; slope toward plot center. Some walking trails and/or game trails crisscross stand and plot. Good coarse woody debris and snags. Worm castings and middens present. Deer browse evident on ash saplings. Top A-horizon is black clay loam and is coarser and more crumbly than underlying gray E-horizon, which is cemented together.

place_name: East Rat Root River Shrub Water Track
remarks: Plot within water track and shrub dominated. Few open pools, patchy distribution. Farther south, water track ends at FPn71 with dense black spruce and tall bog birch (before meeting access winter road). Soil pit with abundant undecayed wood and roots.

place_name: East Rat Root River Forested Peatland
remarks: Community forms terminal end of water track that originates in northeast. Tall hummocks and hollows are generally still with some shallow water. Overstory dominated by Picea mariana suggesting FPn71 but groundcover and degree of surface water suggests more FPn81. Unsure of cutting history; no cut stumps evident. Some coarse woody debris present.

Community forms a marginal bog drain from APn80a1 to the north. Canopy is thin and reflects high water of drain and influence of water track. Peat is on verge of mucky peat. Not many minerotrophic mosses found. The hollows are fully inundated during time of survey. Tall hummocks composed of acidic mosses.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Slope, aspect, and topo context difficult to interpret due to dips and rises inherent within landform and plot. Terrace is about 10 m above water level and probably rarely experiences inundation. Topography is undulating even within terrace with dips and rises running roughly E-W lengthwise. Many large trees were cut so size distribution relatively small. Surrounding areas farther from plot are MHn46a trembling aspen dominated and of small diameter. Severe deer browse on most of the Laportea. No large snags. Few large coarse woody debris, mostly small size classes. Top soil horizon with abundant worm castings, dark brown-black and pH 7.0. Lower horizon dark brown and pH 8.0. Very calcareous medium loamy sand lower horizon. Some middens present and many worms seen in soil pit. No humus layer.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Ridges formed from historic flooding but no real consistent slope. Slope taken from small terrace ridge that is very subtle. Worm castings abundant (>50%) but fine roots still seen. Coarse woody debris common but few snags. Upper horizon black, pH 7.0. Lower horizon dark black-gray, pH 6.5. Gray matrix begins at lower horizon. In the 1930-1940s, according to David Mather (National Register Archaeologist, Heritage Preservation Department, Minnesota Historical Society) landowner Smith may have had this land grazed but only a conjecture.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Plot located in anomaly with conifers and does not represent majority of stand - ecotonal to upslope MHn and downslope FFn. Slope imperceptible, seemingly flat, but based on LIDAR, it slopes up to the north which puts the plot at a toe. Topo context is slightly above the lower "floodplain" closer to the lake where greater green ash and Urtica occur. Coarse woody debris of varying decay and size class present; large diameter paper birch seen decaying on floor. Snags present but generally more prevalent outside plot; no cut stumps. Deer browse impact moderate. Abundant dead Impatiens stalks from previous year; very low ash regeneration and no conifer regeneration. Abundant worm castings but no middens; wormed mull humus with cobbles 60-90% by volume and 30 cm stone observed. Most cobbles in upper 13 cm of humus; few fine roots seen. Gravelly sandy loam (black) cap over clay (tan brown-gray) layer. Moderately well drained estimated.

Plot exhibits fairly rich conditions (e.g. flora and water pH) for forested peatland. Has some distinct wet forest species as well. Good hummock and hollow development. No cut stumps. No deer scat or browse on cedar or other vegetation apparent. Good cedar regeneration. Snags and coarse woody debris common and occurring naturally. Standing water in pools only.

Majority of surrounding site affected by dwarf mistletoe and is open-canopied black spruce and tamarack APn81. Mistletoe damage also seen within plot as some overstory trees have witches broom and low regeneration have bushy appearance. Snags and coarse woody debris accelerated by mistletoe. No recent cutting seen. No deer browse or scat seen. Standing water in hollows only. Commonality of cedar suggests FPn71, but the acidic water pH, high amounts of canopy openings, and low diversity and few minerotrophic species point to APn81.

Charcoal seen in soil. No worms or castings seen. Fungal hyphae bind Oe/Oa; fine roots in upper layers. Average gravel size in mineral soil is 3 mm (1 mm minimum, 7 mm maximum) and all sizes represented. Top A-horizon black; B-horizon rust orange. Very few cut stumps seen within stand. Expected to see more coarse woody debris. Large dead snags of birch seen >45 cm dbh. Deer browse heavy on mountain maple and elderberry. Many boulders on this side slope. Most ground cover occur under canopy gaps.

Stand is a small woodlot on terrace above river. Junky old  rusted car dumped on premises. Large coarse woody debris and snags prominent. No cut stumps but wind breakage on large bur oak and basswood. Soil profile: Top A-horizon black, pH 7.0; gray E-horizon fine loamy sand, pH 6.5; B-horizon starting at 26 cm, bright orange with darker red-brown speckles cemented but not mottled, pH 5.5; Bt horizon at 37 cm muted gray matrix with mottles, pH 4.5. No worms seen but mineral soil is close to surface with castings <50%. Fine roots, Oe, and fungal hyphae seen but patchy. Walking trail crosses stand (hunter created and minimal ecological impact). Ash regeneration good, basswood ok, bur oak poor. Expected succession towards other shade tolerant species.

No cutting seen. Pools dried but mucky at time of sampling but soil pit showed water 13 cm below surface. Good coarse woody debris and microtopography. Some snags present - many leaning trees. Top muck layer is somewhat more hemic than straight black sapric muck of the bottom. However, not enough identifiable material remains and degree of decomposition still suggests muck. Paper birch common throughout; growth stage may be straddling young and mature classification.

Drainage feels more somewhat poorly though keys to poorly; definitely drier than adjacent ash swamp to the south which is poorly drained. Nice humus layer from Oi, Oe, Oa; fine roots abound plus litter stuck together with fungal hyphae. Clay layer angular blocky structure, gray with no orange mottles, pH 7.0. Good coarse woody debris in moderately old decay class. Many snags of balsam poplar and balsam fir. Severe deer browse especially on aspen sapling sprouts. No tall shrub layer; size classes in overstory missing; no hardwoods in subcanopy; no cedar regeneration. Two hunting blinds seen just outside plot though no shooting lanes appeared to have been cut.

Good snags and coarse woody debris within stand. Canopy is very open as stated in 1996 but more weed species in ground layer. Heavy deer browse and bear scat present. Fine roots in humus and A-horizon; no worm activity detected. Lower horizon is finer sandy loam with some clay content approaching a sandy clay loam. Soil horizon color and pH with depth: brown-black, 5.5; dark brown, 4.0; tan, 4.0. Exact plot relocation difficult though 50 cm dbh basswood was relocated. Waypoints taken at plot center and corners: JL-420-2016 marks center; -2016a NE; -2016b SE; -2016c SW; -2016d NW. GPS accuracy between 5-10 m. Tree tags referencing corners: NE #201, 148 degrees  21'6", Tilia 35 cm dbh; SE #202, 266 degrees 7'7", Tilia 11 cm dbh; SW #203, 97 degrees 14'5", Tilia 19 cm dbh; NW #204, 182 degrees 45'7", Tilia 40 cm dbh.

Good quality community. Game trails crisscross through stand but no browse impact. Good hummock and hollow development. Height classes preferred: E6-6, E5-5, E4-4, E1-3. Fairly homogeneous community with height and density of bog birch most variable; canopy cover also variable across NPC. Cover of Carex chordorrhiza frequent but barely 5%. Black spruce noticeably taller than tamarack, many >10m; tamarack mostly <10m. Water pH taken in shallow sparse pool 3 cm deep. Waypoints taken at plot center and corners: JL-421-2016 marks center; -2016a SE; -2016b NE; -2016c SW; -2016d NW. GPS accuracy between 3-7 m. Tree tags referencing corners: SE #205, tree at exact corner, Larix 8 cm dbh; SW #206, 16 degrees 6'8", Larix 9 cm dbh; NW #207, 200 degrees 6'2", Picea 14 cm dbh; NE #208, 145 degrees 8'0", Picea 12 cm dbh.

Plot is situated in a valley between river's levee and first rise terrace. Plot oriented parallel to river. Two percent slope on each side of this valley, along 322 degree line. Abundant windrowed coarse woody debris and bare spots of little vegetation due to prolonged inundation. Acer saccharinum snags common and one stump seen just outside plot. Heavy deer browse on Laportea and Fraxinus pennsylvanica. Many dead, dried stalks of Elymus but with green new growth. Much of the F. pennsylvanica overstory trees outside of plot occur on slight levee rise but within FFn67a. Soil pit shows lenses of fine sand (2nd horizon) and very fine sandy loam (4th horizon) deposits among silt loam. The mottling starts at 3rd horizon at 31 cm and extends down to 4th horizon. The lenses are noticeably sandy to the touch but with some clay or silt as well. Horizon color and pH with depth: gray-black, 7.5; tan-gray, 8.0; tan-gray with orange mottles, 7.5; tan-gray, 7.5. Night crawlers and middens frequent.

Small stand on slight convex shallow ridge adjacent to rich black spruce swamp. Large decayed ~burned? stumps. Much bare ground with spruce needles and twigs. Deep duff layer (20 cm) over silty to clayey sand.

Typical of one of the more diverse and intact patches in a series of seepage meadows on gentle slope in cattle pasture along a ridgetop ravine. Dense and rather tall sedge hummocks. Substrate is fairly firm saturated muck. Plot ~centrally located in ~1-acre seepage meadow zone. Seepage is diffuse; cold, clear water that collects in stream in ravine bottom. Outer edges of seepage zones more degraded, grading to cool-season exotic pasture grasses in adjacent upland settings. Site is poorly to very poorly drained.

Typical of, and centrally located in, rather narrow zone of seepage alder on a low terrace on east side of Kettle River. Plot at base of moderate to very steep, 150 foot w-facing bluff. Small, sandy-bottomed seepage flow occurs in plot. Substrate is saturated muck, >30 cm deep. Average depth to sandstone bedrock is >40 cm. Small sandstone outcrops near plot edge on the nearby slope. No old stumps.

Centrally located in groundwater seepage-maintained meadow on broad alluvial terrace on east side of Kettle River. Plot captures ~40% of a subtle dome that is free of the wetland trees and shrubs (seepage alder and ash) that surround this opening. Moderately quaky, wet deep muck, strongly iron-stained as is the water in shallow depressions between hummocks. Unconsolidated iron-stained muck below a 40 cm thick mucky "mat". Subtle seepage flow in plot. Grades to alder and ash swamp. Opening is ~15 x 30 meters.

Plot typifies the wettest zone of rather broad, boggy shore of Jitterbug Lake; west side of lake, south of portage to Ahsub Lake. Edge of plot very near the open water lake zone of this shallow, boggy lake. Substrate is very quaky and unstable peat. Mat sinks ~12-18 inches under my weight. Shallow "pools" cover ~20% of plot; water up to 15 cm deep in these areas. Beaver dam at lake outlet currently raising water level ~16 inches. Photos taken of plot and setting from multiple angles.

Plot is typical of the broad central zone in wet meadow/fen peatland along a wetland drainage between two bog ponds southwest of Ima Lake. Wetland is recovering from beaver flooding prior to 1991; old defunct dam ~150 meters to North (down gradient). Remains of very old trees act as hummocks in this zone. Substrate is very quaky, deep, saturated peat; water is ankle deep in foot tracks. Grades to zones with much more Chamaedaphne. Photos taken of plot and setting.

Typical of fairly broad (20-40 meters wide) zone on northern shore of Swamp Lake. Plot centrally located in zone ~15 meters from edge of lake. Very quaky, deep, saturated peat; water 15-20 cm deep (lake level somewhat high due to rainy weather / wet spring). Grades away from lake to zone of bog birch then to tamarack swamp (dense, immature and ~even-aged trees with degraded, dense, Typha x glauca-dominated ground layer).

Typical of broad zone (~5-10 acres) of shrub fen in the inter-drumlin peatland complex with subtle string/flark patterning in the adjacent sedge fen. Plot located ~15-20 meters from a drainage ditch that runs parallel to flow direction; fen more open and apparently wetter on opposite (west) side of ditch. Substrate is moderately quaky moist peat >30 cm deep. Grades to tamarack swamp to the southeast.

Plot characterizes central zone of a seepage-maintained peat dome that rises 2-3 feet above lake level on the western shore of Getchell Lake. Substrate is quite buoyant, but moderately firm, deep saturated peat, wet at surface. Dome covers ~1/3 acre; adjacent upland (cultivated) rises ~15 feet above the dome. Outer zones of the wetland degraded by cattle; a narrow strip near lake is heavily grazed. Photos taken of plot and setting. Several (~10?) black terns present on the shallow lake.

Plot centrally located in ~300 square meter wetland on circular peat dome that rises 4-5 feet above adjacent wetland that surrounds small, shallow Wolf Lake. Dome occurs at the base of a moderately steep, ~50-foot, S-facing forested slope in strongly rolling morainal terrain north side of Green Lake. Deep, firm but buoyant peat, saturated to surface. Upper 25 cm is highly decomposed mucky peat, below 25 cm becomes gritty (sandy?) fibric peat. Large buckthorn has invaded the edges of the dome, and heavy buckthorn infestation present in adjacent woods. Dense hybrid cattails in the adjacent wetland surrounding Wolf Lake. Additional but much smaller pockets of seepage meadow occur nearby to the west, these "hanging" on gentle to moderately steep slope settings; however most of the wet meadow here is quite degraded. Wetland was identified as a "fen" by a consulting Forester as part of a Forest Stewardship plan. Landowners are very conservation-minded.

Plot typical of ~2-4 acres of sedge meadow at the head of a fairly robust water track that supports a large spring fen (1/4 mile to the SE). Plot located ~40 meters from edge of gentle to moderately steep cultivated upland. Substrate in plot is firm but buoyant mucky sedge peat (70% decomposed fibric, black, moist). Sedge hummocks are prominent, 45-60 cm high. Typha xglauca and native Phragmites are invading meadow and fen not too far to the southeast. Photos taken of plot and setting. Plot +/- centrally located in meadow zone. No surface water or visible flow here.

Typical of sedge-dominated openings (flarks) in fairly large spring fen along broad water track in large tamarack peatland complex. Substrate is wet, quaky, deep peat; shallow surface water is present, especially along game (deer)trails (which appear to follow the most concentrated flow zones). The fen is being invaded by native Phragmites in some/many areas. Grades to tamarack swamp (immature and +/-even-aged Larix here). Photos taken of plot and setting.

Typical of 15- to 20-meter wide zone bordering a small (~1/2 acre) shallow pond along Hummingbird Lane, northwest of Byer Lake. Edge of plot is 2 meters from edge of pond. Grades outward (away from pond) to wet meadow (mostly invaded by Phalaris arundinacea); surrounding upland is old field/pasture. Substrate in plot: mucky organic quaky "mat", held together by roots; standing water ~10 cm deep (20 cm in foot tracks); at 50 cm down (from surface of the quaky mat) is a solid clay bottom. Photos taken of plot and setting. Located along road to Griffin/Converse "Minnesota Peach" orchard.

Plot located in a groundwater emergence zone, in largest of several such openings amongst dense hybrid and narrow-leaved cattails, on gentle to moderately steep mid-slope of 45-ft high, W- to SW-facing hill in strongly-rolling morainal terrain north of Ella Lake. Substrate is firm but buoyant mucky peat / marl with concretions just below the surface. Small, shallow, marly pools cover 5% of plot. A few small domes are present on the slope including one that is partially in the plot. Hybrid and narrow-leaved cattails have invaded ~85% of this seepage wetland (everywhere except in more robust emergence zones). Photos taken of plot and setting. Black terns on WPA wetland 1/4 mile SW.

Plot is typical of much of a rather extensive patch of stunted spruce and tamarack in rather large peatland south of White Feather Lake, east of the Stuart River. Substrate is deep, saturated, fibric peat. Sphagnum hummocks are 12-24 inches tall. This area was/is likely influenced by beaver flooding and other water level fluctuations on the river which is at +/- same elevation 1/4 mile away. Spruces are commonly "mop-top" form, 3-10 cm dbh; tamarack to 16 cm dbh. No stumps.

Plot characterizes poor fen zone bordering Contest Lake. Located on southern end of the 20-acre lake in the widest portion of what is mostly a rather narrow zone. Edge of the plot is ~5 meters from the lakeshore. Substrate is deep, quaky, saturated peat; water 10 cm deep in foot tracks. Grades to poor conifer swamp (APn81) with stunted trees toward the rolling bedrock upland (mature jack pine with aspen, birch, and black spruce). Photos taken of plot and setting.

Plot is typical of a broad Ericad-dominated peatland zone along the Stuart River at White Feather Lake. Similar vegetation extends in fairly broad riverine band for nearly two miles. Substrate is deep fibric peat, saturated to just below the surface; no woody remains in soil pit. Plot +/- centrally located in this zone ~50 meters from the river and ~100 meters from upland (virgin jack pine-black spruce bedrock woodland).

Plot captures wettest zone(s) of rather narrow poor sedge fen surrounding a tiny (1/4-acre) bog pond in center of a 20-acre spruce bog in strongly rolling bedrock terrain east of White Feather Lake. Edge of plot is at edge of the pond. Very wet and quite quaky peat; water 30-40 cm deep in foot tracks in plot center (deeper closer to pond). Subtly wetter shallow depressions with shallow surface water cover 30% of plot. Grades outward to narrow zone of Carex oligosperma, then to black spruce bog. Surrounding bedrock (granitic) uplands burned in July 1996- major crown fire. Photos taken of plot and setting.

Rectangular plot parallels the boggy western shore of Sundial Lake; the lake shore (edge of the water) forms the long edge of the plot. Substrate is quite quaky saturated peat. No surface water, but water is up to 10 cm deep in foot tracks. Vegetation rather low-saturated in this zone which is rather limited and only occurring quite near the water's edge. Grades to more typical poor ericaceous fen (see Releve B156) which covers ~70% of the boggy shore. Surrounding uplands burned in July 1996 in catastrophic crown fire. Photos taken of plot and setting. T.J.S. Whifeld did Releve #MDL16-24 (DNR #B156) in poor low shrub fen ~90 meters to the south on the same boggy shoreline.

Typical of large patch of primary forest (unlogged) in gently rolling granitic bedrock terrain east of Stuart Lake, south of the portage to Fox Lake. Heinselmann stand-origin is 1894, never logged. Even-aged old-growth. Pinus banksiana mostly 25-30 cm dbh; frequent snags. No stumps. Frequent CWD- mostly large jack pine boles. Soil: 7 cm duff, charcoal common where the duff turns to gray silty-sand (15 cm deep) with numerous stones, then >15 cm rocky tan silty sand. Photos taken of site from multiple angles.

place_name: Driftwood Point (Lake of the Woods- NW Angle)
remarks: Typical of level sand beach zone 30-45 cm above lake level on Driftwood Point, Lake of the Woods. Deep sand, moist at (or just beneath) the surface, fairly coarse-grained. Plot located ~20 meters from the lake to the northeast, ~30 meters to south (over a 2-foot higher sand spit that extends to the east forming the point. Buried lens (5 cm thick) of black organics (peat) at 2 cm from surface; water in soil pit at 25 cm down. Bare sand covers ~20% of plot; vegetative cover heterogeneous- varies from sparse to interrupted. Small driftwood pieces scattered in plot. Photos taken of plot and setting.

place_name: Stony Point (NW Angle- Lake of the Woods)
remarks: Plot typifies the essentially flat top (crest) of a ~3-acre sand bar island in Sand Point Bay, just north of Stony Point, Lake of the Woods. Plot elevation is ~2 feet above lake level. Substrate is fine sand and pea gravel (rounded small stones). Grades to a zone of denser Salix interior, and to another zone of more abundant Potentilla norvegica. Sand bar is 300 meters long x 35 meters wide. Photos taken of plot and setting.

Plot characterizes one of several zones in a heterogeneous marsh-meadow complex along Stony Creek. Centrally located in this zone, ~25 meters from the slack-water creek and 20 meters from the upland. Water depth is 10 cm. Substrate firm: 10 cm deep mucky peat, over ~20 cm of muck, over clayey-muck (>30 cm deep. Vegetation grades nearby to a zone dominated by Typha xglauca, also nearby to a zone dominated by Calamagrotis canadensis, and in deeper water nearer the creek to a zone dominated by Zizania palustris. Deeper water is also present in the Carex lacustris - Acorus calamus marsh zone along a short beaver run, just outside the plot. Photos taken of plot and setting.

Mature mesic forest in fairly narrow band along Stony Creek, west side. Level setting on creekside terrace ~10-15 feet above creek level. Large aspens to 45 cm dbh, large fir to 37 cm. Moderate CWD, mostly large aspen boles (many of which were felled by beavers). Soil: 2 cm litter, 6 cm duff, 20 cm highly decomposed peat, below that is dark grey clay. Grades quickly to wet-mesic cedar (WFn53) further away from the creek (see E. Perry Releve B094). Photos taken of plot from multiple angles.

Typical of older, cedar-dominated portions of designated old-growth patch that varies from WFn55 ash, to younger even-aged WFn53 cedar, to older cedar (similar to plot)which is less common than other two conditions. Tree core: 44 cm dbh Thuja: ~110 years-old. Trees straight to slightly leaning. Substrate: thin litter and humus (heavily wormed), 10 cm deep wormed organic rooting zone, silty organics down to 35 cm, fine gray silty clay below 35 cm deep. CWD rather sparse. Three quite old (and apparently cut) cedar stumps in the plot, these are infrequent to occasional in portions of the larger stand. Inner portion of on point between Youngs Bay and Sugar Point, opposite Flag Island. Photos taken from multiple angles.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Marked with spike at each corner and with DEEP-1 magnets at NE and SW corners. Previous UTM coordinates for rel 7949 are incorrect due to past data entry error (coord.s for 7948 were switched with 7949[corrected 10/2016]). This plot was located following description and hand-drawn map from original surveyor (LAB). Shapefile of GPS points for plot corners was submitted with releve. 2016 was very wet in 2nd half of growing season - many plants still green at time of this sampling. Sorghastrum & Andropogon reach 6ft in height. GPS coord.s for corners are: 44.721561/-94.295574; 44.721561/-94.295696; 44.721477/-94.295694; 44.721465/-94.295571.
GPS readings taken at all 4 corners, the SW corner is listed as Releve location. All corner coordinates listed on Releve form. Re-sample of Releve A836.

Wet mesic prairie on level ground. Open area bordered by cropland to west, aspen to east. Few grasses or sedges with reproductive parts. Re-visit of DNR Relevés #4042 and #9275. GPS coordinates for all 4 corners of plot recorded on form, UTM coordinates used for Relevé are for SW corner.

Few sedges in fruit or flower, cover and presence based on vegetative characteristics and old seedheads. Re-visit of Releve #9276. GPS coordinates for all 4 corners recorded on form. UTM coordinates listed are for SW corner of plot.
Re-visit of DNR Relevés #6791 and #9260. GPS coordinates recorded on form for all 4 corners of plot. UTM coordinates used for Relevé location is SW corner.
Re-visit of DNR Relevés #5340 and #9263. GPS coordinates for all 4 plot corners provided on form. Relevé location given is SW corner of plot.
Wet-mesic brush prairie, near powerline and soybean field. Re-visit of DNR Relevés #9274. GPS coordinates recorded for all 4 corners of plot. UTM coordinates for Relevé are for SW corner.

Wet-mesic/Mesic prairie with scattered brush, evidently the brush was mowed and suckered. Many Populus re-sprouts have giant leaves, superficially resembling P. deltoides, which I doubt is present. Re-survey of Releves #4049 and 9423.

Uniformly dominated by Andropogon, except along west edge, which features a thicket of Populus tremuloides and Salix spp, with a weedy groundlayer- Cirsium arvense common. Re-visit of Releves #5221 and 9247.

Dry Upland Prairie. Collected for prairie monitoring surveys. Area monitored in recent past. Dominated by graminoid cover. Recent animal activity with exposed gravel near burrows. Regal fritillary observed in plot.
Re-visit to Dry Prairie system. Native structure intact.  Dominated by graminoid cover (Bout curt, Andro ger). Shows signs of recent burning.
Mesic system with mix of forbs and graminoids. Re-visit to site.
Old field plot of Bromus inermis. Possibly seeded with prairie species.
Mesic prairie system. Re-visit for prairie monitoring efforts.
Mesic prairie on a slope. Recently burned with no leaf litter.

Mature stand; small canopy gaps common. Plot contains portion of canopy gap. Hummocks relatively low to moderate in height. No standing water present in hollows. Fungal fruiting bodies abundant on date. UTM= SE plot corner.

Undulating landscape. Exposed cobble and stones common, sometimes creating lower pockets. Microtopography abundant. Lrg diameter CWD and snags rare/absent. Deer browse heavy. Deep duff layer. If earthworms present, castings are small. Soil layers: sand component in upper profile very fine, cobbles and stones prevalent. Reddish mottles observed ~25cm. Stopped by coarse fragments @ 30cm. Carex pensylvanica present in stand (>2m from plot). UTM= SE plot corner.

Plot representative of NPC that follows peatland "drain" between two areas of deeper peat. Peat surface highly variable with scattered wet hollows common. Standing water depths ranged from 3-11 cm. Releve UTM location is SW corner of plot.

Mature example of NPC with appropriate structure for growth stage. Stand located along periphery of large peatland complex. No obvious sign of human disturbance. No wet hollows present. Single tree gaps and associated CWD are common in stand. Water table depth at ~25 cm. Releve UTM location is NE plot corner. WP 71.

Landscape with undulating topography. Rocks and boulders scattered in plot and stand. Upper soil profile well mixed by earthworms. UTM = plot center. Two live multi-stemmed trees found in plot, Acer rubrum (12.1, 14.3, & 19.0 cm dbh) and Betula papyrifera (23.9 & 20.8 cm dbh). Largest stems on trees recorded on tree diameter list. Soil horizons and exact textures: AE, E1, E2 (VFSL with ferric iron concentrations), E/Bt (VFS/CL with ferric iron concentrations and clay films on all ped faces) [E/Bt = glossic horizon indicated by degradation and redistribution of the clays in an otherwise argillic horizon]. Parent material: glaciofluvial deposits over subglacial till. Soil excavation deeper than 90 cm presumably stopped by rock restriction but not bedrock.

Undulating landscape. NPC occupies moderate to gradual slopes and level tops. Recent blowdown common in stand. Plot located on relatively level site near upper slope/crest of feature where canopy is still intact. Scattered stones/boulders present, but infrequent. Deer activity moderate. Observed old pine snags with fire scars. Soil profile: at 8 cm sand becomes more reddish in color and volume of coarse fragments increases. Releve UTM location is plot center. WP 89. SNF project plot ID =46. Soil horizons and exact textures: E, Bw1, Bw2, 2C1 (LCOS), 2C2, 2C3 (COS). Parent material: glacial drift over outwash.

NPC surrounds small flowage in narrow valley between bedrock features. Plot located in representative area. Sphagnum species noted in stand, but patchy and infrequent. No bryophytes observed in plot. UTM = plot center.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Large peninsula extending into Lake Vermilion. Stumps and snags with fire scars- may be natural origin stand. White pine regeneration is abundant. Some patches of exposed bedrock present. UTM = SE plot corner.

Small patch NPC on this landscape. Stand occupies shallow valley with gradual slope (and drainage) to Lake Vermilion. Shallow braided channels (both visible and subterranean) bisect stand. Plot straddles narrow flowage with depth of 6-13 cm. Pit and mound features common in plot; one pit with standing water. Near continuous layer of stones and boulders close to surface (muck/sand mix between stones). Depth of layer unknown. Muck humus hard to discern due to worm activity. Litter type is leaves and grass. Releve UTM location is plot center.
Sphagnum fuscum hummocks average 40-45 cm in height. Lower hollows are mostly S. angustifolium. Releve UTM location is plot center.

Island in Lake Vermilion. NPC occupies slopes near lakeshore and level tops; areas shallow to bedrock. Plot variable with both level areas and areas of greater slope near crest of feature. Scattered stumps and snags present. Large red pine CWD. Deer browse moderate to heavy. Stopped by coarse fragments/bedrock at 13 cm. Litter type is a mix of leaves and needles. Releve UTM location is plot center.

Mature forest example. Lacking species indicators; hard to discern between FDn43 and FDn33. Slightly undulating landscape with subtle slopes. Older cut stumps common; CWD and snags uncommon. Plot contains portion of single tree canopy gap (Picea ~40 cm dbh). Releve location UTM coordinates are plot center. One live multi-stemmed Betula papyrifera with all 3 stems measured 19.8, 10.7, & 17.4 cm dbh listed separately on tree diameter list.

Representative of small patch rivershore community along Little Fork River. Plot size modified to best capture the narrow NPC along lower/mid slope of bank. Alluvial deposits appear to be clay loam or silty clay loam. Small patches of exposed sediments are common in stand/plot. Releve UTM coordinates are plot center.

Mature forest with snags and recent CWD common. Canopy gaps common in stand. Plot located in area with relatively intact canopy (includes portion of small gap). Abies CWD common in plot. Evidence of deer browse/sign moderate to high in stand. Upper soil profile highly mixed by worm activity. Large pieces of charcoal were observed. Stopped by boulder restriction at 55 cm. UTM coordinates for Releve location are plot center. Soil horizons: A, Bw, C. Parent material: ablation (supraglacial) till. Some surface cobbles and stones present.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Attempt to re-locate DNR Releve #4915 using original coordinates to establish plot center. Current plot includes canopy gap created by relatively recent blow-down (5 tip-ups in plot). Plot located in level setting, but mircotopography abundant in plot/stand. No evidence of earthworms. Permanent markers established; spikes at each corner and DEEP1 magnets at SE and NW plot corners. See maps and notes for additional details. Releve UTM location is SE plot corner.

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #7; Royal Rove Cliffs
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 years old assoc w/LTP17. UTM=midpoint of plot. CWD common, most well-decayed. Betula pap single and multi-stemmed. Very decayed Thuja cut stumps nearby in NPC patch. Soils: at least 75cm loamy sand/very fine sand; few cobbles, one water-rounded; uniform texture and moisture. Chose moderately well drained for slope position, could be well-drained. Bryos common on CWD and in ground patches.

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #34; Royal Rove Cliffs
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associate w/LTP 65.Abundanr CWD of Betula pap and Populus trem all sizes and states of decay. Plot incl both dense and moderately conifer-shaded grnd layer. No cut stumps obs in plot or nearby but historic selective Pinus harvest likely in the general area. Adjacent to NPC patch w/10-15m tall Thuja subcan, possibly more than 50% cover under canopy of Populus, Betula and occas supercan Pinus strob = FDN43b1 transitioning to FDn43c. UTM = SE corner of plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old assoc w/LTP 65. Broken canopy, Populus blown down or broken in 1999 wind storm event. Two tip-up mounds in plot. Large Picea glauca snag very decayed. Lrg decaying dead/down Pinus strobus. CWD abundant all sizes states of decay. A few boulders less than 1mx1m at surface.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated w/LTP65. Mature forest transitioning to a Thuja canopy. No anthro disturbance evidence obs in plot. Moderate amt of CWD; lrg dbh Betula pap very decayed. Exposed low bedrock shelf on west edge of plot. Larger expanse as low wall nearby OP. Some cobbles and stones @ surface. Plot on slope above small stream. UTM = SE corner of plot. Bryos common on tree bases and decaying wood.

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #6; Cross River Lowlands
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #17. Low amount of CWD, small to medium-sized. No cut stumps observed in plot. Recent harvest nearby. Some browsing evidence on woody spp. Transitional growth stage. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet buried in soil pit. Soil horizons: A, Bw1, Bw2, 2BC, 2C. Glacial drift over lodgment till parent material.

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #33; Lookout Mt. Ridge
remarks: Pot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #64. Old forest. Severely deer browsed. Very decayed cut stump in vicinity, two (cedar) possible in plot. This LTP polygon w/frequent very small drains and wet depressions. Plot w/a few wet depressions <1mx1m. CWD is moderate amt of lrg dbh Betula pap and sm dbh Abies. UTM = center of plot/soil pit location/magnet in soil pit. In this wet June, water filled the pit to approx. 20cm below surface during sampling.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #60. Old-growth conditions except deer browse severe: no expected spp absent, suppression of shrub ht/recruitment. Large Picea glauca dead/down just beyond OP distance in addition to snag OP. Plot location ~20m above transition to level, wetter expression of this NPC. Med-lrg CWD common, at least one >50cm dbh, various states of decay. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet located in soil pit: north 1.5m from 38cm dbh Acer sacc; south 2.5m from 23cm dbh Acer sacc; NW 1m from lrg Acer sacc CWD.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated w/LTP #57. No evidence of deer browsing. No cut stumps observed in plot or vicinity. Abies and Populus CWD w/medium dbh common, one large dbh Thuja charred, very decayed. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit south 1.9m from Populus 37cm dbh and SW 5.5m from Betula pap 31 cm dbh..

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #60. Canopy A. sacch multi-stemmed, ~7 stems from base. Acer sacch regen frequently browsed by deer. Small to medium dbh Abies and Populus CWD comon; one larg dbh, very decayed Thuja?. No cut stumps observed in plot or vicinity. Magnet located in soil pit UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit east 4m from 33cm Betula and north 3m from 29cm Populus.

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #28; Many Rivers Hardwoods
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #60. Plot includes canopy gap of two mature tree tops and one lrg dbh tree fallen w/in past 5 yrs. Within old growth patch. Pit and mound microtopo evident. Abundant lrg-med dbh CWD in various states of decay. Lrg snags. Ephemeral pool nearby. UTM = plot center\soil pit. Magnet in soil pit: 2.8m @288 degrees from 44cm dbh Acer sacch and 1m @186 degrees from 7cm dbh Acer sacch. Occas stones at surface. Looked for but did not find earthworms, but humus seems thin for eworm-free MHn45. E-horizon present @ ~2cm.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #33. Broken canopy. Med-lrg dbh Populus and Abies down in various states of decay. Betula multi-stemmed. No cut stumps obs in plot or vicinity. Bryos patchy on rocks and decaying CWD. Irregular surface topo. Stones occas @ surface. Loamy fines among densely compacted gravel. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in shallow pit adjacent to low-profile moss-covered rock, 2.1m @ 4degrees from 34cm dbh Betula, 2.5m @ 223 degrees from 18cm dbh Abies.

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #24; Blueberry Lk RNA; 3 Cks East
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #60. No cut stumps observed w/in plot or in vicinity. Abundant sm-medium dbh CWD in all states of decay. Scattered recent windthrow trees and deformed shrubs from 12/2015, 11" "bend down" wet snowfall on unfrozen woody veg. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 1.5m @ 156 degrees from 36cm dbh Pinus bank, 2.4m @ 53 degrees from 29cm dbh Abies. No evidence of deer browsing observed.

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #38; near Gunflint Lake
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #65. Mature forest impacted by 1999 blowdown event. Small to medium diameter CDW abundant. Populus trem and Betula pap snags each x2. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit, 2.4m @ 166 degrees from 17cm dbh Betula and 2.2m @ 330 degrees from 7cm dbh Abies.

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #10; Brule Northern Light
npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #23. Possibly old growth stage/condition in irregular terrain of sharp, steep small hills. Located on  slope of one of these. Charcoal@ humus/mineral soil interface. Abundant sm-lrg diameter CWD, well-decayed. Pit and mound microtopo. Bryophytes cover boulders, patchy on grnd and CWD. UTM=plot center/soil plot. Magnet in soil pit 11m @ 76 degrees from 48cm dbh Pinus strobus and 1.4m @ 209 degrees from 16cm dbh Abies. Middle of short steep slope just above windthrow pile-up.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #65. 1999 blowdown event impact created broken canopy. Populus regen in conopy opening. Lrg Populus snag. Standing dead and dying Betula pap. Recent blowndown of 40cm dbh Picea glauca snag. Some moose browse evident. UTM=plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit, 4.5m @ 313 degrees form 23cm dbh Thuja and 1.7m @ 240 degrees form 42 cm dbh Populus trem.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP 357. Betula a mix of multi and single stem. Abundant CWD all sizes and states of decay. Old woodland w/ some old growth character. UTM= plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pitvery near surface, 2.2m @ 216 degrees from 30cm dbh Betula and 3.2m @ 53 degrees from 32cm dbh Pinus banksiana.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 years old associated with LTP #67. Shallow soil pit due to matrix of large rocks. No cut stumps observed. Charcoal present. Moderate amount of sm-medium-sized CWD. Moss/humus covered boulders and stones common at surface. Acer rubrum frost-cracked. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 2.2m @ 353 degrees from 20cm dbh Acer rubrum and 2.8m @ 204 degrees from 44cm dbh Populus trem.

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #9; East Echo Trail
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #23. Unsure if soil depth to bedrock or large boulder. No cut stumps observed. Abundant CWD sm-med-sized in all states of decay, various spp.. Four P. strobus and three Abies no more than 4cm dbh marked w/multiple metal tags. Regen or fuels plot? Charcoal present. Old woodland w/some old growth characteristics. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 3.5m @ 42 degrees from 54cm dbh P. strobus and 4.9m @ 254 degrees from 34cm dbh Populus grand.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #17. On slope of peninsula of Snowbank Lk shore. Plot includes variable understry conditions assoc w/edge of tree fall openings and cobble substrate on west side. In level terrain of this LTP polygon Tilia americana was observed. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit between cut stump (16cm diameter face) to west and tip-up mound to east, large root of which has cut face.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #9. Small-medium sized CWD is common. Angular rocks common @ surface most less than 30cm diameter. Soil profile stopped by bedrock or lrg boulder. Herbaceous cover and frequency of some species may be related to browse severity. UTM=plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 2.6m @20 degrees from 19cm dbh Acer rubrum and 1.2m @186 degrees from 14cm dbh Populus trem and 1.6m @144 degrees from 8cm dbh Populus trem.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #9. Bedrock outcrop at south edge of plot. Abundant CWD small-medium sized Populus. Populus trem regen/recruitment in canopy gap of wind-snapped Populus. In other parts of this NPC patch shrubs dominate understory. UTM=plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 2.4m @318 degrees from 45cm dbh Populus trem and 2.6m @17 degrees from 40cm dbh Pop trem.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old-associated with LTP #3. Betula pap multi-stemmed and single stemmed. Charcoal present. Low amount of CWD, small-medium sized. Very decayed/charred cut stump in plot and others nearby. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 2.4m @244 degrees from 39cm dbh Populus grandi and 2.1m @348 degrees from 9cm dbh Betula pap.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #3. Small amount of CWD, most small-medium sized. Small bedrock outcrop in NW corner of plot. Charcoal present. Cut, charred stumps in vicinity of plot, one in plot. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 3.2m @180 degrees from 35cm dbh Acer rub and 2.9m @60 degrees form 14cm dbh Abies.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #46. Cut charred stump just outside plot. Pit and mound topography. Abundant CWD, multiple sizes, including lrg well-decayed individuals. Old growth characteristics. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 2.9m @288 degrees from 19cm dbh Betula pap and 4.1m @170 degrees from 29cm dbh Pinus strobus and 58cm dbh P. resinosa. Soil horizons: A, Bw (fine sandy loam), 2BC, 2C. Parent material is glacial drift over ablation till/outwash. Excavation past  69 cm impeded by rock.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality NPC common in Johnson Lake Bedrock Complex LTA, here of fire origin circa 1920. Likely severe fire impact in this setting. No cut stumps in this NPC patch. Evidence of historic high-grade harvest, likely of pine, on slope to south. Conifer snags common. CWD abundant, mostly mid-sized and in various states of decay. Evidence of fire disturbance present. Small rock outcrops scattered in NPC patch, not in plot. Irregular microtopography. Small moss patches in low spots. UTM = midpoint of plot.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality NPC in old, possibly old growth stage of NPC common in Johnson Lake Bedrock Complex LTA. CWD amount low in varying degrees of decay, small-medium diameter. No charcoal, no fire scars on large tree boles. Very decayed cut stumps in NPC patch, none in plot vicinity. UTM = plot center
Plot chosen to represent common riparian NPC of low gradient stream and river segments in Johnson Lake Bedrock Complex LTA. Standing water among hummocks ranges from 3-5 cm. UTM = midpoint of plot.

Plot chosen to represent at least 100 years old, originating after harvest. Cut stumps occasional, very decayed, likely some have disappeared. Amount of CWD low, small-sized. Moss covers tree bases and some hummocks present. Wet pools and pits common. Browsing appears to be having significant long term ecological effects as it targets Thuja. Thuja regen present but no recruitment. UTM = midpoint of plot. See NPC condition ranking form for details on browsing impacts.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality NPC in Johnson Lake Bedrock Complex LTA. Low amount of CWD small-medium sized. Standing water pools common = 30-40% of plot area. Some pool bottoms moss-covered, others not. In gently-sloping drainage between highly variable topography of bedrock-controlled hills of woodlands and mesic mixed forests. UTM = midpoint of plot.

Plot chosen to represent old growth forest condition of high-quality NPC type occasional in this site and Johnson Lake Bedrock Complex LTA. Very decayed cut Pinus strobus stumps scattered in NPC patch, two in plot. Slope adjacent to Johnson Lake shore. Tilia Americana (mature) within view outside plot in similar setting. Occasional cobble/ stones/boulders at surface. Variable microtopography. Abundant CWD all sizes and states of decay. One large snag. UTM = midpoint of plot.

Plot chosen to represent high-quality, natural origin, small patch NPC in Johnson Lake Bedrock Complex LTA. Occurring in level to gently-sloping and ecotonal settings. Here between FDn33b and WFn64. Old Populus tremuloides in canopy breaking-up. Snags and abundant CWD in various states of decay, one large diameter in early stages of decay. UTM = midpoint of plot.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot chosen to represent high-quality, natural origin NPC designated by MN as old growth pine. Charcoal present. Irregular microtopography via both pit and mound and bedrock contours. Low (no higher than 1 meter) vertical bedrock wall along 2 sides of plot. Surface bedrock and boulders moss-covered. Abundant CWD, various diameters and stages of decay, including one large diam Populus very decayed. Large, live,~35cm dbh Populus tremuloides near plot. Soil in pockets w/in bedrock matrix. UTM = midpoint of the plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #67. One very decayed cut stump in plot. Low amount of small to medium sized CWD in various states of decay. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 2.4m @331 degrees from 9cm dbh Ostrya vir and 2.9cm @267 from 35cm dbh Populus trem.

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #43; South of Kjosted Lk.
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #67. Most CWD small dbh. Pit and mound microtopography. Occasional very decayed cut stumps, likely P. strobus or resinosa in NPC patch. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 1.7m @240 degrees from 29cm dbh Pinus resinosa and 2.0m @346 degrees from 26cm dbh Pinus banksiana.

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #13; Brule Northern Light
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #33. Abundant CWD small-medium sizes. Charcoal present. Some pit and mound microtopo. No cut stumps observed but likely Pinus harvest in NPC patch in late 19th-early 20th century. Scattered moss-covered boulders @ surface. Betula pap multi-stemmed. Some old growth characteristics. UTM=plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 2.3m @200 degrees from 20cm dbh Betula pap and 1.6m @55 degrees from 17cm dbh Betula pap.

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #31; Nip Jack Headlands
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #64. A few very decayed charred cut stumps observed in NPC patch. Most CWD sm-medium sized various states of decayed. Abies and Betula snags. Stones, boulders occas at surface, moss/herb/humus covered. Coarse fragments in soil minimal up to 49cm then soil pit stopped by large stones/boulders or bedrock. UTM=plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 1.7m @198 degrees from 21cm dbh Abies and 1.7 @332 degrees from 31cm dbh Betula pap.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old  associated with LTP #67. Area around plot recently thinned P. resinosa (more) and P. banksiana (less). Plot area undisturbed. Volume of gravel estimate based on small sample. Low amount of CWD. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 2.8m @10 degrees from 30cm dbh Populus trem and 2.1m @218 degrees from 29cm Abies.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #53. Rock outcrop along north side of plot w/recent tip-up. Sm-medium sized CWD abundant, in various stages of decay. Blowdown of mature Populus 10-15 yrs ago. No cut stumps obs. Lrg dbh legacies missing. Lrg conifers missing from patch and plot. Most damaged trees broken at base. Occasional snags.
