Historic high-grade harvest of conifers likely. UTM=plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 2m @137 degrees form 12cm dbh Populs trem and 3m @28 degrees from 12cm dbh Abies.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #3. Patch of 2016 blowdown adjacent to west side of plot. Plot densely shaded until 2016 blowdown of some canopy Abies in plot subcanopy. Budworm damaged Abies & Picea glauca. Pleurozium and acrocarp w/patchy cover. UTM=plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 3.7m @309 degrees from 49cm dbh Populus trem and 1.6m @336 degrees from 15cm dbh Abies.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #3. Pit and mound microtopo on upper half of plot. Broken canopy from past blowdwn of lrg Picea glauca and P. strobus. Some budworm damage to Abies. Abundant CWD, all states of decay. One very decayed possible cut stump in vicinity of plot. Recent clearcut w/in 50m to east. UTM=plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 2m @256 degrees from 27cm dbh Populus trem and 1.8m @100 degrees from 16cm dbh Populus trem.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #9. Small-medium sized CWD abundant = Populus, Abies, and Betula, many states of decay. No cut stumps observed but likely past harvest and stumps decayed. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 2.5m @20 degrees from 25cm dbh Populus trem and 2.8m @271 degrees from 34cm dbh Abies.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #57. Natural fire origin. Moderate amount of sm-med sized CWD in various states of decay. Betula single stem and multi-stemmed. One pine snag. Bouldery @ surface, moss-covered espec on upper (W) 1/2 of plot. Small wetland adjacent to plot @SE corner. Some old growth characteristics. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 1.0m @232 degrees form 34cm dbh Pinus resinosa and 1.5m @307 degrees form 27cm dbh Pinus strobus.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #17. Moderate amount of sm-med sized CWD, mostly well-decayed. One Populus snag. One possible cut stump, very decayed, likely Picea glauca. Minimal pit and mound microtopo. Evidence of browsing nearly absent. Much of this LTP polygon rock-raked and planted to Picea glauca. NPC at plot could be part of broad ecotonal setting. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 2.7m @52 degrees from 42cm dbh Populus trem and 2.0m @348 degrees from 16cm dbh Acer saccharum.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 years old associated with LTP#17. No cut stumps observed in plot or vicinity. Minimal browsing by moose or deer (unclear which). Small - medium-sized CWD common. UTM= plot center/soil pit; magnet in soil pit 4.6m @22 degrees from 31cm dbh Betula pap and 4.4m @284 degrees from 34cm dbh Betula pap.

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #22; West of Lake Cty. 7
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #60. Broken canopy related to wind damage. Populus trem regen and recruitment common in understory. Sm-medium sized CWD abundant of Populus trem and Abies. Stones and boulders abundant at surface. Highly variable microtopo. UTM=plot center and soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 1.6m @292 degrees form 25cm dbh Populus trem and 1.5m @202 degrees from 16cm dbh Thuja occi. Soil horizons: A, E, Bw1, Bw2 (with iron concentrations). Excavation deeper than 62 cm impeded by large fragment. Lodgment till parent material. Surface stones and boulders 2-10%

place_name: Garden Island, Lake of the Woods
remarks: Plot chosen to represent and document NPC common on Garden Is. in LOW. Beginning just behind the lakeshore's wave/ice push berm, occupies terrain little elevated (<1m, perhaps  no more than.5m) above lake level. Layer of deposited debris common in plot and patch here and elsewhere on island, debris not "windrowed", no ice scars seen on trees. Abundant CWD, w/abundant moss cover. Minimal microtopography. Humus layer black with very little mineral soil; worm castings abundant; fine roots still present in upper 10 cm; clay layer gray and a limestone cobble in soil pit. Plot ~50 meters from northern shore of island. UTM = NW corner of plot.

place_name: Garden Island, Lake of the Woods
remarks: Plot chosen to represent and document high-quality NPC on island in LOW, with old growth qualities, state designated as "future old growth". Moderate amount of CWD, most small-medium diameters; various states of decay. Location ~95 meters from northern shoreline of island. Quercus macrocarpa up to 105 cm dbh observed in NPC patch represented by this plot. No cut stumps observed in plot or patch. UTM = plot center

Plot chosen to represent high-quality NPC common in Warroad Till Plain LTA. NPC patch and plot with significant larch sawfly mortality in Larix canopy sometime after 2010. Snags common, some dead and down. Hummocks range in height from 10-20cm. Narrow, linear wet hollows common, standing water infrequent. Sphagnum spp dominate substrate with feather mosses within this matrix. Plot includes areas with mostly dead canopy and with 50% canopy cover. UTM = plot midpoint

Plot chosen to represent high-quality, natural origin NPC within .5 mile of Lake of the Woods, common in the near level terrain of Warroad Till Plain LTA. Well-developed hummocks and hollows with water-filled pools. No evidence of cut stumps or other anthropogenic disturbance observed in plot or on route between plot and Pickerel Creek. UTM = midpoint of plot.

place_name: Erika's #27, Oak Island, Lake of the Woods
remarks: Plot chosen to represent high-quality, fire-origin NPC on bedrock-controlled terrain of Oak Island in Lake of the Woods. P. resinosa w/somewhat open growth form. No cut stumps observed in plot or nearby on landform. Snags and moderate amount of small-medium dbh CWD in many states of decay. Cobbles and stones frequent at surface, most moss-covered, creating microtopography. Charcoal abundant. UTM = midpoint of plot.

place_name: Erika's #27, Oak Is., Lake of the Woods
remarks: Plot chosen to represent expression of high-quality NPC on Oak Island in Lake of the Woods. In broad, low-gradient drain among bedrock-controlled knolls. No evidence of human disturbance to veg or hydrology. Muck bottomed, water-filled pools with herb and/or floating-leaved cover are ~75% of plot area. Hummocks formed around tree bases discontinuous; feather moss covered. Moderate amount of small to medium dbh CWD, also moss covered. UTM = plot center.

place_name: Erika's #27 Oak Is. Lake of the Woods
remarks: Plot chosen to represent high-quality, natural origin NPC on island in Lake of the Woods. Associated with low, bedrock-controlled knolls in highly variable terrain. No evidence of human disturbance observed in plot or nearby. Occasional stones at surface. Moderate amount of CWD in various states of decay. No charcoal found. UTM = plot center

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #23; Nip Jack Headlands
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #23. Small CWD abundant in plot and medium sized common in NPC patch, all states of decay. Feather mosses common on CWD and ground. Charcoal present. Canopy openings in NPC patch w/much higher cover of tall shrubs than in this plot. Some cobbles/stones scattered at surface, moss-covered. UTM= plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 1.7m @328 degrees from 18cm dbh Abies and 3.7m a@255 degrees from 23cm dbh Abies. Soil horizons: Bw1 (fine sandy loam), Bw2 (loamy fine sand), C (fine sand). Parent material is glacial drift over perhaps ablation till deeper than 81 cm. Excavation beyond 81 cm impeded by large rock.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #64. Abies budworm mortality common in NPC patch. A few old very-decayed cut stumps in plot. One recent lrg Picea mariana blowdown in plot. Small amt of CWD of sm-mediaum-sized. Betula pap is single-stemmed. Charcoal present. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 1.5m @56 degrees from 23cm dbh Betula pap and 4.8m @293 degrees from 30cm dbh Betula pap.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #65. NPC patch and plot impacted by 1999 blowdown damage to Populus trem canopy. Remnant Pinus bank higher up slope. Tip-up in plot. Likely historic high-grade harvest of Pinus strobus in this area. One exposed erratic in plot. Abundant CWD in all states of decay. North 1/2 of plot is moss-covered bedrock. Soil pit in south 1/2 of plot. No evidence of browsing. Feathermoss ground cover except in deepest Abies shade. UTM = plot center and soil pit at tip-up. Magnet in soil pit 2m @60 degrees from 10cm dbh Abies and 2.2m @190 degrees from 8cm dbh Populus.

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #65; Royal Rove Cliffs
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #65. Damage to Populus and Betula canopy trees by 1999 blowdown event winds. Abundant CWD all sizes and states of decay. A few small tip-ups in plot. Browsing minimal, likely moose. UTM = plot center/soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 1.2m @11 degrees from 13cm dbh Abies and 1.3m @282 degrees from 7cm dbh Populus trem.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 yrs old associated with LTP #46. Plot includes Picea mariana windthrow gap. Small - medium-sized CWD common. Outwash near Plouff Creek. UTM = plot center and soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 1.5m @68 degrees from 19cm dbh Picea mariana and 2m @179 degrees from 22cm dbh Picea mariana.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 years-old associated with LTP16. High to moderate amount of CWD, small to medium-sized, various states of decay. Old Populus scenescing, Abies budworm mortality and occasional Picea mariana blowdown. No cut stumps observed. Stones and boulders at surface, moss-covered microtopography. One P. mariana tip-up in plot. E-horizon present. UTM = plot center and soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 2.3m @136 degrees form 20cm dbh Picea mari and 1.7m @ 338 degrees from 36cm dbh Populus trem.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50-years old associated with LTP #64. A few large dbh dead and down Populus trem. Overall, low amount of CWD, most small-sized, senescing Betula tops. UTM = plot center and soil pit. Magnet in soil pit .7m @272 degrees from 15cm dbh Populus grandi and 3.3m @249 degrees from 25cm dbh Betula pap. Soil horizons and exact textures: A, Bw, C (COS). Stones and boulders on surface present. Parent material: outwash. Rock fragments prevented further excavation of soil pit beyond 115 cm.

place_name: SNF LTP Releve #18; Skibo Mill Peatlands
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC at least 50 years-old associated with LTP #57 (SNF). Deep shade. Upland island in matrix of forested peatland. No cut stumps in plot, Betula single stem. Many small standing dead and down, naturally thinned Abies. CWD common, small-medium sized, mostly Populus, one Pinus resinosa. Charcoal abundant. Litter type leaves and needles. UTM = plot center and soil pit. Magnet in soil pit 2.1 m @341 from 21cm dbh Populus tre and 1.7m @282 degrees from 8cm dbh Abies.

Plot marker is magnet buried in soil hole. Site has big, old mossy stumps and repeated furrows are visible throughout area like it was disk-trenched when stand was established. Stand has clear canopy and subcanopy layers. Despite furrows, stand seems pretty intact. Rocks hit at 30 cm soil layer, couldn't go any deeper with auger.
Clay loam soil. Not a very rich or diverse plot. Buried locator (magnet) in center of plot.

Site disturbed by both human (old pine plantation) & natural disturbance (blowdown evidence). Marker type: magnet. LTP 15B. Evidence of deer browse on site. East side of site with abundant exposed boulders/bedrock. Plot set up NW of UTM coordinates. NRCS Soil info: Rollins soil series, F117D NRCS Mapunit.

Natural disturbance at site. LTP 15. Canopy is sparse. Lots of CWD & blowdown on site due to blowdown event of 7/20/2016. Exposed bedrock on site & undulating terrain. Evidence of previous fire-burned stump of very large Pinus & charcoal in soil. Young Acer spic heavily browsed by deer. Soil is fine sandy loam. Permanent marker: Magnet buried ~5 m NE of burnt stump. Plot is set up W & S from UTM point. Litter on forest floor is leaves and needles.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Permanent marker: magnet placed in soils hole. Plot was located ~40 m from edge of Hwy 53 right-of-way. All mature balsam fir in stand were dead from spruce budworm. Plot contained several windthrown balsam fir. No pools of standing water like typically seen in black ash stand. No hummocks. Forest floor litter thickness <1 cm.

Permanent marker: Magnet SE of plot starting point. Plot set up 140 degrees from UTM location (map on releve form). Point moved to get older stand. LTP 14A. Evidence of blowdown within past 50 years, lots of CWD. A couple large old pine stumps form historic logging. CWD mainly Abies and Betula. NRCS soil info: Soil series =Westoo over stratified till. Mapunit=B37B.

Permanent marker: Magnet at Releve UTM location. Plot set up East and South of UTM point. LTP 15. Surrounding area heavily impacted by blowdown event of 7/20/2016. Understory representative of NPC, but canopy blown down on North end of plot. Large amount of CWD, exposed bedrock on site. Charcoal in soil. Soil is fine sandy loam. Litter layer is leaves, needles and moss.

Permanent marker: Magnet 1 meter North of Releve UTM location. LTP 15. Significant blowdown damage from 7/20/2016 weather event surrounding the plot with some Populus blowdown inside plot. Deer browse on Cornus & Fraxinus. Site near a powerline corridor. Soil is very fine sandy loam. After soil layer at 36 cm, coarse fragments are a mixture of cobbles and gravel. Plot set up North and East from UTM location. Plot moved North of powerline to capture appropriate soil.

Permanent marker: Magnet 2 meters west of Releve UTM location. Point moved directly South of parking road (off Fernberg) to capture conifer stand. Plot set up S & W of UTM. Soil is fine sandy loam that is dense till at 46 cm and coarse fragments are a mix of cobbles and gravel. Bedrock located 3 meters from plot. One small worm found. LTP 21. Southern half of plot affected by blowdown event of 7/20/2016, therefore, large amounts of CWD and canopy estimates of cover are low. Understory likely represents forest floor before blowdown with denser canopy. Exposed bedrock on site. Site marked for timber sale. Large fire-scarred pine stump.

Plot adjacent to Bass Lake Trail. LTP28. Exposed bedrock on site. Potentially located in old lakebed of historic Bass Lake before dam broke in 1920's. East side of dry lake ~lacustrine deposits. Plot set up N & W of Releve UTM location. Point moved due to condition of overstory.

Permanent marker: Magnet. Plot set up S & E of Releve UTM location. LTP 14B. Old red/jack pine plantation. CWD throughout stand from snapped pinus. NRCS soil info: Rollins soil series, F117B NRCS Mapunit. From 0-6 cm from surface there is a humus texture. Coarse fragments from 0-54 cm are a mixture of cobbles and gravel.

Permanent marker: Magnet buried ~5 meters west of Releve UTM location. Plot laid out N & W of UTM point. LTP 28. Inside SNF Pinus strobus plantation. 50+ years, stumps on site. Soils are finely textured. Litter 0-2.5 cm, humus 2.5-5.0 cm.

Permanent marker: Magnet at UTM coordinates 610771E, 5285898N. Plot set up S & W of Releve point location. SNF LTP 28A. Pine plantation. Abundant standing dead Pinus banksiana,<10cm dbh. CWD & Betula tip-ups. Soil shows signs of wetness in spring, dry during summer months. Soils 10-19 cm of fine sandy loam. 72-150 cm very fine sandy loam. NRCS soil info: Westoo soil series, B37B NRCS Mapunit.
Permanent marker: Magnet. Plot set up N & E from Releve UTM point. LTP 28A. Moss growing over bedrock pieces with Sphsgnum in depressions. NRCS soil info: Wabuse soil series, B62A NRCS Mapunit.

Permanent marker: magnet. Plot set up N & E of Releve UTM location and moved South to capture canopy. LTP 35. Younger stand with evidence of previous disturbance from blowdown, however, very little CWD. The plot has intermittent low areas that appear to be poorly drained and lack canopy cover. Close to Lake Agnes CRNA and off of Superior Hiking Trail.

Permanent marker: magnet at 713640E,5304243N. Moved plot off FR140/Mink Rd because original location too young. Plot set up S & E of Releve UTM location. Stand located on hillside adjacent to stream and near powerline corridor. Exposed bedrock throughout site. CWD from blowdown in plot center- Abies & Betula pap. LTP 56. Evidence of deer browse on Acer spic and Cornus. Clay/Loam soil.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Permanent marker: magnet in soil hole. Waypoint 12. Forest  floor had small pools of water scattered throughout area. There were also a few scattered unnatural-looking hummocks scattered through the general vicinity and perhaps where a bulldozer blade has been put down in the past. There were a few blown down trees with the root wad well decomposed.

Permanent marker: magnet in soil hole. Old decaying stumps are present. There is a fair amount of insect herbivory on forbs and graminoids, and deer browse evidence on shrubs. A couple deer trails go through Relevé. Plot has very sparse subcanopy. Litter thickness <1 cm. Soil horizons: A, E, Bw (with ferric concentrations), Ex [fragipan characteristics] (with ferric concentrations and iron depletions), Bw' [bisequel Bw horizon], E/Bt [possible glossic horizon] (with ferric concentrations and iron depletions), Bt, Cd. Parent material: ablation till over lodgment till.

Permanent marker: magnet in soil hole. Terrain at this site was part flat soil and part stone/boulder. Entire site is covered by Lycopodium. Stones and boulders looked like half-sunk basketballs and exercise balls covered with Lycopodium. Soil horizons: A, Bw, 2Cd. Parent material: glacial drift over lodgment till. Soil excavation deeper than 71 cm impeded by rock fragments. Alternative NPC classification: FDn43b1.

Permanent marker: magnet in soil hole. Throughout general area, there were a few very old ruts in the soil. They were well vegetated and hard to distinguish. No pools or surface water in plot. Stand lacked a subcanopy. Litter was plant stems and was <1 cm thick. No coarse fragments in soil layer to >53 cm.

Permanent marker: magnet in soil hole. Releve location very restrained. Immediately west is pine plantation with no understory layer (looks very level like it required heavy site prep). Immediately east is old temporary road and young forest. Soil horizons and exact textures: A, E, Bw1, Bw2, E&Bt (sand with sandy loam lamellae), 2C. Parent material glaciofluvial over glaciolacustrine. Landscape/Landform: Lake Plain/Beach.

Permanent marker: magnet in soil hole. Releve in black ash-red maple dominated stand, with scattered pools of standing water and higher ground hummocks. Several large stumps present. A few 50-year old+ overstory trees present, but most of canopy is a younger cohort. Waypoint 6. Soil is a very coarse wet sand. Hit water table at 35 cm.

Permanent marker: magnet in soil hole. SNF Waypoint 16. Old beaver cut saplings present (5-10 cm diameter). A few big old stumps that are very decomposed are present. Old hummocks from past tree tip-ups are also present. Color change of soil at 10 cm.

Permanent marker: magnet in soil hole. Releve survey done by Jack, Anna, & Emma Greenlee. SNF Waypoint 13. Site dominated by aspen. Barbed wire along edge of stand next to road suggests stand was part of grazing allotment in past. First soil layer was very dark suggesting some organic material was incorporated, but wasn't very mucky.

Permanent marker: magnet in soil hole. SNF Waypoint 7. Stand of fairly uniform sized aspen and red maple, high tree density, despite mostly upland herbaceous & graminoid species. Water table hit at 28 cm, rocks hit at 40 cm and could not auger deeper. Litter thickness was <1 cm.
Permanent marker: magnet in soil hole. Soil texture is loam/sand.
Permanent marker: magnet in soil hole. Soil is loam/sand. Wind event 5-10 years ago took the top off several aspens.
Permanent marker: magnet in soil hole. Surface stones and some boulders. A few large stumps present throughout, likely harvested in past. Soil is loam/sand.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Permanent marker: magnet in soil hole. Very shady, mesic site. A few old stumps present as well as large diameter coarse woody debris. A few small surface pools of water present. First soil layer is very dark, like an A-horizon. Leaf litter <1 cm thick.

Permanent marker: magnet in soil hole. Soil is sandy clay loam under thin layer of leaves. Majority below this layer, thick in clay content and smooth when wet. Bedrock was not seen within 50 cm of surface, clay too thick to dig deeper. Plot UTM coordinates are corner/soil pit. Plot goes S & W. Depth to gray or redox features >50 cm.

Permanent marker: magnet. Releve UTM coordinates in NW corner of plot. Keely Creek CRNA on Superior National Forest. Supposedly on LTP 21, but LTP was misclassified. Correct LTP is unknown. Exposed bedrock on site surrounded by blowdown. Charcoal present in soil indicating past fire disturbance. Litter type is moss. Soil texture is loam/sand.

LTP 21C in Cabin Creek CRNA. Lichen on bedrock outcrops. Lots of Betula papyrifera CWD. Disturbed site. Soil series is Greysolon, NRCS Mapunit= F21D. Releve UTM coordinates in NE corner of plot. Gravel, cobbles, and stones in soil layer 15-50 cm.

Plot represents 50+ year old stand in LTP 21D. Located in research natural area. Very little CWD. Evidence of light deer browse. NRCS info: Mesaba soil series, F21D NRCS Mapunit. Coarse fragments in soil layer 0-33 cm was cobble & gravel. Releve UTM coordinate point in SE corner of plot. Plot laid out in Cardinal directions.

Permanent marker: magnet near SW corner of plot @ 673521E, 5285350N. Lake Agnes CRNA. Superior National Forest LTP 21C. Plot along Superior Hiking Trail. Fair amount of CWD (Acer saccharum & Betula pap). Pinus strobus snag just outside plot with dbh of 85 cm. NRCS soil info: Mesaba soil series, F21D NRCS Mapunit. Coarse fragments in soil layer from 7-54 cm are cobbles, stones, & gravel.

LTP 28A, old pine plantation. Very little CWD. Site close to ATV trail. Evidence of deer browse. Green leaf fragments found at 25cm below surface in soil layer, A-B horizon due to bioturbation. Litter is leaves & needles. Numerous earthworms observed. NRCS soil info: Gray calm soil series, F7B NRCS Mapunit. Photos of soils showing bands of clay in sand taken and e-mailed to NRCS. Coarse fragments in soil layer 0-40 cm are gravel, cobble, & stones. Depth in releve to semi-permeable layer and depth to bedrock >200 cm. Plot moved off of 256B due to access issues.

Permanent marker: magnet in NW corner of plot, plot set up N & W of Releve UTM coordinates. LTP 14B. Blowdown area in middle of stand. NRCS soil info: Rollins soil series, F117B NRCS Mapunit. Coarse fragments in soil from 0-58 cm is cobble & gravel.

Permanent marker: magnet. Plot set up 60 degrees from releve UTM coordinates. LTP 14B. Evidence of blowdown on site with thick balsam regeneration. Site 1/2 on slope, 1/2 on flat base with areas of no vegetation where water likely ponds in Spring. Soil is mucky silt loam. Note* LTP is mismapped. NRCS soil info: Aquepts soil series. F5B NRCS Mapunit. Litter is needles and grass.

Permanent marker: magnet at releve UTM coordinates. Superior National Forest LTP 14B. Evidence of blowdown event with snapped snags and abundant CWD. NRCS soil info: Rollins soil series. F124D NRCS Mapunit. Plot set up S & E of releve UTM coordinates. Point was moved slightly to dig pit on side of slope. 1st soil layer (0-7 cm) noted as "A", 2nd (7-9 cm) as "E", 3rd (9-24 cm) as Bw, 4th (24-100 cm) as "C".

Lots of litter. Very depauperate area with white pine in otherwise aspen-birch stand. White pine has 125 rings and was 29.5-inch dbh. Very gentle NW-facing slope. Relevé done as old-growth reconnaissance. Spring season late this year so species list is short. Tree species: Tilia americana (1 tree, 3 boles) and Acer saccharum (4 trees, 15-20 cm dbh).
Forest appears to have a long history of grazing.

Typical of ~2 acres of boggy shore on the western shore of Sundial Lake. This zone covers ~70% of the boggy shore here, remaining ~30% grading to something closer to graminoid poor fen (see Releve B149). Substrate in plot is deep, saturated, moderately quaky peat; "buoyant Sphagnum mat"- T. Whitfeld. +/-Centrally located in this zone, ~10 meters from edge of the lake. Surrounding jack pine-dominated uplands burned in a catastrophic crown fire in July 1996. Lake is loaded with leeches. One or two photos taken of setting.
Rocky- cobbly steep slope ~20 meters downslope from mesic cliff. Releve is mid-slope, above Whitewater River. Rocks covered in moss.
Somewhat junky, but somewhat representative of what is routinely observed as mesic, shady forest that is drier on west-facing slopes. Near road. WP 190.

Gentle toe slope that follows slope and valley floor. This releve is typical of many of these toe-slope areas that are distinct from the valley floor, but also not like the steeper, drier hills above. They are often very similar to the valley floors with abundant Laportea, but with many more drier species too. Juglans average 50-65 cm dbh and white oaks ~30-40 cm. Some Juglans are very large. Waypoints 372-372.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Quite a bit of downed woody material. Several canopy gaps outside plot. Unusually high abundance of Fraxinus pensylvanica seedlings. Oaks large. Seems slightly disturbed in some undefinable way. Moderate amount of leaf litter. Waypoint 218.

River bottom adjacent to Whitewater River. Both ash and walnut have been affected by a late, hard frost which stunted bud/leaf out. Both trees look terrible in all nearby valley bottoms. Nice, large Tilia here, very diverse understory. Not sure if I capture full array of spring ephemerals. Slightly rolling. Soil is sandy loam. Tilia is more common outside plot. Waypoint 196.

Releve to document valley bottom drainage. Done on flat terrace above steeply cut drainageway that slopes slightly to north. Twenty meters to west this flat area gradually rises to steeper slope. This releve is more similar to MHs49. Soil is pure loam with very little sand, very loose and soft. On other side of drainage creek, it's not as flat and quickly starts sloping upwards and is dominated by Tilia and Juglans. Waypoint 289.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Blue Beech) Seepage Swamp
remarks: Plot follows contour of toe slope where this seepage occurs. It's generally about 10 meters wide from the toe slope, with large pools of water common. Plot incorporates pools and small intermittent mucky raised areas. Water shallow, stagnant. Waypoint 249: southeastern-most point for seepage area/pools. Map diagram on releve form.

npc_type_name: Elm - Basswood - Black Ash - (Blue Beech) Forest
remarks: Releve done on terrace close to river. Very open understory. Soil very loamy. Waypoint 212.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Steep, N-facing slope adjacent to where the slightly NE-facing slope meets NW slope. Canopy gaps are occasional to common with large trees in various stages of decay on floor, several of which were large Tilia. CWD from coarse to fine is high. Fair amount of leaf litter. More here than other areas of park. Releve incorporates typical canopy gap, but only corner of it. In this gap is where the majority of tall Staphylea occurs, as well as the Cicuta (on rocks). Somewhat rocky/cobbly. Waypoint 348.

West-facing slope. Burned in the past, evidenced by burn marks on snags and trunks. Just below plot, downslope is a large canopy gap from dead Elm which appears common. Trees are not very large, but largest are open-growth red oaks. Slope ~15-20 degrees. WP 344.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Blue Beech) Seepage Swamp
remarks: Shallow pools of water from seepage are stagnant and follows contours of northeast facing slope. Releve documents only pools and not upland, except where small, raised areas or hummocks weave into releve plot along edges. Waypoint 476.

Not much duff layer. Bouldery on ridgetop of rolling bedrock terrain. Canopy gaps common with many fir down. Dead/dying standing Fir look like they have spruce budworm. Moss cover dominating in these open areas. Releve plot grades quickly into denser Cedar with very little understory vegetation outside plot, which also is where ridge starts to slope down. CWD moderately high. Mostly fir debris & boles, fine sticks. Soil layer color from 5-20 cm is grey-brown. leaves also present in needle litter.

Mostly WFn53 trending. There may be a few stumps in plot, which are decayed and moss covered. Strange abundance of paper birch. Very large, mucky hollows often filled with Chrysoplenium. Dry hummocks very diverse. Lots of Birch leaf litter. Canopy gaps common & releve captures one. No standing water. Waypoint 93.

Should consider including another plot to east of this one for monitoring purposes as it is much more open with more Comptonia. Maybe more what Janet Boe originally captured. Plot put here because it is adjacent to permanent soil data logger. Some areas of stand are very open especially to east. Some of these openings have more hazel and birch than others. CWD moderate to fine. High amount of moss cover. Cut stumps occasional. At NW corner of plot is a red pine =34.5 cm. In the SW corner of plot is a red pine that is Azimuth 174 degrees (almost south) from data logger and is ~12-15 ft away from it, dbh is 43.5 cm. Waypoint 28 (from Kooch-LOW file).

Small areas in releve on west-facing, upper slope, have exposed sand with abundant Cladina. Occasional cut stumps. Jack pine are small, almost stunted. Area may have been sheered in past, jack pine look like they're in subtle rows, because it appears possibly natural origin with no evidence of past discing or trenching. Releve starts at top of sand knob and encompasses west-facing slope. Larger area is rolling, deposit of sand dominated by jack pine. Sand is fine light brown.

No visible moving water, but beginning of large patterned peatland complex. Hollows filled with water, but heavy rain last night. Typical hollow is 2 x 2 feet. Majority of moss cover is Sphagnum centrale. Occasional cut (?) stumps. Hummock height variable. Quite a bit of alder in shrub layer and red maple also seems unusual. Margin of pattern fen. WP 37.

Tamarack, all living- no larch beetle signs. Dense shade in pockets as a result of heavy understory of cedar. Moist hollows common. No standing water. Lots of fine to medium CWD. Southern margin of a larger tamarack-cedar swamp. To south is a zone of cedar that surrounds Pickeral Creek.

All canopy Larix dead from Larch beetle. If Larix were still living, total canopy would be ~50-60% cover. Difficult to estimate cover for canopy. Significant amount of alder, but not dominant. Fair amount of moss cover. Large patches of Carex lacustris in openings, but because of the spruce understory, not completely open to full sun. Hollows moist, but no standing water. WP 134.

Large rock outcrop feature, little to no trees except on margins with occasional jack pine, white spruce, and balsam fir. Abundant lichens. Rock type is dark quartz weathered with chunks of feldspar showing at surface. Mostly solid dome of rock with occasional crevices and boulders. Some parts of rock outcrop are more barren and releve probably includes more Amelanchier and less Juniperus than is typical. Waypoint 163.

Exposed rock is 50-75%. Shallow soil in low pockets which consists of detritus and organic material. Releve on ridge top of rock outcrop which stretches the length (N-S) of the island. Rock is pink granite. Ridge top is level to gently sloping and falls steeply off on the sides (slope 40-50 ft high) to mesic hardwoods below. Rock is rounded with occasional fractures and depressions with more abundant Jack pine, fir, Sphagnum, and occasional Black spruce outside plot. At south end of rock outcrop, bur oak replaces jack pine as savannah tree. WP 190.

Heavily wormed mesic hardwood forest. Heavy browse on Populus tremuloides and Acer spicatum primarily. Soil is compacted. Upper 3-4 cm is silty clay, >40 cm is hard clay. No duff layer. CWD is fine to moderate material and rather sparse. One very large decayed log through center of plot, completely unidentifiable. Aspen is even-aged, with occasional larger Picea in canopy. A few decayed stumps. WP 187. NPC type not certain.

Narrow band of wet meadow on the south side of Youngs Bay. Band of Phragmites and Typha at waters edge, but this releve documents nicer sedge meadow. Water at peat level, lots of thatch. Alder margin to south before cedar swamp. No Sphagnum. WP 155.

Releve captures black ash swamp that is only a narrow band along an unnamed flowing creek. Larger, surrounding                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            area is dominated by cedar swamp. A few cedars scattered throughout, but largely all dominated by Fraxinus, very rich and diverse. Pockets of dense Acer spicatum. Cedar swamp is mostly FPn63, not WFn53. Upper organic horizon is ~4 inches, then 1-2 inches of grey clay, then >6 inches is light grey or gleyed, very fine sandy clay. WP 147.

Relocated original buried magnet and yellow stakes @ SW, SE, & NE corners. Re-established other corners and marked with yellow plastic stakes. Sorbus is only tree still rooted in plot. All historic Jack Pines are standing dead or dead and down. Very dense, tall (>2 m) hazel dominates plot. Plot orientated at 218 degrees, not 170 degrees as indicated in original records (diagram on form). Stand typical of NPC: great fit except dead Jack Pine canopy.

Relocation of Releve #1221. Permanent marker: original magnet buried in plot center, found ~2 ft E of 13-inch Jack Pine. A yellow pencil-sized corner marker from 1988 was found at the NE & NW corner points. Slope was very slight and only visible on western side of center point. Center tree is the largest in the plot. ~10 down, dead Jack Pines in and around unit at 5-10 dbh size. No soil information or tree list provided.

Relocate original plot via buried magnet and established corners w/yellow plastic stakes. Old "woods trail" referenced on original releve form is barely discernible. Many of the Jack Pine in the plot/vicinity are standing dead, dying, or deadfall with few live trees in canopy. Dead jack pine down and covers most of W 1/2 of plot. Original magnet buried at plot center, 2 feet due east of 13.8-inch jack pine.
Red pine plantation arranged in furrowed rows. Numerous old skid trails suggest prior thinning. Basal area ~12, plot relocated via magnet @ plot center, corners re-established.
Found original magnet, re-marked corners. Plot has been thinned since last visit. Oaks from 1997 are no longer present. Red pine slash pile in SE quadrant of plot.

Searched for original magnet for 1 hour (agreed upon time period), could not find magnet. Re-created plot center with a combination of 5 chains from Releve #1224 and slope/aspect information from original plot information. Skid trail through plot. Magnet original location was likely disturbed.

Permanent marker: magnet ~3 inches in soil. Original magnet was found. An 11.8-inch dbh Red Pine tree is 3 ft SW of plot center. The plot is actually about 2 chains from the SW edge of the main harvest landing site. A logging road with year-old slash runs E-W just south of plot center. Plot has also been thinned. N-S logging road (main one) runs right along eastern edge of plot.

Original magnet and corner stakes from 1988 could not be located. Area has been clearcut and is now dominated by dense ~4-inch dbh aspen. New plot established near UTM coordinates given for original plot after extensive search for original magnet. Yellow stakes placed at corners.

8-inch black ash 4.5 feet SW of center of plot. 4.5-inch elm 2.5 feet SE of center. Original magnet could not be found, so a new magnet was established. The northern edge of plot is right next of wet area. (Diagram on releve form).

Plot center is 2.5 feet south of 6-inch bur oak and 2 feet north of 6.2-inch black ash. Original 1988 plot could not be re-located. Plot re-established near given UTM coordinate location under comparable tree canopy. Yellow stakes were placed at each corner and a magnet was buried at plot center.

Could not locate any evidence of 1988 plot. Buried new magnet at plot center, 3 feet NE of 7-inch red maple and 15 ft south of two 7-inch bur oaks. Deep plantation furrows through plot. (Diagram on releve form).

Double-stemmed red maple (6-inch & 4-inch)~6 feet south of center. Five-inch red oak ~7 feet north of center. Original plot center could not be found, so a new plot was established using 1988 notes. Magnet was put at center. The RM & RO (mentioned above) are marked with white and have dotted flagging. Diagram on releve form.

Releve is not typical of stand: less red pine, more paper birch than surrounding area. Original plot was not found. We found topography that matched the description the best. The plot is basically in a bowl. The ridge top is to the south with a 20% slope coming just off the top. The west has a ~6& slope starting within 5 feet of NW corner marker. Northern slope is more slight, ~1-3%. East is basically flat. New magnet was placed between 3-stemmed birch patches. Distance from birches is 5-7 feet. Size of largest birch in each patch is 4.5-6 inches. Diagram map on releve form.

After extensive searching, could not re-locate original buried magnet or corner stakes. Found 31-inch dbh red pine that could be 27-inch red pine mentioned in the original survey. Established plot roughly 30 yards south of it. Twenty-two and 1/2-inch red pine with fork is located 4 feet due north of new plot center. Yellow stakes placed at new plot corners.

Stand has been harvested since plot was established in 1988, and recently replanted with red pine seedlings. Abundant slash, down woody debris. Few standing live trees do remain in cluster within plot. Original magnet located pinned under down tree. Corners re-established and marked with plastic yellow stakes (see diagram on form for layout).

Old magnet found. 18.6-inch dbh red pine 75 feet @20 degrees. Point on north edge of E-W skid road. Very flat with furrows from the plantation. Group of 3, 15-20-inch dbh red pines ~40 feet from NW of center. Recorded as lower quality due to logging and planting.

Twenty-six feet @ 230 degrees from plot center is a 21.5-inch red pine with a fork just below crown. At 21 feet @ 310 degrees is an 11.4-inch spruce from center, surrounded by 5 down logs 5-15 inches dbh. Old magnet found under an ~8-inch CDW. (Diagram on releve form).

Original buried magnet located at plot center, corners re-established and marked with yellow plastic stakes. No canopy trees remain, all logged. Recently planted red pine and white pine seedlings in rows through plot. Large red pine, some smaller spruce and fir surrounds plot, but none fall inside plot.
Permanent marker: 2 foot piece of lathe(?) with flagging. Could not re-locate original plot, re-established plot near given UTM location in similar forest type.
Permanent marker: 2 foot piece of lathe with flagging. Could not re-locate original plot, re-established plot at given UTM location. Map diagram on releve form.

Permanent marker: 2 foot piece of lathe with flagging at plot center. Could not re-locate original plot. Re-established at give UTM location. Original white pine canopy nor stumps present anywhere in vicinity of UTM location. 16-inch red maple ~5 feet west of plot center.

Permanent marker: wooden stake with white flagging. Plot magnet was not found. A new plot center was established as close to GPS point as possible. NW corner has mounding. Some trails are around the plot. White pine poles have been cut and some stacked. Lots of historical and recent birch pole cutting. Map diagram on releve form.

Magnet was found on the NE side of a large aspen tip-up. A 5-inch bur oak is ~5 feet SE of center. To the SW ~15 and 20 feet, there are 2 more bur oaks ~7 feet apart. All oaks are in the plot. Near the northern line there is an aspen snag ~14 inches. Detailed map diagram on releve form.

Permanent marker: 16-inch triangular yellow stake with center magnet. Two corners on 220 degree transect. CNF stand 25/805 from 2016 stand boundaries. Re-sampling of original Releve #1531. Contact the Chippewa NF for management history.

Permanent marker: 16-inch triangular yellow stakes with center magnet. Two corners on 220 degree transect. USFS stand 25/805 from 2016 CNF stand boundaries. Re-measure of Releve #1532. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Permanent marker: 16-inch triangular yellow stakes with center magnet. Two corners on 220 degree transect. USFS stand 33/901 from 2016 CNF stand boundaries. Re-sampling of Releve #1533. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history.

No description of permanent marker type. Stand 25/805 from 2016 USFS stand boundaries. Re-sampling of original Releve #1534. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history. First soil layer 0-14 cm- 2.5 YR 2/1, 2nd soil layer 14 to >28 cm 10 YR 4/4.

Could not re-locate original 1991 plot, re-established plot at given UTM location. New magnet buried 2 feet north of 2-inch jack pine and 4 feet south of 4-inch red pine. Old skid trail runs through plot. Corners marked with 2 foot lathe and flagging.

Plot could not be found again (1997, 2003). New plot center was established near GPS point. Magnet was placed between two 6-inch jack pine in a small (1x4 foot) depression. The plot is thick with jack and red pine, close to a 50-50 mix. Not a unique spot. Map diagram on releve form.

Could not locate original plot, previous attempts to relocate plot also failed in 1997 & 2003. Plot re-established at given UTM location. Magnet buried between two 6-inch jack pines and a multi-stemmed alder. Plot located in red pine/jack pine plantation. Map diagram on releve form.

Permanent marker: Four corner stakes, one in center with metal rebar. East and west corners on 270 degree transects. First soil layer 0-5 cm color 10 YR 2/1, 5-11 cm 10 YR 4/2, 11->30 cm color 10 YR 4/4. Re-sampling of original Releve #1892. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history. Aspect of plot listed as 74 degrees?

Aspect recorded as 100%. Human disturbance recorded on form as a stand modifier for "stand typical of NPC". Permanent marker: Four corner stakes, one in center with magnet. East and west corners on 270 degree transect. First soil layer 0-4 cm, color listed as 10YR 2/1, from 4-10 cm, 10YR 4/3, from 10-30 cm, 10YR 4/4. Re-sampling of original Releve #1893. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Aspect of plot recorded as 224 degrees. Permanent marker: Four yellow stakes and one in center with magnet. Two corners on 270 degree transect. Color of soil layer 0-2 cm is 10YR 2/1, from 2-10.5 cm is 10YR 3/2, from 10.5- >25 cm is 10YR 4/4. Re-sampling of original Releve #1894. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Aspect of plot recorded as 335 degrees. Permanent marker: Four yellow corner stakes with one water stake with magnet(?). East and west corners set up on 270 degree transect. Color of soil layer 0-4 cm is 10YR 2/2, of 4-10.5 cm is 10YR 4/2, of 10.5-21 cm is 10YR 4/3, of 21- >30 cm is 2.5Y 4/4. Re-sampling of original Releve #1895. Contact Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Aspect of plot recorded as 354 degrees. Permanent marker: Four corner stakes, one in center with magnet. East and west stakes on 270 degree transect. Soil color first layer 0-5 cm is 10YR 3/2, from 5-23 cm is 10YR 4/1, from 23- >31 cm is 10YR 5/3. Re-sampling of original Releve #1986. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Aspect of plot recorded as 270 degrees. Permanent marker: Four corner stakes and one in center with magnet. East and west stakes on 270 degree transect. Soil layer color from 0-5 cm is 10YR 4/2, and from 5- >35 cm is 10YR 5/4. Re- sampling of original Releve #1897. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Stand described as having a bit thinner overstory and a bit thicker understory than usual. Magnet found at center, is 7 feet at 60 degrees from a ~7-inch paper birch. Birch is double-wrapped in old pink flagging. Mid to upper slope of 4% slope. A clump of 3 small birches and a 14-inch birch also falls inside plot uphill of center. Basically the whole plot Corylus conuta/Americana up to 8 feet tall. Detailed map diagram on releve form.
Original magnet buried at plot center, re-located along with SE corner stake. Remaining corners re-established.

Stand is atypically spruce-dominated, perhaps more spruce that other areas. Plot center magnet was found at original location, 4.5 feet from a 5.5-inch spruce and a 4.5-inch birch (with a stump between and a large, recently down tree just north). Due to a large hornets nest on south edge of plot a new plot was established. New plot center is 1 chain + 5 feet N of old center and was placed in the center of three 8-10 inch spruce, 2-3 feet from each. Center spruce trees are stripped with white flagging with blue dots. Plot is filled with old down logs. One small (1-inch) red maple is also within 3 feet from plot center. Detailed map diagram on releve form.

Soil photo of spade profile. Found one corner stake, assumed north corner diamond layout. Installed yellow plastic stakes at corners and plot center. No magnet or rebar found. Single old fire scars on N faces of some red pines. No evidence of management or disturbance since 1st sampling. No worms or castings observed. Litter type is needles and leaves. Soil layer color 0-9 cm is 2.5Y 3/1, from 9-17 cm 10YR 3/3, and from 17- >30 cm 10YR 5/?. Re-sampling of original Releve #1945. Contact Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Aspect recorded as 50 degrees. No mention of type of permanent marker. Soil layer color from 0-13.5 cm is 10YR 2/1, from 13.5-17.5 cm is 10YR 3/2, and from 17.5 to >40 cm is 10YR 4/4. Re-sampling of original Releve #2180. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Aspect recorded as 40 degrees. Permanent marker: 10-inch yellow stakes in corners and one in center next to magnet. Two corners and center on transect. Soil layer color at 0-5 cm 10YR 2/1, from 5-10 cm 10YR 3/3, and from 10 to >35 cm is 10YR 4/4. Re-sampling of original Releve #2176. Contact Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Aspect recorded as 50 degrees. Eighteen-inch yellow stakes in the 4 corners. One stake next to magnet in corner. Two corners and center on transect. Soil layer color for 0-4 cm is 10YR 2/1, for 4-8.5 cm is 10YR 3/2, and for 8.5- >35 cm is 10YR 4/4. Re-sampling of original Releve #2177. Contact Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Aspect recorded as 150 degrees. No details about permanent marker type or placement. Soil layer color from 0-5 cm is 10YR 2/1, from 5-12 cm is 10YR 4/2, and from 12 to >26 cm is 10YR 3/4. Re-sampling of original Releve #2181. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Permanent marker: Yellow stakes with pink and orange flagging. Soil layer color from 0-7 cm is 2.5? 4/3, and from 7-30 cm is 7.5YR 3/4. Stand with red pine/white pine supercanopy next to canopy gap. Mid-story and understory of balsam fir. Re-sampling of original Releve #2199. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Permanent marker: Yellow stakes, magnet. Open red pine stand. Paper birch and Balsam fir for mid-story. Soil layer color from 0-7 cm 5YR 4/2, and from 7-30 cm is 10YR 4/4. Re-sampling of original Releve #2200. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Permanent marker: Pink flagging, yellow stakes at corners. Soil layer color from 0-7 cm is 10YR 4/2, and from 7-20+ is 10YR 4/4. Pine and paper birch canopy, balsam fir mid-story and understory some white pine and balsam fir regeneration. Re-sampling of original Releve #2201. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Aspect recorded as 270 degrees. No mention of permanent marker type. Soil layer color from 0-14 cm is 10YR 2/1, from 14-24 cm is 4/2?, and from 24 to >37 cm is 10YR 4/4. Re-sampling of original Releve #2210. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Permanent marker: Magnet is located under tree with vertical orange stripes. Soil layer color from 15-24 cm is 2.5YR 3/2. Re-sampling of original Releve #2141. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history.

Permanent marker: Original magnet buried at plot center. Re-located original magnet, buried at plot center and yellow stake at NW corner. Other 3 corners were reestablished. No jack pines noted in original survey remain in plot, some thinning is evident.

Tallest Picea somewhat mop-topped. Deer trails with fresh droppings apparent. Just west of plot are ~3-foot tall, small-dbh cut stumps- old Christmas tree or treetop cut? No large stumps nor stumps in plot.

Average Fraxinus diameter 6-10", average Thuja 10-16". Becomes steadily wetter and more open and Alnus-dominated to south. Fraxinus dominates in plot moreso than outside plot closer to upland, where Thuja dominates. Plot likely unusually wet (30% standing water) due to higher-than-average rainfall- plants in pools look inundated. Clouds of iron bacteria in some pools.
Re-sampling of original Releve #2178. Contact Chippewa Natl. For. for management history.
RE-sampling of original relee 32179. Contact Chippewa National for management history. Plot marked by yellow plastic stakes at corners + plot center.

Cored Quercus borealis that had 105 rings and a dbh of 23.5 inches. Huge decaying log in stand. Short species list may be partly a function of late Spring. Reconnaissance of old-growth stands with Daren Carlson.

On beach ridge within large peatlands. Forest road about 25m to south. Duff layer soft but appears to have tiny castings, probably Dendrobaena. Condition ranking form completed. No especially large trees or snags in stand. One old cut cedar stump observed. Top layer of soil is A-horizon (black). Some browsed Uvularia. Basal Area Measurement counts for prism plots 1&2: U americana(D) 1,0; F pennsylvania (L) 1,0; A balsamea (L) 5,2; T occidentalis (L) 2,1; T americana (D) 1,0; T americana (L) 3,7; B papyrifera (L) 0,1. Wypt 010 near plot center.

Shallow black A-horizon over muck. Pools few and small--only a few have standing water. Several old cut cedar stumps, but also many logs of fallen cedars up to 50cm dbh at all stages of decomposition. Mosses recorded from soil only,not dead wood. Designated old growth. Basal area counts for prism plots 1&2: Fraxinus nigra(L) 10,0; Abies balsamea(L): 1,5; Thuja occidentalis(L): 1,1; Populus balsamifera(L): 0,1. Wypt 055 near plot center.

Thuja is scattered throughout this stand of lightly acidic Larix and Picea mariana. Plot at grove of Thuja. Pools cover about 30% of plot; only a few have standing water. Most have Sphagnum angustifolium on bottom or are bare. Rich Thuja swamp is many meters to southeast. Some fallen Larix and Abies in plot. Thuja browsed by hares. Possibly FPn63. Basal area counts for prism plots 1&2: Thuja occidentalis(L): 7,5; T. occidentalis(D): 1,0; Abies balsamea(L): 1,0; Larix laricina(L): 3,1; Picea mariana(L): 1,1; Betula papyrifera(L): 1,0. Waypoint 064 near plot center.

Between area with more blowdown and more open canopy and more Picea mariana and Larix and Chamaedaphne to east and denser Thuja to west, but otherwise community seems uniform. Pools cover about 40% of area, mostly very shallow water and pleurocarp and Sphagnum mosses. Lots of treefall and tipped trunks. Very little browsing by hare or deer. Some hummocks >50cm high. May be FPn63. Basal area counts for prism plots 1&2: Thuja occidentalis(L): 15,14; Picea mariana(L): 2,1; Larix laricina(L): 1,0; Abies balsamea(L): 1,0. Waypoint 069 is near plot center.

In far western part of Myrtle Lake Peatland, west of powerline. 15-20 cm dbh P. mariana. Pools cover 50% of plot. Appears to have water flow on air photo. Some small treefall but no logs of canopy tree size. Waypoint 071 near plot center.
Open wet meadow within lowland hardwood forest along creek corridor. Waypoint 105 at southeast corner of plot. Possibly part of an old channel.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: On rolling terrace of Caldwell Brook, including an old flood channel in one corner of plot. Very open understory. There may have been brush clearing for a nearby deer stand, but no sign of it in plot. Very few logs or snags, but there is a component of very old trees (nearby ash >50 cm dbh). Deer browsing is severe, esp. on Acer negundo. Rank is due to earthworms and deer. Waypoint 108 near plot center.

In part of large Thuja swamp with significant Larix and Picea component, much of which has fallen, creating thick young growth. Thuja up to 45cm dbh, Picea average 15cm, Larix average 25cm, Abies 15cm. Cornus browsed heavily. Waypoint 112 near plot center.

Pools have no standing water at this time. They cover about 50% of plot. Some hummocks are covered in Larix needles instead of Sphagnum. In large lakeplain peatland with open fen water track at center. Waypoint 119 is near plot center. Lots of hare browsing on Alnus and Betula.

Edge of large lakeplain peatland with water track at center. West of this community is FPn81(?); at edge of upland to east is more typical FPn63. (There is supercanopy of Larix here.) Pools (no standing water) cover about 35% of plot. Waypoint 120 at plot center.

On upper slope and crest above Big Fork River including both the older forest on the slope and the younger previously cutover forest on the crest. Large Thuja at center of plot - waypoint 123. A few old rotten logs, but few recent falls. Condition ranking form completed. MHn35 or MHn44

Representative of the driest component of a mosaic of MHn44, WFn53, and WFn64. Many small fallen Abies, but less than some gaps nearby--possibly due to budworm. No cut stumps observed. Waypoint 124 at plot center. Condition ranking form completed. Basal Area Measurement counts for prism plots 1&2: Populus tremuloides(L) 7,1; Acer rubrum(L) 2,0; Abies balsamea(D) 3,1; Betula papyrifera(L) 2,0; Thuja occidentalis(L) 4,7; Populus tremuloides(D) 1,0; Abies balsamea(L) 4,2.

About 10cm of hemic peat over about 10cm of sapric peat over clay. Borderline between poorly and very poorly drained. Representative of Thuja-dominated "barely wet" areas between uplands and wetter forests. This releve and B468 represent 2 parts of a mosaic of MHn44, WFn53, and WFn64. This patch of WFn53 is larger than most (~100m across?). Other parts have some larger trees and some old cut stumps. Pool-hummock microtopography is extremely subte. Very little Thuja regen. Condition ranking form complete. Waypoint 125 near plot center.
Sapric peat >50cm, gradually more decomposed at depth. Tussocks abou 40cm tall. Roughly halfway between Valley River and Alnus meadow to north. Waypoint 135 at northeast corner of plot.

Small open graminoid wetland with soft mucky pools covering 80% of area and hummocks with trees and shrubs covering 20%. Surrounded by area of rich Larix-Thuja-Picea swamp within larger water track peatland. Plot is in most open central portion of open wetland. Waypoint 156 at southeast corner of plot.

Two large pine logs lie across plot, one mossy, one more recent. An ancient pine stump nearly rotted away has some charring on it. Other parts of stand have widely scattered Pinus strobus live and dead, but a dozen are visible from plot (in 70-100cm dbh range). Waypoint 186 at plot center. Top 8cm of loam is the A-horizon created by earthworms. Condition ranking form completed.

In mosaic of MHn44 and WFn64. This community has scattered Fraxinus, Ulmus, and Populus trees, but not in plot. Pools (dry now) cover about 80%, hummocks 20%. Waypoint 207 near plot center. Condition ranking form completed.

Waypoint 199 is at plot center. Not many logs in plot, but other parts of stand have more treefall. Humus is combination of mor and moder. Dendroideum is present (1 observed), but no other earthworms. Depression with different species just outside plot. Soil is leached gray. Populus averages 35cm dbh, Picea and Abies 25cm. Condition ranking form completed.

Humus layer appears to have Dendrobaena worm castings. Top layer of sand has been leached gray. Many logs in plot, mostly small Abies, but also medium sized P. banksiana and a large P. tremuloides. Some parts of this stand have larger P. strobus and P. resinosa. Acer spicatum outside plot shows fairly heavy browsing. Condition ranking form completed. FDn32 or FDn43. Waypoint 214 near plot center.

In broad area where water moves north from Myrtle Lake through forested peatland. More Thuja closer to lake. Pools cover about 50% of area. None have water now. FPn82 or FPn81. Waypoint 221 near plot center.

Pools (dry now) cover about 30% of plot. Much of the swamp to the north and northwest was such dense Thuja and Larix that there is hardly any ground layer vegetation, incl. moss. This area has better ground layer. Waypoint 229 near plot center.

The large Pinus strobus is almost dead. It is 7m @ 30degrees from plot center. Lots of logs of all sizes and ages in stand, fewer in plot. B. alleghaniensis trees have all been almost girdled in past near head height, apparently by porcupines. There is a small depression just outside plot w/ wetter spp. Higher ground to southeast appears more like MHn35. Most of stand appears to be MHn44 w/ low spots of WFn53. Soil is incredibly dry and hard. Waypoint 230 at plot center. Condition ranking form completed.

On low sandy plain between road and river to north and forested peatland to south. A few Pinus and Picea are standing dead and a few have blown down while alive. Saw a Dendrobaena worm. Diervilla and Lonicera are browsed by deer. Soil is leached gray. There are old cut stumps in area, but if any of the stumps in plot were cut, they are too rotten to tell. Condition ranking form completed. Waypoint 237 near plot center.

Waypoint 246 is in SE corner of plot. Plot is at edge of beaver meadow, occasionally flooded. Forest is about 20m to northeast. This plot represents the drier shrubs swamps at the upper edge of beaver-controlled wetlands.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: On floodplain terrace, but not clear if it still floods occasionally. It has in the past because one corner of plot is in wet channel cut by past flooding. Plot has less dense 3-4m tall shrub layer than outside plot, mostly Fraxinus. Some old mossy logs outside plot, but less than I'd expect in an old forest. No snags nearby. Many Laportea browsed by deer. Condition ranking form completed. Waypoint 264 near plot center.
Waypoint 269 in southeast corner of plot. In large water track of stunted trees in larger complex peatland. Sphagnum hummocks cover about 85%, pools with no standing water about 15%.

Plot selected to represent the Larix swamp that sometimes occurs between uplands (islands in this case) and water track vegetation (along with FPn63). Pools cover 60% (dry now), hummocks 40%. There are some pleurocarp mosses on pool bottoms. Sphagnum magellanicum and angustifolium are dominant hummock mosses. Canopy trees are 20-25cm dbh. There are several tipped over Thuja and Larix. FPn82 or FPn81. Waypoint 270 near plot center. Trees in plot larger than outside.

Plot represents central portion of large peatland with apparent water movement, but no open water tracks. Closer to edges of peatland are other forested peatland types including FPn63, APn81, and possibly FPn82. Hummocks cover about 80% and pools 20%. Severe browsing of Salix and Amelanchier may be by moose (high up). Some pools have beige algae. FPn81 or FPn82. Waypoint 281 @ plot center.

Waypoint 286 near plot center. Heavy rain last night might affect pH reading. There are old mossy cut stumps--presumably tamarack. Acer and Cornus have been browsed. pH in pool is 6.3, when water taken from seepage after surface moss pulled away is 6.4. Pools cover about 10%, hummocks about 50% of plot.

Releve recorded to represent moderately degraded mesic prairie that grades into wet prairie to the north and south with dry hill prairie to the east, much more shrub cover to the north. Very little duff in this area, potentially this was burned recently. Gallium borale is very abundant throughout area. Grazing history in the distant past.

Releve from WM portion of small wetland basin. There is a nice topo sequence from wet prairie to wet meadow to carex athroides, bullrush and open water. This basin is one of the nicer but others are heavily invaded by RCG and Typha.
Releve to represent extremely degraded wet prairie. Cause of degradation is likely cattle grazing/nutrient enrichment.
Releve in extremely degraded wet prairie. Nicer wetlands are to the south and West of the lake.
Releve from deeper portion of Seepage opening in woodland. Rusty pools below active spring on the east side of this area. Area to the east of here may flood regularly.
Releve from sedge lawn area to the west of a line of cattail and Reed canary grass, with a larger area of Typha to the North.
SHALLOW PEAT OVER WELL DEVELOPED LAYER OF TUFA WITH GROUND WATER FLOWING THROUGH IT, EXTREMELY NICE EXAMPLE OF THIS COMMUNITY. A STRING OF SIMILAR AREAS RUN ALONG THIS SLOPE.
Releve collected from large marsh or seepage meadow for classification.

Calcareous fen running along NW-SE toe slope. Releve sampled in an area with many small marly pools. At a larger scale, there are many well developed areas of fen vegetation separated by small areas of seepage meadows and typha marshes.
Rich fen on floating mat. Area has some impact from nearby road and the north end is more dominated by cattails, but area of the this releve is in very good condition. Water is quite cool.

Releve collected to document annually hayed community which is probably a wet prairie that has lost most of its tall grasses? There are small inclusions of mesic prairie on the north portion. Redtop and carex dominate.

Releve to document a typical wet prairie that has been severely degraded. This appears to have been recovering for a number of years from intense grazing in the past. I would consider this one of the lowest quality examples that I would still map as an NPC.
Releve to document saline wet prairie. Plot stratles a large strip of nearly open salt crusted soil with more vergitation near the north and south portions of the plot.
Releve to document impacted wet prairie on flat loam soil. Seems to be some amount of seepage from the hills to the north but not enough to call this a seepage wet prairie.
Releve to document impacted dry prairie community. The area is recovering from past overgrazing. C rank due to poor grass component and lack of grazing sensitive species.
Releve on degraded dry prairie. It appears to have been over grazed in the distant past, but has had many years to recover.

Releve collected to document annually hayed mesic prairie. According to the landowner this site had mild grazing before 1970. Soil is sandy loam grades into saline wet prairie. More shrub component on neighbors prairie to the east.

This area is currently hayed on an annual basis but had a history of grazing before 1970. Many small sailne pools through this area with different dominate species, some dominated by Poa arida and Carex halli. Soil is covered by sparse salt crust.

Releve from one of the larger open saline patches on the site, the plot has a large open center with more abundant vegetation on the east and west sides. A thick saline crust is present throughout releve.

Releve follows line of more open saline deposits on the soil surface. Center of plot with very sparse vegetation (largely just Poa arida and Triglochin maritima). The area is being grazed but it appears to have little effect on the most saline areas of the prairie.
SNF LTP 62. Waypoint & east is upland hazel and Mountain maple. Best match to LTP is nearer to Sawbill Trail. Water saturation of soil pit at 15cm; extremely wet year so may be higher than normal.

SNF LTP 42. Litter layer also includes leaves. Soil gradually finer texture from surface downward. Sticks present down to 25 cm. Soil smells sulfury. At 25-30 cm, muck and clay mix. At 30 cm and below, taupe color with rusty orange mottling; red/orange color increases with depth. Flowing water observed under surface of soil throughout plot, in holes beneath cedar. Two inches of rainfall occurred 24 hours prior to plot sampling. Standing dead paper birch snags present.

Litter consists of both leaves and needles. Soil pit was wet while digging, but completely filled with water while conducting survey. Soil colors: 0-5 organic, 5-12 brown to gray-brown, 12-44 reddish-brown. Plot located on transition between upland and lowland.

SNF LTP 42. Stand is mixed age with low density aspen and ash (10-12"dbh) and younger ash-aspen (~6"dbh). Moderate to high brush of mostly mountain maple and not much alder. Open pockets of brush where overstory fell down.  Plot located on minor slope. Soils: L1 - dark brown/black with roots and organic matter; L2 - grayish brown; L3 - red brown with grey mottling at less than 5% volume.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: SNF LTP 71. Soil pit filled with water at 25 cm from surface.
SNF LTP 47. Water table hit at 35 cm. Mature lowland black spruce with little evidence of human disturbance. A few small pools of standing water present.

SNF LTP 47. Bottom soil horizon at 44 cm was too wet to texture. Ground water found at 41 cm. This is a productive lowland black spruce stand. No pools of standing water in spite of recent rains; other nearby lowland black spruce stands did have pools. Limited evidence of human disturbance. No recent blowdown.

SNF LTP 71. Mature black ash forest with very dark brown mineral soil. Occasional large surface rock in vicinity, and standing puddles present in hollows. Never reached water table in soil pit but soil auger was not used.
SNF LTP 38 just outside boundary of Sullivan Creek CRNA. Depth to water in soil pit 40 cm. This is a mature black spruce forest.

SNF LTP 47. Canopy gaps nearby and throughout greater stand area but not immediately within plot. Dense, patchy hazelnut occurs throughout greater stand area and one plot corner exhibited this density.

SNF LTP 47 in Southwest Greenwood Creek CRNA. The soil is uniformly dark to 80 cm (photo taken), and seems humus-like. Alternatively, this could be dried organic soil. Ground surface uneven with high and low points resulting from 2-3 foot boulders covered by litter and moss and not from true hummock development from moss. Very moist in low spots. No worm evidence. Litter includes needles and grass. Coarse fragments include cobbles <15% volume.

place_name: St. Louis River Hunter Walking Trail
remarks: SNF LTP 47. Stand has scattered large surface boulders and scattered old stumps. The subcanopy white spruce are all dead. Hit water table at 38 cm. Litter layer also includes needles.

SNF LTP 47. Plot is adjacent to a nearby canopy gap where there are numerous broken off trees - about half of trees are down. Some trees in plot are broken off as well but not many. Depth to water table is 17 cm. This is a productive black spruce stand.
SNF LTP 47. Site is mature paper birch forest on generally SW facing hill. Very rocky, cobbly soil with scattered 0.5-1m diameter boulders on surface. A few old rotting stumps seen in the area.
SNF LTP 47. Mature lowland black spruce forest with heavy Sphagnum moss cover. There was standing water in a few hollows between moss hummocks. Hit the water table at about 60 cm.

SNF LTP 1 in Fall River Fen UBA. Water filled in soil pit to within 6 inches of surface. Site has many old decaying cedar stumps with vegetation growing on the drier hummock bases. In between stump hummocks are low areas with standing water, ferns, Carex spp., and Caltha palustris. Lots of coarse woody debris. Litter layer consists of both needles and leaves.

SNF LTP 71 in Cabin Creek CRNA. Creek running through northern portion of plot. Evidence of blowdown creating coarse woody debris and canopy gaps. LTP delineated along stream riparian corridor. Ecotonal site with upland vegetation (MHn44) on higher slope and riparian vegetation (WFn55) along creek. Drainage class moderately well to well drained. Litter layer consists of needles and leaves.

SNF LTP 71 in Schroeder RNA. Large cedar coarse woody debris in center of plot. Sparse understory. Depressions with standing and running water. Vegetation in understory mainly growing on mounds near cedar bases. Yellow birch and cedar regeneration mainly on nurse logs.

SNF LTP 38 in Schroeder RNA. Plot sampled in transition between upland and lowland to capture upland area in middle of LTP. Northern half is low cedar with sparse understory. Southern half on hill with dense beaked hazelnut coverage and very little coarse woody debris. Stream runs ~15m north of plot. Soil pit dug in transition area between upland and lowland. Litter type consists of both leaves and needles.

SNF LTP 43. Soil layers hard to detect and determine texture due to hole immediately backfilling with water and saturated soils. Lots of downed cedar coarse woody debris. Different species of plants found growing on cedar hummocks, nurse logs, wet depressions, and openings. Lots of microtopography. Both needles and leaves make up litter layer. Able to hear running water below cedars.

SNF LTP 42. A shallow/dry stream runs alongside western edge of plot. Litter layer is less than 1 cm and also consists of decaying bark and twigs. Coarse woody debris of yellow birch and black ash. Middle of plot is very open and dominated by ferns and Thalictrum dasycarpum. Many cobbles and wet depressions throughout plot. Dense areas of hazelnut, tag alder, and red raspberry.

SNF LTP 71 in Lake Agnes CRNA. Never reached mineral soil when digging pit. Large downed cedar in center of plot. Abundant cedar regeneration on hummocks and nurse logs. Upland vegetation found on hummocks at base of trees. Lots of standing water and depressions throughout plot. Plot located downhill from sugar maple stand.

SNF LTP 63. Very sparse understory. Evidence of recent blowdown on north end of plot. No Betula papyrifera standing on site but several downed logs. Feathermoss present on cedar coarse woody debris and trunks. Plot situated 100 m from Border Route Trail. Taxus canadensis near plot at UTM 719137E 5326913N.
SNF LTP 63. Sparse canopy with paper birch coarse woody debris in center of plot. Thick brush cover. Exposed rocks and boulders on hillside. Several depressions from tip-ups.

SNF LTP 63. Very sparse understory except in opening at southern end of plot where blowdown occurred. The rest of stand is thick, young balsam fir with paper birch on hillside with exposed rock. Small creek runs northwest at bottom of hill. Moss growing on coarse woody debris.

SNF LTP 63. Mixing of earthworm castings and soil at top of soil horizon. Heavy deer browse on deciduous shrubs and seedlings. Large exposed boulders on site. Mostly dense conifer stand with little understory except for opening at north end filled with aspen and brush. Big blowdown area along southern portion of plot with coarse woody debris.

SNF LTP 63. Plot on very steep, rocky slope close to Bearskin Lake. Rocks covered in feathermoss. Standing dead paper brich snags ranging from 15-26 cm dbh. Taxus canadensis found on way to plot at UTM 689764E 5326307N.
SNF LTP 38. Blueberry Lake CRNA. Mixing of humus into soil horizon from earthworms. Feathermoss growing on coarse woody debris.

SNF LTP 71. Blueberry Lake CRNA. Fragments of charcoal in soil. Coarse fragments included cobbles in addition to gravel. One small wet depression in SE corner of plot with Sphagnum moss and wetter species. Otherwise, stand has sparse understory of mostly feathermoss with the exception of several small openings where trees have fallen. Plot located on flat area at base of hill.

SNF LTP 43. Evidence of previous fire on charred log. Western portion of plot sparsely vegetated with wetland species. Opening in SE part of plot with denser upland vegetation. Ferns found in low depressions on site. Plot close to snowmobile trail. Leaves present in litter layer in addition to needles.

SNF LTP 42. Past evidence of logging with several stumps. Many downed cedar and yellow birch. Logs covered with moss and cedar and yellow birch seedling regeneration. Evidence of pooled/standing water earlier in the season from discolored litter in low pockets. Leaves in litter layer in addition to needles.

SNF LTP 1. Located in Big Lake-Seven Beavers CRNA. Exposed rocks/boulders on site. Boulders and paper birch and cedar coarse woody debris covered in moss. Standing water between hummocks at tree bases. Plot close to lake shore. Observed dwarf mistletoe on one balsam fir.

SNF LTP 47 in Dragon Lake CRNA. Contour lines show subtle NW aspect imperceptible on the ground. Standing water present only in hollows. Surface pH measured 4 times in different pools. Substrate borders mucky peat and muck with no discernible plant parts other than roots and wood. Very dark to black material. Pit dug in Sphagnum/graminoid hollow and water found 9 cm below surface thatch (roots and drier muck). Litter sparse and only on cedar mounds. Good snags and coarse woody debris; lots of deer scat; hummock and hollow microtopography.

SNF LTP 7. Plot located to best capture low slope leading to swamp but it is a narrow ecotone; plot includes swamp FPn63 to the north and upland FDn/MHn to the south. Upslope (south) side more impacted by past cutting, evident by stumps and dog hair balsam fir. The lower slope (north) FPn63 is higher quality. Soil pit on upslope is very cobbly gravelly mineral soil with no redox features - pure brown color. Water in pit 46 cm below surface. Thick humus layer with charcoal evidence, many roots and cobbles. No real 'A' horizon. Soil on lower slope likely more mucky and very poorly drained; soil on upslope likely moderately well drained; averaged across plot = somewhat PD.

SNF LTP 26 in UBA. Plot located in boulder garden ecosystem along drainage between two uplands and oriented 40 degrees along 40 m side and 310 degrees along 10 m side. NPC uncertain - APn81, FPn62, and FDn32 characteristics. Drainage class unknown. No standing water, but some in interstitial boulder spaces 8 cm deep. Extensive moss coverage on boulders. Just below this moss layer is an organic black muck-mucky peat with evidence of charcoal and no mineral component. Recent heavy rains made all moss and lichen moist. No recent cutting observed. Deer browse seen on deciduous species but no real effect on condition of community. Coarse woody debris common; good snags of sizable jack pine and black spruce.

SNF LTP 34. Plot orientation: 316 and 46 degrees. Plot located on toe slope leading to lowland depression. Evidence of past cutting. Large rocks and boulders seen, especially on upslope side towards upland to the SE. Deer scat seen. Poor cedar regeneration at 2-5 m height. Larger snags and CWD absent. Soil profile done by Jeff Kroll, USFS.

SNF LTP 7. Bouldery black spruce wet-mesic communities lies NE of plot and likely grades into FDn32 outside of LTP 7 polygon. Plot orientation: 135 and 45 degrees. Drainage from NE to SW but at plot level, the slope is too imperceptible. Drainage with deep pools and flow with stones and boulders strewn under the water. Some old, decaying coarse woody debris and smaller <15 cm dbh black ash snags present; no evidence of large legacy trees. No cut stumps or recent logging seen. Soil pit showed rock immediately below MP layer, though muck does occur in rock interstitial spaces. Coarse fragment in muck layer estimated - either boulders or stones. Semi-permeable layer equated to rock at 10 cm. Unsure if bedrock hit or just colluvium collected in drainage. Microtopography with patterned hummocks and hollows.

SNF LTP 26. Plot orientation: NW and NE. Plot located on boulder drainage and associated side slopes but includes both upland and lowland parts - NPC inconsistent; slopes with deeper drift and larger underlying boulders are FDn32c2 with no peatland plants though standing water present in hollows. Standing water limited to <2% areal coverage. Bedrock at surface along drainage (humus absent on exposed boulders under water) but deeper than 45 cm on slopes. Drainage class unknown. Soil pit dug on toe riser; water table 42 cm below moss surface and all mineral soil moist, though colors bright orange-brown with no redox. Charcoal seen in humus. Most boulders covered by Pleurozium schreberi. Coarse woody debris present as are 15 cm dbh black spruce snags. Deer browse seen on thimbleberry.

SNF LTP 7. Plot located in greater FDn43a upland, some cut over with reserved pines. Broader topographic context is gently sloping ESE aspect. Heavy rains evening prior to sampling resulted in pools. Plot with decent-sized trees that haven't been cut as recently as surrounding uplands. Birch snags present; downed logs and little branches present but no large CWD. Old decayed stumps seen from prior cutting. Deer and moose scat seen just outside plot. Boulders/stones poking up from moss just outside plot. Deer browse seen on alder. Very little conifer and deciduous regeneration with open understory. Occasional balsam fir and black spruce knee to waist height.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: SNF LTP 22. Larger LTP polygon encompasses steep banks with upland MHn and FDn species. Plot situated near river's levee, in abandoned channel, and greater "floodplain" flat. Aspect of plot variable due to inclusion of abandoned river channel. Worm castings make up majority of what little soil there is between dense cobble matrix and has low mineral component; heavily wormed, no fine roots. Deer browse seen on mountain maple. Lobaria lichen and Neckera pennata seen on ash trees. Good amount of coarse woody debris, of both ash and elm, in various state of decay; small snags predominate but 20 cm dbh mountain maple snag observed. Stand in a natural disturbance state but no exotic species or recent cutting seen within plot. Reed canary grass seen near river's edge. Flooding surmised to be a very rare occurrence presently.

SNF LTP 7. Plot orientation: NE and NW. Plot located along NW drainage low and toe slopes very near to LTP 24 boundary. Soil pit located on downslope side, and boulders within 24 cm of mucky peat surface. Water table just above rock; pools restricted to surficial boulder crevices.
