Surficial boulders covered in moss but sides exposed and cool air felt between crevices. Microtopography formed by dead wood and boulders. Moss-covered coarse woody debris and snags of black spruce common; no recent cutting. Dwarf mistletoe damage seen on larger spruce. Deer browse commonly seen on blueberry.

SNF LTP 7. LTP plot adjacent to LTP 26 and there did not seem to be a perceptible difference between the two. Both with moss-covered, large boulders and a black spruce overstory. Abundant coarse woody debris from blowdown; snags common and tops broken off of living birches. No recent stumps from logging observed. At 38 cm, soil feels saturated; possible gleying observed at 37 cm. Soil is medium brown, and a 26 cm stone was found. Good humus development with fungal mycelia; fine roots and no worms. Abundant hare browse but not much from deer.

SNF LTP 7. NE corner of plot is within 10 m of Whitefish Lake. Farther inland is a recently harvested stand. Though cutting nearby, none observed within plot. When present, standing water depth is 3 cm; closer to lake, it is up to 23 cm. Some stones/boulders exposed due to tip-up trees. Stand with abundant coarse woody debris but few snags of late-successional species. Soil: Some fine roots found in mucky peat top layer (black) though many small worms seen; castings still make up <50% of mucky peat composition. Second horizon (black-gray) is a mix of mucky peat above and underlying mineral soil. Gray matrix starting at third horizon with orange-tan mottling. Closer to the lake, there is greater abundance of Labrador tea.

SNF LTP 7. Plot orientation: NE and NW. Land slopes 1-2% just outside plot. SW of plot is an area of dog hair balsam fir with little peat, low groundcover diversity, and more trembling aspen mixed in with black spruce overstory: a seemingly drier ecotone on imperceptible rise. Plot with standing water in hollows. Boulders/stones at shallow depth and serve as semi-permeable layer. Sphagnum community a mix of acidic and minerotrophic species with the former mostly occurring under open canopy and the latter in more shaded, balsam fir thickets. Good coarse woody debris of black spruce about same diameter as those standing; few snags, though a 30 cm dbh black spruce snag observed outside of plot. Hollow formed from tip-up black spruce has been completely mossed over. Deer browse seen on some roses.

SNF LTP 7 in Keeley Creek RNA. Plot on toe slope leading to flatter/wetter area to SE. Plot has some upland spp. and exhibits different drainage class on N and NW sides; soil pit dug on NE corner. Cobbles and stones found at 10 cm and equates to semipermeable layer; 8 cm standing water found outside of plot in a pool; water in soil pit was 25 cm below surface. Thin humus layer with fungal mycelia binding Oe/Oa. Mucky peat layer (black-brown) had abundant cobbles and stones; beneath stones was a gravelly substrate intermixed with gray sandy clay loam or sandy clay fine sediment that was too wet to texture properly. Large boulders throughout plot mostly covered by lichen and moss. There was a deep, 30 cm mucky pool over rock that appears ringed by large boulders that help retain water. Moose dung and browse observed on tall red maple. Some coarse woody debris and few snags. Low black spruce regeneration, heavy deer browse, and paucity of snags drops condition rank to 'B'.

SNF LTP 47. Plot surrounded by extensive forest management, but plot is intact more or less. Plot has attributes of both WFn64a and WFn64c. Drier species on elevated black ash tree bases. Soil pit dug to 35 cm and it was saturated and inundated; many wood pieces in black-brown mucky peat substrate. Pleurozium schreberi moss hummock measured for height. High deer browse, low coarse woody debris and snags, little ash regeneration, no large legacy ash, cedar, or spruce all contribute to low condition rank.

SNF LTP 47. Plot situated close to rise to the east of about 1%, where there is some trembling aspen and more open understory. Plot is located on toe/depression and has experienced windthrow with fairly recent coarse woody debris. Some snags seen. Very little spruce regeneration in the shortest height class. Coarse fragment volume estimated and likely stones. Litter negligible - just a few needles at tree bases. Rock under muck layer equated to semipermeable layer. Standing water limited to hollows.

SNF LTP 47. Very pleasant ash swamp; heavy, three day rains made this appear wetter than normal; pools present plus large stones/boulders. Topo lines suggest gradual slope to the north but this is imperceptible on the ground. Stones/boulders encountered at 12 cm and treated as a semipermeable layer. From 12-18 cm, I was able to extract some muck mixed with silty gravel; there is likely a heavy till under the rock. No evidence of recent cutting. Decent coarse woody debris, but no large legacy cedar or spruce logs or snags; most CWD are <20 cm dbh ash. A 56 cm dbh yellow birch observed just outside plot.

SNF LTP 47. Plot is situated in lower topographic context than adjacent area to the north that is drier with more upland species present. Standing water mostly in SE quadrant of plot. This is a young, tamarack stand with heavy bluejoint lawns and dense alder due to canopy openings. Some coarse woody debris, likely black spruce, of similar size as standing trees; snags consists of <12 cm dbh tamarack, though one 21 cm dbh black spruce snag seen. Decent black spruce regeneration. Deer browse common. Soil: top mucky peat layer has many undecomposed roots; 2nd layer is black muck; 3rd layer is black-gray muck with 50/50 mix of organics and sand and fewer cobbles than above layer. Possible outwash sand just beyond depth of soil pit.

SNF LTP 34. Plot situated on toe slope transition from higher FDn32 to wetter black spruce forested peatland; toe slopes on NE and SE corners of plot - flattens to the west. Good jack pine and black spruce coarse woody debris; gaps from tree fall and broken off snags common, especially 4 m tall balsam fir. Deer scat seen. Soil colors of four layers: 1) brown-black 2) gray; parent material derived - not redox feature 3) mottled orange in gray matrix 4) mottled orange in gray matrix. Sandy loam horizon composed of cemented fine sand that can perch water. All horizons moist but water table was 30 cm below surface.

SNF LTP 22. Plot situated close to Sturgeon River. Some floodplain/terrace species present mixed in with typical wet forest species. No recent cutting. Heavy deer browse. Water in soil pit 12 cm below surface. Soil: 1) greasy, black sapric muck 2) mucky gray clay. Very narrow, gray silt lens appears at 47 cm just above clay horizon.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Yellow Birch - Red Maple - Alder Swamp (Eastcentral)
remarks: SNF LTP 47. Stand is very soupy; standing water only 9 cm, but underlying muck is unconsolidated and highly sulfur smelling (stagnant). Surrounding community is alder and very wet with noticeable dying trees. It appears much of stand is in the process of being swamped out. Some peatland species present which suggests community may have been FPn in the past. Lots of black ash snags that will soon fall; a few small-diameter coarse woody debris, many well decayed. Good ash and yellow birch regeneration; doubtful this community will remain - high water will impact future species assemblage. Litter limited to tree bases; muck is reddish brown.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: SNF LTP 7. Plot oriented SE an SW. Most of plot is flat, but land slopes up to NE slightly; thus, E corner of plot is on toe slope. This is a young stand with many aspen snags just outside plot due to wind damage. Coarse woody debris consists of paper birch, trembling aspen, and balsam fir. Some surface boulders inhabit wet hollows. Formerly wet pools indicated by dried, bleached leaf litter. Soil was not saturated at time of sampling but moist. Black wormed mull layer composed entirely of worm castings and had few fine roots (no Oe/Oa) but 15-35% cobbles; middens observed. Tan-orange mottling and reduced gray colors begin just below wormed mull. Cementing of the medium loamy sand begins at 30 cm.

SNF LTP 72. Plot with saturated dark brown mucky pools with lots of wood fibers and small pieces of decomposed leaf litter. This is a maturing black ash stand with declining paper birch - soon will be entirely ash dominated; snags consists of abundant paper birch and few black ash; coarse woody debris consists of medium-sized paper birch and black ash. Oddly, no cedar or white spruce observed. Deer browse lower than comparable ash communities but still considered high.

SNF LTP 7 in Lehtinen Creek CRNA. Plot oriented NE and NW, with wettest zone at south corner. Average drainage is somewhat poorly; two pits dug: the drier one (moderately WD) described in soil profile; the second (poorly drained) with 7 cm fibric peat over gleyed sandy CL. Charcoal and worms seen in humus; humus with some discernible leaves, fine roots, and fungal hyphae. Top mineral horizon is gray-tan with orange streaks and leached charcoal from above. Second horizon has striking, deep orange hues. Most of soil profile was moist; reduced gray splotches begin close to bottom of pit dug to 85 cm below surface where pooling was observed. Large boulder in plot with other stones. Coarse woody debris plentiful with lots of dead balsam fir from spruce budworm. Aspen snags present.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: SNF LTP 8. Plot situated on low and toe slopes and has some MHn46 character, but WFn55 still more appropriate. Soil pit dug on toe slope just above wettest part of plot. Drainage estimated since gray matrix was not seen at depth; gray-tan color of mineral soil presumed to be color of parent material and not from redox. Mull humus, if present, is heavily wormed. Top horizon is a black 'A' with night crawlers and one 2-3 cm pebble excavated. A very large snag of trembling aspen seen; coarse woody debris abundance less than that of snags. Canopy strata has lots of layering to one side of plot but south end very open.

SNF LTP 73. Charcoal seen in brown-black mucky peat layer. Exposed buttressed roots indicates possible burned off peat. Though soil was moist, some Sphagnum surface is dried out. 1st mineral horizon uniformly gray-tan and somewhat cemented; loamier than horizon below. 2nd horizon coarser, tan with streaks and concentrations of bright orange. Good amount of snags and coarse woody debris. Poor black spruce and tamarack regeneration above knee high. Deer browse appears high as seen on red maple and hazelnut.

SNF LTP 8. Plot spans MHn44 and WFn55 with latter closer to western boundary and subtle slope up to the east; slope becomes steeper farther to the east towards upland. Some underlying stones/boulders on NE plot corner. Soil: 'A' horizon black with roots anchored within; 2nd horizon cemented fine loamy sand that is tan matrix with gray and orange redox features. Very little coarse woody debris within plot; snags limited to balsam fir possibly due to spruce budworm - none large.

SNF LTP 7. Plot oriented NE and NW. Plot mostly situated in a trough; slight 1% grade at south corner. Soil: top coarse loamy sand horizon is black-gray; second coarse LS horizon is gray with faint orange-brown and cemented into hardpan. Soil felt dry and powdery. Deer browse line observed on downy arrowwood. Large trembling aspen coarse woody debris of moderate decay class; medium-sized snags abundant resulting in canopy gaps. No black ash observed perhaps due to limited seed source as surrounding community is pine-aspen upland. Good red maple regeneration and white spruce in the 10-20 cm dbh size class. White spruce will form future late-successional canopy.

SNF LTP 47. Part of plot more like WFn64c (far west side) that is flatter, less hummocky, and more Glyceria and Carex stipata. However, majority of plot with noticeable microtopography. Some old, decayed, large cedar coarse woody debris seen just outside of plot; no large snags however, just understory-sized saplings. Prior to sampling, heavy two-day rains occurred in the area - may be reason for late-season standing water. Soil color dark brown-black for both mucky peat and muck layers.

SNF LTP 7. Plot oriented NE and NW. Situated in valley drainage between steep rock wall on SE side and gradual low slope to upland transition on NW side. Interior of plot very poorly drained; parts closer to upland edge with shallower organic layer is somewhat PD and more appropriately WFn55. No standing water observed, but surface is mucky. Both muck and silty clay layers black in color. Greater litter abundance closer to upland but none in interior. Surface boulders common. Moss hummocks of Rhizomnium magnifolium. Abundant worm castings in muck layer. Birch and balsam fir snags observed. Most coarse woody debris consists of abundant, small to medium-sized balsam fir.

SNF LTP 47 in UBA. Plot situated in depression but close to 1-3% upland slope to the SW, where conditions become richer. Some of the uplands to the NE have been burned by wildfire recently. Recent blown over spruce has caused canopy gap in center of plot. No snags observed. Many old snags likely had fallen, adding to coarse woody debris pool, and subsequently mossed over. Deer browse observed on mountain maple and red maple. It is odd to see yellow birch but no cedar or black ash. Mucky peat layer is red-brown and muck layer is brown-black. Standing water, if present, is only 0.5 cm deep.

SNF LTP 22. Plot oriented NE and NW, with higher terrace towards N corner. Plot is slightly on toe of terrace with  1-2% rise; however, majority is on first bottom flat of floodplain. Litter confined towards terrace, otherwise none or little scraps of silver maple leaves. Soil is wormed mineral soil with 8 cm root mat and some Oe present but no humus. Majority of soil profile is dull brown-gray but at 42 cm, khaki tan spots appear. A jet black, almost organic looking 'charred' layer occurs at 40 cm. Excellent coarse woody debris, but not windrowed, and commonly seen snags of moderately-large sizes. There was one large green ash snag. Deer browse prevalent on ash species. Adjacent terrace (~25 cm higher) with thicker ostrich fern, winterberry, and Thalictrum.

SNF LTP 72. Sampled at 4 p.m. after all day rain. Standing water in hollows only. Stand appears to be FPn62 converting to FPn63. Ground layer indicates latter even though black spruce is more numerous in canopy layer than cedar. However, the dense cedar regeneration suggests that there will be eventual cedar canopy. Very nice microtopography and interesting species assemblages. Coarse woody debris of fallen black spruce; canopy openings facilitate cedar recruitment. High deer browse but cedar regeneration still high; many cedar unbrowsed. Mucky peat layer brown-black; muck layer black.

SNF LTP 8. Plot oriented NE and NW. Plot located in a drainage with toe slopes on N and S corners. Toe slopes 1-2% and midsloping upland up to 20%. Heavy rains day prior to sampling. Boulders present but covered by vegetation. Black/dark brown muck substrate with estimated stones underneath. Digging of soil pit difficult due to standing water, stones, and thick roots. Gravelly loamy sand seen exposed just outside plot on toeslope - likely underlying muck within plot. Good coarse woody debris,  some as inputs from adjacent upland (e.g. aspen). This is a young stand without legacy white spruce or large snags. Decent ash regeneration at chest height. Drier species seen on toe slopes but majority of plot located on nadir of drainage and is very wet.

SNF LTP 22. Stand is very wet and mucky. Species composition has some floodplain/terrace character but wet forest species also present. Meadow species occur closer to the river. It appears that the wetness is caused by inundation from a high water table and not due to periodic flooding anymore; soil substrate is organic and not mineral, at least for upper 45 cm. Snags of black ash prevalent. A couple of 20-30 cm dbh coarse woody debris logs present. Deer browse prevalent on elm, winterberry, and ash, but not on alder. Reed canary grass perilously close to plot infiltrating from levee/meadow of stream. County Road 180 may affect hydrology of Pelican River; however, it is uncertain if there is any direct hydrological effect on this community.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: SNF LTP 52. East end of plot with a north-south, low-relief 4 m X 20 m linear mound rising 25-50 cm above level of swamp and appears natural. Similar species as rest of plot but likely better drained. Parallel to this mound on its west side is a dried channel of previously-flowing water. Soil: very sparse humus layer that is full of castings. First mineral horizon is a black, high-organic 'A' horizon; second horizon is a reduced gray matrix with orange mottles. Both clay textures trending towards silty clay. Good snags of large white spruce, smaller black ash, and decent coarse woody debris. Ash regeneration is poor.

SNF LTP 7. Plot situated in localized valley bottom and oriented at 276 (10 m side) and 186 degrees (40 m side) to best capture linear drainage; west end of plot goes up toe slope. This trough is technically without aspect; steepest slope from SW corner at 4%; 1-2% within trough itself. Plot exhibits some marsh vegetation at lowest point and upland species on slopes; larger LTP polygon seems more FDn43b1 with inclusion of APn81/FPn62. Some surface rocks present. Soil pit dug in lowest point. Darkened, matted litter suggests early-season inundation. Muck layer with some mineral component and is black; coarse sand layer tan-orange-gray; sandy clay loam layer orange with redox gray spots - seepage observed at this depth.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: SNF LTP 8. Young stand located in narrow drainage sloping imperceptibly westward. Moderate to small coarse woody debris and no large snags. Heavy deer browse and heavy worming; no large legacy white spruce; decent ash regeneration at 5-10 m height class. Soil: muck layer with abundant castings and black in color; fine roots throughout. At 16 cm, a clayey blue-black sheen layer appears beneath the wormed muck layer.

SNF LTP 8. Subtle 1% slope trending south and increase in wetness where there are open pools; southern 1/3 of plot is inundated and has more alder. NPC changes farther to south to WFn64a. Soil: top muck layer (black) mixed with clayey material transitioning to mucky clay (black) then to clay that exhibits bright yellow and orange in tan-gray, gley matrix. Nice coarse woody debris throughout stand, up to 40 cm dbh; large-diameter snags present of black spruce and trembling aspen. Worm castings present but make up <50% of muck layer.

SNF LTP 52. Very wet ash swamp with no surface water at time of sampling but saturated. Stand appears to be transitioning from former forested peatland to current ash-dominated swamp. A few large cedar, white spruce, and black spruce occur just outside plot. Abundant small to medium-sized coarse woody debris but few large; large snags uncommon. Dark brown mucky peat with abundant decomposing wood.

SNF LTP 7 in Sullivan Creek CRNA. Plot located on gradual 2-3% slope transition from upland conditions to the west and lowland APn80/81 farther east. Black spruce coarse woody debris and snags common. Heavy deer browse seen on mountain ash and red maple. Standing water observed in only one pool; Sphagnum girgensohnii forms moss hummocks. A needle-based mor humus is forming on top of the Sphagnum-based fibric peat. Peat layer is yellow-tan; sandy loam layer is gray-brown; sandy clay loam layer is gray-brown.

Stones and boulders abundant to near continuous (60-90%) at surface with mucky hollows in between. No standing water on date; vegetation minimal in deeper hollows. Patchy muck humus noted. Hard to discern extent of earthworm activity. Soil profile: 1)muck, 2)silty clay (gray) with scattered reddish and lighter gray mottles throughout. Browse heavy to moderate. UTM = SE plot corner.

Stand uniform, mostly even-aged black spruce. Plot contains small canopy gap created by tip-up and several broken spruce tops. Some evidence of old stumps buried under sphagnum. Best estimate of mineral soil at 54 cm is loamy sand. UTM = SE plot corner.

Center of plot with more closed conditions of oak and pine FDn22; two very girthy but short white pines in plot. One 12 cm dbh downed white pine seen with no bark left. Inside this forested patch is a carpet of Carex pensylvanica. Most oaks exhibit stunted form and collar sprouting. Boulders and exposed rocks common; exposed rock (5%) includes crustose lichen growing upon them. Very few coarse woody debris and snags. Condition ranking due to high worming and Carex pensylvanica carpets. Soil pit dug in open and not in forested patch.

High-quality DNR designated old growth, OG7-11, white spruce with some white pine outside of plot. Excellent snags and large coarse woody debris of old white spruce. Many of the living white spruce have broken off tops and are dying. No recent cutting observed. Light worming has yet to affect diverse groundcover. Browse is high and conifer regen is low; however, hardwood regen is adequate. No fire evidence. Recommend continuing old growth management. Soil with nice humus and its fungal mycelia and fine roots. A black-gray 'A' horizon suggests effect of worms. Middle horizon is whitish gray-tan and is sandiest of observed horizons - may be waved-washed till. Third horizon is gray-tan with mixed brown-gray and orange flecks. All soil is moist and  depth to redox is estimated to be between 25-50 cm deep. Wet swales occur throughout plot. Soil pH tested at circumneutral and possibly reflects the carbonates of Koochiching sublobe drift of Des Moines lobe.

Plot orientation: SE and NE. Overall stand has large aspen with nice large snags and coarse woody debris. No cutting or stumps seen. No trails detected. Parts of stand with very dense balsam fir and beaked hazelnut. Good white spruce and balsam fir regeneration; black ash also present. Windthrow from aspen and balsam fir caused canopy gaps. Most of plot is very flat and NE aspect is estimated; seems to slope to WFn on all sides of island. Soil exhibits very nice structure with no evidence of worming, good Oe layer under litter with fungal mycelia - a classic moder humus with fibers at the top and greasy decomposed residue towards the bottom grading into a thin gray-black 'A' horizon. Second horizon is gray-tan and  moist and barely holds together; could be close to a coarse loamy sand rather than sandy loam. Third horizon is gley-gray but no pooling water. Soil pH tested at 7.5-8.0 but no carbonates observed. Soil origin possibly till  over glacial lake clay.

Land slopes imperceptibly to the SE towards the water and gets surprisingly drier but with Leucanthemum vulgare and Cirscium arvense. It terminates at a meadow with abundant Phalaris arundinacea surrounding the water. The presence of Rhamnus frangula is very problematic also. Soil is saturated hemic peat over gray silty clay. Some open pools are present and more Sphagnum moss appears to the north as one approaches APn81 15-20 m away. Surface water pH measured 3x at 4.2, 4.2, and 4.8.

Plot orientation: 162 and 72 degrees. Toe slope on NW corner of otherwise flat plot. Birch presence could be due to fire since charcoal was detected in soil. However, there were no black ash snags, coarse woody debris, stumps, and few living stems >10 cm dbh. Some birch snags present and one 25 cm dbh balsam poplar downed log observed. Ash and cedar regeneration are moderate and poor, respectively. Near the plot, there is a two meter wide creek that eventually flows NW into WMn82b1 and open water. There is likely some subsurface water flow within the plot. Two soil pits dug: upslope - water table 40 cm below surface, charcoal presence, worm castings but Oe and fine roots present, abundant wood pieces, deeper muck layer, though dry, before reaching mucky peat layer; downslope - water table 15 cm below surface, abundant wood pieces.

Plot is flat with no perceptible trending slope though land rises and fall subtly in various directions <1%. Snags and coarse woody debris observed of paper birch and balsam fir. No cut stumps seen. Browse seen commonly on mountain maple. Soil pit exhibited moist but not saturated muck soil within the first 34 cm. Water was easily squeezed out at 34 cm below surface. Color was black to black-brown. There is the slightest of an Oe layer and an 11 cm thick fine root mat above the muck layer.

Plot with no obvious aspect though undulations in the land occur due to past flood deposition causing rises and dips in multiple directions. NW corner of plot more WFn with exposed muck and less leaf litter and Calamagrostis canadensis, Lysimachia thyrsiflora, and Lycopus uniflorus as it transitions to more tag alder and black ash. Plot with few coarse woody debris but snags of black ash common. High deer browse on Corylus americana. One very large branchy American elm occupies 25% of canopy within plot. Soil: top horizon black-gray; second horizon gray with muted orange mottles and moist with visible water seepage.

Sampled to document possible old growth. This is DNR designated old growth OG12-38, but conditions do not confirm; has mature stand characteristics but not quite old growth yet. Plot without obvious slope but some shape is apparent with <1% slope; LIDAR shows subtle SSW aspect. Nice coarse woody debris and snags of white spruce through entire stand, leaving natural canopy openings. Patches occur outside of plot that have greater trembling aspen canopy or aspen over dense cedar subcanopy causing low groundcover diversity and cover. Heavy worm impact (Lumbricus terrestris presence) and deer browse; some shrubs appear hedged by deer, and regeneration of tree species likely impeded. Soil drainage and depth to redox features estimated to be somewhat poorly and greater than 25 cm, respectively. Top horizon is a black 'A' and bottom horizon is a muted tan-gray with mustard-colored flecks. Both are fine sandy clay textures.

Entire river ecosystem typified by FFn57 levees and terraces with abandoned back channels of larger silver maple on frequently flooded FFn67a. Plot slopes in multiple directions to abandoned river channels. Many overstory trees with wind-caused top breakage. Most basswood stems originate from single root crowns. High water marks and moss growth observed on trunks of trees at approximately 70 cm. Top soil horizon black. Second horizon gray-tan with orange mottles.

Lateral groundwater flow possible (see watershed catchment flow) but not obvious on aerial imagery.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners

remarks: Quite local occurrence of mature northern pine-hardwoods along South Fork Whitewater R. Long edge of plot running horizontally along mid-slope of an extremely steep NNW-facing bluff (aspect essentially north here), in a sharp river bend. Plot perched between dolomite cliffs both above (on upper slope) and below (on lower slope). Substrate is rich silty sand; upper slope with sandstone exposed in places (limestone/dolomite above it). No stumps. Too steep and inaccessible to have been grazed. Snags infrequent. Moderate amount of CWD.

Gently sloping mid-slope of drumlin along South Branch of Little Elk R. Supposedly never grazed (and presently little evidence thereof). Scattered supercanopy white pines were removed in distant past; the one in the plot is the only one which was encountered in the 30-acre patch. This patch of forest is unusually rich floristically for central Minnesota- borderline MHs39? Grades downslope into lower diversity (MHc37?) then into WFn55. Snags infrequent, no stumps present. CWD rather sparse. Light earthworm abundance. Heavy deer browse throughout.

Possibly MHs49 due to a number of southern species- unusually rich floristically for central Minnesota. Gentle SE-facing slope of drumlin along South Branch of Little Elk River. This eastern part of 30-acre mesic forest patch is more mature than the West end of the patch; the plot is also in the most floristically rich and moist zone encountered in the patch. Eastern edge of plot ca. 20m from edge of WMA (adjacent cropland). Two-track road ca. 20m to west of plot. Downslope ca. 15m is vernal ash swamp and sedge meadow. Subtle groundwater seepage on slope 20m to south (outside plot). CWD rather sparse. Snags infrequent. A few very old white pine stumps nearby. Earthworms absent or rare. Heavy deer browse throughout 30-acre patch.

Plot +/- centrally located in ~1-2 acre seepage meadow perched on gently sloping terrace along ravine, north side of Interstate 90, in cattle pasture  that is currently rather heavily grazed (though somewhat less grazing pressure in wetland patches). BC(B?)-rank. Groundwater seepage is diffuse. Substrate mostly firm, saturated, black silty muck ~30cm deep then more loamy below 30cm. Edges of plot ~15-20m from edges of the Carex stricta / seepage zone here (upslope/downslope).

Typical of, and centrally located in, ~1/2 acre (30x40m) seepage wetland zone on gently sloping (nearly level) terrace along a ravine in cattle pasture on the North side of Interstate 90. Edges of plot ~15-20m from the edge of the wetland (where vegetation grades to upland cool-season grass due to moderately heavy grazing). Forb poor here. Wet muck, firm.

Perched on lower third of a gentle east-facing slope (~2 degrees), in a broad ravine on the north side of Interstate 90, in a moderately heavily grazed cattle pasture (wetland zones with lower grazing impact than the adjacent uplands which are dominated by typical pasture grasses/weeds). Plot is centrally located in Carex stricta zone, the edges of the plot are ~10-15m from the edge of this zone.  B-rank here- best condition of everything in this rather large seepage wetland complex. Substrate firm to slightly quaky wet muck. Sedge hummocks 4-12" tall.

Typical of, and centrally located in, ~1-acre zone dominated by Carex prairea, in outer portion of an ~8-acre seepage wetland complex on valley bottom between steep 240-foot bluffs. Edges of plot ~5-10m from edge of this zone. Essentially level (~1% northerly slope). Grades to Carex stricta toward the upland (seepage source), and in wetter spots to zones dominated by Scirpus validus. Typha invading in places. Substrate is slightly quaky muck wet, shallow water in foot tracks. Floristically somewhat depauperate? Past grazed. Seepage flows nearby (~20m away- not present in this zone). BC-rank (wetland complex variously degraded, varies from BC- to CD-rank). Sedge hummocks are 4-12 inches tall.

Plot typifies the central zone of ~3/4-acre wetland in similar-sized depression on a broad mid-bluff terrace along the South Fork Whitewater River. Substrate is quaking peat (sedge peat), wet/saturated with ankle-deep water in foot tracks (precipitation has been above average recently). Edge of the plot is fairly close to the outer zone of the small wetland (which is being invaded by Typha X glauca). Also, vegetation grades to an area where Salix petiolaris is fairly common. The releve zone is the main expression of this wetland, covering ~60% of the basin. A-rank. Basin is narrowly rimmed by black ash, then by MHs39.

Typical of old growth mesic pine forest on strongly-rolling moraine. Plot captures much of a moderately steep, 30- to 40-foot, North-facing slope. AB-rank. Natural origin. Grades to areas of denser tall shrubs/understory and back again, and also to areas with fewer pines. CWD sparse- a few large old boles. Snags are infrequent. Old fire-scarred wood (trunks and natural stumps / snags) occasional in the larger stand. Thick needle litter (2cm), duff/humus 3-4cm, 6-8 cm of loamy A-horizon- black, then coarse sand and gravel with numerous stones and small rounded rocks. A few old cut stumps in the vicinity; an old two-track road peters out just to east (south) of this plot.

Typical of better quality natural origin old growth pine on strongly rolling moraine. Plot positioned on irregular terrain- slope varies from North (mostly), to West- and East-facing, to level (at top and bottom of a moderately steep slope). No old stumps. Snags are occasional- a couple large ones in the plot (Pinus strobus, Pinus resinosa). Fire scars on old stumps/boles/snags in the greater vicinity (occasional in the larger stand). CWD is rather sparse though several large old boles (70% decayed) in/near plot. Soil is coarse sand with cobbles, with ~5cm cap of loamy-sand (A-horizon). Fairly thick needle litter (2cm). Photos ~6:15 pm.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Loamy soil on north-facing slope adjacent to drainage ravine. This is somewhat typical of these forests that are on the mesic-dry spectrum on north-facing slopes in GRB area. Several downed trees creating new and old canopy gaps.

Small basin (~lac), with small open water with soft-stem bulrush adjacent to pool. Very loose mat that is easily borken. Bottom is ~2ft under mat. Sparganium forms dense cover, especially in center. Various brown mosses cover mat, <50% cover. Plot does not include open water, and was done in center of basin away from edges. This plot was done in conjunction with a well monitoring site. A well was installed near open water by Keiler Andrews in the spring of 2016.

Plot chosen to represent expression of NPC in Little Fork-Vermillion Uplands Subsec., part of margin of lrg peatland complexes where ecotonal conditions & NPC heterogeneity are common. Graminoid cover =75%. Bryos common on tree boles. Microtopo of hummocks(-)/ hollows(+)water-filled this date, dry by late July. Mesic forest herbs on tree bases. More spp rich than WFn64 elsewhere; staff would call floristics WFn55 elsewhere.Cut cedar stump w/fire scar. Coordinates =SW corner of plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC common in Koochiching Peatlands LTA and habitat of Cardamine pratense v. palustris. Frequent standing water pools; highly variable hummock & hollow microtopo. Moderate amount of CWD. Growth form of Fraxinus and Thuja indicative of water stress. Deer browsing evident. Coordinates = mid-point of plot.

The Helianthus individuals previous identified as H. grosseserratus is intermediate/ambiguous. Stems with scattered stiff hairs. Petioles often >1 cm. Involucral cilia variable in length. Waxy bloom found on a small portion of one stem.

Plot chosen to represent NPC margin of large peatland complex in Littlefork Vermillion Uplands/Kooch Peatlands LTA. Variable microtopography of hummocks(+) and hollows(-). Mistletoe damage/mortality of Picea mariana. No evidence of past harvest. Growth form of Thuja suggests water stress. Coordinates = midpoint of plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC expression common in Kooch Peatlands LTA, in Thuja dominated band at margin of large peatland complex. Occurs between WFn55 (adjacent to upland) and FPn63. No evidence of anthropogenic disturbance. Microtopo well developed. Pools common; moss-covered bottoms. Feather mosses dominate cover of CWD, tree bases and elevated roots. Abundant CWD of all diameters and states of decay. No muck observed. Coordinates = SE corner of plot.

Plot chosen to represent expression of NPC in flat settings among peatlands in Kooch Beach Ridges LTA at margin of large peatland complex. Soils moist to wet. Deer browsing evident but woody veg has low cover not clearly related to browsing. Coordinates = NE corner of plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC expression in Beltrami-Pine Is. Peatlands LTA of Agassiz Lowlands. No standing water on this date suggests pools are shallow. Presence of hummocks and hollows microtopo variable across patch. Hollows/pools small. Pools likely no more than 4cm deep when present. Possible very old, small-medium diameter cut stumps, maybe Thuja. Little to no browsing evident. Bryos and lichens on tree boles; not as abundant as in old forest. Low to moderate amount of CWD. Coordinates = midpoint of plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC expression and condition common in Beltrami Pine Is. Peatlands LTA of Agassiz Lowlands. Mistletoe present in canopy and regen Picea mariana.Broken canopy and subcanopy. Low amount of CWD. Decaying cut stumps evident. Hollows infrequent, mesic to wet this date. Little to no standing water. Coordinates = midpoint of plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC expression in Beltrami-Pine Is. Peatlands LTA of Agassiz Lowlands. Mature to old growth stage. Decaying, old cut stumps in patch none in plot; species unclear. Highly variable microtopo of pools and tree/shrub bases. Pool bottoms moss-covered. Moderate amount of sm-medium diameter CWD, evidence of large diameter CWD, now much decayed. Tip-up just outside plot. Coordinates = mid point of plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC expression as part of fine-grained complex of WFn/FPn communities in Beltrami-Pine Island Peatlands of Agassiz Lowlands. Portions of complex may have been influenced by hydrologic changes associated with ditches to E and W. Cryptograms common on tree boles. Mosses also cover tree bases and abundant CWD. Thuja windthrow (full and partial) common. Pools up to 15 cm deep. Intersecting pools = ~50% of plot. Mesic forest herbs on tree bases and CWD. No standing water this date. No discernible cut stumps. Coordinates = midpoint of plot.

Plot chosen to represent one expression of NPC w/in heterogeneous ecotonal margins of large peatland complexes in Beltrami-Pine Island Peatlands of Agassiz Lowlands. Mostly sm to medium diameter CWD, moderate amount = Abies, Betula and  Thuja. Mosses very patchy on ground; common on CWD and lower tree boles. Old cut stumps (mostly sm diameter) in patch and plot. Severe browsing. Lack of Thuja regen/recruitment does not appear to be browse-related. Soil w/gray colors at 20cm and below. Coordinates = midpoint of plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC associated with Tamarac River and other rivers in Beltrami-Pine Island Peatlands LTA of Agassiz Lowlands. May be located on old river terrace now much elevated above channel, no longer flooded. Deer browsing moderate to severe. CWD in all sizes and decay classes. No cut stumps in plot. MNDNR designated old growth forest. Coordinates = midpoint of plot.

Plot chosen to represent common NPC type and condition in this area of Beltrami-Pine Is. Peatlands LTA in the No. MN & Ontario Peatlands Subsection. Hummocks and hollows well-developed; pools typically small and drawn down on this date. Some hummocks topped by lichens. Moderate amount of old and recent CWD. Mistletoe mortality of Picea mariana; a few dead and down in plot. Evidence of deer browsing is low.Coordinates = midpoint of plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC likely harvested ~1950. Patch variable - some areas w/more P. mariana in canopy, more Thuja in subcanopy, lower cover of Alnus incana. Larix is mature. Well-developed hummock and hollow microtopo - hummocks = 2/3 of plot/hollows = 1/3 of plot. Evidence suggests water probably doesn't stand long in most pools. Minimal evidence of browsing. Coordinates = midpoint of plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC common in small drainages influenced by beaver activity of Beltrami-Pine Is. Beach Ridges LTA of Agassiz Lowlands. Previously beaver flooded, drained and now meadow adjacent to narrow channel. Brown mosses common on peat substrate. Many Thuja and Larix snags at edge of adjacent swamp forest. Regen up to 10m tall of these spp @ margin of meadow. Betula pumila dominant shrub near channel on south side; Alnus incana and B. pumila mix on north side. Thuja and Larix invading among shrubs. Coordinates = midpoint of plot.

Plot chosen to represent remaining portion of formerly large patterned peatland area of large peatland complex with a concentration of flarks. More patchy to south. Here larger, irregular and dominant compared to strings, which dominate to south. Pool water about 2cm deep now after 6 weeks of dry weather. Area of this NPC diminished in this peatland complex as a result of early 20th century ditching. Coordinate = SW corner of plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC patch common in Beltrami-Pine Is. Beach Ridges LTA of Agassiz Lowlands subsection, w/minimal anthropogenic disturbance i.e.scattered pol/post-sized Thuja harvest; none observed in plot. Plot is 75% pools, rest is tree bases and CWD. No standing water on this date after 6 weeks of dry weather. Bryos abundant on Fraxinus boles and bases; lichens on boles. Abundant CWD, all sizes and states of decay. Striking lack of Frax regen/recruitment between 0 to 10m. Browsing severe, but  seedlings also are few. Water table @ 89cm. Coordinates = midpoint of plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC rare in Agassiz Lowlands Subsection. Lichens common on tree boles and branches in addition to the ground. One 21cm DBH Thuja occidentalis just outside plot. One dead and down Abies balsamea 26cm DBH in plot. Litter cover interrupted. Mosses (~10% cover of plot) and lichens (fruticose, cover ~60% of plot) form plot substrate except for exposed rock (w/~95% cover of crustose lichen cover). Two depressions in bedrock where organics have accumulated up to 15cm deep support canopy trees. Low amount of CWD; small to medium dbh size; all Abies. Deer browsing severe. Coordinates = plot center.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Plot chosen to represent portion of state designated lowland hardwoods old growth forest stands along Rapid River. No anthropogenic disturbance in plot. Terrain in plot undulating East to West due to North to South orientation of old river channel w/in plot. Located on one of a series of terraces above current river channel. Mod amnt of lrg to med DBH CWD. Approx. 3.5m above current channel bottom. Another, lower old channel outside plot still has standing water deep enough to prevent herbaceous spp establishment. Soil sampled in high vs low portion of plot. Fraxinus pensylvanica occur elsewhere in NPC patch. Coordinates = NE corner of plot.

Plot chosen to represent old FDn NPC of natural origin, rare in Agassiz Lowlands subsection. Located on small, dome-shaped upland island w/in Extremely Rich Tamarack Swamp (FPn82b) of basin. No recent anthropogenic management. A few cut Pinus res; stumps very decayed and smaller diameter than extant pine. Pit and mound microtopo. Low amount of small dbh CWD. Plot spans crest and portion of slopes on 3 sided i.e includes, crest, upper, mid and lower slopes. Charcoal @ humus/mineral soil contact. Aspect = N,E,W, ranging from 10-18% slope. Soils w/gray 0-10cm. Coordinates = NE corner of plot.
Mesic prairie with a disproportionate amount of Eryngium and Arnoglossum when compared to surrounding prairie. Fairly intact and relatively forb rich.
Mesic prairie at base of slope. Fairly intact, though some invasives present. Forb rich.
Mesic prairie dominated by mixture of grasses and forbs.

Comment under Releve typical of stand: "large shrub strip on west edge." 
Open mesic prairie dominated by graminoids with a diverse assembly of forbs.
Fairly disturbed portion of the site. The north east corner includes a mound likely made by humans. Low graminoid diversity but fairly high forb diversity.
Wet Mesic Prairie System dominated by Andropogon gerardii. Zizia aurea is quite prevalent as well.  6725

Wet prairie community dominated by graminoids. Plot included Asclepias sullivantii. Plot positioned near a gravel road. The ditch between the plot and the road is dominated by a number of invasive non-native species. These may potentially be problematic for the milkweed. Not much diversity in the plot.

place_name: Blu Mounds SP - outside of bison pasture

permanent_plot_type_description: ex. metal tag on nearby tree
remarks: Moved plot upslope to avoid sampling in flat, disturbed area that trail runs through by the river. Size of original plot unknown (~1ha?). Beavers cut down trees in flat terrace at N end. Bearing trees marked at each corner and GPS readings provided. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Metal spike not found, moved plot slightly north of GPS point because plot associated with GPS point was not representative of forest; large tree fall and canopy gap area. Tree canopy seems more open than original American elms gone. Fallen Acer negundo recorded as 4-5m; no DBH. Magnets at NE and SW corners; one bearing tree at each of the four corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Original plot appears to have been partly removed by creek meander and flooding. Lots of sand over vegetation bases. Side/flood channel now cuts through plot. Releve would have been located on ecotone between floodplain and maple basswood; perhaps to characterize dwarf trout lily habitat vs. a single plant community type? Moved releve to north so it would fit in floodplain area, community and not have a side channel through it, debris, etc. No sign of the fence referenced in original releve description. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Releve plot partially on floodplain, partially on maple-basswood slope (MHs39s). Some limestone on surface, 2 large trees down. Soil on slope is silt loam with scattered limestone rocks, flood-deposited loam on terrace with sand patches. Erythronium not flowering at sampling time, so estimates of species cover may be inaccurate. ID of E. propullans based on stolon characteristics. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Walk in from private land, Tom and Carla S. 507-451-7228, 5376 N. Co. Rd. 45. Jerry Iberson, land steward: 507-381-9490. Bearing trees at all 4 corners; magnets at NE and SW corners. Debris piles present in scattered portions of the plot from flooding. Also scattered sand deposits w/ debris. Spring ephemerals fading and hidden by nettles and other veg.; species may have been unseen or cover underestimated. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Context = upper & depression. Irregular knolls, low in central area, steep north-facing slope to creek. Large mature trees. Low area seems recently inundated with water, understory species on more knobby (less wet) areas seem similar, just more abundant. Lots of bare ground in low area. Little understory vegetation in low area near plot center. Some standing dead trees in wet area. Bearing trees at each of 4 corners, and magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Plot moved slightly south of GPS point to better match slope and SW aspect described on releve data. Scattered large tree falls and trunks throughout the forest in this area. Pipe found near western edge (GPS taken). Very sparse understory, dense canopy. Low wet area also in plot. 
Bearing trees and nails at each of 4 corners; magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Dark black topsoil. Bearing trees at all 4 corners. Nails at NE and SE corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Canopy gap in one corner, scattered large old trees, especially Quercus rubra. CWD 5%, >10cm. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Understory degraded, high % non-native, but with Carex assinaboinensis, dominant trees still indicative of dry oak woodland. Juniperus virg. open grown form. A fair bit of coarse wood debris. Large oak and cedar snags frequent. Large boles at all stages of decay. Ribes, Rhamnus, Xanth cuspid, Fraxis low - absence of woodies in 0.5-2m (i.e., deer browse) range. 10% CWD. One bearing tree for each of 4 corners; nail at each corner; magnet at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Plot set up parallel to slope at 210 degrees & 120 degrees. Limestone outcrops occur occasionally on slope. Nails in each of 4 corners; magnet at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Plot laid out 340/160 degrees. Plot approximately 10m east of of 12-14' DBH Quercus ellipsoidalis. About 30m east of toe slope. Gravel in upper soil layers. CWD: cedar stump. Nails at each of 4 corners; magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Just over ridge facing south, 50m south of private land. Plot is mid-slope. Incredibly sandy, many bare soil sites (exposed sand mounds scattered in plot); 25-30% sand. Nails in all 4 corners, magnets at NE and SW corners.
Phemeranthus rugospermus point in GPS. 16 plants (5 flowering) in and near plot (~2-3m outside of plot). Supplemental information and hand-drawn map on field forms.

Plot laid out N/S/E/W, site changed since last survey. Canopy of bur oak, sub-story elm and sugar maple, closes canopy. Satellite reception poor. Open grown oaks present, mostly dominate canopy, with sugar maple, red oak, and other shade tolerant species in understory. Remaining junipers scraggly with few leaves/needles. Hummus thickness =0.2 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners; magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Plot laid out at 220/40 degrees. Northern 1/3 of plot has very little tree cover. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners; magnets at NE and SW corners. A few large canopy trees, openings in tallest canopy. Sparser forb cover under dense shrub areas. Some small limestone (?) rock exposed. Little tree species regeneration. Litter thickness =0.5 cm. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Plot laid out 10/290 degrees (with the slope). Scattered limestone outcrops and stones on soil surface. Very little grass duff and no seed heads from previous year; burned last fall? Plot located lower on slope-60 approx. from overlook.Located in rockier soils. Pin oak ~6m east of center, east side of plot. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.
Nails at all 4 corners; magnets at NE and SW corners.

Plot ~40m north of West Rim Trail, set up plot aligned with slope: 20/110 degrees. Stand seems to have areas with very sparse veg, similar to releve location, and some some canopy openings with more understory veg. No age classes between seedlings and 3m-tall trees-deer-browsed? Signs of animal soil disturbance (digging), old corn cob in plot.
Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners; magnets at NE and SW corners. Sparse understory, a few larger diameter snags in stand. Dense canopy, more than surrounding area. Understory woody species all browsed. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map on field forms.

Canopy i.e. savanna structure still open in upslope ~1/2 of plot, more closed in along lower slope. Trees taller and larger than previous releve (as expected). ~35-40% exposed sand, pieces of chert on surface of sand. Litter thickness =0.25 cm. Litter type both leaves and grass. Coyote scat in plot. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners; magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Access off Minor Road (off Hwy 5). About 800m walk from parking area. Lower slope of long gradual hill. Large open prairie ~10-20 acres with occasional shrubs or trees; ~2% exposed sand. Sandy soil with some on/near surface. Seems to be more mesic and higher weedy species presence than earlier releve. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map on field forms. 
Nails at all 4 corners; magnets at NE and SW corners.

Terrace between steep bluff and middle fork of Whitewater River. Plot laid out approx. in line with river and bluff. Moved slightly from GPS point so plot not dominated by low spot. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners; magnets at NE and SW corners. Missing age classes for woody species from seedlings to ~4-5m; deer? Deer & 2 fawns came through when I was sampling plot. Bare spaces with leaves only in spots. Browsed tops of plants seen. Lilium michiganense browsed; only a few leaves left, no flowers. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map on field forms.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Moved plot about 5m south and east to better match slope, aspect, and descriptions from original releve. Mature sugar maple and red oaks. Forest understory sparse. Bare soil in ~5% of plot. Litter thickness =0.5 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

This is WFn64 transitioning from WFn55; latter is closer to the trail to the east. WFn53 to the west. No large snags but coarse woody debris is present as are tip-ups. Worm score based on worms plus castings seen on hummock of tree bases; no midden count due to inundation of lower parts of plot. Some flat portions of plot approach WFn64c but are localized.

Interesting black spruce overstory with predominant cedar understory; suggests richer black spruce type. No black spruce regeneration, however. Cedar regeneration good despite high deer population and browse seen in surrounding stands. Snags and coarse woody debris prevalent. Some black spruce outside of stand with witches broom growth. Standing water measured in a pool.

GPS point taken at SW plot corner. Plot represents zone transitioning from upland MHn46 to the east and black spruce peatland to the west. Litter occurs only as patches below tree/shrub bases. Soil is mucky peat grading towards muck deeper. Collected Cardamine pratensis (state threatened).

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Ski trails within 10 m of SE plot corner. Topographic context mostly crest with some upper slopes. No Oe/Oa humus, just Oi and directly into wormed mull (did not call it an A-horizon because it did not seem to have enough mineral soil). Castings all over wormed mull. Both mineral horizons tan-gray. Very decayed old sugar maple log but otherwise, no coarse woody debris or snags. No legacy white spruce or white pine. No sugar maple or basswood regeneration. Understory composed mostly of ironwood.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Beyond plot is more trembling aspen and thickets of sugar maple regeneration. Past selective cutting present but plot more intact than surrounding: 95-205 year old mature stage compared to young (<95 years). No humus; below litter is directly black A-horizon, followed by tan-gray loamy sand E-horizon, then orange-tan sandy clay loam Bt-horizon. Both E and Bt were moist but without redox features. Nightcrawlers seen. Large, old decayed coarse woody debris and snags deficient.

Plot situated above WFn55 drainage to the north but topography is very flat with no perceptible aspect. Texture of black A-horizon cannot be determined due to high organic content. Sandy loam E-horizon gray-tan and cemented. Clay Bt horizon brown and is angular blocky. No redox features seen but brown patches occur that are slightly darker than greater soil hue. Bt horizon started to glisten with moisture at 30-35 cm. Drainage is likely at least moderately well though redox was not seen at pit depth; at 35 cm, soil became too clayey to dig. Coarse woody debris sparse; tree regeneration low and no legacy conifers present of large size class. Heavily browsed and wormed soil.

Immediately to ESE is an area that is slightly drier with less Sphagnum moss and all cedar-dominated. North side of plot seems slightly drier. Overall stand is perhaps FPn63 with WFn53 transitions; MHn44c is also present as is APn80/81 farther to the east closest to the road. Standing water occurred only in pools. Surface water pH measured twice at 4.8 and 5.0. Abundant woody debris though none large. Snags uncommon in plot. Heavy deer browse in overall area. Very little black spruce or tamarack regeneration; no seedlings at all.

Plot oriented at 240 and 150, the latter leading downslope. Plot located on a bench below FDn22 crest top. Boulders common in plot. Heavy deer browse on regeneration stratum, though pine regeneration ok. No evidence of cutting or fire. Note: possible pin oak mixed in with red oak, but no acorns to provide positive identification. Sandy loam A-horizon black; coarse loamy sand B-horizon brown-tan and with very coarse gravel mixed in along with cobbles (texture estimated). This plot exhibits relatively mesic conditions perhaps due to bedrock water seepage and the combined large lake effect from Rainy Lake.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot oriented SE and SW. Plot exhibits multiple slopes due to uneveness of bedrock shape - sort of a crest with saddle. Steepest slope off of plot's south midpoint; so NE is steepest aspect though ridge follows SW to NE. No real aspect per se because of saddle but average 10% at NW. Yellow, fungal mycelia observed in humus. Dug soil pit to 15 cm before hitting too much rock - could be bedrock but unsure. Black coarse sandy loam resides above rock and has both stones and cobbles. Abundant smaller coarse woody debris and broken off tops of older pines but no large CWD or snags. Lots of standing pines still appear healthy so there may not be an input of large CWD and snags just yet. Observed bear and deer scat. High deer browse but white pine regeneration ok. No red pine regeneration.

Plot oriented at 210 and 120 degrees. Plot situated on bedrock feature, and at base of rock to the SE is a mesic flat leading to a meadow and FDn43 before leading back up to rock on FDn22/ROn23. Soil becomes thinner and topography steeper with exposed rock on the SE edge where the cliff and sunnier conditions occur. Sandy loam horizon chocolate brown; coarse loamy sand horizon chocolate brown. First cobble found at 27 cm below surface. At 42 cm, a crystallized black platy mineral was found. Nice moder humus. It appears that deep drift was deposited on this rock knob and soil appears mesic. A large stone/boulder prevented further excavation past 56 cm. Excellent coarse woody debris and snags; no cutting or fire evidence. Very high deer browse with some stems hedged. Note: distinguishing red and pin oaks was difficult due to their plastic leaf morphology.

Plot is an exposed ROn23 among matrix FDn22a/c. Topographic context of plot is both crest and upper slope. Slope is up to 28% to the SE but crest is mostly flat. Truly exposed rock without the crustose lichen equals 10% cover. Rocks are magnetized and made for difficulty in setting up correct plot dimensions. Naturally abundant pine snags and coarse woody debris inside and outside of plot. Some deer browse. Just outside plot: red pine, jack pine, white pine, bigtooth aspen, northern pin oak, downy arrowwood, and chokecherry.

Drainage rivulets occur throughout NPC with water flowing towards river. Sandy loam horizon black; sandy clay loam horizon gleyed. Gleyed soil with bluish-gray hue and marl-like limestone found, though rare. Iron concretions and charcoal found in SCL horizon. Even though gleying seen at 17 cm, plot feels more SPD rather than poorly drained. Only SW corner of plot saturated and poorly drained. Excellent coarse woody debris and snags. Metal container found in plot.

Plot situated close to WMn82b wet swale transition to open water/lake. No real slope but mostly flat; however, it does slope imperceptibly to the water. Coarse woody debris abundant from trembling aspen. Beaver cuttings observed nearby. Snail shell seen in moder humus. When digging soil pit, I hit a rock at the mineral soil and could not determine size; good soil structure. No evidence of recent cutting. Ranked plot 'B' instead of 'A' because pine, spruce, basswood missing in canopy.

Plot oriented at NE and NW. Majority of stand is FDn43b1 and WFn55 is nearby to the NW. A 1-m high "crest top" rock knob occurs to the south. Drainage is estimated: either MWD or SPD. Humus with good fine root matrix. Mineral soil uniformly muted gray but without redox features of gleying or iron mottling. One 18 cm cobble pulled out of the 56 cm diameter soil pit, but difficult to say if it truly makes up >15% coarse fragment. Good coarse woody debris of birch that is well-decayed. Large birch snag >40 cm dbh found just outside of plot. Most green ash are just outside plot boundary.

Plot located on a steep slope surrounded by younger dog hair aspen on the ridge. Greater stand also shrubbier, especially where blowdown or cutting have occurred. Some stumps are large and cut long ago, but medium-sized coarse woody debris and snags also present. Top sandy loam horizon black; 2nd SL horizon and SCL horizons all muted gray-brown to tan. Surprisingly, no redox features seen down to 64 cm. Some Oe and fine roots present but castings common on forest floor.

Plot oriented NE and SE. Topographic context is 'lower' in relation to the steep ridge to the NW; immediately within NPC, it is fairly flat. Slope undulates up and down to the SE based on old river flood channels but overall slope is 2%. Part of plot straddles old flood channel but there is no ground cover difference since flooding hasn't occurred for some time. Outside of plot are areas of dense black ash regeneration, especially towards the river to the SE. Top horizon loam approaches a clay loam and is grayish-black; 2nd horizon is a muted gray but not gleyed. Though no redox detected down to 60 cm, moderately well drained soil is expected. A dark organic black layer occurs in the middle of CL layer and could be old organic-rich surface soil buried later by alluvium.

LTP polygon includes very poorly drained mucky depressional drainage SW from plot and parts more similar to this plot. Flowing water 8 cm deep seen within 10 m WNW of plot. Plot located on low/toe slope and feels moister than sugar maple - cedar forest higher up on slope despite similar ground flora. Portion of plot has localized saturated soil, "squishiness", and small pockets of standing water. Soil pit dug near nadir of drainage and some orange streaks appear at bottom horizon. Water rose to 23 cm below surface after digging pit. MP layer brown-black; MU layer black; first SCL black-brown; second SCL orange-brown. On higher slope, humus is present rather than organic MP or MU. NPC feels transitional MHn45b and WFn53. No cut stumps seen. Some stones occur in lowest part of drainage.

Majority of LTP polygon is poorly drained WFn53; plot is an outlier. Overall landscape slopes to the SE towards Lake Superior, but local slope is imperceptible. Plot oriented to fit mostly between dry cobble creek and currently flowing creek; plot runs 320 and 230 degrees. Cobble creek channel occurs at south end of plot. Wetter species occur on lowest bank of old channel; otherwise, species composition mostly indicative of MHn. A 58 cm white spruce found 15 m beyond plot. Nice coarse woody debris and snags; no cut stumps. Top loam layer muted brown; fine SCL light brown; CL gray-brown. Mineral soil from 17-48 cm is slightly cemented and capable of perching water. Some orange flecks begin at 25 cm caused by decaying wood pieces. Moisture and gray colors begin just past 50 cm. Heavy worm infestation.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Plot located near upland transition to the south and wetter conditions to the north. Small gradient slope from S to N. Extremely high deer browse on Impatiens. Nice snags and coarse woody debris; no cut stumps seen. Evidence of surface ponding early in season. Expose rock includes few boulders covered with vegetation. No seepage seen in soil pit but was fresh/moist. First horizon is organic black muck followed by a 2nd layer of gleyed mineral-organic mix with abundant decaying wood pieces and evidence of charcoal. Mineral component likely a SiCL instead of SIL if not for high organic component. Layer semi-permeable due to compacted and dense property. Third layer is gleyed coarse sandy clay loam with bright orange sand grains and includes gravel coarse fragment in addition to the cobbles. Overall drainage is better typed as PD rather than VPD despite >20 cm muck layer.

One large boulder in plot; surficial boulders common throughout swamp NPC. At boundary of organic and mineral soil lies the cobble layer. Organic layer (black-brown) with large decaying wood pieces in muck matrix; water capable of being squeezed out of muck but no ponding at bottom of soil pit nor any standing water. Absence of standing water possibly due to very dry growing season. Clay layer gray. Upland herbs on slight mounds but very wet ash swamp species occur in lowest depressions like Caltha and Glyceria. WFn64c chosen over WFn55a due to thickness of muck layer, absence of orange mottling in the straight gray clay layer, and ground flora tendency towards the wetter spectrum using NPC pairwise computer program.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Plot located near both river and upland; oriented in NE/SE directions. Soil pit dug farthest from river at west corner. Topo lines suggest NE aspect sloping to Rat Root River, and plot can be considered as occurring on toe slope of the upland to the SW. However, there is levee adjacent to stream and thus the plot occurs in a valley drainage/depression; there was about 6 cm of standing water at lowest point of the drainage. Slight upland slope from SE to NW with possibly a 1-2% slope. There are pockets of elevated risers where upland mesic species occur. Seepage of water seen at mineral horizon but no ponding occurred at bottom of pit. Silty muck layer black and clay loam layer gray. Levee near the river with surficial sand deposits and dryer species.

Some old stumps seen, likely cedar. Most decayed wood and fibers occur in MP upper layer. MP layer brown-black; muck layer black-brown. Soil pit dug in hollow, though no water at surface. Once excavated, water quickly filled soil pit to a depth of 5 cm below surface. Good amounts of coarse woody debris, though snags generally small in diameter. Litter occurs only on tree base mounds. Little to no deer browse observed. Only deductions from an A rank are from lack of large-diameter cedar due to past cutting and few snags. Pleasant NPC surrounded by FPn62 farther west with greater black spruce. Some WFn53 characteristics to plot but FPn63 most appropriate classification.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Other areas farther from river are WFn55 but are included within same LTP polygon. No real plot aspect due to rolling topo of old flood channels; however, greater landscape slopes north to river. Steepest slope into old flood channel measured at 16 degrees, but slope percent is variable throughout plot. Top soil horizon is blackish medium-brown caused by organic worm mixing. Second horizon is fine sand of uniform brown with occasional bands of lighter tan and deep orange flecks. Soil pit dug on back slope of levee (south facing). One area of plot (about 10%) is devoid of vegetation because of flood channel and likely still floods each spring. Note: some black ash seedlings may be green ash.

Plot located near LTP 24 to the north. Topo lines indicate gradual NW slope to open wetland but gradient imperceptible on the ground. Heavy weekend rains caused sparse pools of standing water. Never reached mineral soil during excavation; dark brown to black mucky peat approaching straight muck. Seepage seen after pit excavation. Hare browse prevalent but deer browse only seen on mountain maple. Large snags and coarse woody debris absent. Population of Canada yew healthy and seem unbrowsed, but they are short in stature. Regeneration of cedar and spruce poor.

Plot located near LTP 24 polygon to the south. Slope is imperceptible on the ground but topo lines show SE aspect. Litter thickness measured at its thickest on cedar bases. Abundant microtopography with hollows being mucky to wet after 2-3 days of heavy rain. No cut stumps seen; good snags and coarse woody debris plus cedar tip-ups. Top muck layer black and with abundant recalcitrant wood pieces. Water seepage seen at 30 cm; ponding of water occurred at 65 cm. Bottom layer black with slight grayish cast and just barely observed mineral soil mixed with overlying muck (texture estimated as coarse SL); gravel and cobbles occurred at bottom of pit. Thickness of organic layer classifies drainage to VPD despite mix of mesic ground layer species. Bear and moose dung seen. Note: browse on mountain maple may be only moose and not deer.

This LTP should be classified as LTP 42 due to clay substrate. Slope is mostly imperceptible on the ground but topo lines indicate south aspect. At north boundary, slope is about 2% just outside of plot. Litter found up to 5 cm but only on cedar bases; absent on low flats. Drainage types to VPD but ground flora suggests more PD. Only standing water found in drainage channel after 3 days of rain. Cobbles found also only in drainage. Muck layer is black; clay layer, which is almost a SiC with fine sand grains, is subangular to angular blocky gleyed matrix with orange-tan streaking. This is nice, possible old growth due to large diameter cedar, large coarse woody debris and gaps with conifer regeneration. Many seedlings and saplings germinating and growing on nurse logs. No cut stumps seen. Browse is likely only moose and hare with minimal deer. A cobbly ephemeral stream-pool occurs in plot; little vegetation near NE plot corner.

Plot located near Cloquet River and LTP 32 to the SE. No cut stumps and good coarse woody debris and snags. Decent diameter black spruce. Deer trail passes through plot and deer browse moderately high. Peat layer red-brown; fine CL layer gray-black with both gravel and cobble; coarse SCL dark brown with both gravel and cobble; SL medium brown and highly cemented with abundant pebbles about 2.5 cm long. The coarse SCL horizon was wettest layer as it sits directly above perched water of SL layer. All colors throughout depth are muted but no gleys or mottling seen. Hypothetical deposition process: outwash lower horizon followed by moraine-deposited cobbles and clays on top? Peat layer developed at surface due to wetter conditions. Peat layer not uniform across plot with some portions without Sphagnum and appear to have a humus over mineral soil and somewhat poorly drained.

Plot oriented NW and SW. This plot is a drier than expected FPn62 and near LTP change to drier conditions to the SE and wetter to the NW. Plot straddles ecotonal boundary between upland aspen-jack pine and lower, peatier black spruce forested peatland. Plot located to capture somewhat poorly drained conditions. Mucky peat layer dark brown; muck black and with charcoal and burned flakes; coarse LS layer has gleyed colors below 25 cm with deep iron color splotches and lighter orange mottling. Pooling 38 cm below surface observed. Pit dug close to peaty area; higher on slope to SE, there is a moder humus 5 cm thick and worms. High deer browse; good amount of snags and medium to small size coarse woody debris of varying decay; no cut stumps. AB rank due to less regeneration than expected for conifers, no large-diameter legacies, and high deer browse.

Releve in shallow portion of seepage wetland in shallow portion of beaver dam impact.At a larger context , this is located on the upper portion of a large sloping area of peat. Releve located in second pool area, the pools to the west have more marl and iron. M. walker assisted with moss id.

Plot located where N. Sather had described which was a few meters west of the given GPS point. Plot corners in cardinal directions, plot aligned with community edge and is 5 m to west of transition to seepage/shrub area at slightly higher elevation.Magnets in North and south corners.UTMs are S corner.

Releve located in middle of ca. 40 m wide and very long strip if calcareous fen. Much of the surroundings appear to drain to an area of larger pools( ca. 3m wide) that are located outside of the releve. Inside the releve are a number of small pools, some large hummocks, and a small raised area with high shrub cover. Magnets buried in NW and SE corner.

Plot located in fen below FDn44-Aspen woodland and above seepage shrub swamp. Some large shrubs are presnet in fen and on margins. The area ca. one meter downslope of the plot was brush0-mpwed this spring. Some larger hummocks exsist on the West side of the plot.

Releve located near ground water sample wells near the north end of the fen. Around 50 % of the releve was brush mowed this spring. Fen grades into seepage meadow further North and grades into aspen woodland to the east and west. Magnet in SW corner

Plots established before paddock grazing began on site. Series of 3 releves run down fen. 10 m side runs across the draw, capturing most of the fen in a cross-section. lower edge of this releve is located just off raised peat mount.
See releve B774, This is the middle of three releves for monitoring impacts to the fen. this releve spans the peat mound and down into the spring run area. top of mound has open marl pools.

See releve B774- This is one of three releves located in this fen. This releve is the lowest eleveation, located downslope from the raired peat mound. Releve is located fairly close to the two edges, butvegitation is fairly consistant throughout plot. this area has more large hummocks then other areas of the fen.

Releve take to document typical rich fen for this area. Areas of this fen have fairly high shrub cover (ca 50% cover). fairly firm peat mat with water at the surface, grades into tammarack dominated area to the west.
Releve to document a typical rich fen for this area. Many open pools of iron rich water in plot area.
Releve on springy soil on sloping seepage area. there is less typha angustifolia here. Plot contains small open pools with heavy iron coloration.

Releve documenting best area of fen. This area has short Carex lawn dominated by calcareous indicators. to the east of this location, Typha becomes abundant. Plot extends from upland border of fen community to a short way into the taller fen vegetation.

This releve documents an area of wet prairie that appears to have been impacted by grazing in the past. The area has been recovering for a long while. As is common in my experience in areas with this history, Andropogon has become strongly dominant.
A fairly decent size line of seepage weltland runs along a small finger of upland, this grades into rich fen at lower elevations. RCG is invading the larger area due to ditching through the rich fen.
Releve to document wet seepage comunity. To the west, seepage area is more dominated by Typha angustifolia and to the east is upland comunity. Area appears to have been burnt this year.

Releve on impacted dry prairie, plot located on better area of higher slope. Appears to have been grazed hard in the past. Vegetation is around 50% native/non-native. Composition is typical of areas that have had time to recover from intense, long-term grazing.

Releve to document area of degraded prairie. This appears to have a long history of intense, season long grazing but has been recovering for a time. Releve is on middle to lower portion of the slope which has some mesic affinity. The hill to the north has little to no natives left(x rank).
Releve on beach ridge that has become extremely degraded due to history of intense grazing. On the margin of calling this X rank.

Releve documenting wet prairie with a history of grazing but with a long period of recovery. Composition somewhat turned tword grazing increases species, but little non-native cover is present. Mat muhly is ubiquitous in understory. Area to south of here has a history of haying and is in great condition.
Releve to document string of small hills with recovering prairie vegitation, draws are more degraded but stil native dominated.
Releve to document large area of prairie that has become degraded due to intense, season-long grazing in the past.

Releve on dry prairie knob. Draws between these areas are beginning to be become shrubby areas with plenty of buckthorn. Lower areas of the slope apear to be a grass only planting that is strongly dominated by Sorgastrum nutans.  this hill slope has numerous small glacial erratics.

Plot chosen to document old growth stage, long established plant community common in Beltrami-Pine Island Peatlands LTA and Site. No anthropogenic disturbance evident. No larch beetle mortality. No pools; hollows Sphagnum covered. Lower soil strata estimated from small sample. UTM = NW corner of plot.

Plot chosen to represent mesic hardwood forest NPC and condition common on Agassiz beach ridge sandy loam setting. Harvest ~50 yrs ago of Populus and possibly other deciduous spp. Lrg diameter very decayed cut Pinus strobus stump in plot. Other scattered lrg cut stumps in patch. In addition to dead Frax nigra, a few dead mature Populus trem. Pit and mound microtopo. At 35cm soils may be transitioning to loamy sand; too compacted to get deeper. Moist top to bottom even in dry season so far. UTM = NW corner of plot. Condition ranking form completed.

Plot chosen to represent NPC at old growth stage, rare in Beltrami-Pine Is. Peatlands LTA. MN DNR designated Old Growth stand. Small patch; cut stumps scattered throughout. Abundant CWD, all stages of decay and sizes. Pit and mound microtopo. On Agassiz beach ridge setting. Upper mineral soil is grey. No charcoal observed. In patch/OG std one cut stump is P. Strobus ~ 40cm at base. Unsure what other spp were cut in distant past harvest. UTM = midpt of plot. Condition Ranking form completed.

Plot chosen to represent old growth stage NPC, state designated old growth stand in Beltrami-Pine Is. Peatlands LTA in beach ridge setting. Scattered cut stumps, well-decayed, most sm - med diameter. Moderate amt of sm - med CWD of most spp except Acer rubrum. UTM = plot center. Condition ranking form completed.

Plot chosen to represent NPC common in this landscape setting of Beltrami-Pine Is. Peatlands LTA, post harvest disturbance ~80 yrs. Large dbh Thuja nearly absent. Dead and down Abies and Picea mariana CWD of sm-med dbh. Few depressions w/evidence of stding water; all small; shallow to deep. Microtopo assoc. w/tree bases and raised root systems. Wonder if whole NPC may be appropriately considered ecotonal btwn MHn44 and FPn. Patch has small MHn-like islands. UTM = SE corner of plot; Condition Ranking form completed.

Plot chosen to represent NPC and post-harvest condition ~ common in Beltrami-Pine Island LTA. Very well-decayed cut stumps common. Probably Larix. Microtopo subtle; no standing water or evidence of pools. Small dbh CWD common (Abies); on surface, large old Thuja CWD rare. No snags. Browsing evident on shrubs, not on understy Thuja. Soils info from shallow depression; elsewhere there is a humus layer. H2O @ org/mineral contact = 15cm. UTM = center of east boundary of plot. Elsewhere in same patch few forbs among bryos; no shrubs or tree regen; other parts 'barrens'-like w/needle litter and little to no bryos.

Plot chosen to represent NPC and post-harvest condition common in Beltrami-Pine Island LTA. Very well-decayed cut stumps common. Mix of Sphagnum and feather mosses, discontinuous, mostly on CWD, woody bases, stumps. No Brown mosses. Occas small Sphagnum hummocks; depressions and pools small. Soils info from depression; elsewhere there is humus layer. No brown mosses. UTM = NW corner of plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC in Beltrami-Pine Island Peatland LTA; mature at old growth stage. A few lrg, very decayed cut stumps (P. strobus?). Abundant dead and down Abies of small dbh.
