Sm to medium diam CWD abundant. One large dbh dead and down P. balsamifera. Recent blowdown of subcan Picea glauca (18cm dbh) and Abies. Bryos on CWD. Setting is an upland finger or island in WFn. Condition Ranking form completed. UTM = SW corner of plot.

Plot chosen to represent mesic forest type and condition of MNDNR Designated "Old Growth Cedar" stand of Rapid River Till Plain LTA. Condition likely representative of similar NPCs in LTA at mature and old growth stages. Pit and mound microtopo. Small to medium diameter CWD abundant and in various states of decay; most/all Populus. Old decayed cut stumps in patch, none observed in plot. Condition Ranking form completed. UTM = midpoint of plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC type and condition of portion of MNDNR Designated "Old Growth Cedar" stand in Rapid River Till Plain LTA. Adjacent designated stands (Releve B799) are Populus tremuloides dominated w/few Thuja. Cut stumps present, very decayed, various sizes. Pit and mound micro-topo. Low to moderate amount of CWD of small to medium diameter.Adjacent small WFn features. Clay dark grey lightening to grey at 18cm. Condition Ranking form completed. UTM = plot center.

Plot chosen to represent NPC common in Beltrami-Pine Island Peatland LTA. Likely a few very decayed cut stumps in plot and vicinity. Abundant CWD, all states of decay; all but largest size class. Plot not representative of the entire MHn patch. Condition Ranking form completed. UTM = plot center.

Plot chosen to represent NPC common in Beltrami-Pine Island Peatland LTA. Appears to be acidifying to APn80. Unsure of management history, past harvest possible but 100+ yrs ago. Plot area includes areas of both high hummocks and lower, wetter hummocks and hollows. Small amount of small to medium diameter CWD. Located between FPn82 and APn80. UTM = plot center.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Plot chosen to represent one aspect of MHn44 community w/in MNDNR Designated "Old Growth Cedar" stand in Beltrami-Pine Island Peatland LTA. Other portions of stand w/out Thuja - Populus dominated w/ dense understory of shrubs and Abies. Pit and mound micro-topo. Moderate amount of small - medium size CWD, all states of decay. Browsing evident, but abundant moose sign suggests not of deer origin. No evidence of anthropogenic disturbance suggest it could be natural origin NPC. Thuja in scattered groves and individually. Thuja regen observed in areas of stand w/out mature trees. Upper mineral soil layer grey in color. Condition Ranking form completed. UTM = NE corner of plot.

Plot chosen to represent NPC common at margin of large APn80 peatlands and adjacent uplands of Beltrami-Pine Island Peatland LTA. Mineral soil below peat. UTM = NE corner of plot. No hydrological disturbance observed/apparent.

Plot chosen to represent one aspect of highly variable NPC on Beltrami-Pine Island Peatland LTA, on margin of beach ridge at margin of large peatland complex. Unusual large Taxus canadensis population in NPC patch. Abundant CWD, many sizes/states of decay. Pit and mound microtopo. Plot includes shrubby and open understory aspects of NPC patch in this setting. Large snags (Populus trem) present. No cut stumps observed in or near plot location. Condition Ranking form completed. UTM = SE corner of plot.

Plot chosen to represent one expression of NPC on Little-Big Fork Till Plain LTA bedrock controlled part of beach ridge, landform, post harvest ~40yrs. CWD and snags absent. Other portions of patch more clearly FDn32c1. Plot represents common expression on the shallowest soils over bedrock in patch. Soil patchy. Some soil mixing by worms of about half the depth of humus. Patch mostly this expression. Condition Ranking form completed. UTM = ceter point of plot.
Releve documenting hill prairie with a history of grazing.

Even-aged Picea-Larix-Abies peatland in a complex of forested peatland, wet forest, and wet-mesic upland. Sapric peat at least 50cm deep. No mosses where Betula litter has collected. Hollows are small and damp. Relatively flat microtopography. Conducted releve to determine if FPn62. Waypoint 017 near plot center.

Mature Pinus resinosa stand (likely planted) 35-45 cm dbh. Plot placed in part with fewer Pinus, allowing greater diversity of tree species. No snags and only a few small Abies logs. Two old uncut stumps observed and a few old cut Betula and Pinus stumps. Forest road passes through stand about 20m away. Moss only on dead wood and one old tip-up mound. Drainage class based on Graycalm component of B79B soil map unit. Waypoint 019 near plot center.
Hummocks and pools each cover about 50%. Pools are small. Some logs, plus 1 tip-up in plot. Trees average about 15cm dbh. Many Carex too young to identify. Waypoint 029 near plot center.

On imperceptible slope from Populus dominated mesic hardwood forest to southwest toward Thuja dominated wet forest to northeast. Plot is representative of Thuja-dominated transitional zones between uplands and wetlands, which can be very wide in this landscape, but here is only about 50m wide. Solid layer of leaf litter. The shallow depressions are not wet. Vegetatively appears like MHn44c. See old cut spruce stump. Waypoint 061 is in northwest corner of plot. Mosses recorded only from rotten wood.

Not sure if Dendrobaena earthworms are present, or if worm-free. Plot is representative of the upper portions of this beach ridge. Lower on the slope is moister MHn44. See some very old cut stumps. FDn33 or FDn43. Waypoint 063 is near plot center.

Not sure if Dendrobaena earthworms are present or if worm-free. Island in middle of large conifer peatland, likely an old Agassiz sandbar. Parts of island have more uniform 15cm dbh Betula and Abies. Many areas with lots of Abies treefall. Thuja is scattered throughout, but not Pinus. A few old cut Thuja stumps. Waypoint 073 at northeast corner of plot.

Very old cut stumps in plot. Old charred stumps in stand. Scattered Pinus in stand (mostly P. resinosa) are old, but most trees (other species) are 15-20cm dbh. Observed Dendrobaena earthworm in soil pit. Hit impenetrable rocks at 17cm depth. Rocks are covered with various mosses. Drainage class based on Sugarbush component of B79B soil map unit. Waypoint 074 near plot center.

Gray mottling in fine sandy loam 32cm deep. In mosaic of wet forest with shallow depressions and upland forest without depressions, all dominated by Thuja. Plot represents drier portions. Pinus strobus snag is about 130cm dbh, most of tree is now a giant log covered with Thuja seedlings. There are also large Populus logs. Most Thuja are 25-30cm dbh, second growth? Fire scar on Pinus snag. Waypoint 075 near plot center.
Shrubby water track in center of small peatland. Hummocks cover about 90%, depressions about 10%. Waypoint 077 near plot center.

Larix swamp between upland and open rich fen at center of this small peatland. Trees average 8-10cm dbh. Pools mostly covered with pleurocarps, covering about 25% of plot. Waypoint 078 near plot center.

In interior of large water track peatland. This poor swamp lies between rich water track Larix swamp to south and open rich water track to north. Pools are still very full from last week's heavy rain. Pools cover about 50% of plot. Some mosses may be submerged and not observed. Waypoint 089 near plot center.

Scrubby rich fen water track flowing toward Myrtle Lake. Raised acid peatland to east and west. Pools cover about 25% of plot. Pools are deep right now due to heavy rain last week,  probably obscuring some mosses. Waypoint 094 near plot center.

Meadow left when beaver pond drained. Creek with clear water and sand bottom flows about 5m from plot. Meadow corridor is about 70-80m wide with upland on either side. Waypoint 108 is at northeast corner of plot.

Western side of this peatland is rich Thuja. Pools cover about 40% of plot. Thick and tangled. Cornus sericea has been browsed. There is some Thuja regen >0.5m (up to 2m). Waypoint 116 is near plot center.

Plot is representative of the upland forests along the Big Fork River. Downhill towards the river is floodplain terrace. This plot, like most upland forests near the river, have some species richer than typical for MHn44, in this case including Ranunculus recurvatus, Uvularia grandiflora, and Arisaema triphylla. Top loam layer of soil was created by earthworms. Mosses on rotten wood not recorded. Waypoint 129 near plot center.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Growing on long slope down to oxbow of Little Fork River. At this spot the entire slope is approx. 10 degrees--other places steeper, others shallower. The slope is interrupted by regular terraces caused by past soil slumping. A small gully that occasionally runs with runoff cuts through corner of plot (1-2m deep with mossy banks). Large Populus trees are dying and falling. Some Abies logs, but very few Thuja. No cut stumps observed. Waypoint 130 near the center of the plot.

Plot is in small "bay" at edge of large peatland, with nearby upland of pine plantation. Part of bay is graminoid meadow equally dominated by Carex lacustris and C. lasiocarpa. The rest of the bay and a larger area on perifery of peatland is this shrub swamp. Pools cover about 80% of plot. Waypoint 163 is at southeast corner of plot, about 10m from edge of graminoid meadow.

Alnus shrubland at edge of beaver-flooded creek corridor. Calamagrostis meadow to north with Typha in deeper water. Grades slowly into WFn64 to south. Pools cover about 90% of plot. Possibly releve is WFn74. Waypoint 164 is at northwest corner of plot.
Drained beaver meadow along small creek about 1m wide and 70cm deep. Plot is about 3m from creek. Waypoint 166 is at southwest corner of plot.

Plot is full width of meadow starting about 1m above current river level (3m horizontally from river), rising to edge of trees about 2m above water level. This slope is not as steep as typical riverbank meadows in this area. Forest is a marrow band of terrace rising quickly to hardwood forest. Waypoint 177 is near southeast corner of plot.

Mesic hardwood forest on terrace of Little Fork River without floodplain indicators. Appears to be old growth, with large trees, canopy gaps and many large mossy logs. There are a few old cut cedar stumps in and around plot. No Thuja seedlings taller than 50cm. Mosses not recorded from rotten wood. Outside plot there is more Matteuccia and Hydrophyllum. Waypoint 189 is near plot center.

West part of small basin inside old oxbow of Big Fork River, where Thuja is a canopy component. Picea mariana is dominant over entire basin. East part is FPn81 or FPn82. There is groundwater seepage at north edge of basin and headwaters of Trout Brook. High orchid diversity throughout. To north of basin is steep sandy slope with pine plantation on top. Thuja and Cornus are browsed, but some Thuja has reached 2m tall. Releve conducted to determine if FPn62. Waypoint 191 is near plot center.

Old growth pine forest just outside burned area of Cloquet Fire of 1918. Patches of recent severe blowdown nearby, but not in plot. Plot is in portion of pine forest between East Cook Lake Rd and Island Lake. ATV trail passes about 10m to east. Pinus strobus seedlings up to 2m tall are unbrowsed while Corylus is. There is a deer stand just outside plot. Drainage class based on Soil Survey. Waypoint 192 is near plot center.

Plot in imperceptible depression on long, shallow slope up from Valley River, north to the higher ground near Franklin Lake. To the north of this Fraxinus-dominated swamp is a wet-mesic Thuja-Populus forest, and to the south is wet Thuja forest. Some old Thuja logs in plot. Some trees appear to be potential old growth age. Mosses recorded from soil, not rotten wood. Dry pools cover about 80% of plot. Waypoint 193 near plot center.

In wide transition zone (about 500m) between large peatland to south and mesic forests along Sturgeon River. Depressions (dry now) cover about 50% of plot. Appears to be roughly 50-75 years post-harvest, judging by size of trees. No cut stumps observed. Feels like appropriate site for Thuja, but there is none in area. Maybe burned after harvest. There are logs, but none large. Waypoint 195 near plot center.

At edge of large peatland on what appears to be undulating sand deposited in shallow glacial lake water. There is a mosaic of wet forest, forested peatland, and wet-mesic uupland forest on the highest rises. Picea mariana and Abies are common throughout, with more Thuja in wetter areas and more Betula in drier areas. Plot represents wettest of the upland forests. There are old cut stumps in plot, probably spruce. Waypoint 202 is near plot center. Mosses not recorded from wood substrates.

Part of mosaic of community types within wide transition zone between peatland to south and sandy beach ridge to north. Appears to be old growth. Pools, which are now wet but have no standing water, cover about 80% of plot. More Thuja to east, less to west. Mosses not recorded from woody substrates. Waypoint 211 is near plot center.

Part of mosaic of community types within wide transition zone between peatland to south and sandy beach ridge to north. Old cut stumps are so rotten as to be nearly undiscernable (so, not Thuja). There are some damp pools (with leaf litter cover), but microtopographical relief is minimal. Has leaf litter prevented recovery of previous moss layer? Waypoint 212 near plot center.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Silver Maple Terrace Forest
remarks: Plot is partly on wetter flood-cut channel and partly on higher ground. Has some large mossy logs. Waypoint 217 near plot center.
On terrace above reach of flooding from Little Fork River. Below 30cm soil is dry clay too hard to penetrate with probe. Waypoint 218 near plot center.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Plot is typical of a large mature patch on broad, level to gently-sloping ridge top along the lower reaches of Partridge Creek. Trees forest-grown, some with multiple trunks. Trees mostly 35-50 cm dbh, occasionally to 60-90 cm in the larger stand. Snags infrequent. Stumps rare. CWD rather sparse, with occasional larger boles in various decay stages. Tip-up mounds occasional, one in plot. Soil clayey-silt, earthworms moderately abundant; leaf litter mostly intact (13 June). Rather heavy deer browse. Notes: Plot located in a large ridge top stand slated to be logged; stand has been in an interdisciplinary dispute between Forestry & Ecological & Water Resources staff for two years. Selective logging was outcome of the dispute. One of the largest populations of White Ash I've seen in Minnesota (in 25 years). Three (four) EMN monitoring plots were done in this mature patch as well.

Typical of intermittent patches of rich mesic talus in a fairly extensive open talus-talus shrubland complex on the extremely steep upper slope of 250-foot, north-facing bluff along the North Branch Root River at the mouth of Partridge Creek. Grades to semi-wooded areas with Tilia, Ulmus, Celtis, Quercus mac. Substrate is an unstable mix of rich silt and smallish limestone talus pieces from small, much-broken, thinly-bedded, and weakly-cemented limestone cliffs upslope. The Dicentras were noted here in early May. Grades to areas with much more Cystopteris bulbifera. Notes: Other rich mesic talus slopes along Partridge Creek often have much more Cystopteris bulbifera and often more Cornus alternifolia.

Occasional large tree falls and canopy openings. Fair amount of coarse woody debris in stand. No earthworms observed. Needle layer fairly thick. Most stumps seem to be a result of natural blow down. Plot moved from target point, approx. 20 meters West to match 4 degree slope and aspect of original Relevé. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Lower slope of sand hill, area below plot has high sedge area(?); wet-low area. Exposed sand by gopher mounds. Quite a few dead trees in and near plot. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

No plants between ~0.5m and 4-5m. Tree seedlings all short, no saplings. Fallen trees with roots exposed. Tip-ups occasional. Plot moved east from target GPS point to get western edge out of low, wet area ecotone (not described in original releve. Plot set up at 0/90 degrees, N-S, E-W. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map on field forms.

Plot located at mid-slope of gradual S-facing slope, levels out at bottom of slope. Large tree fallen at N end of plot, typical of stand which has occasional small tree falls and canopy openings. Raspberry dense in canopy gap area. Small cedar (<15cm dbh) barely alive in understory. Low diversity, weedy species. Litter thickness =0.5 cm. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map on field forms.

Plot located on steep, S/SW-facing slope between upland Oak Woodland and River Terrace. Plot ran with the slope, 20m just fits between crest and toe of slope. Conduit found and used to locate. Seemed in correct location based on GPS point and other info. Relatively dense canopy, understory somewhat sparsely vegetated. Large Celtis occidentalis on southern border. Litter thickness =0.3cm. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map on field forms.

Located approx 110 meters from top of slope (to west). Plot moved slightly so less of plot was impacted by animal digging. Signs of deer or turkey digging up vegetation, bare spots scratched on ground. Scattered large open-grown trees. Woody species common in understory. Area is weedy, has a lack of fire and is missing age classes of trees. Litter thickness =0.2 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Original slope recorded was 25 degrees NE. Not possible to fit a 20 x 20 at that slope (insufficient space), plus regeneration on the slope does not match likely succession from earlier, original releve. About 1/3 of relevé was placed on steep NE slope and the rest upslope where current vegetation is a better match. Looked for fence posts and barbed wire, none found. Dead Juniperus virginiana in plot. Plant level D6-7m includes large tall, open-grown Quercus, as well as younger trees >10m (2 strata). Small patches of exposed soil. Litter thickness =0.5 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Access to plot by getting permission to drive in and park at base of ski hill. Deer trail up less steep at end of bluff. Approx 150 meters to creek, 100 meters to nearest point on road. Two deer/hiking trails cut through portions of plot. Small prairie grasses & forbs dominated opening in overgrown bluff prairie/savanna. Surrounded by Quercus macrocarpa, Juniperus virginiana, Quercus rubra, and Rhamnus cathartica. Exposed limestone rocks & outcrops. Lots of Monarch caterpillars on on Asclepias verticillata. Grass and forbs in deep soil. Some early flowering plants totally dried up. Lots of buckthorn in treed area around plot. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Access to plot: park off Leduc Ave and walk down hill. Low area downslope of relevé with standing water upslope. A few old bottles, cans observed (past camp site?). Soil seems packed and hard. Understory is lots of bare places ~40% bare ground or leaves. Litter thickness =1-2 cm, exposed rock =0.5%. Some larger old trees, understory and tree regeneration lower, possibly due to deer browse? Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Slope 5% versus flat (0%). The closest flat area was about 50 meters swan and vegetation not a good match there. Metal stake found near where SW corner of plot would be based on GPS coordinates, so used that for SW corner. Use for NE/NW would have placed plot on trail. 20-30% bare soil, understory vegetation sparse and small, short. Previous surveyor used Acer nigrum complex. Many understory plants, only with a few leaves and non-reproductive- ID tricky. Litter thickness =0.2 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: Occasional large, old trees, age unknown, diverse understory, few saplings. Litter thickness = 0.2 cm. Plot center moved ~35 meters NE from GPS point to better match original slope and aspect. Patches of bare soil ~2%. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Overgrown with Rhus glabra and Lonicera species. Only a few small clumps of grass, forbs (prairie species). Stunted, mostly non-flowering, shade-stressed. Scattered limestone fragments. Litter thickness =0.2 cm. Stand not typical due to lack of fire and invasives. Plot ran to fit at 8 x 10 meters between larger oaks, based on original description of sample area. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Topographic context: Crest/upper. Open sand exposed. Less forb diversity that previously sampled. Looked extensively in plot for species previously recorded, but a number weren't found. As described in original relevé, plot was set up so upper edge on crest. NW-facing with ~5 degree slope. Current relevé moved north from target GPS to achieve past aspect. Litter thickness =0.05 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Relatively large, open and high quality. Native species dominated, few to no invasive species. State and private land appear to be managed similarly. Prairie relatively uniform, dense sumac dominates slope. Based on vegetation, site seems more mesic possibly from more rain. Grass dense and robust, several forbs not found. Many decreaser species present, but overall diversity of forbs is moderate, now few invasive species. Litter thickness =0.05 cm. Original notes say a permanent marker was installed, not able to locate. Fairly confident on relevé location based on other descriptors. Plot moved to east from target point to stay on state land. Site laid out at slight angle to N, S, E, W to keep close to fence and be parallel with slope. Vegetation in areas surrounding relevé similar to relevé plot. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Original Relevé location mentions interpretive sign. Found a sign and walked 16 paces east, searched for permanent marker. None found. Is this sign in same location as original Relevé? I then split the difference between sign-based and GPS-based location. Slope and aspect, tree species similar across this section of slope. Steep slope with exposed loose, small rocks and outcrop just downslope of plot. Bare soil over 10-15% of plot. Litter thickness =0.2 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Easy to locate, large patches of similar forest type. Slope and aspect of target point matched original relevé. Plot was oriented parallel with slope. Mostly open-grown, wider around trees. Red oak with barbed wire near SE corner. Original plot post found when sampling, flattened by fallen tree. Soil seems compacted. Dense shrub cover from 0.5-1.5 meters, not possible to accurately access cover in height class 2; 3 separately, as was done for the original relevé. Difficult to distinguish oak species between Q. ellipsoidalis and Q. rubrum. Height: original relevé had trees >35 meters, no trees this tall observed now. Litter thickness =0.1 cm. Ranking of relevé due to lots of Rubus, few saplings, soil/humus layers absent, less shagbark than typically common? Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Target GPS matched slope and aspect. No stakes seen, plot placed with target GPS location ~in center. Steep, rocky site. Litter thickness =0.1 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Moved plot south from target GPS to get plot off trail. Slope and aspect match original Relevé. Two height classes of trees: 6-7 and 5. Few to no smaller trees or tall shrubs. Some of the larger trees are open-grown crown form. Litter thickness =0.5 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Mostly native species, some decreasers missing. Tall species dominate. Vegetation tall & dense like UPs23. Plot worked around target GPS. Lower slope of steep bluff prairie/savanna. Carya ovata in original plot not seen. Evidence of cutting and burning, charred wood and stumps. Rubus species encroaching upslope, also Solidago. Steep, rocky bluff, majority of surface with loose flags of limestone. Andropogon ger & Solidago dense. small and stunted. Hard to assess earthworm extent. Litter thickness =0.2 cm.  Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Set plot location so upper edge was at point where hill just starts to level as described in original relevé. Site rank due to present weedy species, but they are not dominant. Uncertain Relevé stand is typical of NPC: dense canopy, less grass and forbs than usual. Sparse understory. Humus thickness =0.1 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

npc_type_name: White Pine - Sugar Maple - Basswood Forest (Cold Slope)
remarks: Plot located slightly west and south from target point to best match original relevé vegetation. Dominant trees and forbs a good match. Bladdernut present as ~0.5 meter plants. Fallen Abies balsamea on east end of plot. Exposed talus rock in plot, steep drop-off from plot to river. Humus thickness =0.4 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Current relevé located near target GPS and in relationship to birch located nearby. Plot 5 x 20 meters, runs parallel to slope. Plot 1 meter NE of birch, 25 meters to NE corner. Slope and aspect similar to that originally recorded. Portions of prairie nearby mowed, likely for restoration purposes. Gravelly soil with stones on the soil surface. Occasional bur oak and paper birch. Litter thickness =0.1 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks:
Not able to locate stake or log in previous relevé sketch. Many logs down, and many large red oaks in area. Plot moved slightly from target GPS. Laid out N/S/E/W to match original relevé slope, aspect, and orientation. Soil seems packed down. Areas with no leaf cover. Few plants between 0.5-8 meters tall. Litter thickness =0.2 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. 
Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Looked for marker from previous relevé, not found. Could not find live or dead Butternut, or even a solidly NE slope. Place plot on NW-facing half with NE & SW slopes (ie: at GPS point). Relevé rank due to bare soil and top-killed woody understory plants, which are the dominant conditions. Packed soil, few middens obvious, but almost no leaf litter. Ranked high for earthworms. Something seems very unhealthy about the understory. Herbaceous plants also small and sparse, some with yellow leaves. Large tall canopy trees with dense cover. Spoke with Mark White-site recently burned. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Plot moved upslope from target GPS to better match 17 degrees from original relevé. Slope ranges from ~15-20 degrees. Soil seems moist, stumps occasional. Some look like Juniperus virginiana, other species uncertain. No location nearby with just large Quercus ellipsoidalis to guide plot location. Wet area in center of plot- looks like high rain run-off. Possibly due to heavy rain events? Surface soil dark brown, loamy sand. Lots of exposed soil. Limestone flags scattered on surface. Top of green ash fallen in plot. Wet soil species in run-off area: Lycopus, Cyperus, etc. Litter thickness =0.1 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Target point was in older Scotch pine and hazelnut, area not in original relevé, so plot was moved west to match vegetation. Rank of relevé was due to low diversity. Little exposed sandy soil, ~2%. Litter thickness =0.4 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Located on W-facing 7 degree slope near target GPS point. Upslope prairie has dense sumac, downslope similar to plot but with less Sporobolus heterolepsis. Rocky soil. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Target GPS moved to get a more E-aspect (still somewhat E-SE). Location appear representative of this part of the prairie. Typical distribution of prairie plants: ie, patches associated with variations in topography, etc. Grass cover a mix of many co-dominants. Eupatorium purpureum abundant to north and east. Litter thickness =0.5 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Placed plot in depression/flat area as described. Difficult to determine where plot should be located because of Cornus and Phalaris dominance. Low rank given due to Phalaris and Arundinacea dominance. Plot located near large Cornus racemosa clump on slope, just above low depression. Remaining woody species small, often just one stem. Litter thickness =0.3 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Southwest side of Lake Ann. Set up plot near target GPS, but off of well-used trail to south (upslope). Site description and previously observed vegetation match re-sample relevé location. Area contains >50% exposed sand. One small trail along south edge of plot and one light use trail through plot. Sand prairie opening with Quercus ellipsoidalis, Q. macrocarpa patches on most perimeters of opening. Pinus resinosa also in surrounding wooded areas. Vegetation cover seems less than earlier relevé- sand disturbance from wind/trails. Area drier? Litter thickness =0.2 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Also a revisit of DNR Relevé #6987.Located plot based on 4 conduit stakes labeled: HA-1-NE, HA-1-SE, HA-1-SW, & HA-1-NW and as described in notes for Relevé #6987 in 1995. (only NE & NW stakes mentioned in notes). Did not fine ID tag #617. Surface soil texture with some loam. Gently undulating topography in plot to flat. Litter thickness =0.5 cm is leaves and grass & Humus thickness =0.1 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Original sample location appears to have been removed, regraded and railroad tracks laid down. Original location would have gotten more afternoon sun. Remaining vegetation on east side of tracks is mostly weedy species (Verbascum thapsus, Setaria viridis, etc). Current vegetation along tracks has brown leaves- possible herbicide? Most similar location for current plot location established on west side of tracks, a 5 x 20 meter plot run ~parallel to old tracks just at the base of the old RR bed. Linear, disturbed dry prairie between old RR bed (raised) & steep wooded slope to the W. Weedy, but with patches of native species. Gravelly sand,, lots of small stones. Litter thickness =0.3 cm and Humus thickness =0.2 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Target GPS point matched slope, aspect, prior vegetation. Exposed (barely) rocks on west end of plot. Relevé not typical of stand. This area more open, other parts of stand have thick Rhus glabra or Solidago. Central portion of ridge mostly open. To the south Rhus glabra is fairly dense. Both north and south sites have lots of Solidago canadensis, also shrubby upslope. Looked for Arabidgosis, Minuartia, & Euphorbia species previously observed, but not found. If plot was at top of slope, it would be overgrown. Perhaps it was in another location or species are now gone? Litter thickness =0.5 cm & Humus thickness =0.2 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Plot set up on edge of opening as described for original relevé. Included brands from one Quercus ellipsoidalis as tree would likely have grown into plot in 25+ years. Vegetation in location selected also best for previous vegetation observed. Medium-sized gravel on soil surface. Small prairie opening with Quercus ellipsoidalis on upslope edge & sides. Dense Rhamnus cathartica & other woody plants in surrounding forested areas. Evidence of restoration efforts= stumps, cut woody stems, occasional piles of cut brush. Some forbs with heavy herbivory. Litter thickness =0.3 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Placed plot near target GPS point, ~1/2 way up long, relatively steep slope. Located in middle (along slope) of white pine forest. Deer tail through plot running E-W. Laid out 0/90 degrees N/S/E/W. Large diameter white pine to west & north (ie: downslope) of plot. Occasional large dead or fallen Betula papyrifera. Understory sparse. No Besseya bullii observed. Litter thickness =0.5 cm, composed of leaves and needles. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Metal post (T-bar with red painted top) found near GPS target point. Laid out plot at 0/90 degrees N/S/E/W. Measured 10 meters west of stake, then 10 meters north to start locating plot corners. Lots of wildlife trails (deer and turkey abundant in Park). Signs of wildlife scratching on soil surface. Narrow band of oak forest with gravel road downslope and highway at top of slope. Cut stumps and tops from logging in plot and occasional in forest. Open-grown and forest-grown oaks. Open-grown are largest dbh trees. Litter thickness =0.3 cm.  Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Centered plot in remaining canopy (trees & shrubs) opening. Surrounded on all sides by nature and non-native shrubs. Plot is overgrown with shrubs and weedy herbaceous plants. Plot in central remaining opening that has a few remaining Andropogon gerardii, Ratibida pinnata and other prairie/savanna plants. Litter layer contains leaves and grass. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

place_name: Lawrence Wayside; Mn Valley State Rec Area
remarks: Plot placed between oak tree and tracks in opening with diverse prairie grasses and forbs. Laid out plot NE, NW, SE, SW as described for original relevé. Results in plot ~approx parallel to train tracks. Large glacial erratics occasional. Shrubs and tree species encroaching on opening edges. Adjacent woodland savanna to west with understory dominated by Rhamnus cathartica. Grass species dense. Smaller stature forbs may have been out-competed. Several species observed before, for example Viola pellata and Anemone cylindrica not seen. Litter thickness =0.5 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Stand not typical of NPC, degraded. Occasional multi-stemmed oaks. Dense shrub understory. Few forbs with flowers or seeds/fruit. Quercus ellipsoidalis mostly with open-grown form. Litter thickness =0.1 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Place found with only partial downed trees. Mostly from past tree fall as most at a more advanced stage of decay than adjacent blowdown. Post disturbance species observed in blow down area also occurring in the stand sampled, except at much lower abundance. Blowdown area generally stops where white pine is abundant (also somewhat upslope). Carex dominated understory. Occasional large white pine in stand. Island of standing trees in blowdown area. Litter thickness =0.3 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - White Oak - (Sugar Maple) Forest
remarks: White pines occur throughout target stand area, but no white pine recorded on original relevé. No slope or aspect to guide site selection, so plot location selected that contained large Quercus rubra and Ostrya virginiana on SE-facing slope. Close to target GPS point. Large white pine stand with occasional large, open-grown Quercus rubra. Open understory, ~25-35% needles/open area. Litter thickness =0.4 cm, contains leaves and needles. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Plot moved slightly downslope from target point so that top (uphill) side was just below area with lots of rocks fallen from outcrop, since fallen rock was not noted in original relevé. Also the slightly downslope location was a better fit for original relevé vegetation. Bluff along Mississippi River, steep slope about 20 meters downslope of rock outcrop. Humus thickness =0.2 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. 
Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Linear plot 10 x 40 meters along ridge crest and near top of cliff. Site includes ecotonal/drier species. Plot located in ecotone between cliff edge vegetation and north slope forest/woodland. Few forbs or grasses blooming or seeding. Little vegetation from 0.4m to 2-3 meters. Litter thickness =0.4cm composed of leaves and needles. Humus thickness =0.1 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Plot placed near target GPS point: slope & aspect matched & some dominant trees were present. However, understory vegetation dominated by Laportea candensis. To W about 75-100 meters, forest seems better match. Could not be determined whether target point was quite a bit off location or whether trees had fallen & understory conditions were wetter. Location had been checked based on the hanging Quad map, releve near target point. In case differences represent community changes. *Note: Map of community extent (ie: polygon perimeter) would help in locating plot & having a sense of how far plot could be adjusted. Lots of dead elms & fallen trees in general. Dark loam over sand. Few shrubs, saplings. Badger den: sandy soil, mound & tunnel. Very little litter-due to earthworms or other factors? Few castings observed. Bearing trees & nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE & SW corners. Supplemental information & hand-drawn map with field form.

Relevé moved ~50 meters south of target GPS point. Target point was in area with dense Cornus stolonifera, Aspen tremuloides, & Phalaris arundinacea. As per conversation with Dan Wovcha, the target location was approximate and tracking species composition changes in the prairie will be more valuable information than a plot in a woody/weedy area. Humus thickness =0.2 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Sample location moved ~70 meters NW from target GPS point. Slope & vegetation were the best match at this location. Quercus ellipsoidalis (2-10 dbh) have grown up in the savanna and a few more were included in the plot. Plot kept to upper slope as described in original relevé notes. Plot laid out at 330 & 240 degrees. Litter thickness =0.2 cm. Site is canopy opening in sand prairie/savanna. Scattered bur oak, either browsed & <2 meters tall or more mature oaks to 15-20 meters. Quercus ellipsoidalis scattered, ranging in size from 2-10 dbh. Those trees outside plot to ~15 dbh. Exposed sand/soil =5-10%. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Plot placed near target GPS point in center of opening. To the south is a low, wet sedge-dominated swale. To the north,  the terrain becomes more undulating with a greater percent of exposed sand. East and west are tree groves. Plot laid out at 0/90 degrees, N,S,E,W. Areas with Oak cover nearby, sedge meadow to south. Sandy slope 15-20% exposed sand. Soil mosses appear dead- fire? Burned grass clumps in plot (bases of grass. Litter thickness =0.1 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

This site also a re-survey of DNR Relevé #6989. One "T" post and 2 conduit stakes found in the general area near the target GPS for #6989. Stakes labeled HA-602NE, HA-602NW, HA-602SE (tag end broken off). Stake for SW corner not found. Species diversity (forbs) seems lower than previously. Litter thickness =0.1 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. 
Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Target GPS point was in a dense patch of hazelnut. Based on discussion with Dan Wovcha, it was decided that plot be moved to where there was grass and forb dominated vegetation to better capture any changes to savanna understory composition. Area sampled is graminoid and forb dominated. Much of the savanna (60%) has dense patches of hazelnut (Corlyis americana), with areas dominated by hazel. Single stem trees and resprouting multiple stemmed Quercus macrocarpa. Toxicodendron dying back. Cover may have been higher earlier in season. Grass cover tall and dense, smaller stature or bare sand spp. not observed. Litter thickness =0.5 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Located plot near target GPS where large Tilia americana & Quercus rubra were located. Included small portion of canopy gap. Slope & aspect a good match for original relevé. Little tree regeneration. Understory less diverse than original relevé sample. Lower area seems wet. Litter and humus thickness =0.2 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mid-lower portion of long slope to the south. East-facing side of slope. West side of plot placed at old barbwire through oaks (old fence line). Moved upslope somewhat from target GPS to avoid plot being on edge of ravine at bottom of slope. Fence didn’t appear to run directly west. Plot line placed on line between red and white oak with barbwire for western edge. Lower/NE corner mostly without understory vegetation, leaves only ~35% of ground leaf cover and no veg. Occasional limestone flagstone. Canopy gap as a result of dead Quercus rubra and dying Ulmus sp. Litter thickness =0.5cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Plot moved slightly west from target GPS to match original relevé slope and aspect. Laid out 0/90 degrees, N, S, E, W. Rolling sand dunes. Approximately 20% exposed sand, some gopher mounds. Vegetation mostly < 0.5, with taller patches of Andropogon gerardii. Litter thickness =0.1 cm. Topographic context middle to lower aspect. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Target GPS seemed a good match for original relevé location. Plot laid out parallel to slope. Bluff prairie on grass/forb dominated slope. Dead tops of Rhus glabra common. Limestone slabs and smaller chunks of limestone common. Humus thickness =0.2 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Plot moved west to get it on a NW aspect- on the crest of the long ride running NW. To the east side of the ridge faced east. Ecotone between mesic forest on north/east line and cliff/bluff vegetation along western plot boundary. Signs of restoration work in area - cut Juniperus virginiana just down slope from the plot along upper edge of cliff. Burned stumps and charred wood present. Maintenance ATV tracks through the plot (vegetated, but with some disturbance species). Litter thickness =0.1 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Mark White had a GPS point from a Trimble unit. That point was located a few meters east of the target GPS point. Dead bur oak near where target and Trimble point were. No post or tag located. Vegetation does not seem a good match for original relevé, but neither downslope or upslope was any better match. Possibly a rock slide since site was sampled previously? Or possibility of greater amounts of rainfall changed understory species? Plot located on transition area between limestone cliffs/outcrops and more moderately sloped oak forest. Limestone flagstone covers the majority of the ground. Plant community dominated by moisture loving & disturbance response species. Tops of cut Juniperus virginiana scattered on upslope edge of plot (north edge). Charred wood along upper slope edge, also. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Talus slope along base of bluff. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Site description, prior vegetation, and target GPS point all confirmed selected general location of plot, but original plot layout and relationship to farm road (location in plot) is unclear. Quercus ellipsoidalis on edge of plot and downslope, Carya ovata located upslope, so releve plot placed between denser Q. ellip & Carya ovata with lower boundary to include old farm road. This spot resulted in more Quercus alba, however the species present in the re-sampled location (all striata) were representative of the stand. UUnderstory sparse with about 25% exposed soil (no leaves). Recent heavy rains appear to have smoothed soil surface- hard to determine earthworm quantity. Occasional limestone flagstones. Occasional Carya ovata in stand. Higher cover of Qercus cf. ellip downslope. More C. ovata upslope. Litter thickness =0.2 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

Plot location was paced 18 steps from top of ridge, where uphill edge of relevé was placed. Relevé ran along slope 30/300 degrees. Old fenceline or barbwire was searched for, but none found. Current present vegetation seems a good match to original site. Occasional open-grown oaks. Signs of girdling of some trees, particularily Ulmus americana. Charred wood scattered on forest floor, fire-scarred bases of some larger trees on upslope side. Majority of soil in plot exposed, no litter, mostly dead prickly ash. Litter thickness =0.1cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks:
Plot placed downslope enough to get past area with almost no understory vegetation due to steep slope and shifting roots. Plot located between vertical outcrops as no outcrops were described for original relevé. At selected location; slope, aspect and vegetation seemed a good fit to original relevé. Plot laid out at 1300 & 2400 with slope of hill. Hard to determine earthworm presence and abundance- lots of rocks over soil. Limestone rocks scattered over much of soil surface. Most growth covering most rocks. Occasional snags, sparse understory. Rocky outcrops occasional and upslope. Most undersory plants senescing. Litter thickness =0.1 cm. Bearing trees and nails at all 4 corners. Magnets at NE and SW corners. 
Supplemental information and hand-drawn map with field form.
Releve to document typical Calamagrostis dominated wet meadow with bands of Carex aquatilis. There is a separate releve for Carex aquatilis bands. Dense thatch. No mosses noticed.

Larger wet meadow is dominated Calamagrostris, but this releve is to document bands of Carex aquatilis + Rumex. Appears that higher amounts of water move through this part of peat. These bands are a little more diverse than surrounding areas. Bands are visible on color infrared photos.

Plot documents partially treed rock knob that rises significantly higher from surrounding forest. Approx. 50% of plot is exposed rock. This does not include lichen covered areas. Rock is pink granite.
There were lots of other smaller lichens not documented, but we tried to capture most common ones we could ID.

Currently fairly dry, but peat is moist. No standing water. Patches of Phalaris & Cirsium arvense. Oce Acer negundo + Frax nigra-are the only tall trees in opening. No mosses. Thick graninoid thatch surrounding patchy forest dominated by Frax niga + Frax pensylv. with occ. Acer negundo. Ground dom. by Calamagrostis.

Dry mesic prairie typical of NPB parcel. Heavily invaded with B. inermis throughout entire parcel. Native forbs common; native grass uncommon. Rolling hills with wetlands at base(open water). Parcel surrounded by cultivated fields.

Dry, heavily grazed gravel prairie on low ridge running in NW-SE across parcel. Grass is grazed to <5 cm height. Solidago canadensis is prominent. Low wet swales to the SW. Heavily invaded by Bromus inermis and Poa pratensis.
Re-survey of Releve #7984. Fairly degraded portion of a Mesic Prairie system in an area with heavy cattle influence. Photo P8101268
Mesic prairie. Site fairly consistent with surrounding area. Photo P8161391 (NE)

Stand not typical of NPC, appears too homogeneous within. A few of species observed are indicators for WPs54.

place_name: St. Croix State Forest Outside Exclosure
remarks: Was Oak forest; logged, treated with herbicide, and planted to red oak and white ash. Plot's purpose is to track forest succession and deer browse. Nearby Releve placed inside deer exclosure for comparison. Permanent plot. Lines on N-S & E-W compass bearing. State forest stand #153179.

place_name: St. Croix State Forest Outside Exclosure
remarks: Was Oak forest; shelterwood cut, rock raked and treated with herbicide and planted to red oak and white ash. Plot's purpose is to track forest succession and deer browse. Nearby releve placed inside deer exclosure for comparison.

place_name: St. Croix State Forest Outside Exclosure
remarks: Large mound that appears to be an old pile of logs in the plot, covered by weedy species. One large rotted stump in plot. Plot fairly close to open wet pocket of habitat. Soil wormed. Overall, much more open than plot that was in enclosure.

place_name: St. Croix State Forest Deer Exclosure
remarks: Plot is inside deer exclosure. Purpose is to monitor forest in comparison with releve outside exclosure. Shelterwood harvest winter 1994-1995, then rock-raked, and sprayed with herbicides. Red oak and white ash seedlings planted. Rebar marks SW corner. Plot located near SE corner of wire mesh exclosure.

place_name: St. Croix State Forest Deer Exclosure
remarks: Plot is inside deer exclosure, with SW corner marked by rebar. Purpose of plot is to monitor forest in comparison to releve outside exclosure. Shelterwood harvest Winter 1991-1995, then rock raked, sprayed with glyphosate & triclopyr. Red oak and white ash seedlings planted.

Plot in site of former deer exclosure, fencing removed in 2013. Soil wormed. Almost no non-native invasive species. Appears to be regenerating successfully following logging, oak and ash planting, and former deer exclosure. One Quercus rubra tree in plot. Rebar from original visit still in SW corner-sprayed orange. Photos taken at site.

Releve from area with lots of seepage and extremely springy soil located below small tamarack stand with abundant Phragmites. A number of these seepage areas occur
throughout the larger area and many small spring nurs go through the larger peatland. Most are very well developed spring fens communities. Releve is early in penology. Ice domes evident on areal photography.
Releve to document more open wet meadow in this site, dark loam over sand. Phalaris only under small shrubs.
Area degraged past grazing.

Releve located in area of fen with higher B. pumila cover, but also larger area of Carex sterilis, middle of plot with larger cornus has had a lot of deer browse located ca 20 m 5 of CT a_, and shrubby seepage to SW. No marly pools, almost continous moss cover in Carex lawn. Specific cond: 630-800, watr 13.9 degrees C.

109-112 plot ___ cardinal ___.
Erika photo # 49, 48, 50, 51-54
Magnet buried in SE corner.

Moist organic at top of slope, no standing water or visible seepage. Surrounded by reed canary grass dominated area that is very degraded but this was the best part in the whole area. Several small seeps below. This was located near an area that formerly was identified as calcareous fen. There is nothing resembling calc fen and this was the nicest piece in the entire vicinity. It probably measures 15x15m or so.
Releve to document linear fen. Plot running in cardinal directions. UTMs in SE corner.
Area of seepage hill, fairly steep slope, peat mound, area is overrun by buckthorn, and other areas of the peat shelf appear degraded.
Releve to document fairly large area of similar composition. Looks degraded due to bast grazing? perhaps mildly saline?
Thick thatch of dead Juncus, species poor. History of heavy grazing?
Wm impacted by past grazing? Grades into marsh + slightly more Carex dominated areas.
Another example of very forb rich prairie with light warm season grass component. Located on sandy loan and grades into wm to the west. Looks hayed recently, maybe a history of grazing?

Wet prairie swales between small sandy ridges. This area has had intense management for shrub and aspen control and appears to be recovering well. Uplands with low warm season grass component, but very diverse in prairie forbs.
Patches of melilotus with fairly light cover throughout area, plot lands in one.
fairly heavily grazed strip of upland running through pasture.
A great example of dry prairie, looks to have a history of moderate grazing.

Exceedingly species rich, partly due to plot being on slope from dry-dry mesic. Sporobolus heteroleopsis abundant just below Releve on slope. Species marked with "R" were associated with a burrow in lower W corner of plot. Species rich, but plot seems to be lacking evenness. Lots of Bouteloua & Sedum w/only mix of some forbs present.
This area was burned in the spring, fire appears to have knocked back cool season exotics to an impressive degree. Lots of open soil between natives. history of grazing, but not grazed in years.

Well developed peat mound with active seepage from middle surrounded by short sedge lawn. The margins of this plot have some disturbance from grazing, but looks like cattle have mostly stayed out of the active seepage areas.
This area had a lot of water flowing through it this spring but is now slowly flowing. Water chemistry from hand probe: PH:7.62, Conductivity:747, temp 17.4 C, ORP +826, DO .15 mg/L.
Releve in degraded area of wet seepage prairie. Releve location may poorly represent area, which is variable. Water fairly deep under surface, nearby cut down drainage (ca. 0.5m).

Releve located in active pasture. Thistles have been spot sprayed. Upside edge is on SW side of plot and has more grazing impacts and invasive. Reed canary grass stems are sparse between Carex stricta tussocks. Located on a shallow NE facing toe slope within an early glacial river Warren meander or other glacial river valley. NE side of plot is on edge of marsh.
Prairie hillside that has never been grazed. Burned in spring nearly every year but not 2018. No invasive species were found in this plot.

Hummock height 6 inches. Water height about 1 inch above peat, flowing slowly to the south. Open seepage meadow surrounded by aspen trees and thickets of dogwood with other trees and shrubs, including Rhamnus cathartica. Areas outside of releve mostly more degraded, with dense Phalaris or dense woody growth. 

SE corner was where waypoint was taken.

Permanent marker: steel spikes at corners.
UTM Easting/Northing taken from center of plot. 
UTM accuracy: 2-4 m
Slope drops 4 ft in elevation every 33 ft. Moderately steep slope. FSH GPS waypoints 472-475.
Soils: peaty muck at surface. Sedge peat underneath. Don't know depth. Depth of standing water: 0-6 cm.
Remarks: Sample is in upper part of large seepage wetland on toe slopes of steep hills. Wetland extends from here to Florida Creek on moderately steep S-facing slope. Copious groundwater flow. No evidence of marl on surface. Small areas of floating sedge mat. Mostly dominated by Carex stricta. Portions also dominated by Typha latifolia, Cornus sericeus, Carex pellita. Plot is only part of site where we saw Berula. Some Phalaris patches elsewhere in this wetland.

Plot chosen to represent growth stage post fire (2011, fall). Fire severity variable within the FDn32 with P. banksiana dominated canopy, with few Populus tremuloides and Betula papyrifera. Soil depth ranges from 0-20cm. No evidence of previous human disturbance. Moderate amount of cwd. Standing charred snag of each former canopy sp (Pop trem x2). A few tip-up mounds of sand gravelly loam. Represents variable veg response to fire. Plot represents variable conditions of recovery on narrow ridge landform common in landscape south of insula. UTM= NW corner of plot.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to resample releve; precise original location unverifiable; same NPC, patchy, same slope position, original location error unknown. Abundant CWD <20cm dbh; snags of all live tree species, various stages of decay. Lichens on tree boles. UTM= NE corner of plot. Charcoal observed. Betula mix of papyrifera, cordifolia, and hybrids otherwise.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to resample NPC of SNA. Exact location of original releve not very reliable. The plot is in the same NPC patch, similar slope position. Too late in the year for spring ephemerals. Dicentra corms in litter D1-2 at low end of cover class. Possible very decayed cut conifer stump in plot. Exposed cobbles/stones at surface. Soil exam stopped by dense layer of gravel/cobble below the humus. CWD moderate amount, all sizes, most small-medium. UTM=NE corner of plot.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to resample NPC of releve #6634. Original location could not be precisely verified. Moderate amount of small to mid sized CWD. Rocks frequent at surface, single and grouped. Too late in the year for Claytonia spp, but they are likely present. Mineral soil gravel with cobbles and stones. Humus intact in other areas of NPC near plot. Pit and mound microtopography. UTM = midpoint of plot.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to resample 0398 but poor location info. This plot is intended as a resample. Plot located in general area of original, chosen to represent high quality NPC. Old growth forest in this part of SNA. High quality NPC with elements of transition from MHn45a to MHn45c, including old Pinus strobus, which is rare in this landscape. This aspect of ridge landform with many of these old pines. CWD in range of sizes, various states of decay.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to resample 1996 releve #6074. Location close but not exact match. Plot slopes along N-S axis but also to center on E-W axis. P. strobus not fire-scarred. No evidence of past anthro-disturbance. Topo context upper as near top of one side of canyon; middle of mid-range slope. Top damage/mortality to P. strobus. Faint game trail thru plot. Plot terrain irregular via small scale brook topo. Plot incl two several meter long bedrock outcrops about 1m high on E-W axis. Browse impacts to tall shrubs. Moderate amount of CWD; small to med sized.

Plot chosen to represent NPC and condition where Betula canopy gone or senescing, no other functional canopy >2m tall. In other areas in this setting Rubus parviflorus dominates in large patches instead of Diervilla lonicera. Soils shallower on S slope below plot. Rosa acicularis is codominant with Diervilla there. Diervilla = canopy over many forbs. Calamogrostis canadensis on low end of 5-25% cover. Continuous cover of Diervilla over 75% of plot. Lower S 1/2 with a bit more soil. North half with occasional bedrock  at surface, especially in west half. UTM= midpoint of plot.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC and condition typical of NPC in this setting in this portion of the SNA. Located on the SW landing of the main slope (S-facing) plot with multiple aspects. One conifer stump likely cut, very decayed. Small drain along north side with a small area where water pools at NW corner. Claytonia "spuds" in litter. Patch/plot approaches old growth structure. Dense stones at 25 cm. Lg-sm size CWD, mostly Betula. UTM = midpoint of plot.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC type and condition common in this setting in the SNA. P. banksiana mortality of mid-sized dbh trees, creating ___ canopy openings. Small exposures of rocks and bedrock occasional in plot as in patch. Lichens on low ground, exposed rock, CWD, among Pleurozium. Bet papyrifera recruitment suppressed by browse, as are tall shrubs - favoring Diervilla? Vaccinium? CWD small to medium sized is abundant. UTM is midpoint of plot. Charcoal below humus. No worms found in plot.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC and condition in this setting in Cascades SP, with broken senescing deciduous canopy. Abies and Betula sm-med sized CWD abundant. No mineral soil; all wormed mull to bedrock. 30-65% gravel. Betula recruitment limited by deer browsing. Graminoids at low end of range. Fine plant roots present. Decent blowdown of 2 Abies in 5-6 height class. Bryos on ground and well-decayed woods. Lichens present on boles and branches, CWD, and exposed rock. CWD= significant slowing of runoff. UTM= midpoint of plot.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC and condition common to this setting in Cascade SP. Some pit and mound microtopography. A well-decayed stump, likely cut with D&D Betula. Tall shrub and dec. tree regen, present but suppressed by deer browsing. Drainage estimated. Wave-rounded cobbles present in mineral soil. Occasional rock visible on surface. No earthworm middens observed. No charcoal or fire scars on P. strobus observed. CWD= all states of decay, sm-med sized, and various species. UTM= mid point of plot.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to resample natural origin old-growth NPC patch. Needles abundant in litter but leaves by volume. Pit and mound microtopography. No earthworm middens found; fine roots present. Thuja regen common <20cm, no browse observed on these individuals yet. Otherwise deer browse impact is severe. Abundant CWD in many sizes and states of decay, and prominent species except Acer saccharum. UTM= mid point of plot. Bryos on rock. Lichens on tree boles.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to represent large patch in SNA. No cut stumps. Natural origin. Charred, very decayed Thuja stump. No large dbh snags. Dead and dying Abies are wind-thrown. CWD abundant, sm-med sized, various states of decay: Abies is +, Betula is +/- and Populus is -. Bryos on ground, CWD, and exposed bedrock. Lichens on ground, CWD, and tree boles. A few small patches of Peltigera. Fine plant roots present. No middens. Browsing severe. UTM=midpoint of plot. Soil depth ranges from 0-25cm.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC and condition common in this setting in park. Topo context relative to whole lake facing slope. Plot on upper portion of slope below the terrace "break." Selective harvest and fire(s) in early 1900s. Evident pit and mound topo. Two planted/caged P. strobus in plot. E6-6 at 25% cover. No cut stumps in plot. Diervilla cover dense except it is near 0 in the SE quarter. Charcoal present. Mull might be deeper. Fine roots present. UTM= midpoint of plot.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC patch on north-facing slope of SNA. Low small exposed bedrock face in south half of plot. Litter thickness = litter and duff. Litter varies between leaves or needle predominance. Cobbles and stones (bedrock?) below 22cm prevented further soil exam. Exposed bedrock. Large stones, boulders - bryophytes on these and on CWD, roots, and tree bases. CWD common, all states of decay, sm-med sized diameters, most Betula. Populus and Abies; one unknown conifer. UTM= midpoint of plot.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to represent small patch NPC in SNA. Pit and mound microtopography. Little sphagnum ____; feather mosses and other species common on CWD, on boles, and in wet pits. No standing water this date. Water in soil pit at 18cm. Litter is part leaves and part needles. Duff layer is 4cm thick between water and muck. Abundant CWD small-medium sized, all states of decay. UTM= midpoint of plot. Pits are at 50% of plot.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to represent old natural original NPC on north-facing slope of SNA. Potential old growth patch. Big dbh Pinus strobus snag near plot. No evidence of anthro disturbance in plot. Bryos on exposed rock and tree bases. Soil in pockets within matrix substrate of stones and boulders. No middens (earthworm). Other parts of slope above with significant blowdown from fall of 2018. UTM= midpoint of plot.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC typical of ridge setting with both FDn43 and MHn45 communities. Burned in 1936 fire. Saddle of bedrock controlled ridge between knobs with outcrops and FDn32 NPC. Cobbles frequent at surface. Soil assessment blocked by dense cobbles and/or bedrock. Mod amount of sm-med sized CWD; mostly Populus and Betula; all stages of decay. To west spacious slope below knob is MHn45 plot. No cut stumps. Charcoal present. Moose scat present. UTM= midpoint of plot.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to represent small patch NPC of SNA. Some evidence of decaded old disturbance nearby e.g. very decayed cut stump, and overgrown old 2-track access. Plot north boundary follows softened vegetation berm of soil related to this. NW corner of plot with 2 soil mounds; Betula papyrifera growing from them. CWD amount is low in plot, of medium size, various states of decay. Linear patch between WFn53, MHn53, and FDn43. UTM= midpoint of plot. Pit and mound microtopography.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Plot chosen to represent NPC patch common on upper ridge of SNA. Subtype unclear. Natural origin from fires in 1894, 1908(?), 1918, and 1936. Populus roots common at surface. Soil depth to bedrock. Rocks occasional at surface. Subtle microtopo. Betula ___ multi-stemmed. Nearby areas of patch with greater herb richness and diversity and understory Abies. No earthworm middens. Duff in some places, fine roots, could be ERAR of 3. Abundant small-med CWD of Betula, Pop trem, and Abies. No cut stumps. Lichens abundant on tree boles. UTM=midpoint of plot.

Releve re-sampling project. Waypoint 002 is in NE corner.

Below 3 cm of decomposed organic duff is 87 cm of reddish coarse sand with only a few coarse fragments. Dendrobaena earthworms observed. Woodland matches description of releve 7521, but old openings are shaded and very few prairie species remain. Ratio of oaks:aspen increases closer to road, some oaks have open grown branches (one like this in plot). Mosses mostly restricted to logs, except some collected from 2 old tip-up mounds. Charring visible on old stump.

Magnets at NE and SW corners; spikes in all 4 corners.

Basswood dominated mesic-hardwood on loamy sand in Anoka Sand Plain on upland surrounded by old oxbow on rum river with a seepage swamp. Moderate amount of coarse woody debris. Evidence of heavy deer browse (most woody stems hedged). Earthworms present. Little tree regeneration. One basswood (59.3cm DBH) has buttressed base - did soil erode over time?

NRCS data sheet also completed. Slope is 5% across soil pit. Eolian loamy cap over Rainy lobe outwash; soil would be somewhat excessively drained if not for this cap. Soil horizons from top to bottom: A, Bw (FSL), 2C (LCOS). Coarse woody debris and snags of P. tremuloides and B. papyrifera 20-30 cm dbh occur. No recent cutting observed (old pine stumps well decayed and charred stumps occur) but no large conifer coarse woody debris occur in plot; some down P. resinosa outside plot. Poor spruce and pine regen - mostly fir and hazelnut. FDn33a could be a conceivable alternate NPC classification. Soils fit LTP14 concept.

Many large boulder erratics in stand with Polypodium virginianum growing upon them. Surface stones and cobbles also common. More exposed ROn23 exists within greater landform. Excellent pool of CWD and snags. No evidence of recent fire, but no cut stumps seen. Moose dung seen. Shallow Oi/Oe layer (leaves + needles) with humus with fine roots and granular structure. A-horizon mixed in with humus. Soil horizon progression: A (cobbles + gravel), Bw (cobbles + gravel), bedrock. NRCS data sheet completed by Larissa Hindman. Soils fit LTP18 concept. NPC doesn't fit FDn32 well, but better than FDn43 or FDn33.

Possible FDn22 occurs on the crest, but majority of LTP polygon is FDn32c. Soil pit occurs on mid slope. NRCS data form completed by Mike Rokus. Boulders and stones on surface, mostly moss covered. Larger boulders with Carex deflexa growing upon them. Good amount of jack pine snags and coarse woody debris. Deer and moose dung seen. Rokus notes: "very bouldery surface map unit. Stopped due to gravels in profile. Saw numerous exposures walking in. Would map this as Conic-Insula-Rock Outcrop 18-35% slopes in NRCS mapping system." Soil horizon progression: E (St-SL; St/Co: 25%/25%), Bs1 (St-SL; St/Co: 25%/25%), Bs2 (St-SL; St/Co: 25%/25%), C (GRV-SL; Gr: 50%). Rokus classified this as a spodosol due to thickness of E-horizon. Soils fit LTP18 concept better, since depth to bedrock is >20 inches.

Located just below crest on steep hillside with much tree fall and exposed boulders/colluvium. 81 cm red pine just outside plot. Good aspen and jack pine snags/CWD. No evidence of recent cutting or fire/charcoal, though old fire scar on living red maple observed. NRCS soil form completed by Jim Barott. Horizons: E (Co/Gr: 40%/15%), Bw (Co/Gr: 50%/10%), C1 (LCOS; Co/Gr: 25%/25%), C2 (med. sand; Co/Gr: 15%/20%). Drainage is somewhat excessively. Slope is 22% across soil pit. Pit depth limited by coarse fragment. NPC ambiguous because soil is coarse, slope is steep, and surface is rocky, but floristics indicate more mesic conditions than FDn32; jack pine in canopy but thick mountain maple shrub layer and wintergreen and blueberries are sparse. NE aspect plus proximity of water may provide fire shelter. Poor black/white spruce regen. Jack pine and aspen are at their age limit. White spruce, paper birch, and red maple appear to succeed with legacy red pine present. Could become FDn43a.

Plot located near crest top to the NE and large prescribed burn (2019) of ROn and FDn to the south all the way to the Echo Trail. Fire doesn't appear to have affected plot. Large glacial erratic boulders present. Seasonally wet micro-depressions and Sphagnum occur next to boulder-created dips. Charcoal seen in Oe and humus. Deer and bear scat observed. Lots of good CWD and snags occurs - likely pine, though very large pieces absent. No cut stumps observed. Red maple regeneration could impede oak regen in the future. NRCS data form completed by Mike Rokus. Soils fit LTP21 concept. Litter layer composed of both leaves and needles. Soil horizons: Bw1 (Co-SL; Co-Gr-St: 18%), Bw2 (Co-SL; Co-Gr-St: 18%), C (GRV-SL; Gr: 40%), bedrock.

Stand appears marked for future sale. Currently, it is nice, mature aspen with old snags too; abundant 10-20 cm dbh snags present with some 20-30 cm birch and aspen snags. A 40+ cm aspen occurs outside of plot. No cut stumps seen. Surface boulders present. NRCS data form completed by Larissa Hindman. Soil is extremely water-worked till and lacustrine over outwash. Litter depth ranges from less than 1 cm to 2 cm. Soil horizons: A, E (FSL), Btg, Bt, Btk, 2C. Btk horizon has calcareous carbonates that are visibly hardened and white.

Plot located just south of peatland. Abundant hare browse greater than deer browse. No cut stumps seen. Good spruce snags plus birch and aspen. Balsam fir CWD, 20-30 cm dbh common. Plot sampled on gentler slope than desired to capture lacustrine deposit. All nearby LTP53B is on Rainy Till. NRCS data form completed by Larissa Hindman. Soil horizons: A (FSL; cobbles + gravels: 10%), E (FSL; cobbles + gravels: 10%), Bs (FSL), 2Bw1 (LFS), 2Bw2 (LVFS), 3Bt, 4C (SIL or SL). Soil is highly variable and does not fit LTP53 concept. Soil has some form of water-worked history. Perhaps this was a seasonally wet bay with periods of drying and wave-wash. May be better mapped as LTP 56 (reworked lacustrine). Soil is not exactly till since there is no coarse fragments below 16 cm and not exactly outwash since there is a clay loam horizon. Drainage is close to moderately well. Only concentrations seen at 35 cm but no depletions.

Higher elevations to the south may be more FDn43. Slighty more mesic conditions lower on slope to the NW. Fire history may explain black spruce and jack pine canopy even with ground cover mesic indicators. There could also be seed rain from drier upland areas on higher elevation. Semi-permeable layer perches water in this generally FDn landscape. No cut stumps observed; heavy deer and hare browse. Aspen canopy starting to senesce. NRCS data form completed by Jeff Kroll. Horizons: A, E/B, Bt, Btk1, Btk2, 2C (LVFS). Pit excavation limited by rock fragments at 106 cm. Slope is 6% immediately across soil pit. Soils fit LTP53 concept.

Plot located on flat spot/local depression in landscape though greater slope is steadily SE. Aspen snags common as are large balsam fir coarse woody debris.  No cut stumps seen. Hedging of shrubs indicate severe deer browse. NRCS data form completed by Mike Rokus on 7/12/19. Litter composed primarily of needles and secondarily leaves. Horizons: A, E1, E2, Bt, C1, C2 (w/ calcium carbonates). Very fine lacustrine soil fits LTP53 concept. Series: Longsiding (non-glossic).

Some parts of plot steeper than 8 degrees but NPC remains constant. Very bouldery landform on steep slope. Most boulders are moss-covered. Some old cut stumps seen. Good example of young, early successional birch canopy forest. Extremely high deer browse with hedging. NRCS data form completed by Jim Barott on 7/5/19. Some parts of forest floor without humus; when present, about 1 cm thick. Horizons: A (St: 70%), Bw1 (St/Co: 70%/10%), Bw2 (Co/Gr: 50%/12%), C (Co/Gr: 45%/15%). Finer material between boulders likely eroded away and moved downslope, leaving this bouldery landscape at surface. Charcoal seen in soil. Vegetation on boulders suggest woodland, but overall, NPC is FDn43 rather than FDn32.

East end of plot situated in sloped valley draining NE where interrupted fern and lots of blown over coarse woody occur. Stand is very shrubby with lots of light reaching understory; doesn't appear to have burned for quite awhile and no obvious recent cutting. No charcoal seen in Oa. Thick litter layer of needles. Excellent CWD and snags of white pine, cedar, spruce plus some old snags of large aspen. Some parts of plot steeper than 8 degrees and upwards of 20% estimated; probably more appropriately LTP 18C. NRCS data form completed by Jim Barott on 8/2/19. Horizons: E (FSL; Gr: 7%; 10YR 5/2), Bw1 (St/Co: 12%/5%; 10YR 5/2), Bw2 (St/Co: 15%/5%; 10YR 6/4), Bw3 (St/Co: 25%/5%; 10YR 5/4), C (St/Co: 10%/5%; 10YR 7/4).

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Boulders and exposed bedrock faces seen on ledges. No recent cutting seen. Spruce, white pine, and birch snags present. Medium-sized CWD. Charcoal seen on tip-up spruce on bedrock. Hare browse high. Slope is mainly west aspect but part of plot also slopes down to the north, primarily north half of plot. North half also has dense balsam fir regen, less Pleurozium cover, more aspen snags, and more deciduous litter. NRCS data form completed by Larissa Hindman on 7/8/19. Soil series is Barto. Horizons: A (Co: 30%), E (Co: 30%), Bw (Co: 30%), 2R. Could be LTP 21D due to high degree of slope; otherwise, soils fit LTP21 concept.

Plot situated on very steep bedrock high. Surface boulders and stones present. Slope is complex. Some areas of stand are more open due to tip-ups. Greater stand with old cut stumps, even on steep slopes. Likely pines were taken out and NPC was FDn43a before this harvest. Some remnant white pine do remain. More aspen just outside plot.
