Canada yew seen on steep slope. Observed browse assumed to be moose and not deer since only the former's dung seen. NRCS data form completed by Larissa Hindman. Horizons: A (Co/St: 40%/10%), BA (Co/St: 40%/10%), Bw (Co/St: 40%/10%), 2R. Due to depth of soil to bedrock, this better fits LTP18 concept. This is moderately deep loamy mantle over bedrock and results in FDn43 instead of FDn32.

Plot with complex slopes, both NE + N aspects. Canopy gaps common throughout stand with good CWD of fallen paper birch and balsam fir; did not see pine dead wood. Browse observed is assumed to be moose and not deer since browse was on balsam fir and above 2 m on mountain maple. NRCS data form completed by Jim Barott. Some humus present in patches but mostly absent in plot. Depth to bedrock uncertain but a limiting layer was hit at 79 cm preventing further pit excavation. Horizons: A (Gr: 5%), Bw1 (Co/Gr: 10%/5%), Bw2 (Co/Gr: 20%/5%), Bw3 (Co/Gr: 35%/10%), 2C (Co/Gr: 30%/20%). Soils fit LTP18 concept.

Plot located on slope of bedrock high (knob). Overall stand with obvious history of harvest; large decayed pine stumps but none recent. Large cedar possibly harvested along with pine. White pine observed far outside plot. Slope is short; plot spans lower and middle slopes. Lower slope dominant. Sparse boulders/stones occur on lower slope. Snags and CWD mostly of paper birch and balsam fir, though one 20-30 cm dbh white spruce CWD seen just outside plot. Browse assumed to be moose though no scat observed, nor of deer. NRCS data form completed by Larissa Hindman on 7/10/19. Horizons: A (Co: 40%), BA (Co/Gr: 25%/25%), Bw (Co/Gr: 25%/25%). Charcoal seen in soil. Worm rank ranges from 2 with small patches of humus up to 3 cm thick to rank 4. Soils fit LTP18 concept.

Plot is almost imperceptibly flat. NPC in a young jack pine stage of FDn43b1 but many are senescing; no red or white pine regeneration or legacies. 60 cm dbh white spruce just outside plot. Severe deer browse. Much of stand experienced blowdown with many trees down and canopy gaps. No recent cutting, though. NE corner of plot partially in a hunter access foot trail. Dilapidated deer blind occurs. NRCS data form completed by Mike Rokus. Litter consists of both leaves and needles. Drainage is somewhat excessive. Horizons: A (Gr: 1%), Bw1 (Gr: 1%), Bw2 (Gr: 1%), E & Bt (sand & loamy sand; Gr: 1%). E & Bt is parent material with loamy sand lamellae in coarser sand matrix. Lamellae + aeolian mantle likely results in this FDn43 instead of FDn33.

Lower half of plot with gentler slope and with more wet-mesic species. Natural tree fall and canopy gaps throughout stand. Some very large white pine present in greater stand and a 61 cm dbh red pine occurs just outside plot. No recent cutting observed. Nice large snags with cavities in white pine 35-45 cm dbh occur. Micro-depressions in rocks have more wet-mesic species growing. NRCS data form completed by Mike Rokus. Horizons: A (Co/Gr: 5%/10%), Bw (Gr/Co: 25%/10%), R. Two pits were dug, and depth to bedrock ranged from 10-30 cm. Site is a complex of soil: very shallow, shallow, and moderately deep, soil to bedrock. Very little humus, but no worms seen. Charcoal in A-horizon created a very black hue. Surficial boulders present. Cobbles are flat, indicating they were transported a short distance from their source.

Nearby high knobs to the SE and NW within 10 m are likely FDn43. Heavy deer hedging impedes tree regeneration; mountain maple kept short too. No recent cut stumps but recent harvest near to the N. Nice large CWD: cedar, aspen (40+ cm), white spruce, and paper birch that are well-decayed. MHn44c (cedar) surrounding plot but with similar ground cover. NRCS data form completed by Mike Rokus. Humus is almost a mor with fibers throughout and very reddish brown despite presence of small worms. Horizons: A, E, E/Bt (L/C), Bt1, Bt2, BCk, Ck (CL/C/SIL). Bt1 shows concentrations and depletions but Bt2 shows bright clay films indicating episaturation from precipitation and spring ponding. Lacustrine deposit throughout. Very Fine Clayey particle size control - argillic (19-59 cm). C-horizon was CL in upper 25 cm and SIL in lowest 10 cm. Carbonates detected in BCk but strongest fizzing in Ck.

Plot exhibits both MHn44/FDn43 characteristics depending on slope position within plot. Plot adjacent to MHn44c to the north and west; FDn43 to the southeast. Stand with abundant cut stumps possibly of large cedar. Boles of red pine (38 cm) and white pine (42 and 52 cm) just outside of plot on SE upland side of plot. One very large boulder that is vegetation covered also occurs on the SE side of plot. Plot located slightly outside mapped LTP 53B polygon and placed in mapped LTP 8 because latter captured B-slope lacustrine parent material better. Mapped LTP 53B is possibly a sand beach ridge located above glaciolacustrine material on shoulder/top slope. Rainy till occurs on crest. NRCS data form completed by Jeff Kroll. Humus is absent or <1 cm thick. Horizons: A, Bt1, Bt2, Btk, C.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Canadian Shield)
remarks: Plot occurs between bedrock ridges. A bedrock depression at SE corner has more mesic species like interrupted fern. Some old stumps seen but are not from recent cutting. Deer scat seen. Charred stump seen on tip up. NRCS data form completed by Jeff Kroll. Litter layer consists of primarily needles with leaves secondary. Horizons: A (LS with a discontinuous E-horizon), Bw1 (FSL), Bw2 (FSL), C (LCOS), R. Drainage is on the drier side of somewhat poorly. Soil is moderately deep to bedrock (>20") and should be mapped as LTP 18A/B. Soil pit was dug in slight concavity in bedrock controlled till; soil likely does not reflect western upper slope of plot where there are more surface boulders. Downslope NPC could be FDn43a.

Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. NPC growth stage is closest to 35-55 years (transitional) but there is widespread birch die off causing overall age distribution to skew <35 years. Living birch likely 35-55 years. Sparse canopy. Large decayed stumps observed of Pinus spp. and also decaying burned stumps. Plot located in thick Diervilla, but outside of plot are patches of denser Calamagrostis. Heavy deer browse: hedged Diervilla. Hare browse on Picea glauca. Charcoal seen in AB-horizon. Superior lobe clay was not reached in soil pit due to abundance of cobbles.

Additional permanent plot markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Plot with abundant cedar and black ash coarse woody debris. Black ash tree fall has shifted canopy composition to one that is equally or more cedar dominated when compared to original survey. Large-diameter cedar occur and no cut stumps or other signs of disturbance from humans. South boundary of plot drier than rest; quickly transitions to MHn45 just outside plot. Abundant worm castings in muck layer. Water seen flowing. Rocky colluvium occurs in drainage (cobbles over stones in soil pit). Several stones seen at base of tip-ups. Oddly, no Viola spp. occurs that was recorded originally.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Plot situated between steep rock cliff and upper slope that presumably transitions to more basswood-sugar maple canopy. Abundant coarse woody debris but no cut stumps seen. Soil horizons: A (black), BE (red-brown), Bw (reddish). If present at all, humus is wormed mull. Charcoal in A horizon and burned log observed. Very little silt detected throughout profile. However, the two B-horizons, especially Bw, had high clay content for a sandy loam. Would expect to hit clay loam further down beyond 62 cm in Superior lobe parent material.

Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Plot occurs near WFn55 near north corner and just beyond 3 caged white pine saplings. Large white spruce just outside plot, some near 20 m tall. Old charred, cut stump seen and also on birch CWD. Plot exhibits typical dead birch of north shore. Regeneration of aspen good. Snags mostly of paper birch and some aspen. 30 cm dbh CWD of aspen occurs in plot, not captured along CWD perimeter transects. Bracken fern was not fully expanded at time of  survey - cover likely reaches >25% later in the season. Soil horizons: A (black loam), Bw1 (brown very fine loam), Bw2 (tan very fine loam), 2BCr (gray-tan coarse SL), 2Cr. Bedrock not reached but 2Cr horizons is paralithic weathered residuum that breaks apart with shovel impact - interpreted also as semi-permeable layer. Charcoal seen in A-horizon. Soil is likely alluvium/outwash deposited during higher river stage over bedrock residuum.

Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Cedar regeneration is poor but did not see dead/dying cedar mentioned in original survey. Cut stumps not obvious, but there were stumps without accompanying boles suggesting old cuttings. Soil horizons: A (black), Bhg (gray-black), C (red, Superior lobe till). Bhg has high organic matter incorporated from above muck; no redox detected in red clay suggesting soil is saturated from above during spring water perching (episaturated). Standing water sparse, mostly just exposed mucky soil. Soil pit dug 4 m beyond NE plot corner.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Plot near Superior Hiking Trail (SHT) to the east and steep cliff to the west. Plot located on opposite side of SHT than original plot because of difficulty in re-locating original plot with stated vegetation composition. Plot with some rock bench terraces towards E-S boundary. No recent cut stumps observed. Soil horizons: A (black), Bt (reddish brown; cobbles + gravels). Charcoal seen in A-horizon. Bt is noticeably higher in clay content than A. Presumably clay loam or clay occur with greater depth helping moisture retention despite high coarse fraction. Depth to bedrock not reached because soil excavation impeded by high volume of coarse fraction.

Additional permanent plot markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Plot oriented along crest and upper slope in 10x40 m dimension and skirts walking trail. Slope is complex and steeper than 6 degrees in places. Litter, when present, consists of both leaves and needles, but is absent where foot traffic is high. Boulders and exposed bedrock occur at SW corner. Soil horizon: Bw (gravels + cobbles) and is Rainy lobe brown in color. Deer scat and tissue litter occur in plot. No cedar coarse woody debris. High traffic area with low regeneration of all tree species. Ground cover diversity very low. Understory is very shaded. Stumps occur from tree fall as do remnant soft, low stumps now appearing as ground humps. Burrowing animal also in plot.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Additional plot markers: corner stakes and tree tags. NPC on relatively steep, continuous slope. Soil horizons: A (gray-black w/ charcoal), Bt (fine SL; reddish-brown), 2C (coarse SL; deeper brown). A thin E may also be present below the A. This is likely Superior lobe till over Rainy lobe till: Bt has highest clay content and has structure but not cemented. 2C noticeably coarser with more gravels. Cobbles occur throughout profile. Water likely runs off surface and also infiltrates ground rapidly. Hence, no pools or soft footing observed - only a few dried depressions occur. No redox seen but soil did feel very moist at pit bottom. Drainage is estimated. Litter is <1 cm to absent. Exposed boulders/stones occur in and outside plot. Some of the ash have dying crowns but no EAB mortality yet. No cut stumps seen. Buckthorn could be problematic eventually.

Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Plot located in a saddle between two bedrock knolls. Plot dimension chosen to minimize intrusion from knoll side slopes. West boundary partially on side slope of knoll and slopes to plot center at 80 degrees aspect and 10 degree slope. Considerable hare and deer browse. Soil pit dug at center of plot because perimeter was too ecotonal. Some parts of plot with thin humus but mostly absent. <1% exposed rock: stones in SE corner. Soil horizons: A (10YR 2/1), Bw (7.5YR 2.5/2) with cobbles and gravels (<15% and 15-35% respectively). Possible AB horizon below A. Groundcover is monotypic with abundant bracken fern and bush honeysuckle.

Other permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Original plot was surveyed due to presence of Dicentra observed by Lynden Gerdes. Current plot did not capture species because time of year was too late for this spring ephemeral species. Plot occurs near Superior Hiking Trail on N boundary and ephemeral stream on S boundary at the base of Mt. Trudee. Plot occurs both on low (8 deg. at the north boundary) and toe (3 deg. - majority) slopes. Soil horizons: A (7.5YR 2.5/1), Bt1 (Co/Gr: 1/0); 5YR 4/4), Bt2 (Gr/Co: 2/0; 5YR 4/4). Bt horizons distinguished by the high gravel component of Bt2. Drainage estimated, could not dig beyond 34 cm. Fine root layer in wormed mull seen and castings seen. Wormed mull and A-horizon with high organic material that nearly approaches sapric muck consistency. Bt horizons distinguished due to gravelly nature of Bt2.

Additional plot markers: corner stakes and tree tags. Plot slope follows SE drainage but also slopes to stream to the SW and S. Slope is imperceptible on the ground. Lots of windthrown cedar and white spruce. Shrubby patches occur under openings. Hardwood understory component is higher than in original plot. Very old cut stumps seen occasionally but no recent cutting. Coarse woody debris decay is variable and diverse. Soil horizons: sapric muck over Bhg silt loam w/high organics (N2.5/). Slight tinge of bluish-green in Bhg. There would be expected Superior lobe till beneath, but soil pit started filling with water. Water table measured at 39 cm but soil saturated at 25 cm below surface. Bhg is close to a SiCL but high organics prevents easy ribbon texturing. Standing water present in hollows, but majority of plot with no surface water. Some flowing water was seen underfoot in hollows.

Additional permanent markers: corner stakes and tree tags. Plot is near Manitou River and hiking trail downslope. No cutting seen. Abundant and variably-sized and variably-decayed coarse woody debris mostly of cedar and yellow birch. Giant white pine occurs 15 m outside of plot. Soil horizons: E (7.5YR 4/2), EB (5YR 4/2), 2Bw1 (5YR 5/4), 2Bw2 (Co/Gr: 0/0; 5YR 4/4). Some exposed boulders/stones at north corner. Soil is a loamy mantle over slightly coarser Superior lobe sandy loam till. Excavation of soil pit stopped by large angled stone/boulder at 69 cm. No worms were mentioned in original survey but worming evident now.

Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. There are more loose rocks towards downslope side of plot. Upslope, plot is more homogenous with conifers, denser balsam, and less forb cover. Also, nearly all rocks are moss covered. Abundant blowdown and canopy openings. No cutting seen. Groundcover diversity appears greater than in original survey; however, less Vaccinium and lichen cover. Deer scat observed as well as abundant hare browse. Plot is close to road and parking. Soil horizons: A (7.5YR 4/2), Bw (5YR 4/2), R. Unsure if hit bedrock at 22 cm - could be bedrock or just a large boulder. Very sparse needle and leaf litter. In a tip-up, Bw color is 5YR 4/4. Rock benches have exposed faces. However, truly exposed rock is not 15% as was recorded in original survey. Charcoal seen in organic layer.

Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Plot has complex slopes but there is a slight NE slope towards N plot corner. NPC seems to fit MHn35a better than MHn35b as was originally classified. Ephemeral wet hollows occur in plot as do odd ridges of low relief - unsure whether they are legacies of past land use or tree-fallen humps. Coarse woody debris and snag pool scant. Bad infestation of common buckthorn. Soil horizons: A (5YR 2.5/2), AB (gravels <1%; 5YR 5/4), 2Bw (loamy fine sand; gravels <1%; 5YR 4/4), R. Soil appears to be an eolian loamy mantle over a loamy fine sand outwash/alluvium from past higher Lester River stage? Some moss-covered stones occur on surface, <1% cover.

Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Plot appears more mesic than FDn43b2 should be, but alternative classification uncertain. Deer browse is severe; deer trail traverses south side of plot. No recent cutting or stumps seen. Coarse woody debris sizes generally <20 cm paper birch and differs from original survey stating there were medium-large aspen CWD. There are some 20-30 cm balsam fir CWD, however. Soil horizons: A (SL; 5YR 2.5/2), Bw (COSL; 5YR 4/4), 2Bw1 (LCOS; Co/Gr: 0/0; 5YR 4/4), 2Bw2 (FSL; 5YR 5/4). Exposed rock <1% with moss-covered boulders. Soil development possibly glacial Lester River depositing fine alluvium, then stratified LCOS, then Superior lobe till on top with abundant cobbles. Concentrations seen at 62 cm along with fine textures of 2Bw2 - noticeably finer sands slow down water percolation.

permanent_plot_type_description: ex. metal tag on nearby tree
remarks: Only permanent marker is one tree tag at SW corner. Slope of plot is 7% within plot (estimated); upwards of 15-20% slope outside of plot sloping to the lake. Exposed rock is 95%; only some of the shrubs completely cover cobbles underneath. Partially vegetated plot, almost none on east half (downslope). Plot located on highest ridge (upper slope and crest) before land slopes back down to FPn73 to the west. Plot exhibits much less Rubus idaeus and total cover than original survey. No woody debris or signs of human disturbance.

npc_type_name: Paper Birch - Sugar Maple Forest (North Shore)
remarks: Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Plot located about 45 m NW of original plot location (as seen in ArcGIS) to capture even-age paper birch with co-dominant sugar maple. Iron deposits made for difficult plot setup. Sparse CWD, only small to medium paper birch logs. Outside of plot to the SE are large yellow birch and denser sugar maple regen. No recent cutting or other human disturbance seen despite proximity to Matt Willis trail. Soil horizons: Bw1 (fine loam; 5YR 4/4), Bw2 (SL; Co/Gr: 2/0; 5YR 5/4). No worms seen, but they are present due to castings. Worm rank 3 elsewhere beyond soil pit; worm impact is patchy. Moder humus at soil pit with nice root fibers at top and "silty-greasy" gray-black at the bottom. A-horizon, if present, is thin. Bw2 seems cemented Superior lobe till.

No permanent markers possible. Plot sampled immediately after cessation of heavy morning rains. Wet pools up to 11 cm deep. These wet pools are dry normally. 99% cover of exposed rock includes those that are lichen covered. Forbs and graminoids primarily growing in rock crevices. Plot with variable aspects but generally level. High foot traffic and lichen trampling. Weedy species present.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Current plot located on lower slope of terrace plus part of old back channel of Gooseberry River. Plot is within 20 m of Superior Hiking Trial to the north. Plot slopes up to the SE to FDn43. Slope is up to 6 deg. from S boundary to plot center. Slope is 1-3% within terrace. Unlike original survey, no part of plot is 0% slope. No cut stumps seen; some CWD but very few snags. Soil horizons: A (5YR 2.5/2), Bw (2.5YR 4/4), 2Bt (2.5YR 5/4), 3C (2.5YR 4/4). A-horizon with abundant worm castings. Discontinuous charcoal layer in Bw horizon. Possible progression of deposition: 1) Superior lobe till with gravels; 2) low-energy, standing water fine SiCL alluvial or lacustrine deposition; 3) high-energy, flood deposition of LS; 4) aeolian derived loam at the top. Drainage estimated.

Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Landscape is undulating-uneven. No wet pools present though plot occurs in small depression. Slopes SW and SE towards center of plot, where alder is densest. Wettest area occurs just outside plot to the E. Only surface rock is from overturned cedar exposing some large stones. Many old stumps occur, perhaps of cedar. Some cedars are raised on humps of buttressed roots. Low to no conifer regen due to heavy deer browse. Black ash is stunted too after repeated browse. Very little CWD and snags. Soil horizons: A (5YR 4/2), AB (5YR 4/2), 2Btg (2.5YR 5/4), 2C (2.5YR 4/4). 2Btg has less even red coloration than 2C and presence of cobbles. It also has redox depletions. 2C was nicely moist and easy to texture and had even red coloration. A & AB likely aeolian derived while 2Btg and 2C are till/lacustrine origin.

permanent_plot_type_name: Nails with washers in all four corners
remarks: Permanent markers consists of 4 corner stakes and 2 tree tags at SW & NW corners. Plot setup difficult due to iron. NE plot corner located in active ant colony. Plot straddles upper bedrock saddle that slopes steeply to the south. West plot side begins to grade into birch woodland. East plot side, towards Lake Superior, has more exposed bedrock and sparser vegetation. Plot exhibits multiple slopes but steepest is from rock ledge on the north boundary towards center of plot. Depth to bedrock ranges from 0 to 6 cm. 8% exposed bedrock with crustose lichen. Heavy deer browse, many shrubs hedged. Soil occurs primarily in rock crevices and in bedrock saddle. Dark aeolian loam is 2/2 or 2/1 in value/chroma and with worm castings. Did not observe charcoal in soil sample. The thin veneer of soil likely holds just enough moisture for some of the wetter species observed.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Lobaria pulmonaria lichen seen on ash trunk. Slope is steepest from NE corner to center of plot (SW), but multiple slopes exist as plot sits in a bowl between successive river levees. Directly south of plot 10 m away, sits a riser sloping up to an old river levee formed from abandoned oxbow channel (seen from LIDAR). Soil horizons: Bw (COS; 7.5YR 4/2), 2Btg (fine SCL; 5YR 4/2), 3C (LCOS; 5YR 4/4). Plot exhibits varying soil at the surface. At the lowest elevation, in between taller levees, clay occurs at the surface. At the soil pit, on top of levee, coarse stratified sand from high-energy flooding overlays either fine lacustrine from stagnant water or dense till, and this sits on top a gravelly loamy coarse sand C-horizon, presumably derived from another flooding or outwash event. Redox features are difficult to discern. 2Btg likely perches spring flooding, but coarse sands drains rapidly.

npc_type_name: Black Ash - Aspen - Balsam Poplar Swamp (Northeastern)
remarks: Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Plot sits on a terrace above the Gooseberry River. It slopes steeply down to the river and Superior Hiking Trail to the north. A drier NPC occurs at the shoulder of this terrace just north of the plot. Plot is generally flat but there is a greater landscape slope from the SE to the NW. North half of plot is more open with graminoid cover and appears to pool more often or for longer duration during the spring. Southern half is more shrub covered. Deer trail crosses through north half of plot. Hedging seen on vegetation. Cut stumps observed. CWD and snags present but are all aspen and none are of large sizes. No conifer representation in the overstory or regeneration strata. Soil horizons: A (very fine loam; 5YR 4/2), Bhg (very fine clay; 5YR 5/6 - concentrations, 7.5YR 4/1 to N2.5 - depletions). A-horizon is almost a silt loam and is likely an aeolian mantle. Bhg with patches of orange interspersed with grays and neutral hues.

Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Trail is 15 m from SE plot corner. Plot encompasses 3 caged white pines. Original survey indicated 8 caged white pines. Original survey also noted 20-30 cm dbh paper birches. Current plot shows that these birches have succumbed to mortality and now exists as CWD. CWD and snags very limited. Heavy deer browse. Canopy is open with dense shrubs. Soil horizons: A (black), Bw (reddish; Gr/Co: 3/1). Bare patches of soil exist with no litter. Surficial boulders <1% exposed rock. Bw could be a SCL but coarse fraction is too high to discern texture accurately. Bw could also be a C due to degree of coarse material but unsure. Pit excavation impeded by dense cobble layer. Parent material is Superior lobe till. Soil was wet-saturated at 41 cm but no redox seen. I expect denser clay beneath perching up water.

Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Hiking trail within 20 m NE of plot. NPC unsure, but it is closer to FDn43b2 than original classification of MHn45. Soil horizons: A (2.5YR 4/2; Co: <1%), Bw1 (2.5YR 4/4; LCOS Gr/Co: 10%/1%), Bw2 (2.5YR 4/4; LS), 2BC (2.5YR 4/4; FSL). Lots of bare soil and sparse leaf litter. Expect SCL below 2BC as this horizon is getting finer in texture with depth and cemented together. Lithographic discontinuity. Parent material is Superior lobe till or lacustrine overlain by outwash from Split Rock River when it was historically at higher elevation than currently.

Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Hiking trail is nearby at the north side of plot. Slope is short so plot spans upper to toe slopes on north aspect. Crest is just to the south and then drops steeply 20 m from south plot boundary. Decent amount of coarse woody debris of Picea glauca and Betula papyrifera and snags of Betula papyrifera. Observed fire-charred pine stumps also observed in original survey. White spruce regeneration is good. More mesic species occur downslope at north end and where slope flattens out. Upper slope with shallower soil over bedrock. Some fungal mycelia still occur throughout wormed A-horizon, but no humus present. Soil horizons: A (7.5YR 2.5/2), Bw1 (7.5YR 5/4; COSL Co/Gr: 2/0), Bw2 (7.5YR 4/3; Co/Gr: 1/0). Parent material is likely Rainy till.

permanent_plot_type_description: ex. metal tag on nearby tree
remarks: "Permanent markers" consists of 2 tree tags nailed into large drift coarse woody debris which are very liable to shift. Plot is on a busy beach with heavy foot traffic and illegal beach fires. Plot is within 10 m west of non-vegetated lower beach ridges. There are more invasive weedy species than was originally recorded. Sand grains were moist following weekend rains. Plot topographic context is both upper slope and beach ridge crest. Parent material is coarse sands and gravels.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest
remarks: Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. Plot placed on slope with some exposed rock benches. NPC could have had a fire history. Some charred wood in soil possible but not obvious. Soil horizons: AE (5YR 2.5/2), Bw (5YR 4/4). Humus is present but also absent in patches. Soil horizons are likely derived from the aeolian loamy mantle. Surface stones occur but are sparse.

npc_type_name: White Pine - White Spruce - Paper Birch Forest
remarks: Additional permanent markers: tree tags and corner stakes. NPC feels more like MHn44b instead of FDn43c due to appearance of seepage and also heavy clay soil. Some places in and outside of plot seem muckier possibly due to hill slope seepage. Very old cut stumps seen, likely of cedar. CWD present but not large, mostly of medium size birch, spruce and cedar. Birch and cedar seedlings seen on nurse logs. Soil horizons: A (FSL; 5YR 2.5/2), Bw (FSL; 5YR 4/4), 2Btg (2.5YR 4/4; Gr: <1%), 2BCr (10R 5/6 and 10R 5/8; Gr: 1%). No humus but castings <50% of mineral A. Redox seen at 80 cm as gray gravel and coarse sand inclusions 1-2 cm in diameter among red clay matrix. Both 2B horizons approach SiC. 2BCr is disintegrating red rocks. Water table observed at 98 cm; even Bw was moist. This may be a aeolian mantle or alluvial material deposited over dense till or lacustrine. Sand nodules seen in 2Btg possibly deposited from near-shore wave action of old glacial lake. No charcoal seen in soil.

Releve re-sampling project. Waypoint 006 at NE corner. Southeast corner of plot is 19m west of wide grassy trail (Chapel Grove Trail). Formerly dominated by jack pine, but most now dead, standing and fallen. Thin A-horizon of dark loamy sand over brown sand, which becomes reddish with depth. Mosses collected from tip-up mounds, but not logs. Magnets in NE and SW corners; spikes in all 4 corners.

Releve re-sampling project. Also re-sampled in 2013 as Rel A888. Waypoint 011 at SW corner or plot. Thin, dark A-horizon of sandy loam with what appears to be minute earthworm castings. Below that is 26cm of brown sand above rocks. At another spot the rock was 57cm deep. Moss collected from rocks, but not rotten wood. Magnets in NE and SW corners; spikes in all 4 corners; conduit from 2013 left in SW corner.

Releve re-sampling project. Plot also re-sampled in 2012 as A141. Waypoint 030 is at SW corner of plot. In area impacted by severe blowdown, salvage logging, and hydro-ax shearing. Plot is on north side of state trail. South side has been burned more recently with many dead leafless shrub stems. Here some woody plants of several species have branches that have died back this year--with dried up leaves--unclear why. Two large cut oak stumps just outside south edge of plot (with sucker resprouts leaning over plot). Many shrubs show some browsing. Possibly there are Dendrobaena worm castings, but hard to be sure. Magnets in NE and SW corners, spikes in all 4 corners.

Releve re-sampling project. Rel 4734 was across east side of trail. It was re-sampled on west side of trail in 2013 as A887 and marked. Today's plot used same marker. Waypoint 038 is at SW corner of plot. Cut stumps of Q. ellipsoidalis are resprouting as bushes. Snags of Quercus (and 1 P. banksiana) outside plot, but not inside. A few living Quercus trees scattered in area. Steep slope to west down to glacial river swale just outside plot. Severe blowdown in 2011, then salvaged. Stumps are charred from prescribed burning. Magnets in NE and SW corners; spikes at all 4 corners; conduit from 2013 plot left in SW corner.

Releve re-sampling project. Plot also re-sampled in 2012 as A142. Waypoint 043 at SW corner of plot. Community has more central woodland species and fewer prairie spp. than typical for NPC. Soil changes to red sand at 15cm. Plot location originally selected to represent a remnant opening in the jack pine woodland--an inclusion of UPs14a1. Now vegetation in plot is similar to larger area after 2008 blowdown, salvage logging, and prescribed burning. Less Populus sprouting in plot than larger area. Woodland condition ranking form completed, but not used for ranking because not appropriate for UPs communities. Magnets in NE and SW corners; spikes in all 4 corners; conduit pipe from 2012 releve left at SW and NW corners.

Releve re-sampling project. Waypoint 045 is at NE corner of plot. Plot at top of small hill about 10m west of short North-South segment of Matthew Lourey State Trail. Since original releve there has been severe blowdown in 2011, salvage logging, and prescribed burning. There are charred stumps in plot, including some cut. Some Quercus stumps resprouting as bushes. Magnets in NE and SW corners; spikes in all 4 corners.

Releve re-sampling project. Waypoint 040 is at NE corner of plot. Area changed by severe blowdown in 2011, salvage logging, and burned very lightly. More remnant Populus south of plot. It appears a skid trail may have passed through southern part of plot. Magnets in NE and SW corners; spikes at all 4 corners.

Typical of wet/wet-mesic prairie on essentially level terrain with subtle marshy swales. Deep moist loam.

Notes: Grassland Monitoring Team plot (Langhei SNA transect 10)

Typical of wet prairie zone in 40-acre remnant on essentially level terrain with subtle marshy swales. Deep,  moist/wet loam. Location information: SESENE32

Notes: paired with GMT4 & releve #B925
Photos taken with IPAD (GMT unit 5048)

Remarks: Typical of large bluff prairie. Upper slope of very steep 320-foot, south to southwest-facing bluff. Prairie extends nearly entire slope, which is steeper downslope from plot. Soil is mostly silt with abundant dolomite stones and small dolomite outcrops. Last burned in May 2012. Woody invasion is progressing, includes scattered Rhamnus cathartica, and some not far from the plot. Forb richness here is significantly less than on southern bluff (see EMN plot #2068), and there is much more Sorghastrum here (plot captures something near the more mesic [and/or moderately degraded?] end of the bluff prairie spectrum).(SENENE33)

Notes: Rebar buried at all four corners. Azimuth is 120 degrees for the E/W lines, 210 degrees for N/S lines. Rebar (12" long) at each corner, buried flush to soil surface. Waypoints (+/- 9 feet error) taken at all four corners. Corners laid out with a measuring tape.

Relevé corner UTMs: 626061E 4847792N, 626053E 4847795N, 626055E 4847803N, 626064E 484

Remarks: Typical of better portions of a small, heterogeneous, degraded/degrading sedge wetland located near the jct of old Highway 52 and County Road 134 (St. Cloud Industrial Park West). Phalaris arundinacea invasion ongoing; Salix invasion also. Soil is moist, shallow, sandy mucky organics over grey sandy marly clay. Thick litter/thatch. Shallow surface water present earlier in growing season. Species list includes collections and other observations from previous years in May, June, July. 

Notes: Standing water present at 12" down in soil pit.

Location information: NESWSW7

Remarks: Located in a portion of a fairly extensive seepage complex that is perched on the lower third of an east-facing ~80-foot slope on the shore of Lake Sylvia, in a zone where the seepage influence is most concentrated with several seepage outflow rivulets in and near plot, and just downslope of several springheads. Grades to sedge meadow (seepage-fed) with varying amounts of shrubs and small trees. The seepage complex is in a heavily-grazed pasture though the cows have a relatively minor impact in the seepage (wetter) zones.
  
Notes: several dead Larix occur nearby outside plot. Soil saturated to surface; upper 2 cm is brown muck with abundant gritty "marl" concentrations. Below 2 cm down is black muck with abundant gritty marl concentrations.

Plot size and shape are approximate. Location information: NESESE2

Remarks: Typical of sedge meadow zones in a broad seepage complex perched on lower to mid-portion of 180-foot East-facing slope on Lake Sylvia shoreline. Trees and large shrubs are sparse to patchy this zone. Several mature Larix occur on periphery of the plot (both up and down slope). Tall hummocks are predominant feature here. Seepage is diffuse this zone, with direct seepage influence more concentrated upslope near several springheads. Heavily grazed pasture surrounds the wetland but cows have a relatively minor impact in the wetter zones. Soil profile is exposed at the lake shore (due to bad erosion from cattle trampling) 15 m downslope where a buried marl zone and marl-encrusted rocks are visible in the profile. Cows contribute to major erosion where the seepage blanket meets the lake margin. Substrate is moderately buoyant, wet to the surface, with occasional shallow pools between hummocks. Muck over peaty muck, gritty concretions throughout.

Location information: NESESE2
Large hummocks at base of sedges. Photos N, E, S, W and SW marker looking NE.
Some vegetation has been browsed, especially Silphium perfoliatum. Soil saturated at surface, a few hollow spots with standing water approx. 2 inches deep. Carex hummocks were found throughout.

Surrounded by dominant Phragmites. Some Rhamnus cathartica. Found a stake in the releve plot with tag "30." Soil saturated at surface, no standing water. Nearby channels present downslope. Took photo near our center.

Basin between shrub "ridge", Carex lasiocarpa, hummocks tall - up to 2.5 feet. Many many hummocks dominated by Carex sterilis. Scattered others dominated by Muhlenbergia glomerata. Very diverse flora in and outside the plot. Shrubby site in  __  of fen where there are still some open marly pools, shrubs average 1 meter tall.

Photo points from looking all directions. Water samples taken. Moss transect complete!

The marl pools are between cattails to the West and a shrub line (mainly Betula pumila) to the right. Releve is typical of the marl pools on this site - low in stature. About 75% of releve is short sedges mixed with marl pools full of Utricularia. The Triglochins were well mixed with the (cf) Rhynchospora capillacea.

Releve taken in mix of shrubby/cattail edges and open area with lots of water between the lew hummocks. Site burned in wildfire in 2015. "Classic fen". Heavily dominated by graminoids. Forbs mainly below.

Site is thick with Schoenoplectus, in some parts the old stalks block plants below about 1 meter above the ground. Hummocks dominated by Carex sterilis or Muhlenbergia richardsonis with Calamagrostis and Schoenoplectus filling the other spaces. All shrubs short and partly thick. Photos taken: corner N-E-S-W and random mound.
Releve representative of this area. Heavy Brome and KY bluegrass cover throughout. CD rank due to presence of some conservitive prairie species although site is heavily dominated by invasives.
Degraded. This area does not appear to meet many requirements for it to be recognized as a native plant community.

Resample of original releve #1202. Contact Chippewa NF for management history. Found NW corner pencil stake, then center magnet, re-flagged and staked center and corners of plot. Plot arranged in diamond pattern (NW,NE,SW,SE)

Re sample of original releve # 1203. Contact Chippewa NF for management histories. center management found within original area, flagging and 2 corner stakes were found. Plot remarked with yellow plastic stakes at corners.

Re-sample of original releve # 1204. Contact Chippewa National Forest for management history. Original orange flagging on pipe at plot center. magnet found at plot center. Pencil stat found at Southern cornet. Re-staked corners and center with plastic yellow stakes.

Re-sample of original Releve # 1205. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for for the management history. Found blazed tree with original pencil stake on the N corner of plot, found original magnet at plot center. Re-staked corners and center with plastic yellow stakes. Human disturbance observed at site. Some soil information: 0-4cm- 1oyr 2/0, 4>30cm- 5/3.

Re-sample of original Releve #1206. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history. Original pencil stake found at the 60 degree corner and original magnet found in center of plot. Re-staked corners and plot center with pink flagging. Human disturbance observed at site. Some soil information: 0-3cm- 2.5y2.51; 3-7cm- 2.5yr5/3; and 7>30cm- 2.5y5.4

Re-sample of original Releve #1207. Contact the Chippewa National Forest for management history. Original pencil stake found at the 90 degree corner, another found at 180 degrees. Original magnet and flagging found in center of plot. Re-staked corners and plot center with yellow plastic stakes. Human disturbance observed at site. Area looks like it has been harvested and planted awhile ago. Most recent UTM coordinates are accurate, but do not follow old instruction to locate plot. Some soil information: 0-10cm- 2.5y2.5; 10-12cm- 10yr4/2; and 12 to >30cm- 10y4/3.
Releve surveyed by A. Myers and H. Sutton. Yellow plastic stakes placed at corners and in plot center. Some soil information: 0-4cm- 2.5Y 3/2; >4cm- 10YR 4/3.
Releve surveyed by A. Myers and H. Sutton. Yellow plastic stakes placed at corners and in plot center. Some soil information: 0-4cm- 10YR 2/2; 4-13cm- 10YR 4/2; >13cm- 10YR3/1

Re-sample of original Releve #1229. Survey done by A. Myers and H. Sutton. Yellow plastic stakes put in corners and center of plot. Some soil information: 0-3cm- 10YR 2/2; 3-9cm- 25Y3/2; and >9cm- 10YR4/3.
Re-sample of Releve #1238. Survey by M. LaPlant and A. Myers. Some soil information: 0-4cm- 2.5Y3/; 4-17cm- 10YR3; and >17cm- 10YR4. Litter type is leaves and needles.
Re-survey of Releve #1239. Surveyed by m. LaPlant, H. Sutton, and A. Myers. Some soil information: 0-4cm- 10YR3/; 4-9cm- 2.5y 4/1; and >9cm- 10YR4. Litter composed of leaves and needles.

Re-sample of original Releve #1240. Surveyed by M. LaPlant, A, Myers, and H. Sutton. Magnet buried for permanent marker. Litter composed of leaves and needles. Some soil color information: 0-3cm- 2.5Y2.5; 3-7cm- 2.5Y3/; 7-18cm- 2.5Y5/3, and >18cm 10YR4/4.

Substrate mod. well-decomposed sedge peat, though quite a bit of fibrous structure still evident. Greater then 1 m deep peat. Saturated at around 30 cm. This area has numerous shallow depressions with Typha or Phragmites. Walking releve, plot boundary not delineated but cover estimated for 100 m2 plot area.

Plot sampled over an existing pipeline corridor; limited disturbance in recent past. Graminoid dominated system. limited shrub growth in portion within the corridor and dense cover outside of the corridor. Varying microtopography within the corridor. First calcareous fen noted for Red Lake county.

Calcareous fen peat dome; graminoid dominated with exposed marl pockets throughout. Narrow-leaved cattail is becoming an issue within the complex. Fimbristylus puberula, Rhynchospora capillacea, and Scleria verticillata are quite abundant in number. F. puberula is quite extensive within complex.

Heavily trampled site with lichens and bryophyles mostly restricted to divets in the rock surface.Site is located on sloping rock, roughly 24 meters SE of E-W oriented picnic table and 28 meters S-SW of N-S oriented table and 22 meters NE of large split boulder on beach. Prism factor=10.
See additional sheet for location data. Plot is narrow to conform to original Releve and includes a long, narrow rock pool.

Rock outcrop community on SE-facing hilside of Goldrock Point. Overall dominated by Cladina (Cladonia) species and low woody species. Exposed rock throughout with a few scattered rocks/cobbles. Slope 5-10%.

This plot is located around a distinctive triangular rock pool. This is apparently the only pool that holds water for an extended period. I was unable to determine the exact position of Releve #8689, so cardinal directions were used so the entire pool and adjacent vegetation was included. This pool includes a series of high tussocks of Trichopherum and gnarly/stunted Thuja. None of the species present were taller than a 1/2 meter, except the lone Alunus in the plot which was barely taller. The area was searched formany of the conspicuously absent lichens found in the original releve 8689, ie Umbilicaria, but these were absent from the plot and the adjacent areas. Some invasives were observed nearby. Quality of stand was higher quality compared to areas to the north, further upslope.
Rocky shoreline on the protected (landward) side of Sugarloaf Point. Heavy foot traffic observed at site.
Plot is located on SE-facing side of Sugarloaf Point. Overall this is fairly dry site and has experienced heavy foot traffic.

This plot is located on the transition between a cobble beach and the Populus balsamifera-dominated forest adjacent. Though mosses and lichens were a primary goal of this survey, none were present. This is partially due to the presence of wave-wahed debris in the forest which covers most of the ground. Some trails and trampling at the site. General soil texture is soil and rocks. Eleven out of 14 Populus balsamifera found live at site.

Dry/exposed rock outcrop community near the crest of Corundum Point. The plot has been oriented with the cardinal directions so that the outcrop is centered within the Releve, as directed in the original plot. Glacial (?) striations obvious on this feature as noted previously. Trampling also obvious throughout this area, but the damage appears minimal within plot.

Difficult to determine the exact location of Releve #8412. Plot was situated to accommodate a Rock Outcrop community that comprised approximately 40% of the plot as was previously the case. There are no other obvious Rock Outcrops of this size nearby.

Plot is located near the top of Palisade Head in a sloped, rocky/shrub community with some sizable rock ledges and rock faces. Natural disturbance observed at site. Plot area is excessively to somewhat-excessively drained.
Fairly open rock outcrop community dominated by fruticose lichens (primarily Cladonia spp). Trampling in the area, not particularly diverse.

Plot is located on steep, rocky shore on point just north of Crystal Bay. Plot is located near the end of the point where a fissure, which starts just north of the point, opens to a narrow rock pool which runs thru center of the plot. Human disturbance observed at site.

dry, exposed conifer-deciduous forest atop a large point into Lake Superior. Many dead/blowndown Abies throughout. Plot is located under the only Pinus that is around in an effort to smaple the same area of Releve #8699. Natural disturbance was observed at the site. site soil texture is organic.
Narrow ledge above Lake Superior, just north of Shovel Point. Ledges roughly 10 meters above the lake and 10 meters from forest.

Forested plot dominated by Abies. The ground is dominated by mosses and some lichen species with small outcroppings of rock near the NW corner. No permanent marker placed, however the NE corner of plot is an old State Park sign which was previously referenced in DNR Releve #8709.

Plot is located on the transition between a fire-dependent (likely FDn43) community and Lake Superior. Small 1.5 meter cliff is present on northern edge of plot (in plot) and a small semi-permanent rock pool is present in the SE corner of the plot. Small rock "islands" are present just offshore.

Plot is located on a rocky point which appears to be the largest (and furthest into the lake) in the SNA. Angular exposures presnt throughout with the largest one containing the most vascular plants. Xantheria and Lecanora muralis are abundant on high points.
Open rock outcrop community covered primarily with Cladonia (Cladina) species. Very little open bedrock observed in the area. Rock type at site Ferromonzodiorite, base on previous Releve.
Highest condition calcareous fen plant community, Date not reported (June 2020).
Date uncertain.
Negative for HCl
Representative wet meadow community; pools of water/hummock formation. Graminoid dominated (Carex stricta). Positive Test for HCl
Positive test HCl
Wet meadow community with few calciphiles. Positive test for HCl.
Slope 10-20%. Positive test for HCl.
Slightly different from other WMs83 releves, but still WMs83 with reduced diversity. Slope 20-30%. Positive test HCl.
Seepage wetland; graminoid dominated, not much diversity with Phalaris moving in. Slope 20-30%. Positive test for HCl.
Greatest discharge near this location in the wetland complex. Slope 10-20%. positive test for HCl.
Tussock formation with Carex sterilis. Slope 0-10%.
Becoming overgrown with shrubs including Rhamnus cathartica, Cornus stolonifera, Populus tremuloides sp. Seepage wetland with organic soils (histosols- calcareous soils).
Graminoid dominat4ed (Carex stricta) on slope, with seepage on eastern end of Releve. Positive test for HCl.
magnet buried in se corner of plot
Plot located in strip of Carex pelleta dominated seepage wetland. RCG encroaching from East outside of plot. South side of plot invaded with RCG and shrubs. Magnet un SE corner.
Plot near a seepage run that has spread RCG through the N end of plot, better quality to the south.
Releve representative of this small more open area of seepage wetland. A line of RCG and buckthorn encroaching from upslope.
Some mucky pools with areas of thin vegetation, RCG is stunted in areas. Magnet in se corner.

Very strongly dominated by Carex lasiocarpa, upslope ca. 4 m is dense Typha angustifolia, and some dense areas downslope. soil very springy peat. Marly seepage runs through plot. Not much Phalaris in the larger area. Magnet in Se corner.
New releve, down slope of monitoring wells, ground less springy here. Marker nail in Se corner of plot

Plot on lower portion of slope, somewhat ecotonal. Carex lasiocarpa dominated area upslope ca 15m. Small band of RCG and shrubs downslope. Water more slowly flowing then some nearby areas, with small marly pools dominated by spike rush.

Well developed short sedge lawn with abundant Carex sterilis. A line of RCG is ca. 6m east of the edge of plot, with only sparse stunted RCG plants in the SE corner of plot. Down slope Typha becomes more abundant.

Plot around 3 meters from current road, road project marker near north end of plot. Steady flow of groundwater between hummocks. A portion of this plot is strongly dominated by Carex interior and is a short sedge lawn. Soil is fibrous muck with marl deposits at surface.
Area becoming invaded by shrubs with a more open area remaining in the center of the plot. Pools with marl present, but not as abundant as upslope.

Dense shrubs downslope, buckthorn immediately upslope. Plot captures portion of small open sedge dominated strip (ca. 20m x 10m). Did not detect C sterilis, but looks like it's habitat. Springy soil with small open marly pools and mucky peat soil.
magnet in se corner. Plot located on narrow strip (ca 30x15m) of fen with RCG just upslope and buckthorn just downslope. Rcg throughout plot except in sw corner where c sterisils is more abundant.

NPC does not fit either subtype, though FDn43b2 is best, despite its central concept as occurring on the North Shore. Complex slope to the south and southeast. Slope % estimated visually. Slope spans both upper and lower. Lower slope at SE corner. Clearcut to the west and south. Obvious large and small cut stumps. Hare browse abundant. NRCS soil backhoe info on 10/6/20. Soil horizon progression: A, Bw1, Bw2, Bw3, Cd. All sandy loam textures were fine sandy loams. Humus treated as Oe (cobbly MPM), though highly wormed. Within SNF LTP 30B map unit.

NPC does not fit either subtype, though FDn43b2 is best, despite its central concept as occurring on the North Shore. Road is within 15 m to the west. Young stand with few surficial boulders. No worm castings observed. Bleached, mycelia-infused Oe/Oa humus. Abundant hare browse. Within SNF LTP 30A mapping unit. Drier and better drained than comparable Releve C117 though soil description indicates wetter due to placement of soil pit several meters away from vegetation plot. NRCS backhoe soil description on 10/7/20. Drainage is trending towards somewhat poorly. Toimi Soil Series. Horizon progression: A, Bw1, Bw2, 2Bw3, 2Cd.

Plot oriented at 344 and 254 degrees. Plot located near clearcuts and road. Occurs in landscape drainage and fits LTP 1 soil concept. Bouldery drainage with early-season standing water but absent at sampling time. Most of the boulders are moss-covered. Sparse litter above mucky peat layer. Good coarse woody debris and snags. No deer browse observed. High potential for edge effects due to clearcuts. Outside of plot to the north transitions to more open alder-willow with muckier pools and more Sphagnum mounds - looks more typical FPn73. NPC classification uncertain - perhaps it is FPn73 transitioning to some version of WFn53 without cedar. Within SNF LTP 1 mapping unit. NRCS backhoe soil description 10/6/20. Bug Creek Soil Series. Water table found 1 m below surface. Soil horizon progession: Oe (MPT), A (highly organic), Bw, Bg, Cg. Cg has also loamy coarse sand to silt loam textures mixed with the sandy loam.

SNF LTP 31A map unit. Plot located near road to the north and esker directly to the south. Stand previously logged. Perhaps more cedar in the past, and therefore more recognizable as WFn53a. Early spring standing water as evident by dry hollows during sampling. Worm castings and hare browse abundant. NRCS described soils on 9/30/20. Backhoe pit dug in slightly lower landscape position with poorly drained soils than releve plot. Nevins soil series. Horizon progression: O, A, Bw1, Bw2, 2BC, 2Cd. Water at the bottom of excavated pit about 150 cm below surface. Soil information refers to backhoe pit. Releve is somewhat poorly drained, and depth to redox is deeper than 38 cm, and there was no MP organic layer. See original releve data form for exact soil specifications.

SNF LTP 30A map unit. NPC does not fit either subtype, though FDn43b2 is best, despite its central concept as occurring on the North Shore. Releve plot near road, situated on topographic bench and slopes south where more boulder hollows exist in wetter conditions and intermittent pools occur in the spring. 32 year old stand with small-medium aspen snags. Few to no large coarse woody debris. NRCS soil description on 9/29/20. Toimi soil series. Episaturation due to perching of water from densic till. Parent material is ablation till over basal till. Horizon progression: A, Bw1, Bw2, 2BCd, 2Cd (See original data sheet for exact texture and coarse fraction specifications). Surficial exposed stones moss-covered. A-horizon is highly organic. 2BCd horizon is stratified with two different textures.

Large cut stumps. Poor regeneration possibly exacerbated by high deer browse. Browse was not observed but could be so severe that it was impeding most woody regeneration. Moose dung seen and lots of insect damage seen on leaves of shrubs and understory trees. Some surficial boulders present and are mostly moss covered. NRCS soil description on 9/29/20. Toimi soil series. See original data form for detailed soil specifications. Soil horizon progression: A (7.5YR 3/1), Bs (7.5YR 3/4), Bw (10YR 4/4), BC (10YR 5/2), Cd1 (10YR 5/2), Cd2 (10YR 5/2).

Within SNF LTP 31A map unit. Plot located on drumlin near trail and situated between peatlands to the W and E. Lots of moss-covered boulders and very little groundcover, especially under black spruce. Very little litter. Lots of hare browse. Some low wet spots occur with Carex brunnescens and Ribes glandulosum. NPC represents undescribed variant of FDn43 - mesic, moderately well drained black spruce-dominated. Superficially resembles FDn32c2, but floristics is not consistent with that and soil is much deeper than would typically be for woodland NPC. NRCS soil description on 9/28/20. Toimi Series. Drainage of soil map unit is MWD, but pit indicated borderline SWP. 20% of pit face with albic/spodic horizons. Parent material is ablation over basal (densic) till. Soil horizon progression: A, Bw1, Bw2, Bw3, BCd, Cd.

Plot located very near surrounding clearcut. Plot represents small reserve of uncut patch. Cut stumps and trails evident within plot. Surficial stones/boulders present. Abundant worm castings - no humus. Moose dung present. However, did not distinguish between moose and deer browse, though no deer droppings seen. There is a paucity of well-decayed nurse logs for yellow birch and cedar germination. Schizachne purpurascens limited to growing on stones near the surface. Plot does not have sugar maple and therefore is not typical of NPC. Soil description simplified: Clint Tuve 2018 (USFS contractor) described soil nearby but not exactly at releve location. Noted poorly drained and very poorly drained inclusions at the summit and some logging-caused soil disturbance. Soil horizons are a Bw over BCd with redox occurring in lower Bw (just above 38 cm).

Plot without sugar maple that would normally be typical of NPC. Trail is nearby but NPC extends throughout large area. Plot exhibits many cut stumps, many previously large cedars. Appears to have been selectively harvested with cedar-spruce-yellow birch reserves. Ground is very stony with areas where soil have eroded away, leaving stones, boulders, and seasonally wet depressions. Did not distinguish moose versus deer browse; dung seen of neither. NOTE: some difficulty distinguishing Betula cordifolia from B. papyrifera resulting in possible cover estimate errors. No soil info. Toimi Series, however - MWD coarse loamy mantle over dense till with spring perching of water.
Soils not sampled. Transect S5I4-02 crosses the Releve plot (GMT/SPICE transect). No trees. Re-survey of DNR Releve 9020.
Sparse natives in mat of poa and brome duff. Site disturbed in past, now recovering.
One of the better condition areas nearby.

npc_type_name: Red Pine - White Pine Woodland (Minnesota Point)
remarks: Undulating dune ridges on stabilized sand. Plot includes portion of subtle ridge and lower lying areas between ridges. Slope noted is average from plot center. Coarse woody debris present, but not abundant. Large diameter snag with fire scar OP approximately 10m from NE corner. Earthworm rank based on small amount of visible casting on nearby trail. UTM = NE plot corner.

Small patch community on partly stabilized dune between (and integrated with) red pine/white pine woodland and beachgrass dune communities. Litter depth varies depending on proximity to forest and exposure to lake winds. Bare sand and groundcover of moss and lichen in equal proportions in plot. Coarse woody debris minimal; primarily wind/wave distributed driftwood. Juniperus in/outside plot with major needle loss on most branches in 2019. UTM = NE plot corner.
Multi-age sugar maple- basswood forest with very little regen. Low understory, severely wormed. On gentle slope at the toe of steep slope.

Sugar maple, basswood stand with yellow birch- Mutiple-age stand. Heavily wormed with middens and castings.  {can't read} shrub layer, with some dead and down wood. A ceder and Black ash swamp (low area) is nearby.
Multi-age sugar maple, basswood with very little shrub layer located next to an ash swamp. Many sugar maple seedlings. heavily wormed. charcoal on surface.
Multi-age ash swamp in sugar maple/basswood stand. Shrub layer sparse most of plot with standing water. Sandy outwash encroaching front hill to west (eroding).

Plot typical of a 75-meter long x 15-meter (5-20 meters) wide cobble/gravel bar along the south bank of the Root River. Centrally located on nearly level bar, 10-20 cm above the present river level. Bar is inundated during typical years from early spring through mid-summer. River reach is straight here, with gentle current. Deep, coarse sand and gravel with a cap of rounded cobbles, these 1-6 (10) cm in diameter; substrate is moist to the surface. Bare (unvegetated) substrate areas cover 60-80% of the plot / bar. It has been ~5 years since late summer river levels were low enough to expose sand/gravel bars and mud flats in this type of setting.

Typical of a 40-meter long by 15-meter wide silt bar rising up to ~50 cm above the present water level on the south bank of the Root River. Plot 8x12 meters, gently sloping, set 10-15 cm above the water along a slow current reach, ~75 meters upstream from a rapids. Substrate is deep, varying from silt to sandy-silt, moist to the surface. Bar is inundated from early spring to mid-summer most years. It has however been ~5 years since late summer river levels have been low enough to expose river shore communities such as this.

Typical of, and centrally located on, a 60-meter long x 10- to 20-meter wide sand bar on west bank of Root River. Plot ~10 cm above present river level; moderate current just downstream from a moderately large rapids. Deep, moist, moderately coarse sand. The river bank here is a very large, multi-tiered sandbar (continuation of the plot elevation tier), bank rising abruptly 4-5 feet high to an elevation where it only floods during very high water. Upper tier zone is rather weedy, dominated by tall Salix interior and Conyza canadensis. Lower tier / zone (where plot is) is inundated from early spring through mid-summer most years. However, it has been ~5 years since late summer river levels were low enough to expose sand / gravel / cobble bars and mud flats at this elevation.

Backhoe soil pit description near snowmobile trail running west from Mitawan Lake Road, NRCS pit #514 on 8/5/21. Soil horizons: A, Bw1, Bw2, Bw3, 2C (2C-very gravelly coarse sand). Likely some overstory pine planted or seeded. Stumps observed. FDn43 verified over FDn33 with pairwise program (9-7-21; JGL).

Backhoe soil pit description NRCS pit #501 on 8/3/21. Soil horizons: A, Bw1, Bw2 (gravelly loamy coarse sand), BC, C (stratified ice-contact till: 90% GrCOS, 5% LFS, 5% ExGrVCOS). Slope is complex and slopes to the SSW and W. Plot drops down to drainage ~15 m to the south but without noticeably wetter species. Many snags and CWD, though mostly small to medium size of varying species. Litter consists of both leaves and needles. Thin humus with Oe with fungal mycelia. Earthworm rank beween 2 and 3. Deer browse present but not consistently impactful across area. NPC trending towards FDn32 but wetter microhabitats within plot contain mesic indicators. Likely represents undescribed version of FDn43 of aspen-jack pine-spruce common in the Laurentian Uplands. FDn43 verified over FDn32 and FDn33 with pairwise program (9-7-21; JGL).

Backhoe soil pit description NRCS pit #521 on 8/9/21. Soil horizons: A (FSL), Bw1, 2Bw2 (extremely gravelly LCOS), 2C (extremely gravelly COS). Eolian mantle over outwash parent material. Highly disturbed plot with stumps common. Recent harvest of hardwoods plus rutting from logging tracks evident. Wet species strangely occur in these ruts. Moss cover common on ground. No humus but no worms seen either, though castings present - worm presence inferred. Possible Picea glauca present in canopy - difficult to distinguish from P. mariana. FDn32 verified over FDn12, FDn33, FDn43 with pairwise program (9-7-21; JGL).

NRCS backhoe soil pit description, pit #535 completed 8/12/21. Soil horizons: E, Bs, 2BC, 2Cd. Densic contact at 67 cm is semi-permeable layer. Plot orientation at 146 and 236 degrees, parallel to logging road. Plot occurs on upper backslope and crest. Plot side nearest logging road with edge effect windthrow; stumps evident within plot - cedar or pine large diameter. Good cedar regeneration. This was likely a conifer-dominated stand for a long time prior to recent management. Possible spruce budworm mortality on white spruce. Crest of plot trends towards FDn32 due to bedrock being nearer to surface. Some difficulty distinguishing Picea glauce from P. mariana in canopy. FDn43 verified over FDn32 using pairwise NPC program (JGL 9/7/21).

NRCS backhoe soil description, pit #525, completed on 8/10/21. Soil horizons: A, Bw1, Bw2, 2BC (platy structure begins), 2Cd (densic till begins, treated as semipermeable layer), 3C (very fine sandy loam). Iron depletions begin in 2BC. Plot oriented parallel to road at 126 and 216 degrees. Plot occupies toe, lower, and middle backslopes; soil pit at toe. SW 1/3 of plot situated on a series of rising benches leading up to crest of knob. These benches appear human disturbed with stone piles on top of first bench. Slope taken from first bench shooting towards road. All pine counted in prism swing occur outside of plot nearest road. Plot with abundant small to medium diameter coarse woody debris, likely from edge effect windthrow. Birch snags common. Recent shelterwood/clearcut on opposite side of road. Nice fungal mycelia in humus with many fine roots.

NRCS backhoe soil description, pit #529, completed 8/11/21. Soil horizons: A, Bw1, Bw2, 2BC, 2C. Cobbles mixed in with the gravel in all horizons, but minor component. Supraglacial till over lacustrine (possible ice-walled lake plain) parent material. NPC ambiguity. Pairwise program very slightly favors MHn45 over both MHn44 and FDn43 though with significant score overlap. Regardless, this NPC expression is not well described under current classification. Plot situated on silt loam helps retain moisture and likely experiences brief soil saturation in the spring. Dead canopy spruce common. Picea glauca likely planted - aerial photo shows orderly rows. Downslope of plot are areas with nearly bare groundcover. Charcoal seen in soil. Cedar trees occur just outside of plot. Some moss-covered surface stones/boulders. Deer browse is more severe than indicated in browse swing samples: very little woody stems to count.

NRCS backhoe soil description, pit #532, completed 8/12/21. Soil horizons: A, Bw1, Bw2, 2BCd (fine sandy loam; densic contact treated as semi-permeable layer), 2Cd. Plot with lower micro-depressions with more Calamagrostis. NPC subtype either FDn43b1 or FDn43c. Deer browse more severe than recorded in browse swings. Almost all Clintonia fruit have been nipped off. No recent cut stumps seen. Fire scars seen on some trees. Lobaria pulmonaria observed on dead aspen trunk. High coarse woody debris of balsam fir likely due to spruce budworm mortality. Surface stones mostly covered with moss.

NRCS backhoe soil description, pit #531, completed 8/11/21. Soil horizons: A, Bw1, 2Bw2, 2BC, 2Cd (very gravelly loamy coarse sand bordering on extremely gravelly coarse sand). Topography gradually slopes down to river S/SW. NPC ground layer more consistent with FDn43b1, but high cedar component makes it trend FDn43c. Expression of FDn43c becomes stronger as one hikes downslope along Manitou Overlook Trail. Within plot, there are old mossed-over cut stumps that are moderately sized. Some occasional surface stones, mostly moss covered. Litter consists of both needles and leaves.

NRCS backhoe soil description, pit #511, completed 8/4/21. Soil horizons: A, Bw1 (fine SL), Bw2 (fine SL), Bw3, BC (iron concentrations, no depletions), Cd (densic till treated as semipermeable layer). Heavy deer browse. Worm impact score between 3 and 4 - some patchy Oe (duff) but no Oa (humus); castings >50%. Litter is somewhat thick and becomes more decomposed with depth. Charcoal seen in A-horizon. Some surface boulders, many moss-covered. Small-medium sized coarse woody debris. Decent amount of snags of black spruce and jack pine but no large diameters. FDn32 verified over FDn33 and FDn43 with pairwise program (9-29-21; JGL).
Plot captures most of area between dense shrubs and RCG. GPS point in SE corner.
Area drier then expected due to drought. One large open pool with Lemna and liverworts. Carex Prairea very abundant.
One seepage run originates outside of plot on small weedy mound and runs through plot. Plot becoming invaded by RCG from all directions. seepage run with plentiful marl.
Very nice area of wet seepage meadow. I did not locate any area of calc fen anywhere shortly around plot.
Area one of the better developed fen areas in this portion of the site. This area is more mixed seepage wetland and calc fen. RCG is creeping into the community from the west.
Area quite dry even considering drought this year. RCG cover is dense to west. This is an attempt to recapture releve 4995, but i am uncertain if location is correct, old site may be in RCG now.
relevé capturing a more well-developed area of calcareous fen with much less RCG presence around this plot.
Releve to capture one of the pockets of more well-developed calc fen at this site.
Releve in Carex Prareia lawn just North of spring mound. A deeper drainage is located west of the plot and is dominated by larger sedges.
Plot extends to shrub wall to North and captures three quarters of Carex prairea lawn with a portion of Typha dominance to SE. A mid-size elm tree is located near the south end of plot.
Located just off of well site, with shrub line on Northwestern side of plot (plot runs with topography).
Area with somewhat strange composition, seems like areas are degraded. Potentially an impacted calcareous fen, but no indicators detected in this area.
Releve on moderate size peat mound with an open pool on raised surface. this is one of the better calc. fen locations here.
Area has been impacted in the past, not appears to be recovering.

Species list indicates very good fen here, but it has been impacted by cattle using the seepage mound. Currently some areas denuded of vegetation with either wet peat soil or actively upwelling water in marl or degraded tufa pools.
Second in a line of three seepage areas, this area looks like it has gotten a little cattle action this year but not as much as the eastern mound.

Area around seepage mound appears to have been impacted by cattle in the past, large hummocks exist with large areas filled with nothing besides liverworts. Much lower diversity here compared to the two other fen pockets.
Everything I walked through here was a floating mat, and it looks like the entire area is similar from this point. Mat is very loose with some open pools full of water with a rusty sheen.
Cares lacustris dominated wet meadow with lines of shrubs, Did not detect calc fen communities near here. Water is at or just below surface of peat. this area is not a floating mat.
Releve in Carex prairea dominated seepage area, cool water at surface.
Releve near open marly pool, ground springy, mat fairly loose near shallow pool. this is the best developed fen community that I saw on the site.
Overgrown with shrubs, open areas look to be wet meadow. RCG invading in areas.
One of better areas of open dry prairie. Appears to be a history of grazing on the site. Dry Prairie grades into wet prairie/wet meadow. Brome may be suppressed this year due to drought.
Plot located in South pasture with grazing underway by cattle. Plot established to monitor condition of prairie over time and in response to management activities.
Plot established to monitor condition of prairie over time in relation to management activities and other environmental factors. Site is currently grazed and has grazing history.
Plot established to monitor condition of prairie over time in relation to management activities and other environmental factors. Site has grazing history and is currently grazed.

place_name: Lac Qui Parle 36-1 Native Prairie Bank
remarks: Plot established to monitor condition of annually hayed Mesic Prairie. This location represents attempt to re-sample Releve recorded in 1987 (#0132). Exposed rock =0.5m2

place_name: Lac Qui Parle 36-1 Native Prairie Bank
remarks: Plot established to monitor condition of wet prairie community and in particular response to woody management activities over time. UTM coordinates represent center of plot. Location selected with brush cover to monitor management controls.
Plot established to monitor vegetation changes in relation to management activities, particularly grazing over time.

Plot established to document condition of the NPC and measure future change to this Native Prairie Bank conservation easement. UTM coordinates represent SW corner of plot. Site has been grazed annually by sheep for ~50 years.
Plot established to monitor vegetation in relation to management activities over time.
Plot established to monitor changes in vegetation over time, especially in relation to management activities such as grazing and invasive species control.

place_name: Lac Qui Parle 36-1 Native Prairie Bank
remarks: Plot established in native, annually hayed mesic prairie to monitor effect of management and changes in ______ condition over time. UTM coordinates represent plot center.
Plot established to record current condition of Dry Hill Prairie at this candidate Native Prairie Bank easement site. Past grazing. Dense thistle infestation, spraying done in the past.
Plot established to monitor condition of wet saline prairie NPC in relation to grazing, haying, and other management activities over time. UTM coordinates taken at the approx. center of plot.
Plot established to monitor the condition of the native dry prairie in relation to grazing and other management activities. Grazing done on site.

Approximate repeat sample of DNR Releve #0027 (1986). Established to monitor condition of prairie in relation to grazing and other management and environmental change over time. Site grazed annually. UTM coordinates are from approx. center of plot. Surveyor monument found in SE corner of plot.

Plot located in south pasture with grazing underway, though plot area was not grazed. Plot established to monitor condition of the meadow over time and in response to management activities. UTM coordinates from plot center.
Sedge Dominated peatland. Overall landscape is dominated by non-native cattail. Its cover varies from continuous to sparse and absent in small patches. Photos taken from center of plots.

Fibric peat down to around 45cm, before the peat became more uniform (non-fibric). Peat very light and soft. Colder the deeper we went. No water, but damp. Big granite boulder on edge of area. Narrow band of cattails encroaching from the N and Phragmites to east not far away. Extremely dry summer, ditches dry, peatland only slightly damp.

Not peat; gray sandy-silt loam to >2' and coarse sand. Almost pure area of Carex lasiocarpa w/scattered areas of Typha latifolia, Cladium mariscoides,or Phragmites australis. Also very scattered areas w/clumps of forbs, esp Triadenum fraseri, Lobelia kalmia, and Lycopus uniflorus. The species list fits OPp91b, but it was not peat soil if OPp91a? Thick Lasiocarpa thatch throughout the larger area. Leaf litter was rotten and decomposing, Carex layer floating.

Rooting zone of ~72 cm before the core punched through to plot. It was too wet to collect any peat or muck with the corer. Ground had slight jiggles; much more so nearby, obviously with "dupes plot"? Area is wide open sedge-dominated complex. Thick thatch, mainly of Carex lasiocarpa throughout most of area. Litter layer from 3-15 cm. Depth of standing water 3-12 cm.

There's moss scattered throughout. Whole area is scattering or Typha dominated giving way to Carex to Phragmites to Salix. We couldn't get soil samples due to standing water. Fibric roots down ~8-inches, then loose peat. Peat not deep (little bounce). Thick Carex lasiocarpa thatch throughout most of area.

Prairie rich fen community is typical of NPC, but unfortunately typical of area. Plot location is far from community boundary, but is in relatively real, active ditch. Re-survey of original Releve 4315, 4316, or 4317.

Carpet of Carex lasiocarpa w/large patches of Muhlenbergia glomerata. Area with scattered shrub clumps. Little discernable disturbance. Fairly deep with decomposed peat. Peat moist, but no water in very dry years. Few hummocks, they have more round sides. No calcium carbonate visible. Scattered clumps of invasive cattail and canary & regular Phragmites throughout 40 acres. Most shrubs close to the ditch.
Releve done in pocket. Mostly surrounded by the Typha, Phalaris, and Salix. Site dry. Many plants, especially sedges past prime.
NPC close to ditch and road. Open fir area. No Salix within 10 meters of plot and Vert (?) is in lone plant. Very dry.
SE corner of plot is shrubs and cattails. Highest diversity on the SE-NE edge of plot. Site very dry. Sedges mainly dead and buds dispersed.

NPC type based on forbs & soils. Severely degraded, close to an active ditch. Site is typical of others in the area, but not of the OPp91 that was expected. Whole area cattail dominated, now with many classic rich fen species holding on. The majority of the of the plot/area had 6-72 cm of standing water. Plot was on the edge of one of the scattered willow lands where the water depth decreased to 6-18 cm. It was this shallow area where the majority of forbs were found. access from the north was over 1/2 mile through dense cattails. Litter type was grass 0-5 cm thick, it was a very fibric cattail/sedge plot.

Photos and GPS reading from SE corner of Releve. Litter layer is composed of grasses and decomposed sedges. Very few hummocks at site. Plot is very smooth with little roots to 30cm. Below 30cm, started getting some clay lens. Soil not damp, but not cool. Open graminoid dominated peatland with scattered low shrubs and then islands of more shrubby species.

Peat soft and cool, but not wet. ATV track through part of Releve swell. Cattail clump in East. Scattered dense Typha angustifolia and Phragmites clumps throughout peatland. Very low hummocks, soft peat with lots of fine roots.

Rocks on surface w/__ are found as Typha angustifolia. Rock near SE corner is covered with cushion moss. Open sedge meadow area w/many stands of shrubs, Typha angustifolia, Phalaris/Phragmites (outlet)? Floats/strings visible w/higher lines Shrubs/Phalaris areas.

N-central portion on TNC inholding on W side of Beaches WMA. Rich fen. The Releve was placed in cover for the general area. Whole fen gets from? open areas of Carex lasiocarpa dominates to areas of hybrid cattails and native phragmites. The open fen areas are well described in releves from 1990's and those are still accurate. This releve was taken to represent the disturbed areas. Fen is moist at surface and 5-inches to water table. Soil layer 0-1ft color is 10yr22 fibric peat; 1ft-4ft 4-inches color is 10yr21 hemic peat; 4ft 10-inches color is 10yr21 sapric peat; and >4ft 10-inches is coarse gray sand- color 10yr51 with rock chunks, not rounded pebbles (poorly-sorted beach sand.
Surrounding landscape with variable invasion of non-native cattails. cattail abundance relatively low to west of stand, but increases to east of stand.
Plot with low abundance of non-native cattail compared to surrounding area.
Plot with relatively uniform species composition, similar to surrounding area. Reed canary grass limited to single localized patch to east of releve. Photos taken from center of plot.
Plot relatively uniform with a small depression adjacent to east side where non-native cattails are present.
Plot largely representative of OPp91b, transitioning into shrub-carr/marsh complex along southern edge. Landscape appears as a mosaic of these communities.

This is a long fairly skinny spring fen imbedded in this cedar-black spruce-tamarack forest. It has an open canopy with the widest areas no more then ~40-50m. Most wider areas and slightly raised areas are dominated by black spruce and white cedar with a little tamarack. Fen is in excellent shape with high diversity of classic calcareous fen/ spring fen species. No invasive species and minimal encroachment of surrounding forest and no obvious human disturbance. Standing pools and groundwater ca. 15 cm below surface even in this drought year. Near base of Bemis hill where there is a groundwater discharge creating the narrow seep that forms this spring fen. Moss hummocks (15-25cm). Layer of non-sphagnum moss >15cm deep, standing water pools 12-15cm deep.
Hummocky and uneven ground with soil saturated to the surface.
Hummocky and uneven ground with soil saturated to surface. This is a follow-up survey following June. Permanent marker is a buried magnet attached to rebar.
Hummocky and uneven ground with soil saturated to surface. This is a follow-up August survey following June. Permanent marker is a buried magnet attached to rebar.
Hummocky ground with saturation near the surface. Permanent marker is buried magnet attached to rebar.
Hummocky ground with saturation near the surface. Re-visit from June site visit. Permanent marker is a buried magnet attached to rebar.

Hummocky near well nest. Dense invasives to the north; low, fine-leaved graminoid vegetation to the south. Most of the area is lower quality except for small area to the south. Permanent plot marker is a buried magnet attached to rebar.
