Hummocky near well nest. Dense invasives to the north; low, fine-leaved graminoid vegetation to the south. Re-visit from June. Most of the area is lower quality except for small area to south. Permanent marker is buried magnet attached to rebar.
Low, open graminoid fen on raised peat dome; to south is a dense stand of Frangula alnus in eroded gullies. Permanent marker is buried magnet attached to rebar.
Low, open graminoid fen on raised peat dome; to south is a dense stand of Frangula alnus in eroded gullies. This is a re-visit from June. Permanent marker is a buried magnet attached to rebar.
Permanent markers are yellow plastic stakes at corners and plot center. Re-survey of DNR Releve 1974.
Permanent marker is yellow plastic stakes at corners and plot center. Re-survey of DNR Releve 1975.
Permanent markers are a pencil stake at center, and 3 red "J" blazes facing center. Re-survey of DNR Releve #2011.
Permanent markers are two magnets and yellow pencil stake at center. Red "I" paint on 3 red pine. Re-survey of DNR Releve #2010.

Plot is typical of a fairly broad sandbar along the inside of a large bend in the Mississippi River, at an old railroad trestle crossing. Level to gently sloping fine, moist, deep sand; dry at the surface on higher parts of the bar. Plot varies from ~6-20 inches above the present river level. Current is fairly slack here. Water level is low due to an extended drought. The upper tier of this two-level sandbar is 3-10 feet above the river (at the elevation of the adjacent floodplain terrace). Upper tier is dominated by dense Phalaris arundinacea and Salix interior.

Plot is typical of the lower level of a two-tier sandbar on inside of a large bend along a fairly slack water section of the Mississippi River. Setting varies from 0-6" above present water level (recent heavy rains have raised water level somewhat, inundating some sandbar plants). Extended drought conditions prior to the recent rains. Deep, moist tan sand. Moderately large, level to gently-sloping sand bar. The upper tier of the bar is ~4-5 feet above the river and is covered by dense Phalaris arundinacea.

Plot is typical of level to gently-sloping lower-lying portions of a fairly broad sand bar along the Mississippi River. Current is fairly slack here. Setting varies from 0-6" above the present water level (recent heavy rains following an extended drought have submerged some sandbar plants up to 3" deep). Moist, deep, fine sand to sandy-clay, with a thin silty cap in some places. The higher zone of the two-level bar is at the elevation of the adjacent floodplain terrace, this upper zone is dense Phalaris arundinacea.

Forest level. Dominated by several larger Populus grandidentata and a few larger oaks. Zanthoxylum americanum common in shrub layer. Ground layer interrupted to continuous. Pteridium aquilinum will be more dominant as season progresses. Red maple also becoming a significant component.

npc_type_name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bitternut Hickory) Forest
remarks: Mesic hardwood forest on northeast- to east-facing slope in ravine of the St. Croix River valley. Diverse ground layer. No invasive species observed. Sugar maple becoming dominant.
Cattle have access to area on rotation, overall no sig. cattle action in this plot, but margins of the wetland may have had some trample and shrub release.
Plot on seepage mound. Little to no cattle action evident in plot, but peat somewhat undercut in area of hoof action to west, some shrub release on community boundary there.
Fairly small area of wet prairie, area with a lot of duff for WP natives somewhat suppressed.
Composition shifted to disturbance tolerant species, dense duff is suppressing most natives.

Large area of oak savanna. This area burned this spring.  Plot in slightly higher quality area, overall npc is about C rank with BC areas. Poa compress is abundant through much of this area some mod. large areas of FD affinity on higher portion of beach ridge.

Native dominate a few of the slopes in this area, appears to have a long history of grazing and potentially herbicide use. Plot in one of nicer condition areas ca C rank, but overall sits is CD to D rank.
Area has around 5-15% mature oak canopy, with similar cover of native shrubs. Toxicodendron, Poa compressa, and forbs are very abundant in ground layer.
Plot 8-10 meters downslope from edge of wetland, little RCG here, lower portion of plot fairly shruby.
Little RCG in this location, comparatively. Typha angustifolia abundant below and above slope.
A small seepage run is just north of plot with small marl pools. Very springy peat where Carex prairiea dominates. Area becoming invaded with taller shrubs.

Short sedge lawn of Carex sterilis on lower corner of plot. Northern lower slope may have been impacted by past flooding, peat appears degraded in that portion of the plot and more weedy species are present there.
Larger Amorpha fruticosa on S end, fairly consistant cover of RCG through plot, ca 10 m downslope is wall of phragmites and some larger shrubs, better condition just to north of plot.
Around 10 m from water data logger, 1m wide line of RCG upslope.  This area is one of the higher condition areas and extends along slope. Open pools with irony sheen and marl development present.
Plot by last well going downslope, Area probably flooded in 2020, but not this year, some peat degradation potentially from flooding.

Plot in best area of open sedge lawn with well develuped marly pools. Area with plot is in very good condition but overall condition of the area is variable (more in the BC-C range). RCG patches ca 15 m upslope.
Soil Moist to wet in areas with Carex sterilis, Carex interior, and Salix candida. Releve taken in area that appeared to be an old seep/pool area.
Dry sand prairie within dry bur oak savanna/barrens. Releve placed near base/trough of a Glacial Lake Agassiz dune. High quality prairie, with 15-20% of cover consisting of open, exposed sand.
Releve captures calcarous fen community on seepage mound on this area adjacent to sandy old field, with floating mat to the west and downslope.
Releve in area with somewhat more carex intior and C. prariea then typical across site.

Releve to document community found on this sites and others in the area, potentially poorly described by classification?. Wet prairie plants in strange abundances on sandy loam underlaid with gravely clay. Gley/redux features in soil around 6 cm depth.
Releve to document community with odd composition located onj flatter area below beach ridge. Savannah like structure in this area other areas are nice wet prairie with even age aspen at low density.
6" sapric peat on somewhat flatter area under beach ridge. Ditch to NW.
High quality pocket within seepage meadow/prairie complex. Releve has open pools with standing water and calcium carbonate deposits on the surface. This area with shallow hummocks ca 6-8".

Resample of 8900, was A condition in past now overtaken by cattail, with cattail and bullrush upslope and more carex sterilis downslope. More open marl pool further to North and higher elevation, meander survey found R capilacea, and Cladium mariscoides.

Releve located in better area of fen pocket. Most plants on 8-12 inch high hummocks. Soil is moist, no standing water. At a larger scale, phragmites is abudant to the north, and Typha/shrubs are more abundant to the South.
Paired spring and fall releves at this location.

Soil moist but not wet. Marl pools present but dry lined with abd. Ryncospera cap. Plot in middle of moderate sized fen pocket. Cattails encroaching from downslope. Releve about 10m below upland vegetation.

Flat open lawn with squishy peat bounded by short-statured Picea mariana, Thuja occidentalis, Larix laricina. Water chemistry data from greater fen area by Michele Walker (Area Hydrologist). More photos by Shelley Hedtke (Regional SNA Management Specialist). Releve part of spring fen helicopter surveys June 24-27, 2023. Original releve by Paul Glaser, 4214, surveyed July 19, 1980 in same general vicinity but unlikely at exact point.

place_name: Forest Grove Site - Lost River SNA Pine Island SF

remarks: Representative of open fen area w/ equal amounts dominated by graminoids and low shrubs. Water chemistry data collected near SE plot corner. Somewhat quakey, avg. height sedge hummocks 8-12 cm. Moss in pools and on low hummocks. wp = SE plot corner

place_name: Myrtle Lake Peatland Spring Fen WW

remarks: In arm of beaver meadow that's been drained a long time, distinct from creek channel, drier than typical beaver meadow. Upper part dominated by Poa; lower by Calamagrostis. Downhill is center of this arm of basin with denser Calamagrostis. Uphill is about 10m more meadow with some small Abies, Picea, Populus. Beyond that is upland forest of Abies and Populus. Snowmobile trail passes thru 60m west.
In beaver meadow just above some bare mud exposed by the partial draining of a remnant beaver pond.

Small open rich fen between Larix swamp and lakeshore with ice-push ridge. Fen is about 5X the size of the releve. Pool of water about 3cm deep covers about half of the fen and half of the plot. Water trickles down from pool thru low spot in ice-push ridge into the lake. Pool is carpeted with Chara covered with beige calcium deposits.
Small poor fen that still has graminoids left from before the Sphagnum invaded, more graminoids than usual for APn91a
The releve is placed in ravine between dunes with the densest tree cover. The site is probably only lightly burned in prescribed fires. Community probably between FD and UP.

Releve near base of rolling dune feature, in the Fertile Dune complex of Glacial Lake Agassiz. Surrounding site is oak/barren savanna. Microtopography provides some slope aspect from nearly all directions. Open exposed sand 10-20%. Lichen cover ~10%.

Site is a sand/gravel bar in the Rock River, 0.5-1.5 m above the current level of the river. 40-50% of releve is open, exposed sand and gravel. Soil is gravel dominated with sand/silt. Area experienced extreme flooding in late spring/early summer of 2024.

Site is sand/gravel bar in Rock River. Approximately 0.5-1.5 m above the current level of the river. 40-50% of releve is open exposed sand and gravel. Soil is sand dominated with silt and gravel. Area experienced extreme flooding in late spring/early summer of 2024.
small peat dome in pasture managed with haying. Typical composition but hummocks are tall. Some shrub release on margins and ringed by RCG. Mucky peat.
